title: Apollo's Marc Rowan on his $1bn Mubadala deal, AI valuations and Anthropic's IPO
body: Apollo Global Management has snapped up a 10 per cent stake in Mubadala Capital, investing slightly more than $1 billion to help the Abu Dhabi asset manager grow in North America. For Marc Rowan, co-founder and chief executive of Apollo, which manages more than $1 trillion in assets, the deal is part of a strategy of backing like-minded asset managers, even those that compete with his own firm. In this exclusive interview for The Inside Brief , recorded in Abu Dhabi on the day the deal was announced, Mr Rowan speaks to Manus Cranny about the partnership and why he describes the competition between the two firms as healthy. Mr Rowan also explains why, despite the conflict in the region, he believes the Gulf carries less risk today than it did a year ago. He sets out why Apollo plans to increase its investment in the UAE as the region prepares to spend $1 trillion hardening its infrastructure and building alternative routes. He discusses Anthropic’s planned $2 trillion initial public offering, why passive investing has changed how the largest listings are priced, and how he expects a significant AI-related event to eventually prompt regulation. The conversation also turns to the credit case for AI, from chip financing to the record borrowing by hyper scalers, and why Mr Rowan worries most about short-term political decision-making in the US. He reflects on whether AI is a bubble, and why both Blackstone’s Jon Gray and Citadel’s Ken Griffin can be right. The Inside Brief with Manus Cranny is available on YouTube, Apple Podcasts, Spotify and other major platforms.

title: Putin calls Africa 'continent of future'
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Africa is the continent of the future, with a young population that yearns for a good education and a higher standard of living, Russian President Vladimir Putin said.
"We see Africa as the continent of the future, with a very young population striving for education and a higher standard of living. This will inevitably bring about systemic changes across the continent," he said at the summit of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF).
Putin also noted that Russia is promoting the creation of a new investment platform within BRICS, which will also target fast-growing markets. "In this regard, Africa should be among the top priorities," he added.
The Russian president also asked that his warmest regards be conveyed to Nigerian President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, praising his personal commitment to strengthening bilateral ties and cooperation among gas-exporting countries.

title: Putin rules out compromise on Donbas in talks with Nordic leaders – media
body:
Russian President Vladimir Putin told Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store that Russia would not compromise on its objective of taking control of all of Ukraine's Donbas region, Reuters reported , citing a source close to the Kremlin.
Stubb and Store initiated the phone call on Tuesday to urge Putin to end the war against Ukraine and convey their positions on future peace negotiations. The Finnish and Norwegian leaders also called for de-escalation and reaffirmed their support for Ukraine.
According to the Reuters source, the European leaders responded by saying that a just peace was necessary to end the war.
A Kremlin statement on the call, cited by Reuters, said a just and lasting peace could be achieved only if Russia's legitimate interests were fully and unconditionally taken into account.
Bloomberg reported that Stubb and Store wanted to take part in discussions on the future European security architecture, arguing that the outcome of the war would directly affect the security of their countries and Europe as a whole. They stressed that they had spoken as leaders of Finland and Norway, not on behalf of Europe as a whole.
The call came amid renewed diplomatic efforts to end the war. Bloomberg reported that the two leaders linked their contact with Putin to preparations for trilateral talks involving Ukraine, Russia and the United States, which were expected to take place in Abu Dhabi next month.
Earlier, Stubb described the conversation as frank and businesslike.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy also discussed the call with Stubb and Store. He said the European leaders had made clear to Putin that Russia needed to take genuine steps to de-escalate, particularly regarding attacks on Ukraine's energy facilities and infrastructure. Zelenskyy said they also discussed preparations for Ukraine-US-Russia talks planned for November at the team level.
Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen expressed doubt about the effectiveness of the call, saying she saw no indication that Russia wanted peace with Europe.
Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson was also sceptical about its prospects, noting that previous contacts between European leaders and Russia had produced little.

title: Boeing cuts quarterly loss from US$5.3 billion to US$116 million
body:
Boeing reduced its net loss to US$116 million in the third quarter of 2026, from US$5.34 billion a year earlier, as the U.S. manufacturer continued its financial recovery and generated cash for a second consecutive quarter.
Revenue reached US$24.2 billion between July and September, up 4% from US$23.3 billion a year earlier. Boeing also reported an operating profit of US$354 million, compared with a US$4.78 billion operating loss in the same period of 2025.
The sharp year-on-year improvement requires some context. Boeing's third-quarter 2025 results included a US$4.9 billion charge related to delays in the 777X program, making last year's loss unusually large. More recently, the company reported a US$428 million net loss in the second quarter of 2026.
Boeing also generated US$1.50 billion in cash from its operations during the quarter. After spending US$1.03 billion on factories, equipment and other physical investments, US$464 million remained.
This is what companies call free cash flow: in simplified terms, the cash generated by the business after paying for the investments needed to keep it operating and expanding.
It is different from accounting profit, which is why Boeing could report a US$116 million net loss and still generate US$464 million in free cash flow during the same three months.
It was also the second consecutive quarter in which that figure was positive. Boeing generated US$631 million in free cash flow between April and June after consuming US$1.45 billion during the first quarter.
For the first nine months of 2026 combined, Boeing still consumed US$359 million. That compares with US$2.25 billion consumed during the same period last year, showing how substantially the rate at which cash was leaving the company has declined.
The third-quarter figure also came despite approximately US$700 million in payments related to Boeing's settlement with the U.S. Department of Justice.
Boeing ended September with US$20.7 billion in cash and short-term investments, up from US$20.0 billion three months earlier. Its debt remained unchanged at US$45.9 billion, down from US$54.1 billion at the end of 2025.
A major source of Boeing's earnings continues to come from activities other than building new commercial aircraft.
Boeing Global Services generated US$5.57 billion in revenue during the quarter and US$1.02 billion in operating profit. Its 18.3% operating margin means that roughly 18 cents of every dollar in revenue remained as operating profit.
The division includes activities such as aircraft maintenance and modifications, spare parts, training and other support for commercial and military customers.
Boeing Defense, Space & Security also returned a profit. Revenue increased 15% to US$7.94 billion and operating profit reached US$492 million, compared with US$114 million a year earlier. The result included a US$252 million gain from the sale of Boeing's stake in HRL Laboratories.
The contrast is substantial at Boeing Commercial Airplanes. The division delivered 161 aircraft during the quarter and generated US$10.72 billion in revenue, but still posted an operating loss of US$697 million.
That business will be examined separately by Air Data News , as its results include changes in production rates, the delivery mix and costs affecting the 737 and 787 programs.
For Boeing as a whole, the value of orders awaiting delivery or completion reached a record US$745 billion at the end of September, up from US$715 billion just three months earlier. More than 6,300 commercial aircraft accounted for US$612 billion of that backlog.
The company's financial recovery has also allowed it to reduce debt. Boeing ended 2025 with US$54.1 billion in debt, which had fallen to US$47.2 billion after the first quarter and US$45.9 billion by June. It remained at that level at the end of September.

Apple is bringing an AI assistant to its suite of productivity apps , including Keynote, Pages, and Numbers. The assistant, which is built on AI models from Apple and OpenAI, can understand a document’s context to perform tasks like designing, animating, and refining slides in Keynote.
In Pages, Apple says the AI assistant can draft, restructure, and tweak written content. It can also calculate, visualize, and organize data in Numbers, while suggesting chart types and building custom tables.
Keynote, Pages, and Numbers now support the Model Context Protocol on macOS 27 or later, allowing third-party AI agents to plug into the apps. The AI assistant is rolling out in beta to devices compatible with Apple Intelligence. It works on devices running iOS 27, iPadOS 27, or macOS 27 or later.
Several other updates are coming to Apple’s creative apps as well, with Pixelmator Pro introducing a Generate Fill feature that allows you to edit part of an image by describing the changes you want to see. There’s also a redesigned Browser on Mac that uses on-device AI to automatically analyze, classify, and tag added sounds.
Apple is launching an update to Final Cut Pro, too, which brings templates, graphics, titles, and transitions directly into the app through MotionVFX. Apple is also building the Content Hub directly into Final Cut Pro, featuring a library of stock videos, photos, and backgrounds. title: Russia for wider consultations within GECF regarding crisis situations — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Gas-exporting nations need to expand consultations concerning crisis situations in the market and threats to infrastructure, as well as coordinate approaches to supply operations, Russian President Vladimir Putin said at a summit of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF).
"In the gas sector, too, we need to establish our own effective mechanisms for cooperation. In this regard, we propose expanding consultations within the framework of our forum concerning crisis situations in the gas market, in order to assess risks - including physical threats to gas infrastructure - in a timely manner, and to coordinate approaches to carrying out supplies," he said.
The Russian leader cited OPEC+ countries as an example, noting that their joint actions provided for predictability of the market situation and stable supply quantities in the oil market.

title: State closes case against Wontumi, two others over alleged illegal mining
body: The prosecution has closed its case in the trial of former Ashanti Regional Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Bernard Antwi-Boasiako, popularly known as Chairman Wontumi, and two others over alleged illegal mining activities in the Tano-Nimire Forest Reserve. The Republic closed its case at the Accra Criminal Court after calling three witnesses, comprising two former employees of Akonta Mining Company Limited and a detective from the Ghana Police Service. According to the prosecution, the two former employees testified about Mr Antwi-Boasiako’s alleged involvement in the company’s mining activities in the forest reserve. The police detective also tendered drone footage, other audiovisual materials and official communications in evidence to support the testimonies of the former employees. The prosecution said the accused persons had, during cross-examination, sought to distance themselves from mining activities in the Tano-Nimire Forest Reserve. Following the close of the prosecution’s case, counsel for the accused persons asked the court to allow him to recall the first prosecution witness for further cross-examination. The court gave the defence until Friday, October 30, to file a formal application seeking the witness’s recall. The case has been adjourned to November 4 for the court to hear the application. The allegations against Mr Antwi-Boasiako and the other accused persons are yet to be determined by the court.

title: Bayelsa suspends oil firm’s land acquisition over fatal community dispute
body:
The Bayelsa State Government has directed the operator of Oil Mining Lease 29 (OML 29) to suspend all land acquisition activities in Brass Local Government Area of the state.
The directive followed a violent land dispute that claimed one life.
The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that OML 29 is operated by Nembe Exploration and Production Company Ltd.
The company was formerly known as Aiteo Exploration and Production Company, an indigenous oil firm which acquired the oil block following Shell’s divestment in 2014.
This is contained in a statement from Ebiuwou Koku-Obiyai, Bayelsa’s commissioner for information, orientation and strategy, on Tuesday in Yenagoa.
She, however, said the police had restored peace in the affected area.
According to her, the dispute involved Dieama and Okpoama communities and resulted in several persons sustaining severe injuries.
The commissioner said Governor Douye Diri of Bayelsa directed the oil firm to stop all land acquisition activities and processes until further notice.
She added that the governor also urged communities involved, particularly their youths, to maintain peace and avoid actions capable of escalating the dispute.
The commissioner said the government restated its commitment in ensuring a peaceful resolution of the crisis, while appealing to all parties to cooperate with efforts to restore lasting peace in the affected communities.

title: Volume of components for UAVs made in Russia up 80% year-to-date — PM
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. The volume of components for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) produced in Russia climbed by 80% in the first nine months of this year, Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin said.
"A separate national project is dedicated to unmanned aerial systems," he said during a government strategic session focused on technological leadership, adding that Russia is "rapidly continuing to build its capabilities within the framework [of this national project]." "The number of components listed in the Russian registry already grew by almost 80% in the first nine months of this year," the premier added.
"The volume of high value-added products being manufactured is increasing, as is the production of devices," he noted.

title: Tinubu Seeks NASS Approval For $20.5bn, €1.45bn Supplementary Borrowing Plan
body: President Bola Tinubu has written to the National Assembly seeking approval for the Federal Government’s 2026–2027 supplementary external borrowing plan. The plan, valued at $20.5 billion and €1.45 billion, is intended to fund critical infrastructure, agriculture, education and other key sectors of the economy in line with the administration’s development priorities. The latest request comes amid growing debate over the Tinubu administration’s borrowing plans and the country’s rising debt burden. In April, Channels Television reported that the Federal Government increased its planned borrowing for 2026 by ₦11.31 trillion to ₦29.20 trillion, while projecting a fiscal deficit of ₦31.46 trillion and debt-servicing costs of ₦15.81 trillion. The government has faced criticism over its continued reliance on loans despite the removal of the petrol subsidy, which was expected to free up resources for development. The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presidential candidate Peter Obi warned in April that Nigeria was heading towards a debt crisis, arguing that the government had continued borrowing despite the subsidy removal. He also raised concerns about outstanding payments to contractors and the implementation of capital projects. The Emir of Kano, Muhammadu Sanusi II, similarly questioned why the government continued to borrow after ending subsidy payments, arguing that Nigerians should see the benefits of the policy in improved public finances. However, the Federal Government has defended its borrowing strategy, saying the funds are intended to support critical infrastructure and other development priorities. In July, Finance Minister Taiwo Oyedele also rejected claims that the Tinubu administration had borrowed about ₦80 trillion in three years. He explained that the increase in the reported debt stock included the effects of naira depreciation on external debt and the recognition of existing obligations, rather than fresh borrowing alone. The National Assembly had previously approved a $2.347 billion external borrowing request in October 2025 to partly finance the 2025 budget deficit and refinance maturing Eurobonds, alongside a proposed $500 million sovereign sukuk for infrastructure projects. While some economists have argued that borrowing can support development and poverty alleviation when directed towards productive investments, concerns remain over debt servicing, transparency and whether the loans will deliver tangible benefits to Nigerians. title: Saab Gripen Canada Partners: CAE, IMP and Magellan Aerospace
body: Saab plans to work with CAE , IMP and Magellan Aerospace as its principal Canadian industry partners if Gripen E is selected by the Government of Canada. Saab confirms its intention to collaborate with several of Canada’s major international aerospace firms in a first step to establish a broad, coast-to-coast-to-coast ecosystem that will build, deliver and support the Gripen E advanced multi-role fighter, should the Government of Canada proceed with a Gripen acquisition. If selected, Saab and its Canadian partners will establish a comprehensive, in-country capability for the production, final assembly, support and further development of airpower capabilities. The collaboration would also include in-service support (ISS), training and long-term sustainment capabilities. “Canada’s fighter capability is a long-term national investment. Together with CAE, IMP and Magellan Aerospace we are prepared to establish a strong Canadian industrial ecosystem around Gripen that delivers operational effect, national sovereignty and lasting industrial and technological benefits,” says Micael Johansson, President and CEO of Saab. READ: Saab and CAE Sign MOU for Gripen Fighter Training in Canada Saab has signed a new Teaming Agreement with IMP to establish a new final assembly line, for the Gripen fighter in Canada, if Canada decides to acquire the aircraft. IMP will also be responsible for electrical assembly production and ISS for Canada’s Gripens. Saab has signed a new Memorandum of Understanding with Magellan Aerospace to provide local manufacturing of advanced aerostructures, composite structures and structural assemblies in Canada, if Canada decides to acquire the aircraft. Saab has previously signed a Memorandum of Understanding with CAE to deliver advanced fighter pilot and technician training, mission systems engineering and support/sustainment capabilities in Canada, if Canada decides to acquire the aircraft. “We are proud to be selected by Saab to establish a Canadian capability for the production and long-term support of Gripen. While that capability would be established to meet Canada’s requirements, its potential reaches well beyond Canada. We see a real opportunity for IMP to produce and support aircraft for Gripen customers internationally, positioning Canadian industry as an enduring part of the global Gripen program,” says David Gossen, President, IMP Aerospace & Defence . “As a proud Canadian manufacturer, Magellan Aerospace is well-positioned to bring decades of advanced aerospace manufacturing expertise to the Gripen program, supporting the creation of high-tech jobs and sovereign defence capability right here in Canada,” says Haydn Martin, Vice President Business Development, Magellan Aerospace. “CAE has decades of experience contributing to the mission readiness of fighter pilots around the world,” says Pascal Grenier, President, CAE Defense & Security. “We have a longstanding commitment to the Royal Canadian Air Force and its training needs. Should the Government of Canada select the Gripen, CAE is prepared to work with Saab to support Canada’s future fighter force.” These partnerships are designed to strengthen Canada’s sovereign defence capability while contributing to the development of advanced aerospace and defence expertise across the country. When activated, they will add significant new jobs and skills in areas such as high-technology manufacturing, advanced materials, and model-based systems engineering. They will also provide Canada with a self-reliant and sovereign capability to deploy, sustain and enhance a critical national asset for decades to come. Additionally, Saab is engaged with a broad range of Canadian companies, academic institutions and research organizations to further develop a future defence industrial ecosystem in Canada. title: US, Zionist aggression endangers security of global energy
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 27 (MNA) – President Masoud Pezeshkian has addressed the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) in Moscow on Tuesday, highlighting that the US and Ziinist regime's aggression on Iran has put in risk the security of global energy.
Addressing the 8th Summit of Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) in Moscow on Tuesday, the Iranian president drew attention to the severe geopolitical challenges facing global energy markets, specifically pointing to the devastating impacts of foreign military aggression on regional stability.
“The military aggression by the United States and the Zionist regime against the Islamic Republic of Iran, occurring in two phases and in the midst of political negotiations, was one of the most regrettable and dangerous events against global security,” Pezeshkian stated, according to Press TV.
The Iranian president said the attacks destroyed Iran’s energy facilities and disrupted energy transfer processes, thereby endangering the global economy.
Condemning ‘economic terrorism’ and blockades
President Pezeshkian condemned Washington’s use of “economic terrorism,” including through unilateral sanctions and naval and air blockades against Iran, as well as the heavy pressure exerted on other nations to comply with its illegal mandates.
“These illegal actions have seriously jeopardized the stability of energy markets and must be condemned and effectively countered by the world’s major energy suppliers.”
Pezeshkian emphasized the far-reaching consequences of Western militarism in the region.
A call for multilateral energy diplomacy
Praising the GECF, which has been active for over two decades, as a vital symbol of multilateral gas diplomacy, the Iranian president called on member states to expand cooperation in two primary areas of “strategic governance and management” to ensure market stability and boost trade volumes as well as “technical and engineering operations” to foster joint investments across the entire gas value chain.
President Pezeshkian underscored the need to enhance technological capacities to increase productivity and mitigate the environmental impacts of gas production and consumption.
To achieve this, he urged members to translate existing capacities into practical projects, aligning the forum’s long-term strategy with market shifts and the future horizon of global supply and demand.
Iran’s energy resilience amidst sanctions
Highlighting Iran’s position as a founding member of the GECF and the holder of the world’s second-largest proven natural gas reserves, Pezeshkian announced Tehran’s readiness to play a more active role in multilateral diplomacy, knowledge exchange, and infrastructure investment.
He also emphasized Iran’s strategic location at the heart of the world’s most crucial energy corridors, offering foreign investors the opportunity to utilize incentives in the oil, gas, and petrochemical sectors without concern, reaping the benefits of Iran’s unparalleled capacities within a framework of shared interests.
Underscoring the nation’s resilience against years of crippling unilateral sanctions, the president said Iran has successfully leveraged domestic capabilities to boost its natural gas production capacity to 300 billion cubic meters (bcm).
“We have maintained our rank as the third-largest natural gas producer in the world.”
Furthermore, Pezeshkian highlighted that natural gas accounts for a massive 70 percent share of Iran’s domestic energy basket, with 95 percent of the population now connected to the national gas grid.
Concluding his address, Pezeshkian expressed confidence that constructive cooperation among GECF members can ensure the security of supply and demand, the fair pricing of natural gas, and its elevated role in the global energy basket while respecting vital environmental considerations.
He called for the active participation and collaboration of energy ministers, the GECF Secretary-General, and the secretariat staff to achieve these shared goals and navigate the complex geopolitical landscape of the modern energy market.

title: Shirley Frimpong-Manso’s ‘Agency for the Dead’ set for October 30 release
body: Ghanaian filmmaker Shirley Frimpong-Manso is set to release her latest film, Agency for the Dead , in cinemas on Friday, 30 October 2026. The haunted comedy, produced by Sparrow Studios, will screen at Silverbird Cinemas at the Accra Mall and West Hills Mall, and subsequently at other locations across the country including the University of Cape Coast campus. The film features Joselyn Dumas, Yvonne Okoro, Omari Dwamena, George Quaye, Rhoda Ampene, David Dontoh, Mawuli Gavor and Anita Erskine. Written and directed byShirley Frimpong-Manso, Agency for the Dead follows two sisters who stage fake ghost encounters in an attempt to avoid eviction. Their scheme takes an unexpected turn when they inadvertently summon real supernatural entities, leaving them to deal with a series of chaotic events while trying to close the doorway between the living and the dead. The filmmaker described the production as a departure into comedy, drawing inspiration from ghost stories and traditional Ghanaian beliefs about the supernatural. Shirley said the film also draws on childhood memories and familiar Ghanaian folklore, offering audiences a humorous take on stories about ghosts and the afterlife. The filmmaker also expressed confidence in the production’s comedic appeal, describing it as potentially the funniest film her team has made. She also acknowledged the demands of making comedy, noting that getting audiences to laugh requires considerable effort. The film’s release adds to Shirley’s body of work, which includes The Perfect Picture , A Sting in a Tale , Adams Apples , 6 Hours to Christmas , Contract , Potomanto , Love or Something Like That , Rebecca and Potato Potahto . Through Sparrow Studios, she has built a reputation for producing films that explore relationships, family, social expectations and contemporary Ghanaian life. Her previous work has earned her industry recognition, including honours at the Africa Movie Academy Awards and the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards. Beyond Agency for the Dead , Frimpong-Manso is collaborating with fellow filmmaker Peter Sedufia on The 70 Slate , a three-film initiative marking Ghana’s 70th Independence anniversary in 2027. The project brings together her Sparrow Studios and Sedufia’s OldFilm Productions to tell stories reflecting the country’s history, identity and aspirations. The slate comprises The Return of Makunse , scheduled for December 2026; Nkrumah’s Red, Gold and Green , expected in July 2027; and I Told You So , planned for December 2027. The films will explore themes including migration, Ghana’s independence and contemporary society. With Agency for the Dead , Frimpong-Manso turns to supernatural comedy, combining familiar Ghanaian folklore with a story built around deception, unexpected consequences and the boundary between the living and the dead.

title: Israelis head to polls with open wallets as Election Day spending rises sharply from 2022 election
body: Voting in Israel's 26th Knesset elections is underway, and Israelis appear to be using the day off not only to exercise their democratic right but also to open their wallets, according to data released on Tuesday.According to SHVA, the company that manages and develops Israel's national payment system, Israelis spent NIS 250.78 million using payment cards between 8 a.m. and 11 a.m. on Tuesday.The amount marks a significant increase in credit card spending compared to the previous Knesset elections.Over 25% increase from 2022 electionsThis is a 26.5% increase from the same three-hour period during the elections for the 25th Knesset on November 1, 2022, when spending totaled NIS 198.31 million.Spending was also higher than during the local authority elections on January 30, 2024, when Israelis spent NIS 226.81 million in the same hours, a 10.6% increase.The busiest minute of the morning was at 10:57 a.m., when Israelis spent NIS 2.39 million in 60 seconds, completing more than 11,300 transactions.

title: 2027: INEC chairman tasks staff on neutrality, security, operational readiness
body: …Says 13.9m voters in North-East must not be disenfranchised By Ben Ngwakwe, Gombe The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, SAN, has charged electoral officials across the North-East to uphold strict neutrality, strengthen operational preparedness and ensure that no eligible voter is disenfranchised in the 2027 general elections. Amupitan gave the charge on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, at the North-East Zonal Interactive Staff Meeting and Operational Readiness Assessment for the 2027 general elections held in Gombe State. He said the credibility of the forthcoming elections would depend largely on the professionalism, integrity, punctuality and preparedness of electoral personnel at polling units, ward collation centres and local government offices. The INEC chairman warned that administrative negligence, logistical failures, partisan conduct and poor communication could undermine public confidence in the electoral process and provide opportunities for the spread of misinformation. According to him, the commission’s nationwide readiness assessment was designed to identify operational gaps, assess the preparedness of personnel and strengthen institutional capacity ahead of the elections. Amupitan explained that the North-East engagement followed similar exercises in the South-West, North-West and South-East geopolitical zones, adding that the commission’s leadership had undertaken physical inspections of electoral facilities in Gombe as part of its efforts to evaluate preparedness on the ground. He disclosed that the leadership had visited the palace of the Emir of Gombe, Alhaji (Dr.) Abubakar Shehu Abubakar III, CFR, and inspected INEC’s zonal store and Gombe Local Government Area office. He said the inspections were necessary to establish the commission’s actual level of preparedness rather than rely solely on administrative reports from headquarters. “The true integrity of an election is not determined in conference rooms in Abuja; it is forged in the field,” Amupitan said, stressing that the conduct of electoral officials at the grassroots would ultimately shape public perceptions of the 2027 polls. 13.9 million voters in North-East. Highlighting the electoral significance of the North-East, the INEC chairman disclosed that the zone accounted for 13,965,475 registered voters across Bauchi, Borno, Adamawa, Taraba, Gombe and Yobe states. The figure, he said, represented approximately 13.51 per cent of Nigeria’s registered voter population of more than 103 million. A breakdown presented at the meeting showed that Bauchi State had 3,012,547 registered voters, followed by Borno with 2,765,165, Adamawa with 2,431,146, Taraba with 2,254,380, Gombe with 1,768,566 and Yobe with 1,733,671. Gombe State, with 11 local government areas, 114 registration areas and 3,311 polling units, was described as an important operational centre for electoral logistics and regional coordination. Amupitan stressed that the figures represented millions of citizens whose constitutional right to choose their leaders must be protected through transparent, secure and efficient electoral administration. He urged officials to eliminate administrative bottlenecks, improve the distribution and collection of Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), and ensure that logistical shortcomings did not prevent eligible Nigerians from participating in the elections. INEC intensifies preparations for 2027. The post 2027: INEC chairman tasks staff on neutrality, security, operational readiness appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Europe's birth rate hits all-time low
body:
BRUSSELS, October 27. /TASS/. Europe’s birth rate has dipped to its lowest point since 2001, with the total fertility rate standing at 1.34 children per woman in 2024, according to Eurostat, or the European Statistical Office.
The service reported that the lowest rates, below one child per woman, were recorded in 16 regions in Spain, seven regions in Poland, five regions in Italy, three regions in Greece, two regions in Germany, and two - in Lithuania.
According to Eurostat, over the past twenty years, birth rates in the European Union have remained below the natural replacement level of 2.10 children per woman, fluctuating between 1.34 and 1.57.
The total fertility rate (TFR) is the average number of children that are born to a woman through her reproductive years under current age-specific fertility rates.

title: Israel kept committing genocide after Gaza truce, UN inquiry says
body:
Israel continued to commit genocide in Gaza after last October’s US-brokered ceasefire in the enclave, a UN commission said in a report published on Monday that Israel dismissed as part of a “misinformation campaign.”
The report by the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and Israel examined violations against Palestinian civilians, including children, since the start of the conflict between Israel and Hamas on Oct. 7, 2023 up to September this year.
It said Israeli authorities had kept committing “genocidal acts with the genocidal intent to destroy, in whole or in part, the Palestinians in Gaza,” and that the situation had also continued to deteriorate in the occupied West Bank.
Another report by the commission in September last year found that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza and that top Israeli officials including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu incited these acts — accusations that Israel called scandalous.
The Israeli mission in Geneva said the latest report was part of a misinformation campaign to demonize the State of Israel.
“The attempt to destroy the Jewish state … continues today through efforts by actors such as the UN Commission of Inquiry to undermine Israel’s legitimacy and deny its fundamental right to exist and defend itself,” Ambassador Daniel Meron said in a statement.
The commission found that Israeli forces continued using heavy munitions, drones, quadcopters, artillery and sniper fire in densely populated areas during the ceasefire in Gaza.
It said the “Yellow Line” which was presented as a temporary ceasefire demarcation, was encroaching increasingly into Gaza, and becoming a de facto border, which the report said reflected Israel’s expanding territorial control of Gaza.
Palestinian authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed in Israel’s assault on Gaza, launched after Hamas-led fighters killed about 1,200 people in southern Israel on Oct. 7, 2023.
In its report to the UN General Assembly, the commission said the situation in the West Bank had also deteriorated sharply, with the number of Palestinians killed in airstrikes increasing from six between 2008 and Oct. 6, 2023, to 254 between Oct. 7, 2023, and Sept. 30, 2026.
Commission Chair Srinivasan Muralidhar said the intentional killing of Palestinian civilians and destruction of homes in the West Bank formed part of a broader strategy to exterminate and displace Palestinians.
Military operations since January 2025 have led to the largest displacement of Palestinians in the West Bank since 1967, with 34,176 Palestinians remaining displaced as of August 2026, the report said.
The commission also faulted the Palestinian Authority, saying it had targeted Palestinians who voice dissenting views and that journalists and human rights defenders had been killed and injured.

title: Elections committee chief bars UTJ from reporting voter numbers in real time
body: Central Elections Committee chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg issued a temporary order on Tuesday barring United Torah Judaism and its representatives at polling stations from reporting voter turnout figures, prompting the Movement for Quality Government to demand immediate police enforcement nationwide.The order prohibits reporting the number of people who have voted at a polling station either in real time or through periodic updates. Issued following a petition by the movement, it required UTJ to respond by 2:15 p.m.In its response, UTJ said it was complying with the High Court's rulings and was not transmitting information from polling stations. It said it had instructed all its polling-station representatives at 9:27 a.m. not to report voter numbers by any means, before Sohlberg issued Tuesday's order.The party said it had initially understood the October 22 ruling to prohibit only digital reporting and had prepared to transmit figures by other means. It claimed it learned on Tuesday morning of a subsequent decision prohibiting transmission by any means, and issued the instructions after obtaining that decision from the elections committee.UTJ asked Sohlberg to dismiss the petition and award costs, arguing that MQG could have established its compliance by contacting it before filing.The intervention brings to Election Day a dispute that has moved through the elections committee and the High Court of Justice since August: whether representatives stationed inside polling stations to administer and supervise voting may pass information obtained there to their parties for campaigning.The petition followed a report by Channel 13 journalist Yoeli Brim and forms obtained by MQG. The outlet reported that the forms instructed UTJ polling-station representatives to record voter numbers and report them by telephone to a Degel Hatorah system from outside the polling room.In its subsequent letter to Police Commissioner Daniel Levy, senior police officials and Attorney-General Gali Baharav-Miara, MQG said the order had been issued at 1:08 p.m. and requested enforcement “immediately and without delay” at polling stations throughout the country.It also asked police to investigate suspected violations where necessary, collect testimony, identify those involved, and gather and preserve evidence.Movement for Quality Government urges immediate enforcement of court rulings on Election Day“The High Court's decisions and the election committee chairman's order are binding, and on Election Day there is no time to wait,” said Jacqueline Bracha, an attorney in MQG's economic department.“We expect the police to enforce the order issued today at all polling stations immediately, so that voters can vote without fear and without party representatives tracking voter numbers in real time.”The dispute initially concerned reports identifying individual voters who had cast ballots. Systems such as Elector allowed campaigns to compare that information with their databases and contact likely supporters who had not yet voted. The information revealed whether someone voted, not how they voted.Sohlberg prohibited the practice in August, finding that information available to polling-station officials for election administration could not be transferred for party campaigning without legal authorization. He also provided for the committee to release aggregate turnout figures, giving parties information about participation without identifying individual voters.Likud challenge leads elections committee to permit identified reporting under restrictionsLikud challenged the prohibition, including Sohlberg's authority to impose it alone. Under an arrangement approved by the High Court, the issue went before the full elections committee, which voted on September 6 to permit identified reporting subject to restrictions.On September 17, the High Court unanimously overturned that permission. Justices Yael Willner, Alex Stein and Khaled Kabub held that polling-station representatives perform public functions and lack legal authority to transfer identifiable voter information to their parties for campaign purposes. The court also found that the practice violated voters' privacy. Parties remained free to contact voters and encourage participation using information they could lawfully use.The next dispute concerned whether representatives could report numerical totals without identifying anyone.In an October 14 clarification following a request from Likud attorney Ilan Bombach, acting committee director-general Dean Livne permitted polling committee members and party observers to digitally count voters and transmit those numbers to their parties, provided they did not identify the voters.Israel Democracy Guard challenges legality of collecting and transmitting voter informationThe Israel Democracy Guard organization challenged that permission. Its argument was that removing names did not resolve the separate question of whether officials inside polling stations were authorized to collect and transmit information for party headquarters.The state and Likud defended the distinction between numerical reporting and identifying individual voters, arguing that turnout figures could help parties encourage participation.On October 22, the High Court rejected the permission in a two-to-one decision, with Kabub and Justice Ruth Ronnen in the majority and Justice David Mintz dissenting. That ruling barred digital counting and real-time transmission of voter totals by party representatives serving on polling committees or as observers.Tuesday's order specifically addresses UTJ and its representatives, expressly prohibiting periodic reports and real-time updates.

title: Installation of six wind turbines completed at Vento Energy’s 43.2 MW Breti Wind Power Project
body: Vento Energy is developing the 43.2 MW Breti Wind Power Plant project in Georgia. The installation of all six wind turbines at the plant has been successfully completed, marking a significant milestone in the project's implementation. Six Goldwind GWH182-7.2 MW model turbines have been installed at the plant, each with a capacity of 7.2 MW. Goldwind Georgia delivered the project under its integrated PTCI (Project Transportation & Construction Integration) service model, providing full lifecycle support beyond installation. Notably, the Breti Wind Power Plant is the largest wind power plant in Georgia to be fully financed by a local commercial bank. The project is being developed with the financial support of Bank of Georgia. ‘We are delighted to announce the completion of another modern renewable energy project in Georgia, which will soon be integrated into the national power grid. We would like to express our gratitude to all stakeholders involved, with special thanks to Goldwind and Bank of Georgia for their support and valuable contribution to the implementation of this project’, said Zakaria Avaliani , Vento Energy Director ‘The completion of the Breti Wind Power Plant reflects Goldwind’s long-term commitment to Georgia’s energy transition. Since entering the Georgian market in 2024, we have secured nine wind projects totaling 438 MW, and we will continue to bring our integrated delivery capabilities and reliable turbine technology to support the country’s energy independence and sustainable development. We thank Vento Energy, Bank of Georgia, and all partners for their trust and collaboration, ’ said Peter Guo, Business Development Director, Goldwind Georgia. ‘The development of wind energy is one of the pivotal directions for achieving Georgia’s energy independence. Wind power generation complements the winter energy deficit and reduces dependence on imports. This area is of strategic importance for Bank of Georgia. Accordingly, by financing the Breti Wind Power Plant project, we are supporting the development of wind energy in Georgia and strengthening the country’s energy independence,’ said Bondo Tabatadze, Sector Head of Corporate Sales at Bank of Georgia. _____________________________________ Paid for by: Bank Of Georgia

title: Jay-Z announced as 2027 Super Bowl halftime show performer
body:
Jay-Z , the rapper who has helped produce the Super Bowl halftime show , is stepping into the spotlight and will headline the show himself.
The NFL, Apple Music and Roc Nation announced Monday that Jay-Z will be the featured performer for the halftime show on Feb. 14 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, Calif.
The 56-year-old rapper, who celebrated the 30th anniversary of his debut album Reasonable Doubt this year, said, “From Reasonable Doubt to standing on the Super Bowl Halftime stage, this has been a journey.”
“Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world’s biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true,” he added in a statement .
NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said he had one request when the league first reached an agreement with Roc Nation: that Jay-Z take the stage himself “whenever the moment felt right to him.”
“For several years, we’ve had the privilege of working closely with JAŸ-Z and Roc Nation, and I’ve seen the extraordinary impact he has had on the Super Bowl Halftime Show,” Goodell said.
“I couldn’t be more excited for fans around the world to experience the artistry, creativity and cultural impact he will bring to the Super Bowl stage,” he added.
“GOAT’s out of the bag,” Apple Music announced in an Instagram caption .
Roc Nation also shared an Instagram announcement with a photo of Jay-Z, writing, “Super Bowl LXI. Los Angeles. February 14, 2027.”
After days of speculation, Jay-Z is set to return to the stadium where he closed his celebration of the 30th anniversary of Reasonable Doubt , the mogul’s 1996 debut album.
The concerts included three sold-out shows at Yankee Stadium and sold-out performances in London and Paris ahead of a stop at SoFi Stadium over the weekend.
Jay-Z’s Roc Nation has partnered with the NFL since 2019 to advise on and help produce the league’s entertainment presentations, including the Super Bowl halftime show.
At the time, Jay-Z said he had told Goodell, “If this is about me performing at the Super Bowl, then we can just end this conversation now.”
“JAŸ-Z’s impact on global music culture is as profound as it is undeniable,” said Oliver Schusser, Apple’s Vice President of Music and International Content.
“We’ve had the privilege of working closely with him these last few years to bring some of the world’s most exciting and prolific artists to the Super Bowl Halftime Show stage and we are so thrilled that he will be taking that stage himself this year. We know it’s going to be an incredible show,” Schusser added.
Roc Nation will executive produce the halftime show, with Hamish Hamilton directing.
Super Bowl LXI will be the second Super Bowl hosted at the SoFi Stadium after Super Bowl LVI in 2022.
During Super Bowl LVI, Dr. Dre was joined by Snoop Dogg , Mary J. Blige , Eminem and Kendrick Lamar for the halftime show.
At the time, Dr. Dre issued a statement about the halftime show, produced by Jay-Z’s Roc Nation, saying, “The opportunity to perform at the Super Bowl Halftime Show, and to do it in my own backyard, will be one of the biggest thrills of my career.”
“I’m grateful to Jay-Z, Roc Nation, the NFL, and Pepsi as well as Snoop Dogg, Eminem, Mary J. Blige, and Kendrick Lamar for joining me in what will be an unforgettable cultural moment,” Dr. Dre added.
I’m extremely excited to share the stage with my friends for the #PepsiHalftime Show.
This will introduce the next saga of my career…
Bigger and Better than Ever!!! @NBCSports @Pepsi @NFL @RocNation #SBLVI pic.twitter.com/zn1wfJdhp2
During last year’s Super Bowl, Latin superstar Bad Bunny took the stage at Levi Stadium in Santa Clara, Calif. for the halftime show , which averaged 128.2 million viewers from 8:15-8:30 p.m. EST/PST.
That made it the fourth-most watched halftime show behind Kendrick Lamar (133.5 million, 2025), Michael Jackson (133.4 million, 1993) and Usher (129.3 million, 2024).
Bad Bunny, whose real name is Benito Antonio Martínez Ocasio, brought Lady Gaga , Ricky Martin and a whole lot of his native Puerto Rico to his halftime show.
The 32-year-old began the performance in the furrows of faux sugar cane crops, walking past unmistakable Puerto Rican imagery, including farmers in straw hats, men playing dominos and a shaved ice stand, as he performed his 2022 reggaeton hit Tití Me Preguntó . He carried a football and wore an all-white football jersey with the number 64 and his real last name emblazoned on the back.
He also brought out a list of celebrities as he sang Yo Perreo Sola on top of La Casita — a pink and yellow house with a porch, a nod to the homes in San Juan, Puerto Rico. The porch was part of the stage of Bad Bunny’s sold-out 30-day residency in Puerto Rico and he brought it to the Super Bowl to extend his hospitality to stars like Cardi B , Pedro Pascal , Karol G, Jessica Alba , Alix Earle and more.
“God bless America!” he shouted toward the end of his 13-minute halftime show. Then he gave a roll call of the nations of North, South and Central America, including Uruguay, Colombia, Venezuela, Cuba, the United States and Canada.

title: Police arrest alleged fake lawyer after 10 years of impersonation
body:
The Police Command in Ebonyi State has arrested a man, Ugwumba Enyinnaya, for allegedly impersonating and practising as a lawyer for more than 10 years.
Joshua Ukandu, the police spokesperson in Ebonyi State, disclosed this in a press statement issued in Abakaliki on Tuesday.
Mr Ukandu, a police superintendent, said the arrest followed a discreet investigation by operatives after receiving a petition alleging the suspect obtained money by false pretence.
According to him, the petitioner, David Chukwu, alleged that the suspect collected ₦650,000 from him in March 2026 to facilitate the processing and approval of a street-naming request in Ohaozara Local Government Area of the state.
He said the suspect allegedly presented himself as a lawyer with years of legal experience while collecting the money.
Mr Ukandu said preliminary investigations following the arrest revealed that the suspect had allegedly been parading himself as a legal practitioner despite lacking the requisite professional qualifications.
He added that the suspect admitted during interrogation that he was not a lawyer.
The police spokesperson said a search of the suspect’s apartment led to the recovery of several exhibits, including a Nigerian Bar Association seal and a portrait of the suspect dressed in barrister’s regalia.
Other items recovered, according to him, included purported Bachelor of Laws and Master of Laws degree certificates bearing the name of Enugu State University of Science and Technology.
The police also recovered a barrister’s robe and wig, court judgements allegedly procured from the court, and various legal documents purportedly prepared by the suspect.
Mr Ukandu listed some of the documents as powers of attorney and deeds of conveyance.
He said the suspect had been charged to court.
According to the statement, the Commissioner of Police in Ebonyi, Hope Okafor, commended the operatives for their diligence in uncovering the alleged impersonation.
The police reiterated the need for the public to exercise caution when engaging individuals who claim to be lawyers.

title: Average building cost increases by 5.1% in September 2026 -GSS
body: The year-on-year inflation rate measured by the Prime Building Cost Index (PBCI) has increased to 5.1 percent in September 2026 from 4.6 percent in August 2026 By this, building costs were 5.1% higher than a year ago and 0.03% higher than in August 2026. Plant and equipment costs went up 19.1% over the year, and were the main pressure point. The monthly change rate for September 2026 was 0.03 percent. In press release, the Ghana Statistical Service explained that the index tracks the prices of key construction inputs such as building materials, labour, and equipment over time, indexed to the 2023 base year, which is set at 100. “In simple terms, the PBCI shows whether it is becoming more expensive or cheaper to build compared to a previous period. PBCI is used by key stakeholders including investors, developers, contractors, and policy makers to negotiate contracts, adjust bids, budget effectively, and monitor inflation trends in the building sector”, it said. At the group level, the Labour group inflation rate recorded a year-on-year inflation rate of -3.2 percent in September 2026 down from -2.9 in August 2026. The Material group recorded a year-on-year inflation rate of 6.5 percent in September 2026 up from 5.8 percent in August 2026 while the Plant group recorded a year-on-year inflation rate of 19.1 percent up from 17.9 percent in August 2026. At the sub-group level, Reinforcement recorded the highest year-on-year inflation rate of 29.0 percent while the sub-group Steel recorded the lowest year-on-year inflation rate of -8.8 percent. Fourteen sub-groups out of the 23 sub-groups recorded inflation rate above the national average of 5.1 percent. September 2026 PBCI Bulletin Download

title: Gold Fields’ US$4.26bn local spend puts mining value retention in focus
body: Gold Fields Ghana Limited has spent US$4.26 billion on goods and services over five years, including US$2.59 billion in its host communities, putting the spotlight on how mining procurement can translate into lasting economic opportunities for local businesses. The company says 93% of its procurement was undertaken in-country over the same period, with almost 100 community vendors involved in its supply chain. It has tracked host community procurement since 2016 as part of efforts to retain and share more of the economic value generated by its operations with communities hosting its mines. The figures underline the scale of mining-related expenditure flowing through the domestic economy. Mining operations generate significant demand for goods and services, much of it channelled through subcontracted operational services. Transport, fuel, power, maintenance, protective equipment and other supplies create opportunities for domestic businesses, although the extent of the wider economic benefit depends on how much value is retained locally. Gold Fields says its commitment to contracting Ghanaian-owned and controlled businesses predates the introduction of Ghana’s current mining local-content regulations. In 2010, the company contracted a wholly Ghanaian-owned fuel supplier, Zen Petroleum, ahead of the introduction of the Minerals and Mining (Local Content and Local Participation) Regulations, 2020 (L.I. 2431). It also engaged Genser Energy, a Ghanaian-founded and controlled business, as an independent power producer to supply electricity to its Tarkwa and Damang mines. Western Transport Services Limited (WTS), a Ghanaian-owned company, was contracted to provide transportation services at both sites. These examples illustrate how mining procurement can support Ghanaian businesses in providing essential operational services. They also highlight the importance of examining local procurement beyond the headline expenditure figures, including the ownership of suppliers, the nature of goods and services supplied and the capacity created within the domestic economy. Gold Fields’ procurement record will be among the issues providing context for the company’s Suppliers Conference 2026, scheduled for October 28 and 29 under the theme, “Partnership for Enduring Value: Building Resilient Supply Chains Beyond Mining.” The conference is expected to bring together suppliers, business operators and other stakeholders to discuss ways to strengthen local participation and build supply chains capable of meeting the operational demands of the mining industry. The involvement of almost 100 community vendors in Gold Fields’ supply chain provides an existing base from which further local enterprise development could take place. The country’s local-content framework provides a regulatory basis for increasing domestic participation in the mining supply chain. L.I. 2431 sets out requirements aimed at promoting Ghanaian participation in the supply of goods and services to the industry. The suppliers conference is expected to address procurement practices, opportunities for women-owned enterprises, environmental, social and governance considerations, safety and supply-chain disruptions. These issues reflect the need to balance reliable mining operations with broader expectations around local participation and responsible business practices. Disruptions in the supply of critical goods and services can affect production schedules and operating costs. A stronger domestic supplier base can provide additional sources of supply, while giving local businesses a greater stake in the industry’s performance. Gold Fields has also been involved in efforts to support small-scale mining formalisation in collaboration with the World Gold Council, as well as discussions around the potential relinquishment of part of the Tarkwa concession. The company’s wider community engagement includes development initiatives such as the Apinto Government Hospital project. These activities reflect different aspects of the relationship between mining operations and host communities, from economic participation and land access to social infrastructure. Procurement, however, offers a direct channel through which mining companies can engage domestic businesses and influence the distribution of economic opportunities. Gold Fields’ reported US$4.26 billion in-country expenditure and US$2.59 billion in host communities provide a measure of the economic activity associated with its operations.

title: Kryvyi Rih HOAs can receive backup power equipment grants from URCS
body:
Homeowners associations (HOAs) in Kryvyi Rih will be able to receive grant support to purchase backup power equipment from the Ukrainian Red Cross Society (URCS).
"The Ukrainian Red Cross, with the support of the Norwegian Red Cross, is launching a grant support program for HOAs in Kryvyi Rih. The funding will help acquire backup power equipment to ensure the operation of basic in-house systems during prolonged power outages," the URCS reported on Facebook .
The application period began on October 26 and will last through November 15, 2026.
HOAs registered as legal entities that manage apartment buildings in one of the three districts of Kryvyi Rih - Pokrovskyi, Metalurgijnyi, and Saksahanskyi - are eligible to participate in the program.
A single HOA may submit several applications if it manages multiple buildings. A separate application and a corresponding packet of documents must be prepared for each building.
Participation in the program is competitive: applications will be checked for compliance with the terms, and winners will be determined based on the selection results. Submitting an application does not guarantee funding.
The grant amount depends on the height of the building: UAH 100,000 for up to 6 floors inclusive; UAH 200,000 for 7 to 16 floors; UAH 300,000 for 17 floors and above, or for buildings from 4 to 16 floors inclusive with three or more entrances.
Grant funds can be used to purchase gasoline, diesel, or gas generators, inverters, batteries, solar panels, and high-voltage battery control units.
Equipment installation costs, related materials, and other additional expenses are not covered by grant funds. If necessary, HOAs and/or building residents may cover them through their own co-financing.

title: Denmark will strike deep. New cruise missiles
body:
Denmark intends to acquire Joint Strike Missiles for F-35 fighter jets and land-launched Anthem cruise missiles. The new weaponry is designed to enable precision strikes at long distances, including deep within enemy territory. Copenhagen views these capabilities as a reinforcement of national defence and NATO deterrence.
The Danish Ministry of Defence announced the decision on 22 October, presenting the choice of weaponry intended for long-range precision strikes. The Joint Strike Missile (JSM) by Norway’s Kongsberg is set to expand the combat capabilities of F-35 aircraft, while the Anthem cruise missile from the American firm Covenant will allow for target engagement from land-based launchers. In this way, Denmark is developing two complementary methods for using long-range weapons, combining aviation capabilities with land-deployed armament.
Defence Minister Jeppe Bruus noted that the new weaponry is intended to increase Denmark’s defensive capacity and strengthen its contribution to NATO deterrence. According to the ministry, the ability to strike targets deep within enemy territory is intended to discourage aggression and enable a response in the event of an attack. The procurement also responds to allied demand for precision long-range weaponry.
As the ministry pointed out, the purchases are being carried out based on the Defence Minister’s recommendations. However, the selection of the designs does not signify the conclusion of the procurement procedures – the scope and value of the future JSM contract remain subject to negotiation.
The Norwegian defence group Kongsberg reported that Denmark is the seventh country to select JSM missiles. It thus joins Australia, Canada, Germany, Japan, Norway, and the United States. The selection of the weaponry does not yet constitute a contract – the scope and value of the order will be determined in negotiations with the Danish customer. The manufacturer announced it would publish details following the signing of the contract.
The JSM has been adapted for carriage in the internal weapon bays of the F-35A. This allows the fighter to carry out missions with long-range missiles without the need to place them on external hardpoints, thereby maintaining its low observability. The JSM’s design utilises technologies developed for the Naval Strike Missile. According to Kongsberg’s data, the missile reaches subsonic speeds, and its range exceeds 350 km.
Guidance is provided by inertial and satellite navigation systems, supported by a mission planning system. The latter enables route plotting that accounts for topography, allowing the missile to traverse it at low altitude. In the terminal phase of flight, an infrared imaging seeker automatically recognises the target. Strike precision results from the interaction of these systems at successive stages of the mission – from navigation along the planned route to target recognition and guidance in the final phase.
The Anthem cruise missile from the American company Covenant is intended to provide Denmark with the capability to conduct precision strikes from land-based launchers against targets located in the enemy’s rear. Its acquisition will complement the capabilities that JSM missiles carried by the F-35 are to provide for Danish aviation. Copenhagen is thus developing two complementary strike assets, enabling the targeting of distant objectives from both air and land. According to the Ministry of Defence’s intent, the ability to strike deep into enemy territory is meant to increase the credibility of deterrence, signalling that any aggression would meet a response extending beyond the defence of its own territory.
Denmark has selected Covenant's Anthem long-range precision strike system. 🇩🇰 We're proud to partner with DALO and @Forsvarsmin to strengthen Denmark's defence capabilities and advance affordable, scalable deep precision strike capabilities across Europe and @NATO. https://t.co/nySB8ZmHQy
This represents another stage in strengthening Danish coastal defence. NSM missiles play a key role in this, with an additional batch ordered under a contract announced by Kongsberg on 19 October. The agreement, worth approximately 400 million Norwegian kroner (approx. £28.5 million / €34 million), extends an agreement concluded with Norway in 2025 and is being implemented as part of government-to-government cooperation. Denmark has also ordered the NSM for its frigates, developing capabilities to combat enemy vessels from both sea and land-based launchers.
Regarding the JSM, the next step will be to agree on the scope and value of the contract in negotiations between Kongsberg and the Danish recipient. Their outcome and the delivery schedule will allow for an assessment of the scale and pace of the arsenal’s expansion. The actual strengthening of the Danish deterrence potential will then be determined by the armed forces’ readiness to operationally utilise the new weaponry.

title: South Africa evacuation: Minority rejects claims they coached returnees
body: The Minority in Parliament has denied allegations that it paid or attempted to coach some Ghanaian evacuees from South Africa to speak against the government over the handling of their repatriation and related allowances. Addressing a press conference on Tuesday, October 27, the Ranking Member on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, Samuel Abdulai Jinapor, said the Minority had neither paid nor persuaded any of the evacuees to make allegations against the government. His response follows a press conference held by some of the evacuees on Monday, October 26, during which they alleged that some opposition figures had attempted to coach them to speak against the government. Mr Jinapor rejected the claims, insisting that the Minority had not influenced any of the evacuees to speak publicly about the matter. “Let me place on record that at no point in time did the Minority engage, pay, and/or convince any of these people,” he said. He explained that some of the evacuees had decided to speak out after discovering discrepancies between the allowances they were reportedly entitled to receive and the amounts they actually received. The Minority has raised concerns about expenditure on the evacuation exercise, citing alleged duplicate entries, payment records without signatures, missing supporting receipts and claims by some evacuees that they did not receive the amounts recorded against their names. Mr Jinapor said these concerns remained unresolved despite explanations from the Minister for Foreign Affairs, Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa. He therefore renewed the Minority’s call for an independent audit of the evacuation exercise to establish how the funds were spent and address the questions surrounding the payment records. The allegations about the evacuation expenditure and the claims that opposition figures attempted to coach evacuees remain disputed.

title: How Hubtel is rethinking AI in Ghana: Own your data, rent the intelligence
body: From the trader at Makola checking prices on her phone to the graduate in Kumasi searching for work, one question is getting louder across Ghana. Will artificial intelligence make life better, or will it take away what people already have? Ghana has placed its bet. In 2025, it launched a ten-year national AI strategy, and the government has committed $270 million to get the country ready. But for ordinary Ghanaians, the most useful answers may come from a local company that has already tried, stumbled, and found a smarter way forward. That company is Hubtel. Head of Engineering, Augustine Adjei, told the national audience during the premiere of the AI & Ghana documentary on Joy News exactly what Ghana’s AI journey looks like from the inside, and why the country does not need to start big to win. About the Digital Economy Forum The Digital Economy Forum is a national thought-leadership platform conceived by Hubtel to create evidence-based conversations about the technologies, policies and ideas shaping Ghana’s economic future. It combines original documentary storytelling with a televised debate on JoyNews and Joy FM, bringing together government, regulators, businesses, academics and everyday Ghanaians. The maiden edition tackled digital fraud and why trust matters in Ghana’s growing digital economy. The latest edition asked a bigger question: AI and the Ghana economy, opportunity or disruption? For Hubtel, which helps Ghanaians pay bills, send money and order goods, the stakes are personal. A digital economy only grows when people trust it, understand it and can benefit from it. The forum is Hubtel’s way of making sure that conversation happens in public, with the facts on the table and ordinary people in the room. Opportunity or disruption? Both, says Hubtel Asked whether AI is good or bad news for Ghana, Augustine Adjei refused to pick one side. “It is both,” he said. “Growth is hard and painful, but the disruption is a setback while the opportunity is exponential.” He compared it to a catapult. You get pulled back first, and that painful pull is what launches you forward. Change will hurt in places, but those who prepare will move faster than ever. When Hubtel tried to build its own AI Hubtel opened an AI lab in 2023, before chat apps like ChatGPT became part of everyday life. It hired skilled Ghanaian engineers to build AI from scratch. The lab’s biggest project helped the Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) catch power theft. The system flagged meters that seemed not to be paying, traced back through the records and connected the dots. Hubtel also built its own fraud detection and call-centre tools. Then the world moved faster and cheaper. By 2025, global AI companies were selling far more powerful tools for about $20 to $25 a month. Hubtel did what any smart trader does when a better product appears at a lower price. It stopped trying to outbuild the giants and started buying access. Talent Isn’t the Problem Augustine Adjei explained the decision with a picture every Ghanaian understands. “Would you want an Italian chef to cook your fufu and light soup, or an equally competent Ghanaian chef who has lived here all their life?” he asked. The answer is obvious: the Ghanaian chef. But training that chef takes time and money. Until then, you hire the chef who can feed you today while you plan for tomorrow. He was clear that Ghana’s problem has never been brains. “Talent is equally distributed; resources are not,” he said. Hubtel had the people. What it did not have was the hundreds of millions of dollars global firms spend on AI. Own your data, rent the engine Hubtel did not just sign up for a free chatbot. It negotiated directly with leading global AI companies, which were surprised a Ghanaian firm could pay at that level. Under the deal, Hubtel runs the AI inside its own systems, keeps full ownership of its data, and the providers have promised not to use Hubtel’s information to train their models. Augustine Adjei summed up the rule simply: “Own what you can before you scale.” He also shared a funny but serious warning. When Hubtel tested a free AI model and asked it about the company, the model said Hubtel was headquartered in Kigali. AI only knows what you teach it, so Ghanaians must feed it Ghanaian facts. The best example of this thinking is Hubtel’s virtual call centre. Because so many Ghanaians transact on Hubtel every day, the phones ring constantly. An AI agent now answers first and can check a customer’s order status on the spot. It works because all the information it needs already belongs to Hubtel. It is built in Ghana, trained on Ghanaian data and speaks to customers in a Ghanaian accent. For Augustine Adjei, that is the point. “AI is not a thing, it is us. There is no AI without humans,” he said. “If we are biased, AI will be biased.” Honorable Sam George backs the Hubtel approach Communications Minister of Ghana, Honorable Sam George said Hubtel’s story shows why Ghana must fix its data first. “AI models are only as good as their data sets,” he said. Hubtel had found no simple way for companies in Ghana to share data. The Minister said government is building a national data exchange hub to connect about 48 public registries, from the Ghana Health Service to the National Identification Authority, so developers make one request instead of 48. Companies are welcome to join, as long as they contribute data too. On jobs, he echoed Hubtel’s message that people must grow with the technology. “Those who evolve and adapt will survive,” he said. “Those who fail to evolve and adapt will fall off.” Bright Simmons of Imani Africa, the night’s toughest critic of government spending, held up Hubtel as an example of doing AI in the right order: use a proven global tool first, then build local. “If you don’t define your problem extremely well, AI can’t give you answers,” he warned, adding: “We should not stay on the surface.” Five lessons for every Ghanaian You do not need to be a tech company to learn from Hubtel. Whether you run a chop bar, a boutique or a small office, the same rules apply: Start with what you already have. Your customer list, your records and the way you work are your biggest AI asset. Use what works today. Global AI tools are cheap and powerful, so use them while local options grow. Guard your information. Keep control of your data and know where it goes. Teach the AI about Ghana. If a tool thinks Hubtel is in Kigali, it can get your business wrong too. Think before you upload. Augustine Adjei said his phone holds his 74-year-old mother’s medical record, and he would not run it through a public chatbot without protection. Ghana’s AI future will not be decided by one big announcement. It will be shaped by businesses and individuals who test, learn, adjust and keep going. Hubtel has shown a practical path for the whole country: own your data, rent the engine, solve real problems for real customers and keep your people learning. Through the Digital Economy Forum, it is making sure every Ghanaian gets to hear that conversation.

title: Houthis say they repelled attack from pro-Saudi forces near Bab el-Mandeb Strait
body:
DOHA, October 27. /TASS/. The Houthis from the Yemeni rebel movement Ansar Allah have repelled an offensive by Saudi-backed forces south of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, said Yahya Saree, the military representative of the rebels.
"Our armed forces repelled an offensive attempt made by the Saudi enemy from the south of the Bab el-Mandeb [Strait]," Saree said on Telegram.
He said the operation was led by Saudi officer Badr al-Harbi from the operational headquarters in Aden. According to Saree, the Houthis attacked enemy concentrations using ballistic missiles and heavy weapons. The attack destroyed several vehicles, while the advancing forces suffered significant losses in dead and wounded.

title: US, Israeli aggression threatens global energy security, says Iranian president
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. US and Israeli military aggression against Iran has jeopardized global energy security and economic stability by damaging the country’s energy infrastructure, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian told the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) in Moscow.
"The US and the Israeli regime have twice launched military aggression against the Islamic Republic of Iran amid ongoing political negotiations. This regrettable and dangerous development threatens global security. By destroying Iran’s energy infrastructure and disrupting energy transportation, these actions have put global energy security and the economy at risk," Pezeshkian said.
He added that the summit was taking place amid significant geopolitical shifts that pose serious challenges to global energy security.

title: Russian forces strike warehouse belonging to KSD publishing house
body:
According to Ukrinform, the publishing house reported this on Facebook .
“Friends, on the morning when we wanted to congratulate you on Ukrainian Writing and Language Day and share our November announcements, we have completely different, disheartening news. We are forced to report that the enemy has targeted our warehouse . The attack on the area where it is located is ongoing. None of our employees were injured,” the post reads.
The publishing house noted that the consequences of the attack will inevitably affect the release of new titles, which were scheduled to launch on November 5.
The announcements have been postponed to assess the situation and determine how to proceed, the publishing house emphasized, and called for understanding and support.
