title: Europe forgets its ‘green agenda’ amid energy challenges, Putin says
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. European countries have reopened coal mines amid energy challenges, despite their commitment to the "green agenda," Russian President Vladimir Putin said.
"Of course, we need to work together, including with those who support the 'green agenda.' When it became more difficult to address energy challenges, they [European countries] reopened coal enterprises and put them quickly to work. So where is their ‘green agenda’? We need to come together and find balanced solutions," the Russian president said at the summit of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF).

title: Ukraine Develops Ground Robots That Launch Interceptor Drones
body:
A Ukrainian company is beginning to assemble interceptor drones designed to launch from unmanned ground vehicles (UGVs), with specialized launch boxes being developed for their deployment.
Taras Ostapchuk, founder of Ratel Robotics, announced the plans in an interview with Forbes, as cited by RBC-Ukraine .
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The company has previously demonstrated the launch of strike FPV drones from its ground robots. It now plans to adapt the concept to counter aerial threats.
Ratel will initially focus on multi-rotor interceptor drones before moving on to fixed-wing, airplane-type models.
The company is also developing launch boxes for deployment from UGVs and integrated software to enable data exchange between ground and aerial platforms.
Under the concept, a UGV would carry interceptor drones to a designated position and launch them to engage enemy aerial targets.
Ostapchuk told Forbes that integrating different types of unmanned platforms was a key direction in robotics development . By combining their capabilities, the systems could enable operators to perform a wider range of tasks remotely.
Vsviti , which also cited the interview, reported that Ratel is currently focusing on multi-rotor interceptors that do not use jet engines. Fixed-wing drones are planned for a later stage.
The company is also working on unified software for ground, aerial and, eventually, maritime unmanned systems. The software is intended to improve data exchange and interoperability between different platforms.
As part of this effort, the company is testing an autopilot system for ground robots that it plans to adapt for aerial drones.
According to Ostapchuk, Ratel has already invested approximately $200,000 in developing its aerial division. Developing fixed-wing drones could require several million dollars.
Ukrainian troops have completed their first logistics mission using a domestically developed amphibious UGV , traveling more than 40 kilometers (nearly 25 miles) across land and water to deliver supplies to frontline positions, Ukraine’s defense ministry said.
The vehicle can cross rivers, canals, and marshes without switching platforms, allowing it to continue operating where conventional ground robots might be unable to pass.
Meanwhile, Ukraine’s 3rd Army Corps has begun using unmanned ground vehicles for assaults on Russian positions. Its NC13 unit equipped kamikaze robots with Bullspike grenade launchers and deployed them against Russian troops, including positions inside shelters.
The corps has also tested dropping UGVs from Gryphon heavy bombers and used robotic platforms to strike Russian positions and logistics targets up to 15 kilometers (about 9 miles) from the front line.

title: Ethiopian death toll from two attacks on Christians at 60
body:
NAIROBI, October 27. /TASS/. At least 60 people were killed in two attacks by armed groups in the Arsi area of the Oromia region of Ethiopia, Africanews TV channel quoted a statement from the Ethiopian Orthodox Church as saying.
According to the statement from the Holy Synod, 14 people were killed on October 20 in the Merti district, and 46 more on October 24 in the Shirka district. All the dead were Christians. More than 20 houses were burned down in the attacks, and over 20 people were hospitalized with serious injuries.
Earlier, local online publication The Abay Times said armed men killed at least 48 people, including women, children and the elderly, in the settlements of Chole and Birbo in the Shirka district. According to eyewitnesses, the attackers used automatic weapons, looted houses and killed civilians.
The attackers are yet to be established. The Oromian authorities and representatives of the armed opposition accuse each other of carrying out violent acts. The Ethiopian Human Rights Commission said it was investigating the claims.

title: Russia's return to global sports gathers momentum as EU mulls response
body:
BRUSSELS, Belgium — The EU is working on how to stop Russia from laundering its reputation through international sporting events, but as it talks, Moscow creates new facts on the ground.
"Sports and culture must not become vehicles for whitewashing Russian aggression," the EU's top diplomat Kaja Kallas told journalists on Oct. 13.
But since then, there have been at least two instances in which Russia has been able to advance its sports agenda.
Lithuania was stripped of its right to host an April 2027 international pentathlon tournament on Oct. 19 after it refused to grant visas to Russian and Belarusian athletes for the event.
And on Oct. 25, the International Weightlifting Federation announced that its 2030 championship would take place in Moscow, the first time such a high-level contest has been awarded to Russia since it launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
In both cases, the condemnations and expressions of disappointment have come thick and fast.
Lithuania's Foreign Minister Kestutis Budrys called the pentathlon decision "shameful" and said the EU "must tighten restrictions on Russian and Belarusian athletes competing under national colors, expand visa bans and sanctions, and cut support for those enabling state-sponsored propaganda."
And Ukraine's Sports Minister Matvii Bidnyi told public broadcaster Suspilne that Kyiv would boycott the weightlifting tournament in Moscow.
The minister added that he considers the choice of host "an alarming and unacceptable signal," which "suggests that the influence of Russians in some international federations is extremely strong."
Likewise, European Commission spokesperson Eva Hrncirova told the Kyiv Independent that the EU's executive arm "regrets" both of those decisions.
"In line with the autonomy of sport, international federations are responsible for decision-making on where to host international competitions. However, both federations and member states should act in line with EU sanctions and values," Hrncirova said.
Beyond criticism, the EU is also preparing measures in a bid to tackle the issue.
Kallas said on Oct. 13 that the EU's diplomatic arm, the European External Action Service, "together with the Commission, will put forward proposals on how to sustain Russia's isolation in global sports."
And Hrncirova said that "the Commission is facilitating and supporting coordinated action among member states and with like-minded international partners to resist the instrumentalization of sport by Russia and Belarus."
However, it remains unknown when the new measures will be announced. In the meantime, Russia's lobbying to return to sports continues unabated.
Russia's all-out war has taken a heavy toll on Ukraine, with hundreds of Ukrainian athletes and coaches killed and hundreds of sports facilities destroyed by Russian missile and drone attacks.

title: Reps move to tighten rules for EV, CNG vehicle imports, demand local service centres
body: By Gift ChapiOdekina,Abuja The House of Representatives has called for stricter regulations on the importation of electric vehicles (EVs), compressed natural gas (CNG) vehicles and related equipment, proposing mandatory local maintenance centres, genuine spare parts and after-sales support for importers. The lawmakers also urged the Federal Government to establish a transparent licensing framework for companies importing alternative-fuel vehicles, warning against the risk of Nigeria becoming a dumping ground for vehicles without adequate technical support and safety safeguards. The resolution followed a motion sponsored by Rep. Ademorin Kuye during Wednesday’s plenary, where lawmakers raised concerns over consumer protection, vehicle safety, local investment and the country’s readiness for the growing adoption of cleaner transportation technologies. Under the proposed framework, the National Automotive Design and Development Council (NADDC), in collaboration with the Bureau of Public Procurement, Standards Organisation of Nigeria, Nigeria Customs Service and other relevant agencies, would develop clear criteria for approving importers. Companies seeking approval could be required to establish certified service and maintenance centres in Nigeria, provide genuine spare parts and warranty support, and employ and train qualified Nigerian technicians. Other proposed conditions include investment in electric-vehicle charging stations or CNG refuelling facilities, compliance with national safety and environmental standards, and submission of consumer protection and after-sales service plans. The House also proposed a public register of approved importers and infrastructure providers to promote transparency and protect consumers. It stressed that the licensing process should be open, competitive and non-discriminatory, allowing all companies that meet the prescribed requirements to obtain approval. The lawmakers further called for tax incentives, import duty concessions and other fiscal benefits to be tied to compliance with the proposed framework to encourage investment in local infrastructure and technical capacity. Contributing to the debate, Rep. Dominic Okafor warned against allowing Nigeria to become a dumping ground for vehicles manufactured without adequate consideration for the needs of developing countries. He said importers must demonstrate their capacity to maintain the vehicles they bring into the country and provide adequate support to consumers after purchase. “It’s very important to see that all the players in this motion are dressed seriously, so that Nigeria is not made a dumping ground,” Okafor said. He observed that some manufacturers produce different categories of vehicles for Western markets and developing countries, including Nigeria, stressing the need for safeguards to ensure that imported vehicles meet local requirements. Okafor said electric vehicles required sustained technical support, access to spare parts and maintenance facilities, unlike products consumed immediately after purchase. “Electric vehicles are not a one-sell product,” he said, adding that the absence of maintenance centres could leave consumers stranded and expose them to avoidable costs. The lawmaker also raised safety concerns over CNG-powered vehicles and trucks, arguing that companies should not be permitted to import them commercially without adequate facilities and technical safeguards. “Efforts should be made that whoever that importer is issued to has some of these facilities, not just in it as a trading activity,” he added. Similarly, Rep. Kalejaiye Adeboye Paul supported the proposal, saying local maintenance and repair facilities were essential to sustaining Nigeria’s transition to alternative-fuel transportation. He noted that state governments were increasingly embracing the programme, making it necessary to prepare for the long-term implications of importing vehicles without building domestic technical capacity. “But I think that establishing their own centre here in Nigeria for maintenance and repairs is very essential. It has to be a condition for which we can continue to embrace this,” Paul said. He warned that Nigeria’s limited capacity to manufacture or assemble the vehicles could create challenges as adoption increased. “We are not manufacturing here. We are not assembling here. And we do not have what it takes to keep this going,” he said. He warned that Nigeria’s limited capacity to manufacture or assemble the vehicles could create challenges as adoption increased. “We are not manufacturing here. We are not assembling here. And we do not have what it takes to keep this going,” he said. Paul added that the consequences of operating the vehicles without adequate maintenance infrastructure might become more evident over time, urging lawmakers to support the proposed safeguards in the interest of consumers and the country. Rep. Stanley Olajide described the motion as timely, citing global concerns over greenhouse gas emissions and climate change. He said a properly regulated transition to cleaner transportation would enable Nigeria to contribute to environmental protection while advancing its development priorities. “I believe having this framework will not only be responsible as a nation, it will also help us toward the line of having an environment-friendly system where we can actually say we are contributing to the right cause in the world,” Olajide said. Rep. Sada Soli also backed the proposal, arguing that a clear legal framework was needed to support the Federal Government’s clean transportation policy. Soli recalled that the government had announced fiscal incentives for CNG and certain categories of electric vehicles, saying legislation would help establish clear rules for implementing the policy. “What is lacking in this policy is the legal aspect of it,” he said, urging the sponsor to develop the proposal into a bill to provide a comprehensive legal framework for regulating the sector. Soli identified environmental protection, lower transportation costs and employment generation as potential benefits of a well-managed transition to alternative-fuel vehicles. He also argued that the adoption of new transportation technologies could create opportunities for jobs and income generation if supported by appropriate policies and infrastructure. The lawmaker urged the sponsor to take the proposal further, saying the National Assembly should play an active role in establishing the legal framework rather than leaving the responsibility entirely to the executive. “We should not surrender it to the government because the government has built on this policy,” Soli said. The House unanimously adopted the motion and mandated its Committees on Industry, Commerce, Gas Resources, Environment and Legislative Compliance to monitor implementation and report back within four weeks for further legislative action. Following the debate, Speaker Tajudeen Abbas said the motion had received support and encouraged the sponsor to provide additional details on how the proposed policy would operate. title: Oleshky Ceasefire to Last Until Nov. 1, Arakhamia Says
body:
The humanitarian ceasefire around Russian-occupied Oleshky will remain in force until 10:59 p.m. Kyiv time (12:00 a.m. midnight in Moscow) on Nov. 1, David Arakhamia, head of the Servant of the People parliamentary faction, said on Tuesday, Oct. 27.
In a Telegram statement, Arakhamia said the pause began at 3 a.m. Kyiv time Tuesday (1 a.m. UTC; 9 p.m. EDT Monday). Its scheduled expiration on Sunday corresponds to 8:59 p.m. UTC.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
He described the arrangement as the most extensive ceasefire across the largest stretch of Ukraine’s southern front.
“This is the largest de-escalation since 2022,” Arakhamia wrote , crediting US First Lady Melania Trump’s initiative to secure humanitarian access to Oleshky.
In his Tuesday morning update, Ukrainian Human Rights Commissioner Dmytro Lubinets said both sides were complying with the agreement after the localized ceasefire took effect .
“The parties are complying with the agreements we reached,” Lubinets said.
Russia’s Defense Ministry separately confirmed that it had halted fire in the Kherson sector in preparation for the humanitarian operation.
Lubinets said the arrangements were reached with Russian negotiating representative Yana Lantratova through mediation and coordination by Melania Trump.
The humanitarian operation envisages clearing mines from access routes, delivering essential supplies and enabling civilians to leave voluntarily.
An estimated 1,700 to 2,000 residents remain in Oleshky, many of them elderly, amid severe shortages of food, medicine and clean water.
The city, across the Dnipro River from Ukrainian-held Kherson, has been under Russian occupation since the opening stages of the full-scale invasion in 2022.

title: LNG accounts for half of global gas trade now — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. LNG, which currently accounts for half of global trade, could help resolve the issue of disruptions in worldwide gas supplies, Russian President Vladimir Putin said at the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) summit.
The key problem now is the disruption of gas supplies to global markets, he said. "Large volumes of supply have been removed from the market in a short period, with demand remaining unchanged. This means we need to work on optimizing transport routes, taking into account the geographical locations of the Forum’s member countries, through mutual operations among them, that is among us," Putin explained.
The growing flexibility of the gas market driven by the widespread use of liquefied natural gas makes this possible, he noted. "After all, LNG supplies do not depend on international pipelines, and LNG already accounts for about half of global gas trade. I would like to emphasize that replacing lost volumes and revising logistics is no simple task: it is essential to strike a balance between the interests of gas suppliers and consumers, while also fulfilling existing contractual obligations," the Russian leader said.

title: Ansaru claims responsibility for killing of Katsina cleric, Sheikh Masusuka
body:
Jama’atu Ansarul Muslimina Fi Biladis Sudan, popularly known as Ansaru, has claimed responsibility for the killing of Katsina-based Islamic cleric, Sheikh Yahaya Masusuka, PREMIUM TIMES can report.
The cleric was shot dead alongside another man, identified by police as Adamu Abubakar, outside his residence on Monday evening.
The Katsina State Police Command said two armed men riding on a motorcycle opened fire on the two at about 7:30 p.m. before fleeing the scene.
The victims were rushed to a nearby hospital, where they were pronounced dead, according to the police.
The command said it had launched an investigation and deployed tactical and operational teams to track down the assailants.
Mr Masusuka was known for his Quran-centred teachings and advocacy for peaceful coexistence among Nigerians of all faiths. He had also spoken against violent extremism and radicalisation.
Amnesty International condemned his killing and called on Nigerian authorities to investigate the attack and bring those responsible to justice. The organisation also said the cleric had faced threats and intimidation during his life.
In a four-minute video exclusively obtained by PREMIUM TIMES on Tuesday, the terror group said its fighters killed Mr Masusuka around 8:30 pm, citing his interfaith peaceful coexistence, among other things, as reasons for his killing.
Describing the deceased as an arnai (infidel), the group said it was “happy” to announce his killing, which was carried out by “soldiers among soldiers of Allah.”
“Masusuka is an (arnai) infidel, not a Muslim,” the group said. “He was contracted to disrupt Islam and confuse Muslims.”
Ansaru said Mr Masusuka had been invited by [clerics] for a mukabala (debate), but he declined.
The group also issued a warning to “other infidels” who “belittle the Hadiths of the Prophet.
“You should repent. You should stop, or else we are coming for you,” it said.
This development is disturbing, said Taiwo Adebayo, a conflict and security governance researcher with Institute of Security Studies (ISS) Africa.
“This means these are not just a territorial threat as they can track and kill those who don’t agree with their ideology or who they consider threats even if those targets live far away from their bases,” he said.
PREMIUM TIMES understands that Ansaru now operates in Nigeria’s North-central region, years after relocating from the North-west.
The group has faced several crackdowns by Nigerian authorities, most recently the arrests of its leaders, Abu Bara’a and Mallam Mamuda.
The group did not mention those involved in the attack. However, it is unlikely that it would mobilise fighters from its Nigeria-Benin border enclaves for the killing.
“It’s also possible that they outsource the assassination or intelligence gathering leading to the Sheikh to local bandits,” Mr Adebayo said.
“In the early days of Boko Haram insurgency, they operated like this, sending, ordering hits on clerics and political figures in towns, while hiding in the bush,” he added.

title: NSDC enlists Weatherman Foundation to help identify fallen Ukrainian defenders
body:
Secretary of the National Security and Defense Council of Ukraine Ihor Klymenko and Megan Mobbs, head of the R.T. Weatherman Foundation, have discussed future cooperation on identifying the remains of fallen Ukrainian defenders.
"I recently met with Megan Mobbs, head of the R.T. Weatherman Foundation, which implements important humanitarian projects in Ukraine. One of the main topics of our discussion was the identification of the remains of fallen Ukrainian defenders," Klymenko wrote on Telegram on Tuesday.
"The NSDC coordinates work in this area, involving state institutions and experts," Klymenko said. According to him, Mobbs confirmed the foundation's readiness to assist, and the two sides discussed opportunities for future cooperation.
"We also discussed cybersecurity and information security. Against the backdrop of growing Russian threats, these areas require increasingly close cooperation between Ukraine and its international partners. It is important to pool experience and resources to counter challenges that extend far beyond our country's borders," Klymenko said.
"I thank Megan Mobbs and the entire team for their sustained assistance," he added.
The R.T. Weatherman Foundation is a US nonprofit organization founded in 2022 by Elizabeth Weatherman and Andrew Duncan. It has operated in Ukraine since March 2022, focusing on the consequences of the war in three areas: body, including medical care; mind, including PTSD treatment and recovery; and spirit, including the search for and repatriation and identification of war victims, as well as support for the families of the fallen.

title: Building inflation increases to 5.1% in September 2026, but cement inflation stood at -6.1%
body: The year-on-year inflation rate of the Prime Building Cost Index (PBCI) was 5.1% in September 2026, up from 4.6% in August 2026. The monthly change rate for September 2026 was 0.03%. According to the Ghana Statistical Service, building inflation remains low, despite an increase in September 2026. The drivers of the September inflation were plant and equipment costs that went up 19.1% over the year. At the group level, the Labour group inflation rate recorded a year-on-year inflation rate of -3.2% in September 2026, down from -2.9% in August 2026. The Material group recorded a year-on-year inflation rate of 6.5% in September 2026, up from 5.8% in August 2026, while the Plant group recorded a year-on-year inflation rate of 19.1%, up from 17.9% in August 2026. At the sub-group level, Reinforcement recorded the highest year-on-year inflation rate of 29.0%, while the sub-group Steel recorded the lowest year-on-year inflation rate of -8.8%. Fourteen sub-groups out of the 23 sub-groups recorded inflation rates above the national average of 5.1%. The year-on-year inflation halved over the year but has risen since March 2026. What the September figures mean to households For households, structural inputs cost less than a year ago, as cement inflation stood at −6.1% and steel −8.8%. Finishing and installation inputs, however, cost more, with plumbing +27.5%, glazing +20.6%, and tiles +9.2%. The overall building costs are 5.1% higher than in September 2025.

title: Tensions continue to mount as Iraq balances the Iran border crossing closures with national needs
body: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi is caught between the need to restrict arms and drug trafficking through Iranian border crossings and the realities of an economy that has become dependent on cheap produce imported from the neighboring country, Dr. Ronen Zeidel, an Iraq researcher at the Moshe Dayan Center for Middle Eastern and African Studies at Tel Aviv University, told The Jerusalem Post on Tuesday.Authorities closed the al-Shib crossing last week as they upgraded security and detection equipment, an Iraqi official told Reuters on Wednesday. However, Kurdistan Democratic Party lawmaker Salwan Taha Akreyi told Kurdistan24 that Baghdad had shut the crossing at Washington's request to restrict transit to and from Iran and thwart Tehran's efforts to strengthen its militias in Iraq.Speaking a day after Baghdad's Third Karkh Investigative Court issued an arrest warrant for Maysan Provincial Council Chairman Mustafa Da'ir, following a complaint by Zaidi's office over threats of civil disobedience if the crossing remained closed, Zeidel said the “lone expression of dissatisfaction” reflected broader discontent.Da'ir gave Baghdad until Thursday to open the crossing, threatening unrest and warning that he would cut the province off from the rest of the country if his demands went unmetThe country's reliance on cheap shipments from Iran has led residents to neglect local agriculture, and they have become reliant, he said, adding that some who benefit from the transit of criminal goods have a “vested interest” in seeing it reopened swiftly.Iraq governorate benefits from Iran border crossing“Many people in this governorate, particularly those who work in the local administration, benefit from the border crossing. They earn a lot of money from smuggling all kinds of merchandise, especially drugs, arms, and other goods,” he said.“They have a vested interest in keeping the border crossing open at all times. That is why there were so few demonstrations protesting its closure, and why he says what he says. He does not represent the entire population, but rather a certain segment of local society, particularly, I think, his tribe, which benefits from the border crossing. That explains his position.”It is understood that Da'ir comes from the Muhammedawi tribe, one of the most powerful Arab Shia tribes in Iraq.Though the closure may thwart Iranian smuggling attempts, Zeidel acknowledged that Baghdad would find it “difficult” to maintain it in the long term. He explained that rising prices from the loss of cheap Iranian goods, along with protests and pressure from Tehran, would make it increasingly difficult for Baghdad to sustain the closure.Strait of Hormuz blockade increases Iran reliance on land routesThe closure comes as the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz has increased Iran's reliance on land routes through neighboring Iraq and Pakistan for shipments, and the sanctions preventing Iranian flights from landing at the majority of airports have only added to Iran's frustrations, he said.  Tehran strongly condemned the closure of the crossing earlier this week, denying allegations that the al-Shib crossing had been used to traffic drugs and counterfeit currency.“The [closures] drive the Iranian leadership crazy,” Zeidel said, adding that in many ways closing Iran's access to Iraq had become more effective than airstrikes.In response to said frustrations, Zeidel said that Iran-backed militias were likely to escalate economic protests and, potentially, use Iraqi territory to attack Saudi Arabia to bring embarrassment to Baghdad.

title: Zelensky accuses West of intentionally postponing Patriot, NASAMS missile deliveries
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Ukraine’s Vladimir Zelensky has accused Western partners of deliberately delaying deliveries of interceptor missiles for the country’s air defense systems in recent weeks.
Specifically, in a post on his Telegram channel, he described the delays in supplying interceptor missiles for the Patriot and NASAMS air defense systems as "artificial and prolonged."
Kiev had repeatedly complained about a shortage of interceptor missiles for its air defense. On October 15, CNN, citing sources, reported that Ukraine’s stockpile of Patriot missiles had been completely depleted. Later, Vladimir Zelensky voiced complaints about delays in the delivery of American interceptor missiles purchased with funding from European Union countries under the PURL (Prioritized Ukraine Requirements List) mechanism. He accused Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth of holding up the delivery of missiles for the Patriot and NASAMS air defense systems by a month.

title: Babcock and Larus to Develop AI for Submarine Maintenance
body: Babcock Canada (Babcock) i s further enhancing its partnership with Larus to develop an advanced artificial intelligence (AI) sovereign compute platform designed to transform submarine maintenance, sustainment, and operational readiness. Babcock and Larus use cutting-edge AI to transform submarine maintenance capabilities and operational readiness. Building on Babcock’s work as the Prime Contractor of the Victoria In-Service Support Contract, the partnership combines our operational expertise with Larus’ leading AI capabilities, creating a highly secure and predictive system that enables faster and more informed submarine maintenance decision-making. Within a secure environment, the new platform analyzes high volumes of data through the integration of complex submarine maintenance schedules, engineering modifications, mission-critical enhancements, risk assessments, and operational considerations, allowing the software to identify patterns, anticipate risks, and build efficiencies. READ: Canada Awards Victoria In-Service Support Contract Extension to Babcock Babcock first partnered with Larus in 2025 to develop a machine-learning driven predictive support simulation and optimization proof-of-concept for complex fleets. As part of the development process, Babcock and Larus successfully tested an early version of the predictive framework using real-world complex asset management data from a non-defence program. The trial demonstrated the platform’s ability to analyze complex maintenance and operational information in a secure environment, validating the foundational capabilities required to support highly sensitive sovereign defence and submarine sustainment data. “Together with Larus, we continue to innovate and push the envelope to build efficiency by creating a secure, predictive planning framework that allows us to model complex submarine sustainment activities, evaluate maintenance requirements, and develop contingency plans before challenges emerge,” said Tony March, Chief Executive Officer, Babcock Canada. “Beyond improving today’s sustainment operations, this technology will help inform the workforce, skills and industrial capacity requirements needed to support Canada’s future submarine fleet. As Canada moves from a fleet of four submarines to up to twelve under the Canadian Patrol Submarine Project, predictive planning and data-driven decision-making will be essential to ensuring the right people, capabilities, and infrastructure are in place to support the delivery of readily available and safe submarines,” added March. “Canada’s defence programs need trusted AI that is built and operated at home. Babcock has shown real leadership by bringing Canadian SMEs like Larus into its core programs and investing in sovereign capability here in Canada. Together, we are proving that Canadian industry is ready to deliver,” said George Di Nardo, Chief Executive Officer, Larus Technologies. The technology has significant potential beyond submarine sustainment and could be scaled across Canada’s wider defence sectors to support future maintenance, readiness, and operational planning requirements. This strategic research and development collaboration will help strengthen Canadian industrial capability and Canada’s position as an AI leader. To further strengthen the partnership, the companies have signed a Memorandum of Understanding designating Larus as Babcock Canada’s preferred AI supplier and will join Babcock’s established pan- Canadian supply chain network. title: INS Trishul in Civitavecchia: Advancing India–Italy Maritime Partnership
body: By Vani Rao* CIVITAVECCHIA (ROME). When Indian Navy’s tall-ship INS Sudarshini visited Livorno in September 2026, I wrote about the enduring maritime connections between India and Italy and the opportunities to translate this shared heritage into a contemporary partnership. The visit of INS Trishul to Civitavecchia Port this week provides an opportunity to reflect on how this partnership is rapidly progressing, through regular naval engagement, dialogue and a shared commitment to maritime security. An image of the Indian Navy ship INS Trishul, which arrived for a visit at the port of Civitavecchia – Credit – Indian Navy India and Italy are historically maritime nations and peninsulas with long coastlines. Both countries have strategic interests in ensuing the security of sea lanes, freedom of navigation and stability of the international maritime order. For India, maritime cooperation is integral to the vision of MAHASAGAR—Mutual and Holistic Advancement for Security and Growth Across Regions. This vision emphasises partnership, capacity-building and shared prosperity, recognising that the security of the seas is a collective responsibility. India and Italy are pursuing these shared objectives – by broadening and deepening naval engagements. There is also a mutual realisation that for ensuring national and energy security, we need safe and reliable maritime domains. Both countries are prioritising global exports for which maritime trade routes are crucial. As the concept of Indo-Mediterranean gains prominence as one geographic space, naval ships of India and Italy are regularly visiting each other’s ports, as part of their tours of the Mediterranean and the Indo-Pacific regions. At a time when global shipping routes and maritime infrastructure face many challenges, closer cooperation between like-minded partners is timely and necessary. The elevation of our bilateral relations to a Special Strategic Partnership in May 2026, and the announcement of a Defence Industrial Roadmap provide important frameworks for advancing this cooperation. In this backdrop, last week, the inaugural India–Italy Bilateral Maritime Security Dialogue was held in Rome – with participation of key institutional stakeholders from the Navy, Coast Guard, Ministry of Defence, Foreign Ministry and others from both sides. The Dialogue enabled exchange of assessments on the respective maritime security environments, and cooperation in the maritime domain. There was a productive discussion about ways of cooperating in maritime situational awareness, countering illicit maritime activities and safeguarding critical maritime infrastructure. In additional to the bilateral mode, India and Italy will explore cooperation under regional frameworks, and in multilateral organisations. The dialogue paves the way for cooperation between our respective maritime institutions and navies, through capacity building, academic and research exchanges. India has similar dialogues with select countries with which it has close bilateral ties and convergent interests in maritime security. In another step towards strengthening maritime relations, Italian Navy’s ITS Giovanni delle Bande Nere visited Mumbai last week, and did a Passage Exercise (PASSEX) with Indian Navy’s INS Surat in the Indian Ocean. Admiral Giuseppe Berutti Bergotto, Chief of the Italian Navy, visited India at the same time and interacted withhis Indian counterpart, Admiral K. Swaminathan. Such regular meetings allow sharing of professional experience, enhance familiarity with each other’s procedures and foster mutual understanding which underpins effective operational cooperation. India’s participation as an observer in the Italian Navy’s exercise Ex Mare Aperto to witness a major naval exercise provided valuable insights into operational concepts, planning and responses to complex maritime scenarios. INS Trishul’s visit to Civitavecchia port this week includes activities between its crew and Italian naval personnel, courtesy meetings with the Mayor and local dignitaries, and a Passage Exercise with the Italian Navy’s ITS Margottini, before entering the harbour. The diverse activities and professional interactions between the two ships, are yet another step towards increasing familiarity, understanding and confidence – these are essential for effective operational cooperation when circumstances require it. Apart from the bilateral mode of maritime cooperation, India and Italy are already engaging in regional frameworks. Italy is a member of the Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative (IPOI) and a dialogue partner of the Indian Oceans Regional Association (IORA). Italy is also a member of the Information Fusion Center-Indian Ocean Region (IFC-IOR) based in Gurgaon, which focuses on maritime domain awareness, boosting regional information exchanges and maritime security coordination. India and Italy are member nations of the Combined Maritime Forces (CMF) in Bahrain and the Combined Task Force (CTF). In February 2026 India took over leadership of CTF 154 under CMF, a dedicated multinational maritime training and capacity-building task force across the Middle East and surrounding international waters. Both countries are members of the India-Middle East Europe Connectivity Corridor (IMEEC) which seeks to enhance maritime, land, and port infrastructure connectivity between India, Middle East and Europe. As INS Trishul departs Civitavecchia, her visit is a timely reminder that naval diplomacy is an integral aspect of foreign policy and external outreach. Port calls create opportunities for dialogue between naval personnel, engagement with host institutions and closer connections between countries. They also give visible expression to a relationship whose substance is increasingly reflected in structured consultations and practical maritime cooperation. As INS Trishul sets sail from Italian shores, it will carry with it the goodwill generated by this engagement and the promise of further cooperation. The seas that connect India and Italy offer not only routes for commerce, but opportunities to deepen trust, advance security and strengthen a partnership oriented towards peace and prosperity. *Ambassador of India to Italy L'articolo INS Trishul in Civitavecchia: Advancing India–Italy Maritime Partnership proviene da Report Difesa .

title: Troops repel terrorists in Benue, recover two AK-47 rifles
body: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of the Maritime Component of Joint Task Force Operation Whirl Stroke have recovered a cache of arms and other items following an intelligence-led operation in Guma Local Government Area of Benue State on 26 October 2026. A statement signed by Lieutenant Ahmad Zubairu Zubairu, Ag Media Information Officer, said the operation followed credible and actionable intelligence indicating that some criminal elements posing as herders had crossed from Nasarawa State into Guma LGA. “On arrival at the location, the troops came under gunfire from the armed group. “The troops responded effectively, repelled the attack and forced the assailants to flee. No casualty was recorded among the troops. Further exploitation of the area led to the recovery of two AK-47 rifles, four empty AK-47 magazines, eight calves, three mobile phones, a National Identification Number (NIN) document belonging to one Mr Umar Yusuf, and the sum of ₦20 The Force Commander, Joint Task Force Operation Whirl Stroke and General Officer Commanding 5 Division, Nigerian Army, Major General Moses Kolo Gara, commended the troops for their vigilance, proactive response and successful recovery of the items. He charged the troops to strengthen collaboration with local communities and sustain intelligence-led operations to prevent criminal activities and enhance security across the Joint Operations Area. Major General Gara also appreciated members of the public for providing credible and actionable intelligence, as well as for the confidence they continue to repose in the troops. He urged residents to sustain their cooperation with security agencies by promptly reporting suspicious movements and activities. title: Russia tries to drag a village north of Kupiansk into no-man’s-land after its losses in Ukraine’s underground operation
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Russian troops are trying to drag Radkivka, a village on the northern edge of Kupiansk in Kharkiv Oblast, into the gray zone so their infiltration groups can keep reaching the city, Viktor Trehubov, spokesperson for Ukraine’s Joint Forces Grouping, said on national television on 27 October, Ukrinform reported . Russian forces made three attempts to advance toward Radkivka on 26 October, Ukraine’s General Staff reported . Russia has tried for more than a year to retake Kupiansk, a city on the Oskil River, largely by slipping small groups through a disused gas pipeline under the river. They kept using it even after Ukraine said in September 2025 that it had flooded three of the four pipe strings, until Ukrainian troops went into the pipes themselves in Operation Veles, announced on 22 October. Russian groups now have to move above ground The pipe Russian groups used to seep toward Kupiansk has been put out of action, so they now have to go through Radkivka or neighboring Holubivka, Trehubov said. They move along the bank of the Oskil and a nearby tree line, but the foliage will soon be gone, which will make that much harder. When the battlefield became transparent, the war went underground. Khartiia Corps, together with other Defense Forces units, is conducting the underground Operation VELES, and for the first time, we can show the work of our brothers-in-arms in this new dimension of warfare. “We… pic.twitter.com/Af3RqgSIr8 — Khartiia Corps in English (@khartiia_eng) October 21, 2026 On the western bank of the Oskil, Russian forces took losses from Ukraine’s Khartiia Corps and in Operation Veles, and their logistics have “ suffered noticeably ,” Trehubov said. Advancing there is now harder for them than it was a month ago, he added. Viktor Trehubov, spokesperson for Ukraine’s Joint Forces Grouping. Photo: Ukrinform Everything now depends on how the fights for Holubivka and Radkivka end, Trehubov said. “ If Ukrainian control can finally be established there, the Russians will have nowhere much to crawl through ,” he said. Several dozen Russian soldiers remain in low-rise buildings in northern Kupiansk, and Ukrainian forces are working to cut off their rotations, Trehubov said on 23 October. Each side wants the other off its bank of the Oskil On the eastern bank, Russian forces keep pushing toward the village of Podoly and Kupiansk-Vuzlovyi, a railway junction town southeast of Kupiansk, aiming to wipe out Ukraine’s foothold there, Trehubov said. Ukraine wants to destroy the Russian foothold on the western bank. “ For that, we will need to at least somehow throw them out of Dvorichna ,” Trehubov said, referring to a town north of Kupiansk. The US-based Institute for the Study of War (ISW) assessed that Russian forces conducted no offensive operations on the Kupiansk axis on 26 October, likely because Ukraine now controls the pipeline, a view at odds with the General Staff’s report for that day. Ukraine reported confident control of Kupiansk as early as February, yet Russian groups kept slipping into the city for months afterward. Trehubov’s latest assessment stops short of declaring that threat over: Russia will still try to advance, he said.
