title: Air defense chief vists units stationed in south Iran
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 27 (MNA) – The commander of Joint the Khatam al-Anbiya Air Defense Headquarters and the Army Air Defense Force visited the Southeast Air Defense Zone and the defense units stationed on the three islands.
During the inspection visit to the Southeast Air Defense District and the defense units stationed on the three islands of the Persian Gulf recently, Brigadier General Alireza Elhami reviewed the operational capacity and combat readiness of the personnel, met with the troops stationed there, and commended their efforts and role in downing the American A-10 aircraft during the Third Imposed War in summer.
Appreciating the day-to-day efforts and struggles of the army’s air defense forces, he emphasized the importance of maintaining service morale, intensified efforts, ismart monitoring of threats, and improving defense capabilities, and stated: Producing sustainable security and defending calmness for the people are among the main priorities of the army’s air defense.
The commander of the country's Khatam al-Anbiya (PBUH) Joint Air Defense Headquarters also met with the troops deployed in the three islands of the Persian Gulf, and while wishing them strength, emphasized the necessity of maintaining comprehensive combat readiness and improving the operational capacity of the units.
Referring to the capabilities of the army's air defense forces, Brigadier General Elhami described their morale and combat capacity as reliable and ienhancing, adding: The country's air defense, relying on domestic capabilities, will continue its path of progress and strengthening deterrence with force.

title: Putin expects role of natural gas globally to continue to strengthen
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. The role of natural gas as a pillar of the global energy sector, industry, and the agricultural sector will only continue to strengthen, Russian President Vladimir Putin said at the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) summit.
Last year natural gas consumption grew by 1.2% to 4.2 trillion cubic meters, he said, adding that those trends are expected to continue, with global demand for gas projected to rise to 5.5 trillion cubic meters per year.
"Consequently, the role of natural gas as a pillar of the global energy sector, industry, and the agricultural sector, will only continue to strengthen," the Russian leader said.
"This is a serious challenge for the gas industry, especially considering the upheavals it is currently experiencing," he added.

title: Bayelsa govt, CSOs, unite against air pollution
body:
The Bayelsa Ministry of Environment and civil society organisations (CSOs) in the state have called for a stronger collaboration to combat air pollution and protect the state’s ecosystem.
They ‌‌‍‌‍⁠⁠‍‌‌‍‍‌made the call at a stakeholders’ meeting hosted by the ministry of environment on Tuesday in Yenagoa.
The News Agency of Nigeria reports that the collaboration aims to strengthen local initiatives for monitoring and tackling air pollution.
The Commissioner for Environment, Ebi Ben-Ololo, represented by the Permanent Secretary, Hamilton Ekeke, reaffirmed the ministry’s readiness to collaborate with stakeholders to preserve Bayelsa’s ecosystem.
The meeting provided a platform for stakeholders to examine gaps in environmental monitoring and response, particularly in oil-producing communities.
The participants expressed concern over the World Health Organisation’s estimate that air pollution causes about seven million deaths annually worldwide.
Menidin Egbo, coordinator of the Community Environment and Development Network, noted that air pollution monitoring should have been integrated into assessment of oil spill damage since the establishment of the National Oil Spills Detection and Response Agency (NOSDRA) in 2006.
Mr Egbo added that periodic reviews of the operations of NOSDRA in collaboration with relevant stakeholders, could have promoted local technologies in addressing air pollution.
“Such efforts could also have helped to tackle soil degradation, water contamination and the destruction of forests and crops associated with oil spills,” he said.
Ikechukwu Ahaka of the Media Awareness and Justice Initiative said capacity building for stakeholders and government agencies was necessary to improve responses to air pollution.
Mr Ahaka said his organisation was promoting and installing air quality monitoring devices, which runs on open-source technology, to monitor ambient air pollution in the Niger Delta.
He said the initiative was designed to strengthen the capacity of local actors to monitor air quality and address pollution in affected communities.
“Media Awareness and Justice Initiative is also promoting public awareness and building local capacity to generate empirical data on particulate matter and volatile organic compounds.
“The pollutants pose risks to air quality, human health and ecosystem safety,” he said.
Ethel Onyimbo, president of the Oloibiri Women Association, commended Governor Douye Diri of Bayelsa for supporting collaborative initiatives aimed at addressing environmental pollution in the state.
Ms Onyimbo said stronger alliances among stakeholders would reinforce efforts to tackle ambient air pollution through sustained grassroots action.
She described Bayelsa’s government approval to host the governance secretariat of DeltasUnite, a global initiative for protecting vulnerable delta environments, as evidence of the state’s commitment to environmental protection.
She also recalled Governor Diri’s participation in discussions on China-Africa cooperation in river, coastal and delta governance at East China Normal University in Shanghai.
The discussions took place during the opening of the 5th United Nations Ocean Decade Conference on Mega Deltas.
Ms Onyimbo said the collaborative approach to protecting delta ecosystems should be extended to tackling air pollution through community-based interventions.
She expressed concern that developing countries bore a disproportionate share of the health burden associated with air pollution.
She added that women and children, including the unborn, were particularly vulnerable to the harmful effects of outdoor air pollution.
The stakeholders called for sustained cooperation among government agencies, civil society organisations and local communities to strengthen air pollution monitoring and mitigation efforts.

title: Kiev attacked Belgorod Region up to 2,000 times per day last week, killing six — envoy
body:
LUGANSK, October 27. /TASS/. Last week, the Ukrainian armed forces were attacking the Belgorod Region up to 2,000 times a day, killing six and injuring nearly 70 civilians, including three children, Russian Foreign Ministry Ambassador-at-Large Rodion Miroshnik told TASS.
"During the past seven days, the Belgorod Region remained the region most frequently targeted by Ukrainian militants. The Ukrainian armed forces struck the Belgorod region more than 2,000 times. As a result, six civilians were killed, and another 69 people, including three children, were injured," he said.
Miroshnik specified that the Belgorodsky, Borisovsky, Valuisky, Volokonovsky, Graivoronsky, Krasnoyaruzhsky, Rakityansky, and Shebekinsky districts of the Belgorod Region were most frequently targeted by Ukrainian forces. "The facades and windows of apartment buildings, the roofs of private homes, outbuildings and fences, storage facilities, trucks and passenger cars, administrative and office buildings, educational institutions, and industrial enterprises were mainly damaged in the attacks," the diplomat noted.
Earlier, Miroshnik told TASS that over the past week, 313 civilians were affected by Ukrainian shelling: 263 civilians were injured, including seven minors, and 50 people were killed, including a child. Over the past seven days, Kiev has fired more than 8,200 various types of munitions into the territory of Russian regions.

title: Norwegian PM says his call with Putin was substantive, professional
body:
STOCKHOLM, October 27. /TASS/. Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store described his 90-minute conversation on Tuesday with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Finnish leader Alexander Stubb as professional and substantive.
"We talked for 90 minutes. It was meaningful, substantive and it was professional," Store told NRK television channel as he admitted that there are "major differences" between the sides’ positions.
Earlier on Tuesday, Store and Stubb held a phone call with Putin. The three leaders agreed to continue to maintain direct contacts over the phone, the Kremlin recounted.

title: Ex-Iranian leader Ali Khamenei contributed to gas-exporting countries’ cooperation — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Russian President Vladimir Putin highlighted the significant contribution of former Iranian leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei to cooperation among gas-exporting countries, noting that he was one of the most active participants in founding the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF).
"You have quite rightly mentioned the role of the former spiritual leader of the Iranian people, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who was indeed one of the most active participants in the establishment of our forum, and we rightly remember this with gratitude," Putin said, addressing participants at the eighth summit of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) in Moscow, the Russian capital.

title: Ukrainian postal service forms private air defense force, shoots down Russian drones
body:
Ukrainian postal and courier company Nova Poshta has started its own private air defense force and shot down Russian attack drones targeting their facilities, Vyacheslav Klymov, co-owner of the Nova group of companies, revealed at the Kyiv International Economic Forum on Oct. 26.
"We are one of the few companies that has implemented this project. I don't want to disclose the numbers, but we have destroyed 'Shahed' drones, " Klimov said.
Nova Poshta is the largest private postal and courier company in Ukraine, operating over 15,817 branches across the country, and employing over 34,000 people. Its post offices and distribution centers have frequently come under Russian attack .
Despite the ongoing war, business is going well for Nova Poshta. The company quadrupled its net profit compared with last year, according to financial reports published on April 27.
Klimov also emphasised the importance of companies having their own private firefighting capabilities, rather than just waiting for the response of state authorities.
Nova Poshta employees frequently put out significant fires on their premises before the arrival of state emergency service firefighters, Klimov said.
"Now big businesses are looking for fire engines in Europe in order to create their own services. This is our property… who can forbid me from putting out a fire on my own territory?" he said.
Since late summer , Russia has been attacking Ukraine with jet-powered drones, adding to the now-familiar threat posed by conventional Shahed-type drones and missiles. Between larger assaults, successive waves of jet-powered drones now arrive day and night.
Russia's jet-powered drones target civilian infrastructure such as supermarkets , schools , shopping malls , telecommunications infrastructure , data centers , gas stations , and medical facilities .

title: Reps move to halt school fee hikes in tertiary institutions, probe impact on NELFUND
body:
The House of Representatives on Tuesday urged the federal government to halt the recent increase in school fees and other mandatory charges by public tertiary institutions, warning that the development could undermine the objectives of the Nigeria Education Loan Fund (NELFUND).
The call followed a motion moved by Ifeoluwa Ehindero (APC, Ondo) during plenary.
Mr Ehindero said the recent and widespread increases in fees by public universities, polytechnics and colleges of education, in some cases by more than 100 per cent, could create significant disparities in the allocation of education loans and make it difficult for students from less affluent families to access tertiary education.
He said the NELFUND scheme was established by the federal government to provide interest-free loans to indigent students and enable them to pursue tertiary education without financial constraints.
According to him, the loan scheme was designed around existing tuition benchmarks and institutional cost structures, making sudden increases in fees a threat to its sustainability, equity and effectiveness.
“Education is the cornerstone of national development and is recognised as a fundamental state objective under Section 18 of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended),” Mr Ehindero said.
He cited the constitutional provision which requires the government to direct its policies towards ensuring equal and adequate educational opportunities at all levels.
The lawmaker expressed concern that the fee increases were being implemented without broad consultation or sufficient consideration of the economic difficulties facing Nigerian families.
He warned that continued increases could lead to increased student dropouts, campus unrest and declining public confidence in the government’s commitment to affordable education.
Mr Ehindero therefore urged the federal government to increase financial subventions to public tertiary institutions to reduce their reliance on internally generated revenue from student charges.
He also called on the Federal Ministry of Education and the National Universities Commission (NUC) to engage the management of public tertiary institutions with a view to suspending fee increases and reviewing tuition structures in line with current economic realities.
The House further mandated its Committees on University Education, Federal Polytechnics and Higher Technical Education, and Federal Colleges of Education to investigate the extent and justification for the recent fee increases by public tertiary institutions.
The motion was seconded by Inyang Emil (APC, Cross River) and was adopted without debate.
The Speaker, Abbas Tajudeen, who presided over the plenary, referred the matter to the relevant committees for further legislative consideration.
NELFUND was established under the Students Loans (Access to Higher Education) Act 2024 to administer the Federal Government’s student loan scheme.
The fund provides interest-free loans to eligible Nigerian students to cover institutional charges and, where required, upkeep costs, with the aim of removing financial barriers to higher education. The loan scheme is open to eligible students in public universities, polytechnics, colleges of education and other approved higher institutions, with institutional charges paid directly to the schools.

title: Iraq's Al Zaidi dismisses intelligence chief in shake-up of team
body: Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al Zaidi has shaken up his team five months after taking power, dismissing several officials including the head of intelligence and chief of staff. An order signed by Mr Al Zaidi’s new chief of staff Rashad Khalaf Hashim removed intelligence chief Hamid Al Shatri without giving a reason. No replacement has yet been named. Mr Hashim assumed the chief of staff role on Monday, succeeding Ihsan Al Awadi. The order dated October 26 said the changes were to take effect immediately. Mr Al Shatri had been appointed intelligence chief in December 2024 by former prime minister Mohammed Shia Al Sudani, after previously running the National Security Service. After the Iraqi general election last November, Mr Al Shatri’s name circulated as a potential candidate for the prime minister's position during protracted coalition talks that ultimately led to Mr Al Zaidi's appointment. As intelligence chief he had led several security delegations to Syria to discuss counter-terrorism and border security. A letter leaked on social media showed 69 advisers were also being dismissed from Mr Al Zaidi's office. The changes come as Mr Al Zaidi faces a rebellion from a provincial council over the closure of a border crossing with Iran. A Baghdad court on Monday ordered an investigation into the head of Maysan province, Mustafa Duair Abdulhassan. Mr Al Zaidi had called for a probe over the official's calls for civil disobedience if the Al Sheeb border crossing was not reopened. Iraq closed the crossing last week over security concerns at the border, escalating tensions with Iran and pro-Tehran Iraqi politicians. In September, Iraq closed the Shalamcheh crossing as a precautionary security measure after drone attacks on Saudi Arabia. The shutdown has disrupted trade and daily activity in the province. It was expected to impact the prices of basic goods, especially fresh produce and Iranian building materials that dominate southern markets. Mr Al Zaidi, who took office in May, has sought to maintain balanced ties with both Iran and the US while moving to bring armed factions under state control. Some Iran‑aligned groups have complied, while others have resisted.

title: Mbappe apologises for Mao Zedong comment after Chinese sponsors drop him
body: Kylian Mbappe apologised on Tuesday after the Real Madrid star was dropped by major Chinese brands for apparently joking about Mao Zedong in a video that has gone viral. There were also signs of broader repercussions, with state-run The Paper reporting that public television was suspending broadcasts of matches from Spain’s La Liga. The offending video shows Mbappe saying that the funniest internet meme he had seen involving him was of his face photo-shopped onto that of “some guy — I think he’s a Chinese dictator”. This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappe superimposed on an image of Mao. The authenticity of the video could not immediately be verified by AFP Fact Check. “My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world. I apologise to everyone my words have upset,” French forward Mbappe said in a statement in French, Chinese and English. Spain’s La Liga also apologised, saying it “deeply regrets the offence that Kylian Mbappe’s recent comments have caused among Chinese fans. These comments were made in a personal capacity and do not represent La Liga.” In China, jokes about Mao, the country’s founding leader who died in 1976 — and whose drastic policies are also blamed by historians for mass starvation and millions of deaths — remain taboo. Beverage giant Dongpeng, which during this year’s World Cup ran adverts with AI-generated images of Mbappe consuming its sport drink, said it was terminating all cooperation with the France captain. “Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments,” Dongpeng said in a statement. Mengniu, China’s largest dairy producer, and cheesemaker Milkground also said that they were cutting ties with Mbappe, who until now was hugely popular among Chinese fans with millions of social media followers. “Dongpeng Beverage ends cooperation with Mbappe” was the top-trending topic on Chinese social media site Weibo with 430 million views. One Weibo user said the “extremely serious wrong remarks… crossed the red line” and others urged Dongpeng to remove Mbappe’s image from their bottles. Dongqiudi, one of China’s biggest online football outlets, said Mbappe’s remarks were “offensive to China and the Chinese people”. – Furore – In an interview with French sports newspaper L’Equipe, the 27-year-old Mbappe in September addressed a previous meme depicting him as a military dictator. “There’s a part of it that’s funny… but there is another part that’s a bit less funny because of the damage such people have caused throughout history,” he said. China’s foreign ministry said it was aware of the reports regarding Mbappe, who on Monday finished runner-up to English forward Harry Kane in the Ballon d’Or award for the world’s best player. “Words and actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be met with unanimous rejection from all sectors of Chinese society,” spokesman Guo Jiakun told a regular briefing. State media outlet The Paper cited sources at the state broadcaster saying that CCTV has suspended all broadcasts of La Liga matches, and removed all advertisements involving Mbappe. On the CCTV website, La Liga matches this weekend were still on its online viewing schedule. – Drawing China’s ire – Global sports stars who have commented on sensitive topics such as Taiwan, Tibet and Hong Kong have previously caused controversy in China and been dumped by sponsors. China suspended sponsorship deals with the NBA while the state broadcaster pulled NBA games off Chinese television for a year in October 2019. This followed Houston Rockets executive Daryl Morey tweeting “Fight for freedom, stand with Hong Kong”, referring to protests Beijing called separatist and seditious. Adam Zhang, founder of the Beijing-based sports consultancy firm Key-Solution Sports Consulting, speaking before Mbappe apologised, said a rapid response was needed to quell the growing crisis. “It’s crucial to make a sincere statement. The sooner, the better,” Zhang told AFP. Fans made their feelings clear. “I used to really enjoy watching Mbappe play on the pitch,” Zhang Jingqi, 30, who works at a mall in Beijing, said. “But ever since this news broke yesterday I have lost that admiration, sorry to say.” AFP The post Mbappe apologises for Mao Zedong comment after Chinese sponsors drop him appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: SPOTLIGHT: Meet Nigerian lawyer whose firm has produced six SANs without being one
body:
Oghogho Akpata runs a law firm that has produced six Senior Advocates of Nigeria (SAN) even though he is not one himself.
The SAN rank, equivalent to the King’s Counsel (KC) or Queen’s Counsel (QC) in the United Kingdom, is a prestigious title conferred on Nigerian lawyers as a mark of distinction.
As an upper echelon of legal practice, the rank is reserved for lawyers who have been called to the Nigerian bar for at least 10 years. Candidates must have distinguished themselves through exceptional advocacy or academic erudition, making remarkable contributions to the development of Nigerian law.
It grants recipients exclusive privileges in court, such as the right of first audience and the distinction of wearing silk gowns. Outside professional circles, the title commands authority.
Mr Akpata’s non-SAN status is intriguing for many people, particularly legal profession outsiders. It is hard to come to terms with in a society where titles are reverenced.
And it could not have been a question of non-qualification. Sitting at the top of the firm, he fosters the environment that enables lawyers, including those who matured professionally under his mentorship, to attain the rank of SAN in quick succession.
According to his profile on Templars’ website, Mr Akpata has more than 30 years of legal experience in Nigeria’s oil and gas sector. His work covers areas like major energy transactions, project financing and disputes involving multinational companies.
He founded Templars in Lagos in 1995 after working at F.O. Akinrele & Co., according to P.M. EXPRESS. The law firm began with four lawyers and has since grown its operations in Nigeria and Ghana. It now has 157 lawyers, including 28 partners, across the two countries.
The recent conferment of the SAN rank on 68 lawyers, including two from Templars, brought new attention on Mr Aghogho. Many have expressed admiration at what is regarded as his silent professional excellence and an unassuming public persona with scanty media coverage.
While the SAN rank remains an enviable height and an insignia of distinction in the legal profession, lawyers like Mr Akpata quietly show that excellence in the profession goes beyond the title awarded for success in a handful of criteria.
In the last eight years, the law firm has produced six SANs, starting with Adewale Atake in 2018. The rest are Godwin Omoaka, Inam Wilson, Olufemi Oyewole, Igonikon Adekunle and Sadiq Ilegieuno.
Mr Atake, the first on the list by year of elevation who became a SAN in 2018, began his legal career in his elder brother Eyimofe Atake’s chambers before joining Templars.
In an August 2026 interview with PUNCH, Mr Eyimofe recounted working with his younger brother on cases before the Supreme Court.
At Templars, Mr Atake developed a practice in commercial litigation, domestic and international arbitration, and investment disputes, particularly those involving the energy sector. He heads the firm’s Dispute Resolution practice and has represented international oil companies in major disputes with Nigerian government entities.
One notable case involved ExxonMobil and Shell in an arbitration over crude oil entitlements against the Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation (NNPC). The proceedings resulted in an award exceeding $2 billion in favour of the companies, according to Templars.
The Legal Practitioners’ Privileges Committee (LPPC) selected Mr Atake for the rank in 2018. He was sworn in at the Supreme Court in Abuja in September that year.
Another Templars partner elevated to SAN is Mr Omoaka. He attained the rank in 2019. The LPPC selected him in July that year, and he was sworn in at the Supreme Court in Abuja in September.
Mr Omoaka studied law at Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, graduating with a Bachelor of Law in 1997 and was called to the Nigerian Bar after from the Nigerian Law School in September 1999, according to The Nation.
He began his legal career at Muyiwa Obanewa & Co., where he worked from 1999 to 2000, before joining Sofunde, Osakwe, Ogundipe & Belgore as counsel from 2001 to 2002. He later joined TEMPLARS and became a partner in September 2009, according to the African Arbitration Association’s professional directory.
His practice focuses on commercial litigation, oil and gas disputes, arbitration, taxation and maritime law. He also heads TEMPLARS’ real estate practice and is a Fellow of the Chartered Institute of Arbitrators in the United Kingdom.
Mr Wilson, is also TEMPLARS partner elevated to the SAN rank in November 2022.
His practice covers labour and employment law, shipping, aviation and commercial disputes. He heads TEMPLARS’ Labour and Employment and Transportation practices and also works on corporate investigations, white-collar matters and regulatory compliance.
Mr Oyewole attained the rank in September 2025, after 11 years of active legal practice, according to a statement he published on LinkedIn.
Mr Oyewole holds a Master of Law in International Commercial Law from Robert Gordon University in Aberdeen, Scotland. He was appointed a Notary Public of the Federal Republic of Nigeria in 2022.
His practice focuses on commercial litigation, arbitration, corporate investigations and anti-corruption compliance. Among his notable cases was advising JPMorgan Chase in legal proceedings brought by the Federal Republic of Nigeria over payments linked to the sale of Oil Prospecting Licence 245 (OPL 245) to Shell and Eni.
Ms Adekunle is one of the two latest additions to the row of TEMPLARS partners with SAN ranks. She was sworn as a SAN on 12 October, alongside another partner of the firm, Sadiq Ilegieuno.
Ms Adekunle is a commercial litigator and arbitration counsel whose practice focuses on tax disputes. She also handles cases involving the energy, construction, financial services and environmental sectors.
In one notable case, she represented Nigeria LNG Limited in a tax dispute with the Federal Inland Revenue Service over an assessment of about $231 million. The assessment was reduced to approximately $3.25 million while the appeal was pending, according to her profile on TEMPLARS’ website.
For Mr Ilegieuno, one of TEMPLARS pair elevated to the SAN rank on 12 October, he studied law at the University of Benin and obtained a Master of Law from the University of Lagos. He joined TEMPLARS in 2005 and became a partner in 2018.
His practice covers commercial litigation, arbitration, energy and environmental disputes, data protection and regulatory matters. He has represented multinational companies in cases before Nigerian courts and arbitral tribunals.
Mr Akpata praised the two for their elevation to the SAN rank.
“Igonikon and Sadiq have earned this through years of rigour and courage. Their elevation speaks to what a practice becomes when it invests patiently in its people, and we are immensely proud of them,” TEMPLARS’ website quoted him as saying.
Mr Akpata read law at the University of Benin. He is a cousin to former president of the Nigerian Bar Association Olumide Akpata, a senior partner at TEMPLARS until his resignation in 2023 to contest the Edo State governorship election.
His professional career spans commercial law, arbitration and Nigeria’s oil and gas industry.
In interviews over the years, he has discussed the challenges facing the energy sector, the development of commercial arbitration and the firm’s approach to advising clients on major transactions.
In a 2015 interview published in the Sub-Saharan Africa Oil and Gas Handbook, Mr Akpata explained that TEMPLARS was established when Nigeria lacked sophisticated commercial legal services, particularly in the energy sector. The firm initially set out to build a leading oil and gas practice but later expanded into other sectors and became a full-service commercial law firm.
He discussed Nigeria’s prospects as a centre for commercial arbitration in an interview published by The Lawyer in June 2016. Mr Akpata said the Lagos Court of Arbitration had the potential to strengthen Nigeria’s position, but the country needed better security, stronger judicial support and improved hospitality infrastructure to compete with established centres such as London and Singapore.
He also observed that arbitration was becoming an increasingly common way to resolve commercial disputes as businesses recognised that arbitral awards could be enforced internationally. He identified oil and gas, energy, construction and power as sectors likely to generate significant arbitration work. At the time, TEMPLARS was seeking to develop a specialist practice in international arbitration and alternative dispute resolution.
In a July 2018 interview with The Energy Year, Mr Akpata examined changes in Nigeria’s oil and gas industry, including the growing role of indigenous companies. He said local operators were becoming more sophisticated and gaining greater recognition in the industry. He also noted that the Nigerian Oil and Gas Industry Content Development Act 2010 had helped increase Nigerian participation.
Mr Akpata identified regulatory uncertainty as a major risk for investors. Delays in renewing oil leases, he explained, could obstruct funding because investors lacked certainty about when approvals would be granted. He called for clearer rules and timelines. On gas development, he argued that Nigeria needed better incentives, infrastructure and commercially viable pricing to encourage investment and reduce its dependence on crude oil.
In an April 2022 interview with The Energy Year, Mr Akpata discussed the legal and financial structures behind major energy transactions. He highlighted TEMPLARS’ work on Heirs Holdings’ acquisition of a 45 per cent interest in Oil Mining Lease 17 and the associated $1.1 billion financing. He described the transaction as significant because of its financing structure and deferred purchase-price arrangement.
He also explained that TEMPLARS sought to advise clients from the conception of a project through to its completion, rather than limit its role to preparing legal documents. This approach involved understanding clients’ commercial objectives, identifying regulatory and financial risks, and structuring transactions to address them.
Mr Akpata also discussed the implications of the Petroleum Industry Act, which became law in August 2021.
He said the reforms had created demand for regulatory advice, restructuring of existing ventures and renegotiation of production-sharing contracts, while raising the prospect of disputes over existing contractual protections.
Mr Akpata’s profile on Templars’ website showcases accolades he has received regarding his legal practice, including The Chambers Globar Guide ranking him as a Senior Stateperson in Projects & Energy, a status said to be held by only two lawyers in Nigeria.

title: Germany’s Helsing Unveils Low-Cost Highspeed Drone Interceptors
body:
Helsing, a German military AI company, unveiled its Contra AI-controlled autonomous air defense system via a video posted on X on Monday. Helsing described it as a cost-effective system optimized to tackle jet-powered drone and missile attacks.
Helsing’s Contra system is intended to solve the existing air defense conundrum where the only current way of effectively intercepting jet-powered drones such as Russia’s Geran 4s and 5s is the use of multimillion-dollar interceptors.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Contra is intended to control two relatively inexpensive interceptor missiles: the AD-1 Inferno and AD-2 Ambush said to cost less than $100,000 each compared with Patriot PAC-3 missiles at $4-5 million a unit and the NASAMS (AMRAAM / AIM-9X) at around $1million a throw.
The military issues website Defense News cites recent intelligence reports , that Russia is increasing jet-powered drone and cruise missile production, to as much as 4,000 units a month, which, along with launch sites, could bring parts of the EU within range.
While still at the developmental stage, Helsing bills Contra, based on its well-proven Altra C2 platform, as an autonomous AI-based operation that will allow the real-time detection and engagement of hundreds or more drone and missile threats into a single air defense picture.
It is anticipated to be “field-ready” by late 2027, with Helsing saying its seekers rely on European supply chains and is free from Chinese components.
Intercepts would be achieved through a combination of two, advanced radar guided, container-launched missile interceptors whose performance is designed to overlap and supplement each other’s capability.
The AD-1 “Inferno,” which Helsing Chief Executive Gundbert Scherf says is intended as the “workhorse” of the counter-drone system, is powered by a jet engine, and flies at around 700 kph (435 mph) at a range of around 20 kilometers (12 miles). It can loiter over a defended area, swarm with other interceptors, and make repeated passes.
The AD-2 “Ambush,” intended as a rapid interceptor against drones and missiles that break through the AD-1 “net,” has a solid rocket motor and is said to have a flight speed of Mach 2.5 (1,900 mph, 3,000 kph) at a range of in excess of 20 kilometers (12 miles).
Both systems are able to be redirected mid-course by the Contra ground stations with an onboard radar-seeker for all-weather terminal guidance. While designed for, and capable of, stand-alone operation, Helsing said the system is set up to rapidly integrate with third-party counter-drone systems including missile interceptors, lasers, and guns. The company said Contra has already demonstrated such hardware integrations to multiple military customers.
Niklas Köhler, Co-Founder and President of Helsing, says: “Contra ends the air defense dilemma: slow fair-weather drones, or million-euro missiles fired at cheap, mass-produced targets. Our AI links existing sensors and effectors in real time and adds our interceptors, AD-1 and AD-2. With jet and rocket propulsion, a low-cost all-weather radar seeker, and two independent European supply chains, they deliver autonomous fire superiority up to ten kilometers (6+ miles) high – affordable and at industrial scale.”
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: ‎US partners with FG to end hunger, starvation
body: ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ‎‎ABUJA – THE Federal Government has received a major boost in its fight against hunger and child malnutrition, with the United States-backed Operation End Starvation (OES) seeking a direct partnership with the Federal Government to help scale up life-saving nutrition interventions across the country. ‎‎The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, disclosed this in Abuja when he led a delegation from OES and agencies under the Health Ministry to seek collaboration with the First Lady, Senator Oluremi Tinubu. ‎‎The proposed alliance is expected to strengthen Nigeria’s response to acute child malnutrition, with particular attention to vulnerable children, pregnant women and lactating mothers. ‎‎OES Chief Executive Officer, Williams Holdsworth Moore, said the organisation was impressed by Nigeria’s commitment and the capacity of its health leadership, describing the country as a priority site for its global intervention. ‎‎“We have met with the Nigerian health team, and they are one of the best of many we have met,” Moore said. ‎‎He explained that OES, supported by a macro grant from the United States Government and global philanthropists, plans to channel more than one billion dollars annually towards preventing child deaths caused by starvation. ‎‎“We want to move one billion dollars to end starvation in the next two years across Sub-Saharan Africa. The burden is high, but the capacity is also very high,” he said. ‎‎Moore added that the U.S. State Department had approved Nigeria as part of the organisation’s priority outlook, adding that OES wanted to demonstrate successful large-scale investment through direct government partnership within the next two years. ‎‎He explained thatOperation End Starvation, an initiative of the Eleanor Crook Foundation, is a public-private nonprofit focused on ending child malnutrition and starvation-related deaths across Sub-Saharan Africa, including Nigeria. ‎‎Prof. Pate said Nigeria was already implementing strong frameworks to confront malnutrition, citing the National Community Food Bank Programme, which is being delivered in partnership with the Office of the First Lady. ‎‎He said the programme, recently rolled out across the six geopolitical zones, was already recording positive impact and would be expanded to reach more vulnerable households. ‎‎“Nigeria is working hard to scale down its 6.4 million figure of acute child malnutrition, while also attending to the health of pregnant women and lactating mothers,” Pate said. ‎‎“A lot of good things are already happening in the country.” ‎‎The National Community Food Bank Programme is designed to provide nutritious, locally sourced food to children under six, pregnant women, lactating mothers and other high-risk households through community food banks linked to primary healthcare centres. ‎‎The First Lady of Nigeria, Senator Oluremi Tinubu welcomed the delegation and commended the quality of expertise and commitment within Nigeria’s public institutions, saying the country’s health team would justify any support received. ‎‎“It has been a delight working with Prof. Pate, Dr Muyi and others. I also work with the Ministry of Education and others. The manpower we have now in the ministries is so wonderful,” she said. ‎‎The First Lady assured the OES delegation that resources provided through the partnership would be deployed transparently and effectively. ‎‎“I assure you that whatever aid you give us, this health team would put it to good use,” she said. ‎‎She said Nigeria deserved better and that the reforms being undertaken by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu were gradually restoring the country’s systems. ‎‎“Nigeria deserves better, and there is nothing we give to her that is too much because if the system works, it will ultimately come back to us,” the First Lady said. ‎ ‎ The post ‎US partners with FG to end hunger, starvation appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Saskatchewan to unveil throne speech as legislative sessions starts
body:
Saskatchewan Premier Scott Moe’s government is promising to continue cutting personal income taxes.
The Saskatchewan Party government, in its throne speech read out Tuesday in the chamber by Lt.-Gov. Bernadette McIntyre, says that a family of four already doesn’t pay tax on the first $65,000 of income.
McIntyre said the government will follow up on a pledge it made two years ago to lower personal income taxes this year.
“While the current (international) trade disputes are increasing the cost of living for everyone, Saskatchewan continues to be the most affordable place to live in Canada,” she said.
She said the province plans to continue making investments in health care, including hiring more staff and adding addiction treatment beds.
Earlier Tuesday, Moe told reporters his priority is health care.
“We need to see more (health-care staff),” Moe said. “It’s all about making the right investments to improve our health-care system and access to it.”
The premier said the province has connected 18,000 additional residents to primary health providers. It has added more acute care beds and is completing construction of a new urgent care centre in Saskatoon. It has also built a new hospital in Weyburn and is well on its way to finishing a new hospital in Prince Albert.
The province promised multiple bills this fall.
One bill proposes to expand the scope of practice for health-care workers so that they can provide more services and help more patients.
Moe’s government also wants to regulate medical assistance in dying through the Medical Assistance in Dying Additional Safeguards Act.
McIntyre said the province plans to prohibit MAID to anyone under 18 and to those whose sole underlying medical condition is mental illness.
Current federal law already prevents MAID for those under 18, and Ottawa has introduced legislation to prevent MAID for those solely with mental health issues.
Asked why Saskatchewan needs its own legislation, Moe said a provincial law can still have a role.
The province also plans to introduce the protection of economic infrastructure act to ensure critical infrastructure isn’t occupied or blocked.
McIntyre said Bell Canada’s artificial intelligence megaproject southeast of Regina would boost jobs and the economy.
“There are some who would try to block this project and send those jobs, that investment and Canadians’ online data to another country, but Canadians understand the importance of home ice advantage,” she said.
On community safety and addictions, McIntyre said the province plans to hire more police officers and add 250 new addiction treatment beds. The province plans to have 500 addiction spaces operating by March.
There’s also the proposed protection from human trafficking act, which would require those in the hospitality industry and with ride-hailing platforms to report any suspicious human trafficking activity.
Another bill, the mandatory testing and disclosure act, would protect first responders and victims of crime. It would allow responders to seek mandatory testing on people they’ve come in contact with who are suspected of having hepatitis B or C, or HIV.
In education, Saskatchewan also plans to have new provincial literary screeners assess students.
The Opposition said the throne speech shows Moe’s government is tired and out of ideas.
NDP Leader Carla Beck said the speech fails to meet the moment and that New Democrats are planning to propose better ideas.
“You don’t have to settle for this anymore,” Beck said. “People in this province have some of the highest rates of economic and food insecurity.
“ In the birthplace of medicare, we have the worst rates of access to family physicians.”

title: South Africa opens criminal case over baobab trees reportedly destined for Georgia
body: Five large baobab trees — a species native to Africa which can live for up to 2,000 years — remain at a warehouse in Durban, South Africa while authorities investigate possible wrongdoing, the warehouse owner told OC Media . The trees were destined to be exported to Georgia, the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) told local outlet Daily Maverick . The department has opened an investigation as the trees are purported to have been felled and prepared for shipment without a permit. It is not known who ordered the export. Baobab trees have, however, previously been controversially exported to, and later died in, Georgia. In 2024, all eight baobab trees imported in 2023 from Kenya to the Shekvetili Dendrological Park — founded by billionaire, ruling Georgian Dream party founder, former Prime Minister, and tree enthusiast Bidzina Ivanishvili — died the following year. The park blamed the opposition political party United National Movement (UNM) for the trees’ fate. ‘Unfortunately, the stress endured by these unique plants had consequences, and 6–7 months after being planted in Georgia’s soil, all eight baobabs withered’, they wrote at the time. ‘The trees were harvested in the Lephalale Local Municipality, Waterberg District, Limpopo province, and were scheduled for export to Georgia, Europe,’ the DFFE said , regarding the trees in Durban. The warehouse’s owner Africa Global Logistics (AGL) told OC Media that ‘when concerns about the regulatory documentation’ came to their attention, they ‘stopped the proposed shipment’. AGL said that they were ‘not the owner, exporter, or permit holder for the trees, and was not involved in uplifting them or moving them from Limpopo. Responsibility for obtaining and maintaining the required licences, permits, and regulatory approvals rested with the owner and exporter’. The DFFE has not identified those facing criminal prosecution or the owner or exporter yet. The warehouse owner told OC Media that ‘AGL has cooperated with the relevant authorities and will continue to do so. No criminal charges have been brought against AGL in connection with this matter. As the matter remains subject to ongoing processes, AGL will not comment on the conduct or legal position of any other party’. Dr Sarah Venter, founder of the Baobab Foundation, estimated that the trees photographed by the Daily Maverick were ‘probably between 200 and 300 years old, very likely’ — the age at which a baobab reaches maturity. ‘An adult baobab tree often reaches adulthood only after 200 or 300 years. So they’re very slow-growing trees’ — which is one reason why the trees’ removal from their natural habitats can be so damaging. ‘They live for 2,000 years, you know, if you take a baobab tree out of its environment — let’s say the tree’s maybe 200 or 300 years old, you’re actually removing a resource from that environment that could be there for another 1,000 years’. She also highlighted the loss on the local residents and economy without these trees; ‘they use the fruit for food, they use the seed […] for their own medicine and fibre, for food, they also use the bark to weave mats and baskets’. ‘People are able to harvest that fruit for hundreds of years without damaging that tree and that fruit is processed and it is made into this baobab powder, if you google baobab powder, you see it’s a superfood, it’s sold now across the world as a superfood, it’s used as an ingredient in beverages, in juices, in yoghurts, in chocolates, you know — health drinks, energy drinks, that sort of thing’. 'What’s really valuable about this is because the tree only grows in Africa, the benefits of this go back to local people, so it’s a very important income to many local people being able to harvest and sell the fruit’. Venter raised concerns about the treatment of baobabs in Georgia despite the succulent trees being technically ‘really easy to uproot and replant somewhere else’. Ivanishvili-linked dendrological park blasts opposition over death of Kenyan baobab trees All eight baobab trees imported from Kenya to the Ivanishvili-founded Shekvetili Dendrological Park have died, with the park blaming the opposition United National Movement (UNM). In a sharply-worded statement on Friday, the park rebuked what it called ‘ambushing politicos’ and ‘so-called non-governmental organisations’ for raising the alarm over Ivanishvili’s apparent quest to acquire baobab trees from Kenya’s Kilifi region. This turned the issue into an ’ideological battleground on African c OC Media Shota Kincha ‘Georgia has not had a good track record keeping these trees alive in Georgia itself,’ she said, referencing the eight trees that died in 2024. The warehouse owner told OC Media that for the meantime the trees will stay at the Durban warehouse. ‘AGL is not authorised to move or release them while the relevant regulatory and criminal processes are unresolved, and it cannot take unilateral action that might conflict with the authorities’ directions or affect those processes. AGL is concerned about the preservation of the trees and will comply with any lawful direction from the competent authorities on their care, movement, or removal’. Additional reporting by Nino Shurghaia.

title: Sulu gets over 3,000 new teaching positions amid shift to DepEd control
body: MANILA, Philippines – The government approved the creation of over 3,000 teaching positions in Sulu as the province’s education office transitions to the jurisdiction of the Department of Education (DepEd). The DepEd announced on Tuesday, October 27, that the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) approved the creation of the following positions: 3,618 positions for Teacher I to Master Teacher II for kindergarten, elementary, and junior high school Nine teaching-related positions, including Head Teacher I and School Principal I and II In an explanation sent to Rappler, the DepEd said the figure came from the deployment plan it submitted to the DBM. The plan “directly facilitates the structured transition and absorption” of existing personnel of the Ministry of Basic, Higher, and Technical Education in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (MBHTE-BARMM) into the national government framework. Voters in Sulu had rejected the Bangsamoro Organic Law in a 2019 plebiscite, but the province was still initially included in BARMM because the then-ARMM provinces were deemed to have voted as a single bloc. Sulu’s exclusion from the new region was only finalized after a Supreme Court ruling in 2024. By 2025, the province had reverted to the Zamboanga Peninsula , following an executive order issued by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. Must Read Sulu shift to Zamboanga Peninsula tests gov’t ability to keep services running “DepEd, in coordination with the DBM, Regional Office IX, and local government partners, is fast-tracking the deployment and appointment protocols to guarantee that salaries, benefits, and operational support continue without interruption,” the agency said in a news release. Ronelo Al Firmo, the DepEd Zamboanga Peninsula director, said he will also discuss possible promotions for teachers. “Just imagine, may mga magre-retire na pero Teacher I pa rin. Kaya very important talaga na mai-discuss sa kanila ‘yong ECP, ‘yong Expanded Career Progression, para at least before sila mag-retire, at least makatikim man lang sila ng isang promotion,” Firmo told Radyo Pilipinas Jolo . (Just imagine, there will be teachers who will retire as Teacher I. That’s why it’s very important to discuss with them the ECP, the Expanded Career Progression, so that they’ll be able to experience at least one promotion before they retire.) The DepEd announced the formal transition of Sulu’s education office to its jurisdiction on October 20. Along with that was the DBM’s approval of the creation of 84 non-teaching plantilla positions. Of the 84 positions, 40 are held by current MBHTE-BARMM personnel deployed to Sulu, and are already prioritized for absorption under Civil Service Commission rules. Marcos also visited Sulu on October 20 to lead the rollout of the state health insurer’s Yaman ng Kalusugan Program or YAKAP health caravan at Kawmpang Elementary School in Patikul town. The provincial capitol and offices are located in this town. During the budget deliberations at the House of Representatives’ plenary in September, the DepEd committed to absorb Islamic Studies and Arabic Language teachers from the MBHTE-BARMM into the DepEd by January 2027. – Rappler.com

title: Minerals Commission defends termination of Northern Ashanti Mines’ licences over $8.38m debt
body: The Minerals Commission has defended its decision to terminate the mining leases and prospecting licences of Northern Ashanti Mines Limited, formerly Ower Mines, citing more than US$8.38 million in unpaid fees and alleged breaches of the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703). In a statement issued on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, the Commission said it followed the legally prescribed process after the company failed to settle outstanding Annual Mineral Right (AMR) fees or remedy other breaches identified by the regulator. The company has instituted legal proceedings against the State to challenge the termination, according to the Commission. The Commission said Northern Ashanti Mines acquired a mining lease covering 595 cadastral blocks in January 2010. Under Section 24 of Act 703 and the terms of its lease agreement, the company was required to pay annual mineral right fees. However, the Commission said the company had accumulated US$8.33 million in unpaid fees relating to its mining leases for the period from 2010 to 2025, alongside US$49,928 owed on prospecting licences covering 2019 to 2025. On April 14, 2025, the Commission issued Notices to Remedy Breach under Section 68(2) of Act 703 and Regulation 200(3) of the Minerals and Mining Regulations, 2012 (L.I. 2176), requiring the company to settle the outstanding amounts. The Commission said the company failed to comply within the stipulated period. Beyond the unpaid fees, the Commission said its assessment found that Northern Ashanti Mines had not undertaken meaningful mining operations on the concession for more than two years. It said this constituted a breach of Section 69(1) of Act 703. According to the Commission, the company was given an opportunity to regularise its position but failed to remedy the identified breaches. The Commission said it notified the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources on April 7, 2026, requesting that a notice of termination be served on the company. The Minister approved the issuance of the notice on April 24, 2026, and the Commission proceeded with the termination process on April 30, 2026. It maintained that the decision was taken in accordance with the law and that due process had been followed at every stage. The Commission also rejected suggestions that the company’s status as an indigenous business should exempt it from statutory obligations. “Once granted, a holder must abide by the rules, whether they are an indigenous company or not, and this includes the payment of statutory fees and the undertaking of meaningful mining operations,” the Commission stated. The Commission said the terminated mineral rights had reverted to the State, without extinguishing liabilities the company incurred before the termination. It said it would pursue the recovery of the outstanding fees and take steps to protect the affected assets against encroachment and other unlawful activities. “The Commission reserves the right and shall pursue the company to pay all the sums it owes to the State,” the statement said. The Commission confirmed that Northern Ashanti Mines had initiated legal proceedings challenging the termination after acknowledging receipt of the notice. It criticised the company’s media campaign, arguing that its public statements risked undermining the judicial process while the dispute remained before the courts.

title: Carrick to remain Man Utd boss for Chelsea clash – Reports
body: Michael Carrick is set to remain in charge of Manchester United for this weekend’s Premier League match away to Chelsea, according to media reports on Tuesday. Carrick’s future as United manager has been the subject of intense speculation after a run of eight games without a win. Sunday’s 3-0 defeat at home to Bournemouth left the English giants just one point above the Premier League relegation zone. But the BBC, Sky Sports and Britain’s Press Association all reported that former United and England midfielder Carrick would take the team to Stamford Bridge on Saturday. Carrick arrived at United’s Carrington training ground on Tuesday to oversee a routine squad session. The BBC cited “sources” as saying the 45-year-old would be given a chance by the United hierarchy to turn things around at Old Trafford following a terrible start to the season. Carrick was handed a two-year deal in May after overseeing an impressive revival as caretaker boss following United’s struggles under Ruben Amorim. The club recovered to finish third in the Premier League, earning a return to the Champions League. AFP The post Carrick to remain Man Utd boss for Chelsea clash – Reports appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Scores killed in drone strike on Nyala market, South Darfur
body: At least 102 civilians were killed and 113 others injured in a drone strike on Tanqong Market in the Dumaya neighbourhood of Nyala, South Darfur State, on Monday evening, according to local officials and rights groups. Nyala is the administrative capital of Tasis, a parallel government aligned with the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF). Dr. Alaa al-Din Nugud, health minister in the RSF-aligned Tasis government, in South Darfur told Radio Tamazuj on Tuesday that attacks on civilians by the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) continued, citing previous strikes on North al-Wadi, Nyala’s livestock market and Amiet Market in the Abyei area. “On Monday evening, a drone struck Tanqong Market in the Dumaya neighbourhood, west of Nyala, killing 102 civilians and injuring 113 others,” Nugud said. “Immediately after the attack, a medical team was dispatched to the scene to rescue the wounded.” He added that hospitals and health centres had been placed on full alert to treat the injured. Multiple sources said the drones struck the market while it was crowded with shoppers, killing and injuring civilians. Videos reviewed by Radio Tamazuj show victims of the strike being buried in a mass grave. Adam Musa Obama, Executive Director of the independent rights group Darfur Victims Organization, told Radio Tamazuj that his organisation had contacted eyewitnesses who reported that drones associated with the army carried out the attack. “The market was crowded with civilians who were buying their daily necessities and eating breakfast when the air strikes occurred,” Obama said. He said eyewitnesses had reported that 120 people were killed or wounded, while the organisation had documented 14 civilian deaths, including 12 women and six children, in the market during the attack. “We call on the international community to take immediate action to protect civilians and enforce a ban on the use of drones and weapons against civilians in all parts of Sudan,” Obama said. Sudan has been gripped by war between the SAF and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) since April 2023. The conflict has killed large numbers of people, displaced millions and devastated civilian infrastructure across the country. The post Scores killed in drone strike on Nyala market, South Darfur appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Tinubu writes NASS, seeks fresh approval to borrow $20.5bn, €1.05bn
body:
President Bola Tinubu has asked the National Assembly to approve the processing of external loans worth $20.5 billion ($20,517,755,901), and one billion Euros (€1,045,083,643) under the 2026–2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan.
The president said the proposed loans would finance critical projects across various sectors, including infrastructure, agriculture, healthcare, education, water supply, security and employment generation, as well as financial management reforms.
Mr Tinubu’s request was contained in a letter read by the Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, during plenary on Tuesday.
In the letter, the president said the proposed borrowing was necessary to support his administration’s reform agenda, adding that the projects had been selected based on technical and economic evaluations and their expected contributions to the country’s socio-economic development.
“I want to emphasise that the projects and programmes included in the Borrowing Plan were selected based on thorough technical and economic evaluation, as well as their anticipated contribution to the socio-economic development of the country,” he said.
Mr Tinubu said the projects would also promote employment, skills acquisition and entrepreneurship, reduce poverty and improve food security, thereby improving the livelihoods of Nigerian children.
He added that most of the projects and programmes would be implemented across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory.
“These initiatives aim to generate employment, promote skills acquisition, foster entrepreneurship, reduce poverty and enhance food security, all of which improve the livelihood of the Nigerian child.
“In light of the need for significant infrastructure investment in the country and the vast financial resources needed to address this gap, it has become essential to pursue broader external borrowings to close the financing shortfall,” he added.
Mr Tinubu said the funds would be channelled into critical infrastructure projects, particularly in the power, transportation and healthcare sectors.
“Given the urgent nature of these needs and the importance of stabilising the country, it is crucial to seek the consideration and approval of the National Assembly leadership and the entire National Assembly for the 2026–2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan.
“This will enable the government to fulfil its obligations to the Nigerian people through timely disbursements and effective project implementation,” he said.
After reading the letter, Mr Akpabio referred the request to the Senate Committees on Local and Foreign Debts and Appropriations for further scrutiny. He directed the committees to report back within one week.
The latest request comes about five months after the National Assembly approved a $516.3 million loan from Deutsche Bank AG to finance the construction of the Sokoto–Badagry Superhighway, a flagship infrastructure project under the Tinubu administration’s Renewed Hope Agenda.
The loan has a tenure of nine years, including a grace period of up to three years, with an interest rate capped at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange’s Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) plus 5.3 per cent annually.
The facility is backed by insurance from the Islamic Corporation for the Insurance of Investment and Export Credit, the insurance arm of the Islamic Development Bank.
In March, the National Assembly also approved a $6 billion external borrowing plan for the federal government.
Of that amount, $5 billion was to be sourced from First Abu Dhabi Bank to support the national budget, while a $1 billion export finance facility from the United Kingdom, arranged by Citibank, was earmarked for the rehabilitation of Tin Can Island Port and the Lagos Port Complex.
The latest borrowing request comes amid concerns about Nigeria’s rising public debt and the growing cost of servicing government obligations.
Nigeria’s debt burden has increased in recent years as the federal government has relied on domestic and external borrowing to finance budget deficits and infrastructure projects.
Although the country’s debt-to-GDP ratio has generally been considered moderate compared with that of some peer economies, analysts have raised concerns about the government’s limited revenue base and its capacity to meet debt obligations.
A substantial share of government revenue goes towards debt servicing, limiting the funds available for infrastructure, public services and other development priorities.
The International Monetary Fund and the World Bank have repeatedly urged Nigeria to strengthen revenue mobilisation, improve tax collection and ensure that borrowed funds support productive investments capable of generating economic returns.
The federal government has maintained that external borrowing is necessary to address the country’s infrastructure deficit, finance development projects and meet its budgetary obligations. Officials have also argued that borrowing on favourable terms can help manage financing costs and support economic growth.

title: Chechen police offer residents $100,000 for information on militants
body: Zamid Chalaev, commander of the special police regiment of Chechnya’s Interior Ministry, has offered a $100,000 reward for information about people involved in bombings or planning acts of sabotage, state news agency Chechnya Today reported on Monday. The offer comes amid a series of security operations in Chechnya, following an incident in Gudermes district in which security forces killed a man suspected of involvement in sabotage and detained another. The raids have been accompanied by threats from Chechen officials against people suspected of aiding militants, as well as increased security checks across the republic. Chalaev urged residents of the republic to provide security forces with information about people who might be connected to such activities. He said the reward would be paid for ‘substantial’ and ‘valuable’ information. ‘If you would feel distressed and hurt if your child, brother, mother, or sister were harmed in an explosion, you can contact us and provide information. If the information is substantial and valuable, you will be given $100,000’, Chechnya Today quoted Chalaev as saying. The regiment commander also said that people who had been involved in such activities but had not taken part in killings would be helped to get out of the situation. According to him, they would be able to ‘be useful to their homeland’ and receive financial assistance. Kadyrov confirms death in shootout after opposition movement claims unrest in Chechnya The shootout was the first armed incident in Chechnya officially confirmed by authorities in more than a year. OC Media Elizaveta Chukharova Chalaev’s statement came amid an intensification of security operations in Chechnya. Last Thursday, Chechen Head Ramzan Kadyrov said that security forces had killed a man suspected of involvement in acts of sabotage in Gudermes district and detained another. According to Chechen Interior Minister Aslan Iraskhanov, the suspects had carried out an explosion near an administration building last year and were planning an attack on a traffic police checkpoint. At a meeting of law enforcement officials following the killing of a local resident, whom the opposition Chechen channel NIYSO identified as Turpal-Ali Mezhidov, Kadyrov singled out Chalaev’s work for praise and thanked him. In the days following the incident, security forces conducted mass raids and increased patrols on roads and at borders across the republic. The NIYSO reported checks in several localities. Last Monday, Chalaev issued threats against residents suspected by security forces of aiding extremists and militants. In his appeal, he said he would show no restraint towards such people and threatened to shoot without trial or due process anyone who helped the suspects.

title: Knife-wielding man detained after approaching Democrats' Golan during Election Day tour in Tel Aviv
body: A man wielding a knife was detained after approaching The Democrats' Chairman Yair Golan, during a campaign tour to encourage voter turnout at HaMesila Park in Tel Aviv on Tuesday.According to Israel Police, security personnel noticed a suspicious object protruding from beneath the coat of a Jerusalemite in his 20s, standing near Golan. He was detained, and a knife was found in his possession.Police took him to the Lev Tel Aviv police station for questioning.Israel Police had previously raised Golan's threat level to four out of six. On Sunday, the Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency) announced it would assume responsibility for Golan's security, which would be funded by the state.“Incitement and violence will not deter us,” Golan said, following the incident. “This is a direct result of the 'poison machine' operated by [Prime Minister Benjamin] Netanyahu and his Qatari agents.”“I call upon everyone who holds security and democracy dear to go out and vote now, so that we may ensure the country we love so much returns to being a free and safe place.”Kariv claims incident is 'result of Netanyahu's incitement'MK Gilad Kariv condemned the incident in a Tuesday post on X/Twitter, calling the incident the “result of the incitement by Netanyahu and his partners.”“They incited against Yitzhak Rabin, and today they are inciting against Yair Golan,” Kariv wrote. “They will not intimidate us. The Democrats are continuing Rabin's path with a truth [ballot] slip. Only our slip will block their violence. No compromises.”

title: Zabuzhko: Ukraine had culture in 1995, but had lost it by 2005
body:
Ukraine was under information and cultural occupation in the decade between the 1990s and 2000s, writer Oksana Zabuzhko said.
"In 1995, we had culture. In 2005, we no longer had it. We were a branch of the 'great Russian world,' which was engaged in the information occupation of Ukraine throughout the entire pre-war decade, starting around the turn of the 1990s and 2000s. This was the same preparation of Ukraine for co-optation into Russia, carried out on a massive scale and quite successfully in the information and cultural spheres. Accordingly, we were invisible to the outside world. The visibility of any nation is cultural visibility. As long as the political class does not understand this, this country will be condemned to struggle somewhere in the third ranks, among the countries of the Third World," Zabuzhko said at the 12th Kyiv International Economic Forum, themed "People. Business. Economy. What Next?", in Kyiv, answering a question about whether Ukraine had achieved a cultural breakthrough.
She said that before the full-scale war, no one abroad was interested in engaging with the culture of "some invisible country whose future was still unknown."
"But once our glorious armed forces gave a thorough beating in the spring of 2022 to those who were considered the world's second army, my dream finally came true. In October 2022, Lesya Ukrainka's Cassandra premiered to great acclaim at London's Omnibus Theatre," the writer said.
In her view, the most relevant definition for Ukraine today was one given by political figure Vyacheslav Lypynsky: "The sum of values that, in the course of a community's life, have proved most conducive to that community's survival is called culture."
"Motivation wins, spirit wins, and so does what the Ukrainian soldier has and the Russian soldier lacks. That is a cultural difference. It is a sense of defending the values of one's community. Ask our soldiers what they are defending: their home, their land. At the level of one's home, one's land and one's family, at this level of rootedness, we have already defeated the Soviet regime and Russia in what they wanted to do to our ancestors during the Holodomor," Zabuzhko said.
Returning to the notion of a Ukrainian cultural "renaissance," she stressed that an artist would succeed with a domestic audience only if they articulated the collective unconscious. That was when queues would form for cultural products, as had happened with the play The Witch of Konotop at the Ivan Franko National Academic Drama Theatre.
"The state's role is to obtain information from experts about this very wild-growing garden: where to graft and where to water, which areas need watering, and where to put in money and later recoup it, whether through the state budget, patrons or fundraising. That is an entirely separate matter. What grows on its own does grow on its own, as we have seen over the past decade. They introduced quotas for Russian music on FM radio, and suddenly it turned out that a great deal of Ukrainian music had grown wild in the meantime, having spent the previous decade being considered unsuitable for the format," Zabuzhko said.
As reported, Deputy Prime Minister for Humanitarian Policy and Culture Minister Tetiana Berezhna said that, given the vastly unequal resources available for culture in Ukraine and Russia, Ukraine needed to act asymmetrically. She also said there was currently demand among Ukrainian consumers for Ukrainian culture, demand among creators to produce it, and a need to introduce Ukrainian culture to international audiences.

title: 5 siblings killed as tanker rams into tricycle in Gombe
body: Five children from the same family have died after a water tanker rammed into a commercial tricycle conveying them to school in Gombe metropolis. The accident occurred on Tuesday morning near Kanady Academy, along APC Square in the Government Reserved Area (GRA) of the state capital. The deceased were identified as Maryam Mansir Adamu and Usman Mansir Adamu, both Primary Five pupils of Jekadafari Primary School; Hauwau Mansir Adamu of Government Junior Secondary School (GJSS), Jekadafari; Aliyu Mansir Adamu of Government Day Secondary School (GDSS), Ahmadu Gombe; and Fatima Mansir Adamu, whose school was not specified. Three other children were injured in the crash and taken to the hospital for treatment. Kwara: Fallen 33kV power line razes buildings, workshop, vehicle CBN, Chinese firms explore solutions to cross-border payment hurdles The Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) Sector Commander in Gombe State, Samson Kaura, confirmed the incident, saying personnel of the corps arrived at the scene after the initial rescue operation had been completed. Kaura said FRSC officials subsequently visited the hospital to ascertain the number of casualties. A source at the Specialist Hospital, Gombe, said the injured victims and the drivers involved in the accident were taken to the Federal Teaching Hospital, Gombe, for medical attention. The bodies of the five deceased children were deposited at the mortuary. Reacting to the tragedy, Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya described the incident as heartbreaking, saying the loss of five children from one family was a devastating blow to their parents, relatives, schools and the entire state. In a statement issued by his Director-General of Press Affairs, Ismaila Uba Misilli, the governor said the children had died at a tender age when they should have been pursuing their education and looking forward to a promising future. He expressed sympathy with the bereaved family and the Jekadafari community, describing the deaths as an irreparable loss. The governor also prayed for the speedy recovery of the three injured children receiving medical attention. Yahaya called on motorists to exercise caution and responsibility, warning against reckless driving and other dangerous practices that put innocent lives at risk. He urged drivers to obey traffic regulations, maintain safe speeds, avoid dangerous manoeuvres and ensure their vehicles were roadworthy. The governor further stressed the need for heightened vigilance when transporting schoolchildren and other vulnerable passengers, urging road users to make safety their priority. He extended his condolences to the bereaved family, the management and staff of the affected schools, the pupils’ classmates and the wider community. He prayed to Almighty Allah to grant the deceased children Aljannatul Firdaus and give their parents and other family members the strength to bear the loss.

title: NASSCO launches US Navy's T-AO 212
body:
General Dynamics NASSCO has launched T-AO 212, also known as Hull 578, into San Diego Bay.
The vessel slid down the shipyard's ways during the launch, marking a milestone in its construction. NASSCO employees. The shipyard's launch team worked overnight and into the early morning to remove the blocks and cribbing supporting the vessel in preparation for the launch.
T-AO 212 is part of the John Lewis-class fleet replenishment oilers built by NASSCO for the U.S. Navy. The class is designed to replenish fuel and other essential supplies to Navy ships at sea, supporting sustained fleet operations.
The official christening ceremony for T-AO 212 is expected to take place in 2027.
To remind, NASSCO christened and launched the USNS Thurgood Marshall (T-AO 211), the seventh ship in the US Navy's fleet oiler program in June this year.
Fleet oilers serve as a supply lifeline for US Navy vessels carrying out missions across the globe, including in the Western Pacific, Indian Ocean, and beyond.
Crafted for underway replenishment, the oilers transfer fuel, lubricants, fresh water, and small amounts of dry cargo as part of the navy’s combat logistics force. NASSCO designs all new vessels with double hulls to protect against oil spills and to enhance the durability of cargo and ballast tanks.
The vessels measure 227.4 meters in length, with a full-load displacement of approximately 45,223 metric tonnes. Each can carry 157,000 barrels of oil (about 24.96 million liters), along with significant dry cargo and aviation capability, and can reach a top speed of 20 knots (37 km/h).
