title: Charles Bissue: The man who wants a trial but challenges the trial
body: Charles Bissue is an interesting accused person. He says he wants a speedy trial and accuses the Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) of delaying his day in court. Yet, his own legal history raises questions about how eager he has been to let the investigation and prosecution proceed. The OSP’s published records tell part of the story. Since 2023, he has filed 7 cases in respect of a case filed in 2025. The suits include the following: Suit No. J5/8/2025: Republic vs. High Court, Accra Human Rights Division (Court 2); Ex Parte Charles Bissue – Applicant, Office of the Special Prosecutor and Attorney-General – Interested Parties. Suit No. GJ/0098/2023: Republic vs. Office of the Special Prosecutor; Ex Parte Charles Bissue. Suit No. J8/08/2025: Republic vs. High Court, Accra Human Rights Division (Court 2); Ex Parte Charles Bissue – Applicant, Office of the Special Prosecutor and Attorney-General – Interested Parties. Suit No. GJ/0928/2023: Republic vs. District Court, Kaneshie and Office of the Special Prosecutor; Ex Parte Charles Bissue. Suit No. HR/0094/2023: Charles Bissue vs. Office of the Special Prosecutor Suit No. GJ/0358/2023: Charles Bissue vs. OSP, Anas Aremeyaw Anas and Tiger Eye P.I. Suit No. HR/0101/2023: Charles Bissue vs. Kaneshie District Court. h. Suit No. H3/458/2025: Charles Bissue vs. Office of the Special Prosecution, Kaneshie District Court. These are not minor details. They show that legal proceedings initiated by Bissue formed part of the history that preceded his prosecution. Yet, through sections of the media, he has suggested that he has been standing trial since 2017. The OSP was established in 2018. Investigations, civil litigation and criminal trials are not the same thing. One cannot simply collapse them into a single timeline. The OSP eventually filed fresh criminal proceedings on 1 July 2025 under CR/0559/2025, The Republic v Charles Cromwell Nanabanyin Onuawonto Bissue & 2 Ors . Bissue faces nine counts relating to corruption and abuse of public office. Raphael Mensah and Dr Naa Dedei Tagoe are charged in connection with the alleged scheme. All three pleaded not guilty. The case is not about whether Bissue considers the alleged amount small. It concerns allegations that public office was compromised to facilitate the issuance of a concession sticker enabling a business entity to commence mining without a licence. If proved, the alleged conduct would raise serious questions about the integrity of the public process, regardless of the amount involved. Thomas Andy Owusu, who was charged in the earlier case, pleaded guilty and was convicted in June 2025 under a plea agreement. His conviction does not establish Bissue’s guilt, which remains for the court to determine. Now, the dispute has shifted to whether the earlier case was properly discontinued and whether the current proceedings can continue. His lawyers have also raised arguments concerning an earlier police investigation and alleged conflict of interest involving the Special Prosecutor’s past professional association with Anas Aremeyaw Anas. These arguments must be assessed against the relevant court records and rulings. But the central contradiction remains: how does one repeatedly demand a speedy trial while pursuing legal challenges that may prevent the trial from proceeding? Bissue has every right to challenge the prosecution. The court must determine those objections fairly. But a procedural dispute is not automatically the end of a criminal case, just as a prosecution is not proof of guilt. The OSP should not be interested in winning a public-relations contest. Its duty is to pursue justice. If the evidence fails, Bissue must be acquitted. If the prosecution proves its case, the law must take its course. A speedy trial should lead to a judicial determination—not become a slogan used against the prosecution while the proceedings themselves are being challenged.

title: Dutch armed forces chief calls for preparations for large-scale conflict
body:
THE HAGUE, October 27. /TASS/. Dutch Armed Forces Commander General Onno Eichelsheim said the country needed to prepare for a full-scale conflict but did not specify which one.
"We must prepare for a large-scale conflict, although we cannot say with certainty what it will look like," Eichelsheim wrote on his page on X.
Eichelsheim’s remarks come amid a major expansion of the kingdom’s military capabilities. According to a draft budget presented on September 15, 28.9 billion euros is planned to be allocated for defense in 2027. By 2030, the Defense Ministry aims to increase its personnel, including military personnel, reservists and civilian staff, to more than 100,000. The ministry cites, among other reasons, alleged "threats" from Russia to justify the expansion of the country’s military capabilities.
Moscow has repeatedly rejected claims that Russia allegedly plans to attack NATO countries. Russian President Vladimir Putin has described such statements by Western politicians as attempts to intimidate their own populations and justify increased military spending. Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov, in turn, has said that the alliance is pursuing a policy of "rampant militarization" and that portraying Russia as a "threat" is being used to justify a decision to raise NATO member states’ defense spending to 5% of gross domestic product.

title: Troops kill 8 terrorists, recover weapons in Kaduna, Zamfara
body: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Operation Fansan Yamma (OPFY) have neutralised 8 suspected armed terrorists and rescued 3 kidnapped victims in coordinated operations conducted in Katsina, Kaduna and Zamfara States. According to a statement by Captain Tamuno Sinive, Media Information Officer, the operations also led to the recovery of an AK-47 rifle, 3 locally fabricated guns, 3 motorcycles, cutlasses and assorted charms from the terrorists. He said, “On Saturday 24 October 2026, troops of Sector one received a distress call from farmers at Machika Dam, Sabuwa Local Government Area of Katsina State, reporting terrorist activities in the area. “The troops promptly mobilised to the location and engaged the terrorists in a gun battle, resulting in the neutralization of two terrorists, while others fled the area. “In the course of the operation, troops also rescued Mr Suleiman Umar, aged 42, who had been kidnapped by the terrorists. ‘Further exploitation of the area led to the recovery of one AK-47 rifle with a magazine containing rounds of ammunition, as well as one motorcycle. “In another incident on the same day, troops of Sector one, in conjunction with the Civilian Joint Task Force (CJTF), foiled a terrorist ambush along Ungwan Iya, Igabi Local Government Area of Kaduna State, neutralising 6 suspected terrorists. “During the operation, the troops recovered three locally fabricated guns, 2 motorcycles, cutlasses and assorted charms. “The incident occurred when the troops responded to a distress call reporting an attack by suspected armed terrorists at Ungwan Mallami village, during which the terrorists fled with two kidnapped victims. “However, while trailing the terrorists, the troops came under attack but responded swiftly with superior firepower, resulting in the neutralization of the terrorists, while others fled in disarray. “Similarly, troops of Sector 2, rescued two kidnapped victims in Bagega, Anka Local Government Area of Zamfara State, on Sunday, 25 October 2026. “The rescued victims were identified conducting as Mr Shehu Chete, aged 40, and Mr Bugu Bedi, aged 25, both indigenes of Kebbi State. “The troops, while conducting surveillance operations in the general area, observed the activities of suspected terrorists and swiftly responded with a fighting patrol. “On sighting the troops, the terrorists fled the area, abandoning the 2 victims. “The rescued victims were immediately evacuated to Bagega Clinic for medical attention before being moved to the military base for further assessment and subsequent reunion with their families. “Troops are currently dominating the general areas through sustained patrols and search operations aimed at apprehending the terrorists, rescuing kidnapped victims and preventing further attacks towards ensuring the safety of residents. “The Theatre Commander, Joint Task Force North West, Operation has commended the troops of Fansan Yamma for their gallantry and resilience in responding to the attacks. “Members of the public are urged to continue supporting ongoing military operations by providing timely and credible information on suspicious movements and activities within their communities.” The post Troops kill 8 terrorists, recover weapons in Kaduna, Zamfara appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Putin proposes GECF nations team up to optimize gas supply routes
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Gas-exporting nations need to work on optimizing fuel supply routes to markets, Russian President Vladimir Putin said at the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) summit.
"The main problem today is the disruption of gas supplies. Large volumes of supply have dropped out of the market in a short period, while demand has remained unchanged. This means it is necessary to work on optimizing transport routes – taking into account the geographical locations of the Forum’s member countries – by utilizing reciprocal operations among them, that is, among us," he said.
According to the president, addressing the challenges facing the global gas industry requires building cooperation, not barriers, above all among gas-exporting nations. "This should be achieved by leveraging our own capabilities and sovereign technologies, while fostering open, trust-based collaboration rooted in the principles of mutual benefit and respect for one another’s interests," he emphasized.
Putin noted that the increasing flexibility and mobility of the modern gas market – driven by the widespread use of liquefied natural gas (LNG) – makes this possible. "After all, LNG shipments are not dependent on international pipelines. LNG already accounts for approximately half of global gas trade. I must stress that replacing lost volumes and restructuring logistics is no simple task. It is essential to maintain a balance between the interests of gas suppliers and consumers, and to fulfill existing contractual obligations," he explained.

title: 'Raise it high': Sheikh Mohammed calls on UAE public to celebrate Flag Day
body: Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid , Vice President and Ruler of Dubai , on Tuesday urged people across the UAE to mark Flag Day on November 3. Sheikh Mohammed urged government institutions, ministries, schools, universities and the public in all seven emirates to participate by flying the UAE flag. He described it as a symbol of national pride, loyalty and unity. "Raise it high, proud, noble and fluttering in the sky of our country," Sheikh Mohammed said in a message on X. "Next week, on November 3, we celebrate a vital national moment that embodies our love, pride and loyalty to our homeland. We celebrate Flag Day." He said it was an occasion when the entire nation could come together to express their commitment to the country. “A single national moment ... where the homeland and its sons stand ... before the symbol of our honour and glory,” he wrote, reaffirming the deep emotional connection between the UAE ’s national flag and the sacrifices made in service to the country. “Long live the homeland ... long live the flag." الإخوة والأخوات.. نحتفي الأسبوع المقبل، في الثالث من نوفمبر، بلحظة وطنية مهمة تجسد محبتنا وفخرنا وولاءنا لوطننا.. نحتفي بيوم العلم. ندعو الجميع.. مواطنين ومقيمين.. مؤسسات ووزارات.. مدارس وجامعات.. بيوت في كافة الإمارات.. لرفعه عالياً شامخاً عزيزاً خفاقاً في سماء بلادنا.. لحظة… — HH Sheikh Mohammed (@HHShkMohd) October 27, 2026 Although Flag Day is not a public holiday, people across the UAE mark it with pride and a sense of patriotism. This is not the first time Sheikh Mohammed has urged citizens and residents to unite and display the national banner, which he has described as a "symbol of strength and pride". This year, amid Iranian attacks on its regional neighbours, he renewed his call for people across the UAE to fly the flag at their homes in a show of national solidarity. The move further united citizens and residents, with homes and companies rallied to demonstrate their faith in the country and its leadership. “The UAE flag is a symbol of strength and pride,” Sheikh Mohammed said. He expressed deep pride in the nation's leadership, military, economy, workforce and its diverse community. What is Flag Day? Sheikh Mohammed established Flag Day in 2013 to commemorate the late President Sheikh Khalifa's accession in 2004. The occasion has since become a staple of the national calendar. The UAE flag, designed by Abdullah Al Maainah , comprises four colours, known as the pan-Arab colours, which each symbolise a distinct attribute. White represents good deeds and generosity; green is a sign of growth and prosperity; black represents strength, resilience and courage; and red shows the sacrifices made by previous generations of Emiratis in defence of the nation. While Flag Day is observed annually and gives people an opportunity to demonstrate their allegiance to the country, strict rules govern how the symbol can be displayed. Authorities periodically update and distribute these guidelines. When displaying flags indoors, the base can be gold, silver or wooden. The flag must not touch the ground or base and must be at least 20cm to 25cm from the base.

title: Minority demands independent probe into South Africa evacuation costs
body: The Minority in Parliament has called for an independent investigation into the payments made to Ghanaians who were evacuated from South Africa by the Foreign Affairs Ministry. The caucus says an independent probe is necessary to establish the facts surrounding the GH¢49.72 million reportedly spent on evacuating 1,964 Ghanaians between May 27 and September 4, 2026, amid renewed xenophobic attacks. The Minority, during a press conference on Tuesday, October 27, raised concerns about alleged gaps in flight records, inconsistencies in payment registers and duplicate entries in documents relating to the evacuation. “Given the gravity of these revelations and in order to ensure an impartial investigation into the matter, we call on the Minister for Foreign Affairs, Honourable Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, to resign immediately. His handling of this exercise has brought his high office into disrepute,” Ranking Member on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, Samuel Abdulai Jinapor, said. It has also questioned payments for reintegration and transport allowances, arguing that the issues require thorough scrutiny to establish whether there were any financial or administrative irregularities. READ ALSO: Minority demands Ablakwa’s resignation or dismissal over SA evacuation payments The controversy follows the release of documents by the Ministry in response to a Right to Information request, which the Minority says contain discrepancies that require further investigation. Mr Ablakwa has denied allegations of financial impropriety, insisting that the evacuation expenditure is accounted for. He has also called for an independent audit of evacuation exercises undertaken since 2017, including the South Africa operation. The Minority says the investigation must establish accountability and ensure transparency in the management of public funds. It has consequently demanded the immediate resignation of Mr Ablakwa, warning that it will call on President John Dramani Mahama to dismiss him if he fails to step down. The caucus has threatened to initiate a vote of censure against the Minister in Parliament if its demand is not met.

title: Edo Voter Register: Utomi, others demand INEC explanation over alleged AI-generated images
body: By Emmanuel Okogba Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) chieftain and economist, Prof. Pat Utomi, has raised concerns over allegations that artificial intelligence (AI)-generated photographs appear in the Independent National Electoral Commission’s (INEC) online voter register in parts of Edo State. Utomi’s reaction followed posts by social media user Decosule, who called on INEC to explain the presence of what he described as AI-generated images in voter records displayed on the commission’s website. Decosule shared screenshots purportedly taken from the online voter register for polling units in Ward 11, Etsako West Local Government Area, and Udomi in Esan Central Local Government Area, questioning the authenticity of some photographs. He asked the electoral commission to clarify how the images were included in the register, who conducted the voter registration or image-capturing process, and whether the Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) associated with the entries had been collected. In a post reacting to the issue, Utomi warned that questions surrounding the images could undermine public confidence in the country’s electoral process if not properly addressed. “INEC cannot afford to be careless with the credibility of Nigeria’s electoral process. The presence of AI-generated images in a register meant to support our democracy raises serious questions about verification, transparency and accountability. Our democracy is at stake here!” Utomi wrote. Decosule had also claimed to have observed similar images in the register for Udomi in Esan Central, the local government area associated with Edo State Governor Monday Okpebholo. The screenshots shared by Decosule showed voter entries under polling units identified as Iyoku–Utukwe Afashio Booth and Ikabigbo I–Ikabigbo Primary School in Etsako West, as well as Udomi Primary School in Esan Central. Decosule urged INEC to provide an explanation, particularly regarding the origin of the photographs and the processes used to verify voter information. However, the screenshots alone do not independently establish that the images were generated using AI or demonstrate whether any irregularities occurred during voter registration. INEC is yet to provide an official response to clarify the authenticity of the photographs, how they came to appear on the online platform and whether the commission had identified any problems with the records. The post Edo Voter Register: Utomi, others demand INEC explanation over alleged AI-generated images appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Ghana must move from ESG policy commitments to action – Local Government Minister
body: The Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga, has called for stronger institutional coordination, sustainable financing and accountability mechanisms to accelerate the adoption of Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) principles across Ghana’s economy. He said integrating ESG considerations into national policies, institutional practices and private sector operations was essential to promoting responsible investment, protecting natural resources and creating sustainable economic opportunities. Addressing the Ghana National Climate and ESG Policy Summit 2026 at the Mövenpick Ambassador Hotel in Accra on Tuesday, October 27, the Minister said Ghana must move beyond policy commitments to practical and measurable action. “The integration of Environmental, Social and Governance principles into national policies, institutional practices and private-sector operations is therefore not merely a matter of compliance or corporate responsibility. It is a strategic imperative,” he said. He explained that effective implementation would require stronger coordination among government institutions, increased mobilisation of sustainable finance and meaningful partnerships with the private sector, development partners, academia and civil society. The Minister also emphasised the importance of transparency, accountability, institutional capacity and reliable data in advancing sustainability practices. “Public and private institutions alike must be encouraged to adopt credible sustainability practices, strengthen environmental and social risk management, and report their progress against clearly defined standards and measurable indicators,” he said. He noted that the scale and complexity of climate change required a coordinated national response supported by sustained commitment, adequate financing and effective implementation. “Government, on its part, remains committed to advancing policies and partnerships that support climate resilience, environmental protection, sustainable investment and responsible governance,” he added. The Minister urged participants to ensure that the summit produced concrete policy recommendations and institutional commitments rather than ending with discussions alone. “This Summit must therefore serve as more than a forum for discussion. It must be a catalyst for concrete policy recommendations, institutional commitments and actionable strategies,” he said. He welcomed plans for the summit to conclude with a National Communiqué, noting that his ministry would work with local assemblies to advance recommendations relevant to local government. The summit brought together government officials, local government leaders, private sector representatives, development partners and civil society organisations to discuss strategies for strengthening climate resilience and promoting ESG principles in Ghana.

title: Primorye Region Delays Social Benefits to Cover War Expenses
body:
Authorities in Far Eastern Russia’s Primorye region warned residents on Tuesday that they may face delays in receiving government benefits as the regional budget comes under strain from spending on the war against Ukraine.
“Under these conditions, individual social support measures will be funded in stages, so some transfers may occur with temporary delays,” the regional labor and social policy ministry said in a statement posted on Telegram.
Officials did not say how long the delays would last, promising only that all social obligations would be fulfilled “as the necessary funding arrives.”
The announcement comes a week after the Primorye region’s legislative assembly slashed this year’s regional budget by 3.8 billion rubles ($47.1 million) across 18 state programs, including healthcare, affordable housing, education and social support.
Those cuts coincided with 1.5 billion rubles ($18.6 million) being added to the regional reserve fund to support specific groups of people affiliated with the war in Ukraine, like veterans and the families of service members.
Around one in three people in Primorye, a region of 1.8 million, rely on state support across 97 different programs.
Soaring spending on the war continues to strain both the federal government’s budget and those of regions across the country.
Nationwide, Russia’s 2026 budget deficit is expected to reach a record 7.345 trillion rubles ( 88 billion), nearly twice the previous forecast of 3.785 trillion rubles ( 45 billion). That new projection represents 3.2% of GDP compared to the previous target of 1.6%.
President Vladimir Putin said last month that the size of Russia’s budget deficit poses no “critical” risk for the economy and that officials will do everything to keep it under control.

title: GPL 2026/27: ‘I will resign if Samartex engages in match-fixing’ – GM Edmund Ackah
body: FC Samartex 1996 General Manager Edmund Ackah has vowed to resign from his position if the club is found to be involved in match-fixing or any illegal activity. Ackah made the declaration amid concerns over reports linking the club to match manipulation and the absence of several of their matches from television coverage. Speaking in an interview with Asempa FM, the experienced football administrator said he had confidence in the club’s leadership and management. “I will resign from FC Samartex if the club engages in anything illegal or match-fixing,” he stated. “I have heard that our games are not on television because of where we are located and the distance, but that is not fair,” he added. “Our stadium is safe because there are CCTV cameras everywhere, so I don’t know why there will be that decision not to air our games.” The 2024 Ghana Premier League champions currently sit third on the league table. Matchday nine will see Samartex hosts Bibiani Gold Stars at the Nsenkyire Sports Arena on Sunday November 1.

title: Right-leaning voters in Jerusalem share core values for future gov't but split over who should lead
body: Security, religion, and loyalty remain the core values Jerusalem residents shared as they prepared to vote in the 26th Knesset elections, with opinions sharply split over whether Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu should remain prime minister. The Jerusalem Post recently conducted street interviews at Shuk Mahane Yehuda and on Ben Yehuda Street in the city, where residents were asked who they plan to vote for in the elections and their reasons behind the choice.These individuals dictate the fate of the political dynamic of the country for the next four years. All voters interviewed leaned right, but were split over which party should lead. The interviewees were randomized and remained completely anonymous, with their gender being the only characteristic recorded.In a tight race, with the opposition widening its lead, Yashar party head Gadi Eisenkot remains ahead of Netanyahu. About 60% of Israelis favor a unity government, though votes shifting between right-wing parties could decide whether the bloc reaches 61 seats.Many people in Jerusalem said they feel strongly loyal to Netanyahu. Two voters said they would vote to re-elect him, saying, “He is a great ally to America, America is a great ally to him,” and that “his policies are the right ones to follow.”Many citizens, however, remained unsure about who to vote for and said they are relying on their families to influence their decisions.A woman in Nachlaot, who said she wants a government that “supports Torah learning” and "lower prices," admitted that “we love Netanyahu, but I don't understand too much politics, so I'm not sure, I have to ask my husband what exactly we are doing”With 120 seats in the Knesset, and 61 needed to govern, the gap between Israel's coalition and opposition blocs has widened to six seats ahead of Tuesday's Knesset election, despite the two largest parties being separated by just two seats, according to a Maariv poll by Lazar Research published Friday. Several people said they resent Netanyahu and the current government and are voting for his rivals, with one man saying, “probably something not in the current government. I'm not sure I can explain, to be honest. I don't like part of their attitude.”Another female supporter of former prime minister Naftali Bennett said that “the list of people that are with him are going to do good for the country and want to make good rules in Israel.”“He really cares about the country and not about populism or making money for himself,” she added.Current voter turnout expected to surpass that of 2022 electionThe Maariv poll also found that the proportion of Israelis who are certain they will vote in Tuesday's Knesset election continued to rise, reaching 81%. The figure suggests a potential increase in voter turnout compared with the 2022 election, when turnout stood at 71%.In 2022, Likud won about 23% of the vote, Yesh Atid about 17.79%, and the Religious Zionist Party 10.84%, according to the official Knesset website.Voters backing a different right-wing party believe that their religious values feel aligned with those of certain parties such as Shas and RZP, both of which are “good for the religious people, the Haredi people,” according to the people of Jerusalem.Two individuals said they will vote for Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich for a multitude of reasons:     “I think I want to vote Smotrich because I'm part of the party... and I believe in the same values, and I think it's the best way for Israel, for the next [few] years,” said one interviewee.“One of them [the reasons] is bitachon (security). It's a bit funny, but he has that I believe in it. Also, I come from the Religious Zionist community, so he gives me things that I believe in and helps me with what I need,” said another.Many people prioritize safety and security, and the street interview data reports one man in Mahane Yehuda voting for National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir for these exact reasons. Additionally, many people say their rabbis advise them not to share who they plan to vote for. 'Just not Bibi'This week's Maariv poll shows that, nationally, support for the coalition appears to be slipping, and the coalition bloc has weakened by three seats compared with the previous week's poll. In the last days before the vote, akin to the previous poll, 60% of Israelis would prefer the formation of a unity government if the Knesset election produces no clear result.  Some voters interviewed in Jerusalem reflected that shift. “I just know I don't want Bibi,” said a woman in Mahane Yehuda who is leaning toward Bennett, referring to Netanyahu by his nickname.Most, however, said they would back parties in the current coalition, and their answers focused on a right-wing government rather than a unity one. “For sure we want right wing,” said a woman in Nachlaot.

title: Assemblies must lead Ghana’s climate response – Local Government Minister
body: The Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mahama Ayariga, has called on Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies (MMDAs) to take a leading role in Ghana’s response to climate change, urging them to translate national commitments into practical results at the community level. He said the effects of climate change, including flooding, drought, pressure on land and water resources, and threats to farming livelihoods, were being felt directly in districts, making local government institutions central to the country’s green transition. Speaking at the Ghana National Climate and ESG Policy Summit 2026 at the Mövenpick Ambassador Hotel in Accra on Tuesday, October 27, the Minister said climate considerations must be incorporated into the development plans and budgets of local assemblies. “Much of that action will happen at the local level. It is in our districts that the effects of climate change are felt first,” he said. He added that national commitments could only produce meaningful results if local authorities were equipped with the capacity and resources to implement climate policies effectively. “Decentralising the green transition means mainstreaming climate and ESG considerations into the medium-term development plans and budgets of our Assemblies; strengthening the capacity of our Assemblies to plan, finance, deliver and report on climate action,” he said. The Minister said his ministry would continue to collaborate with the Office of the Minister of State for Climate Change and Sustainability, the Ministry of Environment, Science and Technology, the District Assemblies Common Fund (DACF), the National Association of Local Authorities of Ghana and development partners to advance the agenda. He also highlighted the role of traditional authorities in climate action, describing them as “essential partners” because of their position as custodians of land and natural resources. The Minister further stressed the need to ensure that climate policies addressed the needs of vulnerable communities, women, young people and people whose livelihoods depended directly on the natural environment. “A just and equitable transition must remain central to our development agenda, ensuring that the benefits of climate action are broadly shared and that no community is left behind,” he said. He urged local government leaders to demonstrate commitment to climate action by ensuring that the decisions and recommendations emerging from the summit are translated into tangible improvements in their respective communities.

title: Mbappe Apologises For Mao Zedong Comment After Chinese Sponsors Dropped Him
body: Kylian Mbappe apologised on Tuesday after the Real Madrid star was dropped by major Chinese brands for apparently joking about Mao Zedong in a video that has gone viral. There were also signs of broader repercussions, with state-run The paper reported that public television was suspending broadcasts of matches from Spain’s La Liga. The offending video shows Mbappe saying that the funniest internet meme he had seen involving him was of his face photo-shopped onto that of “some guy — I think he’s a Chinese dictator”. This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappe superimposed on an image of Mao. The authenticity of the video could not immediately be verified by AFP Fact Check. “My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world. I apologise to everyone my words have upset,” French forward Mbappe said in a statement in French, Chinese and English. Spain’s La Liga also apologised, saying it “deeply regrets the offence that Kylian Mbappe’s recent comments have caused among Chinese fans. These comments were made in a personal capacity and do not represent La Liga.” In China, jokes about Mao, the country’s founding leader who died in 1976 — and whose drastic policies are also blamed by historians for mass starvation and millions of deaths — remain taboo. Beverage giant Dongpeng, which during this year’s World Cup ran adverts with AI-generated images of Mbappe consuming its sport drink, said it was terminating all cooperation with the France captain. “Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments,” Dongpeng said in a statement. Bottles of Dongpeng Beverage Group’s “Bushuila” electrolyte drink featuring French football star Kylian Mbappe on the packaging are displayed at a convenience store in Beijing on October 27, 2026. (Photo by PEDRO PARDO / AFP) | PEDRO PARDO / AFP Mengniu, China’s largest dairy producer, and cheesemaker Milkground also said that they were cutting ties with Mbappe, who until now was hugely popular among Chinese fans with millions of social media followers. “Dongpeng Beverage ends cooperation with Mbappe” was the top-trending topic on Chinese social media site Weibo with 430 million views. One Weibo user said the “extremely serious wrong remarks… crossed the red line” and others urged Dongpeng to remove Mbappe’s image from their bottles. Dongqiudi, one of China’s biggest online football outlets, said Mbappe’s remarks were “offensive to China and the Chinese people”. Furore In an interview with French sports newspaper L’Equipe, the 27-year-old Mbappe in September addressed a previous meme depicting him as a military dictator. “There’s a part of it that’s funny… but there is another part that’s a bit less funny because of the damage such people have caused throughout history,” he said. China’s foreign ministry said it was aware of the reports regarding Mbappe, who on Monday finished runner-up to English forward Harry Kane in the Ballon d’Or award for the world’s best player. “Words and actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be met with unanimous rejection from all sectors of Chinese society,” spokesman Guo Jiakun told a regular briefing. State media outlet The paper cited sources at the state broadcaster saying that CCTV has suspended all broadcasts of La Liga matches and removed all advertisements involving Mbappe. On the CCTV website, La Liga matches this weekend were still on its online viewing schedule. Drawing China’s Ire Global sports stars who have commented on sensitive topics such as Taiwan, Tibet and Hong Kong have previously caused controversy in China and been dumped by sponsors. China suspended sponsorship deals with the NBA while the state broadcaster pulled NBA games off Chinese television for a year in October 2019. This followed Houston Rockets executive Daryl Morey tweeting, “Fight for freedom, stand with Hong Kong,” referring to protests in Beijing called separatist and seditious. Adam Zhang, founder of the Beijing-based sports consultancy firm Key-Solution Sports Consulting, speaking before Mbappe apologised, said a rapid response was needed to quell the growing crisis. “It’s crucial to make a sincere statement. The sooner, the better,” Zhang told AFP. Fans made their feelings clear. “I used to really enjoy watching Mbappe play on the pitch,” Zhang Jingqi, 30, who works at a mall in Beijing, said. “But ever since this news broke yesterday, I have lost that admiration, sorry to say.” The post Mbappe Apologises For Mao Zedong Comment After Chinese Sponsors Dropped Him appeared first on Channels Television .

title: NCAA probes airline as passenger reports bleeding on Abuja-Calabar flight
body:
The Nigeria Civil Aviation Authorit y (NCAA) has launched an investigation into a passenger’s complaint that poor ventilation and excessive heat aboard a flight from Abuja to Calabar left him bleeding.
The authority’s Director of Public Affairs and Consumer Protection, Michael Achimugu, said the complaint had been referred to its Directorate of Operations, Licensing and Training Standards for investigation.
The complaint followed a post on X by a passenger, Bashir Usman, who said travellers spent about 50 minutes inside the aircraft after its doors were shut, without the engines running or functioning air conditioning.
Mr Usman said the heat became unbearable and he began bleeding before the aircraft eventually arrived in Calabar at 2:04 p.m. on Monday.
He explained that the flight had been scheduled to last about 45 minutes, describing the experience as distressing.
“We boarded at 12:07 p.m. After the aircraft doors were shut, we remained onboard for about 50 minutes without the engines running and, sadly, without functioning air conditioning. The heat became unbearable, and I eventually started bleeding,” he wrote.
Mr Usman added that members of the crew approached him and told him he would have to leave the aircraft because of the bleeding, but he maintained that he was fine.
He credited fellow passengers with supporting him during the incident, saying some took turns fanning him while one woman offered him her personal mini fan.
According to him, the passengers also expressed concern about the heat and the lack of ventilation, after which he was allowed to remain on board.
Mr Usman later thanked those who had travelled with him on the Abuja-Calabar flight on 26 October for their support.
In a response on X, Mr Achimugu said he had spoken with Mr Usman by telephone and expressed sympathy over his experience.
He said the passenger had provided the airline’s name and that the complaint would be referred to the NCAA’s Directorate of Operations, Licensing and Training Standards.
“We would like to know why the aircraft, in this season of extreme heat, had its door shut and no air conditioning/ventilation, according to your account of the incident,” Mr Achimugu wrote.
He said the authority would determine the appropriate action if the passenger’s account was established.
Mr Achimugu also questioned whether the airline’s crew had offered an explanation or apology for the reported conditions during the delay and after the aircraft arrived in Calabar.
However, the NCAA official cautioned passengers against preventing cabin crew from carrying out their safety responsibilities.
He said the crew might not have known the cause of Mr Usman’s bleeding and could have been concerned that he required medical attention.
Mr Achimugu said the crew had to consider the safety of all passengers and could not be expected to assume that the bleeding was harmless.
He also said the recent Ebola scare underscored the need for cabin crew to remain vigilant when a passenger displayed symptoms that could require medical attention.
The regulator’s comments did not establish the name of the airline, whether the aircraft’s air conditioning system had failed, and why the passengers remained onboard for the reported period.
The NCAA is responsible for regulating civil aviation in Nigeria, including overseeing airline operations and protecting passengers’ interests.
Its Nigeria Civil Aviation Regulations, particularly Part 19, set out passengers’ rights and responsibilities as well as airlines’ obligations to travellers.
The authority has previously intervened in complaints involving flight disruptions and airlines’ handling of passengers.
In September, it directed United Nigeria Airlines to improve its operations and comply with passenger-rights requirements following concerns about flight disruptions and communication with travellers.
The NCAA has also yet to announce the outcome of its investigation or any action against the airline.

title: Tinubu seeks Reps’ approval to expand transfer of convicted offenders agreements
body: By Gift ChapiOdekina President Bola Tinubu has transmitted a bill seeking to amend the Transfer of Convicted Offenders (Enactment and Enforcement) Act to the House of Representatives for consideration, with a view to extending its application to countries outside the Commonwealth. In a letter dated October 20, 2026, addressed to the Speaker of the House, Tajudeen Abbas, Tinubu urged lawmakers to consider the proposed legislation expeditiously. The bill, titled Transfer of Convicted Offenders (Enactment and Enforcement) (Amendment) Bill, 2026, seeks to amend the existing law, Cap. T16, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004. According to the President, the proposed amendment is designed to give effect to schemes or agreements between the Federal Government of Nigeria and other countries for the transfer of convicted offenders. The amendment would also empower the President, through an order published in the Federal Gazette, to extend the application of the Act to any country with which Nigeria has entered into such an agreement. Tinubu said the proposed change would enable Nigeria to implement agreements concluded with countries outside the Commonwealth, potentially broadening the scope of international cooperation on the transfer of convicted offenders. Transmitting the bill pursuant to Section 58(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, the President formally requested the consideration of the House of Representatives. “While it is my hope that the House of Representatives will consider this submission expeditiously, please accept, Rt. Hon. Speaker, the assurances of my highest consideration,” Tinubu stated in the letter. The bill is now before the House for consideration. The presidential communication did not specify the countries that could be covered by future agreements or provide details of the proposed implementation arrangements. The post Tinubu seeks Reps’ approval to expand transfer of convicted offenders agreements appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Enugu agency says community participation necessary for sustainable community-based projects
body:
The Enugu State Community and Social Development Agency (CSDA) has said responsible leadership and community participation remains necessary for sustainable community-based intervention projects meant to uplift people’s living condition.
The General Manager of CSDA, Monday Ani, said this on Tuesday in Nchatancha Nike community in Enugu East Local Government Area of the state.
Mr Ani said this while leading the CSDA team on sensitisation and Participatory Rural Appraisal (PRA) exercises, which were extended to four other communities in Enugu East LGA.
It is part of efforts to identify grassroots development priorities under the Nigerian Community Action Resilience and Economic Stimulus (NG-CARES 2.0) intervention programme.
The other four communities visited in the council area are Akpogazi, Nkomoru, Onuogba, and Edem Nike.
Mr Ani stressed that responsible leadership and active community participation were essential to ensuring that identified projects delivered meaningful benefits to the people.
Addressing the elected Community Project Management Committee (CPMC) members, the CSDA boss encouraged them to remain committed to serving their communities and contributing meaningfully to the development of the state.
He charged the CPMC members to be prudent, accountable and transparent in the discharge of their responsibilities, particularly during project implementation.
He emphasised the need for integrity in managing project resources, adherence to established guidelines and decisions that reflected the collective interests of the communities.
“The PRA exercise provides an opportunity for community members to identify their priority needs, express development aspirations and participate actively in shaping intervention projects that will improve their living conditions.
“The initiative aligns with the development vision of the Governor of Enugu State, Peter Ndubuisi Mbah, whose administration continues to promote inclusive grassroots development and improved access to essential services.
“Through CSDA and the NG-CARES platform, the state government is strengthening community participation and ownership.
“This is to ensure that interventions respond to the actual needs of the people and deliver sustainable benefits,” he said.
In response, the member representing Enugu East Rural State Constituency, Raymond Ugwu, who accompanied the CSDA team to visit the communities, applauded the rural development strides of Governor Mbah.
“I must commend the Governor of Enugu State, Peter Ndubuisi Mbah, for having keen interest to see rural communities get direct dividends of democracy.
“The CSDA approach is a community-focused intervention meant to solve the practical and immediate challenges of the rural people in terms of potable water and hygiene facilities among others,” Mr Ugwu said.

title: Swedish PM skeptical of Stubb and Støre's call with Putin – media
body:
Prime Minister of Sweden Ulf Kristersson expressed skepticism regarding the prospects of the telephone conversation between President of Finland Alexander Stubb, Prime Minister of Norway Jonas Gahr Støre, and Kremlin chief Vladimir Putin, noting that previous contacts between European leaders and the Russian side yielded modest results, Swedish television channel SVT reports.
"If negotiations lead to peace, then negotiations are good. My experience shows that the results of previous talks by Germany and France were very modest. And if you look at what Russia is doing on the ground every day, I see nothing to suggest that it seeks peace. It seeks subjugation," Kristersson said, as quoted by the TV channel on Tuesday.
He emphasized that Sweden's position is that peace must be achieved on Ukraine's terms.
As reported earlier, the office of the President of Finland and the government of Norway announced a phone call between Stubb, Støre, and Russian President Vladimir Putin, which took place on Tuesday, October 27. According to Stubb, the discussion was "frank and businesslike."
In turn, Prime Minister of Denmark Mette Frederiksen also expressed skepticism regarding the effectiveness of the telephone conversation between Alexander Stubb, Jonas Gahr Støre, and Vladimir Putin, noting that she sees "no signs that Russia seeks peace with Europe."

title: Tinubu seeks Reps’ approval for ₦269.4bn promissory notes to settle FG debts
body: By Gift ChapiOdekina President Bola Tinubu has asked the National Assembly to approve the establishment and expansion of the Federal Government’s Promissory Note Programme to settle outstanding verified liabilities totalling ₦269.44bn. This was contained in a letter by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume which was read on the floor of the House during plenary in Abuja. The request is aimed at addressing outstanding contractual, project-related and other financial obligations owed to various categories of creditors. In a letter dated August 18, 2026, and received by the Office of the Speaker on October 21, Akume said the liabilities amounted to ₦269,446,402,822.56, following a comprehensive review by relevant ministries, departments and agencies. He said Tinubu had approved the proposal to establish and expand the programme as a mechanism for settling the verified obligations. According to the letter, the programme is designed to provide “a structured, transparent and fiscally responsible framework” for settling the outstanding debts, while ensuring that only verified and validated claims are admitted. The President is seeking legislative approval for the issuance of promissory notes worth ₦269.44bn, or such other amount as may be approved by the National Assembly, to settle the liabilities contained in the accompanying schedule. The request also seeks approval for the inclusion of the identified categories of liabilities and beneficiaries in the programme, subject to final verification, reconciliation and certification by the relevant government agencies. Tinubu further asked the National Assembly to authorise the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, in collaboration with the Debt Management Office and other relevant agencies, to take the necessary steps to implement the programme. Akume explained that the proposal was intended to mitigate the continued accumulation of interest, penalties and other financial costs associated with the outstanding obligations. He said the arrangement would also provide relief to affected creditors and strengthen confidence in the Federal Government’s commitment to honouring legitimate contractual and other obligations. The SGF noted that the Federal Government had previously used the Promissory Note Programme to settle inherited local debts and contractual obligations, following Federal Executive Council approval and subsequent National Assembly approval. He added that the proposed arrangement was expected to facilitate the orderly settlement of the liabilities without imposing an immediate and disproportionate cash-flow burden on the Federal Government. According to the letter, the programme would also support fiscal planning by spreading repayment obligations over an appropriate period in line with prudent debt management principles. Akume urged the House to give the request urgent consideration, citing the magnitude and age of some of the outstanding liabilities and the possibility of further accumulation of interest and associated costs. He said early legislative approval would enable the Federal Government to commence the necessary processes for issuing the promissory notes and bringing the affected liabilities to a close. The detailed schedule of the liabilities, including the relevant categories, beneficiaries, amounts and supporting documentation, was forwarded to the National Assembly for consideration. title: Ontario delayed inspections of 2 career colleges later given ‘fails’: court docs
body:
Ontario delayed inspections of two career colleges that ultimately turned up serious concerns about student financial aid use, which meant the schools received a “fail” only after they had been approved for funding for another year, court records show.
Critics say it points to severe mismanagement of public money and the government has made the wrong people pay the price.
The Ministry of Colleges and Universities sent Academy of Learning locations in Toronto on Bay Street and in Brampton East notices of inspection on Oct. 1, 2024, according to court records, but did not start the in-person inspections until July and August of 2025, respectively.
“I apologize for the delay, which was due to transitions in roles and the implementation of new inspection procedures,” a ministry official wrote in an email to the Brampton East location, looking to schedule an on-site inspection.
That was four days after the schools were sent ministry notices approving their ability to accept Ontario Student Assistance Program-funded tuition for another year.
Correspondence between the schools and the ministry is among hundreds of pages of documents filed in court as Academy of Learning seeks judicial review of the ministry’s ultimate decision in 2026 to bar them from OSAP eligibility for a year, a ban that has now been extended to 2030.
Concerns about OSAP activity at the schools have been raised by various groups and governments, but no misuse has been proven in court. The schools deny allegations that anything improper occurred and have implemented a long list of corrective actions.
Their OSAP approval in 2025 came despite warnings months earlier from both the federal government and the industry’s own association, Career Colleges Ontario. That organization wrote a letter to the ministry in January 2025, flagging “irregularities” in OSAP usage at 10 schools, including the two Academy of Learning locations.
Growth in OSAP applications at most career colleges was flat between 2022 and 2024, Career College Ontario wrote, but the Bay location saw growth of 642 per cent, and Brampton East saw 527 per cent.
In May of 2025, the federal government told the province about serious concerns with those schools. As the federal government detailed to the schools a few months later, those concerns included unusually rapid growth and “evidence of systematic irregularities.”
The schools have said that instead of being viewed as an indicator of risk, growth represents “a reflection of program relevance, responsiveness to workforce needs, and public confidence in the institution’s delivery of quality education.”
Court records show the provincial inspections ultimately found, in September for the Bay location and in March 2026 for the Brampton East location, evidence suggesting third parties were completing the coursework — sometimes entire courses in one day — and a few students who couldn’t name their school or program.
Students may not have responded to the federal government’s verification attempts because they believed them to be scam calls, and other students having difficulty answering questions in interviews “can be reasonably attributed to situational and linguistic factors,” the school wrote in response to the government.
The Academy of Learning also suggests the government is interpreting IP address data incorrectly. Unusually rapid course completion warrants review, they have said.
Successful OSAP applications at those two schools, which share a parent company, totalled $173 million in grants alone in 2024-25, according to data previously obtained by The Canadian Press through a freedom-of-information request. The number rises to $219 million when a North York location that is a branch of Brampton East is added.
In comparison, students at all publicly funded colleges across the province that year received $385 million in provincial grants.
Colleges and Universities Minister Nolan Quinn drastically reduced the amount of OSAP grants that students at universities and publicly funded colleges could receive in the name of “sustainability” as the program was facing rising costs. Those costs were later revealed by The Canadian Press to largely be due to activity at a small number of career colleges.
Quinn has also now paused OSAP payments to students at all career colleges and other private post-secondary institutions as his government and an outside firm conduct a broader review of the issue.
Liberal colleges and universities critic Tyler Watt said those actions make Quinn’s delayed action on potential bad actors all the more baffling.
“Their recent actions, where they’ve completely pulled the rug out from every single student in the private sector, goes to show you that they are willing to take drastic action,” he said.
“It’s not OK at all what they’ve done to students and the people that are following the rules, but there’s no reasonable explanation why they let this go on and wasted this much of taxpayers’ money for as long as they did.”
Green Party Leader Mike Schreiner said the government has failed students and the public.
“This amounts to severe mismanagement of public money by the Ford government,” he wrote in a statement. “For years, this government has been aware of private career colleges breaking the rules and has allowed them to continue to benefit from OSAP.”
NDP critic Peggy Sattler said the government should have acted earlier on the numerous warnings it received.
“The government still dragged its heels on conducting the investigation that it is obligated to do and then blames students for misusing OSAP grants and punishes the entire sector for its own incompetence,” she said.
A spokesperson for Quinn said the inspection process can be long and in-depth.
“As we have stated, these inspections are multifaceted, and include reviewing data within the ministry’s possession, data requested from the institution that is provided to the ministry Inspectors, and in-person inspections,” Bianca Giacoboni wrote in a statement.
“Due to the technical nature of this process, inspections and subsequent investigations can take over a year. The ministry cannot presume the outcome of these investigations until all steps have been completed.”
OSAP applications at those schools actually went down in 2025-26, the province said in court filings. In the case of the Brampton East location, the number of OSAP recipients dropped by 34 per cent from the previous year, compared to growth of 1,347 per cent from 2021-22 to 2024-25.
The decline is timed around the start of the ministry’s in-person inspections, the government says in a document filed in court.
The Academy of Learning says no single factor explains that decline.
“We reject any suggestion that the decline reflects wrongdoing,” the schools wrote in a statement.
“Enrolment fell during a period of significant uncertainty, as students received repeated communications questioning their OSAP funding and our eligibility. Many chose to withdraw, postpone or not start their studies. In the same period, we ended some community partner arrangements and added verification measures.”

title: ‘Today my conscience told me to vote’: Arab Israelis turn out in force to demand change
body: Arab voters have gone to polling stations in substantial numbers across Israel in a surge that could prove decisive in forming the country’s next government. By midmorning on Tuesday, the overall turnout in Israel’s election was the highest since 1981, and that was reflected in Nazareth, which has an almost entirely Arab population of Muslims and Christians. Voters at the Nazareth Baptist School, which was being used as a polling station, told The National they were desperate for change after more than three years of “catastrophe” for Arabs living in Israel since the October 7, 2023, attacks. The high turnout was being seen as bad news for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu , who said there were "huge lines at polling stations" in Arab areas. "The future of our Jewish state hangs in the balance," he said in a plea to supporters to head to the polls. The Arab minority makes up one in five of Israel’s 10 million people, but has had minimal say in the country's political future. But with a heavy turnout, which some political sources said could be “astronomical”, going from 50 per cent to more than 70 per cent, that could change. There is also a realisation among younger and older Arabs that – instead of boycotting elections as many have done in the past, feeling uneasy that their vote would effectively recognise the Israeli state – by joining the political process they can influence its outcome. Arab parties are tipped to win up to 16 seats in the 120-member Knesset, an increase from the current 10, making the conservative Ra’am party led by Mansour Abbas and the Joint List of three united Arab parties potential kingmakers in the next Israeli government. It is expected that the anti- Netanyahu bloc, led by Gadi Eisenkot, will not reach the 61 seats needed for an outright majority. That would mean they need Arab support, either by forming a coalition or by tolerating a minority government. Furthermore, a higher number of Arab votes cast would raise the number of votes needed to cross the 3.25 per cent electoral threshold for a party to enter the Knesset. That could adversely affect smaller hard-right parties and further weaken the Netanyahu bloc. Politics for the good Hasar Zoabi, who voted for the Joint List, argued that “as a minority in Israel we should use our democratic right to vote to try to influence the politics for the good”. One government employee, who did not want to be named, felt people were also being driven to vote by fear because “us Arabs in Israel no longer feel safe, even if you speak Arabic you are stopped, so that is why we are seeing such a big turnout on the streets today”. Simona Fasciani said it was the first time she would go to the polls as “it is very important for Arab people to vote and this will be seen in countries around the world. Arabs must reclaim their position”. But there was some disquiet among elderly voters that the ballot papers were only in Hebrew and they had to ask for translation. Some also spoke about Jewish settlers driving to people’s homes and trying to intimidate them into not voting. There was, at times, a heavy police presence, but the crowds queued peacefully to cast their ballots and place them in a sealed envelope. Political threshold crossed The Arab population has also experienced soaring crime, with one of the highest murder rates in the world, at a time when the national police force has been led by the far-right politician Itamar Ben-Gvir. They have also witnessed the mass demolition of homes in the southern Negev region. While the Arab vote could have a serious impact on the government, it could also be ignored by the Zionist parties of the centre-right, fearing that a coalition with Arab parties would severely damage their standing among Jewish voters. But it is clear that Arab Israelis have crossed a political threshold that could see them increase their political clout, a moment that has drawn comparisons to Catholics securing political representation in Northern Ireland during the Troubles. That this is the most consequential election in Israel’s difficult history has been understood by both young and old. “It has been a horrible situation for Arabs which is why we need to change it,” said Akram Mawaid, an 89-year-old who has rarely gone to the ballot box. “Today my conscience told me to vote.”

title: Tinubu writes Senate, seeks $20.5bn, €1.04bn foreign loans to fund projects
body: …As Senate refers 2026–2027 supplementary borrowing plan to debt committee, gives one week to report By Henry Umoru President Bola Tinubu has written the Senate, seeking approval of a supplementary external borrowing plan of $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion to finance infrastructure and development projects across the country. President Tinubu’s letter was addressed to the President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio. Akpabio, who read the letter on Tuesday during plenary, said the request covers the 2026–2027 fiscal period and targets critical sectors, including power, transportation, agriculture, healthcare, education, water supply and security. Tinubu, who noted that the proposed borrowing was necessary to bridge Nigeria’s infrastructure funding gap, sustain economic growth, generate employment and improve the living conditions of Nigerians, urged the National Assembly to give the plan urgent consideration and approval to facilitate the timely release of funds and implementation of the projects. In the letter, the president said the proposed external financing would support projects and programmes spanning virtually every sector of the economy. “The 2026–2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan cuts across all sectors, with specific emphasis on infrastructure, agriculture, health, education, water supply, growth, security and employment generation, as well as financial management reforms, amongst others,” he said. According to the letter, the proposed facilities total $20,517,755,901 and €1,045,083,643, and the projects had been selected after technical and economic assessments. “I want to emphasise that the projects and programmes included in the Borrowing Plan were selected based on thorough technical and economic evaluation, as well as their anticipated contribution to the socio-economic development of the country,” he said. The president who explained that the proposed investments were expected to create employment opportunities, promote skills acquisition, encourage entrepreneurship, reduce poverty and strengthen food security, said, “These initiatives aim to generate employment, promote skills acquisition, foster entrepreneurship, reduce poverty and enhance food security, all of which improve the livelihood of the Nigerian child.” He disclosed that most of the projects would be executed across the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, stressing that the nationwide spread of the interventions would help address development needs across the federation, adding that the scale of Nigeria’s infrastructure deficit and the financial resources required to address it have made additional external borrowing necessary. “In light of the need for significant infrastructure investment in the country and the vast financial resources needed to address this gap, it has become essential to pursue broader external borrowings to close the financing shortfall,” Tinubu said. He identified power, transportation and healthcare as among the critical sectors expected to benefit from the proposed financing. “These funds will primarily be directed towards critical infrastructure projects in various sectors, including power, transportation and healthcare, amongst others,” the president said. Tinubu, who maintained that prompt consideration of the request would enable the government to meet its obligations to Nigerians through timely disbursement of funds and effective execution of the projects, said, “Given the urgent nature of these needs and the importance of stabilising the country, it is crucial to seek the consideration and approval of the National Assembly leadership and the entire National Assembly for the 2026–2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan.” The President, who noted that legislative approval would enable the government to proceed with the proposed interventions, said, “This will enable the government to fulfil its obligations to the Nigerian people through timely disbursements and effective project implementation.” The President of the Senate thereafter referred the Communication to the Senate Committee on Local and Foreign Debts for further legislative action to report at plenary within one week. The Committee is expected to examine the proposal, potentially in collaboration with the Senate Committee on Appropriations and other relevant committees. The letter, as presented to the Senate, did not provide a detailed project-by-project breakdown of the proposed facilities, the specific financing terms or the amount earmarked for each sector. The National Assembly’s consideration of the request is expected to focus on the proposed financing and its intended development objectives, including the government’s plan to close infrastructure gaps, stimulate economic activities and improve public services. The letter titled “Federal Government 2026-2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plans, read, ” I write in reference to the above subjects and to submit the attached Federal Government 2026-2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plans for consideration and early approval of the National Assembly to ensure prompt implementation of our projects. “The 2026-2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan cuts across all sectors with specific emphasis on infrastructure, agriculture, health, education, water supply, growth, security, and employment generation, as well as financial management reforms, amongst others. “The total facility for the projects and programs under the Borrowing Growing Plan is $20,517,000,000 and €1,045,083,643 respectively and the summary of the breakdown is attached to this presents. “So, Distinguished colleagues, in light of the removal of the critical reforms of my administration, the need to accelerate growth of the national economy provides support for the External Borrowing Plan, which amounts to $20,517,755,901, and €1,045,083,643. ” I want to emphasize that the projects and programs included in the Borrowing Plan were selected based on thorough technical and economic evaluation, as well as their anticipated contribution to the socio-economic development of the country. “These initiatives aim to generate employment, promote skilled acquisition, foster entrepreneurship, reduce poverty and enhance food security, all of which improve the livelihood of the Nigerian child. “The majority of these projects and programs will be implemented across all the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory. In light of the need for significant infrastructure investment in the country and the vast financial resources needed to address this gap, it has become essential to pursue broader external borrowings to close the financing shortfall. “These funds will primarily be directed towards critical infrastructure projects in various sectors, including power, transportation and healthcare, amongst others. “Given the urgent nature of these needs and the importance of stabilizing the country, it is crucial to seek the consideration and approval of the National Assembly leadership and the entire National Assembly for the 2026-2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan. “This will enable the government to fulfill its obligations to the Nigerian people through timely disbursements and effective project implementation. “This request will be looked at by the Committee on Local and Foreign Debts, probably in collaboration with the Preparation and Finance, but majorly by the Committee on Local and Foreign Debts. And you can report back in one week.” The post Tinubu writes Senate, seeks $20.5bn, €1.04bn foreign loans to fund projects appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Public Art Abu Dhabi Biennial reveals Al Ain installations for second edition
body: Oversized red and green beads visible from a hundred metres away are the first signs that something has taken over Al Towayya Roundabout in Al Ain. From a distance, the beads look like flowers, arranged in clusters on the grass. Nearing the roundabout, the complexity of the design becomes apparent. Triangular, circular, floral and teardrop shapes fan out from the centre – all in gold and all linked together. The beads are peppered throughout like gemstones. Roudhah Al Mazrouei ’s installation Tassa , for the second Public Art Abu Dhabi Biennial , is inspired by a traditional Emirati headpiece from her family’s collection. “It actually exists in my parents’ house,” she says. “We’ve worn it in so many events. It’s a way of showing how we grow up with our culture.” Al Mazrouei has drawn inspiration from jewellery before. Her installation Reverie , shown at the 2024 Sikka Art and Design Platform, reimagined an heirloom bracelet belonging to her mother on an oversized scale. Even so, it was smaller than Tassa , which crowns the roundabout in Al Ain and measures 80 metres in diameter. She conceived the installation years ago. The project never materialised, however, and the artist revisited it during this biennial. It was a natural fit, she says, given the event’s theme of Home: A Glossary for a Communal Sense of Place. “I grew up in Al Ain,” she says. “The roundabout was also perfect because I went to school right at the end of this street.” Tassa is the only installation within the city of Al Ain. The other three have been installed at Al Qattara Oasis, and respond to different aspects of the Unesco World Heritage Site and its history. This includes Asuncion Molinos Gordo’s Bil Hana wa Al Afia. The installation – made from rammed earth – alludes to the inner structure of the falaj , branching out in root-like forms similar to the millennia-old irrigation system that can still be seen in the oasis. Stratified into seven layers, it also represents the different historical periods of Al Ain dating back to the Neolithic era. Objects embedded in the rammed earth also represent the passage of history, from earthenware and palm reeds to cassettes and air conditioning remotes that encroach on our current period. Perhaps they are making a point about the continuing effectiveness of the ancient falaj system , which is still used to distribute water on many farms across the country. On the other hand, Reena Saini Kallat’s Thresholds: Requiem (The Last Call) offers insights into an inaccessible past, or even perhaps an alternate dimension where extinct birds still live. The installation features two pairs of conical devices inspired by 20th-century acoustic locators detecting faraway aircraft. Arranged on a listening platform, these devices don’t listen in on the puttering engines of planes, but to the chirping of extinct and critically endangered birds. Several of these species either migrated through, or were native to, the UAE or the wider Gulf. They include the extinct dusky seaside sparrow and the endangered saker falcon. Finally, M’barek Bouchichi’s installation beckons a species of bird that is alive and well: the pigeon. Titled I am not the stone thrown into the water, but the seed sown in the field, the work comprises two pigeon towers made of stainless steel. It solidifies the pigeon tower as a space of refuge by replacing the mud bricks traditionally used for construction with a far more resilient material. The porous patterns on Bouchichi’s towers are significant, rendering traditional Emirati sea shanties in Braille to give a tactile representation of the work songs sung by sailors during their arduous journeys away from home. The installations in Al Ain are the first set to be unveiled as part of the second Public Art Biennial. More will be revealed in Abu Dhabi on November 15. The exhibition runs across both cities until February 15, 2027. The works will collectively explore notions of home as an evolving, shared human experience, exploring how people’s relationships with places are shaped by community, memory and everyday encounters. “What do we mean when we say home? It is one of the most used terms in any language, and yet many aspects of it often go unexamined,” artistic director Elvira Dyangani Ose said in a statement. “Home is not only a location. It is a condition: felt before it is understood, carried in the body before it is articulated in language. “Al Ain is where this edition begins, in an oasis landscape shaped over millennia by co-operation, shared water and collective care. We offer this biennial as a glossary, not as a guide to correct interpretations but as a set of terms to think with. The definitions are partial by design, and yours to complete,” she added/ Public Art Abu Dhabi Biennial is on until February 15, 2027

title: A 4-watt video link passed Ukraine’s state tests, its maker says, and could stretch STING interceptors’ radius from 20 km to 30 km
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); A new video transmitter for Wild Hornets’ drones, including its STING interceptors, has passed state tests, the Ukrainian drone maker told Militarnyi. The module sends a drone’s camera feed to its pilot. The company expects it to widen its interceptors’ operating radius. Russia launched 140 Shahed-type drones at Ukraine overnight on 26 October and 280 the next night , when its main target was Kyiv , Air Force figures as of the morning show. Interceptor drones, which cost dozens of times less than the Shaheds they hunt, are one of Ukraine’s answers. The STING alone downed more than 3,000 drones in its first seven months of use, Wild Hornets says . If the company’s estimate holds, a 30 km radius would let each ground station cover more than twice the area it covers at 20 km. What the testers checked Specialists from the State Research Institute for Testing and Certification of Arms and Military Equipment and the Defense Ministry’s State Quality Assurance Directorate confirmed the module’s declared characteristics on three drone types, the company said. The three were the STING interceptor, the Queen of Hornets cargo platform, and the 10-inch Wild Hornets Digital anti-aircraft drone. Some of the drones’ figures exceeded the values the company had set for them, Wild Hornets told Ukrainian defense outlet Oboronka, without saying which ones. Those figures will enter the official specifications after further field tests, it said. More than double the power The module, called HV VTX Pro, is part of an upgrade to Wild Hornets’ Hornet Vision digital video system. It more than doubles the transmitter’s maximum power, to 4 W. That sends a clear picture farther and makes the feed steadier in crowded airwaves and under electronic jamming, the company said. Hornet Vision Ctrl system. Photo: Wild Hornets Wild Hornets first described the module in August, when it was already in serial production. Its interceptors’ operating radius would grow from around 20 km to 30 km, the company said at the time. That estimate assumed good line of sight and the 360-degree antenna on its ground stations, according to a company statement Interfax-Ukraine quoted . Interception could also become at least 20% more effective against targets flying extremely low, the statement said. Wild Hornets is a Ukrainian company that designs and builds drones, from strike FPV drones and cargo platforms to the STING, which the company says flies at up to 280 km/h to hunt Shaheds. Its drones serve with more than 100 units of Ukraine’s Defense Forces, from the army and the National Guard to military intelligence, the Air Force, and the border guard, according to Interfax-Ukraine.
