title: Agriculture recovery in 2025 was encouraging but uneven, industrial slowdown highlights broader development – ISSER
body: Ghana’s agricultural recovery in 2025 was encouraging but uneven, the Institute of Statistical, Social and Economic Research (ISSER) has stated. According to the research institute from the University of Ghana, sustaining growth will require improvements in productivity, market infrastructure and policy implementation. In its 2025 State of the Ghana Economy Report (SGER), ISSER said expanding effective irrigation, mechanisation and extension services, with greater attention to crop yields will raise agricultural productivity. It also pointed out that improving storage, processing, transport and market access to reduce post-harvest losses and improve producer returns will strengthen markets and value chains. It emphasised that agriculture remains central to Ghana’s food security, rural livelihoods and agro-industrial development; therefore, stronger agricultural growth can improve food availability and support economic activity. However, it cautioned that aggregate growth may conceal weaknesses in individual commodities. Industry Sector On the Industry sector, ISSER said Ghana’s industrial slowdown in 2025 highlights the need to translate mineral sector strength into broader industrial development, supported by competitive manufacturing and greater domestic value addition. it alluded that the sector is important for job creation, value addition and economic diversification. It therefore calls for an industry that translates mineral sector strength into broader industrial development, supported by competitive manufacturing and greater domestic value addition On policy priorities, ISSER called for the strengthening of manufacturing competitiveness by reducing production and financing costs, improving infrastructure and supporting investment in value addition. Similarly, it wants improved energy security and efficiency through addressing electricity sector financial and operational weaknesses, strengthening domestic gas supply and expanding renewable energy. Services Sector For the Services sector, the research firm said it is increasingly important for Ghana’s economic growth, employment and structural transformation. In that regard, modern services such as ICT, finance and logistics can raise productivity across the economy, while education and healthcare support human capital development. However, rapid growth in services does not automatically translate into productive employment or better service delivery. It therefore states that quality, accessibility and productivity of services matter as much as their expansion.

title: Gunmen kill seven in Plateau community
body: Gunmen, on Monday night, stormed Georo community in Jos South Local Government Area of Plateau State, killing seven persons. The attack threw residents of the community into panic. This comes amid high tension in various communities of Mangu, Bokkos and Riyom where the state government recently imposed a dust-to-dawn curfew to maintain order following repeated attacks and killings in the area. Residents said the attackers invaded the community at about 10:20pm, shooting sporadically, killing some persons in their shops and others at a local restaurant. FACT CHECK: No Evidence Tinubu Executed ₦9trn Projects In Kano as Pakistan Claimed 64 students hospitalised after being administered Bilharzia drug in Katsina A member of the community, Mr Bot Silas, who confirmed the incident, said, “The gunmen stormed the community at about 10:20pm and started shooting sporadically. “The attackers came at night and started shooting, forcing residents to scamper for safety. “Some of the victims were killed in their shops, while others were attacked at a local restaurant where food was being prepared. Seven persons were killed in the attack, and the incident caused serious panic among residents of the community.” Reacting to the incident, spokesman of the Berom Youth Moulders-Association, BYM, Rwang Tengwong, condemned the attack and described it as unacceptable. Tengwong said, “The killing of innocent people in Georo is condemnable and must not be allowed to continue. I call on the relevant security agencies to intensify efforts to protect communities and apprehend those responsible for the attack.” “We call on the relevant security agencies to investigate the incident, bring the perpetrators to justice and ensure that residents can live and carry out their legitimate activities without fear.” Spokesperson of the Plateau State police command, SP Alabo Alfred, did not respond to inquiry from our correspondent as of press time.

title: Fallen 33kV power line sparks fire, destroys buildings in Kwara
body:
A fallen 33kV electricity transmission line triggered a fire that damaged residential buildings and businesses in Oloje Phase 2, Ilorin, Kwara State, early Tuesday, the state fire service has said.
The fire, which occurred on Lawyer Lambo Street in Ilorin West Local Government Area, destroyed a vehicle and a vulcanising workshop, while several buildings and businesses sustained damage.
In a statement issued on Tuesday, Hassan Adekunle, spokesperson for the Kwara State Fire Service , said the agency received a distress call and arrived at the scene at 2:41 a.m.
The fire affected two buildings containing four-bedroom flats each and a third building comprising a room-and-parlour self-contained apartment.
The occupants of the self-contained apartment were rescued by community members, according to the statement.
Three vehicles were in one of the flats when the fire broke out. One was completely burnt, while firefighters saved the other two.
The second four-bedroom flat sustained damage, particularly in its kitchen, where electrical appliances, including a freezer, were affected. Its solar power system was also damaged.
An adjoining travel and tours office lost its solar power system, four tubular batteries and other electrical appliances. A nearby vulcanising workshop was also destroyed.
The fire service said preliminary findings indicated that a concrete pole supporting a 33kV transmission line collapsed, causing the line to fall onto a vehicle.
“The fallen line also landed on the vehicle that was burnt, and a spark reportedly ignited its tyre before the fire escalated within a short period,” the agency said.
The fallen transmission line also posed a risk to firefighters, prompting the agency to contact the Ibadan Electricity Distribution Company (IBEDC) control room to request the shutdown of the electricity feeder supplying the affected area.
The Chief Fire Officer, Alabi Muhammed, expressed sympathy with residents, property owners and business operators affected by the incident.
He urged residents to avoid erecting structures beneath high-tension electricity lines and advised property developers to observe safety setbacks around electricity infrastructure.
He also urged residents to report fallen poles, damaged electrical infrastructure and exposed transmission lines to the relevant authorities, warning them not to touch fallen wires or objects in contact with them.
The incident occurred less than 24 hours after another fire destroyed a building comprising three-bedroom flats in Kangile Village, Ilorin South Local Government Area, on Monday.
The fire service did not state whether the two incidents were connected.

title: Maresca defends Donnarumma, Guehi after Man City defeat
body: Manchester City boss Enzo Maresca on Tuesday defended goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma and centre-back Marc Guehi after costly mistakes in their first Premier League defeat of the season at Aston Villa. Nicolas Jackson took advantage of errors from the pair as Villa won 2-1 on Saturday, ending City’s perfect run of seven wins from seven league games. Defeat left City level on points with champions Arsenal at the top of the table, but they are ahead of the Gunners on goal difference. Maresca spoke up for his players ahead of a tough League Cup fourth-round match against Brighton at the Etihad on Wednesday. “Gigio (Donnarumma), I think, since we started, is doing well. Like any player, like any manager, at some point is making some mistakes. “But it’s part of the season. Again, they are playing so many games, so many minutes, that sometimes it’s almost impossible to (not) make some mistakes.” And Maresca said he was “completely happy” with England defender Guehi. “Because in the way he reacts, he’s fantastic, he’s a top guy,” he said. “Again, he’s one of the captains, he’s a leader, and I love Marc, to be honest. “And again, it’s the same with Gigio — when they make some mistakes, they recognise.” Maresca said Donnarumma was among a group of players who had been given time off to recharge after the Villa defeat, also including Erling Haaland, Elliot Anderson, Josko Gvardiol and captain Ruben Dias. “After Villa, we gave five players three days off to recover energy — Erling, Ruben, Elliot, Gigio and Josko,” he said. “They are all on holiday.” AFP The post Maresca defends Donnarumma, Guehi after Man City defeat appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Samuel Jinapor denies Minority coached South Africa evacuees to criticise government
body: The Ranking Member on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, Samuel Abdulai Jinapor, has dismissed allegations that the Minority in Parliament attempted to influence Ghanaians evacuated from South Africa to speak against the government. Speaking at a press conference on Tuesday, October 27, Mr Jinapor said the Minority had not offered money or used any form of persuasion to get the returnees to make allegations about the government’s handling of the evacuation and associated allowances. “Let me place on record that at no point in time did the Minority engage, pay, and/or convince any of these people,” he stated. The denial comes a day after some of the evacuees alleged at a press conference that opposition members had tried to coach them to make statements critical of the government. Mr Jinapor said the Minority had not orchestrated the claims, adding that some evacuees had independently spoken out over alleged differences between the amounts they were supposed to receive and the money they actually collected. The controversy has intensified scrutiny of the evacuation exercise, with the Minority questioning aspects of the expenditure and documentation presented in connection with the payments. Among the concerns raised are alleged duplicate entries, unsigned payment records, missing receipts and claims by some returnees that the amounts recorded against their names did not match what they received. Although Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa has offered explanations regarding the payments, Mr Jinapor said the concerns warranted an independent examination. He reiterated the Minority’s call for an independent audit to establish whether the evacuation funds were properly accounted for and to resolve the disputed payment claims.

title: With El Niño, 2026-2027 northeast monsoon may not be as cold
body: MANILA, Philippines – The northeast monsoon or amihan is here, the weather bureau announced on Tuesday, October 27. The Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical, and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) explained in a statement that it has observed “a surge of northeasterly winds and lower air temperatures over extreme Northern Luzon” in the past few days . The period of the northeast monsoon, also known as the country’s cool and dry season, lasts from October until February or March. It typically brings surges of cold temperatures, especially in January and February. But PAGASA has said that this amihan may be warmer than usual due to the ongoing El Niño , which is predicted to become very strong before the end of 2026 and persist until the first quarter of 2027. El Niño is a natural phenomenon characterized by “unusually warm ocean surface temperatures in the central and eastern Pacific,” according to the World Meteorological Organization. In the Philippines, the phenomenon causes below-normal rainfall and higher temperatures. Forecasts show nearly the entire country will be experiencing drought by the end of February 2027. The onset of the northeast monsoon also comes around three weeks after PAGASA announced the end of the southwest monsoon or habagat . – Rappler.com

title: Five Siblings Killed In Gombe Tricycle-Water Tanker Crash, Gov Yahaya Mourns
body: Tragedy struck in Gombe State on Tuesday as five children from the same family lost their lives in a horrific road accident while commuting to school. The victims were killed after a water tanker ran over a commercial tricycle (popularly known as Keke NAPEP) conveying them to their respective schools. The incident occurred at the Kanadi Academy Junction in Buba Shango, Gombe. The deceased children—all members of the Mansir Adamu family residing in Jekadafari—were identified as Maryam Mansir Adamu and Usman Mansir Adamu, both Primary Five pupils of Jekadafari Primary School; Hauwau Mansir Adamu of GJSS Jekadafari; Aliyu Mansir Adamu of GDSS Ahmadu Gombe; and Fatima Mansir Adamu. Three other children sustained varying degrees of injuries in the crash and are currently receiving medical treatment. ‘A Devastating Loss’ Reacting to the tragedy, Gombe State Governor, Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, expressed deep sorrow over what he described as a devastating loss that has wiped out five promising young lives from a single family. In a statement signed by his Director-General of Press Affairs, Ismaila Uba Misilli, Governor Yahaya described the incident as a heartbreaking tragedy for the entire state. “The loss of five children from one family in a single tragic incident is profoundly painful, not only for their parents and relatives but also for their schools, the Jekadafari community, and the entire people of Gombe State,” the governor said. He lamented that the children’s lives were cut short at a time when they were actively pursuing their education and nurturing their dreams for a bright future. Governor Calls For Road Safety Following the fatal crash, Governor Yahaya issued a stern warning to motorists and commercial drivers across the state regarding reckless road behavior. He urged drivers to adhere strictly to traffic rules, maintain safe driving speeds, refrain from dangerous maneuvers, and ensure that their vehicles are roadworthy before plying public roads. “No commuting is worth the loss of precious human lives,” Governor Yahaya emphasised, stressing the need for heightened road safety measures, particularly when transporting school children and vulnerable commuters. The governor offered prayers for the speedy recovery of the three injured children undergoing treatment and extended his condolences to the Mansir Adamu family, the affected schools, and the Jekadafari community. He prayed that Almighty Allah grant the deceased children Aljannatul Firdaus and give their parents the fortitude to bear the loss. title: Kofi Hayford shines as MC of M.anifest’s ‘Nowhere Cool’ at 10 celebration
body: Broadcaster Kofi Hayford has earned praise for hosting M.anifest’s 10th anniversary celebration of his acclaimed album Nowhere Cool at the Accra Polo Club on Saturday, 24th October 2026. Known for his eloquence and humour, Kofi kept the concert flowing smoothly, introducing the evening’s opening acts and engaging the audience ahead of the headline performance by the celebrated rapper. His delivery, stage presence and ability to connect with the crowd added to the experience of the Nowhere Cool @ 10 Live Experience , which brought together “M.anifans” to celebrate one of M.anifest’s defining projects. The event featured performances from Kwartengg, Anabel Rose, RCee and Arathejay, who helped set the tone for the night before M.anifest took to the stage. The rapper then performed all 14 songs on the 2016 album, giving fans an opportunity to relive the project in its entirety, a decade after its release. He was joined by a line-up of guest performers, including highlife star Kwabena Kwabena, dancehall musician Samini, Worlasi, Ko-Jo Cue, Ria Boss, Kwarteng, Asiama and Cina Soul. Their appearances added to the excitement of a night built around the music, collaborations and lasting impact of Nowhere Cool . Coverage of the concert also highlighted the audience’s enthusiastic response as M.anifest revisited songs from the album. Kofi’s role was to ensure that the programme maintained its rhythm while giving each performer the right introduction and allowing the audience to remain part of the experience. Rather than allowing transitions between acts to interrupt the mood, he kept proceedings moving and engaged the crowd with intermittent performances of lines from some of the rapper’s most popular records. The young broadcaster also performed as a hypeman alongside DJ Afrolektra during a 20-minute set that saw fans singing along to classic Ghanaian bangers. His performance has since drawn positive reactions from some fans who attended the event, with audiences expressing appreciation for the way he handled his responsibilities on the night. Kofi Hayford told Joy Entertainment that “the assignment was another opportunity to demonstrate the skills that have made me a familiar voice across Ghana’s media and entertainment landscape, and I appreciate the opportunity to serve”. Saturday’s event also marked the second time he had been selected to host an occasion connected to M.anifest. In 2025, he hosted the listening party for the rapper’s NRAGT project in Labone, Accra. His latest assignment further strengthens that association, bringing together his professional experience and personal admiration for an artiste whose music he follows closely. Kofi Hayford is a broadcaster, entertainment journalist, voice-over artiste and experienced event host who has built a career around communication and connecting with people. His work across Joy FM and Joy Prime has given him experience engaging different audiences, from radio listeners and television viewers to live event patrons.

title: Russians fabricating ‘successes’ in Velykyi Burluk area, military spox says
body:
Viktor Trehubov, Spokesperson for the Joint Forces Task Force, said this in a televised broadcast, Ukrinform reports.
“Well, they have not managed to expand it significantly. There are no settlements there where they could establish and hold positions effectively; the area consists mostly of tree lines and surrounding fields. So, I would not say there has been any significant expansion. Rather, Russian forces have a fairly widespread presence in the ‘gray zone’ around that settlement.
“Are they trying to drive Ukrainian forces out of there? Yes, they are trying. They are attempting various aggressive actions. But overall, I would not say the situation there is critical at the moment.
“On the other hand, what is characteristic of the Velykyi Burluk area is the absolutely fantastic statistics the Russians report to their own people, and the absolutely fantastic maps they draw for themselves. On the maps they present to their own political leadership, the area has effectively ceased to exist as a contested area and is already shown as occupied by Russian forces. The situation on the ground, however, is exactly the opposite,” Trehubov said.
Asked about the Russian practice of using civilians as cover for military operations, he said the last major attempt of this kind had been recorded about 10 days earlier in the Kupiansk sector.
As reported by Ukrinform, Kharkiv and 12 other settlements in the Kharkiv region came under Russian attack the previous day, leaving three people dead and eight injured.

title: Air Force Spokesperson: Russian forces launch several ballistic missile strikes on Pivdenny Bridge in Kyiv
body:
During the latest attack, Russian forces launched several ballistic missile strikes against the Southern Bridge (Pivdenny) in Kyiv. While such structures are not easily destroyed, repairing the damaged bridge deck will take time, Yuriy Ihnat, a spokesperson for the Air Force of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, stated during a televised marathon on Tuesday.
"Of course, the bridge deck can be repaired—bridges are not as easy to destroy as some might think. Nevertheless, this does cause certain inconveniences, and repairs will take time," Ihnat said.
According to him, the adversary employed 16 ballistic missiles—either Iskander-M missiles or S-400 surface-to-air guided missiles—during the recent attack. Specialists examining the impact site will determine the exact type of missiles used. "The adversary used two types of missiles today: either Iskander-M or S-400 surface-to-air missiles," the spokesperson noted.
Ihnat emphasized that over the past two weeks, Russian forces have focused their missile strikes on Kyiv, launching ballistic missiles in several waves throughout the night and combining them with drone attacks.
"Previously, ballistic missile strikes might have occurred just once a night. Now, they are spread out over several waves of attacks... They launch these strikes in waves, and all of this is accompanied by drone attacks," he said.
As previously reported, Taras Chmut, head of the Come Back Alive foundation and a military analyst, stated in an interview with DW that the complete destruction of bridges in Kyiv by Russian shelling is a possibility, provided the adversary is willing to commit significant resources. At the same time, he noted that destroying a single section of a bridge does not necessarily lead to the collapse of the entire structure; the critical issue remains how quickly a crossing can be restored, at least in some capacity. According to him, even partial damage to bridges could severely complicate urban logistics, particularly the operation of the metro system and public transport.
"I wouldn't rule out such a scenario; if the Russians are determined enough and willing to expend the necessary resources, they could certainly do it," he emphasized.
Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported that on Tuesday, the enemy struck the Pivdenny Bridge in Kyiv, damaging metro infrastructure located on the span.
Kyiv Metro has temporarily suspended service between Osokorky and Chervony Khutir stations on the green line due to the damage to infrastructure on the Pivdenny Bridge. Furthermore, with the Pivdenny Bridge closed, both freight and passenger vehicle traffic have been diverted along alternative routes.

title: Nova Scotia committee to discuss $10B AI data centre planned for Cape Breton
body:
The company behind a controversial $10-billion AI data centre proposed in Cape Breton is trying to reassure Nova Scotians that water will be protected and power rates won’t spike.
Meanwhile, opposition parties say AI data centre regulations need to be legislated in order to ease major worries about the plan.
Representatives from EverWind Fuels were witnesses at a meeting of the standing committee on natural resources and economic development Tuesday to discuss their planned data centre.
The company announced earlier this month that the U.S. artificial intelligence company Anthropic had signed a 20-year lease for a 18,600-square-metre facility in Point Tupper, N.S., that would draw 95 megawatts of electricity during its first phase. Between the Oct. 16 announcement and Tuesday evening, a petition to stop the development of AI data centres in Nova Scotia on Change.org garnered about 23,800 signatures.
“We recognize that a development of this scale raises important questions and concerns, particularly for those communities closest to the project,” Matthew Tinari, EverWind’s chief financial officer, told the committee.
“Nova Scotians deserve clear, factual answers and we’re committed to listening, providing information and addressing those concerns as the development moves forward,” he added.
After the meeting, Tinari told reporters EverWind is proposing a memorandum of understanding that would lay out the company’s commitments to developing the project responsibly.
Tinari said the implementation agreement would commit to preventing rate hikes for household electricity customers, protecting water supply and minimizing water use. He told reporters that the federal and provincial guidelines for data centres would be a “large portion” of the memorandum of understanding.
“What we’ve heard from community is (that) industry should have binding commitments. So we were proposing to the province some type of agreement like that,” Tinari said.
Premier Tim Houston said he recently became aware that EverWind has suggested a memorandum of understanding with the province.
“Like we’ve said from the beginning, the proposal was the first step in this process. The next step for this proposal is for the proponent to undergo consultations with communities, which will help inform any future agreements,” he said in an emailed statement.
The premier would not say if his Progressive Conservative government would make an agreement of this kind legally binding.
EverWind says it will cover the cost of all electricity infrastructure, which is why the project will not increase power rates. The firm says the project would include a closed-loop cooling system using recycled water as well as an external cooling system that would require the use of additional water on very hot days without any wind.
Tinari told the committee the electricity at their proposed centre “is designed to be interruptible,” which means they can be disconnected from the grid during peak energy use or when the province’s electrical grid is “constrained.”
The company estimates the system would use an average of 100,000 litres of water per day in the first phase and an average of 500,000 litres per day when the expansion is complete from a nearby lake. Tinari said the volume of water needed at full capacity represents 1.5 per cent of Landrie Lake’s estimated sustainable daily yield.
Tinari told the committee the data centre would create 2,000 construction jobs and 215 permanent roles in the community.
He said he’s aware of worries coming from community members, and said “their concerns are valid.” The company is set to host community consultation sessions in southeastern Cape Breton next week. Tinari said the company was not able to do any community consultation prior to the announcement because of strict non-disclosure agreements EverWind signed with Anthropic.
“The announcement doesn’t mean that the data centre is turning on tomorrow. The announcement means the conversation is starting,” Tinari said.
EverWind has said it plans to build the data centre by late 2027.
Following Tuesday’s meeting, Opposition NDP Leader Claudia Chender said she has no confidence the government will implement safeguards to protect Nova Scotians from rate hikes or environmental harm.
“We did not see a single concrete assurance for Nova Scotians that their rates will be protected, that the environment will be appropriately protected,” she told reporters.
“A contract would be great, we haven’t seen one … and ideally, let’s have a piece of legislation that governs this novel, giant industry so Nova Scotians know that they’re protected,” Chender added.
Interim Liberal leader Iain Rankin agreed, saying none of the plans presented in Tuesday’s committee replace a regulatory framework, and the project ought to be subjected to an environmental assessment.
Lora MacEachern, deputy minister of environment and climate change, told the committee that the industrial approval process is the right process to ensure the data centre project is managed properly, and it doesn’t need to go through an environmental assessment.
“The industrial approval provisions apply, and those are good, robust processes in place to protect the environment,” MacEachern told reporters after the meeting.
AI data centres are not on the list of projects that would automatically trigger an environmental assessment in Nova Scotia. This list includes quarries, mines, energy generation projects and other industrial facilities.
A recent United Nations University report says the environmental footprint of data centres globally already rivals some of the world’s largest countries. The report also predicts their water and energy use and pollution will double in just four years as use of artificial intelligence grows.

title: Resign, support Obi, KNN replies RMRDC boss
body: .Challenges Shettima to explain subsidy savings, rising debt By Steve Oko The Kwankwaso National Network, KNN, has challenged the Director-General of the Raw Materials Research and Development Council, RMRDC, Prof. Nnanyelugo Ike-Muonso, to resign his appointment and support the presidential ambition of his kinsman, Mr Peter Obi, rather than campaign for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election based on selfish interests. KNN’s reaction followed Ike-Muonso’s recent call on Obi, the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, to drop his ambition and support Tinubu in 2027, arguing that the South should complete its eight-year tenure before power returns to the North. The group, a support network for Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, described the position as disappointing, arguing that Nigeria needed leadership capable of addressing economic hardship, unemployment, insecurity and declining purchasing power rather than continuity with policies it blamed for the country’s difficulties. KNN sought to know how Obi’s emergence as Nigeria’s President in 2027 would disadvantage the South as claimed by Ike-Muonso, asking whether Obi is a Northerner. The group argued that Obi who had declared his intention to be in office for only one term if elected, will only be completing the turn of the South. KNN in a statement by its South East Regional Coordinator, Dr Ukpai Iro Ukpai, said the 2027 election should be about competence, accountability and national recovery, not merely regional power rotation. “2027 is not about the continuation of misgovernance and ineptitude; it is about rescuing Nigeria from total collapse,” the group declared. It described Obi as a credible alternative with national appeal across ethnic and religious divides, urging Nigerians dissatisfied with the current administration to support his presidential project. KNN also criticised Vice President Kashim Shettima over his reported remark that Obi had nothing to offer beyond statistics. Shettima made the comment at the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit, where he questioned Obi’s economic proposals and his opposition to the restoration of petrol subsidy. Challenging the Vice President, KNN said he should counter Obi’s figures with verifiable data rather than make sweeping allegations. The group also demanded explanations for the administration’s borrowing despite its claims of increased fiscal savings following petrol subsidy removal in May 2023. It challenged Shettima to provide a transparent account of the savings generated, how the funds had been deployed and the tangible benefits Nigerians had received. KNN further questioned the progress made in rehabilitating Nigeria’s state-owned refineries, demanding clarity on expenditure, operational capacity and timelines for delivering results. The group argued that Nigerians deserved measurable improvements in living standards, energy security and economic opportunities rather than repeated assurances of recovery. It warned that political rhetoric would not shield the All Progressives Congress, APC, from electoral rejection if the government failed to address citizens’ concerns. KNN maintained that the 2027 election should be determined by candidates’ competence, policy proposals and performance, insisting that Nigerians deserved accountability and a government that prioritised their welfare. The post Resign, support Obi, KNN replies RMRDC boss appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Putin calls Nord Stream bombing full-blown terrorism
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. The bombing of Russia’s Nord Stream gas pipelines is a direct terrorist act, Russian President Vladimir Putin told the Gas Exporting Countries Forum summit.
"Direct terrorist acts were committed against Russian gas pipelines running to Europe. They were blown up," he said.
Putin noted that the global gas industry is experiencing other shocks, including a worsening situation in the Middle East, a global gas center, disruption of customary logistics chains and supply routes, and international barriers to the purchase of specialized equipment and technologies.
Two lines of the Nord Stream and Nord Stream-2 gas pipelines running from Russia to Europe were bombed in 2022 leaving only one line of Nord Stream-2 theoretically operational. Russia’s Prosecutor General's Office initiated a case on an act of international terrorism. The timeframe for restoring the pipes’ functionality is impossible to set.

title: Again, NIS extends special passport intervention exercise in UK
body: The Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS) has announced the extension of the Special Passport Intervention exercise in the United Kingdom (UK) to now run from November 3 to November 27. This is contained in a statement by the NIS Public Relations Officer, DCI Akinsola Akinlabi, made available to news men in Abuja on Tuesday. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) recalls that the NIS initially extended the exercise to run from October 3 to October 30. Akinlabi said that the extension followed sustained demand and the need to accommodate more Nigerians requiring passport services. According to him, the extension in line with the directive of the Minister of Interior, Dr Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, will continue at 56-57 Fleet ST, Temple, London EC4Y 1JU for the full length of the extension period. “Similarly, the exercise will continue in the Nigerian House, 23 Platt LN in Manchester from Nov. 3 to 27, while the exercise at Hilton Convention Centre 13 Smithfield Road in Aberdeen AB24 4NR will run from Nov. 3 to 6. “The extension at Western Leisure Centre, Ely, Cardiff CF5 5HJ is also only extended from Nov. 3 to 6,” he said. The NIS spokesperson reaffirmed the service’s commitment to efficient, transparent and responsive passport service delivery to Nigerians at home and in the diaspora. (NAN)

title: Venus Williams suffers 16th defeat in a row with loss to teenager
body: Venus Williams suffered her 16th loss in a row in singles tennis as the 46-year-old American icon was defeated by teenager Lilli Tagger in straight sets at the Guangzhou Open on Tuesday. Austria’s Tagger, who is 28 years younger than the former world number one, eased through 6-2, 6-2 in southern China. Williams, a seven-time Grand Slam singles champion, last won a singles match on the WTA Tour in July last year. Now ranked 599 in the world, Williams last played at the US Open in August-September, when she lost in the first round in straight sets to Sofia Kenin. Williams won in the doubles with Indonesia’s Janice Tjen in Guangzhou on Monday. They will play again on Wednesday. The 53rd-ranked Tagger faces Magda Linette of Poland in the next round. title: Niger Miners’ deaths: Panel details roles of NSCDC commandant and four officers
body: By Ayobami Okerinde The independent ministerial committee probing the deaths of miners in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) has detailed the alleged roles of the suspended Niger State Commandant, Suberu Aniviye, and four other officers in the incident. The committee accused the officials of various acts of misconduct, including unlawful detention, failure to respond to distress signals, poor supervision and attempts to alter the detention facility before an independent forensic examination. The committee’s chairman, Jonathan Kure, presented the report to the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, in Abuja on Tuesday. In its findings, the panel said Aniviye authorised and supervised the operation without adequate planning, approval or oversight, permitted overcrowding and failed to ensure that detainees were held in accordance with lawful procedures. “The committee found extensive failures of leadership, supervision and professional conduct. State Commandant Suberu Aniviye authorised and supervised the operation without proper planning, approval or oversight,” Kure said. “He permitted overcrowding, failed to ensure lawful detention practices and later issued a false public statement attributing the deaths to a disease outbreak. The committee concluded that his actions reflected gross leadership failure, abuse of authority and serious professional misconduct.” The committee identified CSC Oluwadare Sunday, head of the Investigation Unit, as another officer whose actions contributed to the failures. It said he facilitated unlawful detention practices, disregarded legal and medical concerns and failed to intervene despite knowing that conditions in the detention facility were deteriorating. SC Usman Isah Ndamaka was accused of maintaining overcrowded conditions and instructing subordinates not to open the cell. According to the panel, he also failed to respond appropriately to emergency alerts and participated in cleaning and altering the detention area before independent investigators examined it. The committee further faulted Station Guard ASCI Hassan Mohammed for allegedly failing to open the cell despite repeated distress signals and not adequately escalating the emergency. Another officer, DSC Sule Garba, was accused of profiling detainees, including minors, without adequately protecting their rights. The panel also said he failed to properly document exhibits. DSC Musa Marafa was accused of unlawfully arresting and detaining one Emmanuel Emeka over a civil death dispute. The committee said his actions contributed to Emeka’s continued detention until his death alongside other detainees. Beyond the conduct of the individual officers, the committee identified broader institutional shortcomings within the NSCDC, including inadequate detention facilities, weak custodial oversight, the absence of closed-circuit television monitoring, poor record-keeping and insufficient emergency medical capacity. Other deficiencies listed in the report included ineffective supervision, weak intelligence reporting arrangements, workforce imbalance and chronic underfunding. The panel warned that these weaknesses created conditions in which serious violations could occur without timely detection or intervention. The committee said the investigation also faced challenges that limited aspects of the forensic assessment. It said the detention register for September 16, 2026, was unavailable, while 30 of the 33 deceased persons had been buried before post-mortem examinations could be conducted. It added that the detention area had been cleaned, disinfected and altered before independent forensic investigators arrived, affecting aspects of the examination. Fujifilm is trying to find the right balance of fun and photography with its latest hybrid instant camera. Like its predecessor, the Instax Mini Evo 2 feels less like a retro gimmick, and more like a basic digital camera that just happens to have a built-in printer. It also enjoys some key upgrades: a larger 1/2.77-inch sensor compared to the 1/5-inch sensor on the first Mini Evo , a bigger 4.5-inch rear display with touchscreen controls, and basic video recording too — though only the few seconds leading up to a photo.
Video is limited in other ways compared to modern standards — the MP4 clips can only be saved to a microSD card (though there is internal storage for photos), no audio is recorded, and quality is limited to 560 × 992 pixels and 24FPS, according to DPReview — but it’s still a feature we wouldn’t expect to see on an instant camera. This is also Fujifilm’s first Instax model to feature an LCD touchscreen, ditching the rear controls in favor of a larger display that takes up the entire back of the camera. Other physical controls have been preserved though, including two dials and a film-inspired print lever.
You can use either the dials or touchscreen to access the 10 film and 10 lens effect options that were available on the first Instax Mini Evo, though the selection has changed slightly with this new model. There’s also an Expanded View mode that “gives users a wider field of view than the shooting area.” The camera charges via USB-C, prints 2 x 3-inch Instax Mini format photos, and lets you adjust the exposure, white balance, and flash settings on your snaps.
The Instax Mini Evo 2 will be available for $290 and goes on sale at the end of November. Black is the only available color option, but it still retains the classic retro look that’ll probably land well with the youth market .

title: UPSA Banking and Finance students learn to prepare wills as part of financial literacy drive
body: Level 400 Banking and Finance students at the University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA), have been guided to write their first wills as part of efforts to promote early estate planning and responsible wealth management among young people. The practical exercise formed part of the fifth National Estate and Gift Planning Awareness Conference (NEGPACON 2026), organised by the Centre for Financial Literacy Education Africa (CFLE Africa) in collaboration with the UPSA Faculty of Accounting and Finance. The conference sought to raise awareness of estate planning, succession, wills, and estate and gift tax considerations. Facilitated by lawyer Benjamin Kodwo Agyare, the session introduced students to the practical steps involved in preparing a will, including identifying assets, selecting beneficiaries and clearly stating their wishes. The exercise was designed to help students apply their classroom knowledge to real-life financial decisions and challenge the perception that wills are only necessary for older people or those with substantial wealth. Financial literacy must include wealth transfer Executive Director of CFLE Africa, Peter Asare Nyarko, said financial literacy education should go beyond earning, saving and investing to include protecting and transferring wealth. “We want young people to understand that building wealth is only one part of the journey. They must also understand how that wealth can be protected, preserved and transferred responsibly,” he said. According to him, introducing university students to wills and succession planning would help them develop responsible financial habits early in life. He added that knowledge of estate planning was particularly important for Banking and Finance students, who could eventually work with individuals and families on financial management and wealth preservation. Mr Agyare said the practical approach helped students understand that preparing a will was not exclusively for wealthy or elderly people. The session also highlighted the need to review estate plans as personal circumstances change, including through marriage, having children, acquiring property and establishing businesses. Students welcome practical experience President of the Banking and Finance Students Association, Josephine Gyekyewaah, said the exercise had changed her perception of wills and estate planning. “Before this session, I think many of us saw wills as something for older people or people who already have a lot of property. But going through the process ourselves changed that perspective. It made me realise that estate planning is about being intentional and responsible with whatever you have,” she said. Student participant Ampofo Bright Ntow said the exercise encouraged him to reflect on his assets and how they should be distributed. “The session made me think about the things I already have and the things I hope to acquire in the future. I had never seriously thought about who would benefit from my assets or what would happen to them if I was no longer around,” he said. He added that writing a will made the subject easier to understand by allowing students to consider the decisions involved rather than simply learning about them in theory. Another participant, James Laryea, said the workshop had demonstrated that people did not need to accumulate substantial wealth before considering estate planning. “One of my biggest takeaways is that you don’t have to wait until you have millions of cedis before you start planning. What matters is that you begin to take responsibility for what you have,” he said. He noted that preparing a will provided an opportunity for individuals to communicate their wishes and reduce uncertainty over their assets. Preparing future financial professionals The initiative forms part of efforts to broaden financial education by incorporating succession planning, inheritance and wealth preservation into the training of future financial professionals. Organisers say early exposure to estate planning can help students develop a more comprehensive understanding of personal and family financial management. Through NEGPACON, CFLE Africa is promoting an approach to financial literacy that covers not only wealth creation but also its protection, preservation and responsible transfer. For the participating students, the exercise provided an opportunity to reflect on their present assets, future financial goals and the importance of making informed decisions about their estates.

title: Emir of Qatar, Iran’s leader discuss developments around Hormuz in Moscow
body:
DOHA, October 27. /TASS/. Tamim bin Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, the Emir of Qatar, and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian discussed the situation around the Strait of Hormuz and energy supplies at a meeting in Moscow, the Arab head of state’s office said in a statement.
"At the meeting, the sides considered developments in the region, mostly the course of negotiations, the situation around the Strait of Hormuz and energy supplies as well as topics on the agenda of the summit," the statement reads.
The two leaders met ahead of the 8th Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) summit currently running in Moscow. Their talks were also attended by Qatar’s Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani and Iran’s top diplomat Abbas Araghchi.

title: Inside Tehran talks: Iranians link Houthi de-escalation to US approval of regional truce
body: A day after Saudi Arabia and its two defence-pact partners sent senior officials to Tehran, sources say the clearest outcome is a promise to keep talking, not a deal to de-escalate on any front, including the Houthi attacks on Saudi cities. Officials from the three Makkah pact countries , Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey, flew to Iran as part of a push towards diplomacy and to chart a path towards resolving conflicts in the region. The delegation was led by Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, signalling Saudi urgency amid escalating attacks by the Yemeni rebels against its airports and fears of a new round of war between the US and Iran. Pakistan’s army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir, and Ibrahim Kalin, director of Turkey’s intelligence service, also attended Monday’s meeting in the Iranian capital, which ended with Iranian state media saying the parties agreed to continue discussions. Sources briefed on the talks said they made no clear headway. Representatives of Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey asked the Iranians to persuade the Iran-backed Houthis to halt their attacks on the kingdom. Iran, the sources said, claimed it lacked leverage over its Yemeni allies to do so. Instead, the Iranians asked their guests to use their close relations with the US to persuade Washington to accept Iran’s offer of a two-week pause in hostilities across the region. The pause would allow negotiations to resume in return for the gradual reopening of the Strait of Hormuz . A source in Tehran claimed that Iran is “willing to help”, but added that the Houthis’ condition that Saudi Arabia lift its air blockade on Yemen before any fighting ends remains unchanged. According to a Yemeni source, Iranians also said that any final discussions to reach a lasting agreement with the Houthis should take place in Sanaa. That offer sits beside Iran’s record as the Houthis’ main outside supporter, through training, intelligence, tactical guidance and help in targeting drone and missile attacks. Iranian support has helped the Houthis carry out their most potent and sophisticated attacks yet on Saudi Arabia and its Yemeni allies, the Wall Street Journal reported this month, citing people briefed on intelligence from Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s anti-Houthi alliance. Non-aggression pact Tensions between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis began to escalate in July, when an air strike hit Sanaa International Airport. The Houthis blamed Saudi Arabia. Yemen’s Saudi-backed, internationally recognised government claimed responsibility, saying it had hit the runway to prevent an unauthorised Iranian aircraft from landing. After that attack, the Houthis, who have long bristled at airspace restrictions enforced by Saudi Arabia, announced a “blockade for blockade” policy. They declared an embargo on Saudi shipping in the Red Sea , which has become an important alternative route for the kingdom's oil exports after the Iran war disrupted shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. Analysts say the more pressure Iran has felt, the more the Houthis have escalated their operations. The talks in Tehran followed warnings by the US, Iran and Israel that hostilities could restart at any moment, and one of the focus points during the meeting was on building a regional non-aggression network, a regional source said. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, claimed that the discussions were “very good”, according to state television. He also said Iran and the three Makkah pact countries agreed that regional countries, not outside powers, should ensure security in the region. A day after the meeting, Iran's supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei reiterated his country's "conditions" for ending the war with the US, during a meeting with Mr Rezaei. The discussions with Saudi Arabia and others, though, were not meant to deter a US-Israeli attack on Iran, The National understands. Instead, the aim was to agree on principles and a course of action should fighting resume, so that any new round of hostilities could be brought under control quickly. Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi had called for a non-aggression security pact involving all six Gulf states as well as Iran and Iraq. He said the US would no longer be the primary provider of security in the future, speaking at Girton College, Cambridge. Prince Khalid last visited Tehran in April 2025, when the region was bracing for a different kind of confrontation. He arrived before talks between Iran and the US over Tehran’s nuclear programme, and delivered a message from King Salman to the late supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei. The visit carried symbolic weight at the time. This time, however, hours after the Tehran talks, the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said it had intercepted and destroyed three ballistic missiles launched by the Iran-backed rebels towards the kingdom’s east and four drones towards its south.

title: Ronaldo in line for Portugal return after fallout with coach
body: Cristiano Ronaldo is in Portugal’s preliminary squad for next month’s Nations League matches, opening the door to an international return after his fallout with coach Jorge Jesus, a federation source told AFP on Tuesday. The 41-year-old abruptly left the Portugal camp on September 30 during the opening qualifiers for the Nations League, before accusing Jesus of breaking his word about giving him game time. A spokesperson for the Portuguese football federation (FPF) confirmed reports Ronaldo was in line for a return to the squad ahead of games at home to Denmark and in Wales on November 14 and 17. Jesus will announce his final squad on November 6, the spokesperson added. The FPF last week announced it had handed Ronaldo a 30-day suspension for walking out. The suspension was backdated, meaning he will be free to return by the end of this week. Ronaldo apologised to supporters earlier in October, adding he would accept any punishment that was imposed. In a social media post shortly after deserting his teammates, he accused Jesus of promising to give him playing time against Norway before failing to honour it but insisted he was not retiring from international duty. He said a further bone of contention between him and the coach was Jesus had not mentioned at a press conference prior to the game with Denmark a series of points they had agreed upon. Reigning champions Portugal won all four of their Nations League matches, three of them without Ronaldo, and qualified for the quarter-finals with two games to spare. The five-time Ballon d’Or winner is the all-time top goalscorer and record appearance-maker in men’s international football. Ronaldo, who made his Portugal debut in 2003 at the age of 18, has said this will “probably” be his final year in football. tsc/jde/mw/pi The post Ronaldo in line for Portugal return after fallout with coach appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Detained Niger miners died from dehydration – probe panel
body: The panel constituted to investigate the death of alleged illegal miners in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Niger State Command, has said the miners died from dehydration. Presenting its report to the Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, in Abuja on Tuesday, the chairman of the committee, Jonathan Kure, said the miners suffered acute respiratory failure. He also corrected the earlier reports that 37 miners died in custódy, saying 33 miners were confirmed dead. He said the miners collapsed after calling for water and were ignored by the personnel of the NSCDC. 2027: It’s time to compensate Tinubu for what he did for the north – Bichi Attacks: Terrorists exploiting local grievances, misinformation – NSA He said the detention room was overcrowded and poorly ventilated. He said there were no approvals for the arrests and detention of the miners, adding that they were all detained beyond the legally allowed period. The panel called for a total reform of the NSCDC and compensation for the victims.

title: Finland and Norway leaders speak to Putin before Ukraine peace talks
body: ​The ​leaders ​of ⁠ Finland ⁠and Norway spoke to Russian President Vladimir ⁠Putin on Tuesday to discuss the prospects for a peace deal in Ukraine. Finland’s President Alexander Stubb and Norway’s Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store initiated the call in consultation with Ukraine , they said in a joint statement. The call aimed to directly convey messages to Mr Putin about future negotiations towards ending the war, they said. It related to trilateral talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US planned for Abu Dhabi early in November, they added. Officials from each country have held sporadic talks throughout the war, including two rounds in Abu Dhabi earlier this year. The leaders emphasised their continued and long-standing support for Ukraine and stressed that the war must end and negotiations must resume. “The war comes with enormous human and material costs. The suffering and destruction will impact generations. In the call we stressed the importance of de-escalation”, Mr Store said. Mr Stubb and Mr Store told Mr Putin that attacks on ⁠Ukraine's energy and ​infrastructure ⁠needed ‌to ​be de-escalated, according to Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The two leaders “clearly told the Russian leader that ​real de-escalation ‌steps ⁠are ​needed regarding ​our ‌energy sector ⁠and infrastructure”, Mr Zelenskyy wrote ⁠on Telegram after talking to the two allies. Mr Stubb called the discussion “frank and substantive”. “Ending the war requires direct discussions,” he said. Mr Putin “emphasised that achieving a just and long-term peace is possible only if the legitimate interests of the Russian Federation are fully and unconditionally taken into account”, according to a Kremlin statement on the call. The three leaders agreed to maintain “direct phone contacts”, it said. The talks follow a revived effort to get peace negotiations on track over the war that is now in its fifth year. US President Donald Trump’s special envoy Steve Witkoff visited Mr Putin in St Petersburg last week, after holding talks in Oslo with Mr Zelenskyy and the two Nordic leaders. Mr Witkoff described Mr Putin as a “humanitarian” during the visit. Poor relations Ukraine’s relations with the US are at a new low after Mr Trump struck a diesel deal with Mr Putin earlier this month and tensions flared over the slowing of Starlink internet connections that are vital to Kyiv’s ability to defend against Russian missile attacks. Budget needs are spiralling and the country lacks the air defences needed to fend off Russia’s expected winter onslaught. The call was the first direct contact between Mr Putin and European leaders allied with Kyiv since French President Emmanuel Macron spoke to his Russian counterpart in July last year. Ukraine’s European allies are seeking a seat at the table for discussions about European security, and Mr Store and Mr Stubb have used their countries’ shared border with Russia as justification for being part of the talks. “We are neighbouring countries to Russia,” Mr Stubb said in the statement. “The outcome of this war will have a direct impact on our and the broader European security.” Their two countries have a “shared interest in stability and predictability in the Baltic Sea region and the High North”, the statement said. Attacks Civilian casualties in Ukraine rose by 85 per cent in September as Russia increased drone and missile attacks, according to the UN. At least 328 civilians were killed and 2,105 injured in attacks last month, UN human rights monitors said. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said one person was killed and 14 injured, most of them students, after a Russian strike near a university dormitory overnight. Ukraine has continued long-range drone and missile attacks inside Russia over the past week, targeting military and industrial sites, while civilian infrastructure and residential property have also been damaged. Since Friday, strikes have killed at least 11 people in regions bordering Ukraine and left dozens injured, according to authorities. Ukraine says its forces struck sites linked to Russia’s defence industry, including several chemical plants and a battery plant, as well as a petrochemical facility and logistics hub in Omsk, roughly 2,500km from Ukraine. Mr Stubb and Mr Store, who were both in Helsinki at the time of the call, said they were not speaking on behalf of Europe as a whole. Still, the call drew criticism from Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen, who told local broadcaster TV2 that it was not co-ordinated with other European leaders. She said she was “very sceptical” over what she described as a solo initiative by Norway and Finland.

title: Rosoboronexport order portfolio with Africa accounts for 30% of its total export volume
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Rosoboronexport's (a subsidiary of the Rostec State Corporation) orders from African countries account for about 30% of the company's total volume of signed contracts, the Russian state arms exporter’s CEO Alexander Mikheyev said ahead of the third Russia-Africa Summit, which will be held in Moscow on October 28-29.
Rosoboronexport sees Africa as one of the world’s most promising regions for the development of military-technical cooperation. The current order portfolio with African countries accounts for about 30% of the company’s total signed contracts. "Russia is helping Africa strengthen its defense capabilities and effectively counter all modern security threats and challenges, and our partners view Russia as a guarantor of their security," said Mikheyev, quoted by Rosoboronexport’s press service.
The company CEO noted that, in addition to supplying modern weapons, Rosoboronexport is actively developing military-technological cooperation projects that contribute to the growth and modernization of the national industries of African countries.
The company’s press service also reported that Rosoboronexport will hold a panel session titled "The Architecture of Indivisible Sovereignty: Comprehensive Russian Technologies for Ensuring Stability and Security in African Nations." During the session, Russian and international experts will discuss combating terrorism and cross-border crime, as well as establishing digital sovereignty as the basis for ensuring the internal security of the state. Furthermore, they will talk about Russian mobile technologies designed to protect the population during emergencies and crises. Summit guests will be introduced to Rosoboronexport’s capabilities for developing technological cooperation.
In addition, the company will present advanced projects for organizing the production of Russian small arms, unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), wheeled vehicles, and other products at domestic facilities.

title: Katsina Intensifies Ebola Surveillance, Strengthens Diphtheria Response Ahead Of Polio Campaign
body: The Katsina State Government has stepped up measures to prevent the outbreak of Ebola Virus Disease and curb the spread of diphtheria, while intensifying preparations for the November 2026 polio vaccination campaign. State Commissioner for Health, Hon. Musa Adamu Funtua, disclosed this during the Emergency Preparedness and Response Committee meeting on Ebola readiness, diphtheria outbreak response and preparations for the upcoming polio campaign, held at the Polio Emergency Operations Centre in Katsina. The Commissioner said the recent confirmation of an Ebola case in the Federal Capital Territory on October 20, 2026, underscores the need for heightened vigilance across the country, noting that although Katsina has not recorded any case, the state has been classified as having a moderate risk of importation due to its strategic location and international entry points. He explained that the state has activated a comprehensive preparedness strategy, including the engagement of health authorities at the Umaru Musa Yar’Adua International Airport and other points of entry, enhanced disease surveillance, community sensitisation, harmonisation of a multisectoral response plan, and the designation of the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control isolation facility at the Federal Teaching Hospital, Katsina, to manage any suspected Ebola cases. Hon. Funtua added that the government is also strengthening the capacity of frontline health workers through specialised training, provision of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), infection prevention and control materials, as well as deploying three fully equipped ambulances to serve the state’s three senatorial zones for emergency referrals. According to him, the state is working closely with the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), the Federal Ministry of Health, Port Health Services, the Ministry of Livestock and Grazing Reserves, the Ministry of Environment, development partners, as well as traditional and religious institutions, civil society organisations and community leaders to strengthen disease surveillance and emergency response. On the ongoing diphtheria outbreak, the Commissioner stressed the need to reinforce surveillance, early case detection, prompt referral, contact tracing, vaccination, effective clinical management and community awareness to prevent further transmission and reduce avoidable deaths. He urged local government authorities, health facilities and development partners to close operational gaps by ensuring suspected cases are promptly reported, contacts adequately managed, treatment commodities remain available, and eligible populations receive routine and outbreak-response vaccinations. Speaking on the November 2026 polio immunisation campaign, Hon. Funtua called for thorough planning, quality micro-planning, adequate training of vaccination teams, vaccine and logistics readiness, security coordination, community mobilisation and real-time monitoring to guarantee the success of the exercise. He emphasised that special attention must be given to underserved, mobile and nomadic populations, as well as communities affected by insecurity, to ensure that every eligible child is vaccinated. The Commissioner noted that effective preparedness depends on strong coordination, timely information sharing, adequate resource mobilisation and the implementation of agreed action plans, urging all stakeholders to align their interventions with the state’s public health priorities. The meeting was attended by representatives of relevant Ministries, Departments and Agencies, development partners and other stakeholders, who deliberated on strategies to strengthen Katsina State’s preparedness against public health emergencies.
