title: Why is an Avianca Boeing 787 flying between Barcelona and Abu Dhabi?
body:
An Avianca Boeing 787-8 has begun flying daily between Abu Dhabi and Barcelona, an unusual operation that might suggest the Colombian carrier has quietly opened a route between Spain and the United Arab Emirates. It has not.
Since October 25, Avianca has been operating Etihad Airways flight EY111 from Abu Dhabi to Barcelona and the return EY112 under an ACMI, or wet-lease, agreement. The arrangement is scheduled to remain in place for one year, until October 25, 2027.
Under this type of contract, Avianca supplies the aircraft, flight and cabin crews, maintenance and insurance. Etihad remains responsible for selling the service, which continues to operate under the Emirati carrier's EY flight numbers.
The aircraft currently assigned to the operation is N791AV, a Boeing 787-8 that was flying regular Avianca services between Bogotá and Europe until immediately before beginning work for Etihad.
Follow Air Data News: WhatsApp | Instagram | LinkedIn | Twitter | Facebook
Flight records show N791AV arriving in Barcelona from Bogotá on October 24 as AV172. The following day, it entered Etihad service and has since been flying between Barcelona and Abu Dhabi.
Etihad still operates the other daily frequency between the two cities with its own Boeing 787-9. The result is two daily flights in each direction, but only EY111/112 is operated by Avianca.
Avianca and Etihad were already commercial partners on the route. The EY111/112 flights also carry Avianca codes AV2421 and AV2416, respectively.
The arrangement means an Avianca Dreamliner and its crews will spend a year flying an Etihad route that does not touch Colombia or any other Avianca destination in the Americas.
Avianca currently operates Boeing 787s as the backbone of its own long-haul network, primarily linking Bogotá with Europe and North America. Air Data News reported earlier this year that the airline had 16 passenger Dreamliners, although its widebody fleet is changing as parent Abra Group expands the types available across its airlines.
The Barcelona operation is one of the first visible results of a strategic partnership announced by Abra Group and Etihad at the Farnborough International Airshow in July.
The agreement is intended to connect the companies' networks in Latin America, the Middle East and Asia and includes cooperation beyond conventional codesharing.
The choice of Avianca for the ACMI operation is particularly notable because Abra already has a company specialized in precisely this business.
Abra acquired a stake in Spanish carrier Wamos Air in 2024. Wamos operates Airbus A330 widebodies on wet-lease and charter contracts for other airlines and has previously supplied aircraft to Etihad itself.
The group has since been increasing the role of widebody aircraft across its businesses. Avianca is adding Airbus A330-900s, while GOL has begun long-haul operations using A330 capacity supplied within the Abra structure.

title: Kazakhstan Maps Water Risks Through 2040 as Regional Cooperation Takes Center Stage
body: The Astana Times provides news and information from Kazakhstan and around the world. ASTANA — Kazakhstan is seeking to make water-sharing across Central Asia more transparent through real-time monitoring and shared data as it prepares for possible declines in water availability through 2040. The country does not currently face a nationwide water deficit, but its dependence on rivers flowing across national borders makes water security a regional issue, Water Resources and Irrigation Minister Nurzhan Nurzhigitov said in an interview with Tengrinews published on Oct. 27. Photo credit: Ministry of Water Resurces and Irrigation. Kazakhstan’s average annual river runoff is about 100 billion cubic meters, with approximately 45% of its river water coming from abroad. The economy, agriculture, industry and housing and utilities sectors collectively use about 25 billion cubic meters annually, according to the minister. Water Resources and Irrigation Minister Nurzhan Nurzhigitov. Photo credit: Tengrinews.kz Seven of Kazakhstan’s eight river basins are connected to transboundary waters. The country receives water from the Kyrgyz Republic, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, China and Russia. The dependence is particularly pronounced in the south, where much of the country’s irrigated agriculture is concentrated. About 90% of the water supplied by the Syr Darya River to the Turkistan and Kyzylorda regions is transboundary. Approximately 75% of the water available to the Zhambyl Region from the Chu River comes from Kyrgyzstan. “Water availability has become a strategic issue and a matter of national security,” Nurzhigitov said. Building trust through shared data One of Kazakhstan’s priorities is to improve the transparency and accuracy of information exchanged by countries that share river basins. Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan have agreed to automate water accounting at 10 sites along the Syr Darya, with five in each country. The German Society for International Cooperation, or GIZ, helped prepare the project documentation. Kazakhstan has already built two hydrological monitoring stations using funds from the Turkistan regional administration. The minister said the two countries had jointly checked the stations and could now see the same data in real time. In January 2026, Kazakhstan proposed developing a plan to digitize the entire Syr Darya basin. Tajikistan agreed to participate, and a working group was established involving Kazakhstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan. Its first meeting was planned for early November, with Kyrgyzstan potentially joining the initiative later. “If we digitize the entire basin, we will see how much water flows through it and how each country fulfills its obligations. This will increase trust. There will be no situation where one country says, ‘I sent this much water,’ while another claims it received nothing,” Nurzhigitov said. The plan for automated water accounting across the Syr Darya basin has already been developed and sent to the countries concerned, according to a note accompanying the Tengrinews interview. However, the minister did not specify a timeline or cost for a fully integrated system. The current initiative is narrower than a shared digital platform covering all five Central Asian countries. Its initial working group involves three countries, with Kyrgyzstan expected to be invited later. Kazakhstan is also developing its own water information infrastructure. The ministry is creating a national information system and plans to open public access to selected data in 2027. The ministry is also developing the TALSIM hydrological modeling system for flood forecasting, developed in cooperation with the United Nations Development Program (UNDP), and wants to add drought-prediction capabilities. Cooperation or competition over water? Nurzhigitov emphasized the importance of regional cooperation, saying that water brings Central Asian countries together rather than inevitably pushing them toward conflict. “Water unites us,” he said. In 1992, the five countries’ water ministers signed an agreement in Almaty to use water jointly and rationally. The International Fund for Saving the Aral Sea and its associated commissions provide additional mechanisms for regional dialogue. According to Nurzhigitov, the commissions meet at least four times a year to discuss water forecasts, available volumes and allocation limits. He said there had been no violations of agreed limits over the past three years. Kazakhstan has also proposed a framework convention on the rational use of Central Asia’s water resources. The ministry has approved the draft domestically and sent it to neighboring countries. Discussions are underway to combine the countries’ proposals into common rules that could help limit climate change’s impact. Asked whether one country might decide to take more water than agreed, Nurzhigitov pointed to water diplomacy and the obligations shared by countries along transboundary rivers. “That will not happen, because water diplomacy and accountability exist. These are transboundary rivers, and each country has obligations that must be fulfilled. That is why this will never happen,” he said. Drought exposes the limits of regional agreements Kazakhstan’s experience in 2021 demonstrated the economic and social consequences of severe drought. According to official figures published by the Prime Minister’s press service on Aug. 12, 2021 , 1,161 head of livestock had died in the Mangystau Region by Aug. 10. Another 553 livestock deaths were reported in the Aral district of the Kyzylorda Region amid a lack of water at watering points and dry pastures. Water shortages again threatened agricultural production in the Zhambyl Region in 2023, when low inflows affected the Chu and Talas river basins. Reporting by Kazinform on Aug. 11, 2023 detailed the scale of the shortfall. From April 1 to Aug. 11, inflow into the Kirovsk Reservoir in Kyrgyzstan, which supplies the Talas River, reached just 60 million cubic meters, compared with 300 million cubic meters during the same period a year earlier. Inflow into the Orto-Tokoy Reservoir, which releases water into the Chu River, reached 55 million cubic meters, against 256 million cubic meters in 2022. The shortage put about 4,000 hectares of onions and sugar beets at risk, Kazinform said, citing a regional official from the agency responsible for maintaining hydraulic structures. Tengrinews’ background information accompanying its interview noted that the 2023 shortage was not simply a matter of Kyrgyzstan failing to meet its obligations. Low snowfall and rainfall had also reduced water availability on the Kyrgyz side, leaving both countries affected by the dry conditions. Such episodes highlight a central challenge for the region: agreements can establish rules for sharing water, but they cannot guarantee sufficient supply when river flows decline. Planning for 2040 Nurzhigitov also shared Kazakhstan’s plans for all eight water basins over five-, 10-, and 15-year horizons, extending through 2040. The plans will assess three water-availability scenarios and estimate how much water different sectors could receive under each. The minister said drinking water supplies would take priority if water were scarce. Separately, the ministry’s press service told Tengrinews that the basin plans would account for scenarios involving reductions in water availability of 50% and 75%. The longer-term outlook is a key reason for moving from annual allocation decisions toward more detailed planning. Nurzhigitov said forecasts suggest that water availability across Central Asia could decline by 15 billion cubic meters by 2040. This is a forecast, not a certainty, but it underscores the need to prepare for several possible outcomes. The plans aim to help the government determine where water infrastructure is needed, how to allocate available resources, and which economic activities can be sustained under different conditions. The ministry is also working to reduce losses and improve water efficiency at home. Agriculture accounts for about 60% of Kazakhstan’s water use, according to Nurzhigitov. Water-saving technologies were being applied to more than 700,000 hectares in 2026, with estimated savings of about 1 billion cubic meters. By 2030, Kazakhstan aims to expand the area using such technologies to 1.3 million hectares, potentially saving an additional 2 billion cubic meters. Industrial enterprises are also expected to increase water reuse and recirculation. As part of a broader package of measures, Kazakhstan aims to save and accumulate about 10 billion cubic meters of water by 2030 through infrastructure upgrades, new reservoirs, digitalization and more efficient water use. The post Kazakhstan Maps Water Risks Through 2040 as Regional Cooperation Takes Center Stage appeared first on The Astana Times .

title: Ballon d’Or win ‘feels like a dream’, says Kane as tributes pour in
body: Harry Kane said Tuesday that his Ballon d’Or triumph “feels like a dream” as tributes poured in for the first English winner of the award in a generation. The England and Bayern Munich forward fended off competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe to be named the world’s best men’s footballer at the London Palladium theatre late on Monday. Wembley was lit up to recognise Kane’s achievement, with England’s X account carrying the message: “The home of the world’s best footballer.” The former Tottenham forward is the first Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or since Michael Owen in 2001. The 33-year-old struck a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for club and country last season, propelling the German giants to a league and cup double. The England captain, who also picked up the men’s striker of the year award, scored six times as his side finished third at the World Cup in North America. “It sounds crazy to be honest but it sounds pretty good,” Kane told Sky Sports on Tuesday. “What a special night. An incredible feeling. I’m still just trying to take it all in really. It feels really, really like a dream. “The emotion (when his name was called) was relief, joy, happiness, excitement. There was so much waiting to find out the winner and in that moment it was quite nerve-wracking so to have that kind of release and to be able to share it with everyone there in that theatre was special.” Prince William, patron of the Football Association, praised the England skipper. “What a fantastic achievement and so deserved,” he wrote on Instagram. “A brilliant captain, a remarkable player and someone who has given football fans across the world so many unforgettable moments.” – Superlatives – England boss Thomas Tuchel, who was Bayern boss when Kane arrived in Germany in 2023, said the Three Lions were “lucky” to have him as their leader. “I ran out of superlatives to describe your performances a long time ago, but I’m delighted to see that you have now been formally recognised by the football world,” he said. “To become the first Englishman to win this huge honour in 25 years makes it extra special and we are lucky to have you as our leader.” England and Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice described Kane as “incredible” while Chelsea’s Morgan Rogers, another international teammate, said he was the “best ever”. Bayern Munich president Herbert Hainer said the award was “a proud day for FC Bayern”. “Harry Kane can do it all –- and he scores goals, goals and more goals. He now joins a line with Franz Beckenbauer, Gerd Muller and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge (as previous Ballon d’Or winners) –- that says everything about our history,” he said. “The club and Harry Kane have got together, grown together and achieved the highest aims together. We are proud that this all-round outstanding sportsman and person is part of our FC Bayern family.” Harry Redknapp, former Tottenham manager, described his all-round game as “brilliant”. “It isn’t just his goalscoring that is good, it is his all-round play, and the way he is and the way he is around the players. He is great as the England captain,” he told the BBC. “No one could have deserved this more, it has been a brilliant story.” AFP The post Ballon d’Or win ‘feels like a dream’, says Kane as tributes pour in appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Israelis head to elections with Netanyahu’s legacy on the line
body:
Israeli voters delivered a sharp rebuke Tuesday to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu , with exit polls indicating voters gave his opponents a solid majority in the next parliament. Whether those disparate parties can form a government is uncertain and will likely take weeks of haggling.
The easiest path would involve Netanyahu’s main rival, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot , partnering with Arab-led parties, but that could prove politically difficult and potentially alienate other opposition factions.
Exit polls released early Wednesday by major Israeli TV stations suggested that Netanyahu’s bloc and Eisenkot’s each won about 51 seats, and Arab parties won about 18. That would set the stage for weeks of political jockeying before a prime minister is declared — or another round of elections is called.
Eisenkot said the exit polls show a “lack of confidence” in Netanyahu and vowed to form a new government. Arab voters celebrated the exit polls while supporters of far-right parties aligned with Netanyahu expressed disappointment.
Netanyahu had yet to make a public statement early Wednesday, hours after the exit polls were released.
Like all surveys, exit polls are subject to potential error. Preliminary results are expected in the coming hours. Final results are expected in the coming days and may vary from the exit polls.
An inconclusive result would leave Israel in political limbo after the country’s first national election since Hamas’ Oct. 7, 2023, attack.
The race was widely seen as a referendum on Netanyahu’s nearly unbroken 17-year rule, which had left Israelis bitterly divided on a host of issues even before the deadliest attack in the country’s history. The resulting wars in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran, along with settler violence in the occupied West Bank, have stoked worldwide outrage, straining ties with Israel’s closest allies and fueling a rise in antisemitism.
Among Israelis, the election was broadly viewed as a struggle over the character of the state, pitting Netanyahu and his ultranationalist and religious allies against those seeking to preserve its liberal and secular foundations. The opposition may soon have to grapple with the social divisions — between right and left, and between Jews and Arabs — that have widened during Netanyahu’s long and polarizing rule.
Voter turnout was the highest since 1999, with more than 77% of eligible voters casting ballots, according to the Central Elections Committee. Over 7 million people were eligible to vote, and tens of thousands reportedly arrived from overseas.
Israel’s president will be tasked with asking the party leader with the best prospect of forming a government, usually one with the most seats, to cobble together a coalition. If Netanyahu’s right-wing Likud emerges as the largest party, he could claim that right.
Meanwhile, there will be heavy pressure on Eisenkot to reach a deal with the Arab parties, while Netanyahu and his allies are likely to cast any such alliance as illegitimate and even treasonous.
Netanyahu had warned earlier that Arab parties could make or break the election, saying they were receiving “truly massive support” and heading to the polls in “unprecedented numbers.”
If no one can cobble together a majority coalition, new elections could be held early next year. Israel held five elections between April 2019 and November 2022 because of a similar stalemate.
No single party has ever won an outright majority in the country’s 120-seat parliament, forcing political leaders to forge coalitions. Minority governments are also possible, but they must rely on support or cooperation from parties outside the government to pass legislation.
Netanyahu’s current coalition peaked at 68 members before it began to disintegrate over the past year.
As the exit polls were broadcast, supporters at Eisenkot’s party headquarters jumped for joy, chanting his name.
In a speech early Wednesday that focused on national unity, he pledged to form a government and promised “a new era — an era of hope” for Israelis.
“Today, Israel went out to a referendum over the leadership that will lead Israel in the coming years,” Eisenkot said to cheers from supporters. “The people decided in favor of change.”
Eisenkot warned Netanyahu not to “dare use Israel’s security for your political needs” while he is a caretaker prime minister, an apparent reference to reports that the Israeli leader considered an attack against Iran in the sensitive days leading up the election.
At Netanyahu’s party headquarters, filled mainly with media, the few supporters present chanted Netanyahu’s name, draping themselves in flags with his face on them and kissing posters.
Netanyahu’s supporters see him as a steady hand and a consummate statesman who has led Israel through a war of redemption after the country’s darkest hour. They think he is protecting Israel’s security and Jewish identity in the face of international pressure and liberal elites at home.
His detractors see him as a polarizing leader who, beset by an ongoing corruption trial, dragged out the war in Gaza and its hostage crisis for political reasons. They say he is undermining Israel’s independent judiciary and weakening its democratic underpinnings. And they accuse him of abetting the system that has allowed ultra-Orthodox religious Jews to avoid military conscription.
“The present government is driving the country into the ground,” voter Angela Bengur said in Jerusalem.
Eisenkot is viewed by supporters as a capable leader with sterling security credentials who, along with his likely governing partners, could act as a bulwark against creeping illiberalism. As someone personally touched by the conflict — his son and two nephews were killed in Gaza — his backers believe that he feels deeply the pain that still courses through Israel.
Parties that likely would support Eisenkot have vowed to improve Israel’s international standing and work to conscript ultra-Orthodox men while bolstering the independence of the judiciary.
The elections are about “who serves and who evades service — who takes an active part in building this country and who doesn’t,” said voter Nisso Shitrit in Tel Aviv’s Jaffa neighborhood.
The election is Israel’s first national vote since the Oct. 7 attack that sparked the war in Gaza and related conflicts. In Tel Aviv, families of some killed on Oct. 7 or former hostages held a moment of silence during the vote.
“Remember all those whose voices are no more,” said Yona Adam, whose daughter Mapal Adam was killed.
Israel has found itself increasingly isolated over its conduct in Gaza and the West Bank. Public support among Americans has plummeted, and partners in Europe and elsewhere have slapped sanctions on Israel. Netanyahu faces an international arrest warrant over alleged crimes against humanity in Gaza, allegations he denies.
Also hanging over the election were lingering tensions with Iran. Netanyahu ramped up threats ahead of the vote, warning Tehran it would face “a devastating blow” if it attacked Israel.
Associated Press writers across Israel contributed to this report.

title: Russia ranks first globally in terms of natural gas reserves — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Russia currently ranks first in the world in terms of natural gas reserves and second in terms of production, Russian President Vladimir Putin said at the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) summit.
"Russia is one of the key players in the global gas market. We rank first in the world in terms of natural gas reserves and second in terms of production," he said.
A unique production complex has been established in the country, which makes it possible to diversify gas supplies and develop gas processing, the Russian leader added.

title: Osinbajo demands justice, accountability to end North-central conflicts
body:
Former Vice President Yemi Osinbajo has called for justice, accountability and deliberate reconciliation to address persistent conflicts and social divisions in Nigeria’s North-central region.
He spoke on Monday at a conference organised by the Justice Research Institute, in partnership with the National Institute for Policy and Strategic Studies (NIPSS), Kuru in Plateau State.
Mr Osinbajo said lasting peace would require governments, religious leaders, the political elites and civil society organisations to work together to rebuild trust among communities affected by years of violence.
The conference, themed “Countering Polarisation and Rebuilding Civic Cohesion in North-Central Nigeria: Beyond Tribe and Faith—Reclaiming Our Shared Stories,” brought together stakeholders to discuss practical approaches to addressing divisions and restoring peaceful coexistence.
Mr Osinbajo said rebuilding social cohesion required a deliberate change in how people viewed themselves and related to others across ethnic and religious divides.
“Let’s go back to being brothers and sisters again, and that orientation must be an intentional thing,” he said, stressing that uniting divided communities required deliberate government actions.
Citing South Africa and Rwanda as examples, the former vice president said societies that had experienced severe violence could rebuild relationships through determined leadership and sustained reconciliation efforts.
He referred to the 1994 Rwandan genocide, during which hundreds of thousands of people, predominantly Tutsis, were killed, saying the country’s subsequent reconciliation efforts demonstrated the importance of political commitment to rebuilding social cohesion.
“I think there’s a need for deliberate reconciliation and peacebuilding, and that can only be done by the government in collaboration with civil society groups and religious leaders,” he said.
He added that political and religious leaders, as well as civil society organisations, must promote unity, while governments must demonstrate the political will to address the underlying causes of conflict.
Mr Osinbajo also warned that reconciliation would be difficult without justice and consequences for wrongdoing.
He said victims of land grabbing and other forms of dispossession should have their properties restored, while compensation should be provided where necessary.
“For instance, if you look at the land-grabbing situation, the lands have to be returned to those from whom they have been taken. It’s as simple as that,” he said.
He said failure to restore victims’ losses would leave grievances unresolved and undermine efforts to rebuild trust among communities.
“Similarly, there must be penalty for wrongdoing, and our justice system… requires urgent attention,” he added, calling for improvements in the administration of justice.
In his welcome address, the Director-General of NIPSS, Ayo Omotayo, urged participants to approach the discussions with open minds and without prejudice.
Mr Omotayo said the conference should produce practical recommendations to improve relationships and secure a peaceful future for communities across the North-central region.
The conference chairman, the Emir of Lafia, Sidi Bage, a retired justice, also called for discussions that would produce meaningful solutions, promote justice and address the underlying causes of conflicts.
Mr Bage urged participants to embrace new perspectives and recognise their shared responsibility for building peaceful communities.
The co-chairman and Secretary-General of Jama’atu Nasril Islam, Khalid Aliyu, said rebuilding civic cohesion remained challenging in some communities, partly because of misleading messages from some religious leaders.
Mr Aliyu stressed the importance of responsible religious leadership in promoting understanding, tolerance and peaceful coexistence.
The conference focused on ways to counter ethnic and religious polarisation and rebuild trust in the North-central region, which has experienced recurring communal violence and prolonged tensions among communities.

title: From Criminal Federation to Gang Wars: Rasquiña’s Legacy
body: From Criminal Federation to Gang Wars: Rasquiña’s Legacy An increasingly fragmented underworld has turned Ecuador into a battleground, with rival gangs driving violence to record levels in recent years. Many factors have fueled this crisis, but one criminal figure in particular propelled Ecuador to this moment: Jorge Luis Zambrano, alias “JL,” or “Rasquiña.” SEE ALSO: Jorge Luis Zambrano, alias “Rasquiña” Criminal Profile Rasquiña’s leading role in Ecuador’s criminal scene began in the 2010s. From within the country’s prisons, he turned the Choneros from a gang of common street thugs into a national criminal federation by recruiting youth gangs and groups of thieves, extortionists, and micro-traffickers. Among them were the men who would go on to become the faces of Ecuador’s security crisis: a bank robber and future leader of the Lobos, Wilmer Geovanny Chavarría Barré, alias “Pipo;” a corrupt prison guard who later founded the Tiguerones, William Joffre Alcívar Bautista, alias “Willy;” and the Camacho brothers, leaders of a local youth gang that became the Chone Killers. Under the umbrella of the Choneros, this network of gangs took over the prisons, then launched an aggressive campaign to seize strategic drug trafficking territories around the country. Rasquiña used his gang network as a mercenary criminal army to provide services to transnational drug traffickers, like Mexico’s Sinaloa Cartel , and corruption networks. The model of organized crime he developed endures today, with gangs acting as contractors for criminal elites. In 2020, Rasquiña was murdered shortly after being released from prison in an allegedly corrupt judicial ruling. The alleged gunman was arrested, but the intellectual author behind the hit remains unknown. One theory suggests that Rasquiña was the victim of an internal mutiny led by his right-hand man, José Adolfo Macías Villamar, alias “Fito.” Others point to a calculated power grab by the rapidly ascending Lobos, or that the hit was ordered by drug traffickers wary of Rasquiña’s growing power . The murder led to the breakup of the Choneros network, kickstarting a process of criminal atomization that has continued ever since. SEE ALSO: Rasquiña’s Revolution: How the Choneros Took Ecuador’s Prisons The Lobos , Tiguerones , and Chone Killers formed a new alliance dubbed Nueva Generación (New Generation) and waged war on the Choneros, sending murder rates spiralling. But that alliance was short-lived and gave way to an era characterized by fragmentation, with the gangs splintering into highly unpredictable, constantly shapeshifting and fracturing cells that forge volatile alliances and compete violently for territory. Today, Ecuador faces as many as 48 criminal groups, according to Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED) data reported by Diálogo Américas . In 2024, President Noboa declared the country was in an internal armed conflict with 22 gangs he labeled as terrorist organizations. The United States would later follow suit, adding the Choneros , the Lobos , the Tiguerones , and the Chone Killers to its list of Foreign Terrorist Organizations. Each of them was once part of Rasquiña’s Choneros federation. Read more about Rasquiña’s criminal history and legacy in our InSight Crime profile here . The post From Criminal Federation to Gang Wars: Rasquiña’s Legacy appeared first on InSight Crime .

title: Russian forces strike Ukrainian long-range UAV assembly workshops in past day
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Russian forces struck Ukrainian long-range unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) assembly and storage sites, ammunition depots and enemy deployment areas over the past 24 hours in the special military operation in Ukraine, Russia’s Defense Ministry reported.
"Operational/tactical aircraft, attack unmanned aerial vehicles, missile troops and artillery of the Russian groups of forces struck transport infrastructure facilities used by the Ukrainian army, ammunition depots, workshops producing and sites storing ground robotic platforms and long-range unmanned aerial vehicles, and also temporary deployment areas of Ukrainian armed formations and foreign mercenaries in 148 locations," the ministry said in a statement.
The Ukrainian army lost roughly 1,115 troops in battles with Russian forces in all the frontline areas over the past 24 hours, according to the latest data on the special military operation in Ukraine released by Russia’s Defense Ministry.
The latest figures show that the Ukrainian army lost over 165 troops and three armored combat vehicles in the responsibility area of Russia’s Battlegroup North, more than 230 troops and two armored combat vehicles in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup West and over 150 troops and eight armored combat vehicles in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup South.
During the last 24-hour period, the Ukrainian army also lost over 345 troops, a tank and three armored combat vehicles in the responsibility area of Russia’s Battlegroup Center, more than 195 troops and two armored combat vehicles in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup East and about 30 troops and nine motor vehicles in the responsibility area of the Battlegroup Dnepr, the latest figures show.
Russia’s Battlegroup North inflicted more than 165 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed three enemy armored combat vehicles in its areas of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup North units gained better lines and positions and inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of three mechanized brigades, a motorized infantry brigade and two assault regiments of the Ukrainian army in areas near the settlements of Bugayevka, Rubezhnoye, Veliky Burluk, Izbitskoye and Stary Saltov in the Kharkov Region," the ministry said.
In the Sumy direction, Battlegroup North units struck formations of a mechanized brigade of the Ukrainian army and two territorial defense brigades in areas near the settlements of Sukhodol, Luzhki, Vakalovshchina and Proletarskoye in the Sumy Region, it said.
The Ukrainian army lost more than 165 personnel, three armored combat vehicles and 11 motor vehicles in the areas of responsibility of Russia’s Battlegroup North over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup West inflicted more than 230 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed two enemy armored combat vehicles in its area of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup West units improved their forward positions and inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of two mechanized brigades, an assault brigade of the Ukrainian army and a territorial defense brigade in areas near the settlements of Studenok, Smorodkovka, Glushenkovo, Nizhnyeye Solyonoye and Monachinovka in the Kharkov Region, Donetskoye and Bogorodichnoye in the Donetsk People’s Republic," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost more than 230 personnel, two armored combat vehicles, 14 motor vehicles and a field artillery gun in that frontline area over the past 24 hours, it said.
Russia’s Battlegroup South inflicted more than 150 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed eight enemy armored combat vehicles in its area of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup South units improved their tactical position and inflicted losses on formations of two mechanized brigades, an air assault brigade, a mountain assault brigade of the Ukrainian army and a marine infantry brigade in areas near the settlements of Kramatorsk, Slavyansk, Druzhkovka, Kamyshevakha, Kondratovka and Semyonovka in the Donetsk People’s Republic," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost more than 150 personnel, eight armored combat vehicles, 41 motor vehicles, a Czech-made Vampire multiple rocket launcher and an artillery gun in that frontline area over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup Center inflicted more than 345 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed an enemy tank and three armored combat vehicles in its area of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup Center units gained better lines and positions and inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of two mechanized brigades, an assault brigade, an assault regiment of the Ukrainian army and three National Guard brigades in areas near the settlements of Yakovlevka, Starovarvarovka, Verovka, Viktorovka, Krinitsy, Kalinino, Belozerskoye, Novofyodorovka, Shilovka and Svyatogorovka in the Donetsk People’s Republic," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost more than 345 personnel, a tank, three armored combat vehicles, 13 motor vehicles, a field artillery gun and an electronic warfare station in the responsibility area of Russia’s Battlegroup Center over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup East inflicted more than 195 casualties on Ukrainian troops and destroyed two enemy armored combat vehicles in its area of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup East units advanced into the depth of the enemy’s defenses and inflicted losses on manpower and equipment of an air assault brigade, two assault regiments of the Ukrainian army and a marine infantry brigade in areas near the settlements of Trudoolenovka, Tersyanka, Volnyanka, Barvinovka and Vasilevskoye in the Zaporozhye Region and Gavrilovka in the Dnepropetrovsk Region," the ministry said.
The Ukrainian army lost more than 195 personnel, two armored combat vehicles, three motor vehicles and an artillery gun in that frontline area over the past 24 hours, it specified.
Russia’s Battlegroup Dnepr eliminated roughly 30 Ukrainian troops and destroyed nine enemy motor vehicles in its area of responsibility over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Battlegroup Dnepr units improved their forward positions and inflicted losses on formations of a mechanized brigade and a mountain assault brigade of the Ukrainian army in areas near the settlements of Preobrazhenka and Orekhov in the Zaporozhye Region," the ministry said.
"Up to 30 Ukrainian military personnel and nine motor vehicles were destroyed," it said.
Russian air defense forces intercepted and destroyed 645 Ukrainian unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and two smart bombs over the past 24 hours, the ministry reported.
"Air defense capabilities shot down two guided aerial bombs and 645 fixed-wing unmanned aerial vehicles," the ministry said.
Overall, the Russian Armed Forces have destroyed 674 Ukrainian combat aircraft, 284 helicopters, 272,423 unmanned aerial vehicles, 672 surface-to-air missile systems, 31,425 tanks and other armored combat vehicles, 1,793 multiple rocket launchers, 36,823 field artillery guns and mortars and 75,749 special military motor vehicles since the start of the special military operation, the ministry reported.

title: UN commission finds Russia’s grid strikes are crimes against humanity, citing last winter at minus 21°C. Now they’re intensifying
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Russian authorities committed war crimes and crimes against humanity through attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure, the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on Ukraine said in a report to the UN General Assembly on 26 October. International Criminal Court (ICC) warrants for former Russian Defense Minister Sergei Shoigu and Chief of the General Staff Valery Gerasimov, issued in June 2024 , already covered alleged crimes linked to Russia’s 2022–2023 strikes on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure. The UN commission’s new report reaches into last winter, 2025–2026, and the cumulative toll since 2022, documenting what the attacks did to civilians living through outages in freezing temperatures. “As the cold season approaches, the attacks have intensified once again, raising serious concerns about the threats to civilians’ lives and health,” commission chair Erik Møse said. Russian commanders knew heating facilities were vital The commission said Russian commanders knew that heating facilities in large cities were indispensable to civilians, particularly during winter. Russian authorities also made official declarations about further attacks and referred to a plan to carry them out, it said. It found that Russian authorities intentionally directed attacks against civilian objects, constituting war crimes. The commission also concluded that the attacks were carried out under a state policy aimed at depriving civilians of electricity and other essential energy-dependent services and causing suffering. It classified these acts as crimes against humanity in the form of “other inhumane acts.” Minus 21°C, weeks without heat, and shelters out of reach for older people Last winter, temperatures fell to minus 21°C as millions of Ukrainians endured prolonged disruptions to heating, electricity, water, and gas, the commission said. The commission relied on the accounts of 255 people from Dnipropetrovsk, Kyiv, Kharkiv, Kherson, Mykolaiv, Odesa, Poltava, Zaporizhzhia, and Zhytomyr Oblasts, alongside officials, doctors, and nongovernmental organizations. Older people and those with limited mobility were particularly affected. Fear of becoming trapped in elevators during blackouts prevented some residents from reaching shelters during air raid alerts. They remained in unheated homes, sometimes without access to life-support equipment. A 53-year-old Kyiv resident told investigators he tried to stay awake at night because he feared he might not wake up if he fell asleep in the cold. Meanwhile, school closures disrupted children’s education, and children fell ill in unheated homes, the report said. Russia rejects the findings Russia’s UN mission said Moscow did not recognize the commission’s mandate and dismissed its findings as “falsified data,” the Associated Press reported . The commission also examined Ukrainian attacks on energy infrastructure in Russia and Russian-occupied Ukraine. It said it could not investigate their impact fully because Russia denied access and did not respond to its requests. Foreign recruits trafficked to the front The same report found “compelling evidence” that Russian authorities trafficked men from 29 countries into the Russian armed forces through deception and coercion. Recruitment agents arranged visas and travel, presenting themselves as legitimate businesses. After arriving in Russia, the men were forced to sign military contracts in Russian and were sent to the front, where many were killed or went missing, the commission said. title: Uzbek Labor Migration to Russia Falls 13.2% in First Half of 2026
body: Uzbek citizens accounted for more work-related arrivals in Russia than any other nationality in the first half of 2026, despite a 13.2% decline compared with a year earlier. According to data published by TASS on October 26, Uzbek citizens listed employment as the purpose of entry on 1,178,609 occasions. Tajikistan ranked second with 494,518 entries, followed by Kyrgyzstan with 289,061, Kazakhstan and China. The statistics count border entries rather than individual people: a single worker may have crossed the Russian border several times. The Central Bank of Uzbekistan reported approximately 1.358 million such trips in the first half of 2025, nearly 180,000 more than a year later. Russia remains Uzbekistan’s largest overseas labor market, but the number of Uzbek citizens working in other countries is growing. In 2025, the number of Uzbek workers in the European Union increased by 13.2%, while the figure for Turkey rose by 10.7%. As of July 1, 2026, approximately 70,000 Uzbek citizens were in Turkey, and 102,200 were in South Korea, both increases from a year earlier. These figures reflect the number of citizens present in the respective countries and do not necessarily correspond to employment statistics. Despite the decline in work-related trips, remittances from Russia to Uzbekistan increased by 8.8% in the first half of 2026. For Uzbekistan, remittances are a significant source of household income. The Central Bank has warned that declining labor migration could eventually reduce household incomes and consumer spending. Meanwhile, the number of advertised vacancies in Uzbekistan fell by 9.8% year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026, while competition for jobs intensified. Unpaid wages are another persistent problem. During the first nine months of 2026, Uzbekistan’s Migration Agency handled complaints from 817 citizens concerning unpaid wages and compensation, recovering a total of $850,000 from foreign employers. Of these complaints, 533 came from Russia, 155 from Turkey, and 92 from South Korea. The agency also helped 532 Uzbek citizens recover identity documents withheld by intermediaries or employers. Russia accounted for 331 such cases and Turkey for 185. The Times of Central Asia previously reported that Russia accounted for 72.4% of remittances received by Uzbekistan in the first quarter of 2026, despite its declining share.

title: Kyrgyzstan’s BARS Electric Vehicle Plant Opening Delayed
body: Kyrgyzstan’s BARS electric vehicle assembly plant has missed its planned September opening, with production now expected to begin in late 2026 or spring 2027. In August, the Ministry of Economy and Commerce reported that construction was 75% complete and the plant would begin production by the end of September. However, speaking to residents of Tash-Kumyr and Kara-Kul on October 23, President Sadyr Japarov said the factory might not open until March or April 2027. The plant, covering a 15-hectare site, is designed to produce up to 10,000 vehicles annually, including passenger cars, commercial vehicles, and special-purpose vehicles. Production will initially rely on imported components, with plans to manufacture more parts locally later. The facility could employ around 100 people. According to the ministry, the project is privately financed, while the government has provided the land. The vehicles are intended for domestic sale and export to other Central Asian countries and markets in the Eurasian Economic Union. Japarov’s announcement came during a discussion about replacing city buses that had been in service for 20 to 30 years. He said Kyrgyzstan would develop a program to gradually replace older gasoline- and diesel-powered vehicles with electric ones, including government vehicles, over the next 15 to 20 years. At the beginning of 2026, Kyrgyzstan had 15,278 registered electric vehicles , accounting for 0.8% of its 1.91 million vehicles. By September 1, the number had risen to 30,221 , according to figures provided by the country’s vehicle registration authorities. The BARS plant’s planned annual production capacity is equivalent to roughly one-third of that total. Since 2020, Kyrgyzstan has encouraged electric vehicle imports through customs incentives. In 2025, the duty-free import quota was 10,000 vehicles. For 2026, an initial allocation of 15,000 vehicles was increased to 25,000 in August . The quota was exhausted by the end of September . Imports of electric vehicles subsequently became subject to a customs duty of 15% of their customs value, while the value-added tax exemption for eligible electric vehicles less than five years old remained in place. The number of vehicles imported under the quota cannot be directly compared with the number of registered vehicles. The quota also covers certain hybrids, and customs figures do not establish how many imported vehicles ultimately remain in Kyrgyzstan. In September, the State Customs Service identified five electric vehicles that had been transferred to Russian citizens without payment of the required duties and charges. These cases do not provide sufficient evidence to assess the scale of re-exports.

title: Oleshky residents to be evacuated via Crimea, Russia before returning to Ukraine – media
body:
Residents of occupied Oleshky (Kherson region) who agree to evacuate within a local ceasefire will first be transported to Crimea or Russia before they can return to Ukrainian-controlled territory, Financial Times (FT) reports, citing sources familiar with the negotiations.
According to the report, residents of occupied Oleshky in Kherson region who agree to evacuate within a local ceasefire will first be transported to Crimea or Russia before they can return to Ukrainian-controlled territory, citing sources familiar with the course of negotiations.
The agreements were reached against the backdrop of intensified efforts to resume peace negotiations to end the war in Ukraine.
As reported, Ukraine is introducing a ceasefire in a designated area of temporarily occupied Oleshky (Kherson region) from 3:00 on Tuesday, October 27 until 22:59 on November 1, Kyiv time, to conduct a humanitarian operation.
On Friday, the White House announced that Melania Trump had secured a ceasefire agreement between Russia and Ukraine covering Oleshky to ensure the delivery of humanitarian aid and prepare the evacuation of the civilian population through a designated safe corridor. The local ceasefire will take effect on October 29.
Verkhovna Rada Commissioner for Human Rights Dmytro Lubinets confirmed the agreement on the humanitarian mission in Russia-occupied Oleshky, previously announced by First Lady of the United States Melania Trump, and clarified that it provides for a silence regime, the delivery of humanitarian aid, and free exit for civilians from the city.
In a video address on Friday, Lubinets stated that within the framework of the agreement, a regime of silence would be ensured first, humanitarian cargo would be delivered to Oleshky second, and free movement of the civilian population from Oleshky would be ensured third.
He asked to treat the dissemination of public information regarding the execution of this humanitarian mission with understanding and described its implementation as very complex.
The Ombudsman emphasized that the operation would take place gradually and was maximally complex to implement, adding that he would inform Ukrainian society and show the results of the operation. He noted that as of that day, the Ukrainian side had done and was doing everything to save citizens remaining in Oleshky.

title: Federal government to introduce bill restricting MAID for mental illness
body:
CORRECTION: An earlier version of this story incorrectly said in the lede that the bill would see access to MAID for people whose sole reason for seeking it is mental illness. This should have said that access would be barred, and this article has been updated to reflect the error.
The federal government on Tuesday revealed the details of a bill that would see access to medical assistance in dying (MAID) barred for people whose sole reason for seeking it is mental illness.
Bill C-41, the Medical Assistance in Dying Safeguard Act, would amend the Criminal Code to shield doctors from prosecution when they provide assisted death to an eligible patient who requested it in an advance directive.
“We will work with provinces and territories on implementation, with rigorous safeguards to protect people and ensure the decision remains voluntary and free from external pressure,” Justice Minister Sean Fraser said.
MAID is “deeply personal and complex,” Health Minister Marjorie Michel said.
“Our approach must respect personal autonomy and individual choice while maintaining robust safeguards for those who may be vulnerable,” she said.
While the bill may be able to amend the Criminal Code, the provinces and territories will “organize, regulate, and deliver health care, including MAID assessments and provision,” the federal government said.
In Canada, a person seeking MAID on the basis of mental illness is not eligible to receive it, and the federal government said in February 2024 that it would delay the expansion to mental illness until March 17, 2027.
The new law would prevent the expansion entirely; however, it would still have to pass both the House of Commons and the Senate before the March 17 deadline.
Officials cited “difficulty in assessing an individual’s decision-making capacity when seeking MAID on the basis of a mental illness” as a reason for preventing the expansion of Canada’s MAID laws for mental illness.
Advocacy group Dying With Dignity Canada said it was disappointed by the federal government’s decision to exclude mental illness from the ambit of the law.
“It is stigmatizing and unconstitutional and Dying With Dignity Canada continues to be dismayed in any action that prevents all Canadians from equal access to apply for MAID,” Helen Long, the group’s CEO said.
Often referred to as an “advance directive” or “advance request” in medical parlance, the principle involves a mentally competent person making a written request for MAID, with the intention that it would be honoured later, if and when they lose the capacity to make the decision for themselves: for example, in people suffering from worsening Alzheimer’s or dementia.
In 2024, Quebec became the first, and so far, the only province to authorize residents an early request for MAID.
Quebec’s MAID law is “in compliance” with rules Ottawa is looking to establish, Fraser said.
The federal bill restricts advance directive on MAID only to people who are:
The bill lays out two “tracks” under which a person can receive MAID. The first is in cases of people with incurable illnesses with “death reasonably foreseeable,” for example, someone suffering from cancer nearing the end of their life.
The second track is for people with incurable illnesses with “death not reasonably foreseeable.” This includes, for example, a person with Parkinson’s disease who is not nearing the end of their life but has irreversible decline in their abilities.
Dying With Dignity Canada, which has long advocated for advance directives, says the federal government’s approach is “fundamentally flawed” because it downloads implementation to the provinces and territories.
“Dying With Dignity Canada is disappointed that the Medical Assistance in Dying Safeguards Act includes an exclusion from MAID eligibility for persons whose sole underlying medical condition is a mental illness,” Long said.
The applicant should have prepared the advance request with help from a medical or nurse practitioner and consulted with a medical practitioner who is an expert in their condition or illness.
They should also have been given clear information about their diagnosis, progression of their illness, and the available options to relieve their suffering before they make the decision, and also informed about the mechanism by which they can withdraw their consent to receive MAID.
If a person meets all the eligibility criteria, a second medical doctor or nurse practitioner must provide written confirmation of the eligibility based on the advance request. The two practitioners who provide the confirmation should be independent.
If a person set to receive MAID shows any “refusal or resistance” to receive the procedure through either “words, sounds or gestures,” the procedure must be halted.
If medical practitioners observe a person refusing MAID through words, sounds or gestures, they must wait a minimum of 30 days before they can reassess and resume the procedure.

title: SSPDF says it’s too early to comment on $1.4M compensation order
body: South Sudan’s army spokesman, Maj. Gen. Lul Ruai Koang, said on Tuesday it was too early to comment on a court order requiring the Ministry of Defence to pay $1.4 million in compensation to two people injured in a shooting outside the Juba residence of former National Security Service (NSS) Internal Security Bureau Chief General Akol Koor Kuc. Koang told Radio Tamazuj that the ministry’s leadership needs to review the judgment with its legal team before issuing a response. “I have just read in the media a few minutes ago,” Koang said. “At the moment, it is too early.” He said the ministry’s leadership needs to examine the verdict and seek legal advice before deciding how to respond. “If I am delegated to do it on their behalf, then I would be able to respond,” Koang said. The court on Tuesday awarded Manawa Gabriel Makwach $1,074,180 and Agum Andrea $381,000 in compensation for medical expenses, property losses and moral damages. The total monetary award was $1,455,180, excluding court and legal fees. The court also ordered the defense ministry to pay Makwach 30 head of cattle in accordance with customary tradition after a medical assessment found that he had sustained a 60% disability. The case stemmed from a shooting on November 21, 2024, in which Makwach and Andrea were injured while travelling in their vehicles. Their lawyer, Angelo Thon Pal, said they had initially pursued the matter through the Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs before obtaining permission to sue under Section 33(2) of the Code of Civil Procedures Act, 2007. Pal said the next step is to open an execution file through the court, after which the defense ministry would be summoned to implement the judgment. He said the court would enforce its decisions if the ministry failed to comply. The post SSPDF says it’s too early to comment on $1.4M compensation order appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: MTN: How to make your data last long
body: The Chief Executive Officer (CEO) of MTN Nigeria, Mr Karl Toriola, has urged Nigerians to optimise their mobile phone settings to manage data consumption and prevent unnecessary depletion of their data bundles. Toriola made the plea at the ` Data on Trial` experience organised by MTN Nigeria, on Monday in Abuja. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the event was meant to address public concerns about data consumption and pricing in Nigeria. Toriola said many factors were responsible for MTN data pricing including operational costs face by mobile telecommunication operators. According to him, operators incur significant expenses in providing electricity, transportation and other infrastructure required to maintain telecommunications sites. He said that MTN spent about N4.05 trillion on power in the preceding year, highlighting the cost pressures affecting telecommunications operations. “Even within the context of data being perceived as more expensive in Nigeria, the UK is the example I was giving. “Please, understand that in this country, as well as some other African countries, we are providing power and transportation to all our sites. “The cost of electricity, for instance, is higher here than in the UK,” he said. He explained that Nigerian operators deployed similar telecommunications equipment and technologies used in Europe and the U.S., including Fourth-Generation (4G) and Fifth-Generation (5G) networks. The MTN CEO said that “Data on Trial” was designed to enlighten consumers on how phone settings, online activities and application preferences influenced data consumption. Earlier, the Chairman, House of Representatives Committee on Communications, Mr Peter Akpatason, described the initiative as an opportunity to improve public understanding of data management and address misconceptions about the telecommunications industry. Akpatason said the demonstration helped consumers understand how data was consumed and the measures they could take to prevent avoidable depletion. He said the event also challenged the perception that data prices in Nigeria were higher than in other countries. The lawmaker acknowledged the significant investment in the telecommunications sector, adding, however, that there was room for improved investment to for better service quality. The General Manager, Network Performance and Quality Assurance at MTN Nigeria, Mr Mike Ndukwe, said video streaming, social media activities and automatic downloads were among the factors contributing to rapid data consumption. Ndukwe explained that requesting a video on TikTok required relatively little data, while downloading and streaming the content consumed significantly more, depending on its resolution and duration. He said a 15-second TikTok video could consume between two megabytes (MB) and 20MB, depending on its resolution, adding that high-definition videos generally consumed more data than standard-definition content. According to him, 4G and 5G networks supported higher-quality video streaming, which could increase data consumption when applications automatically selected higher resolutions. Ndukwe said WhatsApp users could also experience rapid data depletion through automatic downloads, status updates, media shared in groups and chat backups. He advised subscribers to disable automatic media downloads, restrict background data usage and configure applications to download large files only when connected to Wi-Fi. The MTN official recommended enabling data-saving features on TikTok and other social media platforms, reducing video resolution and disabling automatic playback where possible. He said MTN provided tools, including the MyMTN app, to enable customers to monitor data usage in real time and receive alerts. He added that the company regularly sensitised subscribers on data-saving measures and offered MTN FiberX as an unlimited data option for customers with high data requirements, subject to applicable terms. Ndukwe said data depletion generally resulted from users’ online activities or phone settings rather than unexplained deductions, urging subscribers to understand how their devices and applications consumed data. (NAN)

title: ANEG Foundation launches climate awareness and tree-planting project at Amedeka
body: The ANEG Foundation has launched a climate awareness and tree-planting initiative at Amedeka, bringing together 35 participants to promote environmental sustainability and encourage young people to take an active role in climate action. The exercise, held on Friday, October 23, 2026, involved climate advocates, Environmental Club students and members of the foundation who planted fruit trees on a designated piece of land. The seedlings included pawpaw, mango, lime and soursop, selected to expand green spaces and promote the environmental benefits of tree planting in local communities. The initiative forms part of the foundation’s efforts to advance climate action, protect the environment and encourage youth participation in building greener and healthier communities. The exercise began at 9:30 a.m. and ended at 11:00 a.m., with participants working together to plant the seedlings and raise awareness about the importance of trees in addressing climate change. Monitoring to support tree survival Beyond the planting exercise, the ANEG Foundation says it will conduct periodic visits to the site to monitor the growth and survival of the seedlings and ensure they receive the necessary care. The foundation says the monitoring process is intended to improve the seedlings’ chances of survival and ensure the project delivers lasting environmental benefits. It plans to extend the initiative to Natriku, Lubuse and Kasunya as part of efforts to reach more communities with its environmental activities. Partners support climate initiative The foundation has expressed appreciation to residents of Amedeka, climate advocates, Environmental Club students and other participants for their contributions to the exercise. It also acknowledged Fairtrade and Golden Exotics Limited for sponsoring the initiative. The ANEG Foundation says the project reflects its broader commitment to community-led environmental protection and inspiring young people to become advocates for climate action. It hopes the initiative will encourage a culture of tree planting and responsible environmental stewardship, with continued monitoring and care expected to be central to its long-term success.

title: Israeli Hollywood star Gal Gadot votes in 26th Israeli Knesset elections
body: Israel's own Wonder Woman, Gal Gadot, posted a video to her Instagram story on Tuesday morning showing her voting in the Israeli elections.No matter how famous she is in Hollywood, Gadot proved her heart is still blue and white as she joined an estimated 70,000-plus Israelis living abroad who returned home to vote.In a video from a typical-looking Israeli polling station, she said, in Hebrew, as she picked up an envelope and went into the voting booth, “That's it. I'm exercising my right to vote, and I'm asking you all to go out and exercise your most basic, most important right, the most democratic right you have, to vote for whoever you believe in... And I hope it's Tuesday and that it's pa'amim ki tov [a Hebrew expression referencing the fact that in the story of the creation of the world in the Bible, it says “good” twice on the third day and Tuesday is the third day of the week in Israel, which has come to mean “a double blessing”], with God's help, and that it will be, for all of us, only good.”At the end, she blows a kiss to the camera. The next story is a photo showing her placing her envelope in the box.She will also appear on the comedy show, Eretz Nehederet (Wonderful Country), on Tuesday night after the polls close. The superstar actress lives most of the year in Los Angeles with her husband, Jaron Varsano, and their four daughters, but is originally from Rosh HaAyin.Gal Gadot receives honorary doctorate from Bar Ilan University She was also in the country on Monday to receive an honorary doctorate from Bar Ilan University as part of a gala celebrating the university's 70th anniversary.US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff also received an honorary doctorate.As she accepted the award, JNS reported that she said, “We've experienced loss, fear and uncertainty here in Israel and in Jewish communities around the world. Antisemitism has always been with us, and unfortunately, it's not going away. As an Israeli and a Jewish woman working internationally, I feel the distance between the home I know and the way we're sometimes portrayed from the outside. No matter how far I travel, Israel's always my home. These are my people, my family.”Gal Gadot emphasizes importance of Israel electionsShe also spoke about the importance of the elections: “In just a few hours, the polls will open for what may be the most momentous election this country has seen in years, or even ever. This is the moment when we must all show up and exercise the most powerful civic right we have: the right to vote, to vote according to our beliefs, with a sense of responsibility for the people, women and men, who call it home.”Gadot can currently be seen in the thriller The Runner on Prime Video and will appear in the next installment of the Fast and Furious franchise, Fast Forever.

title: Border restriction harm Iraq national interests: Iraqi MP
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 27 (MNA) – Karim Aliwi, a member of the Iraqi Parliament’s Security and Defense Committee, says that the Iraqi government deicion to restrict borders withh Iran harm the Iraqis' national interests and sovereignty.
The Iraqi lawmaker's remarks came after the closure of the Al-Sheib border crossing, known as Chazabeh on the Iranian side, on October 21. The crossing is located in Iraq’s Maysan province and serves as an important route for trade between the two countries.
Aliwi stressed that decisions concerning relations with neighboring countries should be made in accordance with Iraq’s national interests and should not be influenced by external pressure.
The closure prompted protests in Maysan province. Some lawmakers and local officials have warned of the decision’s potential economic consequences, including disruptions to cross-border trade and rising commodity prices. The Iraqi Parliament has also formed a committee to investigate the reasons behind the closure. Iraqi officials have cited a review of security and technical arrangements as among the reasons for the decision.

title: Tinubu orders probe into Sheikh Masussuka’s murder
body: President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has condemned the murder of prominent Islamic preacher, Sheikh Yahaya Ibrahim Masussuka, and his friend, Adamu Abubakar, in Dutsin-Ma, Katsina State. The President has also ordered a thorough investigation into the circumstances leading to the death, adding that perpetrators should be brought to book. The gunmen killed the sheikh and his associate in a drive-by shooting incident on Monday evening. Reacting, Bayo Onanuga, Special Adviser to the President on Information and Strategy, said the President was deeply saddened by the news of the killing. The President described the act “as heinous and an assault on the values of peace and sanctity of human life.” Onanuga said President Tinubu has extended his heartfelt condolences to the families of the deceased, their followers, as well as the government and people of Katsina State, over the tragic loss. “The President has directed the Nigeria Police Force and other relevant security agencies to move swiftly, intensify efforts already underway by the Katsina State Police Command, and ensure the perpetrators are tracked down, apprehended, and brought to justice. “President Tinubu prayed for the repose of the souls of the departed and for comfort for all those who mourn their death.”

title: Number of injured in Derhachi, Kharkiv region, reaches 5
body:
The number of people injured in a missile strike on Derhachi has risen, with two more individuals seeking medical attention, reported Oleh Synehubov, head of Kharkiv Regional Military Administration.

"Two more people have sought medical help in Derhachi," Synehubov wrote on his Telegram channel.

title: Government adds red tape to reservation process - MP Friz
body:
The government is complicating the reservation process with new bureaucratic hurdles, Iryna Friz of the European Solidarity faction, a member of the parliamentary Committee on National Security, Defense and Intelligence, believes.
"Instead of simplifying reservation, the government is creating new bureaucratic hurdles for enterprises that ensure the country's defense," Friz told Interfax-Ukraine on Tuesday, commenting on a Cabinet of Ministers resolution changing the rules for the reservation of people liable for military service.
According to the MP, the government has introduced a new bureaucratic filter, the Coordination Center, whose recommendations will determine important reservation decisions. She believes that approval of reservation issues may take more than a month, which creates uncertainty for enterprises, a risk of losing specialists and delays in fulfilling defense orders.
Friz also noted that the changes to the reservation rules create an imbalance in approaches: strict requirements for business, but no special responsibility for officials who drag out decisions.
"This approach by the government is unacceptable: instead of ensuring the stable work of strategic enterprises, it tightens administrative control and shifts the consequences of its own bureaucracy onto business. During the war, the state must produce more weapons, not waste time on approvals! Every extra bureaucratic barrier in the way of defense production is the government's responsibility to the army and the country," Friz said.
The MP also noted a positive provision of the resolution: an increase in the reservation quota for designated defense industry and energy enterprises from 80% to 95%.

title: Local truce in Ukraine. Moscow and Kyiv confirm ceasefire
body:
Russia and Ukraine have confirmed the commencement of a local ceasefire in the area of occupied Oleshky in the Kherson Oblast. The agreement is intended to enable the delivery of humanitarian aid and the evacuation of residents, Reuters reported.
The ceasefire began on 27 October at 02:00 Polish time. The arrangements apply to a limited area and are meant to facilitate a humanitarian operation. They do not signify a suspension of hostilities along the entire front.
It is not yet known whether the objectives regarding aid deliveries and evacuation possibilities will be realised; however, initial reports indicate that the „regime of silence” is being observed.
Despite the local agreement, Russian attacks on other Ukrainian cities continued. The ceasefire near Oleshky does not cover these actions. The town of Oleshky is situated in the Kherson Oblast on the left bank of the Dnipro. For several months, there have been reports of a catastrophic humanitarian situation and a lack of access to medicines and food. Roads to Oleshky are controlled by Russian strike drones, and the delivery of supplies has been possible only by means of unmanned aerial vehicles.

title: The Download: Anthropic’s IPO, smarter power grids, and exercise pills
body: This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. Will the real Anthropic please stand up? After weeks of frenzied speculation, Anthropic has filed its IPO prospectus. The 335-page document (100 pages or so are focused on risks) lays out the company’s unique view of the technology it is building and how it believes it will change the world. But Anthropic has been honing its storytelling skills for years. Its public messaging is a master class in narrative capture, presenting it as different things to different people: an AI safety organization, a profit-driven megacorp, and a group hell-bent on creating superhuman technology. These roles come with huge tensions. Will the IPO reveal the company behind the mask, or lean deeper into the myth-making? Take a new glimpse inside Anthropic . —Will Douglas Heaven This story is from The Algorithm, our weekly AI newsletter. Sign up to receive it in your inbox every Monday. How solid-state transformers could help power the AI boom Transformers are a crucial but nearly invisible part of the US grid, helping efficiently move power across long distances. But they’re complicated and in short supply, and their basic design hasn’t changed much in about a century. As electricity demand rises from EVs, data centers, and more, researchers and companies are looking to modernize these grid staples. Solid-state versions could help ease supply concerns and cut power losses. The technology is still in development, but it could become a crucial part of our future grid. Find out how solid-state transformers could help meet rising electricity demand . —Casey Crownhart Are we there yet? Exercise in a pill We all know exercise is good for us. It builds muscle, strengthens bones, lowers blood pressure, and boosts mood. By deciphering how movement benefits the body, researchers hope to develop medicines that can offer some of the same perks, without the workout. The idea isn’t to replace exercise but to bring its upsides to people who struggle with frailty, disability, or chronic illness. Discover how close researchers are to developing an exercise pill . —Cassandra Willyard This story is part of “Are we there yet?” from the new Impossible issue of MIT Technology Review . The series takes stock of six technologies that have long promised to change the world—and scores them on a progress meter. Over the next six days, we’ll explore each one in The Download. The must-reads I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology. 1 Anthropic has filed for its blockbuster IPO The listing could determine the future of the AI investment boom. ( Reuters $) + The prospectus reveals soaring revenues but also staggering losses. ( NYT $) + Anthropic’s founders will retain voting control after the IPO. ( Verge ) 2 Solar is quietly overtaking nuclear as a global power source Cheap panels and batteries are accelerating the shift. ( BBC ) + The balcony solar boom is coming to the US. ( MIT Technology Review ) 3 OpenAI has announced three new science discoveries They span mathematics, computer science, and physics. ( Verge ) + It’s enlisted expert “shepherds” to publish its breakthroughs. ( Bloomberg $) + Microsoft plans $190 billion in AI spending this year. ( NYT $) 5 The plastics industry knew microplastics could enter the body decades ago Company documents reveal concerns dating back to 1974. ( LA Times $) + No part of the globe is free of human fingerprints.
