title: Chris Hesse’s film legacy takes centre stage at UniMAC-IFT
body: UniMAC-IFT will screen historic footage of Ghana’s independence and early nationhood on 30th October, highlighting veteran cinematographer Rev. Dr Chris Hesse’s efforts to preserve the country’s audiovisual heritage. Ghana’s history has survived in books, monuments and the memories of those who lived through its defining moments. Yet another record of the nation’s past, one capable of bringing its political struggles, cultural expressions and national ambitions vividly back to life, remains vulnerable: the films that captured Ghana as it emerged from colonial rule. For veteran cinematographer Rev. Dr Chris Hesse, preserving these moving images has become a defining part of his legacy. His work safeguarding footage associated with Ghana’s first President, Dr Kwame Nkrumah, has helped keep alive a visual record of the country’s formative years, at a time when the survival of historical film collections has become an urgent cultural concern. That legacy will come into focus on Friday, 30 October, when the University of Media, Arts and Communication’s Institute of Film and Television (UniMAC-IFT), in partnership with the UNESCO Ghana Office, screens historic films to mark the World Day for Audiovisual Heritage. The event, to be held at the institute’s television studio, will feature footage documenting Ghana’s independence celebrations, the inauguration of the First Republican Parliament, the opening of Tema Harbour and Nkrumah’s international engagements. Head of the UNESCO Office in Ghana, H.E. Edmond Moukala, is expected to deliver the keynote address, while Hesse will attend as special guest of honour. The screening offers more than an opportunity to revisit historical events. It raises a fundamental question about who preserves a nation’s visual memory, how that memory is protected and whether future generations will have meaningful access to it. Among the films scheduled for screening are Freedom for Ghana , The Inauguration of the First Republican Parliament , Ghana National Anthem , Progress at Akosombo , Industrial Development in Ghana and Roots of Highlife . The programme also includes Africa Reborn: Birth of the OAU and footage of Nkrumah’s overseas visits. Collectively, the films document a country defining its political identity, developing its infrastructure and establishing relationships across a newly independent Africa and the wider world. They also offer researchers, educators, filmmakers and younger audiences access to original images that can deepen their understanding of events often encountered only through written accounts. The significance of such records becomes clearer when their vulnerability is considered. Many historic productions were recorded on celluloid film, a medium susceptible to deterioration when exposed to unsuitable storage conditions. Preserving these materials requires specialised handling, appropriate environmental conditions, technical expertise and, increasingly, digitisation to facilitate access and support long-term preservation. Hesse’s archive illustrates both the value of preservation and the consequences of leaving it to chance. His collection contains more than 1,000 reels of footage documenting Ghana’s independence era and the wider African liberation movement. The story of these recordings has gained renewed attention through The Eyes of Ghana , a documentary directed by filmmaker Ben Proudfoot that follows Hesse’s efforts to preserve and bring this historical material to wider audiences. The concern extends beyond whether the reels physically survive. Historical footage must also be properly identified, catalogued, documented and made accessible under appropriate copyright and licensing arrangements. Without these systems, valuable recordings can remain effectively invisible, even when they have escaped physical destruction. For Ghana, that represents a cultural and educational loss. Footage of political ceremonies can help historians examine the country’s early institutions, while recordings of infrastructure projects can illuminate changing development priorities. Music and cultural performances preserve aspects of social life that written documents may not fully convey. The importance of protecting these records also connects with Ghana’s broader efforts to safeguard its cultural heritage. In December 2025, UNESCO inscribed highlife music and dance on its Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, recognising a tradition whose rhythms, lyrics and performances reflect Ghanaian life and identity. Preserving audiovisual records can complement such efforts by retaining the images and sounds through which cultural practices, artistic traditions and historical experiences have been expressed and transmitted. The potential benefits also reach the creative economy. Properly preserved and accessible archives can support documentary production, historical films, educational programming and exhibitions. With clear access and licensing frameworks, they can also create opportunities for collaboration between archivists, researchers and contemporary filmmakers seeking to tell Ghanaian stories through authentic historical material. The World Day for Audiovisual Heritage, observed annually on 27 October, draws attention to the need to safeguard films, sound recordings, radio broadcasts and other audiovisual documents. This year’s screening, themed “Your Window to the World”, will bring that international message into a Ghanaian context, connecting the preservation of historical records with the responsibility to make them available to the public. For UniMAC-IFT, the event is an opportunity to place audiovisual preservation at the centre of conversations about film education and the future of Ghana’s screen industries. It also provides a platform to consider how institutions can work with professionals and other stakeholders to protect collections that hold national significance. Ultimately, Hesse’s legacy poses a challenge that extends beyond one cinematographer or one collection of films. His work demonstrates the value of preserving history, but it also raises questions about the institutional support, resources and long-term planning needed to ensure that the responsibility does not rest on individual commitment alone. When the historic footage returns to the screen in Accra, audiences will see more than images of a country’s past. They will encounter evidence of the ambitions, struggles and cultural expressions that helped shape modern Ghana. Whether those images remain available for future generations will depend on what the country does to preserve them today.

title: India calls for comprehensive UNSC reforms, says veto must not serve narrow political interests
body:
By R Anil Kumar

New York/ Bengaluru, Oct 27, 2026. India has reiterated its call for comprehensive reforms of the United Nations Security Council (UNSC), emphasising that the veto power held by its five permanent members must be exercised with restraint and should not become an instrument of narrow political expediency.



Delivering India’s statement at the United Nations in New York, India’s Permanent Representative to the UN, Parvathaneni Harish, said the veto carries significant responsibility, particularly on matters concerning international peace and security.

India has consistently maintained that the veto, currently available only to the five permanent members — China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States — must be exercised responsibly, he said.

Highlighting the historical use of the veto, Harish said it had been exercised 331 times on around 200 resolutions during the UN’s existence. He noted that the disproportionate use of the veto by a limited number of permanent members had raised concerns about the credibility of the Security Council.

He also referred to the UN General Assembly’s adoption of Resolution 76/262 in 2022, which provides for a General Assembly debate following the exercise of a veto in the Security Council. However, he said the continued use of the veto showed that the mechanism had not brought about the expected change in practice.

India Seeks Simultaneous Progress on All Reform Areas:

Harish stressed that veto reform cannot be pursued in isolation and must be addressed alongside other critical aspects of Security Council reform.

These include the categories of membership, regional representation, the Council’s size and working methods, along with the question of the veto.

India called for the early commencement of text-based negotiations with clearly defined timelines and milestones to advance the reform process.

The Indian envoy said limiting the veto alone would not fundamentally alter the decision-making dynamics among the permanent members, underlining the need for a comprehensive approach to reform.

Concern Over Informal Blocking Mechanisms:

Harish also drew attention to what he described as an “effective or de facto veto” in the Council’s working procedures.

He said the requirement for consensus in decisions concerning presidential statements, press statements and sanctions committees could allow a single member to block proposals, sometimes without providing an explanation.

According to India, such informal blocking mechanisms also need to be considered while reforming the Council’s decision-making processes.

India Backs Equal Rights for Permanent Members in an Expanded Council:

Reaffirming India’s alignment with the Common African Position on Security Council reform, Harish said all permanent members of a reformed Council should enjoy the same rights and responsibilities, including the veto for as long as the power continues to exist.

He opposed the creation of a separate category of permanent members with or without veto powers, arguing that such an arrangement could perpetuate existing inequalities.

India maintained that a reformed Security Council must ensure greater fairness and representation while addressing the concerns of countries and regions that remain underrepresented in the current structure.

The call comes amid continuing discussions at the United Nations on reforming the Security Council to make it more representative and responsive to contemporary global challenges.

title: Intel. forces nab dozens of terrorists in SE Iran
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 27 (MNA) – Iran’s intelligence and security forces have arrested several members of the terrorist group Jaish al-Adl [also known as Jaish al-Dhulm], near the town of Bampur in Sistan and Baluchestan Province in southeastern Iran.
Iranian security forces arrested 6 members of a terrorist group in Bampur, southern Sistan and Baluchestan, during a joint operation. Three Kalashnikov rifles, a handgun, 7 magazines and 172 rounds of ammunition were seized from the terrorist group.
The arrests were made on Tuesday during a security operation involving a pursuit, according to local officials.
The deputy governor of Sistan and Baluchestan for security affairs confirmed the arrests, saying security forces were continuing operations to clear the area of terrorists.
He added that the Armed Forces and security agencies would announce further details of the operation in the near future.

title: Vice President calls for stronger role for queen mothers in advancing women’s rights
body: Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang has urged queen mothers to use their influence to strengthen women’s participation in community decision-making. She said traditional leaders play an important role in advancing gender equality and creating opportunities for women to contribute to community development. The Vice President made the call at the Yokama Ligbi (Ideal Woman Day) celebration, held as part of the 133rd Ngmayem Festival of the Manya Krobo Traditional Area in the Eastern Region. She stressed the need to move beyond policy commitments and ensure that measures designed to empower women translate into tangible improvements in their lives. Professor Opoku-Agyemang cited the Social Protection Act 2025, the Social Protection Regulations and the Affirmative Action Regulations 2026, launched earlier this month, as examples of efforts to strengthen support for vulnerable groups and promote equal opportunities. She urged queen mothers to help ensure that women were not excluded from decisions affecting their families and communities. The Vice President also highlighted the proposed Women Development Bank, which is expected to improve access to finance for women who face difficulties securing loans from traditional financial institutions. She said women traders and farmers often struggled to obtain credit because they lacked the collateral or financial records required by lenders. Improving access to finance, she said, would help women expand their businesses and contribute more effectively to Ghana’s economic development. On education, Professor Opoku-Agyemang said the Free Senior High School programme was helping to remove barriers that prevented girls from accessing secondary education. She, however, emphasised that families, schools, traditional authorities and communities must work together to guide young people and prepare them for the future. The Vice President also encouraged young people to remain curious, question existing assumptions and be willing to learn and reconsider their views. Professor Opoku-Agyemang was honoured during the celebration and expressed appreciation to the chiefs, queen mothers, elders and people of the Manya Krobo Traditional Area for the recognition. Yokama Ligbi, meaning Ideal Woman Day, is an annual feature of the Ngmayem Festival that celebrates Krobo women who have distinguished themselves through professional achievements, character and contributions to culture and community development. The initiative was introduced in 2003 by the Paramount Chief of the Manya Krobo Traditional Area, Nene Sakite II, five years after his enstoolment as Konor. Traditionally held on the third day of the week-long festival, the celebration features traditional attire and performances of the Klama dance, highlighting the cultural heritage of the Krobo people.

title: Kwara: Fallen 33kV power line razes buildings, workshop, vehicle
body: A fallen electricity line has sparked a fire that damaged three buildings, destroyed a vulcanising workshop and burnt a vehicle in Oloje Phase 2, Ilorin, Kwara State. The incident occurred in the early hours of Tuesday on Lawyer Lambo Street, Ilorin West Local Government Area of Kwara State. A concrete pole supporting a 33kV transmission line reportedly collapsed which led to the inferno. Occupants of a room-and-parlour apartment, including a family that recently welcomed a newborn baby, were rescued by residents as the fire spread to nearby properties. NCDC: 2027 elections may be postponed if Ebola spreads 64 students hospitalised after being administered Bilharzia drug in Katsina Three vehicles were parked in one of the affected four-bedroom flats when the fire broke out. While one was completely burnt, firefighters prevented the flames from destroying the other two, it was gathered. The fire also damaged the kitchen of another four-bedroom flat, affecting a freezer, other electrical appliances and the building’s solar power system. An adjoining travel and tours office was not spared, as its solar power system, four tubular batteries and other electrical appliances were damaged. A nearby vulcanising workshop was completely destroyed after the fallen transmission line landed on it and the vehicle that was subsequently burnt. The fallen line reportedly generated sparks that ignited the vehicle’s tyre, causing the fire to spread rapidly across the affected properties. Residents said Firefighters arrived at the scene at about 2:41am and contacted the Ibadan Electricity Distribution Company (IBEDC) to disconnect power to the affected area because of the danger posed by the fallen line. The Chief Fire Officer, Alabi Muhammed, confirmed the incident. He urged residents and property developers to observe the required safety setbacks around transmission lines to reduce the risks of fire outbreaks, electrocution and property damage. He also advised residents to report fallen electricity poles, damaged infrastructure and exposed wires to the relevant authorities immediately. Muhammed warned them against touching fallen cables or objects in contact with them. The fire service commended residents who helped rescue the occupants of the affected apartment.

title: Syria says Jordanian airstrikes killed civilians, denies strikes were coordinated
body: The Jordanian Air Force carried out airstrikes in Syria overnight on Monday, targeting terrorists in the wake of an attack on a church in Karak, Jordan. Jordanian security forces also raided a building and detained several suspects in the kingdom.On Tuesday, the Syrian government issued an official statement about the recent airstrikes executed by Jordan in southern Syria, saying they “resulted in several casualties, including women and children.” Syrians are in mourning.They are also angry over reports that up to seven civilians were killed in the airstrike. Levant24, a Syrian channel, showed a flag at half-mast in the wake of the attack. Many feel that their country is too often targeted by airstrikes without any accountability.They have also been protesting over the past week against Israeli raids in southern Syria, in which a civilian was reported killed.Initial reports from Syrian state media SANA say five civilians were killed by Jordan. “Five civilians, including women, children, and an elderly man, were killed in Jordanian airstrikes that targeted several sites in the Daraa countryside, Daraa Health Director Khaled al-Amyan told SANA on Monday.” Al-Amyan identified the man as a 65-year-old man from the Sad Road area in Daraa city, who was taken to Daraa National Hospital and died of shrapnel wounds from the airstrike.At least seven killed in strikesSANA went on to quote the health director as saying that two wounded people in Al-Muzayrib town in the western Daraa countryside had been transferred to Tafs National Hospital for treatment. Jordan's military said its air force targeted “terrorist hideouts” in southern Syria.There are currently many questions in Damascus about the strikes that occurred. While Jordan said that there was coordination with Syria, the Syrian government insisted that “the operation was not coordinated with Damascus in advance,” and it announced that an investigation was underway “while opening communication channels with Amman.”Syria's government has expressed solidarity with the victims and hopes for their full recovery. It confirmed that “relevant national authorities are closely monitoring the situation to assess the needs of the affected population and provide immediate required support and humanitarian relief.”Syria has begun an investigation. Al-Arabiya reported that Amman said it will expand coordination with Damascus in the wake of the incident: “Simultaneously, Syria has opened direct channels of communication with officials in the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan to review the incident.”“The Syrian government underscored the imperative of joint field and security coordination regarding any actions along the border region, emphasizing the need to uphold the sovereignty of the Syrian Arab Republic and preserve the security and stability of both brotherly nations,” the report added.Jordanian airstrikes highlight risks of civilian casualties despite precision weaponsThe attacks by Jordan illustrate the complex challenges militaries face in using air power to fight terrorists despite intelligence gathering and the use of precision weapons. Such weapons provide the illusion that pinpoint strikes will always reach their intended targets, yet it is always possible that those same precision munitions can end up killing civilians.This has been a challenge in many recent conflicts in the region. The United States is investigating the bombing of a girls' school in Iran in February 2026, which killed hundreds.There were also several incidents of civilians being killed in Gaza. In one case, aid workers of the NGO World Central Kitchen were killed in several precision strikes on a land vehicle convoy.The question about the strikes in Syria will now shift to what went wrong.There are also questions about the links between the terrorists who attacked the church and the sites targeted in Syria. Is there a growing danger of ISIS or other terrorist groups in Dara'a in southern Syria? If so, what is the plan for Jordan, Syria, or even Israel to confront this challenge? In the wake of the incidents overnight between Monday and Tuesday, these questions remain pertinent.

title: Ukraine says it hit drone hangars at Crimea’s Hvardiiske. Now an OSINT channel spots 20+ bermed shelters there
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Russia is expanding drone storage at the Hvardiiske military airfield in occupied Crimea, Ukrainian OSINT channel Dnipro Osint reported on 26 October, citing new satellite images. The channel did not say who took the images or when. Ukraine’s Security Service (SBU) said it struck drone hangars at the same airfield in July, and the military said strikes on 13 October damaged four drone storage sites nearby. Hvardiiske has stayed in use since then. Ukraine’s General Staff has listed it among the sites Russia launched attack drones from in every daily report since 7 October . The airfield was on the list again on 24 , 25 , and 27 October, the night Russia aimed its main strike at Kyiv. The new construction, as the channel describes it, adds protected storage at a base Ukraine has already shown it can reach. Shelters and “garages” The images show more than 20 small shelters under construction, each protected by earth berms, the channel said. It also counted about 40 smaller structures it calls “garages.” It said they are meant for storing, servicing, and preparing Geran drones for launch. Geran is the name Russia gives the Iranian-designed Shahed drones: the Shahed-136 became the Geran-2, which Russia now builds itself. The images show at least one hangar damaged by a Ukrainian drone hit, Dnipro Osint noted. Launched from vehicles Hvardiiske, north of Simferopol, uses mobile launch platforms instead of fixed installations, according to Dnipro Osint. Crews load drones onto specially equipped vehicles, which then launch them from the runway. Struck repeatedly since June On 24 June, the SBU said it hit infrastructure at Hvardiiske and at the Saky airbase. On 3 July, the SBU reported that its drones struck two hangars at Hvardiiske that stored Shaheds and aviation equipment. Ukraine’s General Staff said its forces struck the airfield again overnight on 5 July, and the SBU said a day later that it hit three hangars with aviation equipment there. A strike on 3 August destroyed nine aviation-fuel tanks and damaged two aircraft hangars, the General Staff said . Strikes on 13 October damaged four drone storage sites near Hvardiiske, with signs of secondary detonation, it reported two days later. Not the only base Russia is building up Hvardiiske is not the only Russian drone base Ukrainian OSINT channels have flagged this month. On 13 October, the anonymous channel Absolutely Reliable Source said Russia had nearly finished the first section of a launch site for jet-powered Geran-5 drones near Millerovo in Rostov Oblast, with eight launcher positions and 32 drone-preparation spots. Hvardiiske and Millerovo were both among the launch areas the General Staff listed for the night of 27 October, when Russia launched 280 Shahed-type drones, 69 of them jet-powered, with Kyiv as the main target. title: Iran’s top security official meets with Leader Ayat. Khamenei
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 27 (MNA) – Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council (SNSC) Major General Mohsen Rezaei met and held talk with Leader of the Islamic Revolution Ayatollah Seyyed Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei in Tehran on Tuesday.
In his meeting with the secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, the Leader stipulated that enemy’s desperation is a result of Iran’s national resistance.
Officials must pursue Iran’s rights, interests through fulfilment of Iran’s stated conditions, the Leader emphasized.
Iran’s Leader Ayatollah Khamenei has stressed pursuit of Iran’s rights to end war and ‘neither peace not war’ situation.
Khamenei described the Supreme National Security Council and its secretariat as a “crossroads” of policymaking for the country’s affairs, emphasizing the mutual influence of four domains — culture, politics, economy, and security — and the need to ensure that decisions in each domain are accompanied by appropriate complementary measures.
The Leader said that sound and well-grounded decisions require a roadmap based on a comprehensive picture of each action, from its starting point to its conclusion.
Other issues discussed at the meeting included strengthening national cohesion and unity, fostering mutual trust between the people and officials, and making use of the capacities of the Constitution, particularly Article 176, to assist the president and executive bodies in facilitating and accelerating the resolution of the country’s problems.
Safeguarding national and regional security through the management of the Strait of Hormuz and consolidating bilateral relations with neighboring countries on the basis of sustainable and mutual interests were also among the topics addressed.
Ayatollah Mojtaba Hosseini Khamenei described the enemy’s desperation as one of the fruits of national resistance. He also stressed the need for active and timely public information efforts to sustain the people’s participation in defending the country and the political system.
The Leader further emphasized the need to pursue the rights and interests of the Iranian nation and the Resistance Front by securing the conditions set out by Iranian officials for ending the war and the state of “neither war nor peace.”
During the meeting, Rezaei presented a report on the country’s situation in various fields and the efforts underway to address existing issues.

title: Education Minister commends JoyNews, Manasseh Azure for Obuasi SHTS investigation
body: The Education Minister, Haruna Iddrisu, has commended the Multimedia Group Limited and its investigative correspondent Manasseh Azure Awuni for their report on the sexual misconduct allegations at Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS) involving the headmaster and some female students. Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Tuesday, October 27, the Minister praised the media house and the journalist for bringing the matter to public attention. “We should thank Manasseh Azure and JoyFM for the exposé,” he said. “But what is important is for us to establish evidence on all the matters relating to it in order that we can prosecute on the basis of the strength of the evidence,” he added. His commendation follows an investigative report by JoyNews into the allegations, which have sparked public concern over student safety and the management of schools. The Minister’s remarks come as authorities face calls to investigate the allegations and ensure accountability in the handling of the case. Watch the full documentary below.

title: EU Moves to Strengthen Frontex With 30,000 Border Officers and Faster Deportations
body: The European Commission proposes a major expansion of Frontex, including a 30,000-strong border force, a rapid reaction unit and a stronger role in returning migrants who have no legal right to remain in the EU. The European Commission has proposed a major overhaul of the European Union’s border protection system, seeking to strengthen Frontex, accelerate the return of migrants without legal permission to stay and improve the bloc’s ability to respond to migration emergencies. Announced in Brussels on October 27, the proposals would expand Frontex’s operational capabilities, introduce a new European Border and Return Reserve and establish a rapid reaction force capable of deploying to external EU borders at short notice. The Commission said illegal border crossings have fallen by more than half over the past two years, while the EU’s return rate has risen to more than 30 per cent. However, it warned that a changing geopolitical and security environment continues to place pressure on Europe’s external borders, requiring a stronger and more coordinated response. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said the EU must have the resources to protect its borders and determine who can enter the bloc. “Europe will always stand up for the protection of its borders,” von der Leyen said. “Europe decides who comes to our Union and under what circumstances.” She said the proposed changes would enable Frontex to provide greater assistance to member states, including in returning people who do not have the right to remain in the EU. Frontex to expand to 30,000 officers A central element of the proposal is a gradual expansion of Frontex’s standing corps to 30,000 officers. The plan includes the creation of a new European Border and Return Reserve comprising 17,000 officers who would remain available for deployment to support member states when required. The additional reserve would complement the agency’s existing personnel and staff seconded by EU member states. The Commission also wants to strengthen Frontex’s access to modern equipment and technology. Under the proposed changes, the agency could acquire, lease and jointly own equipment, as well as coordinate or participate in joint procurement with member states. This could include digital systems and artificial intelligence tools designed to improve border surveillance, information sharing and operational coordination. The aim is to give European countries access to capabilities that individual states may struggle to develop or maintain independently. Frontex to take a greater role in migrant returns The proposals would significantly expand Frontex’s involvement in returning people who do not have the legal right to remain in the EU. A new Return Coordination Centre would collect and analyse operational information, help coordinate return operations and improve cooperation between member states. Frontex’s support would cover the entire return process, from identifying individuals and providing information about voluntary return options to coordinating removals and assisting with reintegration. The agency would also be permitted to provide technical and operational assistance to non-EU countries carrying out returns. Under the proposal, Frontex could help organise and conduct return operations from one non-EU country to another, provided an agreement had been concluded with the countries concerned. The Commission said these activities would have to comply with fundamental rights and international standards. Magnus Brunner, the EU Commissioner for Internal Affairs and Migration, said the agency should become the bloc’s central actor on returns. He also highlighted the need for Frontex to respond more quickly to emerging security threats and migration emergencies. Rapid reaction force proposed for border emergencies The Commission wants to establish a Quick Reaction Force that could be deployed to the EU’s external borders at very short notice. The force would assist member states facing emergencies or sudden pressure on their borders. According to the proposal, Frontex’s executive director could decide to deploy the force following a request from a member state confronting an emergency. The Commission said the new arrangements were informed in part by lessons from this year’s crisis in Ceuta, the Spanish territory on the North African coast. The proposal also includes a dedicated Online Monitoring and Response Centre to help identify potential threats before they escalate. The centre would have an explicit mandate to monitor publicly accessible social media content for developments relevant to external border management. It would also support action against illegal online content linked to border security risks. Member states would face stronger information-sharing obligations during emergencies, including a requirement to report events with potentially significant consequences for EU borders within 24 hours through the EUROSUR information network. The Commission said these measures would allow authorities to identify emerging threats earlier and coordinate their response more effectively. EU proposes digital system to accelerate returns Alongside the Frontex reforms, the Commission has proposed a separate regulation to digitalise procedures covering returns, readmission and reintegration. The initiative follows the entry into force of the EU’s new Return Regulation on October 16. The proposed digital system would simplify administrative procedures, improve information sharing and establish a common digital interface for managing return cases across the bloc. The Commission said the changes would reduce administrative workloads, accelerate decision-making and improve the collection and exchange of information between national authorities. The digital framework would also support Frontex’s expanded role in coordinating return operations. The Commission said the system would need to comply with EU data protection requirements and fundamental rights safeguards. EU seeks stronger border control amid security concerns Frontex, formally known as the European Border and Coast Guard Agency, has supported EU member states and Schengen-associated countries in managing external borders since 2005. Its responsibilities include assisting with border surveillance, combating cross-border crime, supporting returns and contributing to search and rescue operations. The agency’s mandate was expanded under regulations introduced in 2019, amid growing concerns over migration pressures and security threats. The Commission said the agency’s role has continued to evolve in response to Russia’s war against Ukraine, the COVID-19 pandemic and attempts to use migration as a geopolitical pressure tactic at the EU’s external borders. Henna Virkkunen, the Commission’s Executive Vice-President for Tech Sovereignty, Security and Democracy, said closer cooperation and investment in new capabilities were essential to responding to changing threats. The Commission maintains that effective border management and an efficient return policy are essential to protecting the Schengen area, which allows passport-free travel between participating European countries. It also stressed that border protection and return operations must respect human dignity and fundamental rights. European Parliament and Council to consider proposals The proposals will now be considered by the European Parliament and the Council of the European Union, which must agree on the legislation before it can become law. The Commission said it would support negotiations to advance both the revised Frontex framework and the proposed digital return system. If adopted, the changes would give Frontex a more prominent operational role in European border protection, crisis response and the coordination of migrant returns. Source: European Commission, October 27, 2026. title: IDF imposes West Bank closures, reinforces troops to prevent Election Day violence
body: The IDF began imposing special closures and roadblocks across the West Bank on Monday night to reduce tensions and prevent violence during Tuesday's Election Day, as security forces brace for potential terrorist attacks and incidents of settler violence.Troops stationed along the security barrier have been reinforced amid concerns over potential terrorist attacks, while additional security forces will be deployed to hiking sites throughout the West Bank.Brig. Gen. Kobi Heller, commander of the IDF's Judea and Samaria Division, has been overseeing operations in several locations over the past 24 hours as part of preparations for Election Day.The first measure involves imposing "breathing closures" and temporary roadblocks that allow controlled movement around cities, towns, and villages identified as potential flashpoints for violence.The IDF expects many Israelis to visit hiking sites in the area during the Election Day public holiday. As a result, additional troops will be deployed to secure hiking areas where visits have been coordinated in advance.These measures are being implemented alongside operations led by the Paratroopers Brigade headquarters, under the command of Col. Roi Zweig, to combat nationalist crime in the Shiloh Valley, within the Binyamin Regional Brigade's area of responsibility.However, overnight, security forces were unable to prevent incidents of settler violence in the Binyamin region, including the torching of Palestinian vehicles.IDF working to prevent terror attack on Election DayMeanwhile, troops from the Judea and Samaria Division launched arrest operations in the Qalqilya, Jenin and Nablus districts to increase pressure on the ground amid fears of terrorist attacks. Security forces also conducted field interrogations and warned individuals accused of incitement.A security official told Walla on Tuesday morning that IDF engineering forces were preparing to demolish illegal structures, terrorists' homes and monuments as part of efforts to combat incitement to terrorism and prevent potential copycat attacks.The IDF also decided on Monday night to reinforce troops along the security barrier amid concerns that terrorists could infiltrate Israel.Heller also emphasized the importance of strengthening coordination among security agencies on Election Day, including the Israel Police, the Israel Border Police in the West Bank and the Shin Bet (Israel Security Agency).The increased coordination is intended to ensure a rapid operational response to any incidents that may arise.

title: Turkish man who Azerbaijan declared ‘undesirable’ briefly detained in Istanbul
body: A Turkish religious activist barred from entering Azerbaijan has been detained by Istanbul police over social media posts before being released amid growing tensions between Baku and Ankara. Muhammed Emin Yıldırım, the Istanbul representative of the İslamist media outlet Köklü Değişim Medya, is among 31 Turkish citizens declared undesirable by Azerbaijan. His detention has drawn criticism from religious groups in Turkey, while Islamist politician Fatih Erbakan has accused Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan of yielding to Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev. The developments come amid a dispute over hijab restrictions in Azerbaijani schools and criticism of Baku by Turkish religious figures. Yıldırım, the Istanbul representative of the Turkish media outlet Köklü Değişim Medya, was detained by Istanbul police over social media posts, before being released later that night. Köklü Değişim Medya announced the detention on X on Monday, saying that the case was being followed with the involvement of Yıldırım’s lawyer. Yıldırım was released on Tuesday, according to a subsequent statement from the outlet. In a statement following his release, Yıldırım thanked activists, journalists, and other individuals and organisations for their attention to his detention. ‘The hijab is a commandment of Allah. We will never leave our Azerbaijani sisters who value it alone’, he said, adding that he would continue to defend Muslims and stand with the oppressed against those he described as oppressors. Yıldırım also criticised those who he said prioritised political and commercial interests over responding to injustice and sought to silence people speaking out against it. His detention comes amid heightened tensions between Azerbaijan and Turkey over restrictions on the wearing of hijabs in Azerbaijani schools and Ankara-based religious figures’ criticism of the Azerbaijani government. Explainer | Why are schoolchildren protesting a hijab ban in Azerbaijan? The protests against the hijab ban in schools appear to be some of the largest public demonstrations in years. OC Media Rafig Shahbazov The removal of Oktay Saral from his position as an adviser to Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, which came before Yıldırım’s detention, has drawn criticism in Turkey, particularly from religious groups. Many social media users have also described the developments as a political defeat for Erdoğan. Fatih Erbakan, leader of the Islamist New Welfare Party (Yeniden Refah Partisi), criticised Erdoğan in a post on X, questioning his response to Aliyev. ‘Is this what it means for our president, who says “the world is bigger than five” and is seen as a world leader, to bow down to Ilham Aliyev?’ Erbakan wrote, referring to Erdoğan’s regular invocation of the five permanent members of the UN Security Council. ‘Yet when Aliyev makes a phone call, everything stops. It does not matter whether it concerns the headscarf, human rights, or freedom of belief. The picture that emerges is that Aliyev speaks and we immediately comply. Do you have the right to make the nation experience this shame?’ Erbakan added. Azerbaijan issues arrest warrants for 7 Turkish nationals, including journalists Baku hasn’t provided evidence for its claims that the individuals called for the state to be violently overthrown. OC Media Rafig Shahbazov Earlier, members of Köklü Değişim had held a protest outside Azerbaijan’s Consulate General in Istanbul against restrictions on the wearing of hijabs in Azerbaijani schools. Azerbaijan has also placed seven Turkish citizens on international wanted lists, in a separate move amid increased tensions between Baku and Ankara. Since Tuesday morning, claims have circulated on social media that members of Köklü Değişim in Turkey have been detained or summoned to police stations to give statements. There has been no official confirmation.

title: Russia Says Three Tankers With Diesel En Route to US
body:
Three tankers carrying Russian diesel are en route to the United States, with a fourth expected to depart Wednesday, Moscow said, part of a deal that triggered a fierce Ukrainian and European backlash.
US President Donald Trump this month struck an agreement with Russia’s President Vladimir Putin to ease sanctions in exchange for Moscow releasing diesel onto global markets.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The measure was seen as an attempt to lower fuel prices for American consumers ahead of the US midterm legislative elections on November 3, and drew sharp criticism from Ukraine and its allies.
“At present, three tankers” with Russian fuel are on their way to the United States, Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak told reporters on Tuesday. A fourth was expected to set off on Wednesday, he added.
The first US-bound tanker with Russian diesel departed last week.
According to data from the maritime tracking firm Kpler, it loaded nearly 300,000 barrels of diesel at the Primorsk terminal and was headed to New York.
Relations between Kyiv and Washington have soured since the US-Russia diesel deal, with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky calling it a “weak decision”.

title: Boeing Moves Second MQ-25A Stingray Airframe to Illinois for Final Assembly
body: The airframe is being trucked from Boeing’s St. Louis facility to MidAmerica St. Louis Airport in Mascoutah, Illinois, for final assembly ahead of ground testing. Boeing Defense and Space released a video on Oct. 26, 2026, showing the second MQ-25A Stingray unmanned refueler being rolled out of its facility in St. Louis, Missouri. The company said it is being moved from St. Louis to MidAmerica Airport in Mascoutah, Illinois, “where it will undergo final assembly before beginning ground testing.” The unmanned aircraft, with its wings folded and fuselage covered in white protective wrapping, is first towed by a tug and then transported on a flatbed truck. The airframe will travel approximately 25 miles (40 km) from St. Louis to Mascoutah. The aircraft shown in the video does not appear to have the three nose-mounted air-data probes visible on the first MQ-25A test aircraft, and the Cobham Aerial Refueling Store (ARS) is also absent. These are among the components that will be installed once the aircraft reaches its destination. At Mascoutah, the new MQ-25A will join the first airframe, Bureau Number (BuNo.) 170662, which has been conducting test flights from MidAmerica St. Louis Airport. On Oct. 19, the Navy announced that that airframe was controlled for the first time through a MD-5C Ground Control Station (GCS) aboard the Nimitz-class carrier USS Ronald Reagan (CVN 76). Stingray is making moves. The second MQ-25A moved from St. Louis to MidAmerica Airport @BLVairport, where it will undergo final assembly before beginning ground testing. https://t.co/JdvIvOiFT3 — Boeing Defense (@BoeingDefense) October 26, 2026 The Navy announced on Sept. 30, 2026 , that installation and integration of the UAWC aboard USS Ronald Reagan (CVN 76), which houses the MD-5C GCS, had been completed in August. The first UAWC was installed aboard USS George H.W. Bush (CVN 77) in 2024. The carrier-control demonstration marks a step toward integrating the MQ-25A into carrier operations, although the program’s broader schedule has slipped and it is unsure if the service will go ahead with the planned carrier integration by 2026 . On Sept. 14, 2026, the Navy awarded Boeing a $562 million contract for Lot 1 of the MQ-25A’s Low-Rate Initial Production (LRIP), whose deliveries are expected to begin in 2029. The award funds three aircraft and advance procurement of long-lead components for three more under Lot 2, bringing the total number of MQ-25As under contract to 14. Stingray’s recent test controlled from a carrier The MQ-25A is primarily intended to take over the aerial-refueling role currently performed by F/A-18E/F Super Hornets, allowing more of the crewed aircraft to focus on strike missions. The MQ-25, instead of being controlled by a human pilot on board, will be controlled through the MD-5C GCS by personnel aboard the aircraft carrier. An MQ-25A freshly painted in U.S. Navy livery shown on the ramp in Illinois. | Source: Boeing/Kelsey Chadwick The MD-5C GCS is also intended to provide Command and Control (C2) for the Navy’s future unmanned carrier aircraft. These potentially include Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA) , as the service aspires to add even more unmanned aircraft into its fleet. During the Oct. 19 demonstration, USS Ronald Reagan’s shipboard MD-5C GCS established a beyond-line-of-sight command-and-control link with the MQ-25A while the carrier was underway in the Pacific. The aircraft itself remained on the ground at MidAmerica St. Louis Airport in Mascoutah, Illinois. Boeing explained the aircraft used a Skyhook antenna to connect to the SpaceX satellite constellation. The Navy initially only described the connection as operating over a proliferated low Earth orbit (pLEO) satellite network, without explicitly naming SpaceX. Boeing said command-and-control protocols were routed to the shipboard MD-5C GCS through the Navy’s command, control, communications, computers and intelligence (C4I) network, using spaceborne and terrestrial networks. Navy Air Vehicle Pilots (AVP) aboard the carrier then took control of the aircraft for a series of operational checks before handing control back to the MidAmerica team. @PAEAviation @flynavy https://t.co/7BhchRh6yr — Acting Secretary of the Navy Hung Cao (@SECNAV) October 19, 2026 The trial validated an end-to-end BLOS command-and-control capability. The “sustained BLOS link, enabled a safe handoff and hand back between ground and ship teams, and demonstrated command latency and link integrity consistent with operational requirements,” Boeing added. MD-5C GCS On Sept. 30, the Navy announced that installation and integration of the UAWC aboard USS Ronald Reagan had been completed in August. The work involved 11 ship modifications, all completed concurrently during a single 17-month period rather than through the Navy’s typical multiyear, phased approach. The MD-5C GCS brings together the Navy’s C4I network, Lockheed Martin’s MDCX mission-planning and execution hardware and software, and additional government-produced equipment. The Navy says it has developed shore-based, at-sea, and expeditionary variants of the MD-5 control system to support operations in different environments. “This is a testament to the dedication, technical expertise, and synergy of our joint government and industry teams,” said Capt. Daniel Fucito, Unmanned Carrier Aviation Program Office PMA-268 program manager. “With each new install and milestone, we are closing the gap for our warfighters to give them the capability, capacity, and lethality they need to win the fight.” The USS Ronald Reagan (CVN 76)’s new Unmanned Air Warfare Center houses the Navy’s MD-5C Ground Control Stations that will command and control the MQ-25A Stingray unmanned aerial refueler and future unmanned carrier aircraft. | Source: U.S. Navy

title: Witkoff angrily demanded that Budanov stop strikes on Russian oil refineries — newspaper
body:
PARIS, October 27. /TASS/. US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff reportedly demanded, with apparent irritation, that Kirill Budanov, head of Vladimir Zelensky’s office [listed by Russia as a terrorist and extremist], halt strikes on Russian oil refineries during a meeting with a Ukrainian delegation in Miami, Florida, Le Monde reported this, citing a source.
"Accept this diesel fuel deal and stop shelling Russian oil refineries, you are putting the world at risk!" the newspaper quoted Witkoff as saying.
According to the newspaper, the discussion led to a confrontation between Witkoff and Budanov. Budanov had difficulty controlling his anger, Le Monde wrote.
Another source said the meeting had taken a wrong turn from the outset, as Witkoff and US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner began discussing the postwar world order, pledging to restore Russian gas and oil pipelines to Europe. The diesel deal between the United States and Russia, announced later, dealt an even heavier blow to the Ukrainian delegation, the newspaper reported. "I have never seen them so distressed and concerned," the source said.
Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump held a phone call on October 9, during which they discussed, among other things, petroleum product supplies. The Russian president said that Moscow had reiterated its readiness to supply oil and petroleum products to the United States and global markets.

title: Record carbon dioxide levels will impact us for centuries, says UN weather agency
body:
Levels of carbon dioxide (CO2) and other major greenhouse gases in the atmosphere caused by burning fossil fuels reached record highs in 2025, locking in more long-term global warming, the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) said on Tuesday.
The agency’s latest Greenhouse Gas Bulletin indicates an average global concentration of CO 2 at 426.8 parts per million (ppm) last year, or 153 per cent of the 1750 pre-industrial baseline.
“Every additional part per million matters because it traps additional heat. In effect, we are supercharging the ocean and the atmosphere. That means that heat waves, tropical cyclones, and rainstorms are intensifying faster than our historical baselines prepared us for,” WMO Deputy Secretary-General Ko Barrett told journalists in Geneva.
Equally worrying, levels of methane and nitrous oxide – the second and third most important long-lived greenhouse gases caused by human activities – also hit a new peak in 2025. “Another year, another new record. Greenhouse gases are trapping an unprecedented amount of heat in the atmosphere, providing energy for more extreme weather and associated risks to our economies and societies,” Ms. Barrett stressed.
“The past 11 years have been the warmest on record and this trend is set to continue. CO 2 has a very long lifetime and so will affect the global climate not just for years but for decades and even centuries.”
When the Bulletin was first published in 2004, the annual average level of CO 2 measured by WMO’s Global Atmosphere Watch network of monitoring stations was 377.5 ppm, compared with nearly 427 ppm today.
Growth rates of CO 2 have tripled since the 1960s, accelerating from an annual average increase of 0.8 ppm per year to 2.4 ppm per year in the decade from 2011 to 2020.
The “exceptional [3.5 ppm] surge” of 2023-2024 coincided with a strong El Niño “which reduced the efficiency of the biosphere through more drought, drier vegetation and more wildfires”, said WMO senior scientific officer Oksana Tarasova. She noted that although the 2.8 ppm annual increase from 2024-2025 represented a more modest increase, it was nonetheless “a substantial addition of carbon to the atmosphere from fossil fuel burning. We can expect to see a further increase in concentrations in 2026 because of fossil fuel burning and the development of a powerful El Niño which will impact land carbon sinks as it did in 2023-2024.”
The agency’s Bulletin reports on the amount of gas that accumulates in the atmosphere and not new annual emissions. About half of the total CO 2 emitted each year remains in the atmosphere and the rest is absorbed by Earth’s land ecosystems and oceans.
The U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Annual Greenhouse Gas Index shows that from 1990 to 2025, the warming effect on our climate caused by greenhouse gases increased by 56 per cent, with CO 2 accounting for about 81 per cent of this increase, known as “radiative forcing”.
WMO noted that as countries transform their energy systems towards decarbonization, careful attention should be given to two potent but less abundant trace gases closely related to electricity production and distribution: molecular hydrogen (H 2 ) and sulphur hexafluoride (SF 6 ). Widely used as a spark suppressant in electricity distribution, SF 6 use has risen steadily in the past three decades in line with increased global electrification. “It has an atmospheric lifetime of over 1,000 years and has the highest 100-year global warming potential of approximately 24,300 times that of CO 2 . The increase of SF 6 in 2025 was a record high,” the agency’s report notes. Hydrogen concentration has increased by 5.3 per cent between 2010 and 2024. Hydrogen is being used as an energy storage medium for hard-to-decarbonize sectors such as steelmaking, shipping, and long-duration energy storage, as well as for renewable sources and as an energy source for transport.
“Its leakage into the atmosphere from production facilities, pipelines, storage tanks, and fuel cells poses a growing concern,” WMO said, highlighting that although hydrogen is not a greenhouse gas, “it influences atmospheric chemistry” and has a strong indirect effect on warming, the agency explained. “Both H 2 leakage and SF 6 persistence represent potential threats that could undermine the climate benefits of the energy transition,” WMO said. “Careful monitoring of the composition of Earth’s atmosphere is essential to detect, understand and prevent unintended consequences of these changes.” .
WMO releases the Bulletin to provide authoritative scientific data for negotiators attending the annual UN Climate conference. The aim of the Conference of the Parties meeting (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, from 9 to 20 November is to turn climate commitments into concrete action.

title: Google Gemini Omni: What It Actually Does, What It Costs, and How It Compares
body:
Gemini Omni is a member of Google's Gemini generative model family, built specifically to create output from any combination of input types, starting with video.
Someone generates a short AI video; it's almost right, except the jacket should be yellow instead of red. With most video generation tools, fixing that means writing a new prompt and hoping the rest of the shot survives the regeneration intact — the lighting, the framing, the way the character moved. That specific frustration, having to redo a whole scene to fix one detail, is the actual problem Google built Gemini Omni to solve, and it's worth understanding the real product before deciding whether it delivers on that promise.
This is a straight look at what Gemini Omni is, when it actually shipped, what it can genuinely do, what it costs in real numbers, and where it holds up against the competition and where it doesn't.
Gemini Omni is the newest member of Google's Gemini generative model family, and per Google's own announcement , it's built specifically to create output from any combination of input types, starting with video. You can feed it images, audio, video, and text together, and it generates a video grounded in Gemini's broader reasoning rather than routing the request to a separate, disconnected media model bolted on the side.
It's worth being precise about where this sits next to Google's other generative tools, since the names get confused easily. Nano Banana handles image generation and editing. Veo handles one-shot video generation from a prompt. Omni's actual differentiator isn't that it generates better-looking video than either of those — it's that it lets you keep editing a video through natural conversation, turn after turn, while the model holds onto what you established earlier: the characters, the physics, the scene itself. That's a genuinely different product category than "type a prompt, get a clip."
Google announced Gemini Omni at Google I/O 2026 on May 19, 2026 , in a post authored by Koray Kavukcuoglu, CTO of Google DeepMind and Chief AI Architect at Google. The first model in the family, Gemini Omni Flash, rolled out the same day to consumers through the Gemini app and Google Flow for subscribers on the Google AI Plus, Pro, and Ultra tiers, and at no cost through YouTube Shorts and the YouTube Create app.
Developer access came later. The Gemini API opened access to the model on June 30, 2026, still explicitly tagged as a preview release, under the model ID gemini-omni-flash-preview . The model reached general availability on August 27, 2026, as Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash , and that general availability release wasn't just a version-number bump — it bundled real feature upgrades: scene extension that now analyzes the last ten seconds of a clip for continuity instead of just the final second, extensions stackable up to a total of 40 seconds, a cheaper 360p draft mode for fast iteration, and improved style and character reference handling from uploaded clips. Anyone citing a single "Gemini Omni release date" is collapsing three genuinely distinct milestones into one, and the difference matters if you're trying to understand what was actually available when.
Native multimodality means the model processes text, image, audio, and video together as input, rather than handling each modality through a separate specialized path, which is what gives it more cohesive, consistent output than stitching several single-purpose tools together would produce.
Conversational editing is the headline feature: every follow-up instruction builds on the last one, tracked through an interaction ID rather than requiring you to re-upload or re-describe the video each time, and characters, physics, and scene continuity are meant to hold across that whole editing session. World-knowledge grounding is Google's term for the model combining an intuitive sense of physics — gravity, fluid dynamics, momentum — with Gemini's broader knowledge of history, science, and cultural context, which is what lets it produce something closer to meaningful storytelling than pure photorealistic pattern-matching.
On the generation side specifically, it supports straightforward text-to-video, image-to-video (turning a still photograph, sketch, or product shot into motion), and first-and-last-frame interpolation, where you supply a starting image and an ending image and the model animates a smooth transition between them. It also supports subject and style reference, letting you upload images or short video clips of a specific character, object, or visual style and have the model weave those into a new generated scene. And as of the August general availability release, video extension can add up to 40 seconds total onto an existing clip — generated by the model or uploaded — in successive 10-second increments.
It's worth naming the actual model identifiers rather than speaking vaguely about "the Omni model," since Google itself uses several names across its own documentation. The current, generally available model on the Gemini API is gemini-omni-1.1-flash . The original preview identifier, gemini-omni-flash-preview , still appears in Google Cloud's own model card for the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, where it's explicitly labelled a Generative AI Preview offering with its own separate terms.
On that enterprise platform specifically, the model card lists a 131,072-token maximum input and a roughly 57,920-token maximum output — real technical ceilings worth knowing if you're planning a production integration rather than experimenting casually.
Here's what's worth being honest about rather than guessing at: Google hasn't published a technical paper detailing Omni's exact underlying architecture, the way it has for some other model releases. What's confirmed is that it sits within the Gemini 3.x-era model family by both timing and Google's own positioning, sitting in Google's model documentation alongside Gemini 3.5 through 3.8 Flash variants. Beyond that, claims about its precise internal design would be speculation, and this article isn't going to pretend otherwise.
There are three genuinely separate on-ramps here, serving different audiences, and it's worth being clear about which one actually fits your situation rather than defaulting to whichever is easiest to find.
For everyday use, the Gemini app and Google Flow are the two consumer paths, both included in a Google AI Plus, Pro, or Ultra subscription , alongside a completely free path through YouTube Shorts and the YouTube Create app — no subscription required for that specific route.
For developers, an API key from Google AI Studio and a short script against the Interactions API is the fastest path to testing it directly:
client.interactions.create is the core call, and the model string is the one line that matters most to get right, since gemini-omni-1.1-flash is the current general availability identifier, while some existing tutorials and cached documentation still reference the older gemini-omni-flash-preview string from the June preview window. The response comes back as raw video bytes accessible through interaction.output_video.data , written directly to a file here, though for anything beyond a quick test, Google's documentation recommends URI-based delivery instead of inline bytes, to avoid hitting payload size limits on larger outputs.
For enterprise teams already operating inside Google Cloud's governance and billing structure, the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform — the successor branding for what was Vertex AI — is the intended path, offering the same model behind Google Cloud's existing access control and monitoring tooling.
Here's the actual rate card rather than a vague "it's affordable" claim. On the Gemini API's paid tier, input is billed at \$1.50 per million tokens, text and thinking output at \$9 per million tokens, and video output at \$17.50 per million tokens. Video is billed by a fixed conversion rate of 5,792 tokens per second of 720p output, which works out to roughly \$0.10 per second — a figure Google states directly on its own pricing documentation.
Worked out concretely, a 10-second 720p clip costs approximately \$1.01 in video output alone, before adding whatever small amount the input prompt and any reference images contribute at the much lower input rate. Unlike most other models in the Gemini lineup, Omni currently has no free tier on the API, so the very first test call a developer makes bills to their account, not a rate-limited trial allowance. The practical cost lever worth knowing is the 360p draft mode introduced in the August general availability update — meaningfully cheaper per second than 720p, and useful for iterating on a prompt before committing to a full-resolution render of the version you actually want to keep.
On the strengths side, Gemini Omni 1.1 Flash reached the top of LMArena's community-voted text-to-video leaderboard as of late August 2026 , and placed second on the image-to-video leaderboard, based on real, independently gathered preference data rather than a Google-selected benchmark. Its conversational, stateful editing is also a genuine structural advantage over one-shot generators like OpenAI's Sora or Runway's tools, where changing a single detail typically means writing an entirely new prompt and regenerating from nothing, hoping the parts you liked survive by chance rather than by design.
On the honest counterweight side, Omni's per-second price is effectively identical to Google's own Veo 3.1 Fast at the same \$0.10-per-second headline rate, so it isn't winning on cost at all — it's winning specifically on the editing workflow. A team that only needs a single, clean, one-shot generation with no follow-up revisions genuinely won't see much practical advantage choosing Omni over Veo or a similarly priced competitor, since the price is the same and the differentiator that Omni is actually built around — iterative conversational editing — simply isn't the thing they need.
The fair verdict here isn't about whether Gemini Omni generates impressive-looking video — several tools already do that convincingly. Its real contribution is making the editing process feel like an actual conversation instead of a fresh guess every single time, holding onto a scene's characters, physics, and continuity across turns in a way one-shot generators structurally can't.
Whether that's worth its price and its current gaps — the regional restrictions, the missing voice editing — depends entirely on whether iterative editing is genuinely the bottleneck in your actual workflow, not on which demo reel happened to look more impressive on a given day.
Shittu Olumide is a software engineer and technical writer passionate about leveraging cutting-edge technologies to craft compelling narratives, with a keen eye for detail and a knack for simplifying complex concepts. You can also find Shittu on Twitter .

title: Craft Prospect kicks off PERSEUS project to advance optical communications for space
body:
Craft Prospect is working with Fraunhofer Centre for Applied Photonics (Fraunhofer CAP) and Vector Photonics on a new project exploring the potential of next-generation laser technology for high-performance optical communications in space.
PERSEUS (PCSEL Environmental and Radiation Sensitivity: Evaluation for Use in Space) will investigate whether a promising new laser technology called Photonic-Crystal Surface-Emitting Lasers (PCSELs) is suitable for operation in space and can offer a differentiated capability for both space-to-space and space/ground networks.
The project will evaluate the technology under conditions relevant to space deployment, demonstrate its compatibility with representative spacecraft hardware, and identify the next engineering steps required to move towards a commercial solution.
The project is funded through the Advanced Connectivity Technologies (ACT) programme , delivered by Innovate UK and funded by the Department for Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) . The ACT R&D Programme was announced by Minister Ian Murray during his speech at Connected Britain on 9 September 2026.
PCSEL technology offers the potential to address some of the limitations of existing optical and RF communications systems in space, supporting the move towards longer-range, higher-capacity, and more secure free-space optical links between ground stations, satellites, and potentially deeper-space assets.
By bridging the gap between component and space system, PERSEUS will chart a course from disruptive technology to differentiated on-orbit capability for the fast-growing space market.
The PERSEUS programme will subject PCSELs to a range of test campaigns expected of space qualified technologies, as well as carrying out long-range, high-bandwidth free-space demonstrations to showcase early performance.
PCSEL devices will undergo characterisation and testing, including radiation, vibration, and thermal-vacuum campaigns , to better our understanding of how the technology fares in the launch and space environments.
Furthermore, the project will demonstrate early integration success with other flight-representative hardware for end-to-end data transmission, and develop mission concepts that harness the unique capabilities of PCSELs.
The findings will feed into a future communications system design concept and help define the engineering roadmap required to progress PCSEL technology towards a differentiated space communications solution.
At Craft Prospect, Head of Engineering Kevin Quillien is serving as Project Lead, supported by Chief Engineer Paul Yarr and Systems Engineers Lauryn Atkinson and Kairavi Pandit .
At Fraunhofer CAP , Dr Gerald Bonner is subcontract lead, while at Vector Photonics Dr Richard Taylor serves as subcontract lead and Dr Graham Goldberg as Project Manager.
The project also builds on Craft Prospect’s growing quantum-optical communications capability , including our work on OPS-SAT VOLT , where we are developing and testing space-to-ground free-space quantum and optical communications technologies as part of our wider mission to deliver Smart Secure Space .
Kevin Quillien , Project Lead and Head of Engineering Craft Prospect, said of the project:
‘PERSEUS is an exciting opportunity to take a promising new photonics technology and understand the potential it has to offer the space industry.
‘By carrying out all the necessary early-stage work to test and characterise PCSELs for space, we will build a strong understanding of the potential that the technology offers in building the next generation of communication solutions. We’re looking forward to working with Fraunhofer CAP and Vector Photonics to explore where this roadmap will take us.’
About Craft Prospect Craft Prospect is a Glasgow-based space engineering company advancing its vision of Smart Secure Space through onboard intelligence, quantum technologies, and satellite subsystem innovation. Learn more here .
