title: Kenya: 20 Ebola contacts released from quarantine
body:
Twenty people associated with Kenya’s first case of Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease have been reunited with their families after being released from quarantine following completion of a mandatory 21-day monitoring period.
They were discharged on Monday, according to the UN World Health Organization ( WHO ), which has been assisting the Kenyan authorities with Ebola preparedness since the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) declared an outbreak on 15 May.
Another 98 contacts remain in quarantine .
The people who are now back at home remained asymptomatic during quarantine and underwent standard protocols, including a final health assessment, counselling on post-discharge precautions and follow-up where required before being released.
“ We ask communities to welcome them home warmly ,” said Dr Patrick Amoth, Kenya’s director general for health. “Having completed 21 days without symptoms, they pose no risk of infection to anyone.”
The WHO representative to Kenya, Dr Neema Rusibamayila Kimambo, echoed his message.
“ People who complete quarantine have helped protect their families, their communities and the whole country ,” she said.
Kenya confirmed its first Ebola case on 6 October – a Kenyan man who had been working in the DRC, where the caseload is approaching the 10,000 mark.
He flew back to Kenya via Uganda on 3 October and died in a Nairobi hospital two days later.
The Ministry of Health conducted robust contact tracing of anyone who may have been exposed, including family members, airline passengers and crew, airport workers and medical personnel. By 22 October, all contacts were traced – both in Kenya and abroad – and placed in quarantine.
As of Monday, eight contacts had developed symptoms and were confirmed positive for Ebola disease through laboratory testing. They were immediately transferred to the Ebola treatment centre in Nairobi.
In total, Kenya has reported nine confirmed Ebola cases and two deaths. All are part of one connected group and there is no evidence that the virus has spread to the community.
“ WHO commends the Ministry of Health, the Kenya National Public Health Institute, national and county health teams for their work in responding quickly to every new case ,” said Dr. Kimambo.
The UN agency continues to support Kenya in all aspects of Ebola response, including coordination, disease surveillance, contact tracing, laboratory testing, case management, infection prevention and control, health screening at points of entry, risk communication and community engagement.
Although there is no licensed vaccine or specific treatment for Bundibugyo virus disease, WHO stressed that early detection and supportive care improve chances of recovery.
Meanwhile, “a crucial clinical trial” was launched in the DRC on Friday to determine if vaccines can provide protection against the disease, said WHO’s Dr. Meg Doherty, speaking from the eastern city of Bunia to journalists in Geneva.
The TUMAINI trial platform is designed so that several vaccine candidates can be evaluated within one research framework using a strategy called the ring vaccination approach involving contacts of people with a confirmed case of Ebola.
“Tumaini actually means ‘hope’ in Swahili, and is giving us some hope,” said Dr. Doherty, director of WHO’s Department of Science for Health.
The first vaccine under evaluation is Ervebo which has been effective against Ebola caused by the Zaire virus. It is not yet known if it will have any protective effect against the Bundibugyo strain.
Dr. Doherty attended the launch, where four people were vaccinated.
“It was moving to see this trial begin, just as it has been deeply sad to see the effect of this outbreak on communities,” she said.
“I lived and worked in DRC nearly 40 years ago, and it is quite heartbreaking to see this beautiful country challenged by outbreaks on top of humanitarian crises.”
Last week, WHO convened technical advisory groups that evaluated the evidence on two vaccines designed specifically against Bundibugyo virus: ChAdOx1, developed by the University of Oxford with the Serum Institute of India, and mRNA-1469 developed by the American company Moderna.
Recommendations will be published this week.
“In the meantime, rings are being set up, with people who have a family member sick with Ebola, or who have been exposed to the virus another way,” she said, noting that two rings are currently in place and several more are being prepared.
“Community members are already walking into the site asking to be enrolled, highlighting the intense need for an efficacious vaccine,” she added.
Dr. Doherty explained that a decade ago, WHO and partners used the ring vaccination approach in Guinea during the West African Ebola outbreak to help establish the efficacy of the Ervebo vaccine.
“Today, scientists are building on that experience to seek answers about the Bundibugyo virus,” she said.
The trial is led by the Congolese authorities and is integrated into the ongoing response to the outbreak. It is being managed by the National Public Health and Biomedical Research Institute, known by the French acronym IRNRB.
“We do not yet know for certain when results will begin to emerge. We expect it will take several months,” she said.
“But already, having this trial in place is an important step towards gathering scientific data that will help policy makers reach decisions on vaccine use, and we anticipate, to protect people in this outbreak and future outbreaks.”
Dr Doherty noted that several other vaccines are under development, “and as they go through their initial studies, if they look promising, they too could be brought into this vaccine platform trial.”
The UN’s Ebola coordinator and the head of the World Health Organization (WHO) have deplored the killing of a nurse working to halt the spread of the disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

title: Tinubu Transmits Transfer Of Convicted Offenders Amendment Bill To Senate
body: President Bola Tinubu has transmitted the Transfer of Convicted Offenders Enactment and Enforcement Amendment Bill 2026 to the Senate for consideration. In a letter read during plenary today, the President explained that the proposed legislation seeks to amend the existing law to facilitate the transfer of convicted offenders between Nigeria and other countries under international agreements. The bill also seeks to empower the President, through an order published in the Federal Gazette, to extend the application of the law to countries with which Nigeria has entered into such agreements, including non-Commonwealth nations. President Tinubu urged the Senate to give the proposal expeditious consideration. The bill has been referred to the Senate Committee on Rules and Business for further legislative action. The post Tinubu Transmits Transfer Of Convicted Offenders Amendment Bill To Senate appeared first on Channels Television .

title: FC AshantiGold CEO calls for separate Black Stars team for home-based players
body: FC AshantiGold CEO, Edward Akuoko, has backed the inclusion of locally-based players in the Black Stars urging Ghana to develop a pool of home-based talents capable of stepping in whenever key players of the national team are unavailable. Mr. Akuoko believes Ghana must establish a deliberate system to identify, develop and integrate players from the domestic league into the senior national team to ensure continuity and consistency. Speaking to Luv FM, he said: “We can have a local Black Stars team, and then we can have the foreign base as well, and then we can always blend them so that whenever the foreign ones are not available, the local ones can step in. “I think that history has it that we’ve done this before and it worked for Ghana. A time came when we had a local Black stars that was playing so well to the point that there were times that even the local black stars were even playing much better than even the foreign ones.” According to him, building a reliable pool of locally based players would provide the Black Stars with quality alternatives whenever first-choice players are unavailable due to injuries, suspension other circumstances. “One thing is that when you use the local black stars, first of all, you are able to build cohesion because they are always available at your best and core. “These foreign players sometimes, through no fault of theirs, are not consistent. And we all know that football, to a large extent, is about consistency. I mean, when players are able to play together, train together. “The the the cohesion comes and they’re able to play well. And so if we’re having challenges, I think that it’s not a bad idea,” he added.

title: Putin discussed Ukrainian crisis settlement with Finland’s Stubb, Norway’s Store — Kremlin
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. The settlement of the Ukrainian conflict was the main topic of Russian President Vladimir Putin’s telephone conversation with Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store, the Kremlin’s press office said in a statement on Tuesday.
"The sides exchanged views on the resolution of the Ukrainian crisis," the statement said.
The statement added that results of Putin’s talks with US Special Presidential Envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg on October 21 as well as Stubb and Store’s contacts with Witkoff and Ukraine’s Vladimir Zelensky in Oslo were taken into account.

title: Tinubu asks Senate to approve $20.5bn, €1.04bn foreign loans
body: President Bola Tinubu has asked the Senate to approve $20.51bn and €1.45bn in external borrowing to address funding gaps in the Federal Government’s 2026–2027 supplementary borrowing plan. The President’s request was conveyed in a letter which Senate President Godswill Akpabio read during plenary on Tuesday. According to the letter, the requested funds—specifically $20,517,755,901 and €1,045,083,643—are earmarked to address Nigeria’s persistent infrastructure deficit and bridge critical funding gaps across vital socio-economic sectors. The primary targets for investment include power, transportation, healthcare, education, agriculture, water supply, security, job creation, and financial management reforms. “I submit the attached Federal Government 2026–2027 Supplementary External Borrowing Plan for consideration and early approval of the National Assembly to ensure prompt implementation of our projects,” President Tinubu wrote. He emphasized that the projects selected underwent technical and economic evaluations to maximize their impact on poverty reduction, skill acquisition, entrepreneurship, and national food security. “In light of the need for significant infrastructure investment in the country and the vast financial resources needed to address this gap, it has become essential to pursue prudent external borrowings to close the financing shortfall,” the President added. Following the reading of the letter during plenary, Akpabio noted that elements of the borrowing framework had previously appeared in broader government borrowing blueprints. Akpabio formally referred the request to the Senate Committee on Local and Foreign Debts—led by Senator Haruna Manu—for detailed legislative review, with expected collaboration from the Committees on Appropriations and Finance. “The borrowing plan is attached, but of course, this was even earlier approved in our budget, and also the external borrowing plan was approved as far back as 2025 to 2027,” Akpabio stated. “However, this request will be looked at by the Committee on Local and Foreign Debts… to clarify the scope before further action.” The Senate committee’s upcoming review is expected to determine the exact timeline for disbursements and evaluate how the supplementary request aligns with Nigeria’s existing debt management framework.

title: Court Grants $100m Mareva Order in Chappal Energies Dispute, Bars Asset Takeover
body: Wale Igbintade The Federal High Court in Lagos has issued three interim orders restraining R28 Limited and its Founder, Adebisi Adebutu, from taking over the operational assets of two companies, dealing with financial assets worth up to $100 million and effecting changes to their corporate records. Justice Ambrose Lewis-Allagoa, in an order issued on October 22, 2026, restrained the two respondents from seizing or interfering with the operational premises, management, physical assets, and commercial equipment of Chappal Energies Offshore Limited and Project Odinmin Investments Limited. The Judge also granted a Mareva order restricting dealings with financial assets up to $100 million or its equivalent in other currencies, while directing the Corporate Affairs Commission (CAC) to preserve the companies’ corporate records and reject specified changes to their directorship, shareholding and signatory authority. The orders were made pending the hearing and determination of the applicants’ motion on notice for interlocutory injunction. The suit, marked FHC/LAG/FR/500/2026, was filed on October 14, 2026, by Ufoma Joseph Immanuel, Chappal Energies Offshore Limited and Project Odinmin Investments Limited. The respondents are R28 Limited, Adebutu, Michael Humphries, the CAC, Zenith Bank Plc, Fidelity Bank Plc, Access Bank Plc, and Rand Merchant Bank. Under the Mareva order, R28 Limited and Adebutu, whether acting personally or through their agents, privies, representatives, nominees or other persons acting on their instructions, are restrained from transferring, withdrawing, removing, dissipating, assigning, encumbering or otherwise dealing with funds and other financial assets covered by the order. The restriction applies to monies, deposits and financial assets standing to the credit of accounts maintained in their personal or corporate names, including accounts operated through proxies or shell entities with Zenith Bank, Fidelity Bank, Access Bank or any other commercial bank, financial institution or electronic platform in Nigeria. The financial restraint is capped at $100 million or its equivalent in other currencies. The order does not, however, establish that the sum has been recovered, confiscated or identified in any particular account. It is an interim restriction intended to preserve assets pending further proceedings. On the companies’ operations, Justice Lewis-Allagoa restrained the first and second respondents from entering upon, seizing, taking over or interfering with the operational premises, management, physical assets and commercial equipment of Chappal Energies Offshore Limited and Project Odinmin Investments Limited in Nigeria. The judge also directed the CAC, the fourth respondent, to maintain the status quo in the corporate registers of the two companies and refuse to register changes to their directorship, shareholding or signatory authority submitted by R28 Limited or Adebutu, particularly changes relating to Michael Humphries, the third respondent. The order followed an ex parte application supported by an affidavit sworn to by Immanuel. The court made the orders after considering the application and hearing submissions from the applicants’ counsel, comprising K. Braithwaite, Wogu Christian, Olaoluwakitan Braithwaite and Hilda Nwankwo. In their application, the claimants sought to prevent interference with the companies’ operations and assets, preserve the financial assets covered by the Mareva order and forestall changes to their corporate records pending the determination of their motion for interlocutory injunction. The latest order is one of a series of legal disputes reportedly involving Immanuel, the founder and managing director of Chappal Energies, and Adebutu over a commercial disagreement centred on control and the allotment of shares in the company, which Immanuel founded in 2022. Justice Lewis-Allagoa adjourned the matter till December 4, 2026, for further proceedings.

title: Nigeria Doesn’t Need Tourist President, Adeyeye Tells Atiku
body: Adedayo Akinwale and Hassan Amina in Abuja The Chairman, Board of Directors of the Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA), Senator Dayo Adeyeye, has declared that Nigeria does not need a tourist president who runs to Dubai whenever there is a crisis. Adeyeye stated this while addressing a press conference yesterday in Abuja, describing the Presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Atiku Abubakar as a “jumper” who had defected to six political parties in 19 years. He said Atiku could not fix the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) that made him vice president for eight years, asking how would he fix Nigeria of 230 million people? Adeyeye stated: “My brothers, a man who cannot build a political party cannot build Nigeria of 230 million. PDP to AC to PDP to APC to PDP to ADC. Six parties in 19 years. Small crisis, he runs to Dubai. If he cannot stay to fix PDP that made him vice president, how will he stay to fix Nigeria? “When Obasanjo wanted to crush him, where did he run to? Bourdillon —to Tinubu. Tinubu gave him AC (Action Congress). Gave him a platform. A man who ran to Tinubu for refuge now wants to challenge Tinubu? Asiwaju is his master in politics and nation building.” Adeyeye noted that Atiku lives in Dubai, and only comes when election season comes, contests, loses, and runs back, adding that that is not residence, that is tourism and Nigeria does not need a tourist President. He emphasised that Atiku’s only economic plan is to sell, stressing that as Chairman of the National Council on Privatisation, he sold NITEL, NICON, Ajaokuta steel rolling. Adeyeye added: “He lives in Dubai, comes only when election comes, loses, runs back. His only plan is to sell. As privatization chairman, he sold NITEL, NICON, Ajaokuta – all died. Now he wants to sell NNPC and our new ports. “Tinubu built AD (Alliance for Democracy), built ACN (Action Congress of Nigeria), built APC (All Progressives Congress). Built Lagos from N600 million to N51 billion Internally Generated Revenue (IGR). Built a party, built a city, now building a nation. “Atiku only jumps. Defect, contest, lose, run away. Nigerians must choose: Builder or Jumper? Stayer or Tourist? A President who pays you while alive, or one who lets you die waiting? “Tinubu has done the painful surgery. Let us allow him to complete the healing.” Adeyeye revealed that President Bola Tinubu approved the sum of N758 billion to clear pension liabilities dating back to 2007, with 957,045 pensioners paid. He added that the president reintroduced 100 per cent gratuity under the Exit Benefit Scheme for federal workers in January, ending a 20-year period when retirees went home without gratuity. He added that the administration also cleared the $3.4 billion International Monetary Fund (IMF) loan inherited on assumption of office, with the IMF confirming zero principal as of April 30, 2025. The chairman noted that the administration has commenced repayment of the N22.7 trillion Ways and Means securitised to 40 years, with N613 billion paid as of June this year. He stated: “President Tinubu approved N758 billion to clear pension liabilities dating back to 2007, with 957,045 pensioners paid. “No president has ever done what Tinubu did. In one decision, he approved N758 billion to clear pension debts from 2007.” On debt management, Adeyeye said the administration cleared the $3.4 billion IMF loan inherited on assumption of office, with the IMF confirming zero principal as of April 30, 2025, and had commenced repayment of the N22.7 trillion Ways and Means securitised to 40 years, with N613 billion paid as of June this year. He said removal of fuel subsidy and foreign exchange reforms led to a surge in Federation Account Allocation Committee (FAAC) disbursements from N14.11 trillion in 2024 to N26.5 trillion in 2025, and N33.27 trillion between January and November 2025 alone. Adeyeye cited World Bank data showing GDP growth rising from 3.5 percent in first half of 2024 to 4.2 percent in first half of 2026, inflation declining from 27.6 percent in January 2025 to 15.2 percent in December 2025, and foreign reserves growing from $33 billion in 2023 to $53.8 billion. On governance reforms, he said Tinubu approached the Supreme Court to secure financial autonomy for 774 local governments in a judgment delivered July 11, 2024, and initiated the State Police constitutional amendment, which he said has been approved by 24 of 36 states.

title: Finland, Norway Push Putin for Peace
body:
Russian President Vladimir Putin told Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre on Tuesday, Oct. 27, that President Volodymyr Zelensky should come to Moscow for direct talks, reiterating an earlier invitation that Kyiv rejected as it sought to meet on a neutral ground.
Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov told Russian state broadcaster Vesti that Stubb and Støre had passed on Zelensky’s wish to speak with Putin directly, to which he responded by repeating Moscow’s long-standing offer.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“Our boss repeated that if Zelensky really wants to hold direct negotiations, let him come to Moscow, where he will be provided with all conditions, including in terms of security,” Ushakov said, adding that the meeting between the two leaders would be most meaningful once the negotiating process is complete.
“Some documents will be worked out, namely in the context of a long-term settlement in Ukraine, and after that the leaders of the two countries could meet. The negotiators would be ready to present the documents to them, and the leaders in turn would be ready to sign them,” Ushakov continued.
In early June, Zelensky addressed Putin publicly and directly, in a rare open letter . He proposed ending the war through a face-to-face meeting at a bilateral summit hosted by a neutral country, backed by broader security guarantees from Europe and the United States.
The Kremlin dismissed the proposal at the time, repeating Zelensky could come to Moscow if he wanted to meet.
Stubb and Støre called Putin from Helsinki earlier on Tuesday, urging an end to Russia’s war against Ukraine and the resumption of negotiations.
According to Finland’s presidential office, the two leaders initiated the call in consultation with Ukraine, following their Oct. 20 meeting in Oslo. The conversation was linked to upcoming talks in Abu Dhabi.
Stubb and Støre reaffirmed that their countries would maintain support for Ukraine.
“The discussion was frank and substantive,” Stubb said. “Ending the war requires direct discussions.”
The Finnish president stressed that the war’s outcome would directly affect both neighboring countries and European security.
Støre highlighted the conflict’s human and material costs, warning that its consequences would extend across generations and emphasizing the need for de-escalation.
The leaders spoke for their respective countries rather than Europe as a whole, the official statement said.
The Kremlin, in its own readout of the call provided by Russian state-owned media TASS , confirmed that the discussion was held at the request of the Finnish and Norwegian leaders.
The statement suggests Moscow remains engaged in the US-brokered process ahead of the trilateral talks planned for November with Ukraine, while simultaneously welcoming the agreement to hold negotiations on Ukraine in Abu Dhabi.
Putin reiterated Moscow’s position, giving his assessment of the situation in the conflict zone, while pointing to what the Kremlin calls the war’s “root cause.” According to the Russian president, a just and lasting peace in Ukraine was possible only if Russia’s interests were taken into account.
In his view, NATO and EU countries were pursuing a confrontational policy that was essentially only prolonging the conflict.
According to the readout, Putin had also informed the two leaders of the ongoing humanitarian operation in Russian-occupied Oleshky, in the Kherson region. However, no further details were provided.
Security in the Baltic Sea region and Northern Europe was also on the agenda, the Kremlin confirmed, affirming the importance of international maritime law and freedom of navigation.
All three leaders agreed to keep in direct contact by telephone, going forward.
Zelensky confirmed that he was briefed in great detail following the leaders’ call, noting that Stubb and Støre “made it clear to the Russian leader that real de-escalatory steps are needed.”
As both Finland and Norway border Russia, they have a particular interest in reliable security arrangements, he argued, noting that various formats for engagement with other partners in Europe were on the agenda as well.
“There must be peace, de-escalation is needed,” Zelensky concluded.
Stubb and Støre met Zelensky and US envoy Steve Witkoff in Oslo a week earlier, before Witkoff traveled to St. Petersburg for talks with Putin.
Following that meeting, the Kremlin said Russia was prepared to resume US-mediated negotiations with Ukraine in November .
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Ghanaian twins plead guilty in US$9m international romance scam
body: Two Ghanaian twin brothers have pleaded guilty in the United States to conspiracy to commit wire fraud in an international romance scam that caused victims to lose more than US$9 million. Jamal Abubakari and Kamal Abubakari, both 22, entered their guilty pleas on October 13, 2026. They allegedly operated under the aliases Arrangement and Lancaster, respectively. Their co-conspirator, 53-year-old American woman Amanda Joy Opoku-Boachie, also known as Amanda Joy Glum and Amanda Joy Kessei Bierman, pleaded guilty to the same offence on October 20. According to the US Department of Justice, the three were involved in a criminal network that targeted older Americans through dating websites and social media between July 2024 and April 2026. The group allegedly created false identities to build close relationships with victims, presenting some of the interactions as romantic relationships. They then used fabricated stories to persuade the victims to transfer money into accounts controlled by members of the network, with some of the proceeds sent to accomplices in Ghana and elsewhere. The scheme affected victims in 25 US states, as well as Germany and Austria. Some of those affected in northern Ohio were residents of Edgerton in Williams County. The total financial losses exceeded US$9 million. As part of their plea agreements, the three defendants have agreed to forfeit jewellery seized during their arrests, including luxury watches, rings, chains, medallions and earrings. The investigation was led by the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s Cleveland Division, with support from the US Department of Justice’s Office of International Affairs and law enforcement agencies in Ghana and the United States. Ghanaian agencies involved included the Attorney-General’s Office, the Economic and Organised Crime Office (EOCO), the Ghana Police Service, the Cyber Security Authority, the Narcotics Control Commission, the Financial Intelligence Centre, the Ghana Immigration Service and the National Intelligence Bureau. Each defendant faces a maximum prison sentence of 20 years. A federal district court judge will determine the final sentences after considering the US Sentencing Guidelines and other relevant legal factors.

title: Romanian president: Russian role in sabotage unacceptable
body:
Romanian President Nicusor Dan condemned any involvement of the Russian Federation in acts of sabotage on Romania's territory, calling such actions unacceptable and an element of a systematic hybrid war against Europe, he said on X on Tuesday.
Dan said he strongly condemns any Russian involvement in sabotage in Romania. He said such actions are unacceptable and amount to a serious violation of the country's sovereignty and security, and that no foreign entity has the right to act this way in Romania or other European states.
The head of state stressed that state bodies will act decisively to protect citizens and critical infrastructure after the exposure of a sabotage network linked to an attempted arson at the Carfil defense plant in Brasov on September 14.
He said Russia has used a wide range of tools for years to weaken European democracies, including attempts to influence elections, disinformation campaigns, information warfare, cyberattacks and sabotage, all of which are part of the hybrid war Russia is waging against Europe. In recent weeks, Russia has moved to a new level of provocations against civilian shipping in the Black Sea, he said.
Dan stressed that all of these events are not isolated incidents unrelated to each other but part of a pre-planned and coordinated campaign aimed at sowing discord in European societies and undermining European states' commitment to their own security and collective defense.
He said Romania will act decisively to prevent such incidents, identify those involved and protect citizens and the country's critical infrastructure, while continuing to cooperate closely with its NATO allies and its partners in the European Union.
Dan also noted that the investigations into the sabotage against Carfil again show how often hostile forces use social media to lure people in order to manipulate them and sometimes draw them into illegal acts.
Romanian intelligence exposed a network of saboteurs who, according to the investigation, were coordinated from Russia. They are linked to the attempted arson at the Carfil defense plant in Brasov on September 14.

title: Zelensky talks to Stubb and Støre after their call with Putin
body:
The head of state said this in a Telegram post , according to Ukrinform.
“Spoke with President of Finland Alexander Stubb and Prime Minister of Norway Jonas Gahr Støre following their call today with the Russian leader and as a continuation of our discussions in Oslo with representatives of America, Europe, and NATO. I am grateful for the detailed briefing and for their active support for our diplomacy and the peace efforts we are pursuing together with all our partners,” he wrote.
According to Zelensky, Stubb and Støre clearly told Putin that real de-escalatory steps are needed regarding Ukraine’s energy and infrastructure.
The President also said the conversation covered preparations for a trilateral meeting scheduled for November at the team level, involving Ukrainian, American and Russian teams.
“Finland and Norway, as countries that border Russia, have a particular interest in sound and reliable security arrangements,” he noted.
The head of state said the sides also discussed various formats of cooperation with European partners that could be useful for further supporting diplomacy, Ukraine’s defense and collective security.
“There must be peace, de-escalation is needed, and Russia must stop dragging out the war. I thank everyone who stands with Ukraine!” he added.
As reported, on October 27, Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre held a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

title: Niger miners’ deaths: Committee recommends N1.4bn compensation, dismissal of personnel
body: By Omeiza Ajayi & Enitan Abdultawab The independent ministerial committee investigating the recent deaths of 33 persons in the custody of the Nigerian Security and Civil Defence Corps NSCDC in Minna, Niger State, has recommended compensation amounting to N1.4 billion to families of the victims. In the Executive Summary by the chairman of the Committee, Jonathan Kure, on Tuesday in Abuja when he presented the report to the Minister of Interior, Hon. Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, the committee, which said the deaths were “entirely preventable”, also recommended summary dismissal of personnel whose actions directly caused the deaths of the suspects. It partly reads, “The committee recommends a restitution of the NSCDCD in order to carry out their reforms. The NDSCD also recommends a restitutive package, a compensation of 30m for each of the 33 bereaved families and 10m to each of the 41 survivors, representing a total compensation package of 1.4 billion naira.” “Additional measures include educational support for dependents of deceased victims, medical rehabilitation of survivors, psychological support for affected families, and a formal apology by the federal government.” It recommended administrative sanctions for personnel who failed in their duties but whose actions or inactions were not directly responsible for the deaths. It added that “fatalities resulted from environmental asphyxia caused by oroloneged confinement in a severely overcrowded cell aggravated by heat stress and dehydration.” According to the committee, the operation which led to the arrest of the suspects was without an “operational order” or approval from the national headquarters of the NSCDC. The post Niger miners’ deaths: Committee recommends N1.4bn compensation, dismissal of personnel appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: At least two drones intercepted over Baghdad's Green Zone
body: At least two drones were intercepted near the heavily fortified Green Zone in the Iraqi capital Baghdad on Tuesday, causing a loud bang, security officials said. “The sound heard in Baghdad resulted from the handling of a drone in the vicinity of the Green Zone,” said Maj Gen Saad Maan, the head of the government's Security Media Cell. Another security official confirmed a second one was also shot down. The US embassy's air defence systems were activated after detecting the two drones approaching the perimeter of the Green Zone, he said. Videos on social media showed debris from the two drones in two ​locations. Security forces ⁠were carrying out investigations into their ​origin ‌and targets. No damage or casualties were reported. The heavily fortified Green Zone in central Baghdad houses government buildings, parliament and foreign embassies, including the US Embassy, and is frequently targeted by drones and rockets. Since the outbreak of the Iran war on February 28, the Green Zone has come under repeated attacks. Iran-backed militias grouped under the Islamic Resistance in Iraq launched near-daily drone and rocket strikes on US interests, with the US Embassy — a sprawling complex inside the fortified zone — as their primary target. In one attack, rockets and at least five drones were launched at the embassy in waves, with C-RAM air defences intercepting two drones while a third struck inside the compound, causing a fire and smoke to rise. The Al Rasheed Hotel inside the Green Zone, which also houses diplomatic missions, was also hit. The attacks were framed by the armed factions as solidarity with Iran and as retaliation for US strikes that killed militia commanders. The drone interception comes as Iraq transitions to a post-US-led anti-ISIS coalition. Under a 2024 agreement between Baghdad and Washington, the coalition ended its mission on September 30, with the departure of the last US troops with their equipment. The withdrawal ended the 12-year Operation Inherent Resolve mission that began in 2014 after ISIS seized a third of Iraq. The Pentagon said about 2,500 US personnel had been in Iraq in recent years, down from 170,000 at the height of the 2007 surge. The Combined Joint Task Force is now headquartered in Jordan and continues operations against ISIS in Syria. Baghdad has hailed the withdrawal as an "important milestone" and the start of a new phase based on sovereignty, while Iran-aligned groups claimed it as a victory. However, the exit has also removed a key layer of air defence — including C-RAM and Patriot systems that had protected the Green Zone — raising concerns, particularly in the Kurdish region, about gaps as militia drone attacks continue and ISIS cells remain active.

title: Court ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‌‌‍​⁠​​‌‌​adjourns El-Rufai’s N1bn rights suit against ICPC, AGF, IGP for judgment
body: The Federal High Court in Abuja on Tuesday fixed Dec. 2 for judgment in an N1 billion fundamental rights suit filed by former Gov. Nasir El-Rufai of Kaduna State against the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC). Justice Joyce Abdulmalik fixed the date after lawyers and the parties adopted their processes in the case. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that other respondents in the suit are the Inspector-General (I-G) of Police and the Attorney-General of the Federation (AGF) as the 2nd and 3rd respondents, respectively. When the case was called on Tuesday, El-Rufai’s lawyer was not in court. Justice Abdulmalik then made an order deeming all the processes filed by the former governor adopted. Abdul Mohammed, SAN, who appeared for the ICPC, identified and adopted all their processes, urging the court to dismiss the suit in its entirety. The I-G’s lawyer, ACP Ezekiel Rimamsomte, and Mrs Maimuna Lami-Shiru, Director of Civil Litigation and Public Law, who represented the AGF, equally adopted their separate processes and prayed the court to dismiss the suit. While the proceeding was ongoing, Mr Ubong Akpan, the ex-governor’s counsel, entered the courtroom and apologised for his lateness. When the lawyer sought the permission of the court to allow him to adopt his court’s documents, he was informed by the judge that his processes had already been deemed adopted. Justice Abdulmalik consequently adjourned the matter until Dec. 2 for judgment. NAN reports that the ex-governor had, earlier in the suit, sued the ICPC, the Chief Magistrate at the Magistrate’s Court of the FCT, Abuja; I-G and the AGF as 1st to 4th respondents, respectively. He, however, dropped the name of the magistrate from the case following his inability to specify the name of the magistrate who was sued as the 2nd respondent after the judge made the observation. El-Rufai is, therefore, demanding a N1 billion in damages against ICPC, the I-G and the AGF. The former governor, in the originating motion on notice marked FHC/ABJ/CS/345/2026, dated and filed Feb. 20 by Oluwole Iyamu, SAN, sought seven reliefs. He prayed the court to declare that the invasion and search of his residence at House 12, Mambilla Street, Aso Drive, Abuja, on Feb. 19 at about 2pm by the ICPC and I-G amounts to a gross violation of the applicant’s fundamental rights. He said that it was a violation of the dignity of the human person, personal liberty, fair hearing, and privacy under Sections 34, 35, 36, and 37 of the Constitution.” He urged the court to declare that “any evidence obtained pursuant to the aforesaid invalid warrant and unlawful search is inadmissible in any proceedings against the applicant, as it was procured in breach of constitutional safeguards.” El-Rufai, therefore, sought an order of injunction restraining the respondents and their agents from further relying on, using, or tendering any evidence or items seized during the unlawful search in any investigation, prosecution, or proceedings involving him. He sought an order directing the 1st and 3rd respondents (ICPC and I-G) to forthwith return all items seized from the applicant’s premises during the unlawful search, together with a detailed inventory thereof. He also sought an order awarding the sum of N1,000,000,000.00 (one billion naira) as general, exemplary, and aggravated damages, among others. Responding, in its counter-affidavit, the ICPC said it received a petition against El-Rufai, and acting on the petition, it commenced an investigation, leading to the search at his residence. It argued that its operatives acted under a valid search warrant issued on Feb. 18 and executed on Feb. 19 between 1:37pm and 3:56pm at 12 Mambilla Street, Asokoro, Abuja. The commission said its officials were accompanied by personnel of the Nigeria Police Force and that the exercise was witnessed by El-Rufai’s wife, Hadiza El-Rufai, and his son, Mohammed El-Rufai. The ICPC, which urged the court to dismiss the suit, listed the items allegedly recovered from the residence. The I-G, also in his counter affidavit deposed to by Insp Ewa Anthony, argued that he had the statutory power to detect, arrest, investigate and prosecute offenders. He argued that the search carried out at El-Rufai’s residence was executed pursuant to a search warrant issued by a competent court of law. He disagreed with the ex-governor that the search warrant was invalid, insisting that it was a genuine court order. The police boss said that his officers who carried out the operation complied with all applicable legal procedures in the execution of the search warrant. According to him, the applicant is trying to use the honourable court to shield him away from the security investigation and prosecution in the court of law. He, therefore, prayed the court to dismiss the suit in its entirety. The AGF, in his counter affidavit filed by Lami-Shiru, denied being privy to the facts of the alleged matter. He argued that the ICPC and I-G acted within their statutory functions. According to him, the items seized from the applicant (El-Rufai) by the 1st and 2nd respondents were seized to enable them to conclude an investigation on the applicant. He submitted that the suit was an abuse of court processes because the former governor had two pending suits on the same subject matter before the FCT High Court. The AGF, who argued that El-Rufai’s suit lacked merit, as there is no legal and evidential justification to support all the claims and reliefs sought by him, prayed the court to dismiss it in its entirety. (NAN) The post Court ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‌‌‍​⁠​​‌‌​adjourns El-Rufai’s N1bn rights suit against ICPC, AGF, IGP for judgment appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: GECF countries account for about 40% of global gas exports — Putin
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Member countries of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) account for approximately 40% of global gas exports, Russian President Vladimir Putin stated at the GECF summit.
The Russian leader highlighted that the GECF’s core characteristics - openness, clarity, and objective assessments - are highly significant for both gas producers and consumers, as well as for the global energy sector as a whole.
"Especially considering that, collectively, the Forum’s members hold 70% of the world’s natural gas reserves and account for about 40% of global gas exports," Putin emphasized.
This means that GECF member countries make a significant contribution to ensuring global energy security and the balanced development of states and macro-regions, Putin noted. "This primarily concerns new centers of economic growth in Asia, Africa, and Latin America, where energy consumption is rising, cities are rapidly expanding, industrial facilities are being built, and electricity is increasingly being used in industry, transport, and the digital economy - including in data storage and processing centers," the president explained.

title: Will Trump Nominate Orbán as UN Secretary-General?
body:
According to a report in the Wall Street Journal, the Trump administration is pushing former Hungarian prime minister Viktor Orbán as a candidate for the post of UN Secretary-General. There is speculation that Orbán could even be nominated as a joint candidate by the US, Russia and China. The reports have sparked a lively debate among commentators in Hungary.
Potiential turning point in Hungarian politics
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Orbán’s potential candidacy could have significant repercussions for Hungary, political scientist Gábor Török (Hungary) notes in his blog:
“How would it affect the position of Fidesz and the Hungarian right in general, Viktor Orbán’s role in domestic politics, the political strategy and communication of the Tisza government, the process of holding [the key figures in the Orbán system] to account, and ultimately the mindset of the electorate? It is best to wait for the reports to be confirmed before offering detailed answers, but it already seems certain today that such a decision would represent an unexpected and dramatic turning point in Hungarian politics. Even if it were not a game-changer, it could certainly usher in a new phase in the political game.”
Past comments by Viktor Orbán contradict this speculation, says foreign policy expert István Szent-Iványi (Hungary) in a Facebook post:
“Viktor Orbán has spoken with contempt of those politicians who have ended up at the UN – a group to which, if President Trump gets his way, he himself may soon belong. Let’s take a look at what he said on the matter in 2018: ‘Of course there are bureaucrats, certain politicians, who have failed at home and are then parachuted into the UN, and who would like to continue their political careers and take part in global governance, but these are aberrant personal ambitions.’ Bingo. Spot on.”

title: Hail hits Northern Emirates as Abu Dhabi issues rain alert
body: Authorities urged people to be vigilant as parts of the UAE were hit by hail and heavy rain on Tuesday afternoon - with high winds and dust expected to persist until the evening in some areas. Storm Centre, a popular online weather tracking platform, shared videos of hail and rainfall in Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah. The National Centre of Meteorology said the high winds over some northern, eastern and southern areas could reach speeds of up to 45kph, lifting dust into the skies and hampering visibility. The weather bureau said the alert would be in place until at least 9pm. It comes amid a recent bout of unsettled conditions, particularly in the Northern Emirates. Abu Dhabi Police, meanwhile, urged drivers to exercise caution during bouts of rain in a safety message posted on social media. The force said motorists should abide by variable speed limits displayed on road signs during adverse weather. The NCM's online weather map shows that heavy rain is forecast in Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah and Al Ain until Thursday. الإمارات : الان تساقط البرد على ميدق في الفجيرة #أخبار_الإمارات #مركز_العاصفة 27/10/2026 pic.twitter.com/6lPnDJGHrh — مركز العاصفة (@Storm_centre) October 27, 2026 Despite the unstable autumn conditions, temperatures will remain high across the Emirates in the days to come. The weather bureau predicts daytime temperatures will remain in the mid to high 30s in both Abu Dhabi and Dubai over the next five days and could reach 40°C in Al Ain and remote desert areas of Abu Dhabi. The UAE's average daily temperature in October stands at 29.7°C, according to the NCM's latest monthly weather summary. The mercury has risen this month, however, with the El Nino weather phenomenon playing its part in delaying the typically cooler autumnal weather.

title: Kyrgyzstan Plans to Expand Protected Natural Areas
body: Kyrgyzstan plans to expand its protected natural areas under a draft strategy for 2026–2035. The expansion would bring additional high-altitude glaciers, rocky mountain areas, and state forest lands under protection. The Ministry of Natural Resources, Ecology, and Technical Supervision released the document for public consultation on October 26. An accompanying explanatory note proposes increasing protected land from 11.8% of the country’s territory to 20% by 2030 and 30% by 2035. However, another section of the strategy sets 2030 as the deadline for reaching 30%, leaving the intended timetable unclear. Kyrgyzstan’s protected natural areas currently cover approximately 2.36 million hectares. The increase in protected land in recent years partly reflects the creation of ecological corridors linking protected areas, including the 792,000-hectare Ak Ilbirs corridor in 2025. Under the proposal, the expansion would take place without removing productive pastures from agricultural use. Traditional livestock grazing by local residents would continue to be permitted in buffer zones. The country has ten state nature reserves covering a total of 509,900 hectares and 13 national nature parks spanning 724,900 hectares. The draft strategy calls for upgrading their infrastructure, introducing digital monitoring and recordkeeping systems, and improving training and equipment for park rangers. Other priorities include combating poaching and protecting mountain wildlife, including snow leopards and Tien Shan brown bears, as well as ancient walnut forests and glaciers. Private investors would be allowed to develop tourism facilities in designated recreational zones within national parks. However, the draft would prohibit transferring protected land into private ownership and constructing permanent buildings. The authorities also propose introducing cashless payments for admission tickets to reduce unrecorded revenue. Residents of nearby communities would have opportunities to earn income through guesthouses and other small tourism businesses. The strategy’s authors acknowledge the risk of ecosystem degradation from growing tourist numbers. The document specifically identifies the popular Ala-Archa, Karakol, Chon-Kemin, and Kyrgyz-Ata parks as areas of concern. It proposes limits on visitor numbers along popular routes to reduce littering and damage to vegetation. The strategy would be financed through existing government allocations, income from park visitors, and international grants, with no additional budget spending required, according to its authors. Kyrgyzstan’s nature reserves and national parks received more than 271,000 visitors in 2025, an increase of nearly 24% from the previous year. Revenue from park visits more than doubled to $431,000.

title: Putin attends plenary session of Gas Exporting Countries Forum summit
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Russian President Vladimir Putin is speaking at the plenary session of the eighth summit of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF).
The plenary session is chaired by the head of the Russian state. GECF Secretary General Philip Mshelbila and the heads of delegations of the participating states of the international organization are also scheduled to speak. Some representatives of the observer countries are also expected to speak: Azerbaijan, Angola, Iraq, Malaysia, Mozambique and Senegal.
The session will end with the adoption of the Moscow Declaration of the eighth Summit of Heads of State and Government of the GECF member countries.
Putin is also scheduled to have five bilateral meetings today on the sidelines of the summit - with Iran President Masoud Pezeshkian, Emir of Qatar Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, President of the Republic of Mozambique Daniel Chapo, leader of Equatorial Guinea Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo and Chairman of the Presidential Council of Libya Mohamed al-Menfi.

title: EU-Funded Study Finds Progress, Challenges in Kazakhstan’s Housing Support System
body: The Astana Times provides news and information from Kazakhstan and around the world. ASTANA – A study of housing support in Kazakhstan has found that some recipients experienced greater housing stability and lower living expenses, while others faced challenges with information, registration and housing maintenance, according to findings presented at a conference in Astana on Oct. 23. Photo credit: egov.kz According to the European Union (EU) Delegation to Kazakhstan, the qualitative study was conducted under the European Union-funded Shanyraq project, which focuses on strengthening communities and promoting access to adequate housing. Juana Mera Cabello, deputy head of partnerships at the EU Delegation to Kazakhstan, said access to housing was closely linked to dignity, opportunity and social inclusion. photo credit: EU delegation in Kazakhstan The research drew on 99 interviews, 10 focus groups across 10 cities, inspections at 83 addresses and an analysis of relevant regulations. The findings reflect participants’ experiences and are not statistically representative of all housing-support recipients. Some participants reported fewer forced relocations and less dependence on private landlords. Others said lower regular housing expenses left them with more money for food, health care and education. The findings were presented at the conference, which brought together representatives of the EU Delegation to Kazakhstan, the Ministry of Industry and Construction, Otbasy Bank, the construction sector and civil society organizations. Juana Mera Cabello, deputy head of partnerships at the EU Delegation to Kazakhstan, said access to housing was closely linked to dignity, opportunity and social inclusion. “Accessible housing is a matter of dignity, opportunity and social inclusion. Through the Shanyraq project, the EU supports evidence-based dialogue and action that promote human rights and inclusive social and economic development for all,” she said. The study’s authors presented recommendations covering the housing-support process, from initial consultations to conditions after recipients move into their homes. The authors will next discuss the recommendations with government agencies, developers and experts to identify ways to improve access to housing support and address the challenges identified in the research. The post EU-Funded Study Finds Progress, Challenges in Kazakhstan’s Housing Support System appeared first on The Astana Times .

title: Arab Israelis report receiving call to vote on Election Day in name of murdered girl Sousan Sultan
body: Over 1,000,000 Arab Israeli citizens received a recorded call on Tuesday, Election Day, in which they were asked to vote in the name of an Arab girl who was murdered in 2025.The call was recorded by Sousan Sultan, whose sister, Susan, was killed in April, 2025, and whose husband, Ziad, was murdered in August 2026."My sister was murdered, and she cannot vote in the election," Sousan said in the call. title: BRICS parliamentarians call for peaceful resolution of Israeli-Palestinian conflict
body:
NEW DELHI, October 27. /TASS/. Parliamentarians from the BRICS member countries have reaffirmed their unwavering support for a peaceful resolution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, as well as the right of the Palestinian people to self-determination and the establishment of an independent, sovereign state, says a joint declaration issued following the 12th BRICS International Parliamentary Forum.
"We reaffirm our unwavering support for a peaceful resolution of the Israeli-Palestinian conflict based on the ‘two states for two peoples’ concept, in which both states coexist peacefully and securely, in accordance with international law and relevant United Nations resolutions, and we also reaffirm the right of the Palestinian people to self-determination, freedom, and the establishment of an independent, sovereign state," the document states.
The parliamentarians also express deep concern over the ongoing escalation of tensions in the Middle East and West Asia. They call for the protection of the civilian population and civilian infrastructure.
According to the document, the BRICS parliamentarians called for stepping up efforts, through dialogue and diplomacy, to achieve long-term mutual understanding that will contribute to establishing long-term peace, security, and stability in the region. They emphasized the need to work together to maintain the uninterrupted functioning of global trade, supply chains, and energy flows in accordance with international law the norms.
Russia’s parliamentary delegation led by State Duma Chairman Vyacheslav Volodin is in India, where it is participating in events at the 12th BRICS International Parliamentary Forum. This year, the forum is being held in the Indian capital, which currently holds the BRICS chairmanship. The main theme of the forum is "Fostering Parliaments for People-Centric Development."

title: Connectivity and Redundancy: Major Geoeconomic Projects in the Persian Gulf and the Middle East
body: The geopolitical dynamics in the Middle East will remain fluid, regardless of the outcome of the war in the Persian Gulf. Virtually all regional actors are working to hedge their bets – in terms of security policy, but also through economic adjustments. The focus is on new, secure transport routes to and from the Arab Gulf states. This is not merely about oil or gas, but the overall security of supply chains through multimodal links and connectivity corridors: for energy supplies, other raw materials, goods, data and people. Not every plan will be implemented, but those that are will reshape the geoeconomic landscape and change the region’s geopolitical map. The process could boost regional integration and will impact Europe’s cooperation with the countries in the region.

title: Brazilian Funk’s Kazakh Side Hustle
body: Orpheus took music somewhere it had no business going. Luís Guilherme, known as DJ Guilherme, created a beat that has managed something less fatal but almost as improbable. A Brazilian funk track born in São Paulo has found an unlikely second home in Kazakhstan, where local creators have embraced it as part of their digital culture. BEAT UnderCover – Taqap Taqap (Slowed Reverb) , produced by DJ Guilherme and remixed by Rand0m, was released through Clima Funk in June 2025. It grew out of Só Socadinha , a baile funk single first released in January 2019. The scale of its reception in Central Asia is striking. As of October 8, data from Chartex linked the track to approximately 16.45 million video views across 112 posts in Kazakhstan, and 586,000 views across 13 posts in Uzbekistan. In Uzbekistan, the beat also found its way into football fandom, providing the soundtrack to videos celebrating Abdukodir Khusanov , the Tashkent-born Manchester City defender who became the first Uzbek international to play in the Premier League. The Times of Central Asia spoke to DJ Guilherme about the track’s unexpected success in Central Asia and how it has changed his understanding of where music can find an audience. TCA: When did you first realize something unusual was happening in Kazakhstan? Guilherme: The first clue actually came from a video in Turkey. After that, I noticed growth in my statistics and started receiving notifications from Apple Music for Artists about chart activity in Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan. I began checking the charts and videos every day. Seeing the music appear in different videos and then in the charts made me realize that something bigger was happening. TCA: What stood out about how creators in Kazakhstan were using the track? Guilherme: It was how people were bringing the sound into their own everyday interests. In the videos I followed across the region, I saw edits of lowered cars, car sound systems, clubs, and football. People were using the track to give their videos energy and atmosphere. They didn’t need to know who I was to connect with the music. For someone making music independently in São Paulo, seeing those different uses so far away was a real surprise. TCA: Why do you think the recording connected so strongly with creators in Kazakhstan, and did anything about its reception surprise you? Guilherme: I think the strong kicks, repeating rhythm, and electronic elements may have helped. Those are sounds that can work well with car videos, nightlife, and football edits, even when someone doesn’t understand Portuguese. The slowed versions may also have suited the atmosphere creators wanted. What surprised me was seeing people find their own place for a Brazilian sound without any promotion being aimed at them. I’ve wondered whether its circulation in Turkey helped it reach Central Asia, but I still don’t know the exact route. I’m continuing to look into that. TCA: Before this happened, how much did you know about Kazakhstan or Central Asia as a music market? Has the response changed how you see the region? Guilherme: I knew very little about Kazakhstan or Central Asia, especially as a music market. The response made me curious, and I started watching documentaries and learning more about the region. Now I follow what’s happening there much more closely. It changed how I think about where an audience can come from, and it made me want to understand the people listening to my music, their culture, and what they enjoy. TCA: Did the track appear to reach Uzbekistan through the same kind of online activity? Guilherme: Football edits were one noticeable part of the wider circulation, especially clips involving Abdukodir Khusanov. I watch a lot of football, and I’m a fan of Khusanov too, so seeing my music in those edits was particularly fun for me. It gave me another personal connection with the story around Uzbekistan. I can’t say for certain whether the track reached Uzbekistan through exactly the same route as Kazakhstan, but cars, nightlife, and football were recurring themes in the videos I was seeing across the region. TCA: As an independent artist and label owner, has this changed how you approach new audiences? How can you build on an unexpected response without forcing it? Guilherme: It has made me pay much closer attention to where my music is traveling. As an independent artist and the owner of Clima Funk, I want to understand who is already connecting with the sound and build a relationship with them. I’ve posted a TikTok with a caption in Kazakh, and I’m still researching how this spread began and trying to connect with creators so I can reach more people in the region. Orpheus had to descend into the underworld to find what he was looking for. DJ Guilherme never went looking for Kazakhstan. Somewhere between São Paulo and the Kazakh steppe, his beat crossed half the world without a map or a destination. By the time it arrived, it had taken on a life of its own.

title: Tinubu Decries Murder Of Katsina Cleric, Sheikh Yahaya Masussuka
body: * Directs relevant security agencies to thoroughly investigate the heinous act Deji Elumoye in Abuja President Bola Tinubu has condemned the murder of a prominent Islamic preacher, Sheikh Yahaya Ibrahim Masussuka, and his friend, Adamu Abubakar, in Dutsin-Ma, Katsina State. Unknown gunmen killed the duo in a drive-by shooting incident on Monday evening. The president, who was deeply saddened by the news of the killing, in a release issued on Tuesday by his Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, described the act as heinous and an assault on the values of peace and sanctity of human life. Tinubu extended his heartfelt condolences to the families of the deceased, their followers, as well as the government and people of Katsina State, over the tragic loss. The president has directed the Nigeria Police Force and other relevant security agencies to move swiftly, intensify efforts already underway by the Katsina State Police Command, and ensure the perpetrators are tracked down, apprehended, and brought to justice. Tinubu prayed for the repose of the souls of the departed and comfort for all those who mourn their death.

title: Fourth tanker carrying diesel for export to sail tomorrow — deputy PM Novak
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. A fourth tanker carrying diesel for export is set to depart from Russia on October 28, Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak told reporters on the sidelines of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) summit.
According to Novak, three tankers carrying diesel have already departed from Russian ports.
"We expect it on the 28th," he said, responding to a question about when the fourth tanker would set sail.
On October 23, the deputy prime minister told reporters that the first three fuel tankers were already en route to global markets, including the United States, with significant support from the Russian Direct Investment Fund (RDIF). Novak noted that Rosneft could provide the bulk of diesel exports to global markets and the US.
On October 9, Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump held a phone call to discuss, among other things, the supply of petroleum products. Putin stated that Moscow had confirmed its readiness to supply oil and petroleum products to both American and global markets.
Earlier, Novak told TASS that Russia was beginning to lift its ban on diesel exports ahead of schedule. He indicated that Russia was prepared to supply 300,000 tonnes of diesel in October, 500,000 tonnes in November, and 1 million tonnes in December, with the potential to eventually increase this volume to 3 million tonnes per month.

title: EU allocates $42 million for projects supporting Georgian civil society, but no funds for government
body: The EU will allocate €38 million ($42 million) to new projects supporting people across Georgia, while continuing to withhold direct financial assistance to the Georgian government over what it describes as the country’s democratic backsliding. The decision to continue withholding direct funding to the government comes amid a deterioration in relations between Tbilisi and Brussels. The EU has consistently criticised the ruling Georgian Dream party’s authorities and efforts to adopt repressive legislation. Georgia received EU candidate status in December 2023, conditional on implementing reforms in areas including democracy, the rule of law, and fundamental rights. However, in June 2024, the EU Council concluded that the Georgian government’s actions had effectively halted the country’s EU accession process. Relations deteriorated further in November 2024, when the Georgian authorities announced that they would not pursue EU accession negotiations until 2028. The EU has also criticised democratic backsliding, restrictions on fundamental rights, and anti-EU rhetoric by Georgian officials. In response, the EU Commission suspended bilateral financial assistance directly benefiting the Georgian authorities in June 2024. More than €120 million ($130 million) in assistance was suspended, while funding for civil society and independent media continued. The EU has stressed that its decision to suspend direct assistance to the authorities did not mean it was ending its support for Georgian citizens. ‘Due to Georgia’s democratic backsliding, the European Union no longer provides funding to the Georgian authorities. However, we continue delivering assistance to the people of Georgia’, the EU in Georgia said . The projects will focus on creating economic opportunities in towns and small cities, improving skills for the labour market, supporting rural women and family farms, addressing violence against women and girls, facilitating safe migration, and strengthening climate adaptation and disaster preparedness. The EU will also continue supporting communities living in Abkhazia. The head of cooperation at the EU Delegation to Georgia, Nicholas Cendrowicz, said the new package was part of the bloc’s ‘EU with you’ approach and would be implemented through partner organisations, including agencies from EU member states and UN agencies. ‘We’ll be working with our trusted implementing partners […] so that we can get the support to the Georgian people as quickly as possible’, Cendrowicz said, adding that the projects would begin making a difference for Georgians from the beginning of next year. Cendrowicz highlighted the EU’s contribution to the East–West highway, saying that the journey between Tbilisi and Batumi had become noticeably shorter thanks to EU support. He also addressed the relationship between Georgia’s national identity and its European aspirations. ‘I know that many Georgian people would like to see more of the EU in this country, but they would also like to bring to the EU what makes this country so unique and so special’, Cendrowicz said. ‘There is really no contradiction between these two identities. In fact, people of this country already are both Georgian and European’. The EU’s partnership with Georgia dates back to 1992. Since then, the bloc has provided more than €2 billion ($2.2 billion) in assistance to the country, supporting projects in areas including agriculture, rural development, environmental protection, and transport infrastructure.

title: Company re-exporting phones to Russia is Armenia’s top taxpayer
body: Mobile Centre, an Armenian company involved in the import and re-export of phones and other electronics — mostly to Russia — has been ranked as Armenia’s top taxpayer in the first three quarters of 2026, according to a list compiled by Armenia’s State Revenue Committee (SRC) of the top 1,000 taxpayers. In 2021, according to SRC, Mobile Centre was 42nd on the top 1000 taxpayers list and paid ֏4.4 billion ($12 million). Since 2022, the company jumped up to the top of the taxpayers list, increasing its paid taxes almost 18 times by the end of 2025, ֏77.8 billion ($215 million). By the end of September 2026, the company maintained its top position, paying ֏64.3 billion ($178 million). Following Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 and subsequent Western sanctions, Russia has used former Soviet countries to circumvent the sanctions — importing goods to un-sanctioned countries, and then shipping those goods on to Russia. Telephone and other electronic communication devices dominated Armenia-Russia exports last year. Overall 2025 exports to Russia were around $2.9 billion: accounting for approximately 35% of all exports, The most valuable items were re-exported goods, such as mobile phones ($789 million), TVs ($100 in the first half of 2025), and computers. Alongside Mobile Centre, the rest of the top 10 includes Zangezur Copper-Molybdenum Combine, cigarette manufacturers — Grand Tobacco, Philip Morris Armenia and International Amasis Tabak, two banks — Arshinbank and Ameriabank, two IT companies — Soft Construct and Digitain — which are known for providing software services for the betting industry and Gazprom Armenia, which is a 100% subsidiary of the Russian state energy company Gazprom and manages the import, transport, storage, distribution and sale of natural gas in Armenia. Mobile Centre is an official distributor of smartphones from some of the world's leading manufacturers, including Xiaomi, Apple, and Samsung. The company also sells computers and other electronic items. Mobile Centre is owned by Samvel Aleksanyan, a former member of parliament from the Republican Party and one of Armenia’s wealthiest entrepreneurs who is also the owner of the Yerevan City Supermarket chain. According to the Statistical Committee of Armenia, although Russian-Armenian trade shrank by around 50% to $6.7 billion between January and November 2025, Russia still accounted for 35.5% of Armenia’s total foreign trade. During the first half of 2025, Armenia exported mobile phones worth $332 million and TV sets worth $100 million to Russia. The previous long-standing leader of the top ten taxpayers list was the Zangezur Copper and Molybdenum Combine, which claims to have employed over 4,600 workers in 2025.

title: Spirit Defense to Manufacture Airframes for General Atomics FQ-42 Vengeance Drone
body:
General Atomics Aeronautical Systems, Inc. (GA-ASI) has partnered with Spirit Defense, a Boeing company, to manufacture airframes for its FQ-42 Vengeance Collaborative Combat Aircraft (CCA).
Spirit Defense will serve as a fuselage design-build partner, contributing engineering and advanced manufacturing capabilities from design through production.
GA-ASI secured a U.S. Air Force production contract for the FQ-42 in June. The partnership adds manufacturing capacity, strengthens production resilience and reduces the risk of relying on a single production source.
Founded in 1992, GA-ASI has traditionally manufactured its uncrewed aircraft systems in-house. GA-ASI President David R. Alexander said the partnership would support the Air Force’s planned CCA production expansion.
The FQ-42 is a purpose-built uncrewed fighter developed with the U.S.A.F. as part of its investment in next-generation semi-autonomous combat aircraft. Its modular design is intended to enable rapid integration of mission systems and autonomy software. GA-ASI says its software architecture has been demonstrated in live flight tests across multiple airframes and is designed to support human-machine teaming in complex combat scenarios.
GA-ASI is also discussing international opportunities for its Gambit Series, a family of modular uncrewed combat jets derived from work on the FQ-42, XQ-67A Off-Board Sensing Station and MQ-20 Avenger.
The aircraft are designed for missions including electronic warfare, suppression of enemy air defenses (SEAD), destruction of enemy air defenses (DEAD) and stand-off precision strikes.
