title: Army recover two AK-47 rifles after gunfight in Benue
body:
Troops of Operation Whirl Stroke have recovered two AK-47 rifles and other items after repelling armed men during an operation in Guma Local Government Area of Benue State.
The troops encountered the armed group on Monday after receiving intelligence that suspected criminals posing as herders had crossed from neighbouring Nasarawa State into Guma, according to the military.
In a statement on Monday, Ahmad Zubairu, the acting media information officer of the task force, said the troops came under gunfire on arrival at the location but responded and forced the armed men to flee.
He said the troops recorded no casualties.
A subsequent search of the area led to the recovery of two AK-47 rifles, four empty magazines, eight calves, three mobile phones, a National Identification Number document belonging to Umar Yusuf and ₦20, the statement said.
The Force Commander of Operation Whirl Stroke, Moses Gara, commended the troops for their response and urged them to sustain intelligence-led operations and strengthen collaboration with local communities.
He also called on residents to report suspicious movements and activities to security agencies.
The operation came a day after Operation Whirl Stroke troops rescued two kidnap victims along Naka–Ahume Road in Benue State.
PREMIUM TIMES reported on 26 October that the troops encountered suspected kidnappers during a patrol on the road on 24 October. The suspects fled after a gunfight, abandoning their captives.
One of the rescued victims, Mngunengen Ihom, 36, sustained machete wounds and was taken to Naka General Hospital for treatment.
The two incidents highlight continuing military operations against armed groups and suspected kidnappers in Benue State.

title: Adu-Boahene case: Court adjourns motion challenging prosecution’s account of evidence to Thursday
body: The High Court in Accra has adjourned to Thursday, October 29, a motion alleging that the prosecution in the Kwabena Adu-Boahene trial misrepresented witness testimony and documentary evidence in its written submissions. The application, filed on October 19, asks the court to strike out passages in the prosecution’s response to the accused persons’ submission of no case to answer, which they contend are unsupported by the trial record. At Monday’s hearing, October 26, the judge said the case docket was at his home and that he had only become aware of the motion that morning. The Attorney-General’s Office, which was reportedly served with the application on October 19, had not filed a formal response as of Monday’s hearing. Thursday’s proceedings will take place ahead of the court’s scheduled November 5 ruling on the substantive submission of no case to answer. Kwabena Adu-Boahene, Angela Adjei Boateng and Advantage Solutions Limited filed the motion through their lawyer, Samuel Atta Akyea. They also filed a separate reply to the prosecution’s opposition to their submission of no case to answer. The two filings serve different purposes. The reply challenges the prosecution’s legal arguments for requiring the accused persons to open their defence, while the motion seeks to have specific passages removed on the grounds that they allegedly misstate the evidence presented at trial. Six areas of disputed evidence In his supporting affidavit, Adu-Boahene identifies six categories of statements in the prosecution’s submissions that the applicants say contradict or are not supported by witness testimony and documentary evidence. One concerns the prosecution’s assertion that two witnesses testified that a purchase agreement and an invoice relating to a cyber-defence system were not genuine. The applicants argue that neither witness gave the testimony attributed to them concerning the purchase agreement, admitted as Exhibit X. They note that the second prosecution witness was discharged on April 27, 2026, while the agreement was admitted through the fourth witness on June 22. On the disputed invoices, the affidavit quotes the second witness as saying: “My Lord, it is likely one will be an error.” It also cites her subsequent explanation that she could not determine which invoice contained the error. The applicants contend that these answers do not support the prosecution’s characterisation of the documents as forged or fabricated. A second complaint concerns the prosecution’s assertion that the second witness testified that the National Signals Bureau had no contract with ISC Holdings Limited for a cyber-defence system. According to the affidavit, the witness gave no such evidence and instead acknowledged processing and paying an invoice covering delivery and acceptance milestones for the system. The motion also challenges the prosecution’s interpretation of the witness’s knowledge of an operations account. The applicants say she repeatedly explained that her security clearance did not permit her to know about certain national security accounts and activities. They argue that her testimony cannot support the broader assertion that the institution itself was unaware of the company or its account. Another disputed passage describes a March 2020 invoice as covering a one-time purchase. The affidavit cites testimony in which the witness acknowledged that the amount under discussion was not the full payment and that another invoice relating to the same acquisition had been processed. The application further challenges the prosecution’s assertion that the entire GH¢49.1 million was spent on the accused persons, their friends, associates and families, with none used for an official or approved purpose. The applicants say the third prosecution witness gave no such evidence. They point instead to testimony identifying ISC International Security Consultants Holdings Limited as the beneficiary of two exhibits, with remittance information referring to the procurement of a cyber-defence system. The sixth complaint concerns the prosecution’s reliance on Exhibit H to support an assertion that payments were made from Advantage Solutions Limited’s bank account to Adu-Boahene’s mother for a building project in Kumasi. Exhibit H, a copy of which is attached to the motion, is a photograph of a building. The applicants argue that it contains no banking or accounting information establishing the alleged payments. Their affidavit also cites the fourth prosecution witness as acknowledging that there were “no direct payments from accounts analysed towards Dorchester Heights”, the building identified as the Kumasi project. Applicants allege prosecution presented unsupported claims The applicants argue that introducing facts unsupported by evidence through written submissions amounts to giving evidence from the bar. They contend that the court should remove the disputed passages because they allegedly misrepresent the evidence on record. The prosecution’s October 9 submissions, signed by Deputy Attorney-General Dr Justice Srem-Sai, maintain that sufficient evidence has been presented to establish the essential elements of the offences. The prosecution argues that its case rests substantially on documentary evidence that was not undermined by the defence’s cross-examination and has asked the court to dismiss the submission of no case to answer. Those submissions predate the motion and do not directly address its specific allegations. The prosecution’s failure to file a formal response by Monday does not, in itself, establish the applicants’ claims. The court is expected to hear the application on Thursday, ahead of its November 5 ruling on whether the accused persons have a case to answer.

title: C5+1 Statement Omits Afghanistan, Prioritizes Trans-Caspian Trade
body: The United States and the five Central Asian republics have issued a joint statement on economic and security cooperation that makes no mention of Afghanistan, once a central concern of U.S. regional policy. The document followed the October 19 C5+1 ministerial meeting in Samarkand, Uzbekistan. Afghanistan’s absence from the statement does not mean it has disappeared from negotiations or Washington’s strategic interests. Nevertheless, a comparison with earlier C5+1 documents reveals a shift in the published agenda. Where Washington once placed considerable importance on connecting Central Asia with South Asia through Afghanistan, the latest statement focuses on trade across the Caspian Sea and investment in the region’s minerals. Afghanistan’s Changing Place in C5+1 Talks In July 2021, just weeks before the Taliban retook Kabul, C5+1 participants at a conference in Tashkent explicitly supported closer trade and transport links between Central and South Asia through Afghanistan, as well as efforts to secure peace in the country. That month, the U.S., Uzbekistan, Afghanistan, and Pakistan also announced plans for a quadrilateral platform to support trade and transportation projects linking the two regions. In July 2023, Afghanistan was the subject of a separate C5+1 special session in Astana. Officials called for an inclusive Afghan government that respected women’s rights and backed further development of transport and energy links through the country. A joint statement issued by C5+1 leaders that September described Afghanistan as an important factor in Central Asian security. In the 2026 Samarkand statement, Afghanistan goes unmentioned even in the section on border security and terrorism. However, the October 2023 C5+1 connectivity statement had already highlighted the Trans-Caspian Trade Route, which connects Central Asia to Western markets, and also omitted Afghanistan. For Central Asian countries, the Afghan route remains important in practical terms. Uzbekistan is pursuing plans for a railway through Afghanistan to Pakistan, which would give it access to Indian Ocean ports. Kazakhstan is already a major supplier of food to Afghanistan, exporting around $216 million worth of flour and $122 million of wheat in the first seven months of 2026. In September, Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan also agreed with the United Arab Emirates to study a railway corridor through Afghanistan to Pakistan. Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Turkmenistan all share borders with Afghanistan. Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan also face the prospect of reduced water supplies from the Amu Darya as Afghanistan builds its Qosh Tepa Canal . Afghanistan’s omission from a joint statement should therefore not be taken as a complete account of the policies of all five Central Asian states. What Constrains Washington One possible explanation lies in the U.S. approach to Afghanistan’s current authorities. Washington allows practical contacts with representatives of the Taliban but does not recognize the government it has formed. The movement remains designated as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist , although it is not included in the U.S. Department of State’s separate list of Foreign Terrorist Organizations. The designation restricts dealings with the Taliban, although U.S. sanctions rules permit many commercial transactions involving Afghanistan’s governing institutions, including civilian infrastructure and transportation projects. Restrictions remain on direct financial transfers to the Taliban, subject to specified exceptions. Washington would have to reconcile support for projects involving Afghan authorities with its policy of nonrecognition of the Taliban government and the remaining restrictions. These constraints did not, however, prevent C5+1 participants from backing transport and energy links through Afghanistan in 2023. Pakistan is important to Central Asia’s access to Indian Ocean ports through Afghanistan. But relations between Kabul and Islamabad have deteriorated sharply . Fighting along their border in October 2025 led to the closure of major crossings, and trade disruptions continued into 2026 . An alternative route south runs through Iran and its ports. Here, the constraints arise from U.S.-Iranian relations and Washington’s sanctions policy. Different Routes, Different Priorities The shift in the published agenda cannot be explained solely by Washington’s relationship with Afghanistan. Central Asia has significance in its own right for U.S. economic policy, particularly as a potential source of critical minerals and a destination for American investment. The Trans-Caspian route does not replace southern corridors. It connects different markets, and its viability depends on transit countries’ infrastructure and policies, including tariffs. For Central Asian capitals, choosing between these routes is not necessary. Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan can develop ties with Afghanistan while participating in Trans-Caspian projects and expanding cooperation with the U.S. Moreover, the gradual normalization of contacts with Kabul as part of routine trade and transportation activities could reduce the need to discuss Afghanistan separately at every C5+1 meeting. Afghanistan’s absence from the Samarkand statement therefore allows for at least two interpretations. Washington may have deliberately focused on initiatives that do not require political engagement with the Taliban. Alternatively, Central Asian countries may be increasingly handling Afghan-related issues on their own, reserving the C5+1 format for projects where U.S. participation is most valuable.

title: Iran’s conditions for ending war must be met — supreme leader
body:
TEHRAN, October 27. /TASS/. Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei reiterated that the conditions Iran has put forward for ending the military conflict must be met, according to a post on the supreme leader’s website after his meeting with Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council Mohsen Rezaei.
"The Supreme Leader of the Islamic Revolution <...> emphasized the need for ensuring the rights and interests of the Iranian people and the axis of resistance by fulfilling the conditions set forth by the country’s leadership, with the aim of ending the war and getting out of the ‘neither war nor peace’ state," it said.
Other topics raised at the meeting included issues of defending national and regional security through the administration of the Strait of Hormuz and strengthening bilateral ties with neighboring countries. Rezaei, in turn, briefed the supreme leader on the situation in the country.

title: Katsina Boosts Vocational Skills with N4bn Investment
body: Katsina State Governor, Dikko Umaru Radda, has disclosed that his administration has invested over N4 billion in renovating, upgrading and equipping the Katsina Youth Craft Village (KYCV) to boost vocational skills in the state. Radda disclosed this on Monday during the graduation ceremony of 1,662 trainees held at the Muhammadu Dikko Stadium in Katsina. He explained that the number of graduates represents a 156.79 per cent increase from the 648 trainees recorded at the institution’s maiden graduation ceremony. He said the investment was part of his administration’s Building Your Future Agenda, designed to equip young people with practical skills and transform them from job seekers into job creators. “When this administration came into office, we made a commitment under our Building Your Future Agenda to prioritise youth empowerment, skills acquisition and job creation. We promised to transform our young people from job seekers into job creators,” the governor said. Radda explained that the government had provided modern machines, tools and equipment at the centre to ensure that trainees acquired industry-relevant skills and could establish viable businesses after graduation. “We do not believe in simply issuing certificates and sending our graduates home without the means to put their training into practice. That is why we are providing them with start-up tools and equipment to enable them to establish their businesses,” he added. The governor said the graduates received training in more than 15 trades, including tailoring, welding and fabrication, carpentry, electrical installation, information and communication technology, catering, cosmetology, plumbing and automobile repairs. He also disclosed that the government had established a modern innovation hub and an innovation desk at the centre to encourage creativity, technological advancement and entrepreneurship. Describing vocational education as a critical tool for addressing unemployment, Radda announced plans to establish additional training centres across the state’s 34 local government areas. “Our target is to train and empower more than 5,000 young people through vocational training initiatives before the end of our tenure,” he said. He further revealed that the Katsina State Enterprise Development Agency had supported more than 60,000 beneficiaries through various enterprise development programmes. Radda urged the graduates to make productive use of the start-up packages provided by the government rather than sell them. “I urge you not to sell your start-up packs. Use them to establish your businesses, grow your enterprises and create employment opportunities for others,” he advised. In his remarks, a former governor of the state, Ibrahim Shehu Shema, recalled that the Katsina Youth Craft Village was established during his administration to equip young people, particularly those from rural communities, with practical and marketable skills. He stressed that technical and vocational education remained essential to youth self-reliance, entrepreneurship and economic development. “The importance of technical and vocational education cannot be overemphasised. It provides young people with practical skills to become self-reliant, establish businesses and contribute meaningfully to society,” he said. Earlier, the Coordinator of the Katsina Youth Craft Village, Kabir Abdullahi Kofar Soro, described the graduation ceremony as a significant milestone in the state’s youth empowerment efforts. He highlighted the increase in the number of graduates from 648 at the maiden ceremony to 1,662 at the second edition, attributing the achievement to the state government’s support and expansion of the institution. “This achievement would not have been possible without the direct intervention and support of His Excellency, particularly his commitment to youth development and approval for the expansion of the Katsina Youth Craft Village,” he said.

title: Arakhamia: Ceasefire in Oleshky to last until 22:59 on Nov 1
body:
A ceasefire along the longest stretch of the front line in southern Ukraine began at 3:00 Kyiv time on October 27 and will continue until 22:59 on November 1, as part of an initiative by U.S. First Lady Melania Trump to unblock Oleshky, announced David Arakhamia, head of the Servant of the People parliamentary faction.

"This is the most significant de-escalation since 2022. The ceasefire will last from October 27 until 22:59 on November 1. Every such de-escalation effort brings us closer to the long-awaited peace in Ukraine," Arakhamia wrote on his Telegram channel on Tuesday.

title: 2027: It’s time to compensate Tinubu for what he did for the north – Bichi
body: A member of the House of Representatives, Hon. Abubakar Kabir Abubakar, has said the late President Muhammadu Buhari would not have won the 2015 presidential election without the political support and “strategic intervention” of President Bola Tinubu. Abubakar, who is the Chairman, House Committee on Appropriations representing Bichi Federal Constituency, also said political stakeholders in Kano North Senatorial District had resolved to mobilise at least one million votes for Tinubu’s re-election in 2027 in appreciation of his support for the North and development projects in Kano State. He spoke during a stakeholders’ meeting and inauguration of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Campaign Council for Bichi Federal Constituency in Bichi Local Government Area of Kano State. “Tinubu made the late President Muhammadu Buhari after several unsuccessful attempts to become president. It is now time for us to compensate Tinubu for what he did for the North,” he said. UBA Launches Group-Wide Climate Action Week to Advance Green Finance Businessman builds N2.2bn hospital for Edo community The lawmaker dismissed claims that Tinubu’s policies were deliberately targeted against Northern Nigeria, describing such allegations as insincere and politically motivated. He argued that the president’s approval of major road construction and other development projects across Kano State demonstrated his commitment to the region’s progress. “Those saying President Tinubu does not like the North are not sincere. We have decided to vote massively for the president because of his developmental support for Kano,” he said. Abubakar said several projects being executed in the state would not have been possible without federal government support, adding that the North should reciprocate Tinubu’s political support for Buhari’s emergence in 2015. He said the APC was determined to consolidate its political strength in Kano North and secure massive votes for Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election. “We are not just talking about Bichi or Kano North; we are talking about the whole 44 local government areas. We are talking about the whole of Kano, and we will get what we want,” he declared. The lawmaker disclosed that Kano North had approximately 1.3 million registered voters, expressing confidence that the district could mobilise at least one million votes for the president. The Deputy Governor of Kano State, Murtala Sule Garo, who represented Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf at the event, urged members of the campaign council to mobilise support for all APC candidates. Garo, however, cautioned the campaign team against actions capable of threatening peace and tranquillity in Kano North, urging party supporters to adopt issue-based campaigns to convince voters. Similarly, the Director-General of the APC Presidential and Governorship Campaign Council in Kano, Abdullahi Tijjani Gwarzo, challenged the Bichi campaign team to engage grassroots mobilisers and youth support groups to strengthen the party’s chances. Gwarzo expressed optimism about the APC’s prospects in the 2027 presidential and governorship elections in Kano, while urging party members to shun violence and other actions capable of disrupting peace in the state.

title: Elevate Africa calls for stronger partnerships to unlock Africa’s development potential
body: Elevate Africa has called for stronger connections between the continent’s resources, capital, leadership and opportunities to accelerate development and translate Africa’s potential into tangible results. The call was made at a press conference in Accra ahead of the Elevate Africa Annual Convening 2026, which will be held under the theme “Africa: Defining Her Future.” Co-founder of Elevate Africa, Her Majesty Olori Atuwatsé III, said the continent already had solutions to many of its challenges but needed greater confidence in its ability to implement them. “Africa doesn’t lack solutions. What we lack is the conviction and the confidence in the solutions that we already have,” she said. She said the organisation was working to promote African-led solutions, bring leaders and creators together, and develop talent through its fellowship programme. Elevate Africa Chief Partnership Officer, Dr Rex Idaminabo, said the continent needed to strengthen the links between its existing resources and the capital, leadership and opportunities required to turn its potential into practical outcomes. “Africa does not lack potential. What Africa needs are stronger connections between its resources, capital, leadership, and opportunities,” he said. The organisation is positioning its annual convening as a platform for bringing together people and institutions to discuss how African resources, ideas and talent can be mobilised to shape the continent’s future. The 2026 edition will be held under the theme “Africa: Defining Her Future.”

title: 2026 U17 WWC: Black Maidens eye ‘glory’ after making knockout stages – Adarkwa
body: Head coach of Ghana’s Black Maidens, Nana Joe Adarkwa, says his side are now going all out for the top prize after advancing into the next stage of the 2026 U-17 Women’s World Cup. Ghana booked a place in the knockout phase of the competition following a 2-0 win over Canada in their final group game, ensuring they finished second in Group C, where they set up a clash against debutants Argentina. Adarkwa’s side are in the last 16 of the tournament following their return after failing to appear in the last three editions prior to this year’s competition. The gaffer believes there is only one target from here after reaching the crucial stage of the competition, starting with the clash against the South Americans. “We all saw what happened against Canada, so going forward, they have psyched themselves in terms of motivation, and I know they will deliver against Argentina,” he told CitiSports. “When we were coming to this World Cup, our first target was to cross the group stage. Now that we’ve done that, we want to push Argentina to one side and keep going. So our target right now is to go for the glory and nothing else.” Ghana’s game against Argentina is on Wednesday, October 28, with kickoff scheduled for 18:00 GMT.

title: Iran's supreme leader healthy, in full charge of country — parliament speaker
body:
TEHRAN, October 27. /TASS/. Iran’s supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei is in good health and full charge of the country, Mejlis Chairman Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, who met with him the day before.
"The supreme leader is in tip-top shape, and I saw him with a strong, cheerful spirit, full of hope, in good health and peace of mind, answering questions at will," Ghalibaf wrote on Telegram.
He said that despite heavy losses, the leader maintains an air of serenity, testifying to his strong faith in God and deep trust in the people. According to him, issues of war, the "axis of resistance", diplomacy, negotiations, macroeconomic indicators, as well as economic displacement and the naval blockade were discussed at the meeting.

title: Elbit Wins $200 Million Asia-Pacific Airborne Systems Deal
body:
Elbit Systems has secured contracts worth approximately $200 million from an undisclosed customer in the Asia-Pacific region for airborne intelligence, surveillance, targeting and reconnaissance systems, training solutions and cockpit display equipment. The contracts will be performed over a period of up to five years. Under the agreements, Elbit Systems will supply its SPECTRO 12 multispectral intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance and targeting payload for integration on helicopters. SPECTRO 12 is the latest member of the company’s SPECTRO family and is designed for airborne platforms with tight size, weight and power limitations. According to Elbit Systems, the payload combines high-resolution multispectral sensing with precision targeting capabilities, including a laser designator, as well as AI-based image processing. The system is intended to support long-range target detection, identification, tracking and engagement in complex operational environments and under adverse weather conditions. Support for Airborne Training Systems The contracts also include follow-on support and upgrade services for airborne live training systems already installed on aircraft. These systems are used in live, virtual and constructive training environments and support both air-to-air and air-to-ground scenarios. According to the company, they provide real-time combat simulation, weapon scoring and mission debriefing capabilities designed to improve pilot readiness and training effectiveness. Elbit’s Head-Up Displays Also Included Elbit Systems will also supply advanced Head-Up Display systems. The HUDs feature high-resolution display technology, enhanced video capabilities and relatively low power consumption, and are intended to support both day and night operations across a range of airborne platforms. Bezhalel Machlis, President and CEO of Elbit Systems, said the contracts reflect the company’s ability to combine airborne sensor, training and display technologies across a broad range of missions. The identity of the Asia-Pacific customer was not disclosed. Author: Arie Egozi, Israel Correspondent

title: Tinubu Condemns Murder Of Islamic Cleric Masussuka, Orders Thorough Investigation
body: President Bola Tinubu has condemned the murder of prominent Islamic preacher, Sheikh Yahaya Ibrahim Masussuka, and his friend, Adamu Abubakar, in Dutsin-Ma, Katsina State. The gunmen killed the duo in a drive-by shooting incident on Monday evening. The President, who was deeply saddened by the news of the killing, described the act as heinous and an assault on the values of peace and sanctity of human life, according to a statement by his Special Adviser to the President (Information & Strategy), Bayo Onanuga, on Tuesday. President Tinubu extended his heartfelt condolences to the families of the deceased, their followers, as well as the government and people of Katsina State, over the tragic loss. The President has directed the Nigeria Police Force and other relevant security agencies to move swiftly, intensify efforts already underway by the Katsina State Police Command, and ensure the perpetrators are tracked down, apprehended, and brought to justice. President Tinubu prayed for the repose of the souls of the departed and for comfort for all those who mourn their deaths. The post Tinubu Condemns Murder Of Islamic Cleric Masussuka, Orders Thorough Investigation appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Democrats have a midterm edge, poll shows. And, Israelis vote in high-stakes election
body:
Good morning. You're reading the Up First newsletter. Subscribe here to get it delivered to your inbox, and listen to the Up First podcast for all the news you need to start your day.
A new NPR/PBS News/Marist poll reveals that Democrats hold significant advantages in the midterm elections and are favored to gain control of the U.S. House. But there are also signs suggesting that a potential wave may be limited. The poll highlights key issues influencing voters ; one in three Americans face financial hardships, and four in 10 say their personal finances are worsening. Preserving democracy resonates with Democrats and independents, while immigration ranks as the top issue for MAGA supporters.
A member of the League of Women Voters of Greater Cleveland helps hold the flag during the national anthem before a basketball game on Oct. 26, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. Jason Miller/Getty Images hide caption
A federal judge today hears arguments in the Trump administration's bid to compel California to set aside ballots from voters it alleges may not be citizens. This comes after an appeals court last night declined the administration's request to get involved.
Israelis are voting today in an election that will shape their country's future. This marks the first time since the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas attacks that Israelis can choose their leaders. Voters will decide whether to keep Israel's far-right, longest-serving prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, or replace him with Gadi Eisenkot , a former military chief promising more diplomacy and less extremism. Here's what you need to know about the leading candidates, the issues shaping the vote and what could happen next.
Woman stretching back during remote work break at home office Olga Pankova/Getty Images/Moment RF hide caption
Hours of screen time at your desk can turn you into a stiff, bleary-eyed version of yourself. Prolonged sitting can take a real toll, but a few smart habits can help reset your body and mind. Here are Life Kit 's best strategies to help with the discomfort and health risks that can come from sitting at a desk all day.
Lubelo Mthenjana performs a magic trick involving fire during the annual junior magic contest at the College of Magic in Cape Town, South Africa. Tommy Trenchard for NPR hide caption
Forget flying brooms. Cape Town is home to South Africa's real-world Hogwarts: the College of Magic. Every Saturday, almost 200 students ages 10 to 18 attend classes in a variety of things, including puppetry, mime and clowning, juggling, card tricks, illusions, mentalism, stage magic, theater production and escapology. In 1980, David Gore and a friend came up with the idea of starting a magic school. At the time, South Africa was grappling with apartheid, a brutal system of racial segregation. But from day one, the establishment was multiracial, even though state schools were still strictly segregated. Almost 50 years later, the College of Magic continues to stand out in a city that remains deeply divided along racial and economic lines. These photos capture how the school has turned young dreamers into magicians .
Invasive blue catfish are a problem in the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries, preying on native seafood like the blue crab. To help keep them in check, local schoolchildren are eating catfish for lunch. Ryan Kellman/NPR hide caption

title: OpenAI's partner content arrives in ChatGPT pre-summarized while the rest of the web gets raw scraps
body:
ChatGPT doesn't fetch partner pages live. Instead, it receives them as pre-generated summaries, while regular web pages arrive as raw text snippets. In the prompt, partner entries are placed ahead of all web results. For ranked lists, the summaries name 70 percent of entries in positions 1 through 3 but only 23 percent of those in positions 7 through 10, according to 1,000 cases Konitzny analyzed.
OpenAI had promised partners more prominent placement in ChatGPT back in 2024, and a study from Hamburg later found Springer media appearing far more often in the web interface than through the API. But even partners don't always get cited correctly . Ad Ad

title: Breaking: Probe panel blames miners’ deaths on overcrowding, extreme heat, dehydration
body: By Omeiza Ajayi The independent ministerial committee investigating the recent deaths of 33 persons in the custody of the Nigerian Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) in Minna, Niger State, has unravelled the cause of death of the suspects. In the Executive Summary by the chairman of the Committee, Jonathan Kure, on Tuesday in Abuja, when he presented the report to the Minister of Interior, Hon. Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, the committee cited the causes of death to include “overcrowding, unsuitable detention condition, failure of duty of care, inadequate supervision”. It added that “fatalities resulted from environmental asphyxia caused by prolonged confinement in a severely overcrowded cell aggravated by heat stress and dehydration”. According to the committee, the operation which led to the arrest of the suspects was without an “operational order” or approval from the national headquarters of the NSCDC. The post Breaking: Probe panel blames miners’ deaths on overcrowding, extreme heat, dehydration appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Kremlin briefing addresses situation in Alyoshki, trilateral talks on Ukraine
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Russian President Vladimir Putin’s call with the leaders of Norway and Finland, the situation in Alyoshki, and trilateral talks on Ukraine were the main topics discussed during a briefing by Kremlin Spokesman Dmitry Peskov on Tuesday.
TASS has compiled the key remarks made by the Kremlin spokesman.
- Russian President Vladimir Putin held a phone call with Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store, Peskov confirmed to TASS.
- The Russian Armed Forces’ General Staff stated that, as of 4:00 a.m. Moscow time (1:00 a.m. GMT), hostilities had stopped in the Kherson sector of the line of engagement and a ceasefire had been introduced in connection with the humanitarian operation in Alyoshki, with no violations reported so far. "Our General Staff issued a statement announcing that it had come into effect at 4:00 a.m. So far, there have been no reports of violations," Peskov said.
- The military will release all information on the details of the humanitarian operation in Alyoshki.
- The potential trilateral talks on the settlement of the Ukrainian conflict in Abu Dhabi have not yet been scheduled. "No, there is no date yet," Peskov said.
- President Vladimir Putin and his US counterpart Donald Trump did not discuss promoting former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orban’s candidacy for the post of UN Secretary-General during their recent phone conversation. "No, this issue was not discussed during the most recent telephone call," Peskov said.
- If Orban’s candidacy for the post is proposed, it will be considered. "Should such a candidacy be put forward, it will also be considered," he added.

title: Ukrinform joins National Unity Radio Dictation
body:
Military personnel, Ukrainian actors, writers, musicians and public figures took part in writing the dictation, Ukrinform reports.
The text was written by writer and Russian-Ukrainian war veteran Artur Dron. This year’s dictation is titled A Letter That Never Ends .
“Greetings to the Ukrinform team and to everyone who will be writing the All-Ukrainian National Unity Radio Dictation. Thank you for writing it. Thank you for being part of this history. I hope that the words I wrote, which Dasha and Artur will read to you, will become, in some way, personal and important to you as well. Good luck with the dictation, and may the Ukrainian language unite us all,” Dron said in a video address to Ukrinform.
The dictation text was read live by Ukrainian language and literature teacher Artur Proidakov and public figure and volunteer Dasha Astafieva.
In his video address, Proidakov emphasized that what matters most is not spelling or punctuation mistakes, but unity, at least for the duration of writing and discussing the radio dictation text.
“Good luck during this ritual of unity, the writing of the 2026 radio dictation,” Proidakov said.
Those who took part in writing the radio dictation at Ukrinform included Olha Kononenko, Director General of the National Music House; music producer Yevhen Petrychenko; theater critic Olha Stelmashеvska; Lesia Ukrainka National Academic Theater actress Nataliia Dolia; representatives of the Main Intelligence Directorate, and others.
Participants can submit their dictation for professional review. To do so, they must send the handwritten text by mail to: 26 Khreshchatyk Street, Kyiv, 01001. The postmark must be dated no later than October 28. Alternatively, participants can photograph or scan their handwritten text in .jpg, .png, .jpeg, .tiff or .pdf format and email it to rd@suspilne.media by 11:00 on October 29.
On Thursday, October 29, at 11:00, Suspilne platforms will publish the text of the National Unity Radio Dictation so that everyone can check what they wrote.
As reported by Ukrinform, the All-Ukrainian National Unity Radio Dictation was launched by the Ukrainian Radio team in 2000 to unite people around the Ukrainian language. Held annually, the radio dictation has become the largest Ukrainian-language flash mob, bringing together Ukrainians and Ukrainian-language enthusiasts around the world.

title: Ukrainian Red Cross provides assistance to victims of Russian missile attack on Kyiv
body:
The Ukrainian Red Cross Society (URCS) provided assistance to victims at three locations in Kyiv following an overnight Russian missile attack.

"Volunteers from the Ukrainian Red Cross emergency response team in Kyiv worked at three locations affected by the Russian attack. The teams coordinated with other emergency services and provided assistance to people affected by the attack," URCS said on Facebook Tuesday.

In particular, the team worked team worked near Lisova metro station, where volunteers assisted those affected. Volunteers also took part in rescue operations on the grounds of an educational institution and near a damaged student dormitory.

As previously reported, Russian missile attacks on the capital resulted in one death and ten injuries. A university dormitory, a school building, Kyoto Park, an area near a metro station, residential buildings, and the South Bridge sustained damage.

title: Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi lead record T20 chase as India win NZ series
body: India openers Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav ‌Sooryavanshi teamed up to decimate New Zealand's bowling attack and secure an unassailable lead in the five-match T20 series in Wellington on ⁠Tuesday. Abhishek hit a 35-ball century while teen batting sensation Sooryavanshi cracked 45 from 19 balls to help India chase down the target of 199 inside 14 overs with six wickets in hand. The tourists took a 3-0 lead in the series with ⁠two games to go. Abhishek made 113 off 38 balls, hitting nine fours and 11 sixes as India piled on the records and runs in windy Wellington. It was a record-breaking night for the double world champions as ​Abhishek ⁠combined with 15-year-old Sooryavanshi to score a record 118 runs in the powerplay, beating ​the previous mark (116) set by Romania against Serbia in 2021. India reached 100 runs in just five overs, settling the contest well before the halfway mar. Sooryavanshi opened the innings for the first time in the series as Sanju Samson was pushed down the order. And the left-handed batter matched Abhishek for power and strokeplay during his stay. “That was the plan for us. Just get the momentum for the team and keep going,” said player-of-the-match Abhishek . “Vaibhav started off well, and we took the momentum from there. It is not that easy, but it is down to preparation. Huge shoutout to our coaching staff and our side-arm (bowlers). We had a good practice session yesterday.” The opening pair put on 133 before the promoted Sooryavanshi was caught at long on for 45 trying to slog recalled New Zealand quick Matthew Fisher over his head. Fisher was denied a second wicket when Mitchell Santner dropped Abhishek at cover on 92. Abhishek soon reached his century when he hit Kyle Jamieson to ​the fine leg fence. New Zealand skipper Santner said India bowled well in the death overs to restrict the hosts to under 200. From New Delhi to Wellington ⏩ Abhishek Sharma never forgets to be in his element 🧘‍♂️ #TeamIndia | #NZvIND | @OfficialAbhi04 pic.twitter.com/tmyvJ1VzI9 — BCCI (@BCCI) October 27, 2026 “They (India) bowled well at the end. When the dew comes in, it is tough. Powerplay is such a massive part of this game and they showed us how to bat,” Santner said. The Kiwis will have to regroup quickly as the next match is at Eden Park in Auckland which is an even smaller ground. Batting first, New Zealand made a respectable ⁠198, with number three Daryl Mitchell scoring an unbeaten 89. The hiding New Zealand's bowlers received in the powerplay may be hard to put behind them, though, ahead of the fourth match on ​Friday. “Pretty tough to stop those guys when they're going. We've seen it before, seen it in the IPL and obviously witnessed it here tonight in New Zealand,” Santner said.

title: Obi Vows to Wage War on Corruption, Promises Nigerians Results From Day One
body: • NDC presidential candidate pledges emergency measures on security, agriculture, education, healthcare, electricity • Promises 20% of credit to SMEs, primary healthcare centres in every ward within two years Sunday Aborisade in Abuja Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr Peter Obi, has vowed to wage an uncompromising war against corruption and ensure the transparent management of public resources, declaring that Nigerians would begin to see measurable improvements in governance from the first day of an NDC administration. Obi, who is contesting the January 16, 2027 presidential election with former Kano State governor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, as his running mate, also promised emergency interventions in security, agriculture, education, healthcare and electricity, insisting that Nigeria could no longer afford leadership that blamed previous administrations for its failures. He made the commitments in Abuja at a dinner organised to inaugurate the party’s National Presidential Campaign Council and present certificates of return to its candidates, following the unveiling of its new national secretariat at 393 Etang Obuli Crescent, Jabi, Abuja . The former Anambra State governor said his administration would prioritise problem-solving, accountability and measurable outcomes rather than political excuses, arguing that public officeholders must demonstrate how the country’s resources translate into improved living conditions. “The purpose of governance is to solve problems, not to blame people. Kwankwaso and I will not blame anybody. We will create that new Nigeria that is possible,” he declared. Obi accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of failing to translate increased government revenues and borrowing into commensurate improvements in Nigerians’ living conditions. He said the country needed leadership that would respond directly to the challenges confronting citizens, particularly insecurity, hunger, unemployment, poverty and the rising cost of living. “From my engagements all over Nigeria, Nigerians are looking for new leadership. And we assure you that we will create that new leadership,” he said. Obi made the fight against corruption a central pillar of his campaign, promising to ensure that public funds served the interests of Nigerians rather than being diverted for private benefit. He argued that corruption had weakened public institutions, undermined development spending, discouraged productive investment and contributed to the country’s persistent economic difficulties. Questioning the management of government revenues and borrowed funds under the Tinubu administration, he demanded greater transparency in public expenditure and challenged the Federal Government to account for its spending and development projects. “We must stop people from stealing public money. We must use public money for the public good. And that will be seen, it will be shown,” he said. The NDC candidate insisted that public officials found culpable of corruption must be held accountable in accordance with the law. He also questioned the implementation of the 2023, 2024 and 2025 budgets, alleging that capital expenditure remained below 20 per cent and that contractors were experiencing difficulties receiving payments for completed projects. Obi challenged the Federal Government to provide Nigerians with a detailed account of its expenditure, projects and achievements, arguing that citizens deserved tangible improvements rather than repeated explanations of the country’s problems. “We don’t want you to hire us to tell you about our problem. It’s only in Nigeria that you hire people, and they start reminding you of what happened in the past. “No, we don’t want you to hire us to tell you about our problem. We want you to hire us to improve from today,” he said. On security, Obi promised a more direct presidential response to kidnapping, violent attacks and other threats to lives and property, insisting that the president must demonstrate leadership by visiting communities affected by emergencies. He argued that the country’s security challenges required urgent action and a leadership willing to engage directly with affected communities rather than remain distant from the realities confronting victims. “If they say there is a problem in Jos, he will go to Jos,” he said. Obi pledged to visit communities affected by insecurity in Plateau, Benue, Zamfara, Sokoto and Borno States, among others, and criticised what he described as excessive foreign travel by the president. He maintained that Nigeria needed a leader who would devote greater attention to domestic challenges and demonstrate solidarity with citizens facing violence, displacement and economic hardship. The NDC candidate also promised emergency measures to revive agriculture, particularly in northern Nigeria, where insecurity has disrupted farming activities and restricted access to productive land. He said restoring security in farming communities would enable farmers to return to their fields, increase food production, reduce dependence on imports and strengthen the supply of raw materials to local industries. “We have vast land in the north. When we secure the north, our farmers must go back and produce what we eat and what we use for our industries,” he said. He linked agricultural recovery to the broader task of tackling hunger, stabilising food prices, creating employment and moving the economy away from excessive dependence on consumption and borrowing. Obi also pledged emergency interventions in education, expressing concern over the number of Nigerian children outside the formal school system. He argued that the country could not achieve sustainable development without investing in human capital and ensuring that children from disadvantaged backgrounds had access to quality education. Drawing on his experience as governor of Anambra State, he said education should serve as a pathway to opportunity, regardless of a person’s family background or social connections. “We must create a society where a child of nobody will be somebody without knowing anybody,” he said. On healthcare, Obi renewed his promise to establish a functional primary healthcare centre in every ward within two years of assuming office. He said the proposed intervention would bring basic medical services closer to communities, improve access to treatment and reduce preventable deaths. The former governor also pledged emergency measures to address persistent electricity shortages, describing reliable power supply as indispensable to industrial growth, job creation and economic recovery. “We will declare emergency on generation, transmission, and distribution,” he said. Obi argued that unreliable electricity had increased operating costs for businesses, burdened households and constrained the productive capacity of Nigerian industries. He called for the revival of manufacturing establishments across the country, citing the decline of industries in Kano as an example of the economic consequences of inadequate infrastructure and weak industrial development. He said Nigeria must transition from an economy driven largely by consumption and borrowing to one built on production, investment and job creation. Small and medium-sized enterprises also featured prominently in Obi’s economic proposals, with the NDC candidate promising improved access to credit, tax relief and incentives to stimulate business growth. Citing figures indicating that Nigeria has more than 40 million small businesses, he said the sector remained constrained by limited access to bank financing despite its importance to employment and economic activity. Obi said an NDC administration would work to ensure that more than 20 per cent of credit went to small businesses, arguing that expanding financing opportunities would enable entrepreneurs to grow their operations and employ more Nigerians. “We will put a mark to it. We will ensure that over 20% of credits will go to small businesses. We will support them,” he said. He also promised tax holidays and other incentives to support small businesses, while insisting that government policies must encourage production and enterprise rather than impose burdens that stifle growth. The proposed measures, he said, would form part of a broader economic strategy to expand employment opportunities, strengthen local production and improve household incomes. Turning to the 2027 elections, Obi urged political actors to respect the rights of opposition supporters and refrain from intimidating citizens engaged in lawful political activities. He said political competition should centre on ideas, policies and the credibility of candidates rather than harassment or the suppression of opposing voices. “Humility and civility are not weaknesses. It is a virtue. Good behaviour is not a weakness. It is a virtue,” he said. The NDC presidential candidate also urged Nigerians to defend the integrity of the electoral process, insisting that the forthcoming election should provide citizens with an opportunity to determine their political future through the ballot. “The revolution that is coming is a revolution of the ballot,” he declared. He called for free, fair and credible elections, maintaining that electoral legitimacy remained fundamental to democratic governance and public confidence in political institutions. Earlier, NDC National Chairman, Senator Moses Cleopas, described the gathering as a significant milestone in the party’s preparations for the 2027 general election, saying its emergence was driven by the determination to offer Nigerians a different approach to governance. Cleopas said the party had conducted its primaries within a short period and that the dinner provided an opportunity for candidates, party leaders and other stakeholders to strengthen their commitment to a common political agenda. He identified the inauguration of the National Presidential Campaign Council and the presentation of certificates of return to candidates as major steps in the party’s preparations for the elections. The national chairman disclosed that the certificates contained security codes, warning against unauthorised claims to candidacy and insisting that the party would maintain order and accountability in its electoral process. He challenged candidates to regard their nominations as a responsibility to the electorate rather than a personal achievement, warning that the party would not tolerate unfulfilled campaign promises. Cleopas urged candidates to make realistic commitments and ensure that, if elected, they delivered on their promises to the people. “If we fail to bring water for you in two years, if we open our mouths to say, vote for us again, please don’t vote for us,” he said. He described the party’s political mission as an effort to address the country’s challenges and restore public confidence in leadership. “We are going for a rescue mission; the hope of this country is in NDC,” Cleopas declared. The party’s National Leader, Senator Seriake Dickson, described the new national secretariat as the NDC’s ‘Noah’s Ark’, presenting the facility as a unifying centre for the party as it prepares for the 2027 elections. The secretariat is expected to serve as the party’s administrative headquarters and provide a central base for strategic planning, organisational activities and coordination of its nationwide presidential campaign. The unveiling followed the party’s Third National Executive Committee meeting and formed part of a series of activities designed to strengthen its structures ahead of the general election. The event brought together Cleopas, Dickson, Senator Victor Umeh, who represents Anambra Central in the Senate; Rivers State governorship candidate, Dumo Lulu-Briggs; Adamawa State governorship candidate, Senator Aisha Binani and other party leaders and members. The inauguration of the campaign council and presentation of certificates of return to candidates marked another phase in the NDC’s electoral preparations. With the establishment of its national headquarters and the inauguration of its campaign council, the party is seeking to build a nationwide campaign around accountability, economic recovery, improved public services, security and a different approach to leadership ahead of the 2027 polls.

title: Toluwanisings’ burial dispute deepens as uncle calls for death probe
body:
The family of late Nigerian gospel singer Olayemi “Toluwanisings” Bolaji has insisted that his burial must wait until the authorities determine what caused his death.
PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the “Kabiyesi Olorun Ayo” crooner died after he slumped at his residence in Ibadan, Oyo State on 15 October.
Since then, the family has faced controversy over his burial arrangements, including whether to bury him in a cemetery, at his residence, or in his hometown.
The singer’s uncle, Lawal “Up Lawal” Ademola, made the family’s position clear during an interview with Dunmininu Kingdom , posted on TikTok on Monday.
Speaking on behalf of the family, he called for a transparent and impartial investigation into the death and warned against any attempt to compromise the investigation.
Up Lawal, a health worker, urged the government, community leaders, and security agencies to prevent interference in the investigation.
The younger brother of the singer’s father said: “The family has decided that Sodiq must not be buried on Wednesday. We have informed the musicians, who have since suspended all arrangements for his burial. The family thanks God, as we believe that He is the giver and taker of life. Since Sodiq’s death, we have accepted it as God’s will. However, the family now needs the support of Nigerians and the government because his death has deeply pained and baffled us.
“We are calling on the government, Christians, Muslims, and traditionalists to help us investigate the cause of Sodiq’s death. The whole world knows that Sodiq is dead, but to establish the facts and avoid future controversy, we, the Olayemi family, need to know the cause of his death. We are appealing to everyone to help us get answers.”
Furthermore, Up Lawal said the family had directed that all burial plans for Toluwanisings be suspended, adding that they had already informed their relatives in Ibadan.
He insisted that the family would continue to foot the mortuary bills until investigators completed their work and uncovered the cause of Toluwanisings’ death.
“The government should ensure that the law takes its course and empower the relevant authorities to investigate Sodiq’s death. We do not want to take the law into our own hands. The family is deeply saddened by his death. For this reason, nobody should make further burial arrangements for Sodiq, as we are still grieving and want to know the truth.
“The family has resolved that he must not be buried until the cause of his death is established. We will continue to pay the mortuary fees until the investigation is concluded. Once the cause of his death is established, we will bury him at his house in Ibadan, where his wife currently lives. That is the family’s decision,” said Up Lawal.
He also alleged foul play in the singer’s death, claiming that his wife, workers, and others showed no sign of mourning when he visited Toluwanisings’ house with seven family members
“I represented the head of the family. 7 of us travelled from Ikirun to Ibadan, we got there at about 9:30am, and we met the wife’s mother, the wife’s sisters, PA, and Tolu’s aunt. I was devastated when I saw them watching TV and eating. They put food inside takeaway packs. I had to ask the wife if Tolu was truly Tolu dead because there was no sign of mourning. I told the PA to take me to the morgue so I could see Tolu’s body.
“He refused. I had to call the other family members, and they said I should arrest the PA. That was when he agreed to take us there. I then checked his body. I challenged my wife that there was a day Tolu’s daddy called her, that even if Tolu is not checking on me, you should be checking on m,e, but Tolu quickly took the phone from his wife and said, ‘don’t destroy our home,’ but she denied.”
He said he told Toluwanising’s widow, Elizabeth, that the family wanted to bury the late singer in his own house, but she rejected the idea.
“She said she couldn’t bear to see his grave. I then suggested Ikirun, but she complained that it was too far. I told her she had to choose one.
“Paternal grandmother insists Toluwanising must be buried in his house.”
Meanwhile, Toluwanising’s paternal grandmother, Sabitiyu Olayemi, insisted that the late singer should be buried in the house he built rather than beside his late mother’s grave.
She also accused the singer of neglecting her despite her family’s efforts to care for his mother.
She further claimed that Toluwanising hardly gave her money, alleging that he sent her just N10,000 on three occasions after she complained about his failure to visit her.
“It is my wish for him to be buried inside the house he built; they should not come and put him beside his mother’s grave at all. I will not allow it. We took care of his mother very well, like our own, but Toluwanisings doesn’t call me then, and even when I want to call people, they advise me not to. I didn’t even know he had built a house. I just recently learned that he is a popular Christian singer.
“He never gives me money at all, not even one kobo. It’s even one girl around one time ago that I gave his number to help me call him so that I can even hear his voice and he will just greet me and all. Even when I complain he doesn’t come to see me, he will be like ‘oh mummy, I have been very busy with work,’ and after that he only sent 10 thousand just like three times, and that was it,” the grandmother said.
Meanwhile, as the family continues to demand an investigation into his death, a flyer shared on Toluwanisings’ Instagram page on Tuesday announced a night of tributes in his honour at the Hall of Grace, Jogor Centre, Ibadan.
The event will begin at 3 p.m., with attendees expected to dress in all white.

title: A select should tell you something
body:
Blog about front-end development and the web
Heads up: your browser doesnât support customizable selects yet, so the âafterâ demos below look like ordinary selects. Thatâs also exactly what your visitors would see in this browser. To see the difference, open this page in Chrome or Edge.
There are multiple articles about appearance: base-select and how you can use it. We finally can style a select. The bigger change is what an option can hold. Until now, an option was one line of plain text, so everything a person needed to decide had to fit in a label or be left out. Now an option can carry the thing people actually decide with: a preview, a number, a job title, a warning. They stop reading and working things out, and start recognising.
Below are five selects, each shown before and after. The before is what most forms do today. The after is the same <select> , with the same keyboard behaviour and the same form value. Only what it shows has changed. If you want the mechanics, the Chrome teamâs announcement and MDNâs guide cover them well.
A font picker usually lists names. To choose well, you either already know what Fraunces looks like, or you pick it, look at the result, and come back to try the next one.
When each option is set in its own typeface, the option is the preview. You judge the shape, not the name.
This pattern is not new. We already have in document editors (like Google Docs) and in design tools (like Figma and Photoshop). It just became available for us and all we need is one inline style per option, style="font-family: 'Fraunces', serif" , and the closed control keeps the typeface after you choose. We are also able to show the category of each font, like Serif, Sans, Mono, Display, or Handwriting.
Time zone pickers tend to look like â(GMT+09:00) Tokyoâ. The offset is accurate and almost never what you want. What you want is the time there, so you add the offset to your own time in your head, and maybe get it wrong around midnight.
Show the current time next to each city, plus whether itâs day or night, and the question answers itself before you choose.
This is the only demo that needs JavaScript, because the times come from Intl.DateTimeFormat .
Delivery options are usually a group of radio buttons, each with its details written out as a sentence.
To be fair, radio buttons have a real strength. Every option is visible without a click, and for two or three short choices theyâre the right pattern. But once each option carries a few facts, the facts end up in prose. Comparing means reading every sentence and holding the numbers in your head.
A select with the facts in aligned columns turns that into a glance down a column, in the space of a single field.
At a company of about two hundred people, we had two colleagues with the same name, in different departments. Whenever I had to pick one of them, I went by their job title. Photos help less than youâd think, because people often donât know what a colleague looks like, especially one in another department.
A text-only select gives you two identical options and a guess. Put the title and department under each name and they become two different answers. The closed control keeps the title too, so anyone reviewing the form can see who you picked.
Some options come with consequences. In a plain select, you find out afterwards.
Mark those options in the list and you know while youâre choosing.
The badge appears only on the options that require special attention, and nowhere else.
Every âafterâ in this post is a plain <select> . Keyboard handling, type-to-jump, form submission, select.value , required , validation and the accessible role all stay with the browser, and the control itself needs no JavaScript.
The bigger trade-off is on phones. A native select opens the operating systemâs own picker. It shows a scrolling wheel on iOS, a sheet on Android. Those are familiar, sized for thumbs, and tuned to each platformâs accessibility features. A customizable select doesnât use them; it draws its own list on the page instead.
You donât have to pick one behaviour for everyone. Opt in only where thereâs a mouse or trackpad, and touch devices keep their native picker:
Phone users then see each optionâs text without the extras, which is one more reason the text has to stand on its own. The demos in this post opt in everywhere, so you can try them on any device.
Customizable select is a textbook progressive enhancement. A browser that doesnât support it doesnât break. It shows a regular native select, keeps only the text of each option, and submits the same value. Nobody gets a worse form than they have today. If youâre reading this in Firefox at the time of writing, the âafterâ demos above are exactly what your visitors would see.
That leaves one requirement, and itâs good practice anyway. The text of every option has to make sense on its own. âAhmed Mostafa, Accountant Â· Financeâ, not just a name. âExpress, Tomorrow, $8.50â, not three loose fragments. In the demos, small separator spans that are hidden in the customized version make the plain version read like a sentence. No polyfill needed.
So thereâs no reason to wait. Find the select in your product where people hesitate the most, ask what theyâre really trying to find out, and put that answer inside the option. Leave everything else out.
All licensed under Creative Commons CC0 .

title: Babcock pitches Arrowhead 140 to U.S. Navy as alternative to FF(X) frigate design
body: The Telegraph reported Babcock’s approach, while Navy Lookout said the offer would be submitted jointly with Huntington Ingalls Industries, or HII. Navy Lookout said it could include transferring intellectual property to allow U.S. shipbuilders to construct Arrowhead 140 independently. The reported arrangement would put HII behind both the FF(X) design and a proposed alternative. HII builds FF(X) and the Legend-class Coast Guard cutters from which it was developed. Babcock does not own a U.S. shipyard, making a design license and engineering support a possible route into the program. It already supplies HII under a December 2025 contract for complex components used in Virginia-class Block VI nuclear-powered submarines. The companies are also developing ARMOR Force, a concept in which a Type 31 frigate would command large Romulus uncrewed surface vessels. That cooperation gives them an existing industrial relationship, but does not establish that the Navy will choose Arrowhead 140. Babcock’s naval programs director, Nick Hine, had previously argued that the company should pursue the U.S. frigate opportunity. Discussions with Pentagon representatives had reportedly taken place before the latest reports. Rear Adm. Casey Moton has confirmed a 90-day review of foreign ship designs involving the Pentagon, the Navy and outside specialists. Other reported candidates include Japan’s modified Mogami, South Korea’s Chungnam and Turkey’s İstanbul classes, while Fincantieri Marine Group has expressed interest in offering FREMM Evo. The Navy is continuing work on FF(X) while examining alternatives. Moton said in late September that the first-flight design had completed its critical design review, with the lead ship scheduled for delivery by the end of June 2030.

title: Control of Congress is up for grabs. What's the math for Democrats and Republicans?
body:
A midterm check on unified government puts congressional majorities in play.
With one week until the midterm elections, the majorities of both houses of Congress are in play as voters weigh a midterm check on unified control of government in Washington -- President Donald Trump's hold on the White House and Republican majorities in the House and Senate the past two years.
Republicans hold slim majorities in both the House and Senate and are rallying to preserve them with just days until Election Day.
Democrats on the other hand are trying to make inroads into some traditionally red areas in hopes of picking up crucial seats.
In the House, all 435 seats are on the ballot on Nov. 3 for two-year terms in the 120th Congress. Speaker Mike Johnson of Louisiana currently holds a historically narrow majority: 218 Republicans alongside a single independent, Rep. Kevin Kiley of California, who filed for reelection without party affiliation but continues to generally support the speaker on the floor. Democrats hold 214 seats.
There are also two vacancies in the House following the April resignations of lawmakers with ethics issues -- former Texas Republican Rep. Tony Gonzales and former Florida Democratic Rep. Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick, who attempted a comeback but was rejected by voters in an August primary.
That’s a lengthy way to explain that on Election Night, Johnson effectively begins with a 220-215 edge over Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries.
While Johnson and Republicans defend their legislative record amassed over the past two years -- including the Working Families Tax Cuts Act, formerly known as Trump's "One, Big Beautiful Bill" -- the closing message from the GOP has also starkly warned voters not to embrace “Mamdani madness," a reference to New York City's democratic socialist mayor and the success of some democratic socialist candidates in Democratic primaries this year.
"We are bringing down the cost of living. We are providing more jobs and opportunity for more people. The facts show it and the records show it," Johnson told CBS during a recent interview. "The success goes on and on."
Across the aisle, Jeffries, a Brooklyn Democrat, is striving to become the first Black speaker in U.S. history, campaigning largely on a plank of affordability and anticorruption that directly takes aim at Trump.
"The American people are fed up," Jeffries told reporters this month, adding his belief that Democrats are "on track" to win the House majority.
For Jeffries to get a chance to take the speaker’s gavel, Democrats must attain a net gain of three seats, pushing their numbers to at least 218 -- a simple majority.
In the Senate, 35 of the upper chamber’s 100 seats are on the ballot for six-year terms, including 13 Democratic and 22 Republican seats sprinkled across the political landscape.
Senate Majority Leader John Thune and Republicans currently hold a 53-45 edge over Senate Democrats, who also have two independents that caucus with them, pushing the current minority to 47 seats.
Thune could afford to have a net loss of three GOP seats and still retain the majority, given Vice President JD Vance’s constitutional power to break tie votes in the Senate.
For Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer and Democrats to flip the majority, however, they’ll need to amass a net gain of four seats.
Early voting is underway in many states and Election Day is Nov. 3.
