title: Minority demands Ablakwa’s resignation or dismissal over SA evacuation payments
body: The Minority in Parliament has called on Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa to resign over allegations that some Ghanaians evacuated from South Africa received less than the GH¢5,500 support package announced by the government. They want the President to sack him if he fails to resign. The demand was made by the Ranking Member on Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee, Samuel Abdulai Jinapor, at a press conference at Parliament on Tuesday, October 27. Mr Jinapor also called for a comprehensive independent audit of the evacuation exercise by an internationally reputable accounting firm to establish the facts surrounding the alleged payment shortfalls. “Given the gravity of these revelations and in order to ensure an impartial investigation into the matter, we call on the Minister for Foreign Affairs, Honourable Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, to resign immediately. His handling of this exercise has brought his high office into disrepute,” he said. He argued that the Minister must accept responsibility in line with Section 2.1(j) of President John Dramani Mahama’s 2025 Code of Conduct and Ethics for Political Appointees, which he said requires resignation where a Minister’s actions or leadership result in significant failure, corruption or a breach of public trust. Mr Jinapor further called on President Mahama to terminate Mr Ablakwa’s appointment if he refuses to resign, citing Article 81(a) of the 1992 Constitution. “The President must demonstrate that the standards he has set for his appointees have consequences when public confidence in their stewardship has been seriously undermined,” he added. The demand follows reports that at least three people contacted from the evacuation list claimed they received GH¢2,000 instead of the GH¢5,500 announced by the government. However, Mr Ablakwa has denied the allegations, insisting that all Ghanaians on the evacuation list, including minors, received the full package comprising GH¢5,000 in reintegration support and GH¢500 for transportation. Speaking to the Ghanaian community in Ottawa, Canada, during an official working visit, the Minister said his ministry had received no complaints about payment shortfalls since the evacuation exercise began more than four months ago. He also maintained that no concerns were raised at the airport over missing envelopes or payments below the announced amount.

title: Putin, Stubb, Store agree to maintain direct telephone contacts — Kremlin
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Russian President Vladimir Putin, Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store have agreed to continue maintaining direct telephone contacts, the Kremlin press service said following their conversation.
"The leaders of the three countries agreed to continue maintaining direct telephone contacts," the statement said.
According to the TASS database, this was the first telephone contact between the Russian head of state and the leaders of Finland and Norway since 2022.
Putin and Stubb spoke by phone for the first time today. The previous phone call between the leaders of Russia and Finland took place in May 2022, when Sauli Niinisto was president of Finland. Stubb took office in early 2024. Putin last spoke by phone with Store on March 31, 2022.

title: Osman Ayariga calls for sustainable funding for youth peace initiatives
body: Chief Executive Officer of the National Youth Authority (NYA), Osman Ayariga, has called for sustainable funding, stronger institutional coordination and effective monitoring to support youth-led peacebuilding and security initiatives. Speaking at the ECOWAS Ministerial Consultation on Youth, Peace and Security in Accra on Tuesday, October 27, he said commitments to youth participation must be backed by the resources and structures needed to translate policies into meaningful results. Mr Ayariga stressed that young people needed adequate support to participate effectively in conflict prevention, peacebuilding and efforts to promote stability across Ghana and the West African sub-region. He also highlighted the importance of collaboration among government institutions, youth organisations and other stakeholders to ensure that interventions are coordinated and respond to the needs of young people and their communities. According to him, credible monitoring and accountability mechanisms would be essential to track progress, assess the impact of youth peace initiatives and ensure that resources are used effectively. He said sustained investment in youth participation would help strengthen peacebuilding efforts and support long-term stability across the region.

title: Türkiye reveals new laser weapon. Drones in the crosshairs.
body:
During the Ateş Serbest-2026 exercises, the Turkish enterprise MKE carried out the debut shoot-down of a flying unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) using a laser integrated into the Tolga anti-drone system.
The elimination of the quadcopter-type drone took place at a distance of 760 metres using a quadruple fibre laser with a total power of 20 kW (4 × 5 kW). It can engage targets in three modes: dazzling (at a range of 4,500 to 2,500 metres), sensor damage (up to 2,500 metres), and physical elimination (100–1,500 metres). Thus, this weapon can successfully complement solutions based on machine guns or small-calibre cannons.
The combat module provides 360-degree coverage, ensuring full protection of the designated area. In addition to eliminating aerial targets, it can also be used to engage land and surface objects. Its demonstration during the Ateş Serbest-2026 exercises represents another step in creating an effective anti-drone system based on several types of weaponry.
Laser weaponry also marks a significant stage in the development of Tolga itself, following the successful implementation of an acoustic detection system. The next step will be the integration of ENFAL-17 70mm rocket launchers. It is worth noting that in July, MKE demonstrated the effectiveness of the barrelled weaponry included in Tolga.
Tolga is a very short-range air defence (VSHORAD) system developed by the Turkish enterprise MKE, focused on the elimination of various types of unmanned aerial systems (UAS). It consists of combat modules equipped with M2 heavy machine guns, rotary heavy machine guns, and 20mm and 35mm revolver cannons. In addition to the command and control centre, radar, and jamming system, a single fire unit includes:
Using these, targets can be engaged at distances ranging from 1,700 to 3,000 metres. The Tolga system has an open architecture, allowing for the integration of further weapon and detection systems. MKE intends to include ENFAL-17 70mm rocket launchers, a laser with a total power of 20 kW, and an acoustic detection system. This system enables the detection and classification of aerial threats based on sound signatures and ensures the rapid transmission of collected data via radio waves to other system components.

title: 302,000 Russian soldiers killed or wounded by Ukrainian drones since January, Defense Ministry says
body:
Units of the Ukrainian Defense Forces have killed or severley wounded 302,000 Russian servicemen by using drones since January 2026, the Ukrainian Defense Ministry said on Oct. 27.
"Each defeat is recorded on video in the Delta combat system and verified by the Brave1 defense innovation cluster," the Defense Ministry said.
The Ukrainian military uses an incentive system in which the verified destruction of enemy personnel and military materiel awards combat units points that they can exchange for more drones, electronic warfare equipment, and other gear on an internal marketplace .
In September, 46,230 Russian soldiers were killed or irrecoverably wounded, according to figures published by the Ukrainian General Staff.
Of these, 32,739 were killed or wounded by drones, the figures show, amounting to about 70% of the total.
The highest number of casualties Ukrainian drones inflicted on the Russian military was recorded in March, with almost 34,000 soldiers killed or irrecoverably wounded.
Drones of various types now cause the vast majority of casualties on both sides. "The destruction of enemy manpower using UAVs helps preserve the lives of Ukrainian soldiers, making it difficult for the enemy to approach our positions," the ministry said.
The prevalence of drones from both sides has significantly changed assault tactics , making heavy equipment such as tanks a rare sight on the battlefield.
With the "kill zone" reaching 20 kilometers (12.4 miles), Russia has largely stopped using tanks or other heavy equipment for assault operations, Joint Forces Task Force spokesperson Viktor Trehubov said on Sept. 20. Drones have replaced many of the tanks' roles for both sides, since a tank driving close to the front would be easily spotted and hit by much cheaper drones.

title: Obuasi SHTS sexual abuse allegations should not define secondary education – Haruna Iddrisu
body: Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu has urged the public not to generalise about Ghana’s second-cycle education based on the sexual misconduct allegations at Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS). He said the incident should not be used to judge the standards, discipline and performance of senior high schools across the country. Speaking on Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Tuesday, October 27, Mr Iddrisu maintained that secondary education in Ghana continued to uphold discipline and established standards, despite the concerns raised by the allegations. “Let us not use the Obuasi incident to stereotype. There is everything good and well with secondary education in Ghana; there is discipline, students and teachers are keeping to the rules and standards across the country,” he said. His comments come amid public concern over allegations of sexual misconduct involving the headmaster of Obuasi SHTS, which have prompted calls for accountability and investigations into the circumstances surrounding the case. Mr Iddrisu urged the public to assess the wider secondary education sector on its overall performance rather than allowing a single case to shape perceptions of schools nationwide.

title: Youth must play meaningful role in West Africa’s peace and security – Osman Ayariga
body: Chief Executive Officer of the National Youth Authority (NYA), Osman Ayariga, has called for greater youth participation in decision-making on peace and security, insisting that young people must have a meaningful role in addressing challenges confronting Ghana and the West African sub-region. He made the call at the ECOWAS Ministerial Consultation on Youth, Peace and Security in Accra on Tuesday, October 27, where he reaffirmed Ghana’s commitment to strengthening the contribution of young people to peacebuilding and conflict prevention. Mr Ayariga said young people should not be viewed merely as beneficiaries of peace and security policies but as active partners whose ideas, leadership and experiences could help prevent conflict and promote stability. He said providing young people with opportunities to influence decisions affecting their communities would be critical to building lasting peace, particularly in a region facing security challenges that require cooperation among governments, institutions and citizens. Mr Ayariga urged stakeholders to strengthen platforms for youth engagement and ensure that young people’s contributions translate into practical measures to advance peace, security and regional development.

title: Three tankers with Russian diesel routed to the US — Novak
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Russia has recently dispatched three tankers with diesel fuel on board for exports to the United States, Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak told reporters.
"Three tankers at the moment. The fourth one has not yet departed," Novak said.

title: Rivers Police nab 5 kidnappers who lure victims through dating sites
body: By Davies Iheamnachor Operatives of the Rivers State Police Command have arrested five kidnappers who specialise in luring their victims through online dating sites. The operatives also rescued a female victim in the custody of the abductors who was lured into Port Harcourt through the online platform. The Public Relations Officer of the Command, Blessing Agabe, an Assistant Superintendent of Police, in a statement in Port Harcourt, Tuesday, said the suspects were tracked following intelligence. Agabe stated that the victim, Chinyere, came in from Delta State for a visit and was kidnapped along Igwuruta-Etche Road in Ikwerre Local Government Area of Rivers State. She said: “The Rivers State Police Command has arrested five suspected kidnappers allegedly involved in the abduction of a 24-year-old woman, one Chinyere, along the Igwuruta, Etche Road in Rivers State. “On October 4, 2026, at about 0900 hours, the Command received a complaint that one Chinyere had been kidnapped. The victim had reportedly travelled from Delta State to Port Harcourt on October 3, 2026, to visit a friend when she was abducted along the Igwirita–Etche Road. “Following the directives of the Commissioner of Police, Rivers State Police Command, CP Olugbenga A. Adepoju, psc, mnips, fcai, Upon receipt of the complaint, the operatives of the Command Violent Crime Response Unit (VCRU) Diobu immediately swung into action and arrested the perpetrators of this crime.” Agabe said that the suspects during investigation confessed to the crime, advising members of the public to be careful of dating platforms. She said: “During investigation, the suspects confessed to their involvement in the kidnapping and disclosed information about other kidnapping incidents within Igwuruta and Etche. They further disclosed that they lured victims from within and outside Port Harcourt through online dating sites before abducting them.” The post Rivers Police nab 5 kidnappers who lure victims through dating sites appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Fewer attacks, more deaths recorded in seven northern states after 2023 election – Report
body:
Recorded attacks against civilians declined slightly across seven northern Nigerian states in the six months after the 2023 presidential election, but estimated fatalities associated with those attacks increased, an analysis of conflict records by PREMIUM TIMES has found.
Data supplied by the Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED) project show that incidents classified as violence against civilians fell from 401 in the six months before the 2023 election to 383 afterwards, a decline of 4.5 per cent. Estimated fatalities, however, rose from 549 to 759, an increase of 38.3 per cent.
Most of the net increase in estimated fatalities was concentrated in Benue, where the figure rose from 111 before the election to 315 afterwards. The state’s increase of 204 accounted for almost all the net rise of 210 across the seven states.
The analysis covered Katsina, Zamfara, Sokoto, Kebbi, Kaduna, Niger and Benue. It also examined comparable periods around the 2015 and 2019 presidential elections and changes in recorded violence outside election years.
The findings describe violence recorded during selected periods. They do not establish that the elections caused the attacks or that the incidents were connected to electoral activity.
The decline in recorded incidents after the 2023 election was not uniform. Katsina recorded 93 incidents before polling day and 74 afterwards. Zamfara declined from 100 to 86, Kaduna from 72 to 56, and Kebbi from 12 to six.
Other states moved in the opposite direction. Sokoto rose from 38 incidents before the election to 58 afterwards, while Benue increased from 45 to 61. Niger remained almost unchanged, with 41 incidents before polling day and 42 afterwards.
Estimated fatalities did not follow the same pattern as incident counts. In Zamfara, they increased from 136 to 154 despite a decline in recorded incidents. Sokoto recorded an increase from 45 to 98, while Benue’s estimated fatalities rose from 111 to 315. A decline in the number of recorded attacks does not necessarily mean fewer people were killed.
ACLED’s fatality figures are estimates derived from reported incidents. They should not be treated as independently verified death counts.
PREMIUM TIMES also examined comparable periods around the 2015 and 2019 presidential elections.
In the six months before the 23 February 2019 election, ACLED recorded 83 incidents of violence against civilians across the seven states. The number increased to 147 in the equivalent period afterwards — a rise of 77.1 per cent.
The 2015 comparison showed an increase from 29 to 40 incidents.
Although recorded incidents declined slightly after the 2023 election, their number remained substantially higher than during the corresponding periods around the earlier votes. Across the combined pre- and post-election windows, ACLED recorded 69 incidents around the 2015 election, 230 around 2019, and 784 around 2023.
ACLED recorded 29 incidents before and 40 after the 2015 presidential election, 83 and 147 around the 2019 election, and 401 and 383 around the 2023 election. Each period covers 182 days, excluding election day. Differences in conflict reporting over time limit direct comparisons. [ Credit: Source: ACLED. Data analysis and graphic: PREMIUM TIMES.] These comparisons describe changes in recorded events. They do not establish that presidential elections caused the increases or declines. Changes in the availability and sources of conflict reporting over time must also be considered when interpreting differences between election years.
Katsina recorded one of the sharpest increases in the 2019 comparison.
ACLED logged 10 incidents of violence against civilians in the six months before the election and 37 afterwards. Estimated fatalities associated with those incidents rose from 16 to 161.
The post-election incidents were concentrated in three local government areas: Kankara (10), Batsari (9) and Danmusa (6). Together they accounted for 25 of the state’s 37 recorded incidents. In neighbouring Zamfara, incidents increased from 21 to 31, while estimated fatalities rose from 148 to 360. Shinkafi and Kaura Namoda accounted for eight and seven of the post-election incidents respectively.
The conflict records also show substantial changes outside presidential election years.
In Katsina, ACLED recorded 37 incidents of violence against civilians between 24 February and 24 August 2019. The equivalent 182-day period in 2020 recorded 71 incidents, while the period from 24 February to 23 August 2024 recorded 98.
Zamfara recorded 31 incidents during the 2019 period and 22 in the equivalent period in 2020. The 2024 comparison recorded 130 incidents.
Annual records also show substantially higher incident counts in later years. Across the seven states, ACLED recorded 279 incidents classified as violence against civilians in 2019, compared with 750 in 2023 and 1,192 in 2024.
These figures show that changes in recorded violence were not confined to election periods. However, the number and composition of reporting sources in the dataset also changed over time. Differences in recorded incidents cannot automatically be read as equivalent changes in the underlying level of violence.
While the ACLED records show how violence changed around the elections, reports from INEC and election observers document specific ways insecurity affected voting arrangements in Niger and Katsina states during the 2023 presidential election.
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) reported difficulties deploying personnel and materials to Alawa in Shiroro Local Government Area of Niger State. INEC Chairman Mahmood Yakubu attributed the delay to security concerns, according to an election-day report by PUNCH.
In Katsina, the commission reported the seizure of six Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices by thugs in Safana Local Government Area. Three devices were recovered and replacements deployed, Mr Yakubu said, according to Channels Television.
Election observer Yiaga Africa reported that polling units had been relocated in parts of Shiroro, Mariga, Magama and Rafi local government areas of Niger State following attacks. Its election-day situational statement raised concerns about the effect on voters’ access to polling locations.
INEC’s Report of the 2023 General Election states that special voting arrangements covered 155,101 registered voters across 323 polling units and 42 registration areas in five local government areas of Niger State affected by banditry and flooding. The commission said voting took place at established camps for internally displaced persons under security protection.
Earlier public statements gave different figures. In March 2022, officials identified 270 affected polling units across Mariga, Shiroro, Rafi and Munya. A February 2023 briefing referred to 247 or 248 units, while the final report recorded 323.
The differences may reflect changes in displacement, coverage or administrative definitions. They cannot be compared directly without the underlying schedules.
The European Union Election Observation Mission, in its report on Nigeria’s 2023 general elections, raised wider concerns about the information available to displaced voters on registration, voter cards, polling locations and the implementation of special voting arrangements.
INEC’s report records the scale of the arrangements but does not establish how many of the 155,101 registered voters were accredited or cast ballots. Determining participation would require the final polling-unit schedule, accreditation records and election results.
PREMIUM TIMES examined 17,114 ACLED conflict-event records covering Benue, Kaduna, Katsina, Kebbi, Niger, Sokoto and Zamfara. Of these, 9,354 were classified as violence against civilians.
The incident-level dataset was supplied directly by ACLED on 14 October 2026 following a request submitted on 13 October. The analysis used the event date, state, local government area, event classification and estimated fatality fields. Event identifiers were checked for duplication.
For each presidential election, incidents recorded during the 182 days before polling day were compared with those recorded during the 182 days afterwards. Election days were excluded.
2015: 27 September 2014 to 27 March 2015 and 29 March to 26 September 2015.
2019: 25 August 2018 to 22 February 2019 and 24 February to 24 August 2019.
2023: 27 August 2022 to 24 February 2023 and 26 February to 26 August 2023.
Comparable 182-day periods outside presidential election years were also examined. For the 2019 comparison, the period ran from 24 February to 24 August. In the leap years 2020 and 2024, the equivalent periods ended on 23 August to maintain the same number of days.
The analysis describes changes in recorded incidents and associated estimated fatalities. It does not establish that elections caused those changes or that the attacks were election-related.
ACLED’s records depend partly on the availability and quality of conflict reporting. Its fatality figures are estimates compiled from reported events and should not be treated as independently verified death counts.
Source: Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED), incident-level dataset supplied to PREMIUM TIMES in October 2026.

title: Licence Issuing Suspension: Investors Ask CBN to Refund N100.35m
body: Promoters of Coin Finance Company Limited have demanded the return of N100.35 million paid to the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) to operate as a finance house, following the suspension of new licence applications. A representative of the promoters, Mr Christopher Itua, made the demand in a statement, saying the funds had remained with the apex bank for about 15 months without the proposed institution progressing. According to him, the investors paid N100 million as capital deposit, N100,000 as application fee and N250,000 as licensing fee on July 16, 2025, bringing the total payment to N100.35 million. The payment was made as part of the requirements for licensing Coin Finance Company Ltd as a finance house. Itua said CBN officials informed the promoters in October 2025 that processing of new finance house applications had been suspended until further notice. He explained that following the suspension, he wrote the CBN Department of Financial Policy and Regulation on October 15, 2025, requesting the return of the funds with applicable interest. The promoters later petitioned the CBN Consumer Protection Department on May 18, 2026, and sent a follow-up letter on July 7, but said they had received neither a refund timeline nor a substantive update. “It has now been over 14 months since the CBN took possession of our capital,” Itua said in his latest appeal to the CBN Governor. He said the proposed finance house was designed to address a financing gap at the grassroots and strengthen economic activity at the micro level. “The finance house is meant to boost grassroots empowerment, a sector that is very important to strengthening the micro economy,” he said. Itua noted inadequate institutions serving small businesses and grassroots entrepreneurs remained a major constraint despite improvements in the broader macroeconomic environment. “The macro is doing well, but the micro is not. This is the missing link because there are not enough institutions to power that sector,” he said. According to him, the prolonged retention of the capital had stalled the promoters’ plans to establish the institution and provide financial support at the grassroots. The investors are asking the CBN to calculate applicable interest on the N100.35 million from July 16, 2025, when the funds were deposited, until the date of release. “The prolonged silence and structural failure to return capital deposits directly undermines the Federal Government’s ease-of-doing-business initiatives,” Itua said. The promoters said their payment receipts, transaction documents and previous correspondence had been submitted to support the request. Itua appealed to the CBN Governor to intervene and resolve the matter administratively, stressing that the promoters had repeatedly used the bank’s established channels. They said continued inaction could compel them to pursue further administrative and legal channels, although they preferred to resolve the matter without escalation. The promoters are seeking the immediate return of the N100.35 million, together with applicable interest from July 16, 2025, until the funds are released.

title: Anthropic uses its IPO letter to renew its pledge that Claude will never show ads
body:
Anthropic promises once more to keep ads out of Claude's chat. In its IPO filing cover letter , the company explains why it is passing on a potential massive revenue stream that funds much of the internet. "People bring some of their most important work and most personal questions to Claude, and we want Claude's only incentive to be giving them a helpful answer," Anthropic writes, adding that "once advertising becomes part of a company's revenue targets, the pressure to optimize for engagement tends to grow. We have chosen not to introduce that pressure into Claude." Anthropic previously criticized rival ChatGPT for running chat ads , warning they could be more manipulative than traditional ads .
The ad ban falls under the letter's second category, which puts company values above profit. As another example, Anthropic cites Claude Mythos Preview , then its most powerful model, whose advanced cyber capabilities posed high risks. Adding extra safeguards delayed its release as Claude Fable 5, costing Anthropic revenue and market share against rivals, while the company also gave cyber defenders about $100 million in free Claude credits. As future models grow stronger, Anthropic expects more decisions that forego maximum profit.

title: Russia ready to receive foreign tourists in any numbers — Foreign Ministry
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Russia is ready for a mass influx of foreign tourists and can accommodate them in any numbers, Official Spokeswoman of the Foreign Ministry Maria Zakharova said at the Russia-Africa media forum.
"Everything is ready for the influx, for the mass arrival of foreign tourists. Among other things, our domestic tourism is expanding, but we are fully prepared to welcome foreign tourists to Russia without any quantitative restrictions," she said during a meeting with African journalists at the forum.
All Russian regions have been making preparations for active negotiations aimed at developing the tourism cluster in Russia, Zakharova added.

title: EU countries to receive EUR 4.7B in reimbursement for aid to Ukraine
body:
This was reported by the EU Council press service , according to Ukrinform.
“These decisions mark a major step towards implementing the political agreement reached by EU member states on 25 September 2026 to mobilise €6.6 billion for Ukraine under the EPF,” the press service said.
The package also provides an additional €230 million in funding for the EU Military Assistance Mission in support of Ukraine (EUMAM Ukraine).
The agreement included the provision of €1 billion in new military aid to Ukraine and further reinforcement of EUMAM Ukraine in 2027
It is recalled that, following the latest decisions, the EU’s total support for Ukraine under the EPF has reached €10.8 billion. This amount includes €9.9 billion to reimburse the cost of military assistance provided by member states and €950 million for military training under the EUMAM mission.
The European Peace Facility was established in March 2021 to finance activities under the Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP). In particular, the EPF allows the EU to finance measures aimed at strengthening the defense and military capabilities of third countries, as well as regional and international organizations.
To date, the EU has provided Ukraine with €6.4 billion in support through the European Peace Facility. On September 25, 2025, EU member states agreed to mobilize a total of €6.6 billion, of which €4.9 billion was allocated through the Council decisions adopted today. The EU has also allocated €3.5 billion – extraordinary revenues generated from frozen Russian assets (so-called windfall profits) – through the European Peace Facility to address three of Ukraine’s priority needs: ammunition, air defense and drones. At the same time, military equipment worth more than €1.5 billion was procured directly from Ukraine’s defense industry.

title: Industrial Intelligence: The next growth opportunity for manufacturing
body: Every manufacturer has its own industrial intelligence. Some is documented, and some resides in the knowledge of experienced workers. Consider an experienced operator preparing to restart a line after a changeover. The machine settings matter, but so does knowing how a particular material behaves, what happened during the previous shift, and when an apparently minor variation deserves a closer look. A procedure can describe the sequence, but successful execution depends on the judgment that comes from experience and the organization’s accumulated know-how. That combination is industrial intelligence: a manufacturer’s accumulated know-how, operating practices, production data, and understanding of its own business. The opportunity now is to make more of that intelligence available wherever decisions are made, then connect it to the physical world of manufacturing. The strategic destination is not more agents, but rather to turn the existing business intelligence into an engine for profitable growth. Individual knowledge can be translated into organizational advantage Expertise has limited reach when it stays with one person, inside one system, or within one plant. Leaders now must determine how to extend that reach without stripping away the context that makes the knowledge useful. For example, an engineer evaluating a process change needs more than a production record. They need to understand the circumstances behind it: the equipment configuration, the quality requirements, and the trade-offs an operator made. Connecting those elements can help people apply experience beyond the place where it originated. When individual knowledge becomes widely accessible, innovation can spread to the maintenance workshop, the planning office, the engineering team, and the production floor. More people can contribute because more people can work with what the organization knows. But access to knowledge is only part of the opportunity. Manufacturing ultimately is physical, and it depends on materials, machines, and products. When intelligence participates in action Physical AI describes systems that can perceive conditions, reason about them, and take action within the physical world. By connecting machines and processes, manufacturers get a clearer view of what is happening on the factory floor. Agents can then reason on top of that information to identify patterns, predict problems, and determine the best course of action. Physical AI brings business intelligence into the physical process, allowing machines and systems to respond to changing conditions. Consider a robotic-handling operation encountering variation in the parts arriving at its station. Vision can help the system assess a part’s position. A model informed by the material and task can help determine an appropriate movement. Connected controls can then execute an adjustment within validated limits. The value is not merely seeing the variation; it is responding appropriately. The same principle applies to quality operations. When Toyota Industries connected previously fragmented paint shop data, engineering and operations teams were given the context needed to understand defect drivers. The company reports that analysis cycles fell from five days to under four hours, while its pilot reduced relevant paint defects by about 25%. The breakthrough was not simply identifying another signal; it was helping people understand why defects were occurring and respond before the outcome was locked in. This is the type of situation where industrial intelligence has become essential. Data may reveal what is happening, but industrial intelligence provides the context for what should happen, which constraints cannot be breached, and when uncertainty requires human judgment. Simulation offers a way to examine proposed actions before applying them to equipment. Manufacturers can explore how a change might affect a process in a digital environment. That does not remove the need for physical validation, but it creates room to learn without treating the production line as the first experiment. Responsible deployment, therefore, begins with operational discipline. Leaders need to establish clear authority or what systems may change, reliable connections to equipment, defined safety boundaries, and a record of decisions and actions. People must be able to recognize uncertainty, intervene, and bring equipment to a safe state. Trust rests on those practical arrangements, not on confidence in a model alone. More capable machines, more capable people Manufacturing has long combined human ingenuity with increasingly capable tools. Physical AI extends that relationship. Intelligent equipment can take on suitable repetitive or physically demanding tasks, while agent-assisted operations can help people navigate information-intensive decisions and changing conditions. The aim is not to make machines smarter; it is to see what people can build when knowledge can travel, intelligence can act, and ambition has more room to become reality. Rockwell Automation illustrates the point. At its Singapore plant, technicians use a maintenance copilot that combines manufacturing data, machine manuals, and knowledge captured from experienced workers. This system has reduced the time required for new workers to learn how to troubleshoot hundreds of machines from nine months to three. An engineer could explore more process alternatives before committing to a change. An operator could help improve the system’s response rather than repeatedly managing the same exception. This type of progress requires investment in equipment but also in people: training, time to learn, and playing a meaningful role in shaping how systems work. Machines become more capable so people can become more capable. Industrial Intelligence is the answer to sustainable growth Industrial intelligence connects what a manufacturer knows: the experience of its people, the signals from its operations, and the lessons accumulated over time. Physical AI gives that intelligence a way to act in the physical world, turning knowledge into decisions and decisions into action. The next challenge for industry is not simply to produce more, but to grow without adding complexity at the same rate. Intelligence can help manufacturers turn experience into scalable capability—improving productivity, accelerating innovation, expanding capacity, and enabling people to solve problems that were previously difficult to tackle. The next frontier of industry is not smarter machines or more automated factories; it is businesses that can continuously learn, adapt, and act. The opportunity is to turn the intelligence embedded in every operation into a compounding advantage for growth. Watch the video series to learn how industrial customers are unlocking intelligence across the value chain, and join Microsoft at Microsoft Ignite to see what’s next for Industrial Intelligence. title: Saab introduces Sea Giraffe AMB D naval radar with air target range of up to 250 km
body: The radar can detect, track and classify aircraft, drones, missiles and crewed or uncrewed surface vessels, according to Saab. Its three-dimensional surveillance provides early warning and target information to support decision-making in distributed, multi-domain operations. “Sea Giraffe AMB D takes a proven naval radar capability to the next level, combining increased performance with a low footprint and an architecture built for continuous development,” said Carl-Johan Bergholm, head of Saab’s Surveillance business area. “It is designed to meet the demands of today’s naval forces while giving customers the flexibility to evolve with future threats.” The design includes electronic counter-countermeasures to resist jamming and a modular architecture for integration with other naval systems. Software-defined capabilities allow upgrades as operational requirements change. Sea Giraffe AMB D builds on more than two decades of operational use of Sea Giraffe AMB radars. Saab said the new hardware, software and processing capabilities would improve air surveillance performance in demanding maritime environments.

title: Reps move to halt school fee hikes, probe 100% increases in public institutions
body: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has urged the Federal Government to suspend recent increases in school fees by public tertiary institutions across the country, warning that the hikes could undermine the objectives of the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND). The House also mandated its committees on University Education, Federal Polytechnics and Higher Technical Education, and Federal Colleges of Education to investigate the extent and justification for the fee increases. The resolutions followed a motion sponsored by Hon. Ifeoluwa Ehindero, who expressed concern that some public universities, polytechnics and colleges of education had increased their fees and other mandatory charges by more than 100 per cent. The lawmaker noted that the increases were implemented without broad consultation or adequate consideration of the prevailing economic realities facing Nigerian families. According to the motion, education remains a cornerstone of national development and a fundamental objective of state policy under Section 18 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which requires government to ensure equal and adequate educational opportunities at all levels. The House observed that NELFUND was established by the Federal Government to provide interest-free loans to students in need, enabling them to pursue tertiary education without financial barriers. However, it expressed concern that arbitrary or sudden increases in school fees could undermine the sustainability and effectiveness of the loan scheme, which was designed around existing tuition benchmarks and institutional cost structures. The lawmakers warned that unchecked increases could create disparities in the allocation of education loans and further disadvantage students from low-income households. They also cautioned that the development could lead to increased student dropouts, unrest on campuses and a loss of public confidence in the government’s commitment to affordable education. To address the situation, the House urged the Federal Government to increase financial subventions to public tertiary institutions to reduce their dependence on internally generated revenue through student charges. It also called on the Federal Ministry of Education and the National Universities Commission to engage the managements of public tertiary institutions on suspending the fee increases and conducting a comprehensive review of tuition structures in line with current economic realities. The House further directed the relevant committees to investigate the circumstances surrounding the increases and establish whether the adjustments were justified. The proposed intervention is aimed at protecting access to higher education and ensuring that rising institutional charges do not defeat the objectives of NELFUND, particularly for students from financially disadvantaged backgrounds. The post Reps move to halt school fee hikes, probe 100% increases in public institutions appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: 2027: NSCDC Warns Personnel against Election Bias, Voter Intimidation
body: . Stakeholders Task INEC to conduct free, fair, credible elections Michael Olugbode in Abuja and Ibrahim Oyewale in Lokoja The Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) has warned its personnel against voter intimidation, abuse of citizens and partisan conduct ahead of the 2027 general election, stressing that neutrality and professionalism are essential to protecting Nigerian democracy. The Commandant-General of the Corps, Prof. Ahmed Audi, gave the warning in Abuja while opening a three-day workshop designed to prepare security personnel for election-related duties. This is just as stakeholders in Kogi State have unanimously tasked the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to conduct free, fair and credible elections in 2027 Audi cautioned officers and men of the agency against abandoning their duty posts or obeying unlawful orders, insisting that their overriding responsibility must be to the national interest and the protection of citizens’ democratic rights. The workshop brought together 216 personnel drawn from the 36 state commands, the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) and 18 zonal Commands to strengthen their understanding of the legal, operational and supervisory responsibilities of security agencies during elections. Organised in collaboration with Alnas Consulting Limited, the workshop was built on the theme: ‘Role of Security Agencies in the Conduct of the General Elections in Nigeria: Legal, Field Conduct, Supervisory and Operational Perspectives’. The Commandant-General’s warning came as preparations gather pace for the 2027 elections, with security agencies expected to play a critical role in ensuring that voters can exercise their franchise without intimidation, harassment or undue interference. In his welcome address, the Chief Responsibility Officer of Alnas Consulting Limited, Prof. Nasirdeen Usman, described the NSCDC as a critical component of Nigeria’s security architecture and urged participants to share the knowledge acquired with colleagues in their respective commands. The event also featured goodwill messages from representatives of the Inspector-General of Police, the Director-General of the Department of State Services, the Controller-General of Corrections, the Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Immigration Service and the Chief Executive Officer of TAF Africa, Dr Jake Ekpelle. The NSCDC reiterated its commitment to peaceful elections, effective cooperation among security agencies and the protection of the democratic rights of Nigerians. Meanwhile, stakeholders in Kogi State have unanimously tasked the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to conduct free, fair and credible elections in 2027. This was contained in a communique issued at the end of the critical stakeholders’ meeting held at the headquarters of INEC in Lokoja yesterday. The stakeholders also agreed that INEC shall adequately supply the political parties and their candidates with useful information as far as the 2027 general election is concerned. On security matters, the stakeholders noted that the police shall treat all the candidates equally as far as elections matter is concerned in Kogi State. It was pointed out that all the perpetrators of violent attacks recently be brought to book with immediate effect. They also stated that all candidates and their party leadership shall conduct their political campaigns in accordance with the law and regulations on election matters, and candidates of political parties shall cooperate with INEC and obtain permission from security agencies before going about campaigns. “Candidates of all political parties shall ensure the safety of all the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members participating in the general election. Each political party shall cooperate with security agencies,” the communique stressed. Earlier, the Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC), Dr. Shehu Wahab, explained that the commission is poised to conduct free, fair and credible elections in 2027. Also, the state Commissioner of Police, Naziru Kankafori, stressed that the security agencies would provide enabling environment for the conduct of violence-free elections in Kogi State.

title: IPOB declares total boycott of APC over delays in listing Nnamdi Kanu’s appeal
body: . Accuses FG of frustrating hearing, demands leader’s release By Steve Oko The Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) has declared a total political boycott of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), accusing the Federal Government of frustrating the appeal of its detained leader, Nnamdi Kanu, against his conviction. The pro -Biafra movement said it would boycott APC’s rallies and reject its insignia until Kanu’s appeal is listed for hearing, declaring: “No listing, no participation.” In a statement issued by its Media and Publicity Secretary, Emma Powerful, IPOB accused the government of failing to facilitate the hearing of the appeal against the November 20, 2025 judgment, alleging that the case remained unlisted and that the government had yet to file its respondent’s brief. The group argued that the appeal raised fundamental constitutional questions concerning Kanu’s conviction under a law it claims had been repealed. It urged the relevant authorities to ensure that the appeal proceeds, insisting that the courts should determine the legal issues rather than allow procedural delays to persist. IPOB also raised concerns over what it described as the disappearance of the court file relating to Kanu’s alleged 14-month detention without trial following his discharge by the Court of Appeal on October 13, 2022. The group called for the restoration of the file and accused the authorities of frustrating efforts to secure judicial redress. Beyond Kanu’s legal battle, IPOB accused the Federal Government of applying double standards in its security operations, alleging that military operations, arrests and detentions targeted at people in the South-East contrasted with the handling of armed groups in other parts of the country. The group also criticised former Ebonyi State Governor and Minister of Works, David Umahi, over his role in the 2017 decision by South-East governors to proscribe IPOB, alleging that the move contributed to subsequent security crackdowns in the region. It further warned South-East politicians aligned with the APC against what it described as sacrificing the interests of the Igbo people for political benefits. IPOB, however, directed its supporters to pursue the boycott peacefully, warning against harassment or threats against citizens because of their political affiliations. Reiterating its position, the group demanded Kanu’s immediate and unconditional release, the listing of his appeal and the restoration of the allegedly missing court file. The APC and the Federal Government had yet to respond to the allegations contained in the statement as of the time of filing this report. The post IPOB declares total boycott of APC over delays in listing Nnamdi Kanu’s appeal appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Stubb and Store did not coordinate phone talk with Putin with Europeans — Danish PM
body:
STOCKHOLM, October 27. /TASS/. The phone conversation between Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store with Russian leader Vladimir Putin was not coordinated with European allies, Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said.
"I am very skeptical about this independent initiative of Norway and Finland. It is not coordinated with any of us," the DR radio station quoted her as saying.
Earlier, the office of the Finnish leader said that Stubb and Store acted as representatives of their countries, not Europe in a conversation with Putin.
Frederiksen also disagreed with Stubb and Store’s position.
"I really don't understand what these two countries think can be achieved this way. We also clearly emphasized earlier in messages from the rest of Europe that when others go to Moscow alone, for example, it is important that we, Europeans, travel together," she said in an interview with TV 2.

title: 1 dead, 15 injured as Russia strikes university and surrounding area in Kyiv
body:
Five of the injured are students or university staff, Zelenskyy said.
LONDON -- A Russian attack on the Ukrainian capital, Kyiv, killed at least one and injured another 15, according to Ukrainian officials.
Ballistic missiles hit crowded areas where there are no military facilities nearby, causing "extensive" damage, hitting a university campus and the South bridge amongst other urban structures, Kyiv said.
Five of the injured are students or members of the university's staff, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. The number of injured climbed to 15 on Tuesday, the State Emergency Service of Ukraine said.
The strike on Monday was described by Ukraine as an attack on its civilian infrastructure, which it continues to say is threatened by delays in the delivery of defense munitions.
"The artificial and prolonged delays in the delivery of interceptor packages for Patriot and NASAMS systems, which unfortunately have occurred recently, are directly helping Russia achieve the objectives of its terrorist campaign," Zelenskyy said on Tuesday on his social media account.
Russia launched 16 ballistic missiles, two of which Ukraine shot down, Kyiv said. The attack also included at least 255 drones, according to the Ukrainian Armed Forces.
Russia's Ministry of Defense said its military had targeted Ukraine overnight with a "massive" strike aimed at the Ukrainian defense industry and "transport infrastructure" in Kyiv.
The ministry said in a post on Telegram that it struck "an industrial enterprise producing and storing long- and medium-range unmanned aerial vehicles" in the Ukrainian capital.
In Desnyans'kyi District, where the University stands, five of the victims are students and university staff, officials said.
One of those injured is a 20-year-old woman, who has been hospitalized, according to Kyiv’s Mayor Vitali Klitschko. The strike also damaged part of the campus, Kyoto Park, a nearby metro station and residential buildings.
Rescue operations are underway as there are reports that people may be trapped under the rubble.
There were also strikes on Ukrainian cities: Vinnytsia, Zaporizhzhia, Dnipro, Kharkiv, Odesa, Chernihiv, Sumy, Donetsk, Kherson, and Chernivtsi, wrote Zelenskyy. Missiles targeted energy infrastructure, logistics centers, and urban facilities, Kyiv said.
"Pressure on Russia and real support for Ukraine are needed to change the situation," wrote Zelenskyy.

title: ‘We no longer sleep with two eyes closed’ — Nasarawa lawmaker laments kidnappings
body: By Edwin Philip, Lafia Member representing the Lafia Central constituency at the Nasarawa State House of Assembly, Hon. Solomon Yakubu Akwashiki, has said that the people of his constituency cannot longer sleep with their two eyes closed due to the frequent abduction of the people in the constituency. The lawmaker, while raising the issue on the floor of the House on Tuesday as a matter of public interest, urged the security agencies and the state government to be more committed to protecting the lives and property of its citizens. He said, “Mr Speaker and my honourable colleagues, I rise on a matter of frequent kidnapping in my constituency. “Yesterday, in Agyaragu Lafia, two people were kidnapped. Days back, in Agunji Lafia, people were kidnapped. “As I am talking, the two people kidnapped yesterday are in the hands of the kidnappers, and they are demanding ransom. “Security agencies and the state government should rise up to curtail the rate of kidnapping and other forms of insecurity in my constituency,” he appealed. Reacting to the alarm over a fresh resurgence of kidnapping incidents across the State, the Speaker of the House, Dr Danladi Jatau, said that the State capital and some parts of the State are experiencing frequent abductions that have caused fear and economic setbacks to the State. The speaker appreciated the mover of the motion and other colleagues for their positive contributions on the issue. “The resolution of the House is to the effect that we urge His Excellency, Gov. Abdullahi Sule, to direct all security agencies, the Commissioner of Police, and the DSS and NSCDC to beam their satellites across the state to curtail the rate of kidnapping. “All hands must be on deck, especially Chiefs and Village Heads, in collaboration with Vigilantes to identify strange people in their communities,” he said. The Speaker directed the Clerk of the House to communicate the House resolution to Gov. Sule for his necessary action. Also contributing, Hon. Esson Mairiga Esq, Hon. Onarigu Onah Kana, Hon. Ibrahim Abdullahi Sa’ad, Hon. Suleiman Yakubu Azara, Rt Hon. Abel Yakubu Bala and Hon. Larry Ven-Bawa supported the motion and called on the state government to beef up security across the state in order to curtail the rate of kidnapping in the state. They lamented how kidnapping is affecting the lives of their people negatively. The lawmakers, however, appreciated the efforts of Gov. Sule in terms of security but urged him and security agencies to be more committed to tackling the rate of kidnapping across the state. The lawmakers collectively called on security agencies to intensify operations. They called on both the federal and state governments to purchase sophisticated weapons via technology to tackle insecurity in the state.
