title: Kyiv's Prospekt mall slightly damaged, open - Arricano
body:
The Prospekt shopping and entertainment center in Kyiv, owned by Arricano, suffered minor damage in a Russian strike overnight on Tuesday, the company's press service told Interfax-Ukraine.
"As a result of the enemy attack on Kyiv on October 27, the Prospekt shopping center was damaged. The shopping gallery suffered minor damage and is operating as usual. The Auchan Ukraine hypermarket is temporarily closed today," the company said.
Arricano suspended operation of its City Mall in Zaporizhia in early September, citing the current security situation, after it was significantly damaged in a Russian strike, and said it plans to restore it.
Russian drones struck the Sonyachna Galereya mall in Kryvyi Rih twice on August 21, killing 16 people and injuring 130.
Overnight on July 19, another massive Russian missile strike on Kyiv damaged the construction site of a shopping and entertainment center in Lukianivka that is being built by Arricano. There were no casualties.
Arricano Real Estate PLC (Cyprus) owns four shopping centers in Ukraine through its Ukrainian subsidiaries: Prospekt and RaiON in Kyiv, City Mall in Zaporizhia and Sonyachna Galereya in Kryvyi Rih. It also owns 49.9% of Sky Mall in Kyiv and land plots for the further construction of three facilities that are at the design stage. The company is also building the Lukianivka shopping and entertainment center in Kyiv.

title: FC Ashantigold 04 dismisses head coach Karim Zito
body: FC Ashantigold 04 have dismissed head coach Abdul Karim Zito, assistant coach Ernest Okyere and goalkeeper’s trainer Robert Dabo with immediate effect. The Obuasi-based club announced the decision in a statement on Tuesday, October 27, following a consultative meeting by the Interim Management Committee. The club added that a caretaker coach would take charge of the team until a substantive head coach and technical director is appointed. “Subsequently, a caretaker Coach has been appointed to steer the affairs of the team until the appointment of a substantive Coach/Technical Director. “Management wishes to express our deepest gratitude to the affected officials for their contribution and service to the team thus far, and wishes them the best in their subsequent endeavours.” Zito joined the Division One League side in February 2026, 15 days after resigning from Asante Kotoko, where he had been in charge at the time. The former Dreams FC coach subsequently guided Ashantigold to promotion to the Ghana Premier League. However, the club have endured a mixed start to the 2026/27 campaign, recording three wins, three defeats and two draws in their opening eight matches. Ashantigold currently sit 11th on the league table with 11 points.

title: Tinubu approves 500,000 solar lights for S’East households — Deputy Speaker, Kalu
body: By Steve Oko Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, has said President Bola Tinubu has approved the provision of 500,000 solar-powered lights for rural households in the South-East. Kalu disclosed this at the flag-off of the Renewed Hope Light-Up initiative, during which 26 transformers and 10,000 solar-powered lights and fans were distributed to communities in Bende Federal Constituency, Abia State. He said 42,000 households in the constituency had been earmarked to benefit from the initiative, with the first batch of 10,000 solar-powered lights and fans expected to be delivered within two weeks. According to him, 1,000 units had already been distributed as a pilot scheme, with representatives from the federal constituency’s wards confirming their functionality. Kalu said the initiative was designed to make the benefits of the Renewed Hope Agenda tangible to rural residents, particularly households that had struggled with unreliable electricity supply. He described the planned provision of solar-powered lights to 42,000 households in a single federal constituency as unprecedented, adding that the initiative would help improve access to electricity in underserved communities. The lawmaker representing Bende South Constituency in the Abia State House of Assembly, Emmanuel Ndubuisi, described the intervention as significant, noting that some communities had been without electricity for about two years following transformer failures. A representative of the project contractor, Solar Systems Nigeria, Peter Oko, said the initiative would also provide opportunities for youth training and empowerment. He assured beneficiaries of the company’s commitment to delivering quality and reliable services. Earlier, Director-General of the Ben Kalu Campaign Council, Emma Trump Eke, described the intervention as a landmark project for Bende Federal Constituency. The post Tinubu approves 500,000 solar lights for S’East households — Deputy Speaker, Kalu appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: 2027: APC defends Tinubu’s Kaduna rally speech, says appearance did the job
body: By Ayobami Okerinde The All Progressives Congress (APC) has defended President Bola Tinubu’s speech at its campaign rally in Kaduna, saying his presence at the event was enough to achieve its purpose. The party’s National Publicity Secretary, Felix Morka, said Tinubu did not need to deliver an elaborate speech at the rally, arguing that the event was primarily meant to bring party supporters together and acknowledge their support ahead of the 2027 presidential election. Morka spoke on ARISE News on Tuesday while responding to a question about whether the president’s speech at Saturday’s rally was flat. He said, “All the president needed to do was to show up and say to the people in Kaduna, ‘Thank you for your hospitality, I appreciate your support, please do so again in 2027.’ If that’s all he said, he did the job.” He added, “A campaign rally of that kind in Kaduna is not a policy dialogue where speeches should be given. Even if the president came there and danced and said to the people, ‘I appreciate you, thank you so much,’ and left the stage, he had done the job.” Morka said those who organised the rally were best placed to assess its success, adding that the event was designed to bring together party members, leaders, supporters and other well-wishers to welcome the president. The APC held the rally in Kaduna on Saturday, October 24, as part of its mobilisation campaign ahead of the 2027 general elections, with the state among those Tinubu is expected to visit. At the rally, Tinubu criticised opposition figures who had blamed his administration for hunger and poverty in the country. “I hear my opponents talking about hunger and poverty. Who created it? They did. They created the hunger. They created the poverty we are trying to eradicate,” Tinubu said. He also defended his administration’s record, saying, “We pay salaries regularly. Our governors are working. I am proud of them. They are developing.” Tinubu urged supporters to back his bid for a second term, promising “prosperity, continuity, progress and development.” “To you, the children of our country, it is a promise of second-term prosperity. You will not regret going to vote,” he said. The post 2027: APC defends Tinubu’s Kaduna rally speech, says appearance did the job appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Inside the Skyrian House, Where Skyros Keeps Its Folk Art Alive
body: The traditional Skyrian house, rarely larger than 50 square metres, holds the family memory, folk art and creativity of an entire Greek island. Known as an island of open-hearted, hospitable people, Skyros has a way of winning visitors over from the first moments. Its charm lies in simplicity, authenticity and devotion to tradition. Locals respect their land and rich heritage. However, they have not turned either into a tourism marketing tool. Instead, both give meaning to everyday life across generations. In particular, the Skyrian house offers the clearest proof of that spirit. It is more than a fine example of folk architecture , because it works as a remarkable world in miniature. Why the Skyrian house is a living archive Behind its whitewashed walls, the Skyrian house keeps family memory, folk crafts and refined taste alive. So do the customs and stories that define the island. Two authentic homes in Chora, the island’s main town, show how this works in practice. The first is the Municipal Skyrian Traditional House, which siblings Maria and Andreas Gialouris donated to the local Municipality . Its owners still live in the second, which remains fully functional. Inside, visitors discover how few square metres each home covers. They also see how the heritage of a whole island fits within a single Skyrian house. Pirate lanes and narrow façades Reaching the houses takes a steep climb. Chora clings to a towering rock, and its winding lanes rise in endless flights of steps. Locals call these cobbled uphill alleys the piratika, or ‘pirate lanes’. During frequent raids, they led residents to the safety of the old fortified acropolis while confusing the invaders. The tightly packed homes still form what looks like an impenetrable web. Their façades are so narrow that they resemble dolls’ houses. Shaped like an amphitheatre, Chora also hides behind its imposing rock. As a result, the settlement stays invisible from the sea. Four levels in 45 square metres The two homes face each other. Although they come from different eras and serve different roles, they look strikingly alike. As a rule, a traditional Skyrian house measures between 30 and 50 square metres. Within that limit, its rooms rise vertically over at least two levels. One of the two homes has a façade just 1.5 metres wide. Even so, its 45 square metres stretch across four levels, with a sitting room and a fully working kitchen. The layout follows a clear pattern. Guests gather in the sitting room, while an open loft, the sfas, serves as the children’s bedroom. Directly beneath it sits the apokrevates, the couple’s bedroom. A carved wooden panel known as the bulmes gives this room its privacy. Carved bulmes and miniature furniture Each bulmes showcases the island’s remarkable tradition of wood carving . Despite passing trends, the craft continues to the present day thanks to the passion and dedication of talented craftsmen. Similarly, the ornate carved furniture is almost miniature, so it takes up minimal room. Stools, chairs and cedar chests called tsedrana all follow this rule. Still, each piece carries finely worked patterns. These details reflect the taste of the makers and of the families who chose them. Ceramics and embroidery in every Skyros home Ceramics, weavings and embroidery each play a double role. They carry the culture and traditions of Skyros, yet remain in daily use in the Skyrian house. Copper vessels hang below wooden shelves lined with ceramic plates and jugs. They are the pride of every homemaker, especially the palaia, or ‘old ones’, handed down from earlier generations. Those heirlooms take the most prominent spot, either in the sitting room or by the fgou, the fireplace of the Skyrian house. Every household has plates in the popular agalipa design and the kastriana. It also keeps krasokanata, wine jugs that mark weddings, births and New Year celebrations. Decorative jugs called fyrfyrenia and large water jars known as kryologoi complete the collection. The oath embroidery and a living heritage Embroidery , another remarkable folk craft, holds an equally honoured place. Its motifs carry rich symbolism and often draw on the plants and animals of Skyros. One piece stands out, often framed in a place of honour: the kentima tou orkou, or ‘oath embroidery’. Its geometric design depends on counting every stitch for absolute precision. The work proved so difficult that each woman who finished one swore she would never embroider it again. Overall, the number of small treasures in a Skyrian house is striking. Elsewhere, such objects might serve only as decoration. Here, they express the inventiveness, taste and skill of the islanders. Nor are these crafts a nostalgic nod to the past. Instead, they remain a living heritage, guarded with love inside the Skyrian house so that the next generation can receive it. The layout, furniture and household objects tell of the habits, needs and values of older generations. In this way, each home reveals the way of life that shaped it. Finally, the beauty of Skyros, an island of simplicity, quality and authenticity, lies not only in its landscape. It also shines through in the way its people live, create and brighten their everyday lives. title: Court awards $1.4m to shooting victims outside ex-spy chief’s home
body: A court in South Sudan has awarded $1,455,180 in compensation to a man and a woman injured in a shooting outside the Juba residence of former National Security Service (NSS) Internal Security Bureau Chief General Akol Koor Kuc, following a civil lawsuit against the Ministry of Defence and Veteran Affairs. The judgment was delivered on Tuesday by Justice Ajok Tito Telar, a First Grade County Court judge exercising the powers of a High Court. Representatives of the ministry were absent when the judgment was delivered. The plaintiffs’ lawyer, Angelo Thon Pal, said the court awarded Manawa Gabriel Makwach $274,180 for medical expenses and property losses, including his personal car, as well as $800,000 in moral damages. Agum Andrea was awarded $81,000 for medical expenses and other losses, plus $300,000 in moral damages. The total monetary award is $1,455,180, excluding court and legal fees. Pal said the court also ordered the ministry to pay Makwach 30 head of cattle in accordance with customary tradition, following a medical assessment that found he had sustained a 60% disability. Pal welcomed the judgment, describing it as fair and just, and thanked the judiciary for ruling in favour of the plaintiffs. The case stemmed from a shooting on November 21, 2024, in which Makwach and Andrea were injured while travelling in their vehicles. Speaking after the verdict, Andrea urged the Ministry of Defence to pay the compensation without further delay. She said they had previously engaged with a committee established after the incident but had received no compensation despite submitting files to the relevant authorities. They subsequently sought redress through the courts. “We appeal to the Ministry again that, regardless of where they are, in an urgent way, they intervene and try to see the necessary compensation,” Andrea said. Makwach said he sustained serious injuries, including a broken jaw, and underwent several operations in Juba and Egypt. He said he still needed further medical treatment. He described the judgment as a victory for justice and thanked the judges for ruling in the plaintiffs’ favour. Pal said the plaintiffs had initially pursued the matter through the Ministry of Justice and Constitutional Affairs, which notified the defence ministry of the intended legal proceedings. He said the defence ministry’s legal department had not cooperated with the process, adding that his clients subsequently obtained permission to sue under Section 33(2) of the Code of Civil Procedures Act, 2007. Pal said the next step would be to open an execution file through the court, after which the ministry would be summoned to enforce the judgment. He said the court has mechanisms to enforce its decisions if the ministry failed to comply and expressed confidence that the government institution would respect the ruling. title: Yobe Govt Vaccinates 43,720 Children Against Poliomyelitis
body: The Yobe State government has vaccinated 43,720 children against poliomyelitis during the 2026 supplementary immunisation activities that targeted responses to close immunity gaps across the 17 local government areas of the state. The Commissioner for Health, represented by the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry, Hadiza Sabo, disclosed this at the commemoration of World Polio Day in Damaturu, the state capital. Sabo explained that the figures demonstrate the scale of mobilization and delivery, with vaccination figures above 100 percent, which remind them of the importance of validating target populations and microplanning denominators. “We must use data not only to report progress, but to identify gaps, improve the accuracy of planning, follow up the seven settlements reported as unreached and ensure that every eligible child is accounted for” “These achievements belong to the collective effort of our health teams, community mobilisers, supervisors, surveillance officers, data teams, local government authorities and partners. I particularly acknowledge the commitment of our Royal Fathers, traditional rulers, district and ward heads, religious leaders and community influencers,” she said. The Permanent Secretary, however, adds that the progress made should not be allowed to create a false sense of security, stressing that the remaining rounds of the polio campaigns scheduled for November and December 2026 are critical opportunities to consolidate the gains achieved this year and close the outstanding immunity gaps. “I solicit renewed operational resources, timely mobilization, quality data and, reliable vaccine and cold-chain arrangements, strong social mobilization, quality data and prompt follow-up of missed children and unreached settlements” In his remarks, the State Coordinator of the World Health Organisation, Hamisu Alhassan, charged all parents to ensure their children are taken to the nearest health facility for routine immunization and other essential health services, saying they should not wait for campaigns before protecting their children from the diseases. The post Yobe Govt Vaccinates 43,720 Children Against Poliomyelitis appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Two men charged under UK’s National Security Act over RAF Fairford incident
body: Two men have been charged by British authorities under the UK’s National Security Act over an incident at the Royal Air Force’s (RAF) Fairford airbase in Gloucestershire in September 2026. The investigation was launched after five men were arrested near to RAF Fairford, following reports of suspicious vehicles on September 27, 2026. On October 27, 2026, Counter Terrorism Policing confirmed that Nouman Essghir, 24, a British national from London, was charged with entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the UK, for suspected activity on August 22, 2026. Essghir was first arrested at the incident scene in Gloucestershire on September 27, 2026, and re-arrested on October 20, 2026. A second man, described by police as a 25-year-old dual UK/Iranian national, was also re-arrested on October 20, 2026, and has been released without charge. He remains on police bail following his first arrest on October 1, 2026. In its statement on October 27, 2026, terrorism police said that following the re-arrest of these individuals, detectives also interviewed a further man under caution. As a result, Mohammed Abdul Karim, a 24-year-old British national, also from London, has been charged under Section 3 of the National Security Act 2023, which makes it an offence to assist a foreign intelligence service. “In this case, we believe that country to be Iran,” Head of UK National Counter Terrorism Policing, Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, said. Five other men arrested in connection with the RAF Fairford investigation, remain on police bail. “We have seen a range of incidents in recent months that we believe have been directed by the Iranian state, and as the Director General of Mi5 said just the other week, we are working together to intervene, identify and respond to that threat,” Assistant Commissioner Taylor added. Essghir and Karim will both appear at Westminster Magistrates Court on October 27, 2026. title: Kremlin Woos Trump’s Circle With Business Deals – Le Monde
body:
The Kremlin is courting US President Donald Trump and his inner circle with economic deals before the war against Ukraine ends, while proposals presented to Ukrainian officials in Florida on Friday, Oct. 9, reportedly raised concerns in Kyiv.
According to Le Monde, which cited a diplomat based in Moscow, Russia is seeking to advance business cooperation without first agreeing to a ceasefire.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Kirill Dmitriev, head of the Russian Direct Investment Fund, is leading the effort, promoting potential deals in energy, civilian aviation, rare earth metals, artificial intelligence, and technology.
The newspaper reported that a ceasefire had previously been treated as a prerequisite for restoring US-Russian economic relations, but that condition has now appeared to have been effectively dropped.
During the Florida talks, Trump’s special envoy Steve Witkoff presented Ukrainian negotiators with a postwar “regional prosperity plan” involving Ukraine, Europe, and Russia, according to the report.
The proposal envisaged fully restoring supplies of Russian oil and gas to Europe through Ukrainian territory.
Ukrainian delegates were concerned by similarities between the American proposals and Dmitriev’s ideas for economic cooperation with Russia, the newspaper said.
In a separate report published on Thursday, Oct. 22, Le Monde described Dmitriev’s efforts to attract businessmen close to Trump with energy and Arctic investments.
Speaking at a Moscow forum on Oct. 16, Dmitriev promoted “projects in the Arctic, energy projects, LNG projects, and many other things,” the newspaper stated.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Jay-Z Announced As Super Bowl LXI Halftime Show Headliner
body: Rapper, entrepreneur, and record executive Shawn “Jay-Z” Carter will headline the Super Bowl LXI halftime show in February 2027, the National Football League (NFL) has officially announced. The performance at SoFi Stadium near Los Angeles will mark the first time Carter, 56, takes the stage as the main act for the annual championship game, despite his entertainment company, Roc Nation, having executive produced the halftime showcase since entering into a strategic partnership with the NFL in 2019. Next year’s Super Bowl is scheduled for 14 February 2027. The official booking comes on the heels of two sold-out stadium concerts by Carter in Los Angeles, held as part of a tour celebrating the 30th anniversary of his seminal 1996 debut album, Reasonable Doubt . Reflecting on his journey from releasing his independent debut album three decades ago to securing the world’s most-watched musical stage, the 24-time Grammy Award winner described the upcoming performance as a monumental career milestone: “From ‘Reasonable Doubt’ to standing on the Super Bowl halftime stage, this has been a journey,” Carter said in a statement. “Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world’s biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true.” Who Is Jay-Z? From Brooklyn To Global Mainstream For casual viewers and new audiences unfamiliar with his extensive discography, Jay-Z is one of the most commercially successful and culturally influential figures in modern music history. Emerging from Brooklyn, New York, in the mid-1990s, he built a career spanning 14 number-one albums on the Billboard 200 chart—the most by any solo artist in history. Throughout the 2000s and 2010s, his mainstream catalogue produced global chart-topping anthems including “Empire State of Mind” (featuring Alicia Keys), “99 Problems”, and “Hard Knock Life”. He has also featured on major international pop hits alongside his wife, Beyoncé, including “Crazy in Love” and “Drunk in Love”, as well as co-starring on Rihanna’s 2007 global breakthrough single “Umbrella”. Beyond his musical career, Carter’s business enterprise extends into sports agency management, media streaming, luxury goods, and corporate investments, establishing him as a prominent figure across global entertainment and corporate leadership. The Corporate Partnership And Halftime Legacy The Super Bowl halftime show remains one of the most-watched live musical broadcasts globally, attracting over 100 million television viewers in the United States alone and tens of millions more on digital platforms. In 2019, the NFL partnered with Roc Nation to oversee the league’s live music strategy and social justice entertainment initiatives. Since the partnership began, Roc Nation has curated halftime performances featuring Shakira, Jennifer Lopez, The Weeknd, Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg, Eminem, Rihanna, Usher, Kendrick Lamar, and Bad Bunny. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell noted that convincing Carter to perform personally was a long-standing objective since the corporate alliance was formed. “When we first reached an agreement with Roc Nation to produce the show, I had just one request: that Jay-Z take the stage himself one day, whenever the moment felt right to him,” Goodell said in an official statement. Addressing widespread public speculation regarding potential guest appearances, the NFL highlighted the anticipation surrounding who might join the hip-hop icon on stage in Los Angeles: “Anticipation as to who Jay-Z might have guest star at halftime for the big game will now kick off,” the NFL stated. “Of course, his wife, Beyoncé, will be atop the list.” Production and creative planning for the 14 February 2027 broadcast are slated to begin in late 2026. title: Guns fall silent around Russian-occupied Oleshky so its starving residents can get aid, but Russia’s guarantees remain secret
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); A ceasefire around Russian-occupied Oleshky in Kherson Oblast took effect at 03:00 on 27 October Kyiv time, and both sides were complying with the agreements, Ukraine’s human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets said . Russia’s Defense Ministry reported that its forces had stopped firing on the Kherson axis at 04:00 Moscow time, at the same moment. Russia has kept Oleshky cut off for months. In June, the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine documented worsening shortages of food, medicine, and medical care there and in neighboring Hola Prystan. As of 8 October, Lubinets’ office still saw no practical breakthrough toward an organized evacuation, with 358 residents verified as needing help to leave. The ceasefire is the first step that has to hold before aid can go in and residents can leave, an operation Marc Beckman, the first lady’s chief adviser, expects to take five to seven days. By 09:00 on 27 October, Russian forces were still observing the ceasefire, according to Pavlo Drohal, spokesperson for Ukraine’s 30th Marine Corps. Kyrylo Budanov, head of the Presidential Office, announced that the mission had begun and that Lubinets had gone to the site to coordinate it. Ceasefire planned for occupied Oleshky as residents face starvation and blocked escape routes, White House announces Ceasefire brought forward by two days The White House announced on 23 October that First Lady Melania Trump had secured a localized ceasefire, set to begin on 29 October. The same evening, Russia’s chief of General Staff Valery Gerasimov announced a ceasefire on the Kherson axis from 27 October, with engineering reconnaissance and a secured route for a humanitarian convoy. Ukraine’s General Staff followed , introducing a ceasefire in a designated area from the same hour. Beckman told Ukrinform on 26 October that Russia had moved the ceasefire two days earlier and extended it beyond Oleshky into Kherson Oblast. Lubinets said on 23 October that the mission should effectively begin on 29 October, after demining, adding that the date was not a matter of principle for either side. People in Oleshky wait for food supplies. Photo: BBC A day after the announcement, Lubinets and his Russian counterpart Yana Lantratova, who lead the two negotiating groups, confirmed the timing in an online meeting, he said . According to Lubinets, the agreement covers demining the road to Oleshky, delivering food, water, medicine, and hospital equipment, and safe movement for civilians. Newsmax to document the operation Meanwhile, Melania Trump said she had secured an “impartial American media organization” to accompany the Russian and Ukrainian teams. Beckman named it as Newsmax. He said he had worked directly with the channel’s owner, and that its journalists would record testimony as what he called neutral American observers. Residents could leave for Ukraine or Russia, or stay, Beckman said. He added that Russia had assured Kyiv and Washington it would respect their choice of destination. Both governments asked him not to disclose what guarantees Russia gave or how violations would be handled, he said. He expects the operation to take five to seven days after 29 October, with an extension possible if both sides agree. Diplomat doubts the truce will move peace talks At the same time, Kostiantyn Yelisieiev, Ukraine’s ambassador to the EU in 2010–2015, told Radio NV the truce became possible only through the personal involvement of Donald and Melania Trump. The US president, he said, sees it as a way to show Americans he is bringing peace closer. He said he expects Russia to attempt provocations aimed at pushing residents toward the Russian side. Yelisieiev said he does not share the optimism of those who think Oleshky could push the wider peace process forward. He compared it to the Black Sea grain corridor, a one-off arrangement that no longer works. He warned of a “diplomatic smokescreen” : Russia imitates negotiations while it keeps fighting, hoping Ukraine and its partners weaken over time. Ukrainian drone delivering aid to occupied Oleshky on the night of 4 October. Screenshot from video: Ivan Vyhivskyi / Facebook A town under blockade Oleshky lies on the left bank of the Dnipro, about 4 km from Kherson, and has been occupied since February 2022, Radio Svoboda reported . The White House says it had about 24,000 residents before the war and estimates 1,700 to 2,000 remain, mostly elderly, including about 50 children. Russian troops have also seized food dropped by Ukrainian drones, a local official said. title: Remembering Adnan Kivan: a Legacy With a Future
body:
Two years have passed since Adnan Kivan left us on Oct. 27. I write this as the Chief Executive Officer of the Kyiv Post, but also as someone who misses a trusted friend and mentor.
Whenever we discussed why he bought the newspaper in 2018, he returned to the same principles: defending democracy, protecting free expression, and standing against totalitarianism.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
I believed in his sincerity, but I also owe him an honest admission. Having spent decades in advertising and communications, I had grown used to business leaders speaking about purpose in grand, inspiring terms. Part of me wondered whether these were simply noble ideals – larger than what any single individual or publication could realistically deliver. Only after his passing did I realize how deeply personal those words were.
I eventually learned more about the experiences that shaped Adnan’s youth in Syria: his involvement in student opposition to the Assad regime, the exile that followed, and the terrible price his family paid, with 27 relatives kidnapped, tortured, or killed. That history changed how I understood our conversations.
When Adnan spoke about authoritarianism, he was not debating political theory; he was speaking from direct, painful experience. When he spoke about freedom, he understood intimately what its absence cost.
He saw that same spirit in Ukraine. He recognized the demand for human dignity among the Ukrainians who stood on the Maidan, insisting that their voices mattered and their future was theirs to decide.
Adnan had arrived in Ukraine as a student and built a remarkable life here. Through KADORR Group, he became one of the country’s most successful business leaders. Yet Ukraine was far more to him than a place of business – it was the home where he raised his family and planted his roots.
Adnan Kivan (L) and CEO Luc Chénier (Photo by Kyiv Post) Advertisement
Adnan Kivan (L) and CEO Luc Chénier (Photo by Kyiv Post)
That success brought a quiet obligation to give back: supporting charitable initiatives, aiding Ukrainian defenders, and investing in independent media platforms, including Channel 7, USI News, and Kyiv Post.
When he bought Kyiv Post in 2018, he acquired an institution with a proud history and a civic role extending far beyond a balance sheet. As he put it then: “Without freedom of the press, you cannot have a democracy.” He also saw broader potential for the paper –launching a Ukrainian-language edition, expanding into digital and video journalism, and highlighting Ukraine’s strengths and promise alongside its challenges.
Sustaining a newsroom requires more than goodwill. Salaries must be met, investigative work funded, and operations maintained through peace and crisis. Adnan committed millions of dollars to acquire and sustain Kyiv Post. When Russia launched its full-scale invasion, he provided immediate additional support, ensuring our journalists could continue reporting reliably from the ground for readers around the world.
Adnan Kivan (L) and Chief Editor Bohdan Nahaylo (Photo by Kyiv Post)
Adnan Kivan (L) and Chief Editor Bohdan Nahaylo (Photo by Kyiv Post)
Crucially, he respected editorial independence. As Bohdan Nahaylo, our chief editor since the reorganization in late 2021, recalls: “Adnan was a gentleman and a rare breed. He told me at the outset: ‘You’re a veteran journalist – I trust you. Make Kyiv Post bigger and better and make it Ukraine’s global voice. Show that Ukraine has good things to offer, not simply gloom and doom. That’s all I ask.’ After that, his support was consistent.”
Honoring Adnan’s legacy means looking forward. A newspaper cannot thrive on past gratitude alone; every edition must earn the reader’s trust, and every generation of journalists needs the resources and independence to do their job.
When I think of Adnan now, I wish I had asked more questions during our conversations and recognized sooner how much of his own life informed his support for Kyiv Post. I cannot revisit those moments, but we can honor the trust he placed in us by carrying the work forward with his son Ruslan Kivan , who now continues his father’s legacy with the integrity and purpose.
So, on behalf of everyone at Kyiv Post, our millions of global readers, and everyone in Ukraine and Syria, thank you, Adnan for your dedication, support, and example.
Kyiv Post CEO Luc Chénier is a well-known Canadian public speaker, entrepreneur, author and a seasoned CEO who has spent a better part of his professional career working with international brands and governments by delivering his unique sense of business & marketing skills and impacting their bottom line.

title: E5 reaffirms unwavering support for Ukraine by all available means
body:
This is stated in a joint statement by the defense ministers of the five European countries (the Group of Five/E5) following their meeting in Paris on October 26, Ukrinform reports.
“We will maintain our unwavering commitment to supporting Ukraine in its fight back against Russian aggression. Ukraine’s ability to defend itself now and in the future is critically important to Euro-Atlantic collective security. We stress the need to keep supporting Ukraine by all available means – politically, militarily and financially,” the statement says.
The ministers also reaffirmed their determination to continue countering the activities of Russia’s shadow fleet in accordance with international law and in coordination with partners.
In addition, the five countries expressed support for Ukraine’s pursuit of a lasting peace backed by reliable security guarantees. “We stand united with Ukraine in its determination to secure a lasting peace, underpinned by robust security guarantees. The Coalition of the Willing will contribute to robust and credible security guarantees once a cease-fire or a peace agreement is in place,” the document says.
The defense ministers of the five European countries separately emphasized that Russia poses the most acute and long-term threat to Euro-Atlantic security and stability. The statement notes that Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine, violations of NATO members’ airspace, acts of sabotage and the increasingly active use of hybrid attacks do not weaken the Allies’ unity but, on the contrary, strengthen their determination to defend Alliance territory.
The statement also stresses that Europe must take greater responsibility for its own security. To this end, European Allies plan to strengthen political and military leadership within NATO, modernize their armed forces and deepen defense-industrial cooperation based on common and standardized requirements.
At the same time, the ministers emphasized that the United States remains an indispensable ally and that its continued involvement in ensuring European security is essential to a strong and credible NATO.
The E5 also called for strengthening European defense capabilities within NATO and the European Union, stressing that EU initiatives should complement the Alliance’s activities, avoid duplication and provide opportunities for cooperation with NATO countries that are not members of the European Union.
As reported by Ukrinform, Minister of Defense of Ukraine Yevhenii Khmara addressed representatives of the defense ministries of the E5 countries – Germany, the United Kingdom, France, Poland and Italy – and outlined the critical priorities for supporting Ukraine.

title: US Navy names USS Colorado as first AUKUS submarine based in Australia
body:
The US Navy has selected the first Virginia-class SSN to be assigned to Submarine Rotational Force-West (SRF-West) in Australia from late 2027. The announcement moves AUKUS closer to a persistent US and UK nuclear-powered submarine presence at HMAS Stirling rather than the series of individual visits and maintenance periods conducted so far.
The designation was announced jointly by US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, Australian Defence Minister Richard Marles and UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting. SRF-West is planned to host up to four USN boats and one RN boat on a rotational basis at HMAS Stirling in Western Australia.
USS Colorado arrived today at HMAS Stirling for a scheduled month-long maintenance period, providing a useful rehearsal before she returns as part of the rotational force next year. More than 30 trained Australian civilian technicians from ASC will carry out routine work on a Virginia-class submarine for the first time, supported by specialists from Pearl Harbour Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility.
The maintenance period is the fourth conducted in Western Australia since AUKUS was announced and continues a deliberate progression from hosting visiting submarines to sustaining them with an Australian workforce and locally provided infrastructure. New equipment at Stirling includes an Australian-built safety walkway around the submarine sail, upgrades to Diamantina Pier, a pure-water plant, high-pressure air compressor and dehumidification equipment. SRF-West is intended to give Australian sailors, engineers, regulators and industry the practical experience needed before the Royal Australian Navy takes ownership of its own Virginia-class submarines in the 2030s and later introduces the Anglo-Australian-built SSN-AUKUS boats.
Australia has already supported maintenance periods involving US submarines USS Hawaii and USS Vermont. HMS Anson arrived at HMAS Stirling in February for the first maintenance activity on an RN nuclear-powered submarine in Australia. A trilateral workforce completed around 600 hours of work on the Astute-class boat before she departed early due to events in the Middle East. Anson’s visit demonstrated what AUKUS is trying to achieve, but also exposed one of the difficulties facing the UK contribution. With the RN’s attack submarine fleet under severe availability pressure, committing an Astute-class boat to a sustained rotation thousands of kilometres from home is considerably more demanding for Britain than it is for the much larger US submarine force.
The establishment of Submarine Squadron 3 and supporting US Navy organisations at HMAS Stirling earlier this year has already begun to create the permanent shore structure required for the rotational force. Colorado’s selection now puts a name to the first boat that will operate within it.
Despite concerns after Trump’s second election victory that support for AUKUS was in the balance, the US subsequently recommitted itself to the pact. The naming of the boat shows that Americans are fully backing the project and understand the long-term strategic benefits. The UK position is more difficult; while fully committed to AUKUS and its goals, the backlog of submarine support issues creates a serious dilemma in upholding Pillar 1 requirements. It is likely the RN will manage to have two of its six SSNs active next year, with the return of HMS Audacious and HMS Agamemnon working towards being operational. In the longer term, generating a third active boat would be the likely minimum to allow one to be based in Australia. Given the level of Russian naval activity and the RN’s lack of alternative ASW assets, there will be a very hard choice to make about whether to keep promises on AUKUS or prioritise the threat closer to home.

title: Make LGU funds ‘results-based’ amid pork barrel concerns — World Bank
body: MANILA, Philippines – The World Bank said the proposed P58-billion Local Government Support Fund (LGSF) in the 2027 national budget could help power regional development, but recommended tying allocations to actual project results and encouraging local governments to invest together, amid concerns the fund could become a source of political patronage. Makiko Watanabe, the World Bank’s lead urban specialist for East Asia and the Pacific, said the Philippine government could adopt performance-based or results-based financing to improve accountability and reward local government units (LGUs) that deliver. “The short answer is, yes, we believe that LGSF can support genuine regional development so long as obviously it’s effectively utilized,” Watanabe said when asked by Rappler during the launch of the World Bank’s From Cities to Corridors report on Tuesday, October 27. She suggested that allocations be made “performance-based or results-based” rather than set in advance, and that funding encourage “inter-LGU type of investments” rather than isolated projects. These could include shared transportation and digital infrastructure, as well as disaster resilience projects that have spillover benefits beyond a single municipality or city. World Bank Philippines division director Zafer Mustafaoğlu likewise emphasized the need for accountability, efficient spending, and timely project completion, while suggesting too that authorities should consider the economic potential of neighboring LGUs when allocating resources. The proposed LGSF has drawn scrutiny over concerns that it could be used for discretionary spending and political patronage. Senate finance committee chairperson JV Ejercito has questioned the criteria for distributing the more-than-P58-billion fund and called for safeguards to ensure that allocations address local development needs rather than reward political allies. Senate President Sherwin Gatchalian also said that the LGSF needed to be transparent to promote good governance. Must Read [In This Economy] The 2027 budget: Hocus-pocus prevails once more Issues in local project funding The World Bank’s latest report also identifies weaknesses in how local projects secure funding. Only about 30% of investment proposals endorsed through regional development councils receive funding in a given budget cycle, which may create “uncertainties among LGUs about which of their endorsed priorities will receive the national government support,” the World Bank report said. It also notes that projects outside local annual investment plans (AIP) can receive funding when they have political backing, while planned projects may go unfunded. “While AIP is a standard vehicle for investment planning, [focus group discussion] shows that projects are also budgeted outside the AIP when there is political support, whereas AIP-listed items go unfunded when local priorities do not align,” the World Bank said in its report. SITTING ON CASH? A World Bank analysis of 2023 year-end cash balance as a share of annual operating revenues by urban LGU size shows that LGUs are not utilizing large amounts of cash on hand. Chart from the World Bank’s report Beyond the allocation process, many LGUs struggle to spend the funds they already have. Capital investments account for only about 15% of annual LGU expenditure, while poor project preparation and procurement add to delays. This has left local governments sitting on cash reserves, with large urban LGUs holding an average of P9,263 per person in year-end cash on hand balances in 2023, funds that the World Bank said could have been better used to address infrastructure and service needs. The report’s main recommendation is to shift away from individual LGU support to what it calls interconnected “corridor-based” development, with aligned national and local plans and better project implementation capacity. – Rappler.com

title: Zamfara Accord Party Gov Candidate’s Supporters Protest Omission From INEC List
body: Supporters of the Accord Party governorship candidate in Zamfara State, retired Assistant Inspector-General of Police (AIG) Musa Garba, have expressed concern over the omission of his name from the list published by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) ahead of the 2027 general elections. The concern was raised in a statement issued in Gusau on Tuesday by the Coordinator of the Musa Yusuf Garba (MYG) Foundation, Hamisu Sharu Gusau. According to the statement, the Foundation is seeking urgent intervention by INEC to correct the omission and include the candidate’s name on the relevant official list. The statement reads in part: “On behalf of the good people of Zamfara State, especially members of the MYG Foundation, we wish to inform the general public, political stakeholders, party members, and the media that the name of the Accord Party governorship candidate for the 2027 general elections, AIG Musa Yusuf Garba (Rtd.), is missing from the list published by INEC.” The Foundation explained that the Accord Party had formally written to the electoral commission, requesting the necessary correction and inclusion of its governorship candidate’s name in the relevant official records. It described the omission as a matter of serious concern to the candidate’s supporters and other stakeholders in the state’s democratic process. The Foundation maintained that electoral records and submissions must be handled transparently, fairly, and in accordance with applicable electoral laws and procedures. It therefore called on INEC to urgently investigate the matter, verify the party’s records and submissions, and take appropriate corrective action in line with relevant legal and electoral requirements. The statement further reaffirmed the Accord Party’s commitment to democratic principles, the rule of law, peaceful political participation, and the conduct of free, fair, and credible elections. The Foundation assured party members, supporters, and the general public that the matter was being pursued through the appropriate official channels, expressing optimism that the commission would address the issue promptly. It also appealed to the media, political stakeholders, and the public to remain calm and refrain from spreading unverified information while awaiting INEC’s response. The MYG Foundation reiterated its commitment to protecting the candidate’s legitimate democratic rights and ensuring that all electoral matters are addressed transparently, fairly, and in accordance with the law. title: I Saw Ukraine’s Rapid Adaptation Cycle in Action, and This is What the US Military Should Learn from It
body:
During my time in Ukraine I saw more than a country at war. I saw a defense innovation ecosystem in which the daily imperative to survive drove rapid learning and adaptation. It also exposed a serious weakness in the American model of military technology development. A Ukrainian drone can be jammed, modified to counter the jamming, and sent back into the fight in less time than it takes the US defense system to process a request. That gap is more than a bureaucratic frustration. It is a strategic vulnerability.
When Russian forces jammed a drone’s signal, Ukrainian engineers often developed a fix within days, and sometimes within hours. They changed frequencies, replaced antennas, or adopted new navigation methods. Once the solution worked, it got back to the front quickly. In many cases the drone was flying again within a day or two. As I watched this responsiveness in action, I kept comparing it to how the same problem would move through our system. A US unit that identifies an urgent requirement for change submits a request. The issue enters a process built for review and control. If it is serious enough it may be classified as a Joint Urgent Operational Need or a Joint Emergent Operational Need. Even on that accelerated track it can take up to a year to field an initial solution and as long as two years to deploy it fully. By then the threat may have changed several times. The system will have done what it was designed to do, but too slowly to matter.
The problem is that we do not evaluate our defense industry, or our own institutions, based on how well they adapt when conditions change. We evaluate them based on how well they perform against requirements written in advance. The central flaw is not a lack of talent or technology. It is that we reward compliance over adaptation. We write a requirement, give it to industry, and then judge the final product against that same requirement. In effect we provide the answer key and then reward companies for following it. That approach may work for predictable procurement. It does not work for war.
Even our existing rapid acquisition pathways, including the Middle Tier of Acquisition and urgent operational needs processes, still largely judge solutions against requirements written in advance. They can accelerate delivery of a planned solution, but they do not systematically measure or reward a company’s ability to adapt when the threat changes after the requirement is locked. War is dynamic. Adversaries do not announce their next moves, and the most dangerous threats are often the ones that did not exist when the requirement was drafted. The jamming frequencies used against US systems in a future conflict will not match the ones described in a document written years earlier. They will be the ones an adversary developed last week. Yet we continue to favor companies skilled at preparing for planned events rather than those capable of solving new problems quickly. These skill sets are fundamentally different. One produces compliance. The other fosters adaptation. Innovation experts describe this as the adaptability gap , the distance between how much an organization claims to value adaptability and how much it actually invests in it. In the US defense sector this gap has become structural.
If the threat changes in real time, the Department of Defense’s evaluation model must change with it. Rather than judging fixed products against static standards alone, the department should assess a company’s broader innovation ecosystem and its ability to adapt capability at operational speed. To implement this change, the department should update DFARS 215.304 . That provision already governs evaluation factors used in departmental source selections and provides precedents for assessing attributes beyond the immediate end item, including small business participation, manufacturing readiness, supply chain risk, sustainment, and supplier risk. The regulation therefore already recognizes that a company’s ability to deliver capability depends on more than whether a product meets a point-in-time specification. The central question should be whether its engineers, software teams, production lines, legal staff, and product designers can absorb new battlefield data and convert it into a workable solution in weeks rather than years.
That shift requires new criteria. Contracts could specify maximum two-week turnaround for software updates. This timeline is fast enough to drive real change from today’s multimonth cycles, yet realistic enough to assess responsiveness. Procurement processes could include demonstration phases in which companies must design, test, and field modifications within defined periods using recent threat scenarios. The goal is not to weaken standards. It is to operationalize them in alignment with the demands of modern conflict.
The Department of Defense already has both an immediate mechanism to implement this change and an enduring organization to scale it. Under Project Agincourt, the Direct Reporting Portfolio Manager for Unmanned Systems (DRPM-UxS) is directed to lead the near-term transition and develop the pathway to the Autonomous Warfare Command . While carrying out its current responsibilities, the DRPM-UxS can pilot a revised acquisition model for testing adaptability.
Consider how we often test autonomous systems today. Requirements may state that platforms must operate in a contested electronic warfare environment. Manufacturers arrive at the test range already knowing the frequencies they will face. They prepare for those expected conditions, pass the test, and move toward procurement. A more realistic evaluation would expose the system to the latest electronic warfare signals captured from active battlefields, signals that may not have existed when the requirements were drafted. The system will likely fail. That is not the end of the test. It is the beginning of the real one. At that point we should measure how quickly a company can diagnose the problem, rewrite the software, validate the fix, and scale it into production. If that timeline is measured in years rather than weeks, the company should not win the contract.
Some will argue that the United States is not at war and therefore lacks access to the right battlefield data. That is not a sufficient excuse. Ukrainian partners confront these threats every day. They offer two clear ways to make our testing more realistic. The first is data. Ukrainian partners can share current threat information, from captured jamming signals to evolving enemy tactics, that can keep US testing relevant. The second is access to the environment itself. Ukraine’s Brave1 defense technology cluster runs a program called Test in Ukraine that allows systems to be exposed to live Russian threats in operational conditions. That model is already expanding. New initiatives linking Ukrainian defense firms with NATO partners are creating pathways for allied companies to test systems against real-world threats and learn from one of the most combat-tested innovation ecosystems in the world. The infrastructure for more realistic testing is not hypothetical. It is already taking shape.
This approach comes with legal, security, and intelligence-sharing challenges. Sensitive battlefield data cannot simply move across borders without safeguards. While such concerns are valid, they are implementation problems, not reasons for inaction. With the right protocols and close coordination, realistic testing is possible.
This approach will fail, however, if the Department of Defense demands adaptability from industry while exempting itself from the same standard. The department is emphasizing adaptation, but meanwhile, regulations and policy lag. Today’s incentive structures do not reward program managers for learning quickly. They reward them for clean audits, predictable timelines, and avoiding budget turbulence.
During my time in Special Forces acquisition we had a simple motto: Fail fast. Learn quickly whether something works, stop funding what does not, and move resources to what does. Scaling that mindset across the broader defense enterprise will not be easy, but it is necessary. Performance metrics should track how quickly teams respond to emerging threats and how effectively they adapt. Pilot programs should reward timely iteration, even when it includes short-term failure. Promotions and recognition should go to leaders who move quickly and extract useful lessons from rapid testing, not just those who hit traditional milestones. If we are serious about closing the adaptability gap, we must be willing to accept the risk and invest the necessary money, time, and people.
Testing for adaptability does involve risk. Some tests will fail. Some funding will go to efforts that do not succeed. That is not waste. It is the cost of learning faster than the adversary. A culture that treats every failed test as a scandal will produce a military that looks efficient on paper and loses in practice.
Ukraine did not build an adaptive defense industrial base because it had perfectly written requirements. It built one because it had no alternative. The old model would have cost it the war, so Ukraine replaced it with an ecosystem that learns under pressure. The United States still has time to reform how it tests, fields, and rewards innovation. But that window is narrowing. Russia is adapting in real time, and China is building the industrial and mobilization capacity to outproduce and outlast its opponents in a high-intensity fight—a scale the United States is not yet built to match. The central question is no longer whether America can build advanced systems, but whether those systems and the institutions behind them can evolve fast enough to matter.
Colonel Rachael Hoagland is an Army acquisition corps officer with more than twenty-nine years of service. She most recently served in a dual-hatted role as Science and Technology Division chief and director of the Joint Capabilities Acquisition Cell, and she spent nine months in Ukraine working directly with operational units, the Ministry of Defence, the Defence Procurement Agency, and the domestic defense industry.
The views expressed are those of the author and do not reflect the official position of the United States Military Academy, Department of the Army, or Department of Defense.

title: Russian stock market accelerates on news reports
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. The Russian stock market has accelerated by more than 1% and is at its maximum since June 2026, according to the Moscow Exchange.
Such dynamics is noted amid the reports on the telephone conversation between Russian President Vladimir Putin and President of Finland Alexander Stubb and Prime Minister of Norway Jonas Gahr Stoere.
The MOEX Russia Index gained 1.11% to 2,519.12 points. The RTS Index had an uptick by 1% to 985.92 points.

title: Finnish, Norwegian Leaders Call Putin Ahead of Ukraine Peace Talks
body:
Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre held a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Tuesday to discuss ongoing efforts to end the war in Ukraine, a move that, while coordinated with Kyiv, some European leaders criticized.
Moscow confirmed the call shortly after officials in Helsinki and Oslo released statements about the conversation, which marks the first time a leader from one of Ukraine’s European allies spoke to Putin since French President Emmanuel Macron’s phone call with the Kremlin chief in July 2025.
Stubb’s office said he and Støre initiated the call in order to “discuss Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine and the diplomatic efforts to end the war and promote peace and stability in Europe.”
It said the aim of the outreach, made in consultation with Ukraine, was “to convey messages directly regarding future negotiations to help to end the war to President Putin,” adding that it was also “related to the upcoming meetings to be held in Abu Dhabi.”
“In the call we stressed the importance of de-escalation,” Støre’s office said in its statement about the call with Putin.
Both Finland and Norway said their leaders were speaking as representatives of their respective countries and did not speak on behalf of Europe as a whole.
Still, the phone call with Putin was met with criticism from some European leaders.
Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said she was “very skeptical” of the initiative and did not believe Russia wants peace with Ukraine or Europe.
“ I think we should keep Europe together instead of going solo, ” Frederiksen said, according to Danish media. “We should stand together and speak with one voice and defend ourselves against Russia.”
In its own statement, the Kremlin said Putin “reiterated the root causes” of his decision to order the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
He also “drew attention to the confrontational policies of EU and NATO member states, which he noted serve to prolong the hostilities,” it added.
Stubb, Støre and Putin discussed security and stability in the Baltic Sea and Northern European regions, the Kremlin’s readout added. The three leaders agreed to maintain direct contact moving forward, it said.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he spoke to Stubb and Støre following their call with Putin, adding that he was “ grateful for the detailed briefing and for their active support for our diplomacy and the peace efforts we are pursuing together with all our partners.”
Zelensky emphasized that the Finnish and Norwegian leaders told Putin that concrete steps needed to be taken in order to de-escalate the war, especially when it comes to attacks on energy infrastructure ahead of winter.
“Russia must stop dragging out the war,” he wrote in a post on social media.
Tuesday’s phone call comes a week after Stubb and Støre met with U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff and Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky in Oslo. The purpose of the Oslo talks was to mend strained relations between Kyiv and Washington, as well as to seek a new path out of the war.
Witkoff later met with Putin in St. Petersburg to report on progress in efforts to end the conflict. The Kremlin said it is willing to resume U.S.-mediated peace negotiations in Abu Dhabi as soon as next month, though no exact dates have been set.

title: Sheikh Gumi urges calm over Masussuka’s killing
body: A prominent Islamic scholar, Sheikh Ahmad Gumi, has urged the public to remain calm and allow the authorities to take appropriate action following the killing of Katsina-based cleric, Yahaya Masussuka. Gumi made the appeal in a statement posted on his verified Facebook page hours after the cleric was killed, describing the incident as a serious mistake that could trigger conflict within the Muslim community. The scholar warned that the incident could be exploited to create confusion and division among Muslims, urging people not to take the law into their own hands. He also cited verses from the Qur’an to support his call for restraint, cautioning against actions that could lead to unrest and urging people to refer security-related matters to the appropriate authorities. Be vigilant against phishing scams, cyber fraud, Bank customers advised Businessman builds N2.2bn hospital for Edo community Quoting Qur’an 4:83, Gumi emphasised the importance of referring matters concerning security and fear to those in authority rather than spreading information without proper investigation. He further cited Qur’an 24:63, warning against actions that could lead to trials or painful consequences. Gumi prayed for peace and an end to conflict within the Muslim community. “May Allah grant us peace and remove every form of conflict and division from the community of Prophet Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him). Amen,” he said.

title: Zelenskyy speaks with Stubb, Støre after their talks with Putin – adviser
body:
President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy is holding a telephone conversation with President of Finland Alexander Stubb and Prime Minister of Norway Jonas Gahr Støre following their telephone conversation with Kremlin chief Vladimir Putin, reported Dmytro Lytvyn, adviser to the Head of the Ukrainian State.

"After the call with Putin, the leaders of Finland and Norway are holding a phone call with Zelenskyy," the adviser to the Ukrainian President told journalists in Kyiv on Tuesday.

As reported earlier, the office of the President of Finland and the government of Norway announced a phone call between Stubb, Støre, and Russian President Vladimir Putin, which took place on Tuesday, October 27.

"The discussion was frank and substantive. We are neighboring countries to Russia. The outcome of this war will have a direct impact on our and the broader European security. Ending the war requires direct discussions," Stubb noted.

title: Hindsight: Ghana’s LA 28 Olympic Boxing Qualifier Hosting Rights Explained
body: On Wednesday, October 21, 2026, World Boxing formally informed the Ghana Boxing Federation that Ghana’s bid to host the Olympic Boxing Qualifiers for the Los Angeles 2028 Games had been successful. That decision makes Ghana the seventh country to host the continental qualifiers since 2006, after Senegal (2023), Mauritius (2009), Morocco (2007, 2011 and 2015), and Algeria and Namibia (2007). Ghana’s Pitch Ghana’s bid highlighted the country’s existing infrastructure as proof of its readiness for the tournament. The Borteyman Sports Complex, a $145m facility located about 11.1 miles from the University of Ghana Stadium, was presented as the main venue for hosting the tournament. The plan is to use the 1,000-seat capacity multi-purpose Sports Hall as the main hall for the bouts. Per the International Olympic Committee (IOC) requirements, the venue (in this case, the Sports Hall) must have two boxing rings and a warm-up area equipped with a floor ring, punching bags, and training gear) where athletes and their team officials can prepare before a bout. Although unlikely, if it becomes necessary to host three bouts at the same time, the Borteyman Sports Complex has enough space for that too. It has a 500-seater temporary dome that was originally designed for handball, volleyball, judo, karate, taekwondo, fencing, arm-wrestling, and a five-tennis court complex, as well as a 1,000-seater Centre Court. The 500-seater Centre Hall at the Borteyman Sports Complex If it becomes necessary, that could be redesigned for a third boxing ring to be mounted. As for the ring and its associated equipment, there will be no shortage of such. The rings purchased and used for the 13th African Games in 2024 will do just fine. In terms of organizational expertise, Ghana highlighted its coordination of an incident-free African Games. If you have not noticed by now, the plan does not include the Bukom Boxing Arena. The 4,000-seater facility is not fit for purpose as it cannot host two boxing rings – a key IOC requirement for all host countries. The Bukom Boxing Arena can only accommodate one boxing ring Host City Agreement Subsequent to last week’s announcement, a ‘‘Host City Agreement’’ will be formalized between the International Olympic Committee and Ghana. The Host City Agreement is a binding legal contract between the IOC and a selected city that hosts its tournament. The practice is not alien. For the most part, the agreement clearly spells out all local operating expenses, including public security, police escorts, medical services, and specialized infrastructure upgrades, and whose responsibility it is. In the past, the IOC (and in the case of football, FIFA) has retained all major commercial revenues—including broadcast rights, ticket sales, and official sponsorships—while host cities receive no direct share of those earnings. For Ghana’s part, the government, through the Ministry for Sports and Recreation and the Accra Metropolitan Assembly, will assume all associated costs, including intra-and inter-city transportation, accommodation arrangements, existing boxing infrastructure requirements, etc. However, the operational support and expertise will come from the Ghana Boxing Federation. A tentative date of August 13–22, 2027, has been set for the tournament.

title: Trade turnover between Russia, South Africa above $1 bln per year
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. The bilateral trade turnover between Russia and South Africa is growing and has been above $1 bln per year for four years in a row, said Alexander Kozlov, the Russian Minister of Natural Resources and co-chairman of the joint intergovernmental committee on trade and economic cooperation between Russia and South Africa.
"The bilateral trade turnover is growing every year. And stably, for four consecutive years now, it has been above one billion US dollars. I would like to note that South Africa is among Russia's top six trading partners in Africa," he said.
The primary range of products consists of foods, Kozlov said. "We import fruits, dried fruits, and nuts, while we export wheat. In addition, we sell fertilizers to the republic and buy manganese ore," he added.
Manganese is also key to our joint investment projects, Kozlov stressed. "There are currently two of them: the development of the largest mine in Africa and a metallurgical plant," the minister added.

title: How Aldi is pushing down grocery prices
body:
The discount grocery chain Aldi plans to have more than 3,000 American locations by the end of 2028. Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images North America hide caption
In the summer of 2020, I lived briefly in Ithaca, New York. It's the only time I've lived near Aldi, the grocery store known for low prices. I went twice, and I thought it was fine, but underwhelming. I appreciated the low prices, but it didn't have everything I needed. The store was small and a bit shabby.
I didn't know it yet, but those are the exact ingredients that have made Aldi the fastest-growing grocery chain in America. Per Bloomberg , Aldi plans to have more than 3,000 American locations by the end of 2028, which would be more than any other chain but Walmart. In 2024, Aldi generated some $29 billion in U.S. sales, which is more than Trader Joe's.
Aldi is a German company known for having low, low prices, and it deserves that reputation. Food reporter Deena Shanker told me for my podcast Gastronomics that her experience comparison shopping over many months was that Aldi either matched Walmart on price or was a bit cheaper. Grocers like Wegmans and Kroger have announced defensive price reductions, and an analysis published in late 2023 of Lidl, another German grocer with a very similar model to Aldi's but fewer U.S. stores, found that grocery chains reduced their markups ~7 percent in areas where Lidl stores opened .
All to say: Aldi is disrupting the grocery business and actually lowering prices even as the cost of food—at restaurants and other grocery stores—goes up and up.
Maybe this sounds a bit humdrum. But I found it totally intriguing and perplexing, because…
One necessary but not sufficient explanation for Aldi's low prices is that management is obsessed with efficiency and cutting unnecessary costs. There's no music in stores, because speakers (and licensing fees for muzak) cost money. The staff places products on shelves still in the cardboard boxes they were trucked in on, because artfully unpacking fruits, bread, and jerky sticks would mean higher labor costs. The shabbiness is intentional — it's the cost of cheaper groceries.
But other grocery chains are similarly obsessed with efficiency. Here's one of my favorite examples about Costco, courtesy of Zachary Crockett and The Hustle : "In another instance, reengineering a container of cashews from a circle to a square shape allowed Costco to stack more items in a single truck, reducing the number of shipments by 24,000 pallets per year. For shoppers, this meant cheaper nuts."
Instead, Aldi's disruptively low prices rely on two primary tactics:
Aldi's low prices made their stores very attractive during periods like the Great Recession and today's inflationary era. The Great Recession, especially, enabled their current growth. But if all Aldi offered was bargain prices in shabby stores, customers might flee to Costco, Kroger, or Whole Foods when the economy recovered.
So another key to Aldi's success is that it's fun. Aldi has a famously chaotic-good middle aisle with rotating buys like fun toys, German spätzle, and advent calendars that contain 24 festive cheeses. And its U.S. stores have expanded their offerings (a bit) to attract higher-income customers: Aldi doesn't just have the cheapest apples, but the cheapest honey crisp apples. Not just super-duper cheap wine but well-priced "premium" wine.
Instead of being a sad place to shop when you're low on cash, Aldi has more flea-market energy: a place anyone might go to hunt for good deals and fun finds. Aldi is beloved; many customers are cult-like in their devotion . In some cases, customers line up for new store openings like early iPhone releases.
My main takeaway from researching and analyzing Aldi for several weeks (for an episode of Gastronomics !) is that there's always something new under the sun. American grocery stores are a mature market. They seem pretty stable equilibrium-y. But they are dynamic and always changing. Aldi didn't need futuristic tech to disrupt the industry; just a strategy developed 80 years ago, then tweaked for the American market. In healthy markets, there's always a way in for new competitors.
My other takeaway is greater appreciation for the famous business idiom: "There are only two ways to make money in business: One is to bundle; the other is to unbundle."
The clearest example of bundling and unbundling is probably television. Cable companies bundled hundreds of TV channels together and charged one high fee for all of them. Then streaming services like Netflix made money by unbundling television — by allowing people to pay for just Netflix. Which felt liberating! For a few years. But now customers are annoyed about subscribing to so many streaming services. So streamers are teaming up to form bundles, like getting Disney, Hulu, and HBO Max all for one reduced price. Now, to make money, you gotta bundle.
Even the person who coined the phrase about bundling and unbundling didn't think it's literally the only way to make money. Still, I often failed to see (un)bundling as a powerful framework outside of the media industry. Until I realized that Aldi is unbundling the grocery store.
For a long time, grocery stores got more bundled. People once went to the baker, the butcher, and the greengrocer. Then the super market put all those things under one roof. And then Walmart, Target, and Costco created superstores where you could buy groceries and clothes and big-screen TVs.
Now Aldi is reversing this process by unbundling the grocery store. Not only does Aldi not have the big-screen TVs and dupes of Lululemon hoodies and pants , it doesn't even have everything on your grocery list. Aldi unbundled the part of the grocery business it can do super cheaply, and it intentionally locates Aldi stores near competitor grocery stores so shoppers can easily go grab the last few things on their list (the rest of the bundle).
With this in mind, I've started seeing bundling and unbundling at work in more and more industries. If you look closely at your own, I suspect you will, too.
My third takeaway is that I just didn't live in Ithaca long enough to grok Aldi. If I'd been there longer, I bet I would have made Aldi part of a multi-store strategy. I get it now! Aldi, please come to Colorado (where I live)!
At the start of this post, I asked three questions inspired by Aldi's expansion. The first two, which are about how Aldi achieved a comparative advantage, I feel like I've answered.
The third was whether the American economy can still deliver a bounty of affordable food. I think the way Aldi's growth pressured competitors to keep prices low shows that grocers are not the right target of our ire over food prices. But grocery stores are just one slice of the food world.
Alex Mayyasi is the author of the best-selling book, Planet Money: A Guide to the Economic Forces That Shape Your Life . He writes a Substack newsletter and hosts the podcast Gastronomics about the business of food and how economics shapes what we eat.
