title: Troops kill terrorists, rescue 3 kidnap victims
body: Troops of Operation Fansan Yamma have killed eight suspected terrorists and rescued three kidnapped victims during separate operations in Katsina, Kaduna and Zamfara states. The operations, conducted on October 24 and 25, also led to the recovery of an AK-47 rifle, three locally fabricated guns, three motorcycles, cutlasses and assorted charms. A statement issued by Captain Tamuno Sinivie, Media Information Officer of the Joint Task Force North-West, said the troops killed two suspected terrorists during an operation at Machika Dam in Sabuwa Local Government Area of Katsina State. He said the troops responded to a distress call from farmers who reported terrorist activities in the area. UBA Launches Group-Wide Climate Action Week to Advance Green Finance Kane wins Ballon D’Or, first Englishman in 25 years According to the statement, the troops engaged the suspected terrorists in a gun battle, killing two while others fled. The troops also rescued a 42-year-old man, Suleiman Umar, who was abducted by the terrorists. An AK-47 rifle, a magazine containing ammunition and a motorcycle were recovered during the operation. In a separate incident, troops of Sector One, working with the Civilian Joint Task Force (CJTF), killed six suspected terrorists while foiling an ambush along Ungwan Iya in Igabi Local Government Area of Kaduna State. The statement said the troops had responded to a distress call over an attack on Ungwan Mallami village, where the suspected terrorists abducted two people. It added that the troops came under attack while pursuing the assailants but responded with superior firepower, killing six of them, while others escaped. Three locally fabricated guns, two motorcycles, cutlasses and assorted charms were recovered during the operation. In Zamfara State, troops of Sector Two rescued two kidnapped men during a surveillance operation in Bagega, Anka Local Government Area, on Sunday. The victims were identified as Shehu Chete, 40, and Bugu Bedi, 25, both indigenes of Kebbi State. The statement said the troops spotted suspected terrorists during surveillance and launched a fighting patrol. It added that the assailants fled on sighting the troops, abandoning the two victims. The rescued men were taken to Bagega Clinic for medical attention before being moved to a military base for further assessment and eventual reunion with their families. The task force said troops were continuing patrols and search operations across the affected areas to apprehend fleeing suspects, rescue other abductees and prevent further attacks. The Theatre Commander of Operation Fansan Yamma commended the troops for their courage and resilience in responding to the incidents. He urged residents to support the ongoing operations by providing timely and credible information about suspicious movements and activities in their communities.

title: Russian officials to inspect Georgia’s fruit safety amid suspension of imports of some Georgian drinks
body: Russia’s agricultural watchdog, Rosselkhoznadzor, will visit Georgia from 2 November to inspect the country’s phytosanitary certification system for fruit exported to Russia, the agency announced on Monday. The visit comes after Russia temporarily suspended imports and sales of certain alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages from Georgian producers earlier this month, citing quality control reasons. Moscow has denied that the restrictions were politically motivated. Russia has imposed wide-reaching import restrictions on Armenian goods in recent years. Moscow has cited quality and safety concerns in those cases as well, while critics have suggested the measures were politically motivated amid deteriorating relations between Russia and Armenia. The announcement follows a three-day regional workshop organised by the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH) in Tbilisi from 20–22 October, which brought together regional and international experts to discuss strengthening veterinary product regulatory systems. Representatives of Russia’s Federal Service for Veterinary and Phytosanitary Surveillance (Rosselkhoznadzor) also participated in the workshop. Georgia and Russia have had no diplomatic relations since the 2008 August war but maintain trade and economic relations. The Russian delegation will examine Georgia’s phytosanitary certification system for pome and stone fruits exported to Russia. It will also audit a laboratory that tests plant-based products for pesticide and agrochemical residues before they enter the Russian market. The last time Russia did this kind of inspection was in 2014. Rosselkhoznadzor said the visit, arranged at the invitation of Georgia’s National Food Agency, aims to establish common approaches to controlling goods subject to quarantine requirements. The two sides are also expected to hold video talks on the programme for the visit. ‘The visit aims to establish common approaches to controlling goods subject to quarantine requirements’, Rosselkhoznadzor added. The agency reported that Russia had imported 70,500 tonnes of fruit and vegetable products from Georgia as of 24 October 2026. Its data showed increases in imports of nectarines, apples, blueberries, plums, mandarins, fresh figs, and watermelons compared with the same period a year earlier. On 22 October, Rosselkhoznadzor stated two Georgian dairy-processing plants would gain access to the Russian market from November. The agency said it had initiated a request to the relevant Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) authorities to approve the plants’ inclusion in the register of enterprises from third countries. Russia also expressed readiness to inspect six Georgian fish and seafood producers interested in exporting to Russia. Their products would be eligible to enter the Russian market if the inspections found no violations, the agency said. On 10 October, it emerged that Russia had temporarily suspended the import and sale of some alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks from several Georgian producers. The affected products included wine from Teliani Valley, Tbilvino, and Wine Man; wine and brandy from Askaneli Brothers; beer from the Georgian Beer Company; Coca-Cola produced in Georgia; and Nabeglavi mineral water, produced by Healthy Water. Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova described the restrictions as routine quality-control measures and denied that they were politically motivated. Georgia’s National Food Agency had not provided a response to OC Media ’s questions about the planned Rosselkhoznadzor visit at the time of writing.

title: Sudan Drone Strikes Kill 21, Cause Mass Outages In East
body: Sudan’s warring sides have traded drone strikes that killed 21 people in the western Darfur region and left vast swathes of the country’s east without electricity, medics and witnesses said Tuesday. A drone strike on a market in Nyala, the de facto capital of Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces in Darfur, killed 21 people and wounded at least 40 others, a medical source and witnesses told AFP. One Nyala resident said a market in the city’s north was struck by a drone on Monday around 8:00 pm (1800 GMT). Another said the market was frequented by young men, particularly RSF fighters. “Twenty-one people were killed in last night’s bombing, and more than 40 others injured,” a medic at Nyala Hospital said, though he was unable to identify how many were RSF fighters. Sudan’s military, at war with the RSF since April 2023, regularly strikes Nyala, where the RSF has declared an administration rivalling the army-backed internationally recognised government in Khartoum. The RSF has in turn launched repeated strikes targeting Khartoum’s airport, as well as dams and power stations across the country’s east. On Tuesday, “RSF militia drones targeted the Al-Markhiyat transformer station, disrupting the power supply across large parts of Khartoum and Al-Jazira states,” a source in the national electricity company told AFP on condition of anonymity. The strike comes a day after a coordinated RSF drone attack on six power stations left millions without power in Al-Jazira, White Nile, Sennar and Gedaref states. Famine risk The war is currently being fought primarily via drones, with both sides launching sophisticated attacks from across the country, killing dozens of civilians at a time. In the first three weeks of October alone, drone strikes killed over 300 people and injured hundreds more, according to a UN tally. Since it began, the war has killed more than 200,000 people, aid workers estimate, and has triggered the world’s largest hunger and displacement crises. The United Nations has repeatedly warned that attacks on power stations threaten health and services for millions of people. Close to three million people have returned to Khartoum state since it was recaptured by the army last year, but many have struggled to rebuild their lives in a scarred city. Power and water supplies remain unreliable, much of the capital remains unsafe from unexploded bombs and many struggle to put food on the table in a collapsed economy. On Monday, 30 countries including the United States, France and the United Kingdom warned that urgent action was needed to prevent famine expanding across the country. Sudan is facing “an alarming deterioration” of food security, they said, citing the war, a currency in freefall, higher fuel prices due to the Middle East war and a drought induced by the El Nino climate phenomenon. Sudan’s foreign ministry on Monday insisted the country’s food security was “reassuring”, in an attempt to “refute claims of famine”. It accused “some countries and organisations” of “politically exploiting the humanitarian situation”. The army has for years denied claims of documented famine and has been accused of blocking access to humanitarian aid. AFP The post Sudan Drone Strikes Kill 21, Cause Mass Outages In East appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Roblox downloaded 145GB models from us (including adult content) without asking
body:
By Salaryman on October 26, 2026 Last updated on October 26, 2026
On 15 and 16 October 2026, a crawler that said it belonged to Roblox walked through almost every project on Open3DLab, SFMLab and SmutBase, and proceeded to download complete copies of 1,027 files from 712 projects. 145.5 GB of our creators' work, downloaded for what we assume are AI training purposes.
This post briefly describes what happened, what mitigations were taken, and what this signals for the community at large. A more detailed writeup outlining what we saw in our logs will be posted at a later time.
On Sunday the 18th of October, we noticed a crawler making a large number of requests to our sites and download infrastructure. The crawler sent the same user agent on every request, trellis2-data-sourcing/1.0 (3D foundation model research; [redacted]@roblox.com) . It came from a single Amazon Web Services (AWS) address. It had read the main page of 18,926 projects, which is practically our entire catalogue, in 26,429 requests over a span of 34 hours.
After pulling the project pages, it downloaded complete copies of 1,027 files from 712 projects, 145.5 GB in all, before suspending operations during the weekend. The downloads include 364 files (54.8 GB) from 224 projects on SmutBase, which hosts adult content only. With the SFMLab projects marked adult, 345 of the 712 projects (62.6 GB) are adult content.
The main limiting factor in the number of files downloaded was the crawler's reliance on the free download servers, which have caps on speed limit and number of concurrent downloads. The crawler did not respect our robots.txt, (which it did retrieve), ignored our Terms of Service, (which forbid scraping), and defied the creators' licenses: 423 of the 712 projects are licensed for non-commercial use only. Within the sample it retrieved, it took adult projects at the same rate as everything else. Some examples include models of Eve from Stellar Blade , Mei from Overwatch , and a Horse cock dildo .
We found it on 18 October and blocked further attempts the same morning. The scraper had suspended its activity by that point, and we did not notice any scraper that weekend. We emailed the address in its user agent on 18 October and asked Roblox for comment. We have not had a reply.
The crawler resumed scraping activity on October 19th, with all requests getting blocked by our servers. The scraper did not reduce its download attempts when faced with our blocks, and the scrapes seemed to fit neatly within office hours, only briefly pausing for an hour around lunchtime, and ending activity around the end of the workday (CEST). On the 20th, their scraper made its final return at 8:00, slowly tapering requests from lunchtime onward, likely in an effort to test our rate limiting. The requests stopped around 15:00. We sent another email to Roblox for questions, to which they again did not reply.
This section contains our speculation and assumptions based on public information, and the information we noticed in our logs.
Roblox has been building a "3D foundation model" since at least 2025.In March 2025 Roblox introduced Cube , which it calls its core generative AI system for 3D and 4D. The accompanying paper describes the goal as a foundation model for 3D intelligence. It lists character rigging among the things that model should eventually do, and generating characters and avatars as future work. Its first shape model was trained on roughly 1.5 million 3D assets from licensed and public datasets such as Objaverse, plus free assets from Roblox's own Creator Store whose creators had opted in. In February 2026 Roblox began rolling out "4D generation" built on Cube.
The address in the user agent belongs to a researcher who is among the 40-plus authors of that Cube paper. The researcher's public professional profile says they are building a 3D foundation model at Roblox, and their earlier published work is on 3D reconstruction and real-time 3D rendering. We want to be clear: we don't suggest this researcher did anything on their own initiative or out of the ordinary for their job. A data-collection run like this is a company's decision, and the responsibility for it is Roblox's. But the profile says what the user agent says: the people behind this crawler build 3D foundation models.
The "trellis2" in trellis2-data-sourcing may refer to TRELLIS.2 , an open 3D generation model Microsoft released in late 2025. It may mean the data was meant for training or tuning a model like it, or it may just be a project codename. We don't know. What we can say is that TRELLIS.2's published data toolkit contains no web crawler and no user agent, so this crawler and its label were written for the job. It is also possible that Roblox is re-using the Trellis.2 tooling for its own foundational model and it is re-using these scripts for its next model; the tools are open source.
Our sites are full of things a 3D model-generation system needs and public datasets have relatively little of: complete, textured characters, many of them rigged, in the formats artists actually work in, each with a title, a description and preview images.
Put together, we think the most likely explanation is that the crawler was collecting training or evaluation data for Roblox's 3D foundation model work. We can't prove it, and we don't know whether any of our creators' files ended up in a model.
This isn't the first time Roblox has been criticised for how it treats the people whose work its platform runs on, or for how it handles other people's rights.
None of this proves anything about the crawler, but it strengthens our opinion that Roblox is a deeply unethical business. It shows a company that has repeatedly been accused of putting growth ahead of the people its platform depends on.
More than a third of Roblox's daily users were under 13 in 2025, by its own figures. Its rules ban sexual content, and in 2025 it tightened them further .
Roblox's crawler took 224 projects from a site called SmutBase, which describes itself as exclusively for adult content, and 121 more that are marked adult on SFMLab. It took them at the same rate as everything else: 345 of the 712 projects it downloaded from are adult content. The further scraping attempts did not discriminate between adult content either.
We want to be careful here. We don't think Roblox set out to collect adult content, and we have no evidence that any of it reached a model or a product. The scrapes were likely automated. But that is exactly the problem: as far as our logs show, nobody checked. A crawler working for a company whose platform tens of millions of children use was pointed at an adult site, and it took explicit models without telling them apart from anything else.
Models reproduce what they learn from. If adult training data reaches a model that generates assets for Roblox, the only thing between that data and children is whatever filter Roblox builds afterwards, because its data collection didn't filter anything. Furthermore, when a creator deletes a project, or we remove one for breaking our rules or after a copyright notice, it's gone from our sites, but remains in these datasets. One project the crawler took has already been disabled on SFMLab since. If Roblox still has its copy, that copy is still there.
We're not against adult content. It's our bread and butter. We think consenting adults should be able to access and enjoy this content freely, without the government looking over their shoulder. What we object to is our adult sites being emptied into an exploitative gaming company's training data without anyone asking, and being mixed into content offered to literal children.
For a company being sued by several US states over child safety, "our AI team bulk-downloaded an adult site without looking" is not a good position to be in.
Roblox isn't the worst offender in AI's appetite for other people's work, just the latest to turn up in our logs. It isn't the only AI company in them, either. In the month before we found trellis2-data-sourcing , Meta's AI crawler, Meta-ExternalAgent, made about 380,000 requests to our sites, almost all from Meta's own network, and loaded 211,000 project pages. We have since blocked their crawler as well.
The Roblox trellis2 crawler is the first individual crawler we spotted that actually pulled assets uploaded by our users, in flagrant defiance of any copyright or license that might apply to it. It fits a broader context, of AI labs taking content without permission. Here's what the largest companies have been accused of, and in some cases have admitted:
Now compare how copyright treats everyone else. In the early 2000s Jammie Thomas-Rasset was ordered to pay $222,000 for sharing 24 songs. Internet activist Aaron Swartz faced federal charges carrying decades in prison for downloading academic articles. The Internet Archive, a nonprofit library, lost in court for lending scanned copies of books it owned. Meanwhile, the Internet Archive's online library gets repeatedly scanned by AI companies in return.
We'll be honest about where we stand. We don't like copyright as it exists. We'd like to see it radically reformed, and we wouldn't mourn it if it were abolished. Our community lives in its grey areas every day: many of the models on our sites are fan ports of characters from commercial games, made out of love and shared for free. When a studio sends us a takedown notice, we comply.
While we as small artists and fan communities get copyright used against us, the world's largest companies are committing copyright infringement at a scale unseen in human history. This has been the case since the invention of the internet of course; digital media make duplication, remixing and resharing trivial, but copyright law never caught up. Filesharing stabbed copyright in the gut. AI is just twisting the knife, and completes the creation an unequal system where copyright infringement is only a crime if you're a low net worth individual.
So we aren't asking for stricter copyright laws, or stronger protection for copyright holders. That will only benefit the major entertainment companies like Disney and Adobe who have already stacked the deck in their favor, and are happily making deals with Big-Tech and crushing small creators in the process. We're pointing out that the copyright we have isn't applied equally, and is in practice a two tier system. Individuals face ruinous damages for minor infractions. The largest companies in the world face a cost to be negotiated after the fact, if anyone can afford to sue them. A law that only works downwards gives nobody a reason to respect it, and it can't last in this form.
For time being, we'd like to ask Roblox to respect the norms of this community. You credit people. You respect the license they chose. If you want to use someone's work for something they didn't offer it for, you ask. Those norms cost nothing to follow, and Roblox's crawler followed none of them. This scrape attempt saturated the connections for our free download servers for a couple of days, causing problems for our community of legitimate human users. It shows a lack of respect for the people who make this site what it is. those who produced, shared and host the work that you were about to throw in your AI mixer.
We're sad that the emails we sent to Roblox were not met with a timely response, and would thus like to publicly ask Roblox for its response. These are the questions we'd like Roblox to answer:
We hope Roblox reaches out to us. Also, if you are a person with information on what Roblox is doing, or a fellow site owner who has been targeted, feel free to get in touch as well. We're eager to hear if there's more of a pattern to the scraper's behavior.
We've kept the full export of the relevant log files for auditing by external parties if the need arises.
Open3DLab, SFMLab and SmutBase are three community sites for free 3D resources, run by a small team. SFMLab started in 2014 for Source Filmmaker models. SmutBase followed in 2016 and is exclusively for adult content. Open3DLab, for general-purpose 3D work, joined in 2020. Creators upload characters, props, maps and environments, choose a license for each project, and anyone can download the files for free. All three sites are intended for adults only.
About the redaction. The email address in the user agent is a Roblox employee's work address. We've removed the name: this article is about what the Roblox crawler did, not about one person.
About Attribution. We take the user agent at face value. Anyone can type any email address into a user agent, and the crawler ran from Amazon's cloud, not from Roblox's own network. Nothing we've seen suggests impersonation, and the label fits Roblox's published research closely. Still, it is a self-description, and it's the first thing we'd like Roblox to confirm.

title: BRICS parliaments call for adoption of international terrorism convention
body:
NEW DELHI, October 27. /TASS/. BRICS parliamentarians are calling for the prompt conclusion of work on the Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism and its adoption under UN auspices in a joint statement released following the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum.
"We look forward to further strengthening cooperation in combating terrorism. We call for the prompt conclusion of work on the Comprehensive Convention on International Terrorism and its adoption under the auspices of the United Nations. We call for coordinated measures targeting all individuals and organizations designated as terrorist entities in accordance with UN decisions," the document says.
The parliamentarians strongly condemn all acts of terrorism, regardless of where, when, or by whom perpetrators commit them. They stress that terrorism must not be associated with any religion, nationality, civilization, or ethnic group and that all those who engage in or support terrorist activities must face accountability.
"We strongly condemn the terrorist attack in Jammu and Kashmir on April 22, 2025, which claimed 26 lives and injured many others. We reiterate our commitment to combating terrorism in all its forms and manifestations, including the cross-border movement of terrorist operatives, terrorist financing, and the provision of safe havens for them," the document says.
A Russian parliamentary delegation headed by State Duma Speaker Vyacheslav Volodin is in India to attend events marking the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum. India, which is chairing BRICS this year, is hosting the forum in its capital. The forum’s main theme is "Strengthening Parliaments for People-Centric Development."

title: China brands drop Mbappe for ‘offending national sentiments’
body: Kylian Mbappe was dropped on Tuesday by major Chinese brands after a video circulated of the Real Madrid and France superstar apparently joking about Mao Zedong. There were also signs of broader repercussions, with state-run The Paper reporting that public television was suspending broadcasts of matches from Spain’s La Liga. The offending video shows Mbappe saying that the funniest internet meme he had seen involving him was of his face photo-shopped onto that of “some guy — I think he’s a Chinese dictator”. This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappe superimposed on an image of Mao, one of several using the footballer’s face and other historical figures. The authenticity of the video could not immediately be verified by AFP Fact Check. In China, jokes about Mao, the country’s founding leader who died in 1976 — and whose drastic policies are also blamed by historians for mass starvation and millions of deaths — remain taboo. Beverage giant Dongpeng, which during this year’s World Cup ran adverts with AI-generated images of Mbappe consuming its sports drink, said it was terminating all cooperation with the France captain. “Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments,” Dongpeng said in a statement. Mengniu, China’s largest dairy producer, and cheesemaker Milkground also said that they were cutting ties with Mbappe, who until now was hugely popular among Chinese fans with millions of followers on social media. Mbappe is fondly nicknamed “Guigui”, the Chinese translation of “Turtle”, due to his popularity as a character in a Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles meme. “Dongpeng Beverage ends cooperation with Mbappe” was the top-trending topic on Chinese social media site Weibo with 430 million views. One Weibo user said that the “extremely serious wrong remarks… crossed the red line”. Others urged Dongpeng to remove Mbappe’s image from their energy drink bottles. Dongqiudi, one of China’s biggest online football outlets, said in a statement on Monday evening that Mbappe’s remarks were “offensive to China and the Chinese people”. – Furore – In an interview with French sports newspaper L’Equipe, the 27-year-old Mbappe in September addressed a previous meme depicting him as a military dictator. “There’s a part of it that’s funny… but there is another part that’s a bit less funny because of the damage such people have caused throughout history,” he said. Asked on Tuesday about the controversy, China’s foreign ministry said that it was aware of the reports. “Words and actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be met with unanimous rejection from all sectors of Chinese society,” spokesman Guo Jiakun told a regular briefing. State media outlet The Paper cited sources at the state broadcaster saying that CCTV has suspended all broadcasts of La Liga matches, and that all advertisements involving Mbappe have also been removed. On the CCTV website all searches for “Mbappe” drew no result, although there were still results for “Real Madrid”, and La Liga matches this weekend were still on its online viewing schedule. – Drawing China’s ire – Global sports stars who have commented on sensitive topics such as Taiwan, Tibet and Hong Kong have previously caused controversy in China and been dumped by sponsors there. China suspended sponsorship deals with the NBA while the state broadcaster pulled NBA games off Chinese television for a year in October 2019. This followed Houston Rockets executive Daryl Morey tweeting “Fight for freedom, stand with Hong Kong”, referring to protests Beijing called separatist and seditious. Adam Zhang, founder of the Beijing-based sports consultancy firm Key-Solution Sports Consulting, said that Mbappe’s team needed to act quickly to manage the growing crisis. “It’s crucial to make a sincere statement. The sooner, the better,” Zhang, who has advised many companies on sports advertising strategies, told AFP. Fans made their feelings clear. “I used to really enjoy watching Mbappe play on the pitch,” Zhang Jingqi, 30, who works at a mall in central Beijing, told AFP. “But ever since this news broke yesterday I have lost that admiration, sorry to say.” AFP The post China brands drop Mbappe for ‘offending national sentiments’ appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Ebola: ₦100,000 weekly allowance for quarantined contacts was unplanned – NCDC
body:
The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has revealed that its decision to pay ₦100,000 weekly to people quarantined over possible exposure to Ebola was an unplanned, temporary measure introduced on compassionate grounds after some threatened to leave the facilities.
The NCDC Director-General, Jide Idris, disclosed this on Monday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today, explaining that the agency introduced the payments to address concerns raised by quarantined contacts who said their absence from home was affecting their families and businesses.
Mr Idris said the authorities had taken affected people out of their normal environments for public health reasons, making it necessary to consider their welfare while ensuring they complied with quarantine measures.
“Those people who were in the quarantine area, there are people who never planned to be there. We took them out of their comfort zones to put them there for public health reasons,” he said.
Mr Idris said the agency had taken responsibility for their feeding and accommodation but faced complaints from some quarantined contacts who said they had families to support and businesses to run.
He said some threatened to leave the facilities because of the disruption to their daily lives, a development he described as a potential public health concern.
“If you allow them to leave the place, it’s a public health issue because you don’t know whether they will turn positive or who is ill,” he said.
Mr Idris explained that the financial support was introduced to ease tensions and encourage affected people to remain in quarantine for the period health authorities require.
He said the arrangement was temporary and had not been part of the agency’s original budget.
“It’s a temporary thing because it’s not something we’ve done,” he said, adding that the government had to intervene because the expected support from state governments was not forthcoming.
Mr Idris said state governments were responsible for providing quarantine facilities and the resources needed to manage people placed under public health restrictions.
He said the NCDC stepped in to address the immediate welfare concerns of the quarantined contacts because the necessary support had not been provided.
The agency’s intervention, he explained, was intended to prevent people from leaving designated facilities before completing the required monitoring period.
PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that the NCDC approved a weekly allowance of N100,000 for each person quarantined following possible exposure to Nigeria’s confirmed Ebola patient in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT).
Speaking on Channels Television on Monday, Mr Idris said the number of identified contacts had increased to 54 after authorities traced an Uber driver who transported the patient to the first hospital where she sought treatment.
The contacts include healthcare workers, the patient’s husband, domestic staff and personnel involved in collecting samples.
They are being monitored for 21 days after their last possible exposure, in line with Ebola’s incubation period.
Nigeria confirmed the imported Ebola case on 20 October, its first since the 2014 outbreak. The patient, a 42-year-old Ugandan-born woman living in Abuja, was subsequently evacuated to Switzerland alongside her husband.
The woman is receiving treatment in Geneva, while her husband, who had shown no symptoms, remains in isolation in Zurich.
Following their evacuation, the World Health Organisation said Nigeria had no remaining confirmed Ebola cases, noting that contact monitoring and other public health measures continue.

title: Suspected Ra'am vote bribery case transferred to Lahav 433 as Netanyahu calls for investigation
body: Following the arrest of three Bedouin residents of the Segev Shalom and Ar'ara BaNegev communities are suspected of attempting to bribe citizens to vote for the Arab Ra'am (United Arab List) party on the eve of Election Day, the case was transferred to Lahav 433 on Tuesday.Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemned the incident in a statement.“Three suspects were arrested in possession of envelopes containing cash, along with ballots for Mansour Abbas,” Netanyahu said, calling for a formal investigation into the incident.”Right-wing voters, dear Likud voters, in the face of attempts to compromise the integrity of the elections, you must go out and vote Mahal, vote Likud for the sake of our country!”According to Israeli media reports, the suspects were detained for questioning by police four hours before the polls opened, though not in the vicinity of nearby polling stations nor near those arriving to vote.“We categorically reject attempts by elements within the police to link Ra'am to the compromising of electoral integrity,” the Ra'am party said in response. “The activists were arrested at their homes hours before the polls opened, not in the vicinity of polling stations or voters.”“These are baseless arrests intended to undermine Ra'am and suppress voter turnout within Arab society, as part of [National Security Minister Itamar] Ben-Gvir's political exploitation of Israel Police.”In his own Tuesday statement, Acting Director General of the Central Elections Committee (CEC) attorney Din Livne stated that the three were “caught in their vehicle, not in the vicinity of the polling stations.”“This is an isolated incident,” Livne said, noting that there “are no other such cases.”Police seize thousands of shekels during raid on suspects' homesDuring searches of the suspects' homes, police seized envelopes containing tens of thousands of shekels in cash, along with notes and other items suspected to be connected to the offenses under investigation.The three suspects were transferred to the Southern District's Fraud Unit for questioning and are expected to be brought before a court today as police seek to extend their detention.

title: Ballon d’Or: Barcelona star honours late Nigerian mother after winning Young talent award
body: By Ayobami Okerinde Barcelona and Spain forward Vicky López has paid an emotional tribute to her late Nigerian mother, Joy Felix, after winning the Women’s Young Player of the Year award at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony on Monday. The 20-year-old attacking midfielder dedicated the honour to her mother, who died when she was 11, saying she continued to feel her presence despite her absence. “Mum, although you can’t be with me physically, I feel your presence every day. Everything I’ve achieved I owe to you, so thank you for teaching me never to give up,” López said. “Thank you to everyone in football and let’s keep making this sport better.” The Barcelona star, whose father is Spanish and mother Nigerian, was born in 2006 in Vallecas, a working-class neighbourhood in Madrid. Her journey in football began at an early age, playing in the streets with her older brother, Jesus, when she was just four. Spanish football journalist Irati Vidal told BBC Sport that López’s style was heavily influenced by street football, where she developed the flair, agility and speed that have become part of her game. “Vicky learned her craft on the streets of Vallecas, her style is very street-influenced,” Vidal said. “She used to play for fun while admiring and trying to copy Neymar’s dribbles.” López’s latest recognition follows an impressive 2025-26 campaign in which Barcelona won Liga F, the Copa de la Reina, the Supercopa de España and the UEFA Women’s Champions League. The award was her second consecutive Women’s Young Player of the Year honour, having also won the inaugural edition in 2025. Beyond her club achievements, López has set her sights on representing Spain at the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil. “I think wearing the Spain shirt is a dream that all girls who play football have,” she told Antena 3 Deportes. “For me, winning a World Cup with Spain would be one of the greatest achievements.” Her ambition is also tied to the memory of her mother, whom she has described as a major source of motivation. “For me, my mother is everything. A goal I have in life is to make her proud.” The post Ballon d’Or: Barcelona star honours late Nigerian mother after winning Young talent award appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Norway, Finland call Putin ahead of potential Abu Dhabi peace talks
body:
Editor's note: The article was updated following Russia's read-out of the call, and to include reactions from Ukraine, Denmark, and the EU.
The leaders of Norway and Finland held a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Oct. 27, as part of a renewed push to bring Moscow's war in Ukraine to an end.
"Finland and Norway border Russia. They are firm supporters of Ukraine. The aim of the call was to convey messages directly regarding future negotiations to help to end the war to President Putin," reads a press statement published by the Norwegian and Finnish governments.
The two leaders' call with Putin follows an Oct. 20 meeting in Oslo with Ukrainian, European, and U.S. officials, but they stressed that in the Oct. 27 call, they "did not speak he behalf of Europe as a whole."
"The war comes with enormous human and material costs. The suffering and destruction will impact generations. In the call we stressed the importance of de-escalation," said Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store.
"The outcome of this war will have a direct impact on our and the broader European security. Ending the war requires direct discussions," said Finnish President Alexander Stubb.
The two leaders discussed the call with President Volodymyr Zelensky afterward, who said: "I am grateful for the detailed briefing and for their active support for our diplomacy and the peace efforts we are pursuing together with all our partners."
However, not all European leaders welcomed the news.
Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen told the Danish news channel TV2 that she was "skeptical" of the call and that it had not been coordinated with others.
"I actually don't know what the two countries think can be achieved with this. I think we should stand together and speak with one voice," Frederiksen said.
Meanwhile a European Commission spokesperson reminded that "we have a shared interest in putting an end to this horrific war," in comments sent to the Kyiv Independent.
"On the EU side, we are adamantly committed not just to putting an end to the war but to achieve peace that will be just and sustainable. That is our aim and that is the stance we are defending in the ongoing talks," the spokesperson said.
The call also comes ahead of trilateral peace talks expected in the Emirati capital of Abu Dhabi sometime in November between Ukraine, Russia, and the U.S.
Though Europe is not expected to be at the table for the talks, it is engaging in multiple ways to support Ukraine ahead of any trilateral gathering, with specific countries and the EU itself participating in various talks.
A senior EU official told the Kyiv Independent to expect a round of talks in Europe before the expected Abu Dhabi meeting, after mixed messages from Kyiv had given the impression that there would be Brussels-based peace talks this week.
Finland and Norway rank among Ukraine's strongest supporters. Norway is the only non-EU country to have made a pledge to support Kyiv's 2027 financial needs.
And Finland has provided 35 different packages of financial support, and its tech companies ICEYE and Nokia recently announced a partnership with Ukraine to build out its own satellite communications system.
Russian state news agency TASS confirmed that the call had taken place and provided the Kremlin's main talking points.
Among those points, "The president of the Russian Federation and the leaders of Norway and Finland reaffirmed the importance of complying with international maritime law and the principle of freedom of navigation."
At the time of publication, at least five ships are believed to be carrying Russian diesel to the U.S. : the Maltese-flagged Agioi Fanendes , two further ships reported by the Financial Times, and two additional ships pointed out by Ukraine's sanctions chief, Vladyslav Vlasiuk.
Two of those five ships have been identified as sanctioned vessels belonging to Russia's shadow fleet — the Sierra Leone-flagged tanker Leruo and the Russian-flagged Primorye — which means European authorities are required to stop them if they enter their territorial waters.

title: Gunmen Kill Seven In Fresh Attack On Plateau Community
body: Gunmen have killed seven people in Gero community, Jos South Local Government Area of Plateau State, in a fresh attack that has heightened concerns over the security of residents. The assailants reportedly stormed the community at about 9:30 p.m. on Monday and opened fire on unsuspecting residents at relaxation spots and nearby shops. The National Publicity Secretary of the Berom Youth Moulders Association, Rwang Tengwong, confirmed the attack in a telephone interview with Channels Television, saying seven people were killed. According to him, the bodies of the victims had been deposited in a mortuary. Tengwong called on the Plateau State Government and security agencies to strengthen surveillance and intensify security operations to prevent further attacks and protect residents. He also urged the authorities to ensure that those responsible for the killings were identified, arrested and brought to justice. When contacted, the Police Public Relations Officer of the Plateau State Command, SP Alfred Alabo, confirmed that an incident had occurred in the community. Alabo said the command was making arrangements to visit the area, adding that he could not confirm the casualty figure until he received a full briefing from the Divisional Police Officer in charge of the area. He said the Commissioner of Police’s prompt response reflected the command’s continued efforts to ensure the safety of communities across the state. The police spokesman assured residents that the command would pursue the attackers and ensure they were arrested and brought to book. The post Gunmen Kill Seven In Fresh Attack On Plateau Community appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Lockheed Martin completes acquisition of Ultra Maritime
body:
Lockheed Martin has completed its acquisition of Ultra Maritime, a global defense company specializing in advanced undersea warfare and anti-submarine warfare (ASW) capabilities.
The announcement follows the company's earlier announcement that it would buy Ultra Maritime from Advent for $3.45 billion this summer.
Ultra Maritime develops and delivers mission-critical systems including sonar technologies, sonobuoys, torpedo defense systems, radar solutions, electronic warfare and autonomous maritime sensing platforms.
"Securing the undersea domain starts with giving sailors the tools and confidence to find, track and deter threats that put ships and crews at risk," said Stephanie C. Hill , president, Rotary and Mission Systems at Lockheed Martin.
"This is more than an acquisition – it’s a commitment to unite the best of our technology, capability and people to meet our partners’ urgent and growing demand for undersea warfare capability worldwide.”
Ultra Maritime’s international footprint and portfolio of ASW products, such as its sonobuoys, towed sonar arrays and hull-mounted sonar product lines, will complement and expand Lockheed Martin’s ability to offer sonar solutions across next-gen maritime platforms, it was highlighted.
The Ultra Maritime business is aligned under the Lockheed Martin Rotary and Mission Systems business area.

title: Ukraine hit Alyoshki this week despite humanitarian agreements — envoy
body:
LUGANSK, October 27. /TASS/. Ukraine has continued to strike Alyoshki and remotely mine roads to it despite an agreement on a humanitarian corridor, Ambassador-at-large of the Russian Foreign Ministry Rodion Miroshnik told TASS.
"Despite the agreements on the organization of a humanitarian corridor, the town continued to be under regular shelling by the Ukrainian armed forces, drone attacks, and roads continued to be remotely mined by the Ukrainian side," he said.
Miroshnik quoted the Russian Defense Ministry as saying that field engineering units last week defused more than 300 mines dropped by Kiev on the roads to organize the blockade of Alyoshki. In just seven days, 618 artillery strikes and 644 attacks by enemy drones on Alyoshki were recorded.

title: Nigerian newspapers review: [NESG] We’re rewriting Nigeria’s story of underperformance – Tinubu
body: In today’s Nigerian newspapers review programme, Today in the News, Vanguard leads with President Bola Tinubu saying at the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit Group (NESG) in Abuja that his administration is rewriting Nigeria’s decades-long story of economic underperformance through far-reaching reforms designed to dismantle structural barriers, unlock the nation’s enormous potential and deliver jobs, productivity and shared prosperity. Another headline features the World Health Organisation (WHO) Regional Director for Africa, Dr Mohamed Janabi, saying Nigeria currently has no Ebola cases following the medical evacuation of the patient and her husband to Switzerland. Vanguard also reports that an investigator with the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC), Yakubu Ibrahim, on Monday, told a Federal High Court in Abuja that both the University of Nigeria (UNN) and the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) disowned the degree and discharge certificates presented by former Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, Uche Nnaji, to the Senate for his ministerial screening in 2023. Moving to another newspaper, The Guardian reports that despite 25 State Houses of Assembly endorsing the State Police Bill, persistent fears over political interference, human rights violations and weak accountability have raised questions about whether the proposed safeguards can protect citizens from abuse or remain largely theoretical. The Punch leads with organised labour looking forward to its next action after a crucial meeting with the Federal Government on Tuesday, with the Nigeria Labour Congress and Trade Union Congress demanding concrete proposals on petrol prices, wage negotiations and other unresolved workers’ welfare issues amid the threat of nationwide industrial action. Lastly, Daily Trust reports that the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, said some Nigerians spend as much as 120 per cent of their income on food, forcing them to borrow money or rely on relatives to survive. title: Kyiv’s State University of Trade and Economics damaged, no students or staff killed
body:
As reported by Ukrinform, Minister of Education and Science Andrii Butenko said this in a Facebook post.
“Overnight, Russia once again cynically targeted educational infrastructure. The shelling damaged academic buildings and dormitories of the State University of Trade and Economics,” the minister said.
Butenko added that according to preliminary information, several people were injured. They received the necessary medical assistance. No students or university staff were killed, and information circulated overnight about fatalities has not been confirmed.
He urged everyone involved in the educational process to immediately seek shelter during an air raid alert.
According to Butenko, the university is assessing the damage, while the Ministry of Education and Science is in contact with the university’s management to provide the necessary assistance.
As reported by Ukrinform, the consequences of Russian ballistic strikes in Kyiv since the evening of October 26 were recorded in six districts. A 46-year-old woman was killed and 15 people were injured.
Air defense forces downed two ballistic missiles and 255 drones used by Russian forces to attack Ukraine since the evening of October 26.

title: CBD COP17: Nigeria’s environment minister arrives Armenia for biodiversity talks
body:
Nigeria’s Minister of Environment, Balarabe Lawal, has arrived in Yerevan, the capital of Armenia, to participate in the ongoing 17th session of the United Nations Biodiversity Conference (CBD COP17).
Mr Lawal arrived on Monday, ahead of the high-level segment scheduled for 27 and 28 October, when ministers and other senior government officials are expected to address barriers to implementing the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF), adopted in 2022.
According to the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) Secretariat, approximately 1,500 people, including 140 ministers and deputy ministers of finance and environment, are expected to participate in the high-level segment.
The segment comes as negotiations enter their final stretch, with delegates seeking to translate global biodiversity commitments into concrete action before the conference concludes.
The CBD Secretariat said negotiators made progress during the opening week, adopting four decisions under COP17 on invasive alien species, gender, education and knowledge management.
Eight substantive decisions were also adopted under the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety, covering monitoring and reporting, compliance, and the strengthening of national processes for effective implementation.
Additionally, two decisions advancing the Nagoya Protocol on Access and Benefit-sharing were achieved, focusing on monitoring and reporting and compliance.
Among other issues, the global review of progress towards the biodiversity framework will consider evidence from the State of Biodiversity Action report, launched by UN Secretary-General António Guterres ahead of COP17. The report found widespread national commitment but significant gaps in ambition and implementation.
“COP17 is enabling a total mobilisation of more than $1.8 billion from all sources — governments, philanthropic organisations and investors — in support of strong biodiversity action,” said COP17 President Hambardzum Matevosyan.
“The first week has shown that cooperation can deliver progress. The second week must demonstrate that political commitment can deliver action.”
Since negotiations began last week, biodiversity financing has remained one of the most contentious issues, particularly for developing countries seeking substantial financial support to implement the global framework.
Discussions have focused on mobilising additional public and private funding, improving access to existing resources and redirecting environmentally harmful subsidies towards activities that support nature conservation.
A major issue is the implementation of the Cali Fund, established following COP16 to support benefit-sharing from the commercial use of digital sequence information (DSI) on genetic resources.
The mechanism seeks to ensure that companies benefiting from the commercial use of such information contribute to biodiversity conservation and its sustainable use.
For African countries, the debate is closely linked to equity, resource ownership and the continent’s capacity to finance conservation.
African negotiators argue that the continent’s rich biological resources support commercial activities worldwide, while the benefits generated from their use do not adequately reach the countries and communities from which those resources originate.
They are pushing for benefit-sharing arrangements that deliver tangible financial resources for biodiversity protection, community development and the implementation of national conservation plans.
Negotiators are also discussing ways to mobilise private investment and redirect environmentally harmful subsidies. The global biodiversity framework calls for at least $500 billion annually in harmful incentives to be eliminated or redirected by 2030.
Upon his arrival at the COP17 venue, Mr Lawal was received by Nigerian delegates and national focal points.
The minister also formally presented certificates for the $50,000 Rapid Deployment Mechanism (RDM) grants won by Nigeria and six other countries to Joseph Onoja, director-general of the Nigerian Conservation Foundation (NCF), and members of his team.
PREMIUM TIMES reported earlier that Nigeria and six other countries under the High Ambition Coalition (HAC) for Nature and People won $50,000 seed grants each under the RDM to execute projects aimed at accelerating progress towards their 30×30 conservation targets.
The 30×30 target seeks to ensure that at least 30 per cent of the world’s land and sea areas are effectively conserved and managed by 2030.
Mr Lawal is expected to deliver Nigeria’s national statement during the high-level segment.
As the UN Biodiversity Conference enters its final week, governments face the challenge of resolving outstanding disagreements over biodiversity financing and economic incentives that continue to drive nature loss.
The conference comprises COP17, the 12th Meeting of the Parties to the Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety and the sixth Meeting of the Parties to the Nagoya Protocol on Access and Benefit-sharing. It is scheduled to close on Friday.
The CBD Secretariat said the second week of negotiations must demonstrate that political commitments can translate into action.
Conference organisers said achieving meaningful results would require governments to place biodiversity at the centre of economic and financial decision-making, a priority underscored by the participation of finance ministers.
“Nature is not a luxury we protect when economies can afford it. Nature is what makes economies possible. The arrival of finance ministers at COP17 sends an important signal,” said Inger Andersen, United Nations under-secretary-general and executive director of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP).
“Biodiversity loss is not simply an environmental problem. It is an economic problem, and the solutions must reach into the heart of economic decision-making.”
The scale of the challenge is reflected in financial incentives that continue to drive biodiversity loss, often undermining investments in conservation and restoration.
“Financing the destruction of nature with 30 dollars against every dollar spent restoring it is like paying 30 people to tear down your house for every one hired to rebuild it,” said Astrid Schomaker, executive secretary of the CBD.
Ms Schomaker identified three priorities for translating commitments into results: accountability, alignment and acceleration.
Accountability involves using national reports, scientific evidence and the first global review to identify shortcomings and guide stronger action.
Alignment requires ensuring that public budgets, private investments, economic policies and financial incentives support, rather than undermine, global biodiversity objectives.
Acceleration entails moving faster to implement the framework’s 23 targets by 2030.
“The global review showed us where progress is being made and where we are falling behind,” she said. “Yerevan focuses all Parties on closing those gaps.”
However, closing the gaps will require governments to overcome significant differences in the negotiations.
Major questions remain over which countries and stakeholders should contribute to international biodiversity financing, how much funding should be mobilised and the mechanisms through which the resources should be channelled.
Parties also remain divided over language on reducing or phasing out harmful incentives, including agricultural subsidies.
Other unresolved issues include which commercial users of digital sequence information should contribute to the Cali Fund, arrangements for a new permanent body on Indigenous Peoples and local communities under Article 8(j) of the Convention, and how biodiversity action should align with climate commitments and other international obligations.

title: Houthi official says Egypt’s military support for Saudi declaration of war
body: A Houthi official said Tuesday that the Egyptian parliament’s decision to authorise military support for Saudi Arabia to defend against the Iran-backed group’s attacks was a declaration of war. The comment was part of a long statement reacting to a Monday visit to Tehran by the Saudi defence minister, alongside Pakistan’s army chief and Turkey’s intelligence chief, in a bid to de-escalate tensions in the Middle East war. “It is truly remarkable that while these people go to discuss what they call ‘peace in the region’, Egypt and its parliament declare support for the so-called defence of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and in doing so, declare war against the Republic of Yemen,” said Mohammed Ali al-Houthi, a member of the Houthis’ political bureau, in a Telegram post. Saudi Defence Minister Khalid bin Salman, Pakistan’s army chief General Asim Munir and Turkey’s intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin attended the talks with Mohsen Rezaei, head of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council. They also met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian. Iran, Pakistan and Turkey recently signed a Nato-style defence pact in Mecca that says an attack on one country is to be considered an attack on all three. But since the Houthis ramped up attacks on Saudi Arabia earlier this month, the two other countries have not announced any strikes on the group. Al-Houthi said the pact was “a clear and blatant act of aggression against the Islamic Republic of Iran”, adding that the group was “not afraid of any alliance that may be formed”. In July, Yemen’s conflict flared up again as a fragile 2022 truce fell apart after the Houthis allowed an Iranian plane to land in Yemen’s capital Sanaa, in defiance of Saudi control over Yemeni airspace, setting off a spate of attacks. The Houthis then declared a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and began hitting its ships, territory and oil facilities, before launching a major offensive in September in which they seized Yemeni government-held territory along the Red Sea coast. In response, the Houthis have reported frequent Saudi strikes targeting areas under their control. In October, the Houthis ramped up their attacks on Saudi Arabia, forcing the cancellation of flagship events and a shutdown of Riyadh airport for two weeks. title: Russian ballistic missiles hit a Kyiv university campus, then return before dawn for the Southern Bridge again
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Russia attacked Kyiv with ballistic missiles and drones in two waves, killing one person, injuring civilians, and damaging university dormitories and apartment blocks, the city military administration said . Russian strikes also killed two people in Kharkiv on the evening of 26 October and wounded civilians in four other oblasts overnight. Daytime attacks on 26 October killed people in Donetsk, Dnipropetrovsk, and Kharkiv oblasts. Russia's war against Ukraine grinds on along the front, where on 26 October alone Russian forces dropped 247 guided bombs and used 9,679 kamikaze drones, the General Staff reported . Behind the front, Russian missiles and drones keep hitting Ukrainian cities, while Washington presses Kyiv rather than Moscow. Ukraine was reportedly told to spare Russian refineries or lose US intelligence and arms. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has accused US President Donald Trump of trying to pressure Ukraine into capitulating, and a Ukrainian diplomat argues that Trump treats Ukraine as the weak link to be squeezed. Two ballistic waves hit a Kyiv campus, the center, and the Southern Bridge Shortly after 22:00 on 26 October, Russian missiles hit near a metro station in Kyiv's left-bank Desnianskyi district, Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported . An ambulance crew that had arrived at a call came under fire, and two medics were injured . Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko inspects damage on the Southern Bridge after a Russian ballistic missile strike, 27 October 2026. Photo: Vitali Klitschko/Telegram The missiles struck the grounds of one of Kyiv's universities, its campus, Kyoto Park, nearby homes, and the area beside a metro station, Zelenskyy wrote . “ There is no military facility nearby ,” he said. In Dniprovskyi district, the blast wave blew out windows in a medical facility's intensive care unit, Klitschko said . A three-story non-residential building in the district partly collapsed . Medics treat people beside a damaged ambulance in Kyiv after a Russian attack, 26 October 2026. Photo: DSNS Kyiv The evening strike also damaged the metro between two left-bank stations and the exits of Lisova station, Klitschko said . Explore further Kyiv gets no warning of the first of two Russian ballistic waves, hours after Zelenskyy said US alerts were back A second wave followed before dawn on 27 October. Missiles hit an administrative building in Podilskyi district, Klitschko reported , and at 05:04 he said Russia had hit the Southern (Pivdennyi) Bridge and the metro infrastructure on it. Police closed the bridge to traffic, and green-line trains stopped crossing it. Russian strikes had already damaged metro infrastructure on the same bridge on 22 October. The overnight attack set two non-residential buildings on fire in Obolonskyi district, and two more people were injured . A crater left after a Russian ballistic missile attack on Kyiv, 26 October 2026. Photo: DSNS Kyiv By morning, a 46-year-old woman was dead and 15 people were injured, among them dormitory residents and two medics, the Kyiv City Prosecutor's Office said . Prosecutors counted at least 12 damaged apartment blocks, as well as a burns center, a shopping mall, and a tram. Rescuers work beside a fence pocked by shrapnel in Kyiv after the Russian attacks of 26–27 October 2026. Photo: DSNS Kyiv Kyiv was the main target of the night, the Air Force said , as Russia launched Iskander-M/S-400 ballistic missiles and 280 drones. Air defenses downed two of the missiles and 255 drones. Zelenskyy put the night's total at 16 ballistic missiles and called the attack “ a serious escalation in the Russian operation against our logistics .” He blamed delays in deliveries of interceptors for Patriot and NASAMS air defense systems. “ Artificial and lengthy delays in the delivery of interceptor packages for Patriots and NASAMS, which unfortunately have been happening lately, directly help Russia achieve the goals of its terrorist campaign. Every such delay is a new Russian hit on one target or another .” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy Russian strikes kill two in Kharkiv and wound civilians across Ukraine Russian strikes on Kharkiv's Novobavarskyi district on the evening of 26 October killed two men and injured four people, including a 17-year-old girl, oblast head Oleh Syniehubov said . On the morning of 27 October, a Russian missile hit Izium, damaging eight houses. A building destroyed by a Russian strike in Kharkiv's Novobavarskyi district, 26 October 2026. Photo: Oleh Syniehubov/Telegram In Zaporizhzhia, a Russian strike on a gas station wounded two people, and a later strike on a car wounded a 17-year-old boy, the oblast administration said . In Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, Russian drones and aerial bombs injured three women in Synelnykove district overnight. Houses damaged by a Russian missile strike in Izium, Kharkiv Oblast, 27 October 2026. Photo: Oleh Syniehubov/Telegram In Chernihiv Oblast, Russian attacks set homes on fire and injured six people, including a child, the oblast administration said . In Chernivtsi Oblast, a drone attack damaged an energy facility, cutting power until 02:15 and injuring two security guards, oblast head Ruslan Osypenko said . Russian attacks have also critically damaged electrical equipment in northern Khmelnytskyi Oblast, the regional power company said . Over the past day, Russian attacks killed civilians in Donetsk, Dnipropetrovsk, and Kharkiv oblasts On 26 October, Russian attacks killed three people in Donetsk Oblast and wounded 22, oblast head Vadym Filashkin said . His breakdown puts 16 of the wounded in Yasnohirka, where Russian aircraft dropped guided bombs. A Russian drone strike on Pavlohrad killed one person and wounded seven, and a drone killed a woman in Shevchenkove, Kharkiv Oblast. In Kherson, a Russian drone hit a health facility and wounded a nurse. Most of Konotop in Sumy Oblast has been without power since Russian strikes on 24 October, with no forecast for its return, the mayor said . Patriot systems are the only ones in Ukraine that reliably stop Russia's Iskander-M ballistic missiles, and their missiles have waited almost a month for a US signature. Every week of that wait leaves cities like Kyiv facing waves like this one with fewer interceptors, which is why Kyiv is also asking Lockheed Martin directly for more. It can’t be rebuilt, and world is queuing for more power equipment

title: Full Haskell-like Type Class resolution in Java
body:
This post explores how far Java’s type system can be pushed by building a small Haskell-style type class instance resolution engine entirely in plain Java.
Using only reflection, generic type metadata, and a tiny first-order unifier, we can automatically resolve type class instances (including higher-kinded ones), support overlapping instances, and derive witnesses for arbitrarily nested generic types.
It’s not intended for production, but as an experiment it reveals just how much structure Java actually preserves at runtime — and how surprisingly close it can get to type-level programming without language changes.
You can also jump straight to the full implemention in this gist .
Update: I published a GitHub repo for the project at github.com/garciat/java-type-classes .

However, Dup is now only compatible with types that extend Equatable . Dup is now less capable.
We could have checked at runtime if each object is instanceof Equatable , but that doesn't work very well with generics. And it may fail at runtime.
Dup implements Equatable<Dup<A>> if and only if A implements Equatable<A> .
Also, if you think about it, it is a bit strange that the definition of equality for a type A depends on the object instance. As in, eq() is an instance method.
It would make more sense if equality depended only on the type A itself. Right?
The code is rather simple, but it marks a dramatic change of perspective:
Equality now belongs to the type definition and not to an object instance.
Type classes can be seen as a pattern that allows us to model shared behavior in a way that puts types first AND is entirely compositional.
Now, in the above example, how do we actually use Dup 's eq() ?
We must first construct the witness Eq<Dup<Point>> by chaining calls to the respective Eq witness constructors of Dup and Point .
Then, we use this witness to access/invoke the actual logic that we're after.

With witness constructors as our building blocks, we can recursively construct infinitely many witnesses, as needed.
In Haskell, type class 'implementations' are called instances .
Here, I am calling them witnesses because that's how Java's Architect, Brian Goetz, decided to refer to them in a recent talk he gave about bringing type classes to Java sometime in the future.
Now, wouldn't it be great if we didn't have to manually construct these witnesses?
Which means that the witness() method is able to automatically construct the required witness for Show<List<List<Integer>>> .
First, we must understand some aspects of how Java generics work at runtime.
It is a well-known fact that Java generics get erased at runtime.
However, there are a few scenarios in which generics do get reified!
Note: 'Type Reification' is the process by which type information is made concrete and available at runtime.
This means that Java did preserve the generic type arguments for the supertype Stream<Integer> . (We just need to know where to look for it.)

In order to reduce our search scope, we can define the following convention:
When trying to resolve a witness C<T> for some type class C and a concrete type T , then we only look for witness constructors within the definitions of C and T and nowhere else.

Type unification is the process of finding a substitution that makes two types identical.
For example, given Pair<[A], String> and Pair<Integer, String> , then the substitution {A -> Integer} would make the first type identical to the second.
