title: Nammo to expand rocket motor production with €50 million in EU and Norwegian support
body: The European Commission awarded €25 million to the ROCMAN project through the European Defence Industry Programme’s Industry Ramp-up Acceleration initiative. The Norwegian government will match that contribution. “Europe needs a stronger and more resilient defense industrial base and this investment enables Nammo and our partners to expand capacity faster, strengthen supply security, and deliver the capabilities that allied armed forces need,” said Morten Brandtzæg, Nammo’s president and chief executive officer. The company is investing in production capacity to meet growing demand for missile propulsion systems. ROCMAN also includes improvements to site security and access to essential raw materials and components. Additional storage capacity in Germany is intended to make the supply chain more responsive and better able to handle surges in demand. Six companies are participating: Nammo Raufoss in Norway, Diehl in Germany, an unnamed Irish company, ARCEON in the Netherlands, Magnaghi in Italy and Fast Forward Architects in Belgium. ROCMAN was one of eight strategic projects selected by the European Commission following a competitive process. Nammo said the work would strengthen European defence readiness and support sustained supplies to allied armed forces. It did not disclose a completion date, production targets or the project’s total cost.

title: HGL Wins Award for Generational Excellence in Family Business
body: Honeywell Group Limited (HGL) has won the Generational Excellence in Business Award at the 2026 Family Business Leadership Awards, in recognition of its transition across three generations and its sustained business growth. The award was presented on October 15 at the Mike Adenuga Centre, Ikoyi, Lagos, during the Family Business Summit organised by BusinessDay in partnership with PwC Nigeria. HGL, which formalised its operations in 1972, has evolved from a trading business operating across West Africa into a Nigerian investment holding company with interests in flour milling, real estate, financial services and infrastructure. Foluke Oyeleye, Non-Executive Director, and Tomi Otudeko, Chief Operating Officer, received the award on behalf of the Group. Speaking on the recognition, Otudeko traced the business to her grandmother, noting that her father later formalised it to establish a more structured enterprise. “Honeywell Group started three generations ago from my grandmother. It was my father’s wish to formalise the business, which at the time was trading across West Africa,” she said. “Over 50 years later, the business has been passed down to the third generation, and it is wonderful to be recognised for excellence.” Oyeleye dedicated the award to her parents, attributing the Group’s journey to what she described as God’s grace. She also acknowledged the contributions of HGL’s employees and the support of her six siblings, particularly the leadership of Managing Director Obafemi Otudeko. At the summit, Otudeko participated in a fireside chat titled “More Than a Surname: Building a Reputation That Outlives the Founder,” where she discussed the importance of building credibility alongside an established family legacy. “Legacy may provide a platform, but reputation is earned through consistency, competence, and character,” she said. Oyeleye also spoke at the NextGen Spotlight Session, where she reflected on how businesses can preserve the lessons of previous generations while embracing fresh perspectives. Drawing on her experience outside the family business and her involvement in the team that championed HGL’s investment in Econet, she highlighted the role of inherited knowledge and new ideas in sustaining a business across generations. Family businesses play a significant role in Nigeria’s economy. Findings presented by PwC Nigeria at the 2024 Family Business Summit indicated that they account for more than 70 per cent of the country’s small and medium-sized enterprises and contribute close to half of its gross domestic product. For HGL, the award marks a milestone in a business journey spanning more than five decades. The Group says it remains focused on building businesses and creating lasting value for future generations.

title: C. Equatoria orders schools to charge fees in pounds, threatens closures
body: The Central Equatoria State Ministry of General Education and Instruction on Tuesday ordered all schools to charge tuition fees and related costs in South Sudanese pounds instead of foreign currencies. The directive, issued on Tuesday by caretaker Education Minister Lupai Satimon Andrew, warned that institutions that violate the directive could lose their operating licenses or face closure. The order follows recent inspections that raised concerns over exorbitant school fees charged in US dollars, poor school management, inadequate learning environments, and insufficient daily lesson coverage. “All schools operating in Central Equatoria State (CES) are hereby directed to charge school fees and any related costs in South Sudanese pounds as opposed to foreign currency, including United States Dollars (USD), in the academic year 2027,” Lupai told journalists during a press conference on Tuesday. “Failure to adhere to this order is tantamount to withdrawal of operational license, including possible suspension/closure.” The minister said the order was prompted by concerns over excessive school fees, particularly those charged in foreign currencies, poor school management, inadequate learning environments and insufficient coverage of lessons. He also stated that school land in urban areas must measure 400 by 400 meters and warned that institutions unable to meet the requirements will not be allowed to operate in the state from 2027. “All private school facilities must meet minimum operational standards as indicated in the general education policy of the Ministry of General Education and Instruction (MoGEI), in which school land in the town must measure 400 x 400 meters, including a clean and conducive learning environment to accommodate all school activities,” he stated. “Therefore, any school that cannot conform to the required standard shall not be allowed to operate in Central Equatoria State come 2027.” Minister Lupai further directed schools to observe official working hours, with classes beginning at 8:00 a.m. and ending at 4:00 p.m. He said there should be no admission or movement of pupils/students after 8:00 a.m. “Teacher’s workload and learning coverage; it has been noted that the majority of the schools operate below standards. The general timetable and coverage do not agree as per the fact that schools open late and close early by 12:00 noon,” he said. “Hence, this order is directed to all head teachers, teachers, Inspectors and supervisors to see to it that teachers’ workload of eight periods per day is put to use. Evidence is the scheme of work and copies of lesson plans. The school calendar must be followed strictly.” “All the schools are directed to establish PTAs and school management committees in their respective institutions for easy management, transparency and accountability. Any school that fails to comply with this order shall be punished accordingly,” Minister Lupai concluded. The post C. Equatoria orders schools to charge fees in pounds, threatens closures appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Anosike Vows to Build Common Facility Centre for Aba Leather, Garment Clusters
body: Boniface Okoro in Umuahia The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate for the 2027 elections in Abia State, Dr. Kelechi Anosike, has promised to build a world-class Common Facility Centre (CFC) in Aba to boost the leather and garment clusters. Anosike made the promise in Aba when he met with representatives of the Leather and Garment Clusters, comprising over 200,000 members, as part of his ongoing campaign tour of the commercial city. He said the proposed CFC would be a solar-powered industrial and technical hub equipped with world-class machines to enable Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs), especially young tailors, shoemakers and garment makers who lack capital, to produce international-standard finished products. According to him, “The model would replicate what the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency of Nigeria (SMEDAN) did in Abuja, where tailors register their materials, pay a token of N5,000, now N10,000, to access all machines in the centre to finish jobs for their customers and keep the proceeds. “I said we will set up a solar-powered centre with all kinds of world-class machines. Like what SMEDAN did in Abuja-on the tailoring aspect.” The PDP candidate recalled that a similar facility built in Aba in 2008 by the United Nations Industrial Development Organisation (UNIDO) in partnership with the federal and Abia State Governments was abused, vandalised and eventually abandoned by successive administrations, thereby defeating its empowerment purpose. He said his administration would bring back the concept as a deliberate empowerment strategy, stressing that apart from the CFC, his government would establish a Traders Microfinance Bank to provide interest-free loans and grants to traders and clusters to scale up production and reduce dependence on imports. Anosike argued that while white-collar jobs are limited, thousands of SMEs can be created if government partners traders to produce locally made goods for which Nigeria spends over $10 to $20 billion annually importing, despite having the raw materials in abundance. Anchoring his campaign on what he termed ‘productive welfarism’, the governorship hopeful said his mission is encapsulated in the slogan ‘Aruo Uzo, Aruo Afo’ (build roads, build people), insisting that infrastructure is meaningless if the people are not alive and economically empowered to use it. “I’m a welfarist, and welfarism is not to give you handouts; it’s to empower you to support the state. It is called productive welfarism,” he declared. He criticised what he described as anti-people taxes on the poor, vowing to abolish them, and lamented that despite the increase in federal allocation to Abia State from about N3.5 billion to about N40 billion monthly, there was “zero welfare” to cushion the effects of subsidy removal. In his remarks, the National Secretary of Aba Leather and Garment Clusters, Mr. Ken Anyanwu, said the delegation came to introduce the over 200,000-member body to the candidate and to seek a more detailed engagement on how to upgrade the clusters to world-class status. Anyanwu, who doubled as cooperative president, said Aba leather and garment products are number one in Africa, lamenting that while other countries are wooing Aba artisans, successive Abia State Governments have neglected them. According to him, SMEs remain the pivot of economic growth and should be prioritised by any people-oriented government, pledging the support of the members. He stressed that Anosike’s manifesto holds the key for the clusters. Those at the event included Abia State PDP Deputy Chairman and senatorial candidate for Abia South, Chinyere Onuoha; Aba North/Aba South federal constituency, Bob Ajuzieogu; the Aba Central House of Assembly candidate, Anastasia Uchenna; Hon. Daniel Ajunwa (Obere Agu), and other House of Assembly candidates for the state constituencies. They all urged the people of the state to vote for the PDP in 2026. Also speaking, the state Director, National Youth Service Corps (NYSC), Chris -Monike Chika, appealed to all political parties to ensure the safety of the corps members before, during and after elections in the state, urging them to treat them like their own children.

title: Keeping API keys out of our AI agent's sandbox, and what that doesn't solve
body:
Doozy runs tasks against our customers' databases, Stripe and GitHub from a Slack thread. Here's how the agent does that without ever holding a key, and the risks a missing key doesn't remove.
Shiv Sarthak Sabhlok 27 October 2026 · 9 min read
Doozy is an AI agent people mention in Slack. Someone writes "@Doozy why was Acme charged twice?" in a support thread, and it goes and checks: it queries the database , reads Stripe , looks at the code in GitHub , and posts what it found back in the thread.
So the first question every engineer asks me is about AI agent security, and it's the right one: you're giving an LLM production credentials? This is the long answer. Most of it is deliberately boring. The interesting part is what's left over once the keys are gone.
The agent never holds an API key. Each task runs in a fresh sandbox that holds only a signed, short-lived job token. A credential proxy outside the sandbox checks that token, decides whether the tool is allowed, and adds the real key to that one call. Database queries run read-only, with a timeout and a row cap. That stops keys leaking. It doesn't stop prompt injection misusing the tools you've switched on, so those are the controls that matter most.
Every task runs in its own sandbox, a small VM that exists for that one job and is thrown away after. Nothing in it is a credential for your systems. No API keys, no database password, no model provider key, no GitHub token.
When the agent needs something outside, the call leaves the sandbox and goes to a gateway we run. The gateway decides whether the call is allowed, attaches the right credential, forwards it, and passes the response back. The agent sees results. It never sees the secret that produced them.
None of this is new. A credential proxy, a service that injects keys into requests so the caller never sees them, is an old pattern, the one you'd draw on a whiteboard in five minutes. That's the point. When the thing on the other side of the boundary is a language model that will read anything it can reach, I want the boundary to be the most boring part of the system.
It matters because prompt injection isn't solved, and I don't expect it to be soon. A support ticket, a web page, a PDF someone drops in the thread: any of it can carry instructions. If one gets through, the agent can misuse the tools it has. What it can't do is print a key, write it to a file or send it somewhere, because there isn't one to find.
The sandbox isn't empty. It holds a job token, and every call it makes carries it. If you're thinking "so that's the credential", you're right. The design is about making it a poor one to steal.
The claims are small enough to read at a glance:
So the worst case for a stolen token is someone making the calls this job could already make, through our gateway, for as long as the job runs. That's not nothing, and I come back to it below. It's a lot smaller than a leaked Stripe key that works from anywhere until someone notices.
Every call goes through the same steps, in the same order.
The sandbox's network is fenced too. The cloud metadata endpoint and private address ranges are unreachable from inside it, so the agent can't wander from its VM into the machines around it.
The database connector is where people expect the scariest stories, so it gets the strictest rules, and none of them depend on the prompt. The model writes a query. Before it runs, the gateway wraps it:
Read-only is not the same as safe. The agent can read whatever its database user can read, and it can post that in Slack. The right setup is a user scoped to the tables it needs, on a replica if you have one, and every query it ran is in the thread for anyone to check.
Some work genuinely needs a secret inside the sandbox: a CLI that only takes a token, an SSH key for a deploy. Saying no to all of it would make a lot of real tasks impossible.
So there's one door. The agent asks for a secret by name and says why. The request is logged with its reason, and only then is the value handed in.
This is the part I'm least comfortable with. Once a value is inside, a prompt injection can ask for it too. The log tells you exactly what was asked for and why. It doesn't tell you what happened to the value afterwards. I've accepted that trade because the alternative was a product that can't do half of what teams ask, but if you see a better design, I'd like to hear it.
Taking the keys away removes one failure: losing a credential. It doesn't touch the ones that matter more. Here's what an attacker gets if a prompt injection takes over a job.
So the controls that matter sit on the far side of the gateway: which tools are on, what each one can read, and receipts that put every action in front of the people in the thread. Our security page lists them, and AI and data use covers what the model sees and keeps. A thread turns out to be a good audit surface. People notice when their coworker does something odd in front of them.
The question I keep going back and forth on is whether a person should approve an action before it happens. Today the answer is tools that start off, plus a receipt for everything. Approval on every step turns a coworker back into a form to fill in. Approval on nothing is how you end up in an incident review. I suspect the answer is per tool, but I'd rather hear from people running agents against production than guess.
Update, 30 October: it's per tool now. An admin can set any connected tool to Needs approval. When Doozy wants to use it, the gateway doesn't run the call. It seals the exact arguments and posts them in the thread with Approve and Reject. Approving runs that call, as shown, once. Nothing runs if nobody decides within a day, and every other tool keeps working like a teammate.
When I tested models for this on a synthetic billing investigation, credentials turned out to be the easier problem.
In one run the task folder sat next to the grader. One model found the answer key and graded itself, in all five runs. Moved into a sealed container, it still did the task well, and still spent several steps going through environment variables, /root and /tmp looking for something useful. That's when "give it nothing to find" stopped being a slogan for me.
The harder failure was quieter. Every model family I tested, at least once, told the customer "we've deployed a fix" when the fix only existed as a change in the repo. No key leaked and nothing was deleted. It just said something untrue, confidently, to a customer. So Doozy's operating rules forbid calling something done until it is, and it's the rule that gets broken most.
If you build AI agents that touch production, here's what I'd take from all this. Lock the credentials away early, because it's cheap and mechanical. Then spend the real effort on what the agent can read, what it's allowed to say, and making sure the people around it can see what it did.
If you see a hole in any of this, write to me at [email protected] . I read all of it.
Mention @Doozy in a Slack thread with a real task. It does the work in your own tools, with your keys kept on our side of the boundary, and posts the answer and a receipt for everything it did.
Shiv builds Doozy end to end, from the product to the pages that explain it. Doozy began as an internal tool for a few teams, who still hand it real work every day. These pages are kept in step with what the product does.
Questions about this page? Write to [email protected] .

title: OpenAI's Ted Sanders shares a rule of thumb for picking the right GPT-model
body:
OpenAI's Ted Sanders has categorized the new GPT-6.1 Terra and explained how the company names its language models. According to Sanders, model performance is multidimensional. A model that's great at math won't automatically be good at jokes. Still, most performance gaps come down to one variable: model size. Sanders says OpenAI's model names are difficult to simplify because model size, reasoning effort, and multi-agent systems are distinct dimensions. Combining them into a single "IQ score" would obscure details.
And size doesn't explain everything. Newer, smaller models can outperform older, larger ones through better training data or improved architectures. GPT-6.1 Terra is likely better than the larger Astra at technical communication and roughly matches it in image processing and computer use at a much lower price point, but falls short in most other areas, Sanders says. "If you care about quality only, pick Astra. If you're a bit price sensitive, pick Sol. If you're very price sensitive, pick Terra or Luna."

title: Social Policy Ministry developing new social service standard for victims of missile strikes
body:
Kyiv Regional State Administration, in collaboration with the Ministry of Social Policy, is developing a new standard for a social service designed for those affected by missile strikes, announced Ihor Meschan, Director of the Department of Social Protection of the Population at the Administration.
"Kyiv region is constantly suffering from barbaric Russian air strikes and missile attacks. In effect, we must provide services to those affected. This is, in fact, a brand-new type of service; together with the Ministry of Social Policy, we are currently developing a new standard for services intended for victims of missile strikes," he stated during a press conference at the Interfax-Ukraine news agency on Tuesday .
Photo: Interfax-Ukraine / Oleksandr Zubko Photo: Interfax-Ukraine / Oleksandr Zubko Photo: Interfax-Ukraine / Oleksandr Zubko Photo: Interfax-Ukraine / Oleksandr Zubko Photo: Interfax-Ukraine / Oleksandr Zubko Photo: Interfax-Ukraine / Oleksandr Zubko Photo: Interfax-Ukraine Photo: Interfax-Ukraine From needs assessment to real solutions: How to make social services in kyiv region communities accessible and person-centered
He noted that Kyiv region comprises 69 territorial communities. "Each community is unique; some are very robust and organize social services exceptionally well, in full compliance with all legal requirements. For others, we—along with Caritas Kyiv—provide ongoing guidance to help them meet the state standards established by the Ministry of Social Policy," Meschan said.
According to official data, the population of Kyiv region is 1,790,000. "However, these are pre-war figures; we estimate that the actual number of people living in Kyiv region now exceeds 2 million... It is worth noting that 544,320 of these individuals receive pensions or disability payments. Clearly, this presents a massive challenge, as one in four people is unable to work, and the state must ensure they are cared for," Meschan said.
According to data from Kyiv Regional State Administration, the region is home to 133,832 war veterans, 68,976 combatants, over 13,000 family members of those who died, and 10,451 individuals with disabilities resulting from the war. "Consequently, social services have set as their primary objective the task of supporting the families of the fallen and those who have been wounded, most of whom, unfortunately, subsequently develop a disability," emphasized Meschan.

title: Ghana’s Black Meteors can ‘100%’ end long-standing Olympic absence – Ofei
body: Ghana’s Black Meteors head coach Desmond Ofei is confident the U-23 national team can end their long-standing absence from the Olympic Games by qualifying for the 2028 edition in Los Angeles. The Meteors have not featured at the global showpiece since the 2004 edition in Athens. The team are currently in camp intensifying preparations for their Africa U-23 Cup of Nations qualifying campaign against Libya. “The boys are, like I said, very hungry to prove themselves and to give a good show,” Desmond said. “So, it will be a good game, and we’ll do very well. We’ll do everything in our power to beat Libya and then, in March, take on whoever comes. So, we’ll be ready. We’ll be ready for sure.” Asked whether Ghana could end their Olympic absence, Ofei said: “100%. I believe so because we feel that the time is right. It’s been way too long, and we are preparing really well. The boys are very hungry to prove to the nation that there’s a lot of talent in this country.” Ghana will travel to Libya for the first leg on November 11 before hosting the return fixture six days later. The qualifying campaign consists of three rounds, with seven nations set to join hosts Egypt at the eight-team U-23 Africa Cup of Nations finals.

title: Sandra Mbanefo Obiago, Others to Headline FWIFT Convention 2026
body: Art, cultural expert and curator, Mrs Sandra Mbanefo Obiago will deliver the keynote address at this year’s national convention of Forum of Women in Film and Television Nigeria (FWIFT) holding on Thursday. The event holding at the historic Glover Memorial Hall in Lagos is themed theme “One Industry, Many Voices: We Build Together.” The gathering will unite women across film, television, radio, advertising, and digital media to connect, share insights, and create agency for one another across sectors. Besides presentation by Sandra Mbanefo Obiago, the programme will feature interactive panel discussions, break-out sessions, speed networking, and a fireside chat titled “The Cross Over: A Career Beyond Borders.” A statement by FWIFT noted: “Featured speakers and panellists joining the conversation include media executive Kadaria Ahmed, filmmaker Biodun Stephens, media personality Gbemi Olateru-Olagbegi, executive director Rosemary Egabor-Afolahan, and Esosa Osagiede.” It added that the convention is free and open to the public. “Our goal is to build an interconnected media ecosystem where women across screen, broadcast, and digital platforms can pool resources and create collective momentum. “By bringing together diverse practitioners under one roof, we are establishing practical pathways for cross-industry growth, mentorship, and cross-border careers that elevate African storytelling on the global stage,” it quoted FWIFT leadership as saying. According to statement, the convention is sponsored by the African Women’s Development Fund (AWDF) “FWIFT is a professional organisation dedicated to empowering Nigerian women in screen-based, audio, and digital media through advocacy, skill acquisition, mentorship, and strategic networking. “It is called Forum of Women in Film and Television Nigeria (FWIFT) that gives free support and be reached through fwiftnigeria@gmail.com and https://fwiftnigeria.org/,” it added.

title: Russian attacks across Ukraine kill four, injure 57 over past day, as Kyiv comes under ballistic missile assault
body:
Russian attacks across Ukraine have killed at least four and wounded at least 55 others over the past day, Ukrainian authorities said on Oct. 27, as Russia launched an overnight missile and drone blitz against the capital, Kyiv.
Russian attacks hit Kyiv's Southern Bridge, disrupting metro services, as well as a university campus, an administrative building, and medical centers.
At least one person was killed, and 15 people were injured in the latest Russian attack on the capital, Ukraine's State Emergency Service (DSNS) said. Those injured in the attack include a paramedic, a medical technician, and a 20-year-old university student.
According to the Ukrainian Air Force, Russia attacked Kyiv with an unspecified number of S-400 and Iskander ballistic missiles, launched from Bryansk Oblast, and with 280 strike drones of various types, 69 of which were jet-powered.
Two ballistic missiles and 255 Russian strike drones, including 56 jet-powered drones, were shot down by Ukrainian air defense or suppressed by electronic warfare.
There were 25 locations reported struck by Russian munitions in the capital, as well as 16 locations that were struck by falling debris from downed missiles and drones.
In Chernihiv Oblast, six people, including a 12-year-old child, were injured in a number of Russian attacks, according to regional authorities.
In Chernivtsi Oblast, two men were lightly njured in a Russian drone strike, according to regional authorities.
In Donetsk Oblast, three people were killed and 22 people were injured in a number of Russian attacks, according to regional authorities.
In Kherson Oblast, four people were injured in a number of Russian attacks, according to local authorities. These included a 62-year-old nurse who was injured when a Russian "Molniya" drone struck a hospital in the city of Kherson.
In Sumy Oblast, three people were injured in Russian drone strikes, according to regional authorities.
In Zaporizhia Oblast, five people were injured as a result of Russian attacks, including a 17-year-old boy, according to regional authorities.

title: Stubb, Støre discuss end to Ukraine war with Putin
body: President of Finland Alexander Stubb and Prime Minister of Norway Jonas Gahr Støre held a telephone conversation with Russian President Vladimir Putin, during which they discussed Russia's war against Ukraine, diplomatic efforts to end it, and upcoming peace talks in Abu Dhabi, reports the office of the President of Finland.

title: Delta APC: We ‘ll Run Issue-Based Campaign Devoid of Violence
body: Omon-Julius Onabu in Asaba Delta State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has assured the people of the state of its readiness to run an issue-based and rancour-free campaign towards the 2027 general election. The party therefore, urged political actors in the state to shun all acts of violence, hate speech or inflammatory statements and actions capable of fisrupting the prevailing peace in the state. Chairman of the Media and Publicity Committee of the Delta State APC Campaign Council, Mr Charles Aniagwu, gave the assurance on while unveiling members of the Media and Publicity Committee to journalists in Asaba. Aniagwu, who is also the Delta State Commissioner for Works (Rural Roads) and Public Information, listed other members of the Media Committee to include Mr Valentine Onojeguo (Vice-Chairman), Mr Timi Tonye (Secretary), Sir Festus Ahon (member), Sir Kelly Okolugbo (member) and Mr. Jackson Ekwugum (member). The focus of the state APC’s campaign would be on “the performance of President Bola Tinubu and Governor Sheriff Oborevwori” vis-a-vis their respective administrations’ policies and programmes, Aniagwu stressed. Aniagwu said that the APC would remain focused by explaining the policies and reforms of the federal and state governments, expressing optimism that the programmes would contribute to a better future for Deltans. The media and publicity committee chairman the committee would work closely with journalists to ensure that the electorate received accurate information on the candidates and their programmes. The committee’s responsibility shall transcend the governor and the president to cover all APC candidates contesting elections into the State House of Assembly, House of Representatives, and Senate. Aniagwu said: “We will stay with the issues,” Aniagwu said, urging journalists to partner with the committee in communicating the party’s message to the electorate. He said the campaign would be guided by the need to address governance and matters affecting the welfare of the people, adding that the committee had the experience to respond to questions and provide relevant information on the candidates and their policies. Aniagwu, however, cautioned political actors against statements capable of inciting violence, warning that inflammatory rhetoric could encourage supporters to take the law into their own hands. He stressed that the state government would not tolerate violence, irrespective of the political affiliation or background of those involved. “The governor has warned earlier that nobody is above the law. We will not tolerate violence, irrespective of the divide anybody belongs to,” he said. The APC campaign spokesman said: “We will not get involved in rigging elections. We will show our report card,” expressing confidence that the performance of the Tinubu and Oborevwori administrations would provide the APC with a strong basis to seek re-election. Saying the party believed voters would assess its candidates on their records and policies, he urged political leaders and their supporters to exercise restraint in their public statements, particularly as the electioneering season approaches. While warning against remarks that could provoke attacks or encourage reprisals at polling units, he said; “we are not in a jungle republic. If there is anybody carrying out an action you consider not to be in line with the electoral guidelines, that is why we have the security agencies. Report them and let the law take its course.” He described calls for jungle justice as inimical to the peace and stability of Delta State, urging residents not to be influenced by statements that could turn political disagreements into violence.

title: Finnish and Norwegian leaders spoke with Putin by phone about ending war with Ukraine
body: Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre spoke by phone with Vladimir Putin, the Finnish president’s office said . The statement said the call was ”a follow-up of the meeting in Oslo on 20 October.” That day, the Norwegian capital hosted talks between Donald Trump’s special envoy Steve Witkoff and representatives of Ukraine. Stubb and Støre initiated the call to discuss Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine and the diplomatic efforts to end the war and promote peace and stability in Europe. The statement from the Finnish president’s office said the purpose of the call was to directly convey to President Putin Ukraine’s position on the upcoming peace talks in Abu Dhabi. On October 20, a meeting was held in Oslo between Trump’s special envoy Steve Witkoff and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. Finnish President Alexander Stubb also took part. After this meeting, Witkoff traveled to St. Petersburg, where he met with Putin — then he returned to Oslo and flew to the U.S. from there. Following these talks, the parties agreed to hold a new trilateral meeting between Russia, the U.S., and Ukraine. It will take place after November 4 (that is, after the U.S. midterm elections) in Abu Dhabi. After this latest stage in the return to peace talks between Ukraine and Russia, European countries began looking for a representative who could take part on the EU’s behalf. Among the candidates for this role, The Telegraph named Stubb and Støre, as well as Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, Czech President Petr Pavel, and Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen. title: EDB to Provide Over $30 Million for Astana Data Center Project
body: The Astana Times provides news and information from Kazakhstan and around the world. ASTANA – The Eurasian Development Bank (EDB) will provide $31.2 million in financing for the construction of a commercial data center in Astana, expanding Kazakhstan’s digital infrastructure and computing capacity, the bank announced on Oct. 19. EDB Senior Managing Director Ignatov and AKASHI Data Center Chairman Minkevich highlighted the project’s role in expanding Kazakhstan’s digital infrastructure and positioning the country as an exporter of digital services. Photo: EDB press service The agreement was signed with AKASHI Data Center PLC. The project marks the first data center construction project in the EDB’s investment portfolio. The planned campus will have a total capacity of 100 megawatts (MW), with approximately 10 MW allocated to the first phase. The company estimates the project’s total investment at $354 million. The first phase is scheduled to begin commercial operations in 2027. The facility is designed to provide data storage and processing services for financial institutions, technology companies and cloud service providers. The Uptime Institute has awarded Tier IV Certification of Design Documents for the first phase. Sergey Ignatov, EDB senior managing director and head of the project block, said the investment supports Kazakhstan’s priorities in digitalization and artificial intelligence. The project will expand opportunities for businesses to use modern data infrastructure and support the development of digital services, he said. AKASHI Data Center Chairman of the Management Board Vladislav Minkevich said the project aims to position Kazakhstan as an exporter of digital infrastructure services, attracting international companies seeking to host computing workloads in the country. He said such activity could generate export revenues and increase demand for local engineering, telecommunications and other services. The campus will comprise four independent data center modules, supported by dedicated power and telecommunications infrastructure. One module is being designed for high-density artificial intelligence workloads and high-performance computing, using liquid cooling technology. The facility will operate as a carrier-neutral data center, with four independent optical fiber entry points and connectivity options through Kazakh and international telecommunications operators. The EDB is a multilateral development bank focused on investment and economic integration across Eurasia. As of the end of December 2025, the bank reported that its cumulative portfolio comprised 348 projects with total investments of $22.1 billion. The post EDB to Provide Over $30 Million for Astana Data Center Project appeared first on The Astana Times .

title: Navantia launches seventh corvette for Saudi navy under programme running to 2029
body: The new order follows five corvettes built between 2019 and 2024. Construction is taking place at Navantia’s San Fernando and Puerto Real yards in the Bay of Cádiz, with delivery of the final vessel scheduled for 2029. “Launching one ship every four months is in line with the industrial schedule established for the programme and reflects the commitment of Navantia’s workforce to the customer,” said Ricardo Domínguez, Navantia’s chairman. “Your dedication, experience and professional excellence allow us to say with confidence that Navantia is rigorously fulfilling the commitments it has undertaken.” Navantia will deliver the first ship of the new batch in Spain, while the second and third will go to Saudi Arabia for combat-system work. The fourth and fifth corvettes under the earlier contract followed the same approach. “From today, a new chapter begins: the integration of her systems, testing, sea trials, training, and the road toward full operational readiness,” said Vice Admiral Mohammed Bin Abdulrahman Al-Ghuraybi, chief of staff of the Royal Saudi Naval Forces. “And one day, HMS NEOM will leave these shores and set her course toward the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.” Navantia estimates the contract will generate approximately four million working hours and support an average of 2,200 skilled jobs a day in the Bay of Cádiz. More than 20 subcontractors and 50 suppliers from several countries will participate. An agreement between the Saudi and Spanish navies covers integrated logistics support, crew training and operational evaluation by the Spanish Navy at Rota Naval Base. Navantia will provide support during that period and carry out work during the corvettes’ dry-docking periods in San Fernando. The new vessels will be identical to the first batch, based on Navantia’s Avante 2200 design. Their missions include maritime surveillance, search and rescue, protection of strategic assets, intelligence gathering and anti-submarine, anti-air, anti-surface and electronic warfare. The ships will carry the HAZEM combat system supplied through the SAMINavantia joint venture, HERMESYS communications and DORNA fire control. Other Navantia equipment includes the integrated platform management system and MINERVA integrated bridge.

title: Toronto election 2026: Who’s in and who’s out at city hall
body:
Toronto voters elected seven new councillors Monday, defeating several incumbents and returning one former councillor to city hall.
Longtime councillor Frances Nunziata and mayoral candidate Brad Bradford are among those leaving council, while former Liberal MP Nate Erskine-Smith and former councillor Mike Layton are among the incoming members. Eighteen incumbents were returned to council.
Bradford lost his mayoral bid to Olivia Chow, who will serve her first full term as mayor after winning the 2023 mayoral byelection.
Here’s the full list of who’s in and who’s out at Toronto City Hall, along with the councillors returning to office.
Diana Chan McNally will represent Ward 4 Parkdale-High Park. The ward was previously represented by longtime councillor Gord Perks, who retired earlier this year.
After multiple attempts at securing the job, Chiara Padovani will replace Nunziata – the longest-serving member of city council – as the councillor for Ward 5 York South-Weston.
Former councillor Mike Layton is returning to city hall as the representative for Ward 11 University-Rosedale. The seat was vacated by Dianne Saxe, who ran in Ward 14 Toronto-Danforth.
Curran Stikuts will represent Ward 13 Toronto Centre, taking over the job from incumbent Chris Moise.
Sara Ehrhardt will become councillor for Ward 14 Toronto-Danforth. It was previously represented by Paula Fletcher, who announced her retirement this summer. Saxe finished third in the race.
Nate Erskine-Smith, a former MP who sought the leadership of the Ontario Liberal Party earlier this year, will represent Ward 19 Beaches-East York – the seat vacated by Bradford.
Former Liberal MP Shaun Chen, who resigned from federal politics in August citing lingering health effects from a car crash, will represent Ward 23 Scarborough North – defeating incumbent Jamaal Myers.

Stephen Holyday – Ward 2 Etobicoke Centre
