title: How Nigerians Should Prepare For El Niño — NEMA
body: Nigerians have been advised to take steps to protect themselves against the effects of the El Niño phenomenon. El Niño is a natural climate phenomenon that occurs when sea-surface temperatures in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean become warmer than normal. It is the warm phase of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), which also includes the cooler La Niña phase and neutral conditions. It can disrupt atmospheric circulation and influence rainfall and temperature patterns worldwide, though effects vary by location due to local conditions. In a Monday advisory titled “Super El Niño Is Coming: What You Can Do to Protect Yourself, Your Family and Your Community,” the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) outlined eight measures individuals, households and communities could adopt to reduce the risks and stay safe. It warned that “Super El Niño can cause hotter temperatures, less rainfall, drought, floods and food shortages.” In its Seasonal Climate Prediction Update for August 2026 and the August-September-October 2026 Rainfall Forecast, the Nigerian Meteorological Agency stated, “Analysis of the most recent ocean observations confirms the onset of a strong El Niño event in 2026.” It added that “El Niño continues to intensify steadily and is expected to dominate global climate patterns during the August to October 2026 season.” NiMet also described it as a “super El Niño” with significant implications for Nigeria’s rainfall patterns and noted that it increases the likelihood of above-normal temperatures globally. Measures Recommended By NEMA Include: Reduce Time Under Hot Sun Limit outdoor activities during peak heat hours (11 am – 4 pm). Use shaded areas and wear a hat or cap. Take regular breaks and stay hydrated. Plan your activities for early morning or late evening. Don’t Waste Water Use water wisely and avoid waste. Fix leaks and store water in clean, covered containers. Keep your environment clean to protect water sources. SUPER EL NIÑO IS COMING. ARE YOU PREPARED? As Nigeria prepares for the anticipated 2026/2027 Super El Niño phenomenon, taking precautions early can help protect lives, livelihoods and property. Stay informed through official weather updates, follow safety advisories, prepare your household for possible emergencies, and work with your community to reduce disaster risks. Preparedness starts with you. Protect yourself, protect your family, protect your community. Follow NEMA’s official channels for verified information and safety guidance. #NEMA #SuperElNiño #DisasterPreparedness #EarlyWarning #EarlyAction — NEMA Nigeria (@nemanigeria) October 25, 2026 Extreme Heat Is Coming Stay hydrated – drink clean water regularly. Avoid direct sun between 11 am and 4 pm. Wear light clothing, hats, and use sunscreen. Check on children, the elderly and vulnerable people. Protect Your Health Prevent heat-related illnesses and dehydration. Keep your surroundings clean to avoid malaria and water-borne diseases. Ensure proper sanitation and handwashing. Seek medical help early when unwell. Food Security Store enough food for emergencies. Support local farming and home gardening. Protect your livestock and poultry. Take advantage of agricultural support programmes. Livelihood Use drought-resistant crops and improved farming practices. Diversify income sources. Access government and partner support programmes. Seek Information Follow updates from NEMA, the Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet) and trusted media channels. Heed official advisories and warnings. Report emergencies to NEMA and relevant authorities. Community Action Join community early warning and preparedness efforts. Share information with neighbours and families. Look out for the most vulnerable in your community. The post How Nigerians Should Prepare For El Niño — NEMA appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Channel 14 reporter verbally assaulted, harassed while covering voting in Haifa
body: Channel 14 northern correspondent Gal Tobi was verbally assaulted and harassed while covering voting at a polling station in Haifa's Denya neighborhood on Tuesday morning, she told Walla.Tubi arrived at the polling station alone, without a cameraman. According to her, a man approached her, stood uncomfortably close, and touched her equipment, including during a live broadcast.Tubi said the man accused her of filming people in the background. She explained that she was in a public space and even adjusted the camera angle to ensure that only she appeared on screen. Despite her efforts to accommodate his request, she said the man continued to interfere with her work."Even though I accommodated him so as not to offend anyone, he stood very close to me and harassed me," she said.Tubi claimed the man arrived with two others and later told his companions, "We don't want Channel 14." She also said she heard remarks against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during the incident, while others at the polling station intervened and tried to defend her."They started acting like bullies, disrupted my broadcast and touched my equipment," Tubi recounted. "I was verbally attacked and harassed," she added.The incident left Tubi visibly distressed, and she broke down in tears. She said that she and her colleagues at Channel 14 had encountered similar incidents while carrying out their regular reporting duties.Addressing the incident during a Channel 14 broadcast, Tubi made clear that she intended to continue her journalistic work despite what had happened."We'll get through this and continue bringing you the voices from the field. We won't pay attention to people like that. Not everyone here is like that," she said.'All brothers here'Ofer Winter, chairman of the People of Israel party, condemned the reported attack and harassment of the Channel 14 correspondent in Haifa."We are all brothers here! We must put an end to attacks by one brother against another," he said.Winter called on law enforcement authorities to take action, saying the incident was the latest in a series of similar cases involving journalists and media crews."There is no place for this violence in Israeli society, and any attack on media outlets doing their jobs must be condemned clearly and unequivocally," he said.

title: Britain will not join Canada-led defense bank initiative
body: Britain will not join the Canada-led Defence, Security and Resilience Bank, in a setback to efforts to create the world’s first global defense bank, according to a person familiar with the matter. The two countries instead said on Sunday that they would develop a framework for cooperation between their respective defense-funding initiatives, establishing two distinct but complementary institutions to support each other on investment opportunities and strategic challenges. “We have been working closely to consider how the Multilateral Defence Mechanism (MDM) and Defence, Security and Resilience Bank (DSRB) can best advance our shared objectives,” the statement said. The two governments were unable to agree on key issues including the location of the headquarters of a joint institution, the level of joint procurement, lending to members, and the rules around new members, a second person said. The MDM will focus on accelerating defense investment, joint procurement through financing, and bringing together demand across NATO allies to reduce procurement costs, while the DSRB will complement it by supporting investment in defense industries and supply chains, focusing more on single sovereign lending, the person added. The DSRB, which will be based in Canada, has faced challenges securing support from larger European nations. Reuters was first to report in September last year that Britain had declined to join the project. There were hopes Britain would reconsider its position under new Prime Minister Andy Burnham and his team. Germany had previously declined to join. A spokesperson for the German finance ministry said Germany was an observer in the negotiations on DSRB’s charter and is reviewing open questions. Britain and Canada said the MDM and DSRB will be designed to work in close partnership, so they can support each other on emerging industrial priorities, investment opportunities and strategic financing challenges. The DSRB has been aiming to raise around €100 billion ($112 billion) and use the money to lend at low cost to governments and contractors for defense projects. It will also offer guarantees for lenders financing smaller firms seen as riskier borrowers. So far Albania, Belgium, Greece, Latvia, Luxembourg, Romania, Turkey and Ukraine have pledged their support, along with Canada. Canadian Finance Minister Francois-Philippe Champagne said the group would meet in Luxembourg on Nov. 30 to sign articles of agreement establishing the bank. “Membership (is) open to other allies and close partners who share the Bank’s objective,” he said in a statement. Reuters previously reported that potential members had not joined because of concerns including whether the DSRB can offer cheaper financing than highly rated national governments as well as the amount of capital countries would need to commit, the bank’s governance, and overlaps with existing initiatives. Britain’s Defence Secretary Wes Streeting had recently described the DSRB as a “really interesting and innovative mechanism” and said that he did not see the proposed defense bank and MDM as being in competition. Britain previously declined to join, citing concerns over value for money. Reuters previously reported that Burnham discussed the DSRB alongside the MDM initiative with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney in July and with Luxembourg Prime Minister Luc Frieden during an August visit to Kyiv.

title: Philippine peso’s historic slide continues, hitting record low P64.17 per dollar
body: MANILA, Philippines – The Philippine peso breached the P64-per-dollar level for the first time in history on Tuesday, October 27, sinking to another record low as the local currency continued its losing streak despite the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas’ (BSP) aggressive interest rate hikes. The peso closed at P64.17 against the US dollar, weakening by 22 centavos from its previous record-low finish of P63.95 a day before on Monday, October 26, according to data from the Bankers Association of the Philippines. The local currency opened trading at P63.95 before weakening to an intraday low of P64.20. The historic depreciation comes just days after the BSP delivered a “jumbo,” larger-than-expected 50-basis point rate hike on October 22, bringing its key policy rate to 5.50% as inflationary pressures continued to mount. Despite the peso’s continued slide, BSP Governor Eli Remolona Jr. has maintained that the central bank will not defend the currency at any particular level. “We’re not hiking the policy rate to defend the peso,” Remolona said during a briefing on October 22. “We have estimates of how much the peso has to move before it becomes inflationary, and that’s when we tend to intervene.” Remolona did not disclose the level of depreciation that would trigger intervention, saying it could give currency speculators an advantage. “But there is a threshold. Not every depreciation is inflationary. It has to be significant enough,” he said. The BSP governor explained that intervention would only cushion excessive currency movements rather than stop the peso from weakening altogether. “We don’t end up preventing the peso from depreciating,” Remolona said. The central bank governor said that the BSP’s model does not put any specific significant on psychological thresholds such as the P63:$1 or P64:$1. The peso closed at P63.52 to the dollar on October 23, the day that BSP announced its latest rate hike. Former BSP deputy governor Diwa Gunigundo likewise said the BSP’s rate hikes were done primarily to prevent second round effects of inflation, not to halt the slide of the peso, which is being affected by separate factors. In a DZBB radio interview on Tuesday, Gunigundo pointed to the country’s weak capital flows, balance of payments deficit, and low levels of foreign investment as the fundamental factors behind the peso’s falls. Another non-fundamental shock affecting the peso-dollar exchange rate is what he calls the “cloud of uncertainty” that hangs over investors amid the corruption allegations and political troubles afflicting the Philippines. The former deputy governor said the government should strive to restore investor confidence by tackling corruption, improving rule of law, and speeding up the impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte. A weaker peso makes dollar-denominated imports, such as oil, more expensive for Filipino consumers and businesses, potentially adding to already elevated inflation. For OFW families, a weaker peso may seem like a boon since they get more pesos for every dollar sent home, but that gain is partly eroded if the same currency weakness pushes up the cost of fuel, food, transport, and other everyday expenses anyway. – Rappler.com Must Read Flood control corruption cleanup spooks investors, drags PH growth – World Bank

title: Burna Boy makes history at Ballon d’Or awards
body:
Nigerian singer Burna Boy became the first Nigerian artist to present an award at the Ballon d’Or ceremony, handing the 2026 Sócrates Award to Arsenal forward Bukayo Saka at the London Palladium on Monday night. The Grammy-award-winning singer presented the award to Saka, an England international of Nigerian heritage, during the 70th edition of football’s prestigious individual awards ceremony.
The honour recognises footballers who make significant contributions to humanitarian causes and social development beyond the pitch.
Burna Boy used his appearance to talk about his football academy in Nigeria, explaining that he established the initiative to support the sport’s development in his home country.
“Something I started a few years ago, just to support the football culture back home. Hopefully, inshallah, one day I’ll come back here to see one of my people getting an award in the Ballon d’Or,” he said.
The Grammy-winning singer was introduced on stage by the ceremony’s hosts, Kate Scott and former France international Thierry Henry, before presenting the trophy to Saka.
The appearance adds to Burna Boy’s growing association with major international football events. He previously performed at the 2023 UEFA Champions League final kick-off show in Istanbul, Turkey.
Meanwhile, Burna Boy and Wizkid have also explored the connection between music and football in their 2021 collaboration, “Ballon d’Or,” using the prestigious award as a symbol of excellence and success. His appearance at Monday’s ceremony amplifies his association with football’s biggest stages.
Saka received the Sócrates Award for his charitable work with BigShoe, an organisation that provides medical assistance to children in need.
Through the initiative, the Arsenal forward supported life-changing surgical procedures for about 120 children in Kano State, Nigeria, in 2022.
He undertook the effort in recognition of his Nigerian heritage and helped children access treatment for conditions requiring medical intervention. He subsequently supported procedures for another 100 children in Rwanda, Kenya and Tanzania in 2023.
During his acceptance speech, Saka thanked France Football and highlighted the importance of giving children opportunities to live healthy lives and pursue their ambitions.
He also read a letter from Biringiro, a 14-year-old boy from Rwanda whose eyesight began deteriorating when he was 12. BigShoe provided the child with eye care after his condition made everyday activities, including moving around his home and reading in school, increasingly difficult.
In the letter, Biringiro described how the treatment had changed his life.
“Then thanks to BigShoe, I received the eye care that I needed. Today, I can read the blackboard even from the back of the classroom,” he was quoted as saying.
Reflecting on the initiative, Saka said helping children regain opportunities they might otherwise lose was important to him.
“We know how it feels to be a child and have a ball at your feet and how much joy you have. Every time I have the opportunity to help another kid have that feeling again, that’s important to me,” the striker said.
The 25-year-old footballer added that he worked with his family and BigShoe to support children who lacked access to opportunities others had.
“It’s an honour to be here, and it’s an honour to receive this award. On behalf of all the children we’ve been able to help, thank you,” he said.
France Football established the Sócrates Award in 2022 in collaboration with Peace and Sport. Named after the late Brazilian footballer Sócrates, the honour recognises humanitarian and social initiatives supported by players and their foundations.
Previous recipients include Senegalese forward Sadio Mané, Brazilian forward Vinícius Júnior and Spanish footballer Jenni Hermoso.
The 2026 ceremony marked the first time the Ballon d’Or awards were held in London. The venue was chosen to commemorate the award’s 70th anniversary.
England captain and Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane won the men’s Ballon d’Or, becoming the first Englishman to claim the award since Michael Owen in 2001. Spain’s Alexia Putellas won the women’s prize for the third time.
Other winners included Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal, who received the men’s young talent award, while Unai Simón and Cata Coll won the men’s and women’s goalkeeper honours, respectively. Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona were named men’s and women’s clubs of the year.
Meanwhile, Nigerian footballers have featured in the Ballon d’Or rankings, with Nwankwo Kanu, Finidi George and Victor Ikpeba among the early nominees. Victor Osimhen recorded Nigeria’s highest finish, placing eighth in 2023, while Ademola Lookman finished 14th in 2024.
However, no Nigerian has won the award. Liberia’s George Weah remains the first and only African to win the men’s Ballon d’Or in 1995.
Nigerian singer Adekunle Gold also attended the ceremony’s red carpet, joining Burna Boy in representing the country’s music industry at the event.
The singer, popularly known as AG Baby, shared his excitement, saying, “Another year that I’ll be invited for the Ballon d’Or, and this time, I’ll be performing at the after-party”.
Their appearances follow other occasions when Nigerian artistes have featured at major international football events.
In 2023, Rema became the first African artiste to perform at the Ballon d’Or ceremony, delivering his hit song Calm Down in Paris. He also performed at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.
Burna Boy also performed at the 2023 UEFA Champions League final, while Davido performed at the closing ceremony of the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar.
Recently, Ayra Starr also made history as the first African artist to headline a halftime show at the NFL International Games. The latest appearances highlight the growing presence of Nigerian music stars at major international sporting events.

title: BRICS parliaments call for unilateral sanctions to be lifted
body:
NEW DELHI, October 27. /TASS/. BRICS parliamentarians are calling for the removal of unilateral economic sanctions, as such measures undermine international law, according to a joint statement approved at the 12th BRICS International Parliamentary Forum.
"We condemn the use of unilateral coercive measures that are contrary to international law and reiterate that such measures, particularly in the form of unilateral economic sanctions and secondary sanctions, have wide-ranging adverse effects on human rights, including the right to development, as well as the health and food security of people in the countries concerned. We call for the removal of such unlawful measures, which undermine international law and the principles and purposes of the United Nations Charter," the document says. TASS has obtained a copy of the statement.
BRICS parliamentarians also firmly denounce all violations of international humanitarian law, including deliberate attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure, including on the territories of member states. They also denounce the denial of humanitarian access and attacks on humanitarian personnel. "We stress the need to ensure accountability for all violations of international humanitarian law," the joint statement says.
State Duma Speaker Vyacheslav Volodin is heading the Russian delegation participating in the 12th BRICS International Parliamentary Forum in New Delhi, where India holds the presidency. This year’s forum focuses on "Strengthening Parliaments for People-Centric Development."

title: Qatar emir meets Iran president, energy ties in focus

title: What Israel’s Election Could Change for Ukraine and Relations With Russia
body:
Israelis head to the polls on Tuesday, Oct. 27, in the country’s first national election since the Hamas-led attacks of Oct. 7, 2023. The government that emerges could make consequential decisions for Kyiv, which has spent years seeking greater Israeli military assistance, and now has increasingly valuable experience to offer in return.
Domestic concerns dominate the campaign. In a September Israel Democracy Institute poll , 41% of respondents selected the economy and cost of living among their two leading electoral considerations, while 38% chose foreign affairs and security. Conscription and relations between religion and the state also featured prominently.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Russia’s war against Ukraine nevertheless enters the debate through a question Israelis understand directly: How to confront Iran and the countries helping it.
Opposition leader Yair Lapid has explicitly connected that question to greater assistance for Kyiv. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s government has also acknowledged common interests, although warmer language has yet to settle the limits of military cooperation.
When Russia launched its full-scale invasion, Israel attempted to mediate between Moscow and Kyiv while balancing its relationships with both.
Then-Prime Minister Naftali Bennett traveled to Moscow in March 2022 , met Vladimir Putin and spoke repeatedly with President Volodymyr Zelensky. He subsequently traveled to Berlin to discuss the diplomatic effort with German Chancellor Olaf Scholz. The mediation did not produce a settlement.
Israel provided humanitarian assistance, including a field hospital, while resisting Ukrainian requests for major Israeli weapons systems. Its caution reflected, among other considerations, Russia’s military presence in Syria and Israel’s determination to preserve its ability to strike Iranian-linked targets there.
Netanyahu later signaled that he might reconsider military assistance. In a February 2023 CNN interview , he said he was “definitely considering” it. That statement, however, was not a commitment to deliver particular weapons.
The regional circumstances have since changed dramatically. The Hamas-led attacks, subsequent fighting with Hezbollah, direct conflict with Iran, and the fall of Bashar al-Assad’s government in Syria have altered the security calculations behind Israel’s approach to Moscow.
Israel and Ukraine share a common enemy: Tehran.
Iran has supported Hamas and Hezbollah while supplying Russia with Shahed attack drones and the technology behind their production. Ukraine has consequently accumulated years of experience detecting and intercepting weapons that also threaten Israel.
In March 2026, a source in Zelensky’s office said Ukraine was prepared to share operational experience and domestically produced drones with Israel . Kyiv expected greater military assistance in return, including help with air defense.
The potential exchange changes the relationship. Ukraine is seeking Israeli support while offering knowledge developed through daily combat against Iranian-designed weapons.
Netanyahu acknowledged that common ground in an August letter marking Ukraine’s Independence Day, describing Iran as a threat to both countries. Foreign Minister Gideon Sa’ar also expressed interest in deepening cooperation with Ukraine following contact with Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha in July.
Lapid has made one of the clearest statements about how policy could change after the election.
In a September interview with the Russian-language outlet Ulpan Politika, reported by NAnews , he promised:
“If we return to power, we will do much more than we did then.”
He described Russia as “an ally of Iran,” linking closer ties with Ukraine to Israel’s own security. Lapid also pointed to Ukrainian technologies, particularly those used against drones, as a reason for expanding military cooperation.
He did not identify weapons systems, quantities, or a delivery timetable. His position nevertheless goes beyond a general expression of sympathy – he is proposing greater cooperation as part of the policy his camp would pursue in government.
Lapid also defended the caution of the government he served in during 2022 , arguing that its decisions reflected Israel’s security requirements at the time. His argument now is that the circumstances have changed, including Russia’s relationship with Iran and Ukraine’s technological capabilities.
Support for a stronger relationship is not confined to Netanyahu’s opponents.
Amir Weitmann, a Likud member and vocal advocate of greater assistance to Kyiv, criticized his own government’s approach in a March interview .
“I’m not happy with the behavior of the Israeli government toward Ukraine,” he said.
Weitmann argued that weakening Iran would benefit Ukraine by damaging a supplier of Russian war material. His position demonstrates support within Likud for a stronger partnership, although it is not a government commitment or a party-wide pledge.
Netanyahu’s recent outreach, meanwhile, emphasizes shared threats and closer relations. The distinction for Kyiv is between acknowledging that partnership and authorizing the assistance Ukraine has requested.
Despite the common security interests, relations between the two countries have repeatedly encountered disputes.
One of the sharpest concerns was grain shipments arriving in Haifa in April which Ukraine said had originated in Russian-occupied territory.
The confrontation became public and bitter. Kyiv demanded action, while Israeli officials disputed the handling and supporting documentation of Ukraine’s requests. Sa’ar accused Kyiv of conducting “social diplomacy” – Ukrainian officials maintained that they had already pursued diplomatic channels.
An Israeli importer ultimately rejected the cargo aboard the Panormitis . That decision prevented the shipment from being unloaded, but did not resolve the wider disagreement over how Israel should respond to trade involving occupied Ukrainian territory.
For Ukraine, the issue was both practical and political: Russia was profiting from occupied land while Kyiv struggled to secure action from a potential partner.
Those tensions will remain part of the next government’s inheritance, alongside the discussions about drones and air defense.
Moscow’s relevance to the election extends beyond Israeli policy toward Ukraine.
On Oct. 25, Channel 12 reported that a civilian cybersecurity company working alongside the Shin Bet had disrupted an alleged Russian influence operation involving roughly 80 fictitious social media accounts.
According to The Times of Israel’s account, Channel 12 did not identify the company or disclose the source of its information. The Shin Bet had separately announced the removal of profiles linked to a foreign influence campaign, without publicly establishing in that statement the Russian attribution reported by Channel 12.
An October INSS assessment also examined Russian-linked Doppelganger activity targeting Israeli audiences. Its central concern was the erosion of trust in institutions, the electoral process, and other groups within society, rather than evidence that the operations could deliver victory to a particular party.
Ukraine’s experience investigating Russian influence operations offers another area for cooperation. Sharing information about fabricated stories, impersonated outlets, and coordinated accounts would not require the same political decisions as transferring sensitive weapons.
A source in Jerusalem said in August that major decisions concerning Ukraine were unlikely before the election and the formation of the next government.
Tuesday’s vote determines the composition of the Knesset. Coalition negotiations follow, and could take weeks. Politicians advocating closer cooperation will still have to secure agreement from their governing partners.
An opposition victory would not automatically deliver Israeli weapons to Ukraine. Another Netanyahu-led government would inherit the rapprochement already underway.
Yet, it is the concrete decisions that will matter: whether discussions on drone defense produce agreements, whether assistance expands, and whether Russia’s support for Iran changes the limits Israel places on cooperation with Kyiv.
Both countries will have to translate words into action.
Lesia Dubenko is a Ukrainian political scientist and analyst. A graduate of Lund University (MSc in European Affairs), she covers issues relating to international affairs, migration, and disinformation.

title: Russia strikes military-industrial enterprises, transport infrastructure in Kiev overnight
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Russian forces launched a large-scale overnight attack, hitting military-industrial enterprises and transport infrastructure facilities in Kiev, a logistics center in Kharkov Region, as well as maritime vessels supporting Ukraine, the Russian Defense Ministry reported.
TASS has summarized the main information about the targets struck.
Russian forces conducted a massive overnight strike against targets in Ukraine using precision-guided ground-based weapons and unmanned aerial vehicles, the Russian Defense Ministry reported.
According to the ministry, the strike targeted Ukrainian military-industrial enterprises engaged in the production and storage of cruise missiles and long-and medium-range unmanned aerial vehicles, transport infrastructure facilities in Kiev, a logistics center in Kharkov Region, as well as maritime vessels used to support the Ukrainian army.
The Russian Defense Ministry later clarified that Russian forces had struck an industrial enterprise in Kiev engaged in the production and storage of long-and medium-range unmanned aerial vehicles.
A workshop in Kiev operated by OAKLINE LLC was also hit. The facility is used to assemble and store Fire Point’s long-and medium-range FP-1 and FP-2 unmanned aerial vehicles.
In addition, Russian forces struck the Yuzhny road-and-rail bridge in Kiev, which serves to carry military cargo by road and rail.
A loading and customs terminal run by Regional Logistics Center was also hit in Kharkov Region. The facility is used to store and distribute materiel and dual-use cargo destined to support the Ukrainian army, as well as reconnaissance and strike drones.
In addition, a cargo ship carrying supplies to support the Ukrainian army was struck at sea while heading to the port of Chernomorsk in Odessa Region.
Kiev Mayor Vitaly Klitschko said on his Telegram channel that the Yuzhny Bridge across the Dnieper River had sustained damage. Explosions were reported in the capital overnight, and an air raid alert was issued.
He also reported damage to metro infrastructure, noting that one of the subway lines crosses the bridge.
According to the city administration’s Telegram channel, traffic across the Yuzhny Bridge has been restricted, and metro trains are temporarily suspended.

title: Slavsko Community Partners with Austria’s Hermagor, Home to One of the Largest Ski Areas in the Southern Alps
body:
Slavsko Municipal Council and the Austrian municipality of Hermagor-Pressegger See have signed a Memorandum of Cooperation. The partnership will create a framework for sharing expertise in mountain tourism, infrastructure, public safety, local economic development and sustainability.
For the Slavsko Community, the partnership is particularly valuable because of Hermagor’s experience in transforming a mountain region into a successful year-round tourism destination.
Hermagor-Pressegger See is located in the Austrian state of Carinthia, close to the Italian border. Today, it is a year-round tourism destination and an economic hub for the Gailtal, Gitschtal and Lesachtal valleys. The municipality is home to Nassfeld, one of the largest ski areas in the Southern Alps. In summer, the region attracts visitors with Lake Pressegger See, hiking and cycling trails, mountaineering, fishing, geological trails and a wide range of other outdoor activities.
Hermagor has undergone a significant economic transformation, evolving from a predominantly agricultural area into a thriving tourism-based regional economy. Today, it serves not only as a major tourism destination, but also as an administrative and economic centre for the surrounding area.
This experience is particularly relevant to the Slavsko Community, which is also undergoing a major transformation as it develops a new model for tourism and strengthens its position as a modern mountain destination.
“It is important for us to have partners who have already travelled the path that the Slavsko Community is taking today. Hermagor shows how the development of mountain tourism can benefit not only an individual resort, but the economy of an entire community and the wider region. We want to learn from this experience and adapt it to our own circumstances,” said Bohdan Mychko, Deputy Head of the Slavsko Community.
Downhill ride on the "Pendolino" mountain coaster in summer. Photo: NLW, Daniel Zupan
The Memorandum provides for cooperation and the exchange of expertise in several key areas: • tourism and recreation development in mountain regions; • tourism destination management and ski resort development; • transport and utility infrastructure; • municipal services; • emergency, rescue and fire services; • sustainable development and environmental protection; • support for local entrepreneurship and economic development; • cultural, educational, youth and sports exchanges; • the development of joint projects under European and international programmes.
Family hiking in the Hermagor-Nassfeld region. Photo: NLW
A particular focus will be the exchange of experience in year-round tourism. As the Slavsko Community works to develop Slavsko as a year-round mountain destination, Hermagor’s experience in successfully combining winter ski tourism with a strong summer tourism offer is especially relevant.
“We are pleased to establish this partnership with the Slavsko Community. The exchange of experience between mountain regions can benefit both sides, particularly in tourism, infrastructure development, environmental protection and local governance,” said Leopold Astner, Mayor of Hermagor-Pressegger See.
The partnership will include working meetings, study visits, exchanges of information and best practices, as well as opportunities to participate jointly in European and international programmes. The Memorandum has been signed for a five-year period.
Presentation of traditional Gailtaler Almkäse, Carinthia. Photo: NLW
The Slavsko Community is located in Stryi District, Lviv Region, in the Ukrainian Carpathians. It comprises Slavsko, which serves as the community’s administrative centre, and 15 villages. The area has significant tourism potential thanks to its mountain landscape, natural resources and Slavsko’s long history as one of Ukraine’s best-known ski destinations.
Today, the Slavsko Community is working to become a modern year-round tourism destination by developing infrastructure, supporting local entrepreneurship and creating new opportunities for local residents. One of the key development projects in the area is GORO Mountain Resort, a large-scale year-round mountain resort currently under development near the village of Volosianka.
The community is also expanding its international partnerships and cooperation with other mountain regions to exchange expertise in tourism, infrastructure, sustainable development and local governance.
Church of the Dormition of the Theotokos in Slavske, Ukraine. January 20, 2010 Photo: Haidamac / CC BY-SA 4.0

title: 1 in 8B – An AI-Powered Life Simulator
body:
The library is quiet when Seo-jin sees the email. A book-restoration workshop in Busan would like to meet her on Monday. She has spent years repairing torn pages at the returns desk; this would be her first chance to learn the craft properly. The last train with an affordable seat leaves on Sunday afternoon.
Then her phone lights up. Her mother has sent a photograph of the flickering light above the family shop: “Will you come by on Sunday?” Seo-jin cannot tell whether this is about the light. She leaves the train page open beside the email and turns her phone over. Before closing the library, she needs to make one move.

title: DSS arraigns man over fake Tinubu letter to US president
body: The Department of State Services (DSS) has filed a three-count charge bordering on cybercrime and defamation against a Kaduna man accused of circulating a fake letter purportedly written by President Bola Tinubu to the President of the United States. The suspect, Mubarak Abdullahi, also known as Sardaunan Samari, was arrested on September 28 after allegedly sharing the document on his Facebook page with the caption, “ATIKU IS COMING.” President Tinubu’s Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, disclosed this in a post on X late Monday, saying Abdullahi had been arraigned before Chief Magistrate Court No. 10, Kabala Doki, Kaduna. The tweet read, “An avowed supporter of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar now faces trial in Kaduna for circulating a document purportedly written by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to the President of the United States of America. “The suspect, Mubarak Abdullahi (aka Sardaunan Samari), was arrested on 28 September for sharing the fake document on his Facebook page with the caption “ATIKU IS COMING.” “Mubarak admitted to investigators that he shared the fake document and apologised for his actions. The contrition was not enough. “The DSS arraigned him before Chief Magistrate Court No. 10, Kabala Doki, Kaduna, which ordered his remand at the Nigerian Correctional Centre, Kaduna,” adding that the agency “has filed a three-count charge bordering on cybercrime and defamation against him at the Federal High Court, Kaduna.” Onanuga, however, said the DSS would continue to demonstrate its ability to identify people involved in circulating what he described as misleading information online. Meanwhile, human rights activist and presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC) Omoyele Sowore criticised the arrest, accusing the DSS of being used to suppress dissent. In a post on X on Tuesday, Sowore questioned the agency’s involvement in the case and described the arrest as an attempt to silence a citizen over an online post. “How low will you go, #OfficialAPCNg and the #officialABAT regime? How on earth do you reduce a national security agency like the #OfficialDSSNG to a mere vacuum cleaner, deployed to sweep up dissenting voices in your inordinate ambition to subdue every citizen simply because you are afraid to face the Nigerian people and account for your disastrous reign?” he wrote. Sowore added, “Arresting a hapless citizen for posting a document online – sad! Shame on all of you! A day of reckoning is coming, when you too will be held accountable for your actions. That day is coming sooner than you think. Very soon!” Neither Atiku nor his media aide, Phrank Shaibu, had publicly reacted to the development as of the time of writing. The post DSS arraigns man over fake Tinubu letter to US president appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Russia-Africa summit to strengthen strategic cooperation with continent — Lavrov
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. The third Russia-Africa summit will help strengthen Moscow’s strategic cooperation with African countries, Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov stated in his welcoming address to the organizers and participants of the "Spiritual Bridges: Russia and Africa. A Dialogue for Peace and Creation" international conference.
"Today, Russian-African cooperation is strategic in nature, covering a broad range of issues, from politics and the economy to education and culture. The third Russia-Africa summit, which begins tomorrow in Moscow, will undoubtedly contribute to its further strengthening," the top diplomat noted.
Lavrov emphasized that Russia is interested in seeing the African continent emerge as an influential center of a multipolar world and is also "firmly committed to the inalienable right of Africans to independently determine their own paths and models of development."
The third Russia-Africa summit will take place in Moscow on October 28-29.

title: President Mahama congratulates Brazil’s Lula on re-election
body: President John Dramani Mahama has congratulated Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on his re-election, expressing confidence that the outcome will provide an opportunity to deepen relations between Ghana and Brazil and strengthen cooperation among countries in the Global South. In a message shared on Facebook, President Mahama described Lula’s victory as well-deserved and reaffirmed his commitment to advancing the longstanding ties between the two countries. “Brazil and Ghana share a rich history, and I look forward to further strengthening our bilateral relations,” he said. President Mahama also pointed to the Accra Reset initiative as a platform for the two leaders to advance shared interests, particularly the development priorities of countries in the Global South. “Together, through the Accra Reset initiative, we will continue championing the Global South agenda for the betterment of our peoples,” he added. Lula secured another term after defeating Flávio Bolsonaro of the Liberal Party in Brazil’s presidential runoff election on Sunday, October 25, 2026. Results announced by Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court showed Lula winning 51.79 per cent of valid votes, equivalent to 64,256,232 votes, while Bolsonaro obtained 48.21 per cent, or 59,826,041 votes. The victory extends the tenure of the 80-year-old leader, who returned to Brazil’s presidency in 2023 after previously serving from 2003 to 2010.

title: Heavy to moderate rains, hail lash several wilayats
body:
Muscat: moderate to heavy rain associated with thunderstorms and hail was reported in the governorates of Al Dakhiliyah, North Al Batinah, South Al Batinah, Al Dhahirah, on Tuesday. The Sultanate of Oman is presently being affected by a trough of low pressure with rains expected to continue through Friday. The Wilayat of Samayil in Al Dakhiliyah Governorate experienced heavy rainfall associated with hail and thunderstorms affecting the area of Tawi Al Nas and adjacent areas causing the overflow of Wadi Saqt. title: First Virginia-class submarine selected for AUKUS rotational force
body:
The US Navy has designated the USS Colorado (SSN 788) as the first US Navy Virginia-class fast-attack submarine assigned to Submarine Rotational Force-West (SRF-West) beginning in late 2027.
The announcement comes ahead of the United States Submarine Maintenance Period, which begins later this week and is intended to demonstrate Australia's growing capacity to maintain US and UK nuclear-powered attack submarines.
SRF-West is expected to host up to four US fast-attack submarines and one UK fast-attack submarine on a rotational basis at HMAS Stirling, a Royal Australian Navy base in Western Australia.
The initiative aims to prepare Australia to operate, maintain, and regulate its own conventionally armed, nuclear-powered submarine capability. It will also support submarine deployments by expanding maintenance options and sustainment infrastructure in the region for AUKUS partners.
Established at Australia's invitation and by mutual agreement, SRF-West will operate under applicable international agreements between the United States, Australia, and the UK, including the U.S.-Australia Force Posture Agreement.
Activities under SRF-West will comply with the AUKUS partners' respective international obligations, including the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons and Australia's obligations under the South Pacific Nuclear Free Zone Treaty, also known as the Treaty of Rarotonga.
"The selection of USS Colorado (SSN 788) as the first submarine assigned to SRF-West in 2027 marks a significant milestone for AUKUS Pillar I and is a decisive step in strengthening collective deterrence in the Pacific," according to the officials.

title: Battlefield in Kherson Region’s island area is now “transparent”, military says
body:
Pavlo Drohal, spokesperson for Ukraine’s 30th Marine Corps, told Ukrinform about the situation.
“As for the island area in the Dnipro River delta, the enemy continues to make systematic attempts to advance onto the islands. They try to reach them in small boats, using small assault groups, and attempt to establish positions there so they can infiltrate closer to the right bank. Given the challenging geography and the large number of islands — this is not just the Dnipro River proper, but also its tributaries, forming an extensive island zone with a complex network of waterways — they continue these attempts systematically. The difference is that we can see them because technology makes the battlefield ‘transparent,’ and the airspace is under constant surveillance,” Drohal said.
According to him, Ukrainian defenders spot and destroy Russian troops, in most cases as soon as they begin moving. In autumn, the enemy is trying to use fog and rain as cover, but the outcome remains the same: these groups are destroyed.
“Regarding the attempt to land in Kherson’s Korabel neighborhood, yes, such an attempt was made last week. It was unsuccessful because the enemy was spotted, targeted with weapons, and destroyed,” the spokesperson said.
He added that rumors suggesting an enemy sabotage and reconnaissance group might nevertheless have landed and hidden in the neighborhood were unfounded.
“That is impossible. Those who attempted to land were destroyed. Our defenders are monitoring the area very closely and keeping track of everything happening there,” Drohal emphasized.
He also noted that Russian forces had conducted intensive assaults in the island area in spring and early summer, operating “nonstop.” At the time, there could be as many as 50 assaults a month. The number of attacks subsequently declined: there were no such attempts in July, but they resumed in August and continue to this day.
“In other words, the enemy is experiencing something of a seasonal surge. It is once again imagining that it can advance toward the islands, establish a foothold, and set up positions there. But doing so is extremely difficult in practical terms, and given our countermeasures and constant surveillance, it is virtually impossible,” the spokesperson stressed.
However, Drohal said these failed attempts had not deterred the Russian military command, which continued to send assault groups on missions that amounted to a death sentence, showing little regard for its personnel. Russian servicemen receive some training for combat in these conditions, he added, but the enemy’s assault groups “are not particularly well supplied.”
As for Kherson city, Drohal stressed that Ukrainian forces were doing everything possible to protect it. Although Russian forces launch a huge number of drones, Ukrainian defenders destroy or suppress 90–93% of them.
“We are equally successful in targeting enemy artillery along the Dnipro River axis. Since the beginning of summer, we have destroyed or damaged around 150 enemy artillery systems. Once a gun starts operating in our area, it is tracked almost immediately and survives for only two to three days. The Russian command shows little regard for its artillery either,” the spokesperson said.
The number of artillery attacks in autumn has fallen by a factor of 2.5 compared with spring. While there were around 2,000–2,500 attacks in spring, the current figure is approximately 1,000–1,200, Drohal said.
As reported, Russian artillery shelling along the Dnipro River axis has decreased significantly as Ukrainian Defense Forces successfully destroy Russian artillery systems.
Photo provided by Pavlo Drohal , spokesperson for the Ukrainian Navy’s Marine Corps

title: FACT CHECK: No official statement implies Marcos’ intent to declare war, martial law
body: Claim: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. wants to wage war in Mindanao and against China to avoid liability for graft, as well as to have a reason for declaring martial law. Rating: FALSE Why we fact-checked this: A Facebook page, “Makata ng Bayan,” with 1.1 million followers posted a graphic on October 25 bearing the claim: “ Gusto ni Marcos gerahin ang Mindanao at China para hindi mapanagot sa ninakaw niya! Gagawa ng gulo para may dahilan mag Martial Law kaya sa mga sundalo magising na kayo. ” (Marcos wants to wage war against Mindanao and China to avoid liability for graft! He will create public disorder to justify Martial Law, so soldiers wake up . ) The caption also reads, “ AFP Wag na kayo magpagapos sa pagiging bulag na katapatan, wag na ipagpapatuloy ang pamumuno na puro pang-aapi at kaguluhan. ” (AFP [Armed Forces of the Philippines], do not allow yourselves to be chained by blind loyalty; stop the leadership full of oppression and chaos.) The post has received 9,600 reactions, 3,300 comments, and 5,000 shares as of writing. The facts: There are no official statements from Malacañang, the Presidential Communications Office , or credible news reports confirming that Marcos wants to wage war in Mindanao and against China, and that he plans to declare martial law. The President also can’t declare a state of war. Article VI, Section 23 (1) of the 1987 Constitution states that only Congress has the sole power to do so. The President acts as Commander-in-Chief of the country’s armed forces in accordance with Article VII, Section 18. As such, he has powers to prevent or suppress lawless violence, invasion, or rebellion. The President may declare martial law for a limited period but needs congressional approval for an extension. Bato dela Rosa in Mindanao: The post was made several days after Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) Secretary Juanito Victor “Jonvic” Remulla announced that his department is offering a P50-million reward for those who can help capture International Criminal Court (ICC) suspect Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa. Dela Rosa, who’s facing an arrest warrant for his alleged role in former president Rodrigo Duterte’s war on drugs campaign, is believed to be hiding in Mindanao under the protection of an unnamed armed group. Remulla also warned that any arrest attempt could turn into a bloody confrontation. West Philippine Sea dispute: Maritime rows are at the center of tensions between China and the Philippines. China claims almost all of the South China Sea, including parts of the West Philippine Sea . Filipino maritime frontlines have dealt with harassment and harm at sea from China. In his third State of the Nation Address (SONA) last July, Marcos said , “The Philippines cannot yield. The Philippines cannot waver.” He asserted that the country will continue to find ways to de-escalate tensions with China. Previous fact-checks: Rappler has previously fact-checked similar claims involving Marcos’ supposed war and martial law declaration: FACT CHECK: Marcos did not declare war on China in Day of Valor speech FACT CHECK: Marcos did not declare war against China FACT CHECK: No martial law declaration over army colonel’s ‘withdrawal of support’ – Jade Florido/Rappler.com Jade Florido is a volunteer for Rappler’s Research and Data unit. She is a third-year Development Studies student at the University of the Philippines – Manila. Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

title: Suspected kidnappers ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‌‌‍​​⁠⁠‍‌​attack Kaduna estate, abduct residents
body: Residents of Nuru Suraj Estate in Millennium City area of Kaduna have been thrown into fear following a fresh attack by suspected kidnappers who reportedly abducted about six people in the early hours of Tuesday. A resident who identified herself as Maman Hamid, whose house is close to that of the victims, told the News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) that the attackers gained access to the estate through its second gate before carrying out the operation. Hamza said the incident caused panic among residents, who were left apprehensive over the security situation in the area. She added that military personnel pursued the suspected kidnappers, leading to the rescue of some of the victims even though the kidnapers were able to escape. The number of people rescued and the whereabouts of those still missing were not immediately established as of the time of filing this report. The latest incident has renewed concerns over the safety of residents in Millennium City, a developing residential area that has experienced kidnapping incidents in recent years. Residents have repeatedly expressed concerns about the activities of suspected kidnappers, particularly attacks on residential estates and communities on the outskirts of Kaduna metropolis. The latest attack also highlights concerns over access control at residential estates and the need for stronger security patrols, effective surveillance and prompt responses to distress calls. NAN recalls that in a previous incident in the area, suspected kidnappers reportedly abducted Ahmed Abubakar Zakka, his wife and their infant daughter, Fatima, from Alrahus Estate in Millennium City on the night of Oct. 6, 2026 but were later rescued. On Oct. 12, 2026, police authorities reportedly announced the arrest of eight suspected kidnappers and four alleged informants during operations around Millennium City and Maraban Rido, with AK-47 rifles recovered. The arrests underscored the need to sustain intelligence-led operations against kidnapping networks and those suspected of providing them with information. The latest attack has heightened residents’ calls for stronger security measures, particularly around estate gates and access routes that could be exploited by criminal elements. The Kaduna Police Command is yet to react to the latest incident. (NAN) The post Suspected kidnappers ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍‌‌‍​​⁠⁠‍‌​attack Kaduna estate, abduct residents appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Lagos Dep Gov, Hamzat, Inaugurates UNILAG’S Digital Humanities Facilities Today
body: Sunday Okobi The Deputy Governor of Lagos State, Dr. Obafemi Kadri Hamzat, will today inaugurate the twin facilities of the Centre for Digital Humanities (CEDHUL), the University of Lagos’ flagship hub for research and training at the meeting point of culture and computation. While inaugurating the facilities, Hamzat will lend the full weight of the Lagos State Government to a project that speaks directly to the state’s ambition for innovation, youth empowerment and a future-ready workforce. Speaking ahead of the event, the first professor of Digital Humanities in Nigeria and Sub-Saharan Africa and Founding Director of CEDHUL, Professor Babatunde Olusola Ope-Davies, said: “We are redefining the future of the Humanities… What we celebrate is the fruit of many hands: the university, our partners at home and abroad, and now the Government of Lagos State. We are grateful to His Excellency for standing with us as we open these doors to a new generation of African digital scholars.” The ceremony will also be attended by the Vice-Chancellor of the University of Lagos, Principal Officers, Deans, partners, scholars, students and members of the press at the Centre for Digital Humanities, University of Lagos, Akoka. The inauguration, according to him, will mark a defining moment for CEDHUL, sub-Saharan Africa’s first dedicated Digital Humanities centre. “Founded in 2019, the Centre has grown from a bold idea into a continental reference point, where African languages, archives, cultures and stories meet data, computation and artificial intelligence. The twin facilities will now house the Centre’s Senate-approved Postgraduate Diploma, Master’s and Doctoral programmes in Digital Humanities, the first of their kind in the region,” he said. Ope-Davis added “Hamzat’s presence, and his personal act of inaugurating the facilities, signals a powerful alignment between the Lagos State Government’s vision of a smart, knowledge-driven megacity and the university’s mission to produce scholars who can read both the manuscript and the machine. An engineer, technocrat and long-standing advocate of innovation in public life, the deputy governor brings to the occasion a conviction that Lagos must not only consume technology but shape it.” He described the occasion as “the opening of a doorway, not just a building. “The facilities are where that meeting happens: where we are redefining the future of the humanities; where Africa’s inherited knowledge is preserved, interpreted and carried forward with the tools of the digital age. We are deeply honoured that His Excellency will inaugurate them.”

title: Alatau City Breaks Ground on First Skyscraper in $800 Million Project
body: The Astana Times provides news and information from Kazakhstan and around the world. ASTANA — Kazakhstan’s Alatau City has broken ground on Iconic Complex, a multifunctional development set to become the city’s first skyscraper, with Deputy Prime Minister Kanat Bozumbayev attending the ceremony on Oct. 26, according to the Prime Minister’s press service. The project, scheduled for completion by the end of 2029, includes two towers measuring 272 and 78 meters. Photo credit: Prime Minister’s press service. Click to see the map in full size. The map is designed by The Astana Times. The project, with investments exceeding $800 million, includes two towers measuring 272 and 78 meters. The complex will house offices, residences, a hotel, retail facilities and public spaces. Construction is scheduled for completion by the end of 2029. The city is gradually introducing a special legal regime intended to attract investment and establish a modern governance system. According to the press release, investment in fixed capital in Alatau reached 70.3 billion tenge (US$133 million) in the first nine months of 2026, a 1.6-fold increase. The city’s investment portfolio includes 67 projects worth approximately $6.9 billion, with the potential to create around 55,000 jobs. Infrastructure development is also underway. Work is progressing on 28 projects supported by 35.3 billion tenge (US$ 78.2 million) from the state reserve. These include the reconstruction of the Kokpa-1 substation, water supply facilities and road repairs. Bozumbayev said the project must be completed on schedule and meet high standards of quality and safety during the launch of construction of the first skyscraper on Oct. 26. Photo credit: Prime Minister’s press service. Bozumbayev emphasized the need to meet construction deadlines and comply with seismic safety and energy-efficiency standards. He also called for the involvement of Kazakh companies and specialists. Under its special legal regime, the city has introduced independent technical reviews of project documentation involving international experts, according to the statement. “We expect Iconic Complex to set a new standard for design and construction quality and contribute to Alatau’s development as a modern city. The project must be completed on schedule and meet high standards of quality and safety,” Bozumbayev said. China State Construction Engineering Corporation (CSCEC) is the general contractor, while the architectural concept was developed by the United States-based firm Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM). Building a new economic center Iconic Complex is part of a broader effort to develop Alatau into a regional economic hub combining manufacturing, logistics, technology and finance. In a September analysis, The Astana Times examined whether Kazakhstan could build such a center from scratch, noting that the project’s success would depend on turning investment plans into sustained economic activity and effective governance. The city’s location between Almaty and Konayev, near Almaty International Airport and major transport routes connecting China with Central Asia, the Caucasus, Europe and the Middle East, is central to the government’s economic rationale. Yernar Serik, a trading and investment analyst interviewed for the analysis, said a new economic center could help diversify an economy in which much of the business activity, capital and human resources are concentrated in Almaty and Astana. Economist Anuar Nurtazin, however, cautioned that investment announcements and company registrations alone would not demonstrate success. He said key indicators should include exports, technological supply chains, local production and productivity growth. The analysis also highlighted the importance of infrastructure, predictable regulation and a skilled workforce in determining whether Alatau can develop into an independent economic center rather than an extension of neighboring Almaty. The city’s development plans extend to 2040, with a long-term vision through 2055 being prepared with international firms ARUP and Boston Consulting Group.
