title: Deindustrialization of Ukraine can be considered complete — political scientist
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. The catastrophic state of Ukraine’s metallurgical industry is a consequence of the Kiev regime’s anti-Russian policies, and the country’s deindustrialization is now effectively complete, Ukrainian political scientist Taras Sidorets told TASS in an interview.
"Today, the state of Ukraine’s metallurgical industry is not merely depressing; it is catastrophic. The process of decommunization and deindustrialization is, in effect, complete. There are no longer any major metallurgical plants operating in Ukraine. For the first time in many years of independence, the country has been unable to produce a single ton of steel. In principle, this is the natural outcome of an anti-Russian policy," he said.
However, Sidorets clarified that Ukraine’s deindustrialization began in 1991. At the time of independence, the country’s metallurgical sector comprised more than 130 enterprises, 14 of which formed the backbone of its steelmaking capacity.
"Much has changed since then. Privatization took place: some factories were acquired by private owners and continued operating under new management, while others were privatized and subsequently sold off," the political scientist noted.
"Throughout the entire period of Ukraine’s independence, only one major steel plant was built: Interpipe Steel, whose construction was completed in 2012. Most notably, despite the launch of this facility, Ukraine’s share of global steel production did not increase," Sidorets said.
He noted that between 1991 and 2012, Ukraine’s share of global steel production fell from 6% to just over 2%.
According to figures cited by Sidorets, Ukraine produced approximately 32 million tons of steel in 2012, compared with 21 million tons in 2021. Pig iron production fell from 28 million tons in 2012 to slightly more than 21 million tons in 2021, a decline of around 7 million tons. Finished steel production also decreased, from 26 million tons to 19 million tons over the same period.
In October, Alexander Kalenkov, president of the Ukrmetallurgprom association, told Ukrainian Radio that Ukraine had not produced a single ton of steel in September 2026.
On September 5, ArcelorMittal announced that it would be unable to resume operations at ArcelorMittal Krivoi Rog, Ukraine’s largest metallurgical plant. It was the country’s last major steelworks that had not previously announced a shutdown.
On September 22, the Interpipe Steel plant halted operations. Earlier, on September 18, Zaporozhstal and Kametstal had also suspended production. Another major enterprise, the Dnieper Metallurgical Plant, had effectively ceased operations earlier because of financial difficulties.
Before their shutdowns, ArcelorMittal Krivoi Rog and Zaporozhstal each contributed approximately $90 million annually to the state budget, while Kametstal paid around $56 million.

title: European countries with the largest defense budgets name Russia their main security threat and pledge continued support for Ukraine
body: Defense ministers from the United Kingdom, Germany, Italy, Poland, and France met in Paris on October 26 as members of the E5 group — the countries with the largest defense budgets — to discuss support for Ukraine ahead of winter. After the meeting, the ministers named Russia the main long-term threat to European security and pledged to keep supporting Ukraine despite Washington’s warming relations with Moscow. “Our countries share the assessment that Russia represents the most acute and long-term threat to Euro-Atlantic security and stability,” the final statement reads . Russia’s war against Ukraine and intensifying hybrid attacks in Europe “do not undermine our unity, solidarity and cohesion. On the contrary, they strengthen our determination to pursue the efforts already undertaken to safeguard the integrity and security of Allied territory,” the ministers said. The ministers pledged to continue backing Ukraine but announced no new military or financial aid packages, Bloomberg said . During the meeting, they limited themselves to reaffirming earlier commitments. German Defense Minister Boris Pistorius stressed that the allies would work to preserve U.S. support for Ukraine: “We will do everything we can to ensure that the U.S. also supports Ukraine with supplies, as well as with intelligence and satellite data.” The latest deterioration in relations between Ukraine and the United States is forcing Europe to consider how to help Ukraine without American support, Bloomberg said. Pistorius said the E5 countries are also working with Ukraine on their own air defense system meant to supplement the U.S. Patriot systems. Relations between Kyiv and Washington have deteriorated sharply amid a fuel crisis. Donald Trump first demanded that Ukraine stop striking Russian fuel infrastructure, and when a cease-fire could not be reached , he eased sanctions against Russia, allowing diesel fuel to be sold on the world market. In response, Volodymyr Zelensky accused Trump of trying to force Ukraine into capitulation, saying the United States is delaying shipments of missiles for Patriot air defense systems and restricting the operation of Starlink and Starshield in Ukraine. At Meduza, we are committed to transparency about our use of artificial intelligence in the newsroom. The story you’re reading was written by one of our living, breathing journalists and translated from Russian using an AI model configured to follow our strict editorial standards. This translation process is the result of extensive testing and refinements to ensure our English-language coverage is timely and accurate. A Meduza editor reviews every draft before publication. If you find any errors in this translation, please contact us at reports@meduza.io . To read Meduza’s exclusive content in English, please subscribe to our newsletter .

title: How election officials are working to mitigate growing distrust ahead of midterms
body:
"Our elections, in fact, are safe and secure," one expert told ABC News.
DALLAS, Ga. -- Election officials from coast to coast are facing a slew of challenges ahead of the high-stakes midterms , from the Trump administration's bid to impose itself on state-run elections to last-minute court challenges and threats faced by election workers -- all under a persistent sense of distrust in the voting process itself, some experts told ABC News.
"Usually the temperature is much higher -- and emotions run much hotter -- in a presidential election year than in a midterm election year," said Wendy Weiser, vice president of the nonprofit Brennan Center for Justice at New York University School of Law. "This year, though, the temperature is staying up at a high level."
Election experts broadly lay blame for the elevated sense of distrust in elections this year at the feet of President Donald Trump , whose administration has taken unprecedented steps to question the outcome by levelling unfounded claims of widespread voter fraud.
Trump administration officials say steps they've taken in recent weeks -- including lawsuits in California and Alaska and threats to prosecute election workers -- are meant to ensure the integrity of the election.
But under the weight of those allegations , state officials say the once-collaborative rapport between the federal government and state leaders has in some cases given way to a deep sense of suspicion.
"There's no trust in that relationship," Nevada Secretary of State Francisco Aguilar told ABC News. "In order to have a working relationship, there has to be trust, and the fact that they continue to tear that trust apart and spread the misinformation and the lies that they are about our elections is wrong."
At the same time, people who oversee voting at the county level across the country are frequently fielding questions from voters who say they lack faith in the electoral process. About 6 in 10 Americans are confident the midterm elections will be conducted fairly and accurately, while nearly 4 in 10 Americans and about 3 in 10 voters are not confident , according to an ABC News/Washington Post/Ipsos poll conducted using Ipsos' KnowledgePanel.
"No matter how transparent we are, people always are questioning what we're doing [and] how we're doing it," Deidre Holden, the director of elections and voter registration in Paulding County, Georgia, told ABC News. "I try to explain [that] we have nothing to hide. You're welcome to come in and watch the process."
Holden, who has been an elections official in Georgia for 25 years, said that in her early years in the role, she "used to train people on how to smile and hand out an 'I voted' sticker."
Yet over the last several years, Holden has devoted much of her time to ensuring that everyone at polling places and in the county's ballot processing facility are safe. She currently has a sheriff's deputy stationed at every polling location, and in 2024 she first showed ABC News the active shooter training her poll workers were undertaking as a precaution.
"I'm forever concerned with the security of my staff, with my poll workers, with my voters," Holden said. "You never know what someone's going to do."
Paulding County was once a solidly Republican area, but as the suburban sprawl around Atlanta has increased, the county's population has quadrupled and it is now a purple county with Democrats and Republicans living side by side. With such a partisan divide, Holden said transparency about the process is key.
"Some of our best poll workers have come from the naysayers that didn't trust us and we invited them in and now they're our best workers and our biggest advocates because they get to see behind the scenes, they get see how the sausage is made, how we do things and how we do those things with integrity," Holden said.
The official once again overseeing the election at the state level in Georgia this November is Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger, a Republican who rose to national prominence in January 2021 after receiving a phone call from President Donald Trump.
"All I want to do is this: I just want to find 11,780 votes," Trump told Raffensperger at the time, claiming it was "not possible" that he lost Georgia's 2020 presidential election.
Joe Biden won the 2020 election in the Peach State and Raffensperger certified the results, despite facing criticism from some other Republicans.
"At the end of the day we did our job, we followed the law and we followed the constitution," Raffensperger told ABC News in a recent interview.
"I know I did the right thing, and I feel sorry for people that didn't do the right thing, because at some point, they're going to have to look at themselves in the mirror," he said.
Raffensperger's time in office will end in January. Early voting for the midterms is currently underway in Georgia, and Raffensperger said he is confident that residents will have an accurate idea of the projected election results by midnight after the polls close.
"Those ballots actually in effect will be counted three times just to verify the result, so at the end of the day, we know that the winner won and that's our job," Raffensperger said.
While Raffensperger was on the phone with Trump in 2021, many recent dustups between the federal government and state agencies have involved staffers going back and forth over email and video conferencing.
At the core of the growing friction is the claim by President Trump and DHS officials that the country has a "broken" election system , where they claim 278,000 people who are not U.S. citizens have registered to vote illegally.
Weiser told ABC News that the Trump administration has been attempting to "substantiate their theory that our country is plagued by widespread voter fraud."
"What they've been able to uncover is nothing," Weiser said. "Our elections, in fact, are safe and secure."
The allegations of widespread noncitizen voting have not just been made at press conferences. Over the summer, DHS employees reached out to states around the U.S., sending letters and holding meetings about "the concerning results" of what they called a "preliminary review" of potential noncitizens registered to vote.
Aguilar, the Nevada secretary of state, said members of his office ended up on a video conference call in August with DHS representatives alleging that there could be as many as 15,903 noncitizens registered to vote in Nevada.
One of the DHS officials on the call was Heather Honey, a key figure in the fight to overturn the results of the 2020 presidential election.
While not overtly hostile, a recording of the video conference obtained by ABC News shows palpable tension and some awkward exchanges, as Nevada officials seemed deeply skeptical of the claims made by DHS.
"So what you're saying is the 15,000 number has not been vetted?" a Nevada official asked, according to a recording of the video conference.
"I probably wouldn't use the sentence, 'It hasn't been vetted,'" a DHS representative responded, adding that each individual has not "had a full manual review."
Following the meeting, DHS officials emailed Nevada officials with a new figure -- claiming they found 185 noncitizens on the state's voter rolls during a preliminary sweep. Officials in Nevada said the DHS was wrong, replying later that, after their own review of those 185 individuals, "our records indicate that they were citizens."
In response to a request by ABC News for comment, DHS stood by their work, which they called "a service to Nevada's citizens," and accused Nevada officials of knowingly harboring illegal voters on its lists.
"Nevada knows the 185 names they keep waving around were never the full list of illegal voters," a Homeland Security spokesperson said in an email. "They were only the files [that immigration officials] had finished reviewing at the moment of the call. Since then, [immigration officials] have manually confirmed about 2,000 more aliens from the same list. The review is just beginning."
While voting in the upcoming election will conclude on Nov. 3, there is concern among some election experts that the relationship between federal leaders and their counterparts at the state and local levels might not be easily repairable.
The federal government has traditionally supported state and local officials on a slew of election-related matters, from mitigating foreign threats to cybersecurity. With the fragile state of affairs, some experts fear any Election Day complications could threaten the integrity of the vote.
"Our state and local election officials are going to have fewer resources at their disposal, less intelligence and less ability to coordinate in responding to what might be significant threats going forward because they don't trust the federal government as a partner the way they did," Weiser said.
While trust in how elections are being conducted remains top of mind for voters, election officials like Holden, Aguilar and Raffensperger are working to assure their residents that they should still have faith in the process.
"There's no reason for a voter to ever doubt their ballot," Holden said.
24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

title: Russia Observing Ceasefire in Occupied Oleshky as Humanitarian Mission Begins
body:
Russian forces were observing a localized ceasefire around the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky in the Kherson region as of 9 a.m. on Oct. 27, allowing a humanitarian mission to proceed, Ukraine’s Marine Corps said.
“As of 9 a.m., the enemy is observing the ceasefire introduced as part of the humanitarian mission,” Marine Corps spokesperson Pavlo Drohal said in a Facebook post .
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Ukrainian Marines are monitoring the situation and tracking changes on the ground, Drohal added.
The ceasefire took effect at 3 a.m. Kyiv time on Oct. 27 in a designated area around Oleshky. The operation aims to deliver humanitarian aid and establish safe passage for civilians seeking to leave the occupied city.
The agreement was reached through negotiations between Ukrainian Parliamentary Commissioner for Human Rights Dmytro Lubinets and his Russian counterpart, Yana Lantratova, with mediation from US First Lady Melania Trump.
Oleshky, a Russian-occupied city on the left bank of the Dnipro River opposite Kherson, has faced a worsening humanitarian crisis, with residents reporting severe shortages of food, clean water and medicine.
Before Russia’s full-scale invasion, the city had a population of about 24,000. The White House estimates that between 1,700 and 2,000 people remain, including elderly residents and around 50 children.
The temporary truce is intended to allow humanitarian supplies into the city and establish safe passage for civilians who want to leave. Residents will be able to choose whether to evacuate to Ukrainian-controlled territory or Russia, according to the White House .
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky warned on Oct. 25 that Russian forces could manipulate demining efforts to direct evacuees toward Russia rather than Ukrainian-controlled territory, questioning whether civilians would be able to choose their destination freely.
Ukraine’s human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets, who led Kyiv’s negotiating team, confirmed the agreement and said the operation would be implemented in stages .
Melania Trump said she worked directly with Russian and Ukrainian representatives to coordinate the arrangement.
The localized ceasefire does not constitute a broader halt to Russia’s war against Ukraine, the Kremlin’s spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on Monday.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Two men charged over suspected RAF Fairford airbase terror plot
body: ​Two men ⁠have been charged ​with offences ⁠under ‌the UK's National ​Security Act following an incident in September at RAF Fairford, ​an ‌airbase ⁠used ​by ​the ‌US ⁠to strike ⁠Iran. Mohmed Abdulkarim, 24, has been charged with assisting a foreign intelligence service, while Nouman Essghir, 24, was charged with one offence of entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the UK. Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, the head of national counter terrorism policing, said ​police believed Abdulkarim was assisting Iran . The US ⁠removed its bombers from the base in Gloucestershire, south-west England on security grounds shortly after five British men were arrested nearby in the early hours of September 27. A major incident had been declared after three suspicious vehicles were seen near the airbase. A 25-year-old UK-Iranian dual national has been released without charge following his re-arrest last week. He remains on police bail following his initial arrest at the start of October, counterterror police said. A total of eight men have been arrested in the investigation. Six of the men remain on police bail. “The Crown Prosecution Service has decided to prosecute two individuals with National Security Act offences following a Counter Terrorism Policing investigation into a high-profile incident involving RAF Fairford,” said Frank Ferguson, chief crown prosecutor for the CPS Special Crime and Counter Terrorism Division. “We will continue to work closely with our partners as this complex investigation continues.” British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said at the end of last month ⁠that the activity at Fairford was likely to have been co-ordinated in Iran.

title: Nova Poshta runs private air defense, downs drones - co-owner
body:
Nova Poshta has implemented a private air defense project and has downed Russian strike drones, co-owner of the Nova group of companies Viacheslav Klymov said, according to an Interfax-Ukraine correspondent.
"We are one of the few companies that implemented this project. I don't want to disclose numbers to you, but we have Shahed shootdowns," Klymov said at the 12th Kyiv International Economic Forum (KIEF), 'People. Business. Economy. What Next?', in Kyiv on Monday.
He stressed the importance of further developing private air defense projects and said business can take on functions that were considered the exclusive responsibility of the state before the full-scale invasion.
The Nova Poshta co-founder added that business can also have its own fire services at its production facilities. He cited the company's own experience, where employees themselves put out a significant share of fires caused by attacks without waiting for the State Emergency Service (SES) to arrive.
"Now big businesses are looking in Europe for fire trucks to create their own services. It is our property, what is the problem, who can forbid me to put out a fire on my own territory?" Klymov said.
Nova Poshta's main business remains express delivery of documents, parcels and palletized oversized cargo. It is the leader in express delivery in Ukraine. Its ultimate beneficial owners are Volodymyr Popereshniuk and Viacheslav Klymov.
The company's consolidated net profit rose 24.3% year-on-year to UAH 2.195 billion in the first half of 2026, and its revenue rose 31.8% to UAH 39.127 billion.
As of July 13, 2026, Nova Poshta's network had 54,700 service points: 16,800 branches and 37,900 parcel lockers across Ukraine.

title: Israeli defense tech M&A surges to $3.26 billion in first half of 2026
body: Merger and acquisition activity in Israel's defense technology sector jumped to $3.26 billion in the first half of 2026, an 8.5-fold increase from $384 million in 2025, according to a report by the American consulting giant Frost & Sullivan exclusively seen by Defense & Tech by The Jerusalem Post.The report, presented this week at an industry event in Tel Aviv hosted by law firm Gornitzky in collaboration with defense-focused investment fund Aurelius, found a growing demand for Israeli military technologies, particularly in autonomous systems, sensors, robotics and counter-drone technologies.It examined 44 announced mergers and acquisitions in Israel's aviation and defense sectors between 2023 and 2026, excluding cyber and cyber intelligence transactions. Deal values were publicly disclosed in 22 of those transactions, totaling about $4.1b. The median disclosed deal size was approximately $37.8m. While, in part, a small number of large acquisitions drove the dramatic increase in the 2026 deal value, Frost & Sullivan said the data also point to a broader trend of defense companies seeking to acquire technologies rather than develop them internally."The market is increasingly focused on buying capabilities that can close operational gaps, accelerate time to market and respond quickly to evolving defense requirements," the report said.US-based acquirers accounted for roughly 45% of the transactions reviewed, making them the largest buyer group. Israeli purchasers represented about 30% of acquisitions, while European companies accounted for approximately 11%.More than half of the deals were concentrated in three sectors: defense electronics and sensors, unmanned aerial vehicles and autonomous systems, and ground systems and robotics. According to the report, the wars in Ukraine, the Persian Gulf, Lebanon, and Gaza are not the only reason why the growth of the Israeli defense tech industry has accelerated; the technology has proven its effectiveness and ability to adapt on the battlefield; Israeli defense technologies have attracted increased interest from international buyers for this reason as well.Not slowing downAriel Sagee, a partner at Gornitzky GNY who also leads the firm's defense and defense regulation practices, linked the sector's growth to recent conflict and tense global geopolitics.“The war in Ukraine highlights the need for stable international alliances to ensure the supply chain. Israel cannot be isolated. Ukraine is under two-way pressure - Chinese drone components on the one hand and SpaceX's satellite technology on the other. These two forces pull at it and illustrate the importance of international alliances in building stable defense solutions,” he said.Irit Nudelman, vice president and head of defense consulting for Israel and Europe at Frost & Sullivan, said she expects deal activity to remain strong."We will continue to see significant deals in the coming years, primarily in the fields of anti-drone systems, robotics, underwater systems, space and autonomy," she said, adding that the defense sector is becoming more receptive to technologies developed by start-ups and that maturation of the defense innovation market is likely to continue.Although US and Israeli strategic buyers remain the dominant acquirers, Nudelman said European and Asian firms are more often pursuing partnerships, joint ventures and targeted investments rather than full acquisitions.'The Democratization of lethality'The event also featured a discussion between retired Maj.-Gen. Amir Eshel, a partner at Aurelius and a former commander of the Israel Air Force, and Sagee.Eshel noted that technological advances have expanded access to military capabilities once limited to nation-states."You can call it the democratization of lethality," Eshel said. "Once, states were the sole sovereign that controlled war capabilities; today, organizations and individuals also have state capabilities."He also warned against weakening Israel's domestic defense innovation ecosystem by relocating early-stage companies abroad. He stressed the importance of strengthening supply-chain partnerships rather than pursuing complete self-sufficiency."Full Israeli defense production independence is not possible," Eshel said. "We do not have the raw materials, and there is also a lack of workforce. Nevertheless, Israeli capability can be strengthened, and additionally it is right to create partnerships for the supply chains required by Israel."

title: India Braces For Cyclone Arnab With Evacuations
body: Indian authorities ordered evacuations in southwestern Andhra Pradesh ahead of a severe cyclone expected to make landfall by Wednesday, the national weather office said. Cyclone Arnab is forecast to hit the coast as a “very severe cyclonic storm”, with gusts of up to 140 kilometres (87 miles) per hour, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said in a bulletin on Tuesday. Cyclones, called hurricanes in the North Atlantic and typhoons in the Pacific, are a regular menace in the Bay of Bengal and northern Indian Ocean. The storm season, however, has been turbocharged by the El Nino weather phenomenon that has caused unprecedented warming. Neighbouring Sri Lanka, meanwhile, closed schools with warnings of torrential rain, with the island’s Department of Meteorology warning storms could trigger flash floods and mudslides. The military has been placed on alert, Colombo’s Disaster Management Centre said. India’s weather bureau said it expects the cyclone to result in “total destruction” of thatched houses and create localised flooding, uprooting of power and communication poles, and “widespread damage” to standing crops. State Chief Minister Nara Chandrababu Naidu has ordered the storm be “constantly monitored and advance precautions taken”, his office said in a statement on Monday. Local media reported that Andhra Pradesh authorities had ordered evacuations in key, low-lying areas and shut “all educational institutions” in some districts from Tuesday until Saturday. Over 4,700 pregnant women residing in potentially dangerous localities were moved to hospitals, according to The Indian Express newspaper. AFP The post India Braces For Cyclone Arnab With Evacuations appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Russia and Ukraine Trade Deadly Strikes as Oleshky Ceasefire Begins
body:
Russia and Ukraine have begun a local ceasefire in the occupied town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine, both sides said Tuesday, but strikes continued elsewhere across Ukrainian and Russian territory, with several people being reported killed.
The ceasefire, which the Trump administration announced last week, should allow humanitarian aid deliveries and evacuations from the frontline town as residents grapple with acute shortages of food and medicine.
U.S. First Lady Melania Trump said later Tuesday that the ceasefire had been expanded beyond Oleshky to other parts of the Kherson region to allow humanitarian convoys to pass safely.
“Timing was accelerated two days ahead of schedule to protect the safety of civilians and to facilitate the delivery of critical humanitarian aid,” she said in a post on X. “The ceasefire’s geographic area has expanded beyond Oleshky, within the Kherson region, to provide safe passage for the humanitarian convoys.”
Dmytro Lubinets, Ukraine’s parliamentary commissioner for human rights and head of its negotiating team, confirmed in a Facebook post that Kyiv was observing the ceasefire.
On Telegram, Russia’s Defense Ministry said it stopped shelling in the area of Kherson as it prepared for the ceasefire around Oleshky, which is located nearby.
Despite the local ceasefire, Ukraine and Russia continued to trade strikes elsewhere overnight.
In western Russia’s Bryansk region, Ukrainian drone attacks killed two people and wounded at least six others, Governor Yegor Kovalchuk said Tuesday.
The first victim was killed when an explosive was dropped from a drone, Kovalchuk said. He later confirmed the death of a 67-year-old man in the same area.
Elsewhere, authorities in the Belgorod region said one woman was killed and seven people were injured over the past 24 hours.
Russia’s Defense Ministry said it intercepted 222 Ukrainian drones across Russia and annexed Crimea between Monday night and Tuesday morning.
In Ukraine, a Russian missile attack on Kyiv killed at least one and wounded 15 others, including students in a dormitory. Overnight Russian attacks also killed and injured people in the cities of Kharkiv and Pavlohrad.
Meanwhile, in the partially occupied Zaporizhzhia region, Kremlin-installed authorities said one person was killed and 30 others were injured when a Ukrainian drone struck an inter-regional passenger bus.

title: EKO HOTELS AT 50: THE NIGHT AFRICAN HOSPITALITY STOPPED ASKING FOR A SEAT AT THE GLOBAL TABLE
body: The Legacy Gala & Awards night: Fifty Years of Building More Than a Hotel. Fifty Years of Building a Nation’s Hospitality Identity. In LAGOS, NIGERIA, 2nd of OCTOBER 2026 was written in the sands of time, because some hotels are built to accommodate history. Others are built to make it. For fifty years, Eko Hotels & Suites has done both. Beneath the lights of an extraordinary golden jubilee celebration, one of Africa’s most recognisable hospitality institutions made a statement that extended far beyond the walls of the magnificent Eko Convention Centre. Africa does not lack the capacity to deliver world-class excellence. What it needs are more institutions courageous enough to demonstrate it. The occasion was The Legacy Gala & Awards night, the grand celebration marking fifty years of Eko Hotels & Suites. An evening of African grandeur, international entertainment, cultural pride, distinguished personalities and extraordinary hospitality. But to describe it simply as a glamorous anniversary celebration would be to misunderstand its significance. This was not merely a party. It was fifty years of enterprise taking a bow. Fifty years of memories finding their voices. Fifty years of an institution reminding a continent that excellence is not foreign to Africa. And for one unforgettable evening, history took attendance. A HOTEL BECAME PART OF A NATION’S STORY There are buildings that occupy space, and there are institutions that occupy memory. Eko Hotels & Suites belongs to the latter. Across five decades, its corridors have welcomed presidents and policymakers, entrepreneurs and entertainers, diplomats and dreamers, international visitors and generations of Nigerian families. Within its halls, businesses have been negotiated, friendships formed, cultures celebrated, careers launched and milestones immortalised. For many, Eko Hotels is where Lagos welcomes the world. For others, it is where the world first encounters the warmth, ambition, sophistication and extraordinary possibilities of Lagos. Yet perhaps its greatest achievement is not simply that it has remained standing for fifty years. It is that it has remained RELEVANT. In a world where brands disappear as quickly as trends emerge, longevity is an achievement. But longevity accompanied by reinvention is leadership. Eko Hotels has consistently demonstrated that hospitality must evolve beyond accommodation. It must become an experience. A cultural encounter. An economic opportunity. A reason to travel. A reason to return. Because the greatest hotels do not merely sell rooms. They give destinations a reputation worth travelling for. THAT NIGHT, AFRICA WORE HER CROWN The Legacy Gala & Awards night brought together more than 1,000 distinguished guests, representing an extraordinary convergence of business, government, entertainment, culture and society. Among the dignitaries were Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, Deputy Governor Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, prominent business leaders, industry executives, celebrities and long-standing friends of the institution. It was a gathering that reflected not simply the prestige of a hotel, but the depth of relationships cultivated across generations. The evening’s entertainment brought together internationally celebrated musician Wyclef Jean and Nigerian highlife sensation Flavour, creating a memorable meeting of African and Caribbean musical heritage. Music, fashion, theatrical expression and celebration converged in a spectacle befitting the occasion. Yet, beyond the performances lay a more compelling message. African creativity is not a decorative addition to hospitality. It is one of it’s greatest competitive advantages. Our music travels the world. Our fashion influences global runways. Our cuisine carries the memory of generations. Our storytelling continues to captivate audiences far beyond our borders. And, many started on Eko Hotels grounds. The question is no longer whether Africa possesses what the world desires. The question is whether we are sufficiently intentional about converting these cultural assets into sustainable industries, jobs, investments and compelling destination experiences. At The Gala, Eko Hotels offered its own answer. Africa need not borrow another continent’s identity to earn the world’s admiration. She need only invest boldly enough in her own. There is, however, another story that deserves equal billing. It is the story of the people. Not the famous faces photographed beneath the lights. Not the glittering personalities whose arrival commands applause. But the extraordinary men and women whose daily dedication has sustained Eko Hotels for half a century. The housekeepers who prepare rooms with meticulous care. The waiters who understand that genuine service is an act of dignity. The engineers who keep an enormous hospitality operation functioning. The security personnel who protect its people and promises. The gardeners, technicians, stewards, reservation officers, accountants, sales professionals, event planners, administrative teams and countless others whose contributions rarely make newspaper headlines. These are the custodians of the brand. The quiet architects of its reputation. The human infrastructure behind its commercial success. For fifty years, generations of employees have given their skills, energy, creativity and commitment to an institution that has become part of Nigeria’s hospitality heritage. Their stories may not always appear in annual reports, but their fingerprints are everywhere. A hotel may be built with concrete, steel and capital. But a legacy is built with people who choose, every day, to care. The Chairman, Mr Christopher Chagoury boldly said in an interview. Perhaps, this is one of the most important lessons of Eko Hotels at fifty: buildings can be replicated, interiors redesigned and technology acquired, but a culture of excellence must be nurtured and that culture is ultimately human. The LEADERSHIP UNDERSTANDS THE WEIGHT OF LEGACY Behind every enduring institution is a succession of decisions, investments, sacrifices and moments when leadership chooses long-term value over immediate convenience. The golden jubilee provided an opportunity to recognise the vision and stewardship that have guided Eko Hotels through five decades. Under the leadership of their Managing Director, Mr. Ghassan Faddoul, General Manager Mr. Danny Kioupouroglou and the wider executive management team, the institution continues to strengthen it’s position as a defining hospitality destination. Their collective responsibility extends beyond protecting a celebrated past, to redesigning a future, our past will be proud of, long after we are gone. It is to ensure that the institution remains competitive, innovative and relevant to future generations. The true measure of leadership, after all, is not simply what it achieves during its tenure. It is what remains valuable long after that tenure has ended. Legacy is not the applause we receive while we are present. It is the relevance of what we build when we are no longer in the room. Fifty years of Eko Hotels is therefore not merely a tribute to endurance. It is a testament to institutional stewardship. HOSPITALITY TO DESTINATION ECONOMICS Perhaps the most consequential chapter in Eko Hotels’ evolution is it’s expanding role in connecting hospitality with tourism, culture, entertainment and the creative economy. Through initiatives such as Tropical Christmas Wonderland, Theatre @ Eko Hotels, Hakuna Matata Theme Park and other destination experiences, the institution has increasingly demonstrated how hospitality infrastructure can become a platform for cultural production and economic participation. These initiatives represent a larger philosophy: a hotel should not wait for tourism demand to arrive. It can actively help create the reasons people travel. A theatrical production creates opportunities for performers, designers, musicians, technicians and production professionals. A festive destination experience stimulates spending across accommodation, food, transport, entertainment and retail. A major international conference brings together airlines, logistics providers, service businesses and professionals. This is the multiplier effect of hospitality. It is also a reminder that tourism should not be treated as a decorative sector in national economic planning. It is an interconnected economic ecosystem. Oil may have fed Nigeria’s treasury, but tourism possesses the potential to employ generations of her children. The opportunity is enormous, provided the country develops the infrastructure, policies, investment climate and destination experiences necessary to realise it. Eko Hotels’ evolution offers a practical illustration of what becomes possible when hospitality is approached as an economic engine rather than simply a property business. THE AFRICA LEGACY SUMMIT: WHEN CELEBRATION BECAME CONVERSATION Importantly, Eko Hotels’ golden jubilee did not begin and end with a spectacular gala. Earlier in May, the institution convened the Africa Legacy Summit, bringing together policymakers, scholars, diplomats, tourism professionals, business leaders, creatives and young Africans to explore the future of culture, hospitality, tourism and travel. The summit asked a question of continental importance: How can Africa move beyond celebrating its potential to deliberately building the systems that convert that potential into prosperity? Discussions examined cultural identity, tourism development, investment, sustainability, innovation, youth participation and the economic opportunities emerging across the continent. It was an ambitious expression of the institution’s belief that celebrating fifty years should involve more than remembering the past. It should also contribute to shaping the future. If the Africa Legacy Summit was the intellectual expression of Eko Hotels’ golden jubilee, The Legacy Ball was its cultural and emotional crescendo. One challenged Africa to think differently. The other demonstrated the extraordinary possibilities of African creativity. Together, they communicated a powerful proposition: Africa’s future will not be secured by repeatedly announcing her potential. It will be secured by institutions willing to organise that potential into measurable progress. THE CREATIVE INTELLIGENCE BEHIND THE CELEBRATION For Dr. Iyadunni Gbadebo, Director of Sales and Marketing at Eko Hotels & Suites, the golden jubilee represented a significant opportunity to connect the institution’s history with a larger vision for African hospitality. Over the years, her work in commercial strategy, destination experience development, theatre tourism, event curation and cultural marketing has contributed to initiatives that extend the hotel’s relevance beyond traditional accommodation. Her approach reflects a growing recognition that hospitality brands must compete not only through their facilities, but through the experiences, stories and emotional connections they create. The Legacy Ball formed part of this wider ambition to celebrate institutional achievement while presenting African creativity with confidence and sophistication. As Gbadebo has consistently advocated, the continent must move from simply possessing exceptional cultural assets to developing commercially viable platforms that showcase them. The distinction is critical. Culture alone does not automatically create a tourism economy. It requires vision, investment, production, distribution, marketing and disciplined execution. The world cannot buy an experience we have not had the courage to create. That philosophy has become increasingly visible in Eko Hotels’ evolving portfolio of cultural and experiential initiatives, and the next fifty years begins now. As the celebrations drew to a close, the greater significance of the occasion became unmistakable. Eko Hotels & Suites had not simply commemorated fifty years of existence. It had reaffirmed the importance of building institutions capable of transcending generations. For Nigeria, the lesson is profound. National development is not achieved by government alone. It is strengthened by private enterprises that create employment, attract investment, nurture talent, maintain standards and build international confidence in their destinations. Every enduring African institution becomes evidence that the continent is capable of building and sustaining excellence. And every successful African experience challenges the outdated assumption that world-class quality must arrive from somewhere else. Eko Hotels has spent fifty years welcoming the world to Africa. On one extraordinary night, it reminded the world why Africa deserves to be a destination, not merely a departure point. The golden jubilee was magnificent. The performances were memorable. The personalities were distinguished. But the true achievement was something much greater than spectacle. It was the celebration of an institution, the recognition of its people, the affirmation of it’s leadership and the demonstration of what African hospitality can become when ambition is matched with intention. For fifty years, Eko Hotels has stood as one of Lagos’ defining hospitality landmarks. It’s next challenge is not simply to remain celebrated. It is to remain indispensable. Because the most powerful legacies are not monuments to yesterday. They are foundations upon which tomorrow is built. Fifty years ago, a hotel opened its doors. Five decades later, an institution stands before the world. And if The Legacy Gala proved anything, it is that Africa does not need permission to be extraordinary. She needs more people willing to build the extraordinary — and sustain it. EKO HOTELS & SUITES is 50. The golden years are behind us. The golden possibilities are ahead. title: Beans, water and radios sell out after UK’s stockpile warning
body: Supplies of tinned food, bottled water and equipment such as radios and batteries have been running out in the UK since the government issued a message to prepare for shortages . Online grocer Ocado reported several types of water were unavailable, while items such as beans and soup were also out of stock. Frozen food seller Iceland said it was “clear consumers have listened to the government’s message”, because the company reported a 40 per cent surge in sales of tinned food in recent days, while supermarket chain Booths reported a similar pattern. Retailers such as Robert Dyas and Maplin said they had seen an increase in sales of radios, torches and power banks. "Within hours of the Be Ready announcement we saw people reach for the basics – a torch, a wind-up radio, a power bank. Torch sales nearly quadrupled and radio sales almost doubled in three days," said Ollie Marshall, managing director at Maplin. Last week, the UK published guidance urging people to “be ready” in the event of a national emergency by stocking up on essentials and signing up for government support. Authorities advised households to ensure they could be self-sufficient for three days in an emergency. The UK has been facing threats from bad weather, drought and flooding, as well as artificial intelligence and hostile activity from Russia and Iran. The guidance said households should “take a few simple steps to stay prepared if everyday services are temporarily disrupted”. The online checklist included bottled water and non-perishable foods, as well as hand sanitiser. It also advised people to ensure they had cash and copies of important documents, as well as blankets and warm clothing. The announcement was made before two storms hit the UK at the weekend, when sales of such goods typically rise anyway. Security Minister Dan Jarvis said the move “brings the UK into line with many of our European peers who also have the three-day message at the heart of their campaign”. The advice was good news for outdoor equipment stores. Preppers Shop UK said it had seen a 650 per cent increase in sales of "off-grid" items. Its Facebook page includes advice on what could be included in a "grab and go" bag. Defence Secretary Wes Streeting told BBC’s Newsnight it was "encouraging that people are taking practical steps" to be ready for emergencies. "Having a few everyday essentials at home, from tinned food to torches, helps households prepare for disruption, whether that's flooding, power cuts or burst pipes," he added. "We can all play our part in making Britain more resilient."

title: Russian non-resource non-energy exports up 7.3% in 8M 2026
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Russian non-resource non-energy exports (NRNEE) grew by 7.3% annually and climbed to $109.5 bln in January - August 2026, Minister of Industry and Trade Anton Alikhanov said.
"Non-resource non-energy export continues growing. It increased by 7.3% within eight months of this year and reached $109.5 bln," the minister said. Industrial products account for $80 bln as its part, he added.

title: Angaur residents face drinking water crisis and lost income as El Niño drought deepens
body: By: L.N. Reklai KOROR, Palau (Oct. 24, 2026) — Angaur residents are struggling to secure drinking water and maintain their livelihoods as a prolonged drought linked to a super El Niño threatens Palau and much of the western Pacific. Surrounded by seawater, salty inland lakes and wells with brackish water, Angaur is facing a growing water crisis. Despite having water all around the island, residents depend on drinking water transported from Koror, while the dry conditions are making it harder to find crabs, grow crops and earn income. Melanie Santiago, an Angaurian facing challenges caused by unusually long dry spell. Each week, Angaur State transports residents’ water containers to Koror to be filled with drinking water at no cost to the people. But the service depends on boat transportation and is vulnerable to weather and other conditions that can interrupt deliveries. An Angaur resident traveling to Koror said she counted 82 five-gallon containers and 20 three-gallon containers during the last boat trip. The containers are normally transported about once a week, but the boat had not returned for two weeks, raising concerns about the growing demand for drinking water. “I think there will definitely be more containers since the boat has not been back for sometime,” she said. The delay highlights the challenges residents face in securing enough safe water as the drought continues. “We have water tanks,” said Melanie Santiago, an Angaur resident who sells ukaeb, or processed land crab meat, to supplement her formal income. “But with little rain, we don’t have much water and what is in there is not safe, so we need to get fresh water from Koror.” Wells remain available, but residents question water safety Angaur’s main water source is its underground wells. Although water levels remain adequate, residents say the water is not safe for drinking or cooking. Angaur water wells supplying water to Angaur community. Photo credit: Thoms Afred Thoms Alfred, a Palau Public Utilities employee responsible for Angaur’s water system, said the water levels in the wells remain good. However, residents report concerns about using the water for household needs beyond cleaning and washing clothes. Some residents say bathing in the well water can cause “pink eyes” or skin rashes, although those concerns have not been independently confirmed. One resident said she now brings water from Koror to cook rice rather than use the water from Angaur’s wells. The situation leaves families dependent on water transported by boat, even as delays and limited rainfall make it harder to maintain a reliable supply. Drought threatens crab harvest and family incomes The water shortage is only one part of the hardship facing Angaur residents. The prolonged dry conditions are also affecting two important sources of income for local families: ukaeb, or processed coconut land crab meat, and kebui, or pepper leaves. Santiago said the dry, hot weather drives crabs deeper underground, making them increasingly difficult to find. Plants showing effect of prolonged dry conditions caused by El Nino. Photo: Island Times “When it’s dry and hot like it is now, the crabs go deep underground and it becomes very very hard to find them,” she said. The drought created particular concern when the government ordered 2,500 ukaeb and 2,500 crab cakes from Angaur producers for the Pacific Islands Forum Leaders Summit. Santiago said producers feared they would not be able to fulfill the order because the prolonged dry conditions had made crabs difficult to catch. Fortunately, rain arrived, allowing residents to collect crabs as they emerged from the ground. “We were so worried because it has been so dry for so long, that we could not find any crabs,” Santiago said. “We were worried we may not be able to fulfill our order.” She said residents rushed to catch crabs when the rain came, trying to gather as much as possible to sell. That has become a pattern for Angaur producers: waiting for occasional rainfall and taking advantage of brief opportunities to harvest crabs before the ground dries again. About 60% of residents depend on local products Santiago estimates that about 60% of Angaur residents supplement their income by selling products such as crab meat and kebui. The drought is affecting those livelihoods, particularly for families who depend on the products as their main source of income. “It is even worse for those that have no other means income other than selling their crops and crab products for living,” she said. For those households, the prolonged dry spell threatens not only food and water supplies but also the money needed to support their families. The effects extend beyond crab harvesting and pepper leaves. Other crops, including papayas, betel nut and coconuts, are already facing challenges from invasive macaque monkeys and coconut beetles. The drought is adding another strain. Brown and yellowing leaves on various crops indicate the effects of the dry conditions and raise concerns about further damage if rainfall remains limited. Outlying states face greater hardship While the drought is affecting Babeldaob and other parts of Palau, the impact is particularly severe in smaller, outlying states such as Angaur. Residents must contend with limited local sources of safe drinking water, dependence on boat transportation and declining opportunities to earn income from traditional products. With water levels in wells still adequate but residents questioning the water’s safety, the island’s immediate challenge is securing dependable drinking water while the drought continues. For Angaur families, the consequences are already visible in delayed water deliveries, difficult crab harvests and crops showing signs of stress. The prolonged dry spell is placing pressure on both household needs and the local economy, leaving residents increasingly dependent on rainfall and transportation from Koror. The post Angaur residents face drinking water crisis and lost income as El Niño drought deepens appeared first on Island Times News .

title: The UK is replacing rifles. A multi-billion tender and an opportunity for Polish companies?
body:
As part of the Grayburn programme, with an estimated cost of £2 billion, the implementation of five variants of a new weapon based on a common lower receiver is planned to replace the British Army’s current rifles and carbines. This raises the question of whether the MSBS Grot could be offered in the tender.
Small arms of the SA80 system were developed in the United Kingdom during the 1970s and 1980s, and were introduced into serial production and service in 1985. For years, the SA80 faced criticism regarding its build quality and reliability. Attempts were made to resolve these issues by modernising the L85A1 rifles to the L85A2 version, and subsequently to the L85A3. Modernisation does not solve all problems to a satisfactory degree; furthermore, the weapon itself is ageing, which is why the Grayburn programme has been underway for several years. The UK Ministry of Defence has confirmed that the estimated cost of the project is approximately £2 billion.
Much indicates that the successor to the L85A2 and L85A3 rifles will be an AR15-system weapon or its variant in 5.56 mm calibre for 5.56x45 mm ammunition. The SA80 system itself design-wise utilises solutions from the AR18 system. The project’s implementation is scheduled for the period from July 2029 to the end of March 2045. It is expected that five variants based on a common lower receiver will be deployed, namely:
In addition to the Grayburn project, other programmes are being conducted: Cairns , intended to replace the L7A2 general-purpose machine gun, and the Troubler programme, aimed at implementing a new light machine gun. In the past, the British Army used FN Minimi light machine guns under the designations L108A1 and L110A2. The Shamer programme is also underway, aimed at finding a successor to the L115 and L118 sniper rifles. Previously, the Hunter programme was successfully completed, selecting a new rifle for the Royal Marines and the Ranger Regiment. The winner was the Knight’s Armament KS-1 rifle, which was entered into service under the designation L403A1.
Defence24.pl has contacted PGZ (Polska Grupa Zbrojeniowa) requesting information regarding potential participation in the British proceedings. The group’s „Łucznik”-Radom Arms Factory offers the MSBS Grot system, which has already been delivered to the Polish Armed Forces in well over 200,000 units and is also being used in Ukraine.

title: Africa holds 1/3 of world's natural resources, most remain untapped — Russian ministry
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Approximately one-third of the world's natural resources are located in Africa, and the bulk of this potential remains untapped, the Russian Natural Resources Ministry told TASS ahead of the third Russia-Africa Summit.
"Soviet and later Russian geologists have made a significant contribution to the geological exploration of the African continent. According to current estimates, about one-third of the world's natural resources are concentrated in Africa, yet a substantial portion of this potential has yet to be realized," the ministry said.
In particular, African nations possess significant reserves of rare-earth metals, lithium, gold, and other highly sought-after minerals, the ministry emphasized.
"At the same time, the level of geological exploration varies considerably depending on the country and region," the ministry added.
The third Russia-Africa Summit will take place in Moscow on October 28-29. Earlier, Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova announced that the summit's plenary session, featuring Russian President Vladimir Putin, is scheduled for October 29. The diplomat also noted that a substantial package of intergovernmental agreements and commercial contracts is expected to be signed on the sidelines of the event.

title: Elevate Africa 2026 Convening: Press Conference Sets Stage for Accra Gathering Under “Africa: Defining Her Future”
body: The countdown to one of Africa’s most anticipated leadership gatherings is officially underway. On Monday, October 26, 2026, Elevate Africa held a curtain-raiser press conference in Accra, Ghana, setting the stage for its 2026 Annual Convening. Held under the powerful theme “Africa: Defining Her Future,” the main convening will take place on October 28–29, 2026, at the Mövenpick Ambassador Hotel in Accra, bringing together heads of state, traditional rulers, policymakers, creatives, investors, and diaspora leaders. DAY ONE: THE PRESS CONFERENCE The press conference served as a powerful preview of the conversations to come, with four key voices setting the tone for the days ahead: 1. Her Majesty Olori Atuwatse III — Queen Consort of the Warri Kingdom and Co-Founder of Elevate Africa The Queen Consort delivered a stirring call for African-led solutions, declaring: “Time has come for Africa to take up the pen and write its own future.” She emphasized that meaningful transformation requires collaboration across governments, business, and civil society, stating: “Solutions can only be truly driven by those who are leading nations, leading companies, leading in different sectors.” She also highlighted the Elevate Africa Fellowship, which empowers mid-career professionals to reshape the continent’s narrative from one of problems to one of solutions. 2. Kofi Okyere Darko (KOD) — Director of Diaspora Affairs, Office of the President of Ghana Representing the Ghanaian government, KOD underscored the indispensable role of the global African diaspora. “We can’t elevate Africa to the next level without the participation of the diaspora,” he stated, noting that Africans abroad possess valuable knowledge, skills, networks, and resources that can drive economic transformation. He also highlighted Ghana’s commitment to deepening diaspora engagement beyond tourism, encouraging investment and entrepreneurship. 3. Emmanuel Ikubese — Elevate Africa Fellow (2026 Cohort) Bringing the perspective of emerging leaders, Ikubese advocated for pan-African collaboration among professionals. He argued that the continent’s development relies on collective intelligence and the mobilization of its vast talent pool. 4. Dr. Rex Idaminabo — Chief Partnership Officer, Elevate Africa Closing the session, Dr. Idaminabo framed the convening as a decisive moment for the continent. “Africa’s transformation is a decision, and for that to happen, we want everyone to take part,” he said, emphasizing that the fellowship has united participants from 23 African countries to build resilience and support one another. OTHER KEY VOICES AT THE PRESS CONFERENCE INCLUDE: Prince Moses — Director of Strategy, Africa Prosperity Network (APN) He spoke on economic integration, urging the removal of barriers to the movement of people, capital, and goods across the continent, and highlighted the gap between Africa’s 1.5 billion-person market and its low intra-African trade volume. Grace Nelson — Alumna, Elevate Africa Fellowship She denounced persistent stereotypes about Africa and called for greater visibility for African success stories, stressing that changing the narrative begins with Africans themselves. Kim Schofield — U.S. State Representative, Georgia She underscored the deep ties between Africa and the African American diaspora, stating: “Until Africa is whole, African Americans will never be whole.” WHAT TO EXPECT IN THE COMING DAYS With the main convening set for October 28–29, here is what delegates and observers can look forward to: High-Profile Participation Confirmed attendees include President Julius Maada Bio of Sierra Leone, Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang of Ghana, and former Presidents Goodluck Ebele Jonathan (Nigeria), John Kufuor (Ghana), Joyce Banda (Malawi), and Ameenah Gurib-Fakim (Mauritius). Ministers from Ghana, Nigeria, and Egypt, along with senior officials from the AfCFTA Secretariat, will also participate. Four Pillars of Discussion The convening will center on four interconnected pillars: · Leadership and Governance · Trade, Investment and Doing Business in Africa · Youth Opportunity and Leadership · Diaspora, Return, Creative Economy and Soft Power Threads of Africa Exhibition and Film Awards A major highlight will be the Threads of Africa showcase, celebrating African textile heritage, fashion innovation, and visual storytelling. The 2026 edition of the Threads of Africa Fashion Film Prize will award up to $25,000 in non-dilutive grants to winners, alongside mentorship opportunities and a dedicated showcase at the convening. Key Outcomes The gathering is expected to culminate in the “Accra Declaration,” a youth statement, and a policy brief on the creative economy. Organizers will also launch the “Trade Desk” to connect businesses with investors and the “Africa Ayana” programme for the diaspora, with applications opening in January 2027. WHY IT MATTERS As global power dynamics shift, Africa stands at a defining crossroads. With the youngest population in the world (median age 18), immense cultural influence, and the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) unlocking a market of 1.5 billion people, the continent has a unique opportunity to shape its own destiny. Elevate Africa’s 2026 Convening is not just another conference it is a deliberate step toward narrative reclamation, economic integration, and intergenerational collaboration. As Her Majesty Olori Atuwatse III put it: “Together, we can Elevate Africa.” The post Elevate Africa 2026 Convening: Press Conference Sets Stage for Accra Gathering Under “Africa: Defining Her Future” appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Ukraine Moldova Sign Five-Year Defense Pact Amid Russian Threats
body:
Ukraine and Moldova signed a five-year military-technical cooperation agreement on Monday to strengthen regional security amid Russian threats.
Ukrainian Defense Minister Evgeniy Khmara and Moldovan Defense Minister Anatolie Nosatîi signed the pact on October 27 in the presence of both countries’ prime ministers during Moldovan Prime Minister Vasile Tofan’s visit to Kyiv. Tofan also met Ukrainian Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi and President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
The agreement covers equipment repair and modernization, cyber defense, airspace protection, specialist training, and joint research and development.
According to Ukrainian media, the deal also covers :
EU integration and regional security: Both governments pledged to pursue EU membership together, arguing that parallel accession would strengthen security and economic ties. Leaders discussed Transnistria, Moldova’s breakaway region bordering Ukraine that hosts Russian military personnel. They also agreed to revive the Ukraine-Moldova-Romania Odesa Triangle and resume their intergovernmental trade and economic cooperation commission, with a trilateral prime ministers’ meeting planned but undated.
Borders and transport: The countries plan to extend joint controls to two additional border crossings, with an agreement expected soon. Zelenskyy proposed restoring EU-backed Solidarity Lanes for Ukrainian exports. Koretskyi thanked Moldova for discounted rail freight rates introduced in response to Russian attacks affecting Black Sea trade. Talks also covered Ukrainian support for Moldova’s water supply.
Energy cooperation: Discussions covered gas transit through the Trans-Balkan Corridor, Moldova’s support for the Vertical Gas Corridor, discounted transit arrangements and Moldovan companies’ use of Ukrainian underground gas storage. Ukraine halted Russian gas transit to Europe in January 2025, increasing the importance of alternative regional routes.
