title: Can Black voting power and Trump fatigue break Mississippi's red wall?
body:
Mississippi Democratic Senate nominee Scott Colom speaks at a rally in Columbus, Miss., headlined by former Vice President Kamala Harris on Oct. 22, 2026. Stephen Fowler/NPR hide caption
COLUMBUS, Miss. — On paper, Mississippi's U.S. Senate race seems like the perfect place for a political upset this year, an assertion President Trump's Monday rally there seems to support.
It has the highest share of Black voters in the country, at close to 40%. It's a rural, agriculture-heavy state that is also among the poorest, so higher prices are felt harder.
But Trump won the state by 23 points in 2024, and it's extremely racially polarized, meaning not enough white voters back Democrats for the party to win statewide.
In a midterm environment that has seen hundreds of millions of dollars poured into Senate races in conservative-heavy states like Iowa, Texas, Ohio and Alaska, and a last-minute flood of cash to Kansas , the Magnolia State has been left off of many peoples' radar — and largely out of campaign investments.
Scott Colom, a district attorney and the Democratic Senate nominee in Mississippi, told NPR that's a mistake.
"The reality is, Mississippi has never been a lost cause, we've been a betrayed cause," he said. "The Democratic Party has not been trying to win Mississippi. Let's stop kidding ourselves, right? They spent hundreds of millions of dollars in other states. They spent almost nothing in Mississippi."
Colom is challenging incumbent Republican Cindy Hyde-Smith, who blocked his nomination to be a federal judge during the Biden administration.
In the final weeks of the election, both parties have rushed to spend millions of dollars in Mississippi, as national polling shows a pathway where Democratic enthusiasm and elevated Black turnout, combined with fewer Republican base voters and defections from the party, has made deep red races deeply competitive this cycle.
The crowd listens during a rally with former Vice President Kamala Harris and Mississippi's Democratic Senate nominee Scott Colom in Columbus, Miss., on Oct. 22. Stephen Fowler/NPR hide caption
At a rally for Colom in his hometown high school gym Thursday, about a thousand people showed up to hear the candidate — joined by former Vice President Kamala Harris — give his closing message.
Many attendees expressed optimism for his campaign coupled with a vibe of feeling down about those in power, regardless of party affiliation — citing the war in Iran, rising fuel costs and dissatisfaction with Trump's second term.
That includes Celestine Rice, who said many people were realizing a need to focus on bringing change to the political system and representation.
"Before, we didn't realize how bad it was, but now it's obvious," she said. "The moral compass of this country is gone."
Rice said many people took for granted an era where it seemed the country used to be more focused on taking care of its citizens and now they see that "big money, it doesn't trickle down like they said."
The brunt of the Democratic money and manpower headed to Mississippi is driven by a growing number of those who argue the party's future runs through the South, including Harris, Georgia Sen. Raphael Warnock and former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg.
At the rally, Harris said political changes in the last year and a half were the result of "the most callous, corrupt and incompetent presidential administration we have ever experienced."
"We've been going through that range of emotions from anger to sadness to depression, all of that for a year and a half," she said. "Well guess what? We're 12 days out from an election. And it's time to turn that anger into action."
President Trump embraces Mississippi Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith at a campaign rally on Oct. 26, 2026 in Corinth, Miss. Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images hide caption
About a hundred miles up the road a few days later, Trump, Hyde-Smith and other Mississippi Republicans gathered in Corinth to motivate the party's base to show up and vote next Tuesday.
In a statement ahead of the rally, Hyde-Smith's campaign manager expressed confidence in her reelection bid.
"We are confident that Mississippians will once again send Cindy Hyde-Smith to the U.S. Senate," Jake Monssen said. "Senator Hyde-Smith and President Trump have built a strong working relationship, and she gladly accepted when President Trump offered to help rally voters and support her get-out-the-vote efforts.
"With so much at stake in this election, Mississippians deserve to hear directly from their President about the consequences of electing Democrats, the radical socialist policies being pushed by Scott Colom, and the importance of this election. Team Cindy looks forward to a successful, high-energy event in Corinth," he said.
Speaking ahead of the president, Hyde-Smith touted accomplishments from her time in office and said the choice facing voters "could not be clearer."
"We know what we're looking at: this is socialism versus capitalism, and we know that," she said. "Communism versus democracy, and big government versus the free market. It could not be higher stakes."
Hyde-Smith repeatedly reiterated that it was important for Republicans to get out and vote.
"Endorsements don't win elections, votes win elections," she said.
Mississippi Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith talks to audience members as President Trump holds a campaign rally in support of her reelection campaign on Oct. 26, 2026 in Corinth, Miss. Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images hide caption
For his part, Trump said his visit to Mississippi was because Hyde-Smith was in good shape in her matchup.
"Sometimes when you think somebody's doing so well, nobody votes," Trump said. "'Oh, Cindy's great, she's gonna do no problem, let's stay home.' And then bad things happen, Cindy. That's why I'm here, just get out and vote."
Over the last month, the Republican campaign strategy has been to highlight the investment and attention from national Democrats as proof Colom is too extreme for Mississippi — and have spent heavily on ads saying as much.
"Meet the most radical Senate candidate in our lifetime, Scott Colom," an ad titled "Most Radical" intones. "Twice nominated by Biden, beholden to the far left. As DA, violent crime doubled on his watch."
The Hyde-Smith campaign has spent more than $1.3 million on that ad, according to data from AdImpact.
But Democrats have spent more this month, about $5 million to the Republicans' $3.2 million, with a message that there's no daylight between the unpopular president and down ballot Republicans.
"I mean, the reality is if somebody's doing a good job, it's hard to beat them," he said. "If Cindy Hyde-Smith was focused on the voters, it'd be tough. But it's very clear the voters of Mississippi want to fire her."
The race carries weight beyond Mississippi, or even control of the Senate. It's become a stand in for conversations about the power of Black voters in the South.
Many Southern Republican-led states have rushed to redraw congressional maps that remove opportunities for Black voters to elect candidates of their choice after a Supreme Court ruling earlier this year rolled back part of the Voting Rights Act.
In Mississippi, Republicans have signaled a desire to redraw state legislative and judicial races after the midterms, and Colom said it could extend even further into local elections.
"What that tells us is you're trying to take away power from the voters and give it to the leaders," he said. "That's not how democracy is supposed to work. The voters have to pick the leaders, not the leaders pick the voters."
In a statewide race that can't be gerrymandered, and in an environment favorable to Democrats, history and math still prove to be a challenge. The last Democratic senator from Mississippi came in the early '80s. The last successful Black statewide candidate was during Reconstruction.
Even during the 2018 blue wave, Cindy Hyde-Smith won a special election for this seat by roughly 7 points.
Still, there are many factors that have both parties anxiously awaiting results on Nov. 3, including a pervasive anti-incumbent streak that has shown up in polls and primaries this election cycle coupled with a significant increase in Black voter turnout in states that have early voting.
Ashley Kennedy Shelton, who runs a nonpartisan civic engagement group in Louisiana, told NPR earlier this month that people of all stripes have been expressing frustration and a desire for change.
"I think you're going to see voters truly show up, because folks are just tired," she said. "They're like: 'This doesn't work, and it hasn't been working for quite some time.' I think you're going to see it at the ballot box."

title: Putin orders search engines to steer women seeking abortion information toward ‘social support’ programs instead
body: Russian President Vladimir Putin has ordered the government to draft proposals for changing search engine results on abortion-related queries, according to a list of presidential instructions. Under the instructions, search engines would have to display sites offering “social support to women facing a reproductive choice” before other results when users search for information about abortion. Valentina Matviyenko, speaker of the Federation Council, the upper house of Russia’s parliament, made a similar proposal in May 2026, calling for search engines to change their algorithms so that links to family support centers would appear before abortion-related results. “So that when people type in the search bar for information about clinics where an abortion can be performed, information about family support centers would appear first, and only then the websites of those clinics, including information about the risks of abortion and its health consequences,” she said. Russia has waged a broad campaign to restrict abortion access in recent years. Among other measures, private clinics in 19 regions of the country have stopped performing the procedure altogether. title: Police Arrest Fake Lawyer Operating For Over 11 Years In Ebonyi
body: Operatives of the Nigeria Police Force, Ebonyi State Command, have arrested a suspect for impersonating a legal practitioner and fraudulently parading himself as a barrister and solicitor for over a decade. The arrest followed a discreet investigation launched by the Command after receiving a petition bordering on obtaining money under false pretences. According to a statement released on Tuesday by the Police Public Relations Officer, SP Joshua Ukandu, the suspect allegedly defrauded a victim under the guise of providing legal services. “According to the petition, the suspect allegedly collected the sum of N650,000 from one Mr. David in March 2026 to facilitate the processing and approval for the naming of a street in Ohaozara Local Government Area. The petitioner alleged that the suspect presented himself as an experienced lawyer,” the statement read. Following his arrest, police investigations confirmed that Enyinnaya had been falsely parading himself as a legal practitioner for more than eleven years. During interrogation, the suspect confessed that he possessed no legal qualifications or call-to-bar certification. An execution of a search warrant at his residence led to the recovery of several incriminating items, including: Nigerian Bar Association (NBA) seal, framed portrait of the suspect dressed in full legal regalia, lawyer’s robe and wig, forged Bachelor of Laws (LL.B.) and Master of Laws (LL.M.) degree certificates bearing Enugu State University of Science and Technology. Purported court judgments, as well as various legal documents prepared by him, including Powers of Attorney and Deeds of Conveyance. The Command confirmed that the suspect has been charged to court. Reacting to the arrest, the Commissioner of Police, Ebonyi State Command, CP Hope Urunwa Okafor, commended the operatives for their diligence in uncovering the long-standing impersonation. “Members of the public are strongly advised to verify the credentials of individuals offering legal services and to promptly report suspicious activities to the police,” CP Okafor urged. The post Police Arrest Fake Lawyer Operating For Over 11 Years In Ebonyi appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Airbus secures Life Flight Network order for five H135 helicopters
body: Airbus has secured an order from US-based medical transport service firm Life Flight Network for five new H135 helicopters. Airbus and Life Flight Network representatives met on October 26, 2026, at the Air Medical Transport Conference (AMTC) in Fort Worth, Texas, to finalize the agreement. Life Flight Network provides critical emergency care, deploying both rotor-wing and fixed-wing aircraft as well as ground transport across the Pacific Northwest and Intermountain West. With its latest Airbus order, the US firm has more than doubled its commitment to the H135 aircraft after placing an order for three aircraft in 2025. Life Flight Network “Every investment in our fleet is an investment in the patients and communities who count on us,” Ben Clayton, CEO of Life Flight Network, said. “Across the Pacific Northwest, Intermountain West, and Hawai`i, our crews serve communities separated by mountain ranges, oceans, and vast rural distances. The H135’s advanced safety features and air medical capabilities are well suited to the demands of serving this diverse region.” Clayton added: “We’re pleased to continue our partnership with Airbus as we invest in the future of our fleet and strengthen access to critical care for the communities we serve.” Life Flight Network’s current fleet includes the Bell 429, Bell 407GXi, AW119Kx and the Eurocopter EC135. Its fixed wing fleet includes the Pilatus PC-12 NG. “Life Flight Network provides a vital lifeline to millions of people across the Pacific Northwest, and Airbus is honored by their continued trust in our rotorcraft,” Bart Reijnen, Head of the North America region at Airbus Helicopters, said. “The H135 continues to set the standard for air medical services, combining exceptional reliability, advanced safety technologies, and quiet flight performance so that dedicated clinical teams can carry out their lifesaving work safely and efficiently.” According to Airbus, there are over 1,500 H135 family helicopters in service worldwide, logging more than eight million cumulative flight hours across medical, law enforcement, and utility configurations. title: ‘Go Home’, Obi says Tinubu lacks Energy To Govern Nigeria
body: Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has challenged President Bola Tinubu’s capacity to lead Nigeria. He demanded his exit in 2027 amid growing political controversy over the President’s health. Obi, a former governor of Anambra State, said Nigeria needed a president who could be physically present and energetically confront the country’s economic and security challenges. He insisted that Tinubu’s administration had failed to improve the lives of citizens. “Above all, President Tinubu does not have the energy and resolve required to lead Nigeria today, and he must go home.” “We need him to go home. Nigeria cannot be governed with the energy he has today. Nigeria needs a president who will be available and present”, he said. He spoke in Abuja during the inauguration of the NDC National Campaign Council. At the event, he accused the All Progressives Congress (APC)-led government of worsening poverty, unemployment, corruption and insecurity. Obi’s remarks come amid renewed scrutiny of Tinubu’s health and physical capacity. This followed his announcement that he would not attend every APC campaign rally ahead of the 2027 presidential election. At the inauguration of the APC Presidential Campaign Council on October 14, Tinubu said he had accepted advice to prevent campaign activities from distracting him from governance. He added that the country required his attention. “You will excuse me from going everywhere with you. We have bills to pay. The American creditors cannot wait,” the President said. He maintained that he would still address Nigerians directly during the campaign. The APC’s proposed campaign timetable subsequently indicated that Tinubu would attend rallies in 12 states, leaving party officials to coordinate campaigns in other states. The arrangement triggered criticism from opposition figures and commentators who questioned whether the President should personally engage voters across the country while seeking another term. The ruling party has defended the decision as a strategy to balance governance with electioneering. Obafemi George, a member of the APC Presidential Campaign Council’s media and strategic communications committee, said there was no legal requirement for a presidential candidate to campaign physically in all 36 states. The health debate had also intensified after Tinubu returned to Nigeria on September 29 from an extended stay in Europe, following weeks of speculation during his absence. The President dismissed the concerns, telling journalists: “Ready to kick, ready to walk. There’s nothing wrong.” Obi, however, used the occasion to question the substance of Tinubu’s re-election campaign, arguing that the President should account for his administration’s expenditure and achievements before asking Nigerians for another mandate. “Just last Friday, President Tinubu launched his second general campaign rather than explain to Nigerians what he has used the billions he borrowed to do. “Rather than explain what he has achieved with the 2023, 2024 and 2025 budgets, he chose to blame the opposition for creating poverty”, he said. Tinubu launched his re-election campaign in Kaduna on October 24, defending his administration’s economic reforms and blaming opposition politicians for the country’s poverty and hunger. His government’s removal of the petrol subsidy and foreign-exchange reforms have improved some public-finance indicators. However, it has also contributed to severe cost-of-living pressures that remain a major political issue ahead of the election. Obi said his proposed administration would reject a culture of blame and instead prioritise practical solutions to the country’s problems. “The purpose of governance is to solve problems, not to blame people. I will not blame anybody. We will create that new Nigeria that is possible,” he said. He identified corruption as a central obstacle to national development, pledging a more aggressive campaign against it if elected. “We need a revolution that will turn this country around, and we are committed to that. The APC-led government under President Tinubu has failed Nigeria,” Obi said. The NDC candidate also cited Nigeria’s positions on international terrorism and hunger indices, alongside poverty figures. “There is no single indicator under Tinubu that has improved. When he came into office, our record on terrorism was better. Today, we are number four,”. “When he came in, we were ranked 109th on the hunger list. Today, we are the 117th. When he came in, our poverty ranking was below 140. Today, we are above 140”, he said. The NDC campaign council inauguration was attended by Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, the party’s vice-presidential candidate; Seriake Dickson, its national leader; members of the National Working Committee and other party leaders.

title: INVITATION TO BID: Provision and Installation of A Solar Power System at Media Trust Group Headquarters
body: 1. title: Trade between Russia, CIS countries above $110 bln — Russian Ambassador
body:
DUSHANBE, October 27. /TASS/. Trade volume between Russia and other CIS countries has exceeded $110 bln and is actively growing, Semyon Grigoryev, the Russian Ambassador to Tajikistan, said at the international scientific and practical conference "CIS: Directions and Prospects of Development" opened in Dushanbe.
"We attach particular importance to the close cooperation supported within the Commonwealth in the fields of trade, investment, and high technology. The annual [trade] turnover between Russia and the CIS countries is significant - it is above $110 bln and is growing at double-digit percentage rates," he said.
Trade within the CIS is stable and mutually beneficial, the ambassador said. "Up to 90% of settlements are carried out in national currencies. Large industrial projects are being implemented, and the transcontinental logistics corridors North-South and East-West are being modernized and developed," Grigoryev stressed.
The CIS countries have established mechanisms of multilateral cooperation that are reliable, flexible, and adaptive to current realities, which cover an increasing number of relevant fields of activity, the Russian diplomat added.

title: Ngaraard to hold special election Nov. 24 to fill legislative vacancy
body: By: Eoghan Olkeriil Ngirudelsang NGARAARD, Palau — Elab County in Ngaraard State will hold a special election Nov. 24 to fill the legislative seat left vacant by the death of legislator Harvey Ngirairikl. The Palau Election Commission (PEC) announced Tuesday, Oct. 27, that the 12th Olbetibel – Ngaraard Legislature passed Resolution No. 12-7-4S calling for the special election. Nominating petitions are now available and must be submitted by Nov. 9, the PEC said. The deadline also applies to voter registration, requests for confined voting and absentee ballot requests. title: Deputy Speaker Kalu Flags Off Renewed Hope Light Up Project, Distributes Solar Lights to 42,000 Households, 26 Transformers in Bende
body: Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Benjamin Okezie Kalu, on Monday, flagged off the Renewed Hope Light Up Project in Bende Federal Constituency of Abia State, targeting 42,000 households across the 13 electoral wards of the constituency with solar light. He also distributed 26 power transformers to the Wards to connect communities to the national grid of electricity. Commissioning the solar lights, which marked the second phase of the project, the Deputy Speaker who represents the constituency at the National Assembly described access to power as the pressing need of the people uncovered during a constituency-wide needs assessment. He said: “In representation, one of the key expectations of the office of a representative is to do needs analysis, and in the course of doing needs analysis, we discovered that one of our greatest problems in this federal constituency is darkness, lack of access to power and that has affected our economic life, the security life of the community, the human capacity development and job creation, all of which fall under the proposition of the Renewed Hope Agenda, the eight agenda of the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, who from the start intended to improve the economic life of our nation, starting from the communities; create more jobs; improve the security of our communities, human capacity development, agriculture and food security and the list goes on” The Deputy Speaker said the project has two components, connecting communities to the national grid through the transformer distribution and providing alternative energy through solar for all homes in the constituency. He said the intervention aligns with the eight-point Renewed Hope Agenda of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, which seeks to improve the economic life of Nigerians starting from the communities. “What we are doing today has a multiple effect, a ripple effect that trickles down to different aspects of this Renewed Hope Agenda of Mr. President. Today, we stand as the partners of the Renewed Hope Agenda of Mr. President. We call ourselves Renewed Hope Partners. We are members of APC, Bende constituents who believe in the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria and his agenda to improve the lives of the people of Nigeria starting from Bende federal constituency. “What we are here to do is to drive that vision home, by making it a mission that our people can feel, touch and experience. Light before now to many homes in Bende seemed to be luxury. That has been demystified”, he said. The Deputy Speaker further disclosed that he received approval of the plan from President Tinubu when he presented the figure of 42,000 households with a request to ensure children can read at night without kerosene lanterns and families can power their fans and charge phones. He expressed profound gratitude to the President for his interventions in Bende in particular and in entire South East in general, noting that the Light Up Project is aimed at making its impact felt directly by rural households in Bende. “Let me thank the President for initiating Renewed Hope Agenda which has been the roadmap towards the achievements we have made in the last few years. “There is nothing we are doing in Bende, in Igboland as members of this government that has not been approved by the President. He is a President that loves the south Easterners and he is making sure that most of the landmark initiatives commence from this area of the country. Today, we are saying bye bye to darkness in Bende Federal Constituency”, Kalu said. Explaining that the rollout is in batches of 10,000 households, Kalu said 1,000 solar units have already been distributed to beneficiaries from all electoral wards in the constituency who were present at the ceremony to testify. He said each solar unit will serve for 10 years, revealing that it comes with a maintenance agreement. “The people who are handling this have said that this particular solar will serve our people for 10 good years which means you are not going to look for kerosene to power your lanterns in 10 good years, where to charge your phone, power fan. The arrangement we have made with them is that if anything goes bad, we will invite them to come back and fix it as far as you didn’t break it”, he said. The Deputy Speaker also assured that the first 10,000 of the solar lights distributed on Monday will be completed in the next two weeks before the next batch begins. “In the next two weeks, I am sure this 10,000 will be done with and another 10,000 will come in and that is how we will follow it until we finish”, he said. To ensure accountability and prevent diversion of the solar lights, Kalu said all installations are geo-located and programmed through an app, adding that it is the first time 42,000 homes in a single federal constituency will receive solar power in Nigeria. “All the installations will be geo-located through the App. Let me warn. Don’t take your own meant for Item to Ozuitem, it will not work. They are all programmed. This is the first of its kind in the Federal Republic of Nigeria that 42,000 homes will receive light in a federal constituency”, he said. Also distributing the brand new transformers, Kalu explained that each of the 13 Wards in Bende will receive two transformers to gain access to the national grid and help boost their small scale and medium enterprises. “Just like we promised that the light in Bende is in two phases, we have the one for national grid and then, we have places that have not experienced the effect of national grid. Based on that, we requested for alternative source of energy that is environmentally friendly and we chose solar. But we also know that while solar handles the home, the small and medium scale enterprises across Bende need support to power fridges, welding machines, small scale industries, you need a transformer to pick up power from the national grid. So, we have made provisions for all the Wards. Every Ward in Bende Federal Constituency wil receive two transformers. “The decision on where they will be located will not be based on sentiment and will not be political. It will be needs- influenced decision. It will be decision based on lack of access to electricity. Thereafter, all parts will follow. So, my advise to the leaders when you go back is that these should not be packed in anybody’s home. They should be placed around the place it will be easier to be hooked to the national grid to be begin to serve greater number of the people. “We must choose a location where wider number of our constituents will enjoy access to electricity. We are doing all this because of the ripple effect power brings. If you see us distributing solar fans, it is to prevent the heat waves so that Bende people will not be badly impacted by the heat wave that is coming from the global warming. We also believe that these transformers will add values that will protect us from global warming. “I want to thank Bende people for sending me to Abuja. I want to thank them for making that decision. The decision is what is fetching what is happening here today and many more that we have done as well as much more that we will do in the coming days. “Secure these transformers when it gets to your place. It will be economic sabotage if you tamper with them. They should be protected by the youths, the Presidents-General and the traditional rulers because it is meant to serve Bende communities and everyone in Bende both those in APC and those not in APC. These transformers do not know the colour of political parties. It will serve everyone that I am representing”, Kalu said. The Deputy Speaker also signed a N100 million contract with the Electricity company that installed the transformers for the restoration of light to Item and Alayi Wards, which have been disconnected for years. Some constituents representing the 13 Electoral Wards and the Presidents-General of different town unions who testified to the effective representation of the Deputy Speaker at the commissioning pledged to vote massively for both President Tinubu and Kalu in the 2027 general elections to continue their people-oriented projects.

title: BRICS parliaments advocate for UN reform
body:
NEW DELHI, October 27. /TASS/. Parliamentarians from BRICS member countries are calling for comprehensive reform of the United Nations and its Security Council, according to a joint declaration issued following the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum.
"We emphasize the urgent need to reform the existing international peace and security architecture, which inevitably requires strengthening multilateralism. We advocate for comprehensive UN reform, including of the Security Council. This reform should make the UN more just, equitable, democratic, representative, effective, and efficient so that it better reflects contemporary realities and the needs of the international community," the document noted.
The parliaments of the BRICS countries reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening multilateralism and upholding international law, and pointed to the central role of the UN in the international system. According to the document, within such a system, sovereign states must cooperate to maintain international peace and security, promote sustainable development, and protect democracy, human rights, and fundamental freedoms for all.
A Russian parliamentary delegation led by State Duma Chairman Vyacheslav Volodin is currently in India participating in events at the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum. The event is being held in India's capital this year, as New Delhi currently holds the BRICS chairmanship. The main theme of the forum is "Fostering Parliaments for People-Centric Development.".

title: AI is ruining haunted houses
body:
In 2005, I launched two major projects. The first was Plagiarism Today, the site you're reading this on right now. The second was Bernie Baxter's Traveling Sideshow, a home haunted attraction I run with my partner, Crystal. Both projects are still going on to this day.



In many ways, the two projects are polar opposites to one another. Plagiarism Today is a digital‑first project that grew to become my full‑time job. Bernie Baxter is an almost purely meatspace project that is completely an avocation.



But that's what I love about haunting. It's a creative outlet that built with lumber, paint, and actors. Despite all the walkthrough videos on the internet, there really is no way to experience a haunted house digitally. It's an analog experience that truly does not have a digital equivalent. Haunts are a safe place to unplug and simply live in a truly unique moment.



So, imagine my disappointment when I walked up to my first haunted attraction of the year and was immediately greeted by low‑quality AI art. One of the images was so bad that it even included the Gemini diamond in the lower‑right corner of the page.



A photo taken from a local haunted attraction featuring the Gemini diamond logo



It shouldn't really come as a surprise. In an age of AI menus and AI event flyers, why wouldn't haunts use AI to generate their work? Why would haunted attractions be immune to the same pressures and temptations that other businesses face?



But somehow the betrayal feels even worse.



It's not just because of the love I have for the craft of haunting. It's because of what haunting has meant to me over the decades and why it's an important part of my life.



The AI Invasion Into Haunting







In many ways, the AI invasion into haunting is similar to how it has invaded other businesses. The most visible and noticeable use is generating AI flyers, posters and other marketing materials. The pushback against those flyers has been growing for years and many businesses have been going the other direction, back to hand-drawn promotional materials.



This might be easier to understand if it were just small haunted attractions and home haunts doing it. But that is not the case. Last year, Kennywood found itself in the middle of a controversy over its use of AI art to promote its new haunted attraction. Similarly, The Darkness in St. Louis has also faced heavy backlash over its use of AI in promotional materials.



However, AI art is especially dangerous for haunted attractions. For haunts, promotional materials are also meant to be indicative of what the experience will be like. AI art can, and often does, give a very misleading impression of what the haunted house will be like.



But it's not just the promotional materials. AI art has also seeped into the actual haunted houses themselves. AtmosFX, one of the largest providers of digital projections to the haunt industry, has admitted to using AI to create some of their characters. Haunts, like the one I went to, have also used AI to generate props and other items that are part of the attraction itself.



Finally, many haunts have been accused of selling AI-generated merchandise. That includes Knott's Berry Farm (also Knott's Scary Farm), which sold merchandise that they admitted to being at least partially generated by AI that featured a racist caricature. Fans of Queen Mary Dark Harbor have also complained about the use of AI in the development of their merchandise. Even Disney has been accused of selling AI-generated merchandise in a Haunted Mansion-themed store.



In short, AI is finding its way into every aspect of the haunted house experience. From the promotional materials to the attractions themselves to the merchandise booth afterward.



And I believe that haunting is worse for that. But that's not to say that there aren't ways technology can be used to improve the haunted house experience.



How Technology Can Improve Haunting



Despite its image of being an old‑fashioned industry, the haunted attraction industry is actually very technically savvy overall. Arduinos, Raspberry Pis and other microcontrollers have been used for decades to control prop activation, lighting, sound and other elements.



Haunts also make regular use of LCD screens, projectors and other digital displays as part of their attractions. Tech is also used behind the scenes for everything from designing the attraction to operating it. This is not an industry that has a history of shunning technology and is now racing to embrace AI.



The industry is making use of non-generative AI tools to improve those non‑customer‑facing aspects of the attraction. This includes using AI to time props, sounds, etc. Some have also begun to use such tools in the design phase as a tool to ensure that the haunt meets all the safety and accessibility requirements.



However, other haunts have used AI to draft backstories and character bibles for their actors to use. While this isn’t precisely customer‑facing, it does mean that the human actors are being instructed by AI rather than the other way around.



To be clear, I understand this temptation. Haunted attractions are often run by a handful of people who need to have a broad range of skills. Building, painting, decorating, acting, writing, graphic design, sound engineering, safety management, etc., are all skills haunts need; very few people will be able to do it all. The temptation to let AI backfill your shortcomings is understandable. But art is often most interesting when creators have to work around their limitations.



Nowhere is that more true than haunting. Haunters are constantly fighting against various limitations, including skill, money, time and other resources. That’s a big part of what makes each experience unique. By turning to AI to backfill any gaps, every experience begins to look and feel the same.



Bottom Line



When I go to a new restaurant and see an AI-generated menu, I'm disappointed. When I see an AI-generated flyer for an event, I'm annoyed and much less likely to go.



But with haunting, the betrayal feels different. Not only is this a field I've been involved in for decades, but the whole reason I love it is its creativity and the fact that it is a wholly physical experience. I love things like watching a haunter turn three empty soda bottles, a piece of PVC, and a rotating motor into a working prop.



Haunting is a unique form of artistic expression. It pushes you to find ways around your limitations. Best of all, it's got a great community that shares ideas and helps each other improve. With all that, using AI feels like a surrender. It feels like they aren't trying. While that can be said about any use of generative AI, especially for public‑facing materials, it's especially true here.



The good news is that most haunts seem to be keeping AI out of the haunt itself. The obvious exception to that is the new haunt "Terrors from the Antique Mall," which is put on by an AI company. Most haunts have been content to use AI for their promotional materials and their merchandise (with some using AI-generated props and art).



While that is somewhat positive, it does mean that the entire haunted attraction experience is bookended by AI. Literally the first and last things customers will see are AI-generated.



If this industry is going to survive, let alone thrive, it needs to be a unique experience. The quickest way to kill that is to be like everyone else. The most surefire way to do that is by using AI on public‑facing work.



If any industry should be celebrating originality and pushing to stand out in a sea of sameness, it's the haunted house industry.

title: Palau Prepares Frontline Workers to Detect Bird Flu in Wildlife and Livestock
body: By: Laurel Marewibuel KOROR, Palau – Palau is bringing together government agencies and regional experts this week to strengthen the country’s ability to prevent, detect and respond to highly pathogenic avian influenza, or HPAI, in wildlife. Bureau of Agriculture Director Jodean Remengesau said, “On 26-30 October 2026 at the Palau Royal Resort, the Bureau of Agriculture, Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and the Environment in partnership with the South Pacific Community (SPC) is convening a 5-day capacity building workshop on Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) in Wildlife. The workshop brings together local agency staff from Agriculture, Biosecurity, Environment, Public Health, and Animal Health sectors and hosts subject matter experts from the Australian Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry (DAFF) and Wildlife Health Australia.” Remengesau said, “The workshop also follows a 5-day training and examination week, concluding a four-month-long, mixed in-person and remote learning, Para-veterinarian professional training conducted by SPC and DAFF. Six staff collectively from the Bureau of Agriculture Livestock Division and Koror State Government Animal Shelter Clinic were certified by SPC and DAFF, and witnessed by the Australian Ambassador to Palau, Mr. Tony Sharpe, and BOA Director Ms. Jodean Remengesau.” She said, “The capacity building workshop comes at a critical point when Australia this year detected H5N1 in wild waterfowl, the greater crested tern. Wildlife, including migratory birds and mammals, may pose as carriers of the disease.” “As SPC Dr. Eric puts it, ‘disease threats do not respect borders’,” Remengesau said. She said, “Palauan households, in coping with the increased cost of living, increasingly interact with wildlife, including birds and mammals. Locals raise backyard chickens for fresh eggs, keep roosters or exotic wildlife for pets, and hunt, trade, and consume wild and exotic birds.” Remengesau said, “This particular strain of H5N1 can transmit from birds to cats and pigs, threatening the livestock sector as well.” She said, “By the end of the workshop, participants will have strengthened national capacity for early detection, surveillance, reporting and response to HPAI and other emerging animal diseases; enhanced understanding of wildlife health and the role of migratory birds in disease transmission; improved field competencies in surveillance, sampling, biosafety, and outbreak investigation; promoted collaboration between animal health, wildlife, environmental, biosecurity, and public health sectors through the One Health approach; and supported Palau’s efforts to strengthen national biosecurity systems and preparedness for disease incursions.” Remengesau said, “A prevention-focused action plan that binds and activates cross-sector collaboration through the One Health approach is a key anticipated outcome from the weeklong workshop.” The workshop is delivered under the SPC Pacific Regional Field Training Program for HPAI and Wildlife Health, a regional initiative supporting Pacific Island countries and territories to strengthen preparedness and resilience to emerging and transboundary animal diseases. The post Palau Prepares Frontline Workers to Detect Bird Flu in Wildlife and Livestock appeared first on Island Times News .

title: 27 October 2026
body: Armenia Armenia has published an updated list of its 1,000 largest taxpayers. Mobile Centre, which is involved in importing, selling, and re-exporting equipment such as phones and computers — mainly to Russia — topped the list. Today, Armenia marks the 27th anniversary of the terrorist attack on the parliament, in which Prime Minister Vazgen Sargsyan, Parliamentary Speaker Karen Demirchyan, and other public officials were killed. Over 100 civil society organisations are demanding the withdrawal of a package of legislative amendments to the civil code that limit local governments’ decision-making powers. Azerbaijan President Ilham Aliyev reaffirmed the country’s commitment to secularism in a speech at the 7th World Forum on Intercultural Dialogue in Baku. ‘Unfounded notions that anyone can dictate anything to us will continue to be met with our firm stance’, Aliyev said, in an apparent reference to Turkey’s criticism of Azerbaijan’s hijab ban in schools. Yesterday, Turkish police detained Muhammed Emin Yıldırım, an outspoken critic of Azerbaijan’s hijab ban, only to release him today. Yıldırım, who works with Köklü Değişim Medya , was detained by police in Istanbul on Monday. Georgia Giorgi Pataridze, the head of Special Penitentiary Service, has resigned amid continued controversies surrounding the prison system. The resignation came after the Prosecutor General’s Office recommended the Justice Ministry suspend Giorgi Pataridze in connection with an investigation into the alleged beating of inmate Davit Peikrishvili. Ramaz Tatarashvili has been appointed head of the Special Penitentiary Service. The delegation will study Georgia’s phytosanitary certification system for pome and stone fruits, the agency announced . Students and parents of Tbilisi’s Public School No 10 held a protest yesterday, blocking Dadiani Street. They are demanding the timely completion of the school’s new building, which is under construction. The school was demolished several years ago. Since then, students have had to attend classes in other school buildings or study remotely. Shalva Kereselidze, an MP representing the opposition For Georgia party, said they would give up their parliamentary mandates if the Constitutional Court banned the party. He said that if the Constitutional Court banned his party, parliamentary mandates would have no value or power. Abkhazia Abkhazia will introduce the concept of an ‘undesirable foreign citizen’, said Said Tsvinaria, head of the Migration Service. An official decision is planned to declare people ‘who have been convicted and are serving prison sentences’ undesirable, with a ban on entering the republic. Abkhazia’s cabinet has approved a draft republican budget for 2027, with budget revenues being expected to total ₽16.4 billion ($180 million). This includes ₽5.2 billion ($64 million) in financial assistance from Russia, ₽904 million ($12 million) from the 2026–2028 Investment Programme, and ₽225 million ($2.8 million) in funding for the 2026–2028 state programme supporting economic sectors. South Ossetia Judoka Tamerlan Tmenov has been appointed Sports Minister. He is an Olympic silver and bronze medallist. The North Caucasus North Ossetian Head Sergei Menyailo has ordered the lifting of petrol sales restrictions in the republic, which were introduced amid a fuel crisis in Russia caused by Ukrainian strikes on oil refineries. The restrictions were introduced in late July and allowed local residents to buy up to 40 litres of petrol, while drivers from other regions were limited to 20 litres. Zamid Chalaev, commander of the special police regiment of Chechnya’s Interior Ministry, has urged residents of the republic to report people involved in bombings. He has offered a reward of $100,000 for information on potential suspects. Ingushetia has the lowest average salary in Russia, at ₽42,700 ($470), according to data from Rosstat, Russia’s statistics agency. However, residents commenting on the figures have said that in practice, many people earn two to three times less. A conflict between two residents of Sunzha district in the village of Alkhasy, Ingushetia, ended in one person dying. Three other people were injured in the fight, in which all participants were reported to be related. title: US Secretary of War in trouble. Big shake-up at the Pentagon?
body:
House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries has announced actions to remove Pete Hegseth from the position of US Secretary of Defence if his party regains the majority after the November elections. A motion for the impeachment of the Pentagon chief has already been filed by Republican Congressman Thomas Massie. Simultaneously, Democrats are demanding explanations regarding the restriction of Ukraine’s access to the Starshield system.
In an interview with MS NOW, Jeffries called on Donald Trump to dismiss Hegseth. He announced that if the President fails to do so, the Democrats will address the matter after regaining control of the House of Representatives. He accused the Secretary of Defence of a lack of qualifications and reminded him that he had already demanded his resignation in the spring of 2025.
As noted by The Hill , Jeffries has not yet explicitly declared whether he will support the impeachment motion. According to the portal, the vote is set to take place after Congressmen return to Washington in November.
The initiative in this matter also came from within Republican ranks. On 15 September, Thomas Massie presented eight charges against Hegseth. These concern, among others, conducting warfare against Iran without the required Congressional approval, ignoring restrictions stemming from War Powers regulations, and violating rules regarding the protection of civilians. In the Congressman’s assessment, the Secretary of Defence’s actions violate the constitutional powers of Congress and require him to be held accountable.
A separate issue concerns Ukraine. Democratic Senator Adam Schiff, speaking on NBC’s Sunday programme „Meet the Press”, called for Hegseth, Elon Musk, and others with knowledge of the Starshield bandwidth restrictions — SpaceX’s satellite communication system used by the Ukrainian military — to be questioned under oath.
Schiff pointed to contradictions in public explanations and demanded to determine who was responsible for the restrictions and what impact they had on the military capabilities of the Ukrainian armed forces.

title: Most of Konotop without power for fourth day after Russian Strikes; water supplied on schedule
body:
According to Ukrinform, Konotop Mayor Artem Semenikhin reported this on Telegram.
“Unfortunately, there is no forecast for when power will be restored. No forecast at all,” he wrote.
The previous day, Semenikhin said in an interview with Suspilne that most of the city remained without electricity.
“Educational institutions have been damaged, and even our hospital is currently running on generators. It was a treacherous strike on civilian infrastructure in the middle of the night. We have opened Points of Invincibility. Water is being supplied according to a schedule: from 6:00 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. and from 6:00 p.m. to 9:00 p.m.,” the mayor said.

title: Data centers are a hot-button issue for Ohioans as midterms near
body:
In Ohio, many people are displeased with the state's rapid buildout of data centers. It's a hot-button issue in the midterms, as political candidates from both parties try to ease voter concerns.
MICHEL MARTIN, HOST: Back here in the U.S., Ohio has seen some of the fastest data center growth in the country and some of the fiercest backlash. NPR's Andrea Hsu reports on how the hot-button issue cuts across party lines. UNIDENTIFIED PERSON #1: Can you say, trick or treat? ANDREA HSU, BYLINE: Halloween has come early in the Cincinnati suburb of Fairfield. Pint-sized pirates and princesses weave their way through booths set up by local businesses and churches and other groups. UNIDENTIFIED PERSON #1: You get a prize, and you get a piece of candy. HSU: At this booth, there's something for the grown-ups too. LINDA MOODIE: Do you have any interest in signing a petition while you're here? UNIDENTIFIED PERSON #2: What is it for? MOODIE: To ban large-scale data centers in the state. HSU: That's Linda Moodie with Conserve Ohio. The all-volunteer group has been working to stop the development of huge data centers - the kind used to power AI. They're behind ballot initiatives in 10 communities this fall, and they're still collecting signatures for a statewide ban they hope to get on the ballot in 2027. It's an effort many are happy to back. UNIDENTIFIED PERSON #2: Yeah. Yeah, yeah, yeah. MOODIE: Awesome. Are you a registered voter? HSU: More than a decade ago, tech companies came to Ohio, drawn by the state's inexpensive and abundant land, its energy infrastructure and its generous tax breaks. Like many parents in this crowd, Kyler Osterberger is now worried about the impact the data center boom is having. KYLER OSTERBERGER: Just, like, the resources, electricity, rising costs. HSU: Others fear the pollution new power plants will bring. Linda Moodie is wary about data centers further enabling AI. MOODIE: We don't necessarily trust that the government's going do the right thing. HSU: Whoever gets elected? MOODIE: Yeah. Absolutely. HSU: Data centers have figured prominently in the tight race for a U.S. Senate seat in Ohio. Both candidates are calling for greater accountability, but neither has gone as far as to back a moratorium. The Democrat, former Senator Sherrod Brown, has cast his opponent, current Republican Senator Jon Husted, as the face of data centers. Back when Husted was lieutenant governor, he did champion investments in them. Now Brown's running ads featuring disgruntled Ohioans. (SOUNDBITE OF ARCHIVED RECORDING) UNIDENTIFIED PERSON #3: Even today Husted wants to build more data centers. UNIDENTIFIED PERSON #4: No matter how much water they use. UNIDENTIFIED PERSON #3: Or how much they cost. HSU: For his part, Husted has called Brown hypocritical, pointing to his past support for data centers. And Husted's has been pushing a bill in Washington aimed at getting data centers to pay for things like upgrades to the power grid. (SOUNDBITE OF ARCHIVED RECORDING) JON HUSTED: The Ratepayer Protection Act rests on a principle every American understands - pay your own way. HSU: But to Nick Owens, the problem goes far beyond who's footing the bill. Owens is one of the founders of that grassroots group, Conserve Ohio. I meet him in the village of Mount Orab, an hour east of Cincinnati. We drive through a neighborhood of beautiful homes on big, grassy lots. NICK OWENS: This is the Ohio that people brag about. This is the Ohio people love. HSU: At the end of a block, there's a huge field - part of 1,000 acres that have been sold to a data center developer. There's corn right here, so this is farmland. OWENS: Yeah. I mean, literally, we are feet from the data center property and where you will have the constant hum, noise, pollution, whatever - I mean, literally from these people's backyards, front yards. You know, people don't deserve to live this way. HSU: He says, why not build data centers on old industrial sites instead? OWENS: If we're going to have data centers, those are the prime places. HSU: Owens is an attorney and a lifelong Republican, a former Trump delegate. He won't say how he's voting this fall. But he says the data center issue, along with $6 diesel, is dampening enthusiasm for Republicans. He didn't appreciate Trump's warning that communities that oppose data centers will lose out. OWENS: When, you know, the president says, well, you'll just be poor and backwards, no. I want our regular way of life. HSU: Construction at the site hasn't begun yet. It's not clear when it will. Owen says, because of nondisclosure agreements, people who live here know nothing. For now, all you hear is birds. Andrea Hsu, NPR News in Mount Orab, Ohio. (SOUNDBITE OF SONG, "OHIO!
