title: Ekiti Kingmakers Seek Ooni’s Intervention over in Alara Stool
body: Fidelis David in Akure The kingmakers of Aramoko-Ekiti, Ekiti State, yesterday appealed to the Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Enitan Ogunwusi, to intervene in the protracted process of selecting a new Alara of Aramoko-Ekiti, which they said had remained suspended for six months. The kingmakers, under the Alara-in-Council, urged the Ooni to prevail on Governor Biodun Oyebanji to allow them to reconvene and conclude the selection process, warning that the prolonged vacancy was affecting traditional activities and generating restiveness among youths in the community. In a statement signed by the Head of kingmakers, Julius Oladiran Adebayo, and the Secretary, Kolade Oyebade, also known as Sajowa, the council said the intervention of the foremost Yoruba traditional ruler would help protect the community’s cultural heritage and chieftaincy traditions. The kingmakers said the selection process began in April 2026 in accordance with the Alara of Aramoko Chieftaincy Declaration and the Ekiti State Chieftaincy Law. According to the statement, three princes were shortlisted through Ifa divination conducted by Baba Araba Elebuibon, after which voting by the 12 kingmakers ended in a tie, with six votes each. The council said a second round of voting was expected to resolve the deadlock but alleged that the process was suspended by the state Commissioner for Chieftaincy Affairs, leaving the community without a new traditional ruler six months after the exercise began. “However, six months later, the process remains suspended after the Honourable Commissioner for Chieftaincy Affairs postponed it. Our letters to the government have not received a response,” the kingmakers said. Appealing directly to the Ooni, the council described Aramoko-Ekiti as a community with deep historical and cultural ties to Ile-Ife, the ancestral home of the Yoruba people. “As a town founded by descendants of Oduduwa, Aramoko-Ekiti shares an unbroken cultural and spiritual bond with Ile-Ife. Our customs, our crown, and our chieftaincy rites all emanate from Ife,” the statement said. The kingmakers added that the Alara stool was more than a local traditional institution, describing it as part of the wider Yoruba cultural heritage under the spiritual and cultural influence of the Ooni. “Kabiyesi, we are constrained to run to you as our father and the custodian of Yoruba culture. The stool of Alara remains vacant. Our youths are restive. Our traditional festivals and rites cannot hold,” they said. They urged the Ooni to use his influence to persuade Governor Oyebanji to authorise the immediate resumption of the selection process and enable the kingmakers to complete their assignment in accordance with the law. “We therefore beg Kabiyesi Onirisa to please use your revered office to appeal to Governor Oyebanji to kindly grant permission for the kingmakers to reconvene immediately and complete the selection,” the statement added. The council expressed confidence that the intervention would lead to a peaceful resolution, while appealing to the governor to respect the applicable laws and traditions governing the selection of the new Alara.

title: Iraqi court sentences seven French ISIS members to prison
body: An Iraqi court on Tuesday sentenced seven French ISIS members to prison, in the first verdicts of a trial involving 47 of the country's citizens transferred from Syria , handing down sentences under terrorism laws. The court sentenced six people to 20 years in prison and one was jailed for 15 years. Judge Mohammed Salman, of the Karkh Criminal Court, read out the verdicts one after another. "The court found that the evidence is sufficient to convict you,” he told each defendant. “The charge carries the death penalty, but because you are a young man at the beginning of your life, I have decided to give you a chance to reform yourself and change the course of your life." They joined ISIS during its rule of vast areas of Iraq and Syria. The group held territory from mid-2014 until its defeat in Iraq in 2017 and Syria in 2019. The men were also convicted of participating in terrorist acts threatening public peace and security and endangering people's lives. The judge said the verdicts could be appealed within 30 days. Among those convicted was Mehdi Mohammed, 33, a French citizen of Algerian origin. At his hearing on October 5, he admitted joining ISIS, but said he had been lured on social media during Syria's civil war and pleaded for mercy. Appearing in a yellow prison jumpsuit with his head shaved and hands clasped behind his back, he told the court that as a student in France in 2013 he was troubled by the conflict in Syria. After meeting a man known as Abu Mohammed Al Faransi online, he travelled to Algeria for six months, then in late 2013 flew to Turkey and crossed into Syria with smugglers. "He convinced me to come to Syria and to join the revolution to support them because they are Muslims," Mohammed told the judge. "It was never my intention to join the Islamic State. I was convinced that we, as Muslims, should help the Syrians. I was deceived." The judge appointed him a defence lawyer. The trials began in Baghdad in late September and exposed Europe's unresolved dilemma over what to do with its citizens who joined ISIS. With no international tribunal in place and European countries reluctant to repatriate them, Iraq has become the de facto courtroom for foreign fighters. In a transfer operation between January and February this year, the US military moved 5,704 suspected ISIS detainees to Iraq by plane and bus. Iraq's Supreme Judicial Council said the detainees comprised 67 nationalities and included 474 Iraqis and 3,497 Syrians. They will also be tried in Baghdad. ISIS swept across Syria and Iraq in 2014. Iraq, backed by US-led forces, declared victory over the group in 2017, while the Syrian Democratic Forces defeated ISIS two years later. Iraq has tried thousands of its own citizens accused of joining ISIS. The trials are based on the country's sweeping anti-terrorism law, which carries the death penalty for belonging to a terrorist group. Foreign citizens have faced the same fate, a policy that rights groups have criticised but that Baghdad defends as a matter of sovereignty and deterrence. In 2019, several French citizens transferred from Syria were sentenced to death in Baghdad before their sentences were commuted to life in jail.

title: KOROR: UDUI, KEWII, AND WASAI ATTENDS JICA KCCP TRAINING
body: Jack Udui Jr. of Palau Energy & Water Administration, Keyslee Kewii and Sherwin Wasai of Palau Public Utilities Cooperation are attending JICA’s Knowledge Co-Creation Progam, Energy Transition in PICs PJ – 3 rd Program in Japan (Grid stabilization measures for the expansion of renewable energy). JICA’s Technical Cooperation, Energy Transition in Pacific Island Countries Project, aims to promote energy transition and contribute to the decarbonization of the energy sector in the five target countries through capacity building in power generation planning, grid planning, and demand-side measures. This course, which is one of the components of the project, aims to foster a deeper understanding through site visits and lectures on Japan’s energy transition initiatives. This is the 3 rd course provided by the project primarily focusing on “Grid stabilization measures for the expansion of renewable energy,” while also providing a wide range of learning opportunities. This course is scheduled from October 14 to 31, 2026 in Okinawa, Japan. The post KOROR: UDUI, KEWII, AND WASAI ATTENDS JICA KCCP TRAINING appeared first on Island Times News .

title: Moscow to Restrict Mobile Internet for 3 Days During Putin’s Summits
body:
Russian authorities will restrict mobile internet access within Moscow’s Third Ring Road from Tuesday, Oct. 27 to Tuesday, Oct. 29, citing security concerns during two international events attended by President Vladimir Putin, Russia’s Ministry of Digital Development announced .
The restrictions coincide with the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) on Tuesday and the Russia-Africa summit on Wednesday, Oct. 28, to Thursday, Oct. 29.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Mobile internet will be unavailable from 11:30 a.m. Moscow time on Tuesday and Wednesday, and from 9:30 a.m. on Thursday, the ministry said. Access will be limited to services on an approved “whitelist,” while voice calls, home internet, and Wi-Fi will remain available.
Russian authorities have previously justified mobile internet shutdowns as a measure to counter Ukrainian drone attacks. Ukraine has intensified its strikes on the Moscow region since the fall.
One of the largest recent attacks occurred on Oct. 23 , disrupting air traffic at all four airports serving Moscow. Authorities also evacuated a skyscraper in Moscow City that houses offices of several Russian government agencies, including the Digital Development Ministry.
The GECF forum will take place at Moscow’s World Trade Center, with Putin scheduled to deliver the opening address at 12:45 p.m. Six of the organization’s 12 member countries will be represented at the highest level, Putin’s aide Yuri Ushakov said .
Attendees include the presidents of Iran and Equatorial Guinea, the emir of Qatar and the head of Libya’s Presidential Council. Venezuela’s acting president, Delcy Rodriguez, will join by video link.
The Russia-Africa summit will bring delegations from 48 of Africa’s 54 countries to Moscow, Ushakov said. Twenty-two countries will be represented by their heads of state. Putin is expected to hold more than 20 bilateral meetings during the summit, according to Vedomosti .
Mobile internet outages have previously affected Moscow for extended periods. In March, mobile internet in the city center was unavailable for more than two weeks, with Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov citing the need to ensure security.

title: Kyiv introduces detour routes for freight, passenger transport over Pivdennyi Bridge closure – police
body:
In connection with the closure of the Pivdenny Bridge in Kyiv, freight and passenger vehicle traffic has been temporarily organized along detour routes, reported Head of the Patrol Police Department Oleksiy Biloshytskiy on Telegram.

According to him, freight transport from the Boryspil highway is being directed to Staroboryspilska Street, and further along Boryspilska and Pryvokzalna Streets toward the Darnytsky Bridge.

Passenger cars are recommended to bypass the closed section via Mykoly Bazhana Avenue to the Dniprovska Embankment toward the Darnytsky Bridge and Paton Bridge.

As reported earlier, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko informed that an enemy attack struck the capital's Pivdenny Bridge, damaging metro infrastructure located on it.

title: U S Air Force s First Air-Launched Hypersonic Missile Enters Production
body:
The U.S. Department of the Air Force awarded Lockheed Martin a $694 million contract on September 29 to produce and field the AGM-183A Air-Launched Rapid Response Weapon (ARRW). Awarded under the Department of War’s Enterprise-Wide Agile Acquisition Contract, the deal marks the program’s transition from prototyping and flight testing to production.
Developed for the U.S. Air Force, ARRW is a long-range, non-nuclear hypersonic boost-glide missile designed to strike high-value, hardened land targets and surface combatants. It uses a solid-fuel rocket booster to accelerate beyond Mach 5 before releasing an unpowered hypersonic glide vehicle. The vehicle travels at high speed and can maneuver during flight, potentially complicating interception by advanced air-defense and missile-defense systems.
With a reported range of approximately 1,000 miles (1,600 km), the weapon is intended to engage time-sensitive, heavily defended targets from standoff distances, allowing launch aircraft to remain farther from hostile air defenses. The missile is approximately 22 feet long and weighs about 6,600 pounds. Its destructive effect relies substantially on kinetic energy generated at high speed.
The program previously faced flight-test failures that prompted the Air Force to consider cancellation. The new contract marks a reversal in its trajectory, although production approval does not itself confirm full operational deployment or large-scale availability.
The Air Force has tested ARRW using the B-52H Stratofortress bomber. Operational integration and deployment plans remain subject to further developments. Production quantities and delivery dates have not been disclosed for operational-security reasons.
Hypersonic weapons travel faster than Mach 5, but their military significance also depends on maneuverability, flight profile, guidance and their ability to evade interception.

title: Yei leaders demand better healthcare amid drug shortages
body: Health authorities, religious leaders and community representatives in Central Equatoria State’s Yei River County have demanded improved healthcare services, citing shortages of essential medicines, specialist doctors and medical supplies. The appeal was made on Saturday during a thanksgiving prayer and the reopening of the renovated County Health Department office in Yei. Anglican Bishop Emeritus Hillary Luate urged authorities to strengthen healthcare delivery, saying improved services are essential to raising living standards amid the county’s difficult conditions. “There are shortages of medicines; if you are sick, sometimes you are referred to buy. You find a woman who does not have anything; these are the things that are happening among us. We are calling for God’s protection, and let us begin to improve the services even if the situation is not good,” he said. “It makes us feel safe when our women and kids are delivered safely, where everybody can get the service which will make them very happy.” “If the medical services in yei can make me confident that my family and I can get treatment, get well and continue with life, then it is good,” Bishop Luate said. Representing the Gender Department, Acting Director Ajania Amude called for equal access to reproductive health services for women and girls. She also stressed the need for greater public awareness to prevent gender-based violence. “Ensure that no women and girls are left behind in the county because some of them have special needs,” she said. “It is the department of health to raise awareness on reproductive health, prevention of gender-based violence, and the importance of antenatal care.” Meanwhile, Simon Sebit Musoga, County Health Director, reaffirmed his department’s commitment to improving healthcare services and strengthening health facilities across the county’s five payams. “As we open this office, we renew our commitment to improving access to quality health services in the county,” he stated. “Our priorities include strengthening primary health care services, supporting health facilities and health workers, improving maternal and child health programs, promoting immunization, enhancing disease surveillance, and ensuring that communities receive accurate health information.” “I call upon all stakeholders to remain committed to our shared responsibility to ensure that every action in Yei River County leads to access to essential and quality health care services,” Sebit added. For his part, Emmanuel Taban Seme, caretaker commissioner of Yei River County, appealed to the Central Equatoria State Ministry of Health to ensure timely delivery of medicines to health facilities, warning that delays could lead to drugs expiring before they are used. “It is not right for donors and partners to bring medicines, keep them in the store for a long time, and then they reach us when they are left with a few months before expiring,” he said. “So I want to send my message from the people of Yei through the state health ministry that when the medicines are there, let the consignments be delivered early.” The post Yei leaders demand better healthcare amid drug shortages appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: If the Burnham bounce survives the budget, an early election could be on the cards
body: There is a lot more at stake than trying to boost the public purse in the UK’s budget statement. Westminster is increasingly convinced that, should Labour maintain its lead in the polls after John Healey delivers his autumn budget, Andy Burnham will call a general election. In theory, he does not need to do so until 2029, but a Prime Minister who was not elected on a popular mandate is anxious to get on and stamp his own mark, and this may be the best moment to strike. No one knows what the future holds, but the omens for the UK and its economy are not good. The country is heading into winter with a health service already stretched, household energy prices due to rise in January because of the Iran war, inflation creeping upwards and interest rates, and therefore the cost of borrowing, likely to climb. The trade unions are flexing their muscles and making noises about seeking pay increases for their members, which always presents a Labour, union-supporting PM with a dilemma. Better to press the button and force an election sooner rather than later. Certainly, the clues are stacking up. The Lib Dems are said to have tried to source plastic placards, only to be refused because the Labour Party had placed a large order. In the City, the bets are piling in on an earlier date, and despite not being at the heart of political decision-making, the speculators have an uncanny habit of reading the runes correctly. What they are scrutinising is the opinion polling. Currently, Ipsos puts Labour eight points ahead of the Tories, on 32 per cent. A poll tracker has Labour averaging 29 per cent, the Tories 23 per cent and Reform 21 per cent. It was reported in August that a senior Labour strategist had said they would push for a general election if there was "a steady five-to-eight-point lead". Other factors. The Tories are enjoying something of a resurgence under Kemi Badenoch. Admittedly they start from a low base – they were almost wiped out by Keir Starmer last time – but there is no doubt they’ve rediscovered their mojo. In particular, they see London and the south of England as areas where they can make inroads. They are on natural turf, and the longer Mr Burnham pushes the north at the expense of the south - an inevitable consequence of championing his own region due to the absence of an unlimited amount of cash, and the consequent fact that something must give – the more southerners will turn against him. Should that lavishing on the north be accompanied by tax reforms that those in the south feel are aimed at them, then the Tories could be on a roll. Mr Burnham is determined to make a fist of establishing closer relations with the EU, and possibly even seeking full readmission. It won’t be lost on him or his advisers that while rapprochement makes perfect sense economically, it could come at the cost of forfeiting Labour seats that were pro-Brexit. The MPs in those constituencies are already raising the alarm, saying he risks providing a fillip to Reform. He may regard a national poll, in which EU re-entry is to the fore, as negating the need for another referendum on the issue. As a way of avoiding a repeat of the scarring Brexit battle, that thinking has merit. Whether it is acceptable to EU leaders who will want proof that the UK's change of attitude is for real and is sustainable, is not clear. But a healthy majority, based in part on stronger EU ties, would provide Mr Burnham with the safety blanket to pursue talks with Brussels. The EU featured heavily in Mr Burnham’s Labour conference speech. It was his set-piece that has sent Westminster into overdrive. Yes, prior to the party gathering, he made a point of ruling out an early election. However, he then went on to set out his vision for the UK, not for the year ahead but far into the future. Indeed, it was noticeable he paid such little attention to the present, barely touching on current domestic and foreign issues. It was, in all but name, Labour’s next manifesto. Almost everything he announced, from greater devolution to reconnecting with the EU to a new National Care Service, was not for today or the coming months. All of them will take years to finesse and process. It was obvious too that this is where his interest really lies. Sure, as Prime Minister he is obliged to deal with the day-to-day, but as someone who dreamt long and hard about moving into 10 Downing Street, there was no mistaking his motivation and focus. There are caveats against an early poll. Labour has not been performing well in Scotland, although the decision to approve exploitation of the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea was favourably received there. Whether he gives the nod to extracting oil from the Rosebank field remains to be seen, but that would also lift his party’s Scottish prospects. Another was that Mr Starmer’s surprise landslide will not be repeated and Labour is bound to lose MPs, regardless of how the government and economy are performing. The scale of Mr Starmer’s triumph was seen as a one-off, and there would be casualties. They were thought to be holding Mr Burnham back – while he might win, his majority would be lower than his predecessor’s, so weakening his authority. The feeling in Mr Burnham's camp is that his personal rating is high . They’ve been taken aback by just how well he has gone down, aided by a non-stop flow of TikTok videos and the belief his "man of the people" style is succeeding. There may be some losses, but they are to be expected, given the scale of Mr Starmer’s victory and the Tory capitulation. Mr Burnham would most probably achieve the mandate he seeks. There is one more thought weighing heavily, which is the old Harold Macmillan quote of "events, dear boy, events" when asked for the greatest challenge facing a statesman. So far, Mr Burnham has made some missteps, but nothing serious. Crucially, he managed to handle Donald Trump successfully – as did Mr Starmer at first, only for the US President to turn and undermine him. Best to go now rather than delay. Seared on Labour minds, too, is the example of Gordon Brown, who, like Mr Burnham, became prime minister without a general election. Mr Brown was also doing well in the polls, but instead of calling an election he procrastinated. By the time he did flick the switch, it was too late, and he lost. As for Mr Burnham ruling out an early election on the eve of the conference: well, politicians can always U-turn, can’t they? So Mr Healey may well be presaging the next UK general election as he outlines his spending and revenue-raising plans.

title: Hesburger's first Italian restaurant opens doors in Matera
body:
With the opening of an Italian outlet, the Finnish fast food chain now operates in 10 different countries across Europe.
Finnish fast food chain Hesburger has opened its first ever outlet in Italy.
The restaurant in the city of Matera, in the Basilicata region of southern Italy, officially began welcoming customers on Friday 23 October.
With the opening of the outlet in Matera coming in the wake of similar recent expansions into the Romanian and Polish markets, Hesburger now operates in 10 different countries across Europe.
In a press release, the firm said that the move will create 20 new jobs in the city.
The statement also noted the influential role Italian entrepreneur Venanzia Rizzi , who is originally from Matera but has lived in Finland for a long time, had in bringing the Finnish chain to Italy.
"Matera is my hometown and Finland is my second home country. That's why it's especially wonderful to connect these two important places to me through entrepreneurship," Rizzi said.
Hesburger's statement further added that its arrival in Matera — a city known for its strong food culture — has drawn both "positive and cautious reactions".
"The feedback we've received directly has been positive, and we're happy that our brand is generating interest. Above all, we want to earn the trust of local customers through quality products, friendly service, and a positive customer experience," noted Ieva Salmela , Hesburger's Director of Communications and International Marketing.
When Hesburger's plans were first revealed in September, Italian newspaper La Repubblica reported that some locals were not pleased by the arrival of another fast food chain in their city, coming just months after a similar expansion by McDonald's.
Yle News reporter Ronan Browne explains the cultural and historical context behind Hesburger's expansion into Italy.

title: Kuwait sentences three to death over Iran links and plot to assassinate deputy PM
body: Kuwait has sentenced three men to death for plotting to assassinate the deputy prime minister, collaborating with Iran and joining Hezbollah. The Kuwaiti Criminal Court also sentenced eight others to five years in prison with hard labour, local media reported on Monday. The three men were convicted of harming Kuwait ’s national interests, spying for Iran, plotting to assassinate First Deputy Prime Minister and Interior Minister Sheikh Fahad Yousef Saud Al Sabah , and joining the Lebanese militant group Hezbollah, according to the court’s ruling. The court said directing a group inside Kuwait to assassinate the official responsible for internal security on the instructions of a foreign entity constituted a hostile act against the state. Such an act sought to undermine national security, spread unrest and erode public confidence in the authorities’ ability to protect lives and property, it said. The court added that national security was a right belonging to society as a whole and stressed that Kuwait’s sovereignty could not be challenged by foreign powers or their directives. In August, Kuwait 's security services foiled a terrorist plot aimed at vital infrastructure in the Gulf country and arrested a suspect linked to ISIS before he could carry out an attack. Gulf states have faced security challenges this year amid attacks by Iran and domestic plots in sympathy with the Iranian regime. In March this year, Kuwait arrested dozens of people accused of links to the Lebanese militant group Hezbollah . The Ministry of Interior said six people had confessed to espionage and terrorist activities, including training in "assassination skills". Five were Kuwaiti citizens. It said 14 other suspects, including Kuwaitis, Lebanese and Iranians, had been identified outside the country. In a separate case, authorities detained 14 Kuwaitis and two Lebanese citizens affiliated with the Iran-backed group over a “sabotage plot” in the Gulf nation.

title: Exail introduces Marins M1 INS for small and uncrewed naval platforms
body:
Exail has unveiled the Marins M1, a compact inertial navigation system (INS) designed for smaller naval platforms.
As informed, the INS is intended for RHIBs, fast interception craft, patrol boats, uncrewed surface vessels (USVs) and uncrewed underwater vehicles (UUVs). With Marins M1, Exail extends military-grade inertial navigation to platforms where size, integration and cost are key considerations, according to the company.
Forces are operating a more diverse mix of major combatants, tactical craft and autonomous systems. As smaller and uncrewed platforms take on demanding missions, they need navigation that remains accurate and reliable when GNSS is degraded or unavailable. Their tighter SWaP-C (size, weight, power and cost) constraints make the integration of high-performance inertial navigation particularly demanding.
Marins M1 was developed to address these requirements. Built on fiber optic gyroscope (FOG) technology, it provides the accuracy and stability required to navigate reliably in GNSS-denied environments, Exail noted. It delivers accurate position, heading, roll and pitch data, with a maximum position drift of 1 nautical mile after 3 hours without any external aiding. Combining a compact architecture with a more accessible price point, Marins M1 delivers this level of inertial performance in a solution tailored to smaller platforms.
“A RHIB or a USV operating without GNSS faces the same navigation challenge as a larger vessel, with far less room to address it. With Marins M1, we are making very high-performance FOG navigation accessible to these platforms in a system designed around their constraints," said Madeleine Laguarigue de Survilliers , Naval Navigation Product Manager at Exail.
To remind, Exail recenrly secured a contract to supply its Marins military-grade inertial navigation systems for USVs from an undisclosed navy.

title: Gov’t pays 52,000 teachers’ promotion arrears, 28,000 pending
body: The government has paid the promotion salary arrears of 52,000 teachers, with payments for the remaining 28,000 still outstanding, the Education Minister, Haruna Iddrisu, has disclosed. The Minister said the 52,000 teachers had successfully completed the validation process, out of about 80,000 who were demanding payment of their promotion arrears. On Joy FM’s Super Morning Show on Tuesday, October 27, Mr Iddrisu urged the remaining teachers not to embark on another strike, assuring them that steps were being taken to resolve their concerns. “The 52,000 promotion arrears on the new grade were honoured by the government and paid by the government by October 16. What is outstanding is around 28,000, which includes some non-teachers; they may not be able to get payment because the validation process has not been completed,” he explained. He said his office would meet with the teacher union leadership by the end of Tuesday to discuss the outstanding payments. “I am compelled to invite the teacher unions to an emergency meeting this morning. I have reached out to them.” According to him, the government is working to ensure the remaining teachers receive their arrears by the end of November. He added that an alternative option would be to provide a supplementary allocation for October to facilitate the payments. “Not all of them may get their October salary; we may have to do another supplementary payment or push it to November,” the Minister noted. The disclosure follows the suspension of industrial action by teachers over delays in the payment of their promotion salary arrears.

title: The Overlooked Coral Reef Network: Scientists Say Atolls Deserve Greater Conservation Attention
body: A new international study suggests that atolls, the ring-shaped coral reef ecosystems scattered across the Pacific and Indian oceans, represent one of the world’s largest coral reef networks yet remain underrecognized in global conservation planning. Published in Frontiers in Marine Science , the study found that 309 Indo-Pacific atolls contain more than 27,000 square kilometers of mapped shallow coral reef habitat, accounting for 41.5% of all mapped reef areas surrounding Indo-Pacific islands and nearly 8% of the world’s mapped shallow reefscape. Collectively, atoll reefs occupy nearly as much area as Australia’s Great Barrier Reef. The findings challenge the perception of atolls as isolated or peripheral coral reef systems and suggest they should be more explicitly incorporated into coral conservation strategies. “Atolls are often discussed as small, vulnerable islands, but when we look at the reefs associated with them collectively, they emerge as one of the planet’s major coral reef systems,” said Alex Wegmann , lead author of the study and Lead Scientist for Island Resilience with The Nature Conservancy. “If we want coral reef conservation to reflect the full diversity and scale of the world’s reefs and address the associated challenges, atolls need to be part of that conversation.” The study brings together atoll scientists, conservation practitioners, and community leaders from across the Pacific, Indian Ocean, North America, and Europe. Using a curated database of Indo-Pacific atolls and high-resolution reef mapping from the Allen Coral Atlas and the Interactive Data Portal for Indo-Pacific Atolls , researchers quantified the extent of reef habitat associated with atoll ecosystems and compared it to other globally recognized reef regions. Researchers say the findings are particularly relevant as coral reefs worldwide face increasing pressure from climate change. For decades, atolls have frequently been portrayed as ecosystems destined to disappear beneath rising seas. However, a growing body of research shows that healthy atolls are dynamic systems whose futures depend on the condition of the coral reefs that support them. Intact atoll reefs generate sediment, support island formation, sustain fisheries, and maintain ecological connections between land and sea. “Too often, atolls are framed as doomed landscapes rather than living reef systems with remarkable ecological complexity,” said Sebastian Steibl , atoll scientist from the University of Auckland and co-author of the study. “The science increasingly shows that these systems are dynamic, resilient in important ways, and worthy of far greater attention from the conservation community.” The authors also point to emerging evidence that some atoll reefs may harbor coral communities with elevated heat tolerance, potentially making them important sources of climate-resilient corals in a warming ocean. Research from places such as Palmyra Atoll has documented reef habitats that experienced widespread bleaching during marine heat waves but relatively limited coral mortality. “Atolls offer a unique opportunity to understand how coral reefs can persist under climate stress,” said Hannah Stewart , co-author and coral conservation scientist. “Protecting these systems is not only important for the communities and biodiversity they support today, but also for the lessons they may provide about the future of coral reefs globally.” The study also highlights a challenge unique to atolls: while they collectively form a reef network of global significance, they are spread across dozens of jurisdictions and many small island nations. That geographic dispersion can make them less visible in conservation agendas than large, centrally managed reef systems. For many Pacific and Indian Ocean communities, however, atolls are far more than reef habitats. They are homes, sources of food security, cultural landscapes, and foundations of local economies. “People who live on atolls have long understood the connection between healthy reefs, healthy islands, and healthy communities,” said Dolores deBrum Kattil , co-author and Executive Director of the Marshall Islands Conservation Society. “Recognizing the global importance of atoll reefs should go hand in hand with supporting the communities that depend on them.” The authors emphasize that elevating atolls in coral reef conservation does not mean shifting attention away from places like the Great Barrier Reef or the Coral Triangle. Instead, they argue that conservation strategies should better reflect the full range of reef systems that make up the global coral reef estate. “Protecting coral reefs at a global scale means protecting all major reef systems,” Wegmann said. “This study shows that atolls belong firmly in that category.” The post The Overlooked Coral Reef Network: Scientists Say Atolls Deserve Greater Conservation Attention appeared first on Island Times News .

title: Russia offered help to Gulf states in restoring refineries — minister
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Russia offered help to Arabian Peninsula countries in restoring their damaged refineries, Minister of Industry and Trade Anton Alikhanov said.
"All the global partnerships undergo a strength test now. When oil refineries were hit in the Middle East crisis, we offered help in their restoring to colleagues in the Arabian Peninsula," the minister said.
The Russian industry has already sufficiently developed its oil and gas equipment competencies to become an alternative to global licensors, Alikhanov said. "Even the own system of industry standards competing with API was created, which are being gradually recognized by Arab partners," he stressed.

title: Anduril unveils family of air defence interceptors
body: Anduril has revealed Steelfin, a family of surface-to-air interceptor missiles built on a common two-stage architecture so that one production line can turn out versions for everything from point defence to upper-tier ballistic missile defence, according to the company. The company set out the problem it is addressing, saying adversaries have invested in large volumes of low-cost, mass-producible offensive weapons and that air defence batteries are too often forced to expend exquisite interceptors against lower-cost threats, straining stores of the most critical defensive weapons and putting defenders on the losing side of the cost exchange. Steelfin pairs a first-stage booster, which can take different solid rocket motors to suit range, launch configuration or packing density, with a second-stage terminal interceptor sharing the same airframe, avionics, software, flight control system and interfaces across every variant. Open interfaces between the subsystems in that terminal stage let different seekers and mission systems be fitted without redesigning the missile. Because the variants share an architecture and components, they move through the same production line using the same tooling, technicians and facilities, and Anduril said it is planning to produce on the order of several thousand Steelfin variants a year in the short term, with capacity designed to flex to demand. The same open interfaces allow commercial off-the-shelf components and competition between vendors, widening the supplier base. The missiles are compatible with launch infrastructure already in service, including the M903A2 launcher used by Patriot, the Mk 41 vertical launching system fitted to warships, Typhon and emerging containerised launchers, and are designed to integrate with fielded fire control systems such as Aegis and IBCS. Anduril has completed ballistic testing with representative air vehicles and will begin flight testing next year. The American company has built a European presence over the past two years, with Latvia selecting its Barracuda cruise missile family and a United Kingdom arm working on autonomy, counter-drone systems and command software. Its approach of designing weapons around mass production and common components is the same argument being made by Helsing, which launched its own pair of low-cost interceptors this week. The post Anduril unveils family of air defence interceptors first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: Russian strikes hit Kyiv bridge and subway infrastructure, killing one person and injuring at least 10
body: Russian forces struck Kyiv starting on the evening of October 26, Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. One person died in the shelling, and 10 others were injured, most of them students at a university dormitory. Nine of the injured were hospitalized. Klitschko said the attack hit the Southern Bridge and the subway system. A medical facility was damaged in the Dniprovskyi district, and a shell struck near a university dormitory in the Desnianskyi district. In the Podilskyi district, the strike hit an administrative building. The Kyiv City Military Administration said the attack forced the closure of traffic on the Southern Bridge. The shelling also damaged an aboveground subway structure, disrupting service on the red and green lines. Update. Russia’s Defense Ministry said the strike on Kyiv also hit several drone production and storage facilities, including an assembly shop for FP-1 and FP-2 drones belonging to the Fire Point company. Since the start of October, Russian forces have intensified strikes on bridges over the Dnipro in Kyiv. The Southern Bridge has been attacked at least twice, and the Northern Bridge has also been hit several times. title: On October 28, the Kyiv Security Forum will hold a special event in Brussels to support Ukraine
body:
On October 28, the Kyiv Security Forum (KSF) will hold a special event in Brussels entitled ‘Support Ukraine – Defend Europe’ , bringing together Ukrainian and foreign politicians, diplomats, military personnel and experts. The event will focus on how to help Ukraine withstand the winter, maintain its defence capabilities and prevent Russia from achieving its strategic objectives.
Members of the Kyiv Security Forum Security Council will also participate in the event: Kurt Volker – former U.S. Special Representative for Ukraine Negotiations; Natalie Jaresko – Chair of the Board of Trustees of the Aspen Institute in Kyiv and former Minister of Finance of Ukraine; Admiral Rob Bauer – former Chairman of the NATO Military Committee; Admiral Sir Tony Radakin – former Chief of the British Defence Staff; Danylo Lubkivsky – former Deputy Foreign Minister of Ukraine; as well as serving members of Ukraine’s Defence Forces.
The discussions will be moderated by Mark Lobel , journalist and BBC presenter.
Participants will also discuss how to respond to nuclear threats and further escalation by Russia, as well as how Europe can shift to a stronger model of defence, readiness and unity.
This will be the first high-level security event organised by the Kyiv Security Forum EU Office in Brussels, which was established on the initiative of Arseniy Yatsenyuk. The Office recently began its work in Brussels, continuing the Kyiv Security Forum’s efforts to build Ukraine’s ties with international partners since 2007.
The KSF EU Office in Brussels will serve as a permanent platform for political and expert dialogue with EU and NATO institutions, the governments of partner countries, parliaments, think tanks and civil society.
The work of the KSF’s EU Office will focus on helping to achieve Ukraine’s key strategic objectives: victory over Russian aggression; accession to the European Union and NATO; post-war recovery and reconstruction; accountability for Russia’s aggression and reparations for the damage it has caused; full participation in shaping Europe’s new defence architecture.
The registration of the international non-governmental organisation ‘European Office of the Kyiv Security Forum’ in Belgium was approved by a relevant Royal Decree signed by King Philippe of Belgium.
The Kyiv Security Forum (KSF), founded by the Arseniy Yatsenyuk ‘Open Ukraine’ Foundation, is Ukraine’s leading international platform on issues of war and peace. The KSF events are attended by heads of state and government, politicians, diplomats, military commanders, experts, civil society figures and journalists. The platform’s activities are aimed at keeping Ukraine at the centre of the global agenda, expanding its circle of international partners and building expertise on pressing security issues.

title: Palau at the Center of Geopolitics: But Whose Interests Are We Serving?
body: Dear Editor, President Surangel Whipps Jr. told the BBC in 2025: “No matter what we do, Palau is going to be the center of any military activity because of our location.” That statement may be true geographically, but it raises a deeper question: If Palau cannot change its location, can we change how we choose to respond to it? Palau’s strategic importance is not new. Under Japanese rule and later American administration, our islands were seen as military assets. Today, as U.S.–China competition intensifies, Palau risks becoming a frontline in a geopolitical contest that is not ours to control. Through the Compact of Free Association, the United States provides economic assistance and assumes responsibility for Palau’s defense, while securing strategic rights. These arrangements bring benefits to US, but they also bring risks to Palau. What happens if war breaks out? Will adversaries distinguish between military installations and civilian communities? Will our families, children, and elders be protected simply because Palau is sovereign? No agreement can guarantee that civilians will escape the consequences of conflict. Look at Ukraine and Gaza. This is why leadership matters. Being at the center of geopolitics does not mean surrendering our ability to shape our future. Palau must decide how it participates, what conditions it negotiates, and what safeguards it demands. Our foreign policy should reflect Palau’s national interests, not simply follow Washington’s priorities. Unfortunately, short‑term economic thinking blinds us to long‑term risks. Leaders celebrate millions of dollars, infrastructure projects, and aid packages, but fail to ask what happens to Palau in the next generation. True leadership requires planning for evacuation, civilian protection, land use, and the consequences of regional conflict. We must stop being satisfied with crumbs from someone else’s table. Palau must build its own table, establish its own strategic vision, and negotiate from a position of national purpose. Partnership with the United States matters, but partnership must never replace independent thinking. Our location may be permanent. Our political choices are not. The question is whether we will shape our place in the Pacific or allow others to decide our future for us. Everything for Everyone and Nothing for Ourselves. That is the principle of sovereignty, and the leadership Palau needs today. Your Humble Servant Dudalm Kelulau The Silent Majority The post Palau at the Center of Geopolitics: But Whose Interests Are We Serving? appeared first on Island Times News .

title: ADC demands disclosure on SUVs donated to APC youth leaders
body:
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has demanded details of how seven luxury sport utility vehicles donated to youth leaders of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) were financed.
The opposition party said the vehicles, reportedly valued at about ₦1 billion, amounted to an extravagant display at a time when many Nigerians could barely afford necessities.
In a statement on Monday, the ADC National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, accused the ruling party of putting its political interests ahead of the economic difficulties Nigerians face.
“President Tinubu asks Nigerians to endure hardship while his party distributes luxury vehicles to its political operatives. Apparently, sacrifice is for ordinary Nigerians, while luxury is reserved for those working to keep the APC in power,” he said.
“The APC has found the resources to move its campaign officials around Nigeria. What it has failed to find is a convincing way to make life affordable for the Nigerians whose votes it now seeks.”
Mr Abdullahi also criticised the decision to provide vehicles for political mobilisation ahead of the 2027 elections while many young Nigerians remained unemployed.
“Seven APC youth leaders can receive luxury vehicles, but millions of young Nigerians are still waiting for the jobs, opportunities and economic relief they were promised. Is this the APC’s idea of youth empowerment?” he asked.
The ADC demanded disclosure of the source of funding, including whether public resources were used.
“Nigerians deserve to know who paid for these vehicles. Until that question is answered, the ruling party cannot dismiss legitimate concerns about its priorities,” Mr Abdullahi said.
The controversy followed the presentation of seven Toyota Land Cruiser Prado SUVs to APC youth leaders as part of preparations for the 2027 general elections.
PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that First Lady Oluremi Tinubu acknowledged donating vehicles to the APC youth wing to support grassroots mobilisation.
However, the actual cost of the vehicles and how they were financed have not been independently established.
The ADC statement did not provide evidence that public funds were used to purchase the vehicles.

title: Romania uncovers Russian-coordinated sabotage network suspected of setting fire near defense facility
body:
According to Ukrinform, the report was published by Reuters.
The network was responsible for the September fire at an industrial site in central Romania, located near a state-owned defense industry enterprise,” the report says.
According to Romanian intelligence, the suspects were members of a network coordinated by Russia. The network’s coordinators had assigned it targets including “state and private weapons production facilities, as well as other objectives of military and industrial interest”.
Romanian organized crime prosecutors said they were seeking the extradition of two Belarusian suspects apprehended in Germany and one Ukrainian detainedin Poland who were all suspected of of involvement in the arson attack.
Reuters noted that Romanian President Nicușor Dan had previously accused Russia of waging a hybrid war against countries supporting Ukraine. According to Dan, this included drone incursions into national airspace, cyberattacks, disinformation campaigns, acts of sabotage, and attacks on cargo vessels near Romanian waters.
Russia’s embassy in Bucharest could not immediately been reached for comment, but Moscow has repeatedly denied such accusations, Reuters said.
As Ukrinform previously reported, Romanian President Nicușor Dan accused Russia of escalating attacks threatening NATO’s eastern flank after a cargo vessel sank on Friday following a drone strike near Romania’s Black Sea coast.

title: Ukraine Downs 2 Ballistic Missiles, 255 Russian Drones in Overnight Attack Targeting Kyiv
body:
Ukrainian air defenses shot down or neutralized two Russian ballistic missiles and 255 drones during an overnight attack primarily targeting Kyiv , the Air Force reported on Tuesday, Oct. 27.
Russia launched the attack from 6 p.m. on Monday, Oct. 26, using Iskander-M/S-400 ballistic missiles from Russia’s Bryansk region and 280 strike drones, including Shahed-type unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), Gerbera drones, and Parodiya decoys.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Of the Shahed-type drones, 69 were jet-powered, according to the report on Telegram .
As of 9 a.m. on Tuesday, Ukrainian forces had intercepted or suppressed 257 aerial targets: two ballistic missiles Iskander-M/S-400 type and 255 drones. These included 56 jet-powered Shahed-type UAVs.
Several strike drones remained in the air, and combat operations were ongoing at the time of the report.
Air Force said impacts from Russian aerial weapons were recorded at 25 locations, while debris from intercepted targets fell at 16 locations.
Separately, the State Emergency Service (DSNS) reported that Russian forces carried out more than 40 attacks across five districts of the Dnipropetrovsk region overnight, injuring three people in the Synelnykove district.
Fires broke out in a multi-story residential building, vehicles, private homes and outbuildings. Residential houses also caught fire in the Nikopol and Pavlohrad districts.
In the city of Dnipro and the Kamianske district, infrastructure was damaged and a fire broke out. Rescuers extinguished all the fires, the DSNS reported.
Russian strikes on Kyiv overnight into Tuesday, prompted the closure of the South (Pivdennyi) Bridge, a major crossing connecting the capital’s eastern and western banks of the Dnipro River.
Kyiv Mayor Vitalii Klitschko released the first photos showing damage to the bridge as specialists assessed the extent of the damage.
The Kyiv City Military Administration (KMVA) also reported disruptions on the Green (Syretsko-Pecherska) metro line, with trains operating separately between Syrets and Vydubychi stations and between Osokorky and Chervonyi Khutir stations.
The bridge remains closed to traffic, and authorities have not announced when it will reopen or when normal metro service will resume. The crossing carries both road traffic and part of the Green Line.
In a separate development, Russian ballistic missile strikes damaged an administrative building in Kyiv’s Podilskyi district and non-residential buildings at two other locations.
The attack followed Monday evening strikes on a university campus and nearby residential areas that killed one person and injured over 10 others, most of them students.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: An Ocean of Peace is NOT Built on Occupation: Pacific Civil questions the Pacific Forum on Israel partnership
body: Friday 23rd October 2026 The Blue Pacific is our oceanic home. It is held together by a weave of shared values passed from our forebears’ hands into ours: justice, peace, self-determination and respect for international law. We, the members of the Pacific Regional Non-Governmental Organisations (PRNGO) Alliance, representing our diverse constituencies and mandated by them to promote and protect the interests of Pacific Island peoples, declare our deep concern at the admission of Israel as a partner of the Pacific Islands Forum. The decision taken by our leaders at the 55th Pacific Island Leaders Forum in Palau was announced by Israel, yet the Forum Secretariat has not issued a statement and has already hosted a MASHAV development cooperation Talanoa with Israel. We understand our communities’ real needs for water, food security, agriculture, development and climate adaptation. The urgent need for resources across the region is increasing, and partnerships to secure such are important. Our concern is that the Forum family will welcome, without condition, a state in continuing breach of international law. We reject antisemitism, Islamophobia and anti-Arab racism, and mourn every civilian life lost, Israeli and Palestinian. UPHOLDING INTERNATIONAL LAW In its Advisory Opinion of 19 July 2024, the International Court of Justice found Israel’s occupation of Palestinian territory unlawful. The ICJ stated that Israel must end it “as rapidly as possible” and evacuate all settlers, and all States must neither recognise it as lawful nor “render aid or assistance” in maintaining it. Our region championed the Court’s climate opinion of July 2025: relying on international law to work for our islands. We cannot invoke the Court for our islands and ignore it for Palestine. The Security Council Resolution 2334 (2016) affirms that settlements have “no legal validity” and are “a flagrant violation under international law”. In addition, the Council’s Resolution 478 (1980) calls on States to withdraw their diplomatic missions from Jerusalem. Yet three Forum members in Papua New Guinea, Fiji and Naoero, have opened embassies there, Samoa has announced plans to follow, and Israel’s announcement cites them. Despite the ceasefire announced on 10 October 2025, the violations continue: UN OCHA reports 1,493 Palestinians killed in Gaza and 4,300 Palestinians displaced from the occupied West Bank since then. Human Rights Watch found Israel’s deliberate deprivation of Gaza’s water amounts to extermination and acts of genocide. FAO reports nearly 87 percent of Gaza’s cropland damaged. The war’s emissions, an estimated 33 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent, fall on islands like ours. Water, food and climate security cannot be offered with one hand and destroyed with the other. Under international law, a ceasefire requires a complete halt to the attacks, and allows unimpeded entry of humanitarian relief at scale. It would end unprecedented Israeli settlement expansion and terror, guaranteeing the right of displaced Palestinians to return home, prohibit forcible transfers and end collective punishment. Our Forum Leaders have called on all the world to uphold the UN Charter, including the sovereign equality of all states and the rights of all peoples to exist in peace and security. SAFEGUARDING THE OCEAN OF PEACE In September 2025, our Leaders declared the Blue Pacific as an Ocean of Peace, grounded in the UN Charter and international law. As we said in July, a genuine Ocean of Peace means security “founded on justice, sovereignty, self-determination, environmental stewardship and the wellbeing of our peoples”. It rests on a strong rejection of militarisation and great power rivalry at our expense. A regional partnership with Israel would further facilitate and advance security cooperation, military technologies and infrastructures, in addition to the growing military exercises and security treaties crowding our ocean. Pacific regionalism rests on solidarity based on shared values, not merely on shared resources. This partnership will unravel: not strengthen, that weave. It risks dividing the Forum family, tying our voice at the United Nations to bilateral favours, and making the Pacific complicit in a conflict far from our shores. Who stands to benefit from this partnership? Whose voice will it silence? ANOTHER PERPETRATING STATE The Pacific remembers the cost of occupation, and our peoples continue to struggle under colonisation, nuclear testing and environmental destruction. In Kanaky New Caledonia, Ma’ohi Nui, Guahan and West Papua, the struggle for self-determination continues. West Papua is a long standing item on our Leaders’ agenda. Since 2019, they have asked Indonesia, a Forum Dialogue Partner since 2001, to allow a visit by the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights — a visit Jakarta offered in 2018. It has not eventuated, yet a similar partnership has brought delay: not accountability. Inviting another state that perpetrates occupation and denies self-determination repeats that mistake, and weakens the principle on which our decolonisation depends. The PRNGO Alliance therefore calls upon: ● The Forum Troika — Solomon Islands, Palau and New Zealand, as past, current and incoming Chairs — to reflect on these concerns as it shapes the new partnership arrangements, and to ensure the participation, consultation and consent of our peoples before such decisions are made in their name. ● Forum Leaders to review Israel’s partnership and suspend all engagements until Israel complies with the International Court of Justice and relevant Security Council resolutions, and to hold every partner to that standard, including by pressing Indonesia to allow the UN High Commissioner’s visit to West Papua. ● The Forum Secretariat to publish the basis for this decision and ensure any partnership agreement with Israel commits it to international law. ● Papua New Guinea, Fiji and Naoero to return their embassies to Tel Aviv, consistent with Resolution 478, and Samoa to reconsider its plan. ● All Forum members to ensure no partnership, aid, or security, cyber or surveillance cooperation helps maintain the occupation. Our Forum family is a mat on which everyone enjoys a place to sit. We welcome every partner who joins their strands to that mat, but none who deny other people their place. At the centre of Pacific Regionalism must lie the principle that partnership is measured by justice: not by favours. The post An Ocean of Peace is NOT Built on Occupation: Pacific Civil questions the Pacific Forum on Israel partnership appeared first on Island Times News .

title: The Trump administration is backing Orbán, who blocked a €90 billion EU loan to Ukraine, for UN secretary-general and is counting on support from Moscow and Beijing, WSJ says
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); The Trump administration has encouraged former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán to run for UN secretary-general and discussed a joint US-Russia-China candidacy with Moscow and Beijing, the Wall Street Journal’s (WSJ) editorial board wrote on 25 October, citing sources in three countries. Russia’s biggest ally in the EU, Orbán has been out of office since May, when Péter Magyar became Hungary’s prime minister. The UN secretary-general can influence the war through diplomatic negotiations, mediation, and by drawing the Security Council’s attention to Russia’s aggression. António Guterres’s term ends on 31 December, so the council has to settle on a successor within weeks. According to the WSJ, US officials discussing the next UN chief kept saying they wanted “ someone like Orbán ,” and their Russian and Chinese counterparts agreed. The US then brought the idea to Orbán himself. Russia and China are believed to support his bid based on those earlier talks with Washington, and the plan is for him to be the three countries’ joint candidate. Ukraine warns of Orbán’s veto tactics at the UN Orbán is receptive but has not decided, and he does not want to enter the race unless he is sure he can win, the editorial board wrote. A State Department official counted eight Security Council votes as safe for him and 10 within reach. A candidate needs nine of the 15 votes and no veto from a permanent member. The editorial board asked whether Britain and France, typically cautious in using their veto, would stand in the way. Any announcement is being held until after the 3 November US midterm elections. Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha wrote on X that Orbán as secretary-general would put to good use “ the masterful veto and blackmail skills ” he developed over years of derailing major EU decisions. Ukraine, he added, could share its “ great experience of taking him out for coffee at the right moment ,” a reference to the December 2023 EU summit, where Orbán left the room so the other leaders could open accession talks with Ukraine without his veto. Orbán ran Hungary for 16 years as Putin’s closest EU partner Orbán’s 16 years of “illiberal democracy” eroded democratic values in Hungary. Since 2010, Fidesz has built an enormous partisan media ecosystem . Before the vote, it amended the electoral law twice and gerrymandered more than a third of the electoral districts, so the opposition might need around 55% of the popular vote to win a simple majority. Orbán still lost the 12 April election. Magyar’s Tisza won 138 of 199 seats, a two-thirds majority in parliament. Explore further Voted out and facing investigators, Orbán could reach for UN cover, sources say Orbán kept close ties with Moscow throughout the full-scale war. When he met Putin in Beijing in October 2023, he spoke of “ the military operations and the sanctions ” rather than a war. In summer 2024, while Hungary held the EU Council presidency, he flew to Moscow on what he called a peace mission, and the EU distanced itself from the trip. In November 2025, he went back to Moscow, seeking to keep Hungary’s access to Russian oil and gas. He is widely considered Putin’s closest partner among EU leaders. After that visit, he said the only solution was for Ukraine to become a buffer state again, and that the longer peace was delayed, the more people and territory Ukraine would lose. Then-Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Beijing, 17 October 2023. Photo: Radio Free Europe He used Hungary’s veto against Ukraine until his last weeks in office. In February, Orbán vetoed a €90 billion EU loan to Ukraine amid the disruption of Russian oil supplies through the Druzhba pipeline to Hungary and Slovakia. Hungary lifted its veto in April after repairs to the pipeline were announced. Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó phoned Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov from EU meetings for years with “ live reports on what’s been discussed ,” a European security official told The Washington Post. Szijjártó did not respond to the Post’s request for comment.
