title: Keyless Entry: Hacking SwitchBot Smart Locks
body:
We’ve identified multiple vulnerabilities in devices of the popular SwitchBot Lock Pro smart lock series. The most critical, a cryptographic flaw in their bluetooth communication, allows everyone to silently open smart locks in a software-only attack. No physical tampering is required. Below is a video of the attack in action.
The vulnerability has been fixed, and updated firmware is currently being rolled out to users. According to SwitchBot, it has not received any reports of locks being compromised as a result of this vulnerability.
Smart locks have become very popular in recent years. Especially when it comes to AirBnB-style apartment sharing, but also in corporate environments and private accommodation, people enjoy having locks that don’t require physical keys. So when it came to selecting targets for our regular IoT hacking team event, smart locks were a natural choice.
After some research we cam across the highly praised Switchbot Lock Pro Combo , including a key actuator, pin pad and smartphone app. It is one of the best-rated and most-sold smart locks on Amazon. For roughly 240€ (at the time of writing) it comes with a lot of features - and the Amazon reviewers are happy to share that it works as intended.
Features aside, our main interest was, of course, the device’s security. So we ordered one and had a look. Here is what we found out.
As usual when inspecting IoT devices, we wanted to get our hand on the firmware. But before we dive into that, let’s first look into the target’s features and architecture.
The bundle comes with two hardware devices, an actuator and a key pad. The lock can further be controlled and configured via a smartphone app.
The actuator is mounted onto the inside of the door and encloses the door’s key. When the door is supposed to open, the actuator simply turns the key in the lock.
Switchbot Pro Lock Actuator Promotional Material
The key pad is kept outside the door and communicates with the actuator over Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE). A person can authenticate itself to the system either using a smart card/key fob, using a fingerprint, or - most commonly - by supplying a PIN. The whole system can also be added to a WiFi network, making it possible to control the lock over the Internet.
Now that we have an idea of the feature set, we can start digging.
When hacking a device, it is usually a good idea to first get your hands on its firmware. There are various techniques for accomplishing this, FLASH Dumping for example. Before starting to desolder chips, however, it makes sense to scrape the web for firmware artifacts.
With SwitchBot we got lucky, as the Android app contained the URL for a public S3 bucket containing firmware files. Downloading and analysing these files we found two surprising architectural choices. First, the key pad on the outside of the door actually controls the actuator on the inside , not the other way around. Meaning that the key pad decides if a PIN, fingerprint or key fob is valid and then issues an “UNLOCK” command to the actuator. Secondly, the communication between the key pad and actuator relies on an unprotected, clear-text BLE connection. Authentication between key pad and actuator is done solely on the application level using a home-brewed mechanism.
While the first point already yields a significant attack surface (i.e. let’s dump the key pad and open the door), the second offers a code smell too good to pass up. So we focussed our main energy on exploiting the BLE communication between key pad and actuator.
Once the key pad and actuator are paired, they communicate using unprotected BLE. Meaning that all security of the system depends on application-level protections. So let’s find out how these protections work.
Upon pairing, the key pad and actuator agree on a secret key . Then, everytime the key pad becomes active, it requests a so-called “ nonce ” value from the actuator. For our attack this does not matter. It is noteworthy however, that the nonce is supposed to provide “freshness” between invocations of the protocol but that this implementation uses the same nonce for an entire “session” which can last for multiple commands. After the nonce is received, the key pad encrypts a command, using the secret key and nonce, and sends said command over the BLE connection. Such a command could, for example, be “lock the door”.
The following diagram illustrates how the BLE communication works.
Communication between key pad and actuator (simplified)
Simply by looking at the communication diagram we can see a potential problem: We might be able to simply replay previous “unlock” commands that we have captured. However, that would require us to be within Bluetooth range, sniff the command, and then somehow replay it before the session ends. Since we aren’t writing an academic paper but do actual research: This is boring.
We want to be able to open the lock, first shot, without any physical tampering and without leaving traces.
And, as it turns out, we can accomplish this. But first need some more background on the implementation.
So the key pad/actuator communication is protected using secret-key encryption and a nonce. Digging further into the implementation, and with the help of community-developed libraries , we found out how the encryption is done.
The commands are encrypted using the AES block cipher in counter (CTR) mode. Now, counter mode is an interesting choice, because it doesn’t actually offer any integrity protection. Furthermore, because of its design, turning a block cipher into a stream cipher, bit flips propagate 1:1 from ciphertext to plaintext.
Meaning that: If we change a bit in a ciphertext, upon decryption by the actuator, this exact bit will also be changed in the decrypted plaintext. This is a little-known, but often encountered vulnerability class. So, let’s exploit this fact and open some doors!
A key observation helps us to mount our attack. The key pad’s lock button always sends an encrypted LOCK command, even if the door is already locked. Exploiting the fact that AES CTR is used, we only need to compute the difference between an encrypted LOCK and UNLOCK command. When we XOR this difference (flipping all corresponding bits) into an encrypted LOCK command, the result will be a validly encrypted UNLOCK command. It’s important to note here that this difference has to be computed only once, as it is identical across sessions and devices! We therefore split the attack into a setup phase, run once, and an attack phase that opens a specific lock.
After the one-time setup, the attack works as follows:
As we suspect a lot of vulnerable devices out there, we won’t publish our full exploit here. But using an individual example, you can see why our attack works. So, let’s work through it.
Using one pair of encrypted LOCK and UNLOCK commands, intercepted via BLE, we can compute their XOR difference. This difference is identical across all sessions and all locks using the same firmware. Therefore, we can use this difference as a sort of “master key” to open all SwitchBot Pro locks.
Sniffing an encrypted LOCK and UNLOCK command is done easily using our acquired lock. Then, we simply compute:
Applying (XORing) this difference diff to the encryption of any LOCK command, independent of secret key and nonce, will yield an encrypted unlock command, which we can then send to the actuator.
So, simply by applying our pre-computed, lock-independent, difference vector, we can turn every SwitchBot Pro LOCK command into an UNLOCK command. And we can always capture encrypted LOCK commands on any key pad, simply by pressing the lock button. Neat!
We’ve recorded our attack in action. The video shows the components and our Bluetooth antenna used for sniffing the encrypted LOCK command. On the left you can see the Python script applying the difference to the encrypted LOCK command and sending the crafted encrypted UNLOCK command. The right side of the screen shows that the attack worked: First, a LOCK command is issued by pressing the lock button. Then, the crafted UNLOCK command is send and the actuator turns the key, opening the door \o/ .
It all happens very fast, so maybe you have to re-watch a couple of times to grasp everything.
In accordance with our responsible disclosure guidelines, we notified the SwitchBot team of our findings. They were very responsive (kudos!) and seemed to take the vulnerability seriously. They awarded us a 100€ Amazon voucher for our work.
Before they rolled out a firmware patch, they allowed us to have a look at the updated firmware files.
After we reversed the new firmware, we discovered that they now append a “checksum” to every command. We reimplemented the checksum computation in Python:
So the system now calculates an MD5 hash of the command, secret key and nonce. The first two bytes of this hash then serve as verification tag. This construction is sometimes referred to as YOLO hash and rarely a good idea. Here in particular, the truncation to two bytes allows us to, in principle, brute force all 65,536 possible verification tags. However, this is not necessary.
Because, to our surprise, just the communication between the key pad and actuator got updated. The smartphone app still does not use a verification tag. Which means that our attack still works 1:1, we just need to compute (once!) the difference between a key pad’s encrypted LOCK command and a smartphone issued UNLOCK command. We can then mount our attack using this difference vector, as the actuator then thinks the UNLOCK command comes from a smartphone and does not check the verification tag. We have verified that this variant of our attack works.
When we reported this bypass, SwitchBot provided the following context:
The test firmware pushed to you only includes updates for the Keypad and Lock. The APP has not yet been updated with the new encryption method. We are currently working on implementing encryption upgrades for both the APP and the backend, and the Lock will no longer be compatible with the old encryption method. We need to ensure that this update does not affect other products bound to the APP […].
Backward compatibility is always challenging, especially when it comes to security and IoT devices out in the field.
As we were happy with our full compromise, we did not look too much into other avenues of attack. Noteworthy, however, was that the key pad uses MIFARE Classic 1K key fobs. These are long broken and can be trivially cloned, e.g., using a Flipper Zero . In order to mount this cloning attack, you’d have to get close to a key fob first.
Additionally, while testing the Bluetooth attack, we noticed that the key pad has a tamper detection. If it is removed from the wall, it will play a loud alarm sound and inform the owners via their smartphone. This is implemented using a Hall effect sensor on top of the key pad and can therefore be defeated using a strong magnet. We recommend Neodymium magnets for such purposes ;).
According to SwitchBot, the following versions should have the relevant fixes installed.
Security is hard and IoT devices often times lack good protections. We have to give credit to SwitchBot for even trying to secure their system. Many IoT manufacturers don’t even do that. Hacking this smart lock was a good reminder about the threats IoT devices can pose. Even the more expensive, highly sought after products, are not necessarily immune to attack.
Vulnerabilities like these arise from developers’ mistaken assumptions. In fact, misusing crypto primitives like AES-CTR, aka. cryptographic failure, is one of the most common software security vulnerabilities according OWASP . As it turns out, we offer a cutting-edge Black Hat training on crypto vulnerabilities and audits and testing to help with exactly that!

title: We’re not responsible for hunger in Nigeria – PDP fires back at APC
body: The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) on Monday says it is not responsible for hunger in Nigeria, advising the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to stop the blame game. The PDP National Publicity Secretary, Jungudo Mohammed said this in a statement on Monday in Abuja. According to Mohammed, the PDP’s attention has been drawn to the statement made by the APC Publicity Secretary, Felix Moka, during his appearance on a show on Monday. ”In statement, he blamed the PDP for the hunger and economic hardship currently confronting Nigerians. “The PDP also notes similar remarks reportedly made by President Bola Tinubu in Kaduna during the flag-off of his 2027 re-election campaign. “The PDP considers these statements as attempts to evade responsibility and divert public attention from the pressing challenges facing the country under the APC-led administration. “Our message to the APC is simple: stop the blame game and start taking responsibility. Nigerians deserve solutions, not excuses. “The government in power must address the country’s challenges through concrete, measurable, and sustainable actions that will bring meaningful relief to citizens. “The PDP is not responsible for the hunger Nigerians are experiencing today. The APC must own its record, address the nation’s challenges, and deliver on its promises to Nigerians.” He added that the government in power must answer for its stewardship and present a credible path towards economic recovery, food security, and a better standard of living for all Nigerians. Mohammed said that rather than engaging in political blame games, the APC should explain what it intended to do to make food affordable, support farmers, and strengthen local food production. He also advised the ruling party to tell Nigerians how it intended to create jobs, improve security, fight corruption, improve electricity supply, reduce transportation costs, and restore the purchasing power of ordinary Nigerians, among other pressing concerns. The PDP national publicity secretary further said that while the party acknowledged some of the achievements recorded by President Tinubu’s administration, where applicable, it rejected any attempt to use its 16 years in government as a blanket justification for the shortcomings of the present administration. “Acknowledging any genuine achievements must not be misconstrued as an endorsement of all government policies or an acceptance of attempts to shift responsibility for current economic difficulties to previous PDP-led administrations. “After more than 10 years of APC in office, Nigerians deserve answers, not excuses. “The APC must tell Nigerians what it has achieved, outline the concrete measures it is taking to address the country’s present-day challenges, and demonstrate its commitment to improving the welfare of citizens rather than continually dragging the PDP into its own shortcomings,” he said. Mohammed noted that the economic challenges confronting Nigeria could not be resolved by repeatedly blaming previous PDP-led administrations. He explained that while historical circumstances might provide context, they could not serve as a permanent shield against accountability. He said that every administration must be judged by its policies, achievements, and most importantly, the living conditions of the people it governs. “Nigerians remember the standard of living and the security situation under previous PDP administrations. “Today, citizens are demanding practical solutions, affordable food, economic stability, and improved security, not endless political arguments and blame shifting,” he said. Mohammed said that PDP remained confident that Nigerians would judge political parties by their records, policies, and commitment to the welfare of the people. “We believe that the growing desire among Nigerians for a return to PDP leadership reflects their yearning for better governance, improved living conditions, and a more secure and prosperous country. ( NAN ) The post We’re not responsible for hunger in Nigeria – PDP fires back at APC appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Netanyahu’s political survival on the line as Israel votes
body: JERUSALEM – Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu faces a fight for political survival in Israel’s election on Tuesday, October 27, with voters weighing his leadership after the 2023 Hamas-led attacks, wars in Gaza and with Iran, and Israel’s deepening international isolation. Yet Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving leader with 19 years in office, remains a formidable survivor, with nationalist politics increasingly entrenched and Israel’s fragmented system potentially leaving him best placed to form a government. Opinion polls show a close race between Netanyahu’s Likud party and its right-wing allies and a rival alliance led by Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief of staff and security hawk with backers on the right and in the center. Voters began casting ballots after polling stations opened at 7 am (0500 GMT). The polls close at 10 pm (2000 GMT). Netanyahu has campaigned on his wartime leadership and his alliance with US President Donald Trump, who has endorsed him and joined Israel in waging war on Iran. Netanyahu said on Sunday, October 25, that Trump was prepared to act again to “finally” remove the Iranian threat, but only if Netanyahu remained in power. Eisenkot has accused Netanyahu of “relying on a campaign of fear-mongering, lies and threats,” and said he was confident Trump would work “in full cooperation with any leader chosen by the people.” Netanyahu may again depend on far-right leaders Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich to form a government. Both have faced sanctions from some Western countries that accuse them of inciting violence against Palestinians , while Ben-Gvir’s Jewish Power party has gained support in opinion polls. Neither Netanyahu nor Eisenkot has a clear path to power. If neither can form a governing coalition in the 120-seat parliament, Netanyahu could stay on as caretaker until another election is held next year. The Israeli Central Election Committee said 7.3 million Israelis are eligible to vote, some 330,000 of them for the first time. The October 7 reckoning The election follows one of Israel’s most turbulent periods since its establishment in 1948, shaped by the trauma of the October 7, 2023, Hamas attacks, Israel’s subsequent military assault in Gaza and deep domestic divisions over the policies of Netanyahu’s right-wing government. For many of Netanyahu’s opponents, the election turns on accountability for the security failures of October 7, Israel’s deadliest day. Mali Hajaj, an Education Ministry employee and Eisenkot supporter, said “the most important thing is the establishment of a national inquiry because that’s where our healing will come from.” Lisa Tortor said she hoped Netanyahu would go and “they can form a new government and do some of the repairing of the damage that Bibi has done for Jews all over the world and for Israel, and Israel’s image.” Bibi is Netanyahu’s nickname. But Nof Gabay, an 18-year-old Likud supporter, rejected the idea Netanyahu was to blame for October 7 and called him “the right man for the state of Israel.” “Netanyahu managed the war in the best possible way,” Gabay said. The wartime record Israel flattened much of Gaza in the offensive launched after October 7, when Hamas-led militants killed 1,200 people and took another 251 hostage. Gaza health authorities say Israeli attacks killed 74,000 people. Israel also dealt heavy blows to Iran-backed Hezbollah in Lebanon and traded strikes with Iran before a 12-day aerial campaign against Iranian nuclear sites in 2025 and this year’s joint US-Israeli war. Eisenkot has said Israel’s next government must prevent Iran from acquiring a military nuclear capability, either by force or through an “arrangement” such as a US-backed diplomatic solution. The coalition math Like nearly all Jewish-led parties in Israel, Eisenkot opposes the two-state solution that underpinned decades of peace negotiations with the Palestinians. But he has criticised Jewish settler violence against Palestinians in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, which has surged since 2023 and strained Israel’s ties with Western states, and opposes Netanyahu’s far-right coalition partners Ben-Gvir and Smotrich. In some bastions of Likud support, disenchanted voters have been going door to door to turn voters against Netanyahu. Some have turned away from Netanyahu as he battles corruption charges he denies in a long-running criminal trial. A high turnout among voters from Israel’s Arab minority, Israeli by citizenship but Palestinian by heritage, could help nudge Israel’s complex coalition arithmetic in favor of Eisenkot. Though Eisenkot has ruled out partnering with Arab parties, citing a lack of shared values, analysts see a scenario where they prop up a minority government he leads in order to ensure Netanyahu is removed from office. “My expectation is that we will have only a slight majority either way. No landslide,” said Israeli political analyst Amotz Asa-El of the Shalom Hartman Institute. – Rappler.com

title: Jay-Z To Perform At Super Bowl LXI Halftime Show — NFL
body: Rapper Jay-Z will perform at the Super Bowl LXI halftime show this February in Los Angeles, the NFL announced Monday. Jay-Z’s Roc Nation entertainment company has produced the star-packed Super Bowl halftime show each year since 2020, selecting the headliners, but the hip-hop mogul has not previously performed himself at the event. “When we first reached an agreement with Roc Nation to produce the show, I had just one request: that Jay-Z take the stage himself one day, whenever the moment felt right to him,” NFL commissioner Roger Goodell said in a joint statement. “I couldn’t be more excited for fans around the world to experience the artistry, creativity and cultural impact he will bring to the Super Bowl stage.” The announcement did not specify whether Jay-Z would be the sole headliner. It came after Jay-Z — who is married to pop megastar Beyonce — performed two shows last weekend at Los Angeles’ SoFi Stadium, which will serve as the venue for the Super Bowl on February 14. Those gigs served as the culmination of a year-long tour celebrating the 30th anniversary of his debut album “Reasonable Doubt.” “From ‘Reasonable Doubt’ to standing on the Super Bowl halftime stage, this has been a journey,” said Jay-Z, whose real name is Shawn Carter. “Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world’s biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true.” In an indication of the level of star power Jay-Z could potentially bring with him to the halftime spectacular, he was joined on-stage in Los Angeles by John Legend, DJ Khaled, Dr Dre and Snoop Dogg. title: Calls for change at massive rally in Tel Aviv ahead of Israel election
body: By Laura Tingle and Matthew Doran in Tel Aviv In short: (ABC-Australia) Tens of thousands of people have rallied in Tel Aviv in a final protest against Benjamin Netanyahu and his government. The crowd heard calls for a commission of inquiry into the security failures that led to the October 7 attacks. What’s next? The election for the Israeli parliament occurs on Tuesday. https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-10-25/thousands-rally-in-tel-aviv-days-ahead-of-israel-election/107306000 Share article For two years they came to Hostage Square in Tel Aviv each week to demand their government do more to get their loved ones and friends home from captivity in Gaza. Last night they came in their tens of thousands to demand an independent state commission of inquiry into how the greatest security breach in Israel’s history, and as a result the greatest mass slaughter, had been able to occur in the first place. Three days before an election regarded as the most pivotal in the country’s history, those attending the rally were clear that there needed to be a change of government, not just to get their long-demanded inquiry but because they say Israel’s democracy is under threat. Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has flatly refused to have an independent investigation into the events of October 7, 2023, after thousands of Hamas fighters surged across the border from Gaza. Leaders of opposition parties have pledged an inquiry. Among those leaders who attended the rally were the main rival to Mr Netanyahu, Gadi Eisenkot, as well as Avigdor Liberman, Yair Lapid, Yisrael Beiteinu and Yair Golan. Mali Zender not only lost her daughter Noa on October 7, but as a head nurse at Sheba Hospital treated those hostages who did return from the tunnels of Gaza. “Not everyone has taken responsibility and we do not have answers,” she said. “A country cannot move forward without soul-searching. Leaders cannot demand our faith without taking responsibility. “Do not give up on the truth, and do not give up on our future.” Rabbi Elchanan Danino, whose son Uri was abducted and murdered in Hamas captivity, said an inquiry “will not bring our sons and daughters home, but it is necessary for the futures of our sons and daughters … and for the soldiers who are risking their lives for our existence here.” Repeated cries of “shame” echoed through the sweltering Tel Aviv crowd. But it is not just the cause of getting an inquiry being demanded by many speakers who addressed the rally and many of those attending. Members of the crowd who spoke to the ABC repeatedly spoke of how they believe Israel’s longest-serving prime minister represents a threat to Israel’s democracy, to say there must be a change of government when the election for the Israeli parliament occurs on Tuesday. “Our democracy is torn down and it’s ridiculous that the government that is responsible for this horrible war and for letting us down so many months before is still there,” Aviva Mimouni Bloch told the ABC. Her husband Yuval said: “Probably our greatest war now is against what is happening in our country, where people who are corrupt, incapable, cynical don’t take any responsibility for what is going on.” Orr Rachlevsky said that “we’ve been fighting against the policies of this government who brought Israel into the worst place ever, experiencing the worst massacre of the Jewish people”. “And this is the last week that we have, the last opportunity that we have to save our beloved country as our parents and grandparents built, to be a beacon of hope and justice and love of people and human beings. And we will make this place a better place.” Asked if he was worried what would happen on Tuesday if the current government is returned to office, he said: “This will be the end of the Jewish country. It might take a day or two days or a week or a year, but this will be the end. “It means that the country that my grandparents built is poisoned and beyond any repair. But I don’t believe this will happen.” Ophir Baer said: “We have to make a change.” Ophir and his wife had regularly come to rallies at the square, driving one and a half hours each time. “We did it for many, many months every Saturday, and today it was clear that this is like three days before our big, big chance to make a difference and to actually make a change. So that’s what we’re doing. “If this criminal government, and it is the criminal government, if it would be up to me, I would put all 64 or later 68 Knesset members into jail because all of them are responsible for the people who died, for the people who were murdered, for the people who didn’t come back alive when they could have rescued them a year earlier, at least. “So I think we need a change after those years, after the failure of October 7.” Teenagers Tomer Nahir and Zoya Malka are too young to vote on Tuesday but believe Israel needs a change. “We need to get rid of the corruption that’s going around in the government,” Tomer said. “I’m going to cry if Bibi will be chosen again, because I really hate what he’s doing to our country and what is happening, and that’s why I’m also here today,” Zoya said. Tomar said he was worried the country would be much more divided if Mr Netanyahu was returned to government, and this would cause a lot of tension between groups in the community Almost all others in positions of authority in the lead up to October 7 have lost their jobs or left, except the prime minister. Many Israelis hold him culpable. He has said the only problem on October 7 was that no-one had woken him up when the attack started at 6:29am that day. News stories have repeatedly documented instances where Mr Netanyahu was personally told of a looming threat from Hamas, threats he both ignored and did not pass on. His long hold on power is also under threat because of a series of corruption charges, and because he attempted to circumscribe the powers of the Supreme Court, which many Israelis believe would have given the government untrammelled power. The post Calls for change at massive rally in Tel Aviv ahead of Israel election appeared first on Island Times News .

title: Taraba Killings: Governor extends security measures by six months
body:
The Taraba State Governor, Agbu Kefas, has extended the designation of Karim-Lamido Local Government Area as an area of special security concern for another six months following the deadly attack on Binnari community.
The governor announced the decision on Monday after an emergency security meeting at the T.Y. Danjuma House in Jalingo, the state capital, in response to the 23 October attack that left dozens of residents dead and several families traumatised.
He said the extension was aimed at sustaining security operations in the area, where recurring violence has continued to threaten lives, livelihoods and peaceful coexistence.
Mr Kefas condemned the killings, describing the incident as a painful loss for the affected families and the state .
“We have gathered to mourn those we have lost, support those affected, and agree on the actions required to protect our people,” the governor said.
He reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to protecting lives and property, assuring residents that those responsible for the attack would be identified, arrested and prosecuted.
The governor directed relevant authorities to account for missing persons, establish their whereabouts and support the affected individuals and families.
He also instructed security agencies to investigate the attackers’ movements and possible motives, including whether they were linked to other criminal activities.
Mr Kefas called for a coordinated security response to protect Binnari and neighbouring communities against further attacks.
He urged traditional rulers, ward and village heads, youths and farmers to provide credible information to support ongoing investigations and prevent further violence.
The governor also cautioned residents and media organisations against circulating unverified information that could heighten tension in the affected communities.
Karim-Lamido was previously designated a special area of security concern in January 2026 through Executive Order No. 1, following recurring communal clashes, bandit attacks and farmer-herder conflicts.
However, the latest attack on Binnari has renewed concerns about the effectiveness of existing security measures and the protection of vulnerable rural communities.
The police initially confirmed 10 deaths following the attack on 23 October. Subsequent reports indicated a higher death toll as more bodies were recovered from surrounding areas.
The governor expressed condolences to the bereaved families and the people of Binnari, assuring them of the government’s commitment to restoring peace and preventing further attacks.
He said the extended security designation would sustain attention on the area while the government worked to restore residents’ confidence and address the security challenges confronting the local government.
The government has also called for cooperation among community leaders, residents and security agencies to ensure lasting peace in Karim-Lamido.

title: NATO testing drones in combat operations in Ukraine against Russia — commander
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Drones manufactured in NATO countries are being tested in combat on the line of engagement and used in strikes deep inside Russian territory, Lieutenant General Apty Alaudinov, Deputy Chief of the Main Military-Political Directorate of the Russian Armed Forces and commander of the Akhmat special forces unit, said in an interview with TASS.
"We see that drones manufactured in all these countries, which are members of the NATO alliance, are being tested against us on the line of engagement," he said.
The Akhmat commander noted that these drones differ in type, capability, and flight range. According to him, drones are being deployed in large numbers into Ukrainian territory and tested at the front against Russian forces and equipment, as well as used to carry out strikes deep into Russian territory to cause maximum damage to cities, settlements, and civilian infrastructure.

title: Road to 2027: When Nigeria’s Politics Becomes a Battle for Survival
body: Iyobosa Uwugiaren writes that the killing of a Nigerian Democratic Congress supporter in Enugu State, killing of All Progressives Congress supporters in Ebonyi State, reported attacks on party offices, inflammatory political rhetoric and restrictions on opposition’s access to public facilities raise urgent questions about safety and fairness ahead of Nigeria’s 2027 general election. For a mother in Afa, a community in Udi Local Government Area of Enugu State, the death of her son, Ifeanyi Nwolie, means more than the pain of burying a loved one. She has also lost the person who, according to reports, regularly sent her money to help meet her needs. The support she depended on has been interrupted by a tragedy that brings the human cost of Nigeria’s increasingly hostile political environment into painful focus. Nwolie, a supporter of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), was reportedly shot during political activity on October 10, 2026. He was later buried in his hometown, where the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, arrived after travelling from the United Kingdom through Abuja to attend the funeral. Following the burial, Obi visited the bereaved mother and offered to provide the monthly financial support her son had ordinarily sent her for the 15-month period ending in December, 2027. The gesture offered compassion to a grieving family, but it could not undo the loss. Nor could it answer the question hanging over Nigeria’s approach to the next general election: why should supporting a political party expose anyone to the risk of losing his life? Nwolie’s death does not, by itself, establish a nationwide campaign of politically organised violence. The circumstances of his killing require a credible investigation. But the incident takes on wider significance alongside the reported killing of All Progressives Congress supporters in Ebonyi State, attack on the NDC secretariat in Benin City, Edo State; inflammatory rhetoric attributed to former Deputy President of the Senate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, at a rally in Warri, Delta State; concerns about violence in parts of northern Nigeria; and reports that opposition parties in different states are being prevented from using public spaces and facilities for campaign activities. In Ebonyi State, two suspected political thugs of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) were also killed after they attacked the convoy of the NDC candidate for Ebonyi State House of Assembly, Ezza South Constituency, Mr Rollins Offia Nwali. Security sources told mewsmen in the state that security details attached to the NDC candidate, after securing the safety of Nwali and his team, engaged the hoodlums, who were allegedly armed with AK-47 rifles and pump-action guns. The security operatives returned fire, killing one of the attackers at the scene, while the second reportedly died in the hospital. Together, these developments raise a fundamental question: will Nigerians approach the 2027 election as citizens exercising their democratic rights or as political participants navigating fear, exclusion and unequal opportunities? The threat is not limited to physical violence. When supporters face intimidation and opposition parties struggle to access public venues, the democratic space can narrow long before voting begins. Experts have argued that democracy requires political opponents to compete through ideas, policies, persuasion and votes. Electorate should be free to support candidates without fearing attacks or intimidation. In fact, as argued by a political scientist, Robert A. Dahl, in his seminal work ‘Polyarchy: Participation and Opposition,’ he identifies political contestation and citizen participation as essential dimensions of democracy. His framework emphasises the importance of freedom of expression and association, the right to vote, and the opportunity for political leaders to compete for public support. In particular, the circumstances surrounding Nwolie’s death demand an unbiased investigation. If evidence establishes that he was targeted because of his political affiliation or participation, his killing would represent a grave assault on democratic freedom. The consequences of the killings, ahead of 2027 general election, extend beyond the immediate victims. A supporters’ death leaves relatives and friends grieving; where the persons also provided financial assistance, the families may face additional hardship. Obi’s reported offer to support Nwolie’s mother highlights a dimension of political violence that often receives less attention: its consequences continue long after the funeral. As campaigns build up, the fear of attacks could discourage citizens from attending rallies, joining political organisations or openly expressing their preferences. The challenge for the security authorities and other stakeholders is to ensure that political disagreements do not become threats to personal safety. At a recent political rally in Warri, Delta State, Senator Omo-Agege reportedly urged people to kill anyone attempting to rig an election, using the phrase, “Rig and die.” Yes, opposing electoral malpractice is a legitimate democratic responsibility. Vote-rigging and deliberate manipulation of results deserve investigation and lawful punishment. But some argue safely that defending electoral integrity is different from encouraging people to take the law into their own hands. To be sure, in a polarised environment, aggressive political language can be interpreted as permission to intimidate opponents or engage in violence. Leaders should instead urge supporters to document suspected electoral offences, report them to the appropriate authorities and pursue lawful remedies. Where statements potentially constitute unlawful incitement, competent authorities should investigate impartially, respecting freedom of expression and the law. Political leaders must recognise that defending the ballot cannot mean disregarding the value of human life. Unfolding events suggest that the challenge may extend beyond physical attacks. Reports that opposition parties are being prevented from using public spaces and facilities for campaign activities in different states raise questions about whether parties enjoy a fair opportunity to reach voters. Public halls, open grounds and other government-controlled venues can be important campaign resources, particularly for parties unable to afford expensive private alternatives. If access is selectively denied, political competition becomes uneven before voting begins. Agree that not every refusal to grant access constitutes political persecution. Genuine safety concerns, scheduling conflicts, maintenance requirements and legitimate regulations may justify restrictions. The central issue is whether authorities apply transparent, consistent rules or use administrative decisions to disadvantage political opponents. Where governing parties receive access to venues while comparable opposition applications are rejected without credible explanation, public confidence in the fairness of the process is undermined. That may be the importance of the message that the presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC), Omoyele Sowore, sent recently when he applied to use the Presidential Villa for the inauguration of his campaign council. Within the democratic space, this form of exclusion can be less visible than physical violence but equally consequential for political participation. A party may be legally registered and permitted to contest an election, yet struggle to organise meetings, engage communities or present its programme because access to public facilities is restricted. It may be helpful if state governments and local authorities publish clear rules for allocating public venues, provide written reasons for refusals and establish accessible review procedures. Public facilities are maintained with public resources and taxpayers money, and should not become instruments of partisan advantage. The reported attack on the NDC secretariat in Benin City, with office equipment allegedly carted away, may have added to concerns about the security of political organisations. Party offices support campaign coordination, volunteer mobilisation and engagement with communities. An attack can disrupt these activities, frighten members and discourage participation. The security agencies should investigate the incident to establish what happened, identify those responsible and determine whether the attack was politically motivated. Where criminal responsibility is established, appropriate legal consequences should follow. A consistent response matters. Attacks on opposition organisations must not be ignored because of the identity of the victims, just as allegations against members of governing parties must not be dismissed on political grounds. Concerns about electoral violence in northern Nigeria have also added urgency to the debate. Political leaders and their supporters must resist the temptation to assign blame before facts are established. Credible reporting, impartial investigation and transparent communication are essential to distinguishing verified incidents from partisan allegations. The objective should be to protect citizens, establish responsibility and prevent violence from spreading. The implications are clear. Violence can deter citizens from campaigning or expressing political preferences. Unequal access to public venues can give governing parties practical advantages. Failure to investigate attacks can reinforce perceptions of impunity, while unresolved grievances may heighten tensions after results are announced. These risks do not make a violent or illegitimate election inevitable. They make early intervention essential. The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) should work with political parties, civil society and security agencies to strengthen reporting and monitoring of electoral intimidation. Although INEC cannot resolve every dispute over public facilities, it can raise concerns about barriers to fair political participation. The Nigeria Police Force and other relevant security agencies must investigate reported attacks impartially, protect political gatherings and respond to credible threats. State governments and local authorities must ensure that public venues are allocated according to neutral criteria, with clear explanations where applications are refused. Political parties also have responsibilities. They must discipline members who threaten opponents, reject violence within their ranks and instruct supporters to pursue grievances through lawful channels. Civil society organisations and the media should document incidents and scrutinise decisions that may restrict political participation. The test is whether these institutions act before the campaign reaches its most intense phase, rather than waiting until intimidation or violence has already disrupted the process. Meanwhile, Obi’s reported offer to support Nwolie’s mother recognises the financial consequences of losing a son who contributed to her upkeep. It is a compassionate response, but private generosity cannot replace public accountability. The questions surrounding Nwolie’s death remain urgent: who shot him, what led to the incident, and will those responsible be identified and brought to justice? A credible investigation would provide the family with more than expressions of sympathy. It would demonstrate that political affiliation does not place anyone beyond the protection of the law. The same principle applies to attacks on party offices and restrictions on campaign venues. Authorities must establish the facts, explain their decisions and ensure that political opponents can organise without intimidation or arbitrary obstruction. For the mother in Afa, the money Obi has offered may help meet some of the needs her son once provided for. It cannot bring him home. Her loss should not become another campaign talking point that disappears when political attention shifts elsewhere. Nigeria’s next election should be remembered for the choices voters made, not for the citizens who were killed, intimidated or silenced before they could make them. For Nwolie’s mother, the first measure of justice is straightforward: establish the truth about her son’s death and hold those responsible accountable.

title: El Niño tightens grip on Pacific as authorities warn of drought and extreme weather
body: APIA, 26 OCTOBER 2026 (PMN) — Climate scientists indicate El Niño conditions are strengthening across the central Pacific, raising concerns about below-normal rainfall, higher temperatures and increased drought risk in many island nations. El Niño is a natural climate pattern that occurs when sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern Pacific Ocean become warmer than average, affecting wider weather patterns. In Sāmoa, the Meteorology Division of the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment is urging government agencies, businesses, communities and households to prepare for prolonged dry conditions. Recommended measures include conserving water, protecting crops and livestock, avoiding unnecessary burning during dry conditions and safeguarding vulnerable people from heat-related illnesses. The Meteorological Division says the conditions could place pressure on water supplies, agriculture, public health, energy production and the natural environment. “El Niño also influences tropical cyclone activity across the Southwest Pacific, and Sāmoa faces an elevated risk of tropical cyclone impacts during the 2026-2027 cyclone season.” The Division says rainfall has steadily declined. “Most meteorological observation stations in July recorded normal to below-normal rainfall, followed by well-below-normal rainfall in August, making it one of the driest months on record in Sāmoa. September rainfall ranged from normal to below normal,” the statement said. As Sāmoa approaches the 2026-2027 tropical cyclone season, communities are being urged to remain prepared for severe weather and tropical cyclones regardless of prevailing El Niño conditions. In Palau, Island Times has reported the country has officially entered drought conditions and is under Stage One of its National Drought Action Plan. Maria Ngemaes, from Palau’s National Weather Service, says there has also been little to no rainfall recently, and the conditions could continue through early next year. The Solomon Islands Meteorological Service this week issued its first nationwide Meteorological Drought Warning, with prolonged dry conditions affecting all provinces. According to an Island Sun report Billy Veo, Premier of the Western Province, says the provincial government has requested additional support, including ten 3,000-litre water tanks to support water distribution across Gizo. “Currently, we have only one water truck that is functioning. The other one requires repairs, so we are requesting two additional water trucks from the national government. “The plan is for the water trucks to refill the tanks at scheduled times so that people can access water.” In a statement, climate expert Exsley Taloiburi says early planning is crucial to minimise humanitarian, economic, water and food security impacts. “The business-as-usual reactive responses are insufficient.” He says the latest El Niño system demands proactive, decisive political action that updates lessons from previous weather events for a hotter climate, tighter aid environment and a larger population. Government, meteorological services and disaster authorities in the Pacific are monitoring conditions and preparing response measures to reduce the impacts of the prolonged climate event…. PACNEWS The post El Niño tightens grip on Pacific as authorities warn of drought and extreme weather appeared first on Island Times News .

title: Sanyo-Olu, Bamidele, Oni, Others Mourn Alhaja Taibat Bakare
body: The death of Alhaja Taibat Amope Bakare, Iya Sunnah General of Ansar-ud-Deen in Ekiti State, has been described as a colossal loss to Orun and Igbemo-Ekiti, Ekiti State and the Muslim community. Lagos State Governor, Mr. Babajide Sanwo-Olu, made this known when he led a delegation of prominent dignitaries on a condolence visit to the family of the late Alhaja Bakare in Igbemo-Ekiti. In his condolence message, Sanwo-Olu urged the family to sustain the legacies of the deceased, who served as the Iya Sunnah General of Ansar-ud-Deen in Ekiti State until her demise. He described the late matriarch as a devout Muslim who remained committed to the service of Allah throughout her lifetime. Other dignitaries on the governor’s entourage included the Deputy Governor of Enugu State, Ifeanyi Ossai, and Senator Tokunbo Abiru, alongside other government officials. Similarly, the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate in the last Osun State gubernatorial election, Asiwaju Munirudeen Bola Oyebamiji (AMBO) visited the Bakare family to commiserate with them over their loss. Oyebamiji described the late Alhaja Bakare as a woman who actively promoted Islamic teachings and supported developmental projects through her charitable contributions. In the same vein, former Ekiti State Governor, Asiwaju Segun Oni, urged the family to take solace in God, describing the death of the late matriarch as a transition to glory. He noted that her contributions to the family, religious community and society would continue to speak for her, urging her children and other family members to preserve and institutionalise the legacies she left behind. Meanwhile, the Senate Leader, Senator Michael Opeyemi Bamidele, also led a separate delegation to the bereaved family to express his condolences and offer support during the period of mourning. Members of his delegation included Hon. Steven Fatoba, member of the House of Representatives; Hon. Bolaji Egbeyemi, Deputy Speaker of the Ekiti State House of Assembly; and Chief Remi Oguntuase, alongside other government functionaries. Senator Bamidele prayed to Almighty Allah to grant the deceased eternal rest and give the family the fortitude to bear the loss. Chief Adeniyi Akintola, SAN, recalled his visit to Alhaja shortly before her passing and prayed that Almighty Allah grant her Aljanat Firdaus. The children of the deceased, Alhaji Kola Bakare, Group CEO of Country Petrolite and Gas, and Tajudeen Bakare, Divisional Executive, Business Support, Wema Bank, expressed appreciation to all the visiting dignitaries for creating time in view of the distance and their very busy schedule and for the show of love, their prayers and support for the family.

title: Vladimir Ivic urges focus as Al Ain surge ahead in Asian Champions League
body: Vladimir Ivic says repairing Al Ain’s domestic form remains his top priority after they extended their perfect start in the AFC Champions League Elite. The UAE champions grabbed attention across the continent when they started the competition with a 4-0 thrashing of Cristiano Ronaldo’s Al Nassr last month. They continued their 100 per cent start to the tournament after three games with a 2-1 win over Iran Pro League side Tractor at Hazza Bin Zayed Stadium on Monday night. While they have been sweeping all before them in continental football, their domestic form has dipped of late. It was almost impossible to maintain the standards they had been setting. The Garden City club went undefeated on their way to winning a domestic double last season. Their unbeaten run in the league was halted at 38 games when Shabab Al Ahli beat them earlier this month. The same side also ended their reign as President’s Cup holders. Shabab Al Ahli, who are also in Champions League action against Iranian opposition – Esteghlal – on Tuesday night – beat them 3-2 on Thursday. Skill, vision, delivery 🎯 Yahya Ben Khaleq serves it up for Houssine Rahimi! #ACLElite | #WorldClassAssist | @qatarairways pic.twitter.com/9JqTFAwVbZ — #ACLElite | #ACLTwo (@TheAFCCL) October 26, 2026 The effects of that gruelling extra-time loss were apparent in Al Ain's laboured win over Tractor. Missing their injured talisman Soufiane Rahimi , Al Ain managed to do just enough, with goals from Rami Rabia and Houssine Rahimi being enough for the three points. “It was a very, very tough game for both teams because both teams played on Thursday,” Ivic, the Al Ain coach, said. “Everyone who watched this game could understand, especially in the last 10-15 minutes, it was very, very tough to run, to mark, and easy to lose concentration. “For us we are happy to get three points. I believe that we were the better team and congrats to my guys as they did a professional performance.” The coach acknowledged that the full extent of Soufiane's injury remains unclear. The Morocco striker, who was the player of the tournament when Al Ain were champions of Asia three seasons ago, was in tears as he went off with a leg injury late in the game against Shabab Al Ahli on Thursday. It has been speculated he could be out for the rest of 2026, but Ivic said the prognosis will only be established in the next few days. He says the workload has been testing for his players. “The previous game in the cup [the 3-2 loss to Shabab Al Ahli] was 140 minutes, not 120,” Ivic said. “With the GPS what we know exactly; they played 140 minutes three four days ago, so you can imagine how much energy my players spent. “That’s two games, not one and a half games. It's very difficult. These two competitions are a priority. “We know we have an added cup. We know that we have two Super Cups [domestic and UAE-Qatar] to play, and we have a lot of games in front of us. But for all of us, priority is [UAE Pro League and] Champions League.”

title: Police close entry, exit to Eilat as Election Day storm brings flood risk along Routes 40,12,13
body: Police opened Route 6 northbound and Route 444 near Ben Shemen in central Israel after forest fires broke out nearby on Wednesday and closed them, according to an announcement from the Central District Israel Fire and Rescue Authority.Firefighters and Central District Police forces brought the fires under control on Wednesday afternoon. "Firefighters operated with determination in challenging terrain conditions and stopped the fire from spreading toward residential areas and major roads," Deputy Fire Commissioner Oz Cohen said."As of now, we have achieved full control and containment across all sectors. Crews will remain at the scene for the next several hours until final extinguishing operations are completed and the scene is fully cleared. The public is asked to remain vigilant and follow fire safety instructions," Cohen added.Police also closed all roads leading to and from Eilat and multiple roads in southern Israel until further notice, as rainfall has caused flooding and the risk of flash floods in the region on Election Day.Police have closed Route 90 to vehicle traffic due to flooding at Arava Junction.Earlier on Tuesday, it was announced that Route 40 is closed between Tzihor Junction and Mitzpe Ramon, and Route 13 is closed between Menuha Junction and Tzihor Junction.Despite the closures, those traveling to Ramon Airport will be allowed to exit Eilat.Southern District officers remain deployed across the south and are conducting ongoing situational assessments, police said, to protect the public, prevent loss of life, and keep disruption to daily life to a minimum. Officers from the Southern District and the National Traffic Police have been deployed along the roads to direct traffic. Police urged the public to plan trips in advance, check road conditions, and follow officers' instructions, and warned drivers not to cross flooded roads or enter flood zones.Rain was forecast to start in the southern Negev and quickly spread across large parts of southern Israel, including the Negev Highlands, the Arava, and the Dead Sea area. Heavy rain is expected at times, accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning, wind gusts, and even hail.Flooding may lead to road closures in southern IsraelFurther flooding is possible in streams in the southern Negev, the Arava, the Judean Desert, and the Dead Sea area. The public has been warned to stay away from streambeds, as conditions could be life-threatening.Police previously warned of possible additional road closures in the area on Election Day because of significant rain expected between 2 p.m. and 8 p.m. In addition, all hiking sites between Beersheba and Eilat will be closed for the duration of the storm.Heavy rain has also started in Jerusalem.

title: EM&E strengthening international outreach
body:
The Spanish company EM&E Group, headquartered in Madrid, is participating in Afridex 2026 this week with an eye on strengthening its international outreach towards key players in Africa’s defence sector.
Backed by solid experience in engineering and precision mechanical manufacturing since 1989, the EM&E Group specialises in the design, development, and manufacture of advanced defence and security systems.
“We regard Afridex 2026 as an opportunity to foster dialogue within the context of evolving operational needs and the growing importance of technological innovation,” the company said.
EM&E combines proprietary technology with a focus on reliability, operational effectiveness, and adaptation to different platforms and mission requirements, it said. Its EMOC 120 and 81 mm mortar carrier systems, combining high mobility with heavy firepower, underscore the company’s aim for technologies that respond to current challenges in the defence arena.
The system is designed to provide indirect fire capability from high-mobility vehicles, facilitating ‘shoot-and-scoot’ tactics. It can be deployed in less than 20 seconds for the 120 mm version and 15 seconds for the 81 mm version – a significant advantage to reduce exposure time to potential threats.
It incorporates an advanced recoil management system that enables stable firing from the very first moment and is compatible with EM&E Group’s smart ammunition, featuring a CEP (circular error probable) of 10 meters.
According to the company, the system’s open architecture facilitates integration into various land platforms.
“Another of our strategic areas is the fight against hostile drones, for which we offer the ODIN family C-UAS (counter-unmanned aircraft systems),” EM&E Group stated.
Its new ODIN 6×6 anti-drone system was presented at Eurosatory, the world’s leading defence and aerospace exhibition in Paris earlier this year.
The ODIN anti-drone solution integrates different technologies to address the full threat cycle, from detection and identification to neutralisation. Thanks to the different configurations available, it is highly adaptable and can be tailored to specific customer needs.
According to the company, the ODIN-I multi-sensor and multi-factor system can be mounted on a military support vehicle or a towed platform for easy deployment in the field. In function, it serves as protection against short-range ground, air, and maritime threats with proven high operational precision.
The ODIN-L, integrated into a mobile station, combines sensors, effectors, and a command and control system, allowing it to be rapidly deployed and adapted to various operational scenarios. This C-UAS system is capable of protecting both fixed and temporary facilities, as well as troops deployed in operational zones, thanks to various configurations according to customer needs, ranging from highly mobile solutions to permanent or temporary rapid-deployment solutions.
At Afridex 2026, EM&E Group is also showing some of its remote weapon stations for land and naval platforms.
With their modular design to allow for both day and night operations, these solutions reduce direct exposure of the operators while contributing to improving situational awareness and response capability.
“All of these capabilities reflect EM&E Group’s commitment to engineering, technological development, and the adaptation of solutions to the requirements of different operational environments,” the company affirmed. “With our presence here at Afridex 2026, we continue to advance our internationalisation strategy and reaffirm our interest in driving long-term relationships to collaborate with others in the defence and security spheres.”
To further explore Afridex, the show daily magazine is available here .

title: Atiku’s campaign challenges Shettima over Tinubu’s school records
body:
Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar’s presidential campaign has challenged Vice President Kashim Shettima to explain discrepancies it alleged in President Bola Tinubu’s educational records, after Tinubu criticised Atiku’s schooling.
The exchange followed Mr Shettima’s remarks at the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit in Abuja on Monday, where he criticised Atiku’s proposal to subsidise domestically refined petrol and questioned his qualifications to manage Nigeria’s economy.
Referring to Atiku’s training at the Kano School of Hygiene, the vice president said the former vice president lacked the skills to govern a modern economy. He also questioned Atiku’s knowledge of public health, suggesting that he would struggle to distinguish between influenza and Ebola.
In a statement issued the same day, the Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) Presidential Campaign Council, Phrank Shaibu, accused Mr Shettima of mocking Atiku’s educational background.
“What, exactly, is shameful about Atiku’s education? He completed secondary school, pursued further training and built a life through work,” he said.
Mr Shaibu questioned why a document associated with Mr Tinubu’s Chicago State University records listed Government College Lagos in 1970, although the institution was reportedly established in 1974.
“If Shettima wants to examine school records, he should begin with the man he serves,” he said.
The campaign also referred to the name “Tinubu Bola Adekunle” on an NYSC certificate submitted among the President’s electoral documents, as well as previous legal disputes over his academic history.
The reference to Government College Lagos has been in earlier public controversy. However, the disputed entry does not establish that Mr Tinubu forged his credentials.
The campaign also rejected Mr Shettima’s criticism of Atiku’s proposal for a targeted subsidy on petrol refined in Nigeria.
Atiku has proposed a capped subsidy arrangement subject to independent auditing, which his campaign says would differ from the previous petrol subsidy system.
“If Shettima thinks it cannot be funded, he should show his figures and offer a better way to lower prices,” Mr Shaibu said.
He accused the Tinubu administration of failing to ease the cost of food, transport and fuel.

title: NovaPay increases volume of transfers by 36% in nine months of 2026, number by 12%
body:
The volume of transfers through the international financial service NovaPay (trademark NovaPay) in January-September 2026 grew by 36% compared with the same period of 2025, to UAH 598.7 billion, the company said in a statement on Monday.
According to it, the number of transfers rose by 12%, to 388 million.
"The nine-month results confirm that our solutions are increasingly in demand and that customers are making more active use of digital financial tools. It is important for us not only to increase transaction volumes but also to constantly improve the customer experience, offering new opportunities and convenient solutions," NovaPay CEO Ihor Prykhodko is quoted as saying in the press release.
The financial service noted that in nine months of this year the company paid UAH 1.47 billion in taxes and fees, which is 32% more than in the same period last year.
As reported, in the first half of 2026 NovaPay increased the volume of transfers by 41% compared with the same period of 2025, to UAH 391 billion, while their number rose by 12%, to 258 million.
NovaPay was founded in 2001 as an international financial service that is part of the Nova group (Nova Poshta) and provides financial services online and offline at Nova Poshta branches. In 2023 it became the first non-bank financial institution in Ukraine to obtain an extended license from the National Bank of Ukraine (NBU), which made it possible to open accounts and issue cards, and at the end of last year it became the first non-bank to launch its own financial app with a wide range of financial services.
According to the National Bank of Ukraine, the company accounts for about 22.7% of the total volume of domestic money transfers.

title: Kano Fire Service recovers body of drowned man
body:
The Kano State Fire Service has recovered the body of a 42-year-old man, Sani Kwaru, who fell into an open water reservoir in the Dan Agundi area of the Kano metropolis.
The incident occurred at about 1 p.m. and drew an emergency response after a resident, Hamisu Muhammad, raised an alert.
“At about 13:00 hours, the Kano State Fire Service received a distress call from Hamisu Muhammad reporting that a young man had fallen into open water at Dan Agundi,” the Kano State Fire Service spokesman, Kabiru Jafar, stated in a statement on Monday.
“Upon receiving the distress call, our team immediately mobilised to the scene of the incident.”
“The rescue team launched a search operation upon arrival and retrieved the victim, identified as Sani Uba Kwaru, from the water in an unconscious state”, Mr Jafar said.
He added that following the tragic event, the fire service cautioned residents against unsafe activities around unprotected water bodies.
“The Kano State Fire Service urges members of the public to exercise caution around open water and other potentially dangerous areas,” Mr Jafar added.

title: How you can access free public transportation to get to polling booths on Election Day - explainer
body: Free intercity public transportation is available across Israel on Tuesday, Election Day for the 26th Knesset, with the benefit extending to all passengers, not just eligible voters, according to Walla. The service is funded by the Central Elections Committee.Free travel began at 8 p.m. on Monday and will continue until public transportation services conclude Tuesday night.The benefit applies to about 660 intercity bus routes longer than 15 kilometers, up from 600 routes during the 2022 elections, as well as all Israel Railways lines.However, city buses, light rail services, the Metronit bus rapid transit system, and Haifa's Carmelit underground railway will continue to charge regular fares.Passengers can check whether a specific intercity bus route is included in the arrangement by calling the Transportation Ministry's information hotline at \*8787.How can passengers travel for free?Intercity buses: Passengers can board eligible buses free of charge without presenting identification, obtaining a ticket, or validating a Rav-Kav public transportation card.Israel Railways: Passengers must obtain a special paper ticket from station ticket counters or ticket machines. To avoid unnecessary charges, they should not use tickets or passes loaded onto their Rav-Kav cards or public transportation apps.Additional trains on Jerusalem-Tel Aviv routeDue to anticipated demand, Israel Railways will run three trains per hour in each direction between Jerusalem's Yitzhak Navon Station and Tel Aviv from noon until 8 p.m. Tuesday, up from the usual two trains per hour.Some of the additional services will begin and end at Tel Aviv's HaHagana Station.In addition, police have restricted the number of passengers traveling to and from Jerusalem. Passengers are therefore required to obtain a personal travel voucher in advance for their selected train.Due to expected congestion, railway staff will enforce the voucher requirement. Vouchers can be obtained free of charge through the Israel Railways website.Will travel to Eilat also be free?Different eligibility requirements apply to passengers traveling to and from Eilat.Free travel on these routes is subject to an eligibility check based on the passenger's registered residential address and advance registration through Egged's information center at \*2800.Rail passenger numbers could break 2022 election recordDuring the previous elections for the 25th Knesset on November 1, 2022, Israel Railways recorded a roughly 33% increase in passenger numbers, rising from 249,146 on a typical weekday to 331,706 on Election Day.That record is expected to be broken this year.The free transportation initiative is estimated to cost NIS 3.5 million and will be funded by the Central Elections Committee through the Transportation Ministry.Passengers are advised to check updated schedules and service changes through the Israel Railways website, its official app, the \*5770 information hotline, or the railway's official WhatsApp channel.

title: PHP Foundation ‘under-funded’ with only 1 full-time staff member, director says
body: AMSTERDAM, The Netherlands – The discovery of two serious flaws in PHP this week set off a global scramble to keep websites safe from hackers , showing just how critical the three-decade-old open-source programming language is to the internet. Yet the nonprofit foundation that supports PHP, which may underpin up to 70% of sites globally, operates on a shoestring budget. “We have one full-time staff member (that’s me) and 14 mostly part-time contractors,” Executive Director Elizabeth Barron of the PHP Foundation said via email in an interview on Friday, October 23. Board members are unpaid volunteers, and funding comes from donations and grants. The foundation works with outside researchers and companies, including OpenAI and cybersecurity firms Wiz and Calif, to investigate security flaws and coordinate fixes, including Wednesday’s patches. While Web security company Cloudflare has reported millions of hacking attempts, Barron said the foundation had no evidence hackers were able to exploit the vulnerabilities before they were disclosed, or on sites that have been patched. “We received no further indication from OpenAI, Wiz or Calif, with whom we’re working closely on this issue, regarding any issues on patched systems,” she said. Artificial intelligence has proved both a help and a burden to the foundation. It helped researchers find the flaws, which had been present for a decade, and Barron said it made programmers more efficient. However, it is also increasing maintainers’ workloads. The PHP project is receiving nearly twice as many proposed code changes as a year ago, “yet the number of contributors hasn’t doubled,” she said. Reviewing contributions and bug reports requires “a massive amount of human input and experience.” Recent events have shown how heavily companies and governments rely on PHP, Barron said. “Given that reliance, it is clear that PHP is incredibly under-funded.” – Rappler.com

title: Israel votes in crucial election, Jordan retaliates in Syria and Harry Kane wins Ballon d'Or
body: In today’s episode of Trending Middle East , Israel goes to the polls in a keenly contested election that will determine whether Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu remains in power. Former general Gadi Eisenkot is his strongest challenger, with Arab voter turnout expected to play an important role in the result. Jordan carries out strikes on southern Syria in retaliation for a deadly church attack in Karak that killed nine people. Syrian authorities say at least seven were killed in the strikes, while Damascus disputes Jordan's claim that the operation was co-ordinated between the countries. Meanwhile, Egypt's parliament authorises President Abdel Fattah El Sisi to send troops to defend Saudi Arabia, although no deployment has been announced and Cairo says it will act only if Riyadh requests assistance. In the UAE, US investment company Apollo agrees to take a minority stake in Abu Dhabi's Mubadala Capital, with other strategic investors expected to commit funds to the firm's investment strategies.
