title: Yisrael Beytenu files complaint against Shas distributing kippot amid widespread ballot sabotage
body: Yisrael Beytenu filed a petition with the chairman of the Central Elections Committee (CEC) on Tuesday, demanding an immediate halt to the distribution of kippot bearing the image and name of the late Rabbi Ovadia Yosef outside a polling station in Afula.According to the party, the kippot also featured the inscription "I have chosen the path of faith."Yisrael Beytenu argued that the distribution constituted prohibited election campaigning and the unlawful distribution of gifts to voters."The law applies to everyone, including Shas," Yisrael Beytenu said in a statement.Reservists-Economic Party report missing, defaced ballotsThe Reservists and Economic Party filed a complaint with the CEC on Tuesday following reports of missing and defaced ballot slips at several polling stations across Israel.According to the party, ballot slips bearing its designated voting symbol were missing from several polling stations, while others had been damaged or marked with pens."After Likud's fake news campaign, we received numerous complaints about our ballot slips being defaced or removed," party chairman Yoaz Hendel said.Yashar party claims systematic attempt to disrupt votingGadi Eisenkot's Yashar party also filed a complaint with the Central Elections Committee on Tuesday over suspicions of a systematic attempt to disrupt voting for the party and undermine election integrity, following reports of ballot tampering at polling stations across Israel.According to the party, several incidents were identified in which ballot slips marked "Derech," the party's designated voting symbol, were missing, damaged, or turned over inside voting booths.The party said it had received a series of serious reports from polling stations nationwide concerning the disappearance, damage, and marking of its ballot slips in ways that could result in votes being disqualified."Anyone who tries to steal ballot slips is trying to steal the election. This is a serious violation of election integrity and the fundamental right of Israeli citizens to vote," the party said.Religious Zionist Party alleges deliberate ballot damageEarlier on Election Day, the Religious Zionist Party claimed they had received numerous reports that ballot slips belonging to the party and Likud had been deliberately damaged at several polling stations across Israel, potentially rendering them invalid.According to reports received by the party's election-day headquarters, small tears had been made along the edges of ballot slips from both parties, raising concerns that votes cast using those slips could be disqualified.The party called on the Central Elections Committee to intervene immediately and instruct election integrity inspectors at polling stations to conduct frequent checks of ballot slips to ensure they remain valid.Yisrael Beytenu and People of Israel say slips missingYisrael Beytenu and People of Israel filed separate complaints with the Central Elections Committee on Tuesday after receiving reports that their ballot slips were missing at several stations after voting began in Israel's 26th Knesset election.According to a statement issued by Yisrael Beytenu, ballot slips bearing its electoral symbol were allegedly not placed at polling station No. 45, located at 10 Gamla Street in Kiryat Ono, when voting opened.The Central Elections Committee released a statement clarifying that the station in question had ballots for the party.Similarly, People of Israel reported that the party's ballot slips were missing, and its headquarters received reports from both military and civilian polling stations that its ballot slips had been turned over, making them appear to be blank voting slips.Haredi Public ballots missing, hidden, voters sayVoters said that ballots for the Haredi Public party had been removed from polling stations in Bnei Brak, Modi'in Illit and Jerusalem, with the Civil Election Watch organization saying it had received 23 reports regarding ballots being removed in entire stacks or hidden beneath ballots of other parties, Kan News reported on Tuesday. According to the report, voters could not find ballots for the party at their polling stations, and had to request them from election officials. In Modi'in Illit, one voter said the party's ballots had been hidden beneath those of other parties. "A stack of Haredi Public ballots disappeared instantly," an election observer at Modi'in Illit said, according to Kan. A Bnei Brak voter expressed concern that if voters are forced to request the correct ballots to be provided or found as his wife did, not every woman will do so. "Not every woman will feel comfortable asking polling station officials, all of whom are Haredi, why ballots are missing."B'Yachad files claims that Netanyahu engaged in electioneering, Likud reps tracked votersThe B'Yachad party, led by former prime minister Naftali Bennett, submitted an appeal to the CEC accusing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of illegal electioneering after Netanyahu spoke on haredi (ultra-Orthodox) radio program Kol Barama and urged the public to vote for Likud.Later on Tuesday, B'Yachad said it had received reports from its representatives on the ground that the Elector app was being used at polling stations in a moshav in the Lower Galilee. The party did not name the moshav.Following the reports, the party filed a second complaint with the Central Elections Committee. Elections Committee rejects first B'Yachad claim The Central Elections Committee declared that claims circulating regarding Likud representatives in polling booths across the country illegally tracking voters using an app were false after B'Yachad issued a formal complaint shortly after Election Day kicked off.“An isolated report was received concerning photography at a polling station in Moshav Yarhiv. The polling station committee member who took the photographs understood her mistake after the guidelines were explained to her and stopped taking pictures," the CEC stated.“The committee reiterates that party representatives at polling stations are prohibited from providing their parties with information about whether an individual has arrived at a polling station or cast a ballot, including through apps. These guidelines are binding on all parties and their representatives.”The Likud party denied any wrongdoing, stating that the party has set up booths outside of polling stations and that voters can volunteer the relevant information."This has nothing to do with the polling station 'representatives,' to whom voters are required to identify themselves,” the party stated.Polls opened at 7 a.m. Tuesday at 12,018 polling stations for the country's 7,331,981 eligible voters, with 36 lists competing for the Knesset's 120 seats. Neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc nor the opposition is assured of a majority, and Netanyahu will remain caretaker prime minister until a new government is sworn in, whatever the outcome.

title: Marc Rowan on why Apollo has taken a $1 billion stake in Mubadala Capital
body: Apollo Global Management has invested more than $1 billion in Mubadala Capital as it aims to boost the Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth fund's expansion in North America, Apollo's chief executive has said. The investment, which gives New York-based Apollo a 10 per cent stake in Mubadala Capital, is part of its strategy to partner with "other like-minded asset managers who we respect and have economic alignment that is good for them and good for us", Marc Rowan exclusively told The National in an interview in Abu Dhabi. "Mubadala is, among the sovereign funds, probably the most advanced in the creation of its own asset manager, and this is a chance for us to help them accelerate their growth, particularly in North America," he said. Apollo's investment in Mubadala is "a little over a billion dollars", Mr Rowan added. Other strategic investors will also join as minority shareholders in Mubadala Capital , with an expected commitment of $5 billion to the firm’s investment strategies. Apollo, which has about $1.05 trillion in assets under management, is also planning to increase the scale of its investment in the UAE, while describing its competition with Mubadala as "healthy" and its relationship with Mubadala's chief executive, Khaldoon Al Mubarak, as having a healthy level of "respect". Apollo has maintained close ties with Mubadala Investment Company in recent years, including a $2.5 billion private credit joint venture and a series of financing partnerships. Abu Dhabi developer Aldar Properties earlier this year raised $1 billion in funding from Apollo to support its growth . The relationship forms part of the Abu Dhabi sovereign investor's efforts to expand its global investment network and deepen partnerships with major international asset managers. "The asset management business is incredibly competitive and the notion that it's a zero-sum game, I think, is a false notion. We're all friends and competitors, so I look at our business more broadly," Mr Rowan said. "We power competitive asset managers and, with Mubadala, we get to power someone who is a partner, and they will build an asset management competitor to what we do. All good." 'A trillion dollars for infrastructure' Mr Rowan said Apollo was confident about doing more business in the UAE. Although he acknowledged lingering risks in the region as a result of geopolitical conflicts, he said that businesses had been able to adapt. "You are going to see us ramp up our activity here tremendously. It goes to this whole notion of what is risk. Is it riskier today here, or was it riskier a year ago? Common sense says it's riskier today," Mr Rowan said. "[But] everyone has adapted to the situation. We now know what the outcome is. It doesn't mean there won't be continued hostilities, but in terms of the unknown, we have less risk today than we did a year ago." Mr Rowan also expects countries in the region to spend about $1 trillion "hardening" their infrastructure, building alternative routes, transport systems and "all of the other things that this level of hostility has now pointed out need to be done". Those regional investments will also include ventures into artificial intelligence, which makes the region "so dynamic", he said. "We want to be a part of all of it. That doesn't mean we will do all of it because the scale of capital is beyond anything one firm or one organisation can do," he said. "What we're seeing in the region is a recognition that the capital needed to do everything that these countries need to do will have to be global capital." Pragmatic on AI Last week, Citadel chief executive Ken Griffin and Blackstone president Jon Gray gave contrasting views on AI. Mr Griffin said the sector was "almost certainly" in a bubble, while Mr Gray continues to bet big on the technology, taking up stakes in OpenAI and building a $200-billion data centre portfolio. Mr Rowan, however, sits in the middle. He said both arguments can be true, noting how the dynamics of the AI market are balancing themselves. "We are seeing unbelievable demand for compute, particularly in a supply-constrained market in the short term, and to the extent we get regulation and we have anti-data centre sentiment, those people who hold existing powered assets are going to see their assets go up in value because what they are able to provide is something that's in short supply," Mr Rowan said. "Jon is right on that, at least for the foreseeable future ... the valuation at which someone is willing to pay reflects their bet not only on what's happening currently, but that this will continue in the future," he added. Meanwhile, as interest rates and the cost of capital have been going up, the market has yet to go through a correction, which is what has historically happened, Mr Rowan said. "And on that side, I think Ken is stating the obvious. We have not seen the normal economic behaviour associated with this."

title: JetBlue revenue jumps 21% but airline still loses US$257 million
body:
JetBlue Airways increased revenue by 21.1% in the third quarter of 2026 despite operating only slightly more capacity, but the improvement was not enough to prevent the U.S. carrier from posting a US$257 million net loss.
Revenue reached US$2.81 billion, up from US$2.32 billion a year earlier, while capacity increased just 2.3% and the number of passengers carried rose 2.2%.
The figures show that JetBlue is earning considerably more from essentially the same amount of flying. The average passenger fare increased 19.2%, from US$205.67 to US$245.11, while passenger revenue per available seat mile rose 19.2%.
JetBlue said corporate revenue increased 25%, while both its premium products and regular Main cabin recorded double-digit increases in revenue per available seat mile. Fort Lauderdale, where the airline has been expanding rapidly, recorded a 15% increase in unit revenue despite capacity growing by more than 65%.
Follow Air Data News: WhatsApp | Instagram | LinkedIn | Twitter | Facebook
The improvement provides evidence that parts of JetBlue's JetForward turnaround plan are producing results. The airline has been changing its network, improving revenue management and investing more heavily in products aimed at passengers willing to pay higher fares.
That strategy includes BlueFirst , its new domestic first-class cabin scheduled to enter service in December. The product will initially be installed on Airbus A220s and later expanded to A320-family aircraft, adding another premium option below the airline's Mint business class.
The problem for JetBlue is that its expenses are rising almost as quickly. Fuel provides the clearest example. The airline consumed 222 million gallons (840 million liters) during the quarter, only slightly more than the 217 million gallons (821 million liters) used a year earlier.
But its average fuel price jumped 57.4%, from US$2.49 to US$3.91 per gallon (US$0.66 to US$1.03 per liter).
JetBlue consequently spent US$868 million on fuel during the quarter, US$329 million more than the US$539 million spent in the same period of 2025. That increase alone absorbed about two-thirds of the additional US$490 million in revenue generated by the airline.
JetBlue estimates that stronger revenue allowed it to recover about 87% of the increase in fuel prices, better than the 70% to 80% it had previously expected.
Other expenses also increased. Salaries, wages and benefits rose 9.4%, while costs excluding fuel increased 7% for each seat mile flown. Operational disruptions accounted for about four percentage points of that increase and cost the airline approximately US$19 million.
The result was a US$144 million operating loss, compared with US$100 million a year earlier. After interest and other financial expenses, JetBlue reported a US$257 million net loss, up from US$143 million in the third quarter of 2025.
For the first nine months of 2026, the airline has accumulated a net loss of US$823 million, compared with US$425 million during the same period last year.
Those losses are putting pressure on JetBlue's balance sheet. The airline ended September with US$1.26 billion in cash, down from US$1.95 billion at the end of 2025. Short-term investments declined from US$531 million to US$368 million over the same period.
Combined cash and investments therefore fell by about US$851 million in nine months.
Debt, meanwhile, remained largely unchanged at approximately US$8.4 billion. JetBlue incurred US$149 million in interest expense during the third quarter alone and expects approximately US$590 million for the full year.
The carrier says it has US$2.2 billion in available liquidity, although that figure includes a US$600 million revolving credit facility that has not been drawn.
JetBlue also expects to raise approximately US$250 million during the fourth quarter through financing backed by aircraft. It says it still has about US$7 billion in unencumbered assets, including approximately US$2.8 billion in aircraft and engines.
JetBlue is simultaneously trying to limit how much cash it needs to spend on new aircraft. The carrier had 298 aircraft at the end of September: 129 Airbus A320s, 102 A321-family aircraft and 67 A220-300s.
The A220 has effectively become JetBlue's growth aircraft for the remainder of the decade. The airline expects 12 deliveries in 2026, eight of which had already occurred by the end of September, followed by seven aircraft in 2027, nine in 2028, ten in 2029 and two in 2030.
Only two A321neos are currently scheduled for delivery through 2030. That reflects a major fleet decision announced in 2024, when JetBlue deferred 44 A321neo-family aircraft that had been scheduled for delivery between 2025 and 2029. Most are now expected after 2030, reducing near-term capital expenditure.
The move came as JetBlue was also dealing with prolonged groundings caused by inspections of Pratt & Whitney PW1100G engines powering part of its Airbus fleet. Six aircraft remained grounded because of the issue during the third quarter of 2025.
The airline has since completed another major fleet transition by retiring its Embraer E190s , leaving it with an all-Airbus operating fleet. It also decided against adding the long-range A321XLR to its network and arranged to sell the two aircraft it had ordered.
JetBlue currently lists 42 A321neos and one A220 for delivery after 2030 and retains options for another 20 A220s.
JetBlue expects its commercial improvement to continue during the fourth quarter, forecasting revenue per available seat mile to increase between 18% and 22% while capacity grows only 3% to 4%.
Fuel, however, is expected to become considerably more expensive. The airline is forecasting an average price of US$4.64 per gallon (US$1.23 per liter) during the fourth quarter, about 85% higher than a year earlier and well above the US$3.91 paid in the third quarter.
JetBlue continues to target sustainable operating profitability in 2027 and positive free cash flow between late 2027 and 2028.

title: Air defenses neutralize two ballistic missiles, 255 drones in overnight Russian attack on Ukraine
body:
Ukraine’s Air Force reported this on Telegram , according to Ukrinform.
Starting at 6 p.m. on Monday, October 26, Russian forces attacked Ukraine with Iskander-M/S-400 missiles launched from Russia’s Bryansk region and 280 strike UAVs, including Shahed drones (69 of them jet-powered), Gerbera drones, and Parody-type decoy drones. The drones were launched from Oryol, Millerovo, Kursk, Shatalovo, and Primorsko-Akhtarsk in Russia, as well as from temporarily occupied Donetsk and Hvardiiske in Crimea.
The air attack was countered by Ukrainian Defense Forces aircraft, anti-aircraft missile units, electronic warfare units, unmanned systems units, and mobile air defense groups.
According to preliminary data, as of 9 a.m. on Tuesday, October 27, air defenses had destroyed or suppressed 257 targets: two ballistic missiles and 255 drones.
Hits were recorded at 25 locations, while debris from downed targets fell at 16 locations.
Several attack drones remaine in the air, and air defense operations are ongoing.
As Ukrinform previously reported , Russian ballistic missile strikes carried out since the evening of October 26 affected six districts of Kyiv. A 46-year-old woman was killed, and 15 people were injured.
Source: Air Force of the Armed Forces of Ukraine via Telegram

title: Mbappe Dropped By Chinese Brands For ‘Offending National Sentiments’
body: Kylian Mbappe was dropped Tuesday by two major brands in China after a video circulated online in which the French football star apparently joked about former leader Mao Zedong. “Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments,” drinks giant Dongpeng said in a statement, adding that “with immediate effect we are terminating all cooperation with Kylian Mbappe”. Mengniu, China’s largest dairy producer, also cut ties with the Real Madrid and France forward. “With immediate effect our company is terminating all cooperation with Kylian Mbappe,” Mengniu said in a statement. “Mengniu firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any words or actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people,” it added. The announcements came after a video emerged online with Mbappe saying that the funniest internet meme he had seen was of his face photoshopped onto that of “some guy — I think he’s a Chinese dictator”. This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappe superimposed on an image of Mao, one of several using the footballer’s face and other historical figures. The authenticity of the video could not immediately be verified by AFP Fact Check. “Dongpeng Beverage ends cooperation with Mbappe” was the top-trending topic on Chinese social media site Weibo. The 27-year-old Mbappe lost out to Harry Kane for the Ballon d’Or on Monday. AFP The post Mbappe Dropped By Chinese Brands For ‘Offending National Sentiments’ appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Jigawa students depart for China for advanced courses in agriculture
body:
In continuation of its drive for agricultural transformation, the Jigawa State Government is sending 65 scholars to the People’s Republic of China for postgraduate studies in agriculture and related disciplines under the second phase of its agricultural capacity development programme.
The students include 50 Master’s enrollees and 15 PhD candidates selected under the Jigawa–China Agricultural Capacity Cooperation Programme (ACCP), secured through the bilateral scholarship framework of the Government of the People’s Republic of China.
The Jigawa State Agricultural Transformation Agency (JATA) is implementing the programme in collaboration with the state’s Ministry of Higher Education.
Speaking at the farewell ceremony for the scholars, Governor Umar Namadi said the initiative was another important step in the administration’s commitment to human capital development and agricultural transformation.
“Today’s event represents another important step in the implementation of our 12-Point Agenda, particularly our commitment to human capital development,” he said.
According to Governor Namadi, agricultural transformation requires sustained investment in skilled manpower, scientific research, innovation and technology.
“Our commitment to human capital development and agricultural transformation must go hand in hand. We cannot transform agriculture without developing the manpower required to drive that transformation. Equally, we cannot achieve meaningful progress in agriculture without embracing science, research, innovation and technology.”
Under the programme, the 50 master’s students will undertake three-year full postgraduate programmes, while the 15 doctoral candidates will pursue five-year PhD programmes.
Their fields of study cover a broad range of disciplines relevant to the state’s agricultural development priorities, including soil and water conservation, desertification control, forest ecology, vegetable science, crop science, crop genetics and breeding, agricultural entomology and pest control, plant pathology, agricultural engineering, food science and engineering, animal genetics and breeding, poultry genetics and breeding, aquatic science, environmental science and engineering, and rural and regional development, including rural finance and insurance.
Namadi emphasised the need to strengthen agricultural research institutions, highlighting his administration’s efforts to transform the Jigawa State Agricultural Research Institute into one of Nigeria’s leading state-owned agricultural research institutions.
He further stated that his administration had continued to sponsor local agricultural research on crops particularly important to Jigawa State, including sesame, wheat, rice and hibiscus. He explained that the research aimed to identify practical ways to enhance crop production and yields, boost farmers’ earnings, and strengthen their livelihoods.
“We want to understand how research can help farmers produce more, increase their earnings and improve their livelihoods. Ultimately, when we improve the yield of smallholder farmers, we also improve their incomes,” he said.
The governor disclosed that another group of 16 students, whose programmes were initially scheduled to take place in Russia, would have their studies transferred to China due to the security situation there. He anticipated that the students would leave soon.
He noted that his administration’s investment in human capital extended beyond agriculture to education, information and communication technology, and other critical sectors, stressing that investment in people remained central to sustainable development.
Addressing the departing scholars, Governor Namadi urged them to remain focused on their academic programmes, respect the laws and culture of their host country, and conduct themselves responsibly as ambassadors of Jigawa State and Nigeria.
“The resources being invested in you are public funds—taxpayers’ money entrusted to us for the development of our people.
“You must therefore see yourselves as having a responsibility to the people of Jigawa State. When you complete your studies and return, we expect you to put your acquired knowledge and skills to work in the service of our state and its people.”

title: John Jinapor holds policy dialogue with IMANI on Ghana’s energy sector
body: The Minister for Energy and Green Transition, Dr John Abdulai Jinapor, has held a strategic policy dialogue with the IMANI Centre for Policy and Education to discuss government policies and progress in Ghana’s energy sector. The engagement focused on developments in the power and petroleum sectors, as well as the government’s plans for renewable energy. It provided an opportunity for both sides to exchange views on policies implemented so far and the broader vision for the sector. Dr Jinapor described the discussions as frank and constructive, emphasising the importance of engaging policy institutions to assess progress and improve decision-making. He said such engagements were essential to strengthening accountability, refining policies and ensuring that interventions in the energy sector respond effectively to the country’s needs. The Minister reaffirmed the importance of building a more resilient, efficient and sustainable energy sector to support Ghana’s development, with continued dialogue among stakeholders expected to contribute to improved policy outcomes.

title: Super Lig: Osimhen lifts Galatasaray to top spot with two goals against Fenerbahce
body:
Super Eagles striker Victor Osimhen delivered a decisive performance in one of Turkish football’s biggest fixtures, scoring twice to inspire Galatasaray to a 2-1 victory over bitter Istanbul rivals Fenerbahce in the Intercontinental Derby.
The Nigeria international struck in both halves of the first period to put Galatasaray in control before the break, helping the reigning title contenders return to the summit of the Turkish Super Lig and extend their unbeaten run against Fenerbahce to five consecutive league meetings.
With the pressure mounting in a fiercely contested derby, Osimhen once again demonstrated his value to Galatasaray’s title ambitions, combining sharp movement with clinical finishing to make the difference against their city rivals.
The 27-year-old opened the scoring in the 29th minute, capping a well-worked attacking move after receiving a pass from Baris Alper Yilmaz. Osimhen showed composure inside the penalty area before directing his effort into the bottom corner, leaving the Fenerbahce defence with little opportunity to recover.
The goal gave Galatasaray the early advantage in a match where the smallest details were always likely to prove decisive. Osimhen, however, was not finished.
Five minutes before the interval, the Super Eagles striker struck again to double his side’s lead. Davinson Sanchez saw his effort heading towards goal, and Osimhen reacted sharply to redirect the ball into the net in the 44th minute.
His second goal handed Galatasaray a commanding 2-0 advantage heading into half-time and placed Fenerbahce under considerable pressure ahead of the restart.
Osimhen continued to trouble the opposition after the break as Galatasaray looked to strengthen their grip on the contest. The Nigerian forward remained a constant threat in the attacking third, while the hosts also came close to extending their advantage through Ismail Jakobs.
Both players went close with headers that struck the woodwork, denying Galatasaray the opportunity to put the result beyond doubt and leaving the door open for a Fenerbahce response.
That opening became more significant in the 62nd minute when Irfan Can Kahveci produced a spectacular bicycle kick to reduce the deficit to 2-1.
The goal injected fresh life into the contest and set up a tense final period, with Fenerbahce searching for an equaliser and Galatasaray forced to protect the advantage established by their Nigerian striker.
Despite the mounting pressure, Galatasaray held firm to secure all three points and claim a crucial victory in the battle for domestic supremacy.
Beyond his two goals, Osimhen’s overall contribution reflected the influence he exerted throughout the encounter.
The striker registered seven shots, three on target, converting two into goals. He completed seven of his 10 passes and recorded 25 touches as he remained actively involved in Galatasaray’s attacking play.
He also competed in individual duels, winning two of his four ground duels and two of his four aerial contests.
While his stats highlighted his involvement across the pitch, his finishing ultimately separated the two sides. Osimhen made his opportunities count at crucial moments, giving Galatasaray the cushion they needed to withstand Fenerbahce’s second-half fightback.
His brace further underlined his importance to a Galatasaray side pursuing another successful league campaign, particularly in a fixture where the result carries significance beyond the three points on offer.
The victory marked Galatasaray’s fourth win in their last five matches across all competitions, providing a timely boost to their title challenge and restoring them to the top of the Turkish Super Lig.
The win also extended their recent dominance in the Intercontinental Derby, with the club now unbeaten in their last five Turkish Super Lig meetings against Fenerbahce.
For Fenerbahce, the defeat represented another setback in a difficult run of league results. They remain fifth in the standings after managing just one victory in their previous four league matches.
Although Kahveci’s spectacular strike ensured a tense finish, Fenerbahce were unable to find the equaliser needed to deny their rivals a significant result.
For Galatasaray, Osimhen’s two goals proved decisive in a derby that could carry considerable weight in the title race. The Nigerian forward delivered when his team needed him most, helping his side reclaim top spot while strengthening their recent advantage over one of their fiercest rivals.

title: Dimaampao vies to be PH’s first Muslim chief justice, vows a ‘more human judiciary’
body: MANILA, Philippines – There have only been two Muslim associate justices of the Supreme Court (SC) in its 125 years of existence. First was late former associate justice Abdulwahid Bidin of Tawi-Tawi, who was appointed to the High Court by the late former president Corazon Aquino in 1987; and incumbent Associate Justice Japar Dimaampao , who was elevated to the SC in September 2021 by former president Rodrigo Duterte. Dimaampao took one of the seats for associate justices that was vacated by Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo when the latter became chief magistrate. The justice is once again vying to replace Gesmundo, this time, as SC chief justice. “[My experience] has reminded me that the law belongs not only to those who practice it, but ultimately to the people whom it is meant to serve,” said Dimaampao during the Judicial and Bar Council’s (JBC) public interview for aspirants on Monday, October 26. “If given the opportunity to serve as chief justice, I will bring with me not only experience, but humility borne of experience…. For I believe that leadership in the judiciary is not about standing over others. It is about standing with them in pursuit of judicial independence… in pursuit of justice, and in fruitful service to the Filipino people.” Dimaampao is one of the five SC associate justices in the running to become Gesmundo’s successor. The JBC has concluded the interviews on Monday and will proceed to deliberations. Afterwards, the council will submit to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. a short list of nominees. Marcos would then appoint the country’s 28th chief justice. Currently, Dimaampao is the second most junior among the candidates and is holding seat no. 11 at the High Court. If chosen, Dimaampao will serve for seven years or until 2033. During the interview, Dimaampao promised that apart from technological innovation, the public would feel that the justice system is working under his term, if ever appointed. He said he would serve with humility and dedication, explaining that his decision to bid for the position was motivated by his desire to give back. “After 2027, our role is to build not only a more modern judiciary but to develop a more human judiciary – one that is trusted by the people, accessible to the vulnerable, and resilient in times of crisis,” said Dimaampao. “It must also be one that is prepared for challenges of a future we have yet to fully pursue.” Play Video Visions for the court Dimaampao said the SC would address the problem about delays in cases if he become chief justice. He also said he would keep the Court abreast of global trends in justice, particularly the use of artificial intelligence. If appointed, he said these would be implemented in the first three years of his term. Dimaampao said he wants court decisions to be easily understood by ordinary people. “It must be shown to them that the decision has the following qualities: One, clear in reasoning. Two, consistent in doctrine. Three, concise in expression. And then, the fourth one is that it is just in result,” he explained. Dimaampao also discussed the Bar examinations, which are administered by the SC every year. He said he is known as a strict but reasonable professor, but believes that the qualifying exams for lawyers should test the examinees’ analytical ability. “And if we are restricted on that, there will be less passers,” he explained. JBC member Senator Kiko Pangilinan asked one question to all the candidates. He asked them whether it was the justice’s system failure that there were lesser people held accountable in corruption cases. Dimaampao said he would propose measures to make the Court graft-free: institutionalize transparency and digitalization, and build a culture of integrity. He also said he wants to decentralize oversight and include civil tracking in these cases. “If I will be given that opportunity to serve, I will be guided by this ‘ Fiat justitia ruat caelumet ‘ (Let justice be done though the heavens fall),” the justice explained. “We must sponsor seminars on ethics and remind these people of the judiciary about their duty. Particularly judges – they must be reminded of their constitutional duty.” What type of justice will Dimaampao be? During the interview, Dimaampao said he believes that the maxim “ dura lex sed lex ” (the law is harsh but is the law) should be reviewed. For him, if the application of the law would cause irreparable damage to the parties, courts should consider applying this maxim with caution. “To my mind there has to be an exception to that. Yes, the law must be followed. But if it results in a irreparable injury or damage to the parties, why can we treat that as an exception to the law? And there we attend substantial justice and fairness,” he explained. Dimaampao was asked when the SC should exercise its power of judicial review – or the mandate to revisit whether another branch of government has erred in following rules and violated the Constitution. He said judicial restraint is a constitutional philosophy and that courts should exercise their constitutional authority with caution. He also spoke of social justice. Dimaampao said justice is for everyone, regardless of their socio-economic standing. Play Video “Never prefer the poor simply because they are poor, [and] reject the rich simply because they are rich,” he said. If named chief magistrate, Dimaampao said he would adhere to the concept of collegiality and would respect all members of the bench. The public, according to him, should expect that he would be a model in following constitutional standards and independence. Dimaampao said he hopes to be remembered not only as the country’s first Muslim chief justice but also for the legacy he leaves to the judiciary. “I would like to be remembered not simply as the first Muslim to serve as chief justice but as a chief justice who upheld the supremacy of the Constitution, defended and protected the independence of the judiciary, and ensured that justice was served without fear or favor,” Dimaampao said. “Me being [the] first Muslim to serve as Chief Justice is a milestone. But I hope that this legacy will go beyond my identity. I want to show that regardless of one’s religion, ethnicity or background, every Filipino deserves equal protection under the law and equal access to justice,” he added. – Rappler.com

title: FG’s reforms rewrite Nigeria’s economic underperformance story – Tinubu
body: President Bola Tinubu says his administration is rewriting Nigeria’s decades-long story of economic underperformance through far-reaching reforms designed to unlock the country’s enormous economic potential. Tinubu, represented by Vice-President Kashim Shettima, stated this on Monday at the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit held in Abuja. The president said his administration began its tenure with difficult economic decisions aimed at addressing structural challenges that had hindered Nigeria’s growth and development for decades. “There is no shortcut to economic growth,” stressing that the government had embarked on a difficult economic reset to establish a sustainable foundation for national prosperity. According to him, the administration is pursuing its original mission of transforming Nigeria’s economic fortunes and reversing years of performance below the country’s potential. “We came to rewrite the story of a nation that has performed below its potential for far too long,” Tinubu said. He explained that the reforms were necessary to dismantle longstanding economic barriers, strengthen national productivity and create opportunities for Nigerians across different sectors. The president said rescuing the economy involved more than improving economic indicators, noting that the ultimate objective was to improve livelihoods and expand opportunities for citizens. “For us, rescuing the economy means rescuing livelihoods and transforming the fortunes of young jobseekers, farmers, manufacturers, entrepreneurs and innovators,” he said. Tinubu stressed that economic stability remained essential to harnessing the opportunities presented by Nigeria’s growing population and abundant human and natural resources. “We cannot harness the immense opportunities offered by our growing population without first stabilising the economy,” he said. He said the administration had created conditions for the public and private sectors to invest, expand their operations and generate productive employment. According to him, the government has introduced reforms to dismantle structural barriers that prevented the country’s resources from translating into widespread prosperity. “These reforms are restoring confidence, strengthening our economic foundations and laying the groundwork for sustainable growth,” the President said. Tinubu said the administration was encouraged by the progress recorded so far, adding that the next phase required greater attention to productivity, employment quality and the effective utilisation of the workforce. He stressed the need to improve the quality of work, reduce underemployment and harness the potential of Nigeria’s underutilised workforce. The President said sustainable prosperity would require greater productivity from workers, businesses and investments across the economy. “Our pursuit of prosperity demands greater productivity from every worker, enterprise and investment,” he said. He noted that the government must assess infrastructure investments based on the economic activities they generate, while education should be evaluated by the skills and productivity it delivers. “We must judge infrastructure by the economic activity it generates and education by the skills and productivity it delivers,” Tinubu said. He added that industrial policies should be measured by their impact on the competitiveness of Nigerian businesses and their ability to stimulate investment, technological advancement, exports and employment. The president said the achievements of his administration’s economic reforms had been documented. He cited figures from the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) showing that Nigeria’s inflation-adjusted gross domestic product grew by 3.89 per cent in the first quarter of 2026, compared with 3.13 per cent in the corresponding period of 2025. On economic diversification, Tinubu said non-oil activities accounted for 96.08 per cent of the country’s GDP, while manufacturing grew by 3.29 per cent and the oil sector expanded by 2.57 per cent. He said the figures had strengthened the government’s confidence in its economic recovery strategy and efforts to diversify the country’s sources of growth. However, Tinubu emphasised that the administration’s ambition extended beyond favourable economic statistics to achieving measurable improvements in the living conditions of Nigerians. He disclosed that Nigeria’s capital importation reached 10.37 billion dollars in the first quarter of 2026, representing an increase of 83.83 per cent over the corresponding period in 2025, with contributions from portfolio and foreign direct investments. The President said the government would continue to ease regulatory burdens, strengthen transparency, ensure policy predictability and expand access to finance to attract more investments. He explained that the administration’s tax reforms were designed to establish a modern and equitable system capable of financing development while providing businesses with greater certainty. Tinubu said the government would maintain fiscal discipline in investments across critical sectors, including energy, agriculture and solid minerals, while reforming the electricity market to improve power supply and attract investments in generation, transmission, distribution and alternative energy. Earlier, the United Nations Deputy Secretary-General, Dr Amina Mohammed, assessed the economic reforms implemented under the Tinubu administration and called for their urgent consolidation and stabilisation, alongside effective management of expectations among citizens and other stakeholders. Mohammed also commended the African Development Bank (AfDB) for its new financial architecture for development across Africa, particularly its prioritisation of financing programmes designed to deliver impactful development. (NAN) The post FG’s reforms rewrite Nigeria’s economic underperformance story – Tinubu appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: One dead in bus strike on Zaporozhye Region, 222 downed UAVs: overnight attacks' aftermath
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Air defenses intercepted and destroyed 222 Ukrainian drones over Russia overnight, the Defense Ministry reported.
A drone attacked a passenger bus traveling from Simferopol to Moscow near the city of Primorsk in the Zaporozhye Region, killing one person.
One civilian was killed and six others were injured in Ukrainian attacks on the Bryansk Region.
TASS has compiled key information on the aftermath of the attacks.
- On-duty air defenses intercepted and destroyed 222 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones over Russia overnight, the Defense Ministry reported.
- According to its statement, the drones were downed over the Novgorod, Tver, Belgorod, Bryansk, Kursk, Kaluga, Oryol, Tula, Voronezh, Smolensk, Rostov, and Krasnodar Regions, Crimea, as well as over the Black Sea.
- A Simferopol-Moscow passenger bus was attacked by a drone near Primorsk in the Zaporozhye Region, Governor Yevgeny Balitsky reported on his Max channel.
- There were 31 people on the bus in total.
- All the injured were taken to the hospital.
- A civilian was killed and six others were injured as a result of Ukrainian attacks on the Bryansk Region, Governor Yegor Kovalchuk wrote on his Max channel.
- He specified that a man was killed when he stepped on tubed explosives that had been dropped from a drone.
- Explosive ordnance disposal teams from the Defense Ministry are on the scene.
- Three apartment buildings and 11 cars were damaged.
- Law enforcement and emergency services are on the scene.

title: Iran to pursue peace with dignity, not back down from rights
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 27 (MNA) – Iran’s Government Spokeswoman Fatemeh Mohajerani has emphasized that administration of President Pezeshkian will pursue peace with dignity and will not back down in defending the country.
Speaking in her weekly press briefing on Tuesday, she pointed to looking into the livelihood of noble people of the country as top priority of the government, reiterating, “The government is obligated to resolve the livelihood-related issues of the people from all walks of life.”
All government officials believe that people’s livelihood should be taken into serious consideration as top priority and this issue is currently being pursued by the administration, Mohajerani underlined.
Mohajerani then pointed to the economic pressures stemming from wars imposed against the country [12-, and 40-day wars], such as rising prices, various threats, and an economic blockade, adding, “It is a matter of regret to say that these issues have eroded and mitigated the purchasing power of some households to a great extent and effective steps have been taken in order to solve the problems facing the noble people of the country.”
Elsewhere in her remarks, the government spokesperson emphasized the need for safeguarding the national interests and pursuing a dignified peace, stressing that it [government] is pursuing the peace seriously and will make its utmost efforts in line with safeguarding the national interests of the country.
Highlighting that safeguarding national interests and protecting the country's territorial integrity are among the government's top priorities, Mohajerani stated, “Pursuing a "peace with dignity" does not mean disregarding the necessity of defending the nation. Islamic Republic of Iran will vigorously defend its national interests and territorial integrity against any aggression with utmost power.”

title: PenCom pushes early pension savings among Gen Z, informal workers
body:
The National Pension Commission (PenCom) has urged young Nigerians to begin saving for retirement early, warning that delaying contributions could significantly reduce the wealth they accumulate over their working lives.
Omolola Oloworaran, the commission’s director-general, gave the advice on Monday during the youth engagement and opening ceremony of the 2026 National Pension Week, scheduled to run from 26 to 30 October.
Ms Oloworaran said people should start pension planning during their productive years rather than when retirement approaches, stressing that early contributions let savings grow through compound returns.
“Your pension is not about the day you stop working; it is about the decision you make whilst you are still working,” she said.
She explained that PenCom began the week’s activities with young people to encourage them to take responsibility for their financial futures and strengthen participation in Nigeria’s pension system.
According to her, the commission is seeking to build a pension system that accommodates the changing nature of work, including entrepreneurship, freelancing, technology and other forms of self-employment.
“The old pension system was built for a different world: one employer, one salary, 35 years in office. So let me make you a promise: we will not ask you to fit into an old system. We will build a system that fits the work that you do,” she said.
Ms Oloworaran illustrated the benefits of starting early with two hypothetical workers, Tolu and Emeka, who each save N10,000 monthly but begin contributing at different ages.
She said Tolu starts at age 20 and saves until age 60, while Emeka begins at 40 and contributes the same amount until retirement.
According to her illustration, Tolu would contribute approximately N4.8 million over 40 years, while Emeka would contribute N2.4 million over 20 years.
Assuming an annual return of 15 per cent, compounded over the respective periods, she said Tolu’s savings could grow to about N113 million, compared with approximately N13 million for Emeka.
She said the illustration showed how starting early could produce substantially greater retirement savings, even when monthly contributions were identical.
“Tolu did not earn more. Tolu did not work harder. Tolu simply started earlier, and that is the power of compounding,” she said.
Ms Oloworaran acknowledged the financial pressures confronting young Nigerians, including rent, family responsibilities, education costs and the rising cost of living.
However, she urged young Nigerians, including those in the informal sector, to make saving part of their financial habits as their earnings increase.
“The greatest advantage you have is not how much you earn today. It is time,” she said.
The director-general said Nigerians do not need formal employment to start preparing for retirement, pointing to the Personal Pension Plan as an option for people outside the conventional employer-employee arrangement.
She said entrepreneurs, artisans, farmers, freelancers, technology professionals and content creators could contribute towards retirement savings based on their circumstances.
“You no longer have to wait for a formal job before you start saving for retirement,” she said.
Ms Oloworaran also pledged to make pensions easier to understand and access, improve digital services, strengthen oversight of pension operators and incorporate feedback from young Nigerians into the system.
She said younger workers increasingly expected speed, transparency, and digital access, adding that pension providers needed to make it easier to open accounts and participate.
“If a young Nigerian can order food in two clicks, opening a pension account must not take one day to open,” she said.
She also encouraged young people to balance current spending with long-term financial security, warning against letting current consumption habits undermine their future wellbeing.
“Real financial success is not just what enters your account. It is what you keep, what you build and what you protect,” she said.
At the event, Arese Ugwu, the acting managing director of the National Association of Securities Dealers (NASD), lamented that Nigerian schools and universities did not adequately teach financial literacy and retirement planning, leaving many young people without the knowledge needed to manage their finances.
She urged young earners to build a savings culture early, regardless of income level or competing financial responsibilities.
“If you don’t learn how to set aside income for your savings or your future when you have 10 naira, you’re not going to be able to learn how to set aside income when you have 100 million,” she said.
Ms Ugwu recommended budgeting as a starting point, suggesting that individuals allocate 70 per cent of their income to living expenses, 20 per cent to long-term financial goals and 10 per cent to emergency savings.
She said distinguishing between money saved for immediate spending and money reserved for long-term financial security was essential to building wealth.
Moreover, Timi Agbaje, managing partner at Versed Attorneys, said pension communication needed to reflect the immediate concerns and aspirations of younger Nigerians rather than focus exclusively on retirement at age 60.
He said messages about pensions often failed to resonate with young people facing high rents, financial pressures and uncertainty about their careers.
According to Mr Agbaje, pension campaigns could attract greater interest by presenting savings as a means of achieving independence, freedom and financial choices.
“When we start selling independence, freedom, and choices, young people can connect with that,” he said.
He also urged pension stakeholders to use social media and familiar digital trends to encourage young people to discuss their savings habits and make retirement planning more relevant to their everyday lives.
Omonzele Okpere, a fund manager at Stanbic IBTC Pension Managers, also highlighted the importance of compound returns and starting early.
She explained that contributions accumulated over time could provide financial support when individuals could no longer earn income through their usual work.
Ms Okpere also outlined how Nigeria’s contributory pension system operates, explaining the respective roles of PenCom, pension fund administrators (PFAs) and pension fund custodians (PFCs).
She said the commission regulates the system, PFAs administer retirement savings accounts, and PFCs receive and hold pension contributions.
According to her, contributions are invested across different asset classes, including money-market instruments, treasury bills, bonds, government securities and alternative investments, in line with regulatory guidelines.
“So the funds are invested in assets like money markets, fixed income instruments like your treasury bills, your bonds, your government securities, alternative assets. The goal is to diversify the portfolio such that risk in the long term is diversified,” Ms Okpere added.
Under the contributory pension arrangement she described, employers contribute at least 10 per cent of an employee’s monthly emoluments, while employees contribute 8 per cent, bringing the combined contribution to 18 per cent.
Ms Okpere said the separation of regulatory, administrative and custodial responsibilities helps safeguard pension contributions.

title: Platinum futures drop below $1,500 per ounce — market data
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Platinum futures on the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) fell below $1,500 per Troy ounce for the first time since November 21, 2025, according to trading data.
