title: WWE Crown Jewel 'still set' to go ahead in Riyadh: Start time, matches, tickets and how to watch in the UAE
body: WWE is returning to Saudi Arabia for Crown Jewel, with the annual wrestling event scheduled to take place in Riyadh on November 7. The show will feature some of WWE's biggest stars, including Roman Reigns, Sami Zayn , Liv Morgan and Chelsea Green , with two championship matches confirmed during Monday Night Raw on October 12. The event is still scheduled to take place in Riyadh despite recent missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia. Speaking to Fox News on October 23, TKO Group Holdings chief executive Ari Emanuel confirmed the plans were unchanged, saying: "Right now, everything is still set." However, he said the company was monitoring the situation daily and considering alternative locations should the event need to be moved. Crown Jewel is part of Riyadh Season and continues WWE's partnership with Saudi Arabia, a partnership that began in 2018. The kingdom is also preparing to host WrestleMania 43 in 2027, which will be the first time WWE's flagship event has taken place outside North America. Here is everything you need to know about Crown Jewel 2026. When and where is Crown Jewel being held? Crown Jewel will take place on November 7 at Riyadh Season Stadium in the King Abdullah Financial District. What time will the event begin? The main show is scheduled to begin at 10pm Saudi Arabia time, which is 11pm in the UAE. How much do tickets cost? Tickets went on sale on October 2 through Webook. Prices range from 80 Saudi riyals to 600 Saudi riyals ($21 to $160), depending on seating category. Availability and prices may change closer to the event. How can fans watch from the UAE? Crown Jewel will stream live on Netflix in the UAE and other international markets covered by WWE's streaming agreement. In the US, the event will be available through the ESPN app with an ESPN Unlimited subscription. Which matches have been announced? Four matches have been confirmed for Crown Jewel, including two champion-versus-champion contests, a Last Man Standing match and a tag team title bout. World heavyweight champion Roman Reigns is scheduled to face WWE champion Sami Zayn for the men's Crown Jewel Championship. Zayn won his first WWE championship at Night of Champions in Riyadh in June, before losing it nine days later. He recaptured the title on September 11. The two have a long history together, having previously been allies in The Bloodline before their relationship broke down. Women's world champion Liv Morgan is set to take on WWE women's champion Chelsea Green for the women's Crown Jewel Championship. Their rivalry developed on Raw, when Morgan dismissed Green's championship reign before Green lost a non-title match against Roxanne Perez. Both contests follow Crown Jewel's champion-versus-champion format, with separate titles awarded to the winners rather than either wrestler's existing championship being defended. Seth Rollins and Stephanie Vaquer won the respective men's and women's Crown Jewel titles at last year's event in Perth, Australia. Cody Rhodes will face his former mentor Randy Orton in a Last Man Standing match, following an announcement on SmackDown on October 23. The rivalry intensified after Orton attacked Rhodes following their WrestleMania 42 encounter. In a Last Man Standing match, victory is secured when an opponent is unable to return to their feet before the referee's count of 10. World tag team champions Bron Breakker and Austin Theory, collectively known as The Vision, will defend their titles against Penta and Je'Von Evans. The match was confirmed during Raw on October 26 after the challengers confronted the champions following an attack. More matches may be announced before the November 7 event.

title: Ballon d’Or: Harry Kane’s crowning moment
body: Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or triumph is the crowning moment for a player whose trophy collection does not do justice to his remarkable talent and consistency. The Bayern Munich striker, 33, is the first Englishman to win football’s most coveted individual honour since Michael Owen in 2001. Kane’s numbers are staggering and the England captain appears to be improving with age, with 73 goals for club and country last season. In September he became the fastest player to reach 100 Bundesliga goals, hitting the landmark on his 98th league appearance for Bayern. He is also Tottenham’s all-time leading scorer with 280 goals, England’s record scorer with 91, and the highest-scoring English player in the Champions League (58). But for all his personal achievements in club and international football, Kane’s medal collection is limited to German domestic triumphs since he arrived at Bayern in 2023. He was on the losing side for Tottenham in the 2019 Champions League final against Liverpool and was in England teams that twice lost the European Championship final. Kane’s lethal finishing is not the only string to his bow. Honing an instinct he first developed as a youth team player, Kane has also blossomed into a gifted playmaker. “I feel like I’ve always had the passing range and the vision and the football brain — the game understanding — throughout my whole career, and I think that’s just flourished these last couple of years especially, these last few years since I’ve been here at Bayern,” he told UEFA.com. – Ageing like fine wine – The clean-cut Kane, married to his childhood sweetheart Katie Goodland, is an understated throwback in an era of football bling. But it has not always been plain sailing for a player who struggled to make an impression early in his career with Tottenham and was farmed out to other clubs on loan. There were almost two years between Kane’s first Spurs goal, against Shamrock Rovers in 2011, and his next, against Hull in 2013. Even after his breakthrough season in 2014/15, he was dubbed a “one-season wonder”, an accusation that has proved laughably wide of the mark. Bayern boss Vincent Kompany has spoken of Kane’s numerous qualities, including his distribution, work rate and “game intelligence”. “To combine that side of his game with the numbers he has, you have to do the job to help the team progress and then still arrive in the box, so it is not an easy thing,” Kompany said. “That is something we have seen and been able to enjoy, and that was maybe underestimated at the time in England, but he is ageing like fine wine so I am just enjoying seeing that side of his game for us as well.” Bayern teammate Jonathan Tah praised Kane’s remarkable work ethic after seeing it up close. “I played against him a lot and every time he got better — now I’m playing with him I see why,” he told the Times. “He’s never satisfied, you see him working before and after training. He’s the greatest finisher I’ve seen in my life — and he’s still working on it.” jw/smg/gj The post Ballon d’Or: Harry Kane’s crowning moment appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Israel To Give Verdict On Netanyahu As Polls Declared Open
body: A deeply divided Israel headed to the polls on Tuesday for the first time since Hamas’s October 7, 2023 attack, with voters delivering their verdict on veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the country’s rightward drift. Israelis are casting their ballots in the shadow of three years of multi-front regional wars triggered by October 7, with the trauma still fresh and questions over accountability and security central to the campaign. The close-fought vote comes as Israel looks increasingly isolated on the world stage, driven by a devastating military campaign in Gaza, soaring settlement construction and violence in the occupied West Bank, along with a move towards hard-right religious nationalism. The last opinion polls to be published showed Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, running neck and neck with his main centrist rival Gadi Eisenkot, a political novice and former military chief whose mild manner is seen as the antithesis of the incumbent. “I want change in our country. I want a good democratic centrist government,” Alexandra, 65, told AFP at a Jerusalem polling station, where a few dozen people waited to vote early in the morning. Some 7.3 million people are eligible to vote, with hundreds of thousands of young people due to cast their ballot for the first time. Surveys show they overwhelmingly identify as centre-right or right-wing. Far-right Otzma Yehudit party leader Itamar Ben Gvir arrives to cast his ballot at a polling station in the settlement of Kiryat Arba, in the Israeli-occupied West Bank, on October 27, 2026, on the day of Israel’s legislative election. (Photo by Ilia YEFIMOVICH / AFP) | Ilia YEFIMOVICH / AFP Tens of thousands of Israelis are estimated to have flown in from abroad to vote in an election seen as crucial to deciding the future character of their country. “I think this is one of the most important election days in the history of the state of Israel,” Uriel Brandler, a 58-year-old real estate agent, told AFP in Jerusalem the day before the vote, saying he hoped for change. Netanyahu, 77, has served as Israel’s prime minister on and off for more than 19 years. The wily political operator focused heavily on his security credentials during his campaign, playing on his relationship with US President Donald Trump and insisting he is the only one who can keep Israelis safe. In the years since October 7, Netanyahu led multiple wars that have seen Israeli forces reduce Gaza to rubble, occupy southern Lebanon and, for the first time, pummel arch-foe Iran with US help. At home, Israelis have faced bombardment from Iran, Hamas, Lebanese militant group Hezbollah, and Yemen’s Houthi rebels. Polling slips are seen at a polling station in the Arab-Israeli town of Umm al-Fahm on October 27, 2026, on the day of Israel’s legislative election. ‘Not Afraid To Take Action’ Zipporah Bennett, an 85-year-old retiree, said she was voting for Netanyahu “because he has had the experience of navigating the country through a lot of difficult seasons”, praising his support from the US and adding: “He’s a man who’s not afraid to take action.” Netanyahu returned to power in December 2022, bringing into his coalition far-right ultra-nationalists who have since seen their political clout skyrocket. Wearing his trademark noose-shaped lapel pin, far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir cast his ballot in the West Bank settlement of Kiryat Arba, where his supporters had set up banners and speakers. The opposition has scorned Netanyahu for his backing of ultra-Orthodox parties fighting to keep exemptions for religious Jewish students from drafting into the military, which faces personnel shortages. But one of the biggest criticisms levelled at the premier is his failure to take responsibility for the October 7 attack, the deadliest day in the country’s history. Eisenkot, 66, has pledged to establish an independent state commission of inquiry into the security failures that led to the attack, something Netanyahu’s government has resisted. Seeking to unseat the premier is an informal bloc of parties led by Eisenkot’s Yashar and spanning from the right to the centre-left. Eisenkot has vowed to prevent the creation of a Palestinian state and expressed support for Israeli settlements, but has promised to crack down on violent settlers. An aerial view shows a campaign billboard depicting Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of the Likud party and US President Donald Trump in Tel Aviv on October 26, 2026, on the eve of the Israel’s legislative elections. (Photo by JACK GUEZ / AFP) | JACK GUEZ / AFP Neither Eisenkot nor Netanyahu has publicly said they would partner with the predominantly Arab lists, which represent some 21 percent of Israel’s population and could become kingmakers if the results are as close as expected. Yousef Jabareen, who heads one of the Arab-majority lists, told AFP he hoped for a high turnout among his community to help topple Netanyahu’s coalition, after voting in the northern town of Umm al Fahm. Most polling stations will close at 10 pm (2000 GMT). Final results could take days to trickle in, and it is highly unlikely that any single party will come close to the 61 seats needed for a majority in the 120-member parliament. Cobbling together any coalition could take weeks or months, with possible new elections on the horizon if negotiations fail. AFP The post Israel To Give Verdict On Netanyahu As Polls Declared Open appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Japan to keep stakes in Sakhalin projects — government
body:
TOKYO, October 27. /TASS/. Japan intends at present to keep its stakes in Sakhalin 1 and Sakhalin 2 oil and gas projects in Russia in view of their criticality for energy security, according to the Japan’s Energy White Paper annual report prepared by the economy ministry.
"From the standpoint of supporting stable energy supplies in the midterm and long term, Japan currently intends to keep its stakes in Sakhalin 1 and Sakhalin 2 projects," the document indicates. Japan received 8.6% of its total liquefied natural gas imports from the Sakhalin 2 project in 2025, turning Russia into the third supplier of this fuel for Tokyo, according to the report. Oil is not currently purchased from the Sakhalin 1 project.
"The Sakhalin 1 and Sakhalin 2 projects providing for oil and natural gas production are located very close to Japan as compared to other countries and regions, including the Middle East, making it possible to reduce transportation time and costs," the document indicates. Furthermore, according to the report, delivery routes from these projects do not go through dangerous bottlenecks, like through the Strait of Hormuz.

title: Finance Ministry prepares plan to prevent increase in deficit, fund defense, for next government
body: Even before the exit poll results of today's elections are known, the Finance Ministry has already prepared a plan that includes a series of harsh economic measures, intended, among other things, to finance the defense budget and prevent an increase in the deficit and the debt-to-GDP ratio.Some of the measures were planned in cooperation with the Bank of Israel. The next government will be responsible for implementing the policy.In addition, after Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich subsidized gasoline prices by NIS 1 per liter over the past two months to prevent price increases, the subsidy, which has cost more than half a billion shekels, will end Saturday night. As a result, gasoline prices will surge by at least NIS 1 per liter at midnight on Saturday, and may rise further as global fuel prices climb.The price of a liter of self-service 95-octane gasoline is expected to reach NIS 8.90. However, the dollar's roughly 1% decline against the shekel yesterday will help moderate the increase.Higher fuel prices are expected to trigger price increases across a range of other goods and services whose rates have so far been frozen at the government's initiative, including electricity, water, and public transportation. This is expected to drive up the Consumer Price Index.The freeze on adjustments to income tax brackets, tax credit points, and National Insurance contributions, along with the current VAT rate, will remain in place in 2027 under existing automatic budgetary provisions.Revenue from these measures is estimated at NIS 10 billion. In addition to ending the gasoline subsidy, further tax measures will be proposed to boost state revenue.These include mandatory reporting of income from residential property rentals and taxation of rental income from the first shekel earned. Currently, rental income of up to NIS 5,654 per month is exempt from tax. Some of these legislative initiatives have been held up in the Knesset Finance Committee.Another proposal would impose a tax on international content providers operating in Israel, commonly referred to as the "Netflix tax." Another measure expected to be implemented is a reduction in tax benefits on pension contributions, along with a recommendation to eliminate VAT exemptions for sectors that currently benefit from them.Economic measures aim to fund increased defense budgetBroader macroeconomic measures are aimed at finding sources of funding for the required increase in the defense budget, which is expected to reach NIS 187 billion.One almost certain source of funding will be sharp cuts to coalition funds, alongside sweeping efficiency measures across government ministry budgets.The main challenge facing the coalition forming the next government will be the immediate need to pass a 2027 budget, or potentially a two-year budget covering 2027 and 2028. The budget must include comprehensive reforms under the Economic Arrangements Law.As a result, the Finance Ministry is unlikely to secure approval by the end of 2027, so it will need to prepare a continuing budget.The timetable for implementing these measures is tight, and the parties that make up the new coalition will have to begin taking action even before the next government is formed.Stock exchange unfazed by Netanyahu crypto economy warningMeanwhile, the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange appeared unfazed yesterday by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's dire economic warnings over the weekend concerning the crypto economy.Trading opened lower yesterday, the final trading day before the elections, against the backdrop of Netanyahu's statements warning of possible sanctions, cuts to US aid, and the prospect of a shift toward a shadow economy.However, the trend quickly reversed, and the stock market moved into positive territory, with the exception of banking stocks.The stock exchange has declined since the beginning of the month amid uncertainty over the elections. Now, however, traders appear to be cautiously optimistic about the possibility of change.

title: CBD COP17: Experts explore new conservation models to advance Africa’s 30×30 goals
body:
Representatives of African governments and civil society organisations on Monday discussed emerging conservation models that could help countries across the continent achieve the global 30×30 biodiversity target.
The experts spoke during a panel session on the sidelines of the ongoing United Nations Biodiversity Conference (CBD COP17) in Yerevan, Armenia.
The event was organised by the Nigerian Conservation Foundation (NCF) in partnership with the World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF).
The session, themed “Emerging Conservation Models for 30×30 Goals in Africa: Catalysing Policy to Action,” was moderated by Adedamola Ogunsesan, NCF’s Director of Technical Programmes.
The panellists included Daniel Jidda of Nigeria’s Federal Ministry of Environment; Allan Dauchi, Chief Natural Resources Officer at Zambia’s Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources and the country’s CBD focal point; Amina Mbarouk, Assistant National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) Coordinator for Tanzania; Sylvia Dorbor, Sustainable Finance Coordinator at the Society for the Conservation of Nature of Liberia; and Tiwonge Gawa of the Wildlife and Environmental Society of Malawi (WESM), a BirdLife partner.
According to the organisers, the session aimed to showcase emerging and community-led conservation models in five African countries that contribute to Target 3 of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF), while strengthening climate resilience and local livelihoods.
The discussions also focused on how the models could be formally recognised in National Biodiversity Strategies and Action Plans (NBSAPs), Other Effective Area-Based Conservation Measures (OECM) registers and national biodiversity reports submitted to the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD).
The organisers said the session would further identify the policy, land-tenure and financing reforms needed to translate conservation commitments into action at national and sub-national levels.
Another objective was to establish a regional peer-learning platform connecting CBD national focal points with conservation organisations across West and Central Africa.
Speaking at the event, Durrel Halleson, Head of Policy and Partnerships for Africa at WWF International, said discussions at COP17 had centred on mobilising additional financing to help African countries meet their biodiversity commitments.
He identified Other Effective Area-Based Conservation Measures (OECMs) as one approach that could expand conservation efforts across the continent.
“We have an opportunity here to really bring this up, talk about OECMs, scale it up, to become one of those ways to reach target 30×30,” he said.
OECMs are geographically defined areas outside formally designated protected areas that deliver sustained, effective and positive outcomes for the long-term conservation of biodiversity.
Target 3 of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework commits countries to ensuring that at least 30 per cent of terrestrial, inland water, coastal and marine areas are effectively conserved and managed by 2030.
However, in many parts of West and Central Africa, translating these commitments into tangible conservation outcomes remains a challenge.
Limited funding for protected areas, contested land tenure and the dependence of rural communities on natural resources have complicated conservation efforts across the region.
Emerging approaches include community and Indigenous-conserved areas, women-led natural resource management groups, faith-based conservation initiatives, land trusts, forest and mangrove co-management arrangements, and cross-border ecological corridors.
These models can support biodiversity conservation while strengthening local livelihoods and resilience to climate change.
Despite their potential, many remain poorly financed or insufficiently recognised in national conservation policies and reporting frameworks, limiting their contribution to countries’ progress towards the 30×30 target.
The session therefore brought conservation practitioners and CBD national focal points together to explore how successful community-led initiatives could gain formal recognition, secure sustainable financing and contribute more effectively to national biodiversity targets.

title: Khmara calls on E5 nations to transfer 10% of their air defense missile stocks to Ukraine in exchange for contracted future deliveries
body:
In an address to defense officials from the E5 group (Germany, the United Kingdom, France, Poland, and Italy), Ukrainian Defense Minister Yevhen Khmara proposed that these partners transfer 10% of their existing stocks of interceptor missiles for Patriot and IRIS-T systems to Kyiv. In exchange, Ukraine would offer future deliveries—already contracted and financed via a European Union loan—to replenish those stocks. Khmara also proposed establishing joint production of drones within the territories of these allied nations, the Ukrainian Ministry of Defense reported on Monday.
"We are proposing not just to increase procurement, but to scale up the joint production of Ukrainian drones within the territories of other countries. This will allow us to boost production capacity and provide Ukraine with the necessary drones, while also strengthening the defense capabilities of our partners," Khmara stated.
According to Khmara, Ukraine requires solutions that will bolster the nation's defenses immediately while also enabling long-term defense planning for 2027. The minister identified the strengthening of air defense as the primary critical priority, noting that an immediate exchange—drawing from allies' existing stockpiles in return for future deliveries under Ukraine’s current contracts—would allow for the rapid protection of Ukrainian cities and serve as a model for other nations. Furthermore, Ukraine has an urgent need for man-portable air-defense systems (MANPADS) to counter Russian jet-powered drones; the country is seeking both the transfer of such systems from partners' existing inventories and funding for new acquisitions.
The head of the defense department identified the development of unmanned systems as the second priority, noting that Ukrainian enterprises have the capacity to double their drone production by 2027, provided that funding is delivered on time.
Khmara emphasized that Ukraine strives for a just and lasting peace—a goal that requires strength, readiness to defend the nation, and the timely provision of necessary weaponry to the armed forces.

title: General Staff: Russia has lost 1,581,840 troops in Ukraine since Feb. 24, 2022
body:
Russia has lost 1,581,840 troops in Ukraine since the beginning of its full-scale invasion on Feb. 24, 2022, the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reported on Oct. 27.
The number includes 1,400 casualties that Russian forces suffered over the past day.
According to the report , Russia has also lost 12,448 tanks, 25,609 armored combat vehicles, 167,472 vehicles and fuel tanks, 51,653 artillery systems, 2,241 multiple-launch rocket systems, 1,727 air defense systems, 449 aircraft, 356 helicopters, 3,025 unmanned ground vehicles, 35 ships and boats, and two submarines.
Ukraine's General Staff has not revealed its own losses during the full-scale invasion, citing operational secrecy. Independent Western think-tank reports agree that the Russian casualties significantly surpass Ukraine's losses, with the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) estimating the ratio to be "roughly 2.5:1 or 2:1."
A January 2026 CSIS report said Ukraine has likely suffered between 500,000 and 600,000 casualties from February 2022 to December 2025, of which between 100,000 and 140,000 are thought to be killed in action.
While Ukrainian officials rarely disclose the figure, President Volodymyr Zelensky told France TV on Feb. 4 that at least 55,000 Ukrainian soldiers have been killed in action since the beginning of the full-scale war, in addition to significant numbers who are missing in action.
The intensity of Russian drone attacks and the fighting has made it extremely difficult for Ukraine to retrieve the bodies of fallen soldiers, which are needed for DNA confirmation.

title: Rybakina Defends Ningbo Open Title to Boost WTA Lead
body: The Astana Times provides news and information from Kazakhstan and around the world. Kazakhstan’s Elena Rybakina strengthened her position at the top of the Women’s Tennis Association (WTA) rankings after winning the Ningbo Open in China on Oct.26, Tengri Sport reported. Photo credit: IMAGO / VCG Rybakina secured the title by defeating Canada’s Leylah Fernandez 6-2, 6-2 in the final, successfully defending her Ningbo Open championship. Photo credit: tennis updates Rybakina’s ranking points increased from 9,196 to 9,501 following her title win. She now leads Belarusian Aryna Sabalenka by 1,951 points, with Sabalenka holding 7,550 points. title: Bilateral ceasefire announced in Oleshky; humanitarian mission underway – President’s Office
body:
Head of the President’s of Ukraine, Kyrylo Budanov, has announced the commencement of a humanitarian mission in Oleshky.
"An important humanitarian mission has begun in Oleshky. A bilateral ceasefire has been declared in the area where the mission is taking place," Budanov wrote on his Telegram channel on Tuesday.
According to him, the Ukrainian Parliament Commissioner for Human Rights (Ombudsman), Dmytro Lubinets, has traveled to the site and will be responsible for coordinating the process. "We are in constant communication," Budanov added.
"It is critically important that this mission to rescue our people is carried out successfully and safely. I am sincerely grateful to everyone involved in conducting and supporting this operation," Budanov wrote.
As Lubinets reported on Facebook, a ceasefire went into effect in Kherson region at 3:00 a.m. on October 27. "The parties are adhering to the agreements reached by us as heads of the negotiating teams along with the Russian Commissioner for Human Rights Yana Lantratova. I will continue to keep the public informed, with a primary focus on the safety of civilians in Oleshky and the implementation of the agreements reached," he wrote.
The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine also announced that a ceasefire had been established in Oleshky on October 27 to facilitate a humanitarian operation.
On October 23, U.S. First Lady Melania Trump stated that an agreement had been reached between Ukraine and Russia for a ceasefire in the area of ​​the temporarily occupied town of Oleshky, in Kherson region, to allow for a humanitarian operation.
Ukrainian ombudsman Lubinets confirmed that Ukraine and Russia had reached agreements to conduct a humanitarian mission in the temporarily occupied town of Oleshky, in Kherson region. These agreements provide for a ceasefire, the delivery of humanitarian aid, technical demining, and the free movement of civilians.

title: Russian companies may find any mineral resources in Africa
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Russian companies have competencies for exploration to search for all types of mineral resources in Africa and the priorities for exploration areas are determined based on the requests of the countries, the Russian Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment told TASS ahead of the third Russia-Africa Summit.
"As for the types of raw materials, Russian organizations have competencies in the field of prospecting and evaluating deposits of all types of mineral resources. Priorities are determined based on the mineral resource potential of a specific country, as well as upon relevant requests from African partners," the ministry noted.
Furthermore, Russia's scientific and technological expertise makes it possible to strengthen cooperation with African nations in studying mineral raw materials, determining the composition and properties of minerals and ore, and assessing the prospects for their industrial use, the ministry added.
The third Russia-Africa Summit will take place in Moscow on October 28-29.

title: Russia Claims New Electronic Warfare System Can Counter Frequency-Hopping Drones
body:
Russia has developed a new electronic warfare (EW) system, Yastreb 1.0 (Hawk 1.0), designed to jam drones that rapidly change frequencies to evade defensive systems.
One of the systems with serial number 0001, was featured on the defense ministry-owned Zvezda TV channel.
Igor Potapov, a developer of electronic warfare and unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) systems and an expert with the People's Front, said the system scans for threats while maintaining radio silence and activates jamming only when a threat is detected. This approach is intended to prevent specialized equipment from detecting the system through its radio emissions.
The device’s range depends on its configuration. Equipment demonstrated for vehicle protection reportedly operates over several kilometers, while different antennas can extend the range to tens of kilometers. The system can also reportedly intercept images from a moving drone and transmit them to headquarters.
Yastreb 1.0 features six magnetic mounting points for vehicle installation, designed to remain secure at speed and when encountering obstacles such as tree branches.
Separately, Eduard Baghdasaryan, an academician at the Russian Engineering Academy, has said electronic warfare systems can generate interference in frequency bands used by satellite systems. However, the report does not establish that Yastreb 1.0 itself can disrupt satellite communications or navigation.

title: Humanitarian mission gets underway in Oleshky, Budanov says
body:
Kyrylo Budanov, Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine, announced this on Facebook , according to Ukrinform.
“An important humanitarian mission has begun in Oleshky. A bilateral ceasefire has been declared in the area. Dmytro Lubinets, the Ukrainian Parliament Commissioner for Human Rights, has traveled to the site and will coordinate the process. We are in constant contact,” Budanov said.
It was critically important for the rescue mission to proceed successfully and safely, he said.
Budanov thanked everyone involved in carrying out and supporting the operation, emphasizing that every Ukrainian life is invaluable.
As Ukrinform previously reported, Dmytro Lubinets, the Ukrainian Parliament Commissioner for Human Rights, announced that a ceasefire had taken effect in the area around the temporarily occupied city of Oleshky in the Kherson region and that the Ukrainian side was honoring the agreements.

title: Ethiopia Earns UN Investment Award with Focus on Safaricom’s Digital Expansion
body: The Ethiopian Investment Commission (EIC) has received a United Nations award for its efforts in promoting investment in the digital economy, with Safaricom Ethiopia’s telecommunications infrastructure and the M-PESA mobile money platform cited as key vehicles for advancing digital connectivity and financial inclusion. The commission was honored with the 2026 UN Investment Promotion Award at the ninth World Investment Forum in Doha, Qatar, according to UN Trade and Development (UNCTAD). The accolade comes amid a strong upward trend in foreign direct investment. Ethiopia attracted USD 1.432 billion in FDI during the first quarter of the 2026/27 Ethiopian fiscal year, marking a 49 percent increase compared to the same period last year. During the quarter, the EIC issued 179 new investment licenses, while 81 projects entered implementation and 66 commenced production, generating over 22,000 jobs. UNCTAD commended the commission’s pivotal role in facilitating investment in digital infrastructure. By March 31, 2026, Safaricom Ethiopia expanded its reach to 13.6 million active subscribers and 3,504 network sites, bringing 4G coverage to 59 percent of the population, while M-PESA registered 5.2 million customers. The EIC’s winning submission was selected from 48 entries representing 40 countries, focusing on initiatives that attract investment into the digital economy. Four other international organizations were also recognized: the Caribbean Export Development Agency for regional investment promotion through the Caribbean Investment Forum; Invest KOREA for driving investments into semiconductor materials, components, and equipment; Invest Qatar for its Startup Qatar initiative; and Morocco’s Tanger Med Zones for investments in digital services, including the ALTEN Delivery Center Maroc. UNCTAD has presented the Investment Promotion Awards annually since 2002. While the international honor highlights the commission’s effective promotion strategies, Ethiopia’s latest FDI figures offer a concrete measure of the tangible capital flowing into the country’s expanding economy.

title: Israel to Give Verdict on Netanyahu in Pivotal Election
body:
A deeply divided Israel headed to the polls on Tuesday for the first time since Hamas’s October 7, 2023 attack, with voters delivering their verdict on veteran Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the country’s rightward drift.
Israelis are casting their ballots in the shadow of three years of multi-front regional wars triggered by October 7, with the trauma still fresh and questions over accountability and security central to the campaign.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The close-fought vote comes as Israel looks increasingly isolated on the world stage, driven by a devastating military campaign in Gaza, soaring settlement construction and violence in the occupied West Bank, along with a move towards hard-right religious nationalism.
The last opinion polls to be published showed Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, running neck and neck with his main centrist rival Gadi Eisenkot, a political novice and former military chief whose mild manner is seen as the antithesis of the incumbent.
“I want change in our country. I want a good democratic centrist government,” Alexandra, 65, told AFP at a Jerusalem polling station, where a few dozen people waited to vote early in the morning.
Some 7.3 million people are eligible to vote, with hundreds of thousands of young people due to cast their ballot for the first time. Surveys show they overwhelmingly identify as centre-right or right-wing.
Tens of thousands of Israelis are estimated to have flown in from abroad to vote in an election seen as crucial to deciding the future character of their country.
“I think this is one of the most important election days in the history of the state of Israel,” Uriel Brandler, a 58-year-old real estate agent, told AFP in Jerusalem the day before the vote, saying he hoped for change.
Netanyahu, 77, has served as Israel’s prime minister on and off for more than 19 years.
The wily political operator focused heavily on his security credentials during his campaign, playing on his relationship with US President Donald Trump and insisting he is the only one who can keep Israelis safe.
In the years since October 7, Netanyahu led multiple wars that have seen Israeli forces reduce Gaza to rubble, occupy southern Lebanon and for the first time pummel arch-foe Iran with US help.
At home, Israelis have faced bombardment from Iran, Hamas, Lebanese militant group Hezbollah, and Yemen’s Houthi rebels.
Zipporah Bennett, an 85-year-old retiree, said she was voting for Netanyahu “because he has had the experience of navigating the country through a lot of difficult seasons”, praising his support from the US and adding: “He’s a man who’s not afraid to take action.”
Netanyahu returned to power in December 2022, bringing into his coalition far-right ultra-nationalists who have since seen their political clout skyrocket.
Wearing his trademark noose-shaped lapel pin, far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir cast his ballot in the West Bank settlement of Kiryat Arba, where his supporters had set up banners and speakers.
The opposition has scorned Netanyahu for his backing of ultra-Orthodox parties fighting to keep exemptions for religious Jewish students from drafting into the military, which faces personnel shortages.
But one of the biggest criticisms levelled at the premier is his failure to take responsibility for the October 7 attack, the deadliest day in the country’s history.
Eisenkot, 66, has pledged to establish an independent state commission of inquiry into the security failures that led to the attack, something Netanyahu’s government has resisted.
Seeking to unseat the premier is an informal bloc of parties led by Eisenkot’s Yashar and spanning from the right to the centre-left.
Eisenkot has vowed to prevent the creation of a Palestinian state and expressed support for Israeli settlements, but has promised to crack down on violent settlers.
Neither Eisenkot nor Netanyahu has publicly said they would partner with the predominantly Arab lists, which represent some 21 percent of Israel’s population and who could become kingmakers if the results are as close as expected.
Yousef Jabareen, who heads one of the Arab-majority lists, told AFP he hoped for a high turnout among his community to help topple Netanyahu’s coalition, after voting in the northern town of Umm al Fahm.
Most polling stations will close at 10 pm (2000 GMT).
Final results could take days to trickle in and it is highly unlikely that any single party will come close to the 61 seats needed for a majority in the 120-member parliament.
Cobbling together any coalition could take weeks or months, with possible new elections on the horizon if negotiations fail.

title: Russia attacks two medical facilities in Kyiv – Klitschko
body:
Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko has said that two medical facilities on the left bank of Kyiv were damaged in Russian strikes on Kyiv on Monday, windows were blown out by the blast wave, and there have been no reports of casualties, he wrote on Telegram.

"One of the medical facilities in the Dniprovsky district was damaged as a result of the enemy shelling. The blast wave blew out windows in the intensive care unit. There are no casualties at the moment," the statement said.

Klitschko also said that in another medical facility in the Dniprovsky district windows were damaged by the blast wave, and there were no casualties among staff or patients.

title: War update: 196 combat engagements on frontline in past day as Russian pressure intensifies on Pokrovsk, Kostiantynivka axes
body:
According to Ukrinform, the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reported this in a Facebook update on the battlefield situation as of 8 a.m. on Tuesday, October 27.
Russian forces launched one missile strike and 72 airstrikes, dropping 247 guided glide bombs.
In addition, Russian troops used 9,679 kamikaze drones and carried out 2,518 attacks, including 12 using multiple-launch rocket systems (MLRS).
Russian forces struck Bezsalivka, Korenyok, Tovstodubove, Ulanove, Rohizne, Neskuchne, Bachivsk, Vovkivka, Hirky, Novovasylivka, Mykolaivka, Yastrubshchyna, Marchyshyna Buda, Luzhky, Potapivka, Sopych, Kucheriivka, Stara Huta, and Kharkivka in the Sumy region, as well as Huta-Studenetska, Mykhalchyna-Sloboda, Karpovychi, Kliusy, Hirsk, and Yanzhulivka in the Chernihiv region. Korenyok was also hit by an airstrike.
Ukraine’s Missile Forces and Artillery struck three areas where Russian personnel and military equipment were concentrated.
On the North Slobozhanshchyna and Kursk axes, Russian forces conducted one assault, launched three strikes using five guided glide bombs, and carried out 44 attacks, two of them using MLRS.
On the South Slobozhanshchyna axis, Ukrainian forces repelled six Russian attacks. Russian forces also attacked on the Kupiansk axis, near Volokhivske, Okhrimivka, Shabelne, and Chuhunivka.
Russian forces launched three assaults toward Radkivka.
On the Lyman axis, Russian troops conducted seven assault operations toward Zelena Dolyna, Kolodiazi, and Lyman.
On the Sloviansk axis, Russian forces launched three attacks near Ozerne, Kryva Luka, and Mykolaivka.
On the Kramatorsk axis, Russian forces conducted no assault operations.
On the Kostiantynivka axis, 22 Russian attacks were reported. Russian troops conducted offensive operations near Kostiantynivka and toward Oleksiievo-Druzhkivka, Novoselivka, Raiske, Novopavlivka, Vilne, and Kucheriiv Yar.
Russian forces launched 26 attacks on the Pokrovsk axis, attempting to advance toward Novyi Donbas, Dobropillia, Vilne, Sviatohorivka, Svitle, Myrne, Serhiivka, Molodetske, Novomykolaivka, and Filiia.
On the Oleksandrivka axis, Russian forces launched one assault toward Piddubne.
On the Huliaipole axis, Russian forces launched 15 attacks, attempting to advance toward Ternuvate, Yehorivka, Rizdvianka, Vozdvyzhivka, Nove Zaporizhzhia, Verkhnia Tersa, Hirke, and Charivne.
On the Orikhiv and Dnipro River axes, Russian forces conducted no assault operations.
No signs of Russian forces forming offensive groupings were detected on the Volyn and Polissia axes.
As Ukrinform previously reported, Russia’s estimated total military personnel losses since the start of its full-scale invasion of Ukraine on February 24, 2022, stood at approximately 1,581,840 as of October 27, 2026.

title: Draft Bill Caps Foreign Portfolio Ownership at 15pc in Listed Ethiopian Firms
body: Stakeholder Scrutinize Bill over Caps, Custody, and Repatriation Ethiopia’s proposed foreign portfolio investment (FPI) regulation has triggered intense debate over capital repatriation, investor confidence, and the readiness of local financial institutions, as stakeholders gathered on October 26, 2026 for a public consultation in Addis Ababa. The draft regulation, spearheaded by the Ethiopian Capital Market Authority (ECMA), establishes a comprehensive legal framework designed to deepen financial markets, enhance liquidity, bridge domestic savings gaps, and integrate Ethiopia into the global financial ecosystem. However, it also introduces strict ownership ceilings and operational safeguards for international capital. Under the proposed rules, a single Foreign Portfolio Investor—including affiliates and persons acting in concert—is strictly prohibited from holding more than 10 percent of an issuer’s total paid-up capital directly or indirectly, unless a higher limit is permitted under sector-specific laws. However, Category I FPIs (comprising governments, central banks, sovereign wealth funds, multilateral organizations, and regulated pension funds) may hold up to 15 percent, subject to prior approval from the Authority, while Category II covers all other eligible entities, including corporates, foundations, and non-resident retail investors. Furthermore, any acquisition exceeding the 10 percent ceiling requires mandatory ECMA approval. If an investor breaches the threshold due to circumstances beyond their control—such as corporate restructuring or mergers—they must notify the Authority and their designated custodian within five business days and divest the excess holding within 15 business days. The draft also caps total combined FPI shareholding in a single listed company at 30 percent. Crucially, FPIs are barred from holding board seats or participating in management; doing so risks reclassification as Foreign Direct Investment (FDI). Presenting the draft at the ECMA office, Assefa Sumoro, Senior Capital Market Advisor at the Authority, emphasized that the framework establishes robust macro-prudential safeguards, empowering regulators to respond to exceptional market stress, including foreign-exchange pressures. To manage systemic risks, the bill proposes a high-level Coordination Committee chaired by the Minister of Finance, drawing members from the National Bank of Ethiopia (NBE), ECMA, the Ethiopian Investment Commission, the Ministry of Trade and Regional Integration, and the Financial Intelligence Service. Despite these assurances, market participants raised sharp concerns regarding practical implementation and investor sentiment. Gemechu Waktola (PhD), Group CEO of i-Capital Africa, questioned whether the regulatory framework provides adequate comfort to risk-risk-averse international capital. “Over the past two months alone, I have had many encounters with potential investors, and the recurring perception is that Ethiopia is not investment-friendly,” Gemechu remarked, suggesting that restrictions should be scaled dynamically based on investment size. Gemechu also criticized the mandatory one-year minimum holding period for investments, noting its impracticality for short-term maturities. “If an instrument has only six months left until maturity and someone buys it, what happens?” he asked, while also echoing widespread anxieties over foreign exchange availability and the guaranteed repatriation of proceeds. While the draft allows investors to freely repatriate capital gains, dividends, and interest through authorized dealers, it also empowers the NBE to impose temporary capital flow management measures for up to 180 days during exceptional macroeconomic crises like severe FX shortages. Officials noted that ECMA retains the flexibility to adjust or waive holding periods via directives based on instrument type and market conditions. Custodian eligibility also emerged as a major sticking point. The draft requires all FPI assets to be safekept through ECMA-licensed Designated Custodians. While commercial banks licensed by the NBE are permitted to offer custody services provided they meet rigorous capital adequacy, ring-fencing, and Basel compliance standards, participants flagged ambiguities regarding terms like “material non-compliance.” Critics argued that vague legal phrasing could invite subjective interpretations and proposed anchoring standards to the NBE’s CAMEL rating system. Yehualashet Abebe, Licensing and Registration Officer at ECMA, acknowledged the feedback, stating that the Authority will review the wording to minimize subjectivity. He noted that no local commercial banks have yet been officially licensed or applied for custody operations, partly due to the evolving legal architecture. Meanwhile, Naol Duga of Synestate recommended adopting structured corporate identifiers, such as Legal Entity Identifiers (LEIs) issued via Bloomberg, alongside national identification frameworks like Fayda for individuals to streamline transparency and verification. ECMA officials stated that the feedback gathered from the public consultation will be integrated into the finalization of the regulatory framework before it is formally enacted.

title: Nigerians need president with competence, capacity, compassion, commitment – Peter Obi
body: By Henry Umoru ABUJA – The presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, has described the kind of leader Nigerians need. Read Also: * Full list: NDC unveils 2027 presidential campaign council * 2027: APC dismisses NDC’s allegation of blocking venues, billboards for campaign According to the former Anambra State governor, the administration of President Bola Tinubu lacked “competence, capacity, compassion and commitment required to address the country’s problems,” insisting that Nigerians needed a president who would be available and responsive. He spoke on Monday night in Abuja at the inauguration of the party’s 118-member National Presidential Campaign Council ahead of January 16, 2027, where certificates of return were presented to NDC candidates. Peter Obi called for a new leadership for Nigeria, saying the country is facing serious challenges under the present administration. Obi said: “Everything is collapsing. Nigerians are looking for new leadership, and I can assure you that we will provide it.” Obi, who is contesting the presidency alongside his running mate, Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, noted that the country needed a fundamental change in leadership, governance philosophy and public resource management, insisting that Nigerians could no longer afford a government that failed to address their most pressing challenges. NEC meeting The events followed an emergency meeting of the party’s National Executive Committee, NEC, and the inauguration of the newly acquired national secretariat at 393 Etang Obuli Crescent, Jabi, Abuja, which is expected to serve as the party’s administrative headquarters and presidential campaign coordination centre. The NDC intensified its preparations for the 2027 general elections with the inauguration of its newly acquired national secretariat in Jabi, Abuja, the formal inauguration of its National Presidential Campaign Council and the presentation of certificates of return to candidates elected to contest on the party’s platform. The NDC presidential candidate, who warned against electoral malpractice ahead of the 2027 general elections, said the NDC would demand a free, fair and credible election. He urged supporters to go into the country and campaign for the party, just as he warned those who might harass NDC supporters or attempt to manipulate the election that the party would resist such actions. Obi said the party would focus on making Nigeria work and restoring the confidence of Nigerians in their country. Addressing party leaders and supporters at the dinner, Obi painted a grim picture of Nigeria’s socioeconomic conditions, citing poverty, unemployment, insecurity, corruption and the education crisis as evidence of what he described as the failure of the present administration. He argued that the responsibility of government was to solve problems rather than blame political opponents, insisting that an NDC administration would be judged by the improvements it delivered to citizens. The purpose of governance is to solve problems, not to blame people. Kwankwaso and I will not blame anybody. We will create that new Nigeria that is possible,” Obi declared. Economic woes Obi accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of presiding over worsening economic hardship and declining national performance. He argued that the resources available to the government had not translated into meaningful improvements in the lives of ordinary Nigerians, said Nigerians were increasingly demanding a different kind of leadership, one capable of responding decisively to the country’s challenges and demonstrating accountability in the management of public funds. “From my engagements all over Nigeria, Nigerians are looking for new leadership. And we assure you that we will create that new leadership,” he said. Obi who maintained that the country needed leaders with the competence, capacity, compassion, commitment and physical availability required to address the demands of national governance, argued that the president of Nigeria must be accessible to citizens, responsive to emergencies and willing to visit communities affected by insecurity, rather than remain distant from the realities confronting the population. Declares war on corruption The NDC Presidential Candidate who pledged to launch what he described as an unprecedented battle against corruption, which he identified as a major obstacle to economic development, effective public service delivery and national prosperity, argued that corruption undermined the impact of public expenditure, weakened institutions, discouraged productive investment and deprived citizens of essential services. He maintained that the country’s economic difficulties could not be separated from questions about how public revenues and borrowed funds had been managed, adding, Let me tell you why we must fight corruption head on,” Obi said, questioning the outcomes of the substantial borrowing and expenditure undertaken by the Federal Government in recent years. Obi who also challenged the Tinubu administration to account for the resources it had raised and explain why, despite the availability of public funds, Nigerians continued to experience widespread hardship, said the country needed a system in which public officials could be held accountable for their decisions and public money was demonstrably applied to projects and services that benefited citizens. “We must stop people from stealing public money. We must use public money for public good. And that will be seen, it will be shown,” he said. Obi promised that any public official found culpable of corruption under his proposed administration would be required to answer for their actions, stressing that accountability would be a central principle of his government, just as he called for a fundamental change in the political culture that, in his view, had allowed public officeholders to make promises without being held to measurable standards of performance. The presidential candidate who explained that the NDC would not seek public office merely to explain the difficulties inherited from previous administrations, argued, the party would ask Nigerians to assess its performance through tangible improvements in public services, economic opportunities and the general welfare of citizens. “We don’t want you to hire us to tell you about our problem. It’s only in Nigeria that you hire people and they start reminding you of what happened in the past. No, we don’t want you to hire us. We want you to hire us to improve from today,” he said. Promises emergency measures on security, agriculture Obi identified insecurity as another critical area requiring immediate and sustained government intervention, promising to prioritise security and ensure that communities affected by violence, kidnapping and other criminal activities received decisive attention. He criticised what he described as the failure of political leadership to demonstrate sufficient urgency in responding to security emergencies, insisting that a Nigerian president must be willing to confront crises wherever they occur. Using the kidnapping of large numbers of people as an example, Obi who argued that government officials should not remain detached from operations aimed at rescuing victims and restoring peace to affected communities, said, “If they say there is a problem in Jos, he will go to Jos,” Obi said, outlining his vision of a president who would be physically present and directly engaged when Nigerians faced emergencies. He added that his proposed administration would take the fight against insecurity to affected areas, particularly communities where residents had been displaced or prevented from engaging in farming and other productive activities. Obi also pledged to declare an emergency in agriculture, particularly in the northern part of the country, where he said vast agricultural potential remained underutilised because of insecurity and other constraints. He argued that securing farming communities would enable farmers to return to their fields, increase domestic food production, supply raw materials to industries and reduce Nigeria’s dependence on imported goods. “We have vast land in the north. When we secure the north, our farmers must go back and produce what we eat and what we use for our industries,” he said. The NDC candidate linked agricultural recovery to the broader objective of reducing hunger, creating employment, stabilising food prices and strengthening the country’s productive base. He said his proposed government would also prioritise education, healthcare and electricity, stressing that the challenges confronting those sectors required coordinated interventions backed by clear performance targets. Education: Obi targets out-of-school children On education, Obi expressed concern over the number of Nigerian children reportedly outside the formal school system, arguing that the country could not achieve sustainable development while millions of young people were denied access to basic education. He pledged to make basic education more accessible and improve its quality, promising that his administration would work to drastically reduce the number of out-of-school children. The former Anambra governor cited his experience in the education sector during his tenure in the state, while also acknowledging the work of other political figures in promoting access to schooling. He maintained that education policy under an NDC administration would be assessed through measurable outcomes rather than announcements and political declarations. For Obi, improving access to education is not merely a social welfare commitment but a necessary investment in human capital, economic productivity and the country’s long-term competitiveness. He argued that children from poor households should not be denied opportunities because of their parents’ economic circumstances or lack of access to influential political connections. The presidential candidate said the NDC wanted to build a society in which ability, opportunity and hard work would matter more than personal connections. “We must create a society where a child of nobody will be somebody without knowing anybody,” he said, calling for an end to what he described as a culture of exclusion and abuse of public trust. 22-year target for primary healthcare in every ward In the health sector, Obi renewed his commitment to strengthening primary healthcare, saying that his proposed administration would work towards establishing a functional primary healthcare centre in every ward in Nigeria within two years. He argued that preventable deaths, particularly those associated with inadequate access to medical facilities and essential services, should no longer be accepted as an inevitable feature of life in the country. The NDC candidate said his government would prioritise accessible healthcare services and ensure that public resources were directed towards improving the conditions under which Nigerians receive medical attention. He also linked improved healthcare delivery to the broader need for effective planning, responsible expenditure and accountability across government institutions. According to Obi, Nigerians should be able to assess progress through visible improvements in healthcare access and service delivery rather than promises that remain unfulfilled after elections. His pledge formed part of a wider commitment to establish measurable benchmarks across key sectors, including education, security, agriculture and electricity. Power sector overhaul, industrial revival Obi also promised an emergency intervention in the electricity sector, arguing that reliable power supply was indispensable to economic growth, industrial expansion and employment creation. He said an NDC administration would prioritise electricity generation, transmission and distribution, insisting that Nigeria could not achieve its economic potential without a substantial improvement in power supply. “We will declare emergency on generation, transmission and distribution,” he said. The former governor argued that unreliable electricity had placed enormous burdens on households, small businesses, manufacturers and service providers, forcing many enterprises to contend with high operating costs and reduced productivity. He promised that improvements in electricity supply would be measurable and visible to Nigerians, rather than remaining an unfulfilled campaign promise. Obi also called for the revival of industries across the country, particularly manufacturing concerns that once provided employment and supported local economic activity. Referring to industrial establishments in Kano, he asked how the country could restore manufacturing capacity and bring abandoned or struggling industries back into productive operation. He argued that Nigeria’s economic recovery required a shift from excessive dependence on consumption and borrowing towards production, enterprise development and the expansion of domestic industrial capacity. The NDC candidate said a functioning industrial sector would help create jobs, increase household incomes, stimulate demand for locally produced goods and strengthen the country’s economic base. He also emphasised the need to support young Nigerians seeking employment and those interested in establishing businesses. NDC targets greater access to credit for SMEs Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) featured prominently in Obi’s economic proposals, with the presidential candidate promising measures to improve access to credit and reduce the burdens facing small businesses. He argued that small businesses were essential to job creation and economic resilience but remained constrained by inadequate financing, high operating costs and multiple taxes and levies. Obi cited figures indicating that Nigeria had more than 40 million SMEs, while claiming that they received less than five per cent of bank lending and credit. He promised that an NDC administration would seek to increase the proportion of credit flowing to small businesses to more than 20 per cent, alongside other measures aimed at helping enterprises expand and create employment. “We will put a mark to it. We will ensure that over 20% of the credits will go to small businesses. We will support them,” he said. He also promised to explore tax holidays and other forms of relief to enable small enterprises to survive their early stages of operation and grow into sustainable businesses. According to him, the current burden of taxation and levies on small businesses discourages entrepreneurship and undermines the ability of young Nigerians to create their own employment opportunities. The NDC candidate argued that a more supportive business environment would help unlock the potential of entrepreneurs, strengthen domestic production and reduce the pressure on government to provide jobs directly for every unemployed person. His proposals, he said, would form part of a wider effort to make the economy more productive and ensure that growth translated into improved living standards. Questions Tinubu over borrowing, public expenditure Obi who also challenged the Federal Government to explain the results achieved with the revenue generated and loans obtained during the Tinubu administration, questioned why the country continued to experience severe economic hardship despite the administration’s claims of improved revenue generation. The presidential candidate referred to the budgets for 2023, 2024 and 2025, arguing that the level of capital expenditure and the reported difficulties facing contractors raised questions about the implementation of government projects. He alleged that capital expenditure had failed to reach 20 per cent across the three budget years, while contractors and suppliers working for government were facing payment difficulties. These claims were central to his argument that corruption and poor management had prevented public expenditure from producing the intended economic benefits. Obi challenged the government to provide Nigerians with a detailed account of the projects executed, the resources expended and the measurable improvements delivered across the country. He also criticised what he described as the failure of the administration to communicate adequately with citizens about its performance. The former governor said his campaign would insist on transparency and accountability, adding that Nigerians deserved to know how public funds were being used and what results they were producing. He maintained that his proposed administration would not ask citizens to accept excuses where measurable improvements were expected. Condemns political harassment, calls for issue-based campaigns Obi also addressed the treatment of NDC supporters and the atmosphere surrounding political mobilisation, warning against the harassment of Nigerians seeking to support the party. He appealed to political actors to maintain civility and recognise that peaceful conduct should not be interpreted as weakness. “Humility and civility is not weakness. It is a virtue. Good behaviour is not weakness. It is a virtue,” he said. He warned against the use of intimidation in political competition, insisting that the 2027 elections should be fought on the strength of ideas, policy proposals and the credibility of candidates. The NDC presidential candidate pledged to campaign across every state of the federation, saying he wanted to engage Nigerians directly and explain the party’s plans for national recovery. He also called for free, fair and credible elections, warning against attempts to manipulate the electoral process. “The revolution that is coming is a revolution of the ballot,” he said, emphasising that the party intended to pursue political change through the democratic process. Obi urged NDC candidates and supporters to take the party’s message to communities across the country, insisting that the presidential contest should provide Nigerians with a clear choice between competing visions for the country. He also promised that his proposed administration would confront the high cost of living and work towards restoring public confidence in government. Pledges presidential accessibility, domestic engagement A recurring theme in Obi’s address was his insistence that the president must be available to respond to national challenges and engage directly with Nigerians. He criticised what he described as excessive foreign travel by President Tinubu and argued that the country needed a leader who would devote sufficient time and attention to domestic problems. Obi said that, if elected, he would prioritise engagement with communities affected by insecurity, poverty and economic dislocation, including states where residents had suffered repeated attacks. He specifically mentioned communities in Plateau, Benue, Zamfara, Sokoto and Borno as places where national leadership should demonstrate solidarity with citizens facing insecurity. The presidential candidate argued that leaders should not retreat from areas experiencing crises but should demonstrate a willingness to confront the challenges and support affected populations. He also pledged to spend his holidays within Nigeria, using the opportunity to engage with communities and understand their circumstances. For Obi, presidential accessibility is closely linked to accountability, responsiveness and the ability to make government institutions work more effectively for citizens. He maintained that Nigerians needed a president who would not only make promises during election campaigns but remain available to monitor implementation and address failures after assuming office Earlier in his remarks, the NDC National Leader, Senator Henry Seriake Dickson, said the party was formed to strengthen Nigeria’s multi-party democracy and prevent the country from becoming a one-party state. The former Bayelsa State governor who criticised the direction of the APC-led government, particularly on security, corruption and the economy, saying the NDC was offering Nigerians a new political alternative, urged party members and candidates to take the message of a “new Nigeria that is possible” to communities across the country, stressing that the party’s campaign would be based on ideas rather than violence. On his part, the National Chairman of the NDC, Senator Moses Cleopas said the party had demonstrated its capacity by conducting its primaries, selecting candidates and preparing for the 2027 elections within a short period. Cleopas who noted that the party would not make promises it could not fulfill if elected, said that its candidates must be accountable to Nigerians if elected, adding that the certificates of return presented to the candidates contained security codes, warning that anyone attempting to forge or falsely claim a certificate would be committing a criminal offence. “If we fail to bring water for you in two years, if we open our mouth to say, vote for us again, please don’t vote for us,” he said. The chairman maintained that the NDC was determined to establish a political culture in which promises would be treated as obligations and voters would have clear grounds on which to assess elected officials. He urged candidates to approach their campaigns with a sense of responsibility, describing the party’s political mission as an effort to rescue the country from its present difficulties. “We are going for a rescue mission, that the hope of this country is in NDC,” he said. Cleopas also invoked religious imagery to emphasise unity within the party, expressing confidence that the leadership would guide the organisation in the right direction. He called on candidates and supporters to remain committed to the party’s objectives and work to convince Nigerians of the merits of its proposals. The NDC Gubernatorial Candidate in Adamawa State, Senator Aisha Binani expressed appreciation to the party leadership for giving her the opportunity to contest on its platform, assuring that women would mobilise massively for the party. Also speaking, former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, SGF, Babachir Lawal whonurged NDC supporters to actively monitor the voting, counting and collation processes during the 2027 elections, advised voters to prepare for a long election day by taking food and essential medication to polling units. title: Ebola: Uganda orders 21-day quarantine for citizens returning from DR Congo
body:
Uganda has ordered citizens returning from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) to undergo a 21-day quarantine as authorities intensify measures to prevent further transmission of Ebola amid infections reported in Nigeria and Kenya.
According to a report by Al Jazeera, the Health Minister Chris Baryomunsi announced the measure at a news conference in Kampala, saying the government had strengthened surveillance at Entebbe International Airport and land border crossings.
The Ministry of Health said returning Ugandans with a history of travel to the DRC would bear the cost of their quarantine. Incoming travellers are also required to complete forms containing their contact details to facilitate follow-up by health authorities.
The measures come amid investigations into the source of Nigeria’s first confirmed Ebola case in more than a decade and a possible connection between the Nigerian and Kenyan infections.
Uganda declared its Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak over in July after recording 20 infections and two deaths, according to the country’s Ministry of Health. It maintains that it has no active Ebola infections .
However, the source of Nigeria’s imported case remains under investigation, with conflicting accounts emerging about the infected woman’s movements before she tested positive.
Swiss authorities have said a Ugandan-born woman married to a Swiss diplomat contracted Ebola during a visit to Uganda in September.
Nigeria confirmed her infection on 20 October after she returned to Abuja on 3 October.
The 42-year-old woman developed symptoms days after arriving in the country and initially sought treatment at a private hospital, believing she had malaria, before being admitted to another facility.
PREMIUM TIMES previously reported that the woman had spent about two and a half weeks in Uganda before returning to Nigeria through Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, where she had a two-hour stopover.
At the briefing, Mr Baryomunsi questioned the conclusion that she contracted the virus in Uganda.
He said relatives who had previously visited the DRC had met the woman in a Kampala suburb, raising questions about whether investigators had adequately examined that possible route of exposure.
“We should speak science, not politics,” he said.
Mr Baryomunsi said 60 people identified in Uganda following possible contact with the Kenyan patient had completed 21 days of monitoring and been discharged.
The current regional response follows a major Ebola outbreak in the DRC, where infections were first reported in May.
The WHO had recorded 9,704 cases and 4,687 deaths in the country as of 20 October.
The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo virus, a species of Ebola virus for which there is no approved vaccine or specific treatment.
Ebola spreads primarily through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person, or with contaminated objects and surfaces.
The incubation period can last up to 21 days, making the identification and monitoring of contacts important to detecting infections before they lead to further transmission.
The WHO has called for stronger surveillance and cooperation between countries while advising against travel and trade restrictions on affected countries.

title: Jamestown fishermen threaten demo over delayed operationalisation of cold store
body: Some fishermen at the Jamestown Fishing Harbour have threatened to stage a protest if the cold storage facility at the harbour is not operational by December 31, 2026. The fishermen say the delay in putting the facility to use has made it difficult to preserve their catch, resulting in significant post-harvest losses despite increased fish landings. Speaking to Accra-based Citi News, the Chief Fisherman at Jamestown, Nii Armah Wulu, said the facility had remained non-functional since the harbour was opened to the public, leaving fishermen without a crucial means of storing excess fish. He explained that some fishermen had resorted to drying surplus fish along the streets to prevent their catch from going bad. However, the practice was halted following concerns from city authorities, compounding the challenges faced by the fishing community. According to Wulu, repeated assurances from management that steps were being taken to make the facility operational have failed to ease the fishermen’s frustration, as they continue to struggle with preserving their catch. He warned that the fishermen would resort to a symbolic protest by wearing red bands if the facility remained non-operational by the end of the year. “Management continues to assure us that efforts are underway to operationalise the facility. However, frustrated by the prolonged delay, we have resolved to wear red bands in protest if the cold storage facility is not operational by the end of the year,” he said. The fishermen are urging the relevant authorities to expedite work to make the facility functional and help reduce losses associated with the poor preservation of excess fish.

title: Oklahoma City Swingman exits on stretcher following gruesome leg injury
body: Oklahoma City Thunder guard Jaylen Williams sustained a severe injury during the dying moments of a tightly contested game against the Los Angeles Clippers. The Thunder guard was fouled in a back-and-forth game against the Clippers with less than two minutes to go in the final period. With the Thunder leading late in the fourth quarter, Williams attempted a dunk over two defenders but landed awkwardly, causing a severe injury to his lower leg and ankle. Medical personnel rushed out to cover his leg with towels to hide the severity of the damage. He was then placed in an air cast and stretchered off the court as he gave a reassuring thumbs-up to the fans. An official timeline for the injury has not been released, but the former All-Star is expected to miss the remainder of the season. This is a particularly heartbreaking blow to the 2025 champions, considering Williams missed most of the previous season with lingering wrist and hamstring injuries. The reigning league MVP Gilgeous-Alexander weighed in on losing his co-star during a post-game interview, where he was asked how the team planned to push through the early stages of the season despite the loss. “We have no choice, it’s what we signed up for, and it’s obviously going to be tough without a player like that. “He’s not down forever, he’ll be back better than ever, we just have to hold the floor down until he gets back,” he said. The Thunder went on to win 108-101 at home, recording their first three wins of the season. They aim to maintain their unbeaten streak as they head to Phoenix to face the Suns on October 26.

title: Global initiative support group to inaugurate canvassers, friday in Ughelli
body: A formidable political support group, the Global Initiative Support Group for Sheriff 2027, will inaugurate Coordinators and Canvassers across the 25 Local Government Areas of Delta State, on Friday, October 30, at Oharisi Primary School, Ughelli, Delta State. The inauguration ceremony, scheduled for 10am, will be performed by the Delta State Chairman of the All Progressives Congress, APC, Chief Solomon Arenyeka. Convener of the group, Sir Festus Ahon, its Chairman, Chief Josiah Ntekume, and Secretary, Barr. Abednego Dikame disclosed in a statement issued in Asaba, Monday. The inauguration is expected to formally empower the Coordinators and Canvassers of the group to go into the streets across the state, including rural and riverine communities, to Canvass votes for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu, Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and all APC candidates in the 2027 elections. The choice of Ughelli as the venue places the event within the political landscape of Delta State, where political groups and grassroots mobilisation remain important features of party activities. The presence of Arenyeka, who is expected to inaugurate the group, is also expected to lend political significance to the occasion as members of the group formally begin their activities.
