title: Experts Urge Women to Use Legal Rights against Abuse
body: Blessing Ibunge in Port Harcourt Women have been urged to stand against gender-based violence, protect their property, understand their legal rights and develop the courage to overcome personal and societal challenges. The call was made by the Director of the Office of the Public Defender, Dr Evelyn Membere Asimiea, and the Co-Pastor of Gateway International Church, Dr Manuela George Izunwa, at the church’s annual Beautiful Life Women’s Convention in Port Harcourt, Rivers State. The convention, themed “Lady Gibbor: Building Women of Might,” brought together women from the church’s branches in Port Harcourt and across States in Nigeria for spiritual renewal, legal enlightenment and personal development. Speaking on the topic, “A Woman and Her Legal Rights,” Asimiea said every woman deserved dignity, security, property ownership and protection from all forms of abuse, stressing that religious beliefs should not be used to justify violence or injustice. “Marriage does not make a woman her husband’s property. Being a Christian does not mean that a woman must accept abuse. And forgiveness does not mean that you must remain in danger,” she said. She urged women to stop treating domestic violence as a private family matter, noting that abuse could be physical, sexual, emotional, psychological or economic. According to her, women experiencing violence should seek appropriate assistance, including medical attention, counselling, police intervention and legal protection, depending on their circumstances. “As women, we need to change one attitude. Instead of asking a woman, ‘What did you do to make him angry?’ let us sometimes ask, ‘Are you safe?’ That question may save a life,” she said. Asimiea also advised women to safeguard their property and financial interests by keeping relevant documents, recording business transactions and seeking legal advice before signing agreements. She emphasised that daughters should not be discriminated against in inheritance matters because of their gender, urging mothers to educate their daughters about property ownership, financial management and their legal entitlements. “A right that you do not know about can easily be taken away from you. And a right that you know about but do not know how to enforce may remain only words in a law book,” she said. The public defender further encouraged women to seek assistance early rather than wait until disputes over property, inheritance, finances or domestic violence became crises. In her remarks, Izunwa stressed that women’s strength was developed through deliberate training, personal growth and courageous action rather than inherited or determined solely by personality. “Being a mighty woman is built, not inherited,” she said, adding that a woman could be quiet, gentle and still possess extraordinary strength. She urged women not to allow past disappointments, mistakes or difficult circumstances to define their future, encouraging them to focus on personal development rather than compare their journeys with those of others. “You do not become a woman of might by accident. You become one through training,” she said. Earlier, the President of the church’s Women’s Ministry, Pastor Meg Lawal, described the convention as an annual platform for transformation, empowerment and spiritual renewal, aimed at building women who could excel in their homes, careers, ministries and communities. Lawal said the gathering was intended to equip women with the knowledge, confidence and spiritual strength to navigate challenges and contribute meaningfully to their families and society. She appreciated the Co-Pastor , Dr Izunwa, for “your love, encouragement, motherly care and unwavering presence in the affairs of the Women’s Ministry. Your support means so much to us, and we are truly grateful to have you as our mother.” To the women, she added: “As we navigate the different seasons of our lives, balancing our responsibilities in our homes, careers, ministries, and communities, I encourage you never underestimate the power of a woman who knows her God, understands her purpose, and refuses to surrender her destiny to the challenges of life”. The ministry’s Publicity Secretary, Mrs Ann Godwin, said the Beautiful Life Summit was designed to address issues affecting women, including legal protection, entrepreneurship and career advancement.

title: Ghana needs TRUST laws to stop the theft of its Children’s Inheritance
body: By Agnes Akos Sowu, GIMPA Law School, Greenhill. Imagine this: a twenty-five-year-old in Labadi watches strangers build mansions on land his ancestors preserved. His community’s custodians disposed of it. The proceeds bought cars, funded extravagance and disappeared. He cannot afford a plot. His children will inherit stories about land that should have secured their future. Elsewhere, galamsey swallows a girl’s family farm and poisons their river. Others take the gold. She inherits devastation. This is how a generation robs its descendants. A TRUST is a legal arrangement in which trustees hold and manage property for the benefit of others, called beneficiaries, or for a legally recognised purpose. Trustees must follow binding rules, avoid improper personal gain and account for their stewardship. Breaches can attract court remedies. For Ghana, protection must extend to communities today and generations unborn. Other jurisdictions offer practical lessons. Britain’s National Trust holds designated land under restrictions preventing voluntary sale, preserving it for successive generations while allowing compatible uses. Alaska’s Permanent Fund invests mineral revenues under constitutional protection. Norway channels petroleum income into a sovereign wealth fund, with spending guided by expected investment returns. Exhaustible resources thereby become financial assets capable of supporting future generations. These funds differ from ordinary private TRUSTS, but demonstrate the value of disciplined stewardship. Ghana’s Constitution already recognises fiduciary obligations over communal land and trusteeship over public land and minerals. Those obligations must bite. Lawyers who knowingly help custodians squander communal assets do more than fail their profession: they help one generation disinherit the next. Parliament should enact a Land and Natural Resources Trusteeship Act, requiring community TRUSTS for substantial customary land transactions, protected accounts, independent audits, beneficiary representation and enforceable remedies, consistent with constitutional ownership and revenue arrangements. The law must protect both land that should never be disposed of and proceeds from land lawfully developed. Mining operators must fund community benefits and separately secured rehabilitation obligations. Illegal mining demands prosecution. Publish transactions. Disclose conflicts. Empower beneficiaries to challenge abuse. Remove dishonest trustees and recover misappropriated assets. A TRUST without enforcement is another feeding trough. A chief’s reign ends. A government leaves office. A family head dies. The dispossession survives them.

title: Russia’s Battlegroup North artillery eliminates over 60 Ukrainian troops, 13 vehicles
body:
KURSK, October 27. /TASS/. Artillery crews of Russia’s Battlegroup North struck Ukrainian personnel and equipment in the Kharkov and Sumy Regions overnight, eliminating more than 60 militants and 13 vehicles across the two regions, the battlegroup told TASS.
"Overnight, artillery crews of the Battlegroup North, in coordination with unmanned systems forces operators, carried out more than 200 fire missions. Using artillery and multiple-launch rocket system strikes, they destroyed 17 Ukrainian unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) control centers, 63 personnel, and 13 enemy all-terrain vehicles, the battlegroup reported.
