title: Russian stock indices up as trading on Moscow Exchange opens
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. The Russian stock indices are showing positive dynamics at the start of the main trading session, according to Moscow Exchange data. The yuan exchange rate is also rising.
At the opening of the main trading session, the MOEX and RTS indices were both up by 0.34%, reaching 2,499.82 and 978.37 points, respectively, as of 09:00 a.m. Moscow time. The yuan-to-ruble exchange rate rose by 5.2 kopecks from the previous session's close, reaching 12.138 rubles.
By 09:16 a.m. Moscow time, the MOEX index’s growth had slowed, with the index reaching 2,497.99 points (+0.26%), while the RTS index stood at 977.65 points (+0.26%). Meanwhile, the yuan exchange rate saw its growth ease to 12.126 rubles (+4.05 kopecks).
At the start of the morning trading session, the MOEX index had fallen by 0.12% to 2,488.58 points, according to data as of 07:00 a.m. Moscow time.

title: Radda Mourns Slain Islamic Cleric Masussuka, Orders Investigation Into Killing
body: Katsina State Governor, Malam Dikko Umaru Radda, has expressed deep sorrow over the killing of prominent Islamic scholar, Sheikh Masussuka, describing him as a respected advocate of peace, religious tolerance and interfaith harmony, while directing security agencies to ensure those behind the attack are identified and prosecuted. Sheikh Masussuka was reportedly killed alongside an associate by unidentified gunmen riding motorcycles outside his residence in Dutsin-Ma Local Government Area on Monday night, October 26, 2026. Governor Radda, who described the incident as shocking and heartbreaking, extended his heartfelt condolences to the bereaved family, the Islamic community and all those affected by the tragic loss. He urged the family to remain steadfast in faith and seek solace in the will of Almighty Allah during the difficult period. “I urge the bereaved family to take solace in the will of Almighty Allah and remain steadfast in faith during this difficult period. May Allah grant them the strength and patience to bear this painful loss,” the Governor said. The Governor assured that the circumstances surrounding the killing would be thoroughly investigated, stressing that those responsible would not escape justice. “Those behind this heinous act must be brought to justice. I urge the relevant security agencies to conduct a thorough investigation and ensure that the perpetrators face the full weight of the law,” he stated. Governor Radda also appealed to residents to remain calm, cooperate with security agencies, and provide credible information to assist ongoing investigations, while cautioning against actions that could escalate tensions or disrupt public peace. He described the late Sheikh Masussuka as a distinguished Islamic cleric whose Qur’an-based teachings promoted peaceful coexistence, interfaith understanding and moderation, noting that he consistently spoke against violent extremism and radicalisation. In a statement signed by his Chief Press Secretary, Ibrahim Kaula Mohammed, Governor Radda prayed that Almighty Allah forgive the deceased, grant him Aljannatul Firdaus, and comfort his family, associates and the entire Muslim Ummah in this moment of grief. The post Radda Mourns Slain Islamic Cleric Masussuka, Orders Investigation Into Killing appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Nigeria welcomes international defence leaders as Afridex opens in Lagos
body:
The inaugural Africa International Defence Exhibition (Afridex) opened at Eko Atlantic in Lagos on Monday 26 October, bringing together defence leaders, official delegations and international industry representatives to discuss Africa’s security priorities and opportunities for cooperation.
Organised by dmg events in partnership with the Defence Industries Corporation of Nigeria (DICON), and backed by the Federal Government of Nigeria and the Ministry of Defence, the event runs until 29 October.
Covering land, maritime, air, space and cyber capabilities, Afridex connects African governments and armed forces with defence manufacturers, technology providers and specialist suppliers. Its exhibition and conference programme focuses on operational readiness, procurement and the development of local defence industries.
Guests at the opening ceremony included President of the Senate, Senator Godswill Akpabio, General Birame Diop, President of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) Commission, Dr Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, Deputy Governor of Lagos State, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (Rtd), OFR, Nigeria’s Minister of Defence, Dr Bello Muhammed Matawalle MON, Honourable Minister of State for Defence & Chairman of the DICON Board and Major General Babatunde Ibrahim Alaya, Director General of the Defence Industries Corporation of Nigeria (DICON).
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu was represented at the opening ceremony by Akpabio. “We gather with a shared responsibility: to secure our nations, protect our people and safeguard Africa’s future. From the Gulf of Guinea to the Sahel, from our territorial borders to cyberspace and outer space, the threats confronting us are becoming more complex and interconnected,” he said.
“They threaten lives and livelihoods, disrupt trade and weaken the foundations of development. Africa’s security must therefore command our collective attention, because there can be no enduring prosperity where fear governs daily life”, he added.
Akpabio stressed that “Afridex 2026 marks a renewed determination to turn African potential into African capability. Let the partnerships formed here strengthen our readiness; let the knowledge exchanged here inspire our innovators; and let the commitments made here produce results our people can see. We owe them nations where peace creates opportunity, where service earns trust and where the future can be approached with confidence.”
Welcoming delegates on behalf of the Lagos State Government, Hamzat, said: “Security is the first condition of any economy. Lagos, Nigeria’s commercial centre and one of Africa’s largest cities, depends on it every single day.” He noted that modern security systems increasingly depend on surveillance technology, effective communication, cooperation between agencies and public confidence and disclosed that the Lagos State Government was rebuilding its Command and Control Centre while expanding closed-circuit television surveillance to improve security monitoring and coordination.
The governor encouraged stronger partnerships across maritime, aviation, land, space and cybersecurity operations. He encouraged participants “to use these four days to turn dialogue into partnership and leave African forces better equipped and our economy stronger.”
Matawalle said Afridex provided an important platform for African countries to share knowledge, showcase innovations and establish strategic partnerships to strengthen their defence capabilities, urging international partners and exhibitors to pursue practical collaborations that would deliver sustainable benefits, particularly in technology transfer, indigenous production, research and development.
Musa said: “Afridex started as a strategic vision, and I’m glad to see that today the ideas have come to fruition.” Highlighting the opportunity for international industry, he added: “Nigeria has the population, has the landmass and has the reach, and Africa has the requirement for this. So anybody who invests in Nigeria is investing wisely.” He added that the Bola Tinubu administration is committed to modernising the Nigerain Armed Forces through strengthened indigenous defence production and the development of new capabilities.
Alaya said: “Afridex is more than an exhibition. It is a strategic platform for translating ambition into action” and was intended to promote technological innovation and strengthen Africa’s defence manufacturing capacity.
He explained that DICON, established in 1964 to produce military equipment for Nigeria’s security institutions, was undergoing reforms aimed at improving its operations and industrial relevance. A landmark was the DICON Act of 2023, which encourages expanding local production and partnerships with private manufacturers, research organisations and international technology companies.
He said the exhibition would provide opportunities for investment, technical cooperation and the development of sustainable defence industries across Africa. The success of Afridex would be determined by the partnerships and industrial projects established after the event, he added.
Following ceremonial welcomes and senior-level addresses, VIPs and official delegations toured the exhibition, meeting participating companies to explore equipment, technologies and services relevant to their operational requirements.
For more Afridex news, read the Show Daily magazine here.

title: Opinion| Malicious prosecution of Machar and co-accused: A conspiracy to bury political opposition, engineer succession
body: I consider the prosecution of Dr. Riek Machar Teny and his seven co-accused a deeply troubling test of whether South Sudan’s justice system serves the law or the political interests of the ruling SPLM Party. When criminal proceedings become instruments for eliminating political competitors, the courtroom ceases to be a sanctuary of justice and becomes a theatre of political persecution. The central question is straightforward: where is the credible evidence that Dr. Machar formed, commanded, financed, or exercised effective control over the White Army in the March 2025 Nasir attack? After subjecting Machar to prolonged confinement and the other accused to detention, the state must establish individual criminal responsibility through admissible evidence, not ethnic association, political rivalry or collective suspicion. Allegations of torture must also be independently investigated; detention alone does not establish torture, just as a criminal charge does not establish guilt. Five fundamental gaps in the prosecution’s case First, command responsibility cannot be manufactured from ethnic identity. In his defense testimony reported on 26 October 2026, Machar described the White Army as a decentralised community-based force whose members organise locally, elect their own leaders and operate without formal SPLA-IO registration, military rations or an established chain of command linking them to him. The prosecution must prove the relevant superior-subordinate relationship and the applicable elements of criminal responsibility, not simply point to his Nuer identity. Second, the prosecution’s own investigative evidence requires scrutiny. Reports of lead investigator General Basilio Thomas Wani’s testimony that investigators lacked material evidence connecting Machar and his co-accused to White Army leader Tor Gile Thoan raise a fundamental question about the evidentiary foundation of the case. If accurately reported, that admission seriously weakens the alleged command link; it does not, by itself, determine every charge. Third, political association is not proof of conspiracy. The prosecution must establish an agreement and the required criminal intent through reliable evidence. Public speeches, political relationships, and the fact that armed civilians participated in violence cannot substitute for proof that Machar ordered, planned, or knowingly contributed to the alleged crimes. Fourth, Machar’s reported account of communications intended to de-escalate tensions and arrange the safe reception of transitioning SSPDF soldiers deserves serious examination. If the original documents support that account, they may contradict the allegation that he directed an attack. The court should assess the complete communications, their context and their authenticity rather than accept selective interpretations. Fifth, the state must distinguish evidence from inference. Questions raised during the proceedings about digital forensics, device seizures and the handling of technical evidence demand transparent judicial scrutiny. Any evidence obtained unlawfully, rendered unreliable or insufficiently authenticated must be assessed under the applicable rules of evidence and fair-trial guarantees. These gaps do not automatically prove Machar’s innocence or establish malicious prosecution as a completed legal finding. They do, however, make it essential that the prosecution prove every element beyond reasonable doubt and that the court remain independent of political pressure. The White Army, Gelweng and the politics of selective justice The White Army did not emerge simply because Dr. Machar entered politics. Community-based armed youth formations have historical roots in local systems of protection, cattle defence, intercommunal conflict and the security vacuum that successive administrations failed to address. Their historical development predates South Sudan’s independence, although the precise origins and evolution of the White Army require careful historical documentation. The proliferation of modern firearms has transformed the capacity of these formations without necessarily converting them into centrally commanded national armies. The comparison with Gelweng and Titweng formations in Bahr el Ghazal exposes the danger of selective prosecution. These community-based forces, associated particularly with Dinka cattle-keeping communities, have also operated within local security and political environments. If armed youth associated with one community attack government forces, the law must establish the individual responsibility of those who planned, ordered or participated in the crimes. It cannot presume that every governor or political leader sharing their ethnicity commands them. The same standard must apply to President Salva Kiir Mayardit if credible evidence establishes his criminal responsibility for any alleged unlawful violence involving Gelweng forces against Nuer communities. His office cannot confer immunity from the law, just as Machar’s opposition leadership cannot establish guilt by itself. Equal justice means equal standards of evidence, not equal numbers of political enemies prosecuted. A political conspiracy and a failed succession strategy? I cannot ignore the political context. When senior government figures, including former Information Minister Michael Makuei Lueth, have publicly expressed that they do not need Machar in politics, their statements invite legitimate scrutiny of whether the prosecution is entangled with a broader project to exclude him from political life. Such statements do not independently prove a conspiracy, but they make judicial independence and prosecutorial impartiality especially important. My concern is that the criminal process may have become entangled with a succession strategy intended to weaken the opposition, remove Machar from the political equation, and reshape the country’s leadership without genuine political competition. If that was the objective, the strategy risks failing on its own terms: a political rival cannot legitimately be eliminated through criminal proceedings unless the state proves the charges according to law. The prosecution against Dr. Riek Machar and seven others can appropriately be referred to as abuse of process , politicisation of justice , selective prosecution and, where the requisite elements are established, malicious prosecution . Article 19 of South Sudan’s Transitional Constitution guarantees fair-trial protections, while Article 14 of the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights protects equality before courts, the presumption of innocence and fair-trial rights. These safeguards prohibit the state from treating political opposition as a substitute for criminal evidence. The African Court’s judgment in Ajavon v Benin also illustrates the importance of judicial independence and fair-trial guarantees where politically consequential criminal proceedings are challenged. The precise applicability of any precedent must be assessed against the facts and jurisdiction of the South Sudan proceedings. Conclusion: Justice must not become a political weapon My position is unequivocal: prosecute those responsible for the Nasir killings, including crimes against SSPDF soldiers, but establish responsibility through credible evidence and lawful procedures. Investigate every comparable offence, regardless of the perpetrator’s ethnicity, military affiliation, or political office. Do not turn the White Army into a legal shortcut for criminalising the Nuer community, or Gelweng and Titweng into politically protected exceptions. If the state cannot establish the alleged command relationship, criminal intent and individual responsibility, the prosecution must fail on the charges that remain unproved. If evidence establishes that proceedings were deliberately initiated for an improper political purpose, the appropriate remedies should follow under the law. South Sudan cannot build national unity by prosecuting one community’s political leadership while excusing comparable conduct among the powerful. A court must determine guilt; a ruling party must not dictate it. The rule of law must survive the political ambitions of those who govern, or justice will become merely another weapon in the power struggle. The writer is a South Sudanese constitutional lawyer, academic, and political figure. He studied law at Makerere University in Kampala, Uganda. He is an independent legal researcher and constitutional expert and serves as a lecturer and Deputy Dean of the College of Law at Starford International University in Juba. He is also a member of the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement-in-Opposition (SPLM-IO). He can be reached via nhomngekjuol@gmail.com . The views expressed in ‘opinion’ articles published by Radio Tamazuj are solely those of the writer. The veracity of any claims made is the responsibility of the author, not Radio Tamazuj. The post Opinion| Malicious prosecution of Machar and co-accused: A conspiracy to bury political opposition, engineer succession appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Man killed in revenge attack in Koch County
body: The authorities in Koch County in Unity State have confirmed that a 25-year-old man identified as Jima Kuany Thot was killed during a traditional dance rehearsal in Koch County headquarters last Friday. Brigadier General Samuel Machul of the county police said the incident happened on Friday at around 11:30 p.m. during a dance practice when Maet Gatkuoth Guol, 28, shot and killed Kuany in an apparent revenge attack. “It happened on Friday night when Maet Gatkuoth Guol, 28, shot the victim, identified as Jima Kuany Thot, 25, dead. It was a revenge killing, and we are looking for the murderer to arrest and arraign him in court,” he said. “However, we decided that the traditional dance should continue, but we have a special joint force that will monitor the situation during their dance.” Gen. Machul added that no arrest has been made, but that county authorities have launched an investigation into the incident and to arrest the suspect. He urged local youth to refrain from the culture of revenge and cyclic killings. The post Man killed in revenge attack in Koch County appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Judge extends court-ordered block on Trump’s renovation plans for public golf course
body:
A federal judge has agreed to extend an order blocking the Trump administration’s renovation plans for a century-old public golf course in the nation’s capital
WASHINGTON -- A federal judge agreed Monday to extend an order blocking the Trump administration’s renovation plans for a century-old public golf course in the nation’s capital.
U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes issued a preliminary injunction that temporarily bars the government from removing or damaging any additional trees on the East Potomac Golf Course. The administration must give 10 days’ notice in writing before making any "irreparable modification” to any “forms or features” of the course while the lawsuit is active.
“The Court earlier stated, ‘I am not the Lorax. I do not speak for the trees.’ The Court still does not speak for the trees. It speaks only for the rule of law,” Reyes wrote.
Reyes expressed astonishment that the government has asked her to “not to believe the sitting President” and disregard Trump’s statements about his plans for the golf course renovations.
“This started as a case about golf. That good walk spoiled. But it has become much more,” Reyes wrote. “It now forces the Court to reconcile assertions by President Donald J. Trump with the sworn testimony of multiple government employees and the argument of senior Department of Justice attorneys.”
On Oct. 18, Trump announced plans on social media to close the golf course for 15 months, starting Nov. 15, and redevelop the 106-year-old park and course despite a court challenge by the D.C. Preservation League and two golfers. A day later, Trump posted that the work would start immediately.
Reyes, who was nominated to the bench by Democratic President Joe Biden, previously ordered the administration to suspend work on the project until at least Oct. 26.
Trump was asked about the case late Monday night as he arrived back at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland following a rally in Mississippi and indicated that work on the golf course will proceed as planned.
“It has the go-ahead. The judge feels that she would like to approve it as it goes along. And I didn’t know she was an architectural critic of golf courses,” Trump said sarcastically.
He added of the judge: “She knows nothing about that, so we’ll appeal that” while also calling his planned overhaul a “beautiful project for Washington, D.C.”
Trump later in a social media post reiterated a statement he made Oct. 18 that the course would close for 15 months. “We are closing the East Potomac Golf Course Site as scheduled on November 15th in order to renovate and rebuild for Competitive (with other such projects!), Safety, Modernization, and Aesthetic reasons," he wrote.
The plaintiffs challenging the project, DC Preservation League and two golfers, claim the work is inflicting irreversible damage. At a hearing, the judge excoriated the government after workers cut down at least 400 trees over a holiday weekend with little notice to the plaintiffs.
The course renovation project is part of the Republican president’s aggressive campaign to leave his personal imprint on Washington’s historic landscape. Those plans include construction of a huge ballroom at the White House, a massive arch and the creation of a National Garden of American Heroes in West Potomac Park. DC Preservation League is part of a coalition of organizations, including the Cultural Landscape Foundation and one D.C. resident, who have filed lawsuit challenging those plans.
Reyes rejected the administration’s request for her to recuse herself from the case. The government questioned her impartiality and accused her of engaging in “egregious” behavior from the bench during an emergency hearing in the case.
In Monday's ruling Reyes stressed that she had hoped the parties could have resolved their dispute without judicial intervention. She noted that she had denied plaintiffs’ previous requests.
“The Court would much prefer not to have to resolve Lorax v. Once‑ler redux. Indeed, for months, the Court declined to intervene,” she wrote.
But she said the government forced her hand by bulldozing hundreds of trees without any notice, doing “what it assured all it would not do.”
Reyes quoted from a golf-related opinion written by the late Supreme Court Justice Antonin Scalia, a conservative icon, in stressing the temporary nature of her own decision.
“Here, golf and government have again clashed,” Reyes wrote. “By issuing this preliminary injunction, the Court does not end the round: it simply marks the ball until the parties can fully and fairly litigate this case.
Democracy Forward President & CEO Skye Perryman, whose organization is co-counsel representing the plaintiffs, called the ruling “a big win that will rightly protect East Potomac Park from further irreparable harm.” She added, in an email, that the move will stop activities “while the case continues, and we are eager to argue the case in court.”
An earlier version of this story incorrectly referred to Perryman as “he.” This version corrects her identity to “she.”
Associated Press reporters Gary Fields and Will Weissert contributed.

title: WFP sees potential for Chinese technology to boost rice farming in Aweil
body: Rice farmers in Aweil are looking to improve farming technology and equipment to increase production, as the World Food Programme (WFP) sees potential for agricultural cooperation with China to help communities make better use of land suitable for rice cultivation. Santino Akech, a 45-year-old farmer in Aweil, said his community had begun cultivating rice after repeated flooding affected sorghum grown in lowland areas. “When the floods came, it affected some farms in the lowland areas,” he said. “It affected sorghum, but the rice succeeded.” He said farmers harvested 42 bags of rice weighing 90 kilograms each from four feddans last year. At the time of the interview, he still had 13 bags in storage. Akech said the income from rice had helped farmers pay school fees and medical expenses. Working in groups had also allowed them to expand cultivation and save money through village savings and loan associations. However, he said farmers need more support to increase production, including access to ox-ploughs to prepare land on time. “We are not demanding tractors,” he said, explaining that government tractors were not always available when farmers needed them. He said farmers could contribute towards the cost of ox-ploughs because some already owned bulls. The challenges facing Akech and other farmers are among the issues that WFP says must be addressed if rice production is to expand in Northern Bahr el Ghazal and other parts of South Sudan. Haileselassie Berhanu, head of the WFP Aweil Field Office, said the UN agency has been working with communities to explore how flood-prone land could be used for rice cultivation instead of allowing excess water to destroy crops. He said communities had experienced repeated flooding over several years, damaging sorghum, a major crop in the area. WFP and farmers began experimenting with rice on a small scale before gradually expanding cultivation. Berhanu said more than 2,100 farmers are participating in rice cultivation this year, with approximately 1,000 hectares planted across the wider initiative. He said the program still needed agricultural machinery, improved seeds, training and equipment for harvesting, drying, threshing and polishing rice. “The rice, the type of rice, if we need technical expertise, is very important,” Berhanu said, referring to the potential for support from China. He said technical assistance from countries with long experience in rice cultivation could help South Sudanese farmers improve production and make better use of available land. Chinese Ambassador to South Sudan Ma Qiang, who visited agricultural activities in Aweil, said the area had favorable natural conditions for rice production and that the initiative had potential to contribute to local food production. The envoy said China had previously donated agricultural machinery to local communities and that there was room for further cooperation in agricultural technology. “There is great potential,” Amb. Ma said, adding that cooperation with the national and local governments and international partners could help improve food production. The ambassador also cautioned that natural resources, including water, could become a problem when not properly managed, highlighting the need for better management of flooding. Meanwhile, WFP Country Representative Muntina Chimuka said rice cultivation could contribute to food security by helping communities grow their own crops and diversify their food sources. She said the rice crop at the site they visited appeared promising, despite dry conditions that had affected other agricultural areas. However, she said expanding such initiatives would depend on available resources and stronger government copoeration. WFP relies on voluntary contributions to fund its operations, Chimuka said, adding that climate change and unpredictable weather were making agricultural production increasingly difficult. She urged state and national authorities to work with communities to identify suitable locations and rice varieties for cultivation. Deng Deng Bol, caretaker minister of agriculture, environment and forestry in Northern Bahr el Ghazal State, said farmers needed equipment and training to improve production. He also identified storage facilities as an important requirement for farmers seeking to preserve their harvests. He said the state had fertile land suitable for agriculture, but farmers continued to face challenges from changing weather patterns. Flooding affected crops in the previous year, while drought has affected rice, sorghum and other crops this year. For farmers such as Akech, the immediate concern is getting the equipment needed to cultivate more land and harvest crops on time. He said rice had shown promise in the lowlands, where flooding had repeatedly damaged other crops. While WFP sees potential for agricultural cooperation with China, the expansion of rice farming will depend on access to appropriate technology, training, resources, and effective water management. Aweil communities hope that better support will allow them to turn flood-prone land into a more reliable source of food and income. The post WFP sees potential for Chinese technology to boost rice farming in Aweil appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: 3 teenagers jailed for 3 months over theft in Leer
body: The police in Unity State’s Leer County have said three teenagers who were apprehended for stealing public property in Leer Town have been transferred to the prison service after being found guilty and sentenced to three months in prison last week. Police investigator Gatjang Gatnor said the three boys, aged between 15 and 17, were handed over to the town chief’s council by security personnel before being transferred to the prison service last Tuesday. He said some unruly teenagers sleep near the fences of institutions, while waiting for opportunities to steal property. “Security personnel handed three boys, aged 15, 16 and 17, over to the town chiefs’ council. The boys were then transferred to prison services after receiving three-month prison sentences,” he stated. “Some of these teenagers reportedly sleep near the fences of institutions such as the forestry department, waiting for opportunities to steal property.” He said the police are pursuing the remaining suspects and that they will be held accountable through the justice system. “The police are continuing to search for the remaining suspects to arrest them and bring them to justice,” Gatnor added. Police have urged continued cooperation in efforts to protect community property and bring those suspected of involvement in theft before the justice system. The post 3 teenagers jailed for 3 months over theft in Leer appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .

title: Police Launch Manhunt As Gunmen Kill Prominent Islamic Cleric, Associate In Katsina
body: The Katsina State Police Command has launched a full-scale manhunt for suspected gunmen responsible for the killing of prominent Islamic scholar, Sheikh Yahaya Masussuka, and his associate, Adamu Abubakar, in Dutsin-Ma Local Government Area of the state. The Command said the attack occurred at about 7:30 p.m. on Monday, October 26, 2026, when two armed men riding a motorcycle reportedly opened fire on the victims in front of the cleric’s residence, inflicting fatal gunshot wounds. According to the Police, the Divisional Police Officer (DPO) in Dutsin-Ma swiftly mobilised a team of operatives to the scene after receiving a distress report. The victims were immediately evacuated to the nearest hospital, where they were confirmed dead by a medical doctor. Reacting to the incident, the Commissioner of Police, Katsina State Command, CP Ali Umar Fage, ordered the immediate deployment of tactical and operational teams to intensify the search for the fleeing suspects. The Police said investigations are already underway, with efforts being stepped up to identify, apprehend and prosecute those responsible for the deadly attack. CP Fage expressed deep condolences to the bereaved families, friends and followers of the deceased, as well as the people of Dutsin-Ma Local Government Area, assuring residents that the Command remains committed to ensuring justice is served. The Command also appealed for public cooperation, urging anyone with useful information that could aid the investigation to come forward. A statement by the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Abubakar Sadiq, said further updates on the investigation would be communicated as developments unfold. The post Police Launch Manhunt As Gunmen Kill Prominent Islamic Cleric, Associate In Katsina appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Iran offers education to Azerbaijani girls in hijabs, Baku calls it interference
body: Iran offers education to Azerbaijani girls Azerbaijan and Iran have exchanged fresh accusations amid public discontent in parts of Azerbaijani society over new secular school uniform rules that have effectively banned the wearing of hijabs in schools. Iran has offered to enrol Azerbaijani girls wearing hijabs in Iranian schools and universities. In response, Azerbaijan’s Ministry of Science and Education said the remarks were inappropriate and amounted to an attempt to interfere in the country’s education policy. The ministry also pointed out that there were no schools or universities in Iran offering education in Azerbaijani, despite the fact that, according to the ministry, around 40 million ethnic Azerbaijanis live in Iran. “ For decades, they have been deprived of the opportunity to receive education in their native language ,” Azerbaijan’s Education Ministry said. 'Take off your hijab and come into class': what is happening in Azerbaijan’s schools? 37 people have been arrested during protests against requirements that school uniforms and teachers’ clothing comply with secular dress codes Invitation to study extended to schoolchildren On 22 October, Iran’s Minister of Science, Research and Technology, Hossein Simaei-Sarraf, published a video address inviting Azerbaijani girls to study at Iranian universities. He addressed his appeal to girls who, he said, were being forced to give up wearing hijabs in order to receive an education in Azerbaijan. On 25 October, Iran’s First Vice-President Mohammad Reza Aref joined the initiative. He called on the ministers of health and education, as well as the head of Islamic Azad University, to make arrangements for admitting schoolchildren and university students from Azerbaijan. The offer, initially limited to higher education, was thus extended to schoolchildren. However, the specific admission conditions remain unclear. It is not known which educational institutions would accept the students, what language classes would be taught in, who would cover the costs or how accommodation for underage students and their parents would be arranged. Azerbaijan's deputy prime minister visits Iran: what interests are bringing Baku and Tehran closer? At meetings in Tehran, Azerbaijan’s deputy prime minister discussed electricity supplies, border infrastructure and transport routes. Baku reminds Tehran of Azerbaijani-language education issue On 26 October, Azerbaijan’s Ministry of Science and Education responded to the Iranian minister’s statement. The ministry described interference in Azerbaijan’s education policy as unacceptable and urged Iranian officials to “deal with their own country’s problems”. Baku’s main criticism concerns the lack of opportunities to receive education in Azerbaijani in Iran. According to the ministry, there are no schools teaching in Azerbaijani in the country, nor is the language used as a medium of instruction at universities. Baku maintains that ethnic Azerbaijanis living in Iran have been deprived of the opportunity to receive education in their native language for decades. In response to the neighbouring country’s statements about protecting Azerbaijani girls’ right to education, Baku has raised the issue of the language rights of ethnic Azerbaijanis living in Iran. A separate practical question concerns the language in which the invited schoolchildren would be taught. While studying abroad in a foreign language is possible, it may require language training and support with adaptation. The Iranian proposal does not specify how the necessary arrangements would be made. Iran envoy: Georgia not the only destination for Iranians The embassy published a map of the Black Sea region showing only half of Georgia’s territory. How did dispute over wearing hijabs in Azerbaijan begin? A new wave of controversy began after Azerbaijan’s Cabinet of Ministers amended school uniform regulations on 21 September. Under the decree, the use of “additional items of clothing that undermine the uniformity of school uniforms and contradict the principle of secular education” is prohibited. Although the hijab is not explicitly mentioned in the document, complaints subsequently emerged that schoolgirls wearing headscarves were being barred from attending classes. Protests took place at several schools in Baku and other parts of Azerbaijan, involving students and parents. Some students refused to attend classes in solidarity with their classmates who wear hijabs. Police intervened during the protests. On 12 October, the Interior Ministry reported that 37 people had been detained in connection with incidents following the introduction of the new school uniform rules. According to the ministry, those detained were suspected of disturbing public order. A criminal case was also reportedly opened. Reports later emerged that another 200 people had been detained after taking part in a protest near the 28 May metro station in Baku. Criminal cases were also reportedly opened against some of them. Why Azerbaijan sees Talysh activism as security threat Kamal Isayev is serving an eight-and-a-half-year prison sentence, while concerns grow over Iqbal Abilov’s health in solitary confinement. Education dispute turns into political row Iranian officials have presented their initiative as an attempt to help girls wearing hijabs continue their education. However, the link between the offer and restrictions in Azerbaijan gives it a political dimension. Tehran is openly criticising Baku’s education policy and appealing to families dissatisfied with the restrictions. Azerbaijan’s response also focuses primarily on the political aspect of the issue rather than the conditions for admitting students. Instead of discussing arrangements for their enrolment in Iranian educational institutions, the ministry has accused Tehran of interfering in the country’s internal affairs and highlighted the lack of opportunities for ethnic Azerbaijanis living in Iran to receive education in their native language. However, the mutual accusations do not resolve either problem. Limited opportunities to receive education in Azerbaijani in Iran do not address complaints about schoolgirls wearing hijabs being barred from attending classes in Azerbaijan. In turn, Iran’s offer does not resolve the issue preventing these girls from continuing their education at their own schools. title: Troops kill eight suspected terrorists, rescue three abductees in three states – Military
body:
Troops of Operation Fansan Yamma killed eight suspected terrorists and rescued three kidnapped persons in separate operations in Katsina, Kaduna and Zamfara states over the weekend, the military has said.
The operations, conducted on 24 and 25 October, also led to the recovery of an AK-47 rifle, three locally fabricated guns, three motorcycles and other items.
The Media Information Officer of the Joint Task Force North-west, Tamuno Sinivie, disclosed this in a statement on Monday.
Mr Sinivie, a captain, said troops responded to a distress call from farmers around Machika Dam in Sabuwa Local Government Area of Katsina State on Saturday, following reports of suspected terrorist activities.
The troops engaged the suspects in a gun battle, killing two of them while others escaped, according to the statement.
A 42-year-old kidnap victim, Suleiman Umar, was rescued during the encounter. The troops also recovered an AK-47 rifle, ammunition and a motorcycle.
In neighbouring Kaduna State, six suspected terrorists were killed when troops and members of the Civilian Joint Task Force (CJTF) came under attack along Ungwan Iya in Igabi Local Government Area.
The troops had been pursuing armed men who reportedly attacked Ungwan Mallami village and abducted two residents.
Mr Sinivie said the suspects ambushed the troops during the pursuit, but six were killed in the ensuing exchange of gunfire.
Three locally fabricated guns, two motorcycles, cutlasses and assorted charms were recovered.
The military did not say whether the two residents abducted from Ungwan Mallami were rescued or remained in captivity.
In Zamfara State, troops rescued two kidnapped persons at Bagega in Anka Local Government Area on Sunday.
The victims, Shehu Chete, 40, and Bugu Bedi, 25, both from Kebbi State, were reportedly abandoned by their captors when soldiers approached their location during a surveillance operation.
They were taken to Bagega Clinic for medical attention before being moved to a military base.
Mr Sinivie said troops were continuing patrols in the affected areas to track fleeing suspects and prevent further attacks.
The military’s account of the encounters and the reported casualty figures could not be independently verified by PREMIUM TIMES.

title: Election Day: A complete guide to Israel’s political parties and what they stand for
body: Israelis head to the polls today to elect the country's next Knesset, with parties competing for votes and a chance to shape the country's future.But what does each party stand for, who leads it, and what are its key policies and priorities?The Jerusalem Post has prepared a series of explainers breaking down the platforms, leaders, and main positions of all the main parties running in the election.Explore our guides below to learn what each party stands for before casting your vote.What does Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar stand for?Led by former IDF chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot, Yashar is a centrist party focused on national security, government reform, and replacing Benjamin Netanyahu. Yashar is part of the opposition bloc.Ballot letters: דרך | Explore Yashar's policies and platformWhat does Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud stand for?Led by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Likud is a right-wing party that emphasizes national security, Jewish nationalism, and a strong stance against Palestinian statehood. The Likud heads the right-wing bloc and Netanyahu's sitting coalition.Ballot letters: מחל | Explore Likud's policies and platformWhat does Naftali Bennett's B'Yachad stand for?Led by former prime minister Naftali Bennett, B'Yachad is a centrist party focused on government reform, economic growth, and the enlistment of haredi (ultra-Orthodox) men into the IDF. B'Yachad is part of the opposition bloc.Ballot letters: רק | Explore B'Yachad's policies and platformWhat does Yair Golan's Democrats stand for?Led by Yair Golan, the Democrats is a left-wing, Zionist party that emphasizes liberal democracy, civil rights, education reform, and a greater equality in military service. The Democrats is part of the opposition bloc.Ballot letters: אמת | Explore the Democrats' policies and platformWhat does Avigdor Liberman's Yisrael Beytenu stand for?Led by Avigdor Liberman, Yisrael Beytenu is a right-wing, secular nationalist party focused on national security, a tougher stance against Hamas, and reducing the influence of religious parties in government. Yisrael Beytenu is part of the opposition bloc.Ballot letter: ל | Explore Yisrael Beytenu's policies and platformWhat does Itamar Ben-Gvir's Otzma Yehudit stand for?Led by National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir, Otzma Yehudit is a far-right nationalist party that advocates a hardline approach to security threats, expanded Jewish settlement, and tougher law enforcement. Otzma Yehudit is part of the Netanyahu bloc and the sitting coalition.Ballot letter: ב | Explore Otzma Yehudit's policies and platformWhat do the Joint List and Ra'am stand for?The Joint List and Ra'am represent different strands of Arab Israeli politics. The Joint List is generally left-wing and emphasizes equality, civil rights, and Palestinian national rights, while Mansour Abbas's Ra'am takes a more pragmatic approach focused on tackling crime, securing funding, and improving living conditions in Arab communities.Ballot letters: ודם (Joint List); עמ (Ra'am) | Explore the Joint List and Ra'am's policies and platformWhat do Shas and United Torah Judaism stand for?Shas and United Torah Judaism (UTJ) are ultra-Orthodox (haredi) parties that prioritize protecting the status of religious institutions in Israel and maintaining broad exemptions from IDF service for yeshiva students.Shas primarily represents Sephardi and Mizrahi haredi and religious Jews, while UTJ represents Ashkenazi haredi communities. Both parties are part of the Netanyahu bloc and were part of the sitting coalition.Ballot letters: שס (Shas); ג (UTJ) | Explore Shas and United Torah Judaism's policies and platformWhat does Bezalel Smotrich's RZP-Zehut stand for?Led by Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich and Zehut leader Moshe Feiglin, Religious Zionist Party-Zehut is a far-right, religious-nationalist party that supports expanding West Bank settlements, applying Israeli sovereignty over the territory, and advancing judicial reform. RZP is part of the Netanyahu bloc and the sitting coalition.Ballot letter: ט | Explore Religious Zionist Party's policies and platformWhat about the parties hovering above - or below - the electoral threshold?Several parties are fighting to secure enough votes to enter the Knesset, with the 3.25% electoral threshold determining which lists win parliamentary representation. For these parties, even a small shift in voter support could determine whether they enter the next Knesset or leave their supporters without representation.Recent polls have placed the People of Israel party and the Reservists-Economic Party near the threshold, with their standings varying between surveys. Their results could have a significant impact on the balance between the political blocs.Led by former IDF general Ofer Winter, People of Israel is a right-wing party that supports Benjamin Netanyahu for prime minister and calls for new leadership outside the political establishment.It makes haredi enlistment a condition for joining a government, rejects blanket exemptions for yeshiva students, and advocates a hardline security policy, including voluntary emigration from Gaza.The Reservists-Economic Party, led by former minister Yoaz Hendel and economist Yaron Zelekha, combines a right-leaning Zionist and security agenda with an emphasis on economic reform. The party says it will join only a Zionist government and demands that a universal conscription law be passed before a government is formed.Led by Moti Leitner, the Haredi Public Party seeks to offer an alternative to the established ultra-Orthodox parties, Shas and United Torah Judaism. It supports broader haredi military or national service, core-curriculum studies including math and English, and greater accountability from haredi political leadership.Ballot letters: ך (People of Israel); די (Reservists-Economic Party); זך (Haredi Public) | Explore these parties' policies and platforms

title: FACT CHECK: Marcos did not call for SC shutdown over budget ruling
body: Claim: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said he wants to shut down the Supreme Court (SC) after it ruled parts of the 2024 to 2026 national budgets unconstitutional. Rating: FALSE Why we fact-checked this: A video posted by Facebook user Ka’abs on October 24 claims, in overlaid text, that Marcos is speaking to reporters while being asked about a petition to the SC regarding the 2025 national budget. The text reads, “Dahil sa pagbunyag ng Supreme Court ng kabulastugan mo” and “Ngayon gusto mo ipa-shutdown ang Supreme Court, ano ka hilo?” (Because the Supreme Court exposed your wrongdoing, now you want the SC shut down. What’s wrong with you?) The caption repeats the text, followed by raised-fist and crocodile emojis. As of writing, the video has garnered over 795,000 views, 10,000 reactions, 3,400 comments, and 2,900 shares. The facts: No Palace statement or credible report shows Marcos seeking the SC’s shutdown. The clip’s original context shows he was referring to government operations. The part of him saying that everything will be “shut down” was taken out of context from a January 2025 video , and sensationalized. The original video shows an interview with Marcos in Cebu City, where he was asked what his administration would do if the SC ruled in favor of voiding the 2025 national budget. He answered, “No, we shut down everything.” This was after former executive secretary Vic Rodriguez and Davao Representative Isidro Ungab asked the Court to void the 2025 national budget. He then accused the petitioners of wanting “the government to cease working” so their “destabilization” could continue. He added that the solicitor general had assured him the budget was constitutionally sound. Rodriguez countered that the government would operate under a reenacted budget and “will never shut down.” Recent SC ruling: The clip resurfaced after the SC’s October 20 ruling on the 2024 and 2025 General Appropriations Acts as unconstitutional. On October 21, Palace Press Officer Claire Castro said Malacañang disagreed with parts of the ruling and had directed the Office of the Solicitor General to seek reconsideration. She added that the decision was not yet final, so spending under the 2026 budget would continue. In a 121-page decision written by Senior Associate Justice Marvic Leonen, the Court voted 13-2 to declare Congress’ P449.5-billion increase in 2024 unprogrammed appropriations and a P17.99-billion increase in the 2025 DPWH Special Road Fund as unconstitutional. It also struck down the SAGIP lump-sum allocations in the 2024 and 2025 budgets and key unprogrammed appropriations provisions in the 2026 budget. The SC ruled that the lower chamber committed grave abuse of discretion by exceeding the constitutional cap on the President’s recommended appropriations. It applied the doctrine of operative fact, which protects spending already made in good faith. (READ: 5 practical effects of SC ruling on unprogrammed appropriations ) Court spokesperson Camille Ting said the ruling is not yet final, and the solicitor general may file a motion for reconsideration within 15 days from notice. Navotas Representative Toby Tiangco said the ruling could prompt new impeachment complaints against Marcos once the one-year bar expires in February. – Cyril Bocar/Rappler.com Efren Cyril Bocar is a journalist from Llorente, Eastern Samar who graduated with a degree in English Language Studies at the Visayas State University. Cyril is also a graduate of the Aries Rufo Journalism Fellowship of Rappler for 2024. Keep us aware of suspicious Facebook pages, groups, accounts, websites, articles, or photos in your network by contacting us at factcheck@rappler.com. Let us battle disinformation one Fact Check at a time.

title: Iran remains proud, steadfast with its talented youth
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 27 (MNA) – Stating championship is a manifestation of will and determination of a nation that believes rights must be claimed, Iran’s President Masoud Pezeshkian emphasized Iran remains proud and steadfast thanks to its talented youth.
In a post on his X account late on Monday, Pezeshkian referred to the national Greco-Roman wrestling team’s championship, and wrote, “The champions of Iran’s national Greco-Roman wrestling team have once again reached the pinnacle of the world.”
He seized this opportunity to thank Iran’s national Greco-Roman wrestling team who once again raised the glorious name of the Islamic Iran on the international stages.
He reiterated that the Islamic Iran will remain proud and steadfast thanks to its talented youth.
The Iranian national Greco-Roman wrestling team claimed the world championship title earlier than the championships in Kazakhstan wraps up.
Despite the early win, the national Iranian Greco-Roman team has the chance to win four gold medals and one bronze medal across the six remaining weight classes.

title: Harry Kane becomes first Englishman in 25 years to win Ballon d'Or
body:
England's soccer player Harry Kane wins the trophy for striker of the year during the Ballon d'Or ceremony at the London Palladium Theatre in London, England, Monday, Oct. 26, 2026 . Kin Cheung/AP hide caption
LONDON — Harry Kane became the first Englishman in 25 years to win the Ballon d'Or on Monday thanks to his prolific scoring last season.
Kane scored 73 goals for club and country last campaign — he was Europe's top scorer — and smashed scoring records in Germany for Bayern Munich and at the World Cup, where he captained England to a third-place finish.
The 33-year-old Kane says winning the prestigious individual award was built on so much more.
"Anything is possible with hard work, when no one else is watching, to go through the ups and downs, to learn through resilience, determination and self-belief," an emotional Kane said in a message to young players, after reflecting on his early career struggles.
"My journey wasn't straightforward. I wasn't the kid who went straight to the top. I had to experience the downs," he added. "I had to fight my way to be the very best right now. I hope that can give you inspiration as well."
Kane was followed in the voting by Kylian Mbappé, Lamine Yamal — voted best young talent for a third straight year — 2024 winner Rodri and record eight-time winner Lionel Messi.
Kane thanked his teammates, coaches, parents, children — "It's past your bedtime" — and wife Kate, " my best friend. We've been through ups and downs for sure. You're my biggest supporter. You always want the best for me."
Kane led Bayern to the Bundesliga and German Cup double, scoring a hat trick against Stuttgart in the cup final. Bayern also reached the Champions League semifinals.
At the World Cup, he scored six times to pass Gary Lineker as England's all-time leading World Cup scorer and placed himself among the all-time top five in tournament history. His lineup lost to Argentina in the semifinals but beat Mbappé's France for third place, England's best World Cup placing in 60 years.
An Englishman hadn't won the Ballon d'Or since Michael Owen in 2001.
"It's massive for England, for our country. (The ceremony) being here in London was a good omen for me," Kane said. "It's been too long. Certainly (there have been) incredible English players... To put us back on the map, to put us here with this trophy I'm extremely proud. Playing for England is my biggest honor, the thing I love to do the most."
England coach Thomas Tuchel told Kane the Three Lions are "lucky to have you as our leader."
"I ran out of superlatives to describe your performances a long time ago, but I'm delighted to see that you have now been formally recognized by the football world," Tuchel said.
Fans packed the streets and climbed light poles near the London Palladium, where the event was held, for a glimpse of the arriving athletes. Kane stopped to sign autographs on his way in.
They stayed through the ceremony and chanted Kane's name as he left the theater near Oxford Circus after midnight.
Kane planned to celebrate with family and friends, but just a little.
"We have a cup game on Wednesday so it can't get too messy," Kane said, noting he has an early Tuesday flight back to Munich in time for team training.
Monday's ceremony was held in London for the first time in recognition of the inaugural winner 70 years ago, England's Stanley Matthews in 1956.
Spain's London City Lionesses' Alexia Putellas wins the player of the year trophy during the Ballon d'Or ceremony at the London Palladium Theatre in London, England, Monday, Oct. 26, 2026 . Kin Cheung/AP hide caption
Earlier, Spain star Alexia Putellas won her record-equaling third women's Ballon d'Or after leading her former club Barcelona to multiple trophies last season including the Women's Champions League.
Putellas, who joined London City Lionesses in the offseason, also helped Spain win the Women's Nations League last December.
The 32-year-old midfielder ended Spain teammate Aitana Bonmati's three-year reign.
Putellas won the prestigious award in 2021 and 2022, tore her ACL and saw Bonmati rise to stardom. Bonmati, who completed her women's Ballon d'Or three-peat in 2025, was not on this year's shortlist after breaking her leg in December.
There wasn't a women's Ballon d'Or until 2018, when Ada Hegerberg won it.
Putellas urged young players to approach the sport with "love and passion."
"Believe in yourself, that's the most important thing," she said. "If you have a dream, go for it, even if at some point you have to start from zero."
Putellas had joined Barcelona in 2012 and called her time at the Catalan club "something special."
"I'm really grateful for having 14 seasons as a player (at Barcelona)," she said. "What I experienced last year was like a perfect story."

title: Trump and Rubio plan to visit oil tanker carrying Venezuelan crude in Texas
body:
President Donald Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio plan to showcase a newly arrived oil tanker filled with Venezuelan crude in Texas on Tuesday
WASHINGTON -- President Donald Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Tuesday plan to show off a newly arrived oil tanker filled with Venezuelan crude to be processed in Texas refineries, according to a congressional aide and two U.S. officials.
The visit to Port Arthur, Texas, comes on the same day that Trump is campaigning in the state for Republican candidates in the midterms.
The president has rallies scheduled in Corpus Christi and Lubbock. Trump is trying to shore up support for U.S. Senate candidate Ken Paxton, who is locked in a tight race with Democratic candidate James Talarico.
It’s not clear whether Rubio, who also serves as Trump's national security adviser, would take part in any campaign events. But it's the first time that he's hitting the road with Trump as the president barnstorms the country.
The two U.S. officials and the congressional aide spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss Rubio's plans before they were publicly announced.
It's highly unusual for the nation's top diplomat to participate in political travel. Rubio's trip would be the latest example of how Trump's second presidency has blurred the lines between governing and campaigning. Attorney General Todd Blanche has already been appearing at rallies alongside Republican candidates.
Rubio previously ran for president in 2016 and is considered a top prospect in 2028. He has not said whether he will run, and his political activities have been limited since becoming secretary of state.

title: UBA Launches Group-Wide Climate Action Week to Advance Green Finance
body: United Bank for Africa (UBA) Plc has launched a Group-wide Climate Action Week to deepen climate awareness, promote responsible environmental practices and advance sustainable finance across its African and international operations. The five-day campaign, running from October 26 to 30, 2026, is themed “Banking on Africa’s Climate Future” and reflects the Bank’s commitment to integrating environmental responsibility into its operations, customer engagement and financing solutions. The initiative commenced with the deployment of waste segregation bins across UBA offices and measures to reduce the use of single-use plastics at the Bank’s head offices. These activities underscore UBA’s commitment to translating sustainability principles into practical actions within its workplace and across its wider ecosystem. Throughout the week, UBA will disseminate educational content across its media and digital platforms to highlight the causes and consequences of climate change, including its impact on food prices, energy consumption and urban flooding. The campaign will also promote responsible plastic disposal, recycling and the critical role of financial institutions in financing clean energy, sustainable agriculture and other environmentally responsible businesses. As part of the campaign’s community engagement component, UBA staff volunteers will participate in a Group-wide clean-up exercise on Saturday, November 7, in major cities across its markets. In Nigeria, the exercise will take place in Lagos, Kano and Port Harcourt, mobilising employees to contribute directly to cleaner and healthier communities. UBA’s Group Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer, Oliver Alawuba, emphasised the importance of collective responsibility in addressing the growing impact of climate change. “Climate change is no longer a distant environmental concern; it is increasingly shaping everyday life across Africa. We see its effects in rising food costs, increased energy demand and flooding that disrupts homes, businesses and livelihoods. “At UBA, we believe that building a sustainable future requires collective action, beginning with the choices we make at work, at home and in our communities. Through this Climate Action Week, we are encouraging every member of the UBA Tribe, alongside our customers and other stakeholders, to embrace practical, sustainable habits and inspire others to do the same,” Alawuba said. As part of its stakeholder engagement activities, UBA will sponsor Climate Convergence Week in Lagos on Friday, October 30, where the Bank will deliver a speaking session and participate in a panel discussion. The engagement will provide an opportunity to showcase UBA Green Finance, highlight the Bank’s sustainability initiatives and explore how financial institutions can support Africa’s transition to a more sustainable and climate-resilient economy. Alawuba, noted that climate considerations were increasingly important to business resilience, risk management and long-term economic growth. “Climate change presents significant risks to businesses, communities and economies. These risks can affect business continuity, operating costs and financial performance, making sustainability an increasingly important consideration for both businesses and the financial institutions that support them. “Through UBA Green Finance, we seek to support eligible businesses investing in cleaner technologies and more sustainable operations. By helping customers explore financing solutions aligned with their needs, we can contribute to a more resilient private sector while unlocking opportunities for sustainable economic growth across Africa,” Alawuba further said. In a further step towards strengthening its sustainability capabilities, UBA is set to join the Sustainability Professionals Institute of Nigeria (SPIN). The move is expected to deepen the Bank’s environmental, social and governance (ESG) expertise and support the continued professional development of its employees in sustainability-related disciplines. The Climate Action Week forms part of UBA’s broader sustainability strategy, which integrates environmental responsibility into its Customer First philosophy through responsible business practices, employee engagement, community initiatives and green finance. By combining awareness, practical action and financing solutions, the Bank aims to encourage more sustainable choices while supporting businesses and communities in navigating the challenges and opportunities of climate change.

title: The Mythical Man-Month in the Age of AI
body:
Last weekend I watched four people desperately trying to get a laptop to connect to a screen. I was happily observing their efforts, with zero intent to join in.
But someone nudged me: can't you have a look at it?
My reply: "Haha sorry no! My experience is that adding more people will not solve this problem any quicker".
I was of course -- indirectly -- referring to Brooks's Law:
"Adding manpower to a late software project makes it later."
It was formulated by computer scientist Frederick P. Brooks Jr. in his 1975 book The Mythical Man-Month, based on his experience managing the IBM OS/360 project.
However I got to thinking. Does this still hold up in the age of AI agents and LLMs?
At first glance, you’d think no. The traditional bottlenecks -- onboarding time, endless stand-ups, and office politics -- disappear overnight. An AI agent is up to speed in milliseconds and doesn't demand a coffee break.
But when you look closer, and the law hasn't vanished. It just mutated.
The famous "Baby Problem" remains: nine agents still can’t deliver a baby in one month. Sequential tasks are still sequential.
Overhead hasn't disappeared; it shifted: instead of managing people, you are now managing agents. Someone still needs to define "done", review the code, catch hallucinations, and stitch the pieces together.
Throw nine autonomous agents at a single codebase without crystal-clear orchestration, and they will happily rewrite each other's work in a high-speed loop.
Maybe the 2026 update to Brooks’s Law should be:
"Adding agents to a project with unclear requirements gets you the wrong answer faster."
