title: Postava impresses in first NHL start
body:
EDMONTON – Netminder Michal Postava was rock solid in his first NHL start for the Detroit Red Wings on Monday.
Postava made 25 saves and added three more in the shootout session to earn the win. Lucas Raymond scored the shootout winner and had a pair of assists as the Red Wings came away with a 4-3 victory over the Edmonton Oilers.
“It’s amazing, I feel like a kid,” Postava said. “I watched all those NHL games when I was young, and I didn’t expect to one day be in the net and win the game. Now I’m just so happy.
“I just wanted to enjoy the game and try to help the guys and make some saves. That was the only mentality that I had.”
Postava, a 24-year-old undrafted netminder from Czechia, was actually appearing in his second career game, replacing John Gibson in the third period of a 5-2 win against the Vancouver Canucks last Thursday.
He became just the third Red Wings goaltender in the past quarter century to win in his first NHL start, joining Petr Mrazek (2013) and Jimmy Howard (2005).
“I was excited and a little nervous, just like I am for every game,” Postava said. “But it was my first NHL start so I just tried to enjoy the game and play my best hockey and I think I can be better next time, but it was an important win for us.”
Postava also became the third goaltender in NHL history to win his first career start against a team that featured the NHL’s top two leading scorers entering play in Edmonton forwards Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl.
“It’s crazy,” Postava said. “You look at how many points they have so far and I think they’re two of the best players in the world right now, so maybe it was more amazing for me to win.”
Detroit head coach Todd McLellan was impressed with his young goalie.
“He’s very athletic, we think he anticipates so well, he can read where the shot release is going,” McLellan said. “He’s been in our organization for a year-and-a-half now. When you trade a first-round draft pick, a future goalie away (Sebastian Cossa) you should know what you have and we had a pretty good idea that Postava was what you saw tonight.”
Viktor Arvidsson, Emmitt Finnie and Dylan Larkin scored in regulation for the Red Wings (5-4-3) who went 2-1-1 on their Northwestern road trip.
“We finished off the road trip in the right way, so it’s been good,” Arvidsson said. “I’m happy for the team that we can go home and have a good road trip behind us.”
Detroit trailed three times in Monday’s contest and tied the game once again with just 1:17 remaining in the third and their goalie pulled as a bouncing puck came to Larkin in front and he shovelled in just his second of the season.
It was the third time this season that Detroit has scored a game-tying goal in the final two minutes of regulation, which stands as the most among all clubs.
“Against this team you can’t let them get the next one,” McLellan said. “They get rolling, they get a lot of confidence, but we responded appropriately all three times. We’ve been a pretty resilient group for most of the season, and we saw it again tonight.”
Arvidsson’s goal came on the power play. It was his fourth, trailing only Draisaitl (six) and Nick Schmaltz (five) in that category.
Moritz Seider recorded an assist to tie Dennis Seidenberg (207) for the third-most helpers from a German defenceman in NHL history.
Vasily Podkolzin, Isaac Howard and Colton Dach replied for the Oilers (8-2-2) who have dropped two straight and also lost forward Zach Hyman to what looked to be a concussion.
McDavid extended his season-starting points streak to 12 games, now with a staggering 34 points in that span. He matched the longest season-opening assist streak in NHL history, equalling Sebastian Aho, Ken Linseman and Wayne Gretzky.
This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 26, 2026.

title: Jay-Z picks himself to headline the Super Bowl halftime show in Southern California
body:
FILE - Jay-Z gestures from the sidelines prior to the NFL Super Bowl 59 football game, Feb. 9, 2025, in New Orleans. Frank Franklin II/AP hide caption
LOS ANGELES — The man who has helped produce the Super Bowl halftime show is stepping into the spotlight: Jay-Z will headline the show himself.
The NFL, Apple Music and Roc Nation announced Monday night that Jay-Z will be the featured performer for the halftime festivities on Feb. 14 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.
NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said he had one request when the league first reached an agreement with Roc Nation: that Jay-Z take the stage himself "whenever the moment felt right to him."
"From 'Reasonable Doubt' to standing on the Super Bowl halftime stage, this has been a journey," Jay-Z said in a statement. "Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world's biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true."
After days of speculation, Jay-Z is set to return to the stadium where he closed his celebration of the 30th anniversary of "Reasonable Doubt," the mogul's 1996 debut album. The concerts included three sold-out shows at Yankee Stadium and sold-out performances in London and Paris ahead of a stop at SoFi Stadium over the weekend.
Jay-Z's Roc Nation has partnered with the NFL since 2019 to advise on and help produce the league's entertainment presentations, including the Super Bowl halftime show. At the time, Jay-Z said he had told Goodell, "If this is about me performing at the Super Bowl, then we can just end this conversation now."
Seven years later, Jay-Z is ready to perform after all.
Jay-Z, born Shawn Carter, has won 25 Grammy Awards and received 89 nominations, the second-most in history behind his wife, Beyoncé — who has performed at two Super Bowls. His catalog also includes the albums "The Blueprint" and "The Black Album," and hit songs such as "Hard Knock Life (Ghetto Anthem)," "99 Problems" and "Empire State of Mind," his collaboration with Alicia Keys.
Last year, "Reasonable Doubt" was inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame.
His recent concerts brought out a rotating cast of guests. At SoFi Stadium, his daughter Blue Ivy played piano on "The Story of O.J." and "Dead Presidents," while Scarface, John Legend and DJ Khaled joined him on opening night. Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg and Too $hort appeared during Saturday's finale.
Earlier in the run, Beyoncé, Rihanna, Eminem and Nas were among the guests at Yankee Stadium.
Jay-Z has built a career as an executive and entrepreneur. The Brooklyn rapper co-founded Roc-A-Fella Records and founded Roc Nation in 2008, building it into an entertainment company that works with artists and athletes.
Jay-Z became the first rapper inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame in 2017 and joined the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2021. He is also a four-time Emmy winner.
Roc Nation will executive produce the halftime show, with Hamish Hamilton directing.
The halftime show has collected Emmys in recent years. Bad Bunny's performance in February won a record seven, including best variety special (live), while Kendrick Lamar's show last year won for music direction.

title: Brewers rout the Rays 10-1 to move within a win of their first World Series title
body:
Milwaukee Brewers' Garrett Mitchell, left, celebrates past Tampa Bay Rays catcher Nick Fortes after scoring during the fifth inning of Game 3 of baseball's World Series, Monday, Oct. 26, 2026, in St. Petersburg, Fla., between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Tampa Bay Rays. Ashley Landis/AP hide caption
ST. PETERSBURG, Fla. — Jackson Chourio set the tone at the plate, Brice Turang sparked an historic offensive outburst and Robert Gasser shut the door on the mound.
The Milwaukee Brewers are one victory from their first World Series title after routing the Tampa Bay Rays 10-1 on Monday night thanks to a trio of young players who have shined in October.
Chourio bookended Milwaukee's eight-run fifth inning with two of his four hits, and Turang's two-run single opened a barrage of scoring with two outs.
"He was tremendous. Locked in. Gives us a big lift," Brewers manager Pat Murphy said about Chourio, who has eight hits in three Series games.
Gasser, a rookie left-hander, pitched one-hit ball and faced the minimum through six innings as Milwaukee rolled to a 3-0 lead in this Fall Classic. Game 4 is Tuesday night at Tropicana Field, where many Brewers fans showed up Monday and cheered from behind the visitors' dugout.
"It is really cool when you go on the road in such an intense atmosphere to have that support," Gasser said. "Normally it's 35,000 against nine, but tonight we had 20,000 people behind us."
Gasser allowed a line-drive single to Yandy Díaz leading off the bottom of the first and then retired 14 straight before Victor Mesa Jr. walked to begin the Tampa Bay sixth.
Tampa Bay Rays pitcher Cam Booser leaves the game during the fifth inning of Game 3 of baseball's World Series, Monday, Oct. 26, 2026, in St. Petersburg, Fla., between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Tampa Bay Rays. Ashley Landis/AP hide caption
With the help of a caught stealing and a double play, Gasser became the first starter to face the minimum 18 batters through six innings of a World Series game since Arizona's Curt Schilling in 2001 — and the first lefty to do it since Sandy Koufax for the Los Angeles Dodgers in 1965.
Chourio finished 4 for 5 with a double. Turang and William Contreras each went 3 for 5 as Milwaukee racked up 16 hits off "Fastball Freddy" Peralta and five relievers to win its eighth straight game — tying the record for a single postseason.
"I think that you could say this is one of my better games," Chourio said through a translator. "Really I was just taking every at-bat like it could be my last and trying to find any way I could to get on base."
Of the 43 previous major league teams to fall behind 3-0 in a best-of-seven postseason series, only the 2004 Boston Red Sox rallied to win four straight when they beat the New York Yankees in the American League Championship Series.
"It's kind of that chip and a chair mentality," Rays manager Kevin Cash said. "We've got a seat at the table. We've got to do something with the chip. Obviously the only thing we can do is win tomorrow."
Gasser became the first starter for Milwaukee to get an out in the sixth inning this postseason. He's allowed one run in 15 innings over three starts, all on the road.
Peralta, the MVP of the ALCS against Cleveland, ran out of gas against the Brewers. He was charged with five runs and seven hits in 4 2/3 innings against his former team.
"Just a little out of sync. I think he felt really good. Tried to power through it a little bit," Cash said. "Just inconsistencies in and out of the strike zone led to a bunch of really good at-bats by the Brewer lineup."
After a pair of tense, down-to-the-final-pitch, one-run games in Milwaukee, the Brewers put this one out of reach in the fifth with a postseason-record seven straight hits — all with two outs.
It was the first time in World Series history a team scored eight two-out runs in one inning.
"I was sitting in the dugout getting ready to go. There was two outs, and next thing you know, 40 minutes later, I have to go out on the field," Gasser said. "It was special. I had a smile on my face the whole time. It's just surreal when something like that happens."
Chourio began the rally with a one-out single and then stole second with two outs. Christian Yelich walked, and Peralta exited after Contreras' infield single loaded the bases.
The inning appeared to end when third baseman Junior Caminero fielded Contreras' bouncer and threw to second base for a forceout. But the call at second was overturned after a replay review, and Cam Booser entered.
Turang ripped a liner that shortstop Taylor Walls couldn't short hop. It bounced off his glove and rolled into shallow center field for a two-run single.
Garrett Mitchell followed with an RBI single, Cooper Pratt grounded a two-run double down the left-field line and Sal Frelick lined a run-scoring double to make it 8-0.
"It's definitely deflating," Cash said. "How could it not be?"
Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Brandon Woodruff celebrates their win with catcher Gary Sánchez in Game 3 of baseball's World Series, Monday, Oct. 26, 2026, in St. Petersburg, Fla., between the Milwaukee Brewers and the Tampa Bay Rays. Ashley Landis/AP hide caption
Cole Sulser replaced Booser and allowed an RBI single to David Hamilton and an RBI double to the 22-year-old Chourio, who became the second-youngest player with four hits and a stolen base in a World Series game behind Ty Cobb in 1908.
Murphy has compared Chourio to Pro Basketball Hall of Famer Kobe Bryant.
"Kobe was one of the best basketball players of all-time," Chourio said. "I had the opportunity to read his book, some of it at least, but the discipline he had, I think that's what you try to (take) from the great ones. You just take little things you can take from them and implement it into your own game. Hopefully I'm doing a little bit of that."
Brandon Woodruff pitched the ninth for the Brewers, allowing one run and two hits in his first appearance in 3 1/2 months. The two-time All-Star had been sidelined by a shoulder injury that originally was thought to require surgery.
Of the 25 previous teams that took a 3-0 lead in the World Series, 21 swept and four won in five games.
Originally the Seattle Pilots for one season in 1969, the franchise moved to Milwaukee and was renamed the Brewers in 1970. Their only other World Series trip came as an AL team and ended with a Game 7 loss to St. Louis in 1982.
Led by the 67-year-old Murphy, the Brewers need just one more win to end their championship drought.
The Rays led the AL with 98 wins in the regular season, swept the Yankees in three games in the Division Series and beat the Guardians in six games in the ALCS.
But they made uncharacteristic mistakes on the bases and defense during the first two games in Milwaukee, and completely unraveled at home.
Tampa Bay also has never won a World Series in 29 seasons. The Rays lost to the Phillies in five games in 2008 and to the Dodgers in six games in 2020.
Wearing their white Devil Rays uniforms, they were eager to play in front of their home fans at the quirky, cavernous Trop, which had its roof shredded by Hurricane Milton in October 2024 and needed major renovations.
But their cowbell-ringing, towel-waving fans among a sellout crowd of 40,388 couldn't lift them past the surging Brewers.
Milwaukee led the majors with 103 wins, beat the Padres in four games in their NLDS and swept the Dodgers in the NLCS. With a win in Game 4, the Brewers would become the first team to sweep an LCS and World Series since the 1976 Cincinnati Reds.
Griffin Jax is scheduled to start Game 4 for Tampa Bay. The Brewers hadn't announced a starter.
"We've been preparing for this day a lot," Chourio said. "We have one more to lock in for tomorrow to complete the mission."

title: Iran slams US economic sanctions to destabilize energy market
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 27 (MNA) – Strongly condemning unilateral US economic sanctions for destabilizing the global energy markets, Iran’s caretaker oil minister says global energy security strictly hinges on respecting national sovereignty.
Addressing the 28th Ministerial Meeting of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) in Moscow, Hamid Bovard emphasized that the recent US-Israeli war against Iran has once again proven that energy security is not merely an economic or technical issue.
Bovard opened his remarks by honoring the martyrs of the recent US-Israeli aggression against Iran, paying special tribute to the martyred Leader of the Islamic Revolution, Ayatollah Seyyed Ali Khamenei, as well as innocent civilians, including the children of the Minab school and athletes of the Lamerd sports club.
He warned that such acts of aggression have consequences that extend far beyond regional borders, threatening global energy supply and economic development.
"US military interventions in various regions, including the Persian Gulf, and unilateral economic sanctions not only target the legitimate rights and interests of the Iranian nation but also negatively impact the climate of trust, investment security, and the predictability of global energy markets," Bovard stated.
Highlighting the GECF's 25th anniversary, the Acting Oil Minister called for a unified front against unbalanced climate regulations, specifically criticizing mechanisms like the European Union’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), which threaten to impose unfair restrictions on energy trade and investment.
Bovard proposed an ambitious new roadmap for the GECF secretariat to increase the share of natural gas in the global energy mix to an unprecedented 30 percent.
According to the forum's global gas outlook, worldwide demand for natural gas is projected to surge by 31 percent to over 5,400 billion cubic meters (bcm) by 2055, raising its share in the global energy basket from 23 to 26 percent.

title: Zelensky after Russian strike on Kyiv: Delays in air defense support Ukraine enable terrorism
body:
Volodymyr Zelensky made this statement on Telegram , according to Ukrinform.
“Russian ballistic missiles struck the grounds of one of Kyiv’s universities and the surrounding area—essentially the campus, Kyoto Park, the area near the metro station, and residential buildings. It is not yet known exactly how many people were affected. But, unfortunately, there are casualties. There are wounded. Rescue operations are ongoing. There is extensive damage, and there are reports that people may be trapped under the rubble,” he wrote, noting that all relevant emergency services on the ground are doing their job—rescuing people.
Zelensky emphasized that the missiles struck in very crowded areas where there are no military facilities nearby—this was simply an attack on the city and its infrastructure.
Unfortunately, the head of state warned, there may be repeat strikes.
“And it is precisely under such conditions—when the threat is constant, when strikes can occur at any moment and target cities and villages—that artificial delays by air defense forces only aid the terrorists,” the President stated.
He noted that it is important for political agreements to be promptly implemented at the operational level. It is also important for partners to understand that Ukraine needs the proper tools to destroy Russian ballistic missile launchers. According to Zelensky, this would be the most effective way to save lives.
“It is important for the world to see that Russia demonstrates nothing but a desire to kill and continue the war. Ukraine must not be left to face this alone, and it is entirely Russia’s fault that the war is still ongoing and people are still dying. Please, take care of yourselves. All partners should stand with Ukraine in protecting lives,” the President of Ukraine concluded.
As reported, on the evening of October 26, Russian troops launched a ballistic missile strike on Kyiv. As of 11:24 p.m., one person was reported dead and ten wounded.

title: FBI arrests 9 Nigerians, tracks $11m in fresh fraud crackdown — US Mission
body: By Nkiruka Nnorom & Marvellous Chukwunenye The United States Mission in Nigeria has announced a major breakthrough in the fight against transnational cybercrime, with the Federal Bureau of Investigation, FBI, arresting nine suspects in Nigeria in an operation targeting scam centres stealing billions of dollars from Americans. FBI Director, Kash Patel, disclosed this in a post on X which was reposted by the US Mission in Nigeria, saying the operation, code-named Operation Blackout, is taking the fight directly to international cybercriminal networks. According to Patel, the Nigeria operation delivered nine arrests, seizure of 53 electronic devices and identification of $11 million in potentially freezable funds across multiple countries. “Operation Blackout is taking the fight directly to the international cybercriminal networks stealing billions from Americans,” Patel said. “These scam centers exploit innocent victims, steal life savings, and operate across international borders believing they are beyond the reach of law enforcement. They’re wrong,” he stated. He commended Nigerian law enforcement and partners in London for their cooperation. “Thanks to Nigerian law enforcement and our partners in London for their outstanding cooperation,” Patel said, warning: “To the criminals targeting Americans from overseas: Justice will fibd you.” While the FBI did not name the Nigerian agency involved or the locations of the arrests, the operation is part of a wider international enforcement exercise coordinated from London. According to the US Department of Justice, the broader crackdown resulted in 28 arrests across Nigeria and Ghana and the seizure of hundreds of electronic devices. The operation also involved Meta and 14 other technology companies, leading to the removal of more than 3.7 million fraudulent accounts, pages and groups linked to West African scam networks. Reports indicate that 19 of the arrests were made in Ghana, where 117 victims, said to have been trafficked and forced to work in a residential compound running scam operations, are pending repatriation to Nigeria. The arrests come amid heightened US-Nigeria cooperation on cybercrime. In September, South African authorities handed over six Nigerians to FBI officials over allegations of defrauding more than 100 women in a romance scam scheme. In August, the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission, EFCC, extradited two Nigerians to the US over alleged online sexual exploitation and sextortion of two teenage boys who later died by suicide. In August 2025, the FBI arrested 22 Nigerians for alleged involvement in financially motivated sextortion schemes linked to a rise in suicides among American teenagers. The FBI said Nigerian authorities will prosecute the nine suspects arrested in the latest operation for violations of Nigerian law, while investigations continue to freeze the $11 million identified across several countries. The post FBI arrests 9 Nigerians, tracks $11m in fresh fraud crackdown — US Mission appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: NESG presents mixed outcomes for Nigeria’s economic reforms
body: •Says stabilisation creates conditions for progress but doesn’t deliver it By Emeka Anaeto, Business Editor Amid ongoing debates among stakeholders over the performance of Nigeria’s three-and-a-half-year-old economic reforms, the Nigerian Economic Summit Group (NESG) has declared that the reforms have so far delivered a mixed bag of outcomes, with negative gaps far outweighing the positives. Welcoming an array of Nigerian business elites at the 32nd edition of the Nigeria Economic Summit in Abuja yesterday, the Chairman of NESG, Mr Niyi Yusuf, said that although the reforms had delivered a measure of stability, stabilisation may create conditions for economic progress but does not deliver it. Dissecting the major outcomes of the reforms so far, Yusuf stated: “Nigeria’s economic performance presents a mixed picture. Key macro indicators are improving, but significant constraints limit the transmission of these gains to businesses and households. “Real GDP grew by 4.43% year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026, compared with 3.89% in the first quarter. Headline inflation stood at 14.63% in September, down from 34.8% in 2024. Gross external reserves reached approximately US$55.1 billion in October 2026. “These developments deserve recognition.” He added: “However, food inflation remained at 19.59% in September. Slower inflation does not mean prices have become affordable; it means they are rising more slowly from levels that already strain household budgets. “The productive economy also faces constraints. Electricity and gas sector output reportedly contracted by approximately 11.6% in the first half of 2026, as generation fell from 5,400 MW in Q4 2025 to 4,454 MW in Q2 2026. Maximum lending rates stood at about 29.2% in August, while private-sector credit declined to 18.1% of GDP.” He further noted: “Nigeria attracted approximately US$23.2 billion in foreign capital inflows so far in 2026, but portfolio investment dominated, with foreign direct investment accounting for only a small proportion. “Public debt is rising and stood at N166.79 trillion in June 2026, while debt servicing has moderated to about 50% of federal revenue. However, transformation requires patient capital and longer-term investment in productive assets.” Giving NESG’s overall position on the performance of the reforms so far, Yusuf stated: “These reforms have imposed considerable pressure on households and businesses, but they have also created an opportunity to reconsider the foundations of our socio-economic development. “Our responsibility now is to ensure that reform translates into stronger enterprises, better jobs, more productive workers, rising incomes, improved living standards and shared prosperity. This is the central purpose of NES #32. “Nigeria’s recent reforms, including petrol subsidy removal, foreign exchange liberalisation, fiscal restructuring, tax reforms and recapitalisation of the banking sector, represent significant changes to our economic policy framework. “These measures were necessary to address distortions that weakened public finances and constrained the efficient allocation of resources. “However, stabilisation creates the conditions for progress; it does not automatically deliver it. For instance, a more stable exchange rate does not, by itself, make a manufacturer competitive. “For households, reform must mean decent jobs, greater purchasing power, improved security and reduced poverty. “For businesses, it must mean lower production costs, reliable infrastructure, including power, higher productivity and affordable financing.” Yusuf also outlined the focus of the 2026 NESG under the theme, “Growth that Works: Delivering Jobs, Productivity and Shared Prosperity,” saying it expresses a fundamental proposition: economic growth must create value, expand opportunity and improve lives. He stated: “GDP growth alone cannot tell us whether enterprises are becoming more competitive or households are better off. We must judge success by the quality of jobs, the productivity of businesses and how widely prosperity reaches our people. “Three interdependent priorities guide this Summit: Productivity, which asks how to reduce production costs, optimise outputs and strengthen competitiveness; Human Capital, which asks how to invest in education, healthcare, nutrition and skills; and Resilience, which asks how to help households and businesses withstand shocks. “These three priorities reinforce one another. Skilled workers are more productive when enterprises have reliable infrastructure and access to technology. “Competitive businesses generate jobs and expand investment when there are predictable regulations, fair competition and an efficient legal system. “Effective public services, including security and social protection systems, help households sustain their participation in the economy. “Our ambition must therefore extend beyond a larger economy to a more productive one that creates better jobs, secures livelihoods and delivers inclusive prosperity.” Giving direction on the way forward for the reforms, Yusuf stated: “The next phase of reforms must prioritise lower production costs, reliable infrastructure, productive investment and more effective public expenditure. “We must also confront poverty, food insecurity and gaps in access to quality education, healthcare, nutrition and productive work. We must not only talk about the fortunes of our past, but also build wealth for present and future generations. “Nigeria’s large and youthful population is a substantial opportunity, but it will translate into prosperity only if we equip people with relevant skills and connect them to productive opportunities. “We must look beyond the unemployment headline to informality, job quality and incomes. Having work does not necessarily mean earning an adequate income. “We must strengthen the link between education and employment through technical and vocational training, digital capabilities and industry-relevant skills, and expand opportunities in agriculture and agro-processing, manufacturing, construction, tourism and digital services. “The private sector will be central to Nigeria’s transformation: businesses organise production, employ workers and connect markets. Yet they cannot fulfil this role without an enabling operating environment. “Our entrepreneurs are remarkably resilient, but resilience should not excuse an environment that makes productivity unnecessarily expensive. “Unreliable electricity, expensive financing, poor transport infrastructure, insecurity and regulatory uncertainty raise costs and increase volatility, especially for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises. “The government must sustain economic stability, provide essential public goods and ensure regulatory predictability. Businesses, in turn, must invest in technology, skills, local supply chains and export competitiveness.” The post NESG presents mixed outcomes for Nigeria’s economic reforms appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Reps pass vote of confidence in Tinubu, NNPC boss
body: •Dismiss money laundering petition against EVP By Gift ChapiOdekina Abuja—The House of Representatives Committee on Petroleum Resources (Downstream) has dismissed a petition alleging conflict of interest and money laundering against NNPC’s Executive Vice President (Downstream), Dr. Mumuni Dagazau, saying the petitioners failed to provide documentary evidence to substantiate their claims. It also passed a vote of confidence on President Bola Tinubu and the Group Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited, NNPCL, citing improvements in domestic refining, crude oil supply and stability in the downstream petroleum sector. Chairman of the committee, Ikenga Imo Ugochinyere, announced the decisions during proceedings on pending matters and the federal government’s downstream sector reforms in Abuja yesterday. Ugochinyere said the committee’s decision followed a review of its subcommittee’s report, which found that the petitioners, the Coalition for Transparency and Accountability in Nigeria’s Petroleum Sector, failed to substantiate their allegations against Dagazau. According to him, the petitioners appeared before the subcommittee on October 21 but presented newspaper clippings rather than documentary evidence to support allegations as serious as money laundering. He said they were given further opportunities to provide supporting documents but failed to return on Thursday and Friday, October 22 and 23. On the other hand, he said Dagazau honoured the committee’s invitation through his representatives, who responded to the inquiries raised by the subcommittee. “An allegation is not evidence, and a newspaper clipping is not proof,” Ugochinyere said, announcing the dismissal of the petition in its entirety. The committee chairman condemned what he described as a frivolous petition, warning that the National Assembly would not allow its oversight proceedings to become a platform for unsubstantiated attacks on public officials. He, however, maintained that the committee remained open to investigating allegations of wrongdoing against public officers where credible evidence was provided. The committee also granted its subcommittee investigating NIPCO Plc an additional 14 days to conclude its assignment. Reps reject blanket fuel subsidy return On the contentious issue of fuel subsidy, the committee chairman argued that a return to the former nationwide subsidy regime would impose a significant burden on public finances. He said Nigerians consumed about 50 million litres of petrol daily and that, based on the federal government’s estimates, restoring the former pump price would cost more than N20 trillion annually. According to him, such expenditure will approach the total amount shared among the federal, state and local governments through the Federation Account in 2025. “A blanket subsidy does not lower the cost of fuel; it only changes who pays, and when,” he said. Ugochinyere argued that relief measures should instead be targeted, temporary and affordable, insisting that any subsidy proposal must clearly state its cost, funding source and expected pump price. He cited recent interventions by NNPC Retail, including a N66-per-litre petrol discount introduced on October 1 and an October 8 announcement that the company would forgo its profit margin and sell petrol at cost for 30 days. He said the intervention prioritised commercial transport operators responsible for moving passengers and food across the country. According to him, the arrangement was not a return to subsidy because the relief was being provided through NNPC Retail’s profit margin rather than a direct charge on the public treasury. CNG expansion, refinery rehabilitation The committee chairman also highlighted developments in the rehabilitation of the Port Harcourt and Warri refineries, saying prospective technical partners had conducted on-site assessments to determine how the facilities could return to reliable and commercially sustainable operations. He said the reforms had also expanded investment opportunities in the CNG and LPG markets, with more than 120,000 vehicles now running on CNG. NNPC Limited, he added, had acquired 500 CNG-powered trucks for petroleum product distribution and delivered 35 CNG hybrid buses to the Presidential CNG Initiative. Ugochinyere further disclosed that NNPC Retail commissioned its first solar-powered smart energy station in Abuja in September, combining petrol, cooking gas, CNG and electric vehicle charging facilities. He said between 50 and 70 similar stations were expected to be rolled out nationwide within six months. The committee chairman attributed the developments to the Tinubu administration’s reforms and commended NNPC’s management and Dagazau for their contributions to the downstream sector. Committee unveils energy security roadmap To sustain the gains, Ugochinyere said the committee had adopted a nine-pillar Roadmap to Downstream Energy Security, covering enforceable crude supply obligations for domestic refineries, amendments to the Petroleum Industry Act, a regulated import market and the establishment of a national strategic stock. Other priorities include nationwide fuel-quality laboratories, accelerated CNG and gas infrastructure development, improved pipeline security, fair and transparent pricing with targeted relief, and firm timelines for the rehabilitation of state-owned refineries. He said the committee would continue to monitor the implementation of the reforms and hold relevant agencies accountable for their performance. “The Renewed Hope downstream sector agenda is working,” he said. The committee’s decisions come amid continuing pressure on petrol prices following the removal of fuel subsidy and volatility in international crude oil markets, developments that continue to affect transportation costs, food prices and household spending across Nigeria. The post Reps pass vote of confidence in Tinubu, NNPC boss appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Ebola fight: Misinformation is our worst enemy — GHS boss
body: The Director-General of the Ghana Health Service (GHS), Dr Samuel Kaba Akoriyea, has warned that misinformation could undermine Ghana’s efforts to prepare for a possible Ebola outbreak, urging journalists and social media users to verify information before publishing or sharing it. He has appealed to the media, content creators and users of platforms such as TikTok and WhatsApp to rely on official sources for updates on the disease, cautioning that inaccurate or misleading reports could complicate public health communication at a time when clear, credible information is critical. “Our worst enemy is misinformation,” Dr Akoriyea said on Joy News’ PM Express on Monday, October 26. He urged the public to cross-check claims with the Ghana Health Service and the Ministry of Health before circulating them. “Ghana Health Service website is there, the Ministry of Health website is there, the Minister is there, I’m there, we have PROs, cross-check before you come out,” he appealed. The GHS Director-General said the speed at which information circulates online made verification especially important, as people could easily misrepresent health developments or spread claims that had not been confirmed. “In this era, people miscommunicate a lot,” he added. Dr Akoriyea said Ghana had intensified its preparedness measures to strengthen its ability to respond if an Ebola case were detected, although the true test of readiness would come when the country had to manage an actual case. “We have increased our preparedness to make sure that we tighten all the knots,” he said. “Until we get a case, we might not be able to prove our readiness and even no matter how ready you are, no matter how ready you are, when you get a case, it’s a different story.” He said it was nevertheless better for the country to prepare thoroughly before a possible outbreak than to be caught unprepared. “But it’s better to be prepared, right, and get a case and do commit very few errors than not to be prepared at all,” he said. The Director-General cited Ghana’s experience during the COVID-19 pandemic as an important foundation for strengthening its response to future health emergencies. He said the availability of the Ga East Municipal Hospital and the University of Ghana Medical Centre (UGMC) had been an advantage during the pandemic, adding that lessons from that period were informing efforts to improve the country’s preparedness. “I remember we were extremely prepared, and we’re so fortunate as a country during COVID that we had Ga East already built, we had UGMC already built, and we are building on that to make sure that whatever we have done or we had done, now we can even make it better,” he said. Trusted information critical The appeal comes amid heightened concern over Ebola and the need for countries to strengthen surveillance, preparedness and public communication as outbreaks are reported in parts of Africa. Ebola is a severe viral disease that can spread through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person who is showing symptoms, or with contaminated materials. Prompt identification, isolation and appropriate care of suspected cases, alongside effective contact tracing and infection prevention, are important to containing transmission. Public health authorities also rely on accurate information to explain risks, clarify what is known about an outbreak and communicate recommended precautions. False claims can fuel fear, undermine trust in health authorities and encourage people to act on advice that has not been medically verified.

title: Gridin shows off superb shot, Griddy celebration
body:
CALGARY – First two-goal game. First three-point game. First on-ice Griddy.
It was a night of NHL firsts for Matvei Gridin on Monday as the 20-year-old right-winger led the red-hot Calgary Flames to their fourth consecutive win with a 5-2 decision against the Toronto Maple Leafs.
“So obviously my nickname is Griddy and I was thinking about that for a long time, and I thought it was a good moment to do that,” said Gridin who did the Griddy after his power-play goal 25 seconds into the second period, which gave Calgary a 3-0 lead.
“Up by three, having fun, and it’s like I don’t know, just do it,” said Gridin with a smile.
Had he been practising the namesake dance move?
Flames coach Ryan Huska wasn’t about to throw cold water on the viral moment for the excited forward.
“He’s a young guy. Scored a nice goal. That’s the way I look at it.”
Selected 28th in the 2024 NHL draft, Gridin was set up for the chance on a long pass from fellow 2024 first-rounder, Zayne Parekh, who was drafted ninth.
“I didn’t see it coming,” Parekh admitted about the celebration. “I backed up and let him do it, but I mean he’s having fun. There’s no ill thought in his head. He’s just a kid having fun, and you know we’re having fun as a team, and this hockey is a lot of fun right now.”
After posting 20 points (six goals, 14 assists) in 37 games a year ago as a rookie, big things were expected in his sophomore season, but the Russian got off to a slow start with just one assist through his first six games.
But he’s found his game since with seven points in his last five games including four goals in his last four, moving him into the team lead.
“Beginning of the year, he wasn’t really moving his feet,” said Huska. “So the plays he was trying to make, he was standing still, and there were a lot of turnovers coming off his stick. But now, his feet are moving, and he’s a very dangerous guy when he’s playing that way.”
Sergei Bobrovsky found that out the hard way.
Gridin’s first goal that opened the scoring at 10:05 of the first period came on a wicked shot from a sharp angle that beat the Maple Leafs goaltender over his shoulder and just inside the post.
His second goal was similar, taking a pass from Parekh and ripping another shot top corner, this time over Bobrovsky’s opposite shoulder.
“I just told him before the draw, like if you see it, just be ready. And all I saw was his stick was touching the ceiling, and he wanted that thing, so I got it to him. And I mean, what a shot! Yeah, special.”
Gridin says his shot has always been one of his best skills.
“It was always the weapon. Working on it since childhood. Always got a good shot. Just gotta shoot more, I guess.”
Parekh predicts more goals to come and, who knows, maybe more Griddy’s.
“He’s never shied away from the puck,” said the defenceman. “He wants that thing more than anyone. It’s fun to watch. He’s gonna score a lot of goals in this league.”
Gridin’s breakout has come in lockstep with the club’s improved play after Calgary got off to a franchise-worst 0-5-0 start. With five wins in their last six, a win on Wednesday against the Oilers in Edmonton would get the Flames back to .500.
“We look like a faster team right now because I think we’re doing things the right way,” said Huska. “We’re playing a simpler brand of hockey, and it’s resulting in more opportunities. And the guys are now having success, so you can see the confidence starting to grow.”
“Sometimes you have to take a deep breath at times, too. Like it’s a long season, and we really put ourselves behind the eight ball with the way it started, but there was a lot of those games where we felt like we were doing things the right way. … So it’s just a matter of staying with it.”
Mikael Backlund also scored for the Flames in his return to the lineup after missing two games due to an upper body injury.
“The group has grown a lot since early in the year, and it’s nice to put a few wins together here at home,” said the Flames captain. “It’s been fun watching the team, but I’d rather be with them on the ice.”
This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 26, 2026.

title: Zionist regime holds Knesset elections
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 27 (MNA) – Voting began in the Zionist regime's parliamentary elections on Tuesday as it faces security, political and economic challenges, with 7.33 million eligible voters and 38 lists competing for 120 Knesset seats.
Voting began on Tuesday in the Zionist regime's parliamentary elections, with settlers of the occupied territories casting ballots for the 26th Knesset amid security, political and economic challenges.
More than 7.33 million people are eligible to vote, and 38 electoral lists are competing for 120 parliamentary seats, according to Al-Jazeera. The central elections committee of the Zionist regime put the number of eligible voters at 7,331,981, an increase of 543,177 compared with the November 2022 elections.
All settlers from the occupied territories aged at least 18 whose names are registered on the voters' list are entitled to take part.
Television networks of the Zionist regime will publish exit poll estimates immediately after the main polling stations close at 10 p.m. on Tuesday. These are statistical estimates and should not be considered as official election results. Official results will emerge gradually overnight and on Wednesday as votes from regular polling stations are counted and protocols are transferred to the central elections committee. Counting of ballots in double envelopes and reviews of possible violations will continue in the following days. According to the announced schedule, final official results will be published by Wednesday, Nov. 4, 2026, at the latest.

title: Adnoc Drilling expects unconventional rebound in 2027 after third-quarter lull
body: Adnoc Drilling expects its unconventional drilling business to recover and hit record levels next year, after a lull between development phases weighed on third-quarter revenue, chief financial officer Youssef Salem said. “By next year is when we expect to have that significant ramp-up, and then unconventional [will] go back to become even higher than what it was until Q2,” Mr Salem told The National in an interview on Tuesday, after the company released its quarterly results. Net profit attributable to owners of the company fell 0.8 per cent annually to $365.4 million in the third quarter from $368.2 million a year earlier, the company said in a bourse filing to the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange, where its shares are traded. Revenue declined marginally to $1.25 billion. The company had completed almost 80 per cent of the first phase of its unconventional drilling by the second quarter, Mr Salem said. He described the third quarter as “a transitionary period” before the second phase ramps up as Adnoc finalises investment decisions and partnerships. He added that he expects the fourth quarter to be “broadly similar” to the third, with a slight increase. In the first nine months, Aldar Drilling's net profit rose 0.7 per cent to $1.07 billion. Revenue climbed more than 2 per cent to a record $3.7 billion, driven by onshore and offshore drilling businesses and the consolidation of regional operations. Ebitda (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation) increased 2 per cent to $1.66 billion. The company is also pressing ahead with regional growth. It was the lowest bidder for two jack-up rigs tendered by Kuwait Oil Company and is awaiting the final award, Mr Salem said. It is building four rigs in China for deployment in Oman and Kuwait next year. Those will add to the 30 rigs it gained by acquiring SLB’s land rig business in Oman and Kuwait and MB Petroleum Services. Egypt is “a market we see a big opportunity in, and hence we’re keen to start entering”, he said. Enersol, Adnoc Drilling's technology investment venture with Alpha Dhabi, has invested $750 million so far and has another $750 million to deploy. The company expects to land at the lower end of its net profit guidance, Mr Salem said. The regional conflict has raised costs, including transportation, and supply chain problems forced it to build up inventory. Most of those costs are passed on to clients because the majority of its contracts are long-term and cost-plus. “Even if it’s towards the low end of the range ... we see that as demonstrating strong resilience,” he said. Drill-to-Operate strategy The company also launched Drill-to-Operate, the next phase of its growth strategy, which is expected to let it generate more revenue from each well and expand its presence in regional energy markets. “We are now extending that capability across the full well lifecycle to capture more value from every well and expand the markets and services in which we operate,” chief executive Abdulla Al Messabi said. Adnoc Drilling is among the companies at the centre of the UAE 's ambitions to reach five million barrels per day of crude oil production capacity by 2027. It also expects more drilling opportunities in gasfield development. In July, it won a $365 million contract on Adnoc’s $6.2 billion Umm Shaif gas cap project. In the first nine months, onshore drilling revenue rose 5 per cent, supported by the consolidation of regional operations. Offshore revenue rose 4 per cent after adding new capacity, including an AI-enabled island rig deployed in June. The planned phasing of unconventional activity and the repurposing of some onshore rigs partly offset that growth. Dividend The board approved a third-quarter dividend of $350 million, comprising a base payout of $262.5 million and a discretionary dividend of $87.5 million, the company said. A further $87.5 million discretionary payout is expected in April, subject to shareholder approval. That would take the 2026 total to $1.225 billion, up 22.5 per cent from last year. The discretionary dividend “is not committed to be repeated”, but the approach behind it is “definitely a recurring philosophy”, Mr Salem said. The company has revised its leverage guidance to between one and two times Ebitda, from up to two times previously, to avoid an “inefficient capital structure”. Outlook Adnoc Drilling is sticking to its full-year guidance of $5 billion in revenue and about $1.45 billion in net profit. It expects free cash flow of $1.2 billion to $1.3 billion, excluding acquisitions. For 2027, it forecasts low-to-mid single-digit revenue growth. Net profit is expected to remain broadly stable, however, as higher depreciation and financing costs from its expansion offset gains from increased activity.

title: Alberta gambled on leaving Canada. Who won that battle?
body:
The Province of Alberta is staying in Canada. 75% of voters rejected the separatists’ ambitions. But the referendum may have produced some unexpected winners and losers.
Alberta Premier Danielle Smith appears to have secured important concessions from Ottawa by raising the prospect of separation. Yet her political gamble may have come at a high price; while strengthening Alberta’s bargaining position, she may have weakened her own.
The Canadian province of Alberta held a referendum in which voters were asked whether to begin the process of separating from Canada. With 75% voting against separation and a 65% voter turnout, there will be no further steps toward secession. The result was largely predictable, but the Alberta saga had kept the entire country on edge for months. Fears of a Canadian version of Brexit were real, prompting mainstream politicians from across the political spectrum to rally behind the “Forever Canadian” campaign.
The vote in Alberta came at a particularly difficult moment for Canadian unity. With a newly elected minority separatist government in Quebec and US President Donald Trump imposing tariffs on Canada and repeatedly suggesting it could become America’s 51st state, the country was already facing considerable political pressure. Against this backdrop, Alberta’s independence movement emerged as another major challenge to the stability of the Canadian federation and its global image as a stable and predictable country.
The roots of the referendum can be traced back to a confrontation between Alberta and the federal government in early 2025. In March, Premier Danielle Smith warned that Canada’s unity could face a crisis unless Prime Minister Mark Carney removed federal environmental regulations that, in her view, were holding back Alberta’s energy industry. The dispute soon moved beyond energy policy and into the question of Alberta’s future within Canada. The following month, Smith’s government introduced legislative changes that made it easier for citizens, including supporters of independence, to initiate referendums.
The separatist movement initially tried to force a vote through citizen-led petitions, but two such initiatives ran into legal obstacles. Premier Smith subsequently took the initiative herself, proposing a referendum that would allow Albertans to choose between maintaining the province’s place in Canada and taking the first step toward a future, binding vote on independence. Throughout the process, she maintained that she wanted Alberta to remain part of Canada. Her position was that Albertans deserved the opportunity to express their views directly. Nevertheless, by allowing the independence question to dominate provincial politics, she also strengthened a movement whose ambitions went far beyond her own.
At first, the strategy appeared to work. The threat of separation helped Alberta secure a promise from the federal government that previous governments had resisted. A pipeline to the West Coast that would enable the export of the province’s most valuable natural resource, bitumen extracted from Alberta’s oil sands, was assured.
The political confrontation also produced an unexpected shift in relations between the provincial and federal governments. After years of tensions, Alberta and Ottawa began finding common ground, particularly over the development of energy infrastructure. The proposed pipeline became a symbol of this new cooperation. The change was also visible during the referendum campaign, when Premier Smith and Prime Minister Carney, despite their political differences, appeared together to encourage Albertans to remain in Canada.
The referendum, in which 75% of voters chose to remain in the Canadian federation, was also a political gamble aimed at securing greater autonomy and concessions for Alberta from the federal government. In that sense, the strategy seems to have paid off. But its biggest loser may turn out to be the very politician who initiated it. Premier Smith may have won concessions for Alberta, but in doing so, she risks losing control of the political forces she helped unleash.
Despite calling on Albertans to vote in favour of remaining in Canada, Premier Smith appears to have alienated different groups for different reasons: separatists who feel their ambitions have been unfulfilled, voters who question the need for the referendum, and Canadians elsewhere in the country who see her strategy as a threat to national unity.
Meanwhile, one of the biggest beneficiaries of this political gamble may be Prime Minister Mark Carney. The referendum gave him an opportunity to present himself as a defender of Canadian unity while strengthening his political standing in a province traditionally hostile to his party. What began as a challenge to federal authority may ultimately have reinforced it.
The consequences could be particularly serious for Premier Smith’s own United Conservative Party (UCP). Rather than abandoning their ambitions after the referendum defeat, separatist activists may seek greater influence within the party and want to see more independence supporters elected to the provincial legislature. At the same time, conservative voters are questioning whether the referendum was worth its political and, importantly, financial costs. These competing pressures could deepen divisions within the UCP and undermine Smith’s authority as both party leader and premier.
The irony is that Smith’s strategy may have succeeded in extracting concessions from Ottawa while creating new political problems at home. By using the threat of separation as leverage, she helped bring Alberta’s grievances to the national stage. But she also legitimized a movement whose ambitions extend far beyond her own political agenda. Now that voters have rejected independence, she must find a way to reunite a divided conservative movement without losing the political gains she secured.
Alberta has voted against independence, but separatist sentiment is nothing new in Canada. Prime Minister Carney is now fighting to defend his country on multiple fronts, not only to protect it against US trade pressure and threats to Canadian sovereignty, but also to keep the country united in the face of those challenges.
For Danielle Smith, however, the challenge may be even more personal. She gambled on separatism to strengthen Alberta’s position within Canada. Whether she can survive the political consequences of that gamble remains an open question.

title: Nigerians now spend 120% of income on food – Oyedele
body: The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has said some Nigerians spend as much as 120 per cent of their income on food, forcing them to borrow money or rely on relatives to survive. Oyedele spoke at Chatham House in London, where he said a government survey showed that food expenses exceeded the incomes of some households. “In fact, there was a survey we did that shows that up to 120 per cent of household income is spent on food. Like, how do you spend 120 per cent of your income? You borrow food before the end of the month,” he said. The minister said Nigeria’s poverty rate remained above 50 per cent despite an unemployment rate of about five per cent, pointing to the growing number of people who work but still struggle to meet their basic needs. Gov Yusuf vows to sack appointees who sell empowerment items NDC and the battle within “That tells you something. As a policymaker, you don’t sit back and say we don’t have unemployment. You have working poor,” he said. Oyedele attributed the pressure on households to high food prices, which he said were not falling as quickly as headline inflation. Food inflation stood at 19.6 per cent in September. “Headline inflation is falling faster than the price of a basket of tomatoes, gari, and beans. And this widens inequality,” he said. “Macroeconomic stability means little to a mother who still cannot afford food,” he added. The minister also said Nigeria had no taxes on fuel, arguing that the pressure on household budgets was linked to deeper structural problems rather than fuel taxes. He identified low agricultural yields, seasonal farming, post-harvest losses, poor storage and logistics, high transport costs and insecurity in farming communities as major factors driving food prices. He cited losses of up to 60 per cent of tomatoes after harvest as an example of the challenges facing the agricultural sector. On measures to address the situation, Oyedele said the government was investing in agricultural technology, irrigation to support year-round farming, improved storage facilities and access to finance for smallholder farmers. He said the administration was also providing direct support through a cash transfer programme that had reached more than 10 million “In the short term, the administration is providing direct support through a cash transfer programme that has reached more than 10 million households. Payments are made digitally and beneficiaries are verified with National Identification Numbers to reduce leakage,” he said. Oyedele said the government was prioritising agriculture and non-tradable services, which together employ 81.4 per cent of working Nigerians. He said the aim was to grow the sectors faster than the overall economy, increase incomes and gradually reduce dependence on cash transfers.

title: Local ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump starts in southern Ukraine
body:
In this undated image from video provided by the Ukrainian 34th Separate Marine Brigade "Borysfen" on Sept. 22, 2026, smoke rises from a residential neighborhood in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky in the Kherson region of Ukraine. Ukrainian 34th Separate Marine B/via AP hide caption
MYKOLAIV, Ukraine — A localized ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia took effect early Tuesday ahead of a humanitarian mission brokered by U.S. first lady Melania Trump, as missile attacks resumed in Kyiv.
The local pause in fighting started at 3 a.m. to allow an aid mission into the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine later this week.
According to her office, Melania Trump led talks with civilian negotiators from Russia and Ukraine after meeting with U.N. officials who briefed her on the situation in the town.
The aid mission is planned ahead of a new round of U.S.-brokered talks between Russia and Ukraine expected next month aimed at ending the war after more than 4½ years of fighting.
Up to 2,000 people are stranded in Oleshky with dwindling food and medicine. They are unable to leave because of explosive mines and drone attacks in the area, according to the U.N.
Russian and Ukrainian negotiators as well as the militaries of the two countries confirmed in separate statements that the ceasefire had begun.
Emergency workers clear debris and damaged road infrastructure near a destroyed car following a Russian overnight strike in Kyiv, Ukraine, Tuesday, Oct. 27, 2026. Dan Bashakov/AP hide caption
The local ceasefire is due to last through Saturday, or longer, though deep mistrust between Russia and Ukraine has thwarted previous attempts at ceasefires.
Minutes after 3 a.m., multiple ballistic missile explosions shook Kyiv and air alerts sounded in multiple parts of the country.
Late Monday, the capital also came under attack, when Russian ballistic missiles damaged the grounds of a university in Kyiv, killing one person and leaving 10 injured, city officials said. In Kharkiv, Ukraine's second-largest city, authorities said attacks late Monday killed two people and injured four.
"It is important that the world sees that Russia is showing nothing but a desire to kill and continue waging war," Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy wrote in an online post shortly afterward.
Oleshky is in the partially occupied Kherson region, about 550 kilometers (340 miles) southeast of Kyiv, where the Dnipro River separates Russian and Ukrainian forces.
It was captured by Moscow's forces on the first day of their full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Further calamity struck in June 2023 when floodwaters inundated the town due to a dam collapse.
Oleshky sits across the Dnipro River from the city of Kherson, the region's administrative capital. Russian forces seized Kherson in the early stages of the 2022 invasion but retreated across the river several months later.
Negotiators involved in the aid mission said doctors, medicines, food supplies and water would be taken to Oleshky before evacuation corridors are opened.

title: Baidu Open-Sources Unlimited OCR 2 for Hundred-Page Document Parsing
body: Baidu has released Unlimited OCR 2 , an open-source OCR model built for very long documents. The 3B model parses books, filings and reports of hundreds of pages in one request. Its core change is SR-SWA, a sparse attention scheme that keeps per-step decoding cost nearly flat. Weights ship under the MIT license , with code on GitHub . TL;DR Size: 3.34B parameters . Active parameters not disclosed. Max position length 131,072 tokens. Runs on: 1 CUDA GPU in BF16. Baidu tested on an NVIDIA A800-80GB. BF16 weights total about 6.7 GB. Performance: first place on both multi-page benchmarks Baidu tested, against 9 other models (self-reported). Best: 77.1 overall on MarathonDocBench (hundreds of pages). The next model, Kimi-K3, scores 33.7. Worst: 48.2 on heading hierarchy (TEDS) on MarathonDocBench, its lowest sub-score. What is Unlimited OCR 2? Unlimited OCR 2 is a 3B vision-language model from Baidu that turns ordered page images into structured text. Output covers text, tables, formulas, figures, headings and reading order. It succeeds Unlimited-OCR , released in June 2026 to push DeepSeek-OCR further. The config keeps a DeepSeek-OCR style layout. A SAM ViT-B plus CLIP-L encoder feeds a 12-layer mixture-of-experts decoder. Each token routes to 6 of 64 experts, plus 2 shared experts. The DeepSeek-OCR paper describes this decoder as DeepSeek3B-MoE-A570M. Baidu does not state an active count for version 2. In multi-page mode, each page costs 273 image tokens. How does SR-SWA work? Full attention cost grows quadratically with sequence length. During decoding, each new token scans a longer KV cache. At 273 image tokens per page, 100 pages add 27,300 input tokens before any output. SR-SWA stands for Sparse Reference Sliding Window Attention. It compresses text-visual attention into a fixed set of working references. Baidu’s model card gives 512 tokens as the example size. The config pairs a 128-token local window with top-16 selection over 32-token blocks. That is 16 blocks of 32 tokens, matching the 512-token budget. This keeps per-step latency and memory nearly constant as documents grow. It calls the result ‘unlimited-horizon’ parsing within a finite context window. Image encoding and total runtime still rise with page count. #mtp-uo2-embed{background:transparent!important;border:0!important;} #mtp-uo2-embed iframe{width:100%!important;border:0!important;display:block!important;background:transparent!important;} #mtp-uo2-embed hr,#mtp-uo2-embed p:empty,#mtp-uo2-embed del,#mtp-uo2-embed s{display:none!important;} (function(){var f=document.getElementById('mtp-uo2-frame');window.addEventListener('message',function(e){if(e.data&&e.data.mtpEmbed==='uo2'&&e.data.height&&e.source===f.contentWindow){f.style.height=e.data.height+'px';}});})(); How does it score on MPDocBench and MarathonDocBench? Baidu team tests on MPDocBench, with dozens of pages per document, and MarathonDocBench, with hundreds. MPDocBench-Parse is a public benchmark of 433 documents and 3,246 pages. We could not find a public MarathonDocBench release. Per Baidu’s leaderboard chart , Unlimited OCR 2 scores 84.6 on MPDocBench. Qwen3.8-Max follows at 78.3, then Qwen-3.8-Flash-Next at 77.4. On MarathonDocBench it scores 77.1. Kimi-K3 is next at 33.7, then Gemini-3.8-Flash at 28.6. The drop between benchmarks is the real story. Qwen3.8-Max falls from 78.3 to 22.9 on hundred-page documents. Unlimited OCR 2 falls 7.5 points. Its predecessor, Unlimited-OCR, scores 0.0 on MarathonDocBench. Sub-scores (MPDocBench / MarathonDocBench): Text: 94.8 / 89.6 Formula: 89.4 / 87.9 Reading order: 92.3 / 85.3 Tables: 87.8 / 74.8 Heading hierarchy: 60.1 / 48.2 Single-metric margins on MPDocBench are thin. Qwen3.8-Max scores 94.3 on text and 89.2 on formulas. All figures are self-reported and appear only in a chart image. Comparison with other open OCR models Unlimited OCR 2 Unlimited-OCR DeepSeek-OCR-2 PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 Developer Baidu Baidu DeepSeek Baidu PaddlePaddle Parameters 3.34B 3.34B 3.39B 0.96B Active parameters Not disclosed Not disclosed Not disclosed Not disclosed License MIT MIT Apache 2.0 Apache 2.0 Paper / release Oct 2026 ( report ) Jun 2026 ( arXiv ) Jan 2026 ( arXiv ) Jun 2026 ( arXiv ) Long-document mechanism SR-SWA, 512-token reference set Multi-page infer_multi , no SR-SWA Not disclosed Not disclosed MPDocBench overall 84.6 (Baidu) 61.9 (Baidu) Not reported Not reported MarathonDocBench overall 77.1 (Baidu) 0.0 (Baidu) Not reported Not reported Serving Transformers, custom SGLang Transformers, vLLM , SGLang Transformers, SGLang PaddleOCR, Transformers Parameter counts and licenses from each model’s Hugging Face page. Benchmark scores from Baidu’s chart . How do you run Unlimited OCR 2? The model card lists Transformers for quick tests and SGLang for serving. In Transformers, infer handles 1 page with dynamic tiling, called gundam mode. infer_multi parses every page of a document in 1 request, so the model keeps cross-page context. Loading requires trust_remote_code=True , which runs Python code from the repo. SGLang serving uses a customized wheel from Baidu, not upstream SGLang. Baidu’s example schedules 10 pages per window and reuses the previous window’s KV tail. Smaller windows cut peak memory but weaken cross-page merging. Baidu warns a default bias setting can trigger a 462 MiB allocation and run out of memory. Key Takeaways Unlimited OCR 2 is a 3.34B, MIT-licensed OCR model from Baidu. SR-SWA caps attention at a fixed 512-token reference set. It scores 77.1 on MarathonDocBench, against 33.7 for the next model. Heading hierarchy is the weak spot, at 48.2 on long documents. All benchmark numbers are Baidu’s own. Check out the model card , the technical report and the GitHub repo .
