title: Education expert calls for teacher training to bridge gaps
body: The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Secondary Education Board Desk Officer for Robotic Education, Aishatu Jafaar Suleiman, has called for extensive teachers’ training and retraining to bridge the educational gaps between teachers and students in the FCT. Sulaiman spoke in Abuja on Monday during a sensitisation programme organised by Change a Child Community Initiative, at the Government Day Secondary School, Dutse Alhaji and Government Secondary School, Kubwa, in the Bwari Area Council. She said the administration of the FCT Minister, Nyesom Wike, is doing its best in terms of renovation of schools, provision of materials and infrastructure, but more needs to be done in teachers’ development. According to her, “The government is doing its best, and there has been so much improvement in the renovation of schools and the provision of learning materials, but teachers are in dire need of training. “We are not asking for too much, but for training and retraining so that we can give our best. “Despite not being in the class at the moment, I still train and pay for online courses that I believe will be beneficial to my profession because once a teacher, you’re always a teacher,” she said. Similarly, Founder and Lead Educator, Change a Child Community Initiative, Blessing Okwuchukwu Awamba, said the Initiative was birthed with the mindset of catching school children young and inculcating values that are needed for national development as the vices in society have continued to surge. She disclosed that the programme, which is set to run for five years, has been designed for expansion to various states, with a few states already in the kitty as beneficiaries. She said the themes, which are all-encompassing, have been well thought of and carefully selected to tally with the socioeconomic challenges being experienced within the particular geographical locations.

title: ‘Astronomical’ Arab turnout could reshape Israeli politics in key election
body: Read the latest on Israel's election here An “astronomical” turnout of Arab voters is expected in the Israeli elections on Tuesday, with the possibility that their politicians could significantly influence the next government, political sources have told The National . Senior opposition officials have also said there is a possibility of a coalition or agreed minority government with the Arab parties, if the mainstream parties do not win an outright majority. Opinion polls have now closed under Israeli law, with the final ones showing the opposition with a potential 56 seats, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud party on 50 with the Arab parties taking 14 in the 120-seat Knesset. With 61 seats needed to form a government, the opposition led by Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot could either form a minority government with tacit Arab party support or go into a coalition with the Ra’am party, led by Mansour Abbas. Arab influence could also be strengthened by a surge in votes for its two main parties – Ra'am and the Joint List – with turnout expected to rise from about 50 per cent to 70 per cent of the two million people who make up 20 per cent of Israel ’s total population. “After what they have witnessed over the past three years, they have understood the difference between bad and worse,” said an Israeli political observer, referring to the hard-right parties that have influenced politics. If the bloc against Mr Netanyahu takes power, then significant steps would be taken to halt the settler violence and illegal dwellings in the occupied West Bank , an opposition source said. “We will clamp down on settler violence, which has gone on for too long, because it is a disgrace to the country and because it is wrong," he said. "We will also stop wildcat home building because we believe in law and order.” A coalition involving Ra’am is one of three possible outcomes from the election. The other two are either a coalition between the centre-right and ultra-orthodox parties or a “government of unity” that would be likely to have Mr Eisenkot as prime minister, but would also include Mr Netanyahu ’s Likud. There are also many unknowns and other factors at play that could still affect the outcome. About 700,000 young people will vote for the first time – the last election was in 2022 – and it is not known which way the group that went through Covid, Israeli judicial reforms, the October 7 attacks and military service will vote. There are up to 70,000 Israelis living abroad who have flown back to the country to vote – the majority are understood to be against Mr Netanyahu – alongside a similar number of Russian emigres, who fled after the 2022 Ukraine invasion, who are thought to be in the more liberal camp. Key issues for Israel, which observers say are existential, are also at play. Some officials believe getting the ultra-Orthodox into conscripted military service is important to Israel’s security, but their parties object. There are 72,000 ultra-Orthodox young men aged 18 to 21 who are listed as “deserters” for not joining up. There is also talk of a “declaration of independence” that would give the country a written constitution, alongside term-limits for prime ministers. Mr Netanyahu has served for almost 20 years over three spells in office. Israel also faces other crises, including the imposition of international sanctions from European countries and a plummeting birth rate, except among the Arab and ultra-Orthodox population. About 50 per cent of school children are from those two groups. But some observers believe that, come dawn on Wednesday, Israel will simply resume the status quo, with the idea of Zionist parties working with Arab groups unacceptable to too many people. “My concern is that they will opt for the unity government [with Mr Netanyahu] because they are cowards and it is politically convenient,” one opposition figure said.

title: Russia, Ukraine begin localized ceasefire to allow for humanitarian operation in Oleshky
body: Russia and Ukraine have started a localized ceasefire to allow for a humanitarian operation to begin in the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky, both sides said on Tuesday.Russia's defense ministry said on Telegram it stopped shelling in the direction of the Ukrainian city of Kherson from 4 a.m. Moscow time (0100 GMT) to prepare for the humanitarian operation in Oleshky, just across the Dnipro River from Kherson.Dmytro Lubinets, Ukraine's parliament commissioner for human rights, confirmed in a Facebook post that the ceasefire has started at the same time."As head of the Ukrainian negotiating team, I confirm that the Ukrainian side is honoring its commitments," he wrote.Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a localized ceasefire around the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine, an arrangement that will enable aid deliveries and allow evacuations from a frontline town suffering acute shortages of food and medicine.Oleshky lies on the eastern bank of the Dnipro in Ukraine's southern region of Kherson, opposite the city of Kherson, which is held by Ukrainian forces.Oleshku seized by Russia during first days of February 2022 invasionRussian troops seized Oleshky during the first days of their February 2022 invasion and have controlled it ever since. The White House said last week that US first lady Melania Trump helped to secure the Oleshky ceasefire.Elsewhere in Ukraine, a Russian missile attack on the Ukrainian capital Kyiv on Monday killed at least one person and injured 10, including students at a dormitory, with the attacks also killing and injuring people in the cities of Kharkiv and Pavlohrad.New explosions were heard on Tuesday morning in Kyiv, a Reuters witness said.

title: Attacks: Terrorists exploiting local grievances, misinformation – NSA
body: The National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu, said terrorist groups exploit porous borders, local grievances, illicit financial networks, digital platforms and online radicalisation to expand their operations across Africa. He said the evolving threat in Nigeria requires stronger intelligence coordination, sustained partnerships and practical cooperation among African countries and their international partners. Ribadu stated these on Monday at the headquarters of the National Counter-Terrorism Centre, Abuja, during the opening session of the High-Level African Lessons Learned Forum on Counter-Terrorism Cooperation, Intelligence Sharing and Emerging Technologies. The NSA called for stronger global and regional cooperation, intelligence sharing and responsible use of emerging technologies to combat terrorism and violent extremism in Africa. According to him, Nigeria’s experience over the past 15 years had shown that military operations alone could not provide a sustainable solution to terrorism. He added that Nigeria had continued to pursue a whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach to counter-terrorism and countering violent extremism. “Terrorist groups are exploiting porous borders, local grievances, illicit financial networks, digital platforms, misinformation, online radicalisation and emerging technologies. “While security operations remain necessary, they must be complemented by intelligence coordination, law enforcement, financial intelligence, justice, strategic communications, prevention, rehabilitation, reintegration, reconciliation, community resilience, education, youth engagement, research, training and technology-enabled analysis,” he said. The National Coordinator of NCTC, Maj.-Gen. Adamu Laka, said the forum was designed to help African countries compare experiences, identify effective strategies and strengthen cooperation against terrorism. Laka said terrorist groups were increasingly exploiting technology, illicit financial flows, corruption and criminal networks to advance their activities. He stressed that military action must be complemented by prevention, rehabilitation, reintegration, criminal justice and community resilience.

title: ‘Cancer survivors, caregivers deserve strong support systems’
body: Healthcare professionals, cancer survivors, caregivers, policymakers and other advocates have called for stronger policies and support systems to improve the quality of life of people living beyond a cancer diagnosis. The call was made at the cancer survivorship forum, “Beyond the Diagnosis: The Untold Realities of Cancer Survivorship and Caregiving,” organised by the African Medical Centre of Excellence (AMCE) in partnership with Project PINK BLUE in Abuja as part of its Cancer Survivorship Initiative. Daily Trust reports that the gathering brought together a diverse group of stakeholders to examine the often-overlooked realities faced by cancer survivors and caregivers, including the physical, emotional, social and financial challenges that frequently persist long after treatment has ended. Speaking at the gathering, Chief Medical Officer of AMCE, Dr. Aisha Umar, said cancer care must extend beyond diagnosis and treatment to include survivorship and long-term wellbeing. She said, “As advances in medicine continue to improve cancer outcomes, we must ensure that survivors are not left to navigate the next chapter of their journey alone. “Comprehensive cancer care must address not only treatment, but also rehabilitation, mental health, social reintegration and long-term quality of life. “Survivorship is an essential part of the cancer care continuum, and it is our collective responsibility to ensure that patients and their families receive the support they need to thrive.” Participants shared personal experiences and professional insights on the realities of living with and beyond cancer, highlighting the resilience of survivors and the critical role caregivers play in supporting treatment and recovery.

title: Gov Yusuf vows to sack appointees who sell empowerment items
body: Kano State Governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, has threatened to sack any political appointee or party official found selling empowerment items distributed to constituents by the senator representing Kano South Senatorial District. The governor, who was represented by the Kano State Chairman of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Umar Haruna Doguwa, gave the warning during the Senator representing Kano South, Abdurrahman Kawu Sumaila’s 12th empowerment programme, where 16 vehicles, 400 motorcycles and 600 sewing machines were distributed to beneficiaries on Monday. He urged beneficiaries to use the items for their intended purposes, stressing that the intervention was designed to improve their welfare, strengthen small businesses and promote economic empowerment. Yusuf also expressed optimism that the APC would emerge victorious in the 2027 general elections, urging party members to intensify their efforts towards achieving the party’s electoral objectives. The senator’s empowerment programme saw 16 vehicles presented to APC local government chairmen, while 400 motorcycles were distributed to party executives across the district. Similarly, 200 tailors received empowerment packages comprising two standard sewing machines and one industrial sewing machine each, to strengthen their businesses and enable them to employ and train others. Speaking at the event, the senator said the initiative reflected his commitment to translating the confidence reposed in him by the people into tangible development, economic independence and sustainable livelihoods. He acknowledged the economic and developmental challenges experienced over the past three years but maintained that his commitment to delivering dividends of democracy to the people of Kano South remained unwavering.

title: NMA raises alarm over increasing liver, kidney diseases among Ondo youths
body: The Nigerian Medical Association (NMA), Ondo State chapter, has raised the alarm over the proliferation of counterfeit and adulterated beverages in the state, warning that the consumption of potentially harmful drinks may be contributing to cases of liver cirrhosis and kidney disease among young people. The association called on the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission (FCCPC) and relevant government authorities to launch an immediate crackdown on fake alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages, warning that the products pose a serious threat to public health. The NMA Chairman in Ondo State, Dr Roland Arohunmolase, raised the concerns while speaking with journalists in Akure on Monday, citing clinical observations of young people developing serious health conditions at ages when such diseases are traditionally uncommon. Although he said the association could not provide definitive figures for cases recorded in recent months because some were still under investigation, Arohunmolase expressed concern over the increasing number of young people presenting with liver and kidney diseases. “Traditionally, when you profile some diseases, there are certain age groups in which you do not commonly find them. When a disease no longer conforms to its traditional profile, it becomes a cause for concern,” he said. He added, “For instance, I don’t expect a child of 15 years or someone between 15 and 18 to develop liver cirrhosis. You begin to wonder why that would happen. “Similarly, we are finding liver cirrhosis and kidney disease among young people between the ages of 22 and 30. I think it calls for caution.” According to him, the consumption of unhealthy alcoholic drinks and other potentially contaminated beverages could be among the risk factors associated with the conditions, although further investigations would be required to establish the causes of individual cases. Arohunmolase also recalled previous incidents involving suspected adulterated drinks in Odigbo and Irele, saying the reported deaths highlighted the urgency of tackling the menace.

title: Gunmen kill Islamic cleric, associate in Katsina
body: Suspected bandits have killed a prominent Islamic cleric, Sheikh Yahaya Masussuka, and his associate in Dutsin-Ma Local Government Area of Katsina State. The attack occurred at about 9 pm on Monday at the entrance to the cleric’s residence in Dutsin-Ma town, where the assailants reportedly opened fire on the two men. The victims were rushed to Dutsin-Ma Hospital for emergency medical attention but were later confirmed dead. The killing has thrown the community into mourning, particularly followers of the cleric and residents who knew him. As of the time of filing this report, details about the identity of the attackers and the motive behind the killing remained unclear. Security agents kill ISWAP commander, 15 others in Borno PDP kicks as Dankwambo’s name appears on Gombe APC campaign list The Katsina State Police Command has confirmed the death of the Islamic scholar. It was also gathered that Sheikh Masussuka had planned to organise a religious gathering in Katsina State later this week. The late cleric had previously been involved in controversies over his religious teachings. On November 18, 2025, the Katsina State Government announced that he would be required to defend his teachings before a committee of Islamic scholars. However, there was no indication as of press time that the earlier controversy was connected to Monday night’s killing. The police had yet to provide further details on the circumstances of the attack or announce any arrests as of press time.

title: 2027 Campaign Billboards: How states are pricing opposition out of sight
body: *APM fights back, goes to court *We’re not discriminating against any party – States *It can cream off 80% of allowed campaign limit By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA – A growing number of state governments are charging presidential candidates tens and even hundreds of millions of naira for the right to display posters and billboards, raising fears that visibility is being priced beyond the reach of opposition parties less than three months to the January 16, 2027 election. Campaigns for the Presidential and National Assembly polls opened on August 19. By then, several states had already published fee schedules, and the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, had cleared 19 presidential candidates. Abia sets the highest rate. Its signage agency charges N200 million for a presidential candidate, N150 million for a governorship candidate, N100 million for a senatorial candidate, N50 million for the House of Representatives and N20 million for the State Assembly. Enugu and Kogi each demand N150 million from presidential candidates. Cross River is reported at N150 million, Rivers at N75 million and Anambra at N50 million, a five-fold rise on its 2022 presidential fee of N10 million. The contrast with other states shows how arbitrary the figures are. Kano charges about N1.15 million and draws no distinction between political and commercial billboards. Kaduna assesses fees site by site. Imo asks senatorial candidates for N5 million, plus application and inspection charges. A question of arithmetic The sums matter because of the spending ceiling in the Electoral Act 2026, which caps a presidential candidate’s election expenses at N10 billion and a governorship candidate’s at N3 billion. If Abia’s N200 million applied in all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory, permits alone would cost N7.4 billion, or 74 per cent of the presidential cap, before a single rally, jingle or vehicle is paid for. The Allied Peoples Movement, APM, and its presidential candidate, Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde, argue that such fees could consume more than 80 per cent of the ceiling. They have asked the Abia High Court in suit HC/214/2026 to declare the N200 million fee unconstitutional and void. No hearing date had been announced at the last report, and no court has ruled on the legality of any of these fees. Not simply an APC tyranny The opposition has described the fees as a ruling-party tactic. The African Democratic Congress, ADC, said they are targeted at the opposition and has vowed to challenge them. The Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, said the states involved are mostly controlled by the All Progressives Congress, APC. But the record is more complicated. The N200 million fee in Abia was imposed by the administration of Governor Alex Otti of the Labour Party, LP. In Oyo, the APC accuses the APM-led state government of directing its signage agency to clamp down on non-APM campaigners. Enugu and Kogi, both APC-controlled, are among the states where the opposition’s complaints are sharpest. That cuts both ways. It weakens the claim of a single party’s master plan, but it strengthens the broader point that incumbent governments in several parties now control the gate to public advertising space. What the states say Governments insist the charges are administrative. Abia says its schedule applies to every party and that it “will not discriminate against any political party or any candidate.” Kogi State Information Commissioner, Kingsley Fanwo, said the rules bind APC candidates as well, adding that “the government is for everybody.” Enugu’s APC says it is paying the fee itself. The states cite their powers over physical planning and urban aesthetics, and Abia says a billboard collapse in Aba in 2025 informed its approach. Critics are not persuaded. A political scientist at Bayero University, Kano, Prof. Kamilu Sani Fage, argues that ruling parties will probably pay with public funds, while opposition candidates pay from their own pockets. Abia’s opposition, the ADC and the PDP, also question whether state agencies have the power to levy these fees at all. For Prof. Fage, the timing is the problem. “It is wrong to introduce such measures now,” he said. The Out-of-Home Advertising Association of Nigeria wants states to keep to gazetted tariffs. The Advertising Regulatory Council of Nigeria, ARCON, has said state agencies have no authority to approve political adverts before they are displayed. Legal gap The Electoral Act is silent on billboard placement, leaving it to state and local laws, according to a constitutional lawyer, Kehinde Oloje. That gap is what states are using. Opponents point to the Act’s prohibition on using state apparatus to favour or disadvantage any candidate to the spending cap, and to the constitutional rights to free expression and association in sections 39 and 40. However, states are relying on their Land Use Act powers, even though there are arguments that outdoor advertising fees should be collected by local councils. Early effects The impact is already visible. In Lagos, where the signage agency’s rates are not campaign-specific, many opposition candidates had not placed any signboard since campaigns opened. In Imo, the Action People’s Party, APP, says it is paying even though the charges are high. In Abia, the APC governorship candidate, Eric Opah, says “workers, pensioners and traders” will be his billboards rather than paid-space. The shift matters because billboards are cheap per exposure and durable, which is why politicians favour them. Candidates who cannot afford them are left with radio (especially the private ones), social media and town halls. Way forward Stakeholders are asking INEC to issue guidelines separating administrative fees from campaign expenses, and the National Assembly to cap state levies on political advertising. They want states to publish who has paid and who has been waived, and the courts to rule early enough on the matter. INEC’s chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN, has said the commission will track illegal campaign spending and that broadcasters must give all parties equal access. title: Russian ballistic missile attack on Kyiv kills one, injures 10 and damages medical facilities and school
body:
An Ukrinform correspondent reported the explosions.
The Ukrainian Air Force warned of the threat of ballistic missile strikes from Bryansk and detected several missiles heading toward the capital.
An air raid alert was declared in Kyiv and several regions.
Mayor Vitali Klitschko and the Kyiv City Military Administration are reporting on the consequences of the enemy attack.

title: Meghan to co-host Junior MasterChef Australia
body: The Duchess of Sussex has been confirmed as a co-hostof the new season of Junior MasterChef Australia. Meghan will join the 2027 series as a “special guest” with fellow host Poh Ling Yeow, according to Australia’s Channel 10. The Duchess said she “can’t wait” to join the programme after appearing as a guest judge on MasterChef Australia last year. The show drew its largest Sunday audience since 2023, according to a statement from Paramount ANZ. The announcement comes as Meghan faces increased scrutiny due to her father Thomas Markle being accused of child sexual abuse. He denies the allegations. The BBC understands Meghan broke contact with her father last year , telling him she and authorities knew he had abused young girls. Markle has strongly rejected the accusations as “lies” used to destroy his reputation. Meghan’s return to Australia follows a four-day tour of the country she and Prince Harry undertook in April. Meghan’s MasterChef debut was announced on the second day of the tour, a Wednesday when the Duchess was notably absent from public appearances. That evening, it was revealed she had been filming an episode. It is understood she was not paid for her appearance. Australia’s Network 10, which airs the series as part of Paramount ANZ, did not respond to a question from the BBC about whether Meghan would be paid for the Junior MasterChef season. “I love cooking with my own kids, so seeing what these young stars create in the kitchen is going to be a lot of fun,” Meghan said in a statement. In August, the Sussexes announced they were moving back to the UK from California. The couple left the UK and stepped back from their royal duties in early 2020, before settling in California in March that year. They launched media careers that included a high-profile interview with Oprah Winfrey and deals with Netflix and Spotify. Meghan’s lifestyle and cookery show on Netflix, With Love, Meghan, ran for two series and a Christmas special but did not perform well with audiences. She also launched lifestyle brand As Ever, which includes a food range, but in March it ended its partnership with the streaming platform . Last year, she registered her trademark in more than a dozen product categories in Australia, including cookware and table linen.

title: 64 students hospitalised after being administered Bilharzia drug in Katsina
body: Sixty-four students of Government Science Secondary School, Batagarawa, Katsina State, have been hospitalised after reportedly developing adverse reactions to drugs administered to them during a Bilharzia treatment and prevention exercise. The students were taken to Ahmadi Rimi General Hospital and Turai Yar’Adua Maternal and Child Hospital in Katsina after experiencing symptoms including vomiting, abdominal discomfort and dizziness. The incident sparked anxiety among parents and members of the school community, particularly after some of the affected students were reportedly brought to the hospital unconscious. “They were brought to the hospital unconscious,” the Medical Director of Ahmadi Rimi General Hospital, Dr Auwal Sani, said. He added that the affected students were responding to treatment. A parent, who visited his children at the hospital, also confirmed to Daily Trust that they are recovering. Two of the affected students, Abubakar Muhammad Khairi and Hassan Muhammad, who spoke to Daily Trust, said the drugs were administered after their heights had been measured. According to the students, the number of tablets given to each student varied, with some receiving three tablets, others two, and some one tablet, depending on their height. It was not immediately clear whether height was the sole basis for determining the dosage or whether other clinical considerations were taken into account. A parent, Maaruf Sani, who visited his affected children at the hospital, said they had recovered from the reactions. The Katsina State Commissioner for Basic and Secondary Education, Yusuf Sulaiman Jibia, confirmed the incident, saying all the affected students had recovered and were being prepared to return to school. “The affected students have fully recovered, and we are making arrangements for their return to school,” Jibia said. He explained that the drug administration exercise was carried out by the Primary Health Care authorities in collaboration with Batagarawa Local Government Area. The commissioner assured parents and residents that there was no cause for alarm, saying the government would investigate the incident to establish what went wrong. Jibia added that the students were being provided with food before their return to school. Bilharzia, also known as schistosomiasis, is a parasitic disease associated with exposure to contaminated freshwater. However, the precise cause of the reactions experienced by the students remains unclear. No official findings had been released as of the time of filing this report to establish whether the incident was linked to the medication, its dosage or other factors. Officials said preventive treatment programmes are conducted in affected communities to reduce the burden of the disease.

title: Trump campaigns in Mississippi, highlighting Republicans' challenges
body:
President Donald Trump arrives at a campaign rally at Crossroads Arena, in Corinth, Miss., Monday, Oct. 26, 2026. Jacquelyn Martin/AP hide caption
CORINTH, Miss. — President Donald Trump campaigned Monday in Mississippi, as he continued a closing midterm rally blitz that has highlighted Republicans' challenges ahead of an election that could drastically shift power in Washington and statehouses across the country.
"I'm here because Cindy's doing great, but I just got to make sure. I can't take a chance," Trump told the crowd, his voice audibly hoarse, as he worked to boost Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, who is facing a surprisingly stiff challenge from Democrat Scott Colom.
Colom was spotted at the rally site, too, creating the rare spectacle of Trump's staunchest supporters interacting directly with a figure the president would soon go on to denigrate as a "Marxist radical" and "fake" and "shameless phony who pretends to be a moderate" from the stage.
Mississippi, among the nation's most reliably Republican states, is not where the Republicans envisioned needing a late-October stop from the president. But Colom is one of many Democratic underdogs who have managed to expand the House and Senate battleground maps because of widespread voter discontent over inflation, the Iran war and other aspects of Trump's second presidency.
He said he had planned to go to the rally site to listen to what was on Trump supporters' minds.
"They actually deserve a senator that will listen to them, that actually cares about what they think, actually cares about what they're going through," Colom said ahead of the president's arrival.
Trump's event kicks off a week of aggressive campaigning that will include more stops in states he won comfortably in 2024, including Texas, South Carolina and Iowa. Trump also plans to hold a rally Saturday in Salina, Kansas, officials announced late Monday, marking his second visit to the state in less than two weeks.
Former Vice President Kamala Harris speaks at Women for Crowley event Monday, Oct. 26, 2026, in Milwaukee. Nam Y. Huh/AP hide caption
Top Democratic candidates and their surrogates were also greeting voters — more than 30 million of whom have already cast ballots, according to data collected by The Associated Press from election administrators across the country — as they try to end Republicans' threadbare majority in the House, reclaim control of the Senate and claw back power in state capitals.
Former Vice President Kamala Harris, Democrats' 2024 presidential candidate, campaigned in Wisconsin with Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley, who faces Rep. Tom Tiffany, a Trump ally, in the governor's race. If elected, Crowley would be the first Black governor to lead the battleground state.
"This is a tight race because the stakes are so high," Harris said at an event billed as a "Women for Crowley" rally.
Meanwhile, in Michigan, Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed distanced himself from an ad created by a group called Rebellion PAC that blames high grocery prices on U.S. support for Israel.
"This ad is not affiliated in any way with the Abdul for Senate campaign," a spokesperson for El-Sayed, Roxie Richner, said in a statement about the spot, which features a couple discussing U.S. support for Israel as they shop for groceries.
"Apparently it's costing us a lot of money to drop bombs on Gaza," the woman says.
The ad had been condemned by U.S. Rep. Haley Stevens, who narrowly lost to El-Sayed in the Democratic primary.
The way to win Michigan "is not by blaming the high costs of our goods on the only Jewish homeland in the world," Stevens wrote on X.
El-Sayed, who would be the country's first Muslim senator, has denounced antisemitism while fiercely criticizing Israel for its military operations in Gaza — a position that has been a frequent point of attack for both Republicans and supporters of Israel in his party.
Vice President JD Vance reacts after speaking at a campaign rally at Bozeman Yellowstone International Airport, Monday, Oct. 26, 2026, in Belgrade, Mont. Finn Gomez//POOL Getty Images North America hide caption
Vice President JD Vance returned to Kansas to stump for Sen. Roger Marshall, who finds himself in a tight contest with Democratic nominee and pastor Adam Hamilton. Hundreds of people were gathered inside the warehouse of a steel-fabricating company in north Topeka in a state where Democrats haven't won a Senate race since 1932.
Marshall, who has raised far less money than Hamilton, told the crowd that Trump is on the ballot, even if his name doesn't appear, because of how Democrats will thwart his agenda if they win control of Congress.
"Democrats are coming out like it's a presidential year," he said, calling on the GOP to match Democrats' energy.
Jace Sullivan, a 50-year-old electrician from Topeka who describes himself as "85% Republican," said Trump supporters need to "circle the wagons" and get out to vote.
Wearing a red "JD Vance for President 2028" shirt, he said he thinks Trump is rightly working to keep Iran from getting nuclear weapons.
"Gas prices are high and it does suck, but it's a means to an end," Sullivan said.
Trump, at the Mississippi rally, said he had, in fact, expected gas prices to rise even higher than they had.
"It worked out fine and it'll be over soon," he said of the war with Iran.
Earlier, Vance was in Belgrade, Montana, to campaign with Republican Aaron Flint, who is facing Democrat Sam Forstag in the race for the state's 1st Congressional District, and Republican Senate candidate Kurt Alme.
Despite the visits to ruby red states, Sen. Tim Scott, who serves as chairman of the National Republican Senatorial Committee, told The Associated Press Monday that GOP candidates are "closing very strongly" in races across the country, including South Carolina, which Trump is set to visit for the second time in as many weeks to stump for GOP Sen. Darline Graham.
"One of the reasons why we will be in the majority is because he has invested the time and the energy on the campaign trail," Scott said on the sidelines of U.S. Rep. Russell Fry's 3rd Annual Freedom Fry event.
But it's Trump's visit to Mississippi that perhaps brings the midterm landscape into the sharpest relief with just a week of campaigning left.
To be sure, Hyde-Smith, who is vying for her second full term, remains the favorite in a state Trump won three times by an average of nearly 20 percentage points.
But Colom, a local prosecutor who would make history as Mississippi's first Black senator since post-Civil War Reconstruction, is looking to parlay inflation, Trump's lagging popularity and Hyde-Smith's mistakes into an upset.
Senate Democrats' super PAC has been a late entry in the contest, with a $1.2 million investment. Mississippians have not chosen a new Democratic senator since 1947, and Democrats last won a Senate race there when that senator, the onetime segregationist John Stennis, won his last reelection in 1982.
In New York, meanwhile, one of the party's most vulnerable House members pulled from Trump's campaign playbook. Rep. Mike Lawler, who is in a tight race with Democrat Cait Conley in New York City's northern suburbs, manned a McDonald's drive-thru — mimicking something Trump did two years ago, even as Lawler has tried to emphasize his independence from the president.

title: Kane wins Ballon D’Or, first Englishman in 25 years
body: Harry Kane has won his first ever Ballon d’Or award at the ceremony held in London on Monday night. The Bayern Munich and England international beat a host of players including Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal to the award. He is the first Englishman to win the award in 25 years, since Michael Owen in 2001. Kane takes over from last year’s winner Ousmane Dembele, and is the first player from Bayern Munich to win the gold trophy in 45 years since Karl-Heinz Rummenigge in 1981. Kane wins the award on the back of a free-scoring season that ended with the Bundesliga title, DFB Cup, and a third place finish at the 2026 FIFA World Cup with England. He scored a record 71 goals in the season to also win the golden shoe award. Kane, who won the Bundesliga highest goalscorer last season, was also named the best men’s striker of the year at the ceremony. Other awards of the night included Yamal as the men’s best young talent of the year, while Spain dominated with seven awards. The men and women World Cup champions won the best coach and goalkeeper awards in both male and female categories, among others.

title: Israeli voters head to polling stations to deliver Netanyahu verdict
body: Polls have opened across Israel in one of the most momentous elections in its history as voters deliver their verdict on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu 's wartime leadership. Mr Netanyahu is seeking re-election after a four-year term defined by the catastrophic security failure of the attacks on October 7, 2023, Israel's destructive war on Gaza and the country's subsequent campaigns in Lebanon, Iran and across the region. Polls suggest a close race that could result in long coalition talks just as Middle East countries try to restore stability. Forecasters give Gadi Eisenkot, a former senior general, the best chance of unseating Mr Netanyahu from a variety of opposition candidates . Voters from the country's Arab minority could play a key role. Political sources have told The National their turnout is expected to be “astronomical”. Senior opposition officials have also said there is a possibility of a coalition or agreement for a minority government with the Arab parties. “After what they have witnessed over the past three years, they have understood the difference between bad and worse,” said an Israeli political observer, referring to the hard-right parties that have shaped Mr Netanyahu's government. Voting centres close at 10pm Israeli time, when exit polls will give a first indication of the results. Preliminary results will emerge as votes are counted overnight. Opposition supporters used the campaign's final days to call for a formal inquiry into the October 7 attacks, something Mr Netanyahu has resisted. He has countered with steps to underline his hardline security position, from warning of a "second Holocaust" if Iran is allowed to rearm, to ordering an operation of questionable military value in the occupied West Bank. In the final hours before Tuesday, the opposition also rallied behind Israel's military chief of staff, Lt Gen Eyal Zamir, amid reports that Mr Netanyahu plans to fire him if he regains power, after the pair were said to have fallen out over the Prime Minister's efforts to restart fighting with Iran for political reasons. "Chief of Staff Zamir will conclude his role only in accordance with the date stipulated by law," Mr Eisenkot wrote in a post on X on Monday evening. "Tomorrow the people of Israel will elect a prime minister whose considerations will always be for the good of Israel, who will never act out of political interests at the expense of Israel's security and the fighters of the [Israel military]." Mr Netanyahu called the reports "another piece of fake news". "I have no intention of firing the Chief of Staff and we will continue working together for Israel's security. I do intend to permanently remove the Iranian nuclear threat. I will do so together with my friend President [Donald] Trump, and we will also sign peace agreements with additional countries." With Israel's standing abroad badly damaged, notably by its devastating campaign in Gaza and settlement expansion in the West Bank, Mr Netanyahu has quoted support from Mr Trump as a key selling point. Mr Trump issued a late message of endorsement, hailing a "great relationship in winning together". Mr Eisenkot has kept his policies vague, running on a brand of down-to-earth honesty. But most of the main candidates hold belligerent views towards Iran and few are enthusiastic about the idea of a Palestinian state, although some have offered hints of conciliation. An alliance of former prime ministers Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid has declined in the polls. Gazans have expressed little optimism about the vote. Palestinian political analyst Mustafa Ibrahim said he did not believe the situation would change significantly whether Mr Netanyahu wins or loses. Many Gazans are nonetheless hoping he loses, holding him responsible for mass destruction of the territory during a war that has killed more than 70,000 people. About 7.3 million Israelis are eligible to vote for the 120-member Knesset. There are 36 parties running, although most are not expected to win enough votes to enter parliament. Israel has a history of political deadlock. Between 2019 and 2022, the country held five elections as parties repeatedly struggled to form stable governments. Mr Netanyahu – who has led Israel for all but 18 months since 2009 – would remain as a caretaker prime minister during a period of coalition talks. Some believe he might use such a deadlock to his advantage, possibly by initiating a new round of fighting with Iran. “If Benjamin Netanyahu wins again, I’m genuinely scared for this country. I don’t think I have a future here,” Romy Schlegel-Cohen, 17, told The National in Tel Aviv's Hostage Square. Reports claim Mr Netanyahu had been pushing for a joint US-Israeli strike on Iran before the election, which Mr Trump did not approve. Mr Eisenkot said he had “full trust” in the military.

title: VIDEO: Tornado kills 4 construction workers in Antalya
body: TEHRAN, Oct. 27 (MNA) – A tornado struck Antalya, Turkey, killed four construction workers, one injured, and damaged worker containers and a construction crane.

title: Police arrest 35-year-old man over alleged rape of 11-year-old girl
body:
The police in Cross River State have arrested a 35-year-old man over the alleged rape of an 11-year-old girl in Yala Local Government Area of the state.
Police said the suspect, Okputu Bright, was arrested after the victim’s father reported the incident at the Okpoma Divisional Police Headquarters on 24 October.
In a statement on Sunday, police spokesperson Sunday Eitokpah said the alleged incident occurred on 18 October.
According to the police, the father alleged that Mr Bright lured the girl and sexually assaulted her before leaving her at a location within the community.
The police said the child had been referred to a general hospital for medical examination, while the suspect was arrested and detained.
“The Command has directed that the investigation be concluded promptly and the case file transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) for further investigation, in accordance with established procedures,” the statement said.
The Commissioner of Police in the state, Ajo Ordue, reiterated the command’s commitment to protecting children and other vulnerable persons.
Mr Ordue urged residents to report suspected sexual offences promptly and assured the public that the allegations would be handled professionally, with due regard for the child’s welfare and confidentiality.
The police also warned against circulating information or images that could identify the child or expose her to harm further.
“The Command emphasises that the suspect remains presumed innocent unless proven guilty by a court of competent jurisdiction,” the statement added.
The arrest comes amid other reported cases of sexual offences involving minors in Cross River.
In August, PREMIUM TIMES reported the arrest of two men, aged 68 and 70, over the alleged attempted rape of a 12-year-old girl in Calabar. The police said the girl’s father reported the incident.
In June, a Family Court in Calabar sentenced 41-year-old Endurance Sandy to life imprisonment for raping an 11-year-old girl. The case commenced in 2021.
In May, the Family Court in Calabar sentenced 27-year-old Edidiong Nyojole to life imprisonment for raping a 13-year-old girl. The court also ordered him to pay the victim N1 million in compensation.

title: Bandits shoot resident, rustle 28 cattle in Sokoto community
body: Armed bandits have attacked Gidan Sarki, a community near Usmanu Danfodiyo University, Sokoto (UDUS), shooting a resident in the leg and rustling 28 cows. The attack occurred around 9pm on Sunday in the community located behind the university’s Jummat Mosque, triggering panic among residents. The Sokoto State Police Command confirmed the incident, saying the attackers shot the owner of the livestock before escaping with the animals. A senior police officer told our correspondent that the attack appeared to have targeted the victim’s household because of the large number of livestock kept there. “The attackers invaded a house in Gidan Sarki and shot the owner, identified as Malam Shehu Muhammad, in the leg. He is responding to treatment. “They also rustled 28 cows belonging to him and his son, Mustapha Shehu,” the officer said. He added that the police received information about the attack and directed the divisional police officer in charge of Wamakko Local Government Area to mobilise personnel to the community. The police spokesperson, Ahmed Rufa’i, also confirmed the incident. Residents said the attackers had threatened members of the community and demanded that students living in the area be brought out. “They threatened us to bring out the students living in this community, but thank God it was during the holiday, although some newly admitted students were reportedly around for registration,” a resident said. According to a university staff member who spoke on condition of anonymity, the students were not residing on the main campus. The staff member confirmed that the affected community was near the university but stressed that the attack did not occur within the institution’s main campus. Efforts to obtain an official comment from the university were unsuccessful, as its spokesperson, Isma’il Muhammad Yauri, declined to comment, saying the institution was not involved in the incident. Background The latest incident comes amid previous security incidents involving communities around the university, although authorities have distinguished attacks outside the campus from incidents within its premises. On November 18, 2023, the university management refuted a report published by a national daily (not daily Trust) alleging that gunmen had attacked its main campus, killing one person and injuring others. In a statement, the university’s spokesperson, Isma’il Muhammad Yauri, said the incident occurred in Dundayen Bakin Gulbi, a village about two kilometres from the institution, and not within the university. The management described the report as false and unfounded, adding that the university maintained security arrangements through collaboration with state security agencies and its internal security network. Earlier, on October 3, 2023, the police confirmed an armed robbery at the university’s mini-market. The police spokesperson, ASP Ahmad Rufa’i, said about six hoodlums attacked shops, injured two shop owners and stole items, including beverages and food products. He said security personnel responded to the incident and deployed two patrol teams within the university. The university’s Dean of Student Affairs, Professor Umar Aliyu, also described the incident as armed robbery rather than a bandit attack, explaining that the assailants fired shots into the air to scare people away before looting shops. He said the attackers did not enter student hostels or staff residences and that normalcy was restored following the deployment of security personnel.

title: Businessman builds N2.2bn hospital for Edo community
body: An oil services tycoon, Chief Leemon Ikpea, has built a 62-bed hospital worth N2.2 billion in Ewatto, Esan South East Local Government Area of Edo State. Ikpea, a philanthropist and founder of the Agbonjagwe Leemon Ikpea Foundation, said the hospital was built to improve access to healthcare for residents of Ewatto and neighbouring communities. The medical centre, which was commissioned on Monday, October 19, 2026 and named after the founder, was built at an estimated cost of N2.227 billion. The facility is equipped with modern medical equipment and is expected to reduce the difficulties faced by residents who had to travel considerable distances to access healthcare, particularly during emergencies. The centre will provide a range of services, including emergency and urgent care, maternal and child health, diagnostic and laboratory services and general medical care. Speaking at the commissioning, Ikpea said that the project was conceived in response to the healthcare challenges faced by Ewatto and the surrounding communities. Ikpea said, “I firmly believe that one of the most meaningful legacies any individual can leave behind is an institution that continues to improve and preserve human lives long after the individual is gone. It is my sincere hope that this medical centre will become such a legacy.” He added, “We are particularly encouraged by the continuing efforts of both the Federal and Edo State governments to strengthen healthcare infrastructure and improve access to healthcare services. We hope that this facility will become a valuable partner in those efforts.” Ikpea said the centre would provide healthcare and create opportunities for medical professionals to work and train, adding that it was intended to ensure mothers, children and elderly people could access timely medical attention without travelling long distances, while emergencies receive prompt care. Acknowledging the contributions of the Federal and the Edo State Governments, Ikpea urged the residents of Ewatto and the neighbouring communities to take ownership of the facility and ensure its proper maintenance. The Governor of Edo State, Monday Okpebholo, commended Chief Ikpea, saying his life as a philanthropists was exemplified by the lives he had touched. He praised Ikpea for the “extraordinary healthcare investment he brought to his people.” The Minister of Health, Prof Muhammad Ali Pate, commended Chief Ikpea for complementing the government’s efforts to improve access to quality healthcare, describing the medical centre as a significant contribution to healthcare delivery in the community. The Onojie of Ekpoma Kingdom, His Royal Highness Barrister Antony Ehiozojie Abumere II, congratulated Ikpea on the establishment of the medical centre, describing it as a valuable contribution to the health and wellbeing of the people of Esanland. Also, the Onogie of Igueben, HRM Ehiogie Eluojierior, commended Ikpea’s achievements and the human investment initiatives of his foundation across Edo State, urging other capable individuals to emulate his efforts in providing healthcare facilities.

title: Bandits kill man, abduct wife in Katsina
body: Bandits have killed a man and abducted his wife in a fresh attack on Karofi community, Dutsin-Ma Local Government Area of Katsina State after weeks of relative calm. The attack occurred on Sunday night, October 25, barely three days after bandits abducted another woman, 25-year-old Rukayya, the wife of Sule Mai Kaji, in the same community on Thursday, October 23. The latest incident has thrown Karofi into mourning and renewed concerns over the effectiveness of community-driven peace efforts. Some residents reportedly fled to Dutsin-Ma town, about 12 kilometres away for safety. NDC and the battle within Security agents kill ISWAP commander, 15 others in Borno The victim of Sunday’s attack was identified as Ya’u Faduma, who was killed before his wife was taken away by the assailants. A resident who identified himself simply as Babangida Karofi told Daily Trust that the killings and abductions have left residents increasingly worried about their safety. Another resident, Maikudi Mai Petur Karofi, said the gunmen operated for about an hour before leaving with their victim after killing her husband. He described the incident as devastating, saying residents had been thrown into confusion and were uncertain about what might happen next. Mai Petur also confirmed that some residents had started leaving the community for Dutsin-Ma town, approximately 12 kilometres away, amid growing fears of further attacks. Meanwhile, residents of Baggagadi, Radda and Kuki communities in Dutsin-Ma and Charanchi local government areas have renewed calls for urgent security intervention, urging the authorities to prioritise the protection of lives and property. Hassan Yusuf, a resident of Kuki, said suspected bandits operating from neighbouring Matazu Local Government Area had been terrorising communities in the area for weeks. When contacted, the Katsina State Police Command spokesperson, DSP Sadik Aliyu, said he would verify the information and call back. However, he had yet to return the call as of the time of filing this report. Similarly, neither the Katsina State Government nor any security agency had issued an official statement on the reported incidents as of press time.

title: Security agents kill ISWAP commander, 15 others in Borno
body: Troops of Operation Hadin Kai have killed a high-ranking terrorist commander, Abu Zubiru, alongside 15 other insurgents. According to a statement released on Monday by the spokesman for Operation Hadin Kai, Captain Mohammed Goni, the terrorists were neutralised during a series of coordinated air and artillery strikes targeting three suspected insurgent enclaves in the Tunbunma area of South Lake Chad. Goni said the precise military operation was executed between 1:00 a.m. and 2:00 a.m. on October 26, 2026. The strikes were launched following actionable intelligence regarding the convergence of key terrorist leaders and fighters in the region. NIGERIA DAILY: How Did Binnari’s Death Toll Rise from 10 to 58? 3 killed in road crash involving Niger gov’s convoy He said a subsequent battle damage assessment (BDA) confirmed the deaths of 16 fighters. Among the casualties, alongside Abu Zubiru, were two of his close associates identified as Baana Nglewa and Jindullah Sadiq. The operation also reported that Abu Saleem, whom intelligence identified as the Wali (Governor) of Tunbunma, sustained severe injuries during the bombardment, alongside seven other terrorists. The latest offensive adds to a string of recent victories for the military in the region. According to Operation Hadin Kai, a total of 37 terrorists have been neutralised over the past 72 hours of sustained military operations in the North East.

title: 3 killed in road crash involving Niger gov’s convoy
body: Three people have died in a road crash at Gidan Mangoro community on Minna-Bida Road, Niger State. The accident occurred on Monday following a head-on collision between a Hilux van traveling in the convoy of the Niger State Governor, Mohammed Umaru Bago and a private car. A resident of Gidan Mangoro, Danjuma Umar, told Daily Trust that the accident happened around 11 am when the governor was returning from Bida. He said the occupants of the private car were suspected to be postgraduate students of the Federal University of Technology, Minna. Wiretapping: Court fixes Nov 25 for El-Rufai’s trial Nigeria needs $6bn equipment to achieve 3mbpd oil output – PETAN “The people in the private car died instantly, while those in the government Hilux were seriously injured. “The accident was caused by a wrongful overtaking by the Hilux in the governor’s convoy. The other car was in their lane when the Hilux rammed into them,” he said. He said the private vehicle was driven by a woman who was a resident of Gidan Mangoro community. A staff member of the Minna General Hospital, however, told Daily Trust that two people were brought to the hospital dead, while the third person died at the hospital’s emergency unit where he was hospitalised. Some of the injured victims were referred to the IBB Specialist Hospital for advanced treatment. Daily Trust gathered that one of the occupants of the Hilux van was a former council chairman whose legs got fractured. The Niger State Sector Commander of the Federal Road Safety Corps, Aishat Sa’adu, confirmed the crash. She, however, said before her men could arrive at the scene, the victims had been evacuated. She also confirmed that there were casualties but could not give the number of people involved.

title: Delta extends retirement age for clinical health workers
body:
Governor Sheriff Oborevwori of Delta State has approved an extension of the retirement age for skilled clinical health professionals in government hospitals from 60 to 65 years.
The policy also extends the maximum length of service from 35 to 40 years, whichever comes first.
Mr Oborevwori announced the development in Asaba on Monday.
He said the initiative aimed to address manpower shortages, retain experienced medical personnel and strengthen healthcare delivery in the state.
The governor also said the policy covers 26 categories of skilled clinical health professionals actively engaged in clinical services in government hospitals.
According to him, these include medical officers, nursing officers, pharmacists, medical laboratory scientists, physiotherapists, radiographers, optometrists, psychologists, dental officers, community health officers and audiologists.
Others include dieticians, medical laboratory technicians, pharmacy technicians, X-ray technicians, dental technologists, dental therapists, prosthetic and orthoptists, among others.
Mr Oborevwori said the extension followed appeals by the Delta Council of the National Association of Nigeria Nurses and Midwives and the state chapter of the Nigerian Medical Association .
“The associations have sought the adoption of the policy in Delta following its approval at the federal level,” he said.
The governor explained that eligible officers seeking the extension must apply through their respective chief medical directors six months before attaining 60 years of age or completing 35 years in service.
“Applicants are also required to present medical certificates of fitness, while chief medical directors are expected to forward applications to the Ministry of Health for screening and approval by the commissioner,” he added.
Mr Oborevwori clarified that the policy does not cover skilled clinical health professionals serving in ministries and extra-ministerial departments.
He said the extension was specifically designed for personnel actively engaged in clinical practice in government hospitals.
He expressed confidence that retaining experienced and medically fit personnel would help preserve professional expertise and institutional knowledge within the state’s public hospital system.
The governor added that the policy took effect from the date of approval, subject to the prescribed application, screening and approval procedures.

title: Awula Serwah urges Mahama to reaffirm mining licence requirements
body: The Executive Director of Eco-Conscious Citizens, Awula Serwah, has urged President John Dramani Mahama to publicly reaffirm the legal requirements governing mining, warning that recent comments by Ghana Gold Board Chief Executive Officer Sammy Gyamfi risk sending the wrong signal to small-scale miners. She says the government must make it clear that no one is permitted to undertake mining without the appropriate licence and other regulatory approvals, amid ongoing efforts to clamp down on illegal mining. Awula Serwah warned that any suggestion that miners could operate without the necessary authorisation could weaken the work of the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) and other groups fighting irresponsible mining. She said illegal mining continues to pose serious threats through the pollution of water bodies, destruction of forest reserves and loss of agricultural land. She also stressed that a mining licence is essential to ensure operators work only in approved areas, adding that securing one does not necessarily mean all other regulatory conditions have been met. Depending on the operation, miners may also require permits from the Environmental Protection Agency and approvals from relevant water authorities. Speaking to Channel One TV on Monday, October 26, she said the President should assure the public that the government was not endorsing unlawful mining. “The President should come out and let Ghanaians know that they are not encouraging lawlessness, and anybody who wants to mine must first obtain a licence,” she said. She further cautioned that encouraging mining without a licence could amount to a criminal offence, insisting that the law must be respected as the country intensifies efforts to address the environmental damage caused by illegal mining.

title: How Climate Change Could Reshape Migration Across Central Asia
body: The Astana Times provides news and information from Kazakhstan and around the world. ASTANA – Climate change does not always force people to move from their homes overnight. Sometimes, it slowly takes away the reasons to stay. A farmer working on degraded land. Photo credit: UNDP Uzbekistan For farmers and livestock herders, rising temperatures, prolonged droughts and reduced water supplies can mean declining harvests, shrinking pastureland and lost income. What begins as an environmental problem can become an economic one, influencing whether families stay or seek opportunities elsewhere. Across Central Asia, such pressures could increasingly shape patterns of migration, even as researchers struggle to determine how much of the movement can be attributed directly to climate change. Climate-related migration can take many forms. People may leave suddenly after floods or other disasters, or gradually as drought, water scarcity and declining agricultural productivity undermine their livelihoods. Such movements can be temporary or permanent, occurring within national borders or across them. Climate pressures often overlap with economic and social factors, making it difficult to identify a single reason why people move. Where climate change may drive movement In Central Asia, climate change could drive as many as 2.4 million people to move within their own countries by 2050, according to a pessimistic scenario modeled in the World Bank’s 2021 Groundswell report. Under alternative scenarios involving more inclusive development or lower emissions, the projected number falls to 1.9 million and 1.7 million, respectively. Globally, the report estimates as many as 216 million people may move within their countries by 2050 across six regions. Climate change could also reshape patterns of migration, making some areas more attractive, while increasing pressure to leave others. The World Bank identified the Ferghana Valley, areas around Tashkent and Dushanbe, and parts of Kazakhstan, including Astana, Karagandy and Kostanai, as potential destinations for internal climate migrants, where changes in water availability and crop productivity could create more favorable livelihood opportunities. By contrast, parts of southern Kazakhstan, areas surrounding the Ferghana Valley in Uzbekistan and Tajikistan, and the vicinity of Bishkek could become hotspots of climate-related out-migration as water availability and agricultural productivity decline. Nugzar Kokhreidze. Photo credit: personal archive These projections, however, do not account for the longer-term effects of glacier melt on Central Asia’s rivers, which could alter water availability and migration patterns. “Climate change already has an impact on migration in Eurasia,” Nugzar Kokhreidze, a climate advocate, co-founder and chairman of the Dialogue of Generations Research-Intellectual Club, told The Astana Times. Determining how much climate change already influences migration is far from straightforward. People move for economic, social and political reasons, often under pressures that are difficult to disentangle from a changing environment. “However, it is difficult to say that ‘climate migrants’ constitute a proper, separate and clearly identifiable category. Migration has many causes,” Kokhreidze said. “At the same time, we cannot say that migration is caused only by economic factors. Even if a person leaves after losing their home, the underlying reasons could include repeated droughts, water scarcity and decreasing harvests. Based on this example, we can say that economic pressure becomes a mechanism through which climate change affects migration,” he explained. Environmental pressures already affect communities While climate models offer projections of future migration, there is evidence of how environmental pressures are already affecting the population. Kokhreidze said the strongest evidence in Central Asia comes from sudden disasters and long-term environmental degradation, rather than official statistics identifying people as climate migrants. “For example, Kazakhstan’s 2024 floods resulted in nearly 120,000 evacuations. The Aral Sea region, particularly Karakalpakstan, also shows how environmental degradation, water scarcity, health risks, and the loss of livelihoods can contribute to outmigration,” he said. Nearly 120,000 people were displaced during massive floods in Kazakhstan in 2024. Photo credit: Kazakhstan’s Ministry of Emergency Situations Kokhreidze cautioned, however, that the crisis cannot be attributed solely to climate change, given the significant role of decades of water mismanagement and economic hardship. Looking ahead, he also identified the lower Amu Darya basin, southern Kazakhstan, water-stressed areas surrounding the Ferghana Valley and glacier-dependent communities in the Kyrgyz Republic and Tajikistan as particularly vulnerable to climate-related pressures over the next decade. “These are modelled scenarios, not precise forecasts,” he added. Similar pressures are emerging in the South Caucasus, where they range from landslides and floods in mountainous areas to drought and water scarcity in agricultural regions. In Georgia, for example, dozens of villages have been abandoned or experienced displacement because of landslides over the past four decades, according to World Bank research cited by Kokhreidze. “Mountainous and coastal areas, including Adjara, north-western Georgia, and parts of Mtskheta-Mtianeti, remain exposed to floods, landslides, mudflows, and glacier-related risks. Eastern agricultural regions, particularly Kakheti and Kvemo Kartli, are vulnerable to drought, heat, water scarcity, and land degradation,” he said. In Armenia, water stress and mounting pressures on agriculture in the Ararat Valley could cause further internal migration toward Yerevan. “IOM projections estimate between 12,000 and 52,000 internal climate migrants by 2050, although these figures represent scenarios rather than observed migration,” he said. Climate migration remains difficult to measure The scale of climate-related migration remains challenging to measure. The Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre (IDMC) recorded 29.9 million internal displacements triggered by disasters worldwide in 2025, down from a record 45.8 million in 2024, according to its Global Report on Internal Displacement 2026. Internal displacements triggered by disasters. Photo credit: IDMC The figures reflect forced movements, including repeated displacement of the same individuals, rather than the number of distinct people who have migrated. They also include disasters that cannot necessarily be attributed to climate change. When asked what policymakers should look at when determining which factors impact a decision to move, Kokhreidze suggested paying attention to a “clear chain of evidence.” “ Migration data should demonstrate that departures, evacuations, or changes in seasonal migration increased after climate-related impacts, particularly in the most exposed communities. Household surveys and personal interviews are also important because they can show whether drought, water scarcity, or extreme heat materially influenced the decision to move, even when employment and income were reported as the immediate reasons,” he explained. Kokhreidze said that while increasingly frequent or intense environmental hazards, including floods, droughts and desertification, are consistent with risks identified by climate scientists, available migration data are often insufficient to establish a direct causal link. “At the same time, the absence of sufficient data does not mean that such a relationship does not exist. At this stage, we rely on documented observations, qualitative information, and emerging datasets rather than complete long-term statistics because we are observing climate change and its consequences while they are still unfolding,” he explained. Researchers should examine environmental conditions alongside changes in livelihoods, migration statistics and personal accounts to determine whether climate pressures influenced people’s decisions to move. Equally important, he noted, is recognizing that the absence of migration does not necessarily mean communities are unaffected by climate change. The difficulty is compounded by social and economic inequalities that determine how communities experience environmental risks and whether relocation is even possible. The IOM has highlighted how poverty, social inequality and inadequate infrastructure can leave some communities disproportionately exposed to environmental hazards, with fewer resources to prepare, recover or adapt. The ability to migrate also depends on financial resources. Research discussed by Stanford University climate migration scholar Hélène Benveniste suggests that middle-income households are often more likely to move in response to climate risks than those at either end of the income spectrum. Researchers refer to the situation in which people want to leave but cannot as “involuntary immobility,” suggesting that the absence of migration does not necessarily indicate lower exposure to climate risks. Policy response Governments are increasingly acknowledging the connection between climate change and migration, but experts say that international efforts to address it remain fragmented. The 2018 Global Compact for Safe, Orderly and Regular Migration, a nonbinding United Nations agreement, calls on countries to address environmental pressures that force people to leave their homes and expand opportunities for regular migration. The Paris Agreement has also helped bring human displacement into international climate negotiations, with mechanisms established to help countries plan for climate-related migration and address the losses associated with it. The IOM’s World Migration Report 2026 warns that growing skepticism toward migration, fragmented climate policies and competing global priorities are narrowing the political space for action, even as climate-related hazards increasingly influence where people live. The report calls for a shift away from treating climate-related migration solely as a crisis, emphasizing policies that allow people to move safely while helping vulnerable communities adapt and remain where they are when possible. Local governments also have an important role to play. Cities and municipalities are often the first to confront the consequences of climate-related population movements, however, many lack the resources, detailed data and institutional support needed to respond effectively. For Central Asia, the findings raise a question. Are local authorities preparing for the demographic changes that a warming climate could bring? The post How Climate Change Could Reshape Migration Across Central Asia appeared first on The Astana Times .

title: NESG: We’re rewriting Nigeria’s story of under-performance — Tinubu
body: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu said yesterday that his administration is rewriting Nigeria’s decades-long story of economic under-performance through far-reaching reforms designed to dismantle structural barriers, unlock the nation’s enormous potential and deliver jobs, productivity and shared prosperity. He also said the administration is currently undertaking what it came into office to achieve — rewriting the story of a nation that had performed below its potential for far too long. Speaking when he formally declared open the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit Group, NESG, in Abuja yesterday, President Tinubu, who was represented by Vice President Kashim Shettima, noted that his administration began on a difficult note because there was no shortcut to economic growth. “We came to rewrite the story of a nation that has performed below its potential for far too long. But there is no shortcut to economic growth. This is why we began with a difficult reset. For us, rescuing the economy means rescuing livelihoods and transforming the fortunes of young job seekers, farmers, manufacturers, entrepreneurs and innovators. “We cannot harness the immense opportunities offered by our growing population without first stabilising the economy. We must also create the conditions for the public and private sectors to invest, expand and generate productive employment,” he explained. Tinubu observed that the summit’s theme, “Growth That Works: Delivering Jobs, Productivity and Shared Prosperity,” was built on the ambition of the previous edition of the annual event to achieve a prosperous and inclusive Nigeria by 2030. He noted that his administration had “since set in motion a series of reforms to dismantle the structural barriers that have prevented our abundant human and natural resources from yielding prosperity. “These reforms are restoring confidence, strengthening our economic foundations and laying the groundwork for sustainable growth.” The President noted that the administration was encouraged by what it had accomplished so far, acknowledging that creating jobs was only half the task. ‘Need to improve quality of work’ While noting there is need to improve the quality of work, reduce underemployment and harness the potential of the country’s under-utilised workforce, Tinubu said: “Our pursuit of prosperity demands greater productivity from every worker, enterprise and investment. We must judge infrastructure by the economic activity it generates and education by the skills and productivity it delivers. “We must judge industrial policy by the competitiveness of our firms and investment incentives by the capital, technology, exports and jobs they attract.” The President outlined what he described as the achievements of his administration’s reforms, saying they had been well-documented. He cited figures from the National Bureau of Statistics, NBS, indicating that Nigeria’s inflation-adjusted GDP grew by 3.89% in the first quarter of 2026, compared with 3.13% a year earlier. On economic diversification, he stated that “non-oil activities accounted for 96.08% of GDP, while manufacturing grew by 3.29% and the oil sector by 2.57%,” emphasising that the gains had reinforced his administration’s confidence in the path of recovery and diversification. President Tinubu stated, however, that his administration’s ambition must go beyond favourable statistics, even as the development narrative is changing and investor confidence is returning. Outlining his administration’s gains so far, the President said: “In the first quarter of 2026, our capital importation reached $10.37 billion, an increase of 83.83% over the corresponding period in 2025. “This comprised both portfolio and foreign direct investment. We will, therefore, continue to ease regulatory burdens, strengthen transparency and policy predictability and expand access to finance. “Our tax reforms seek to build a modern, equitable system that finances development and gives businesses certainty. This discipline must guide our investments in all sectors of the economy, including energy, agriculture and solid minerals. “We are reforming the electricity market to improve supply and attract investment in generation, transmission, distribution and alternative energy.” On agriculture, the President said the administration is connecting farms to storage facilities, processing centres and markets, while expanding irrigation, mechanisation, finance and rural infrastructure. He added that government is also seeking to move beyond extraction into domestic processing, industrial production and exports in the solid minerals sector. He, however, noted that despite the gains of his administration’s economic reforms, the task remains far from finished, even as young Nigerians have demonstrated their capacity to compete globally in technology, financial services and the creative industries. Consolidate, stabilise, Amina Mohammed urges govt On her part, the United Nations Deputy Secretary-General, Dr. Amina Mohammed, assessed the reforms implemented under the Tinubu administration, acknowledging the gains but urged urgent consolidation and stabilisation, as well as the effective management of expectations among citizens and other stakeholders. She also applauded the African Development Bank, AfDB, for its new financial architecture for development across the African continent, particularly its prioritisation of financing programmes that target impactful development. In his remarks, Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Dr. Taiwo Oyedele, presented the Nigerian Economic Policy Framework, which he described as a national economic doctrine that established how Nigeria made economic decisions and measured real progress. The minister invited members of the Nigerian Economic Summit Group, NESG, and private sector experts to make valuable contributions to the development of the framework by rigorously critiquing the draft proposal with facts and figures. He said the principles underpinning the framework include enterprise, open but fair markets, and whole-of-government coherence. The minister also listed key areas of focus in the proposed framework, including economic stability, human capital development and productivity, among others. Task before experts at summit — NESG chairman In his welcome address, the Chairman of the NESG, Mr. Olaniyi Yusuf, said participation at the 32nd summit reflected stakeholders’ commitment to contributing to inclusive and impactful growth, while acknowledging the Federal Government’s efforts to improve the ease of doing business in the country.
