title: TOR unveils a sweeping four-year transformation agenda
body: The Tema Oil Refinery (TOR) has announced a sweeping four-year transformation agenda to quadruple its refining footprint, diversify its asset base, and embed social infrastructure in its revival story. Mr Edmond Kombat, TOR’s Managing Director, unveiled the “Restoration and Legacy Projects” programme for 2026 to 2029 at the Government Accountability Series Press Conference at the Presidency in Accra. He described it as a blueprint that “looks further ahead” than routine maintenance and positions the national refiner for long-term strategic relevance. He reiterated that the programme’s core was a major capacity expansion. Mr Kombat disclosed that TOR proposed a brownfield expansion of the existing refinery from 45,000 barrels per stream day (bpsd) to 85,000 bpsd. In addition, TOR would develop a new greenfield refinery with a capacity of 115,000 bpsd, bringing its total processing capacity to 200,000 bpsd. “This is not merely an upgrade; it is a re-industrialisation of TOR,” Mr Kombat said. “The combination of brownfield and greenfield investments will position the refinery to meet Ghana’s growing petroleum product demand while creating opportunities for export and value addition.” Mr Kombat emphasised that the restoration agenda extended beyond industrial infrastructure. The programme includes building a Specialist Hospital with a Burns and Trauma Centre, a facility he said would ensure that “TOR’s revival leaves behind something that serves people as well as plants.” The Hospital, he said, was expected to address a critical gap in Emergency and Burns Care within the Tema industrial enclave and the wider Greater Accra Region, where industrial accidents and thermal injuries require specialised attention. To tackle accommodation challenges within the Tema enclave, the MD said TOR is working closely with the Ghana Home Ownership Fund to build a staff housing project on existing TOR land. Mr Kombat said the initiative would ease workers’ housing burden and support the broader development of the industrial city. “Our people are our greatest asset. A restored TOR must also mean a better quality of life for those who keep the plant running,” he said. The Managing Director reaffirmed TOR’s commitment to pursuing the programme with discipline, transparency, and partnership. “We will pursue these projects with the urgency and seriousness they deserve. The Restoration and Legacy Projects are about securing TOR’s future and leaving a lasting legacy for Ghana,” Mr Kombat stated.

title: Russian envoy highlights equality among members of post-Soviet security bloc
body:
MINSK, October 27. /TASS/. The Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) has established itself as a body where decisions are made based on common goals and objectives, Russian Ambassador to Belarus Boris Gryzlov said in an interview with the National Defense magazine.
"The CSTO has established itself as an organization where decisions are made based on common goals and objectives, and members are not divided into primary and secondary ones. Preserving this approach is crucial. Russia is fully interested in strengthening peace and stability in Eurasia, which is why it will continue to consistently promote the interests of collective security," he said.
According to Gryzlov, the CSTO is successfully fulfilling its tasks despite rapid changes in the global situation and in the organization's zone of responsibility, as hybrid threats are intensifying, and military and political pressure is accompanied by information, economic and other forms of attacks.
The Russian envoy noted that security issues could not be considered in isolation from the global situation, as "the excessive ambitions of Westerners have led to the collapse of the system of global security agreements."
"In contrast, the CSTO has never sought to become a bloc aimed at confrontation. This is what makes our approach fundamentally different from the North Atlantic Alliance’s behavior. NATO’s actions only increase tensions in the countries and regions where it is present in any form," Gryzlov stressed.

title: SAWA Program: Agri-Impact, PwC Ghana partner to strengthen consortium firms
body: Agri-Impact Ltd has signed a four-year agreement with PwC Ghana to strengthen the institutional capacity of consortium partners implementing the Sustainable Aquaculture for Women Advancement (SAWA) Program. Signed on October 26, 2026, at Agri-Impact’s office, the agreement builds on three years of collaboration under the Harnessing Agricultural Productivity and Prosperity for Youth (HAPPY) Program, through which PwC supported Agri-Impact’s institutional development. The partnership will help participating agribusiness firms strengthen their organisational systems, improve performance, and scale operations to create more dignified, fulfilling work opportunities for young women under the SAWA Program, a Mastercard Foundation initiative in partnership with Agri-Impact. SAWA Program seeks to unlock 60,000 dignified and fulfilling work opportunities for young women aged 18 to 35, including young women with disabilities in Ghana’s aquaculture sector. Speaking at the signing ceremony, Agri-Impact’s Chief Executive Officer, Dr. (h.c.) Daniel Fahene Acquaye, said the decision to extend institutional strengthening support to other consortium partners followed the benefits his organisation had gained from working with PwC. He said the support had enhanced Agri-Impact’s visibility and capacity to manage large-scale agricultural and agribusiness projects in Ghana and the Caribbean, unlocking more opportunities for youth. “We have seen the benefits and importance of institutional strengthening, especially for local and indigenous companies,” Dr Acquaye said. He explained that Agri-Impact had proposed to the Mastercard Foundation that it extend similar support to other private sector partners, noting that stronger businesses were better positioned to grow and create more employment opportunities for young people. “The more we strengthen the private sector, the more opportunities we create for young people,” he said. Dr Acquaye emphasised that PwC’s role would be collaborative, helping participating firms build the capacity to expand and become more competitive rather than focusing on audits. He expressed hope that the four-year engagement would produce stronger indigenous agribusiness brands with improved scale, quality, performance and resilience. For his part, PwC Ghana Partner Hayfron Aboagye said the partnership aligned with the firm’s purpose of building trust in society and helping solve important problems. He said PwC is committed to supporting indigenous agribusinesses to build on the sector’s already recorded growth. “We are excited to partner with Agri-Impact and the Mastercard Foundation for this great support. We believe that, at the end of the four-year journey, we will be seeing big brands coming out of this intervention,” Mr Aboagye said. Other members of the SAWA consortium are expected to sign their respective agreements in the coming days. About the SAWA Program The Sustainable Aquaculture for Women Advancement (SAWA) Program is a four-year Mastercard Foundation initiative, in partnership with Agri-Impact Ltd, running from 2026 to 2030. It aims to address systemic constraints in Ghana’s aquaculture sector while expanding inclusive economic opportunities across the tilapia and catfish value chains. The program seeks to create 60,000 dignified, fulfilling jobs for young women aged 18 to 35, including 3,000 young women with disabilities. Agri-Impact leads implementation with Newage Agric Solutions Ltd, AgroKings Limited, the Fisheries Commission, CEL and TechnoServe. Anchor partners Aglow, Afrigem Global, and Naple Betta, along with the Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), provide additional support. PwC serves as the program’s institutional strengthening partner.

title: Raymond completes Red Wings’ rally with SO winner
body:
EDMONTON – Lucas Raymond scored the shootout winner and had a pair of assists in regulation time as the Detroit Red Wings posted a 4-3 victory over the Edmonton Oilers on Monday.
Viktor Arvidsson, Emmitt Finnie and Dylan Larkin scored in regulation for the Red Wings (5-4-3) who went 2-1-1 on their Northwestern road trip.
Michal Postava made 25 stops and added three more in the shootout session to earn the win in Detroit’s net.
Vasily Podkolzin, Isaac Howard and Colton Dach replied for the Oilers (8-2-2), who have lost two straight as well as forward Zach Hyman to what looked to be a concussion.
Netminder Tristan Jarry made 26 saves for Edmonton.
Red Wings: Postava made his first NHL start. The 24-year-old undrafted netminder from Czechia was actually appearing in his second career game, replacing John Gibson in the third period of a 5-2 win against Vancouver last Thursday.
Oilers: Connor McDavid extended his season-starting points streak to 12 games, now with a staggering 34 points in that span. He set a new Oilers record for most points before Nov. 1, and also matched the longest season-opening assist streak in NHL history, equalling Sebastian Aho, Ken Linseman and Wayne Gretzky.
Detroit tied the game for a third time with just 1:17 remaining in the third and their goalie pulled as a bouncing puck came to Larkin in front and he shovelled in just his second of the season to send the game to extra time.
The Oilers came into the game with a fair amount of recent success against Detroit, going 6-1-2 in their last nine overall and 4-0-2 in their last six home meetings.
Red Wings: Host the Chicago Blackhawks on Thursday.
Oilers: Host the Calgary Flames on Wednesday.
This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 26, 2026.

title: Netanyahu's cousin refuses to vote for Likud, cites party's four sins in 'moral-public sphere'

elements of the democratic regime, even in the midst of the war.""Under the 'legal reform,' it sought to concentrate almost unlimited power in its hands, empty the control mechanisms of their content, and pave the way for a regime with dictatorial characteristics."He explained that, in an April 2023 speech, he "warned of the danger to the independence of the judicial system, in the spirit of the values I absorbed at home with my mother, Supreme Court Justice Shoshana Netanyahu."The Judicial Reform debates completely divided the country: "Society was torn from within, national cohesion was shattered, and senior security officials warned of the security danger," Nathan wrote.Israeli perceptions of safety, security destroyedThe October 7 massacre occurred during this government's four-year term, Nathan noted, citing it as one of the reasons he would no longer vote Likud."On October 7, the concept of containing Hamas, which the prime minister had led for years, with the aim of buying peace through funds from Qatar and economic concessions, was shattered."Not only was this idea that the prime minister was containing Hamas shattered, Nathan says, but "In reality, under the auspices of this policy, the terrorist organization grew stronger and prepared for the murderous attack."The Hamas attack was a significant failure by the current Israeli government, Nathan argued. "Some 1,200 civilians and security forces were murdered and killed in the worst disaster to hit Israel since its founding. Towns were occupied, families were massacred in their homes, civilians were burned alive, women were sexually assaulted, and 251 people were kidnapped to Gaza.""The war that broke out also exacted a terrible price of hundreds of dead and bereaved families and tens of thousands of wounded in body and mind.""Israel has since been mired in an ongoing campaign on several fronts, with no clear end in sight," he wrote. "Its international standing has declined to an abysmal low, and its propaganda has failed in the battle for global public opinion."Government didn't do enough to support its citizens, Nathan arguesNathan also accused the government of "violating the covenant between the state and its citizens."Its "continued incompetence in education, health, transportation, and the struggle over the cost of living was exposed even more clearly after the disaster [Oct. 7], when citizens and volunteers filled the governmental vacuum."Citizens supported each other; they "assisted evacuees and victims, the families of the kidnapped set up a struggle headquarters, and communities in the encirclement and the north are struggling for their rehabilitation," Nathan said, arguing that ordinary people were doing what the government should have done by default.He also addressed the Haredi (ultra-Orthodox) draft exemption under this "sin.""Reservists have repeatedly left their families and sources of livelihood, and many have paid with their bodies and lives. On the other hand, the government continues to promote exemption from service for the ultra-Orthodox and allocate huge sums to appease the ultra-Orthodox parties, for reasons of coalition survival, while grossly trampling on the principle of equality of burden."Refusal to bear responsibilityNathan also focuses on another key issue for voters in the Israeli election: whether or not a state commission of inquiry into October 7 should be established."With our Prime Minister, the responsibility always lies with someone else," he argued. "The most serious expression of this is the refusal to establish a national commission of inquiry.""Why, despite widespread public support, was such a committee not established more than three years after the massacre? Is it possible that the greatest national disaster of all does not require the establishment of a state investigation committee? Government responsibility is not conditional on criminal guilt, but it does require accountability to the public," he argued."I will not vote for Likud under its current leadership, and I have even announced the immediate termination of my membership in the movement. I will consider renewing it when a leadership that is not tainted by these shortcomings is elected."Referencing a quote from the prophet Amos, Nathan concluded his letter by saying, "For three crimes of the Israeli government — and for four I will not choose them!"

title: Tarkwa Nsuaem NDC Elections: Incumbent Chairman, Secretary lose seats
body: John Justice Abban, the 2020 Parliament Candidate for the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in the Tarkwa Nsuaem Constituency, has defeated Mr Danladi Salifu, the party’s incumbent constituency chairman, at the party’s constituency executives’ election held at the weekend. Mr Abban, who is popularly known as ‘DJ ’, polled 1,008 votes to defeat Mr Salifu, who had 857 votes. Mr. Stephen Ayombisa, the incumbent secretary, also failed to retain his seat; he had 481 votes, while Mr Joseph Baker obtained 589 votes. Mr. George Enimil, however, secured 784 votes for the secretary position he held years back before Mr Ayombisa defeated him for it. Mr Kwasi Adam won the deputy secretary position with 972 votes, against 879 votes for Mr. Eric Gyimah. Madam Diana Awuah, who garnered 202 votes, defeated Madam Gifty Efua Nyinaku, who had 44 votes for the woman’s organiser position. For deputy woman organiser, Madam Emilia Eshun was elected with 145 votes, and Madam Jamilatu Fuseni lost with 103 votes. For the position of Organiser, Mr Nuhu Yahaya polled 934 votes for the seat, and Nana Oheneba Boakye had 924 votes; for the position of Deputy Organiser, Ali Salifu had 843 votes, Daniel Yakubu 525 votes, Frank Mensah 435 votes, and Emmanuel Adu Amoah 43 votes. The Treasurer position went to Madam Fayadatu Yakubu, who polled 937 votes against that of Mr Anthony Kojo Otoo, who had 916 votes. Madam Patience Nzeh took the position of Deputy Treasurer with 847 votes, Mr Emmanuel Kofi Musah with 816, and Mr Mohammed Abdullah with 386. Mr Ibrahim Diallo won the position of Youth Organiser with 110 votes, followed by Mr Richard Nsoh with 106 votes, while Deputy Youth Organiser went to Mr Justice Abban with 111 votes, followed by Madam Emilia Anafo with 106 votes. Mr Francise Benevolent Abban became the next Communication Officer, with 976 votes, followed by Mr. William Appiah with 883 votes. The Deputy Communication Officer position was taken by Mr. Isaac Atinoto with 968 votes, followed by Mr. Bismark Asante with 898 votes. The Youth representative, Mr Tamimu Salifu, whose contender was Mr Emmanuel Arthur. Mr. Hafiz Alasco, the Western Regional Zongo Caucus Coordinator, swore all the elected executives into office after the Electoral Commission officer certified the results. The newly elected Chairman, Mr Abban, expressed gratitude to the delegates for the confidence reposed in him and pledged to lead with fairness, strengthen the party structure at all levels, and work tirelessly to ensure victory for the NDC in the next elections. A total of 1,858 delegates participated in the exercise, which was peaceful.

title: No violating vessel safe in Strait of Hormuz
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 27 (MNA) – Iran's armed forces chief said the Strait of Hormuz is completely closed and no violating vessel will be safe, with IRGC and Army forces exercising full control over the Persian Gulf and Sea of Oman.
Iran's Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces said the Strait of Hormuz is completely closed and that no violating vessel will be safe, rejecting US claims that the strategic waterway is open and free.
Major General Abdollahi said the Islamic Revolution Guard Corps' naval and ground forces have full control and surveillance over the coasts of the Persian Gulf, its islands and the Strait of Hormuz, and that any movement in the area is under strict monitoring. He said the waterway is managed by the powerful Islamic Revolution Guard Corps Navy.
During a visit to the coasts of the Sea of Oman, Abdollahi said the Army's naval and ground forces, with high readiness and morale, have full control and surveillance over the free waters of the Sea of Oman and its coasts. They are monitoring all enemy movements in the region and will not allow violating vessels to transit, he said.
The visits were attended by commanders of the Islamic Revolution Guard Corps Navy and the Army Navy.
He warned that any violating vessel that seeks to transit outside the designated route and Iranian arrangements for any reason will have its security endangered and will suffer serious damage.
Abdollahi said the armed forces in the Persian Gulf region, the islands, the Strait of Hormuz and the coasts of the Sea of Oman are more ready than before, with new and more advanced equipment, and are present in the region with power and authority. They will confront any evil and aggression by the enemy more severely than before, he said.

title: North- East Region turns to solar-powered water system to tackle climate change
body: The North-East Regional Coordinating Council is promoting solar-powered water systems and dry-season farming to help communities adapt to climate change as rivers dry up and traditional irrigation sources become increasingly unreliable. The initiative aims to improve households’ and public institutions’ access to water while supporting year-round farming through solar-powered groundwater extraction. Mr Ibrahim Tia, the North-East Regional Minister, told the Ghana News Agency that climate change was increasingly affecting water availability and making farming along river bodies less sustainable, requiring communities to explore alternative water sources. “We cannot rely on our river bodies. Climate change is fast catching up with us, and the only way is to explore other opportunities available for our activities,” he said. He said the Council was working with district assemblies and development partners to extend access to water to communities, schools and other public facilities. The Minister said solar-powered water systems offer a more sustainable option because they use sunlight, a readily available resource, to pump groundwater without the recurring fuel costs of conventional pumping systems. Mr Tia said communities would mainly be responsible for the relatively low maintenance costs of the systems. The Minister said the Council was also pursuing plans to expand dry-season farming by drilling boreholes on suitable farmlands and equipping them with solar-powered pumping systems to support irrigation throughout the year. He said the approach would reduce farmers’ dependence on rivers, which were increasingly drying up, and allow them to cultivate fertile lands that could otherwise remain underused during the dry season. The initiative is expected to create additional opportunities for farmers to increase production and improve their incomes while strengthening the region’s capacity to cope with changing rainfall patterns. Mr Tia noted preparatory work was underway to establish facilities in each district to support the programme, with some infrastructure expected to be completed by the end of November. The initiative forms part of broader efforts to strengthen local resilience to climate change through investments in water infrastructure, renewable energy and climate-smart agriculture. The region relies heavily on rain-fed subsistence farming and is experiencing shorter rainy seasons, delayed rains, and dry spells that lead to lower crop yields, massive crop failures, and significant post-harvest losses. It is also witnessing prolonged dry seasons and rising temperatures that dry up water bodies, lower water tables, and degrade topsoil. Seasonal hunger peaks sharply during lean periods (such as May–June) because households cannot store or produce enough food year-round. Declining farm incomes narrow economic options, pushing young people to migrate south and increasing competition for scarce natural resources—which can fuel local farmer-herder tensions.

title: Zelensky enacts NSDC decision on national security strategy
body:
The corresponding decree No. 1066/2026 has been published on the President’s website, according to Ukrinform.
According to this resolution, the Secretary of the National Security and Defense Council is tasked, in particular, with organizing the work to update the National Security Strategy, which was approved by Presidential Decree No. 392/2020 of September 14, 2020, “On the Resolution of the National Security and Defense Council of Ukraine of September 14, 2020, ‘On the National Security Strategy of Ukraine’” (as amended by Presidential Decree No. 16/2025 of January 6, 2025).
In addition, the NSDC Secretariat, in cooperation with the National Institute for Strategic Studies and with the involvement of relevant government agencies, civil society institutions, and foreign experts, must prepare proposals within three months regarding amendments to the Strategy for consideration by the National Security and Defense Council.
The Secretary of the National Security and Defense Council is responsible for overseeing the implementation of this decision.
The decree takes effect on the date of its publication.
As reported by Ukrinform, on October 25, Zelensky announced a security meeting in Brussels , during which initiatives to end the war will be discussed. Representatives from the United States, Ukraine, the European Union, and NATO will participate.

title: Ellembelle NDC Chairman-elect poised to unite members ahead of 2028 victory
body: Shaibu Dauda Abdulai, the Ellembelle National Democratic Congress (NDC) Constituency Chairman-elect, has pledged to unite and reconcile party faithful to retain power in December 2028. He made his intentions and vision clear in a statement after his victory in last Saturday’s Ellembelle NDC Constituency election at Ampain in the Western Region. “Comrades, the campaign is over. The election is over. Now is the time to heal wounds, reconcile and bring everybody on board,” the statement said. Mr Abdulai, popularly called Vanda, expressed special appreciation to Mr Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, the Member of Parliament for Ellembelle; Mr Joseph Armah Agyekum, the District Chief Executive for the area; delegates and all members at the 160 branches for the peace, transparency and fairness which characterised the polls. He noted that this was ample testimony that internal democracy had been entrenched in the NDC as a party and, by extension, as the government. Mr Abdulai, who is the Personal Assistant to the Member of Parliament, Mr Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, acknowledged the efforts of delegates who “stood in long queues, sacrificed your time, resources and voted for hope, unity and progress”. He said, “I do not take this mandate for granted. I promise to lead with respect and dignity for every branch.” Outlining his vision for the party, the Ellembelle NDC Chairman-elect pledged to serve as Chairman for all and to run an open-door, all-inclusive administration. Mr Abdulai promised, “to work in total loyalty and support for the MP, DCE and all stakeholders to make the Ellembelle NDC more attractive, united and strong and work hard to retain the Ellembelle seat and increase votes come 2028.”

title: Kiev mayor reports damage to South Bridge across Dnieper River
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. The South Bridge across the Dnieper River in Kiev was damaged in overnight explosions, Mayor Vitaly Klitschko wrote on Telegram.
According to him, subway infrastructure was also damaged as one of the subway lines runs across the bridge.
The city administration said on Telegram that traffic on the South Bridge had been restricted and subway services had been suspended.
Damage to bridges in Kiev has been reported repeatedly since early October.
The South Bridge carries significant volumes of cargo between Ukrainian regions. According to Ukraine’s Strana media outlet, the bridge is also important for military deliveries.

title: Regional states should take responsibility for their own security: Sayyid Badr
body:
Sayyid Badr bin Hamad al Busaidi, Foreign Minister, affirmed that the Sultanate of Oman continues its diplomatic efforts to enhance security and stability in the Gulf region. This is pursued by facilitating dialogue between parties, working towards the resolution of conflicts, building trust, and advocating for the establishment of a comprehensive regional security framework that includes all states bordering the Gulf. This came during a lecture delivered on Monday by Sayyid Badr at the University of Cambridge in the United Kingdom, titled 'Comprehensive Security in the Gulf,' which was attended by diplomats, experts, and academics specialising in foreign policy. The minister said that the Sultanate of Oman — which maintains peaceful relations with all its neighbours — bases its policy on the recognition that its own security is contingent upon the security of its regional environment. This understanding drives Oman to persist in its outreach to countries in the region, aiming to settle disputes, preserve peace, and expand its reach. Sayyid Badr also highlighted Oman’s role in facilitating negotiations between the United States and Iran over the past two years, which sought to reach a settlement regarding Iran’s nuclear file and end decades of hostility between the two nations. He noted that, in Oman’s view, the negotiations had achieved significant progress and that reaching an agreement had been within the grasp of both parties. He highlighted the efforts made by the Sultanate of Oman — through high-level talks and technical consultations with Iran — to establish interim arrangements aimed at ensuring freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz. He emphasised that the implementation of such arrangements requires a practical understanding between Iran and the United States, as well as a willingness from both sides to make concessions. He further said that recent negotiating experiences underscore the importance of regional states taking responsibility for their own security, rather than relying excessively on external powers. He called for the initiation of a new regional dialogue — involving the six Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states, Iraq, and Iran — to build a security framework rooted in cooperation and mutual trust. Sayyid Badr pointed to an initiative that took place in Muscat in 1976, when the foreign ministers of the eight states bordering the Gulf met to discuss collective security arrangements. He suggested that reviving the ambition behind that initiative offers an opportunity to launch a more inclusive regional process to address current challenges. The minister affirmed that the Sultanate of Oman advocates for a non-aggression pact among these eight states as a fundamental step towards establishing sustainable regional security. He stressed that external partnerships should evolve into major economic investments within these eight nations, serving a supportive role while prioritising the collective responsibility of the regional states themselves to design, develop, and implement their own security arrangements.

title: Ghana explores AI to predict Ebola and other health threats — GHS
body: The Ghana Health Service (GHS) is exploring the use of artificial intelligence (AI) to help anticipate disease outbreaks and strengthen emergency planning as the country steps up preparations against the threat of Ebola. The Director-General of the GHS, Dr Samuel Kaba Akoriyea, said health officials were considering how emerging technologies could improve the assessment of public health risks and support timely decisions when infectious diseases threaten to cross national borders. He said the discussions formed part of broader preparedness efforts following reports of Ebola outbreaks in parts of Africa and concerns about the potential spread of the disease through international travel. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Monday, October 26, Dr Kaba Akoriyea said the proposed use of AI was intended to help authorities better anticipate developments and plan their response. “From there, I move into a meeting where we are talking about technology and how to even use AI to help predict what will happen,” he revealed. Technology to support early warning The exploration of AI comes as public health authorities face the challenge of identifying infectious disease threats in a world where people travel frequently between countries and outbreaks can have implications beyond the communities in which they begin. Predictive technologies can help analyse information such as disease trends, population movement and environmental conditions to identify emerging risks and guide decisions on where surveillance and resources may be needed. For Ghana, such tools could potentially complement existing disease monitoring systems by helping officials identify areas requiring closer attention and plan interventions before a health emergency escalates. However, the effectiveness of AI-based systems would depend on the availability of reliable and timely data, appropriate technical expertise and the capacity of health authorities to act on the information generated. The technology would not replace laboratory diagnosis, clinical assessment or established outbreak response measures. Rather, it could serve as an additional tool to support decisions by public health officials. Ghana remains in preparedness phase Dr Kaba Akoriyea stressed that Ghana was preparing for a possible Ebola threat, rather than announcing the detection of an outbreak in the country. “But now, let me say that when it comes to Ebola, we are in the face of preparedness,” he noted. The GHS has reported conducting simulation exercises and coordinating with other state institutions as part of efforts to strengthen the country’s response arrangements. The Director-General has also described the work of the Public Health Emergency Operations Centre at Pantang, which monitors international health developments and supports emergency coordination. The preparedness effort involves multiple agencies, including those responsible for health, security, education and disaster management, reflecting the need for a coordinated response if a suspected case is identified. Ghana’s regional engagements are also important because of the movement of people across borders and the need for countries to share information about emerging health risks. Surveillance remains critical Ebola is a severe viral disease that can cause serious illness and death. It spreads through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person who is symptomatic or with contaminated materials. Symptoms may develop between two and 21 days after exposure. Consequently, a person who has been infected may not appear ill when travelling, making surveillance, accurate traveller information and appropriate follow-up important elements of outbreak preparedness. Public health responses typically involve the rapid identification and assessment of suspected cases, laboratory testing, isolation and clinical care where indicated, contact tracing, infection prevention and control, and public education.

title: Refining Ghanaian crude in Ghana keeps value onshore – TOR MD
body: Edmond Kombat, Managing Director (MD) of the Tema Oil Refinery (TOR), underscored the strategic importance of refining Ghanaian crude oil domestically, calling it a critical step toward retaining value in the national economy and fulfilling the President’s value-addition vision. “Refining Ghanaian crude in Ghana keeps value onshore. It fulfils the value addition vision of the President for Ghana,” Mr Kombat said in his remarks at the Government Accountability Press Conference, at the Jubilee House in Accra. He said the turnaround maintenance ran from August 1 to October 30, 2025, adding that after the maintenance works were completed, the National Petroleum Authority (NPA) inspected the plant, confirmed compliance with mandatory safety and operational requirements, and cleared TOR to resume refining. He said crude processing started on December 19, 2025, with all product streams going to storage for the first time in years. Mr Kombat said since May 2026, TOR has received four five-million-barrel crude cargoes: Bonga, Baleine, Bonnie Light, and, on July 15, Ghana’s Jubilee Medium Sweet crude, an indigenous crude delivered aboard MT Apache. He said the TOR paid in full for the Jubilee cargo, making it the refinery’s first Jubilee cargo in a decade. The MD said the President commissioned the refurbished Crude Distillation Unit on August 1, 2026. Mr Kombat said the refinery then received another parcel of Ghanaian indigenous crude, 950,000 barrels of Sankofa crude, on 25 September 2026 from our sister agency, the Ghana National Petroleum Company (GNPC). He noted that the refinery’s operations now represent a landmark achievement in the country’s petroleum sector. “We are witnessing Ghanaian crude being refined by Ghanaian engineers in a Ghanaian refinery, effectively linking the Ghanaian petroleum upstream, midstream and downstream together,” he said. The MD highlighted the role of strategic offtake partnerships in strengthening the domestic refining ecosystem. “Our offtake partnerships, including our engagement with GOIL on the 2026 arrangement, were intended to increase the supply of locally refined products, improve security of supply, and support greater price stability at the pump,” he explained. He further disclosed that, but for the restoration of TOR and other government-supported domestic production, fuel prices in the last two pricing windows could have sold between GHS22 and GHS32 per litre. Mr Kombat said the revamp of TOR guaranteed Ghana and its Sahelian Neighbours Fuel Security and Availability. He said TOR’s close working relationship with the National Petroleum Authority, Bulk Oil Storage and Transportation Company Limited (BOST), and other Petroleum Service providers has increased Burkina Faso’s National Oil Company’s petroleum product movement through Ghana from 15 per cent in 2024 to 40 per cent as at today. On expansion and work ahead, Mr Kombat said engineers from Verga Engineering are working with TOR’s technical team to complete the tie-in and commission the F-61 this month. This, he said, would allow the Crude Distillation Unit to move from its current throughput of about 28,000 bpd to its nameplate capacity of 45,000 bpd to 55,000 bpd. In the medium term, they plan to install a new air cooler to raise capacity to 60,000 bpd and replace the 6,500 barrel-a-day catalytic reformers with a 10,000 barrel-per-day continuous catalytic reformer. He noted that the new 120-ton boiler had been installed, while work on the RFCC turnaround and SCADA system continues. Mr Kombat said on August 1, the President directed the Minister of Energy and Green Transition to work with the TOR Board and Management on a strategic roadmap to raise processing capacity to 100,000 barrels a day, with a further plan to increase it to 200,000 barrels per day as the end state. He also announced plans to restructure TOR so that it could operate on sound commercial principles, without political interference.

title: Drone attack on passenger bus in Zaporozhye Region kills one person — governor
body:
MELITOPOL, October 27. /TASS/. A Ukrainian drone struck a bus traveling from Simferopol to Moscow in the Zaporozhye Region, killing one person, Governor Yevgeny Balitsky said.
"The enemy carried out a cynical attack on a passenger bus traveling from Simferopol to Moscow. There were 31 people on board, and one person was killed. The attack took place near the town of Primorsk. All those injured have been taken to the hospital. The passengers who did not require hospitalization were provided with accommodation and meals. I remain in contact with emergency services," he wrote on the Max social media platform.

title: Your past prescriptions haven’t helped developing countries – TOR MD tells IMF
body: Edmond Kombat, the Managing Director of the Tema Oil Refinery Limited (TOR), has challenged the International Monetary Fund (IMF) over its long-standing prescriptions for state-owned enterprises. He noted that the Fund appears to be revising its literature because its past advice “hasn’t helped” developing countries. Mr Kombat responded to a question about the reason for the recent visit by an IMF delegation to the state-owned Oil Refinery at the Government Accountability Series Press Conference held at the Presidency in Accra. Mr Kombat said the Fund had written extensively about Ghana’s energy sector, including TOR. He traced the country’s history with IMF-backed programmes—from the Economic Recovery Programme to the Financial Sector Recovery Programme and the Divestiture of State Enterprises—and observed that the Fund had traditionally promoted private business and “usually they don’t like state entities running businesses.” “But it looks like they are changing their literature, because most of those prescriptions that they give actually haven’t helped the developing countries,” he said. He said in Ghana, state-owned enterprises were beginning to show that state institutions could work and work very well. “And we were happy to receive them and show them that under His Excellency President John Dramani Mahama, state entities are working, and are working profitably, and are not the loss-making entities,” Mr Kombat added. He noted that the IMF delegation seemed impressed, reiterating that “but we also remain guarded.”

title: Keeping Critical Data in Canada: How ThinkOn and AVSS Are Building a Sovereign Platform for Public Safety and Defence
body:
Council of Canadian Innovators | Conseil canadien des innovateurs (CCI)
ThinkOn and AVSS have built a Canadian-hosted platform that keeps sensitive public safety and defence information under Canadian control.
A drone flying above an emergency can show responders what crews on the ground cannot. It can identify a blocked road, track changing conditions or give a command team a clearer picture of where help is needed.
That information is only useful if it reaches the right people quickly. For police and defence organizations, where the resulting video and location data are stored also matters.
Toronto-based cloud provider ThinkOn and Canadian aerospace technology company Aerial Vehicle Safety Solutions Inc. (AVSS) have partnered to address both challenges.
The companies have integrated their technologies to provide a Canadian-hosted way to use the Team Awareness Kit (TAK), a platform that brings operational information together in a shared digital view. Live video and drone telemetry, including location and flight information, can be sent directly into TAK and viewed by personnel using connected devices in the field.
For responders, the experience remains familiar. The difference is behind the screen.
Instead of operating on infrastructure controlled by a foreign cloud provider, the TAK server runs on ThinkOn’s Canadian platform. The drone data feeding the system remains hosted in Canada under Canadian ownership and control.
“Agencies have never had to choose between best-in-class technology and knowing exactly where their data lives. They just haven’t had a sovereign option for TAK until now,” said Craig McLellan , Chief Executive Officer of ThinkOn .
Large foreign cloud platforms have become the default environment for many TAK deployments. Agencies are often left to design and maintain the systems surrounding the platform, while sensitive information may be stored on infrastructure outside Canadian jurisdiction.
Agencies already using TAK through a foreign provider can move to a Canadian environment without retraining personnel or changing their daily work. Those deploying TAK for the first time can begin with a Canadian-hosted system.
ThinkOn has spent more than a decade helping organizations manage and protect their data. AVSS, founded in 2017, designs and manufactures drone components and safety systems in Canada. Its products include parachute recovery systems, payload delivery equipment, ground control stations, motors and electronics. They are now used in more than 35 countries.
Together, the companies have connected Canadian-built drone technology with Canadian-controlled digital infrastructure.
The partnership also reflects a broader question facing governments as technology becomes more central to public safety and national defence. It is not enough to consider what a system can do. Decision-makers must also consider who owns the infrastructure and where the resulting data are stored.
“Drones only make a difference in an emergency if the right people can see what the drone sees, the moment it matters,” said Josh Ogden , Chief Executive Officer of AVSS . “This partnership with ThinkOn closes that gap on a platform Canadian agencies can trust completely.”
In the field, the change may be difficult to spot. Responders will still receive the same information on the same screens. Behind them, however, the images, locations and operational details will be impervious to foreign interference and remain in Canada.
This article is part of CCI’s “By Canadian Innovators” series, which showcases how members of the Council of Canadian Innovators work with homegrown companies to fuel their growth and make Canada more prosperous. Each story in this series highlights the unique contributions of these companies to building a more prosperous, innovation-driven economy. To learn more about the companies CCI works with to build a more prosperous Canada, visit our member directory.

title: IWI’s Arbel Anti-Drone System Deployed in Thailand
body:
KIRYAT GAT – IWI (Israel Weapon Industries), an SK Group company and global leader in small arms manufacturing, has delivered its ARBEL Anti-Drone System (ADS) to Thailand’s Ministry of Defence. Following integration into its existing rifles and on-site training by IWI, the ARBEL ADS has been deployed and is now operational for day and night use.
The ARBEL ADS is a computerized fire control system designed to dramatically improve hit probability and lethality. When the shooter pulls the trigger, the first round is discharged mechanically, as in any standard rifle. While the trigger remains pulled, the system controls the fire cadence at an optimal rate. This eliminates the need for complex trigger work, one of the most challenging aspects of marksmanship in dynamic scenarios, allowing the shooter to focus on target tracking and aiming. In drone interception scenarios, where targets are small, fast-moving, and maneuver unpredictably at a distance, ARBEL ADS automates follow-up shots to enable accurate, repeatable engagements, even in high-pressure environments. The system gives soldiers effective standoff capabilities across a wide range of operational settings.
Unlike other counter-drone solutions that require specialized platforms or sensors, ARBEL ADS integrates directly into the soldier’s existing weapon without the need for external equipment or retraining. Its plug-and-play design lets soldiers use familiar weapons with standard 5.56 ammunition without having to learn a new platform. Optics-agnostic and compatible with a wide range of sighting systems, from red dots and LPVOs to thermal and night vision devices, ARBEL ADS adapts to the shooter’s preferred setup.
“Small tactical drones have become a direct and growing threat to soldiers on the battlefield. We developed the ARBEL ADS to give soldiers an effective means of defending themselves against this evolving threat, while providing armed forces with a critical tactical advantage in an increasingly complex battlespace,” said SK Group’s Vice Chairman Ronen Hamudot.
IWI offers two procurement options for the ARBEL ADS: either as part of a complete IWI-manufactured rifle or installed in a customer’s existing weapon. Thailand’s Ministry of Defence selected the latter, with IWI completing the integration in Thailand by replacing the rifle’s lower receiver with the ARBEL ADS. This approach enables militaries to upgrade their existing platforms locally without replacing their rifle inventories or procuring entirely new weapons.
Thailand military officials are in discussions with IWI about an additional order for its ARBEL Anti-Drone Systems.
Across Southeast Asia, several countries are at various stages of the procurement process, with additional deployments expected in the coming months.
“As Southeast Asian militaries place greater emphasis on counter-drone capabilities, Thailand’s adoption of ARBEL ADS reflects this growing operational priority. We see rising demand across the region for solutions that can help soldiers meet this challenge,” said SK Group Vice President Doron Korol, who oversees the APAC region.
IWI (Israel Weapon Industries), part of the SK Group, is the main supplier to the Israeli Army and Israeli Police, with combat-proven products used by military, law enforcement and special forces in over 60 countries across diverse operational environments. Renowned for developing the iconic UZI, IWI continues to set benchmarks in firearm innovation and reliability, developing advanced systems like the ARAD, the NEGEV light machine gun, and the TAVOR. For more information, visit: https://iwi.net .
SK Group, founded by noted Israeli industrialist Samy Katsav, is a leading holding company known for driving innovation across multiple strategic industries. Its portfolio comprises globally recognized companies, such as IWI (Israel Weapon Industries), Meprolight, Camero-Tech, ELVO, Israel Shipyards, Israel Shipyards Port, Uni-Scope Optical Solutions and Oshira. Collectively, these companies employ over 2,000 people, unified by a commitment to innovation and operational excellence. SK Group’s companies serve military, law enforcement and civilian markets in over 60 countries. For more information, visit: https://sk-g.net/ .

title: Ghana activates Ebola preparedness system, conducts simulation exercises — GHS
body: The Ghana Health Service (GHS) says it has activated its preparedness arrangements for Ebola and conducted simulation exercises as part of efforts to strengthen the country’s ability to respond to a possible outbreak. The Director-General of the GHS, Dr Samuel Kaba Akoriyea, said the institution was monitoring developments across affected countries and coordinating with relevant institutions to assess potential risks to Ghana. He said the country had intensified surveillance and emergency planning following reports of Ebola outbreaks in parts of Africa, including the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Uganda, as well as concerns about possible cross-border transmission. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Monday, October 26, Dr Kaba Akoriyea said Ghana was in the preparedness phase and had begun testing its response arrangements through simulation exercises. “So here you are, you have an outbreak in Congo, Uganda, and then you see it coming to Kenya, and we have airlines that come indirectly, day in, day out. Then from there, you see it get to Nigeria. And as I talk to you, I’m always in touch with my colleagues in those countries to know exactly what is happening,” he explained. Emergency operations centre on alert Dr Kaba Akoriyea said the GHS was using its Public Health Emergency Operations Centre at Pantang to monitor international health developments and coordinate preparedness activities. He said the centre operated around the clock, allowing health officials to track emerging threats and respond to developments that could have implications for Ghana. “We’ve put it out there all the time. Every second, microsecond of the day, we scan, and we know exactly what is happening in any part of the world. It’s there,” he sated. “You can go and see. We don’t sleep, work 24 hours, and we see whatever is happening.” The Director-General said the Service had carried out about three simulation exercises since concerns about the disease emerged in the region, adding that preparedness activities had begun earlier when the outbreak in the DRC was reported. “Yesterday, I’ll tell you, we’ve already done about three simulation exercises since we heard of the issue in Kenya. “When it started in DRC, we activated our system. In Congo, in Kenya, we started with simulation exercise.” Simulation exercises are used to test how institutions would coordinate their response to a public health emergency, including the identification and management of suspected cases, communication between agencies and the mobilisation of resources. 33 agencies involved in preparedness Dr Kaba Akoriyea said Ghana’s preparations involved a broad range of institutions beyond the health sector, reflecting the need for a coordinated response if an outbreak occurred. He said he had attended meetings involving agencies responsible for education, security, social welfare, local government and emergency management. “And today, alone, I have gone to meetings where we have cross-border issues. “And I can provide you with the list, and you can cross-check. You have education, you have military, you have police, you have welfare, you have local government, you have all the necessary agencies, present including NADMO, you have them all, about 33 agencies.” He named the Food and Drugs Authority, the National Disaster Management Organisation (NADMO), the National Commission for Civic Education, the Ghana Education Service, the Veterinary Services Department, the National Peace Council and the Ghana Armed Forces among the institutions involved. The involvement of multiple agencies is intended to support coordination in areas such as emergency response, public communication, security, logistics and the management of people who may be affected by a health emergency. Cross-border cooperation The GHS Director-General said Ghana was also working with neighbouring countries to strengthen cooperation on infectious diseases and other health threats that could move across borders. He cited recent engagements with counterparts in Burkina Faso and Côte d’Ivoire, as well as a tripartite meeting to compare developments and discuss possible responses. He said the meetings were particularly important because of the movement of people across borders and the need for countries to share information promptly. “So we’ve held a cross-border meeting with our counterparts in Burkina, we’ve had one with our counterparts in Côte d’Ivoire, Ivory Coast, and we’ve had a tripartite meeting to know what is happening there and what is happening here. How do we compare those and solve these issues?”

title: Apple to replace iPhone Duos with damaged screens but does not explain fault
body: iPhone Duo users with cracked and pixelated screens will get replacements, Apple said on Monday night, after a storm of negative publicity dubbed "crackgate". The tech giant is yet to say what has caused an issue that threatened to mar the most expensive phone in its line-up. “We are aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units,” the US technology company's representative told The National in a statement, without disclosing what was causing the issue. “If users experience issues with their iPhone Duo display, they should contact AppleCare for a replacement," Apple said. The company representative further said that the response to iPhone Duo from early users has been "incredibly positive". "We are seeing exciting things from developers who are rapidly updating their apps to take advantage of its unique form factor." Apple’s response comes days after customers complained of damaged screens on its newly launched iPhone Duo, with some early buyers reporting cracks and display failures only hours after using the device. Images shared on Reddit appear to show damage concentrated around the hinge of the device’s inner display, with vertical cracks running down the centre and bright lines extending across the right side of the screen. Some affected devices also reportedly had dead pixels, raising concerns about the durability of the foldable display, which is one of the Duo’s biggest selling points. Apple began shipping the phone last week amid strong demand, with initial online orders selling out within minutes and customers queuing at shops worldwide. But reports of damaged screens began to emerge at the weekend, with social media users sharing images of cracks and bright lines appearing on the device's inner display, particularly where the phone folds. The complaints added to the challenges Apple faces as it enters a foldable smartphone market already occupied by Samsung and Google, both of which have several years' experience developing devices with flexible displays. The Duo's prices in the UAE range from Dh8,499 to Dh13,599 ($2,314 to $3,702), and there are extended shipping times due to overwhelming demand.

title: Is Europe starting to come to its senses on Ukraine?
body:
Finland and Norway are hinting at the need for a new approach to the continent's relationship with Russia
The Trump administration’s latest initiative to end the Ukraine war is creating heartburn in Europe .
“We have to pressure the aggressor to stop the war, not the victim to surrender,” said European Union High Representative Kaja Kallas. “Squeezing Ukraine is not the right approach, and that's why Europe is standing by Ukraine.” Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, meanwhile, insists Russia has no genuine desire for peace, pointing in particular to Russian strikes on Ukrainian civilians.
This moral language frames the conflict as a zero-sum, good-versus-evil struggle. In this light, Europeans have no choice but to unite behind Ukraine to stop Russian President Vladimir Putin.
But not all European leaders are talking this way. The press conference in Oslo on Oct. 20 featuring Zelenskyy, Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre and Finnish President Alexander Stubb was full of constructive language about ending the conflict. Stubb said the Oslo summit was the result of "substantive progress" made "under the radar." Støre emphasised that "Europe has to be at the table" to secure a "lasting peace." Europe, it seems, is not united on a negotiated end to the conflict.
Then on Tuesday, the two held a call with Putin unofficially, in an effort at de-escalation, according to reports . "We are neighboring countries to Russia," Stubb said in a statement afterwards. "The outcome of this war will have a direct impact on our and the broader European security. Ending the war requires direct discussions.”
The Oslo summit was no bolt from the blue; Finnish and Norwegian representatives have been preparing the ground for several months. At last week’s Warsaw Security Forum, Norwegian Foreign Minister Espen Barth Eide avoided the usual binary of Ukraine’s victory or capitulation. He stressed that since the Europeans are now paying for the war, they should also lead the diplomacy to end it. Eide noted that a peace agreement could secure a democratic, independent Ukraine integrated into the EU with 80% of its original territory. Advancing this point among more hawkish European colleagues, Eide struck a tone of hope rather than fear. In an interview last Saturday, Eide noted that Europe must contribute concrete proposals for a post-war security architecture: "in the long run, we need to return to a normal relationship with Russia after the war (....) some kind of order must be restored.”
During his recent visit to the Norwegian Institute of International Affairs, Stubb presented a complementary argument. Restating his case for a “value-based realism,” he argued that European states should be faithful to their values but would not resolve the conflict by rigidly clinging to the moral high ground. Stubb urged the audience to keep “cooler heads”; fostering a “war mentality” would make it near impossible to conceive of peace.
Eide and Stubb are moving in a different direction from those who claim “victory” over Russia – however defined – is a prerequisite for future European security. They reject the mantra of ex-NATO Secretary General Stoltenberg that “ weapons are the way to peace ” and emphasize the military reality that neither side has the resources to win decisively.
This is a noble recognition of reality. Offensive actions from both sides have repeatedly failed to produce a breakthrough. Costs keep rising for both warring parties, while gains have become increasingly meager. Europe, Ukraine, and Russia are stuck in a war that cannot be won on the terms set by either side.
Continuing the current course brings problems for all sides. Putin faces an overheating economy and increasing social fatigue and anxiety. Even if Russia destroys more and more Ukrainian infrastructure from the air, land offensives are likely to incur heavy losses. Ukraine's situation is even tougher. Its chronic manpower shortages have led to intensified forced mobilization and increased social strains. Blockaded at sea and bombarded from the air, Ukraine is also short of money and weapons, constantly appealing to Western allies to plug the gaps.
The European coalition behind Ukraine faces serious problems of its own. Many European states are facing a sovereign debt crisis as war costs mount. The EU has been unable to persuade Belgium to make use of Russia’s frozen assets to fund the war. All the while, the dirty reality is that, since the war began, Europe has spent more on Russian energy imports than on weapons for Ukraine.
At the same time, Ukraine’s campaign of intensified deep strikes on Russia – supported by the Europeans and greenlit by the Trump Administration in spring 2026 – has failed to pressure Putin into a ceasefire. Without U.S. intelligence and weapons supplies, Europe lacks the military leverage to continue this effort on its own. There is no viable European war plan , only reactive crisis management and ad hoc solutions about Ukraine, coupled with repeated hyping of Russia’s “hybrid war” threat.
Tuesday’s meeting in Oslo provides a way out of this mess. As Stubb said at Tuesday’s press conference : “Peace requires patience. But unfortunately, war does not wait. People are dying each and every day. Our job is to do what we can to end it.” Norway and Finland are communicating the urgency of ending a senseless war. Referring to the recent spat between Trump and Zelensky, Støre advised against dwelling on past disagreements: “What matters now is what lies ahead of us.”
On the same day, Kaja Kallas looked back in anger. She accused the Trump administration of trying to “push Ukraine into surrender” on “Putin’s terms.” Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen, for her part, presented Ukraine as Europe’s only protection: “If we allow Ukraine to fall, we will open the way for Russia to advance into other parts of Europe.”
One can understand fears that, if Ukraine is rendered neutral with limits on its armed forces, Russia would hold the whip hand over Europe. Nobody wants to let Moscow dictate the terms of the European security architecture through violence. But at this point, Europe’s rejection of a “dirty deal” could mean impotently watching Ukraine’s destruction over the next six months. How would this outcome improve European security or prestige?
Norway and Finland have offered the most constructive European response to U.S. diplomacy since Trump returned to the White House. They offer Europe a new language of patient diplomacy to replace maximalist rhetoric. This is in line with both countries’ previous experience mediating and building bridges with Russia. It also recognizes a basic fact: all protracted wars not settled decisively on the battlefield — which is to say, the vast majority of wars — end in negotiated settlements between the aggressor and the defender. America’s signature is absolutely necessary to secure such an outcome.
Mainstream analysis seems unable to accept these realities. It is stuck in moral posturing or fearmongering. There is still little serious discussion of what compromises might be struck. The 28-point plan that U.S.-Russian diplomacy developed in 2025 should not be equated with Ukraine’s capitulation, nor is it a recipe for turning Ukraine into Belarus. Ukraine would enter the EU, receive reconstruction assistance, and retain armed forces on a level comparable to Finland's. It is time to return to the core points on which a deal must be struck.
Russia has responded positively to the proposals sent from Oslo. Ukraine, Russia, and the U.S. have agreed to a three-way summit in November, according to Zelensky. The key question now is whether other European governments will take the Oslo initiative seriously and agree on who can represent Europe in these talks. Dmitri Peskov, Putin’s press secretary, has cautiously welcomed the idea that Alexander Stubb could represent Europe in the negotiations.
Finland and Norway’s more moderate language is a crucial first step toward a shared European understanding that continuing the war in its current form is self-defeating. As Eide observed at the U.N. last month, “diplomacy can work – if we allow it to.”
But first, Europe must decide: will it support or sabotage the U.S. effort to build a diplomatic off-ramp?

title: Reagan & Gorby: What happened in Reykjavik didn't stay in Reykjavik
body:
Forty years later, their efforts remind us of what is possible if leaders are willing to take chances and buck their foreign policy establishments
Before 1986, a city named Reykjavík was best remembered for the “Match of the Century.” International eyes fixated on Iceland’s capital for the World Chess Championship of 1972. The American prodigy Bobby Fischer dethroned the USSR’s defending champ Boris Spassky, ending a quarter-century of Soviet chess domination. Meanwhile on the global chessboard, the Cold War, with its mind-boggling defense budgets and ICBM stockpiles, continued.
Fourteen years later, Reykjavík became synonymous with a different kind of U.S.-Soviet meeting with far greater stakes for humankind. The story of how President Ronald Reagan and General Secretary Mikhail Gorbachev wound up there for two days of meetings 40 Octobers ago — and the progress they made toward a shared goal of eliminating nuclear bombs — should resonate in our dangerous age of nuclear tension and profligate weapons modernization .
Their efforts, however incomplete, remind us a better world is possible if leaders are willing to take chances, buck their foreign policy establishments, and speak truth about the madness of developing costly weapons that threaten human extinction.
Reykjavík wasn’t supposed to be a formal summit. A spy scandal almost prevented it. Reagan and Gorbachev ultimately failed to reach a breakthrough. Yet their efforts soon bore fruit. But first, why was distant Reykjavík chosen anyway?
“Halfway between us and them, and none of the big powers will be offended!” explained Gorbachev to his top foreign-policy adviser, Anatoly Chernyaev, in late summer 1986, according to the eminent chronicler of Soviet diplomatic history Archie Brown.
Gorbachev’s written invitation asked Reagan to come to “a quick one-on-one meeting … maybe just for one day, to engage in a strictly confidential, private, and frank discussion.” The Soviet premier insisted “all other matters” should be set aside. Other matters were indeed straining the relationship beyond arms control and either side’s tenuous adherence to existing nuclear treaties — not least the wars in Afghanistan, Nicaragua, and Angola, as well as Reagan’s ongoing criticism of the USSR’s human rights record.
Then, in late August, the KGB arrested an unlucky American journalist named Nicholas Daniloff in Moscow, a blatant retaliation for the FBI’s arrest of a Soviet employee at the U.N. who was caught attempting to pry secrets from a U.S. defense contractor. Secretary of State George Shultz made clear to his Soviet counterpart that there’d be no meeting until “Daniloff was safely back in the United States,” noted Brown.
Daniloff was released , and the summit convened just 11 days later. “Both Reagan and Gorbachev (in sharp contrast with many senior officials in their administrations and the military in both their countries) were in favor, in principle, of getting rid of all nuclear weapons,” Brown tells Responsible Statecraft.
Reagan’s genuine abhorrence of nuclear weapons contradicted his reputation as a warmonger. His critics could caricature the American actor-turned-politician, but Reagan’s early hard-line gave the Kremlin legitimate reasons to distrust him, according to presidential historian Jeffrey Engel.
Reagan’s first term “was marked by belligerence, reckless rhetoric, military build-up, threats, and accusations,” Engel tells RS. “The second was a quest for better superpower relations… by the end of the first term he’d become aware of just how dangerous his own rhetoric was proving, and wanting a partner for peace, he merely had to wait until one appeared.” Gorbachev appeared in 1985, and one of his core foreign policy priorities would be to reduce the crushing weight of military spending on the Soviet economy.
On the afternoon of the second and final day at Reykjavík, the two leaders sought to break the limited framework of arms control for the uncharted, even radical territory of arms elimination , as described by historian Odd Arne Westad.
“Gorbachev decided to go all-out to break the dynamics of the arms race and prevent the militarization of space,” wrote Westad in his overview of the Cold War. He called for removing all U.S. and Soviet intermediate-range nuclear missiles from Europe , excepting British and French weapons. As for ICBMs, Gorbachev proposed a 50% reduction as long as Reagan agreed not to deploy his beloved Strategic Defense Initiative, which critics derisively labeled “Star Wars,” for the next decade.
Reagan responded with an even bigger idea: eliminate all ballistic missiles within ten years. Gorbachev pushed further: get rid of all nuclear weapons, not only the missiles. “But Reagan would not budge on SDI,” according to Westad, even though the satellite system was light years from being operable. (Space-based defense against ICBMs remains a fantasy to this day.)
“Reykjavík came unexpectedly close to an unexpectedly ambitious agreement,” read a State Department summary written immediately afterward, cited by Brown. The summit was not a failure, however, as the face-to-face meetings nurtured a rapport between the leaders and created momentum toward a deal.
In Washington on Dec. 8, 1987, Reagan and Gorbachev signed the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty despite domestic criticism in both countries. It eliminated all U.S. and Soviet nuclear and conventional land-based ballistic and cruise missiles with ranges of 500 to 5,500 kilometers.
“For the first time in history, the language of arms control was replaced by arms reduction,” Reagan announced. “Of course this required a dramatic shift in thinking and it took conventional wisdom some time to catch up. Reaction, to say the least, was mixed. To some, the ‘zero-option’ was impossibly visionary and unrealistic. To others, merely a propaganda ploy. But with patience, determination, and commitment, we’ve made this impossible vision a reality.”
The INF Treaty ushered in the high tide of arms reduction and detente, as the nightmare of nuclear apocalypse gave way to visions of a nuclear-free planet. With the Cold War effectively over, START I followed in July 1991, requiring major cuts to the number of deployed strategic nuclear warheads. And for the next 20 years, a global non-proliferation consensus fostered several more pacts. The last major treaty was New START, signed by President Barack Obama and Russian President Dmitry Medvedev in 2010.
The once-promising Reagan-Gorbachev idea is long dead. The U.S. and Russia possess more than 10,000 warheads, or roughly 87% percent of the world’s total and many more than necessary to destroy the Earth several times over. No bilateral treaties limiting the U.S. and Russian arsenals remain in effect, and new countries may be verging on going nuclear.
“The breakdown in arms control after 2010 mirrors the deterioration in the U.S.-Russian relationship caused primarily by differences over Ukraine,” historian and Kennan Institute director Michael Kimmage tells RS. Washington and Moscow cannot afford to have short memories: “Both the U.S. and the Soviet Union impoverished themselves, in different ways, through Cold War military spending… Today, the image of great powers as fundamentally unable to communicate with one another is a metaphor… with any number of ominous implications.”
Faced with a future of nuclear anarchy, the world would be wise to recommit itself to achieving Gorbachev’s vision, which he shared upon signing the INF Treaty.
“May December 8, 1987, become a date that will be inscribed in the history books, a date that will mark the watershed separating the era of a mounting risk of nuclear war from the era of a demilitarization of human life.”

title: What if Dems didn't scuttle Henry Wallace VP nomination in 1944?
body:
The anti-imperialist who coined "century of the common man" was already vice president when he was prevented by party bosses from running with FDR again.
Angelenos are in for a treat. Some little-known but extraordinarily-consequential history is being presented in an absolutely riveting 50-actor immersive play aptly titled “Convention,” which opened at Hollywood’s Industry Loft on October 16.
The play asks the audience to imagine how different — how much better, more peaceful, and more prosperous — the world would have been if there had been no atomic bombings in World War II and no Cold War; if we had ended colonialism in 1945 and France and the U.S. had never invaded Vietnam; or if women’s rights and civil rights had flourished in the immediate postwar period.
This may seem like far-fetched speculation today, but most Americans would be surprised to learn how close we may have come to such a different outcome.
The show turns on the moment, 82 years ago, when former Secretary of Agriculture and then-Vice President Henry A. Wallace came within a hairsbreadth of getting the Democratic renomination for vice president. Therefore, if not for a determined Democratic party machine, Wallace would have become president on April 12, 1945 , when Franklin D. Roosevelt passed away, having won reelection for an unprecedented fourth term barely five months earlier.
Sadly, Wallace, a true visionary, has largely been expunged from American memory. Historian Arthur Schlesinger insisted that Wallace, an Iowa corn geneticist, had been the “best secretary of agriculture this country has ever had.” He certainly managed to rescue the devastated agricultural economy during Roosevelt’s first New Deal term. When Democratic Party “bosses” refused to put Wallace, who hailed from a prominent Republican farm family, on the ticket as vice president in 1940 , Roosevelt threatened to turn down the nomination, and the party bosses yielded.
As vice president, Wallace famously championed the anti-imperialist, pro-working class “century of the common man,” which he opposed to Henry Luce’s vision of a U.S.-dominated “American century.” Despite entertaining such radical views, Wallace’s popularity soared. When time came to nominate the next vice president at the party convention in July 1944, Wallace had the overwhelming support of national Democrats, as evidenced in a Gallup Poll released the first day of the convention showing that 65% of Democratic voters wanted him back on the ticket. Only 2% preferred Missouri Senator Harry Truman.
But this time the conservative and often corrupt party bosses demanded their pound of flesh. Roosevelt was too weak and near death to fight for Wallace the way he did in 1940, much to the chagrin of Eleanor and the Roosevelt children. In the end, the president acquiesced to the bosses’ demand that he dump Wallace.
Still, the outcome was far from determined. At the convention, Wallace’s seconding speech for Roosevelt triggered a wild, spontaneous, prolonged demonstration. Florida Senator Claude Pepper realized that, if he could fight his way to the microphone and place Wallace’s name in nomination, Wallace would sweep the convention. With Chicago Mayor Edward Kelly and party head Robert Hannegan screaming for adjournment, their handpicked chair Samuel Jackson announced a motion to adjourn. Despite the overwhelming majority of delegates shouting their opposition, Jackson said the motion passed and the convention was ended for that evening. He later admitted that he was under strict orders not to let Wallace be nominated. When the gavel landed, Pepper was only five feet from the microphone.
Had he taken the extra step and nominated Wallace in the midst of that frenzy, history could have been fundamentally different. The Cold War and the nuclear arms race may well have been avoided. Instead, the bosses regained control. The deals kicked in and Truman secured the nomination.
Roosevelt begged Wallace to remain in the cabinet, and Wallace became secretary of commerce . From that position, Wallace, soon the last surviving New Dealer in the Truman inner circle, waged a tireless and often lonely fight to persuade Truman to abandon his confrontational stance toward the Soviets and seek peaceful coexistence. He repeatedly implored Truman to understand how American actions around the world — including the U.S. monopoly and testing of atomic bombs, skyrocketing military spending, and expanding global network of military bases — looked to the Soviets, who had just lost 27 million people and much of their economy defeating the Nazis.
While Wallace’s importuning initially influenced the president, the preponderance of Cold Warriors who surrounded Truman ultimately prevailed, and Wallace’s sage counsel went unheeded.
Roosevelt family members and their allies in the still-powerful progressive wing of the party continued to support Wallace, but his outspoken opposition to the burgeoning nuclear arms race and to the demonization of America’s erstwhile Soviet allies was more than Truman, Secretary of State James Byrnes, and other anti-communist hardliners could countenance.
On September 12, 1946, Wallace delivered an impassioned speech before 20,000 people at New York’s Madison Square Garden, a speech that Truman had explicitly approved and one whose message is needed as much today as it was 80 years ago. “Tonight I want to talk about peace,” he said, warning that “he who trusts in the atom bomb will sooner or later perish by the atom bomb.” He deplored war-inducing “oil rivalries” and rejected “this war-with-Russia talk” as “criminal foolishness.” Eight days later, Truman fired him, and the dream of a peaceful world faded.
That night, Wallace told a national radio audience , “Winning the peace is more important than high office…The success or failure of our foreign policy will mean the difference between life and death for our children and grandchildren…It may mean the difference between the existence and the extinction of man and of the world.”
Somehow, often more by luck than by statesmanship, we’ve so far managed to avoid Wallace’s worst fears. But with increased saber-rattling and a growing threat of nuclear war, there is no guarantee our luck won’t run out.

title: Ebola: Ghana has not dropped the ball on disease screening – Prof Amuasi
body: Prof John Amuasi, Leader of Global Health at the KCCR, has rejected suggestions that Ghana has let its disease screening systems slip since the COVID-19 pandemic. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Monday, he said screening at entry points must match the prevailing risk. He argued that testing every arriving traveller for Ebola would be impractical. “No, I wouldn’t say so,” he said when asked whether Ghana had dropped the ball. His comments come after Nigeria confirmed an imported Ebola case on October 20. The patient developed symptoms four days after arriving from Uganda. Investigations into the source of infection remain ongoing, according to the World Health Organisation. Elsewhere, Kenya had recorded nine confirmed cases and two deaths as of October 25. Uganda also recorded cases earlier in the outbreak, but the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control says its outbreak has ended. Prof Amuasi said the Nigerian case illustrated the limits of airport screening. “There is no way that the Nigerian authorities could have caught this at the airport unless they were doing an active test of everybody coming in to see if they had Ebola, which is simply not practicable.” He explained that highly intensive screening cannot be maintained every day without a clear reason. He said the immediate priority should be stronger information gathering and better guidance for travellers. “So this is why I’m saying that for now, what needs to be done, and I hope it is being done, is to augment the data collection on every single individual who comes.” He acknowledged that collecting more information could raise privacy concerns. But he stressed its importance. “It may be a bit intrusive, but is very critical,” he said. Prof Amuasi also proposed giving arriving travellers leaflets. These should explain symptoms to watch for, whom to contact and where to seek care if they become ill. His defence of the screening approach came with a qualification. He called for stronger data collection but did not confirm whether it was already happening. He said a confirmed case would require a different response. “But beyond that, any other measure is not very helpful at this point. If we did have a case, it would change the dynamics entirely.”

title: Trump describes summer ceasefire with Iran as ‘waste of time’
body:
WASHINGTON, October 27. /TASS/. The summer ceasefire with Iran was "a waste of time," US President Donald Trump said.
