It stated, “On behalf of the Northern Senators Forum, we commiserate with His Excellency the governor of Taraba State, the people of Taraba, and the bereaved families of Binari community in Karim-Lamido LGA over the barbaric attack of Friday 23rd October. “We received with shock the murder of innocent worshippers, vigilantes, women and children shortly after Juma’at prayers, and we share in your grief at this difficult time.” Beyond expressing condolences, the senators called for a coordinated security response to prevent further attacks and restore confidence among residents of the affected communities. They urged the leadership of the police, DSS, and NSCDC to deploy additional personnel and operational resources to the area. The forum also called for the establishment of a Forward Operating Base to strengthen security coverage across the Karim-Lamido and River Benue corridor. It appealed to the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) and well-meaning individuals and organisations to provide urgent humanitarian assistance to victims and affected families. The senators demanded a thorough investigation into the killings and the arrest and prosecution of those responsible. While offering prayers for the victims and their families, they expressed hope that peace would return to the affected communities. Death Toll Rises to 58, Taraba Govt Provides Relief Taraba State Police Command confirmed that 15 more people died when the boat in which they were trying to escape from the attackers capsized. The incident brought the death toll from Friday’s attack to 58. Giving an update on the casualty, the command’s Police Public Relations Officer (PPRO), ASP Victor Mshelizah, disclosed that the additional bodies were recovered from surrounding bushes and a river after a mishap. Mshelizah stated that he had spoken with the Divisional Police Officer (DPO) in the area, who briefed him on the latest developments. He said, “I just spoke with the DPO on the latest development in the area. He told me that 23 more bodies were recovered, while another 15 persons who were trying to escape from the attack through the river capsized and died.” He said the victims, “because they were trying to run away from the attackers, they overloaded the canoe and it capsized in the river. Some of the bodies are missing, while 15 were recovered from the river.” The police spokesperson assured residents that the command remained committed to restoring lasting peace and protecting life and property in the community. In his response to Governor Agbu Kefas’ directive, Taraba State Government delivered emergency relief materials, which included essential supplies to victims of the attack, less than 24 hours after the incident. The intervention, coordinated by Taraba State Emergency Management Agency (TSEMA), included on-the-ground assessment of the destruction. The operation was led by Executive Secretary of TSEMA, Dr Echuseh Audu. Audu stated that the intervention was aimed at providing immediate succour to victims while the government worked towards the community’s recovery. She explained, “We are here on behalf of the Taraba State government to show solidarity and provide immediate succour to our brothers and sisters in Binnari. His Excellency has directed that no victim of this dastardly act be left unattended to. “This is just the first phase of intervention. The government is committed to not only providing food, shelter materials, and essential supplies, but also ensuring long-term recovery and security for the community.”

title: Russian troops evacuate 87 civilians from Kupyansk-Uzlovoy — diplomat
body:
DONETSK, October 27. /TASS/. Russian troops have evacuated 87 civilians from Kupyansk-Uzlovoy in the Kharkov Region, Russian Foreign Ministry Ambassador-at-Large Rodion Miroshnik said.
"Service members from the 153rd Tank Regiment of the 47th Tank division, led by the regimental commander, callsign Trinadtsaty, and the assault team commander, callsign Rumyn, carried out a large-scale humanitarian operation to evacuate civilians from the liberated city of Kupyansk-Uzlovoy. A group of civilians was found in the basement of an apartment building in the southern part of the city, which until recently was controlled by the enemy. Troops led by a commander with the callsign Maga used electronic warfare equipment and drones to establish a corridor stretching more than 20 kilometers, providing passage and cover along a route where Ukrainian forces had remotely planted landmines," he wrote on Telegram.
Miroshnik added that Ukrainian forces had carried out a series of mortar and drone attacks on civilians during the evacuation, causing casualties. A total of 87 people were evacuated over three days.

title: Russian Strike Damages Kyiv’s South Bridge, Traffic Disrupted
body:
Russian strikes on Kyiv overnight into Tuesday, Oct. 27, prompted traffic restrictions on the South (Pivdennyi) Bridge, a major transport crossing connecting the capital’s eastern and western banks of the Dnipro River.
The Kyiv City Military Administration (KMVA) announced the restrictions following the attack and warned residents to account for disruptions when planning their journeys.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Service on the Green (Syretsko-Pecherska) metro line was also disrupted, with trains operating separately between Syrets and Vydubychi stations and between Osokorky and Chervonyi Khutir, according to the KMVA .
South Bridge is being inspected for damage following a Russian attack, Kyiv Mayor Vitalii Klitschko later said in a Telegram post. Specialists are assessing the extent of the damage, and the bridge is currently closed to traffic.
Klitschko also released the first photos showing the aftermath of the Russian strike on the bridge.
There is currently no information on when the bridge will reopen to traffic or when metro service on this section of the line will resume.
The South Bridge carries both road traffic and a section of the Green Line, making it a critical connection across the Dnipro.
The disruption follows repeated Russian attacks on the crossing earlier in October, including strikes that damaged metro infrastructure and forced temporary suspensions of road and rail traffic.
In a separate development overnight, Klitschko reported that Russian ballistic strikes hit an administrative building in Kyiv’s Podilskyi district and non-residential buildings at two other locations.
The latest attack followed Monday evening’s missile strikes on a university campus and residential neighborhoods, which killed one person and injured 10 others, most of them students.

title: Gridin scores twice as Flames win fourth straight
body:
CALGARY – Matvei Gridin scored twice as the surging Calgary Flames made it four straight wins and a perfect homestand with a 5-2 NHL victory over the Toronto Maple Leafs on Monday.
Mikael Backlund also scored for Calgary (5-6-0), while Joel Farabee and Martin Pospisil added empty-netters. Farabee, who also had an assist, and Matt Coronato, who had a pair of helpers, extended their point streaks to five games.
Easton Cowan and William Nylander replied for Toronto (7-5-2), whose four-game win streak was halted.
Making his fourth straight start for the Flames, Devin Cooley made 26 stops to improve to 4-2-0.
Sergei Bobrovsky had 30 saves for Toronto. He falls to 3-4-2.
Calgary grabbed control of the game halfway through the first period on goals less than two minutes apart by Gridin and Backlund.
Gridin’s opening goal at 10:05 came from a sharp angle off the left wing when he picked the top corner on Bobrovsky’s short side.
Gridin’s second of the night and the eventual game-winner, was scored on the power play 25 seconds into the second period. It was another top corner snipe, this one over Bobrovsky’s other shoulder. The 20-year-old’s four goals, which have come in the last four games, leads the club.
Maple Leafs: RW Kirill Marchenko (lower body) left the game early in the second period after he went into the boards awkwardly after a hit from Yegor Sharangovich. Auston Matthews had an assist on Nylander’s goal for his 800th NHL point. He becomes the fastest player in Leafs history to reach that milestone.
Flames: Backlund (upper body) returned after missing two games. Four straight starts for Cooley is a career-high. He’s stopped (126 of 132) for a .955 save percentage over that stretch.
Leading 2-0 after 20 minutes, the Flames picked up where they left off in the second when Gridin scored just 25 seconds into the period, giving the home side a three-goal cushion. The Leafs entered the game with the league’s No. 1 penalty kill.
Calgary beat Toronto for the first time since Feb. 10, 2022. The Leafs had won the last eight meetings. It was Toronto’s longest active winning streak against any opponent.
Maple Leafs: Visit the Seattle Kraken on Wednesday.
Flames: Visit the Edmonton Oilers on Wednesday.
This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 26, 2026.

title: DTN@100: Osoba, Amuka-Pemu, Ogunbiyi to Lead National Dialogue
body: Ayodeji Ake Veteran journalist and former Ogun State governor, Aremo Olusegun Osoba, publisher of Vanguard Newspapers, Olorogun Sam Amuka-Pemu, and former Managing Director of Daily Times, Dr Yemi Ogunbiyi, will lead a national dialogue organised by Daily Times Nigeria (DTN) as part of activities marking the newspaper’s centenary celebration. The DTN@100 Shaping the Future TownHall and National Conversation is scheduled to hold on November 3, 2026, at Harbour Point, 4 Wilmot Point Road, Victoria Island, Lagos. Osoba, a former Managing Director of Daily Times, will superintend the event, while Amuka-Pemu, a former editor of The Sunday Times, and Ogunbiyi, Chairman of Tanus Communications, will serve as co-chairs. The event is designed to deepen discussions on Nigeria’s achievements, recognise individuals who have contributed to the country’s development and promote a more positive perception of Nigeria internationally. According to a statement issued by the organisers, the conversation will bring together professionals from the technology, entrepreneurship, media and strategic communications sectors to examine Nigeria’s progress and explore opportunities for shaping its future. Among those expected to provide perspectives on the discussions are Microsoft’s Chief Growth and AI Officer for Africa and the Middle East, Mrs Olatomiwa Williams; co-founder of Flutterwave and Andela and Chief Executive Officer of Future Africa, Mr. Iyin Aboyeji; and media personality and strategic communications expert, Mr Chude Jideonwo, who is also a co-founder of RED Media. The discussion will be anchored by Mr. Cheta Nwanze, Managing Director of Folio Communications, publishers of Daily Times, and founder of SBM Research. The TownHall and National Conversation is the second major activity under the multi-layered DTN@100 centenary celebration, which runs from June 1, 2026, to June 1, 2027. Activities scheduled for the Lagos event include the Honouring the Past Exhibition, which will showcase Nigerians who helped shape the country’s history, as documented in the archives of Daily Times over its 100 years of reporting. The programme will also feature the DTN@100 Times Heroes Awards, designed to recognise individuals whose leadership, patriotism and service to humanity have contributed to Nigeria’s development and those helping to shape its future. The centenary celebration builds on the inaugural DTN@100 Times Heroes Awards, held in Abuja on September 3, 2026, under the theme, “Honouring the Past, Shaping the Future.” As part of the broader initiative, Folio Group, owners of Daily Times, has committed the newspaper’s archives to the development of The Nigerian Grand Book (Magnum Opus), a 700-page national souvenir intended to document Nigeria’s story for a global audience. The project is positioned by the organisers as a tool for improving Nigeria’s international image through a comprehensive account of the country’s history, achievements and influential personalities. The initiative also informed the decision to recognise 100 of the most impactful Nigerians, past and present, through the Times Heroes Awards during the centenary year. In the statement, signed by the Chairman of Folio Africa and Publisher of Daily Times, Mr. Fidelis Anosike, the organisers said the activities were part of efforts to celebrate the newspaper’s legacy while encouraging conversations about Nigeria’s future. The centenary programme seeks to connect the country’s historical achievements with contemporary leadership, innovation and service, while providing a platform for stakeholders to reflect on Nigeria’s place in the world.

title: Telecel Foundation equips 100 hearing-impaired students with practical STEM skills
body: The Telecel Foundation extended its commitment to inclusive learning to the Volta School for the Deaf in Hohoe, Volta Region, where 100 students took part in hands-on robotics training as part of Telecel Ghana’s Care Month celebrations. Facilitated by the Mingo Foundation, the workshop introduced students to practical STEM concepts through engaging activities designed to build creativity, teamwork and problem-solving skills. The initiative underscored a simple principle: every child, regardless of ability, deserves the opportunity to explore science, technology, engineering and mathematics and fulfil their potential. Speaking at the event, Rita Agyeiwaa Rockson, Foundation, Sustainability and External Communications Manager at Telecel Ghana, described the initiative as the Foundation’s way of creating meaningful impact during Care Month. “At Telecel, Care Month is dedicated to our customers and employees across Ghana. For the Foundation, we wanted to provide care that truly counts, which is why we are here today. Seeing these students grasp basic engineering concepts so quickly and build their projects with minimal guidance proves that ability should never define potential. Every child deserves the opportunity to become tomorrow’s engineer, innovator or problem-solver.” The school’s headmaster, Joe Innocent Kodjo Tsameny, thanked the Telecel Foundation for the robotics training. “Opportunities like this help bring out the potential in our students. As the world becomes increasingly digital, I am pleased they are gaining practical, hands-on robotics experience. This training has enabled them to apply the concepts they have learned in theory. He said. Telecel employee volunteers worked alongside the students throughout the day, offering guidance and encouragement as they completed their projects. One of the day’s standout participants was 13-year-old Makafui, the first among her peers to complete her project. Speaking through a sign language interpreter, she shared that the experience had inspired her to dream bigger. “I was very happy to finish first. The facilitators helped us understand each step, and I really enjoyed building my project. This training has inspired me to pursue a career in STEM. Thank you, Telecel Foundation, for giving us this opportunity.” Through initiatives like this, the Telecel Foundation continues to expand access to quality learning opportunities, equipping more young people with the confidence, skills, and inspiration to help shape the future through STEM.

title: JUDGE ASKS FOR NOTIFICATION AS PUBLIC GOLF COURSE PROJECT, IN WASHINGTON, D.C., IS BUILT. DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR TO APPEAL THIS UNCONSTITUTIONAL REQUEST. We are closing the East Potomac Golf Course Site as scheduled on November 15th in order to renovate and rebuild for Competitive (with other such projects!), Safety, Modernization, and Aesthetic reasons. We believe this Project is totally “as of right,” and that the judge does not have the Constitutional Right to “ask for or receive notices,” which are time-consuming, unnecessary, expensive, and unconstitutional. We will immediately appeal this decision. When completed, it is anticipated that this Course, which will be open to the Public, at a reduced rate for those living in Washington, D.C., will be one of the finest anywhere in the World! It will be fully capable of holding Major Events such as The U.S. Open, The PGA Championship, The Ryder Cup, and The Presidents Cup, which will bring Great Economic Benefits, Growth, and Prestige to Washington, D.C. and, indeed, the entire surrounding area. The Development of this World Championship Public Facility must begin, immediately, if it is to be completed in a timely and seasonal manner. To have to give advanced notices to a judge who has no expertise in Golf, Architecture, Landscaping, Construction, or anything else having to do with building such a World Class Project, is not fair, appropriate, or Constitutional. The soil, grass, sand bunkers, tees, fairways, greens, seawalls, small and nondescript buildings, and virtually every other element of the existing Course and grounds are far beyond their intended or expected life. In its current form, the Course is extremely dangerous to play, in that the narrow and nondescript fairways are far too close together, leading to a constant barrage of people being hit with wayward shots, and the echoing throughout the air of the word, “FORE!” The judge has absolutely no right to hold up this very important and beautiful Project. We are asking the D.C. Circuit Court for immediate remedy. Thank you for your attention to this matter. President DONALD J. TRUMP

title: Jay-Z to headline Super Bowl 2027 half-time show
body: Jay-Z will perform at the Super Bowl half-time show next year, bringing three decades of hip-hop hits to one of music’s most-watched stages. The rapper will perform at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, on February 14 for the Apple Music Super Bowl LXI Half-Time Show. “From [debut album] Reasonable Doubt to standing on the Super Bowl half-time stage, this has been a journey,” Jay-Z said in a statement. “Thirty years of music, work and culture on the world’s biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true.” View this post on Instagram His appearance will follow those of his wife, Beyonce, who headlined the show in New Orleans in 2013, reuniting with Destiny’s Child bandmates Kelly Rowland and Michelle Williams. Beyonce returned in 2016 as a guest during Coldplay’s headline set, performing alongside the band and Bruno Mars. The announcement caps a busy anniversary year for Jay-Z, whose “Jay-Z 30” celebrations have marked three decades since Reasonable Doubt was released and 25 years since The Blueprint was launched. After headlining Philadelphia’s Roots Picnic in May, he played three sold-out shows at Yankee Stadium in July, with Beyonce and their daughter, Blue Ivy Carter , among the guests. Further performances took him to Paris and London before two closing nights at SoFi Stadium at the weekend. Those concerts featured appearances by Dr Dre, Snoop Dogg, John Legend, DJ Khaled, Scarface, Too Short and Blue Ivy, giving the rapper an introduction to the venue he will return to in February. The celebrations also included Jay-Z in 8 , an eight-part documentary series in which he discussed songs from across his catalogue with producer Rick Rubin. Jay-Z follows Bad Bunny , whose half-time performance this year celebrated his Puerto Rican heritage with a set featuring a sugar cane field and a neighbourhood scene. Lady Gaga and Ricky Martin joined him as surprise performers. Other recent half-time headliners include Kendrick Lamar , Usher, Rihanna and The Weeknd.

title: Kaduna And The Meaning of Tinubu’s Second March
body: Tunde Rahman History has a way of choosing its own geography. When President Bola Ahmed Tinubu chose Kaduna to flag off his 2027 re-election campaign on Saturday, October 24, 2026, he chose more than a location. He was sending a historic message. Kaduna is Nigeria’s political ground zero. From here, the old Northern Region administered the entire North. It was here that alliances were forged. By starting his campaign where the North still feels its pulse, Tinubu told northern Nigeria, “I have not forgotten you.” Ranchers Bees Stadium, Kaduna, the rally venue, was packed with party supporters and sympathisers who had thronged the stadium from as early as 7 am. Some supporters slept overnight at the stadium. President Tinubu’s speech was deliberate, confident, and unusually personal. “My good people of Kaduna, it’s good to be back here again. You have listened to many speeches. I’m not going to bore you down. I’m happy to be here with you.” The President thanked Kaduna people for their support in the 2023 election, but stated that he had come to seek their support again for a second mandate to keep a promise of prosperity, continuity, progress and development. For three years, Tinubu’s biggest vulnerability has been the economy. On Saturday, he did not dodge it. He said: “I hear my opponents talking about hunger and poverty. Who created it? They did. They created the hunger. We are trying to eradicate it.” He declared that his administration had demonstrated its commitment to improving Nigerians’ welfare through economic reforms, regular salary payments, and development initiatives implemented by APC Governors across the federation. President Tinubu could not have chosen Kaduna without addressing insecurity. Three years ago, Birnin-Gwari was synonymous with fear. Today, the Kaduna-Abuja road is safer, and farming is returning to Giwa and Soba. Tinubu credited the military push and Governor Uba Sani’s non-kinetic approach. Governor Uba Sani himself highlighted these achievements in security, infrastructure, and more, commending the President for his support and interventions in the state. For Kaduna, that resonance matters more than any statistic from Abuja. Unlike in 2023, President Tinubu came to Kaduna this time with receipts showing his performance. These include GDP steady growth, falling inflation, naira stability, doubled FAAC allocations to states, rising foreign reserves, infrastructure renewal, NELFUND loans for indigent students, and consumer credit for young people, among others. The message was clear: The first term was surgery; the second term will be recovery, progress and prosperity. It is a powerful argument, because even his critics admit state governors now have more money than ever. President Tinubu doubled down on the governors’ performance: “We pay salaries regularly. Our governors are working. I’m proud of them. They are developing. I salute all our governors today. I can see the development strides they are making in their various states.” For the North, it’s a debt repaid. President Tinubu got about 62% of his votes from the North in 2023. He made promises to the region. He has kept his promises in terms of road and rail infrastructure, interventions in healthcare, improving security, and governmental appointments, The Kaduna rally also included key strategic moments worth mentioning. Both Vice President Kashim Shettima and Tinubu/ Shettima Presidential Campaign Director-General, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, harped on Tinubu’s strategic support for key Northerners in the previous bid for the presidency. In 2007, President Tinubu offered former Vice President Atiku Abubakar his ACN platform to run when former President Obasanjo hounded him out of the PDP. The President also backed Nuhu Ribadu in 2011 and late Muhammadu Buhari to be president in 2015 and 2019. According to them, Tinubu supported our sons for 20 years. Now, we should support him again for a second term. VP Shettima maintained that supporting Tinubu’s re-election is a matter of honour, integrity, political loyalty, and appreciation for the President’s contributions to advancing Northern political leaders over the years. With VP Shettima beside him, APC National Chairman Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, Campaign DG Yari, and even former opponents like FCT Minister Nyesom Wike and Governors Chukwuma Soludo and Ademola Adeleke now on his expanded Campaign Council, President Tinubu projected something the opposition lacks—a broad national coalition. Why Kaduna Matters for 2027 The APC says it wants 2 million votes from Kaduna State. That is ambitious, but the symbolism is more important than the number. If President Tinubu can hold the North-West, with a Sokoto rally billed for December 5 and Kano for December 17, win the South-West, and split North-Central, the math becomes very difficult for Atiku’s ADC, Makinde’s APM, and Obi/Kwankwaso’s camp to solve. The opposition is still running from one small party to another. Tinubu is running on a solid pan-Nigerian structure. Last Saturday in Kaduna, President Tinubu did not just flag off a campaign. He framed the 2027 election as a choice between continuity and chaos, between finishing the reforms and abandoning them midway. He is clear about what he thinks should be done: finish the job. •Rahman, Senior Special Assistant to President Tinubu on Media and Special Duties, is a Fellow of the Nigerian Guild of Editors.

title: Obuasi SHTS abuse allegations: WILI demands independent probe, protection for students
body: Women in Leadership International (WILI) has called for a thorough, independent investigation into allegations of sexual abuse involving female students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School. The organisation also wants immediate protection and support for affected students, amid reports that some complaints may not have received timely attention. In a statement, WILI expressed concern about the alleged abuse and questions surrounding how the complaints were handled. “Schools must be places of learning, safety and opportunity, not environments where children fear exploitation, intimidation or abuse by those entrusted with their care,” it said. WILI acknowledged steps taken by the Ghana Education Service and other relevant authorities to investigate. However, it said the seriousness of the allegations required an impartial and transparent process. The investigation, it said, must establish the facts, examine possible institutional failures and ensure accountability wherever wrongdoing is established. The organisation also raised concerns about reports that some affected students and families may have faced pressure or intimidation. “No girl should be afraid to report abuse. No parent should fear consequences for seeking justice for their child. And no position of authority should place anyone beyond scrutiny,” the statement said. WILI urged investigators to examine all credible allegations, including any failures to report, prevent or respond appropriately to suspected abuse. It called for confidential counselling, protection from intimidation and access to appropriate medical and legal assistance for affected students. The organisation stressed that the investigation and any related disruptions must not undermine the girls’ education or future opportunities. It also urged authorities to strengthen safeguarding systems in schools through accessible reporting channels, clear professional boundaries, mandatory reporting procedures and effective accountability mechanisms. WILI requested regular public updates on the investigation, while protecting the privacy, dignity and safety of students and preserving the integrity of the process. The organisation acknowledged the right of every accused person to due process and the presumption of innocence. It said these principles must coexist with the duty to protect children and investigate complaints promptly. It appealed to government institutions, school authorities, parents, civil society organisations and communities to work together to make schools safer for girls. “A girl’s education should open doors to her future, not expose her to harm,” the statement said. “Protecting our girls is not optional. It is a collective responsibility.”

title: 2027: Let The Game Begin, Let Sanity Prevail
body: REUBEN ABATI With the inauguration of the campaign council of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) on October 9, that of the Nigeria Democratic Council (NDC) yesterday, October 25, and the flag-off of the campaigns of the All Progressives Congress (APC) on Saturday, October 24, all three being the main political parties in Nigeria’s three-way race, we may assume towards the 2027 general elections, the race, the countdown, clearly has begun. It is an important electoral moment for Nigeria, the eighth time since the return to democracy in Nigeria (1999, 2003, 2007, 2011, 2015, 2019, 2023). Again, Nigeria’s democracy, its institutions, and the people’s choice will be put to the test. There are 18 political parties on the ballot leading the race but the aforementioned three would seem to present us with an interesting three-way race. The highest point was reached last Saturday when President Tinubu launched, his party, APC’s campaign in Kaduna. It was a well-organized rally put together by Governor Uba Sani of Kaduna who welcomed President Tinubu, his wife and others with gratitude and the promise of the generous hospitality of the people of Kaduna State. It was on the whole a good outing and a joyous event, with the RaRaRa musical band singing a number of songs: including the anthems A4A, and Omo Ologo to which the President and the Vice President, Senator Kashim Shettima danced with great excitement. Then there were the colourful Kaduna women for Asiwaju/Shettima, and a mammoth crowd which raised questions about alleged claims that the APC candidate and incumbent President has no major following in the North. There have been arguments about the authenticity of the images and reports on social media, but the caveat is that social media does not always represent reality, and it is not known that elections are won by a social media mob. It is real human beings, eligible and empowered accordingly that win elections. It is therefore important that the President in his campaign speech asked his audience: do you have your PVC? He promised the people that should they give him a second term in office, he would deliver growth, opportunity, prosperity, and recovery. The choice of Kaduna as the venue of the APC flag-off is instructive. The Governor of the state, Uba Sani is a right-hand man, and a favourite of President Tinubu in the North. He must be happy indeed that he was chosen as the host of the APC flag-off. And that for another reason: the former Governor of Kaduna State, Mallam Nasir el-Rufai is not exactly a friend of the incumbent administration, which ironically, he helped to create. To drive home this point, Nasir el-Rufai, a founding father of the APC, has been in security detention, toing and froing from the courts, for over seven months, and there is no guarantee that the Tinubu administration will allow him to be released until after the 2027 elections. Tinubu going to Kaduna State is a show of strength as in who is Nasir el-Rufai to challenge the President or the Federal Government of Nigeria? In spite of Nasir el-Rufai, who is out on a long, lonely season, the APC, Uba Sani and Tinubu put up a massive show in what could have been with el-Rufai on his feet and on the ground, a major battlefield. Kaduna is also a strategic political capital of the North, the home of virtually all the powerful figures of the North. What became a question mark in the Kaduna flag-off rally, however, is that the President and his team arrived three hours behind schedule, they arrived late in the afternoon at a rally scheduled for 10 am by which time many of the persons in attendance had become restless. No politician, no matter how highly placed, should treat the voting public so shabbily. Those who seek to govern and occupy public offices must learn to be punctual. Keeping the people under the sun and hoping to solicit for their votes is contemptuous. It should not happen again. As it turned out, the Tinubu campaign team members shot themselves in the foot. They had to start rushing the programme and found themselves in the uncomfortable position of struggling among themselves for the microphone and for time. The other major highlight of President Tinubu’s maiden outing in the 2027 campaign process of which he had said previously that he will show up only in 12 of the 36 states of the Federation, was his statement that no one should blame him if there is hunger and poverty in the land because it is his opponents who created hunger and poverty. He is only trying to eradicate it. His opponents are just heckling him. I am uncomfortable with this claim. If President Tinubu’s opponents created multi-dimensional poverty, it is his duty to eradicate it. He must be reminded that he once said that he met many problems on the ground when he succeeded President Buhari and it was his duty to deal with both the liabilities and the assets that he inherited, government being a continuity. He had also promised then that he would resolve the crisis of electricity supply in the country within six months. When he now turns around and blames the opposition, he misses the point. Which opposition? Atiku who left office as a Vice President in 2007, with the worst testimonial that anyone could ever get from his boss? Or Peter Obi whose main pedigree is on social media and the streets of diaspora Nigeria? Or Omoyele Sowore who even if he were to become President would organize a protest against himself before suddenly realizing the truth of his own self-indictment? President Tinubu should have stayed on his message of a second term of consolidation, prosperity and growth for the people, and his advice that the people should make sure they have their PVCs and vote for him. Many commentators have taken him up on the subject of poverty and hunger. They claim that as President, he has done nothing to help the people in this regard. By the way, saying that will amount to misinformation, disinformation and outright blackmail. I have argued elsewhere, that nobody has the right to misinform the Nigerian public because it is convenient to do so, and to tell lies shamefacedly is a poor test of character and ability. The current campaign process is driven by too much ignorance and malice. The truth is that the Tinubu administration launched a $3.5 billion poverty alleviation programme along with a Hope Package which comprises Hope Governance, Hope Primary Health Care, Hope Education, Ward Development programme, NELFUND for Nigerian students, and the Renewed Hope Baby Support Programme. There is also a programme called NG-Cares worth about $1. 25 million, there is also a Ward Development programme and a $300 million Solutions for Internally Displaced and Host Communities programme, in addition to other social intervention programmes. The duty of an informed commentator is to interrogate the process, implications and the impact of these programmes: Were they effective? What was their impact? Were they transparent? How best could they be redesigned and improved upon? The government can also be held accountable. Unfortunately, one of Nigeria’s major problems is that its electoral process, every season, indeed public debate, is often overtaken by beer parlour talk even in places where more reasoned analysis is required. That disease called “opinionitis” is back on our shores. Nigerian politics, as we approach the 2027 elections, should be driven by decency and sanity. Politicians must realize that they have a bounden duty to preserve the integrity of the same country they seek to govern. If they uproot the country because of their selfish ambitions, there will be nothing left for the average citizen. Politicians should allow sanity to prevail. We are all living witnesses to the Peace Accord that was signed in August 2026 by the political parties with a promise that they will protect the integrity of the electoral process. The time has come for the National Peace Committee to review its methodology and ask critical questions, ahead of its next meeting on January 14, 2027, in the face of the prevalence of discord in Nigerian politics. Of what use is a peace accord that politicians sign and then go ahead to do the opposite at all levels? In August, one Senator Francis Fadahunsi, (APC, Osun East) openly threatened to attack and kill members of the Accord Party in the state. He was invited by the Osun Police Command. He lied to the Police, they gave him a handshake and that was it. Many deaths were recorded during the Osun Gubernatorial election. Today, the same Governor whose followers were allegedly killed by APC thugs is President Tinubu’s campaigner-in-chief in Osun State. Dele Farotimi has said it all in a book of the same title: “Do Not Die In Their War (2021).” They will end their war on their own terms and you will be in the mortuary, a casualty, a loss to your loved ones. Voter, beware! In Edo State, in October, a Jarret Tenebe, Chair of the state branch of the APC boasted that whoever opposes the APC in Edo State will be treated to a prayer round of “AK-47 Fire”. He has since claimed that he said this in the same context as “Holy Ghost Fire”, a popular Nigerian saying. Except that intelligent people have not been able to establish a connection in this regard. Mikhail Kalashnikov, the Russian small arms designer, hero of the Russian Federation, hero of Socialist Labour, who invented the AK47 in 1947, before his death in December 2013, wrote to the Russian Orthodox Church to beg for forgiveness for inventing a rifle that had killed so many. In Nigeria, in 2026, it is the same rifle that a Nigerian politician celebrates as a weapon of recourse, not at war but for a simple, civilian election among compatriots. In October 2026, Rotimi Amaechi, a former Speaker of the Rivers State Assembly, a former two-time Rivers state Governor and a former Minister of the Federation, declared that if the people of Edo State were to vote for President Bola Tinubu in 2027, then all Edo people should be considered mad. He said “only thieves and mad people can vote for Tinubu in 2027.” Must people vote by force? Where is the threat of madness coming from? A few days ago, a former Senate Deputy President, also a former APC member, now in the NDC threatened that anyone who rigs the 2027 election in Urhoboland should be ready to die. “We will kill whoever rigs”! , he declared. He has not denied saying so. Nor has he blamed AI which is the latest lying machine that Nigerian politicians have discovered. They often speak so indecently and they claim it is AI that has misrepresented them. There must be decency in politics. There are existing laws to deal with electoral offences- Sections 118 -133 of the Electoral Act 2026 which must be enforced and not treated as dead law at the very moment their enforcement is required. It is most unfortunate that the worst of all are the ones who find it easy to occupy leadership positions. Now that the 2027 games have begun as it were, we suggest that Nigeria’s 2027 electoral process should be driven by issues and ideas, not gossip, personality attacks, or the thinking that the man who shouts the loudest deserves to win. Elections should not be won by those who burn posters and billboards belonging to the opposition or those who threaten to kill. Democracy is about choice and the people must be allowed to choose freely. Increased voter turn-out in a run off, has recently made the difference in the just concluded Presidential elections in Brazil. The Nigerian voter must be confident enough that he or she is safe and that his or her vote will be protected and counted on election day. After 2027, there should be a country to run.

title: Horwath among incumbents ousted across Greater Toronto and Hamilton Area
body:
Election night in the Greater Toronto and Hamilton Area (GTHA) delivered some upsets, with several incumbent mayors losing their bids for re-election.
Former Ontario NDP leader Andrea Horwath , who became Hamilton’s mayor in 2022 after her party’s provincial defeat, was in a distant third place at 14 per cent with 177 of 207 polls reporting as of 11:24 p.m.
Horwath trailed city councillor Rob Cooper who had 32 per cent of the vote and Canadian Institute of Steel Production CEO Keanin Loomis, who had 41 per cent of the vote.
Loomis claimed victory in a speech shortly before 11 p.m., saying he was “at a loss for words.”
“Tonight is about more than winning an election, it’s about hope, it’s about change, and it’s about believing again in what this city can be,” Loomis said.
It’s a reversal from 2022 when Horwath beat Loomis by just under 1,700 votes. Loomis noted that loss, saying he listened to what residents had to say before coming back to win in 2026, calling it a “true Hamilton story.”
Canada’s longest-serving mayor has lost his job after 15 consecutive terms.
Milton’s Gord Krantz was first elected as mayor in 1980, after previously serving as a councillor from 1965 until 1980.
But with all polls reporting Monday night, Krantz trailed Coun. George Minakakis by a 20-point margin.
Krantz isn’t the only long-time mayor poised to lose his seat.
In Oakville, five-term incumbent mayor Rob Burton finished in third place, having received only 20 per cent of the vote. Long-time councillor Jeff Knoll, who has served since 2000, has 36 per cent of the vote and is the mayor-elect, according to unofficial results.
The night started, though, with incumbent Mississauga mayor Carolyn Parrish losing her re-election bid after about two years in office.
Rookie city councillor Alvin Tedjo soared past her and former mayor Bonnie Crombie to win the election, receiving roughly 74,000 votes with all polls reporting as of 11:24 p.m.
“This wasn’t a normal election. We haven’t had a normal two-and-a-half years. These are tough times that we’re living in,” Parrish said in her concession speech.
While some incumbents in the GTHA have lost re-election, others are returning with relatively sizeable outcomes of more than half of the vote.
Toronto Mayor Olivia Chow won re-election with about 54 per cent of the vote, besting councillor Brad Bradford who received roughly 41 per cent.
Brampton Mayor Patrick Brown also saw victory Monday night, being re-elected to his third term in office with about 54 per cent of the vote.
But some GTHA mayors saw even larger margins of victory on election night, with former Ontario Liberal leader and Vaughan Mayor Steven Del Duca winning 81.5 per cent of the vote with 71 of 71 polls reporting.
Richmond Hill Mayor David West is also heading back to city hall after getting 83 per cent of the vote with all polls reporting.
Markham city council will also see Mayor Frank Scarpitti back at the helm for another term, after taking 72 per cent of the vote.

title: U.S AFRICOM Commander: ISIS Defections in Nigeria Rise Over 200% After May Operation
body: … Identifies terrorist financing as a critical challenge …Seeks to reopen dialogue with Sahel states after ECOWAS Exit Chiemelie Ezeobi The number of ISIS members defecting in Nigeria has increased by more than 200 per cent since a joint operation by Nigerian and United States forces in May, the Commander of the United States Africa Command (AFRICOM), General Dagvin Anderson, has said. Anderson, who disclosed this in an exclusive interview with THISDAY yesterday on the sidelines of the ongoing Africa International Defence Exhibition (AFRIDEX), in Lagos, attributed the development to the impact of the operation against a senior ISIS figure and subsequent military operations by Nigerian forces, saying it indicated that some members of the terrorist organisation were reconsidering their involvement. Commending the partnership between the Nigerian Armed Forces, Nigerian intelligence agencies and the United States, he said it had been instrumental in the operation, which targeted Abu-Bilal al-Minuki, whom he described as the world’s second-highest-ranking ISIS terrorist. “The partnership with the Nigerian Armed Forces and Nigerian intelligence was exceptional, and that’s what really enabled that partnership to happen and to take out the number two terrorist in the world for ISIS,” Anderson said. He added that Nigeria had continued to conduct operations against ISIS following the May operation, while the United States had sustained its cooperation with Nigerian security forces. Anderson described the current security relationship between both countries as strong, saying the United States provides intelligence, specialised capabilities and training, while Nigeria contributes its knowledge of local and regional security conditions. “Some of it is intelligence, but also understanding of the terrorist network globally. And so Nigeria brings the regional and local understanding, while we bring the global network understanding, and together that becomes very powerful,” he said. He said the United States had provided training in intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance, as well as targeting, and would continue to consider requests for specialised training for Nigerian forces. On military operations, Anderson said the cooperation that happened in May in Borno State, within the Lake Chad Basin, saw both countries working to disrupt terrorist movements. However, he stressed that military assistance alone could not resolve Nigeria’s security challenges, including terrorism and kidnapping, arguing that investment in governance, development, education and economic opportunities was necessary to address their underlying drivers. “Ultimately, for the terrorism and insecurity, it needs to be an investment in governance, an investment in development,” he said, adding that sustainable opportunities could help prevent young people from turning to terrorism and criminal activities. On the withdrawal of Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger from ECOWAS and what it portends for security for the continent, the General said the United States was seeking to reopen dialogue with the three countries, now members of the Alliance of Sahel States, to strengthen cooperation against shared security threats. He said renewed engagement could facilitate intelligence sharing and training, but stressed that communication must first be re-established. Anderson also identified terrorist financing as a critical challenge, saying the United States could contribute global intelligence and cyber capabilities while Nigeria provides local knowledge of financial networks and money laundering methods. On maritime security, he said the United States had supported maritime operations centres, radar systems and emerging technologies to improve monitoring of the Gulf of Guinea and other West African waters. He identified piracy, smuggling, drug trafficking and illegal fishing as major concerns but said he could not confirm plans for additional vessel acquisitions. Assessing progress, Anderson said the increase in ISIS defections was one indicator of success, alongside reductions in attacks and violence. He also commended Nigeria’s programme to reintegrate defectors into society. He said AFRICOM would continue to focus its limited resources on priority threats and capable partners, while urging greater investment in local economic opportunities to channel Africa’s growing youth population into productive activities. “How do you take the growing youth population and channel that energy for a positive effort? And to me, that’s what we all need to work on, but it has to be done locally,” he said.

title: How EKOBA 81/82 Set is Preserving the Legacy of Eko Boys’ High School 44 Years After Graduation
body: Eko Boys’ High School alumni classes of 1981 and 1982 recently held their first grand reunion after over 44 years of graduating from the institution. The meeting, which brought together over 50 old boys of the 113-year-old institution, served as an opportunity for the alumni body to renew its commitment to preserving the school’s legacy for generations to come. Esther Oluku reports The popular axiom that 20 friends cannot play for 20 years did not apply on October 9, 2026, when the gates of Eko Boys’ High School, Mushin, Lagos, opened to over 50 former students who showed up for a reunion to honour the memory of their alma mater. Decked in immaculate white pants and shirts, some had the standard wine-coloured waistcoats to match, while others had wine vests and jackets. This recreation of the school’s uniform was sealed off with wine-and-white-coloured fez caps so that when the host called the meeting to order at a few minutes past 12 pm, all rose in unity to recite the school anthem, which had bound them together over forty-four years ago. This 2026 reunion is the first public reunion of the Eko Boys’ High School Old Boys Association (EKOBA) set of 1981/1982, taking the participants, now in their 60s, back in time. The Homecoming The event opened with a symposium on October 9th at the Reverend W.B. Euba Memorial Hall, bringing together present students of the school in conversation with the alumni body. The purpose of the meeting was to inspire students towards pursuing their individual dreams and aspirations. In his opening address, President, EKOBA 81/82, Mr. Johnson Folayan, stated that the meeting was a celebration of enduring friendship and a moment of giving back to the institution which had moulded them into accomplished men. “We walked through the gates of this school as young, ambitious boys. Today, we return as accomplished men and true custodians of a rich legacy. One of the starting points of this legacy is Eko Boys’ High School, and we can’t tell our story without the mention of the school. “This reunion is far more than a social gathering; it stands as a monument to our resilience, our lifelong friendships, and our unwavering commitment to giving back to the school that shaped our character. “Today (Friday, October 9, 2026), we are here to reconnect with ourselves and with our Almamater. This is the core of Reunion 2026, and I would advise us to take the opportunity in both ways,” he said. EKOBA National President, Mr. Tito Ganiyu Nurudeen, encouraged students to exert their minds and consciousness towards believing in the possibility of attaining their dreams. “If anyone says to you that is impossible,” he said, “they are lying to you. Your job is to settle down and do the best you can. There is no doubt in my mind that you will do extremely well.” He also urged students not to yield to the temptation of taking the easy path to success, saying that success requires time, discipline and determination. On his part, immediate Past President, EKOBA 81/82, Mr. Kayode Elliot, urged students to take advantage of the power of talent to attain success in life. “It is not everybody that will be successful in academics. That is why we have introduced the basketball court and the lawn tennis court. Also, pick an interest in sports. If academics is not working for you, then let sports work for you,” he said. Encouraging Academic Excellence Folayan, speaking during the symposium, stated that, in furtherance of the commitment of EKOBA 81/82 to encouraging academic excellence, the alumni body was opening a cash reward for the best graduating students of each class. The best graduating students from Senior Secondary School Three will get a cash reward of N100,000; the best graduating students from Senior Secondary School One and Two will get N75,000 each, while the best graduating students from Junior Secondary School One, Two and Three will get N50,000 each. Also, the EKOBA National President stated that, with the school’s recent upgrade to model school status, the association was working in collaboration with the state government to bring back the boarding arm of the school as it was four and a half decades ago. “To ensure that you do well in school, we are working with the Lagos State Ministry of Education right now. We are bringing the full boarding house and staff quarters to Eko Boys’ High School by September next year. “By September 2027, there will be a full boarding house with new students coming in. They will go into the boarding house and have time to study. They will be fed, clothed and disciplined,” he enthused. A Journey in Service Since its establishment as a social service club in 1996, EKOBA 81/82 has supported the school with a multi-million-naira basketball court, 13 computers, two table tennis sets, and a one-million-naira donation towards the construction of the Rev. Benjamin W. Euba Memorial Hall, among others. The reunion did not end as a celebration of memories alone. EKOBA 81/82 reaffirmed its commitment to impacting the institution that had nurtured them by donating a nine-room toilet block to the school. Speaking on the donation, Folayan explained that they had chosen the renovation of a nine-room toilet block to improve the hygiene level of the students. “When we got here, we realised that there was no toilet. As a matter of fact, the hygiene level was very, very bad. I couldn’t have entered the toilet to use it, and these were supposed to be our children growing up. “So, we felt that it was a need and the young boys should grow up knowing that there is a facility called a good toilet for the purpose of hygiene and for them to have that mental awareness that they can actually use good facilities too, like their mates,” he said. The facility is fitted with running water and was commissioned to serve the junior secondary school students of Eko Boys’ High School. In his remark, EKOBA National President, Tito Nurudeen, explained that while the toilet is one in a series of projects the EKOBA 81/82 Service Club has undertaken since its inception, the toilet project alone is valued at over six million naira. He added that, as part of plans to sustain the facility, the alumni body had hired dedicated staff to ensure that the toilet is always kept clean. The group, during the Gala Night on October 10, 2026, also launched a fundraiser targeted at procuring 20 air conditioning units for the Rev. W.B. Euba Hall, valued at eight hundred and fifty thousand naira (N850,000) each, amounting to a cumulative cost of seventeen million naira (N17,000,000). The presentation of the air conditioning units, Folayan said, would take place during the school’s Founder’s Day event next year. Reliving Past Memories For many attendees, the nostalgia of their younger days came in pockets of memories of how the school had shaped their journeys through various career paths into adulthood. Vice President, EKOBA 81/82, Mr. Dayo Oni, speaking on the sidelines of the Gala Night, said that the event presented an opportunity to relive youthful memories, share in the joy of seeing old schoolmates again, and reflect on life after many years apart. “I always want to give credence to God because there are few of us that started from class one; some along the way couldn’t make it. It is a good thing to have friends that we’ve seen in the last 45 years. “We had the homecoming, which was memorable, and we did a lot of things together. Those things we did when we were young, and we all had fun,” he said. Secretary General, EKOBA 81/82, Mr. Mike Oduniyi, said: “We thank God after 44, 45 years of leaving the school, God Almighty has kept us alive. The least among us is 60 years old. Therefore, we believe we should celebrate ourselves while we are still alive.” Eko Boys’ High School was founded by Rev. William Benjamin Euba on January 13, 1913, with a vision to provide high-quality education to less privileged children.

title: Upper East specialists seek urgent equipment boost as GMTF eases cancer care costs
body: Medical specialists in the Upper East Region have called for the swift delivery of diagnostic equipment to complement the financial relief provided by the Ghana Medical Trust Fund (GMTF). They say the Fund is helping patients afford specialised treatment, but better-equipped facilities are essential for early diagnosis and effective care, particularly for breast cancer. The appeal came during an engagement with GMTF management, led by Administrator Adjoa Obuobia Darko-Opoku, as part of its nationwide stakeholder consultations. The Medical Director of the Upper East Regional Hospital, Dr Joseph Kojo Tambil, commended the Fund for supporting several patients at the facility. He said the assistance relieved families who would otherwise struggle to pay for treatment. Expanding that support, he added, would help more patients with chronic conditions access specialised care. However, Dr Tambil urged the Fund to expedite the delivery of equipment promised to the hospital, particularly for breast cancer diagnosis. He said the equipment would strengthen diagnostic services, support early detection and improve treatment outcomes. A surgeon at the hospital, Dr Victor Dassa, highlighted the emotional and financial burden cancer places on patients and their families. He said treatment costs could severely strain household finances and prevent some patients from getting the care they need. Dr Dassa described the Fund as an important intervention for families facing these difficulties and stressed the need for sustained support. In response, Ms Darko-Opoku acknowledged the additional challenges patients face when they must travel long distances for specialised services. She said transport costs could compound the difficulties families already face in financing treatment. The Administrator explained that the Fund’s mandate extended beyond financial assistance. Access to quality care also depended on appropriate infrastructure, diagnostic equipment and specialised services. She stressed the importance of strengthening facilities in underserved communities to ensure that financial support translated into better patient care. The consultations aim to identify gaps in specialised healthcare, strengthen partnerships with medical professionals, and tailor the Fund’s interventions to patients’ and health facilities’ needs.

title: Jay-Z announced as Super Bowl LXI halftime show performer
body:
Jay-Z is taking the Super Bowl LXI halftime stage.
The rapper announced during Monday Night Football the he will be the Super Bowl LXI halftime show performer.
"From 'Reasonable Doubt' to standing on the Super Bowl Halftime stage, this has been a journey," Jay-Z said in a statement, referring to his debut album from 1996. "Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world's biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true."
Super Bowl LXI will take place on Sunday, Feb. 14, 2027, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.
Jay-Z's entertainment company Roc Nation produces the NFL's Super Bowl halftime show, leaving the "99 Problems" singer in charge of selecting the widely watched performer each year.
Roc Nation partners with the NFL and Apple Music on the annual halftime show.
NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said in a statement Monday that he has been waiting for Jay-Z to take the stage himself at the Super Bowl.
"When we first reached an agreement with Roc Nation to produce the show, I had just one request: that Jay-Z take the stage himself one day, whenever the moment felt right to him," Goodell said. "I couldn’t be more excited for fans around the world to experience the artistry, creativity and cultural impact he will bring to the Super Bowl stage.”
Super Bowl LXI will be the second Super Bowl hosted at SoFi Stadium, following Super Bowl LVI in 2022.
During Super Bowl LVI, Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg, Eminem, Mary J. Blige, Kendrick Lamar, 50 Cent and Anderson .Paak headlined the halftime show and performed a medley of their greatest hits.
The artists also honored Los Angeles with a celebration of West Coast hip-hop culture and local landmarks in the stage design.
Their performance won the Primetime Emmy Award for outstanding variety special (live) and also won Emmys for outstanding production design for a variety special and outstanding music direction.
During last year's Super Bowl, Bad Bunny took the stage during halftime at Levi Stadium in Santa Clara, California, bringing his Puerto Rican culture to the stage along with a collection of his hit songs.
The 2027 Super Bowl will air on ABC and ESPN and will be streamed on the ESPN App and NFL+ on mobile.
The Walt Disney Co. is the parent company of ABC News and ESPN.
24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

title: TOR slashes debt from $650m to $300m, MD reveals
body: The Tema Oil Refinery (TOR) has reduced its debt burden from $650 million to about $300 million under a restructuring programme supported by the Energy Sector Levies Act (ESLA), Mr Edmond Kombat, Managing Director (MD) of TOR, has announced. Mr Kombat said it has also settled its exposures to four banks, and the debt reduction formed part of broader efforts to restore the financial viability of the state-owned refinery. Delivering a speech on the refinery’s turnaround during the Government Accountability Series Press Conference at the Presidency in Accra recounted that when the National Democratic Congress (NDC) government handed over to the New Patriotic Party (NPP) administration in January 2017, the TOR was operational. The refinery has processed about five million barrels of crude in 2016, with about two million barrels remaining in storage at the time of the handover. Mr Kombat noted that key infrastructure and equipment had been secured, including the offshore mooring facility, into which approximately $90 million in capital was injected in March 2017, as well as a new furnace and boiler to support continued operations. The Managing Director indicated that the restructuring and infrastructure investments were aimed at positioning TOR to operate more efficiently and sustainably, reducing its reliance on state support while strengthening its contribution to Ghana’s downstream petroleum sector. He said the Refinery had also shown that Ghana could refine its own crude, stating that in December 2016, TOR received its first delivery of Ghanaian indigenous crude from the TEN field for domestic refining aboard MT Bodeira. He noted that by the time the current Management took office in 2025, TOR’s position had deteriorated. “The Company had accumulated losses of about GH¢10 billion, and its debt had risen from $300 million in 2016 to about US$517 million,” Mr Kombat said. He noted that the Crude Distillation Unit (CDU) had been out of operation since April 2021; while the Residue Fluid Catalytic Cracking (RFCC) Unit had been shut down since 2019. He said these major units had not received the required maintenance, and TOR had been reduced largely to renting out storage space to petroleum service providers, instead of carrying out its core mandate. Mr Kombat reiterated that they met a Refinery that was not refining and a tank farm used only for limited storage. He said much of the infrastructure was run down or obsolete, and 18 out of the refinery’s 59 storage tanks were out of service and that some of the storage tanks had been out of service since 2004. Mr Kombat said TOR had not filed audited financial statements for six consecutive years, 2019 to 2024; saying, “for six years, the Refinery had no Audited Accounts”. He said the Company owed GH¢200 million to the Ghana Revenue Authority and GH¢20 million to the SSNIT, in addition to amounts owed to the Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) and the Ghana Water Company as well as GH¢190 million in outstanding obligations to staff provident fund, retirees and resignees. The MD said TOR was several years delinquent in statutory payments. He said staff morale was low, staff were leaving, the workforce was divided, and more than 300 petitions over delayed promotions, some dating back to 10 years were awaiting review. Mr Kombat said the Refinery also owed other commercial entities and state-owned companies including Ghana National Petroleum Corporation (GNPC) and the Volta River Authority (VRA). “The refinery was on the verge of being sold or leased for $21m. By the end of 2024, TOR had negative equity of GH¢7.6billion,” the MD said. Mr Kombat noted that between 2019 to 2024, TOR sold third party products belonging to three petroleum services providers, valued at millions of dollars to pay staff salaries without the knowledge of the product owners. Touching on what had changed since May 2025, Mr Kombat said since May 2025, under President John Dramani Mahama’s Reset Agenda, Management of TOR had taken steps to rebuild the company from within, beginning with people and stronger cash controls. He said they reviewed the outstanding promotion petitions and addressed eligible cases and that they also extended the operating hours at the refinery’s loading gantry, improved cash controls and accountability in product handling, worked to restore confidence and won back private petroleum companies and regional partners to store and lift products at TOR. Mr Kombat said these measures formed part of Project Restore TOR, a broader recovery programme to return the refinery into operations, improve its financial position and prepare it for long-term sustainability. He reiterated that Management made the rehabilitation and restart of the Crude Distillation Unit (CDU) its immediate operational priority. He said a Turnaround Maintenance Committee was constituted, and the work was funded solely from TOR’s IGF and carried out by TOR’s engineers and technicians. This, he said, was necessary to address years of deferred maintenance and prepare the plant for safe and reliable operations.

title: Russia rejects findings of UN Commission on Ukraine — permanent mission
body:
UNITED NATIONS, October 27. /TASS/. Russia does not recognize the mandate of the Independent International Commission of Inquiry on Ukraine and rejects its findings as being based on fabricated data, Moscow’s permanent mission to the United Nations said in a statement, commenting on a report presented to the UN General Assembly.
"Russia does not recognize the mandate of the commission, which was established by a resolution adopted by the politicized UN Human Rights Council. The commission's conclusions are based on fabricated data provided by the Ukrainian authorities through the Kiev mission of the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights," the statement reads.
"The mission has long lost its neutrality, effectively turning into an agency seeking to legitimize allegations against Russia while failing to notice crimes committed by the Ukrainian armed forces," Russian diplomats said. In their view, the very existence and activities of the commission on Ukraine expose a crisis in the United Nations’ work that needs to be addressed.

title: ‘A national emergency’: Bay Area Israelis fly home to vote in pivotal election
body: This article was produced by J.–The Jewish News of Northern California in partnership with the Jewish Telegraphic Agency.Ayelet Frank was one of the first people to check in on Sunday, Oct. 25, for a nonstop flight from San Francisco to Tel Aviv. A resident of Redwood City, California, since she left Israel in 1984, she is flying back for one reason: to vote in the Oct. 27 election.It's the first time in her more than 40 years abroad that she is going back to cast a ballot.Election about Israel's very existence, Frank says“This election is unique. It's very different than any other,” she told J. “It's about Israel's very existence. This election is between the destruction of the country, or building it up in a positive way.”A native of Kibbutz Ein Harod in the Jezreel Valley, she is spending only two days in Israel before returning to California. It's a long way to travel just to vote, but, she said, “It's that important.” Frank was one of 271 passengers on El Al flight 48, which landed in Israel less than 24 hours before the polls open. It was the first nonstop flight from San Francisco to Israel since the Oct. 7, 2023 Hamas attack. Many on board were part of what one organizing group estimates is a wave of 67,000 Israelis abroad flying home for an election widely seen as a referendum on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. In a tight race, the Israel Democracy Institute said that many voters could swing nearly two Knesset seats.Those travelers are spending thousands of dollars for the chance to cast their ballots in what many are calling the most consequential election in Israel's history. The mood in the boarding area at the San Francisco International Airport was buoyant. Lots of people seemed to know one another and were running up to hug friends and chat excitedly. There were families with children and plenty of babies in strollers and carriers. There were a smattering of black kippahs as well as one Hasidic family. There were also Israeli residents returning home from vacation in the Bay Area. But judging from the conversations as well as from people interviewed by J., most passengers were Israeli expats flying back to vote. Capitola resident Udi Pardo left Israel in 1983, a year before Frank. Most of his family still lives in Israel and he visits twice a year. But for him, this was his first time flying home for an election. “I never tried to go and vote before because I don't live there,” he said. “But now it's a national emergency. I can't not go.”“Israel is on the verge of an abyss,” he continued, saying that he has not yet decided between Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar and Naftali Bennett's B'Yachad — both center-right parties opposed to Netanyahu's government. “We need to bring back sanity to Israel and to Israeli politics and reestablish liberal democracy because it's about to disappear.”First election since October 7 MassacreThe Oct. 27 election is the first since the Hamas attack and the war that followed. The stakes are so high, pundits say, that Israelis living abroad are flying home to vote in what appear to be unprecedented numbers. Israel does not allow absentee voting, except for diplomats and other state employees posted abroad, so expats who want to cast a ballot must do so in person.The 67,000 estimate comes from Fly & Vote, a project of the U.S.-based America Israel Democracy Coalition to help expats navigate the logistics of participating in the election. The group cautioned that the figure is based on a voluntary August survey and its own registration data, not a count of arrivals. No comparable data exists for previous elections.Israel's Likud-led government has tried to impede Fly & Vote's efforts with legal action, which was blocked in October by Israel's Supreme Court. The government reportedly also considered closing or slowing down traffic at Ben Gurion International Airport in the days before the election. Analysts say this is because Netanyahu and his allies believe that many, if not most, of those responding to Fly & Vote's initiative will vote against the current government. Indeed, that seemed to be true of most of the expats on this El Al flight from San Francisco. Every person interviewed spoke about the “need for change” in Israel's government, and those who declared their support for candidates mentioned either Eisenkot or leaders of other anti-Netanyahu parties. The Silicon Valley-based Israeli expat group UnXeptable, which emerged to protest Netanyahu's judicial overhaul and has become a major anti-Netanyahu voice globally, had a large presence on the flight, with about a dozen key members sporting light blue T-shirts emblazoned with the date of the election and the Hebrew words for “Flight for Change.” They were handing out shirts to any other passengers who would take them, some of whom put them on right away. Local TV stations showed up for an UnXeptable press conference held at the check-in counter.Roni Bar-Niv of Sunnyvale is one of several people interviewed who is spending just a few days in Israel, in her case enough time to vote, turn around and fly back to the Hebrew-language school she runs near her Silicon Valley home.In the 26 years since she left Givatayim, a suburb of Tel Aviv, Bar-Niv said, she visits Israel four or five times a year but she, too, has never flown back to vote until now.“I thought I didn't need to vote because I don't live there,” she said. But everything changed, she added, after Oct. 7. “If we pay taxes — we have an apartment there — and if we send money for the war effort, and if we have children there — my daughter made aliyah five years ago — we need to go and vote,” she said. “The direction our country is going is very bad, for Israelis living there and for us also.”Berkeley resident Rivka Amado left Jerusalem 22 years ago. A retired ethics professor and Ladino singer, she said it's the duty of Israeli expats to show up.“This election is critical, and it's important for every Israeli to vote, whether you live here or there,” she said. The surge in emigration since Oct. 7 has also swelled the pool of Israelis abroad. Some 82,800 Israelis left the country in 2024, according to Israel's Central Bureau of Statistics, up from 55,000 in 2023. More than 69,000 left in 2025, the Times of Israel reported, the second straight year that emigration outpaced immigration.Gilad Kariv, an opposition lawmaker from the Democrats party who chairs the Knesset's Diaspora Affairs Committee, has warned of a “tsunami of emigration,” according to the Jerusalem Post. He has called it a “strategic threat to the future of Israel” tied to the government's conduct. J Street regional director Shimrit Braun Kamin (left) hugs Galit Lipsitz Goldental near the El Al counter at San Francisco International Airport, Oct. 25, 2026. (Aaron Levy-Wolins/J. Staff/Report for America)Experts point to the war in Gaza and opposition to Netanyahu's judicial overhaul as driving forces, suggesting that many recent emigrants are critical of the government.Thirty-seven parties are on the Oct. 27 ballot, but only about a dozen are expected to clear the 3.25% electoral threshold needed to win Knesset seats. With Netanyahu's Likud party polling neck-and-neck with his main opponent, Eisenkot's Yashar party — the final pre-election polls show Yashar winning 22 to 23 seats to Likud's 19 to 21 — every seat matters. Neither party is projected to win a clear majority, meaning either one will have to negotiate intensely to form a governing coalition.That's why these expats have ponied up the dough, packed their bags and jumped on planes. Eyal, a tech designer in his 40s who has been living in Mountain View since 2004, declined to give his last name because of his former job in the Israeli military. This, too, is his first trip home to vote. In general, he said that he agrees with Israelis who believe expats should not have a voice in elections that no longer affect them personally. “But in this particular election, I think a lot of Israelis want us to come and vote,” he said. “I know my parents do.”Shlomi from Sunnyvale, who left Israel more than 15 years ago and also declined to give his last name, is worried that if there is not a new government, Israel's brain drain will accelerate.“We are in the final moments,” he said, likening Israel's political situation to a soccer game. “If the government doesn't change, I think a lot of good people who contribute to the future of the country will leave Israel.”Shlomi is also worried that Israel will lose its partnership with the United States. “It's not about right or left,” he said, declining to say how he'll vote. “It's about dignity, about taking responsibility, about leaders that actually make decisions for the people rather than their personal benefit.”Iddo Tal, a Jerusalem native, has lived in Palo Alto for 15 years, where he is a tech entrepreneur and teaches fundraising to startup founders around the world. He has launched “five start-ups and two kids,” he said, joking that “the kids have been a huge success.” Unlike most of those interviewed, he has traveled back to vote before. He made the trip to visit his parents but timed it around an election.“They always say every election is historic, and they're always right,” he said.Tal believes expats should vote, saying it keeps Israelis at home and abroad closely connected. “There's something very exciting about making the Israeli diaspora part of Israel [proper], by coming back to fight, to raise money, to vote,” Tal said.Hadar Aviram teaches law at UC Law San Francisco while studying to become a rabbi through Hebrew Union College. Born in Israel, she grew up “all over the world” and landed in San Francisco in 2001 for grad school. She wore one of the blue UnXeptable shirts and has joined some of the group's protests.“Let's start with taking accountability for the Oct. 7 massacre and the ensuing war,” she said. “And long before that, we were all hostages to this hateful, bigoted, corrupt government.… I'm flying to release us from him, and him from us.”She bristles at people who don't understand why Israelis like her feel so strongly about this election.“If some of those ignorant folks ask what Zionism is, I invite them to look around at all the people here who have packed their bags and emptied their savings accounts because they want to save their country,” she said, waving at the crowded boarding area. “When you love something very, very, very much, you are willing to go to great lengths to save it.”

title: ‘Ghana was very high risk, but we were fortunate’ – Prof Amuasi on 2014–15 Ebola outbreak
body: Ghana faced a very high risk of Ebola during the 2014–15 West African outbreak, despite recording no cases, Global Health Leader at the KCCR, Prof John Amuasi, has said. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Monday, he described Ghana’s escape as fortunate. He also questioned whether airport temperature checks can detect infected travellers. “Ghana was very high risk, but we were fortunate we did not get any cases,” he told host Kofi Agyei. His comments followed a question about whether Ghana’s lack of recorded cases reflected inadequate screening during the outbreak. Prof Amuasi explained that screening identifies people with possible symptoms. Testing must then establish whether they have the disease. He said headaches, fever and a generally sick appearance were not specific to Ebola. Detecting those symptoms alone could not confirm an infection. The regional experience showed how quickly the disease could cross borders. Nigeria’s outbreak began in July 2014, after an infected traveller arrived from Liberia. It recorded 20 cases and eight deaths. Senegal recorded one confirmed case and no deaths. Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone bore the greatest burden. The wider epidemic continued into 2016, with 28,610 reported cases and 11,308 deaths across those three countries, according to the US Centres for Disease Control and Prevention . For Prof Amuasi, monitoring travellers after arrival deserves greater attention. “The key is keeping tabs on every single person who is coming in,” he said. He suggested that authorities could consider mandatory check-ins for basic signs and symptoms every two to three days. “I mean, it’s going to be a bit painful, but maybe that’s a more efficient thing, better thing to do.” He ruled out testing every arriving passenger. “But certainly, we cannot introduce mass testing for Ebola for every single person there who lands. That’s not practicable.” At the time of the interview, he said Ghana had no confirmed or suspected case. He therefore stressed public awareness, particularly among people entering the country. “And right now, given that there is no confirmed or even suspected case in the country, there is really nothing more to do than make people aware.”

title: Anthropic discloses month-long training pause, AI security breaches in IPO filing
body: Anthropic paused training of its next-generation flagship AI model for more than a month over security concerns, while four of its AI agents accessed live external computer systems during testing, its initial public offering filing showed on Monday, October 26.
