The Claude maker said in the filing’s risk factors section that it had delayed pre-training of a new “frontier” base model to strengthen safeguards against the theft of model weights and intellectual property. The disclosure highlights the safety challenges facing developers of increasingly powerful AI models, some of whose creators have warned the technology could eventually escape human control. Rival OpenAI also paused some training earlier this year over safety concerns after its models hacked Hugging Face. The incidents illustrate how unexpected safety failures could disrupt development and deployment of models central to Anthropic’s growth as it prepares for a widely anticipated stock market debut. Anthropic warned that training pauses could delay revenue and leave it trailing competitors. The company devoted about 94 pages to risk factors, more than in its confidential filing seen by Reuters. Sandbox escape The filing also detailed previously undisclosed safety evaluation failures in which four AI models escaped their testing environments and accessed real-world computer systems, with sessions lasting between 10 and 34 hours. Anthropic said an error during cybersecurity tests with a third-party partner left the testing environment connected to the internet despite instructions that web access be disabled. In one instance, an early version of the model continued pursuing an impossible evaluation task, discovered a stored password and used it to gain administrator access to a third party’s system. It then obtained additional credentials, changed system settings and accessed an individual’s personal data. The filing did not identify the external parties involved. Anthropic said it notified all affected parties and found no evidence that the models had sought to evade human oversight or coordinate with each other. It subsequently suspended certain pre-release cybersecurity evaluations and paused higher-risk reinforcement learning environments. Separately, the company said on Sunday that Claude had bypassed a paywall and accessed publicly available aggregate voter counts from the US state of Georgia without human authorization. – Rappler.com

title: House of Consecration Ministry celebrates 15 years with four-day anniversary event
body: House of Consecration Ministry has marked its 15th anniversary with a four-day celebration under the theme “Revealing Jesus,” featuring prominent ministers of the Gospel, including Dr. Mensa Otabil, Archbishop Nicholas Duncan-Williams and Bishop Frank Ofosu-Appiah. The celebration brought together Christian leaders, members of the congregation and worshippers for preaching, prayer, praise and thanksgiving, reflecting on the ministry’s journey and its vision for the future. Founded in February 2011 by Rev. Kingsley Adjei Agyemang and his wife, Lady Ivy Adjei Agyemang, the ministry began as a small gathering at Social Welfare in Madina. By December that year, it had moved to its own premises and held its first prophetic crossover service. Fifteen years later, the anniversary celebration provided an opportunity to reflect on the ministry’s growth and reaffirm its commitment to teaching God’s Word and building believers in spiritual maturity. On the first day, Dr. Mensa Otabil after his sermon joined Rev. Kingsley and Lady Ivy for the dedication of the church premises, marked by the unveiling of a dedication plaque and a ribbon-cutting ceremony. For day two, Bishop Frank Ofosu-Appiah delivered a message emphasising spiritual maturity, vision and the importance of understanding and applying the Word of God. Archbishop Nicholas Duncan-Williams led an intense prayer session on day three, highlighting the importance of intercession, spiritual authority and praying for church and national leaders. The celebration also featured musical ministrations by Min. Becky Bonney, Min. Paolo, Efe Grace and Uncle Ato, whose performances enriched the sessions of praise and worship throughout the four-day event. The programme concluded with a Thanksgiving Service, during which the congregation expressed gratitude for the ministry’s 15-year journey and looked ahead to the years to come. Reflecting on the milestone, Rev. Kingsley Adjei Agyemang expressed gratitude to God for sustaining the ministry since its establishment and thanked his wife, Lady Ivy, the congregation, guest ministers, music ministers, volunteers and all who contributed to the success of the celebration. “Looking back at where we started in February 2011 and seeing what God has done over these 15 years fills our hearts with gratitude. What began as a small gathering in Madina has become a testimony of God’s faithfulness, and we do not take His grace for granted,” he said. He added that the support and commitment of those who participated in the celebration had made the occasion memorable. “As we celebrate this milestone, we recognise that there is more work to be done. Our commitment is to continue teaching the Word of God, building believers in spiritual maturity and revealing Jesus in our community and beyond,” he said. As House of Consecration Ministry enters its next chapter, its leadership remains focused on strengthening believers through biblical teaching, prayer and service, while building on the foundations established over the past 15 years. The anniversary marked not only a celebration of the ministry’s journey but also a renewed commitment to its mission, with its leadership expressing faith and expectation for the years ahead.

title: ROSOBORONEXPORT to Unveil “Anti-Drone Dome” Project at the Third Russia-Africa Summit
body:
ROSOBORONEXPORT JSC (part of the Rostec State Corporation) will unveil its latest Anti-Drone Dome concept for protecting the population, troops and facilities against drone attacks during the third Russia-Africa Summit, which will take place at Moscow’s Gostiny Dvor on October 28–29, 2026.
The Anti-Drone Dome is designed to protect the population, as well as strategic and infrastructure facilities, bridges, buildings, fuel & energy facilities, and troop deployment sites against drone attacks.
Options for protecting transport convoys and vehicles carrying high-profile persons or sensitive cargo are also offered.
The project was developed by ROSOBORONEXPORT in collaboration with leading Russian counter-UAS manufacturers and representatives from specialized law enforcement agencies. It is based on the practical experience gained in countering UAVs during military and counter-terrorism operations in recent years.
“Protecting critical infrastructure against UAVs has become a cornerstone of national and economic security, as well as a foundation for further technological development. A proper structure and the implementation of such a system contribute significantly to demonstrating the effectiveness of both government administration and business operations; they help safeguard supply chains and signal to investors that their investments are secure. ROSOBORONEXPORT offers to build a robust local C-UAS system adaptable to a specific partner and a specific facility. All the tools and solutions employed have proved effective in real-world conditions,” – stated Alexander Mikheev, Director General of ROSOBORONEXPORT .
The project is a multi-layered system comprising assets for airspace surveillance, engagement and electronic suppression of UAVs, a geoinformation system integrated into an automated command-and-control framework, and physical protection measures.
During the third Russia-Africa Summit, ROSOBORONEXPORT will present to its partners the concept itself, as well as solutions designed to build the “Anti-drone Dome.”
These include hard-kill countermeasures designed to physically destroy UAVs, such as the Pantsir-SMD-E ADMS and Pantsir-S1M ADMGS (developed by High-Precision Systems), the Verba MANPADS, the TKB-1167 aerial target engagement system, as well as Rostec’s Citadel 30mm air defence artillery system which fires shrapnel airburst rounds.
In the very near future, the range of hard-kill countermeasures against UAVs will be expanded to include mass-produced laser systems, as well as electromagnetic pulse (EMP) systems currently in the final stages of testing.
The Company is also presenting detection and electronic countermeasures (ECM) systems designed to disrupt drone control and navigation channels such as the Silok, Repellent-Patrol, Sky-Hunter 4PC and Radeskan in the Anti-Drone version.
The “Anti-Drone Dome” is a comprehensive system; its components and functionality are tailored to the specific requirements of each customer, taking into account the unique characteristics of the facility being protected.
All of its components have been developed and are manufactured in Russia.

title: Jordan’s unity remains its strongest defence
body: Last Friday, gunmen opened fire at St George’s Greek Orthodox Church in the village of Hamoud in Jordan’s Karak governorate, killing nine people and injuring 40. The attack, which authorities have described as a "heinous act of terrorism”, was intended as a deadly strike on the Hashemite kingdom’s Christian community and its social fabric. Yet far from sowing division in its society, it appears to have galvanised a country already dealing with challenges on a number of fronts. This is both noteworthy and encouraging. Jordan has had to deal with numerous attacks in the past months. Missiles and drones linked to Iran threaten its security. War rages in neighbouring Lebanon. Its border with Syria remains vulnerable to drug-smuggling networks . Unrest in the West Bank carries risks for it. It is home to millions of Palestinian and Syrian refugees. And yet with each challenge, Jordanians have risen to the occasion. Friday’s attack was intended to do more than just kill and wound ordinary, defenceless people attending the funeral of a loved one. By taking aim at a church, the objective was to strike at the principle that Jordanians of different faiths belong equally to their country. It is notable, then, that moments after the attack, King Abdullah II insisted that such dastardly acts won’t undermine national unity . “What happened today was an attack on all Jordanians,” he said. Prime Minister Jafar Hassan also struck a defiant tone as he blamed “blind extremism” for the attack. “We will not allow society to go down this path,” he added. Terrorism seeks to create cleavages that outlast any attack, and such aims should not be given oxygen The overwhelming response from Jordanians of all walks, from political leaders to members of the clergy to ordinary citizens, has been one of unity . People from across the country travelled to Hamoud to attend the victims’ funeral at the same church, offering support and succour to those bereaved, with a clear message that their Christians brothers and sisters are part of their country’s history and future. The presence of Queen Rania and Crown Prince Hussein, and other members of the royal family at the funeral reinforced that message. Leaders from around the world have also expressed solidarity with Jordan. Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, conveyed the UAE’s support for Jordan, reflecting a regional recognition that attacks on civilians and places of worship threaten everyone’s security and prosperity. Security will no doubt dominate Jordanian national conversation in the foreseeable future. Within days of King Abdullah ordering security forces to respond with “an iron fist”, three suspects have been arrested . More are likely to follow. But while counter-terrorism missions should be given their space to tackle the more immediate threats, it’s important never to lose sight of the longer-term challenge of consistently dealing with extremism at a societal level. It is also important to keep in mind all that makes Jordan a dynamic and pluralistic society, and a country that people around the region and the world hold in high regard. Terrorism seeks to create cleavages that outlast any attack, and such aims should not be given oxygen. Whether it is excusing violence, or casting minorities as outsiders, such thinking could end up advancing the same divisive purpose. Put simply, the key is knitting a strong social fabric. Jordan has shown once more that its social fabric remains its biggest asset.

title: UAE's AI power advantage faces its biggest test yet
body: For most of the AI boom , the bottleneck was chips . Increasingly, it is electricity . In the US, the world’s largest data centre market , the grid interconnection queue holds about 2,300GW of projects, and new AI campuses can wait years for the electricity they need. TrendForce estimates that by 2030, global data centre demand could exceed available grid capacity by more than 250GW. That shift has made the UAE’s natural advantage – abundant energy and the ability to build quickly – valuable. The question is whether that advantage can be sustained. What is being built Two projects are often confused. The UAE-US AI Campus is the master plan, a site of about 26 square kilometres near Abu Dhabi designed to host up to 5GW of data centres. Stargate UAE is its first phase, a 1GW cluster built by G42 with OpenAI, Oracle, Nvidia, Cisco and SoftBank. Its first 200MW are expected to come on line this year. Everything beyond that first phase remains on paper. The power ledger Abundance is a claim that should be tested with numbers. The UAE consumed about 173TWh of electricity in 2025, according to Wood Mackenzie. Data centres used about 3TWh hours of that, or 2 per cent. What AI demand means for the UAE grid Measure Figure Source UAE electricity demand, 2025 About 173TWh Wood Mackenzie Data centre demand, 2025 About 3TWh, 2% of total Wood Mackenzie Stargate UAE at 1GW, full load About 8.8TWh a year, 5% of national demand Author’s calculation Full 5GW campus, full load About 44TWh a year, a quarter of national demand Author’s calculation Barakah nuclear plant 5.6GW, about 21% of output Plant data, Wood Mackenzie The maths is striking. Running at full load, Stargate’s first gigawatt alone would use almost three times as much electricity as every data centre in the country does today. The full campus would add demand equal to a quarter of current national consumption. No country has that much spare capacity sitting idle. It has to be built. The UAE is building it, and that is where the advantage becomes concrete. This year, Masdar and the Emirates Water and Electricity Company (Ewec) reached financial close on a $6.1 billion project that pairs 5.2GW of solar with 19GWh of batteries to deliver 1GW of round-the-clock power. Due in 2027, it is the first project of its kind at this scale. Taqa and Ewec are also building a 1GW gas-fired plant at Al Dhafra, financed at $980 million, specifically to supply data centres. Add Barakah’s nuclear baseload and existing gas-fired capacity, and few markets can assemble firm, low-cost power as quickly. Speed is the real competitive edge. In the UAE, state-backed entities plan generation, transmission and much of the demand together. In the US, a developer can wait years in a queue behind other projects. That co-ordination, more than the energy itself, is the advantage competitors find hardest to copy. Capacity is not delivery Generating power is one task. Delivering it reliably and cleanly to the right sites is another. Wood Mackenzie notes that the UAE does not yet permit corporate or virtual power purchase agreements, and that renewables are procured only through utility auctions. For hyperscalers with clean-energy commitments, that limits how they can buy green power – a gap rival hubs may close first. The regional war has added a harder test. In March, Iranian strikes damaged two Amazon Web Services data centres in the UAE, and in April an Iranian military video named Stargate as a target. In September, Reuters reported that the UAE was reworking the 5GW master plan into a network of smaller sites, with underground facilities, air defences and duplicated power and cooling. The first phase is going ahead, though it is unclear how far it has progressed. This month, Mohsen Rezaei, a former commander of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, warned that data centres and AI facilities across the region could be targeted if the conflict resumed. Dispersal changes the power equation. Every additional site needs its own grid connection, backup generation and cooling. Large AI training runs also work best when chips sit close together, so splitting clusters can reduce performance. The UAE’s power advantage now has to be delivered to more places, at higher cost, and defended by military force. What would make the advantage last Keep supply ahead of demand . The 2027 round-the-clock solar project and new gas capacity are the right signals. Further phases of the campus should be matched, gigawatt for gigawatt, with committed new generation. Open the market for clean power . Allowing corporate power purchase agreements would let global tech companies meet their own climate targets in the UAE, removing a reason to build elsewhere. Price resilience into the offer . Hardened, redundant sites cost more, but that protection is also a selling point. Few markets can promise capacity that is protected by design. Secure the chips that use the power . The UAE’s access to advanced US chips without individual licences runs until about April 2027. Power without processors is idle capacity. The verdict The UAE does not control the world’s energy for AI. But it holds a natural advantage in abundant, low-cost power, and a structural one in its ability to plan and build at speed. On current evidence, that combination is real and is already attracting the world’s leading AI companies. It becomes a lasting strategic advantage only if the UAE proves it can deliver that power securely, to dispersed sites, through a regional war. That is the test of the next two years. Andrea Zanon is senior adviser to entrepreneurs and global leaders, with more than 20 years of experience in economic strategy, market access and geopolitical risk

title: EU official calls for urgent action to keep path to peace open in Yemen
body: A senior EU official has called for concrete action "in the coming days" to halt renewed fighting in Yemen and salvage the possibility of a political solution. In an interview with The National , the EU ambassador to Yemen, Patrick Simonnet, warned the recent escalation threatens not only civilian lives but also years of diplomatic progress aimed at ending the conflict. "Concrete steps are needed in the coming days, rather than weeks, to halt the escalation , protect civilians and ease their suffering," he said. As Yemen faces renewed hostilities and mounting uncertainty over its political future, Mr Simonnet stressed that military action alone cannot end the country's protracted conflict. “The path to a political settlement has unfortunately become more difficult, but it remains essential," he told The National. "The challenges have grown, but so has the urgency of finding a political solution that delivers lasting peace for Yemen and security for its neighbours." "Military developments may change the situation on the ground, but they cannot, on their own, resolve the underlying political differences or deliver lasting stability," he added. The ambassador's warning comes amid a sharp escalation in fighting in Yemen that has threatened to unravel years of relative calm following a UN-brokered truce in 2022. On October 9, UN special envoy Hans Grundberg warned that Yemen had "slid back into full-scale war ", with hostilities spreading across multiple front lines. Yemen's already fragile peace process was tested in February when it became entangled in the wider regional conflict involving the US, Iran and Israel. The latest Houthi escalation began in July when the rebels launched a campaign and seized Yemen’s western coast. The Yemeni government and the Saudi-led coalition responded with air strikes and a counter-attack , while the Iran-backed Houthis intensified strikes on Saudi cities at an unprecedented pace. They have since launched deadly attacks on Saudi civilian airports , oil installations and military sites, turning the kingdom into a pressure point in the wider regional war. The Houthis have been fighting the Yemeni government since seizing Sanaa in 2014. Saudi Arabia intervened in 2015 at the head of a coalition of regional allies to support the government against the rebels. But de-escalation beyond the country's borders would not, on its own, resolve its internal divisions, Mr Simonnet said. "Yemen’s conflict has its own roots, but it has become increasingly intertwined with regional tensions. Both dimensions must be addressed ," he told The National. "Regional de-escalation would help, but Yemen still needs an inclusive political settlement that addresses Yemenis’ own concerns and aspirations. We must therefore keep Yemen’s political process alive." Humanitarian fall-out Beyond the need for a political settlement, Mr Simonnet stressed that Yemen's humanitarian crisis and the needs of its people must not be overlooked amid growing international concern over regional security. "Yemen has returned to international attention, but sadly because of renewed escalation and its implications for regional security. The concern is that this attention focuses primarily on missiles and shipping routes, while Yemenis’ political aspirations and daily needs receive less consideration," he told The National. "Families need food, clean water, health care, education and a reliable income. They also need a credible prospect of peace. Keeping those priorities at the centre of our engagement is essential," he added. The ambassador emphasised the need to "translate renewed international attention into sustained engagement with Yemen’s people, its economy and its institutions". "Humanitarian assistance must reach those who need it, and Yemenis must have a meaningful voice in shaping their country’s future," he said. The latest escalation has compounded Yemen's humanitarian crisis, displacing more than 250,000 people since June 2026, according to UN figures. Mr Simonnet expressed deep concern over Houthi attacks in Aden and the prolonged siege of Taiz , which has further restricted access to scarce essential supplies. "We have strongly condemned the attacks on the Maashiq presidential compound and Aden airport, and called on the Houthis to immediately lift their siege of Taiz and allow food, water, medicines and fuel into the city. These attacks must stop, and civilians and civilian infrastructure must be protected," he told The National. Mr Simonnet said the bloc remains committed to supporting Yemen's government and people, with an immediate focus on efforts to end the escalation, protect civilians and address growing humanitarian needs. On Sunday, the EU announced the allocation of €22.5 million in humanitarian aid to Yemen, in addition to the €87.5 million previously allocated for 2026, to "address the consequences of the renewed conflict escalation and the critical needs of millions of people".

title: Oleshky ceasefire begins, Budanov says
body:
A localized ceasefire in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky has been "expanded… within Kherson (Oblast)," U.S. First Lady Melania Trump said in a post on social media on Oct. 27.
The ceasefire, which came into effect in the early hours of the morning, initially covered Oleshky and surrounding areas in Kherson Oblast and is meant to allow the safe evacuation of civilians and the delivery of humanitarian aid over the coming days.
Trump did not specify the extent of the expanded ceasefire but Tetiana Shelest, head of communications for Ukraine's human rights ombudsman, Dmytro Lubinets, told reporters it now covered the entirety of Kherson Oblast.
According to a statement from Lubinets, the ceasefire was being "fully honored," with Ukraine and Russia adhering to the agreement as of 5:30 p.m. on Oct. 27.
"I hope that everything will continue in accordance with the agreed plan and that we will be able to help the civilians in Oleshky who are eagerly awaiting assistance," he added.
Oleshky has been under Russian occupation since the early days of the full-scale invasion. Located just across the Dnipro River from Kherson , it has been effectively blockaded by Russian forces, who prevent humanitarian aid from entering.
Residents face severe shortages of food, water, and electricity. Mined roads and constant drone attacks make safe evacuation virtually impossible, and civilians trying to flee on the only roads in and out of the city are frequently targeted by drones.
Trump added that the timing was accelerated by two days to protect civilians and facilitate the delivery of humanitarian aid.
THE CEASEFIRE HAS COMMENCED The ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia took effect at 4:00am Moscow time on October 27, 2026. Timing was accelerated two days ahead of schedule to protect the safety of civilians and to facilitate the delivery of critical humanitarian aid. The…
Earlier, Kyrylo Budanov, head of the Office of the President of Ukraine, confirmed a "bilateral ceasefire" began in the embattled Oleshky, in a statement on Oct. 27.
The ceasefire will last until Nov. 1, David Arakhamia , the parliamentary leader of the president's Servant of the People party, said in a later post on social media. Lubinets added that the ceasefire will remain in effect until 10:59 p.m. Kyiv time on Nov. 1.
The agreements were reached in negotiations with Yana Lantratova, head of the Russian negotiating team.
The Russian Defense Ministry announced that Russian forces had stopped fighting in the area in preparation for the humanitarian mission.
Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said on Oct. 27 that the Russian military would provide all details of the humanitarian operation in Oleshky, as reported by the Russian state news agency TASS. He added that there were no reports of ceasefire violations as of 11 a.m. Kyiv time.
The Russian-installed head of occupied Kherson Oblast, Volodymyr Saldo , claimed on Oct. 27 that temporary accommodation for residents evacuated from Oleshky had been prepared in the other occupied part of Kherson Oblast, occupied Crimea, and in other Russian regions, Russian media reported.
He added that Oleshky residents will have a choice – either to stay in Russia or to travel to Ukrainian-controlled territory "to reunite with their families."
According to Saldo, the humanitarian mission is scheduled to begin on October 29, while the mined road to Oleshky is currently being cleared.
The Ombudsman's office representatives told Oleshky residents that the demining mission has already started, but the evacuation of the civilians will start on Oct. 30, the Kyiv Independent learned.
The worsening humanitarian crisis in the city has drawn international attention in recent weeks, including from Pope Leo XIV.
Lubinets said on Sept. 16 that more than 6,000 people may remain in Oleshky and the surrounding area, including about 200 children. His office said it had previously verified 358 people who urgently need assistance to leave safely.
In spring 2026, evacuation volunteers still managed to help Oleshky residents leave for other occupied settlements in Kherson Oblast or Ukraine-controlled areas in exhausting multi-day trips through Russia and Belarus. But in recent months, dangers posed by drone attacks, artillery fire, and mined roads have made evacuation by road almost impossible .
Within minutes of the Oleshky ceasefire beginning, Russian forces launched a wave of ballistic missiles at other parts of Ukraine, including Kyiv .

title: Will the public change its mind about Meghan?
body: The allegations of sexual abuse against Thomas Markle have put his daughter Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, under an uncomfortable spotlight. She has been dealing with this potential news time bomb out of sight for seven years, while sharing so much about her life in TV series and interviews. Thomas Markle has strongly rejected the claims as “lies” used to destroy his reputation. But could this complicated story prove to be a turning point for Meghan, who has had a complicated and often hostile relationship with the UK public? What has emerged so far calls into question some of the criticism she’s faced. Thomas Markle has strongly denied the allegations against him Meghan, who recently moved back to the UK with Prince Harry and their children, has frequently been accused of cutting off those once close to her. Her treatment of her father was seen as a prime example. “She ditched her family, ditched her dad, ditched most of her old friends, split Harry from William,” wrote one commentator in 2020. “Get on a plane and go see the poor man before it’s too late,” she was told on social media about her father. All of that might need to be viewed in a different and more sympathetic light. By 2019, Meghan had received disturbing allegations about Thomas Markle in a letter from her father’s first wife, Roslyn Loveless. She says that is why she kept her distance and didn’t bring her children to him, including when she moved to the United States with her family. The police shared that letter with Meghan when she was classified as a working royal. It’s not clear who else knew about the letter, including Palace officials, but it must have been a sensitive matter for her. According to the Sussexes’ spokesman, Meghan believed an investigation into the allegations was underway, presumably while she was on official trips and had to put on a brave face. There was also criticism levelled at Meghan in December 2025 when her father was in hospital in the Philippines, undergoing the amputation of his leg. “I don’t want to die estranged from Meghan. I want to meet my grandkids. It might be nice to meet her husband too,” Markle told the Mail on Sunday at the time. There was a media storm about whether Meghan was going to reach out to her father, culminating in a letter being delivered from her to her father, which at the time was assumed to be well-wishes. But that whole episode looks different in hindsight. That letter was far more fraught. It revealed that Meghan knew about the allegations against her father. We now understand that Meghan was telling him he would never see his grandchildren. Thomas Markle has strongly denied all the allegations against him, saying they are “sick lies” which are trying to destroy his reputation. His daughter Samantha Markle has also rejected the claims, saying the stories are “fake news” and “clickbait”. “There will be no legal action against my dad with no evidence in so many flimsy stories and my dad never had access to any such content and was in the hospital most of the time that he was there,” she wrote on X on Sunday. Samantha also challenges the credibility of the letter written by her mother, Roslyn Loveless, which was shared with Meghan in 2019 and contained details of allegations of sexual abuse against Thomas Markle. Thomas Markle in a photo with his daughter Meghan When you look through photos of Meghan at events over the last seven years, you wonder what was going on behind the familiar smile. Those years have seen Netflix films, a tell-all memoir by Prince Harry, cookery series, podcasts and TV interviews. But a hidden narrative has been running in the background. Meghan’s supporters have pointed to other factors in how she has been treated, with racism and sexism part of that toxic mix. But maybe there was also a sense of not knowing the authentic person behind the polished Brand Meghan. On Instagram, she has curated her life to look idyllic, but perhaps she’ll get a more generous hearing now that her back story is as messy and imperfect as everyone else’s. It could still be an uphill struggle to become more popular, beyond her own vocal, core group of supporters. A survey from YouGov earlier this month found 22% of people had a positive view of Meghan, compared with 49% who dislike her. That suggests there is still some way to go before Meghan fully wins the trust of the public. Fascination, yes. But affection, not always. For the British public, Californian Meghan hasn’t always translated well. But perhaps this complex, still developing story – and the light it sheds on previous years – might mean there’s a more rounded view of her in the future.

title: Michael Eamon elected mayor of Peterborough, Ont. with 36.5% of the vote
body:
The early bird does get the worm as Michael Eamon, the first candidate to file nomination papers in his community, was elected mayor of the City of Peterborough, Ont., on Monday night.
Eamon entered his name into the mayoral race on May 1, and then six other candidates came forward as Mayor Jeff Leal this summer announced he would not be seeking re-election.
With all seven tabulator locations reporting, Eamon received 10,867 votes — 36.5 per cent of the 29,773 votes cast.
He finished well ahead of runner-up Neil Morton, who received 7,372 votes (24.8 per cent) and longtime city councillor Keith Riel with 5,990 votes (20.1 per cent).
Other candidates included Rebecca Schillemat (2,526 votes or 8.5 per cent), Trent University student Jacob Méthot (1,112 votes or 3.7 per cent), Brian Lumsden (1,106 votes or 3.7 per cent) and Rob Hailman (800 votes or 2.7 per cent). Lumsden previously ran for mayor in 2022, finishing with 2.78 per cent of the votes.
Eamon, principal of the Catharine Parr Traill College at Trent University, also teaches history but his professional experience focuses on administration and management on the federal government level in Ottawa and at Trent. Along with four history degrees, Eamon also holds certificates in project management, project planning and control, procurement, change management and cultural resource management.
In a statement, Eamon commended the other candidates in a “long,” six-month campaign and praised their efforts and dedication.
“You brought many good ideas to the table. And you made it abundantly clear how much you care for this community,” said Eamon. “I hope you will continue to use your skills for the betterment of our city.”
Eamon specifically thanked Riel for his 16 years as a councillor for Ward 4 (Ashburnham).
The mayor-elect also offered his congratulations to all the candidates who were elected to council.
“Enjoy your well-earned victories. We have a lot of work ahead of us,” he said. “I’m looking forward to working with each and every one of you. I look forward to meeting with you in the coming weeks to learn about your priorities so we can hit the ground running after the inauguration. And to everyone who ran — Thank you! We can’t have a democracy without caring, committed people who come forward every four years to offer their skills and their service to make the city better.”
Eamon will be joined on city council with five incumbents and five new councillors.

title: OpenAI Launches GPT-6.1 Terra, Halving GPT-6.1 Sol’s API Price for Agent Work
body: OpenAI has released GPT-6.1 Terra , a fast model for visual reasoning, computer use and writing. It replaces GPT-5.6 Terra and is live in the API as gpt-6.1-terra . Standard pricing is $1 per million input tokens and $5 per million output tokens . For teams automating screens, forms and documents at volume, GPT-6.1 Terra changes the cost math. TL;DR Size: 1.05M-token context, 128K max output. Runs on: OpenAI-hosted only (API, ChatGPT Work, Codex). Closed weights. Performance: Near GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra on vision and computer use, at lower cost. Best: 85.5% on MMMU-Pro (Vision) at max effort, 1.2 points behind GPT-6 Astra. Worst: 50.3% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, behind GPT-6.1 Sol (55.9%) and Claude Sonnet 5.5 (70.6%). What is GPT-6.1 Terra? GPT-6.1 Terra is an OpenAI reasoning model built for high-volume visual and computer-use work. It accepts text and image input and returns text . The context window is 1,050,000 tokens, with up to 128,000 output tokens. Its knowledge cutoff is June 1, 2026. Reasoning effort runs from none to max , with medium as the default. Tool calling requires the Responses API. Supported tools include computer use, hosted shell, code interpreter, web search, file search and MCP. OpenAI’s listed use cases include matching product photos to catalog entries and interpreting technical drawings. How does GPT-6.1 Terra perform on computer use? OpenAI’s main influential test is Agents’ Last Exam v1 , a set of professional computer tasks. One task turns architectural drawings into a 3D model. At medium effort, Terra scores 57.6% at $0.29 per task. GPT-5.6 Terra scored 42.6% at $0.84 on the same setting. GPT-6 Astra also scores 57.6% at medium, but costs $4.82 per task. At max effort, Terra reaches 60.0% at $1.01 per task. Claude Opus 5.5 scores 63.2% at $8.82 per task on the same chart. OpenAI says Terra completes tasks over 3 times faster than GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol. On the OSWorld 2.1 offline set, Terra scores 66.7% at medium and 74.2% at max. GPT-5.6 Terra peaked at 57.1%. GPT-6.1 Sol reaches 78.0%, GPT-6 Astra 80.9% and Claude Sonnet 5.5 83.9%. How strong is its visual reasoning? On MMMU-Pro (Vision), Terra scores 85.5% at max effort. GPT-6.1 Sol scores 86.3% and GPT-6 Astra 86.7%. GPT-5.6 Terra topped out at 81.7%. Terra’s max-effort run costs $0.012 per task, against $0.065 for Astra. window.addEventListener("message",function(e){if(e.data&&e.data.mtpTerraH){var f=document.getElementById("mtp-t61-frame");if(f){f.style.height=e.data.mtpTerraH+"px";}}}); Did factuality and coding improve? On OpenAI’s internal set of error-inducing prompts, the low-effort error rate fell from 53.6% to 16.7%. At max effort, it fell 18 points to 4.3%. The set is adversarial by design, so production error rates will differ. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, Terra solves 50.3% at max effort, up from 21.5% for GPT-5.6 Terra. It still trails GPT-6.1 Sol (55.9%), GPT-6 Astra (58.2%) and Claude Sonnet 5.5 (70.6%). OpenAI itself recommends Sol or Astra for the most complex coding tasks. On Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1, Terra scores 58.3% at $4.15 per task. That beats GPT-6.1 Sol’s 57.0% at $5.47. Claude Opus 5.5 with fallbacks scores 63.3% at $23.21. How much does GPT-6.1 Terra cost, and where is it available? Standard API pricing is $1 input, $0.05 cached input and $5 output per million tokens. Batch and Flex are 50% cheaper. Fast mode costs 2x Standard. Prompts above 272K input tokens bill at 2x input and 1.5x output. That is half of GPT-6.1 Sol’s $2/$10 and one-tenth of GPT-6 Astra’s $10/$50 . Claude Opus 5.5 lists at $4/$20. In ChatGPT, Terra is live for Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex. GPT-6.1 Terra vs competitors Feature GPT-6.1 Terra GPT-6.1 Sol GPT-6 Astra Claude Opus 5.5 Claude Sonnet 5.5 Parameters Not disclosed Not disclosed Not disclosed Not disclosed Not disclosed Context window 1.05M 1.05M 1.05M 1M 1M Max output 128K 128K 128K 128K 128K Knowledge cutoff Jun 1, 2026 Apr 30, 2026 Apr 30, 2026 Jun 2026 Jun 2026 API price (in/out per 1M) $1 / $5 $2 / $10 $10 / $50 $4 / $20 $2 / $10 Weights Closed Closed Closed Closed Closed Agents’ Last Exam v1 (max) 60.0% ($1.01/task) 58.6% ($2.00/task) 59.3% ($7.24/task) 63.2% ($8.82/task) Not shown MMMU-Pro Vision (max) 85.5% 86.3% 86.7% Not shown Not shown OSWorld 2.1 offline (max) 74.2% 78.0% 80.9% Not shown 83.9% Terminal-Bench 4.0 (max) 50.3% 55.9% 58.2% Not shown 70.6% Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 (max) 58.3% 57.0% 68.1% 63.3% (with fallbacks) Not shown Benchmark scores and per-task costs are read from OpenAI’s launch charts and are self-reported. Specs and prices come from each vendor’s model page. Claude prices: Anthropic pricing . Key Takeaways GPT-6.1 Terra costs $1/$5 per million tokens, half of GPT-6.1 Sol. It matches GPT-6 Astra’s 57.6% on Agents’ Last Exam at $0.29 per task. MMMU-Pro hits 85.5%, within 1.2 points of Astra. Coding still lags: 50.3% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 vs Sonnet 5.5’s 70.6%. All scores are OpenAI-reported; parameters and hardware are undisclosed. Check out the OpenAI announcement , the API model page and the system card addendum . title: Ban or tiered limits? Meta, gov’t agencies discuss child online safety
body: MANILA, Philippines – As Congress moves to reconcile legislation prohibiting minors from accessing social media and other high-risk digital services, Meta, the company behind Facebook and Instagram, hosted a forum to discuss children’s online safety on Monday, October 26, at the Ayala Malls Glorietta Activity Center. Meta, together with the Department of Information and Communications Technology-Cybercrime Investigation and Coordinating Center (DICT-CICC), Department of Education (DepEd), National Youth Commission (NYC), and other stakeholders, hosted the forum to kick off the Digital Dialogue In Real Life, a free interactive exhibition that aims to take a comprehensive approach to youth digital well-being in the Philippines. The exhibit will run from Monday, October 26 to Friday, October 30. The forum covered what platforms and families can do, from parental controls to conversations at home. This comes after incidents of school violence were reported nationwide, with investigators examining possible online influences , and as lawmakers weigh bills restricting minors’ access to social media. ‘Not yet satisfied’ with platforms’ commitment During Meta’s event, DICT-CICC Director IV Noel Carlo Gracilla said that “children’s safety cannot be matched by promises alone.” “Although we have secured [the platforms’] commitments, the CICC is not yet satisfied…. What we need to see is their action and effective solutions that will leave good results for our young people,” Gracilla said in his welcome message, speaking in Filipino. He did, however, credit Meta’s quick responses to CICC requests with helping curb young people’s exposure to inappropriate content. He said the agency met in recent months with Discord, Reddit, Meta, and Roblox to raise concerns about their in-app safety features, especially for content unsuitable for minors. At least eight incidents of school violence in the Philippines have been reported in 2026, including three deadly school shootings. Such incidents have prompted authorities to seek commitments from social media platforms. Must Watch What school shootings in PH have in common In August , after the second deadly shooting took place in Zamboanga City , the DICT said Meta and Roblox had agreed to enhance child-safety protections for users in the Philippines, including age verification and parental controls. Senator Risa Hontiveros also said in the same month that the Philippine government had secured a commitment from Meta to provide user data to law enforcement when there is an imminent threat of violence. Ban or tiered limits? Meta kicked off the exhibit with a forum to explore practical ways to address the risks children face online today. Among the panelists were: Gio Tingson, head of public policy, Meta Philippines Joseph Francisco Ortega, chairperson, NYC Razzel Requesto, director IV, DepEd Ysrael Diloy, child protection specialist, Stairway Foundation Niel Steve Kintanar, external relations officer, Psychological Association of the Philippines Mariel Kliatchko, influencer mom and school owner The forum took place as Congress weighs whether to ban children from social media altogether. Under the Senate-approved Safe Media Access and Responsible Technology for Kids in Digital Spaces (SMART KIDS) bill, social media accounts determined as being owned or used by a minor will be suspended, restricted, disabled, or removed. It will also prevent users below 18 years old from creating accounts. Diloy argued that a ban would push children out of online spaces where they have rights to expression and information. “The rights holders are the children. The duty bearers are us, the adults. It’s our obligation to ensure the safety of the spaces the children move in, and to ensure that the children reap the benefits of technology,” Diloy said in Filipino. “What we’re hoping for is for tech platforms to have accountability and responsibility,” Diloy said, adding that Meta’s launch of Teen Accounts with parental supervision tools is a welcome step. Must Read Why Congress should think twice about banning under-18s from social media Meta’s Digital Dialogue IRL builds on its Screen Smart Philippines initiative, launched in June, which educates parents and teens about the safety features built into Teen Accounts across its products: Instagram, Facebook, Messenger, and Threads. The protections in Teen Accounts include default private accounts, messaging restrictions, sensitive content limits, daily 60-minute time limit reminders, and a “sleep mode” that mutes notifications between 10 pm and 7 am. Teens cannot opt out or loosen these settings without a parent’s permission. “Learning from other jurisdictions, without naming any country, we saw that bans are ineffective,” Tingson told Rappler on the sidelines of the event, saying that their solution is a tiered approach. He argued that giving a five-year-old and an 18-year-old the same restrictions online would not address the core problem. “Their dimension of learning, of exploration, of responsibility is very different, so you want to make sure that the experience is appropriate. Because if we push people outside of the platform by doing bans, it’s either they circumvent it, or they delay learning,” he said. Early evidence from Australia’s restrictions on social media for children under 16 years old found that roughly eight in ten children continued using social media despite the ban. Hontiveros, the only senator to vote against the SMART KIDS bill, also earlier suggested a tiered access by age instead of a blanket ban. Must Read FAST FACTS: What changed in final version of the under-18 social media ban bill? ‘Connection before correction’ But whatever safety features social media platforms roll out only matter if families use them. Tingson told Rappler on the sidelines of the event that they’re still working on getting people to sign up for the Teen Accounts, saying: “We really need help in pushing for awareness in people enrolling.” For the other members of the panel, using the features starts with a conversation between parent and child. “Connection before correction. We can correct, we can punish. We can do all that. But do we understand [why we’re doing it]?” Kliatchko said in a mix of English and Filipino. The influencer mom said that parents should protect, but it should be done with preparation. “You cannot just forbid your children to play Minecraft or Roblox…. You have to understand it. You have to be able to explain why [you’re setting boundaries],” she said. Others on the panel echoed her. Kintanar said research shows relationships matter for mental health and well-being, while Ortega said parents can’t set limits for children they haven’t connected with. Must Read Preventing school violence starts at home, but gov’t must step up A bigger problem outside the Philippines The panel’s advice puts parents at the center. But what happens when even engaged parents become inundated with the apps’ features that are alleged to be built to hold teens’ attention? Must Read [DECODED] Child safety isn’t a parenting problem. It’s a platform failure. Earlier this year, documents, primarily internal communications at the social media companies, were unsealed and shown in a Los Angeles trial brought by a young woman who said Instagram and YouTube fueled her addiction and depression . In March, the jury found Meta and YouTube liable for negligently designing products that harmed her. Meta has since appealed. In August, a separate federal trial began on claims by 29 different US states . All 29 accused Meta of improperly collecting children’s data, and four lead states also alleged it deliberately designed Facebook and Instagram to hook children and misled the public about their safety. Meta denied the claims and said it has strong protections for teenagers. About a week in, a federal judge approved an $18-billion settlement . Meta agreed without admitting wrongdoing, so the court made no finding on the states’ claims. – Rappler.com

title: Machete-wielding mob attacks health workers responding to Ebola in Congo
body: Angry youths armed with machetes attacked two community health workers raising ​awareness about the Ebola outbreak in eastern Congo, killing one and wounding the other, according to officials and ‌a memo seen by Reuters on Monday, in the latest in a series of attacks fueled by misinformation. The worker who was killed was an experienced nurse who had worked at the general hospital in the town of Bafwasende in Tshopo province, and was recently tasked with helping to ​raise awareness about the deadly virus in the local community, where he was a well-known figure, a local official ​, and the memo said. “We are shocked at how the population turned against this nurse. It is ⁠impossible to believe that he was mistaken for a stranger,” a local health official told Reuters. The attack took place on Friday ​afternoon, when the nurse and a colleague, a teacher also working on community outreach, stopped to check on a lot of ​land. A group building a home next door began accusing them of spreading the disease by contaminating water. “Here are the people that are spreading the Ebola virus through people’s toilets and rivers!” they shouted, according to the memo shared by a health official. The angry group was ​joined by youths wielding machetes and batons, who attacked the pair. The nurse died on the spot before the hospital’s ​emergency services could reach them, the memo said, while the teacher survived. MISINFORMATION FUELING ATTACK Tshopo is among eight provinces in Congo that are battling a ‌fast-spreading outbreak of the Bundibugyo species of the Ebola virus. Congo’s public health institute reported 9,964 confirmed cases and a 48.6% fatality rate since the outbreak was declared in May. Attacks on health workers have targeted hospitals , vehicles and staff involved in the Ebola response, underscoring the challenge of building trust among the population. The local official said health workers in Bafwasende, where the latest ​attack took place, are sheltering at ​the general hospital under ⁠police guard, too afraid to go home, while the army also briefly deployed to the area. “None of the nurses has slept at their homes because they fear for their security,” the official ​added. Only days earlier, an angry mob attacked another community worker raising awareness about Ebola, and ​set his house ⁠on fire, the memo said. Reuters previously reported on how the rapid spread of health misinformation posed a threat to healthcare workers in eastern Congo even before Ebola began to spread, with multiple health workers killed in Tshopo after they were accused of spreading an imaginary disease ⁠that caused ​male genitals to atrophy. “The killing of a nurse yesterday in Bafwasende is ​a loss to the Ebola response and an even greater loss to patients,” Julien Harneis, the senior United Nations Ebola coordinator, said in a post on ​X on Sunday.

title: Putin to take part in Eighth Gas Exporting Countries Forum summit
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. Russian President Vladimir Putin will take part in the Eighth Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) summit in Moscow.
The event is scheduled to begin at 12:45 p.m. Moscow time (9:45 a.m. GMT) at the International Trade Center. According to the Kremlin, the Russian leader will welcome the guests before a group photo. The plenary session, chaired by Putin, is set to begin at 1:00 p.m.
The Russian president will deliver the opening address, highlighting the importance of natural gas as a source of energy that supports economic growth. He will also discuss problems facing the gas industry and outline priorities for solving them.
Putin will then give the floor to GECF Secretary General Philip Mshelbila and the heads of delegations from member states. Representatives of several observer countries, including Mozambique, Angola, Azerbaijan, Iraq, Malaysia and Senegal, are also expected to address the forum.
The Russian president is also expected to hold five bilateral meetings during the day, including with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Qatari Emir Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, Mozambican President Daniel Chapo, Equatorial Guinean President Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo and Libyan Presidential Council Chairman Mohammad al-Menfi.
The Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) is an intergovernmental organization that aims to strengthen cooperation and dialogue among gas-producing and exporting countries and promote stability and safety in the global gas market. The forum’s first ministerial meeting took place in Tehran in 2001.
The GECF member states are Russia, Iran, Algeria, Bolivia, Egypt, Equatorial Guinea, Libya, Nigeria, Qatar, Trinidad and Tobago, the United Arab Emirates and Venezuela. Angola, Azerbaijan, Iraq, Malaysia, Mauritania, Mozambique, Peru and Senegal participate as observer countries.
GECF member states account for about 70% of the world’s proven gas reserves, 38% of global gas production, 42% of global gas exports and 47% of liquefied natural gas (LNG) exports.

title: Who will be VP if Sara Duterte is convicted?
body: Even before Vice President Sara Duterte ’s impeachment trial reaches a verdict, the question of who could replace her is already stirring debates among senator-judges. Under the Constitution, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. has the authority to nominate Duterte’s possible successor from among the sitting lawmakers but the decision will still be subject to congressional confirmation. Article VII, Section 9 of the 1987 Constitution states: “Whenever there is a vacancy in the Office of the Vice President during the term for which he was elected, the President shall nominate a Vice-President from among the Members of the Senate and the House of Representatives who shall assume office upon confirmation by a majority vote of all the Members of both Houses of the Congress, voting separately.” Over the weekend, Senate impeachment court presiding officer Francis “Chiz” Escudero explained that while Marcos has the authority to nominate Duterte’s possible successor, the nominee must also meet the constitutional qualifications for vice president, including the age requirement. This narrows the pool of potential nominees to sitting members of Congress who meet the constitutional requirements, including Escudero himself. “I have yet to receive offers but as I’ve said before, I would not accept it because of a simple reason: conflict of interest,” Escudero said in his podcast. “We tried her case so personally, I don’t think accepting that would be proper,” he added. Senate Minority Leader Alan Peter Cayetano lauded Escudero and urged other senator-judges to issue similar commitment to decline such proposals, citing the need to maintain political neutrality in the trial. “It’s essential that in all impeachment proceedings, senator-judges are politically neutral and will have no incentive to convict except for evidence that proves the article/s of impeachment,” he said. Cayetano’s remarks, however, did not sit well with Senator Panfilo “Ping” Lacson, who cautioned against preempting the decisions of other senator-judges. “He should not preempt the decision of other senator-judges. Selecting the successor is under the prerogative of the President but of course, subject to the confirmation of the Congress,” Lacson said, adding he would decline if he would be offered such position. “But I think [Cayetano’s statement] is uncalled for,” the senator added. So what would Marcos look for in a successor? For political science professor Jean Franco of the University of the Philippines Diliman, the choice of a successor would involve more than simply filling a vacancy. The President would have to consider the political implications of his nominee and whether that person could be trusted to assume the country’s highest office if necessary. Franco identified several qualities Marcos might look for in a potential successor: Someone who can help elevate public trust in the administration Someone who can tell Marcos the truth Someone whom the First Lady [Liza Araneta-Marcos] likes and whom she can get a long with Most importantly, someone who is ready to be President Someone who is friendly to members of the House of Representatives and the Senate since they will concur with the appointment Franco also said calls for senator-judges to declare they would refuse offers may not exactly paint a picture of impartiality. “I think there is no need for that call actually, since in the first place, no senator in his right mind will publicly say that he/she wants to be vice president even if they secretly want to be one,” Franco told Rappler. “Moreover, having this call amplifies the talk that the Vice President will be convicted, but at the same time, if she is convicted, it is not because she is guilty but because some senators are aiming for her position,” Franco added. No names have publicly emerged as possible appointees, but as Senator JV Ejercito puts it, discussing who will succeed the Vice President — at this time — may still be too “premature”. “I don’t think it is proper to discuss who will succeed the vice president because her trial remains ongoing. It’s still too premature,” said Ejercito. Who will likely be the President’s choice, is the big question. – Rappler.com

title: Appeals court declines to step in on Trump administration's California voting case
body:
The judge called the DOJ's request a "self-constructed" emergency.
A 9th Circuit Court of Appeals panel on Monday rejected a request from the Justice Department for an immediate order demanding California segregate roughly 20,000 mail-in ballots from individuals the Trump administration claims are likely non-citizens.
The 2-1 ruling from the panel said the appeals court lacks jurisdiction at this stage in the litigation, punting it back to district court, which has a hearing on the DOJ lawsuit set for Tuesday afternoon.
Circuit Judge Mark Bennett, who was appointed by President Donald Trump, and Circuit Judge Gabriel Sanchez, a President Joe Biden appointee, ruled against the administration's request, with Circuit Judge Patrick Bumatay, who was appointed by Trump, dissenting.
In their ruling, Bennett and Sanchez wrote: "The United States’s claimed emergency, at least in part, is a self-constructed one. At least part of the delay here is attributable to the United States’s own delay in filing suit, in realizing that existing California state law governs the issuance and processing of ballots, in recognizing that California has millions of registered voters and processes ballots on a schedule aligned with that scale, and in communicating to the court its desired relief."
Earlier this month, the DOJ filed suit against California , accusing the state of failing to review a list of alleged noncitizens that the Trump administration claimed were sent mail-in ballots for next week's midterm election.
In court papers filed earlier last week, Los Angeles officials said a preliminary analysis of 200 of the names on the 20,000-person list, included a "high percentage" of individuals who say they were born in the U.S. and many more who have no voting history at all.
Of those 200 individuals, officials said, nearly 40% "indicate that they were born in the United States, which is strong evidence of citizenship; and 71.2% of the records have no voting history," according to a filing.
In a rare Sunday emergency hearing, the Justice Department's efforts to have the appeals court quickly rule on its lawsuit faced considerable skepticism from the panel.
Bennett repeatedly questioned whether the appeals court had jurisdiction to step in at this stage in the litigation and expressed considerable constitutional concerns over the lawsuit itself.
"I don't see how we have jurisdiction," Bennett said to DOJ attorney Matthew Donnelly after pressing him over the timeline of the government's decision to seek emergency appeal when a hearing before the district judge is already set for Tuesday.
Donnelly claimed that the DOJ's decision to seek relief from the appeals court came after disclosures by California of the numbers of mail-in ballots already being processed in advance of the election -- which number in the hundreds of thousands.
Bennett's most significant concerns appeared to be the nature of the lawsuit and it appearing to directly contradict the Constitution's Elections Clause -- which mandates that states have jurisdictions over the manner their elections are run.
"How can the legislature making laws with regard to the manner of holding elections be preempted by a criminal statute passed by the Congress, especially when both the Congress and the California Legislature have made it illegal for non-citizens to vote?" he asked.
Donnelly repeatedly pointed to DOJ's position that the way California is administering its elections -- and not acting on the hard drive of potential 20,000 likely non-citizens -- infringes on the federal government's ability to enforce the federal statute barring voting by illegal immigrants.

title: Ghana cannot PCR-test every arriving passenger for Ebola – Prof Amuasi
body: Ghana cannot PCR-test every arriving passenger for Ebola, Prof John Amuasi said. He wants accurate passenger records and reliable follow-up to be central to the country’s response. The Leader of Global Health at the Kumasi Centre for Collaborative Research in Tropical Medicine (KCCR) said airport temperature checks offer limited protection against detecting imported cases. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Monday, he warned against placing too much confidence in visible screening measures. “Temperature checks, use of alcohol and rubs, all these things are nice. They give people some level of confidence, but the reality is that they are not going to catch Ebola cases for you.” He said testing was needed, but screening every arrival with laboratory tests wasn’t feasible. “What is needed is actually the ability to test, and this doesn’t exist as it stands right now. We can’t be doing PCR tests for everyone coming in.” His comments come as Ebola cases beyond DR Congo sharpen concerns about cross-border spread. Nigeria confirmed an imported case on October 20. According to the WHO, the woman developed symptoms four days after arriving from Uganda. Investigations into the source of her infection were ongoing. The patient was evacuated to Switzerland on Monday, October 26, according to the Associated Press. In Kenya, the WHO reported nine cases, including one death, as of October 20. Eight cases were linked to the first imported patient, who travelled from DR Congo through Uganda. For Prof Amuasi, Ghana’s priority should be ensuring they can reach passengers after they enter the country. “So for me, the single most important thing is being able to collect as accurate data as possible on every single person who comes off the plane in this country, making sure that the phone numbers they submit are accurate and finding a way of verifying it.” He also called for arrangements to locate travellers when necessary. Arrivals should know the designated facilities and contact channels to use if symptoms develop. He stressed that education should target people entering Ghana. Authorities must collect detailed information that allows effective follow-up. “But for the other visual things we see, like alcohol rub and the temperature text, they are nice. They help people to be more confident and comfortable. But at this stage right now, they don’t count very much,” he added.

title: Conny Glenn stuns Bryan Paterson to win mayoral bid in Kingston, Ont.
body:
Voters in Kingston, Ont., turned to a new face to lead the city, electing Conny Glenn to be their new mayor on Monday night, ending incumbent Bryan Paterson’s bid for a fourth consecutive term in the role.
In a narrow victory, Glenn — who served as councillor for Sydenham District for the past four years — garnered 16,451 votes – or 43.25 per cent of the 38,246 ballots cast from 26 of 26 tabulators, according to unofficial results on the City of Kingston’s website.
Paterson received 15,658 votes, or 41.17 per cent of the votes.
“The reality is it’s difficult to run against an incumbent – I know Bryan ran a hard race, I wouldn’t expect anything less out of him,” said Glenn. “And I do want to send out good wishes to my opponents, they ran good races.”
Glenn becomes the third woman voted as mayor in Kingston
“What we’ve seen over the last four years is a lot of women that have stepped down from their roles as elected politicians, councillors, mayors, because of a lot of abuse,” she said following her victory. “So it’s important that women continue to run, it’s important that we step up”
Vanessa Menasah, who stepped down from her role as the city’s manager of diversity, equity and inclusion, finished a distant third with 5,351 votes or 14.06 per cent of the vote while Grant Bedard received 542 votes (1.48 per cent).
Paterson was the city’s 96th mayor and was re-elected to his third consecutive term in 2022 in which he garnered over 74 per cent of the vote. Overall voter turnout was 31.12 per cent in that election. Prior to being mayor he also served a term as a city councillor.
Last year Paterson took a leave of absence as mayor to run as a candidate for the Conservatives but lost to longtime Liberal MP Mark Gerretsen.
In this year’s municipal election, the city reported advance voter turnout at 12.42 per cent ahead of election day Monday. More than 14,000 people voted online.

title: Russia expanding recruitment of African mercenaries amid heavy losses in Ukraine war – Bloomberg
body:
As reported by Ukrinform, Bloomberg reported this, citing a presentation obtained from people familiar with the work of Ukrainian intelligence.
Russia is now turning its attention to countries with low levels of democracy, limited press freedom and weak judicial systems.
The countries where Russia has stepped up recruitment include Zimbabwe, Burundi and Sierra Leone.
According to the presentation, between January 1 and September 30, Russia recruited 699 men from Burundi, compared with 30 for the whole of 2025, and 530 Zimbabwean nationals, up from 65 previously.
Other countries where a significant increase in recruitment has been observed include the Democratic Republic of Congo, Sierra Leone, Sudan and Cameroon.
Moscow took this step after Kenya and South Africa introduced measures to prevent men from leaving the country to take part in Russia’s war against Ukraine.
The Russian recruitment program is aimed at “offsetting massive losses and a shortage of people to mobilize.”
Russia has never publicly acknowledged recruiting foreigners to take part in combat operations against Ukraine.
The Kremlin has claimed that Russia has sufficient manpower to continue the war. Last month, Kremlin leader Vladimir Putin dismissed suggestions that he was preparing to announce another wave of mobilization in the country.
However, concern is growing in a number of African countries over Russia’s efforts to recruit their citizens. Given the relative poverty in Africa, people can be more easily lured to Russia, often with false promises of civilian employment, for example in catering or transportation.
Recruits are also offered substantial one-time payments upon signing a contract, high salaries and the opportunity to obtain Russian citizenship.
As reported by Ukrinform, in the spring of this year, the Center for Countering Disinformation under Ukraine’s National Security and Defense Council said the Kremlin had changed its approach to recruiting foreigners into the Russian army for the war against Ukraine, with recruitment now being carried out on a systematic basis.

title: French Daily Le Parisien Hails Mani as Greece’s Little-Known Paradise
body: Forget the crowded Cyclades. The Mani peninsula in the southern Peloponnese is one of Greece’s best-kept secrets, according to French daily Le Parisien, which praises its mountain villages, traditional tavernas, crystal-clear coves and spectacular caves. In a travel feature for its weekend magazine published on 24 October, journalist Dominique Savidan describes Mani as a region “too often overlooked in favour of the Cyclades islands”, where visitors can still find the authentic landscapes of Homer’s Odyssey . The Mani peninsula, a land that has to be earned Mani lies about three and a half hours’ drive from Athens. Le Parisien says it is a place that “has to be earned”: a car is the only practical way to get around, on winding roads squeezed between the sea and the mountains. Along the way, the 2,400-metre peaks of Taygetus, the highest mountain in the Peloponnese, appear between the bends. The paper notes that the region’s isolation and fortified villages helped the Maniots keep their independence for centuries, holding out against the Romans, the Venetians and the Ottoman Turks. Le Parisien paints a picture of endless olive groves, empty beaches, small Byzantine chapels and fishing villages still untouched by mass tourism. Its advice is to take a seat at a seaside taverna with an ouzo or a frappé and enjoy the mild, sunny weather of the late season. Areopoli, where the revolution began The first stop is Areopoli, about 80 kilometres from Kalamata airport. Cars stay in a free car park outside the village, leaving its cobbled lanes, lined with bougainvillea and traditional stone tower houses, to people on foot. Areopolis/Photo: Giorgos Detsis It was here, on 17 March 1821, that Petros Mavromichalis, known as Petrobey, the last bey of Mani, declared the Greek War of Independence. A bronze statue of him stands in the Square of the Immortals (Plateia Athanaton), and his house has been turned into a museum, Le Parisien reports. The underground lake of Diros The highlight for the French paper is the Diros caves, which it calls among the most spectacular in Europe. Visitors explore a “cathedral” of stalactites and stalagmites by boat, in a silence broken only by the sound of dripping water, before finishing on foot along a narrow path past petrified waterfalls and strangely shaped limestone formations. Only a fraction of the system is open to the public: 1,500 metres out of 14,700 metres mapped, according to Le Parisien, which puts entry at €12. Seafood at Limeni Fifteen kilometres from Diros, the tiny village of Limeni has no beach, but steps between its stone houses lead straight into the turquoise water. Locals travel to eat at Kourmas, a waterfront seafood restaurant that Le Parisien calls the best in the area. It recommends fried octopus, the catch of the day or fresh prawns, washed down with a glass of Malvasia, the white wine of the region’s best-known grape, for about €30 a head. Limeni and Pirgos Mavromichali/Photo: Giorgos Detsis Monemvasia, the “Gibraltar of Greece” About an hour and a half’s drive from Limeni is Monemvasia, the fortified town on a rock rising more than 300 metres from the sea, reached from the mainland by a single causeway. Cars are banned, so visitors wander its narrow lanes on foot, past Venetian-style houses and more than 20 Byzantine churches. A half-hour climb leads to the ruins of the upper town and the 12th-century church of Agia Sofia, with sweeping views along the coast. Cape Tainaro, the gate to the underworld At the southern tip of the peninsula is Cape Tainaro (Cape Matapan), the southernmost point of mainland Greece. Le Parisien recommends the walk of just over two kilometres along a rocky, shadeless path to the lighthouse, built in 1892. In Greek mythology, the cape was known as a gateway to the underworld, because its caves were said to lead to Hades. Ruins of a sanctuary of Poseidon can still be seen there, along with a mosaic floor. A hotel at the end of the world The trip ends past the deserted tower village of Vathia, at the Marmari Paradise Beach hotel, which has 18 stone-walled rooms with sea-view terraces and a private sandy beach. Rooms start from €147, the paper says, and the owner, Nikos, greets guests with a sunset cocktail and local cooking. Getting there Le Parisien notes that Transavia runs a weekly Sunday flight from Paris to Kalamata until 1 November, with fares from €38 one way, followed by an 80-kilometre drive to Areopoli. For souvenirs, it suggests local olive oil and Malvasia wine.
