title: Agric Minister backs Black Challenge with cash and Agribusiness pledge
body: Minister for Food and Agriculture Eric Opoku has donated GH¢50,000 to Ghana’s national amputee football team, the Black Challenge, and pledged a poultry enterprise package for eight locally based players, linking World Cup preparations with economic opportunities beyond the pitch. The proposed package includes battery cages, laying birds, feed and technical expertise. Opoku said Deputy Minister John Dumelo would coordinate the support after the players return from the tournament in Mexico. The commitment gives substance to the link between agriculture and sport: backing athletes to represent Ghana while helping them build businesses and contribute to the country’s food production. Opoku announced the support during a visit to the team’s training session at the University of Ghana. He was accompanied by Dumelo, the ministry’s Chief Director and its budget officer. “You are going to hold the flag of Ghana, and our presence here indicates that the whole nation is behind you,” he told the players. The minister said the team needed motivational and financial support to prepare for the international assignment, urging the players to compete with confidence. “You are stronger than you know,” he said, encouraging them to make Ghana proud. The GH¢50,000 donation follows a GH¢100,000 contribution from dancehall artiste Stonebwoy. Together, the two contributions amount to GH¢150,000 in support for the team’s preparations. Opoku said he had been informed that the team comprised eight locally based players and seven based in Turkey. He invited the eight players based in Ghana to join the government’s Nkoko Nketenkete poultry programme after the World Cup. “The Ministry of Food and Agriculture is putting together a special package, so as soon as you return, get in touch with us,” he said. “The Honourable Dumelo will handle all of you.” Listing the proposed assistance, Opoku said the ministry would provide cages, laying birds, feed and the technical expertise to establish the players as poultry farmers, adding that the intention was for them to “have something to live on.” The announcement extends the discussion of athlete welfare to income during and after competitive sport. For the players, a viable poultry enterprise could help support their households while they continue training and competing. Opoku also connected the pledge to the ministry’s national responsibility to produce enough food for Ghanaians and generate a surplus for export. Nkoko Nketenkete is the household and backyard poultry component of the Feed Ghana Programme, launched by President John Dramani Mahama. The programme’s stated aims include improving food security and household incomes through increased domestic production. Extending participation to the Black Challenge would give that agricultural agenda a practical expression of inclusion, recognising athletes with disabilities as potential entrepreneurs and producers. If delivered with accessible training, suitable facilities and continuing technical support, the package could provide an example for cooperation between sports institutions and agricultural agencies. The broader opportunity is to create pathways through which other Para athletes can participate in agribusiness on terms suited to their interests and circumstances. The players have been asked to contact the ministry after returning from Mexico. The commitment now gives the ministry and the team a clear basis for agreeing how the promised enterprises will be established and supported. Ghana will face Angola, Colombia and Iraq in Group D of the 2026 World Amputee Football Federation World Cup, scheduled for 13–22 November in San Juan de los Lagos, Mexico. Twenty-four national teams will compete for the title. As the Black Challenge prepare for that contest, Opoku’s message combines national backing with a prospect of greater economic independence. “You have the full support of the entire citizenry of this country,” he assured the players.

title: Trump says Brazil election looked 'rigged', defeated Bolsonaro's party recognizes Lula win
body: US President Donald Trump said on Monday that leftist incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's surprise win in Brazil's presidential vote "looked like another rigged election," although the party of defeated right-winger Flávio Bolsonaro later acknowledged the result.The son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, Flavio Bolsonaro, has refused to concede defeat in Sunday's presidential election, saying he would seek the annulment of Lula's victory after the Supreme Court extended voting by two hours.Later on Monday, however, Bolsonaro's Liberal Party said it acknowledged the runoff result in a statement signed by the party's head, Valdemar Costa Neto."We recognize the presidential election results," Costa Neto said. "But we believe the issues raised need to be properly clarified."Bolsonaro, who has not commented publicly since his party's statement, said earlier on Monday he would comply with a federal police order to hand over his passports following a visit to his father, who is under house arrest, and denied he was planning to flee Brazil.Trump did not endorse Bolsonaro ahead of the vote, although Reuters has reported that officials from his State Department led a campaign to return the Bolsonaros to power."I didn't take sides, but it looked like another rigged election," Trump told reporters, without providing any evidence. "It looked very bad to me."Bolsonaro lost to Lula by over 4 million votes, a clear result that will be challenging for him to overturn. Fewer than 35,000 votes, or some 0.03% of the total, were cast in the extra two hours of voting ordered by the Supreme Court, according to an analysis of electoral records by Insper professor Pedro Burgos."I just think it had a very bad look, the election, the way it was tabulated," Trump said. "The extension given was very strange."Vice President Geraldo Alckmin later defended Brazil's electoral system, saying in a TV interview with Rede Vanguarda that Trump's remarks were "totally wrong" and "unfounded."Neither Trump nor Jair Bolsonaro accepted their election losses in 2020 and 2022, respectively. Brazil's former president was handed a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup after losing to Lula.Analysts do not expect Flavio Bolsonaro to be able to build the same anti-democratic movement as his father in 2022.Markets roiled by Lula win World leaders have already widely congratulated Lula on his unprecedented fourth mandate, which was greeted with dismay by investors who had been betting on a Bolsonaro win.Brazil's real BRL= fell 8.1% against the dollar in its biggest one-day drop since 2002, while the stock exchange marked its steepest one-day fall since 2020."The initial selloff could moderate as election-related positions are unwound, but investors will demand convincing fiscal commitments before rebuilding exposure," said Pantheon Macroeconomics' chief Latin America economist Andres Abadia.Lula's victory defied polls, precedent and global anti-incumbent sentiment to put the brakes on a wave of right-wing election victories across Latin America. He trailed Bolsonaro in the first round, but managed to convince voters to come out for him in the runoff.Pollsters said a higher-than-expected turnout and an improved social media campaign helped power Lula to victory.During the campaign, Lula pointed to his track record of cutting poverty and inequality while also highlighting record-low unemployment, illiteracy and deforestation, but his fourth term may prove challenging.He will face an uphill battle for his agenda in a Congress packed with Bolsonaro allies after a surge of conservative voters in the first round of the general election pushed the Brazilian legislature further to the right.

title: Israeli man arrested in Thailand on suspicion of drugging women, secretly filming sex
body: Bangkok police arrested a 54-year-old Israeli man last Friday on suspicion of meeting women through dating apps, inviting them to his apartment, and serving them cakes suspected of containing drugs before having sex with them and secretly recording the encounters.According to a police statement, officers searching his apartment seized methamphetamine, drug-packaging equipment, and a mobile phone containing numerous intimate videos. Investigators also discovered that the Israeli had stayed in Thailand without a valid visa for 2,095 days, or nearly six years.Thai media identified the suspect as Tomer Kahiri. He was reportedly known in Thailand as “Tom,” “Tommy,” or “Tom Yum Kung,” after the popular Thai soup.He was arrested at an apartment building in Bangkok's Huai Khwang district in a joint operation involving the capital's narcotics suppression unit and immigration police. A 44-year-old Thai woman was arrested with him.Investigation followed tip to Thai narcotics authoritiesAccording to the police statement, the investigation began after information was received by the hotline of Thailand's narcotics suppression authorities. The informant described an Israeli man with an eagle tattoo on his left arm who allegedly contacted women through dating apps and invited them to his home.According to the tip, the women experienced hot flashes and increased sexual arousal after eating cakes he had prepared for them. They subsequently had sex with him, which police suspected was recorded without their knowledge.Police suspected the cakes contained drugs, but laboratory test results confirming their contents had not been made public.The investigation was led by Major General Teeradet Thamsuthee, deputy chief of Bangkok police responsible for narcotics suppression. With assistance from immigration police, investigators discovered that the suspect's visa had expired 2,095 days earlier.During surveillance, officers observed numerous women entering and leaving his apartment. Police said the suspect did not have regular employment and spent most of his time at home, but had enough money to support himself.Drugs, cakes and intimate videos found on phoneDuring the raid, police seized 15 grams of crystal methamphetamine, 50 bags used for packaging drugs, an electronic scale, a tray of cakes suspected of containing drugs, and a mobile phone.According to police, an examination of the phone revealed messages concerning the purchase of drugs for resale, along with numerous videos showing sexual encounters with different women on a sofa in the apartment. The encounters were allegedly filmed without the women's knowledge.The man denied that the seized drugs belonged to him.According to the police statement, he claimed during his arrest that he had connections to an influential person who could secure his release within two hours. He demanded the names of the officers involved in the raid and threatened to have them transferred or fired. Police also alleged that he threatened to kill one of the officers involved in the operation.The Israeli man was accused of possessing a dangerous drug, overstaying his visa, refusing to undergo a drug test, and disobeying law enforcement officials. The Thai woman arrested with him was suspected of possessing and using methamphetamine.The police statement did not say that the Israeli had, at that stage, been formally charged with drugging women or secretly recording intimate encounters without their consent. Both suspects and the seized evidence were transferred to Huai Khwang police station for further legal proceedings.According to Thai media reports, the Israeli denied all the allegations against him. He reportedly described himself as a former Israeli soldier and businessman involved in textile exports. He also said he had two children and had moved to Thailand after separating from his partner because he loved the country and found its residents friendly.

title: Wiretapping: Court fixes Nov 25 for El-Rufai’s trial
body: A Federal High Court in Abuja has fixed November 25 for former Kaduna State Governor Nasir El-Rufai to open his defence in the ongoing trial over alleged unlawful interception of telephone conversations. Justice Joyce Abdulmalik fixed the date on Monday after dismissing a no-case submission filed by El-Rufai, ruling that the prosecution had presented sufficient evidence to require him to defend himself against the charges. The court’s decision followed arguments by the defence and prosecution over whether the evidence presented by the Federal Government established a prima facie case against the former governor. El-Rufai is facing a five-count amended charge filed by the Department of State Services (DSS) over allegations that he unlawfully intercepted telephone conversations linked to the National Security Adviser, Nuhu Ribadu. The case arose from comments El-Rufai made during an interview on Arise TV’s Prime Time programme in February 2026, when he said “someone wiretapped” Ribadu’s phone, enabling him to listen to the NSA instructing security operatives to arrest him. The Federal Government had called two witnesses before closing its case, prompting El-Rufai to file a no-case submission, asking the court to discharge and acquit him without requiring him to enter his defence. Moving the application on Monday, his counsel, Paul Erokoro, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), argued that the prosecution had failed to establish a prima facie case against his client. He urged the court to uphold the application and discharge and acquit the former governor of the five-count amended charge. However, prosecution counsel Oluwole Aladedoye urged the court to dismiss the application, arguing that the oral and documentary evidence presented was sufficient to require El-Rufai to defend himself. In her ruling, Justice Abdulmalik upheld the prosecution’s position and ordered the former governor to open his defence. The court subsequently adjourned the case until November 25 for him to do so.

title: Economy Ministry again revises 2026 GDP forecast downward
body:
According to an Ukrinform correspondent, Minister of Economy and Environment Oleksandr Kravchenko told the Kyiv International Economic Forum that at the start of the year the expected GDP growth forecast for 2026 stood at 2.4%. In June, the ministry cut its projection to 1.6% for 2026 and 1.3% for 2027.
“We are now revising the forecast again. There is no final figure yet, but we already see a minus 1–1.5 percentage points compared with our June estimate,” Kravchenko said.
He cited several reasons for the downgrade, including the blockade of Ukraine’s seaports, intensified Russian attacks and, to some extent, the postponement of capital budget spending to the end of the year.
Kravchenko said damage from strikes has already reached about USD 8 billion, with losses expected to rise to USD 10 billion by year‑end. While most losses in the first half of the year were concentrated in the energy sector, in the second half all sectors of the economy have been affected.
“We need reserves and a set of tools to support business. This is also about systemic risks for the economy and our budget revenues,” he noted.
As reported, in the first nine months of 2026 the state budget fell short of planned revenues by UAH 50 billion, including UAH 32 billion in August–September.

title: Russian forces introduce ceasefire in Kherson direction
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. The Russian Armed Forces introduced a ceasefire in the Kherson direction at 4:00 a.m. Moscow time (1:00 a.m. GMT) to prepare for a humanitarian operation near Alyoshki, the Defense Ministry said in a statement.
"As part of preparations for a humanitarian operation near the town of Alyoshki in the Kherson Region, the Russian Armed Forces ceased fire in the Kherson direction at 4:00 a.m. Moscow time on October 27," the statement reads.
Russian Chief of the General Staff Army General Valery Gerasimov announced on October 23 that the Russian Armed Forces would cease fire in the Kherson direction at 4:00 a.m. Moscow time on October 27 to allow for a humanitarian operation in Alyoshki.
According to the Russian Defense Ministry, the Kiev regime has been shelling roads leading to Alyoshki and extensively using drones to destroy vehicles. Ukrainian forces have also been using unmanned aerial vehicles to lay mines along roads to prevent civilian evacuations and impede the delivery of foods, medicine and other essential supplies to Alyoshki.
Over the past week alone, the Kiev regime carried out 18 artillery strikes and more than 120 drone strikes on Alyoshki and main roads in the area, while Russian troops devised over 300 landmines and other explosive devices.
On September 21, Russian Presidential Spokesman Dmitry Peskov described the situation in Alyoshki as critical, saying that food and medicine could not be delivered there amid ongoing Ukrainian shelling and drone attacks. Russian President Vladimir Putin and his US counterpart Donald Trump held a phone call on October 9. Putin said the parties had agreed that Russian Human Rights Commissioner Yana Lantratova would remain in constant contact with US First Lady Melania Trump's office.
Peskov pointed out on October 26 that the agreement to conduct a humanitarian operation in Alyoshki could set a precedent for similar missions in other areas. He particularly highlighted the United States’ direct and constructive role in coordinating the process. Peskov added that Russia hoped Ukraine would honor all agreements concerning the humanitarian mission in Alyoshki.

title: We did not cause hardship – PDP
body: The Peoples Democratic Party, PDP backed by the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike has criticised President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC for saying that the prevailing hardship in the country was caused by the opposition. Speaking at the APC presidential campaign flag-off at the Kaduna Township Stadium on Saturday, President Tinubu said his government was working to eradicate the hardship caused by the opposition. “You created hunger and poverty,’ the President berated the opposition. Meanwhile, reacting to the development, Jungudo Haruna Mohammed, National Publicity Secretary of the PDP denied that the opposition especially the PDP was responsible for the hardship in the country, asking the APC to own up to its responsibility. The PDP said it considered these statements as “attempts to evade responsibility and divert public attention from the pressing challenges facing the country under the APC-led administration.” The PDP spokesman argued that rather than engaging in political blame games, the APC should explain what it intends to do to make “food affordable, support farmers, strengthen local food production, create jobs, improve security, fight corruption, improve electricity supply, reduce transportation costs, and restore the purchasing power of ordinary Nigerians, among other pressing concerns.” “We firmly reject any attempt to use the PDP’s sixteen years in government as a blanket justification for the shortcomings of the present administration. “After more than APC’s 10years in office, Nigerians deserve answers, not excuses. The APC must tell Nigerians what it has achieved, outline the concrete measures it is taking to address the country’s present day challenges, and demonstrate its commitment to improving the welfare of citizens rather than continually dragging the PDP into its own shortcomings. “The PDP maintains that the economic challenges confronting Nigeria cannot be resolved by repeatedly blaming previous PDP-led administrations. While historical circumstances may provide context, they cannot serve as a permanent shield against accountability. “Every administration must be judged by its policies, decisions, achievements, and, most importantly, the living conditions of the people it governs.” the statement said. PDP said Nigerians are demanding practical solutions, affordable food, economic stability, and improved security, not endless political arguments and blame shifting, adding that they remain confident that Nigerians will judge political parties by their records, policies, and commitment to the welfare of the people. “We believe that the growing desire among Nigerians for a return to PDP leadership reflects their yearning for better governance, improved living conditions, and a more secure and prosperous country. “The PDP is not responsible for the hunger Nigerians are experiencing today. The APC must own its record, address the nation’s challenges, and deliver on its promises to Nigerians. The government in power must answer for its stewardship and present a credible path towards economic recovery, food security, and a better standard of living for all Nigerians.” PDP said.

title: We’re not part of Rainbow Coalition — Ondo PDP candidate
body: The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) candidate for the Akure North/Akure South Federal Constituency, Babatunde Faro, has stated that the party has not joined the Wike-led Rainbow Coalition, pending directives from its national leadership. Faro stated this during a press conference in Akure, Ondo State, explaining that the PDP leadership has yet to communicate its official position on the proposed coalition to members at the grassroots level. “On the Wike Rainbow Coalition, we know that we can take a decision to be part of them, but we have not received any order from the national leadership, so we don’t belong yet,” he said. When asked which presidential candidate he would support in the 2027 general election, Faro maintained that the PDP’s presidential candidate remains Sandy Ojang Onor. “Our presidential candidate still remains Sandy Onor as the PDP candidate,” he declared. According to him, the party will make a firm decision regarding possible coalitions and alliances with other political parties closer to the 2027 general election. “One month or so to the 2027 poll, the party will take a firm decision on any coalition levels or any alliances with any party. And from then, as a party man, I am obligated and bound by it, and I will make my own position known,” Faro said. Addressing the conduct of the upcoming 2027 elections, Faro urged the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to improve its operational efficiency and ensure that votes count.

title: 2027: Come out, your vote will count, NOA tells Nigerians
body: The National Orientation Agency (NOA) has urged Nigerians to turn out in large numbers to vote in the 2027 general elections, insisting that every vote counts and citizens should not allow themselves to be discouraged by voter apathy. The agency also stated that it is building on the successes recorded during the recent elections in Ekiti and Osun states to strengthen voter mobilization and promote peaceful, credible, and inclusive elections in 2027. The Zonal Director of NOA, Southwest Zone, Kehinde Martins Ogunkuade, stated this on Monday during an interview in Abeokuta, Ogun State, while outlining the agency’s mobilization strategies ahead of the next general elections. Ogunkuade said the experience gained from the Ekiti and Osun elections provided valuable lessons that will guide the agency’s efforts across the Southwest region. “I was part of the team that worked in Ekiti and Osun states, and, by the grace of God, we witnessed improvements in voter participation. This reflects, in part, the work carried out by the agency. We mobilised citizens and encouraged them to come out and exercise their civic responsibilities,” he said. He added that the NOA is intensifying its grassroots engagement and stakeholder collaboration to achieve even better results in the forthcoming elections. “Building on the experience in Ekiti and Osun states, we are confident that similar efforts can produce positive results across other states in our zone. When people feel secure, they are more likely to participate,” Ogunkuade said. He explained that the agency would continue to engage citizens on the importance of voting while working with security agencies to reassure voters about their safety during elections. According to him, the NOA’s mobilization campaign was officially flagged off on October 15, marking the commencement of activities across its directorates and states to encourage greater public participation in the 2027 general elections.

title: U.S. Army Activates New Guam Air Defence Battalion as China and North Korea Bolster Missile Forces
body: The U.S. Army has activated a new air defence battalion on Guam to strengthen protection of the strategically critical territory, which continues to play a central role in facilitating planned offensives into East Asia. The 3rd Battalion, 43rd Air Defence Artillery Regiment, was formally at Andersen Air Force Base, assuming responsibilities previously handled by Task Force Talon. The transition marks a shift towards establishing a permanent air and missile defence presence on the island. Task Force Talon began its rotational mission in 2013, initially focusing on defending Guam against potential North Korean ballistic missile attacks. The rapid expansion of both China and North Korea’s missile forces have broadened the mission’s scope considerably. The Pentagon initiated plans for the Guam Defense System in 2023 to address threats from ballistic, cruise and hypersonic missiles, reflecting concerns about the vulnerability of American bases to long-range precision strikes during a potential conflict in the region. The island was at the time expected to field up to 20 new air defence sites as part of efforts to tremendously improve the survivability of important facilities there, with significant new airspace restrictions are also expected to be put in place. Regarding the capabilities expected to be introduced reports at the time noted: "The missile defence system would be able to defend Guam a full 360 degrees around the entirety of the island. The 360-degree capability would be achieved by distributing/placing system components at multiple locations around the island.”Guam currently hosts six Army THAAD launchers, while U.S. Navy warships equipped with the Aegis combat system can provide additional defensive support when assigned to the island’s protection. The new battalion is expected to operate several complementary air defence systems, including the medium altitude Patriot and high altitude THAAD systems, alongside the Intermediate Fires Protection Capability (IFPC) currently under development. THAAD is designed primarily to intercept ballistic missiles during the terminal phase of their flight, while Patriot provides additional defence against aircraft and various missile threats. IFPC is intended to address shorter-range threats, including cruise missiles, unmanned aerial vehicles and other aerial weapons, providing another layer of protection within the wider defensive network. The Army intends to integrate these systems into a coordinated defensive architecture connecting sensors, command-and-control infrastructure, launchers and interceptors. In parallel to efforts to strengthen Guam’s missile defences, the U.S. Military has also sought to diversify its range of facilities for power projection into East Asia including through expansion of facilities on Wake Island and in Northern Australia , all of which are expected to also be able to serve as staging grounds for B-21 nuclear capable bombers. A primary challenge to the U.S. Armed Forces’ ability o operate from these facilities remains the advanced ballistic missile strike capabilities of Chinese and North Korean forces. North Korea began flight testing ballistic missiles with hypersonic glide vehicles in 2021, and has since brought the Hwasong-16B into service, which integrates such one such vehicle and significantly improves on the capabilities of the preceding Hwasong-12 ‘Guam Kiiller’ missile. Existing U.S. missile defence systems have proven incapable of intercepting even more basic Iranian hypersonic missiles, while the Patriot has proven far from reliable against even relatively basic targets.

title: ADC, APC bicker over campaign issues
body: The African Democratic Congress (ADC) and the All Progressives Congress (APC) have differed over what should constitute issues in the current campaigns to woo voters in the presidential election. The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council had in a statement accused the ADC of failing to pay party workers for over 12 months. Replying, the ADC said they understand the APC’s desperation to change the conversation, saying “The real issue is the cost of living. The real issue is the absence of jobs and opportunities for our young people. The real issue is the insecurity that continues to threaten lives, livelihoods, and communities across the country. National Publicity Secretary of the ADC Bolaji Abdullahi, in a statement added that “When a government has no achievements to defend, it must manufacture allegations to discuss. “These are the issues on which this government must be judged, and no amount of propaganda can redeem it.” The opposition party said “It is becoming increasingly clear that the APC has decided to run its 2027 campaign on allegations against the opposition rather than achievements of its own. That is what happens when a government has spent years making promises it cannot keep and excuses it cannot defend.” The party therefore advised the APC campaign to spend less time inventing stories about the ADC and more time explaining why Nigerians should reward their party with another term “after the hardship, insecurity and economic uncertainty of the last three years.” In a statement issued on Monday, the spokesperson for the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Dele Alake, described the non-payment of staff salaries as “wicked and reprehensible,” arguing that it exposes the “emptiness and insincerity” of opposition leaders positioning themselves as alternative governance choices for Nigeria. “We find it unconscionable that a political party that has made many grandiose promises to hoodwink Nigerians owes its workers for more than 12 months,” Alake stated. “Owing staff who come to work every day and who rely on the salaries for their daily sustenance is wicked and reprehensible. A party that cannot pay its cleaners and workforce cannot be entrusted with our country’s affairs.”

title: Ex-FBI chief Comey faces third prosecution attempt by Trump Justice Department
body: The US Justice Department is attempting to prosecute former FBI Director James Comey for a third time, the latest case accusing him of sharing sensitive national security information in 2016, according to court documents made public on Monday.The case was revealed in a court document known as a "criminal information" that the Justice Department said it filed to stop the 10-year statute of limitations on the offense from expiring earlier this month.The document filed in Washington federal court charges Comey with transmitting and conspiring to transmit national defense information. It alleges he shared classified information with a reporter from the New York Times in October 2016.Comey said in an Instagram video that "they're back again" and referenced the Justice Department, but did not provide further details. "I'm still innocent," he added. Comey's lawyers have already asked a judge to dismiss the case, arguing it is legally improper.The new case adds to the legal fights facing Comey, whom the Justice Department has already charged twice, accusing him of lying to Congress about media leaks and threatening US President Donald Trump in a social media post. A judge dismissed the false statements case, while the threats case remains pending.Comey did not commit crimes, lawyer allegesComey's lawyer, Patrick Fitzgerald, said in a statement that the document "purports to charge Mr. Comey with crimes that he did not commit." The criminal information was filed on October 5, but was unsealed on Monday at the request of Comey's lawyers.A Justice Department spokesperson described the maneuver to halt the statute of limitations as a "widely recognized practice in federal court.""This is an ongoing criminal investigation, and we will not comment further," the spokesperson said in a statement.

title: Rappler Recap: What are Zalameda, Dimaampao, and Marquez’s plans as chief justice bets?
body: MANILA, Philippines – Associate Justices Rodil Zalameda, Japar Dimaampao, and Jose Midas Marquez faced the Judicial and Bar Council on Monday, October 26, as they bid to become the country’s next Supreme Court Chief Justice. If they are chosen to succeed Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo , what would they do as head of the judiciary? Justice reporter Jairo Bolledo shares in this recap. – Rappler.com

title: Cohere says Alibaba’s Qwen model tried to send a file to Beijing
body:
Canadian AI company Cohere said on Monday that it found one of Alibaba’s newest AI models, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, trying to upload a file to a server in Beijing during a routine cybersecurity test, even though the model had said in its own notes that it wouldn’t use any tools.
The incident initially raised fears that the model had undermined a fundamental promise to businesses — that self-hosting an open-weight model keeps data in-house. But those early fears of corporate espionage were short-lived. Researchers quickly dismissed the threat, saying it was likely a by-product of messy training environments that cause models to unexpectedly act outside their instructions rather than a deliberate attempt to secretly send sensitive information to China.
The incident began on Friday during an evaluation in which the Qwen model was asked to write a rule for catching malware downloads. According to a blog post from Cohere, the model’s written reasoning explicitly stated it would not use any external tools. Yet in the very next step, it attempted to send a test string (a short piece of placeholder text) to an external server before being blocked by a security sandbox.
Cohere said it could not tell whether the behavior was deliberate or a leftover from its training.
Asked about the debate over the model’s intent, Cohere co-founder Ivan Zhang told TechCrunch that Cohere has seen its own models pick up strange habits in training simulators.
“It’s really hard to assign intention or motivation. We’ve read our own model traces, we’ve seen reward hacks, and sometimes these models get really creative when it comes to trying to break out their sandboxes,” Zhang said. (Reward hacks are shortcuts a model finds to earn credit without doing a task as intended.)
To teach an AI model to act as an agent that takes actions on its own, companies like Alibaba train it in thousands of practice setups, sort of like flight simulators for software. The model is rewarded every time it finishes a task in a simulator, and it picks up habits along the way. If these practice setups routinely stored files on Alibaba’s cloud servers, models could learn to save files there by default.
Critics also argued that the incident could have been caused by the way Cohere investigated the behavior , steering the model toward it instead of measuring how often Qwen does it on its own.
To find what triggered the upload attempt, Cohere supplied the beginning of a network command (an instruction telling one computer to connect to another) and let the model finish it. Because it processed thousands of routine network commands during its training, the model acted like a highly advanced autocomplete — often filling in web addresses, some of them for Alibaba’s servers.
Cohere said the original upload attempt happened without any such help, but that the behavior is rare.
After developers asked for more evidence, Cohere released the raw traces from its tests on Monday evening on the AI developer platform Hugging Face, along with a script so others could try to reproduce the behavior.
One initial skeptic, after going through the traces, rated the evidence as strong that Qwen can invent suspicious web addresses, but found no evidence that Alibaba planted a backdoor or that Qwen was deliberately hiding its intent.
The incident lands as governments are deciding how far to push back on Chinese AI. Last week, the Department of Homeland Security ordered federal civilian agencies to remove the Chinese AI developer DeepSeek’s products from their systems.
In its blog post, Cohere called on governments to clarify whether their restrictions on Chinese AI also apply to models running on government computers.
“I’m not asking for full regulation of these open-weights models,” Zhang told TechCrunch, adding that companies should treat open models like any program downloaded from the internet.
Cohere, which sells its own AI models to governments, stands to benefit if officials grow warier of free Chinese alternatives.

title: China Fits Type 08 Infantry Fighting Vehicle with Anti-Drone Cages
body:
China has fitted a Type 08 infantry fighting vehicle (IFV) with metal roof cages and side grilles designed to provide additional protection against drone attacks.
Footage aired by Chinese state broadcaster CCTV News o n Wednesday showed the modified vehicle during the ongoing Karakoram 2026 China-Pakistan joint army exercise in Korla, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region.
The Type 08's roof cage and side grilles represent a tactical response to the growing threat posed by unmanned aerial systems. Chinese military affairs expert Song Zhongping told the Global Times that conflicts in Russia-Ukraine and the Middle East have demonstrated the vulnerability of armored vehicles to drones.
Russian tanks have increasingly incorporated roof protection, additional armor and electronic warfare equipment against first-person-view (FPV) drones and other unmanned systems, which threaten upper surfaces, rear sections and engine compartments.
In November 2025, Xinhua News Agency cited German broadcaster n-tv in reporting on Russian countermeasures against suicide drones, including improvised armor nicknamed “turtle shell,” “porcupine” and “hedgehog” tanks.
According to CCTV, reconnaissance vehicles and drones initially monitor targets inside a simulated terrorist camp, tracking opposing forces in real time. Snipers then take elevated positions, drone swarms conduct simulated suicide strikes against exposed targets, and ground-based armored fire provides additional coverage.
The Type 08 transports assault troops toward the target after the fire-strike phase. Additional Type 08s deliver clearance teams, which dismount and advance into the camp. Robotic dogs scout building interiors ahead of the troops to improve situational awareness and reduce personnel exposure.
Song said terrorist groups could also use drones for sabotage, requiring the People's Liberation Army (PLA) to develop effective countermeasures. He added that high-altitude terrain may demand specialized drone and counter-drone tactics, making realistic exercises essential for refining operational procedures.

title: NLC steps in to avert November 2 JUSAG strike
body: The National Labour Commission (NLC) has moved to prevent a looming disruption in the Judicial Service, directing the Minister of Jobs, Labour and Employment Relations to engage the Judicial Service Staff Association of Ghana (JUSAG) over its planned industrial action. The intervention follows JUSAG’s threat to begin an indefinite strike on November 2, 2026, over delays in approving and implementing a proposed review of salaries and related allowances for Judicial Service staff. In a letter dated October 26, 2026, the Commission asked the Minister to initiate discussions with the association and the relevant government stakeholders to resolve the dispute before the planned walkout. The NLC has also requested a report on the outcome of the engagement by Friday, November 6, 2026. As part of its intervention, the Commission advised JUSAG to suspend the planned strike, citing Section 161 of the Labour Act, 2003 (Act 651). Salary review dispute JUSAG had notified the Commission of its intended industrial action in a letter dated October 23, 2026, warning that its members would withdraw their services if the government failed to address their concerns over the salary review. The association is demanding approval of the Judicial Council’s recommendations for a 2026 salary review by the end of October, with the revised salaries to be paid in November. It is also seeking arrears covering January to October 2026. The dispute centres on delays in completing the review and implementing the proposed adjustments, with the association setting November 2 as the deadline for action. The planned strike could affect administrative and support services within the Judicial Service if the dispute remains unresolved. The extent of any disruption would depend on the participation of members and the status of negotiations. NLC seeks dialogue The Commission’s directive places responsibility on the Labour Minister to bring the parties and relevant government institutions to the negotiating table in an effort to settle the outstanding issues. The NLC’s intervention is aimed at resolving the disagreement through engagement and preventing an industrial action that could disrupt the work of the Judicial Service. The letter was signed by the Commission’s Executive Secretary, Dr Bernice A. Welbeck, and copied to the Office of the President, the Judicial Secretary, the Attorney-General and Minister for Justice, the Minister of Finance, and JUSAG General Secretary Abdulai Yakubu, among other recipients. With the strike deadline approaching, the proposed engagement is expected to focus on the status of the Judicial Council’s salary review recommendations, the approval process and arrangements for paying the revised salaries and arrears. The NLC has asked the Minister to report on the outcome of the discussions by November 6, five days after the date JUSAG has set for the commencement of its planned strike.

title: Nigeria supplies 127m barrels to local refineries in 9 months
body: Nigeria’s domestic refineries received more than 127 million barrels of Nigerian crude oil and condensate between January and September 2026 as the Federal Government intensifies efforts to strengthen local refining and reduce dependence on imported petroleum products. The Commission Chief Executive of the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC), Mrs. Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan, disclosed this at the 20th anniversary edition of OTL Africa Downstream Energy Week in Lagos on Monday. NUPRC is also consulting producers, refiners and other stakeholders on a domestic crude swap framework. “Under it, a refiner could receive crude from the nearest suitable production or export point instead of moving an allocated grade over long distances, which could take an estimated three to four dollars off the cost of every barrel,” he added. On production, Eyesan said Nigeria recorded an average of 1.717 million barrels per day of crude oil and condensate in September, a 2.34 per cent increase over August. Crude oil production alone averaged 1.53 million barrels per day, marking the fifth consecutive month the industry met or exceeded its quota. She attributed the improvement to better asset integrity, enhanced security of evacuation infrastructure, stronger collaboration with operators and sustained regulatory efforts to restore shut-in production. On the 2026 Licensing Round, she said the 40 blocks on offer would be subjected to a transparent evaluation process, with published criteria and mandatory disclosure of beneficial ownership. The NUPRC boss added that the Commission was enforcing the drill-or-drop principle to discourage speculative holding of licences, noting that 22 recent awardees were expected to contribute at least 250,000 barrels per day within five years. She reaffirmed the Commission’s commitment to meeting the Domestic Gas Delivery Obligation and working with the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) to align refinery demand with crude supply planning, ensuring that upstream gains translate into tangible benefits for households, industries and power generation. Meanwhile, the Authority Chief Executive of the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA), Engr. Rabiu Abdullahi Umar, said locally refined petrol now accounted for three out of every four litres consumed in Nigeria. He described the development as a major shift for a country that had historically depended heavily on imported petroleum products. However, Umar disclosed that petrol consumption exceeded supply in September, with daily consumption estimated at 44.4 million litres against supply of 38.7 million litres. The shortfall was covered from existing stocks. To guard against future disruptions, he said the Authority was targeting sufficient petroleum product stocks to cover between 30 and 45 days of national demand. Umar also acknowledged that Nigeria lacked reliable data on actual fuel consumption, despite decades of petroleum market operations. “No consumption data yet. We are working on this because up till now no data to show that this fuel station supplied this volume, that supplied that volume,” he said. He explained that the NMDPRA was working with an information technology firm to develop a system capable of tracking distribution and establishing more reliable consumption figures. As part of efforts to improve transparency, the Authority was reviewing internal licences and had signed a memorandum of understanding with the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission. Umar also disclosed that seven petroleum product testing laboratories had been launched in Port Harcourt, with two additional facilities expected before the end of the year, bringing the total to nine. He said the Authority had also launched the second revision of the Gas Transportation Network Code to strengthen the framework governing gas transportation infrastructure. Speaking at the event, President Bola Tinubu said Nigeria’s energy resources could drive prosperity across Africa, reaffirming his administration’s ambition to support the emergence of a regional energy hub. The president whose message was delivered by the Permanent Secretary, Ministry of Petroleum Resources, Mrs. Patience Oyekunle, emphasised the need for regional cooperation and an investment-driven, environmentally responsible energy sector. Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu said energy security was fundamental to economic security, warning that high and unreliable energy costs affected transport fares, manufacturing, food distribution and small businesses. He cited the growth of domestic refining as evidence of changing supply dynamics, noting that the Dangote Refinery produced about 42 million litres of petrol daily in August, while petrol imports fell by 26 per cent to approximately 14.6 million litres per day. Sanwo-Olu said Lagos was also reducing transport fuel demand through investments in rail services and cleaner energy. He disclosed that 152 First and Last Mile buses had been converted to compressed natural gas (CNG), cutting fuel costs by nearly half, while 2,000 CNG-powered trucks had been introduced under haulage reforms. He urged industry stakeholders to prioritise expanded storage and distribution infrastructure, financing for downstream and gas projects, and measures to ensure that the gains from domestic refining translated into stable and affordable prices for consumers.

title: Syria closes border crossing with Jordan after airstrikes
body:
BEIRUT, October 27. /TASS/. Syria’s General Authority of Borders and Customs has closed the Nasib border crossing with Jordan to passenger and freight transport, the agency said in a statement on X.
"We announce the temporary closure of the border crossing due to the situation in the Daraa Governorate," the statement reads. "Passenger and commercial traffic has been suspended in both directions to ensure the safety of travelers and border service personnel," the agency added.
Earlier, the Syrian Foreign Ministry said it had notified Amman of the decision, citing Jordan’s failure to coordinate its operations in Syria.
"We express deep regret over civilian casualties in Daraa caused by Jordanian airstrikes," the statement added.
On October 26, the Jordanian Air Force carried out strikes in southern Syria, targeting extremist groups reportedly linked to the terrorists behind a recent attack on St. George’s Orthodox Church in Jordan’s Al-Karak Governorate. According to Jordan’s Health Ministry, the October 23 terrorist attack killed nine people and injured 34 others.

title: PDP kicks as Dankwambo’s name appears on Gombe APC campaign list
body: There is growing confusion in Gombe State following the appearance of the name of former Governor Ibrahim Hassan Dankwambo on the list of the All Progressives Congress (APC) Campaign Council. Dankwambo, who is the leader of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in the state, is contesting for the Gombe North Senatorial seat in the 2027 general elections under the PDP platform. The list, published in national dailies on Monday, includes Dankwambo as a member of the APC campaign structure—a development that has stirred confusion among PDP supporters in the state. However, the state chapter of the PDP has officially disassociated Dankwambo from the APC’s advisory and campaign council list. The 666-member campaign council, chaired by Governor Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya, contains the names of prominent APC figures, including Senator Muhammad Danjuma Goje, Senator Usman Bayero Nafada, and Senator Sa’idu Ahmed Alkali. Senator Dankwambo’s name is listed alongside these top party chieftains appointed to drive the APC campaign ahead of the 2027 elections. Specifically, Senator Dankwambo appears at number seven on the 666-member campaign council list and number six on the 66-member advisory council, placing him above key figures within the state APC. The development is already generating intense reactions. As a former governor and serving political leader, Dankwambo is widely regarded as the face of the PDP in Gombe State, making his inclusion on the ruling party’s campaign list a major talking point. The inclusion has sparked questions about whether the senator has defected to the APC or relinquished his senatorial bid to enter into an alliance with the ruling party in the state. This development comes at a time when former Minister of Communications and Digital Economy, Prof. Isa Ali Pantami, is fighting to secure a place on the ballot under the PDP after his name was omitted from the final list released by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). Our correspondent reports that Dankwambo belongs to the faction of the PDP led by the Minister of the FCT, Barr. Nyesom Wike. The State Publicity Secretary of the PDP, Abdulkadir Ahmad Dukku, said in a statement that the inclusion of Dankwambo’s name on the APC campaign list was intended to create confusion among PDP members and supporters in the state. “Our attention has been drawn to the publication of a list of members of the APC campaign council in Gombe State, recently published in national dailies and across social media platforms,” Dukku said. “The list, which contains the name of the Gombe State PDP Leader, Senator Ibrahim Hassan Dankwambo, as a member of the Advisory Committee of the APC Campaign Council in Gombe State, is fake and intended to cause confusion among members and supporters of the PDP in the state.” He further disassociated the party and its leader from the purported list, adding that Senator Dankwambo was unaware of the development. The publicity secretary stressed that Dankwambo remains a leading member of the PDP at both state and national levels and is “also the PDP senatorial candidate for Gombe North in the forthcoming general elections.” Dukku accused the ruling APC in the state of engaging in “fabricated acts, calculated to cause mistrust and chaos among members and supporters of the PDP in Gombe State ahead of the 2027 general elections.”

title: 2027 polls: INEC opens online access to preliminary voters’ register
body: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has made the preliminary register of voters for the 2027 general election available online following concerns over the accessibility of the register. The commission, in a statement issued on Monday by Mohammed Kudu Haruna, Chairman of its Information and Voter Education Committee (IVEC), said the online publication was an additional measure to complement the physical display of the register conducted nationwide from October 9 to 15, 2026. INEC said the exercise was conducted in accordance with Section 19 of the Electoral Act, 2026, to enable registered voters to inspect their particulars and submit claims and objections as prescribed by law. The commission said it had taken note of concerns raised by Nigerians and other stakeholders over the need to make the register accessible online in addition to the physical display at registration areas. “Accordingly, and in furtherance of its commitment to transparency, accessibility and public confidence in the electoral process, the Commission has decided to make available on its online platform the same Preliminary Register of Voters earlier displayed at the Registration Areas,” the statement said. The register can be accessed through **https://display.inecnigeria.org**. INEC said the online platform was intended to facilitate wider public access to the register, while processing of claims and objections arising from the exercise continued. It added that the process would precede the certification and publication of the final register of voters scheduled for December 15, 2026. The commission appreciated the continued interest and constructive engagement of Nigerians and other stakeholders, reaffirming its commitment to transparency, accountability and the implementation of the Electoral Act, 2026, towards delivering credible elections.

title: Drop your presidential bid, support Tinubu, Kaduna APC tells Atiku
body: The Kaduna State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has urged former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar to withdraw from the 2027 presidential race and support President Bola Tinubu, asserting that the North has clearly demonstrated its preference for the incumbent. According to the party, the massive turnout at the APC presidential campaign flag-off in Kaduna on Saturday proved that Atiku can no longer rely on northern votes to push his presidential ambitions. The APC State Publicity Secretary, Mohammed Sani Haruna, made the call on Monday during a press briefing in Kaduna, where he described the crowd at the rally as overwhelming evidence of growing support for Tinubu across the region. Haruna urged Atiku to align with Tinubu in the interest of national unity, recalling what he described as the President’s past political gesture toward the former Vice-President. “It is on record that President Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu did Atiku Abubakar a favour by giving him a platform in 2011 to contest for the presidency of Nigeria,” Haruna said. He argued that Atiku should reciprocate that gesture by supporting Tinubu rather than seeking another bid for the nation’s top office. “There is no better time to align with Mr. President and show his patriotism for Nigeria than now—to work for the greater interest of the country,” Haruna added. The APC spokesperson also advised Atiku, who is approaching 80 years of age, to drop his presidential ambition, warning that another failed attempt could expose him to further political embarrassment. He noted that the Kaduna rally had shattered opposition expectations of securing dominant support in the North, a zone long considered central to Atiku’s electoral calculations. Haruna accused Atiku and other opposition figures of exploiting ethnic, religious, and regional sentiments to court northern voters, rather than highlighting tangible contributions to the region’s development. Addressing claims circulating on social media that crowd footage from the rally was generated using Artificial Intelligence (AI) and that attendees were paid to be there, the party spokesman dismissed the allegations as baseless. He insisted that the turnout was purely organic, pointing out that thousands of supporters arrived early and waited patiently for hours to gain entry. “People slept over at the venue. People queued as early as 4:00 a.m. to gain access into the stadium. You cannot buy that kind of sentiment,” he emphasized.

title: INEC’s missteps
body: In ordinary times, the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is in eye of the storm. As a consequence, it is often awash with controversy. With less than ninety days to the conduct of the 2027 General Elections, the Commission is expected to come under more intense and comprehensive scrutiny. This is more so when recently, the Commission’s Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, addressed a World Press Conference and Stakeholders’ Meeting at the International Conference Centre (Abuja) and explained INEC’s preparedness for the 2027 General Elections. Since that conference, which overarching objective was a “a call to action” on the electoral front, things have taken a frenzied turn at the Commission. The INEC chairman has since visited a number of the Commission’s offices outside Abuja. He has vowed, at one such engagement, that the glitch that visited the 2023 General Elections, and which smeared them, would not be allowed to rear its ugly head in the 2027 General Elections. The preliminary Register of Voters, as demanded by law, was displayed, nationwide, for Claims and Objections. Widespread publicity preceded the exercise. If the Commission’s work took a fevered pitch in the aftermath of the World Press Conference, and if the preliminary Register of Voters was displayed for Claims and Objections, it was alas, not uploaded on the Commission’s website as demanded by the Electoral Act 2026. The Act says, in clear and unmistakable terms, that: “Subject to the provision section 9(6) of this Act, the Commission shall, not later than 90 days to a general election, appoint a period of seven days during which a copy of the voters’ register for each Local Government, Area Council or Ward shall be displayed or published for public scrutiny at every registration area and on its official website or any website established by the Commission for that purpose.” Nick Dazang is a former director at the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). Not a few stakeholders – the media, civil society and political parties – visited the Commission’s website to scrutinise an online copy of the preliminary Register of Voters. But they did that without success and to no avail: they were, instead, advised to check back. There is no doubting the fact that the Commission published the provisional Register of Voters for the Claims and Objections which took place between 9th to 15th October. But that did not suffice. Neither was the Commission in full compliance with the law which insists that the same preliminary Register of Voters should be displayed on its website as well. By failing to upload the preliminary Register of Voters on its website, the Commission opens itself to the accusation of opacity and lack of transparency. Or the allegation that it has something to hide. Additionally, when the Commission fails to abide by laws it has freely given unto or bequeathed itself, it speaks clearly to corporate indiscipline and sloth. Besides, how does INEC, as chief driver of our elections, command the moral high ground or take its appropriate place as leader of the electoral process when it violates the sanctity of the laws that inform and govern elections? How can it beam the light that other lesser stakeholders in the electoral process may follow? As if this misstep were not bad enough, INEC recently effected a minor deployment/reshuffle of its Directors. Such deployments and re-organisations are routine. They go with all Ministries, Departments and Agencies (MDAs). In the instance of INEC, such deployments and re-organisations are usually effected long before the conduct of elections. That way, the directors involved have ample time to settle down and get acclimatised to their new roles. Eyebrows are seldom raised as to the purport of such deployments. But when such deployments are carried out at the eve of general elections, they are bound to elicit the notice of stakeholders and to arouse controversy. The particular deployment that continues to stir controversy is that of the Director, Electoral Operations. The Director must be deserving of her appointment. This may be what informed her deployment in the first instance. But given the cruciality of that department to the conduct of the 2027 General Elections and her spousal relationship to a prominent player in one of the Presidential Campaign Councils(PCC), the Commission ought to have exercised circumspection and sensitivity. It is possible that in carrying out this deployment, the Commission was not informed or cognisant of her relationship to a prominent politician and one of the spokespersons of a presidential campaign. Now that this is common knowledge, the Commission needs to act promptly. In doing this, it has a number of options. The Commission can direct the director to recuse herself of her functions until after the conduct of the elections. Her Deputy (Director) Electoral Operations should then be directed to act in the position (of substantive Director), subject, of course, to the considerations of merit and federal character. To proceed as things are will do considerable violence to the Commission’s core values of neutrality and impartiality. It will also be an egregious assault on the level playing field which INEC ought to provide to all contestants. These will in turn impact negatively on the credibility and integrity of the elections. INEC should redress its steps. It will assure all contestants that it has no preferred candidate or that it has “no dog in the fight”. Furthermore, such a redress will align with its mission to make the 2027 General Elections “a global benchmark for transparency, integrity and peace”.

title: The prince, the General, the fallen ally: The mechanics of neutralization (I)
body: There is nothing new under the sun and nothing new in the spectacle now unfolding between President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and his former ally, Nasir Ahmad El-Rufai. What the public sees as betrayal is the oldest choreography in the theatre of power. El-Rufai’s restrained statement—that he seeks neither revenge nor retribution, that accountability belongs to Almighty Allah—is noble. But peace with circumstance is not the same as understanding circumstance. What has happened to him is not unique. The Greeks knew it. The Romans perfected it. The Italians codified it. Nigeria is now living it. Machiavelli’s The Prince was never a moral treatise but a clinical dissection of how power is acquired, held, and lost. In Chapter Seven he warns that princes who rise through the arms and fortune of others stand on shaky ground, depending on those who elevated them; the prince who rises through the strength of others must eventually neutralise those others—or be neutralised by them. Tinubu understood this instinctively. When El-Rufai delivered the northern votes that made Tinubu’s presidency possible in 2023, he was no mere supporter. He was a kingmaker—a general who mobilised troops, secured territory, and handed victory to his prince. According to former minister Solomon Dalung, El-Rufai created Tinubu; remove El-Rufai, and Tinubu would not have won in 2023. This was never friendship but a calculated transaction. El-Rufai needed Tinubu for post-gubernatorial relevance; Tinubu needed northern legitimacy. Machiavelli warns that a prince must never fully trust those who serve out of their own ambition. The alliance was always destined to fracture because it was built on utility, not trust. The nomination process was the masterstroke. When Tinubu submitted his ministerial list in July 2023, El-Rufai’s name was conspicuously included. It appeared a reward for loyalty. Machiavelli would have recognised it as a feint. By nominating El-Rufai, Tinubu achieved three objectives: he shifted blame for rejection onto the Senate; he placed El-Rufai under public scrutiny and security clearance; and bought time to consolidate a loyalist cabinet. This is indirect action—achieving the goal while concealing the hand. In Chapter Eighteen, Machiavelli advises that the prince be a great feigner and dissembler. The nomination was appearance; the rejection was reality; the Senate bridged the distance. The Senate’s rejection on alleged security grounds was not due process but performance of it. Other governors with comparable or more troubling profiles were cleared without incident. They were pliable, unambitious, or sufficiently indebted to the presidency. El-Rufai was none of these. His independent stature, northern network, and capacity to mobilise made him a liability in a cabinet Tinubu intended to control absolutely. The Senate became the intermediary that performed the unpopular act while the president preserved plausible deniability. El-Rufai later confirmed this. In a 2025 interview, he said: “The president did not want me in his cabinet. He changed his mind.” He called the security clearance a “smokescreen,” noting that “less qualified” nominees were confirmed “because the president made a call.” This transforms the Machiavellian reading from inference to documented allegation. History offers chilling parallels. In Rome, Sejanus, prefect of the Praetorian Guard under Tiberius, was the emperor’s most trusted ally. He eliminated rivals and became second most powerful. But he became too capable, too indispensable. Tiberius orchestrated his fall via letters read before the Senate. Sejanus was condemned by the Senate, strangled in prison, and his body cast down the Gemonian Stairs for the mob to abuse. Like El-Rufai, he was elevated, used, and neutralised through institutional machinery. The difference is that El-Rufai survived. The Ottoman devshirme offers a colder version: Christian boys elevated to the highest offices, but with no independent family or tribal base, destroyable by the silent bowstring. El-Rufai is no devshirme servant. He has an independent base—which is precisely why he was neutralised. The prince fears not the servant who owes everything to him, but the ally who can stand alone. Nor is this experience peculiar to El-Rufai, or to politics, or to our century; it is the common inheritance of mankind, written into the scriptures of all faiths and the chronicles of all nations. History gave us Julius Caesar, struck down by Brutus, the man he had pardoned—”Et tu, Brute?” is the eternal cry of every leader who finds the dagger in a friend’s hand. The Bible is a catalogue of such wounds: Joseph sold by his own brothers; David betrayed by Absalom and Ahithophel; Job abandoned by accusing friends; Jesus delivered for thirty pieces of silver by Judas, denied by Peter, deserted by Demas. Islam tells the same truth. The Quran recounts Yusuf—”the best of stories”—whose brothers cast him into a well, yet God raised him to the treasury of Egypt and made him say to his betrayers, “No blame upon you today.” The Prophet Muhammad himself was stoned at Ta’if and tested at Uhud when the archers abandoned their posts; and Karbala remains the enduring testimony that those who invite a leader may be the first to abandon him. The Quran consoles every betrayed soul: “You will surely be tested in your possessions and in yourselves” (3:186), and “perhaps you hate a thing and it is good for you” (2:216). What El-Rufai now feels is therefore no aberration but a rite of passage—painful, yes, but part of life and, rightly borne, an experience worth the while. It is also a reminder that not everyone is ready for the bullet. Betrayal breaks some and refines others; only those with the constitution to absorb it without bitterness can convert the wound into wisdom. El-Rufai’s own testimony invites deeper reflection, stated diplomatically yet forcefully. As a Muslim he knows that power belongs to God alone, who gives and withdraws it as He wills. Dominion is His; He gives and takes as He pleases. The lesson cuts both ways. The prince now seated must never assume permanence, for the same Hand that elevated him can lower him. The ally now cast aside must never assume his season has ended, for the same Hand that permitted his humiliation can restore him. God uses human beings as instruments—Tinubu was in part El-Rufai’s instrument, just as El-Rufai now appears Tinubu’s casualty; both remain instruments in a design neither controls. This is no licence for fatalism but a call for humility and vigilance. Human beings must be careful with assumptions, whether of invincibility or of irrelevance. The prudent man plans, prepares, and waits—but does not presume to know the decree. Nigeria’s system is patrimonial. Power flows through personal ties, patronage, and ethnic alliances, not impersonal institutions. The prince cannot rely on institutional loyalty; he must rely on individuals whose loyalty lasts only as long as their interests align. El-Rufai’s base is the North. Tinubu needed northern legitimacy to win; once elected, he had to prevent El-Rufai from using the North independently. The rejection was never merely about security. It was about restructuring the North’s relationship with the centre, ensuring northern leaders owed their positions to Tinubu, not to El-Rufai. This is divide-and-rule. Machiavelli would have recognised it instantly.

title: England, Bayern forward Kane crowned 2026 Ballon d'Or winner
body: Harry Kane completed his long quest for football's highest individual honor on Monday, with the Bayern Munich and England striker winning the Ballon d'Or after a record-breaking season that cemented his status as one of the game's greatest goalscorers.Kane is the first Englishman to win the prestigious award in 25 years, after Michael Owen won it in 2001."Wow, wow, wow!" Kane said after taking the stage. "I am almost speechless. Being here in London makes it extra special. It feels like a good omen for me tonight. Thank you to everyone who voted for me. I can imagine it was tough this year."Some world-class players in the room tonight. Congratulations to all the winners and nominees tonight, and an impressive showing of determination and hard work can really achieve."Spain midfielder Alexia Putellas won the Ballon d'Or Féminin for the third time.Kane's move to Bayern in 2023 brought the team trophies that had long eluded him. In 2025-26, he coupled that success with goalscoring numbers that made him the leading Ballon d'Or candidate.The England captain produced the most prolific campaign of his life, scoring 61 goals in 51 games for Bayern across all competitions as the German giants completed a domestic league and cup double.By the end of the season, Kane had established himself as Europe's leading goalscorer, turning every competition into a showcase of his finishing ability.His influence stretched far beyond club football. As England embarked on another attempt to end decades of hurt at the World Cup, Kane once again emerged as the team's driving force.He scored six goals during the tournament and led England to the semi-finals, combining his clinical finishing with the leadership and composure that have defined his international career.In many ways, the award represents the culmination of a remarkable journey. Few players have experienced a career arc quite like Kane's.Once struggling to establish himself at Tottenham Hotspur as a youngster, being sent out on numerous loans, he developed into one of the most complete center forwards of his generation, capable of scoring every type of goal while also functioning as a playmaker.The Ballon d'Or has often rewarded players whose success was built on flair and spectacle, but Kane's triumph is a tribute to consistency, intelligence and productivity on an exceptional scale.Week after week, he delivered. Match after match, he decided contests. There were no prolonged slumps and few quiet nights.His numbers were almost impossible to ignore.Kane finished the campaign with 73 goals for club and country, a total rarely seen in the modern era. More importantly, those goals arrived in moments of genuine significance, helping Bayern collect trophies and driving England deep into the biggest tournament in the sport.Fierce competitionThe competition for this year's award was fierce. Kylian Mbappe broke World Cup scoring records. Lamine Yamal helped Spain to World Cup glory. Yet voters ultimately chose Kane, whose excellence lasted the entire season.At 33, Kane has finally claimed the game's highest individual honor, adding a Ballon d'Or to a legacy that already places him among football's greatest strikers as England's all-time leading marksman and their record World Cup scorer.Putellas was presented with the women's award after winning the treble with Barcelona in the 2025-26 campaign, in addition to the Spanish Super Cup. She moved to Women's Super League side London City Lionesses in July after 14 years at Barca.

title: How the BC Conservatives plan to tackle crime and public safety
body:
B.C.’s newly elected Conservative government is promising to tackle crime and public safety.
The Conservatives pledged to end open drug use, improve access to mental health care and empower police to enforce the Mental Health Act to connect people with mandatory treatment.
“Here is what British Columbians told us over the past few years,” B.C.’s Premier-designate Lorne Doerkson said on Sunday.
“They want a province that they can afford. They want an emergency room that is open at 2 a.m. when their child is sick. They want a main street they can walk down safely; they want good jobs, and they want their kids to be able to build a life here instead of packing up for another part of the country.”
One Vancouver small business owner is optimistic that things will change.
Kurtis Lemon says he’s witnessed public drug use and street disorder outside his downtown Vancouver flower shop.
“There’s nobody here that’s holding anybody accountable at all,” he told Global News.
“They’re just free to do whatever they want, steal from retailers to buy drugs and it needs to stop.”
Criminal lawyer Ravi Hira says the provincial government has the powers to act on those campaign promises, unlike the forced treatment David Eby’s NDP tried to implement.
“You may have some mental health problems, but you’re able to consent or not consent to treatment and what he was doing through his legislation, which was found to be unconstitutional, was to take that right away and leave it with a bureaucrat,” he said.
The BC Conservatives’ plan has not been tested in court.
The Safe Streets campaign pledge included hiring 250 more police officers and adding 500 RCMP officers over five years in rural communities plagued by crime.
“Our justice system has basically been stuck due to a lack of judges, a lack of resources and for 10 years the NDP didn’t care,” Hira said.
The Conservatives also promised to hire 50 new prosecutors, work with Ottawa to fund 20 more trial judges and add sheriff and court capacity, so delays don’t allow criminals to walk free.
Lemon, who beat his own severe addiction to cocaine, said consequences are needed to spur rapid change.
“If we’re just standing around waiting for these people to put their hand up and ask for help or say I’m ready for help, I don’t think that we’re gonna solve the problem,” he said.
“Some of these people are so far gone past the point of asking for help or giving themselves a chance to get some help.”

title: What to know as JPMorgan sets up merchant bank
body: American financial services giant JPMorgan Chase & Co. has moved closer to establishing a merchant bank in Nigeria after receiving approval-in-principle from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), a development that could expand corporate financing options and deepen the country’s access to international capital. The approval, granted last week allows the bank to proceed with plans to establish JPMorgan Merchant Bank Nigeria Limited, subject to the completion of outstanding regulatory and operational requirements. The development marks a significant step in JPMorgan’s expansion in Africa’s largest economy, where it has maintained a representative office in Lagos for several years. If granted a final licence, the proposed merchant bank would provide a broader platform for the US lender to serve Nigerian corporations, financial institutions and institutional investors. N50bn deposit for licence As part of the licensing process, JPMorgan reportedly deposited N50 billion, equivalent to about $38 million, with the CBN to meet the minimum capital requirement for a nationally licensed merchant bank. Daily Trust reports that the deposit fulfilled a key requirement but did not automatically guarantee approval to commence operations. The bank must still satisfy the remaining regulatory conditions, complete the necessary incorporation and operational arrangements, and obtain final authorisation from the CBN before beginning business. JPMorgan had reportedly indicated plans to commence operations before the end of 2026, subject to regulatory clearance. Five Nigerians appointed to leadership positions The proposed institution has secured approval for seven board members, including five Nigerians with experience spanning banking, monetary policy, financial technology, law and corporate management. Adedapo Olagunju, who has headed JPMorgan’s West Africa business since 2018, is expected to serve as managing director. He previously held senior positions at Access Bank and Investment Banking & Trust Company, now part of Stanbic IBTC. Chinedum Nzelu Izunwanne, known professionally as Chi Nzelu, is also among the appointees. He is JPMorgan’s global head of macro electronic trading and has experience in foreign exchange, financial technology, automation and risk management. Former acting CBN Governor Sarah Omotunde Alade has been appointed an independent non-executive director. She served as deputy governor of the apex bank from 2007 to 2017 and briefly became acting governor in 2014. She later served as special adviser to the President on finance and the economy. Another independent non-executive director, Olukonyinsola Ajayi, popularly known as Konyin Ajayi, is a partner at Olaniwun Ajayi LP, with expertise in banking, project finance, capital markets, mergers and acquisitions, energy and infrastructure. Seni Adetu, a corporate executive with more than three decades of multinational leadership experience, completes the list of five Nigerian appointees. He previously led Guinness Nigeria and East African Breweries and held senior positions at Coca-Cola and Diageo. Their appointments bring regulatory, financial, legal and corporate expertise to the proposed bank’s leadership. What the bank will offer JPMorgan Merchant Bank Nigeria Limited is expected to focus on wholesale banking, corporate finance, structured financing, treasury services, capital markets and advisory services. Its operations could also create opportunities in trade finance, payments, lending and cross-border transactions, depending on the final scope of its licence.
