title: Ebola: Ghana must track incoming travellers, not rely on temperature checks – Prof Amuasi
body: Ghana must prioritise effective surveillance and the tracking of incoming travellers in its preparations against Ebola, rather than rely heavily on temperature checks and hand sanitisers at airports, a public health expert has warned. Professor John Amuasi, Head of Global Health at the School of Public Health, Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), said visible screening measures offered limited assurance because people infected with the virus might not show symptoms when they arrived in the country. He said the country’s preparedness should focus on collecting accurate information on travellers, verifying their contact details and ensuring they could be reached quickly if they developed symptoms after arrival. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Monday, October 26, Professor Amuasi said Ghana needed to strengthen its surveillance systems to identify and follow up on people who might have been exposed to the virus. His comments come amid concerns about the risk of cross-border transmission as African countries respond to Ebola cases and strengthen measures to prevent further spread. Professor Amuasi, who is also a research leader at the Kumasi Centre for Collaborative Research in Tropical Medicine (KCCR), said the experience of recent cases underscored the importance of surveillance at points of entry and the ability to follow up on travellers after they had entered a country. Surveillance beyond the airport The professor said airport screening could not, on its own, reliably identify all infected travellers, particularly those who were not yet showing symptoms. He said measures such as temperature checks and hand sanitiser stations could reassure the public but should not be mistaken for a comprehensive system for detecting Ebola. “What I was trying to explain was that it’s easy to put a bunch of measures in place at the airport, you know, these temperature checks and doing the hand sanitiser thing, but there’s a little bit to which this is helpful. And this is why I am not personally too alarmed about what has been put in place at the airport in terms of what you can see with your eyes,” he explained. He stressed that the absence of visible symptoms did not necessarily mean a traveller posed no public health concern, making follow-up systems an important part of outbreak preparedness. “Nobody is going to be coming off an aeroplane, in fact, or even jumping off an aeroplane when they are visibly sick with signs and symptoms of Ebola. And therefore, your ability to catch it when someone is coming off a plane is really limited,” he stated. Professor Amuasi said the effectiveness of Ghana’s response would depend on whether health authorities could identify people who might have been exposed and take appropriate action if symptoms emerged. “Temperature checks, use of alcohol, hand rubs – all these things are nice. They give people some level of confidence. But the reality is that they are not going to catch Ebola cases for you,” he noted. Reliable data, prompt follow-up The KNUST academic said a more effective approach would involve gathering accurate information from incoming travellers and establishing reliable means of contacting them after arrival. He said authorities should verify telephone numbers and have mechanisms to locate travellers when necessary, while providing clear instructions on where to report if they developed symptoms. “What is needed is actually the ability to test. And this doesn’t exist as it stands right now. We can’t be doing PCR tests for everyone coming in.” Professor Amuasi acknowledged that testing every person entering Ghana would not be practical. He argued, however, that accurate traveller information and an effective follow-up system would help public health officials respond more quickly when a potential exposure was identified. “So for me, the single most important thing is being able to collect as accurate data as possible on every single person who comes off a plane in this country, making sure that the phone numbers they submit are accurate and finding a way of verifying it, making sure that we have a way of being able to geolocate them if necessary, and also making sure that they are able to report to designated facilities or via the phone lines or other contact means if they come down with any of the symptoms. So for me, the education is more towards those who are coming into the country and ensuring that we’re able to collect as detailed data as possible of those coming in. But for the other visual things we see like the alcohol hand rub and the temperature checks, they are nice.” He added that the visible measures had a role in reassuring travellers but should not distract from the need for effective surveillance and follow-up. “They help people to be more confident and comfortable. But at this stage right now, they don’t come to bear.” Nigeria’s experience Professor Amuasi also urged caution in interpreting reports of Ebola cases in the region, saying the situation in Nigeria needed to be understood in the context of the known exposure and subsequent response. He said the World Health Organisation (WHO) had indicated that there was no active Ebola case in Nigeria at the time of his comments, following the evacuation of the infected person. “Currently, as we speak, the WHO is indicating that there is no active case of Ebola in Nigeria right now because the one person who had it has been evacuated. Of course, we will need to wait for a while to see whether there was any further transmission.” The situation, he said, reinforced the importance of tracing contacts and monitoring people who might have been exposed, rather than depending exclusively on checks conducted when travellers first arrive.

title: Libya says international aviation restrictions lifted after 11 years
body: Libya’s Ministry of Transport said on Monday that the UN’s International Civil Aviation Organisation removed airspace restrictions it issued in 2015 during the country’s civil war. The ministry said ICAO Secretary General Juan Carlos Salazar announced the decision, formally issued on October 23, at the opening of a meeting of civil aviation officials from the Middle East in Doha. “This measure comes as ​a result of the notable progress made and the confidence placed ⁠in the capabilities of the Libyan civil aviation sector in recent times,” ​the Tripoli-based Ministry of Transport said in a statement on its verified Facebook ​page. The ministry, in a separate statement, said the North African country has received requests for permits to transit Libyan airspace that it characterised as “unprecedented demand from international airlines.” “The total number ​of permits registered for 2026-2027 winter season has surged to 61,968 flights ​per month, effective from this November,” the ministry said, calling it a significant jump from ‌an ⁠average of 2,000 transit flights per month during the 2025-2026 season. “Such an increase will generate substantial financial revenues using Libyan airspace,” it added. Libya slid into chaos after the fall of Muammar Gaddafi in a NATO-backed uprising in 2011. Three years later, a civil war broke out between armed factions vying for power and divided the country between eastern and western administrations. The war caused damage to ​up to 20 aircraft, including Airbus (AIR.PA), models, at Tripoli International ​Airport ⁠in 2014. Few airlines currently operate flights in and out of Libya, and they have long been limited to destinations such as Tunisia, Jordan, Turkey, Egypt, Saudi Arabia ​, and Sudan. The ministry added that ICAO would circulate the decision to all 193 member states for implementation.

title: Osi Samuels Assumes office as APIN CEO
body: Dr. Jay Osi Samuels has assumed office as the new Chief Executive Officer of APIN Public Health Initiatives with effect from October 1, 2026, succeeding Prof. Prosper Okonkwo, the organisation’s pioneer chief executive. Samuels, who previously served as Deputy Chief Executive Officer, Programmes, joined APIN in 2006. His appointment brings to the top role a member of the leadership team who has helped direct its public health programmes and institutional development. The leadership transition follows APIN’s 25th anniversary celebrations and opens a new chapter for an indigenous organisation whose work has grown from HIV prevention and treatment to a broader range of public health interventions. Okonkwo joined APIN as a Project Manager in 2004 and became its pioneer CEO in 2007. His tenure spanned the organisation’s development into an independent Nigerian institution working with government, universities and international development partners. APIN started as a Harvard School of Public Health project supported by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation. It became an independent non-governmental organisation in 2007 and subsequently assumed direct responsibility for programmes previously managed through Harvard. Its work has included HIV services supported by the United States President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief through the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. During Okonkwo’s tenure, APIN broadened its activities to include tuberculosis, malaria, maternal and child health, and health systems strengthening. Its programmes have supported health facilities through laboratory development, workforce training and improved information systems, alongside clinical services and community interventions. Okonkwo’s contributions to public health also earned him the Health Activism Award at the 2023 BudgIT Active Citizens Awards, where he was the inaugural recipient in that category. Samuels holds a medical degree from the University of Ibadan and a Master of Science degree in Epidemiology from Harvard T Chan School of Public Health. Before joining APIN, he worked as a research associate at Harvard, studying the molecular epidemiology of HIV in Nigeria. His experience covers public health programme management, research and health systems strengthening. As Deputy CEO, Programmes, Samuels oversaw APIN’s programme directorates, guided the implementation of donor-funded interventions and coordinated new business development. The role involved supporting health facilities to deliver sustainable services while aligning programme objectives with responsible resource management. His work has also included leadership in electronic medical records and mobile health, alongside APIN’s contributions to national health data systems. These areas connect the organisation’s service delivery experience with the use of information to improve programme performance and patient care. Addressing the staff of the organisation shortly after assuming office, Samuels paid tribute to Okonkwo and outlined an agenda to protect APIN’s core programmes while building its capacity as a broader health systems institution. “Grants begin and end. Projects begin and end. Donor priorities change. Institutions must endure,” he explained; calling for a more diversified resource base and stronger partnerships with government, philanthropy, academia and the private sector. His priorities include developing the APIN Research Institute, advancing digital transformation and positioning the organisation for opportunities beyond Nigeria. He also outlined plans to use his first 100 days to listen across teams and strengthen governance, financial management, procurement and programme performance. He called for accountability at every level, including the chief executive’s, and the need to keep patients at the centre of programme decisions. Samuels reminded staff that “behind every number in our reports is a human being.” “The first twenty-five years gave us a legacy. The next twenty-five years should give us a responsibility,” he stated.

title: Ukraine Slams Moscow Hosting 2030 Weightlifting Worlds, Demands Reversal
body:
Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha condemned the International Weightlifting Federation’s (IWF) decision to award Moscow the 2030 World Weightlifting Championships, calling it “unacceptable” and urging international sporting bodies to reverse the move, which he warned could normalize Russia’s aggression against Ukraine.
In a statement on X on Monday, Oct. 26, Sybiha said the decision was unprecedented since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“The decision by the International Weightlifting Federation to award Moscow the 2030 World Championships is unacceptable,” he wrote.
He warned that the move could pave the way for major international sporting events to return to Russia despite its continuing war against Ukraine.
“Russia continues to kill Ukrainians, including athletes. It is immoral to grant Moscow the privilege of hosting a major international sporting event while its aggression continues,” Sybiha said.
The foreign minister argued that Moscow could use the championships to portray itself as returning to normal international relations without ending its invasion or facing accountability.
“We must not allow the Kremlin to use international sport to claim recognition, legitimacy. or a return to business as usual without ending its aggression or facing accountability,” he wrote.
Sybiha called on the IWF, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) and the wider international sporting community to overturn the decision.
Ukraine’s Minister of Youth and Sports, Matvii Bidnyi, said Ukrainian athletes would not compete at the 2030 World Championships if the tournament went ahead in Moscow.
“Ukrainian athletes will not go there,” Bidnyi told UNN .
The minister said Ukraine would use legal, political, and diplomatic channels to challenge the decision and seek support from international partners.
According to Interfax-Ukraine , Kyiv is preparing formal appeals to the IWF and IOC, demanding a new, transparent selection process for the championship’s host country.
Bidnyi also plans to raise the issue with European sports ministers, including representatives of EU member states and the Council of Europe.
He stressed that Ukraine generally favors continued participation in international competitions rather than leaving the sporting arena to Russian athletes, but said holding a world championship in Moscow presented an exceptional situation.
The minister warned that the Kremlin would use the event for propaganda and to portray Russia as internationally rehabilitated despite its continuing military campaign.
The IWF announced on Sunday, Oct. 25, that its Executive Board had selected Moscow to host the 2030 World Championships.
It is the first time since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 that an international federation overseeing an Olympic sport has awarded Russia an event of this level.
The federation also selected Ahmedabad, India, to host the 2029 senior World Championships, while Kosovo and Venezuela were awarded youth and junior tournaments in 2028.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Romanian intelligence identifies Russian sabotage network thought to have caused industrial fire
body: Romania's Intelligence Service said on Monday it had identified a sabotage network coordinated by Russia, which it believed was responsible for a fire in September at an industrial site in central Romania near a state-owned weapons company.The European Union and NATO states share a land border of more than 600 km (370 miles) with Ukraine, and centrist president Nicusor Dan has said it is the target of a hybrid war waged by Russia to destabilize nations that support Kyiv.The attacks range from drone incursions into Romanian airspace to cyberattacks, disinformation campaigns, acts of sabotage and attacks on cargo vessels near Romanian waters, Dan has said.Russia's embassy in Bucharest could not immediately be reached for comment outside business hours, but Moscow has repeatedly denied such accusations.Romanian organized crime prosecutors said they were seeking the extradition of two Belarusian suspects apprehended in Germany and one Ukrainian detained in Poland who were all suspected of involvement in the arson case.The Intelligence Service said all three were part of the network coordinated by Russia, whose coordinators had assigned it targets including "state and private weapons production facilities, as well as other objectives of military and industrial interest."NATO members Romania, Bulgaria, Poland targets of recent Russian attacksA year ago, Poland and Romania detained eight people suspected of involvement in a Russian plan to send exploding parcels to Ukraine.Dan accused Russia of escalating its attacks on NATO's eastern flank this month after a series of drone strikes on cargo vessels in the Black Sea.At least eight cargo ships have been hit off the coast of NATO members Romania and Bulgaria in the past three weeks. Some 34 sailors are reported dead or missing.

title: Shitty Screenshare
body:
Did you know OBS or FFmpeg can go directly into a video conference? You configure everything, so you control exactly the quality you are going to get. WHIP support means these tools now speak the protocol of video conferencing.
Send them an angry email. Tell them you don't want their crappy proprietary client. You want open standards that let you bring the tools you prefer.
WHIP is an open standard for sending live video to a service using WebRTC. Your provider gives you a server URL and a stream key, called a bearer token. Before to join a conference call each client had to run custom code. That means FFmpeg/OBS would never be able to join.
A lack of control. Your browser is picking a bitrate, codec or resolution that doesn't match what you need.
OBS and FFmpeg let you choose your resolution, frame rate, bitrate, and codec. You can tune those settings for the content you're sharing and the hardware and connection you have.
OBS Virtual Camera sends your OBS scene to the conferencing app as a webcam. You can pick the layout of your stream, but the conferencing app still handles encoding.
See the OBS WHIP setup guide I try and keep it up to date.
I work on WHIP in OBS. I'm tired of shitty screenshares when it is easily fixed.

title: Jay-Z picks himself to headline the Super Bowl halftime show
body: The man who helped produce the Super Bowl halftime show is stepping into the spotlight: Jay-Z will headline it. The NFL , Apple Music, and Roc Nation announced Monday night that Jay-Z will headline the halftime festivities on Feb. 14 at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell said he had one request when the league first reached an agreement with Roc Nation: that Jay-Z take the stage himself “whenever the moment felt right to him.” “From ‘Reasonable Doubt’ to standing on the Super Bowl halftime stage, this has been a journey,” Jay-Z said in a statement. “Thirty years of music, work, and culture on the world’s biggest stage. This run continues to be a dream come true.” After days of speculation , Jay-Z is set to return to the stadium where he closed his celebration of the 30th anniversary of “Reasonable Doubt,” the mogul’s 1996 debut album. The concerts included three sold-out shows at Yankee Stadium and sold-out performances in London and Paris, ahead of a weekend stop at SoFi Stadium. Jay-Z’s Roc Nation has partnered with the NFL since 2019 to advise on and help produce the league’s entertainment presentations, including the Super Bowl halftime show. At the time, Jay-Z told Goodell, “If this is about me performing at the Super Bowl, then we can just end this conversation now.” Seven years later, Jay-Z is ready to perform. Jay-Z, born Shawn Carter, has won 25 Grammy Awards and received 89 nominations, the second-most in history behind his wife, Beyoncé — who has performed at two Super Bowls. His catalogue also includes the albums “The Blueprint” and “The Black Album,” and hit songs such as “Hard Knock Life (Ghetto Anthem),” “99 Problems” and “Empire State of Mind,” his collaboration with Alicia Keys. Last year, “Reasonable Doubt” was inducted into the Grammy Hall of Fame. His recent concerts brought out a rotating cast of guests. At SoFi Stadium, his daughter Blue Ivy played piano on “The Story of O.J.” and “Dead Presidents,” while Scarface, John Legend and DJ Khaled joined him on opening night. Dr Dre, Snoop Dogg and Too $hort appeared during Saturday’s finale. Earlier in the run, Beyoncé, Rihanna, Eminem and Nas were among the guests at Yankee Stadium. Jay-Z has built a career as an executive and entrepreneur. The Brooklyn rapper co-founded Roc-A-Fella Records and founded Roc Nation in 2008, building it into an entertainment company that works with artists and athletes. Jay-Z became the first rapper inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame in 2017 and joined the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2021. He is also a four-time Emmy winner. Roc Nation will executive produce the halftime show, with Hamish Hamilton directing. The halftime show has collected Emmys in recent years. Bad Bunny’s February performance won a record seven Emmys, including Best Variety Special (Live), while Kendrick Lamar’s show last year won for music direction.

title: Greece and Allies Reject Turkey-Libya Maritime Deal as Illegal (VID)
body: Greece, Egypt, Cyprus, Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates and the European Union have rejected the 2019 Turkey-Libya maritime memorandum, declaring it contrary to international law and incapable of providing a legal basis for maritime boundary delimitation or producing legal effects for third states. Greek Foreign Minister George Gerapetritis delivered the joint statement on behalf of the six participants following Libya’s House of Representatives’ recent decision to ratify the memorandum, which concerns the delimitation of maritime jurisdiction areas in the Mediterranean. “The memorandum remains null and void, runs counter to international law and cannot constitute a lawful basis for the delimitation of maritime zones or produce legal effects for third states,” Gerapetritis said. The joint statement warned that the Libyan parliament’s decision raised serious concerns about regional security and stability. It also highlighted a broader challenge to the international legal order: ensuring that unilateral bilateral agreements do not undermine established international law or infringe on the rights of third states. Gerapetritis stressed that the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), together with customary international law, provides the legal framework for delimiting maritime zones. These rules, he said, are fundamental to predictability, legal certainty and peaceful relations between states. He cautioned that accepting bilateral agreements that disregard applicable international law would set a dangerous precedent, undermining the international legal order and the principles that underpin the peaceful settlement of disputes. The statement said the memorandum disregards the geographical realities of the Mediterranean and the maritime rights of coastal states, including the rights of islands under UNCLOS. It added that the Libyan parliament’s ratification did not change the memorandum’s legal status. Six parties reaffirm support for a united Libya The six participants reaffirmed their commitment to reunifying Libya’s institutions and supporting the prospect of a united and prosperous country. They stressed that a stable Libya that actively participates in regional cooperation is essential to peace and security across the Mediterranean. They also said Libya’s political transition and relations with neighbouring countries must respect international law and the principles of good neighbourly relations. Greece remains open to maritime talks with Libya The statement also addressed bilateral talks between Greece and Libya on maritime boundary delimitation. It said Greece had pursued negotiations in good faith and in accordance with international law and remained ready to continue them. “Respect for international law is an essential prerequisite for regional stability and for maintaining a rules-based international order,” Gerapetritis said. The joint declaration followed the Libyan House of Representatives’ approval of the 2019 memorandum on October 20. The European Union has also stated that the agreement infringes the sovereign rights of third states, does not comply with the law of the sea and is null and void. title: Trump approval rises from record low to 32% ahead of midterm election - poll
body: US President Donald Trump's public approval rating inched higher to 32%, up a percentage point from last week's record low, ahead of the November 3 midterm elections that will decide which party controls Congress, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll completed on Monday.Trump's fellow Republicans are fighting to retain the party's majorities in the House of Representatives and Senate.The five-day nationwide poll also showed that registered voters broadly favored Democrats over Republicans by 47% to 36% when asked which party they would pick for Congress in what is known as a "generic ballot" question. Some 11% said they did not know who they would vote for if the election were held today.That gap of 11 percentage points between Democrats and Republicans was 1 percentage point tighter than in a Reuters/Ipsos poll that closed on October 19. The latest poll additionally asked undecided voters which party they were leaning toward. Factoring in their responses, the national race appeared somewhat tighter, with Democrats leading by 9 percentage points, 50% to 41%.For Republicans, losing control of either chamber could complicate Trump's agenda in the last two years ​of his second term as president.Generic ballot polls are national polls that provide an overall view of which party poll respondents would like to see in charge in Congress. While these polls provide a view of national public sentiment, they do not ‌capture the nuances of the state-by-state and district-by-district contests that determine control of the Senate and House, contests in which Republicans hold some structural advantages.Steep Senate climb for democratsPolitical analysts generally see the Democrats having a good chance of winning control of the House, but think they face a steeper climb to win the Senate.It remains to be seen how many voters will actually cast ballots. The voters who appeared most likely to vote still favored Democrats over Republicans by 9 points, 53% to 44%.The fight for Congress has appeared to turn on views around inflation, which has surged since Trump ordered military strikes on Iran in February that sent gasoline prices higher. Some 73% of voters in the poll said their cost of living was heading in the wrong direction.Prior to the start of the war, Reuters/Ipsos polls showed voters preferring Republicans over Democrats as the better stewards of the US economy. The latest poll showed 37% of voters said Democrats have a better approach to the economy, compared to 33% who picked Republicans on the issue.The poll also suggested Democratic voters were more excited about voting, with 46% of Democrats saying they were very enthusiastic about the midterms, compared to 30% of Republicans who said the same.The Reuters/Ipsos poll, which was conducted online, gathered responses from 1,679 US adults, including 1,280 registered voters, and had a margin of error of 2 percentage points for all adults and 3 percentage points for registered voters.

title: Greek President Calls for Freedom and Prosperity at Liberation Anniversary
body: Greek President Konstantinos Tasoulas called for freedom, security, peace and prosperity for the people of Thessaloniki and Macedonia on Tuesday, as the city marked the 114th anniversary of its liberation from Ottoman rule. Tasoulas delivered his message after an official doxology at the Church of Saint Demetrios, led by Archbishop Ieronymos, as Thessaloniki celebrated both its patron saint and the anniversary of its liberation. “Today, Thessaloniki celebrates a double occasion. It celebrates its ever-vigilant guardian, Saint Demetrios the Myrrh-streamer, and the 114th anniversary of its liberation from approximately five centuries of Ottoman rule,” Tasoulas said. He paid tribute to those who died to bring Macedonia and Thessaloniki into the Greek national fold, recalling the First Balkan War and the events of 114 years ago. “Today, we remembered how, 114 years ago, during the First Balkan War, our country, Greece, stood united before the book of its destiny and wrote a new chapter in its history,” he said. “That chapter brought the Greek flags and the Greek army back here, to Greek Macedonia.” Tasoulas said Thessaloniki and Macedonia would continue to lead under the protection of Saint Demetrios and remain worthy of the freedom their people had won. “Being worthy of freedom means security, peace, progress and prosperity for its people,” he said, before wishing the public well. Officials attend Saint Demetrios service Upon his arrival at the church, Tasoulas received a welcome from Chief of the Hellenic National Defence General Staff General Dimitrios Houpis; Deputy Interior Minister for Macedonia and Thrace Kostas Gioulekas, representing the government; MP Dimitris Kouvelas, representing the Speaker of Parliament; Central Macedonia Deputy Regional Governor Konstantinos Gioutikas; Thessaloniki Mayor Stelios Angeloudis; and Metropolitan Philotheos of Thessaloniki. A military honour guard also paid tribute. The service drew senior political figures, including main opposition leader and PASOK-KINAL president Nikos Androulakis; European Commissioner for Sustainable Transport and Tourism Apostolos Tzitzikostas; NIKI president Dimitris Natsios; and Maria Karystianou, president of Hope for Democracy. Deputy ministers Stavros Kalafatis, Nikos Tachiaos, Elena Rapti, Anna Efthymiou and Nikos Papaioannou also attended, alongside MPs Stratos Simopoulos, Diamantis Golidakis, Dimitris Vartzopoulos, Fanis Papas, Petros Pappas, Rania Thraskia, Michalis Chourdakis and Giannis Amanatidis. MEP Emmanouil Fragkos and Central Union of Municipalities of Greece (KEDE) president and Ampelokipoi-Menemeni Mayor Lazaros Kyrizoglou also attended, among other officials. title: Jordanian airstrikes kill five civilians in southern Syria, officials say
body:
BEIRUT, October 27. /TASS/. Jordanian airstrikes killed at least five civilians in southern Syria, the administration of Syria’s Daraa Governorate said in a statement on X.
"Women and children are among those killed, as well as a 65-year-old man," the statement reads.
According to the authorities, the fatalities were recorded in the Tariq Al-Sadd neighborhood, while additional casualties were reported in the town of Al-Muzayrib in western Daraa.
Earlier, the Jordanian Air Force carried out strikes in southern Syria targeting extremist groups reportedly linked to the terrorists behind a recent attack on St. George’s Orthodox Church in Jordan’s Al-Karak Governorate. According to Jordan’s Health Ministry, the October 23 terrorist attack killed nine people and injured 34 others.

title: USAF Orders ARRW Hypersonic Missile Into Production, The Same Weapon It Nearly Cancelled
body: The U.S. Air Force has handed Lockheed Martin a $694 million contract for the production of AGM-183A Air-launched Rapid Response Weapon (ARRW) hypersonic missiles . In 2023, the service had moved to cancel ARRW , which had been in line to be the U.S. military’s first operational hypersonic weapon. At the time, we had reservations about the service’s intent and speculated the missile could make a major comeback or continue development in a classified setting. The program has since made an incredible turnaround, and there are already plans for another variant that will be able to use an all-new seeker to hit moving targets, including enemy warships . The ARRW contract was awarded on September 29, but only announced today . It is not immediately clear how many missiles are to be built under this deal or when the Air Force expects to start taking delivery of them. The Air Force has previously disclosed plans to integrate the missiles onto its B-52 and B-1 bombers . Other aircraft with sufficiently large payload capacities and physical space to carry outsized stores could potentially carry AGM-183As, or variants thereof, in the future. A B-1 bomber seen carrying an ARRW missile, or a relevant test article, on an external pylon during a flight test. USAF capture “The contract was executed under the Department of War’s Enterprise-Wide Agile Acquisition Contract to modernize America’s Arsenal of Freedom,” according to an Air Force press release . “This milestone marks the formal transition of the boost-glide hypersonic missile program from prototyping and flight testing into production, solidifying the Air Force’s commitment to fielding standoff, high-speed strike options.” As noted here, the AGM-183A is a so-called boost-glide vehicle-type hypersonic weapon, which uses a rocket booster to bring it first to an optimal speed and altitude. The nose cone on ARRW then breaks away, and a wedge-shaped unpowered boost-glide vehicle concealed within is released. A rendering depicting an ARRW hypersonic missile’s nose cone breaking away to reveal the unpowered boost-glide vehicle inside. Lockheed Martin The vehicle then glides to its target along a relatively shallow flight path within the Earth’s atmosphere at hypersonic speed, defined as anything above Mach 5. It is capable of maneuvering along the way, sometimes erratically. The mix of speed, flight trajectory, and maneuverability creates significant challenges for opponents in terms of spotting and tracking the glide vehicle, let alone attempting to intercept it. As a result, hypersonic weapons of this type offer particular benefits for piercing enemy air defenses to very rapidly strike time-sensitive and otherwise high-value targets. The ARRW production contract “is a turning point in our advanced weapons roadmap,” Secretary of the Air Force Troy Meink said in a statement accompanying today’s release. “By moving ARRW from test to production, we’re providing our combatant commanders with a credible, high-speed strike weapon capable of penetrating the most advanced anti-access and area-denial systems.” “Fielding ARRW enhances our ability to hold targets at risk anywhere around the world,” Air Force Chief of Staff Gen. Ken Wilsbach said in his own statement. “This hypersonic weapon provides the Joint Force a flexible and rapid response option for highly contested environments.” A graphic offering a very general comparison of the typical flight trajectories of hypersonic boost-glide vehicle weapons and air-breathing hypersonic cruise missiles, as well as aeroballistic (or quasi-ballistic) missiles and traditional ballistic missiles. GAO As mentioned, the Air Force had moved to cancel ARRW in 2023, following a number of failed flight tests . The explicit intent at the time was to shift resources to the Hypersonic Attack Cruise Missile (HACM) effort. HACM is an air-breathing hypersonic cruise missile that functions in a completely different way from ARRW. HACM is still in development, and the program has now moved into flight testing, as TWZ was first to report earlier this month. There had already been steady signs in recent years that ARRW’s fortunes were changing and that it had not actually been axed , despite the Air Force’s stated plans to do so. The Air Force’s 2026 Fiscal Year budget request last year confirmed that the service had fully rebooted the program and was seeking new funding to procure actual missiles. The service’s 2027 Fiscal Year budget request, released earlier this year, revealed further plans “to begin [ARRW] INC 2 [Increment 2] technology efforts such as but not limited to integrating pre-planned product improvements, design, trade studies, hardware upgrades, facilitization, affordability initiatives, and testing.” A live AGM-183A ARRW missile seen under the wing of a B-52 bomber at Andersen Air Force Base on Guam ahead of a test in 2024. USAF A request for $296 million would support “the design, test, and evaluation of Air-Launched Rapid Response Weapon (ARRW) Increment 2 with terminal seeker and data link capability and other cost reduction production initiatives into ARRW,” those same documents added. In general, the U.S. Air Force has historically framed hypersonic weapons, including ARRW and HACM, as being especially critical for success in future conflicts, especially high-end fights, such as one in the Pacific against China. This was underscored by the launch of an AGM-183A with a live warhead from a B-52 flying from Andersen Air Force Base on Guam in 2024. The future anti-ship variant could be even more relevant in a Pacific context. As TWZ has written previously : “…the Guam test sent clear signals to China. The Air Force has made no secret of how important it views the development and fielding of hypersonic weapons as part of larger preparations for a potential future high-end fight against the Chinese People’s Liberation Army (PLA) in the Pacific. This is further underscored by the fact that the mention of the ‘terminal seeker and data link capability’ for Increment 2 of ARRW is actually contained in the Pacific Deterrence Initiative (PDI) section of the Pentagon’s Fiscal Year 2027 budget request.” A low-quality image of an ARRW after launch during a previous live-fire flight test. USAF “ In the context of a major conflict in the Pacific, there would also be a very high demand for prompt, long-range anti-ship capability. The ability to conduct those strikes even in the face of dense anti-air defenses would be even more attractive for engaging very high-value vessels, such as China’s growing fleets of aircraft carriers or big deck amphibious assault ships . The PLA Navy’s (PLAN) combat fleets, overall, continue to grow in scale and scope at a prodigious rate, as well. This, in turn, has put additional emphasis on the development and fielding of new and improved anti-ship capabilities that can be air-launched , as well as employed from the maritime and ground domains , across the U.S. military in recent years. Increment 2 ARRWs could also offer another means to strike mobile, high-value targets on land, such as ballistic missile transporter-erector-launchers . ” China’s aircraft carriers Shandong , at left, and Liaoning , at right, sail together, along with various escorts, as elements of their air wings fly overhead, in 2024. Chinese state media “ For its part, the PLA has been actively developing and fielding various types of hypersonic weapons , including boost-glide vehicle designs . Its ever-growing arsenal of traditional ballistic missiles now includes several air-launched types, including ones with nuclear and conventional warheads . The latter are widely believed to be capable of being employed against enemy ships, as well as targets on land. ” If nothing else, after moving to cancel the ARRW three years ago, the Air Force has now fully reversed course and has placed its first order for production examples of this hypersonic missile. Contact the author: joe@twz.com The post USAF Orders ARRW Hypersonic Missile Into Production, The Same Weapon It Nearly Cancelled appeared first on TWZ .

title: Ellinikon Project Developers Appoints Evi Kostaki as New CEO
body: LAMDA Development will appoint Evi Kostaki as chief executive officer on January 1, 2027, succeeding Odysseas Athanasiou, who will step down after 18 years in the role and 21 years with the company. Athanasiou will leave the CEO position on December 31, 2026, after playing a central role in LAMDA’s growth and the development of the Ellinikon urban regeneration project in Athens. He will become an adviser to Consolidated Lamda Holdings (CLH) from January 1, focusing on relations with institutional bodies and government authorities. The company’s board appointed Kostaki, an executive with more than 25 years of international experience, to lead its next phase of growth. She most recently served as Group Chief Financial Officer and a member of the Executive Board at Swiss banking group Julius Baer. Kostaki brings extensive experience in financial management, strategy, mergers and acquisitions, asset management and business transformation. She served as Julius Baer’s Group CFO and Executive Board member from July 2022 to August 2026. During Athanasiou’s tenure, LAMDA developed into one of southeastern Europe’s leading property development and management groups. The company increased its total assets fivefold to approximately €5 billion and quadrupled its net asset value (NAV) to around €1.5 billion. Athanasiou also played a decisive role in securing and advancing the Ellinikon investment, helping the company overcome complex institutional, licensing, financing and construction challenges and launch what the announcement describes as Europe’s largest urban regeneration project. He also strengthened LAMDA’s shopping centre and marina businesses after taking charge during the height of Greece’s financial crisis. Latsis praises Athanasiou’s leadership Dr Spyros Latsis said Athanasiou had played a pivotal role in shaping LAMDA into the company it is today, guiding it through major challenges ranging from the financial crisis to the undertaking and implementation of Ellinikon. Latsis thanked Athanasiou for his contribution and the relationship of trust they had built over the years. He said Athanasiou’s continued involvement through CLH would allow the group to benefit from his experience and business judgement. He also welcomed Kostaki, expressing confidence that her fresh perspective and leadership experience would support LAMDA’s next stage of development. Stefanos Kotsolis, chairman of LAMDA’s board, also thanked Athanasiou for his dedication and leadership, saying he had helped establish a strong foundation for the company’s future. Kotsolis welcomed Kostaki and said the board looked forward to working with her to advance the company’s strategic priorities. Athanasiou to retain his LAMDA shareholding Athanasiou described his time at LAMDA as much more than the most significant chapter of his professional career. He said he had embraced Latsis’s vision and worked with the company’s employees to turn it into reality. He called the project a life mission and said LAMDA had transformed itself through successive crises and exceptionally demanding conditions, bringing Ellinikon from a long-standing promise to an active development project. Athanasiou said he believed the transition marked the right time to close one chapter and begin another. He also confirmed that he would retain his shareholding in LAMDA, citing his continued confidence in the company’s prospects. Kostaki sets out priorities for LAMDA Kostaki thanked the board and shareholders for their confidence and acknowledged Athanasiou’s contribution to the company’s development. She highlighted LAMDA’s recurring revenue base from its shopping centres and marinas, while noting that Ellinikon was moving from construction towards the delivery phase. The company expects its first residents to arrive within the next two years. Kostaki said her priorities would include maintaining the company’s momentum, meeting commitments to customers and the Greek state, fulfilling promises to local communities, growing shopping centre and marina revenues, and maintaining the financial discipline that has strengthened investor confidence. She added that she looked forward to advancing LAMDA’s strategic vision alongside its team. Evi Kostaki’s professional background Kostaki served as Julius Baer’s Group CFO and a member of its Executive Board from July 2022 to August 2026. She previously held roles at the bank as managing director and deputy group CFO, deputy head of investment management and head of alternatives, and deputy head of corporate development and strategy. Before joining Julius Baer, she served as director of corporate finance and business development at National Bank of Greece from January 2009 to July 2013. Earlier in her career, she held positions at Beltest Shipping Ltd., Eurobank EFG, Webster Financial Advisors, Morgan Stanley Asset Management and Merrill Lynch Investment Managers in Athens, New York and Connecticut. Kostaki also served on the board of AMINA Bank AG, a Swiss-regulated cryptocurrency bank based in Zug, from May 2020 to April 2026. During that period, she chaired its Nomination and Compensation Committee from 2021 to 2022. Her other board positions included Three Rock Capital Management, an Irish investment fund manager, from January 2020 to September 2022, and NSC Asesores, a Mexican wealth management firm, from January 2016 to February 2022. Kostaki holds a master’s degree in public policy, specialising in finance, from the University of Chicago and a bachelor’s degree in social sciences and economics from the London School of Economics. She also holds the Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA) designation. title: Section 88 Limits Reps’ Power to Summon Telecoms CEOs, Lawyer Says
body: A lawyer, and public analyst Sesan Bankole, has said Section 88 of the 1999 Constitution limits the investigative powers of the National Assembly, arguing that legislative inquiries must be tied to lawmaking or the investigation of the management of public funds appropriated by the legislature. Bankole, who was commenting on the House of Representatives’ summons of telecommunications operators over poor network quality, said the lawmakers could invite companies in the public interest but could not assume the regulatory responsibilities of the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC). He also described the summons as sub judice, saying the invitation came while a related lawsuit instituted by the Association of Licensed Telecommunications Operators of Nigeria (ALTON) remained pending before the courts. The suit, reportedly filed in 2018, challenges repeated legislative summonses of telecommunications executives over matters ALTON considers to fall within the NCC’s regulatory jurisdiction. According to Bankole, the courts have interpreted Section 88 as permitting investigations for the purpose of making or amending laws, or examining the management of budgeted public funds. He cited Tony Momoh v. Senate (1982), page 205, arguing that investigations beyond the constitutionally permitted purposes were invalid. “Any investigation that goes beyond making laws or exposing corruption in the management of budgeted public funds is invalid,” Bankole said. He added that the National Assembly could not regulate telecommunications operators or impose fines, insisting that such responsibilities belonged to the NCC. “And they can’t regulate or impose fine; that is the work of the regulator, which is the NCC,” he said. The lawyer’s comments followed the House of Representatives’ decision on October 21 to summon the chief executives of four telecommunications operators to appear before an ad hoc committee on October 28 over what it described as poor network quality. The committee threatened arrest over non-compliance. Bankole also argued that the chief executives did not necessarily have to appear personally, saying the companies could appoint representatives to attend the hearing. “By the Companies and Allied Matters Act, a telecom is a legal entity that can be represented by any such person appointed by the legal entity,” he said. The lawmakers say the summons comes amid persistent complaints by subscribers about dropped calls, slow data speeds and service interruptions affecting businesses and everyday communication. Telecommunications operators are licensed and regulated by the NCC under the Nigerian Communications Act 2003, which provides the framework for regulating the industry and enforcing applicable quality-of-service requirements. Bankole maintained that the National Assembly’s primary responsibility was to make laws that provide an enabling environment, rather than take over the functions of the sector’s statutory regulator.

title: Verify travellers’ phone numbers to help trace Ebola cases – Prof Amuasi
body: Prof John Amuasi, Leader of Global Health at the KCCR, has urged Ghana to verify travellers’ phone numbers to help authorities trace them if they develop Ebola symptoms after arrival. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Monday, he said accurate passenger information should be central to the country’s preparedness. Airport temperature checks alone would offer limited protection. “So for me, the single most important thing is being able to collect as accurate data as possible on every single person who comes off the plane in this country, making sure that the phone numbers they submit are accurate and finding a way of verifying it.” His call comes amid imported Ebola cases in Nigeria and Kenya. Nigeria confirmed a case in Abuja on October 20 in a woman who had travelled from Uganda. According to Nigeria’s disease control agency, she arrived on October 3 and developed symptoms four days later. Kenya had recorded nine cases by October 20, according to the World Health Organisation. Its first patient travelled from DR Congo through Uganda. The eight additional cases were known contacts of that patient. Prof Amuasi said screening passengers for visible illness would miss people who had not yet developed symptoms. “The point I was making is that nobody is going to be coming off an aeroplane or even jumping on an aeroplane when they are visibly sick with signs and symptoms of Ebola, and therefore your ability to catch it when someone is coming off a plane is really limited.” He questioned how much reassurance routine airport measures should provide. “Temperature checks, use of alcohol and rubs, all these things are nice. They give people some level of confidence, but the reality is that they are not going to catch Ebola cases for you.” He said testing was needed. However, screening every arriving traveller with a PCR test was not feasible. “We can’t be doing PCR tests for everyone coming in.” He, therefore, called for detailed arrival records, a way to locate travellers when necessary, and clear instructions on reporting symptoms. Travellers should know which designated facilities to visit and which telephone lines to use if they become unwell, he said. For Prof Amuasi, educating arriving passengers and ensuring they can be reached must be priorities in Ghana’s Ebola preparedness.

title: NIMASA, ITF Endorse MOU on Seafarer Well-being
body: The Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety Agency (NIMASA) and the International Transport Workers’ Federation (ITF) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) aimed at promoting the mental health and wellbeing of Nigerian seafarers and cadets through training, awareness and capacity building. This was the high point of a three-day Seafarers’ and Cadets’ Wellbeing Awareness and Train the Trainers Programme with the theme, “Stress: Understanding, Early Management and Coping,” organised by NIMASA in collaboration with the ITF. Speaking at the event, the Director General of NIMASA, Dr. Dayo Mobereola disclosed that the partnership would support capacity building and the integration of the wellbeing module into maritime training curricula, with plans to make seafarer wellbeing a permanent component of preparations for life at sea. Represented by the Executive Director, Maritime Labour and Cabotage Services, Mr Jibril Abba, he said “seafarers’ wellbeing is essential to safe shipping and NIMASA is committed to protecting maritime workers’ welfare. This programme would equip maritime training institutions, Agency officers and union partners with the skills to identify and manage stress and provide psychological first aid when necessary”. He emphasised the importance of addressing the psychological challenges associated with life at sea, including stress, anxiety, depression and burnout. Citing a 2019 study commissioned by the ITF in collaboration with Yale University, he noted that one in four seafarers surveyed showed signs of depression, while approximately one in six exhibited signs of anxiety. Also speaking, the ITF Africa Regional Secretary, Mr Safiyanu Dauda Mohammed, who signed the MoU on behalf of ITF noted that this MoU was the first of its kind that the ITF was going into with any country in Africa. According to him, “it is very exciting for me because it is the first in Africa, and we are starting with Nigeria. Seafarers are very critical workers in the maritime sector. So it is very important to prioritise their wellbeing and welfare, to mitigate their anxiety and depression”. In his remarks, the President-General of the Maritime Workers Union of Nigeria, Comrade Francis Bunu applauded the development saying “we need seafarers to be mentally sound while doing their job and that is why today is a very significant day for the seafarer in Nigeria”.

title: Why the Netherlands Must Hold the Line on ASML
body:
Node for semiconductors: US President Donald Trump with Netherlands Prime Minister Rob Jetten in the White House. Image: ANP / Alamy Stock
If the Netherlands agrees to US export controls, it must be mindful of its vulnerability to retaliatory measures from Beijing.
Over recent decades, Dutch technology giant ASML has become a vital node in the global economy. The company is the market leader for the photolithography systems used for semiconductor manufacturing and the worldâs only manufacturer of the much-coveted extreme ultraviolet (EUV) machines. Without ASML, industries depending on advanced chips, such as AI, telecommunications and aerospace, would be severely hindered. The firm is expanding its manufacturing capacity but is still expected to struggle to meet the ever-growing demand for its products.
This technological relevance has also placed ASML at the centre of the ongoing USâChina tech race. After years of American pressure, the Netherlands has repeatedly restricted exports of semiconductor manufacturing equipment to China. However, the current Dutch government has recently pushed back against the pending US MATCH Act designed to limit ASMLâs China exports even further, with Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten raising concerns directly with US President Donald Trump.
While Washingtonâs anxiety over Beijingâs semiconductor advances is understandable, the Netherlands has good reasons to oppose further export restrictions.
Restricting lithography exports to China might slow down advanced Chinese chip production in the short term. However, this could prove a short-sighted strategy. Chinese lithography technology is evolving, but its deep ultraviolet (DUV) machines remain roughly a decade behind ASMLâs most advanced equipment. Further restrictions risk strengthening Beijingâs motivation to develop indigenous alternatives at scale, accelerating investments into the domestic Chinese lithography and chip industry.
Proponents of export restrictions warn that ASML sales to China could enable technological leapfrogs, a concern echoed by US lawmakers supporting the MATCH Act. Historically, Beijing has continuously absorbed foreign technologies while developing domestic alternatives. Notable examples of this are Chinaâs high-speed rail market , where Beijing used technology transfers from Germany, France, Japan and Canada to boost competitive domestic alternatives, and Beijingâs vibrant electric vehicle (EV) market, which similarly benefitted from early partnerships with European auto manufacturers.
It would therefore be naÃ¯ve to assume that access to ASML equipment would fully dissuade China from expanding its own lithography capabilities. After all, Beijing understands the value of economic and technological self-sufficiency well.
Yet, concerns over Chinaâs ability to leapfrog this technology should not be overstated. Beijingâs determination for indigenisation does not mean that it can instantly replicate ASMLâs advanced machines. Lithography machines are difficult to fully reverse engineer. ASML sits atop a complex and sophisticated ecosystem of highly specialised technologies and suppliers that took decades to develop and fine-tune. In 2025, the Dutch company sourced from 5,100 suppliers and spent an impressive â¬4.7 billion on R&D to continue developing the next generation of lithography technology. Its improvement cycle and the continuous improvement of speed and accuracy of its machines add additional challenges for competitors that not only have to catch up, but also keep pace with future upgrades. Jos Benschop, ASMLâs executive vice president of technology, once described one of its machines as âthe most complex machine built by mankindâ.
Help your search results show more from RUSI. Adding RUSI as a preferred source on Google means our analysis appears more prominently.
The complexity of lithography technology means that access to foreign equipment on its own may not yield the same benefits as in other industries. Policy research suggests that China has struggled more to close technological gaps in industries with long learning cycles and a reliance on tacit knowledge. For instance, despite decades of access to advanced British and Russian military jet engines, China has historically struggled to develop and produce competitive indigenous military jet engines. Similarly, China continues to depend on foreign suppliers of high-end precision machine tools used in manufacturing despite having years of investment.
This dependency on ASML technology has made it a key chokepoint in the US-China AI race but also made it one of Europeâs most important sources of technological and economic power. The firm is the EUâs most valuable listed company and stands out on a continent struggling to compete with the high-tech industries of China and the US. Much of its revenue comes from China, which is forecast to account for 20% of its total revenue in 2026, primarily through sales of less-advanced lithography tools.
While Europe has legitimate security concerns over Chinaâs technological rise, its interests do not necessarily align with Washingtonâs. The US wishes to curb Chinaâs high-tech and AI industries, but Europe has an interest in maintaining this rare economic and geopolitical chokepoint. For as long as Beijing remains interested in accessing ASMLâs lithography equipment, the Hague and Brussels have a dependency to leverage in their political and economic relationships with China â including during the ongoing EUâChina trade negotiations and beyond.

Get a weekly round-up of the latest commentary and research straight into your inbox.
ASMLâs specialised supplier ecosystem is an asset, but it is not immune to global supply chain risks. If the Netherlands allows the company and its products to become tools within Washingtonâs China policy, it must be mindful of its vulnerability to retaliatory measures. Beijingâs recent sanctioning of Sindlhauser Materials, a key ASML supplier, is a clear example of its dependency on Chinese critical mineral supply chains and shows that export control standoffs can have severe commercial consequences. The impact has been significant, prompting the EU to negotiate sanction reliefs with China. Beijing has proposed lifting these restrictions in exchange for EU sanctions relief for Yusha Group, a Chinese textile firm accused of supplying European technology to Russia. As part of this agreement, however, Yusha would refrain from exporting banned products to Russia military-linked buyers. This engagement underlines the importance Beijing attaches to ASMLâs supply chain and the leverage it brings in EU-China relations.
The Dutch government should be cautious in how it proceeds when managing ASMLâs export licences. It should continue coordinating with Washington to safeguard critical technologies, but also resist measures that would undermine one of Europeâs rare technological chokepoints. Preserving ASMLâs access to the Chinese market would benefit the European lithography industry and grant the Netherlands and the EU much-needed economic leverage with which to safeguard their own strategic interests.
