title: SOFEX 2026 Opens with Middle East Special Operations Commanders Conference in Aqaba
body:
MESOC 2026 brings together military and government officials to discuss emerging threats, unmanned systems and multinational special operations cooperation
The 12th Biennial Middle East Special Operations Commanders Conference (MESOC) took place in Aqaba on Monday, October 26, under the patronage of HRH Prince Faisal bin Al Hussein, ahead of the opening of the 15th Special Operations Forces Exhibition and Conference (SOFEX 2026).
Held from 9:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m., MESOC brought together senior military and government officials to discuss evolving security challenges, counterterrorism, regional and global conflicts, emerging technologies and strategic planning for future operations.
The conference was attended by Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff Maj. Gen. Majdi Al Harasis and Public Security Director Maj. Gen. Obaidallah Maaytah, alongside senior officers from the Jordan Armed Forces–Arab Army, security agencies, partner nations and other official representatives.
Discussions focused on technical innovation, the integration of unmanned aerial systems (UAS) into asymmetric warfare, joint fusion and targeting centres, military diplomacy and multi-domain cooperation.
Jordan Highlights Its Role in Regional and International Security
SOFEX Company Chairman Ayman Batran said Jordan's hosting of the conference reinforced the Kingdom's international standing as a reliable partner in counterterrorism, strengthening security measures, developing institutional and operational capabilities, and facilitating the exchange of expertise.
He added that the event reflected Jordan's role in supporting regional and international security and peace.
Batran described this year's SOFEX as particularly significant amid an increasingly complex and rapidly evolving security and operational environment. He emphasised the importance of sharing knowledge and operational experience to strengthen readiness and improve responses to emerging threats, particularly in the fields of unmanned systems and counter-unmanned aerial systems.
In his address, the Special Forces commander highlighted the importance of anticipating and forecasting change rather than simply reacting to emerging threats. He stressed that contemporary security challenges require stronger institutional integration and the development of international strategic partnerships.
This year's emphasis on knowledge and innovation, multi-domain operations and international military cooperation was also identified as an important factor in strengthening regional resilience and developing capabilities to address future threats.
Three Sessions Address Emerging Operational Challenges
The conference featured three main sessions examining the relationship between operational requirements, technological development and combat readiness.
Participants discussed how to bridge the gap between theory and practice, as well as the contributions of the military, academic and industrial sectors to innovation and capability development.
Other topics included the integration of unmanned aerial systems with special operations forces in asymmetric warfare across multiple domains, the opportunities and challenges associated with joint fusion and targeting centres, and the role of military diplomacy and unconventional humanitarian missions.
The discussions underscored the growing importance of technological innovation, information sharing and multinational cooperation in preparing special operations forces for increasingly complex operational environments.
SOFEX 2026 to Showcase Defence and Security Technologies
SOFEX 2026 will open on Tuesday, October 27, at the Aqaba exhibition and conference grounds, under royal patronage and with the support of the Jordan Armed Forces. The three-day event will bring together military delegations, government officials, defence specialists, manufacturers and industry representatives from around the world.
According to figures released by the organisers, more than 400 official delegations representing 75 countries and 350 exhibiting companies from 38 countries are participating in the event. The exhibition aims to showcase the latest weapons, equipment and defence and security technologies while promoting international cooperation and the exchange of expertise.
Held biennially under the patronage of His Majesty King Abdullah II, SOFEX combines exhibition activities with live demonstrations, workshops, official engagements, shooting-range activities and performances by the Jordan Armed Forces.
According to figures released by the organisers, seven Turkish companies had registered to participate in SOFEX 2026: ASELSAN, ATEŞCİ, ASFAT, DASAL, MKE, YILMAZ and YILTEX ARMOR.
As one of the event's official media partners, Defence Türkiye will cover SOFEX 2026 on-site over two days, reporting on the latest developments, notable products, technologies and capabilities, as well as key trends shaping the defence and security industries.
The opening programme on October 27 includes an official ceremony, speeches, a royal tour of the exhibition halls, a performance by the Jordan Armed Forces Musical Band, an air show by the Royal Jordanian Falcons and shooting-range activities.
On October 28, scheduled activities include a workshop for non-commissioned officers, live demonstrations by exhibitors, a workshop on the role of women in the armed forces, shooting-range activities, a performance by the Jordan Armed Forces Band and an air show by the Royal Jordanian Falcons.
The final day, October 29, will feature another non-commissioned officers workshop, tactical displays by exhibitors, a live-firing demonstration, performances by the Jordan Armed Forces Band and the Royal Jordanian Falcons, and the SOFEX 2026 press conference. The exhibition is scheduled to close at 5:00 p.m.

title: UBA Launches Climate Action to Advance Green Finance, Sustainability
body: Kayode Tokede United Bank for Africa (UBA) Plc, has launched a Group-wide Climate Action Week to deepen climate awareness, promote responsible environmental practices and advance sustainable finance across its African and international operations. The five-day campaign is with themed, “Banking on Africa’s Climate Future” and reflects the Bank’s commitment to integrating environmental responsibility into its operations, customer engagement and financing solutions. The initiative commenced with the deployment of waste segregation bins across UBA offices and measures to reduce the use of single-use plastics at the Bank’s head offices. These activities underscore UBA’s commitment to translating sustainability principles into practical actions within its workplace and across its wider ecosystem. UBA’s Group Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer, Oliver Alawuba, emphasised the importance of collective responsibility in addressing the growing impact of climate change. “Climate change is no longer a distant environmental concern; it is increasingly shaping everyday life across Africa. We see its effects in rising food costs, increased energy demand and flooding that disrupts homes, businesses and livelihoods. “At UBA, we believe that building a sustainable future requires collective action, beginning with the choices we make at work, at home and in our communities. Through this Climate Action Week, we are encouraging every member of the UBA Tribe, alongside our customers and other stakeholders, to embrace practical, sustainable habits and inspire others to do the same,” Alawuba said. Alawuba, noted that climate considerations were increasingly important to business resilience, risk management and long-term economic growth. “Climate change presents significant risks to businesses, communities and economies. These risks can affect business continuity, operating costs and financial performance, making sustainability an increasingly important consideration for both businesses and the financial institutions that support them. “Through UBA Green Finance, we seek to support eligible businesses investing in cleaner technologies and more sustainable operations. By helping customers explore financing solutions aligned with their needs, we can contribute to a more resilient private sector while unlocking opportunities for sustainable economic growth across Africa,” Alawuba further said.

title: Firm Drives Financing of Oil Palm Industry to Boost National Output
body: Oluchi Chibuzor Reftop Holdings has continued to expand its footprint in driving innovative financing models of Nigeria’s agricultural financing model through allotment of 2,700 acres of land to subscribers under its PalmCrest Agro-Real Estate Project to boost national oil palm output by 5 percent in 2031. This for the company marks a significant milestone in its drive to combine real estate investment with oil-palm plantation development. This is also as the company has set a target of five-years plan to build its own oil palm refinery that would be capable of meeting 5 per cent Nigeria’s national output and thereby pushing the country to top 2 in world production. Speaking in Lagos, recently the Managing Director of Reftop Holdings, Dr. David Assogba, said the project was designed to create opportunities for investors to participate in land ownership while supporting the development of productive agricultural assets. He said that PalmCrest is Reftop’s flagship agro-real-estate initiative, built around the ownership of agricultural land, oil-palm cultivation and professionally managed plantation operations. He explained that its first two project phases cover 5,200 acres and have attracted approximately 2,100 subscribers, reflecting growing participation in its agro-real estate investment model noting agriculture remains the next frontier. “The model combines land ownership with the development and management of productive oil-palm farms. The concept connects land acquisition with productive farming, particularly oil-palm cultivation, allowing subscribers to participate in agriculture without having to personally manage the day-to-day activities of a plantation,” he said. Presenting a technical report, the Chief Operating Officer, Reftop Homes Limited, Emmanuel Oluwatosin,said that so far 2700 acres has been allocated to subscribers, while 150,000 seedlings are ready for transplanting and 40,000 oil-palm seedlings are being nursed.

title: 2026 Insurance Industry Awards and Consumer Nite Holds Nov 6
body: The Annual Insurance Industry Awards and Consumers’ Nite will hold in November. The Award is the biggest social platform of the Nigerian Insurance Industry. This year’s edition will take place at the Stable Event Centre Surulere, Lagos. The organisers Almond Productions Limited, said the sole purpose of the awards since inception in 2018 remained to recognise and reward the outstanding efforts of the men and women across the different arms of the insurance industry who work tirelessly to promote and sell insurance often in challenging circumstances, as well as companies and institutions in the insurance eco-system that are leading the change in their operations and delivering value to Nigerians. The Chief Executive Officer Almond, Faith Ugwuode observed that while insurance awareness and penetration is still low without doubt, players in the sector were putting in the work to make more Nigerians see and appreciate the value of insurance through health insurance, lfe insurance, agricultural insurance, annuity and general insurance products. Ugwuode said in line with the tradition of the Annual Awards to celebrate icons and industry leaders in their lifetime, Mr. Opeoluwa Emmanuel Oredugba will be honoured with the 2026 Insurance Life Achievers Award for his over four decades of impact in the insurance industry.

title: Lessons for the Philippines: AI content surge bypassed Brazil’s election rules — report
body: Political maneuvering for the 2028 Philippine polls is expected to begin early next year, and Brazil’s 2026 presidential election offers a look ahead at the digital threat landscape. During the first round of Brazil’s race, AI political content appeared in feeds nearly once per hour, according to fact-checking agency Agência Lupa. Through its VigIA project, Lupa confirmed that 920 of 1,941 election-related posts were AI-generated from August 16 to September 28. Over half (60%) were deepfakes, which are synthetic media depicting real people doing something they never did. AI DISINFORMATION. Screenshots of AI-created posts during the first round of Brazil’s presidential election. Graphics from Agência Lupa Brazil’s Superior Electoral Court (TSE) has regulated AI in elections since 2024, banning deepfakes while requiring disclosure labels for other AI campaign materials. However, the court ruled in September that the deepfake ban applies to content characterized as electoral propaganda. The ruling came after the TSE voted not to penalize presidential candidate Senator Flávio Bolsonaro for showing AI-generated images of his imprisoned father, former president Jair Bolsonaro , endorsing him during a private Liberal Party (PL) convention. The court determined the photo was intended for a private event, not for public broadcast. The senior Bolsonaro is facing a 27-year sentence after plotting a coup following his 2022 defeat to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva . Unlabeled AI content dominates Lupa found that 60% of analyzed AI posts lacked transparency labels from post authors. Even among the 40% of the posts showing disclosures, transparency was rarely voluntary. Nearly 60% of the labeled content were tagged by platforms, while native watermarks from AI tools like Google Gemini appeared in only 20 posts. NO AI LABELS. Screenshots of deepfakes posted on Facebook without AI disclosures. Graphics from Agência Lupa Under TSE’s rules, candidates and parties must declare if campaign materials use AI. But Lupa discovered that almost half (47%) of synthetic media originated from voters operating outside candidate disclosure rules. Official candidate accounts comprised only 24.5% of the analyzed AI content, while 27% came from anonymous profiles. Agência Lupa founder Cristina Tardáguila emphasized that this lack of disclosure exposes how easily rules are bypassed. “What we have seen so far is nobody cares about these rules. They are not being truly respected. And the norms, they are not being enforced,” Tardáguila told Rappler. Promoting candidates, attacking rivals Lupa reported that 45% of analyzed AI content aimed to promote candidates in Brazil’s elections. Humorous or satirical posts comprised 27%, a category Tardáguila described as particularly dangerous for information integrity. “As a fact-checker, you cannot fact-check humor,” Tardáguila shared. Humor is playing a big role here because what we’re seeing is that the politician’s supporters, if they want to play with a scenario that accuses the other candidate of doing something, they just appeal to humor.” Must Read [DECODED] When politicians meme their way into your feed Direct attacks on candidates accounted for 24.6% of posts, while nearly 3% were neutral voter guides. President Lula of the Workers’ Party (PT) was the politician most portrayed in synthetic media. He was depicted in humorous contexts in 39% of his cases, while 34% were personal attacks and criticisms of his administration. Only about 25% featuring Lula was promotional. SYNTHETIC IMAGES. Screenshots of AI-generated photos involving Brazil’s presidential candidates Lula and Bolsonaro, which have been removed on social media. Graphics from Agência Lupa His opponent, Senator Bolsonaro, trailed in second. Unlike Lula, 40% of AI content featuring Bolsonaro aimed to boost his campaign. Humorous posts made up 28% of his cases, while 27% were smear campaigns. Beyond political figures, Lupa identified journalists as deepfake targets, with synthetic videos showing news anchors reporting false survey polls or fake election outcomes. FAKE RESULTS. Screenshots of AI-generated videos showing journalists presenting false poll results. Graphics from Agência Lupa Old tactics now driven by AI Disinformation is not new to Brazil. During the 2022 race, the Carter Center documented disinformation networks targeting the voting process and candidates, with Lula bearing the majority of the attacks. Research by #ShePersisted and The Nerve in 2024 similarly highlighted gender-based attacks against female political figures during Jair Bolsonaro’s term. What sets 2026 apart is how AI reinforced those tactics, triggering what Lupa’s initial VigIA report described as “an avalanche of content generated by artificial intelligence.” Lupa recorded 64 election-related AI-generated posts published between October 1 and 5, a mandatory campaign blackout period set by TSE before the first round. MORE DEEPFAKES. Screenshots of deepfakes involving President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro circulated during the prohibited campaign period in Brazil’s elections. Graphics from Agência Lupa Must Read AI biggest challenge of fact-checking elections around the world – experts Tardáguila noted that while Lupa actively works with electoral courts to monitor synthetic content and alert platforms, a challenge remains. “We have clear rules from the justice system, clear rules from the social media platforms. They are being fully and truly disrespected by all stakeholders,” she stated, adding that the “biggest loophole is the lack of [law] enforcement.” Senator Flávio Bolsonaro led the first round with 47% of the votes last October 4. But President Lula won his reelection after securing more than 51% of the votes in Brazil’s runoff election on October 25. Must Read Lula, Brazil’s iconic working-class president, wins historic 4th term in dramatic comeback A warning for the Philippines’ upcoming polls Brazil’s struggle with AI political content offers a critical lesson for the Philippines, a country with a similar digital threat landscape. From Our Archives [DECODED] The Philippines and Brazil have a lot in common. Online toxicity is one. Investigations into global propaganda networks, such as Cambridge Analytica ’s operations in both countries, show how microtargeting and coordinated campaigns take hold not long before voters cast their ballots. In response to these issues and the rise of generative AI, the Commission on Elections issued Resolution No. 11064 to regulate AI use in campaigns, requiring transparency disclosures. But findings from the fact-checking initiative Tsek.ph revealed that deepfakes were still weaponized during the 2025 midterm elections to red-tag political figures and fabricate endorsements, alongside the spread of shallowfakes. Rappler also observed that deepfakes became a major disinformation tool in the Philippines last year. From Our Archives Lack of legal teeth vs online disinformation casts long shadow over 2025 polls Brazil’s experience gives a reality check for the Philippines: electoral regulations are only the first step. Without enforcement and accountability, the rampant spread of AI content will continue to bypass election guardrails, leaving voters to navigate an increasingly manipulated digital landscape. – Rappler.com

title: Kane Ends England’s 25-year Wait, Wins Ballon d’Or
body: *Saka wins Sócrates Award, Yamal awarded the Young Talent for the Third year Duro Ikhazuagbe with agency report England’s Three Lions Captain, Harry Kane, on Monday night became the first English player to win the Ballon d’Or since Michael Owen in 2001 after being crowned the world’s best player at a ceremony at the London Palladium. Bukayo Saka, Arsenal forward with Nigerian ancestry, was also amongst the winners last night as he won the Socrates Award. The 33-year-old Bayern Munich striker Kane is the fifth Englishman to win in total, with Stanley Matthews (1956), Bobby Charlton (1966) and Kevin Keegan (1978 and 1979) the others. Denis Law of Scotland (1964) and Northern Ireland’s George Best (1968) are the other winners from the United Kingdom. Kane scored 61 goals in 51 club matches last season, the most a Bayern player has ever struck in one campaign. Including England matches, it was 73 goals – plus eight assists – in 65 matches. Only one player at a club in Europe’s top five leagues has ever scored more goals in a season. But he wins it despite not lifting either of football’s biggest prizes last season, having lost in both the World Cup and Champions League semi-finals. Remarkably the Three Lions captain becomes the first Bayern player to win the Ballon d’Or since Karl-Heinz Rummenigge in 1981. BBC Sport looks at why Kane won it and how unusual it is to do so without securing one of those major trophies. Kane’s Record-breaking 2025-26 Season In term of trophies, Kane may have ‘only’ lifted the German double last season. But that more than doubled his career trophy total – having also won the Bundesliga the season before. But in terms of individual output Kane – whose previous best Ballon d’Or finish was 10th – was unmatched last season. His 61 goals in all competitions for Bayern was 19 more than any other player in Europe’s top five leagues managed. In fact it was the most anyone has recorded since Cristiano Ronaldo also notched 61 for Real Madrid 11 years ago. He was the Bundesliga’s top scorer with 36 goals – 17 clear of anyone else. In the Champions League he scored 14 for the beaten semi-finalists. In the German Cup he scored 10 goals, including a hat-trick in the 3-0 win over Stuttgart in the final, and he also netted once in the German Super Cup. No player has ever scored so many goals in a season for Bayern, a club who have had legendary goalscorers like Gerd Muller, Rummenigge and more recently Robert Lewandowski in their ranks. Kane’s 12 goals for England last season – including six at the World Cup – take him up a total of 73. Only one player in history from Europe’s top leagues has scored more in a season, Lionel Messi’s 82 for Barcelona and Argentina in 2011-12. Next on the list are Muller (72 in 1972-73), Cristiano Ronaldo (66 in both 2011-12 and 2014-15), former Brazil striker Ronaldo (66 in 1996-97), Erling Haaland (64 in 2022-23) and Luis Suarez (64 in 2015-16). Former England striker Alan Shearer recently told BBC Sport: “The winner of the Ballon d’Or should be Harry Kane. “His numbers for the last 12 to 18 months have been absolutely sensational for Bayern and for England. For that reason, he should get it.” Another ex-Three Lions player Danny Murphy added: “His goalscoring has been relentless, brilliant. He’s had one of the best seasons of his career and it’ll be a great reward for him if he gets the trophy. “He’s been brilliant at Bayern Munich since he’s been there, adapted really well and he’s been the best centre forward in the world for the last 12 months.” OTHER CATEGORIES WINNERS Award Category Winner Club / National Team Men’s Young Talent of the Year (Kopa Trophy) Lamine Yamal Barcelona / Spain Women’s Young Talent of the Year Vicky Lopez Barcelona / Spain Men’s Coach of the Year Luis de la Fuente Spain Women’s Coach of the Year Pere Romeu Barcelona Men’s Goalkeeper of the Year Unai Simon Athletic Club / Spain Women’s Goalkeeper of the Year Cata Coll Barcelona / Spain Sócrates Award (Humanitarian) Bukayo Saka Arsenal / England Men’s Club of the Year Paris Saint-Germain Paris Saint-Germain Women’s Club of the Year Barcelona Femeni Barcelo

title: Greek Robotics Firm Brings Robots Into the Workplace (VIDEO)
body: Robots are moving beyond laboratories and science fiction into warehouses, hotels, industrial facilities and rescue operations, as advances in robotics create new opportunities for businesses and society, according to Pavlos Tsiapos, founder and CEO of AVRION Robotics. “Humanoid robots have left the studios and even the robotics laboratories and entered the present,” Tsiapos said. “They are here with us to add value to production and work alongside people.” The company’s humanoid robot, Phoebus, demonstrates how the technology can interact with people, perform movements such as handshakes and hugs, dance, guide users and retrieve information. “I am Phoebus, a humanoid robot from AVRION Robotics. I can talk to you, perform movements such as a handshake or a hug, dance, help you navigate or search for information,” the robot explains. Robots Transform Industry and Logistics Robotic systems already operate across several sectors, including manufacturing and logistics, where they support warehouse operations and production lines and can work continuously. AVRION Robotics develops a range of robotic solutions for industrial operations, security and environments where robots interact directly with people, Tsiapos said. In hospitality, robots can assist with routine tasks, provide information and guide visitors, potentially improving customer service while allowing staff to focus on other responsibilities. “We are currently preparing the first pilot hotel, which will operate almost autonomously using robotic solutions,” Tsiapos said. Phoebus said businesses could use humanoid robots to welcome customers, conduct tours and answer questions. Robots Could Improve Workplace Safety Robotic technology also offers potential safety benefits in factories and other hazardous environments. Tsiapos said robots could identify risks that human workers might not notice, helping businesses monitor dangerous areas and reduce exposure to workplace hazards. These applications extend beyond humanoid robots to other robotic systems, including platforms designed for inspection and monitoring. By deploying robots in hazardous settings, businesses could use technology to support workers and improve their ability to identify potential dangers. Human Creativity Remains Irreplaceable, AVRION CEO Says Despite the potential benefits, advances in robotics have raised concerns about misuse and the impact of automation on human work. Tsiapos said such concerns were understandable given the scale of the technological changes underway. However, he argued that current robotic systems should primarily help people concentrate on tasks where they can contribute greater value. “Robotic solutions are here to help people focus on where they can truly offer greater value and accomplish more,” he said. “Their creativity and spirit remain irreplaceable.” His comments reflect a vision in which robots complement human capabilities rather than replace the qualities that distinguish people. Chinese Robotics Exhibition Highlights Rapid Progress Tsiapos recently visited a major robotics trade exhibition in China, where he observed the rapid development of humanoid robots and their physical capabilities. “We saw robots taking their first steps in 2022 and 2023. In 2024 and 2025, we watched them dance, and this year we saw them surpass human records,” he said. He stressed that the significance of these achievements lies not in robots jumping over obstacles or running 100-metre races for their own sake, but in what they demonstrate about the pace of technological progress. The advances offer a glimpse of the capabilities that robotic systems could bring to practical applications, he said, adding that robots are now ready to address real-world needs. Robotics is no longer simply a vision of the future. As companies explore applications in manufacturing, hospitality, security and other sectors, the technology is increasingly becoming part of everyday life. title: GPT-6.1 Terra
body:
GPT-6.1 Terra ( via ) It's always interesting to note which aspects of a new model are emphasized in the release announcement.
In the case of GPT-6.1 Terra, OpenAI went with visual reasoning and computer use:
We’re introducing GPT-6.1 Terra , a fast, efficient model that combines detailed visual reasoning and precise computer use alongside clearer, more natural writing. A significant step up from GPT‑5.6 Terra, it excels at the communication and computer-based tasks that fill the workday, from drafting proposals and interpreting technical drawings to filling out forms and editing videos.
Terra sits in the same position as Sonnet in the Anthropic model collection - not the cheapest or the most expensive, making it harder to decide when to use it.
Computer use is a good example of a task that benefits from a less expensive model, since you might put it to work on automated, repetitive tasks.
OpenAI's Ted Sanders provided some useful advice in a comment on Hacker News:
In the case of GPT-6.1 Terra, I'd say Terra is probably better than Astra and Sol at technical communication, similar on vision and computer use (but much faster!), and a bit worse on most other things. For API developers, it's a nice midrange option if you want something cheaper than Sol but a lot smarter than Luna (especially for vision / computer use / communication). For subscribers, it's not a bombshell release - if you're hitting usage limits, maybe it helps you go a bit further, and if you want clearer communication or faster computer use, it can be a nice option to select.
Here are the pelicans for the different reasoning levels. This pelican for "max" cost 11.3161 cents and took 4 minutes and 11 seconds:
Here's a new comparison grid showing pelicans for every reasoning level of OpenAI's current frontier lineup: GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6.1 Terra, and GPT-6 Luna.
GPT-6.1 Terra is priced at $1/million input tokens and $5/million output - almost half the price of GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-6.1 Sol, and around 10x the price of GPT-6 Luna.
This is a link post by Simon Willison, posted on 26th October 2026 .

title: Cricket: Nigeria’s YellowGreens in First-ever T20i Dramatic Win over Uganda
body: *Seal spot in T20 World Cup Africa sub-regional qualifiers Nigeria’s stocks in the game of cricket has continued to rise following the country’s senior men’s team, YellowGreens’ defeat of Uganda by one run in a last-ball thriller, ending a long wait for a maiden men’s T20I victory over their East African rivals. YellowGreens’ Isaac Danladi and Selim Salau were selected for tournament honours. The YellowGreens, have recorded a historic milestone in Nigerian cricket, securing their first-ever men’s Twenty20 International (T20I) victory over Uganda with a dramatic one-run win at the ICC Men’s T20 World Cup Africa Sub-Regional Qualifier C in Abuja last Sunday. In a contest that went down to the final delivery at the Moshood Abiola National Stadium cricket venue, Nigeria successfully defended a target of 149 to defeat one of Africa’s established cricketing sides and conclude their qualifying campaign on a memorable note. Beyond the victory, the result represented a significant breakthrough in the historical rivalry between the two nations. Uganda had traditionally dominated their men’s T20I encounters, winning the overwhelming majority of their previous meetings. Nigeria’s narrow triumph therefore marked not only a crucial tournament result but also a landmark achievement for the YellowGreens. With both teams already assured of qualification for the 2027 ICC Men’s T20 World Cup Africa Qualifier, the encounter offered an opportunity to establish supremacy between two of the competition’s strongest sides. Nigeria seized that opportunity in unforgettable fashion. After winning the toss and electing to bat, Nigeria made an aggressive start, with openers Isaac Danladi and Selim Salau immediately putting Uganda’s bowling attack under pressure. The pair combined for an opening partnership of 68 runs from just 7.2 overs, giving the YellowGreens early momentum and laying the foundation for a competitive total. Danladi was particularly impressive, scoring 47 runs from 28 deliveries, including three fours and four sixes. His attacking innings earned him the Player of the Match award and proved crucial in a contest ultimately decided by the narrowest of margins. Salau contributed 30 runs from 24 balls, striking four boundaries and a six before falling to Uganda’s Joseph Baguma. Baguma emerged as Uganda’s most effective bowler, finishing with figures of four wickets for 21 runs in four overs and preventing Nigeria from building an even larger total. Ali Rahmon also made a valuable contribution, scoring 35 runs from 23 deliveries, including three fours and two sixes. Despite Uganda’s efforts to restrict the scoring in the closing stages, Nigeria were eventually bowled out for 148 in 19.4 overs, setting their opponents a target of 149. Uganda’s chase suffered an early setback as Nigeria’s bowlers struck in the opening overs, dismissing Raghav Dhawan and Robinson Obuya to put the visitors under immediate pressure. Abdullahi Ismail claimed both early wickets, giving Nigeria the breakthrough they needed to defend their total. Uganda captain Riazat Ali Shah, however, responded with a remarkable counterattack that brought his side back into contention. Shah scored 60 runs from 35 deliveries, striking five sixes and three fours to keep Uganda firmly in the contest. His aggressive innings shifted the pressure back onto the Nigerian bowlers and raised the possibility of an Ugandan victory. The victory over Uganda brought their sub-regional campaign to a fitting conclusion: an unbeaten run, qualification secured, individual awards earned and a historic breakthrough against one of their toughest continental rivals. Nigeria now turn their attention to the 2027 Africa Qualifier, carrying the confidence of a team that has shown it can compete, endure pressure and make history. The YellowGreens have conquered the sub-regional stage and broken new ground against Uganda. The road to the 2028 ICC Men’s T20 World Cup continues.

title: Ikpeme Motivates Flamingos ahead Mexico Clash on Thursday
body: The Acting General Secretary of Nigeria Football Federation (NFF), Dr Emmanuel Ikpeme, has commended Nigeria’s U17 girls, Flamingos for their impressive 3-1 victory over two-time winners Korea DPR on Friday, which secured their place in the Round of 16 at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. During a visit to the team’s training session on Monday morning, Ikpeme urged the players to carry the same determination into their knockout match against Mexico on Thursday, October 29. He encouraged the team to take each game as it comes and remain focused on reaching the quarter-finals. The NFF scribe also promised to be present at the Round of 16 match to support the Flamingos as they continue their World Cup campaign. Nigeria have scored a total of six goals in their three matches so far at the tournament, with Oluwakemi Adegbuyi and Oluebube Umejiaku accounting for two each. Precious Oscar scored the second goal against Puerto Rico while Rodiat Kanyinsola Yusuf netted from a free-kick against Korea DPR. Thursday’s encounter is a clash of former FIFA U17 Women’s World Cup bronze medallists. Nigeria picked up the bronze medals after a dramatic penalty-shootout win over Germany in the third-place match in India four years ago, while Mexico defeated Brazil 3-1 on penalties after a 1-1 draw to win bronze medals at last year’s tournament also staged by Morocco. In India, the Flamingos led Germany 3-0 after 63 minutes, but Germany drew level before the final whistle. However, Nigeria won the shootout 3-2 at the DY Patil Stadium in Navi Mumbai to attain the podium for the first time in the history of the competition.

title: Super 4 Race Intensifies at Nat Idowu U16 Football League
body: The race for a place in the Super 4 of the Nathaniel Idowu Under-16 Football League 2026 has reached a thrilling climax following a dramatic Week 8, setting the stage for a blockbuster final round of fixtures on Saturday, 31 October 2026. Unbeaten Young 11 FA have already secured their place in the Super 4, but three spots remain up for grabs with five teams still firmly in contention heading into Week 9. At the New Maracana Sports Complex, Tolu, Ajegunle United SC kept their qualification hopes alive with a hard-fought 2-1 victory over St. Petersburg FA. Goals from Adogha Peter in the 13th minute and Onyeabuchi Okoli in the 50th minute proved decisive as Ajegunle claimed a vital three points. Atico FA also breathed new life into their campaign with a thrilling 4-3 win over Moore Wins Foundation FA. Haruna Usman, Korede Olabiyi, Ayomide Oyebanji and Opeyemi Ajiboye all found the net in an entertaining seven-goal encounter. Bright Stars SA produced one of the biggest surprises of the weekend, defeating SC Heritage 2-1 away from home. Feranmi Akinwale scored twice in the 20th and 48th minutes to overturn Norbert Theodore’s opener and propel Bright Stars back into Super 4 contention. At the Nathaniel Idowu Football Pitch, Oregie, Divinely Blessed FA recorded a comfortable 3-0 victory over bottom-placed Seraphic FA, while league leaders Young 11 FA once again demonstrated their resilience by coming from behind twice to earn a 2-2 draw against second-placed Fortune FA. Bamidele Waris and Adebayo Lateef were on target for Fortune FA, but Daniel Hameed and Quadri Azeez responded for Young 11 to preserve their unbeaten record. title: International Breweries’s Profit Drops by 5.74% to N54.51bn in 9 Months
body: Kayode Tokede Following a 119.25 per cent growth in income tax expense, International Breweries Plc yesterday announced unaudited nine months ended September 30, 2026 with profit after tax closing at N54.5 billion, a 5.74 per cent from N57.83 billion reported in nine months ended September 30, 2025. International Breweries in the period posted N35.93 billion income tax expense in nine months of 2026 from N16.39billion in nine months of 2025, a critical factor that led to 5.74 per cent drop in profit after tax. The brewery marker on the Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX) disclosed that its profit before tax, however, closed nine months of 2026 at N90.44 billion, about 21.86 per cent increase when compared to N74.22 billion reported in nine months ended September 30, 2025. The company in its profit & loss figures declared N482.61billion revenue in nine months of 2026, representing an increase of 2.12 per cent from N472.6 billion in nine months of 2025. Despite double digit inflation, International Breweries posted N286.7 billion cost of sales in nine months of 2026, which is 8.02 per cent drop from N311.64 billion in nine months of 2025. With the interest in revenue and drop in cost of sales, the company declared N195.94 billion gross profit in nine months of 2026, about 21.76 per cent increase over N160.93 billion in nine months of 2025. The improvement suggests that the brewer generated more gross profit from each naira of sales, although rising operating expenses continued to absorb part of those gains. Administrative, marketing, and distribution expenses increased 26.1 percent to N116.16 billion from N92.09 billion in the nine months to September 2025. The increase reflects higher spending across operating and commercial activities, including advertising, promotion, and distribution expenses, which rose to N75.14 billion from N54.98 billion. From the balance sheet position, the company declared a total assets of N692.03 billion as of September 30, 20026, down by 6.45 per cent from N739.74 billion in 2025. Property, plant and equipment increased to N370.36 billion from N339.53 billion, reflecting continued investment in the company’s productive assets. Current assets declined to N273.63 billion from N314.34 billion, largely due to the reduction in cash and cash equivalents and inventories. Total liabilities fell to N221.70 billion from N239.92 billion. The company disclosed that it had no outstanding loans or overdrafts at the end of the reporting period, although it continued to carry lease liabilities. AB InBev Nigeria Holdings BV held a 96.01 per cent equity interest in International Breweries at September 30, according to the filing, leaving a free float of 2.55 per cent. The brewer’s earnings per share declined to N0.32 for the nine months, from N0.34 in the corresponding period of 2025. The company closed yesterday at N9.30 per share on the Exchange . International Breweries began the year with a share price of N14.00 but has since lost 50.54 per cent Year till Date (YtD) of that valuation.

title: Georgiadis and Konstantopoulou Clash in Parliament Over Israel (VID)
body: Greek Health Minister Adonis Georgiadis and Freedom of Sailing party leader Zoe Konstantopoulou exchanged personal insults and accusations in Parliament during a heated confrontation over Georgiadis’s attendance at a meeting with Israeli officials in Athens on 12 October. Konstantopoulou accused Georgiadis of attending a “secret meeting” at the Athens Club with the Israeli ambassador, Israel’s Minister of Technology and other figures. She questioned whether he had attended in his official capacity and whether Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis and the Speaker of Parliament had received prior notification. Georgiadis rejected the suggestion that the meeting was secret, saying the event had attracted around 200 guests in central Athens. He also confirmed that he had not informed the prime minister or the Speaker, arguing that he did not need their permission to attend. The exchange escalated as both politicians traded accusations, with Konstantopoulou calling Georgiadis a “fascist” and the minister asking whether she considered herself a “national prosecutor”. Konstantopoulou Questions Meeting With Israeli Officials Konstantopoulou opened the exchange with an ironic remark, telling the health minister that she wanted to ask him something serious rather than distract him from his “acrobatics and exclamations”. She accused Georgiadis of secretly meeting members of his party alongside groups and figures she associated with international Zionism. She also questioned whether the meeting served the interests of a foreign state. Georgiadis responded that Konstantopoulou had confused him with another politician, referring to an earlier incident involving her confrontation with PASOK MP Christos Christidis. He dismissed the allegation of secrecy, arguing that a meeting attended by 200 people in central Athens could hardly qualify as secret. He also challenged the suggestion that his failure to post about the event on social media justified the accusations against him. The minister defended Greece’s strategic relationship with Israel, tracing its development to 2010 under former prime minister George Papandreou. He cited Israel’s position on the Turkey-Libya maritime memorandum and cooperation on the electricity interconnection between the countries as examples of shared strategic interests. Konstantopoulou Says She Will Pursue Legal Action The confrontation intensified when Konstantopoulou called Georgiadis a “fascist” and referred to the sale of antisemitic books by Konstantinos Plevris. She also criticised Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, whom she described as a friend of Georgiadis, and said she would seek accountability. “I am pursuing you through criminal proceedings in this parliamentary question, and you should take that into account,” Konstantopoulou told the minister, arguing that he had contradicted himself. Georgiadis reacted angrily, asking whether she had threatened to put him in prison and dismissing her remarks with the question: “Who do you think you are, madam? The national prosecutor?” Georgiadis Accuses Konstantopoulou of Betraying Greece The exchange became increasingly personal as Georgiadis defended the strategic relationship between Greece and Israel, arguing that the two countries’ national interests “coincide absolutely”. “I’m a fascist, and you’re not a traitor to Greece?” he asked Konstantopoulou, accusing her of acting against the relationship between the two countries. Konstantopoulou responded with the word “fearless”, prompting another personal attack from the minister. “Who destroyed your character and made you such a show-off?” Georgiadis asked. He returned the “fascist” accusation, criticising her for speaking rudely to parliamentary colleagues and threatening them. The confrontation ended amid continued tension, with Georgiadis reiterating that he had attended the meeting and defending his decision to participate. The exchange highlighted the deep political divisions surrounding Greece’s relationship with Israel, as well as the increasingly personal tone of parliamentary debate.
