title: NYSC, UNN disowned ex-minister Uche Nnaji’s certificates, ICPC witness tells court
body: An investigator with the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC), Yakubu Ibrahim, on Monday, told a Federal High Court in Abuja that both the University of Nigeria (UNN) and the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) disowned the degree and discharge certificates presented by former Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, Uche Nnaji, to the Senate for his ministerial screening in 2023. The witness, Suprintendent of Police, Yakubu Ibrahim, testified as the first prosecution witness in the trial of Nnaji, who is facing a six-count charge marked FHC/ABJ/CR/389/2026, bordering on alleged corruption, fraud, conferring corrupt advantage and providing false information through the alleged presentation of forged university degree and national service certificates. The investigator, who was led in evidence by the prosecution counsel, J. A. Mumini (SAN), said he was part of the ICPC team that investigated two petitions against the defendant. The witness said his team was assigned to investigate the matter after the commission received two separate petitions alleging certificate forgery against Nnaji. He said the Chairman of the Special Task Force directed an investigation, prompting the commission to request relevant documents from the National Assembly, the Office of the Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), University of Nigeria, Nsukka and the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC). He told the court that the team wrote to UNN to authenticate the Bachelor of Science certificate in Microbiology/Biochemistry allegedly submitted by Nnaji to the Senate. According to him, the university responded that it did not issue the certificate to the governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Enugu for the 2027 election. The witness added that the team also contacted the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) over a discharge certificate 15th May 1986, but the NYSC equally disowned it, maintaining that it did not issue any such certificate to the ex-minister. Ibrahim further told the court that UNN supplied the investigators with the defendant’s academic records, including a notice of withdrawal issued over his failure to obtain the required grade in a course. When shown copies of the correspondence between the ICPC and the two institutions, the witness identified the documents, following which the prosecution sought to tender them in evidence. Defence counsel, Wole Olanipekun (SAN), said he would allow the documents to be admitted at that stage but reserve his objection until later. On the steps taken to interview the defendant, Ibrahim said the head of his section issued an invitation, but investigators could not locate his address. He said a copy of the invitation, dated May 5, 2026, was subsequently sent to the defendant’s email address and WhatsApp number. According to the witness, after Nnaji failed to honour the invitation, the ICPC liaised with the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) to effect his arrest on July 1. He added that the defendant was questioned and made statements dated July 1 and 2. During cross-examination by Olanipekun, the witness admitted that he did not visit UNN during the investigation and did not know the faculty to which the defendant had been admitted. He, however, said members of the investigating team interviewed the university’s Registrar. Asked whether the team established where the alleged certificates were forged, Ibrahim said he did not know. He also said the defendant made no comment on the allegations when questioned by investigators. On whether the team investigated where Nnaji undertook his national service, the witness said it did not because the NYSC had stated that it did not issue the certificate. “The NYSC said the certificate was not issued by it, which was why we didn’t inquire where he served,” he told the court. The witness also confirmed seeing a notice of withdrawal supplied by UNN. When asked to identify it, he identified the document, marked Exhibit C, dated November 7, 1984. He said the university explained in its letter the policy governing the grades required for the award of a certificate saying if one failed four times, the person was not qualified. Ibrahim said Nnaji failed at two stages and did not write the examination at the third stage for medical reasons. “The witness said, “the defendant went ahead to write the supplementary examination for which he did not register.” Ibrahim further testified that UNN confirmed that the BSc certificate in Microbiology and Biochemistry attributed to the defendant was not issued by the university. Olanipekun suggested that a subsequent letter dated March 18, 1985, rescinded the earlier withdrawal notice. Ibrahim agreed, adding that the withdrawal notice related to a course in General Microbiology. The witness also told the court that investigators did not establish the number of years a student studying Microbiology was expected to spend at the university. At the conclusion of cross-examination, the prosecution did not re-examine the witness, following which Justice Joyce Abdulmalik discharged him and adjourned further hearing until November 3. Meanwhile, it is recalled that Nnaji, who resigned as minister following the certificates forgery scandal did not include the controversial degree certificate in his Independent National Electoral Commissioner (INEC) filing ahead of the 2027 election in which he flies the flag of the PDP. The post NYSC, UNN disowned ex-minister Uche Nnaji’s certificates, ICPC witness tells court appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: NERC Holds Training on Handling of Customer Complaints
body: The Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC), has concluded a three-day capacity-building programme for members of its Forum Offices across the country. The training, themed: “Strengthening Forum Members in Delivering Quality Rulings and Resolution of Complaints,” is designed to enhance the capacity of forum members in effectively adjudicating customer complaints and resolving disputes within the Nigerian Electricity Supply Industry (NESI). Welcoming participants to the programme, the Chairman of NERC, Dr. Musiliu Oseni, represented by the Director, Economic Regulation Division, Mr. Abba Terab, commended the members for their commitment to safeguarding consumer rights and contributing to improved service delivery by Electricity Distribution Companies (Discos). “It is important that we continue to strengthen your capacity and keep you abreast of developments within the electricity market, particularly changes in the legal and regulatory framework. This will ensure that you are well informed and better equipped to discharge your responsibilities in resolving customer disputes with the Discos,” he said. Also speaking, NERC Commissioner, Stakeholder Management Division (SMD), Mrs. Aisha Mahmud, represented by the Head, International Relations and Stakeholder Secretariat, SMD, Mrs. Regina Osuagwu described the contributions of Forum Members as invaluable to both NERC and electricity consumers nationwide. She noted that the electricity sector has witnessed significant reforms in recent years, making continuous training essential for effective complaint resolution.

title: NISO to Advance Integrated Electricity Market
body: The Managing Director and Chief Executive of the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO), Bello Mohammed, has proposed a NISO–State Technical Working Group to strengthen collaboration with state stakeholders. Mohammed argued that this will also help to advance the development of an integrated electricity market in line with the Electricity Act 2023. He made the proposal while making a presentation at the National Workshop on the Electricity Act 2023, at the State House Auditorium, Presidential Villa, Abuja, the organisation said ina. statement. Mohammed also proposed an annual energy planning summit involving NISO and the states to assess energy resources and forecast electricity demand. He stressed the importance of harmonised technical standards, data sharing and effective coordination between state electricity markets and the interconnected national grid. Other proposals, according to the statement,include developing a national state coordination framework, institutionalising integrated planning and adopting a phased implementation roadmap. He explained that the goal is not to centralise electricity markets, but to ensure they work together effectively within a reliable and well-managed electricity system.

title: Local Petrol Output Exceeds 12bn Litres, Imports Hit 7.67bn Litres in 13 Months
body: Emmanuel Addeh in Abuja Nigeria’s domestic refineries supplied 12.01 billion litres of petrol, accounting for 61.2 per cent of the total 19.68 billion litres of petrol pumped into the market from September 2025 to September 2026, while it imported 7.67 billion litres of petrol, representing 38.8 per cent of total supply, fresh industry data has shown. The figures, contained in the September 2026 factsheet of the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) underscored the growing contribution of local refining to Nigeria’s fuel supply, although imports remained significant in meeting domestic demand. According to the data, petrol imports were relatively high towards the end of 2025, averaging 22.1 million litres daily in September before surging to 52.1 million litres per day in November, equivalent to about 1.56 billion litres for the month. Domestic supply averaged 19.5 million litres daily in November. While the proponents of total local refining argue that every litre imported puts pressure on foreign exchange reserves, leads to capital flight and kills local industries, the import side maintains that Nigeria cannot rely solely on a single refinery for its fuel, stressing that it will lead to a monopoly. However, Imports remained elevated in December at 42.2 million litres per day, while domestic supply stood at 32 million litres daily. Combined, the two sources supplied an average of 74.2 million litres per day, the highest monthly rate cited in the data. The balance shifted in early 2026 as domestic refinery output increased and petrol imports declined. By February, imports had fallen to an average of 3 million litres per day, compared with domestic supply of 29.4 million litres daily. According to the data, the gap widened further in April, when local refineries supplied 40.7 million litres per day against imports of 3.7 million litres. Domestic supply rose to 41.5 million litres daily in May, while imports averaged 5.9 million litres. But the improvement in local supply did not prevent a contraction in overall receipts in September. Petrol receipts fell to 38.7 million litres per day, comprising 28.5 million litres from domestic sources and 10.2 million litres from imports. The regulator attributed the decline partly to a 21 per cent month-on-month fall in domestic supply and a 30 per cent drop in imports. It also identified the exhaustion of approved import permits among major trading companies as a factor affecting supply. Also, diesel imports totalled 2.60 billion litres over the period, while domestic refineries supplied approximately 4 billion litres, bringing total supply to about 6.61 billion litres. Domestic refineries accounted for 60.5 per cent of diesel supply, averaging 10.1 million litres per day, while imports handled by oil marketing companies averaged 6.6 million litres daily. Import volumes varied considerably. In February 2026, total diesel receipts reached 24.8 million litres per day, including 15.9 million litres from oil marketing companies. Imports by the companies fell to zero in May and June before recovering to 7.9 million litres per day in July and 1.3 million litres in August. By September, total diesel receipts had declined to 8.7 million litres per day, comprising 8.1 million litres from domestic refineries and 0.6 million litres from imports. In the aviation fuel market, domestic receipts of Aviation Turbine Kerosene (ATK), commonly known as jet fuel, totalled 1.04 billion litres during the review period. Average daily receipts stood at 2.6 million litres, rising to 3.9 million litres in December 2025 before reaching 3.3 million litres in September 2026, 6 per cent higher than in August. The Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) market also recorded a substantial domestic contribution. Total supply reached 1.86 million tonnes over the 13 months, comprising 1.56 million tonnes from domestic sources and about 301,300 tonnes from imports by oil marketing companies. Domestic processing plants supplied 83.9 per cent of the market, with imports accounting for the remaining 16.1 per cent. NLNG and Seplat Energy supplied LPG by vessel, representing 54.3 per cent of total market supply, while other processing plants accounted for 26.4 per cent through truck deliveries. The Dangote Refinery contributed 15.1 per cent. Besides, LPG imports peaked at 5.3 kilotonnes per day in July 2026. The expansion in domestic petroleum product supply also coincided with a rise in crude oil allocations to local refineries. The NUPRC data from January to July 2026 showed average daily crude oil lifting of 1.61 million barrels, of which domestic refineries received about 460,000 barrels per day, or 29 per cent. The allocation compared with 280,000 barrels per day in 2025 and 220,000 barrels per day in 2024. Direct crude exports averaged 1.15 million barrels per day, accounting for the remaining 71 per cent of liftings.

title: BOI Establishes 15 Tech Hubs, Supports Young Fashion Entrepreneurs with Solar Power Installation
body: Dike Onwuamaeze The Bank of Industry (BOI) has said that it created 15 tech and innovation hubs across the country, which have impacted over 9,220 aspiring entrepreneurs and led to the creation of 950 startups. The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Bank of Industry (BOI) is Dr. Olasupo Olusi disclosed this in a chat with newsmen in Lagos. This, he said, were executed under the “BOI Innovation Tech Hub Program,” as part of its Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR). He said the creation of innovative hubs were based on the recognition of the pivotal role that technology and innovation play in driving economic growth, fostering entrepreneurship, and solving pressing societal challenges. He said the BOI has created has created 15 tech and innovation hubs across the country since 2018, which have impacted over 9,220 aspiring entrepreneurs and led to the creation of 950 startups across the nation. “The bank’s objective in funding and sponsoring Tech/Innovation hubs is to nurture talent, drive economic development and fostering collaboration and knowledge sharing. We aim to provide aspiring entrepreneurs and innovators with the resources, mentorship and infrastructure they need to turn their ideas into reality. Through hackathons, and incubation programs, we empower individuals to unleash their full potential and drive positive change in their communities. “Through these hubs we have contributed to the development of vibrant ecosystems that attract investment, create jobs, and spur entrepreneurship. These hubs have driven economic activity, attracting startups, investors, and talent, and fostering a culture of innovation that propels entire industries forward. By fuelling innovation, we not only strengthen the competitiveness of our economy but also position ourselves at the forefront of technological advancement,” he said. According to him, tech and innovation hubs provide platforms for collaboration, enabling individuals and organisations to exchange ideas, share knowledge, and form partnerships. He said: “The hubs facilitate cross-pollination of ideas, encourage interdisciplinary collaboration, and foster a culture of open innovation. Through initiatives such as networking events, workshops, and knowledge-sharing sessions, we create opportunities for meaningful connections and collective learning, driving innovation at scale.” Speaking on the intervention, Lead Youth and Skills Thematic Champion at BOI, Mrs. Aderonke Akinluyi, said that the project reflected the bank’s commitment to removing practical barriers that prevent young Nigerians from turning their skills into sustainable enterprises. Akinluyi said: “For young entrepreneurs, access to reliable power is not simply an infrastructure issue; it is a productivity, competitiveness and, ultimately, a livelihood issue. By providing these fashion entrepreneurs with clean and dependable energy, we are helping them lower their operating costs, which will ultimately increase their profit margins. “At the BOI, in line with our youth and skills thematic area, our commitment is to equip young Nigerians with the skills and resources to build enterprises that translate their potential into sustainable economic value.” Highlighting the impact of the installation, the Secretary, Lagos Island Artisans, Adebayo Kafayat Adebukonla, said that reliable electricity is already improving how beneficiaries serve their customers. Adebukonla said: “Before this solar installation, constant power outages made it difficult to meet deadlines and grow our businesses. Now, with a reliable and steady electricity supply, we can deliver finished clothes to our customers on time while reducing our carbon footprint. This has boosted customer confidence and it is inspiring more young people in our community to pursue careers in fashion design.”

title: Court dismisses DOJ's request to force California to set aside ballots
body: Washington — A federal appeals court on Monday dismissed the Justice Department's effort to force California election officials to set aside thousands of ballots that the Trump administration claims may have been cast by alleged noncitizens.The U.S. Court of Appeals for the 9th Circuit said in a 2-1 decision that it lacked jurisdiction over the appeal and granted a motion by the top elections official from Los Angeles County to dismiss the effort. The federal government, Judges Mark Bennett and Gabriel Sanchez said, failed to allow a federal district court "adequate opportunity" to consider its request for temporary relief. Judge Patrick Bumatay dissented.The two judges faulted the Justice Department for waiting until less than three weeks before the midterm elections on Nov. 3 to file its lawsuit and only seeking a temporary restraining order from the district court last week. They also pointed out that the department had sought a temporary restraining order as California was already processing ballots."The United States's claimed emergency, at least in part, is a self-constructed one," the 9th Circuit said in an unsigned opinion. "At least part of the delay here is attributable to the United States's own delay in filing suit, in realizing that existing California state law governs the issuance and processing of ballots, in recognizing that California has millions of registered voters and processes ballots on a schedule aligned with that scale, and in communicating to the court its desired relief."Both Bennett, appointed by President Trump, and Sanchez, tapped by former President Joe Biden, authored concurring opinions. Bennett said that even if the court had reached the legal merits of the Justice Department's effort, he would have rejected its bid to force California to set aside the ballots that may be cast by ineligible voters.Bumatay, who dissented, said the federal government has an interest in protecting the integrity of federal elections."The question — does the federal government have the power to stop this potential attack on the integrity of our elections? Under both federal law and the Constitution, the answer must be 'yes,'" the judge, a Trump appointee, wrote. "Simply, the federal government has a sovereign interest in safeguarding federal elections and ensuring that the votes of noncitizens do not undermine our electoral results."California Gov. Gavin Newsom said the 9th Circuit's decision is a "positive development and a welcome speed bump to Trump's disgusting attacks on the Constitution and our country's democracy.""Trump is illegally trying to seize powers in the Constitution entrusted to others so he can stay in power. This lawsuit is just the latest step," he said in a statement. "Make no mistake: Trump's assault on democracy won't slow down."Dispute over list of votersThe fast-moving dispute over California's mail ballots was filed earlier this month after Acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter sent letters to California's secretary of state and the top election official in Los Angeles County, Dean Logan, which gave them 48 hours to review a list of more than 20,000 registered voters who the Trump administration believes are "likely" noncitizens and were sent mail ballots.Los Angeles County told McCotter in a letter dated Oct. 15 that the list of suspected noncitizens contained addresses of registered voters throughout the state, and said his letter did not include information about how the list had been compiled. The county also told McCotter the letter did not provide any information as to how the county was to confirm citizenship status.A lawyer for Los Angeles County said the Justice Department was asking Logan, the registrar-recorder and county clerk, "to engage in an unlawful course of conduct."On the same day that the county sent McCotter its response, the Justice Department sued California, Secretary of State Shirley Weber and Logan, and claimed that state officials had failed to work collaboratively with the federal government to identify any noncitizens registered to vote in the state and protect the integrity of elections.The Justice Department asked a federal judge to order California to put aside mail ballots of people it has identified as suspected noncitizens and to independently verify their citizenship status before counting their ballots.The judge overseeing the case, David O. Carter, scheduled a hearing for Tuesday afternoon on the Trump administration's request for a temporary restraining order. But the following day, the Justice Department took the extraordinary step of filing an appeal with the 9th Circuit.Government lawyers argued that because Carter had not yet ruled on their request for emergency relief, his "silence" amounted to a "constructive denial" of their effort to require California to set aside the mail ballots returned by the voters on the Trump administration's list.The three-judge 9th Circuit panel then held a rare Sunday oral argument session, during which at least two of the judges appeared skeptical of the Justice Department's request for the court to step in.The 11th-hour lawsuit against California officials was filed less than three weeks before the November midterm elections, when voters across the country will decide which party controls the House and Senate. In California, elections officials began mailing ballots in early October. Los Angeles County has already processed an estimated 550,000 mail ballots, according to court filings.In the months leading up to the midterms, Mr. Trump has attempted to exert more federal control over elections and pushed Congress to enact a package of voting regulations, including requiring proof of citizenship to register to vote.The president has repeatedly claimed that hundreds of thousands of noncitizens are registered to vote in federal elections, including more than 190,000 in California. Both federal and California law prohibit noncitizens from voting.But the Department of Homeland Security has declined to provide California election officials with an explanation of how it identified those alleged ineligible voters.Instead, in its lawsuit, the Justice Department said the DHS compares information about voter rolls with internal data to identify potential matches between registered voters and possible noncitizens, and then uses "third-party software" to identify matches between voter information and data about that person compiled by the software program. The Trump administration also said it uses internal records and data from the Social Security Administration.But California officials have argued that the Justice Department's lawsuit does not contain any allegations that those suspected noncitizens will even vote unlawfully in the general election. Lawyers for Logan, the Los Angeles County registrar-recorder and county clerk, also said that the relief sought by the Trump administration exceeds the executive branch's constitutional authority.The Constitution's Elections Clause gives states the power to set the "times, places and manners" of congressional elections unless Congress steps in.Amid the ongoing litigation, lawyers for Logan and Los Angeles County said they attempted to analyze the data from the Trump administration's list of alleged noncitizens. The list includes 7,035 records with county addresses, they said. County officials reviewed a sample of 200 of those records and found 112 of them correspond to voter registrations that were canceled or inactive, so no ballot was mailed to that person.Most of the people in the sample had never voted, and more than one-quarter of them listed a birthplace in the U.S., according to a Los Angeles County election official.Federal prosecutors sent more letters to at least 18 other California county registrars on Friday with lists of alleged noncitizens registered to vote. The Justice Department demanded the elections officials set aside ballots cast by those it believes are ineligible to vote.The Justice Department could ask the full 9th Circuit to reconsider its appeal, and the panel gave the government until 7 p.m. local time to make such a request.

title: NUPRC: 10 New Regulations Under Development, 19 Gazetted
body: Emmanuel Addeh The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) has gazetted 19 regulations and is currently developing an additional 10 regulations for the upstream petroleum sector, the upstream regulator has said. Senior Regulatory Officer, Regulations and Special Investigations, Mrs Emmanuella Senlong, said this during a presentation at a two-day National Workshop on the Electricity Act 2023 (as amended), at the State House Banquet Hall, Presidential Villa, Abuja. “To date, the NUPRC has gazetted 19 sector-specific regulations, with 10 additional regulations currently under development, and issued 25 operational guidelines covering critical areas across the upstream value chain”, Senlong revealed in a statement. According to Senlong, establishing legal frameworks is only the first step, as true success relies on closing the implementation gap through demonstrable statutory compliance. She said in order to achieve this, the commission is addressing legacy challenges and overlapping obligations by implementing standardised reporting templates, risk-based inspection protocols, and auditable yearly compliance assessments. Organised by Allstates Management Partners Solutions Limited (AMPSL) in collaboration with the Office of the Vice President, the workshop themed: “Empowering the States: Reviewing the Electricity Act 2023” brought together representatives of federal and state governments, regulatory institutions, industry operators, investors and development partners to examine opportunities for effective implementation of the Act. At the two-day workshop, the commission expressed its commitment to the successful implementation of the Electricity Act. Central to this commitment, the commission said, is its strategic role in implementing Domestic Gas Delivery Obligations (DGDO), which require gas producers to make prescribed volumes available to the domestic market. Meanwhile, NUPRC Chief Executive, Mrs. Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan, has urged staff of the commission to go the extra mile in the performance of their duties. Eyesan said this at a conference organised in commemoration of Customer Service Week 2026. The NUPRC boss who was represented by the Director, Host Community, Mrs. Ejioro Ufondu, said the theme ‘Going the extra mile’ was instructive. “Going the extra mile is not simply about doing more; it is about doing better, responding faster, taking ownership, and making a meaningful difference in the experience of those we serve. We take regulating the industry as a service,” she said.

title: Ikpea Donates N2.2bn Medical Centre to Ewatto Community
body: A philanthropist and the founder of the Agbonjagwe Leemon Ikpea Foundation, Dr Leemon Ikpea, has donated a 62-bed medical centre to the Ewatto, Esan South East Local Government Area of Edo State to improve access to healthcare in the area and the neighbouring communities. The medical centre, which was commissioned on Monday October 19, 2026 and named after the founder, was built at the estimated cost of N2.227 billion. The facility is equipped with modern medical equipment and is expected to reduce the difficulties faced by residents who had to travel considerable distances to access healthcare, particularly during emergencies. Speaking at the ceremony, Ikpea said that the project was conceived in response to the healthcare challenges being faced by Ewatto and the surrounding communities. Ikpea said, “I firmly believe that one of the most meaningful legacies any individual can leave behind is an institution that continues to improve and preserve human lives long after the individual is gone. It is my sincere hope that this Medical Centre will become such a legacy.” Speaking at the commissioning, the governor of Edo State, Monday Okpebholo, commended Chief Ikpea, saying his life as a philanthropists was exemplified by the lives he had touched. He praised Ikpea for the “extraordinary healthcare investment” he brought to his people”. Okpebholo said, “You have demonstrated that your true success is not measured by what you have achieved, but by the lives you have touched. You built more than hope; you have brought quality healthcare closer to the people.” Commissioning the facility, the Minister of Health, Prof Muhammad Ali Pate, commended Chief Ikpea for complementing the government’s efforts to improve access to quality healthcare, describing the medical centre as a significant contribution to healthcare delivery in the community. In a goodwill message, the Onojie of Ekpoma Kingdom, His Royal Highness Barrister Antony Ehiozojie Abumere II, congratulated Ikpea on the establishment of the medical centre, describing it as a valuable contribution to the health and wellbeing of the people of Esanland.

title: FG Commissions Power Projects in Kano, Katsina to Boost Supply
body: The Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, has inaugurated transmission substation projects in Kano and Katsina States, adding 240MW at the 330kV level and 376MW at the 132kV level to Nigeria’s transmission network. The projects are expected to strengthen bulk electricity supply, ease pressure on existing substations and improve power delivery to industrial, commercial and residential consumers in the two states, a statement in Abuja by the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) stated. In Katsina, Tegbe commissioned two 60MVA power transformers at the Kankia Transmission Substation, increasing its installed capacity from 60MVA to 150MVA. He also performed the groundbreaking ceremony for a new 120MVA transmission substation at Mashi and inspected ongoing work on a 200MVA gas-insulated substation at the 330kV Katsina Substation. Speaking at Mashi, the minister said the new substation, upon completion, would provide an additional 96MW to improve electricity supply to the community and neighbouring areas. He disclosed that issues relating to right-of-way and compensation for project-affected persons had been resolved, paving the way for construction to commence. The minister said the projects, implemented by the federal government through the Federal Ministry of Power and the TCN, were aimed at strengthening transmission infrastructure and improving electricity supply across Katsina State. In Kano, Tegbe commissioned transmission projects at Walalambe, Kumbotso, Dakata and Dan Agundi substations. The projects included two 40MVA transformers at Walalambe, 300MVA and 100MVA transformers at Kumbotso, and 100MVA transformers each at Dakata and Dan Agundi. In his remarks, the Managing Director of TCN, Sule Abdulaziz, said the projects would address transmission capacity constraints and improve the delivery of bulk electricity to distribution companies for onward supply to consumers. He added that the works included modernising control rooms with digital control and protection panels, expanding the 33kV busbar and installing additional outgoing feeders.

title: ProvidusUnity Bank Graduates Over 100 Entrepreneurs from SME Programme
body: Nume Ekeghe ProvidusUnity Bank has graduated more than 100 entrepreneurs from the sixth cohort of its SME Development Programme, continuing its efforts to help small businesses overcome the challenges that often stand in the way of growth. The three-month programme, organised in partnership with the Enterprise Development Centre (EDC) of Pan-Atlantic University, brought together small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) owners from Lagos, Abuja and Port Harcourt.\Speaking at the graduation ceremony held in Lagos, Head of Business Development at ProvidusUnity Bank, Ernest Elue, said the initiative was designed to address the capacity gaps that often constrain the growth of SMEs and limit their contribution to national development. He said, “For us, this programme goes beyond training entrepreneurs. It is about building an ecosystem where small businesses can access the knowledge, networks, and support required to achieve long-term sustainability and growth. SMEs remain the backbone of the Nigerian economy, and investing in their success is an investment in the country’s future. “Over the years, we have remained committed to supporting entrepreneurs with the tools and capabilities needed to scale their businesses. Through our partnership with the Enterprise Development Centre, we are helping to nurture resilient enterprises that create jobs, stimulate innovation, and contribute meaningfully to economic prosperity.” Participants described the programme as a transformative experience that provided practical solutions to real business challenges and strengthened their capacity for growth. Founder of Danny Palm Oil, Ukponi Bahan, said the programme provided valuable insights that would support the company’s next phase of expansion. “The training challenged us to think differently about our business and sharpen our growth strategy. The sessions on operations, planning, and sustainability were particularly valuable as we prepare for future growth.”

Less than a month after its mass release of hundreds of manuscripts that it said contained solutions to long-standing mathematics questions, OpenAI is back with three more “major” discoveries in math, computer science, and physics . What’s different this time is the choice to have external experts that OpenAI describes as “shepherds” guiding the results in computer science and physics, while for the math problem it says that they advised it to release the AI output for researchers to work through their own explanations.
Local smoothing for the Euclidean wave equation. The proof uses an auxiliary partial differential equation to establish Sogge’s local smoothing for waves in every spatial dimension at least two. It also yields the Kakeya maximal and dimension conjectures and Stein’s spherical restriction estimates throughout the interior of the conjectured range. We are releasing the model output directly, as we did in our October 6 release.
The Exponential Time Hypothesis is False. The paper gives a deterministic algorithm that exactly counts satisfying assignments of fixed-width CNF formulas in subexponential time and polynomial space. The case of 3-SAT refutes the Exponential Time Hypothesis. An independent working group of computer scientists led by Russell Impagliazzo, Ramamohan Paturi, and Ryan Williams will examine and explain the proof. At the group’s request, we are making the materials public immediately so others can examine them as well.
This approach could have its own issues, the company admits, and the AGMAI panel of math advisers OpenAI put together just said yesterday that “we recommend that AI companies do not adopt” the practices of designating certain people to receive the output first, citing unequal access, borrowed reputation, and biased selection as a few of the issues. Instead, they recommended that in the future, AI labs release output on scholarly repositories, with Lean-formalized proofs, info on how the problems were chosen, funding for people working on understanding the results, and other information.
The physics information has not been released in full, but is a “mathematically rigorous existence proof of certain interacting quantum field theories containing gauge fields and fermions in four dimensions, including Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD) and a unified completion of the Standard Model of particle physics.” According to OpenAI, “David Gross will lead a group including Michael Douglas, Arthur Jaffe, Igor Klebanov, and Nikita Nekrasov that will shepherd this work.”
The computer science collaboration is said to prove that the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH) , which has been widely believed to be true, is actually false. OpenAI says verification of the result will be guided by a group of three experts that includes UC San Diego’s Russell Impagliazzo and Ramamohan Paturi, who were part of the group that originally proposed it in 1999 , as well as MIT professor Ryan Williams . The group decided to release the AI output write-up and Lean proof on GitHub today .
They also released an open letter to the community asking for input on how to examine the claim, and about setting norms for dealing with AI-generated breakthroughs:
We would welcome discussion of three broader questions:
What expectations should govern early access to AI-generated results, disclosure of conflicts of interest, and the use of unpublished material for subsequent research?
How should credit recognize both new discoveries and the work of checking, fixing, simplifying, explaining, and extending them?
How can we support students and researchers as methods and research directions change, while preserving the understanding and judgment needed to question results and develop new ideas?
There’s similar documentation for the math breakthrough, where its model “produced a proof of the local smoothing conjecture in every dimension and therefore also resolve the Kakeya conjecture and Stein’s restriction conjecture in all dimensions.” Just a few months ago, NYU professor Hong Wang was awarded a prestigious Fields Medal by the International Mathematical Union for resolving the Kakeya conjecture in three dimensions.

title: Partisans gather intelligence on security at substation in Russian-occupied Dzhankoi
body:
According to Ukrinform, ATESH reported this on Telegram .
“The occupiers have integrated Dzhankoi’s power grid into the supply system for their military grouping. The Dzhankoi military airfield is located here and is home to the 39th Separate Guards Helicopter Regiment of the 27th Mixed Aviation Division of Russia’s 4th Air Force and Air Defense Army. Mi-8, Mi-35M, Mi-28 and Ka-52 helicopters are stationed at the airfield,” the statement said.
The facility is also used to receive military aircraft, store equipment and supply Russian troops.
ATESH noted that the Dzhankoi energy hub has come under attack repeatedly.
Overnight on December 14, 2025, monitoring sources reported a suspected strike and fire at the 330 kV Dzhankoi substation.
In the evening of January 13, 2026, local sources reported that another fire broke out at the substation following an attack, leaving parts of the city and surrounding district without electricity.
Overnight on June 29, the 413th Raid Regiment reported striking the Dzhankoi substation. Overnight on July 3, monitoring sources reported another fire at the facility following a drone attack.
The military airfield has also been targeted. In April 2024, a strike put four S-400 launchers, three radar stations, an air defense command post and the Fundament-M system out of action.
In July 2026, the Security Service of Ukraine (SSU) struck repeaters used by Russian Orion unmanned aerial vehicles, as well as weapons and equipment storage facilities.
“Our agents are among those tasked with protecting military facilities in Crimea. That is why Russian air defenses only detect some targets after the explosion,” the ATESH said.
As Ukrinform reported, agents of the ATESH partisan movement destroyed a communications tower near Shebekino in Russia’s Belgorod region, disrupting a repeater that Russian troops used to maintain a stable signal for drone targeting and control.

title: UCP backbencher Shane Getson quits legislature on eve of fall sitting
body:
A plainspoken, two-term Alberta United Conservative backbencher who courted controversy is quitting the job effective immediately.
Shane Getson says he is leaving due to personal and family reasons but does not elaborate.
“I can no longer give the time and attention that I have over the last seven years,” Getson said Monday in a statement written for local newspapers and shared by caucus.
“Providing anything less would diminish both my responsibilities to the people I serve and to my family.”
Getson has represented Lac. Ste. Anne-Parkland, a mostly rural riding northwest of Edmonton, since 2019.
In his time, he was known for speeches and comments riling up the political left.
In his goodbye statement, Getson writes, “Don’t chase the wackado woke, DEI, socialist easy fix for nothing ideas because of emotions getting ahead of logic.
“At the same time, keep your ears and minds open. Listen to different perspectives.”
Getson never served in cabinet but for a time was the United Conservative caucus whip.
He made headlines for controversial comments, including comparing transgender surgery to livestock castration in 2025. He later spoke of overcoming his own childhood abuse through religion, sports and hard work.

title: Government Credit Jumps to N39.4tn, Private Sector Credit Hits N11.4tn
body: Nume Ekeghe Credit to the federal government expanded by 63.1 per cent year-on-year to N39.40 trillion in September 2026, outpacing the 15.7 per cent growth in private-sector credit, as the latest Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) data showed contrasting movements in lending to both segments of the economy. The CBN money and credit statistics showed that credit to government rose from N24.16 trillion in September 2025 to N39.40 trillion in September 2026, an increase of N15.24 trillion. Credit to the private sector, meanwhile, climbed from N72.53 trillion to N83.93 trillion, adding N11.41 trillion over the same period. The difference in growth rates is significant. government credit expanded approximately four times faster than private-sector credit, while the increase in financing to government exceeded the additional credit extended to businesses by N3.83 trillion. A month-by-month examination of the figures reveals a volatile 12-month trajectory for both segments, with government credit accelerating towards the end of 2025 before retreating in the middle of 2026 and rebounding sharply in September. Private-sector credit also experienced considerable fluctuations, rising above N94 trillion early in 2026 before falling back to the N80 trillion range. In September 2025, credit to government stood at N24.16 trillion, while private-sector credit was N72.53 trillion. By October, government credit had increased to N24.79 trillion and private-sector credit to N74.41 trillion. The upward movement continued in November, when government credit reached N26.35 trillion and private-sector credit rose marginally to N74.63 trillion. December marked a more pronounced shift. Credit to government jumped to N34.22 trillion, an increase of N7.87 trillion from November, while private-sector credit rose to N75.83 trillion. The expansion in government credit continued into January 2026, reaching N37.87 trillion. Private-sector credit, however, surged to N93.74 trillion, up from N75.83 trillion in December. In February, government credit increased further to N39.36 trillion, while private-sector credit climbed to N94.61 trillion, the highest level recorded in the supplied monthly series. The subsequent figures, however, showed a reversal in private-sector credit. By April, it had fallen to N80.73 trillion, a decline of N13.88 trillion, or about 14.7 per cent, from February. Government credit stood at N39.63 trillion in April, remaining close to its February level.

title: NACC Hosts Executive Breakfast on U.S. EB-5 Investor Immigration Programme
body: The Nigerian-American Chamber of Commerce (NACC) has organised an exclusive Executive Breakfast Roundtable Discussion aimed at enlightening Nigerian business leaders, investors and high-net-worth individuals on opportunities available through the United States EB-5 Immigrant Investor Programme. The event, held on Thursday, October 22, 2026, in Lagos, focused on the theme, “Exploring the U.S. EB-5 Immigrant Investor Programme: A Strategic Pathway to U.S. Permanent Residency and Global Mobility.” The discussion was designed to provide insights into how eligible investors can leverage the EB-5 programme to pursue permanent residency in the United States through qualifying investments, while exploring broader opportunities for international business expansion and global mobility. National President of the Nigerian-American Chamber of Commerce, Sheriff Balogun, served as Chief Host, while Moussa Ndiaye, Vice President of Business Development and Head of EMEA at U.S. Immigration Fund, the guest speaker, took the participants through navigating the immigrant investor programme . title: McGill law student says she received death threats after defending convicted murderer Jeffrey Ewert
body:
A McGill University law student says she has received online threats after publicly defending convicted murderer Jeffrey Ewert, who was taken back into custody Saturday after his conditional release was suspended.
Amy Haysom said she met Ewert on their first day at McGill Law in September and developed a friendship with him before learning about his criminal past.
“He was this quiet, reserved gentleman, long braids, really lovely energy,” Haysom said.
She said Ewert later told her he was a convicted murderer and, as required under his release conditions, notified his parole officer about their developing friendship.
“One person I did need to speak to when I developed a friendship was his parole officer, so she was very involved with him on a daily basis,” Haysom said.
Haysom said she never felt unsafe around Ewert and continues to support him, despite receiving death threats online for defending him.
“We agree to a carceral system that agrees to reintegration,” she said. “And I would like to think we are not just talking about it in the mind, but what does it look like in action” she told Global News on Monday.
“I don’t think it’s OK to say, ‘Not in my backyard.'”
Ewert, who is now in his 60s, was convicted in the 1980s of second-degree murder and attempted murder involving violent attacks committed in British Columbia against two female victims, one of whom was 15.
In 1984, Ewert choked a 19-year-old woman unconscious, sexually assaulted her and then dumped her in the Fraser River, where she was later found dead.
Six weeks later, Miller said Ewert strangled the 15-year-old girl unconscious in his adoptive parents’ Surrey basement, drove her to a drainage ditch, where he left her to die after her head struck the pavement when he dragged her out.
She survived, but was paralyzed for life with severe brain damage.
Ewert was convicted of first-degree murder and attempted murder and spent 40 years in federal prison and was granted day parole in 2025.
Ewert had been attending law school at McGill since September, but news of his studies began circulating in early October. He was subsequently barred from campus.
On Friday, Ewert was remanded into custody after the Correctional Service of Canada suspended his conditional release.
CSC said a warrant was issued for Ewert and that such a warrant may be issued when “there are reasonable grounds to believe that the offender has breached a condition of release or that the risk they present can no longer be safely managed in the community.”
The correctional service said his case is being reviewed in accordance with its post-release decision-making process, which may include further consideration by the Parole Board of Canada.
No further details about the suspension have been released.
Haysom said Ewert interacted online with females who turned out to be AI-generated. She said she spoke to him about what she considered potentially inappropriate language, including comments he wrote such as “you’re hot,” but said she was not aware of anything more disturbing.
The controversy surrounding Ewert has divided students at McGill.
Many students said they were uncomfortable with Ewert attending the university.
“That he even got out of jail is ridiculous, and that he is able to pursue an education and take advantage of the system. It’s baffling,” McGill student Julia Klein said. Another university student Olivia Ho-Foster told Global she feels a lot safer now that Ewert is no longer on campus.
Some students had previously said they believed Ewert should have the right to rehabilitation and an education .
McGill previously told Global News that privacy laws prevented the university from discussing individual student cases, but said the safety and security of students is paramount.
The university also said it would review its admissions processes to ensure a similar situation does not happen again. In a letter to students, the administration said it remained committed to second chances and the power of education to transform lives, while stressing that student safety comes first.
Criminal lawyer Eric Sutton said the prison system is designed to allow people convicted of crimes to eventually pursue a normal life.
“What he did 40 years ago, which was abhorrent, does not necessarily define the person today,” Sutton said.
But Sutton said Ewert would also have been aware of the conditions attached to his release.
“There seems to be a number of people who reported inappropriate behaviour,” he said. “He has to take responsibility for his actions. If that evidence is compelling, he will have to live with the consequences.”
Ewert’s return to custody came shortly after former prosecutor and retired judge Rick Miller, who prosecuted him decades ago, spoke publicly about the case.
“This guy was the most brutal and evil that I dealt with,” Miller told Global News last week.
Miller said he had taken comfort in believing Ewert would remain incarcerated for the rest of his life.
“Ewert had raised a defence in both cases of insanity,” Miller said. “The psychiatrist that the Crown called said that wasn’t true, that he was in fact a psychopathic killer.”
“I always took solace from belief and understanding that he would remain in custody until he died, but then he didn’t,” Miller said.

title: Ebola outbreak: Better to prepare well than to feel sorry later — Dr Agyemang
body: The Member of Parliament (MP) for Abuakwa South, Dr Kingsley Agyemang, has raised concerns about Ghana’s preparedness to contain a possible Ebola outbreak, warning that inadequate border health surveillance and limited public education could leave the country vulnerable. He says the country should be doing more to strengthen its health systems and prepare communities, particularly along major entry points, as concerns grow over the spread of Ebola in parts of Africa. Dr Agyemang, a member of Parliament’s Health Committee, said Ghana’s extensive trade and travel links with Nigeria made the threat one that could not be treated lightly. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Monday, October 26, he questioned the level of preparedness since he first raised concerns about the issue earlier in the year. “We have to prepare well rather than to be very sorry about this whole thing,” he stated. “Preparing for a cross-border infection is something that we all have to be very much concerned about. From where I sit, as I hinted on your network somewhere in March this year, our preparedness towards the Ebola issue has not been that rigorous, and I expect to see more. You should be worried, because you see there’s a lot of cross-border trade between Ghana and Nigeria”. Dr Agyemang said the movement of people and goods between Ghana and Nigeria, including commercial transport and haulage operations, required stronger surveillance and a coordinated public health response. He warned that frequent travel between the two countries could create opportunities for an infectious disease to cross borders, making early detection and prompt intervention critical. “We have a lot of Ghanaians that go to Nigeria every now and then. There’s a huge haulage of transactional trade between Ghana and Nigeria, and it means that we have to be on the lookout for it, and we have to prepare adequately towards that, but from what I see, I do not see that being done properly.” The MP said Ghana should have been better positioned to respond to emerging infectious disease threats, drawing lessons from the disruption caused by the COVID-19 pandemic. “We should have been very much ahead of the game, given the ravaging effect that the COVID-19 had on our healthcare. We have a lot of learning to have learned from.” He argued that the experience of COVID-19 should have prompted sustained investment in disease surveillance, emergency preparedness and the capacity of health facilities to respond to outbreaks. Border communities need attention Dr Agyemang also expressed concern about what he described as inadequate strengthening of health systems at key land entry points. He cited Aflao, Akanu, Paga, Nkwanta and Hamile among the locations where he believed greater attention was needed to improve the country’s readiness to detect and respond to a possible cross-border infection. “This cross-border infection, I mean, if you look at our land travel, I do not see it. For instance, if you take a place like Aflao, Akanu, Paga, Nkwanta, Hamile, and others, I do not see much strengthening of the healthcare system.” He repeated his concern about the lack of visible improvements in preparedness at the borders, saying the country needed to ensure that its health facilities and surveillance arrangements could respond effectively to a potential outbreak. “I do not see much strengthening of the healthcare system.” His concerns highlight the importance of disease surveillance at land borders, where health authorities need to identify suspected cases quickly, assess travellers when indicated and ensure that referral and response systems are in place. However, the MP’s assessment was based on his observations. An official assessment from the relevant health authorities would be needed to establish the current level of preparedness at the named entry points. Public education gap Beyond border surveillance and health infrastructure, Dr Agyemang questioned the apparent lack of public education on Ebola, arguing that people needed clear information on the disease and how to respond to a possible threat. He challenged media organisations and health authorities to intensify awareness campaigns, saying public communication should form part of the country’s preparedness strategy. “I believe that your network is among the 1% networks in Ghana. Have you played any commercial or any health promotion on Ebola? Have you seen anything run? Not yet. All the municipal and district health directories, there does not seem to be any activation or promotion of Ebola.” He said the apparent absence of sustained public education was worrying, given the potential consequences of an outbreak and the importance of helping people recognise symptoms, seek medical care promptly and follow public health guidance. “There has not been much promotion, and it is very concerning. If the whole multimedia has not played a commercial that seeks to promote Ebola or how we should behave, then it is really troubling.” Dr Agyemang’s remarks place the spotlight on the need for timely, accurate public information alongside preparedness measures at ports of entry and health facilities. Public education on Ebola should be based on guidance from health authorities, with clear information on symptoms, transmission, when to seek medical attention and how suspected cases should be managed.

title: DOJ seeking to charge Comey with conspiring to disclose national defense information
body:
The case relates to disclosures published in the New York Times in 2016.
Over the last month, a legal fight has been playing out behind closed doors about the Department of Justice’s ongoing investigation into former FBI Director James Comey over the alleged mishandling of classified information dating back more than a decade ago.
According to newly unsealed court records, prosecutors allege that Comey broke the law by directing FBI staff to leak information to a New York Times reporter for an article published on Oct. 5, 2016, titled “Yahoo Said to Have Aided U.S. Email Surveillance by Adapting Spam Filter.”
“The United States' investigation has uncovered evidence that former FBI Director, James B. Comey, sought to correct misinformation which had appeared in the press by way of Reuters the day before,” prosecutors wrote in their response to Comey’s motion to dismiss earlier this month. “Mr. Comey directed staff to speak to [the New York Times reporter] about specific accuracy concerns related to the Reuters article, and thereby illegally transferred classified information.”
The article in question centered on whether the Department of Justice sought a court order from the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court to force Yahoo to search for communications between members of a foreign terrorist organization. According to court filings, Comey sought to correct claims in a Reuters story published the previous day that Yahoo “secretly built a custom software program to search all of its customers' incoming emails for specific information provided by U.S. intelligence officials.”
Prosecutors with the Department of Justice filed the charges against Comey via what's known as a “criminal information,” which does not require the approval of a grand jury. It was filed under seal on Oct. 5.
Department of Justice lawyers argue that by filing a criminal information within 10 years of the alleged crime, they stopped the clock on the statute of limitations and secured a months-long extension to secure an indictment.
“The Department filed a waiverless criminal information to toll the statute of limitations as it relates to allegations concerning former FBI Director Comey. Filing a criminal information to toll the statute of limitations is a widely recognized practice in federal court and has been approved by multiple Circuit Courts of Appeals. This is an ongoing criminal investigation, and we will not comment further,” a Department of Justice account said on social media.
However, Comey’s lawyers argue that the statute of limitations to bring a criminal information actually expired five years ago and the rule prosecutors cited to secure an extension only applies to indictments. They also argued that the Washington, D.C., Circuit Court has not approved the practice of tolling the statute of limitations via a criminal information.
“Because the default five-year statute of limitations for federal felonies has long since elapsed on the alleged offenses, and the government's information does not meet the express statutory requirement for an extended ten-year limitations period, the information is untimely and must be dismissed,” Comey’s lawyers wrote in their motion to dismiss.
Prosecutors pushed back on that argument, claiming that the federal law in question applies to both indictments and information and arguing that “the case comes down to a syllogism" in federal law.
“Given the seriousness of espionage offenses, and given the deficiencies of the prior statute-of-limitations period in capturing treasonous conduct threatening this nation, Congress intended to lengthen the time to prosecute acts of espionage – not to split that time by instrument,” prosecutors wrote.
Comey also faces federal charges of threatening Trump after a federal grand jury indicted Comey on two charges in April after he posted a picture on his Instagram account of seashells spelling out "8647," which federal prosecutors say constituted a threat against the president's life.
Comey's lawyers are seeking to have that case thrown out. His defense lawyers argued that Trump's repeated calls for Comey's prosecution and criticism of his public statement "leave no doubt as to his genuine animus" and demonstrate that the case against him for allegedly threatening to kill Trump by posting photos of seashells on a beach is vindictive.
"The ensuing indictment is not based on a good faith application of the law to the facts; instead, it effectuates a yearslong campaign by the President to use the criminal process to punish Mr. Comey for his protected speech and because of the President's deep-seated animosity," Comey's lawyers wrote.

title: Tambuwal, Dan’iya Mourn Olugbemi
body: Onuminya Innocent in Sokoto Former Governor of Sokoto State and Distinguished Senator Aminu Waziri Tambuwal, CFR, and the Governorship Candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Sokoto State, Hon. Manir Muhammad Dan’iya, have expressed deep sorrow over the death of veteran journalist and prolific writer, Mr. Adeniyi Olugbemi, describing his passing as a painful loss to the journalism profession and the media community in Sokoto State and Nigeria at large. In separate condolence messages, both leaders described Olugbemi as a dedicated journalist whose commitment to professional ethics, fearless reporting and public service earned him respect among colleagues and within the wider media industry. Senator Tambuwal said: “The death of Adeniyi Olugbemi is a painful loss to the journalism profession and the entire media community. He was a dedicated professional whose commitment to truth, responsible reporting and public accountability made meaningful contributions to our society.” He noted that Olugbemi’s passing had created a significant vacuum in the media community, particularly among journalists in Sokoto State, where he spent years reporting on public affairs and contributing to informed public discourse. “Through his pen, Olugbemi gave voice to the voiceless, brought important issues to public attention and upheld the values of journalism as a critical pillar of democracy. His contributions will remain part of the enduring legacy he leaves behind,” Tambuwal added. On his part, Dan’iya, in a statement signed by his Media Aide, Aminu Abdullahi, paid tribute to the late Olugbemi for his professionalism, commitment to ethical journalism and dedication to public service, describing him as a respected media practitioner whose fearless reporting strengthened the role of the media in a democratic society. Both leaders acknowledged Olugbemi’s extensive career across several media organisations, including Tribune The Sun The Punch Leadership Newspaper and The Triumph Publishing Company, where he demonstrated a commitment to responsible journalism and the public interest. They also acknowledged his contribution through The Guild Magazine, an independent publication he founded, through which he continued to contribute to journalism, mentor younger reporters and promote responsible media practice. Dan’iya observed that Olugbemi’s work went beyond reporting events, as his writings helped draw attention to important societal issues and gave visibility to the concerns of ordinary citizens, particularly the less privileged, at a time when credible journalism remains essential to democratic governance and national development. Both leaders extended heartfelt condolences to the immediate family of the deceased, the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ), particularly the Correspondents’ Chapel in Sokoto State, his colleagues, associates and the entire media community, praying God to grant them strength and fortitude to bear the irreparable loss. “May Almighty God forgive his shortcomings, accept his good deeds and grant him eternal rest. May He comfort his family, friends, colleagues and all those mourning his passing. Adeniyi Olugbemi may be gone, but his contributions to journalism and public service will remain part of the legacy he leaves behind,” Dan’iya said, as Tambuwal urged journalists to sustain the values of integrity, courage, fairness and public service that defined Olugbemi’s professional calling.

title: De la Fuente Wins Men’s Ballon d’Or Coach Of The Year
body: Luis de la Fuente won the Ballon d’Or for men’s coach of the year on Monday after leading Spain to World Cup glory. “Teamwork makes us invincible. This is a great honour,” de la Fuente said after collecting the award at a ceremony in London. “The secret is to work with very generous players that put the team first. We’ve got such an amazing pool of talent, the best in the world, so as a coach I have such a great amount of talent to work with. So this is their success,” he added. In an age of coaches who were previously star players, 65-year-old de la Fuente stands out as a technician who worked his way up through the national coaching ranks in Spain. After a solid career as a player led to an undistinguished stint in club coaching, he was flicking through the sports pages in 2013 when he saw an advert placed by the Spanish Football Federation for a youth team coach. He applied, got the job with Spain’s Under-19s, and 13 years later some of the players from that squad were part of the teams he has led to victory in the Nations League, Euro 2024 and then the World Cup. De la Fuente insisted from the start in the United States this summer that he had the strongest squad in the tournament, even when they stumbled to a goalless draw against World Cup debutants Cape Verde in their opening match. They built momentum with each match and dispatched one of the pre-tournament favourites, France, in a clinical 2-0 win in the semi-final. In a tight final against Lionel Messi’s Argentina in New Jersey, de la Fuente’s men kept their cool in the face of muscular tactics from the opposition and Ferran Torres smashed in the winning goal for a 1-0 victory. “This is recognition for a job very well done over many years,” de la Fuente told AFP. “I believe Spanish football, both in terms of coaching and the game itself, serves as an example of excellent youth development, which ultimately paves the way for future success.” The women’s coaching award also went to a Spaniard as Barcelona’s Pere Romeu was rewarded for masterminding a season in which they won the Spanish league, Spanish cup, Super Cup and Champions League. AFP The post De la Fuente Wins Men’s Ballon d’Or Coach Of The Year appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Airport temperature checks offer comfort but won’t catch Ebola – Prof Amuasi
body: Prof John Amuasi, Global Health Lead at the KCCR, warned that airport temperature checks will not catch Ebola cases. He wants Ghana to prioritise accurate passenger records and reliable ways to trace arrivals. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Monday, he said visible screening measures offer reassurance but do little to detect infected travellers. “Temperature checks, use of alcohol and rubs, all these things are nice. They give people some level of confidence, but the reality is that they are not going to catch Ebola cases for you,” he said. Prof Amuasi said people visibly sick with Ebola symptoms were unlikely to board aircraft. That limits what officials can detect when passengers arrive. “What is needed is actually the ability to test, and this doesn’t exist as it stands right now. We can’t be doing PCR tests for everyone coming in.” His warning comes as Nigeria and Kenya respond to Ebola cases. Nigeria confirmed an imported case in Abuja on October 20. The patient arrived from Uganda on October 3 and developed symptoms four days later. By October 24, authorities had identified 53 contacts for follow-up, according to the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention. Kenya had recorded nine confirmed cases, including two deaths, by October 25. All were linked to its first imported case. Uganda has also reported cases, where the outbreak has ended, according to the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control. For Prof Amuasi, Ghana’s priority should be collecting information that allows authorities to find travellers if they later develop symptoms. “So for me, the single most important thing is being able to collect as accurate data as possible on every single person who comes off the plane in this country, making sure that the phone numbers they submit are accurate and finding a way of verifying it.” He also called for ways to locate arrivals when necessary. Travellers should know which designated facilities to visit and which telephone lines to use if symptoms develop. He said education should focus on people entering the country. Authorities must ensure they understand how to report illness after leaving the airport. “But for the other visual things we see, like alcohol rub and the temperature text, they are nice. They help people to be more confident and comfortable. But at this stage right now, they don’t count very much,” he stated.

title: PDP speaks on Tinubu’s claim opposition caused hunger, poverty
body:
The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has rejected President Bola Tinubu’s claim that opposition politicians were responsible for the hunger and poverty confronting Nigerians, accusing the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of attempting to evade responsibility for the country’s economic challenges.
The party, said blaming the opposition would not address the rising cost of living, food insecurity, unemployment and other difficulties facing Nigerians.
Jungudo Mohammed, the PDP national publicity secretary, stated this in a statement on Monday in response to remarks by Mr Tinubu and the ruling party.
“The PDP considers these statements as attempts to evade responsibility and divert public attention from the pressing challenges facing the country under the APC-led administration,” he said.
Mr Mohammed urged the APC to focus on addressing the country’s economic challenges rather than engaging in political blame games.
“Rather than engaging in political blame games, the APC should explain what it intends to do to make food affordable, support farmers, strengthen local food production, create jobs, improve security, fight corruption, improve electricity supply, reduce transportation costs, and restore the purchasing power of ordinary Nigerians, among other pressing concerns,” he said.
At the flag-off of his re-election campaign in Kaduna on Saturday, Mr Tinubu accused opposition politicians of creating hunger and poverty in the country, insisting that his administration was working to eradicate both.
“I have heard the opposition talking about hunger and poverty. Who created them? They did. They created the hunger; they created the poverty. We are trying to eradicate it,” the president said.
Earlier on Monday, the APC National Publicity Secretary, Felix Morka, made a similar argument, saying the foundations of Nigeria’s current poverty crisis were laid before Mr Tinubu assumed office in May 2023.
Mr Morka argued that former leaders should not portray the economic hardship as a problem that emerged under the current administration.
In his response, Mr Mohammed acknowledged some of the achievements of Mr Tinubu’s administration but rejected the arguement that the PDP’s 16 years in power provided a blanket justification for the current government’s shortcomings.
“While the PDP acknowledges some of the achievements recorded by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s administration, where applicable, we firmly reject any attempt to use the PDP’s sixteen years in government as a blanket justification for the shortcomings of the present administration,” he said.
He added that acknowledging the administration’s achievements should not be interpreted as an endorsement of all its policies or an acceptance of attempts to transfer responsibility for current economic difficulties to previous PDP-led governments.
Mr Mohammed said that after more than a decade in power, the APC should account for its performance and explain the concrete measures it was taking to improve Nigerians’ living conditions.
“After more than APC’s 10 years in office, Nigerians deserve answers, not excuses. The APC must tell Nigerians what it has achieved, outline the concrete measures it is taking to address the country’s present-day challenges, and demonstrate its commitment to improving the welfare of citizens rather than continually dragging the PDP into its own shortcomings,” he said.
He argued that although past administrations could provide historical context for the country’s economic difficulties, they could not serve as a permanent shield against accountability.
“The PDP maintains that the economic challenges confronting Nigeria cannot be resolved by repeatedly blaming previous PDP-led administrations. While historical circumstances may provide context, they cannot serve as a permanent shield against accountability. Every administration must be judged by its policies, decisions, achievements, and, most importantly, the living conditions of the people it governs,” he added.
The PDP spokesperson also defended the party’s record during its 16 years in power, from 1999 to 2015, claiming that Nigerians enjoyed a better standard of living and security under previous PDP administrations.
“Nigerians remember the standard of living and the security situation under previous PDP administrations. Today, citizens are demanding practical solutions, affordable food, economic stability, and improved security, not endless political arguments and blame shifting,” he said.
Mr Mohammed expressed confidence that Nigerians would judge political parties by their records, policies and commitment to public welfare.
He also said the desire among Nigerians for a return to PDP leadership reflected their demand for better governance, improved living conditions and a more secure country.
The PDP spokesperson urged the president and the ruling party to stop blaming opposition parties and take responsibility for the country’s challenges.
“Our message to the APC is simple: stop the blame game and start taking responsibility. Nigerians deserve solutions, not excuses. The government in power must address the country’s challenges through concrete, measurable, and sustainable actions that will bring meaningful relief to citizens.
“The PDP is not responsible for the hunger Nigerians are experiencing today. The APC must own its record, address the nation’s challenges, and deliver on its promises to Nigerians. The government in power must answer for its stewardship and present a credible path towards economic recovery, food security, and a better standard of living for all Nigerians,” he added.

title: Ballon d’or 2026: Harry Kane wins ahead of Kylian Mbappé, Lamine Yamal; first Englishman in 25 years
body: Harry Kane has become the first Englishman to win the Ballon d’Or in 25 years after beating Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal to the award in London on Monday. Kane scored 73 goals in a breathtaking 2025-26 season across all competitions for Bayern Munich and England, enough to earn him the European Golden Shoe award. In Germany last season, Kane inspired Bayern to a Bundesliga and DFB Pokal double. His 14 goals in the Champions League last season — where Bayern fell at the semifinal stage to eventual winners Paris Saint-Germain — was bettered only by Kylian Mbappe of Real Madrid(15). He captained England at the World Cup where they finished third, their best result since winning it in 1966, scoring six goals along the way including two late strikes to rescue his side against DR Congo and a strike against Mexico at the Azteca in the round of 16. This season, Kane equalled a record held by Peter Shilton since 1990 for the most England caps after a 125th appearance. Already his country’s leading scorer, he has extended that tally to 91 goals.

title: Tsitsipas Pulls Out of Basel Amid Shoulder Concerns
body: Stefanos Tsitsipas has pulled out of the Swiss Indoors in a Tsitsipas Basel withdrawal that raises fresh questions over his right shoulder. The Greek star withdrew from the ATP 500 event in Switzerland on Sunday 25 October. Its main draw began a day later. Tsitsipas had been drawn to face American Taylor Fritz, the world No. 12, in the first round. A lucky loser will now take his place in the draw. What led to the Tsitsipas Basel withdrawal Tsitsipas arrived in Switzerland after a strong week at the Almaty Open in Kazakhstan, where he reached the semi-finals. His campaign there began with an opening win over Aleksandar Kovacevic . He then beat Australian James Duckworth 6-3, 6-4 in the quarter-finals. However, he lost his semi-final on Saturday 24 October to Georgian qualifier Nikoloz Basilashvili 6-4, 6-7(5), 6-3. Towards the end of that match, Tsitsipas appeared to be struggling with discomfort in his right shoulder. That sparked concern ahead of his next events. Still, there has been no official confirmation that the shoulder problem caused him to pull out. As a result, it remains unclear whether the discomfort he showed in Almaty is linked to his decision to skip the Swiss tournament. Paris Masters next Next on the 28-year-old’s schedule is the Paris Masters, which runs from 31 October to 8 November . It is one of the biggest events of the late season. After the Tsitsipas Basel withdrawal, his participation in the French capital is now the key question. The state of his right shoulder is likely to shape his plans for the rest of the year. His Almaty run produced only his second semi-final of the season and his first on hard courts since February 2025. It followed a quarter-final run in Shanghai . No reason has yet been given for the Tsitsipas Basel withdrawal.
