title: Greece Plans Facelift for Dozens of Athens Rail Stations
body: Greece will renovate dozens of Athens rail stations on the suburban railway and Metro Line 1, making them cleaner and more accessible, Alternate Minister George Kotsiras said. The Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport wants a cleaner, more functional network. Alongside frequent and reliable services, it aims to make public transport more attractive. “We are seeking an overall transformation of urban rail stations across the Athens metropolitan area,” Kotsiras said. “Our aim is to ensure that the hundreds of thousands of people who pass through Metro and suburban railway stations every day can travel in comfort and dignity,” he added. Railways of Greece, Hellenic Rail Estate and STASY, the Athens urban rail operator, are working together on the plans. National and European funds will pay for them. Which Athens rail stations come first First, more than 20 suburban stations in Attica will receive improvements. Renovation also continues at stations on all three Athens Metro lines. A tender to renovate the Ano Liosia, Metamorfosi, Iraklio, Kifisias and Pentelis suburban stations is nearing completion. After the contract is signed, work should take four months. Once work starts, crews will waterproof canopies, repair floors and steps, remove graffiti and fix seating. They will also upgrade lighting and electronic passenger displays. Separately, Railways of Greece is upgrading 12 stations, nine of them in Attica, and expects to finish in spring 2027. Those nine are Sfendali, Avlonas, Afidnes, Piraeus, Athens (Larissa Station), Agios Stefanos, Acharnes, Agios Ioannis Rentis and Agioi Anargyroi. Cleaning and graffiti removal are under way at three more Athens rail stations: Neratziotissa, Acharnes Railway Centre and Rouf. Authorities also plan a full renovation of Neratziotissa, a key interchange with Metro Line 1. Accessibility on Metro Line 1 On the former ISAP line, crews have finished work at Omonia, Victoria, Petralona and Kifisia. Monastiraki is now under renovation, and the first fully refurbished train is already in service. To improve access, all lifts and escalators at Line 1 Athens rail stations are due for replacement. Accessibility works at Kallithea start shortly and should take 12 months. Kallithea will then serve as a model for the remaining 23 Line 1 stations. Those works are expected to draw on the Social Climate Fund, an EU fund set up to help vulnerable households . Digital mapping and navigation tools for people with disabilities will follow across the Athens and Thessaloniki Metro networks. In addition, 33 railway stations nationwide will get accessibility upgrades. The plans add to wider rail investment, including Thessaloniki’s own suburban line and remote traffic management on the main line . Taken together, the works aim to make Athens rail stations easier for every passenger to use. title: Ballon d’Or 2026: Harry Kane wins 2026 Men’s Striker of the Year award
body: Bayern Munich and England striker Harry Kane has won the 2026 Men’s Striker of the Year award at the Ballon d’Or ceremony in London after an outstanding goalscoring campaign for club and country. The England captain received the honour on Monday, recognising his prolific performances during the 2025/26 season. Kane entered the ceremony as one of the leading contenders for the men’s Ballon d’Or after establishing himself as one of the most productive forwards in world football. Kane scored 73 goals and made 8 assists for club and country in 65 appearances in the 2025/26 season. The 33-year-old has continued to lead Bayern Munich’s attack since joining the German champions from Tottenham Hotspur in August 2023. His arrival in the Bundesliga marked a new chapter in his career after spending nearly two decades in English football, including his rise to become Tottenham’s all-time leading goalscorer. Kane has also maintained his importance to England, where he serves as captain and remains a central figure in the national team’s pursuit of major international honours. His latest individual recognition comes as he challenges for the biggest prize of the evening, the men’s Ballon d’Or. Kane emerged as a leading candidate following a season in which his goalscoring record and influence for Bayern made him one of the favourites for the award. The striker’s achievement adds another milestone to a career defined by remarkable consistency, intelligent movement and clinical finishing.

title: Greek FM Gerapetritis Faces Libya Criticism Over Haftar Policy
body: In a pointed Gerapetritis Libya criticism, news site Lawandorder.gr has accused Foreign Minister Giorgos Gerapetritis of letting eastern Libya drift towards Turkey before a key maritime vote. Its column appeared on Thursday 22 October under a pen name. It followed the decision by Libya’s eastern-based House of Representatives on 20 October to approve the 2019 Turkish–Libyan memorandum . According to the outlet, the vote overturned the idea that eastern Libya could act as a barrier to Ankara. It called the result “a serious blow” to Greek strategy and blamed the Foreign Ministry and Gerapetritis personally. In its view, a country’s foreign policy rests on its ability “to build alliances, influence developments and prevent faits accomplis” . Legal assurances alone do not meet that test, it wrote. Haftar and the Gerapetritis Libya criticism At the heart of the Gerapetritis Libya criticism is the eastern camp of Field Marshal Khalifa Haftar. Greece had invested politically in contacts with eastern Libya, the outlet noted. Previously, as foreign minister until 2023, Nikos Dendias built ties with Haftar and kept channels open, it added. Now the parliament linked to the Haftar camp has backed the deal Athens rejects . His son, Saddam Haftar, also welcomed the decisions as a step beyond old differences, Lawandorder.gr wrote. For the outlet, Ankara has widened its influence where it once met strong resistance. “What did Athens do to keep its influence in eastern Libya active?” it asked. However, the Gerapetritis Libya criticism cannot be brushed aside by citing international law, it argued. Diplomacy “requires constant presence, a plan and results” , it wrote. Samaras and the minister’s reply The Gerapetritis Libya criticism echoes former prime minister Antonis Samaras, who attacked Gerapetritis and Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis on 20 October. Events in Libya “irreparably expose” the minister, “who assured us of the exact opposite” , Samaras said. He also said Mitsotakis agreed with the minister on everything “instead of having already dismissed him” . In a radio interview the next day, Gerapetritis hit back. Samaras was driven by “a very deep intolerance” and “political hostility” , he said. “We have no national defeat,” the minister added. Preventing the ratification “was not in Greece’s hands” , he said. Officially, Athens holds that the memorandum is “illegal, null and void” and has no legal effect. Gerapetritis has also said Greece has the means to block its use in practice. Still, Lawandorder.gr said the legal argument and the political reality on the ground differ. In its view, the clash with Samaras also shifted the debate from substance to a personal feud. Instead, the outlet called for a wider strategy in Greek foreign policy. That would mean contacts with all Libyan sides, coordination with Egypt and Cyprus, and pressure through the European Union. Finally, the Gerapetritis Libya criticism closes on a warning. “In foreign policy, what counts is not only what you say you do not recognise, but what you allow others to achieve,” it said. title: Trump’s media bans ‘deprive the public’, press freedom groups argue
body: Press freedom groups are suing the Trump administration over its efforts to block mainstream US news outlets from covering the White House, according to court filings. The six plaintiffs, including scholars, advocates, and journalists, argue that media bans issued by the White House violate the First Amendment of the US Constitution, which protects the press and freedom of speech. Their lawsuit follows a separate legal challenge by CNN, Politico, and MSNOW over the White House’s attempts to revoke or restrict their press access. The Knight First Amendment Institute and Yale Law School’s Media and Information Access Clinic filed the legal case on the plaintiffs’ behalf. The six plaintiffs have asked a New York federal court to declare that the White House’s selective media bans violate the First Amendment and to block the administration from enforcing them. In court filings, the plaintiffs allege they can no longer do their work without access to information delivered by the White House press. The White House policy, they argue, “deprives the public” of reporting and forces journalists covering Donald Trump “to account for the possibility that a critical or ill-advised word about the president may result in their access being summarily restricted or revoked”. Such a ban has a “distorting effect” on White House coverage, the court filing argues. The BBC has asked the White House for comment. The White House has, however, continued to selectively bar journalists, which news organisations in the US argue violates their press freedom protections. CNN, for instance, has threatened further legal action as its reporters continue to be denied access aboard Air Force One. Last week, the White House banned a correspondent from the Independent from covering the president’s trip to Iowa after Trump berated the reporter from the UK news outlet during a news conference. In his second term, Trump has also moved to bring conservative bloggers, influencers and other “new media” figures into the press room, arguing it is necessary to provide diverse perspectives in White House coverage. In February, the White House announced it was taking control of the press pool – the small group of journalists that has access to the president on any given day – which for more than a century had been managed by the White House Correspondents’ Association. That same month, the White House moved to bar Associated Press journalists from spaces with limited access, such as the Oval Office or Air Force One, because the outlet used the term “Gulf of Mexico” rather than “Gulf of America”. AP filed a lawsuit, and the case remains ongoing. Trump last week confirmed he was considering moving the entire press corps from the White House grounds after reports said he was contemplating rebuilding a swimming pool beneath the James S. Brady briefing room. “I am thinking about moving the press, and putting them in a different location,” he wrote on Truth Social. “I will use that location for very badly needed space.” The lawsuit did not ask a judge to award financial damages, only to require the defendants to cover their legal fees if they win. Since Donald Trump returned to office in January 2025, the White House has engaged in a standoff with many longstanding US media outlets, which the president has frequently accused of publishing “fake news”. Last month, it banned reporters from CNN, Politico and MSNOW from the White House, leading several other media organisations to temporarily suspend their pooled coverage of the president in protest. The affected news outlets sued, arguing the White House illegally discriminated against them because of their coverage. A federal judge later ordered the White House to restore the impacted journalists’ credentials while the lawsuit plays out. The reporters later said they were allowed back into the White House complex.

title: Abia PDP guber candidate, Anosike, vows common facility centre for Aba leather, garment clusters
body: The Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, governorship candidate for the 2027 election in Abia State, Dr. Kelechi Anosike, has promised to build a world-class Common Facility Centre, CFC, in Aba to boost the leather and garment clusters. Anosike made the promise in Aba when he met with representatives of the Leather and Garment Clusters, comprising over 200,000 members, as part of his ongoing campaign tour of the commercial city. He said the proposed CFC would be a solar-powered industrial and technical hub equipped with world-class machines to enable Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs), especially young tailors, shoemakers and garment makers who lack capital, to produce international-standard finished products. According to him, the model would replicate what the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency of Nigeria, SMEDAN, did in Abuja, where tailors register their materials, pay a token of N5,000, now N10,000, to access all machines in the centre to finish jobs for their customers and keep the proceeds. “I said we will set up a centre, solar powered, with all kinds of world best machines. Like what SMEDAN did in Abuja, like the tailoring aspect,” he said. The PDP candidate recalled that a similar facility built in Aba in 2008 by the United Nations Industrial Development Organisation, UNIDO, in partnership with the Federal and Abia State Governments was abused, vandalised and eventually abandoned by successive administrations, thereby defeating its empowerment purpose. He said his administration would bring back the concept as a deliberate empowerment strategy, stressing that apart from the CFC, his government would establish a Traders Microfinance Bank to provide interest-free loans and grants to traders and clusters to scale up production and reduce dependence on imports. Anosike argued that while white-collar jobs are limited, thousands of SMEs can be created if government partners with traders to produce locally made goods for which Nigeria spends over $10 to $20 billion annually importing, despite having the raw materials in abundance. Anchoring his campaign on what he termed “productive welfarism,” the governorship hopeful said his mission is encapsulated in the slogan ‘Aruo Uzo, Aruo Afo’ (build roads, build people), insisting that infrastructure is meaningless if the people are not alive and economically empowered to use it. “I’m a welfarist and the welfarism is not to give you handouts, it’s to empower you to support the state. It is called productive welfarism,” he declared. He criticised what he described as anti-people taxes on the poor, vowing to abolish them, and lamented that despite the increase in federal allocation to Abia from about N3.5 billion to about N40 billion monthly, there was “zero welfare” to cushion the effects of subsidy removal. In his remarks, the National Secretary of Aba Leather and Garment Clusters, Mr. Ken Anyanwu, said the delegation came to introduce the over 200,000-member body to the candidate and to seek a more detailed engagement on how to upgrade the clusters to world-class status. Anyanwu, who doubled as Cooperative President, said Aba leather and garment products are number one in Africa, lamenting that while other countries are wooing Aba artisans, successive Abia governments have neglected them. According to him, SMEs remain the pivot of economic growth and should be prioritised by any people-oriented government, pledging the support of the members. He stressed that Anosike’s manifesto holds key for the clusters. Those at the event include, Abia PDP Deputy Chairman and Senatorial candidate for Abia South, Chinyere Onuoha, Aba North/Aba South Federal Constituency, Bob Ajuzieogu, the Aba Centra House of Assembly candidate, Anastasia Uchenna and Hon. Daniel Ajunwa (Obere Agu), House of Assembly candidates for State constituencies in Abia. They all urged the people of Abia to vote for PDP in 2026.. title: 'Complete fabrication': Netanyahu, Katz deny plans to fire IDF chief Zamir ahead of election
body: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Office and Defense Minister Israel Katz denied reported plans to dismiss IDF Chief of Staff Lt.-Gen. Eyal Zamir on Monday, amid reports of tensions between the political and military leadership over Iran, a day before the Knesset elections.Katz condemned the reports, claiming they were part of an attempt to harm the Likud Party ahead of Tuesday's elections."The reports published this evening about an intention to dismiss Chief of Staff Zamir are a complete fabrication and an outright lie," the defense minister said.According to Katz, the reports were part of a series of security-related claims circulated over the past 24 hours that he alleged were intended to damage Likud's election chances.Katz stressed that he had personally recommended Zamir's appointment as IDF chief of staff and that their cooperation would continue."We are working together for the security of the State of Israel, with unprecedented historic achievements, and that is how I intend to continue acting in the future," he said.Netanyahu's Office also rejected the reports concerning relations between the prime minister and the IDF chief of staff, issuing a brief response: "Complete fake news from beginning to end."Netanyahu personally denied the reports in a post on X/Twitter on Monday, writing: "More fake news from the panic-mongering Channels 12 and 13 on the eve of the elections: I do not intend to dismiss the chief of staff, and we will continue working together for Israel's security. I do intend to eliminate the Iranian nuclear threat once and for all. I will do so together with my friend President Trump, and we will also sign peace agreements with additional countries."עוד פייק ניוז בערוצי התבהלה 12 ו-13 בערב הבחירות: אני לא מתכוון לפטר את הרמטכ״ל, ונמשיך לעבוד יחד לביטחון ישראל. אני כן מתכוון להסיר סופית את האיום הגרעיני האיראני. אעשה זאת יחד עם ידידי הנשיא טראמפ, ונחתום גם על הסכמי שלום עם מדינות נוספות— Benjamin Netanyahu - בנימין נתניהו (@netanyahu) October 26, 2026Eisenkot: Zamir will remain in office, Netanyahu will leave after electionsFormer IDF chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot, chairman of the Yashar Party, declared on Monday that Zamir would leave his position only when the law stipulates, while Netanyahu would leave office after the elections and the formation of the next government."Tomorrow, the people of Israel will elect a prime minister whose considerations will always be for the good of Israel, who will never act out of political interests at the expense of Israel's security and IDF soldiers," Eisenkot said.Reports of Netanyahu-Zamir confrontation over IranThe denials follow reports over the past 24 hours of unusual tensions between Netanyahu and Zamir concerning the possibility of an Israeli strike on Iran.Channel 12 News reported on Sunday evening that Netanyahu and Zamir had clashed over the Iranian issue, while defense officials sought to emphasize that military decisions were made solely on professional grounds.The IDF Spokesperson's Unit addressed the reports on Monday, stating that the military was on high alert across all fronts.The statement stressed that the IDF's operational activities and guiding considerations were based solely on security, professional, and national interests, and that any portrayal suggesting otherwise was misleading.Earlier, Katz also denied claims of disagreements between the political leadership and the military over Iran.According to Katz, coordination between the prime minister, the defense minister, and the IDF was complete, and there had been no intention to initiate an Israeli attack on Iran before the elections.However, he made clear that Israel would respond forcefully if attacked by Iran.The statements came one day before polling stations were set to open, with relations between the political leadership and the military's top brass at the center of public debate.

title: Zalameda’s promises as chief justice bet: Solve case delays, more benefits for court staff
body: MANILA, Philippines – Associate Justice Rodil Zalameda says he knows the plight of ordinary employees so he intends to focus on their welfare – among other innovations in the judiciary – should he become the country’s 28th Chief Justice. “After passing the Bar in 1988, I began my career as a branch clerk of court of the Regional Trial Court of Makati. This gave me an appreciation of the challenges faced by our court employees,” Zalameda said during his public interview with the Judicial and Bar Council (JBC) on Monday, October 26. “The Judiciary is often spoken of in terms of judges, justices, decisions, and jurisprudence. But behind every decision are countless employees who perform their duties quietly and without recognition. I understand their challenges because I have been where many of them are,” he said. Zalameda is one of the five candidates for chief justice, vying to replace Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo, who will retire on November 6. The aspiring chief justice currently holds seat No. 7 at the High Court. After serving for years at the Court of Appeals, he was appointed to the Supreme Court (SC) by then-president Rodrigo Duterte in August 2019. After the public interviews, the JBC will send a short list of nominees to President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., who has the power to make the appointment. If chosen, Zalameda will serve for around seven years or until 2033. During the Monday interview, JBC members asked Zalameda how much would be a workable budget for him if he is ever appointed as chief justice. He said any increase in the Court’s budget “will be greatly appreciated.” They then asked him, if given additional funds, what would be his top priorities. Zalameda said he will focus on building additional courthouses to address delays in dispensing cases, using technology for more efficient processes, and increasing the benefits of judiciary employees. “The judiciary must also confront delays that continue to burden litigants. I recognize that not all cases require the same amount of time and effort. We must consider their nature and complexity, the number of parties and witnesses, the volume of evidence, the length of proceedings, and the issues that must be resolved,” he said. Zalameda also explained that there’s a discrepancy between the benefits that appellate court employees and lower courts employees receive. He said a study should be done to look into this disparity. “I just want to cite an example: There is a perennial problem here with respect to the discrepancy between the allowances given to the appellate court employees and those in the trial courts. There was a time that the difference was I think more than 50%,” the aspiring chief magistrate explained. “I think we have to review this and if we could get some funds…to supplement their budget for their allowances. That would be a good idea,” he added. What type of justice will Zalameda be? Zalameda said he strongly believes in separation of powers, and that each branch of the government — executive, legislature, and the judiciary — is by bound by its own constitutional mandate. He explained that he is a follower of the Constitution and always follows his conscience. For him, a chief justice must be a servant of the judiciary and should work with litigants, lawyers, court staff, judges, and with fellow justices. “The role is to create an environment where problems are heard, solutions are developed, good ideas are supported, and people are given the tools to fulfill their responsibilities. Leadership is ultimately about service, accountability, and enabling others to succeed,” Zalameda said. As the chief magistrate, Zalameda said he also intends to lead with collegiality. He said he will respect his fellow members of the SC en banc. “Collegiality does not mean the absence of disagreement. It means we can disagree without becoming disagreeable, and remain, after the debate and the vote, members of one Court serving one Constitution. This is the kind of collegiality I hope to strengthen – one built on mutual respect, professional trust, and a shared commitment to the institution,” said Zalameda. More tangible changes To address case backlogs, apart from building more courthouses, Zalameda said there should be equal distribution of cases among judges based not on quantity, but based on the nature of the case, their complexity, and the parties involved. The justice said he will launch a study to address this matter. The Office of the Court Administrator could be the office assigned for this, he explained. Zalameda said he also believes that courts should be more transparent to minimize graft and corruption. “We have to minimize also graft and corruption and the trust of the court should be established so that we can have later on high respect for the nation,” he explained. “I think we have to gain the trust of the people in the domain of justice. I want Supreme Court which is being seen by the people as their last bastion.” He also explained that his judicial philosophy — the principle that guides him in deciding cases — is legal pragmatism. Zalameda said he believes that decisions should have real-life impact. “In this principle of first prudence, you use the law as a tool to decide on cases, but we have to consider the realities, the cause and effect, that may result, and the effect on the people with respect to the decision which we made,” he said. – Rappler.com

title: Libya-Turkey maritime deal threatens Mediterranean stability, six parties warn
body: Greece, Bahrain, Cyprus, Egypt, the EU and the UAE warned on Monday that Libya’s approval of a disputed maritime agreement with Turkey threatens regional stability in the Mediterranean. Delivering the joint statement to reporters in New York, Greek Foreign Minister George Gerapetritis said the vote by Libya’s eastern-based House of Representatives to ratify the 2019 preliminary agreement “raises serious concerns for regional security and stability”. “The so-called Turkish Libyan Memorandum...disregards geographical realities and the maritime entitlements of all relevant coastal States, including the maritime entitlements of islands under UNCLOS,” Mr Gerapetritis said, referring to the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea. The agreement, signed by Ankara and the internationally recognised Libyan government in Tripoli, western Libya, establishes a maritime corridor between Turkey's southern coast and Libya's northern coast, allowing the two countries to assert economic rights over potentially lucrative oil and gas reserves beneath the Mediterranean seabed. The deal has long been a source of friction with Greece, Egypt and Cyprus, which argue that it disregards their maritime rights and violates international law. "Accepting bilateral arrangements that disregard the applicable rules and principles of the law of the sea would set a dangerous precedent, undermining the international legal order," the diplomat added. Libya's UN envoy, Taher El Sonni, defended the agreement, telling The National it was a "sovereign decision" and that countries challenging it should pursue legal avenues, including the International Court of Justice. “We see that this is a legitimate agreement, but we respect also all views of all neighbouring countries, and we try to have bilateral discussions with them,” he said. title: Greece warns Libya’s Turkey maritime deal threatens Mediterranean stability
body: Greece warned on Monday that Libya’s approval of a disputed maritime agreement with Turkey threatens stability in the Mediterranean. Greece's Foreign Minister, George Gerapetritis, told reporters in New York that the vote by Libya’s House of Representatives in the country's east to finally ratify a 2019 preliminary agreement with Turkey “raises serious concerns for regional security and stability". "It also highlights a broader challenge to the international legal order, ensuring that arbitrary bilateral arrangements do not undermine established rules of international law or prejudice the rights of other states," he added. Mr Gerapetritis delivered the joint statement with Bahrain, Cyprus, Egypt, the EU and the UAE. The agreement, signed by Ankara and the internationally recognised Libyan government in Tripoli, western Libya, establishes a maritime corridor between Turkey's southern coast and Libya's northern coast, allowing the two countries to assert economic rights over potentially lucrative oil and gas reserves beneath the Mediterranean seabed. Libya’s rival eastern administration, led by military commander Khalifa Haftar, opposed the agreement for years. At the time it was signed, Libya was in the middle of a civil war. Turkey has since strengthened ties with Mr Haftar and his allies while maintaining its close relationship with the government in Tripoli, allowing Ankara to work with both sides of Libya’s divided leadership. The agreement, however, has fuelled tension with neighbouring countries, particularly Greece, Egypt and Cyprus. Mr Gerapetritis said the deal ignores the maritime entitlements of Greek islands protected under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea, which can be used to arbitrate territorial disputes. The agreement could also complicate plans for the EastMed pipeline, a proposed project to transport natural gas from Israel and Cyprus through Greece to Europe. The pipeline is intended to strengthen Europe's energy security, but its planned route crosses waters claimed by Turkey and Libya under the deal. "Turkey and Libya have no adjacent coasts and no opposite coasts and, therefore, no common maritime boundaries," a diplomat, who asked not to be identified due to the sensitivity of the matter, told The National. "The memorandum is null and void and produces no legal consequences. Equally, its purported ratification too is contrary to international law and of no legal effect." "Accepting bilateral arrangements that disregard the applicable rules and principles of the law of the sea would set a dangerous precedent, undermining the international legal order," the diplomat added. Libya's UN envoy, Taher El Sonni, defended the agreement, telling The National it was a "sovereign decision" and that countries challenging it should pursue legal avenues, including the International Court of Justice. “We see that this is a legitimate agreement, but we respect also all views of all neighbouring countries, and we try to have bilateral discussions with them,” he said. The EU has also criticised the agreement, saying it violates the sovereign rights of third countries and does not comply with the law of the sea. UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres told reporters on Monday in Cairo that violations of international law governing maritime agreements were unacceptable, and agreements that were incompatible with the convention should not be recognised or accepted. Egypt, a long-time supporter of the eastern Libyan authorities, also rejected the deal last week, stating that the deal was null and void and would have no legal effect in Cairo. Cairo and Athens had signed their own maritime delimitation agreement in August 2020. title: Footage Shows Iranian Missile Breaking Through Three Rounds of Patriot Air Defence Fire to Strike Key Base
body: Previously unseen footage circulating online has shown an Iranian ballistic missile striking at Al Dhafra Air Base near Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, and evading at least three surface-to-air interceptors launched by nearby MIM-104 Patriot air defence systems. The footage has provided further evidence corroborating multiple prior reports that Patriot systems have been ineffective against Iranian missile strikes. In the initial hours of hostilities in February, footage showed Patriot systems in Qatar consistently failing to intercept Iranian ballistic missiles. In mid-March a crew member from a civilian ship sailing through the Gulf of Oman filmed two Iranian ballistic missiles striking oil facilities at the United Arab Emirates port of Fujairah, and failed efforts by local forces to use a Patriot system. The aforementioned three pieces of footage all showed three interceptors launched against each Iranian ballistic missile, rather than the standard two, indicating an awareness of the lower than advertised probability of kill. PAC-3 interceptors cost approximately $4-6 million dollars, with export clients in Arab world typically paying closer to $6 million, bringing the cost of each interception attempt against Iranian short range missiles costing under $400,000 to around $18 million. This has ensured that air defence efforts are almost totally unsustainable. The capabilities of the U.S. and its strategic partners’ regional air defence network has been severely diminished since the outbreak of hostilities, with Iranian precision strikes having destroyed the sole AN/FPS-132 radar based outside the U.S., which was located in Qatar, and two AN/TPY-2 radars from THAAD systems in Jordan and the United Arab Emirates, as well as multiple lower value radar systems.

title: [UPDATED] Kane Edges Yamal, Mbappe To Taste Ballon d’Or Glory
body: Harry Kane became England’s first Ballon d’Or winner in 25 years in his native London on Monday, beating stiff competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe. Alexia Putellas claimed the women’s prize for a third time, extending Spain’s dominance of the award, thanks to her role in leading Barcelona to last season’s Champions League before moving to London City Lionesses. The first-ever Ballon d’Or ceremony on English soil got off to an inauspicious start as the London traffic caused a delay of nearly an hour, with many of the star names arriving late. But there was a happy ending for the hometown hero as Kane collected the crowning glory of his career to date. England and Bayern Munich forward Harry Kane smiles after receiving the Ballon d’Or award for the best male footballer during the 2026 Ballon d’Or France Football award ceremony at the Palladium Theatre in London on October 26, 2026. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP) The 33-year-old Bayern Munich forward struck a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for club and country last season, propelling the German giants to a league and cup double. He also scored six times as England finished third at the World Cup. “Without you guys (his Bayern Munich teammates) and the rest of the team it wouldn’t be possible; the way you guys push me, the way we compete. So thank you very much,” he said after collecting the award. Kane’s medal collection is limited to German domestic triumphs since he arrived at Bayern in 2023. He was on the losing side for Tottenham in the 2019 Champions League final against Liverpool and twice tasted bitter defeat in the final of the European Championship with England. Spain and Barcelona midfielder Alexia Putellas (centre) and England and Bayern Munich forward Harry Kane (right) pose after receiving their Ballon d’Or awards for the best female and male footballer during the 2026 Ballon d’Or France Football award ceremony at the Palladium Theatre in London on October 26, 2026. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP) But his remarkable goalscoring consistency has earned him the highest individual award in football. “Making the move to Bayern Munich was a big step in my career,” Kane told AFP earlier. “Some people saw it as a risk, but for me it was always about improving and seeing if I could get better around the teammates, the team, the club, and it has pushed me onto another level. “Being a number nine for Bayern and England, you are expected to score goals and to do that the number of times I did last year is something I’m really proud of,” he added. Putellas Back On Top Winner in 2021 and 2022, Putellas’s third Ballon d’Or caps her return to the top of the women’s game after an anterior cruciate ligament injury derailed her rise four years ago. England and Bayern Munich forward Harry Kane smiles after receiving the Ballon d’Or award for the best male footballer during the 2026 Ballon d’Or France Football award ceremony at the Palladium Theatre in London on October 26, 2026. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP) Putellas succeeds Spain teammate Aitana Bonmatí, the winner the past three years, who was sidelined by a leg break for most of last season. “Ever since I suffered the injury, I’ve been trying to enjoy every moment as if it were my last, because you never know if it’ll happen again,” Putellas told AFP in an interview last month. “I never felt that the (Ballon d’Or) trophy was ‘mine’… Having already experienced it once, I’m able to enjoy it even more now,” she added. Yamal made the boldest fashion statement of the contenders with a pink flower on the front of his black suit. The Barcelona winger scooped up the first award of the night for young talent of the year for the third consecutive time. But the 19-year-old fell short of becoming the youngest ever Ballon d’Or winner after he failed to produce his best form during Spain’s World Cup success. Mbappe got the better of Yamal with two goals as Real Madrid edged Barcelona 2-1 in El Clasico on Sunday. But his wait to win the Ballon d’Or goes on despite his prolific year for France and Real Madrid. Luis de la Fuente beat out Paris Saint-Germain’s Luis Enrique and Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta to be named men’s coach of the year after leading Spain to World Cup glory. “I’m really privileged to work with a team of such high quality on a professional and human level,” said de la Fuente. Barcelona’s Pere Romeu scooped the prize for women’s coach of the year. Arsenal’s Bukayo Saka won the Socrates award for his humanitarian work. Paris Saint-Germain missed out on any of the main individual awards despite winning a second consecutive Champions League, but did have the consolation of men’s club of the year. Spanish duo Unai Simón and Cata Coll were named best men’s and women’s goalkeeper. AFP The post [UPDATED] Kane Edges Yamal, Mbappe To Taste Ballon d’Or Glory appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Harry Kane crowned 2026 Ballon d’Or winner
body: England captain Harry Kane has been crowned the winner of the 2026 Ballon d’Or, claiming football’s most prestigious individual award. The Bayern Munich striker emerged as the standout player at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony, held on Monday, October 26, after an outstanding year for club and country. Kane’s triumph marks a major milestone in his career, recognising his performances for Bayern Munich and the England national team. The England international has established himself as one of the world’s leading forwards, combining prolific goalscoring with his ability to create opportunities for teammates. His victory comes after intense competition from several leading contenders, including Paris Saint-Germain’s Ousmane Dembélé, Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappé and Barcelona youngster Lamine Yamal. The Ballon d’Or, organised by France Football, recognises the best footballer over the relevant assessment period. Kane’s win adds another landmark achievement to a career that has seen him become England’s all-time leading goalscorer and one of the most prolific strikers in European football. title: Survival LLM: AI assistant and emergency library that runs on your own computer
body:
Survival LLM is a free AI assistant and emergency library that runs entirely on your own computer. Ask it how to keep food safe in a blackout, treat a burn, or purify water, and it answers from trusted sources and shows you exactly where each answer came from.
Free and open source. Set it up while you have internet; after that it needs none.
The AI model and the library live on your computer. Nothing you ask leaves it.
Every answer lists the articles it read. Click one to read it yourself, with the exact passage highlighted.
Medical references, FEMA and CDC guidance, survival manuals, how-to guides, repair guides and about 930,000 Wikipedia articles.
The app is the same everywhere. When it opens, it checks your computer's memory and downloads the AI model that fits. More memory means a smarter model.
"Right" means it got the main point of official guidance right on 22 blackout and first-aid questions, graded blind, in our tests on an earlier build of the library ( how we tested ). Smaller models make more mistakes, so the app always shows the source to check.
Plus the library: a 9 GB download for everything (19 GB once installed), or 1.3 GB (3 GB installed) without Wikipedia and iFixit. Free disk space needed: the model's size plus 5 GB, plus about 27 GB while the full library installs (10 GB for the smaller one). Apple Silicon Macs (M1 or newer) with macOS 14 Sonoma or newer, and 64-bit Windows 10 or 11.
Setup takes 20 minutes to about 2½ hours, depending on your computer and your internet speed. You only click for about 5 minutes; the rest is downloading.
Plain-text copies of openly licensed (some for non-commercial use only) and public-domain references, searchable in a fraction of a second:
Each source keeps its own license, shown with every article; see the full list with licenses .
AI models make mistakes, the small ones more often. Every answer shows the articles it used, so you can check.
No account, no tracking. Your questions never leave your computer, and once set up it works with the internet off.
Add PDFs, Word documents, ebooks and notes, like your generator's manual or your family's emergency plan, and the AI searches them too. They stay on your computer.
Check for updates, at the bottom of the app, installs a new version in one click and keeps your models, library and files.
On a MacBook Pro we measured about 100 W while it answers, for 5 to 40 seconds per question: a full battery answers roughly 100 to 300. A small generator or power station runs it easily.
Already have it? Click Check for updates at the bottom of the app.

title: Apple says it will replace iPhone Duo handsets with screen problems
body: Apple says it will replace iPhone Duo handsets with screen problems that developed just days after the highly anticipated smartphone went on sale. Photos posted by social media users show lines that appeared on the screens of the technology giant’s first-ever foldable device , which has a starting price of £1,999 ($2,668) in the UK. Apple said it is aware of “an issue impacting the inner display on a small number” of units and urged affected users to contact the company for a replacement. The Duo’s launch, which drew long queues at Apple stores worldwide last week, comes as the brand tries to reinvigorate its catalogue and challenge rivals’ foldable phones. Some Duo owners also posted photos online showing cracks along the screen’s centre crease, while others reported a crunching noise when opening the device. An iPhone Duo user, Justin Lokos, posted an image of a device with lines across the right side of the display and later uploaded a picture of a new handset alongside the broken one, thanking an Apple store in New York for its help. The extent of the issue remains unclear. Apple did not say how many devices were affected, while some images showing faulty devices may have been created using artificial intelligence. The Duo’s 7.6-inch (19.3cm) inner display is held together by a central hinge – a complex piece of engineering that has resulted in flaws in the folding devices made by some of Apple’s competitors. Samsung’s first foldable phone, the Galaxy Fold, suffered an early setback in 2019 when reviewers reported broken screens on the devices. Apple boss John Ternus showing off the new iPhone Duo Android users already have a broad selection of foldable phones to choose from, technology that Apple spent years developing before the Duo’s release. The folding device is Apple’s most expensive iPhone ever, costing up to £3,199 for the most well-equipped models. The Duo marks Apple’s first major iPhone redesign in almost two decades and was unveiled by new chief executive John Ternus, who took over from Tim Cook in September. When closed, the Duo looks like a wider iPhone, then opens into a device resembling a small tablet. “Others have created foldables that just feel like two phones awkwardly stuck together”, Ternus told an audience at Apple’s California headquarters last month. He said the Duo would “redefine the experience of using a foldable phone”.

title: Mitsotakis Aide Michalis Bekiris Steps Aside, Vows Court Fight
body: Michalis Bekiris has temporarily stepped aside as director of Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis’ office in Parliament, after days of controversy over his studies and his status in the role. Bekiris told Mitsotakis of his decision on Monday. He will stay away from his duties until the courts clarify the case, he said. Before his decision, opposition parties, including PASOK, had demanded his removal from the post. The dispute centred on his studies and the status under which he carries out his duties. In response, the Mitsotakis aide rejected the claims. “For a month now, I have been facing an unprecedented campaign of personal targeting,” he said. Michalis Bekiris rejects accusations Specifically, Michalis Bekiris said “lies, slanders and innuendo” are aimed at hurting him and his family. His decision is “exclusively personal” , he added. “It is neither a retreat nor an acceptance of any accusation,” he said. He described it as “a conscious choice of dignity and responsibility” . Above all, he does not want his presence used as a pretext for continuing the confrontation. He also accused parties and political figures of uncritically adopting what is circulating, while trying to hurt the government. Bekiris compared his case with that of his friend Giorgos Mylonakis. Once again, the “feeding frenzy” has gone beyond every limit, he said. Earlier, he had said he works voluntarily in the Prime Minister’s political offices and receives no salary. Elections and court action Still, Michalis Bekiris thanked Mitsotakis for his trust and friendship after many years of close cooperation. Their relationship goes beyond politics, he said. “I am temporarily stepping aside from my duties, but not from the principles, the values and the people with whom I have travelled all these years,” he said. He also pledged to stand by Mitsotakis at the upcoming elections . Bekiris is a former New Democracy MP for Achaia, first elected in 2004. Later, he served as deputy transport minister from January 2009 until the end of the Karamanlis government. He took over the Parliament office in July 2019, soon after Mitsotakis became Prime Minister . Finally, Michalis Bekiris pointed to the courts. “The rest we will say in the courts,” he said. There, those who make and spread claims against him “will be called on to prove them” . title: Olympiacos Files Formal Complaints Against Panathinaikos Owner
body: Olympiacos BC has filed two complaints against Panathinaikos BC owner Dimitris Giannakopoulos and his club with EuroLeague Basketball and the Greek Basketball League (GBL), citing his social media posts and alleged offensive conduct by Panathinaikos supporters during a game against Baskonia on 22 October 2026. The Piraeus-based club confirmed the complaints in an official statement after Giannakopoulos referred to the moves in Instagram Stories on his personal account. Olympiacos alleges that Panathinaikos supporters displayed an insulting banner and chanted an offensive slogan during the team’s EuroLeague game against Baskonia at the OAKA arena. The club also accuses Giannakopoulos of publishing defamatory, insulting and threatening statements about Olympiacos and its head coach, Giorgos Bartzokas. The complaints address separate incidents. Olympiacos has asked EuroLeague Basketball to examine the alleged conduct at the Baskonia game, while its complaint to the GBL concerns Giannakopoulos’s social media statements published on 23 October. Olympiacos complaint to EuroLeague Basketball In its complaint to EuroLeague Basketball, Olympiacos alleges that hundreds of Panathinaikos supporters displayed a banner during the 22 October game against Baskonia Vitoria-Gasteiz. The banner accused Olympiacos of involvement in match-fixing and illicit payments and included an abusive reference to Piraeus, the club’s home city. The complaint also alleges that supporters chanted an offensive slogan referring to basketball referee Vasiliki Tsaroucha, GBL president Vangelis Liolios and Bartzokas. According to Olympiacos, Giannakopoulos subsequently published photographs and videos of the incidents on his Instagram account, which the club says had more than 647,000 followers at the time. Olympiacos argues that the posts amplified the offensive material and that Giannakopoulos effectively endorsed its content by sharing it publicly. The club maintains that the supporters’ conduct and Giannakopoulos’s posts, considered separately and together, defamed and insulted Olympiacos and Bartzokas. Olympiacos has asked EuroLeague Basketball to initiate disciplinary proceedings against Panathinaikos BC and Giannakopoulos and impose the appropriate sanctions. Olympiacos complaint to the Greek Basketball League Olympiacos’s complaint to the GBL focuses on Giannakopoulos’s Instagram post from approximately 4 a.m. on 23 October. The post featured a photograph of Bartzokas speaking at a press conference, overlaid with statements that Olympiacos describes as defamatory, insulting and threatening. The club’s filing cites several passages, including remarks about Olympiacos’s relegation to Greece’s second division in 2019 and allegations concerning suspected corruption in Greek basketball. Olympiacos also takes issue with a statement that it interprets as a threat of further violence against Bartzokas. The club links the wording to an assault on the coach at the Peace and Friendship Stadium (SEF) in October 2014, following an Olympiacos defeat against Panathinaikos in a Greek Cup game. Olympiacos says it condemned that incident at the time and notes that Bartzokas later described the experience as shocking. The complaint further alleges that Giannakopoulos falsely associated Olympiacos with a judicial investigation into suspected bribery and match manipulation involving basketball referee Vasiliki Tsaroucha and other individuals. Olympiacos argues that the statements wrongly suggest that the club participated in, or benefited from, the alleged offences. It also accuses Giannakopoulos of insulting the club’s historic emblem and damaging the reputation of its management, players, coach, supporters and members. The club has asked the GBL to examine the alleged disciplinary offences under Article 55, paragraph 3, of its disciplinary regulations and impose the applicable penalties on both Giannakopoulos and Panathinaikos BC. The allegations outlined in the complaints represent Olympiacos’s position. The filings do not, in themselves, establish that the alleged misconduct or offences occurred. title: Raytheon says investment of over $800 million supports doubling SPY-6 radar output by 2028
body: The radar is already in full-rate production, and USS Ted Stevens is the fourth commissioned U.S. Navy ship equipped with SPY-6. RTX expects the number to exceed 50 over the next decade, with additional systems in assembly and trials. “The investment we’ve made in automation allows us to build at high rates,” said Jason Rathbone, Raytheon’s executive director of Naval Radars. “It reduces the cost of these products and improves quality and reliability.” The production effort runs alongside testing on land and at sea, including successful live-fire events aboard USS Jack H. Lucas. RTX says the program is on track to complete 60 live firings in operational testing in 2027. SPY-6 is designed to help ships detect and classify simultaneous threats, including ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, uncrewed aircraft and electronic warfare platforms. Raytheon describes attacks involving large numbers of different weapons as a central challenge for naval air defense. “Our enemies aren’t just shooting one missile at a time. They’re sending hundreds, trying to overwhelm the systems on our ships,” said John Tobin, Raytheon’s director of Naval Radars. Each SPY-6 variant uses common building blocks called Radar Modular Assemblies, allowing the radar to be configured for different ships and missions. The design supports installation on new ships and retrofits to existing vessels, while preserving common elements for training, maintenance and sustainment. “We are just scratching the surface of what SPY-6 can deliver,” said Jen Gauthier, Raytheon’s vice president of Naval Systems & Sustainment. “It has the capability necessary to meet the threats of today and can easily be upgraded to address the threats of tomorrow.” Raytheon says software updates can address new threats without requiring wholesale hardware replacement. It also sees potential to integrate SPY-6 with combat management systems used by allied navies, supporting wider adoption and collaborative threat tracking. Go deeper: Raytheon .

title: BC Conservatives lay out goals for first 100 days in office
body:
BC Conservative Premier-designate Lorne Doerkson has started sketching out a series of goals for his first 100 days in office, and the scale of challenges facing the new government is starting to come into focus.
Among the first orders of business is to secure his own leadership on paper, as Doerkson is still technically the interim leader of the party.
“I’m leader and that’s an administrative detail and there will be more information on that imminently,” Doerkson said on Sunday .
He also needs to choose a cabinet, with health and finance being the biggest portfolios, and determine when the legislature will resume.
“I don’t want to rule out a fall session,” Doerkson said.
“I think it’s important to keep that option available and open to us. Of course, we have much to do before we can get there to make that decision.”
Doerkson also announced on Sunday that his government will launch an independent review of the province’s finances.
David Eby inherited a $6 billion surplus from John Horgan, but the current deficit is projected at $14 billion.
“We need to see a credible path back to a balanced budget,” Bridgitte Anderson, president and CEO of the Greater Vancouver Board of Trade said.
“And so that is going to take time, but we’re really hoping to further understand from the Conservative government what that timeline looks like.”
Hamish Telford, a political science professor at the University of the Fraser Valley, said that Doerkson does have some challenges ahead of him, including addressing B.C.’s Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act (DRIPA).
“Through the leadership campaign last year, they all wanted to repeal DRIPA, all the candidates,” he said.
“That was an article of faith during the campaign, and he reiterated that on Saturday night. And we know that First Nations in this province are totally opposed to that, and so there’s going to be a confrontation ahead of us if they do indeed go forward with it.”
On Monday, Grand Chief Stewart Phillip, president of the Union of British Columbia Indian Chiefs, said , “We’re not going to stand idly by while the government-elect does, in fact, rip it up.
The road ahead for the BC NDP is also unknown.
They have to find an interim leader, but it is not clear when, or who, that will be.
“These are very early days and the NDP does not have to be in a rush,” Telford said.
“They’ve got some veterans there to sort of guide them through this, but certainly there are people like Niki Sharma and Bowinn Ma that are going to be in the caucus who I think would be early frontrunners.
“Ravi Kahlon did not contest this election, but he’s long been thought to be interested in leadership. And there may be others out there who were not elected this time around or have not been at the provincial level, coming out of the municipal level. So the NDP really should give itself time. They’ve got four years here to choose the right person.”

title: Oikonomopoulos Holds Greek Airplay Chart No. 1 as Argiros Climbs
body: Nikos Oikonomopoulos holds No. 1 on the Greek Airplay Chart for a further week with “Enoho Kormi”, as the top three stay unchanged for 19–25 October 2026. The Official IFPI Airplay Chart powered by MediaInspector publishes the weekly Top 20 of Greek-repertoire songs on AirplayChart.gr . In week 43 of the Greek Airplay Chart, Thodoris Ferris stays at No. 2 with “Eipes”, while APON holds No. 3 with “Kantada”. “Enoho Kormi” was also No. 1 in week 42, as Greek City Times reported on 19 October. Heaven Music put out the song as a single on 30 June 2026, according to its Spotify listing . In addition, “Eipes” is a single that Panik Platinum issued on 5 December 2025. Similarly, “Kantada” comes from APON’s 2026 album “Ixogenia” on Panik Records. Greek City Times also covered the song’s music video in June. Four acts still have two songs on the Greek Airplay Chart: Oikonomopoulos, Vissi, Lioliou and Sabanis. “Me Liga Logia” rises one place to No. 13 for Oikonomopoulos. title: Choriatiko Bakery Suspects Face Criminal Organisation Charges
body: Suspects arrested in the case involving To Choriatiko (Το Χωριάτικο), a Greek bakery chain , face a series of serious felony charges as prosecutors investigate alleged criminal activity linked to the business and a network of companies. The prosecutor has brought charges against the suspects, depending on each person’s alleged role, including: Forming, directing or participating in a criminal organisation. Fraud against the Greek state and public-law legal entities involving more than €120,000. Tax evasion exceeding €150,000 through inaccurate tax declarations and failure to remit VAT. Aiding and abetting tax evasion. Late payment of employer and employee social security contributions, a misdemeanour. Forgery involving more than €120,000. Pimping jointly and repeatedly. Robbery committed jointly. Joint fraud, classified as a misdemeanour. Repeated breaches of residence restrictions. An aggravated form of money laundering. Following a decision by Athens Court of First Instance head Christoforos Limou, the case file was assigned to an investigating magistrate and two assistant magistrates because of the large number of defendants. The accused are expected to request additional time to prepare their statements. Alleged police bribery case also comes into focus A separate investigation involving Angelos Giannakopoulos has also drawn attention, focusing on allegations of bribery involving a police officer who served on Mykonos. According to reporting by Ta Nea , authorities have examined allegations that payments and inside information helped people obtain advance knowledge of police operations and inspections. Investigators have reportedly examined claims that Giannakopoulos had access to information about police movements and planned inspections of businesses in Attica and Mykonos. The case also concerns a senior non-commissioned police officer who allegedly passed on confidential information from within the force. Authorities arrested the officer in the summer of 2025. The officer’s trial is scheduled to begin on Friday, October 30, 2026. The allegations in both cases remain subject to judicial proceedings. title: Red Warnings for 28 October as Storms Flood Attica Streets
body: Greece’s weather service has issued red warnings for parts of the country on Wednesday 28 October, the national “Ochi Day” holiday, after storms turned streets into rivers in Attica and authorities put nine areas on full alert. The Hellenic National Meteorological Service (EMY) on Monday upgraded its weather bulletin to an emergency bulletin for dangerous weather. It forecasts heavy rain and thunderstorms, with local hail, mainly in eastern Greece, from Monday 26 October until at least Wednesday 28 October, according to the updated bulletin . Where the red warnings apply On Monday, the Dodecanese was under a red warning until late in the evening. Tuesday 27 October brings a lull in some areas, with orange warnings for Attica until the morning, Evia and the Sporades, the Dodecanese from midday, the eastern Aegean islands, and Magnesia and Larissa in Thessaly from the evening. The weather is forecast to worsen again on Wednesday. EMY has issued red warnings for: Magnesia and Larissa, until late at night the Sporades and Evia, until late in the evening the Dodecanese Attica is under an orange warning on Wednesday from the early hours until midday, as are the eastern Aegean islands and eastern Central Greece (mainly Fthiotida and Viotia), Kathimerini reported . Red Code until Thursday After meetings of the Risk Assessment Committee and the Civil Protection Coordinating Body, attended by Climate Crisis and Civil Protection Minister Evangelos Tournas, the General Secretariat for Civil Protection placed nine areas on “Red Code” mobilisation from Monday 26 to Thursday 29 October, the ministry announced . They are Evia, Fthiotida, Viotia, the Sporades, Magnesia, Larissa and the Dodecanese, plus the whole regions of Attica and the North Aegean. Attica and the North Aegean were included as a precaution because the ground was already soaked from earlier rain, the ministry said. The Fire Service has activated its flood response plan, while the armed forces, police and Coast Guard are on standby. Tournas stressed the need for readiness ahead of the heavy holiday traffic around 28 October. The Risk Assessment Committee expects the weather to ease on Tuesday, with rain and local storms in eastern and southern Greece, before a fresh deterioration on Wednesday, mainly in eastern Thessaly, the Northern Sporades, eastern Central Greece, Evia and Skyros. The committee is due to meet again on Tuesday. Flooded streets across Attica The storms hit Attica hard on Sunday night. Streets in Mandra and Glyfada turned into torrents and Traffic Police closed Karamanli Avenue in Voula towards Piraeus, between Vasileos Pavlou Street and Kritis Square, because of the build-up of water. The road later reopened. On Monday, flooding on Poseidonos Avenue in Palaio Faliro left traffic squeezed into one lane, and there were kilometres-long queues on Kifisou, Vouliagmenis and Alimou-Katechaki avenues citing Traffic Police. Roads also flooded in Koropi. Weather stations of the National Observatory of Athens and meteo.gr recorded 104 millimetres of rain at Lofos Chasani in Elliniko and 96mm in Koropi over Sunday and Monday, up to 5.50pm Monday. The highest total in the country was 133mm at Amoni Sofikou in Corinthia. On Sunday night, during the downpour, three members of one family died when their car went into the sea at the port of Piraeus. The cause is under investigation. Schools shut on Kos On Kos, Mayor Theodosis Nikitaras ordered all schools, kindergartens and childcare centres to stay shut on Tuesday 27 October, and the municipality urged residents to avoid unnecessary travel, Schools across Greece are closed on Wednesday for the national holiday. Wet weather for the parades Wednesday’s deterioration comes as towns across Greece prepare to hold student and military parades for the anniversary. Meteorologist Theodoros Kolydas noted that the main forecasting models differ widely on how much rain will fall in Thessaly on the day, with maximum totals of 249.8mm in ICON-EU, 102.8mm in ECMWF and 48.4mm in GFS. He urged the public to rely on EMY’s official warnings, Parapolitika reported . Anyone in the affected areas should follow updates from EMY and Civil Protection and the instructions of local authorities. In an emergency, call 112.
