title: Lula wins fourth term in dramatic Brazil election comeback
body: Brazil’s President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has won a fourth term in office in a dramatic comeback over his right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro. Left-wing leader Lula took 51.79% of votes, becoming the first president since Brazil’s return to civilian rule in 1985 to be elected after losing the first round of voting. Lula told jubilant crowds his victory was a “loss for negativity, lies”, adding “long live democracy”. Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of convicted former president Jair Bolsonaro, has so far refused to recognise the result and called for it to be annulled. World leaders have congratulated Lula on his re-election. Bolsonaro’s rejection comes as no surprise to observers. His father did the same. But a challenge appears unlikely to succeed. Firstly, it seems to centre on the unprecedented decision by the Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin to extend voting nationwide by two hours. Some Bolsonaro fans are pointing out that Zanin was once Lula’s lawyer and alleging bias. But both teams had requested an extension to voting times – Lula’s had argued that voters in São Paulo and Bahia could not get to the polling stations because of a lack of buses, while Bolsonaro’s campaign cited heavy rain in some areas in the south of the country and in São Paulo as their reason. Both knew every vote would count and did not want their side to miss out. The president of the Supreme Electoral Court Kássio Nunes Marques – appointed by Jair Bolsonaro – confirmed Lula’s victory and said that the voter extension did not change the outcome of the race. The sheer gap between the two candidates’ tallies – 4.4 million votes – makes the result more difficult to challenge.The result came as a surprise after Flávio Bolsonaro won the first round on 4 October with 47% of votes ahead of Lula’s 45%. But Lula’s camp gained momentum ahead of election day, focusing on boosting voter turnout after 33 million people did not vote in round one. Sunday saw the largest drop in abstention between the two rounds of a presidential election since 1989. Bolsonaro had been poised to give a victory speech and said the result should be annulled, calling it “inexplicable”. As his disconsolate supporters left the house in Brasília where their candidate had been watching the result, Lula took to the streets in São Paulo to celebrate. “This, my fourth term, will be the best of any president in the history of this country,” the former metal worker told supporters. “It will be the one in which I listen most to the Brazilian people.” After pulling off this victory, Lula faces big hurdles: a divided country, an opponent that won’t recognise the result, and a hostile Congress packed full of Bolsonaro allies. Markets reacted negatively to the unexpected outcome. The Sao Paolo stock exchange opened 15% down, sparking a brief suspension before recovering slightly. Interest rate futures rose as investors scrutinised Lula’s fiscal plans. Reacting to the result, US President Donald Trump suggested the election had been stolen. “I didn’t take sides, but it looked like another rigged election,” he told reporters on Monday, without providing evidence or more details. “It looked very bad to me.” Other world leaders from across the political spectrum have congratulated Lula. Mexico’s left-wing President Claudia Sheinbaum said in a post on X: “The people of Brazil won.” Peru’s right-wing President Keiko Fujimori praised Brazil’s “democratic day”. Similar messages were shared by the presidents of Chile and Ecuador. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney noted that their two countries had already “flourished under our partnership”. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said “democracy and multilateralism” had won. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez – also a left-wing leader – called it a “great victory”. French President Emmanuel Macron said the two nations should work “in service of a more just world”. South African President Cyril Ramaphosa called Lula’s victory one for the “global south and progressive forces throughout the world”. In a video posted on Instagram later on Monday, Flávio Bolsonaro said police had told him to hand over his passports and had been banned from leaving the country. Trump has previously shown support for Bolsonaro’s father Jair, who is currently serving a 27-year prison sentence after being convicted of a coup attempt after losing the 2022 elections to Lula. Flávio Bolsonaro met Trump at the White House earlier this year to bid for his support. Lula, who turns 81 on Tuesday, has already been president for three non-consecutive terms, serving two terms between January 2003 to December 2010, and again from January 2023. His win makes him the first in Brazilian history to secure a fourth term, which will last until 2030. But this has been a bitterly fought campaign and the new term – set to start on 5 January – comes amid significant constraints at home and abroad, including animosity from the US president. Referring to what Trump has called the “Donroe Doctrine” – which seeks to establish US dominance in the Western Hemisphere – Lula used his victory speech to insist that Brazil “will not accept being anyone’s backyard”. Lula has also bucked a wider trend in Latin America, where voters in countries such as Argentina, Chile and Colombia have put right-wing candidates and parties in power.

title: Lions set to face familiar foe in West semifinal
body:
SURREY – The B.C. Lions are well aware of what they’re up against this week.
When they host the Saskatchewan Roughriders in the CFL’s West Division semifinal on Saturday, it will be the fourth time this season the two teams have faced off.
It will also be the third year in a row these squads meet in the playoffs.
“We know what they’ll do,” said Lions defensive lineman Mathieu Betts. “It’s just on us to execute better. And I think we have the players to be able to match well.”
B.C. and Saskatchewan come in with identical 10-8 regular-season records. The Lions won the 2026 series 2-1, but the Riders have eliminated the Lions from the playoffs two years in a row.
The defending Grey Cup-champion Riders are a fundamentally sound team that should never be taken lightly, said Lions head coach Buck Pierce.
“Really, for us, being able to change the pace or dictate the pace on offence and how we want to play is key, right?” he said. “And if you look back at the games that we’ve had this year, (they’re) close physical ball games that are going to come down to the fourth quarter. And I’m expecting really nothing different.”
The most recent matchup between the two sides came on Sept. 25, when B.C. took a 31-24 home victory in a game that saw star Lions quarterback Nathan Rourke pass for 375 yards with four touchdowns.
That doesn’t mean Saturday’s contest will look similar, Rourke said.
“They’ll have something different for us. They always do. They always have a wrinkle,” he said.
“They’ll do their self scouting, they’ll have a plan for us. I think there might be some changes in the back end, trying to figure out who their personnel is and all that kind of stuff, getting some people who are healthy again. But ultimately we know that we’re going to have to play our best to beat these guys.”
The very best athletes evolve in important moments, said Lions receiver Jevon Cottoy.
“There’s different types of players that come playoff time,” he said. “We get excited for the playoffs, because we’ve talked about it since the off-season, since training camp, that this is where we want to be. So, big time players have to step up in these moments. We just got to make sure we do what we got to do.”
Stepping up in big moments has become a theme for the Lions this season.
The team struggled early and got off to a 1-5 record. Even then, everyone inside the organization expected B.C. to earn its way back to the playoffs, Rourke said.
“Our year certainly didn’t start the way we wanted to, but we’ve always trusted our process,” he said. “We believe in our guys, believe in our locker room, believe in where we’re going.”
The Lions rebounded from the tough start with a 9-1 run and clinched a home playoff game, then closed out the regular-season campaign with a pair of losses as the team sat several top players.
The group’s resilience has become its defining trait, Pierce said.
“Just proud of the way that we’ve continued to focus on ourselves and not let results define you, or not let success define you,” said the head coach.
Now B.C. needs another victory on Saturday to keep playing.
The winner of Saturday’s game will visit the Edmonton Elks in the West Division final on Nov. 7. The Elks finished first in the West to earn a bye this week.
“This is just a step on the journey,” Rourke said. “And like every week that we’ve taken, we’ve taken it one step at a time. And we’re gonna give this all our attention and focus because these guys deserve it.”
This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 26, 2026.

title: Anthropic warns of ‘catastrophic risk’ to humankind ahead of blockbuster share listing
body: Anthropic has warned artificial intelligence (AI) could pose “catastrophic or existential risks to humanity” as it unveiled details of its planned blockbuster stock market listing in the US. The firm’s valuation is expected to exceed SpaceX’s, the biggest-ever listing, which was valued at about $1.8 trillion in the summer. Anthropic has not yet disclosed the number of shares to be released, the price range, or a listing date. The Claude chatbot developer reported $16.3bn (£12.2bn) of revenue in the first half of the year, with losses of more than $80.7bn. Anthropic, which said it will list on the Nasdaq under the symbol ANT, will be the first fully AI-focused company to go public, making it a test case for the future of the technology. In a filing ahead of its listing, Anthropic said policymakers, regulators, researchers, and people within its organisation had raised concerns that AI systems posed a significant risk to humanity. ‘Bold but sane’ In Anthropic’s new documents, it reiterated promises it has made in the past to develop AI in a way that is beneficial to people, while at the same time warning investors of its dangers. Anthropic detailed losses in its financial filings that exceeded its revenue for the first half of the year, but said it would often make forward investments “that may seem irresponsibly large at first glance”. “In general, we will aim to be bold but sane, and to win trust with a track record of successful bets,” the tech giant said. Its success depends largely on its ability to develop the most advanced AI models, Anthropic said, adding, “any failure to do so could adversely affect our business”. Across about 90 pages detailing possible risk factors, Anthropic set out the potential threats to its ability to safely and competitively develop AI. Anthropic warned it relies on a cluster of cloud computing providers, Taiwanese chipmakers already facing huge demand and data centres concentrated in the US. It also warned of “regulatory action arising from harms associated with our AI models”- citing concerns over AI being used by children or individuals at risk of suicide – and uncertainty about where and how it might be held liable for actions taken by its systems. However, Anthropic also used the filing to laud the potential benefits of the tech itself, envisioning it unlocking “millions of virtual agents with the ability to revolutionise every area of human endeavour” across a range of fields. “We believe that AI is one of the most consequential technologies in human history,” the firm said. Anthropic said AI would also “profoundly accelerate the rate of progress in biology and medicine”, potentially finding cures to diseases including cancer and Alzheimer’s. The firm added it could also establish “sustained acceleration in economic growth” by boosting productivity. ‘Significant milestone’ Matt Orton, chief market strategist at investment management firm Raymond James Investment, said investors expected to see rapid growth as well as rapid financial losses in Anthropic’s finances, so Monday’s filing would not come as a surprise. “Getting the details from this filing, I think will help provide the market with more visibility, because we need to know where its revenue growth is coming from,” he told the BBC. Peter Andersen, founder of Andersen Capital Management, told Reuters that Anthropic’s plans to list was “a significant milestone in the development of artificial intelligence”. He added that the outcome of its stock market debut would be “fairly indicative of the sentiment” among investors to continue ploughing cash into AI development. It said advanced AI systems “could, if not developed, deployed, and operated with appropriate safeguards, oversight, and security measures, pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity, particularly if such systems were misused, replicated, weaponised, or allowed to operate with a high degree of autonomy”. Anthropic was founded five years ago by chief executive Dario Amodei, his sister Daniela Amodei and five others, and announced its intention to go public in June. Its main rival, OpenAI, quickly followed suit. That listing is now expected to occur early next year, according to a person familiar with OpenAI’s plans. Those announcements were followed by a wave of cyber-security and other technological breaches involving their AI agents – bots designed to operate somewhat autonomously. Current and former staff of both companies also warned AI technology was being developed without the ability to protect humanity from possible future harms enacted by AI tools. As Anthropic revealed its stock debut plans on Monday, the owners of the rights to Elvis Presley’s music sued the AI firm accusing it of using hundreds of the rock-and-roll star’s songs to train its chatbot Claude.

title: Mazonakis Death Probe: Antidote Vials Traced to Athens Clinic, Reports Say
body: Investigators looking into the death of singer Giorgos Mazonakis have traced two vials of a sedation antidote, seized from the Kolonaki practice where he collapsed, back to a major Athens hospital, according to Greek media reports on Monday 26 October. The vials, believed to contain Anexate (flumazenil), had originally been supplied by the manufacturer DEMO to Euroclinic, a large private clinic in Athens, To Vima reported , citing its police reporter Vasilis Lambropoulos. Investigators now want to know how the drug ended up in a private practice on Karneadou Street. What happened on 9 September Mazonakis, one of Greece’s best-known singers, died on Wednesday 9 September, aged 54, after collapsing during a plasmapheresis session at the Karneadou Street practice in the upmarket Kolonaki district. Plasmapheresis is a procedure in which blood plasma is separated and removed from the body. The two doctors who ran the practice, Ioanna Gaka and Ilias Theodoropoulos, were initially prosecuted for exposure resulting in death. After their testimony to the 32nd investigating magistrate, they were remanded in custody on an upgraded charge of homicide with possible intent by omission. Both doctors deny the charge. Their lawyers called the upgrade “completely unjustified” and said they would appeal against the detention. According to Kathimerini, a police forensic report found that the emergency call to the ambulance service EKAB was made about 50 minutes after the plasmapheresis machine’s first alert. The couple have argued that EKAB bears responsibility, saying paramedics arrived with a carry chair rather than a stretcher and that CPR was interrupted while the singer was carried down to the ambulance. Toxicology and the antidote Toxicology tests ordered by the singer’s family found eight substances in his blood, including the sedative midazolam, the anaesthetic propofol and flumazenil, which reverses the effects of midazolam. Results from the state’s own tests at Aristotle University of Thessaloniki were still awaited at the time. On 15 October, on the investigating magistrate’s orders, police searched the Karneadou Street practice again in the presence of a prosecutor and the defence lawyers. They found two vials that appeared to contain Anexat How the vials were traced According to MEGA, as reported by Enikos , the University of Athens toxicology laboratories checked the codes on the vials and corresponded with DEMO. That is how they identified Euroclinic as the place the vials had first been supplied to. The same reports say an anaesthetist who worked at that clinic was the person the accused doctor contacted while she was looking for an antidote to midazolam. The key question for the authorities, To Vima reported, is how the drugs got from the clinic to the Karneadou Street practice, and whether the anaesthetist removed them without the clinic management’s knowledge. Investigators are examining that possibility, but it has not been confirmed, Newsit reported . The reports say a new check was carried out at the clinic within the past few hours to trace the drugs’ route. The reports do not suggest any wrongdoing by Euroclinic’s management. At the time of writing, GCT could not find any public comment from the clinic. Differences in the test results Lambropoulos also reported differences between the family’s private toxicology tests and the official state investigation. The private tests detected the midazolam antidote, which so far does not appear in the state findings. The state tests reportedly found an additional toxic substance that the private analysis did not record. Investigators will assess the findings alongside the rest of the evidence in the case. The investigation is continuing. title: [UPDATED] Alexia Putellas Wins 2026 Women’s Ballon d’Or
body: Alexia Putellas picked up her third Ballon d’Or in her new home city of London on Monday, crowning a spectacular return to the top of women’s football after injury cut her down in her prime. Putellas previously picked up the prize for the best player in the world in 2021 and 2022 as the creative heartbeat of an all-conquering Barcelona side. But an anterior cruciate ligament tear just as she was preparing for Spain’s bid to win Euro 2022 derailed her rise to global stardom. Spain and Barcelona midfielder Alexia Putellas and England and Bayern Munich forward Harry Kane pose with their trophies on stage after receiving their Ballon d’Or awards for the best female and male footballer during the 2026 Ballon d’Or France Football award ceremony at the Palladium Theatre in London on October 26, 2026. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP) Putellas recovered to play a bit part role in Spain’s World Cup triumph a year later, but was overshadowed by teammate Aitana Bonmatí for both club and country as it took nearly two years to rediscover her best form. “Ever since I suffered the injury, I’ve been trying to enjoy every moment as if it were my last, because you never know if it’ll happen again,” Putellas told AFP in an interview last month. Bonmati took on the mantle of the world’s best player, becoming a three-time Ballon d’Or winner between 2023 and 2025 until she was also sidelined by a leg break. With the emphasis back on Putellas, she rose to the challenge, helping Barcelona regain the Champions League last season in dominant fashion. “I never felt that the (Ballon d’Or) trophy was ‘mine’… Having already experienced it once, I’m able to enjoy it even more now,” she added. Having achieved all that she could in Catalonia, Putellas embarked on a new adventure, joining London City Lionesses. Owned by American businesswoman Michele Kang, the Lionesses are aiming to break the mould as the only fully independent team in England’s top division. “It’s a complete change in my life. It’s a constant, daily learning process: the culture, the language, moving to a new country, a new city,” said the 32-year-old. “I knew that if I ever had to end my time at Barca, it wouldn’t make much sense to repeat what I’d already experienced in the next chapter, mainly because it’s impossible. “It had to be something completely different. It’s practically a brand-new club, with everything yet to be written, so I’m trying to bring that winning culture and mentality with me.” The Putellas effect is already being felt in the English Women’s Super League with the Lionesses sat just behind Chelsea and Manchester City at the top of the table and ahead of traditional giants Arsenal. The move could also benefit Spain’s chances of retaining the World Cup next year with their star player facing a lesser workload without European football this season. “It was one of the things I took into account. There’s a long way to go, and my focus is on the day-to-day, but I also believe that these kinds of environments are what will prepare me to perform at my best,” she said. For now, there is a Ballon d’Or to savor and a new life in London to build. AFP The post [UPDATED] Alexia Putellas Wins 2026 Women’s Ballon d’Or appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Cross-request KV cache exposure in the GLM-5.3 Workers AI model (155 responses)
body:
On September 8, 2026, we were alerted by a security researcher, Gadi Evron from Knostic , to a tenant isolation issue affecting the GLM-5.3 Workers AI model ( @cf/zai-org/glm-5.3 ) starting on August 27, 2026. We have remediated the issue, and we restored the model on September 9. We have confirmed that no other model hosted on Workers AI was affected.
Between August 27 and September 9, a small number of customers using the GLM 5.3 Workers AI model received responses that contained data from other customers' requests made to the same model shortly before theirs. In total, 155 responses were affected, all to prompts longer than 681,280 tokens.
After excluding our own testing and the researcher's, the requests we identified are consistent in timing and volume with ordinary long-context use, not with someone repeatedly exploiting the bug. We found no evidence of deliberate exploitation.
Today we are publishing this report alongside a post fromÂ SGLang, the open-source inference engine that we use, as a coordinated disclosure.Â This post describes the bug that caused this issue, our response timeline, and the subsequent hardening we have conducted on our production SGLang deployments. We also detail our continued efforts with the upstream maintainers of SGLang to address this and similar bugs.
GLM is a text generation model from Z.ai Â that is built for agentic coding workflows; it is one of the many models Â available through Workers AI. Gadi Evron submitted a report on September 8 through our HackerOne program stating that very long prompts sent to @cf/zai-org/glm-5.3 Â on Workers AI sometimes returned text that belonged to other users' sessions. Cloudflare reproduced the issue the next morning and took the model offline within 40 minutes of declaring an incident. We then deployed a corrected configuration and a patched inference engine, and restored service the same day. Â
This specific report of cross-request KV cache exposure was the result of two overlapping issues. The first was a misconfiguration of the open-source inference engine, SGLang, used by Cloudflare. We deployed GLM 5.3 with a 1,048,576-token context window, but the KV cache pool on our prefill GPUs only had room for 681,280 tokens. We were aware of this mismatch before launch. We expected the engine to return an error for any prompt it could not process, and our long-context tests returned successful responses, so we did not believe this to be an issue.
The second was a bug in how SGLang handled the resulting over-length requests in disaggregated prefill/decode mode. A prompt that did not fit the pool was internally marked as rejected and replaced with a one-token placeholder, but instead of aborting the request and returning a client error, prefill generated the KV cache for the placeholder prompt and transferred it to the decode node. The decode node received a "transfer complete" message and assumed that prefill overwrote the KV cache from previous requests with the full prompt for this request, when in fact it left the majority of the previous state intact. The decode node subsequently generated a response while attending over stale cache pages that still held data from earlier requests. As a result, responses to prompts longer than 681,280 tokens could contain data from other users' GLM 5.3 sessions.
After disabling the model , we took the following actions to correct this vulnerability before restoring public access to it:
To fix our configuration, we made the pool hold the full context. Â We adjusted our GLM 5.3 configuration to match our GLM 5.2 configuration, which freed enough GPU memory that the prefill KV pool now holds about 2.04 million tokens, roughly twice the 1,048,576-token context length. A prompt that fits the context window now always fits the pool, so the rejection path is never reached for a valid request. This alone prevents the bug from being exercised.
To fix the engine, we also made the rejection path safe. Â Relying on pool size alone is fragile: any change to quantization, tensor parallelism, CUDA graph sizes, or a future model version changes the pool size in a way that's easy to miss. Furthermore, there may be other situations in which the prefill scheduler can reject a request and trigger the same bug. To prevent this, we also patched the engine so that a request carrying a pending rejection is retired at the disaggregation admission queue, with its original error, before any bootstrap, allocation, or KV transfer happens. We proposed this upstream as #38704 , which also had the decode node verify that the number of tokens transferred matches the number it reserved. The fix was already on SGLang main in #36988 , merged September 6 for a related failure path but not yet released. The maintainers also merged #38935 , which rejects these requests earlier, following our approach.
We validated both changes against the researcher's reproduction script and our own canary-marker tests before restoring the model.
Workers AI runs GLM 5.3 with SGLang in a disaggregated configuration: a pool of prefill GPUs processes the prompt and produces the model's KV cache for it, then hands that cache over remote direct memory access (RDMA), via Mooncake , to a pool of decode GPUs that generate the response. We have written about this architecture before in our posts on high-performance LLMs Â andÂ smaller, faster, safer models .
The KV cache in GPU memory is a shared pool of fixed-size pages. Each request is assigned pages when it is admitted and releases them when it finishes. Pages are not currently zeroed between requests; the next request that gets a page simply overwrites it. This approach is common among inference engines and is necessary to achieve the best performance, but it means that the inference engine is responsible for tracking ownership of these memory pages. KV cache page ownership and lifetime tracking has to deal with not just shared ownership within a node (KV cache offload and token generation both access the memory with different lifetimes), but also ownership that is technically shared with the remote prefill node (which holds a simultaneous mutable reference to the page).
Furthermore, the size of this pool is not a configuration value. SGLang sizes it at startup from whatever GPU memory remains after loading the model weights. The model's advertised context length is a separate configuration value. Nothing forces the two to agree, and it is our job to check that they do.
On our GLM 5.3 prefill nodes with our configuration, the pool came to 681,280 tokens while the model's context length is 1,048,576 tokens. The selected KV pool size is printed by SGLang in logs during startup and exposed as a metric. We were aware of this size mismatch; however, during pre-launch testing we observed successful HTTP status codes and a streaming body with no error frames during benchmarking. We assumed that the engine was capable of gracefully handling the difference between the KV cache pool and requested context window via streaming or some other mechanism.
This was one critical gap in our testing: we only validated HTTP response codes and engine performance at long contexts, without validating model output and coherence.Â We now check KV pool size against context length directly, from the running engine, before any disaggregated deployment change ships, rather than inferring it from response codes.
In v0.5.21, the SGLang team has now addressed this bug in how it was handling prompts longer than the KV pool size. Hereâs what was happening before.
When a prompt arrived that was longer than the KV pool could hold, SGLang's scheduler rejected it. The rejection path ( Req.set_finish_with_abort ) recorded the error to be returned to the client and swapped the prompt for a one-token placeholder so that the request could drain through the normal batch machinery without allocating real memory. On a single-node deployment this worked: the placeholder ran, the batch finished, and the client received an error.
In disaggregated modeÂ such as we operate, the admission queues on both prefill and decode checked whether a request was finished , not whether it was rejected . A rejected request reported itself as live. So:
Every request over the threshold behaved this way. This bug had been reported to SGLang by another user as issue #30233 Â on July 6, 2026, which Cloudflare noticed while investigating this incident. We had been flagging these types of issues with SGLang since v0.5.10 and this security incident sped up work that Cloudflare had already started in collaboration with the SGLang team. The patch for this issue was released in SGLang v0.5.20, with follow-ups in v0.5.21 and v0.5.22, and is available for all other operators dependent on SGLang to use. We highly recommend all operators update SGLang dependencies to v0.5.22 or later. For more details on specific PRs, read on below.
GLM 5.3 was the only model affected by this bug. Every other disaggregated deployment on Workers AI has KV pools larger than its context length on both prefill and decode, so no request could reach the rejection path. We have applied the engine fix and the hardening described below to every model we serve with SGLang, and our deployment checks require them for every new deployment.
GLM 5.3 launched on Workers AI with a prefill KV pool smaller than its context window. The exposure was present from launch.
Cloudflare begins verifying the HackerOne report.
Security incident declared. Product Security reproduced the leak using two independent accounts within 25 minutes.
After confirming the scope of the issue, GLM 5.3 was setÂ to private. Requests return HTTP 400. Status page updated.
Root cause identified as the prefill pool being smaller than the context length. Canary prefill node with a larger pool confirmed not susceptible.
All prefill nodes rolled to the corrected configuration.
Full deployment rebuilt with the corrected configuration plus a Cloudflare-authored engine patch that correctly returns errors for requests rejected by the prefill scheduler. Validated against the researcher's reproduction script.
Meeting with the SGLang maintainers (RadixArk CTO and core engineers) to agree on upstream fixes.
Additional hardening rolled to all production SGLang deployments (details below).
Upstream SGLang merges the admission fix, per-transfer checksums, abort-ACK preservation, and turns deferred KV release on by default.
Coordinated publication with the researcher and RadixArk.
This bug belongs to a class of KV cache memory-safety bugs that Cloudflare has been working to address for several months. In each case, a page is freed, reused, or read while something else still has a claim on it. We see two common causes.
The first is page lifetime within a single node. Several tasks on a decode node can hold the same page at once: token generation, offload to host memory, the KV transfer receiver, and the abort and error paths. If one of them frees the page while another is still using it, a new request can be given that page while it is still being read or written. Our earlier fixes for decode offload ( #24226 , #30899 ) and double release on grammar errors ( #30937 ) were of this kind.
The second is a race across nodes. When a request is aborted while prefill is still writing its KV cache to decode over RDMA, the writes already sent cannot be recalled. If decode frees those pages right away, those pages can be given to another request, and the late writes land in that request's KV cache. Cloudflare has contributed to the effort to fix this race through proposed fixes ( #31357 , #38961 ) and a reproduction script ( #32564 ). In both cases the result is corrupted output, or one user's data in another user's response, with no error raised. The bug in this incident was different: a rejected request went through the handoff every time, rather than by a timing accident. But it had the same result: decode reading pages this request never wrote. None of these covered the failure in this incident in which prefill rejected the request, and decode never learned of it.
All of these changes were released to our disaggregated production deployments.
We met with the SGLang maintainers at RadixArk on September 10, the day after the incident. We agreed that RadixArk would investigate the race conditions we had reported, upstream the integrity-checking idea, and build reproduction tests for this class of bug.
The following have landed on SGLang main to address this incident and related KV cache race conditions, and all but one are included in v0.5.22. Operators running disaggregated SGLang should update to v0.5.22 or backport these patches as needed.Â
Retires aborted prefill requests before their result reaches decode. This stops the exposure in this incident.
Rejects these requests at admission, before any bootstrap, allocation, or KV transfer. Follows the approach in Cloudflare's draft patch, #38704 .
sgl-router Â cancels both halves of a request on client disconnect or prefill failure.
Enables deferred KV release only on backends that support it, then turns it on by default.
Fixes cases where the drain confirmation was lost, so releases happen on confirmation instead of waiting out the timeout.
Holds pages on every transfer failure, not only decode-initiated aborts.
Fixes a regression in the abort notification path.
A failed Mooncake send no longer reports its writes as drained.
Tags abort messages per request so a reused ID cannot consume a stale confirmation. Adds MORI support.
Shares the prefill-to-decode failure notification across Mooncake, NIXL, and MORI.
Optional cap on Mooncake transfer batch size, so one timed-out call cannot leave an unbounded number of writes in flight.
Decode waits for an in-progress offload to host memory before retracting a request and freeing its pages. Authored by Cloudflare.
Keeps tensor-parallel ranks in agreement when a host-memory cache restore fails.
Adds --disaggregation-enable-kv-checksum : decode verifies a checksum of the transferred KV before generating. Cleanup in #39729 , merged and awaiting release.
Fixes for SGLang's KV canary, which detects and logs potential corruption.
Metrics for deferred release: count, duration, and whether each hold ended on drain confirmation or timeout.
These follow-ups are still works in progress:
If you run SGLang in disaggregated prefill/decode mode, we recommend the following:
Configuration checks and lifecycle fixes reduce the number of ways a page can be misused. They do not make misuse impossible, and this incident is a reminder that the next bug will have a shape we have not seen. The durable answer is for the engine to detect, at read time, that a request is about to attend over a page it does not own, and fail that one request rather than return someone else's data.
We built a prototype of this over the summer and described it in August . Every physical KV page carries a tag that changes when the page is reallocated, each request records the tags it expects, and the mapping is checked before decode reads the cache. In our tests it cost under 1% in throughput and tail latency. We tested it on GLM 5.2 in mid-August, but disabled it shortly afterwards due to reliability issues.
The prototype was also tied to specific attention backends and model architectures, so it could not be a general fix. We are working with the SGLang team to build a production version into the engine that works across every model, rather than maintaining Cloudflare-specific patches. The per-transfer checksum in #39500 Â is a first step: it validates the handoff from prefill to decode. Page-level tags go further, because they check every read, including reads long after the transfer.
RDMA copies data directly from one nodeâs memory to anotherâs. Itâs vital for the two machines to agree on where the data goes, how large it is, and when itâs finished; any mismatch can cause the receiver to read the wrong data. This bug is an example of a consistency failure in a distributed system, in which the two machines had inconsistent views of the state of that system.
Elsewhere in Cloudflare, we have put effort into proving the safety of distributed systems using formal verification methods. Topaz Â enables conflict-free IP selection for our authoritative DNS servers. Models of Meerkatâs Â QuePaxa implementation have demonstrated consistency bugs that were subsequently fixed.
We are now directing our experience in formal methods to KV cache transfer engines. This will start with modeling and proving the safety of an RDMA-based KV cache transfer protocol. The goal is to model our production SGLangâs distributed KV cache system using Mooncake, then track and fix any divergence from the safety properties we want to guarantee. The aim is to prove â as far as possible â that a bug like this cannot occur again. Realistically, we expect gaps in what the provers can tell us, but proving the rest of the system allows us to more closely review and monitor those gaps.
We are publishing this report as part of a coordinated disclosure. We want to thank the researcher, Gadi Evron, who reported this through our HackerOne program with a clear, reproducible script and gave us time to fix it and to coordinate with the SGLang maintainers before publishing. We also want to thank the SGLang team at RadixArk, who treated this as their problem as well as ours and landed the upstream fixes with urgency.
If you find a security issue in Workers AI, please report it at hackerone.com/cloudflare .

title: Ballon d’Or 2026: Alexia Putellas wins Best Women’s Player award for third time
body: Barcelona midfielder Alexia Putellas has won the 2026 Women’s Ballon d’Or, claiming the prestigious individual award for the third time in her career. The Spanish international was crowned the best women’s footballer at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony, adding another major individual honour to her impressive career. Putellas, one of the most decorated players in women’s football, previously won the award in 2021 and 2022, becoming the first woman to claim the Women’s Ballon d’Or in consecutive years. Her latest triumph further strengthens her legacy as one of the leading figures in the women’s game, following years of success with Barcelona and the Spain national team. The midfielder has played a key role in Barcelona’s dominance in domestic and European competitions, earning recognition for her technical ability, creativity and leadership. Winning the award for a third time places Putellas among the most successful recipients in the history of the Women’s Ballon d’Or. title: Polish Sejm Speaker: Threat from Russia is growing
body:
Czarzasty made the remarks at a convention of the Left party in Rzeszów, Ukrinform reports, citing Polish Radio .
“There is currently no threat of Russian troops entering Poland and war breaking out here. I am not trying to cause panic, but a responsible politician must recognize that, two kilometers from the Polish border, a jet-powered drone struck a locomotive. They must also take note of the fact that we are suddenly seeing drones on the Baltic Sea beaches. They must see all these provocations,” the speaker said.
The Sejm speaker also urged Polish President Karol Nawrocki not to claim that he does not see the growing threat from Russia.
Czarzasty was responding to an interview Nawrocki gave to Rzeczpospolita, in which the Polish president said he “does not see any fundamental change in the level of the Russian threat.”
As reported by Ukrinform, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk has warned that Russia could escalate tensions before Christmas, including by stepping up acts of sabotage and provocations in Poland.

title: Russo-Ukrainian war, day 1706: In two weeks, Washington sanctioned court prosecuting Putin, waived its own sanctions on Russia, and called him humanitarian
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); Exclusive A short guide to the linguicide of the Ukrainian language | Infographics (updated) . Full speed returned to Ukraine’s satellite links on Saturday morning. “We simply enforced our terms,” Musk claims after blaming Washington for 10 days . The SpaceX owner, who had earlier said the US government decides such limits, wrote that his company had closed a gap he says Ukrainian troops used for drone strikes. This is the fancy new F-16 Ukraine could get. It’s not what its pilots need most. . Ukraine could buy newly built F-16 Block 70/72s from US firm Lockheed Martin. But that's not the greatest need. Ukraine now fights two enemies. One is America . In two weeks, Washington sanctioned the court prosecuting Putin, waived its own sanctions on Russia, and called him a humanitarian. Military For the third time this year, Ukrainian drones hit Russia’s rocket-fuel rubber plant in Samara Oblast. This time they reach the raw-material shop feeding it . OSINT channels recorded fires at the same butyl-rubber shops in April and September. Captured Russians say there is one place on Kupiansk front they will not go: “Orion” safety corridor . Ukrainian robot unit says it built that corridor, and runs supply and evacuation through it with almost no losses. Russia apparently meant a tank division for Druzhkivka. A Ukrainian push in the south drew the bigger part of it away . A Ukrainian observer says the larger part of the division ended up defending near Velyka Novosilka rather than attacking toward the Donbas fortress cities. Plane parts for Russia’s air force, rubber for its industry—Voronezh’s factories came under drone attack . The aircraft plant belongs to Russia's state aviation holding, and the rubber plant to the petrochemical giant Sibur. Intelligence and technology Ukraine plans to rebuild its air force on NATO’s model by 2035. Its Air Force already knows which fighter it wants next, and why . Ukraine’s F-16s face thousands of Russian targets a month, many of them worn jets bought secondhand. Ukrainian intelligence: Russia can probably add 10–15 Su-34 bombers a year, but no new Tu-95s or Tu-22M3s . Ukraine’s military intelligence also listed Russian jets destroyed or critically damaged in 2026, including two Tu-95MS bombers hit at Engels. Ukraine raises its stalled Patriot request with Washington again after almost a month without Hegseth’s signature . The order came after a meeting with Ukraine’s defense minister, foreign minister, and army chief on supplies of air defense interceptors. International Ukraine’s Zelenskyy welcomes Student List’s win in Serbia and says Kyiv is “ready to keep increasing cooperation” . The party itself plan to end the trade that brought Ukraine €800 million in ammunition. 17 public broadcasters mapped Russia’s hybrid war on Europe. Germany: four dots . One point on the map may stand for several incidents of the same type nearby or in quick succession. Kazakhstan prepares a list for Moscow, Kenya appeals to Kyiv: three governments try to get citizens out of Russia’s war . Kyrgyzstan says some of its migrants are forced into contracts, and Russia told Kenya that unit commanders rule on requests to quit, case by case. More than a US briefing: Brussels security talks on Ukraine planned for 27 or 28 October, Kyiv says . Zelenskyy also ruled out neutrality and limits on Ukraine’s army as the Kremlin says Putin is ready in principle for new three-way talks in mid-November. Humanitarian and social impact Sixteen Ukrainian doctors who work near fighting went through three Western trauma programs in one week. American surgeons led drills . On the front line, drones and shrapnel often tear through several parts of a soldier’s body at once. Guided bombs on Izium, strikes on Zaporizhzhia: Russian overnight attacks wound six, later strikes kill three . It was the second night running that Russia sent at least 140 drones, and strikes hit 15 locations both times. Drones keep sinking ships off Romania and Bulgaria—French and US patrol planes are watching . Days after NATO promised more planes and forensic teams, a drone sank a cargo ship near Constanța, killing a Ukrainian sailor. Political and legal developments Russia promises “favorable conditions” to European firms a month after seizing control of Nestlé and Auchan . In a state TV interview, the Kremlin’s leader claimed Russia’s friends in Europe nearly cried when European companies had to leave, while his own decrees handed the Russian businesses of firms that stayed to Kremlin-picked managers. Ukraine is stalling EU-required reform of bureau that can raid any official, risking European money it badly needs . The version the government may pass would satisfy Brussels on paper but leave the State Bureau of Investigation under the President’s Office. Read our earlier daily review here .

title: Labourer fined GH¢120,000 for possessing and selling cannabis and tramadol
body: A 20-year-old labourer, Kojo Sah Nkrumah, has been fined GH¢120,000 by the Tarkwa Circuit Court for possessing and selling cannabis and tramadol without lawful authority. Nkrumah, who pleaded guilty to two counts of possession and selling of narcotic drugs without lawful authority, will serve three years in prison in default of payment. The court, presided over by Ms Bernice Mensimah Ackon, convicted and sentenced him on his own plea. Prosecuting, Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) Samuel Ahiabor told the court that the complainants were police officers stationed at the Western Central Regional Formed Police Unit (RFPU) Base in Tarkwa. He said Nkrumah, a resident of Tarkwa Railway Station, was arrested at about 0130 hours on January 21, 2025, during a routine night patrol by a police team, led by Chief Inspector Issahaque Yahaya. The prosecution said the officers extended their patrol to the Tarkwa Railway Station, where they found Nkrumah seated under a shed selling substances suspected to be narcotic drugs. A search of a takeaway bag in his possession uncovered 81 pieces of wrapped dried leaves suspected to be cannabis, seven sachets of tramadol and GH¢240 in cash, believed to be proceeds from the sale of the substances. The prosecution said officers subsequently escorted Nkrumah to the Tarkwa Police Station with the exhibits. On April 25, 2025, the exhibits were sent to the Forensic Crime Laboratory in Accra for examination. A report received on May 13, 2025, showed that the plant material tested positive for delta-9-tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), the principal psychoactive compound in cannabis, with a gross weight of 139.61 grammes.

title: Chris Brown given suspended eight-month prison sentence over nightclub attack
body: US singer Chris Brown has avoided jail after striking a man twice in the head with a glass tequila bottle in a London nightclub. The R&B star was given an eight-month prison sentence, suspended for 12 months, over the attack at private members’ club Tape in Mayfair, in the early hours of 19 February 2023. Brown’s vocal coach, rapper Omololu Akinlolu, who joined the attack, was sentenced to four months’ imprisonment, suspended for 12 months. Both men, who had pleaded guilty to affray, were also ordered to pay £1,500 in costs. Judge Tony Baumgartner said Brown’s use of the glass bottle to hit the victim twice over the head “was plainly dangerous”, adding that the violence of the attack was “intense”. The sentence means Brown will not be imprisoned unless he commits another offence during the 12-month period of suspension. The court heard Brown’s attack on music producer Abraham ‘Abe’ Diaw left the victim in need of hospital treatment for his injuries. In sentencing, Judge Baumgartner said: “The repeated use of a glass bottle in that way, especially aimed at the head, was plainly dangerous, it carried the risk of delivering a more serious injury than was ultimately sustained.” CCTV footage was shown where Brown struck Diaw four times with the bottle, connecting twice with his head, and then hitting his shoulder. Sentencing Brown, Judge Baumgartner said: “This was not planned violence. It was nevertheless serious violence by two people in a crowded nightclub.” Chris Brown (left) and Omololu Akinlolu were sentenced at Southwark Crown Court on Monday The judge told Brown: “Violence of this kind in a crowded nightclub is serious, it creates an obvious risk, not only to the person against whom it is directed, but also to others nearby.” He added that Brown’s conduct was “particularly dangerous” and that he had to be “physically pulled away” from the attack. The judge said Brown’s fame, commercial success and professional standing “do not entitle you to special treatment – the law applies equally to everyone”. But judge Baumgartner also said he had noted Brown’s guilty plea, compliance with bail conditions, and the impact a custodial sentence would have on Brown’s children, and said the singer’s “risk of further offending is low”. Brown and Akinlolu pleaded guilty to a charge of affray at Southwark Crown Court in July. The singer was due to face a trial on more serious charges, which he denied and which were later dropped. These were assault, attempting to cause grievous bodily harm, and having an offensive weapon. Following Brown and Akinlolu’s guilty pleas, the CPS released a statement outlining that Brown had approached Diaw on the dance floor, hitting him over the head with a glass bottle twice, before Akinlolu then punched Diaw in the head. “They continued their assault whilst the victim attempted to flee through the club,” the CPS said. “The victim was kicked while he was seated defenceless on the floor.” Judge Baumgartner told the pair that while he had concluded they had both crossed the threshold for jail, this year’s changes to sentencing laws meant he had to put off doing so unless there were exceptional reasons. “I have considered whether the seriousness of the offending, taken together with the need for punishment and deterrence, amounts to exceptional circumstances requiring immediate imprisonment. I have concluded, in relation to each of you, that it does not,” he said. “These were serious offences deserving of custodial sentences, but the circumstances do not justify displacing the [new legal] requirement that those sentences be suspended.” Brown’s vocal coach, rapper Omololu Akinlolu, also previously pleaded guilty to affray On Monday, the court was shown three pieces of CCTV footage from inside Tape nightclub on the night of the attack. The attack lasted no more than 20 seconds, but Brown could be seen hitting the victim four times with a tequila bottle, twice to the head. Prosecutor, Heidi Stonecliffe KC, described the weapon as a “heavy square-shaped tequila bottle” and said Diaw was approached by Brown at around 03:00. The footage showed that the nightclub was very small and packed at the time. The defence described Chris Brown as a “dedicated and loving father of four children,” someone who is “positive and present”. The singer is described as having lived “a good and law-abiding life” since his last conviction in 2013. The defence described the events at Tape nightclub as a “short and deeply regretted incident”. Brown’s defence lawyer told the court that he apologises to all those present at the club at the time of the attack. “This is an ugly and unattractive incident,” Sallie Bennett-Jenkins KC said. “It is, however, an incident which was very short-lived, lasting something more than 17 seconds but no more than 20. “It is something which undoubtedly would have caused distress to those who are present and for which Mr Brown… offers a profound apology to all those present.” The court heard Akinlolu “genuinely believed” that Brown was “under attack” when he joined the attack, punching Diaw. Brown was described as being like a “brother” to Akinlolu, his lawyer Laurie-Anne Power KC told the court. She added: “He genuinely believed him to be under attack and became involved, and thereafter accepts his initial involvement very quickly evolved into the events he has pleaded guilty to.” Diaw was taken to St Mary’s Hospital in London after the attack. Ms Stonecliffe KC said he was discharged with “pain relief and a diagnosis of head injury and superficial injury of the knee”. An MRI scan taken in early March showed a “high grade injury to a ligament on the inner side of the left knee”, the court heard. Defending Brown, Ms Bennett-Jenkins KC said there was a “relatively low level of force” and disputed how significant the injuries were. The defence argued that the attack left no fractures or broken skin and there was an absence of serious injuries. Diaw, the victim, was “not supportive of the prosecution” and “withdrew” his support some time after the incident, the court heard. Chris Brown is one of R&B’s most successful singers, with hits including Yeah 3x and Forever Brown and Akinlolu stood, faced each other, and clasped hands after the judge finished his sentencing remarks before walking out of the glass dock. Loud cheers rang out outside the court as Chris Brown left the building and appeared to stop to sign an autograph. After the sentencing, Brown shared a video from inside his car on his Instagram story, showing him looking out the window before turning to the camera and giving a thumbs-up. Affray is an offence under the Public Order Act, and a person is deemed guilty in law if they use or threaten “unlawful violence towards another” with their behaviour, leading someone to fear for their personal safety. Brown, 37, is considered one of the biggest stars in R&B, with a string of hit songs including Turn Up The Music, Ayo, Freaky Friday, Run It, Forever, Yeah 3x and Don’t Wake Me Up.

title: US Air Force plans US$1 billion Nellis complex for F-47 operational testing
body:
The U.S. Air Force plans to spend about US$1.06 billion on a new complex at Nellis Air Force Base in Nevada to support operational testing of the Boeing F-47, providing the first detailed picture of the infrastructure being prepared for the sixth-generation fighter.
A draft solicitation released on October 22 calls for a dedicated F-47 campus with aircraft hangars, laboratories, simulator facilities, maintenance areas and supporting infrastructure. The first major facilities are scheduled to be completed in March 2031, about three years after the fighter's planned first flight.
The Air Force intends to select up to four design-build teams, although it prefers a single contractor capable of handling the initial projects. An award is targeted for February 2027, followed by design and preconstruction work through November of that year and approximately 40 months of construction.
The first phase includes a 116,745-square-foot (10,846-square-meter) combined operations and maintenance hangar, a 39,200-square-foot (3,642-square-meter) reprogramming laboratory and a 40,903-square-foot (3,800-square-meter) simulator facility.
Follow Air Data News: WhatsApp | Instagram | LinkedIn | Twitter | Facebook
An aircraft apron covering about 1.15 million square feet (107,000 square meters), equipped with sunshades, will also be built on the eastern side of Nellis.
The facilities provide some indication of how the Air Force intends to conduct operational testing of an aircraft whose capabilities remain largely classified.
According to Air Force budget documents, the reprogramming laboratory will maintain avionics-specific hardware and allow rapid reprogramming and validation of mission data. It will include space for reprogramming engineers, intelligence and information technology personnel, data management and a server farm.
The simulator complex will have four bays and integration space for multi-platform testing and training, allowing the F-47 to be evaluated in scenarios involving other aircraft and systems.
Both installations will contain highly secured areas designed to handle classified and Special Access Program activities.
Additional facilities planned through 2032 include a fuel-system maintenance hangar, a low-observable corrosion-control hangar, a weapons-load training hangar, a consolidated maintenance facility and a maintenance training center.
The Air Force had already disclosed in its fiscal year 2027 budget proposal that Nellis would host F-47 operational testing. It requested US$730.7 million for the project during the fiscal year, against a total authorized cost of US$1.057 billion.
Nellis currently performs combined developmental and operational testing of another Boeing fighter, the F-15EX Eagle II.
The construction program adds another element to preparations for the F-47 after Boeing began manufacturing the first aircraft in 2025.
The Air Force selected Boeing in March 2025 for the engineering and manufacturing development phase of the Next Generation Air Dominance fighter program. The aircraft is intended to eventually replace the Lockheed Martin F-22 Raptor.
The first F-47 is expected to fly in 2028. Air Force officials said this year that the program remained on schedule and had reached what they described as an "unprecedented" level of maturity during engineering and manufacturing development.
The service is also changing how the new fighter will be evaluated. Air Force Test Center commander Brig. Gen. Mark Massaro said earlier this month that developmental and operational testing will be more closely integrated, with simulation and virtual environments used to accelerate the campaign rather than treating the two phases as largely sequential programs.
That approach makes the simulator and reprogramming facilities at Nellis particularly relevant. The F-47 is being developed not simply as a replacement for the F-22 but as one element of the wider Next Generation Air Dominance architecture, which also includes Collaborative Combat Aircraft, new weapons and networked mission systems.
The Air Force has previously disclosed that the F-47 is expected to exceed Mach 2 and have a combat radius greater than 1,000 nautical miles (1,852 km). The service has indicated a requirement for more than 185 aircraft.
Nellis has been confirmed as the operational test location, but the Air Force has not yet announced the first operational base for the F-47.

title: Ballon d’or 2026: De la Fuente wins coach of the Year Award after Spain’s World Cup triumph
body: Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente has been named the 2026 Men’s Coach of the Year at the Ballon d’Or ceremony in London, capping a remarkable year in which he led the national team to FIFA World Cup glory. The 65-year-old claimed the Johan Cruyff Trophy on Monday, October 26, after Spain defeated Argentina 1-0 in the World Cup final on July 19, securing the country’s second men’s world title. De la Fuente’s latest achievement adds another major honour to a coaching career that has flourished since he took charge of Spain’s senior national team in December 2022. His World Cup success has also placed him among the most accomplished coaches in Spanish football, following the country’s victories at the 2023 UEFA Nations League and Euro 2024. De la Fuente beats coaching heavyweights The Spanish tactician emerged ahead of an impressive shortlist featuring Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta, Paris Saint-Germain’s Luis Enrique, Aston Villa boss Unai Emery and Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany. The award recognises De la Fuente’s work in guiding Spain through a successful international campaign, culminating in victory over Argentina in a dramatic final that was decided in extra time. Spain secured the trophy through Ferran Torres’ 106th-minute strike after Argentina had held them goalless during normal time. The victory also made De la Fuente the oldest coach to win the men’s FIFA World Cup, at 65 years and 28 days, surpassing the previous record held by compatriot Vicente del Bosque, who led Spain to the 2010 title. Spain’s historic World Cup campaign Spain’s triumph was built on a disciplined and largely dominant tournament performance. De la Fuente’s side went unbeaten throughout their eight matches at the expanded 2026 World Cup, conceding just one goal during the competition. Goalkeeper Unai Simón also recorded seven clean sheets, setting a tournament record for the most shutouts by a goalkeeper in a single men’s World Cup edition. Spain’s victory over Argentina further strengthened the country’s position among international football’s leading forces, adding the world title to its recent continental and international successes. The achievement also made Spain the first country to hold the men’s and women’s FIFA World Cup titles simultaneously, following the women’s team’s triumph in 2023. A new milestone for Spain’s coach The Johan Cruyff Trophy gives De la Fuente individual recognition for the success he has overseen with Spain, following years of development work within the country’s national-team system. Before taking charge of the senior side, he worked with Spain’s youth teams, helping develop players who have since become central to the national team’s success. His senior-team achievements include the 2023 Nations League, Euro 2024 and the 2026 World Cup, a run of major honours that has established his reputation among Europe’s leading international coaches. The 2026 award also places a national-team manager at the top of a category whose previous winners came from the club game, marking a significant moment for international coaching. For De la Fuente, the recognition completes an extraordinary year in which Spain returned to the summit of world football and his work on the touchline earned one of the sport’s most prestigious individual coaching honours.

title: James Comey faces potential prosecution again from Trump admin
body:
The Trump administration is attempting to prosecute James Comey for what it calls a decade-old leak of classified information, an effort the former FBI director’s lawyers immediately dismissed as invalid and outside the time limit for when the Justice Department can file a case.
The allegations from the Justice Department came in documents unsealed Monday in federal court in Washington that shed light on a fight that has played out behind closed doors over the last month. It comes as prosecutors try to bring what would be the third criminal case against Comey, a longtime critic and foe of President Donald Trump , since the Republican returned to the White House last year.
“Well, they’re back — again,” Comey said in a video statement released after the documents dropped. “It would almost be funny if it weren’t such an appalling abuse of the Department of Justice – one that we cannot become numb to. Nothing’s changed with me; I’m still innocent, I’m still not afraid of these people — and I still believe in an independent federal judiciary.”
The Justice Department, for its part, said it had filed what’s known as a criminal information to extend the 10-year statute of limitations for bringing a case.
“Filing a criminal information to toll the statute of limitations is a widely recognized practice in federal court and has been approved by multiple Circuit Courts of Appeals. This is an ongoing criminal investigation, and we will not comment further,” a department spokesperson said.
Comey was the FBI director when Trump took office in 2017, having been appointed by then-President Barack Obama, a Democrat, and serving before that as a senior Justice Department official in President George W. Bush’s Republican administration.
But the relationship was strained from the start, including after Comey resisted a request by Trump at a private dinner to pledge his personal loyalty to the president — an overture that so unnerved the FBI director that he documented it in a contemporaneous memorandum.
Trump fired Comey in May 2017 amid an FBI investigation into potential ties between Russia and Trump’s campaign. That inquiry, later taken over by special counsel Robert Mueller, found that while Russia interfered in the 2016 election and the Trump team welcomed the help, there was insufficient evidence to prove a criminal collaboration.

title: Otti celebrates Ebitu Ukiwe at 86, urges Nigeria to recognise his contribution to democracy
body:
Governor Alex Otti of Abia State has felicitated with an illustrious Abia statesman and former Chief of General Staff, Commodore Ebitu Okoh Ukiwe, on the occasion of his 86th birthday.
The felicitation is contained in a message issued on Monday, 26 October by Ferdinand Ekeoma, the special adviser on media and publicity to Governor Otti.
In the goodwill birthday message, Governor Otti extolled the revered statesman, describing him as a distinguished Nigerian with sound character and a proven track record of excellence.
According to the Governor: “It is a thing of joy to celebrate a father figure; a distinguished Nigerian statesman and an accomplished military professional with sound character and a proven track record of excellence.
“Ochiagha Ebitu Okoh Ukiwe is, by all estimations, a national icon with sound principles and impeccable character. He is indeed the pride of Abia, hence we are glad and proud to celebrate him on a day like this.”
Governor Otti recalled how Commodore Ukiwe resigned his exalted position as the number two citizen of the country to uphold his principles and reputation, describing him as a rare gem who should be referenced as a great example to the present generation of politicians and public office holders.
The Abia Chief Executive also remembered the role Commodore Ukiwe played in the fight to restore democracy in Nigeria when he led other compatriots to form NADECO which fought for the restoration of the 12 June, 1993 victory of the late Chief M.K.O Abiola, and called on the nation to give him his due recognition for the exemplary roles he played for the peace of the nation and for the restoration of democracy.
Governor Otti disclosed that his government will roll out the drums to celebrate Commodore Ukiwe’s 86th birthday as a mark of honour and recognition of his service to the nation and humanity.
Governor Otti, on behalf of his family, the government and people of Abia State, thanked Commodore Ukiwe for being the pride of Abia State, and prayed God to uphold and bless him with good health to celebrate many more beautiful birthdays ahead in sound health.

title: Pennant has more than 50 stitches after dog attack
body: Former Premier League footballer Jermaine Pennant says he needed more than 50 stitches after being mauled by a dog. The 43-year-old was walking his two dogs in north London last week when he was attacked by a German Shepherd. The former Liverpool and Stoke City winger said the dog latched on to his leg and refused to let go as he tried to protect his own dog, King. King then intervened to help fight off the attacking dog, preventing “what could’ve been a horrendous situation”, Pennant said in a post on Instagram., Pennant told the Sun he required more than 50 stitches to his right leg after sustaining four bite wounds in the attack and receiving hospital treatment. He added that King was unhurt, but did not give details about the German Shepherd. He said he declined to report the attack to police. “So I was attacked by a German Shepherd. I tried to protect King, but the dog got my leg. I was on the floor with the dog still attached, with no sign of letting go, until King intervened, as he didn’t know what was going on,” said Pennant. “But the minute he did, he fought the dog off and saved what could’ve been a horrendous situation for me. “King was unhurt, with a little nip on his leg, but had blood all over him which wasn’t mine. At this point I forgot the agony I was in, and my heart sank, but it wasn’t King’s.” The picture uploaded to Instagram shows Pennant with a bandage on his leg alongside King on a sofa, while he also thanked his partner, Mimmi Montgomery, for looking after them. “My hero still protecting me and trying to look after me. King, you’re a legend, love you, man’s best friend. Thanks, Mimmi Montgomery, for taking care of us both.” Pennant, a Talksport pundit, made 231 Premier League appearances in a 19-year career before retiring in 2018. At 15, before his professional debut, Pennant became the most expensive trainee in English football when he joined Arsenal from Notts County for £2.5m.

title: Work Advances on Road Cutting Ioannina–Albania Trip to 40 Minutes
body: Work on the Ioannina-Kakavia road is moving ahead in Epirus, and once it opens, drivers should reach the Albanian border from Ioannina in about 35 to 40 minutes. The new route runs for about 70 kilometres north of the city. It forms part of the Orient/East-Med trans-European transport corridor. On a wider scale, the road also belongs to the “Blue Corridor”, which links Trieste in Italy with Kalamata. A new video shows the progress so far. It follows the route from the Egnatia Odos junction, past the Zoodochos area and the Ioannina Industrial Area. Where work on the Ioannina-Kakavia road stands Crews are active at three main points. These are Kosmira, Asvestochori and the junction that will join the new route to the Ionia Odos and Egnatia Odos motorways. At that junction, plans include a bridge of about 560 metres with 14 spans. Earthworks also continue along the alignment. The Ioannina-Kakavia road has two sections. From Ioannina to Kalpaki, the first stretch covers 46.4 kilometres with six grade-separated junctions. These include an optional 1.47-kilometre link at Passaron. A second section will upgrade the existing 23.1-kilometre road from Kalpaki to the Kakavia border station. Together, the two sections will act as the western north–south axis of the Egnatia Odos. Crews are building the extension of the Ionia Odos as an expressway. Unlike a full motorway, it has sections of 2+1 lanes. Antirrio to Albania in two hours and 15 minutes When the works finish, the main axis will start at Antirrio. It will then pass through Messolonghi, Agrinio, Arta and Ioannina before ending at Kakavia. Once complete, the full trip of about 264 kilometres should take around two hours and 15 minutes. The budget for the Ioannina-Kakavia road stands at €310 million. It is the biggest new road project in Epirus since the Ionia Odos opened in full in 2017. The project also joins other road plans, such as a new motorway in western Greece . Planners also want the road to end the isolation of mountain villages in the area. At the same time, they hope Epirus becomes a gateway for trade and tourism between Western Europe and the southern Balkans. Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis attended the contract signing at Kalpaki in December 2024. There, he described the road as “a bridge of friendship between Greece and Albania” . He added that the project mattered above all to the Greek national minority in Albania. Kakavia, where the Ioannina-Kakavia road ends, is a key crossing for travel between the two countries. Previously, Greece and Albania have also worked together at the border . According to an update in June on the government’s official roads website, the Ioannina-Kakavia road should be complete in December 2029. title: Ebola: Why Nigeria evacuated patient to Switzerland – NCDC
body:
Nigeria’s decision to evacuate its confirmed Ebola patient to Switzerland was based on diplomatic considerations, human rights and international health regulations, the Director-General of the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), Jide Idris, has revealed.
Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Monday, Mr Idris said the federal government approved the transfer after consultations with the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate, and assurances that adequate infection prevention measures would be maintained throughout the journey.
The clarification follows an earlier report that the patient, a woman who is the wife of a Swiss diplomat in Nigeria, was evacuated through the private jet wing of the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport in Abuja.
Mr Idris dismissed suggestions that the government had secretly removed the patient from Nigeria, saying the evacuation followed a formal request from the Swiss Embassy.
“I won’t use the word ‘snuck out’. That’s a no-brainer. It is the first time something like that has happened,” he said.
He said the government weighed the implications of the transfer for public health, international health regulations and the patient’s rights before granting approval.
According to him, officials ensured that infection prevention and control protocols were followed from the hospital where the patient was receiving treatment to the aircraft that transported her.
Mr Idris said the patient had tested positive twice before her evacuation, explaining that improvements in her clinical condition did not necessarily mean she had cleared the virus.
He commended the Nigerian medical team for stabilising her condition, which he said had deteriorated to the point of multiple organ failure.
“There are no drugs to deal with this virus,” Mr Idris said, referring to the absence of an established antiviral treatment specifically targeting the Bundibugyo virus responsible for the current outbreak.
Mr Pate earlier confirmed that Nigeria’s Ebola patient and her husband arrived safely in Switzerland on Monday following their medical evacuation from Abuja.
In an update posted on his official X account, Mr Pate said the patient was receiving treatment at Geneva University Hospitals, while her husband had been placed in isolation at University Hospital Zurich.
“The Swiss authorities have confirmed that the patient and her spouse arrived safely in Switzerland today,” he said.
Nigeria confirmed its first Ebola case on 20 October, after a 42-year-old Ugandan-born woman living in Abuja tested positive for the disease.
The patient had returned to Nigeria on 3 October after travelling to Uganda and developed symptoms few days later.
She was subsequently admitted to a health facility in Abuja, where she received treatment in isolation before her evacuation to Switzerland on Monday.
Following her evacuation, the World Health Organisation (WHO) said Nigeria had no active confirmed Ebola cases, although contact monitoring and other containment measures were continuing.
The WHO said Nigeria was continuing to monitor 52 contacts, while Switzerland had taken responsibility for the patient’s care and monitoring her husband, who was among the 53 contacts previously identified.
The NCDC had earlier identified 53 primary contacts linked to the confirmed case, including healthcare workers, the patient’s husband, domestic staff and personnel involved in collecting samples.
Health authorities are monitoring the contacts for possible symptoms to detect any additional infections and prevent further transmission.
Mr Pate had earlier said Nigeria could declare the Ebola outbreak over as early as 7 December if no further confirmed or probable cases were detected.
Mr Idris urged Nigerians to maintain good hand hygiene and exercise caution during mass gatherings, particularly where close physical contact could occur.
He said handwashing could reduce the spread of several infectious diseases, while recommending measures to limit unnecessary physical contact in crowded settings.
However, he stressed that Ebola is not airborne. The virus spreads primarily through direct contact with the blood or other bodily fluids of an infected person, or with contaminated materials.
He advised people who develop symptoms consistent with Ebola, particularly after contact with a suspected or confirmed case, to seek prompt medical guidance.
Mr Idris also cautioned against relying on herbal mixtures to prevent or cure the disease, saying there was no established evidence that such preparations could prevent or treat Ebola. He warned that some herbal products could also cause harmful side effects.

title: AUKUS: USS Colorado Announced as First Submarine for SRF – West
body: U.S. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, Australian Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Defence Richard Marles, and UK Secretary of State for Defence Wes Streeting are pleased to announce the designation of the USS Colorado (SSN 788) as the first U.S. Navy Virginia-class fast-attack submarine assigned to Submarine Rotational Force-West (SRF-West) beginning in late 2027. U.S. Department of War press release This announcement comes ahead of the upcoming United States Submarine Maintenance Period, which begins later this week and will further demonstrate Australia’s growing ability to sustain U.S. and UK nuclear-powered fast-attack submarines. SRF-West is projected to host up to four U.S. fast-attack submarines and one UK fast-attack submarine on a rotational basis at HMAS Stirling, a Royal Australian Navy base in Western Australia. SRF-West will accelerate Australia’s readiness to own, operate, maintain, and regulate a sovereign, conventionally armed, nuclear-powered submarine capability, as well as support submarine deployments by expanding maintenance options and sustainment infrastructure in the region for AUKUS partners. SRF-West, established at Australia’s invitation and as mutually determined, will operate in accordance with relevant international agreements between and among the United States, Australia, and the UK, including the United States – Australia Force Posture Agreement. AUKUS activities associated with SRF-West will be conducted consistent with the AUKUS partners’ respective international obligations, including those under the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons, and Australia’s obligations under the South Pacific Nuclear Free Zone Treaty (Treaty of Rarotonga). As President Trump has stated, and Prime Minister Albanese and Prime Minister Burnham have reaffirmed, AUKUS is moving “full steam ahead.” The selection of USS Colorado (SSN 788) as the first submarine assigned to SRF-West in 2027 marks a significant milestone for AUKUS Pillar I and is a decisive step in strengthening collective deterrence in the Pacific. – End – The post AUKUS: USS Colorado Announced as First Submarine for SRF – West appeared first on Naval News .
