title: Trump faces backlash after invoking 9/11 in verbal assault on El-Sayed
body: US President Donald Trump is facing a backlash after invoking 9/11 as part of a verbal assault on Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic candidate for the US Senate in Michigan. Speaking at a rally in the state on Sunday, Trump accused El-Sayed of being “a jihadist”. He introduced as a guest speaker the father of a passenger who fought back against the 9/11 hijackers. Trump also suggested that El-Sayed would “have to go through a metal detector before he’s allowed to go into the Senate”. Critics condemned Trump’s attack as Islamophobic. El-Sayed himself responded to Trump’s decision to refer to him by his middle name, Mohamed, saying during a rally of his own: “I’ll be Senator Mohamed to you, bro.” He also said: “They think that by pointing at my name and my faith, that somehow you’re going to ignore the fact that you can’t afford your gas or your groceries, can’t see a doctor.” Appearing alongside him, Senator Bernie Sanders said: “The reason they are using Islamophobia against Abdul is because they have nothing to say about the real issues.” El-Sayed is taking on Republican candidate Mike Rogers on 3 November. The race is expected to be one of the closest in the midterm elections, and is proving to be particularly bitter. The seat is considered to be one of just a handful that could decide the balance of power in Congress. It is currently held by the Democrats. El-Sayed, a former public health official who was born in the US to Egyptian parents, will be the first Muslim elected to the US Senate if he wins the seat. He has previously dismissed the various attacks made against him by both Trump and Rogers and denied any connection to extremist groups. During his remarks on Sunday, Trump said: “If Abdul and the Democrats win, they will open the floodgates and invite hordes of jihadis to our shores, creating a nightmare of violence and terror until you cannot even have a Christmas.” Trump made a variety of allegations against El-Sayed and his family members, including that he was a member of the Muslim Brotherhood. He introduced as a guest speaker the father of Todd Beamer, a man from Michigan who was part of a group of passengers who fought back against the hijackers of United Airlines Flight 93, before the plane crashed in a field in Pennsylvania. “Michigan needs to stand up and fight, just like Todd did, to stop a jihadist from walking into the Capitol,” Trump said. Claims centre on proscribed Muslim Brotherhood El-Sayed’s opponents have sought to link him to the Muslim Brotherhood, an Islamist organisation that was founded in Egypt. Trump designated certain chapters of it as Foreign Terrorist Organisations earlier this year. Some of the scrutiny of the affiliations of El-Sayed and his family members relates to their writings from more than a decade ago. A social media post in 2012 by El-Sayed’s half-sister, Eman Abdelhadi, appeared to refer to the movement, saying “my family has long been MB”. El-Sayed’s team have previously distanced him from other comments by Abdelhadi. Critics have also pointed to an opinion piece El-Sayed wrote in Huffington Post in 2011 about pro-democracy protesters in Egypt. In it, he acknowledged concerns that “supporting democracy in Egypt might allow the country to fall to the hands of the Muslim Brotherhood”. A year later he also allegedly signed an open letter by Egyptian Americans. In it, the group urged Mohamed Morsi, Egypt’s first democratically elected president and a leader of the Muslim Brotherhood, to “purge the media and police” following the toppling of the authoritarian regime in the Arab Spring. This letter has not been discussed by El-Sayed. El-Sayed has previously denied any connection to the Muslim Brotherhood and has stressed his loyalty to the United States. Asked recently at a town hall event whether he would disavow the organisation, he responded: “Absolutely.” Also in 2012, El-Sayed’s current opponent Rogers, who was then a US representative and chairing the House Intelligence Committee, appeared to call for cautious engagement with the Muslim Brotherhood, telling Reuters : “Do I think there are moderate Muslim Brotherhood individuals we are going to have to reach out to and talk to? Yes but we are going to have to watch it carefully.” HA Hellyer, senior associate fellow at the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI) and an expert on Egypt, says the row has more to do with Islamophobia on the political right in the US than with the Trump administration’s actual position on the Muslim Brotherhood. “If the accusation is to be taken sincerely, then [Trump] should surely have a problem with engaging with any government that has engaged positively with the Brotherhood or with groups that are even more to the right of the Brotherhood,” Hellyer told the BBC. “He clearly has not done that.” ‘Crossing a red line’ Among the others who condemned Trump’s attacks were one of his key supporters ahead of the 2024 presidential election. “The president’s statements are out of line,” Bishara Bahbah told the Associated Press. “They are crossing a red line. They are racist.” Bahbah was the founder of Arab Americans for Trump, a group believed to have been important in helping the president connect with a wider range of voters two years ago. The group later changed its name, removing the reference to Trump. Trump clinched the White House in 2024 after victories in Michigan, which has a prominent population of Arab Americans, and a number of other swing states. Asked about accusations of Islamophobia, White House spokesman Davis Ingle said: “Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed wants to massively raise taxes, advocates for defunding the police, and wants to destroy the Michigan auto industry by banning gasoline powered vehicles. “President Trump will continue to call out complete and total extremists like El-Sayed without apology.”

title: Inmate serving life sentence escapes prison
body:
Jacob Morley, 28, was serving a life sentence for first-degree murder.
Authorities have located the truck allegedly stolen by a convicted murderer who escaped prison in Tennessee, but his location remains unknown, the Tennessee Bureau of Investigations (TBI) announced on Tuesday.
The truck was found in Marion, Illinois, amid the search for the escapee, Jacob Morley, according to TBI. A local resident who had seen a news report on the escapee and stolen truck called TBI to report seeing the vehicle parked behind a business, police in Marion said.
"There was no evidence that Morley was still in the vicinity of the vehicle," the Marion Police Department said, adding that a search of the city on Tuesday "had negative results on locating Morley."
Morley, 28, who is serving a life sentence, escaped from the Northwest Correctional Complex in Tiptonville over the weekend, the Tennessee Department of Correction (TDOC) announced Monday.
"At approximately 11:30 p.m. on October 25, 2026, staff at NWCX confirmed Morley was unaccounted for and immediately conducted an emergency count and search of the facility," the agency said .
Security cameras "confirmed Morley breached the perimeter fence and exited the facility in his TDOC uniform," officials said.
On Monday, authorities released a photo of a truck sought in connection with the inmate. The Tennessee Bureau of Investigation (TBI) said newly obtained footage "shows Morley stealing a white 2008 Ford F-350, Tennessee tag 138BBQV" at approximately 1 a.m. Monday from the 400 block of Keystone Drive.
The truck was marked with Lindamood Planting Company on the side, according to TBI.
There were several sightings of the truck, including passing the Hornbeak Fire Department in West Tennessee early Monday, before it was located in Marion on Tuesday, authorities said.
TDOC said it is working with local, state and federal law enforcement to apprehend Morley.
"TDOC is committed to protecting the safety of the public and is asking the community to immediately contact law enforcement with any sightings or information," the agency said in a statement.
According to TDOC, Morley was serving a life sentence for a conviction in Carter County, Tennessee, for crimes including first-degree murder, aggravated burglary, tampering with evidence, evading arrest and vandalism.
TBI announced Monday that Morley was added to the state's Most Wanted list, and offered a reward up to $2,500 for information leading to his arrest.
Morley "should be considered dangerous," TBI said .
Authorities are asking residents in the area to review "home security and doorbell cameras, trail and hunting cameras, and other surveillance systems" for potential sightings.
TDOC said authorities have "cleared buildings and structures in the surrounding area."
The Tennessee Highway Patrol is also joining the search effort, according to TDOC, with aviation assets and state troopers helping the search.
A wanted poster from the TDOC describes Morley as 5 feet, 11 inches tall and weighing 240 pounds with green eyes and brown hair.
"If you have any information regarding the whereabouts of Jacob Morley, please contact the Tennessee Department of Correction at 1-844-832-3463 or 911," the poster read.
An updated wanted poster lists 1 (800) TBI-FIND.
Sheriff Bryan Avery of the Lake County Sheriff's Office, where the prison is located, asked the public to remain "vigilant and exercise caution."
"Anyone who encounters or believes they have spotted Morley should not approach, confront, or attempt to apprehend him," Avery said in a statement Monday. "Instead, immediately dial 911 and provide any relevant information to law enforcement."
Northwest Correctional Complex is a prison with "the operating capacity to house 1,776 male inmates with custody levels ranging from minimum to close," according to the Tennessee Department of Correction.
According to ABC News Tennessee affiliate WJHL , Morley was found guilty of murder in 2022.
Morley was sentenced to life in prison for the murder of Cody Birchfield, a previously missing man whose body was discovered buried underneath Morley's home in March 2022, according to WJHL.
The victim's sister said she is "reliving this horrible tragedy all over again."
"But this time I find myself asking the public for help to find my brother's murderer when he should be in prison locked away," Carrie Norman said in a statement.

title: ASUU-IMSU Urges Imo Govt To Resolve Strike, Gives Conditions For Resumption
body: The Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU), Imo State University (IMSU) branch, has appealed to the Imo State Government, the university’s Visitor and Governing Council, to urgently intervene in its ongoing strike, insisting that academic activities will not resume until outstanding welfare issues are addressed. The union warned that the prolonged industrial action was damaging the academic calendar, institutional reputation and students’ academic progress, calling on the relevant authorities to facilitate a lasting resolution through genuine negotiations. ASUU-IMSU Chairman, Stephen Oguji, made the appeal during a press conference at the university premises in Owerri, the Imo State capital, on Monday. He said the union had outlined conditions for suspending the strike, which began on August 10, 2026, to demand full implementation of the 2025 Federal Government-ASUU agreement, signed in December 2025 and effective from January 1, 2026. The conditions include payment of September and October salaries at the new rate, a time-bound agreement for the payment of salary arrears covering January to August 2026, and the release of all withheld salaries. Others are the constitution of a committee to conduct elections for heads of department, cancellation of examinations and postgraduate defences conducted during the strike, and a formal agreement guaranteeing that members would not be victimised for participating in the industrial action. The union also demanded written commitments with clear timelines for settling outstanding postgraduate allowances, pension-related obligations and earned academic allowances. Oguji said the union had written seven letters to the university administration and held two engagements with management before embarking on the strike. It also wrote three letters to the governing council and held two engagements with relevant stakeholders, but the efforts failed to produce a satisfactory resolution. He noted that several other universities that embarked on similar strikes over related issues had resolved their disputes, while IMSU remained embroiled in the crisis 77 days after the industrial action began. The union also faulted the university management’s decision to commence second-semester examinations for the 2025/2026 academic session on Monday, despite the ongoing strike. It alleged that non-academic and casual staff had been engaged to conduct examinations, insisting that the move could not be regarded as a restoration of normal academic activities. ASUU-IMSU further alleged that the management wrote to the university’s Visitor claiming that the union was not on strike, a position it rejected. According to Oguji, an engagement with the expanded university management on August 27 led to the establishment of a committee to address the dispute, but the process stalled after the committee indicated that it could only consider certain aspects of the agreement. He added that subsequent meetings with the governing council’s subcommittee on ASUU on October 20 and 22 also failed to produce a concrete resolution, as the union was again asked to suspend the strike to allow further dialogue. The chairman maintained that the union was not opposed to negotiations but would no longer accept assurances without measurable results, citing previous engagements in 2024 that failed to resolve the underlying issues. The union also expressed concern over the non-payment of September salaries to affected academic staff, alleging that non-academic staff had received their salaries while lecturers remained unpaid. It called for an explanation and the immediate payment of outstanding salaries. While acknowledging the hardship the strike had caused students and parents, ASUU-IMSU insisted that conducting examinations amid an unresolved dispute would not protect academic standards or restore confidence in the university’s academic processes. The union reaffirmed its readiness for peaceful negotiations but declared that the strike would continue until the 2025 agreement was implemented and outstanding issues addressed through written, time-bound, and verifiable commitments. The post ASUU-IMSU Urges Imo Govt To Resolve Strike, Gives Conditions For Resumption appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Trump denies discussing Netanyahu request for another endorsement: ‘I never spoke about it’
body: US President Donald Trump appeared to deny on Monday that he had discussed issuing an additional endorsement of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ahead of Israel's elections.Speaking to reporters while boarding Air Force One on his way to a campaign rally in Mississippi, Trump was asked directly whether Netanyahu had requested the second endorsement.“I never spoke about it,” the president replied.“I put out both endorsements. I put out both,” Trump said, adding, “I think he's done a very good job as prime minister under very trying conditions.”Trump's response contradicts accounts provided by US officials to The Jerusalem Post, who said Netanyahu had been making intensive efforts to persuade the American president to issue another public statement of support, after the initial endorsement failed to produce a significant shift in the polls.Axios also reported that Netanyahu had spoken with Trump twice within three days and asked him to reinforce his public support. According to the report, the prime minister even suggested possible wording for additional endorsements and requested that Trump speak with Israeli journalists to emphasize his backing.The Likud party denied the report that Netanyahu had requested the president's endorsement.Trump on Brazil's election: 'I like Lula,' but vote counting had 'a very bad look'During the same exchange, Trump was also asked about Brazil's presidential election, in which incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva defeated right-wing candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, son of former President Jair Bolsonaro.Asked whether he intended to take any action regarding the election results, Trump replied: “I'm not running Brazil. I'm running the USA.”Nevertheless, the American president criticized the conduct of the election and the vote-counting process.“I like Lula. I get along with him very well,” Trump said. “I just think it had a very bad look. The election, the way it was tabulated.”He later added: “The extension given was very strange.”His remarks referred to a decision by Brazil's Supreme Court to extend voting by two hours during the election's second round. The decision followed complaints of disruptions to public transportation but sparked significant political controversy.

title: Three Family Members Die as Car Plunges Into Piraeus Port
body: An 82-year-old man, his wife and their adult son have died in a Piraeus port accident after their car plunged into the sea at Gate E2 on Sunday night. All three were pronounced dead at Attikon University General Hospital, the Hellenic Coast Guard said . Greek media identified the passengers as the driver’s 72-year-old wife and their 45-year-old son. Initial reports, which Greek City Times carried on Monday , put the toll at one dead. At that stage, rescuers had pulled two elderly occupants out unconscious. Heavy rain was falling when the car went into the water. The father most likely lost control of the car in the poor conditions, Greek media reported. Rescue effort at Gate E2 Port officers in Tzelepi received the alert on Sunday evening, the Coast Guard said. Crews on a patrol boat and a pilot boat then located the driver and pulled him from the water unconscious. Divers from the Coast Guard’s Underwater Missions Unit later found two more people inside the submerged car. A private crane lifted the vehicle out, and rescuers freed a woman and a man, both unconscious. Officials gave the woman’s age as 78 and the man’s as 41, while media reports put them at 72 and 45. Ambulances from the National Emergency Aid Centre (EKAB) took all three to Attikon. Following the recovery, investigators from the 1st Port Department of Tzelepi have opened a preliminary inquiry into the Piraeus port accident. Autopsies will take place at the Piraeus forensic service, the Coast Guard said. Private boats also joined the search at the Port of Piraeus as well. No marine pollution occurred. Calls for safety checks George Vallis heads the Panhellenic Union of Private and Professional Yacht Crews (PEPIETH). He called for a full inquiry into the Piraeus port accident. “It is necessary to fully investigate the causes,” Vallis said, urging authorities to examine all available footage from the port’s security cameras. In addition, he asked whether clearer markings should separate land from sea during heavy rain and poor visibility. Such markings matter most when no ship sits at the quay as a visual reference, he said. “No human life is expendable,” Vallis said, before offering his condolences to the family. So far, the Coast Guard has not named the three victims of the Piraeus port accident. Results from the autopsies and the preliminary investigation are still pending. title: Ballon d’or 2026: Lamine Yamal makes history with third straight Kopa Trophy win
body: Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal has made football history after winning the 2026 Kopa Trophy for the third consecutive year, becoming the first player to claim the award three times. The 19-year-old Spain international received the honour at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony in London on Monday, October 26, following another impressive season in which he helped Barcelona win La Liga and the Spanish Super Cup before playing a key role in Spain’s 2026 FIFA World Cup triumph. Yamal’s latest success extends his dominance in the award, which recognises the best young footballer under the age of 21. He previously won the trophy in 2024 and 2025. His third consecutive victory puts him ahead of previous winners, including Kylian Mbappé, Matthijs de Ligt, Pedri, Gavi and Jude Bellingham, who have each won the award once. The Barcelona star beat several highly rated young players to retain the honour, including teammate Pau Cubarsí, Yan Diomande, Lennart Karl, Warren Zaïre-Emery and Johan Manzambi. Yamal’s achievement comes after a successful 2025-2026 campaign at both club and international levels. He was instrumental in Barcelona’s domestic success and featured prominently in Spain’s run to the World Cup title, which they secured with a 1-0 victory over Argentina in the final. His performances have continued to strengthen his reputation as one of the most exciting talents in world football, with his dribbling, creativity and attacking influence making him a key figure for both Barcelona and Spain. Despite his personal achievement, Yamal expressed a preference for his Barcelona teammate Cubarsí to have won the award, according to reports from the ceremony. He praised the defender’s performances while expressing gratitude to his club and national team. Yamal’s third Kopa Trophy also adds to Barcelona’s impressive record in the award’s history. The club previously produced winners Pedri in 2021 and Gavi in 2022, before Yamal began his consecutive run in 2024. The 2020 edition was not awarded, while Mbappé won the inaugural prize in 2018, de Ligt claimed it in 2019 and Bellingham was named the winner in 2023. At 19, Yamal remains eligible for the award in future editions before turning 22, giving him the opportunity to extend his record. His latest triumph further cements his status among the leading young players in the game, as attention turns to whether he can translate his growing collection of individual honours into further success with Barcelona and Spain.

title: 'Legitimazes Jihad': Foreign Affairs Ministry slams UN report accusing Israel of genocide
body: The Foreign Affairs Ministry on Monday called the report from a United Nations commission accusing Israel of genocide a "propaganda document detached from reality, aimed at undermining Israel's right to self-defense, delegitimizing the Jewish state, and legitimizing jihadist terrorism against its citizens."The UN commission released a report Monday accusing Israel of committing war crimes and crimes against humanity in the West Bank and Gaza.The report also mentioned wrongdoings by the Palestinian Authority, claiming that it had pushed for arbitrary arrests, detention, torture and the targeting of journalists, activists and human rights defenders.The Commission of Inquiry (COI) report, issued under the auspices of the politicized UN Human Rights Council, is not a human rights report but a propaganda document detached from reality, aimed at undermining Israel's right to self-defense, delegitimizing the Jewish state, and legitimizing jihadist terrorism against its citizens. The Commission, which was established in 2021, was flawed from the outset and has targeted Israel exclusively since day one. Its activities are an example of the vast UN resources, funding, and personnel devoted to advancing anti-Israel propaganda. This false report says far more about the political agenda of the body behind it than it does about Israel. The fact that the so-called “report” parrots the narrative of terrorist organizations word for word is clear proof of its true nature and motives. This is the shameful legacy of the UN Secretary-General and the High Commissioner for Human Rights.— Israel Foreign Ministry (@IsraelMFA) October 26, 2026In contrast, Hamas is named exactly twice, and neither mention accused Hamas of committing a crime or other wrongdoing.The UN reported an increase in the number of Palestinian deaths in the West Bank, with almost 500 Palestinians killed annually in the West Bank since 2022, which were the highest numbers recorded since the UN started collecting data on the topic in 2005.The report also claimed that Israel is continuing to commit “genocidal acts”  with the “intent to destroy the Palestinian people, in whole or in part” in spite of a ceasefire agreement that went into effect in October 2025.The report focused on Palestinian casualties in the West Bank due to Israeli military action and settler violence, as well as analysis of elected MKs and senior military officials.“The intentional killing and injuring of Palestinian civilians and destruction of homes in the West Bank combined with Israel's persistent denial of responsibility form part of a broader strategy to exterminate and displace Palestinians and impose conditions of life that are unliveable,” said Srinivasan Muralidhar, an Indian jurist who currently serves as the chair of the Commission of Inquiry.Report cites increase in West Bank airstrike deathsThe Commission reported a sharp increase in Palestinian deaths caused by airstrikes in the West Bank since October 7, 2023. Six Palestinians were killed by airstrikes between 2008 and October 6, 2023, compared with 254 between October 7, 2023, and September 30, 2026, according to the commission's findings.It said airstrikes had become more frequent following the launch of Operation Iron Wall in January 2025, particularly in refugee camps and areas around Jenin, Tulkarm, Tubas and Nablus.The Commission described the operation as a shift toward widespread destruction of Palestinian housing and infrastructure and the clearing of refugee camps. It cited the IDF's stated aim to “dismantle and restor[e] the operational freedom of action for IDF forces”, while reconstruction of the infrastructure is considered to be “endangering the citizens of the State of Israel and the military forces”. Commission's analysis of statements by Israeli officialsThe commission also cited statements by Israeli officials including Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich and IDF Central Command chief Maj.-Gen. Avi Bluth in assessing Israeli military conduct and the intentions behind operations in the West Bank.Smotrich referred to “two million Nazis” in the West Bank in November 2023, citing a poll on Palestinian support for the October 7 Hamas massacre. In November 2024, he said “The only way to remove the danger of a Palestinian terror state from the agenda is to apply Israeli sovereignty to Jewish settlement in the entire Judea and Samaria,” he said. In January 2025, he wrote that Fondouk, Nablus and Jenin should “look like Jabalia,”.The Commission also highlighted a reported May 2026 statement by Bluth that Israeli soldiers were “killing like we haven't since 1967.”Report alleges sexual violence against detaineesThe Commission said it had verified four additional cases of sexual violence against Palestinian detainees since its March 2025 report on gender-based violence. Two victims were from the West Bank. The cases included alleged gang rape, genital violence, groping, threats of sexual violence, forced nudity, and searches conducted without an apparent security justification.One case involved a male detainee at Megiddo Prison in 2025. He was allegedly blindfolded, forced to remove his lower garments, and repeatedly raped with objects during interrogation. The Commission alleged that guards mocked and photographed him, threatened to mutilate his genitals and threatened sexual violence against his family and colleagues. The detainee reportedly suffered serious injuries, including rectal bleeding, without receiving medical treatment.The Commission claimed that the cases it investigated involving torture, rape and other forms of sexual violence were not isolated incidents. It alleged that these acts formed part of a broader attack against the civilian population and concluded that Israeli authorities and security forces had committed crimes against humanity involving torture, rape and other forms of sexual violence.Israel has rejected previous allegations by the Commission of Inquiry that its forces systematically used sexual and gender-based violence against Palestinian detainees, describing the claims as unfounded and disputing the Commission's verification methods. In a March 2025 response, the Foreign Ministry said the IDF had rules prohibiting such misconduct and mechanisms for investigating allegations.Commission also reports abuses by Palestinian AuthorityThe report also accused the Palestinian Authority of suppressing political dissent through arbitrary arrests, detention, torture and the targeting of journalists, activists and human rights defenders.It cited reports of excessive force during West Bank protests in October 2023, when at least two men, a boy and a girl, were killed in Ramallah, Tubas and Jenin. The PA accepted responsibility for the death of the boy, who was run over by a security forces vehicle during clashes with protesters.The Commission also investigated the December 2024 killing of a Palestinian journalism student in Jenin refugee camp who had documented alleged abuses by Palestinian security forces. Witnesses said a security force member had threatened to shoot her the previous day. She was killed by a single shot to the neck near her home.The report said information conflicted on whether clashes were underway at the time. Palestinian security forces had a significant presence in the area, and their spokesman blamed the killing on “outlaws,” saying the case was under investigation. The Commission said key witnesses had not been asked to testify.It also reported cases of arbitrary detention, including instances in which the PA allegedly ignored court orders for detainees' release.The Commission concluded that the PA had violated the right to life and the right to security of person and had failed to conduct prompt, effective and impartial investigations into killings or provide effective remedies to victims and their families.

title: Constitutional Amendment: Ondo Assembly passes state police bill
body:
The Ondo State House of Assembly on Monday unanimously voted in support of the State Police after considering the constitutional amendment bill transmitted to it by the National Assembly .
The House backed the bill after an extensive deliberation in plenary, presided over by the Speaker, Olamide Oladiji.
While presenting the bill’s recommendations, the Leader of the House, Olatunji Oshati, explained that state policing system is expected to improve security operations through a decentralised approach that allows law enforcement to respond more effectively to grassroots security threats.
In his remarks, Mr Oladiji expressed optimism that the initiative would ease the operational pressure on the existing federal police structure by providing an additional layer of security and improving coordination in responding to threats.
According to him, beyond tackling crime, state policing is expected to strengthen intelligence -led policing by enabling security personnel to develop closer relationships with traditional rulers, community leaders, traders, farmers, and other stakeholders.
After the passage of the bill, the Speaker directed the Clerk of the Assembly to transmit it to the National Assembly alongside the observations made by the House.
Twenty-five states have so far approved the Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, which provides for the establishment of state police services, satisfying the two-thirds majority requirement for its enactment as contained in Section 9 of the Nigerian Constitution.
The states are Adamawa, Akwa Ibom, Anambra, Bayelsa, Benue, Cross River, Delta, Edo, Ekiti, Enugu, Gombe, Imo, Kaduna, Kebbi and Kwara.
Others are Nasarawa, Ogun, Ondo, Osun, Oyo, Plateau, Rivers, Taraba, Yobe and Zamfara.

title: Alan Watts Predicted LLM Usage in 1951
body:
“Plus ça change , plus c’est la même chose.” -Alphonse Karr The more things change, the more they stay the same, so the saying goes. I often find myself thinking this when reading philosophy from ~300 BC, where great minds are struggling over the same issues in society that I myself am wrestling with. There is a sense of ease for me that this struggle is not something new, nor am I facing it alone.
The same feeling struck me while reading Alan Watt’s brilliant book The Wisdom of Insecurity , a strangely calming tome from an era where people were very anxious – it was written six years after the United States revealed that they had discovered an unbelievably destructive weapon that had ended the Pacific front of World War II and redefined what a show of force looked like. Since the cat was out of the bag (or rather the cow was out of the gate ), it could also be used to turn the entire world into a barren, radioactive wasteland. Not fun.
We have plenty to worry about in 2026 on top of nuclear weapons, and our screens and algorithms make sure we are aware of every excruciating detail. An obvious one these days is “AI”, a new restructuring of power and efficiency that has thrown entire fields of research into identity crises and exuberance (mine included).
So it was quite comforting to know that Watts was already tuned into the probability that things like large language models would come into being, in an eerily accurate way, long before modems were in our pockets:
“Already man uses innumerable gadgets to displace the work done by bodily organs in the animals, and it would surely be in line with this tendency to externalize the reasoning functions of the brain–and thus hand over the government of life to electromagnetic monsters. In other words, the interests and goals of rationality are not those of man as a whole organism. If we are to continue to live for the future, and to make the chief work of the mind prediction and calculation, man must eventually become a parasitic appendage to a mass of clockwork.”
Whew! Mr. Watts was never one to mince words, and his thoughts parallel those of the great contemporary thinker Corey Doctorow , warning us to avoid the trap of becoming a “reverse centaur” , again… Watts called it in 1951!
So I am sharing this to join the effort of reminding as many people as possible to maintain their agency, have the courage to be imperfect, learn and grow together, and to remember that a large language model will not invent a new dance unless there is someone instructing it to do so, rather than getting up and dancing spontaneously and experiencing the sheer joy of wiggling their body in an interesting way to the sound of music with their friends.

title: St. Petersburg schoolteacher who reportedly served in Russia’s war against Ukraine suspected of killing his 2-year-old son and the boy’s grandmother
body: A math and physical education teacher in St. Petersburg is suspected of two murders and an attempted murder. Local news outlets Fontanka and Rotonda reported that the victims were a 2-year-old boy and his 58-year-old grandmother. The child’s mother survived. Passersby found her badly beaten near a building in the Solnechny Gorod residential complex in the city’s Krasnoselsky district. Fontanka reported that Anastasia, 32, escaped through a ground-floor apartment window. She is now in the hospital. The suspect is a 40-year-old teacher named Dmitry. According to media reports, he worked at a school in the Krasnoselsky district where Anastasia taught history and social studies. Her mother taught English at another school. Dmitry and Anastasia were not married. The child who was killed was their son. The television channel 78 reported that Dmitry recently returned from the war in Ukraine. According to the channel, he “didn’t want to stand by during the special military operation” and went to the Kursk region after Ukrainian forces were driven out, serving there in a mobile fire unit. In August, after returning from the war, he suggested that he and Anastasia break up. A friend of Anastasia’s told the channel that the couple’s relationship had soured even before Dmitry left for the war. She said he was intensely jealous of Anastasia and had “aggression issues.” After their son was born, Anastasia moved into her own apartment with the child and was afraid to be alone with Dmitry. He nevertheless came by almost every day to take their son for walks. Dmitry is believed to have come over again on Sunday, killed Anastasia’s mother and the child, hidden the boy’s body in the refrigerator, and beaten Anastasia. Fontanka reported that a note from the suspect was found at the scene of the killings. He wrote that “being a ‘weekend dad’ infuriated him” and that “it irritated him that while he was looking after the child,” Anastasia was “off somewhere enjoying herself.” Dmitry suspected his partner of cheating and doubted that he was the boy’s father. The suspect fled, and a search is underway. According to Fontanka, police believe Dmitry may have died by suicide. title: Greece Raises Childcare Vouchers 10% as Income Limits Climb
body: Greek childcare vouchers will rise in value by 10% for 2026–2027, while higher income limits will let more families claim a subsidised place at nurseries and day-care centres. The Ministry of Social Cohesion and Family set out the changes in a new joint ministerial decision on Monday. Also, families with three children can now get a reduced-value voucher regardless of income. Under the decision, income limits for vouchers rise by €2,000. In addition, a second call for applications will follow, so more parents can join the scheme. The move adds to earlier incentives for families with children . “We managed to secure more support for families with children,” Social Cohesion and Family Minister Domna Minewschailidou said. In her words, the decision is “one more step so that more parents have access to preschool care, can work and can organise their daily lives better” . How much Greek childcare vouchers are worth The 10% rise covers Greek childcare vouchers for infant, infant-toddler and children’s centres. An infant place with meals rises from €3,239 to €3,563. Similarly, a toddler place with meals climbs from €2,612 to €2,873. In turn, the reduced-value voucher increases from €2,178 to €2,396. The higher amounts apply automatically to Greek childcare vouchers that families already hold, so parents do not need to apply again. Also, reduced-value vouchers convert to full value when families now meet the higher income limits. New income limits for families Full-value vouchers now cover families earning up to €29,000 with up to two children. The limit is €32,000 for three children, €35,000 for four and €38,000 for five or more. For reduced-value vouchers, the limit for families with up to two children climbs from €35,000 to €37,000. At the same time, the €38,000 cap for three-child families no longer applies. As a result, three-child families can claim Greek childcare vouchers at the reduced value regardless of income. Large families with four or more children already enjoy the same right. “We particularly support families raising three or more children, because we know their needs are greater,” Michailidou said. Next, the Hellenic Agency for Local Development and Local Government (EETAA) will issue a second call for Greek childcare vouchers for 2026–2027. It will open to newly eligible families that do not already hold a voucher. Earlier, the agency’s first call for applications ran from 18 July to 5 August 2026, with a budget of €393 million. Likewise, a second call last year approved vouchers for more than 6,000 children. Michailidou co-signed the decision with five ministers and deputy ministers, including Interior Minister Theodoros Livanios and Digital Governance Minister Dimitris Papastergiou. title: Russian Missiles Strike Kyiv University Campus – 1 Killed, 15 Wounded, Mostly Students
body:
Russian ballistic missiles struck a university campus and surrounding residential areas in Kyiv late Monday, Oct. 26, killing at least one person and injuring over 10 others, most of them students, as emergency crews searched damaged buildings for people feared trapped under rubble.
The strikes hit the grounds of a university near Kyoto Park and Lisova metro station on the eastern bank of the Dnipro River, damaging student dormitories, residential buildings, and medical facilities.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Kyiv Mayor Vitalii Klitschko said nine of the wounded were hospitalized, including three in serious condition.
President Volodymyr Zelensky warned that further strikes were possible as Russian Shahed drone attacks continued against the capital and other Ukrainian cities.
“There is extensive damage, and there are also reports that people may be trapped under the rubble,” Zelensky wrote on social media .
The Ukrainian leader stressed that the missiles struck crowded civilian areas where, he said, there were no military facilities nearby.
“Unfortunately, there may be more strikes coming,” Zelensky added.
At 8:30 a.m. on Tuesday, the Kyiv City Military Administration (KMVA) reported that the number of casualties had risen to 15.
“Overnight, the enemy attacked the capital with ballistic missiles and [unmanned aerial vehicles] UAVs. As a result of the Russian Federation’s terrorist actions, damage has been recorded in three districts of Kyiv,” the report reads.
Of the 15 casualties, 12 have been hospitalized.
According to the State Emergency Service (DSNS), two fires broke out in non-residential buildings in the Obolonskyi district. Rescuers have extinguished both fires. Two casualties were reported in the district.
In the Holosiivskyi district, the Russian attack damaged transport infrastructure.
The university affected by the attack was identified as the State University of Trade and Economics (SUTE), located on Kyoto Street in Kyiv’s Desnianskyi district.
The institution, founded in 1946, is one of the capital’s major public universities, with more than 15,000 students across six faculties, according to its official profile .
The university specializes in economics, international trade, finance, law, information technology, and management.
Russia’s ballistic strike landed near a university dormitory, shattering windows and injuring residents, according to Klitschko.
The mayor initially reported that a 20-year-old woman was hospitalized following the strike near the dormitory.
In a subsequent update , Klitschko said most of the 10 people injured in the attack were students living in university accommodation. Nine were taken to hospital.
Ukraine’s State Emergency Service reported damage to university buildings, dormitories and nearby residential properties.
KMVA also reported damage to a school building in the Desnianskyi district.
A paramedic and an emergency medical technician suffered injuries after their ambulance came under fire in the Desnianskyi district, according to the mayor. Their injuries were not considered critical.
A strike near Lisova metro station also set a private vehicle on fire, while nearby residential infrastructure sustained damage.
In the Dniprovskyi district, a three-story non-residential building was partially destroyed, with emergency workers discovering the body of one person in its basement, according to the State Emergency Service.
The destruction extended across residential, educational and medical facilities in the two districts.
Zelensky renewed his call for faster deliveries of Western air defense systems and ammunition, warning that delays were leaving Ukrainian cities vulnerable to further Russian missile strikes.
He said Ukraine continued to face a constant threat from ballistic missiles that could strike populated areas with little warning.
Under such circumstances, he argued, “artificial delays in providing air defense to Ukraine help terror.”
The president called for political agreements on defense assistance to be implemented promptly, stressing that Ukraine needed sufficient weapons not only to intercept incoming missiles but also to destroy Russian launchers.
The latest attack came amid an intensified Russian missile and drone campaign against Ukraine, with Kyiv’s residential neighborhoods, transport facilities, and civilian infrastructure repeatedly affected.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Melania Trump ready to continue humanitarian efforts in Ukraine after Oleshky operation, senior adviser says
body:
This was stated by Marc Beckman, senior advisor to the U.S. First Lady, in an interview with Ukrinform .
According to him, Melania Trump’s attention is currently focused on the humanitarian operation in Oleshky, where, in her assessment, the situation is approaching catastrophic levels.
“I think it will take five to seven days after October 29 to ensure that everything we’re planning is carried out. After that, if the First Lady is welcomed again by President Zelensky and President Putin, I’m sure she will continue these humanitarian efforts,” Beckman said.
He added that the U.S. First Lady is also working directly with Ukraine and Russia on the next phase of reuniting Ukrainian children with their families.
Beckman explained that the U.S. First Lady’s decision to join the humanitarian operation in Oleshky was a continuation of her previous work on returning children.
According to him, during the six previous operations, the team succeeded in facilitating the reunification of 34 children, forcibly displaced by Russia, with their families. As part of this effort, the First Lady’s team established channels of communication with the Ukrainian and Russian sides.
“We had already built a relationship based on trust and good faith, putting humanitarian efforts above geopolitical differences during the war,” the adviser noted.
According to him, Melania Trump initially established contact with the Ukrainian side, which supported her initiative. She subsequently discussed the matter with Russian leadership.
Beckman explained that over a month ago, Ukrainian leadership granted the First Lady written permission to act as a mediator, after which she received similar written permission from the Russian president.
“The First Lady has always felt that children, women, and the elderly should be placed above political ideology or geopolitical differences, and certainly above war,” said the senior advisor.
He emphasized that Melania Trump will continue to do everything possible within the framework of humanitarian initiatives to help Ukrainians and people in other countries around the world.
As previously reported, Marc Beckman, chief advisor to U.S. First Lady Melania Trump, stated in an interview with Ukrinform that Russia had assured Ukraine and the U.S. that it would respect the choice of residents of the temporarily occupied town of Oleshky in the Kherson region regarding their evacuation destination.

title: Cyprus’ First Gas Field Moves to Construction After $1.8bn Deals
body: The Cronos gas field off Cyprus has moved into its construction phase, after Eni signed contracts worth up to US$1.8 billion at the Presidential Palace in Nicosia on Monday. The Italian energy company signed the main contracts for engineering, procurement, construction, installation and drilling. It is the first Cypriot hydrocarbon field to reach development, about 15 years after gas was first found in Cyprus’ exclusive economic zone. President Nikos Christodoulides called the investment “a strong vote of confidence in our country’s energy prospects” . He also linked the project to a stronger economy and more room for state investment. Energy Minister Michalis Damianos told the ceremony it was “an important step in Cyprus’ transition from exploration and discovery to the development and production of our natural gas resources” . What the Cronos gas field contracts cover The work includes subsea production and control systems, gas pipelines, a floating control unit and the drilling of the wells. In total, the plan foresees four subsea production wells. At its peak, the Cronos gas field should produce about 500 million cubic feet of gas a day. Eni plans to start production in the first half of 2028. The field sits in Block 6 of Cyprus’ exclusive economic zone, about 185 kilometres southwest of the island. Eni discovered it in 2022, before the partners finished the Cronos-2 appraisal in 2024. According to the partners’ estimates, the Cronos gas field holds more than three trillion cubic feet of gas in place. However, that figure is not the same as the amount the partners can finally recover and sell. Eni operates Block 6 with a 50% stake, while France’s TotalEnergies holds the other 50%. Separately, US company McDermott has already won a large share of the subsea work, valued at US$500–750 million. Gas to reach Europe through Egypt Gas from the Cronos gas field will not go directly to Cyprus for power generation. Instead, a subsea pipeline will carry it to existing facilities at Egypt’s Zohr field for processing, as part of the planned route to Europe via Egypt and Greece . From there, the Damietta plant will liquefy the gas so tankers can ship it, mainly to Europe. Using Egyptian infrastructure cuts both cost and construction time, because Cyprus does not need its own liquefaction terminal. At full capacity, output will equal about 2.8 million tonnes of liquefied natural gas a year. The export route rests on a February 2025 agreement between Cyprus, Egypt, Eni and TotalEnergies. Earlier, on 28 July, Eni and TotalEnergies took the final investment decision on the project. Damianos said the Cronos gas field’s importance goes beyond the size of its reserves, as it is the first real attempt to turn Cyprus’ offshore discoveries into commercial gas. Still, the US$1.8 billion is the value of the infrastructure contracts, not direct income for the Cypriot state. Future state revenue will depend on sales, gas prices, development costs and the revenue-sharing terms. Also, because the gas is meant for export, the Cronos gas field will not automatically lower electricity bills in Cyprus. title: Israeli army reports strikes across Gaza Strip
body:
TEL AVIV, October 27. /TASS/. The Israeli military has carried out a series of strikes on the Gaza Strip, the army press service reported.
According to the report, the strikes targeted areas in northern, southern and central Gaza.
The attacks killed four members of Hamas and Islamic Jihad, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said. The military also said it had identified "a military structure in the northern Gaza Strip that was used as a sniper position targeting IDF troops."
Besides, IDF troops identified three militants emerging from a tunnel shaft in the Khan Younis area, beyond the Yellow Line demarcation boundary. An airstrike was carried out on the shaft and the militants, the army said, adding that secondary explosions were observed.

title: Riyadh Air moves operations 250 miles away from Riyadh after Houthi attacks
body:
Riyadh Air has moved part of its operation about 250 miles (400 km) north of the Saudi capital after repeated Houthi attacks severely disrupted King Khalid International Airport, forcing the young airline to operate a reduced network from Al Qassim.
The temporary arrangement began on October 25 and covers flights to London Heathrow, Cairo, Jeddah, Dhaka, Lahore and Islamabad. Other routes that Riyadh Air had launched during its rapid expansion from its home hub have been suspended.
The move does not put the airline's aircraft beyond the range of Houthi missiles and drones. Al Qassim instead offers an alternative to keeping the fleet concentrated at an airport that has repeatedly been targeted and has suffered severe operational restrictions.
The scale of the disruption in Riyadh has been exceptional. According to aviation analytics company Cirium , 4,071 of the 4,736 flights scheduled at King Khalid International between October 8 and 25 were cancelled, equivalent to 86% of the airport's planned operation.
Follow Air Data News: WhatsApp | Instagram | LinkedIn | Twitter | Facebook
The airport was hit during a series of Houthi attacks this month. A strike on October 10 killed 13 people , and the facility remained closed for several days before a limited reopening. The Houthis have continued to claim attacks against Riyadh since operations began to resume.
The situation has also prompted several foreign airlines to suspend services to the Saudi capital, with some cancellations extending into November.
Riyadh Air has created an unusual ground operation to preserve service for passengers originating in the capital.
Travelers can check in and hand over their baggage in Riyadh before being transported by coach to Al Qassim Airport. The road journey takes about 4.5 hours.
The airline schedules the buses to leave Riyadh six hours and 15 minutes before flight departure, allowing passengers to reach Al Qassim about one hour and 45 minutes before takeoff. Travelers can also make their own way to the airport.
Al Qassim is not immune to the regional security threat, and its location does not prevent it from being reached by long-range weapons. Moving aircraft there instead disperses Riyadh Air's operation away from the airport that has become a recurring target and remains subject to cancellations and restrictions.
The crisis interrupted Riyadh Air's expansion only months after the Saudi carrier began full commercial operations on June 10 .
Its network had already grown to 16 destinations, including Riyadh itself and services to Jeddah, Cairo, Dubai, London, Manchester, Madrid, Milan, Mumbai, Islamabad, Lahore, Dhaka, Bangkok, Kuala Lumpur and Manila. Jakarta had also been announced, with flights scheduled to begin in November.
The airline is now offering Al Qassim as an alternative only for passengers booked to London Heathrow, Cairo, Islamabad, Lahore, Dhaka and Jeddah. Services to destinations including Dubai, Madrid, Manchester, Mumbai, Bangkok, Kuala Lumpur and Manila have been affected by cancellations from Riyadh.
Riyadh Air was created around a hub-and-spoke operation at King Khalid International Airport and plans to serve more than 100 destinations by 2030. The current arrangement therefore preserves only a small portion of the network it had begun building around the Saudi capital.
The disruption comes as Riyadh Air rapidly builds both its operating fleet and one of the largest aircraft order books among startup airlines. The carrier currently has ten Boeing 787-9s in its fleet, six of them listed as active and four parked as of October 25.
Riyadh Air initially ordered 39 787-9s with options for another 33 aircraft. At the Farnborough International Airshow in July, it exercised options for 28 additional Dreamliners and introduced the larger 787-10 into its plans, converting 20 aircraft to the new variant. Once 17 aircraft from the latest transaction are finalized, the airline's firm 787 order book will reach 67 aircraft.
The Dreamliner, however, is only one of three aircraft families selected by Riyadh Air. The carrier also has 60 Airbus A321neo-family aircraft planned for its short- and medium-haul network. The first A321neo is scheduled for delivery in November, with commercial service expected to begin in early 2027. The fleet will eventually be divided between 30 standard A321neos and 30 longer-range A321LRs.
Riyadh Air has also ordered 25 Airbus A350-1000s and holds purchase rights for another 25. The widebody order was announced in 2025 and will give the airline a larger long-haul aircraft alongside the 787-9 and 787-10.
Together, the 787, A321neo and A350 programs form a planned fleet of 182 aircraft. Riyadh Air expects to use them to build a network of more than 100 destinations by 2030.

title: Air Force Launches ARRW, Its First Hypersonic Weapon, into Production
body: The Air Force awarded Lockheed Martin a $694 million contract to produce its first-ever hypersonic missile, the Air-Launched Rapid Response Weapon, the service announced Oct. 26. The decision advances ARRW from testing into production, a major milestone for a long-sought capability. The Air Force, citing operational security concerns, withheld details on how many it ordered or when they must be delivered. Budget documents describe ARRW as a standoff weapon and “a lethal capability against high-value time-sensitive targets.” It is too large to go on most fighter jets and will initially be fielded on the B-52 and has also reportedly been tested on the B-1. A multistage boost-glide weapon, it uses a rocket booster to accelerate to hypersonic speed, when the booster separates and falls away, leaving a glide vehicle that can maneuver to its target at five times the speed of sound. or greater—at least 3,800 miles per hour or just over a mile per second. “This is a turning point in our advanced weapons roadmap,” said Secretary of the Air Force Troy Meink in a statement. “By moving ARRW from test to production, we’re providing our combatant commanders with a credible, high-speed strike weapon capable of penetrating the most advanced anti-access and area-denial systems.” ARRW development began in 2018 when the Air Force signed Lockheed to a design contract worth up to $480 million . The program built on the joint DARPA-Air Force X-51, and sought to deliver a prototype capability by 2021. The Air Force conducted captive carry tests in 2019 and that same year awarded Lockheed a $988.8 million contract modification for critical design review. The first operational flight test was planned by the end of 2020, with initial operational capability projected in 2022. But the first launch test, delayed to April 2021, failed and two more failures followed . The first successful test came in May 2022—at which point funding became a problem. In 2021, Congress stripped funds for 12 ARRW missiles from the fiscal 2022 budget plan, and the Air Force zeroed out funds for 2023. In March 2023, the Air Force’s top civilian acquisition executive, Andrew Hunter, said the program would end without purchases. Air Force leaders said they would focus instead on the smaller Hypersonic Attack Cruise Missile and other reusable hypersonic systems. In 2025, however, then-Chief of Staff of the Air Force Gen. David Allvin told Congress the Air Force would buy ARRW, and the fiscal 2026 budget allotted $362 million for that purpose. The contract was awarded Sept. 29, 2026, but the decision was not announced until a month later. The Air Force’s 2027 budget request included $452 million for ARRW production. That budget is currently stalled in Congress, and the Pentagon is operating under a continuing resolution based on 2026 funding levels. The Future Years Defense Plan projects procurement from 2028 to 2031 to range from $556 million to $621 million per year. Quantities are dubbed “controlled unclassified information,” and not publicly released. “Fielding ARRW enhances our ability to hold targets at risk anywhere around the world,” Chief of Staff of the Air Force Gen. Kenneth Wilsbach said in a statement. “This hypersonic weapon provides the Joint Force a flexible and rapid response option for highly contested environments.” The post Air Force Launches ARRW, Its First Hypersonic Weapon, into Production appeared first on Air & Space Forces Magazine .

title: Amelley Djosu: The culture we create, the abuse we excuse and the responsibility of Ghana’s creative industry
body: The allegations of sexual abuse involving 19 students at Obuasi Senior High Technical School have renewed a difficult conversation about the safety of young people, the abuse of authority and the systems meant to protect them. The allegations must be investigated thoroughly and treated seriously without prejudging the outcome. Yet the wider questions they raise cannot wait for a verdict. What kind of society are we building when young people may struggle to recognise abuse, report it or trust that someone will protect them? As a marketing communications strategist, creative entrepreneur and advocate for responsible creative practice, I believe this conversation must extend beyond schools and law enforcement. It must include the media, musicians, filmmakers, comedians, influencers, brands and everyone whose work shapes public attitudes. Sexual abuse is not caused by music videos, comedy skits or social media trends alone. But the culture we create can either challenge the abuse of power or make it easier to excuse. When entertainment shapes what society tolerates Creativity reflects society, but it also influences how society sees itself. Music, film, comedy and digital content shape ideas about relationships, gender, power and acceptable behaviour, particularly among young audiences. Consider the objectification of women in some music videos, lyrics that reduce them to sexual objects, and scenes that portray unwanted touching or persistent sexual advances as playful or harmless. Add online skits that turn harassment into comedy without questioning the behaviour, and a troubling pattern emerges. The problem is not that art explores sexuality, attraction or adult relationships. Artistic freedom matters, and provocative content should not automatically be treated as harmful. The concern is what happens when entertainment repeatedly blurs the line between attraction and entitlement, persistence and coercion, or humour and humiliation. When a woman’s refusal becomes a challenge to overcome, or a child’s vulnerability becomes entertainment, audiences risk becoming less sensitive to the harm beneath the joke. Representation does not automatically determine behaviour, and responsibility for abuse rests with the person who commits it. But creatives cannot dismiss their cultural influence simply because their work is entertainment. The question is not whether creatives are responsible for every social problem. It is whether they are willing to take responsibility for the messages they choose to amplify. Consent is not a trend, it is a standard. Consent requires a clear, voluntary agreement. It cannot be inferred from silence, fear, a previous flirtation or a relationship. Nor does a position of authority give anyone the right to exploit another person. Where children are concerned, the responsibility is even greater. Teachers, coaches, religious leaders and other adults entrusted with their care have a duty to protect, not exploit. No creative narrative should blur the distinction between safeguarding a child and sexualising one. The Obuasi allegations therefore demand more than public outrage. They require credible investigations, protection for complainants, accountability where wrongdoing is established, and safe channels for reporting misconduct. Institutions must not confuse protecting their reputation with protecting vulnerable people. The creative industry also has a role. Comedians can challenge harmful behaviour without trivialising abuse. Musicians can create compelling work without reducing women to props. Filmmakers can portray difficult realities without glamourising exploitation. Influencers can use their platforms to make conversations about consent, boundaries and safeguarding more accessible. Actor and content creator Jeffrey Nortey, for instance, has used skits to address consent, inappropriate advances and the abuse of minors. His work illustrates how comedy can open up difficult conversations without sacrificing entertainment. With thoughtful writing, humour can do more than attract attention. It can challenge audiences to reconsider what they have come to accept. Responsibility must run through the creative value chain This responsibility cannot rest on individual artists alone. Producers, directors, scriptwriters, publicists, talent managers, media organisations, advertisers and sponsors all influence what gets made, funded, promoted and celebrated. Brands should look beyond reach and engagement when choosing creative partners. Popularity matters, but so do professional conduct and judgement. Content that attracts millions of views while normalising harassment may generate attention without building meaningful brand value. Media organisations, too, must report allegations responsibly. Sensational headlines, unnecessary exposure of complainants and speculative commentary can deepen the harm. Reporting should avoid victim-blaming, protect identities where required and clearly distinguish allegations from established findings. Practical safeguards are equally important. Production houses and event organisers should establish clear codes of conduct, protect minors, provide safe reporting channels and respond seriously to complaints. Creative organisations can help by developing professional standards and ensuring members are held accountable. Awareness campaigns alone are not enough. A powerful public message about consent means little if the people delivering it tolerate harassment behind the scenes. Beyond outrage, towards cultural change Ghana has no shortage of public condemnation when disturbing allegations emerge. The challenge is turning outrage into lasting change. Parents and schools must help young people understand boundaries and feel safe speaking up. Authorities must investigate complaints fairly and thoroughly. Institutions must guard against retaliation. The media must report responsibly, and the creative industry must examine what it normalises in the pursuit of views, applause and commercial success. Blaming music, comedy or popular culture for the actions of abusers would be simplistic and unfair. Sexual abuse involves individual choices, unequal power and failures of accountability. But culture influences how harmful behaviour is interpreted, challenged or excused. Creatives are therefore part of the conversation, not because they are responsible for every harm, but because they have the reach to challenge harmful attitudes and make healthier ones visible. The measure of a socially conscious creative industry is not how quickly it joins a trending conversation after a scandal. It is whether its work and professional practices help build a culture in which consent is respected, children are protected and abuse is never treated as entertainment. We cannot expect art to solve every social problem. We can, however, expect those who shape public culture to think carefully about the world their work helps create. Our creative industry cannot control every individual who abuses power. But it can help change what society tolerates, what it celebrates and what it refuses to excuse. That responsibility is not a distraction from creativity. It is part of what makes influence worth having. About the author: Amelley Djosu is a marketing communications strategist, creative entrepreneur and journalist who writes on the intersections of culture, creativity, commerce and social responsibility. She is interested in how Ghana’s creative industry can use its influence to shape public conversations, promote professional standards and contribute to meaningful social change.

title: Why Instagram is adding long-form videos
body: Instagram is to introduce long-form videos to the platform, despite being opposed to the idea for several years. On Monday, head of Instagram Adam Mosseri appeared in a video with the platform's vice president of products, Tessa Lyons, where he said a long-form video section called "Features" would be introduced in the weeks ahead. "We’re excited to give creators more room to tell their stories with the communities they've already built here," a caption accompanying the video read. Since introducing Reels, a short-form vertical video feature that followed in the success of TikTok, Meta has tended to prioritise videos that were under 90 seconds, insisting that users preferred shorter videos. "There's just so much different format now happening around creativity and storytelling on video that we want to make sure that we're doing a good job of serving," Ms Lyons said during the video. She said the Instagram team had analysed data that showed users were interested in longer videos. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Adam Mosseri (@mosseri) "We know that people like to get together in persona and actually watch Reels and video together, and we see this happening on TV, so we've been working on a TV version of Reels and we know that to do that well, we need more than just short-form video." On Threads, Mr Mosseri posted a video showing him with two prominent content creators, Colin and Samir, in which he explained more about the long-form video update. Users will be able to upload horizontal videos lasting up to 90 minutes, and those videos will be accessible through shorter versions of the video seen in the platform's Reels section, he said. According to the Hollywood Reporter , Meta indicated it would be testing the long-form videos with select US creators after a successful trial in Brazil. Meta also said its Instagram for TV app was now available for the Apple TV platform in the US. The app will also incorporate Instagram's long-form Features content.

title: Why Instagram is adding long-form videos
body: Instagram is to introduce long-form videos to the platform, despite being opposed to the idea for several years. On Monday, head of Instagram Adam Mosseri appeared in a video with the platform's vice president of products, Tessa Lyons, where he said a long-form video section called "Features" would be introduced in the weeks ahead. "We’re excited to give creators more room to tell their stories with the communities they've already built here," a caption accompanying the video read. Since introducing Reels, a short-form vertical video feature that followed in the success of TikTok, Meta has tended to prioritise videos that were under 90 seconds, insisting that users preferred shorter videos. "There's just so much different format now happening around creativity and storytelling on video that we want to make sure that we're doing a good job of serving," Ms Lyons said during the video. She said the Instagram team had analysed data that showed users were interested in longer videos. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Adam Mosseri (@mosseri) "We know that people like to get together in persona and actually watch Reels and video together, and we see this happening on TV, so we've been working on a TV version of Reels and we know that to do that well, we need more than just short-form video." On Threads, Mr Mosseri posted a video showing him with two prominent content creators, Colin and Samir, in which he explained more about the long-form video update. Users will be able to upload horizontal videos lasting up to 90 minutes, and those videos will be accessible through shorter versions of the video seen in the platform's Reels section, he said. According to the Hollywood Reporter , Meta indicated it would be testing the long-form videos with select US creators after a successful trial in Brazil. Meta also said its Instagram for TV app was now available for the Apple TV platform in the US. The app will also incorporate Instagram's long-form Features content.

body: Nigerian music star Burna Boy presented the Socrates Award to Arsenal forward Bukayo Saka at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony. The Afrobeats singer took to the stage to present the award to the England international during the prestigious football awards ceremony, bringing together two prominent figures from the worlds of music and football. title: Troops Kill 16 Suspected ISWAP Terrorists In Lake Chad Basin
body: The Joint Task Force (North East), Operation HADIN KAI (OPHK), has killed 16 suspected Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) fighters during coordinated air and artillery strikes on three suspected terrorist locations in the Tunbunma area of South Lake Chad. It said that the operation, which followed intelligence on the presence of key terrorist leaders and fighters, was part of efforts to sustain its relentless offensive against terrorist networks in the Lake Chad Basin, The Acting Military Information Officer. Captain Mohammed Goni, in a statement on Monday, said the operation was conducted between 1 a.m. and 2 a.m. on October 26, 2026, using air and ground weapon systems to engage the identified locations. “Battle Damage Assessment indicates that 16 ISWAP fighters were neutralised across the targeted locations,” the statement read in part. “Among those reportedly killed were Abu Zubiru, an Arab national, and two associates, Baana Nglewa and Jindullah Sadiq, alongside other fighters. Additionally, Abu Saleem, identified as the Wali of Tunbunma, sustained severe injuries alongside seven others.” Operation HADIN KAI reaffirmed that there is no hiding place for terrorists, adding that it remains committed to restoring peace and normalcy while conducting intelligence-led operations against terrorist elements in the North East. It urged members of the public to provide timely and credible information to security agencies to support ongoing counter-terrorism operations. This came as troops of the Joint Task Force North-West, Operation FANSAN YAMMA, neutralised eight suspected terrorists and rescued three kidnapped victims during coordinated operations in Katsina, Kaduna and Zamfara States. The operations also led to the recovery of an AK-47 rifle, three locally fabricated guns, three motorcycles, cutlasses and assorted charms. The Media Information Officer of the Joint Task Force, Captain Tamuno Sinivie, in a statement issued on Monday, explained that troops of Sector One, acting on a distress call from farmers at Machika Dam in Sabuwa Local Government Area of Katsina State on Saturday, October 24, engaged suspected terrorists in a gun battle, neutralising two of them while others fled. The post Troops Kill 16 Suspected ISWAP Terrorists In Lake Chad Basin appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Trump hits back at Obama over Saddam ‘Cheesecake Factory’ jab
body: US President Donald Trump hit back at Barack Obama on Monday after the former president jokingly said his successor’s White House looked as if it were a cheesecake restaurant run by Saddam Hussein. “For you to say it’s a Cheesecake Factory, that just shows why you were a lousy president,” Trump said in a three-minute diatribe when asked about Obama’s comments over the weekend. “Guys like Obama, they would pass the front door, they would see the broken masonry… He doesn’t notice dirt and filth where the walls haven’t been cleaned for years,” Trump told reporters as he headed for his latest midterm election rally. Cheesecake Factory is a popular restaurant chain known for its lengthy list of indulgent dishes and an eclectic interior design. Obama made a series of scathing criticisms of Republican Trump’s “chaos and cruelty” as he hit the stump for Democrats in Ohio and Michigan ahead of next week’s midterm elections. But it was Obama’s jabs at billionaire Trump’s prized renovations at the White House — including building a massive ballroom and adding gold-leafed ornamentation throughout the Oval Office — that really appeared to sting. “He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory,” Obama said on Saturday, referring to the Iraqi dictator who was executed in 2006 following the US invasion of Iraq. Trump has long had a bitter rivalry with Obama. He launched his own political career by pushing the racist and false “birther” conspiracy theory that the Democrat was lying about being born in the United States. But Trump’s rant over the cheesecake comments was also a sign of the 80-year-old’s increasingly short temper as the midterms loom. On Sunday night, Trump sent his longest ever post on his Truth Social network — a 1,300-word screed in which he railed not about Iran or the economy but about US comedian Bill Maher. Last week Trump also lashed out at a series of reporters as he faced questions about the midterms, in which Republicans face losing control of Congress, and his dealings with Russia.
