As it prepares to go public , Anthropic’s S-1 filing makes generative AI’s methane dependency glaringly obvious.
“Competition for access to electrical supply and data center locations with adequate power availability is intense.”
In documents filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission Monday, Anthropic acknowledges that data centers are becoming increasingly reliant on “natural gas” — the fossil fuel industry’s marketing term for what is primarily methane — leaving the company’s AI data center buildout vulnerable to rising fuel costs and existing supply chain constraints. And in a possible catch-22, Anthropic admits that rising global temperatures — a symptom of burning fossil fuels — will increase the company’s operating costs.
“Competition for access to electrical supply and data center locations with adequate power availability is intense,” Anthropic says, adding that some of its planned data centers rely on electricity generated by natural gas turbines on-site. Anthropic leases capacity from hyperscalers, but it announced a $50 billion dollar plan last year to expand data centers in Texas and New York.
The US, the epicenter for data centers globally, is planning to build more fossil fuel generation capacity than it has in a decade as data centers demand more electricity. Donald Trump’s administration has sought to kill renewable energy projects while tilting the regulatory landscape in favor of fossil fuels , which Trump claims is a more important energy source for powering data centers around the clock than solar and wind farms that generate power intermittently.
Now, a shortage of gas turbines is slowing data center construction . Some developers are installing gas engines on-site as a way to avoid long wait times to connect to power grids. Developers are also turning to more simple turbine technology at these sites as they face backlogs from turbine manufacturers, making on-site power generation less efficient and more polluting as a result.
Data center electricity demand could wipe out decades of gains in air quality over the next five years, one recent Texas-based study found — raising levels of soot, smog-forming pollutants, and planet-heating carbon dioxide. Even as data centers create more greenhouse gas pollution, Anthropic’s S-1 points to climate change as a risk to its bottom line. It will have to pay more for electricity and water to cool servers at data centers as temperatures climb.
Nevertheless, Anthropic expects increased competition for natural gas and pipeline capacity from hyperscalers and cloud service providers rushing to build their own data centers. “This competition could drive up the price of natural gas,” the company notes.
Gas makes up the biggest chunk of the US electricity mix, 40 percent of the nation’s power generation . And Americans are already feeling the pain of rising costs as utilities scramble to upgrade energy infrastructure and meet rising power demand.
Pissed-off residents have successfully blocked dozens of proposed data centers across the US . Anthropic acknowledges that the specter of ballooning utility bills is enough to interfere with a data center project. “If our efforts to secure electrical power are perceived to affect other utility customers and the broader grid, regulators may impose conditions, standby charges, or other requirements intended to address such impacts,” it says.
If regulators push data center developers to shoulder more of the costs for new energy infrastructure, Anthropic says that could also raise its operating costs. And without a secure gas supply and the pipelines to transport the fuel, the company says, it might need to delay or abandon planned data center projects altogether.
Ultimately, these challenges could stunt Anthropic’s growth:
Any failure to secure access to adequate electrical power, any legal, regulatory, or other administrative action or change limiting the availability of electricity, or any significant increase in energy or compliance costs, could adversely affect our cost structure and limit our ability to scale our compute infrastructure, develop and deploy our models, and service our customers.

title: Russia sentences an IT specialist to 13 years for donating to Ukraine’s military. Binance helped investigators prove their case.
body: The Second Western District Military Court has sentenced Yuri Belenky, a 49-year-old IT specialist, to 13 years in prison for financing terrorism, the human rights group Department One reported. Belenky will serve the first three years in prison before being transferred to a high-security penal colony. The court also fined him 500,000 rubles and ordered the confiscation of another 126,000 rubles. News of Belenky’s detention emerged in late 2025. He had lived in Bulgaria since 2015 and regularly visited Russia. He was detained at Sheremetyevo Airport in September 2025, initially jailed for the administrative offense of petty hooliganism, and then charged with financing terrorism. The case stemmed from donations to an account whose details blogger Arkady Babchenko had published. Russian investigators were able to prove that the transfers took place “thanks to a detailed report that the cryptocurrency exchange Binance sent in response to a request from the Investigative Committee,” Department One said. title: Mobile internet to be restricted in central Moscow October 27-29 during Russia-Africa and gas exporters’ summits
body: Mobile internet access in central Moscow could be restricted from October 27 to 29, Russia’s Digital Development Ministry said. The restrictions are planned inside the Third Ring Road during the day, starting at 11:30 a.m. on October 27 and 28 and at 9:30 a.m. on October 29. The ministry said the restrictions were needed to ensure security during the Russia-Africa summit and the Gas Exporting Countries Forum summit. Websites exempt from the restrictions, voice calls, and Wi-Fi will remain available in Moscow on those days, the ministry said. The Gas Exporting Countries Forum will take place in Moscow on October 27, followed by the Russia-Africa summit on October 28 and 29. Russian presidential aide Yuri Ushakov previously said that 22 African leaders would attend the Russia-Africa summit. The presidents of Iran and Equatorial Guinea and the emir of Qatar will attend the Gas Exporting Countries Forum. Mobile Internet blackouts in Russia The Kremlin says it’s cutting off mobile Internet access for security reasons. Muscovites say they’re resigning themselves to regular blackouts. ‘We’re back in the early 2000s’ Mobile Internet blackouts are now routine in many Russian regions. title: Jordan strikes southern Syria after linking church attackers to 'terrorist groups'
body: Jordan said on Monday its air force struck what it described as militant hideouts in southern Syria after determining that the suspects behind last week's deadly church attack in the kingdom were linked to "terrorist groups" operating there.The armed forces said the operation was conducted in coordination with Damascus. There was no immediate comment from Syrian authorities. Five civilians, including women and children, were killed as a result of the Jordanian strikes, a health official told Syria's state news agency.There was no immediate comment from Jordan on that account.Hours earlier, senior government security officials said their security forces had arrested two brothers and their brother-in-law after a shootout on Monday over the church violence that killed nine people."God willing, they only represent themselves," said Jordan's Director of Public Security, Major-General Obeidallah al-Maaytah.Such violence is highly unusual in Jordan, a relatively stable US ally in the Middle East. Friday's attack on the Christian minority prompted King Abdullah to order security forces to respond with an "iron fist."In a press conference, al-Maaytah and Interior Minister Mazen al-Faraya said the country would not tolerate extremist terrorism."The file has not yet been closed; investigations are still ongoing. As of today, there are no indications of any links between them and other cells," al-Faraya added.At least 34 injured after gunmen attack funeral serviceFriday's assault during a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in the village of Hamoud, about 120 km (75 miles) southwest of the capital, Amman, also wounded at least 34 people. Witnesses said gunmen opened fire for several minutes. The suspects, who lived near Hamoud, will face justice, said the security officials. The three suspects were named in the press briefing.Reuters video footage showed a building pockmarked by the exchange of fire in the village of al-Judayyda, in Karak governorate.Jordan's Public Security Directorate said in a statement carried by state media that security forces located the suspects while they were hiding in an abandoned house. They refused to surrender and attacked security forces, who returned fire and arrested all three after wounding them.No security personnel were injured, and security forces found a number of firearms and rounds of ammunition in the suspects' possession.There has been no claim of responsibility for the church attack.Jordan, a US partner in the fight against extremism, has foiled Islamist militant plots in the past. The security officials did not name any Islamist groups in the press conference.Syria condemns strikes, launches investigationSyria's government condemned the strikes, claiming they had been carried out "without prior coordination or notification from the Syrian side," state-run Sana news agency said in a Tuesday report. The government also expressed its "full solidarity" with the affected Syrian families and "heartfelt condolences to the martyrs' families," the report said. It added that authorities are closely monitoring the situation and will provide "immediate required support and humanitarian relief.Additionally, it said that "comprehensive investigations" have been launched to "establish the full circumstances of the targeting" and underscored the importance of joint security coordination between the two countries. Syria also closed the Nassib border crossing with Jordan and suspended passenger and commercial traffic from both sides.

title: Israel’s moment of truth: Knesset election pivotal to future US-Israel relationship - opinion
body: The upcoming election in Israel will likely prove pivotal in determining whether the ongoing erosion in support for Israel in the United States devolves further into a full rupture that makes both Americans and Israelis less secure.As Americans, we are not interested in picking winners and losers. Israelis should decide such things, but our friends there should understand the consequences of their decisions.Our colleague Mark Dubowitz has recently warned of possible American financial warfare against Israel. Some of this risk is linked to a growing campaign of antisemitism and anti-Zionism that has exploded since the October 7 terror attacks plunged the Middle East into conflict. But some of this is also linked to senseless violence in the West Bank and other concerns.If the next government in Israel, regardless of who leads it, fails to punish and end lawlessness and cruelty by anarchists in the West Bank, there could be painful consequences. We firmly support Israel's right to exist and defend itself and believe that America is safer, and US interests in the Middle East are more secure, when a strong Israel works closely with Washington. We are proud that America and Israel have fought together to defend common interests and to counter common enemies.Enemies of US engaged in unprecedented cooperation, understand value of partnershipsAmerica's enemies – namely the Axis of Aggressors, consisting of China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea – are engaged in unprecedented cooperation. Our foes understand the value of partnerships.America needs partners, too, especially capable and motivated partners like Israel. We need Israel's muscles in the Middle East so we can focus more on deterring and defeating aggression by Beijing, Moscow, or Pyongyang. Americans also benefit from Israel's defense-technology expertise and defense-acquisition agility, which can help ensure American warfighters wield the best weapons.But we are witnessing a sad paradox with Israel. On one hand, Israel has demonstrated that it is the most powerful military in the Middle East, worthy of closer cooperation with the United States. Israel has battled back and gained the upper hand in a regional war that it neither started nor wanted. And yet, in the United States, Israel is more unpopular than it has been in years. This is clear in recent polls from Pew, Gallup, and the Ronald Reagan Institute.This is a strategic liability for Israel. A steep decline in approval could lead the next Congress and US administration to adopt policies that undermine our bilateral relationship, including defense cooperation. That would materially damage the security of both the US and Israel.Some in Israel may respond by shrugging and saying, “Fine, Israel will just become independent and self-sufficient in its defense production and arm itself.” But that is not possible. Israel is heavily reliant on major American-made platforms and will remain so for decades.True defense production independence doesn't just require assembly lines in Israel. It also requires suppliers and raw materials in Israel. Many of the inputs for Israeli-produced weapons are imported, meaning a hostile administration could try to block them. Israel's enemies are actively working to drive a wedge between Washington and Jerusalem. The goal is to slowly but surely deprive Israel of the means to defend itself. Unfortunately, those enemies are capitalizing on some Israeli unforced errors.It is certainly true that some of the withering criticism of Israel will continue regardless of the country's policies. It is also true that enemies are increasingly well-organized and funded, and they are conducting information warfare against the United States and Israel.But explaining the negative shift in opinion in America solely through those dynamics is simply unrealistic. Such efforts ignore the agency of the Israeli government and encourage a dangerous apathy in terms of undertaking necessary reforms. The rule of law and the distinction between combatant and noncombatant are a primary difference between defenders of Western civilization and the terrorists who murdered innocents on September 11, 2001, and October 7, 2023.US-Israel security cooperation needed more than everAs threats to Americans grow, we need US-Israel security cooperation more than ever. And Israel needs continued American diplomatic and defense cooperation. But this could prove difficult if some Israeli policies continue.Battles against the terrorist regime in Iran and its proxies will continue, as will the fight against disinformation and blind hate that unfairly targets Israel. But that does not absolve Israel from making some crucial decisions about its own conduct. The fate of the US-Israel alliance could hang in the balance. Bradley Bowman is senior director of the Center on Military and Political Power at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD). Jonathan Schanzer is executive director at FDD.

title: Blakeman’s bank statements don’t match his disclosure reports
body: 🚨🚨MUST READ🚨🚨: Mayor Zohran Mamdani and a group of fellow basketball enthusiasts have been secretly using the NYPD Police Academy’s gymnasium in Queens to play pickup ball, according to four people familiar with the games. The mayor and his crew typically show up around 10 or 11 p.m. and enter surreptitiously through a loading dock before hitting the court. While sports fanaticism has often buoyed the political brand of past mayors, Mamdani’s choice of venue is raising eyebrows. Read the story from POLITICO’s Graham Rayman, Chris Sommerfeldt and Joe Anuta here . FINANCE FLAWS: Republican gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman’s campaign finance disclosure reports have been plagued by inaccuracies since the spring. Copies of the campaign’s bank statements obtained by POLITICO suggest his filings might have even more problems than previously suspected. According to a disclosure report submitted to the state Board of Elections earlier this month, the Blakeman campaign had only $178,000 in the bank as of Sept. 28. Yet the campaign’s checking account had a balance of $1.7 million on Sept. 28, according to TD Bank’s monthly statement. The bank records also show dozens of transactions that are missing from his campaign finance filings. On July 29, for example, the bank statements identified the campaign using a check with the number 1156 to make a $13,500 payment to an unspecified recipient. Yet Blakeman’s campaign finance reports do not identify any transactions that used check number 1156. It also hasn’t shown a single payment totaling $13,500 at any point over the past year. In addition, there are instances in which the bank records show apparent contributions to the campaign that never show up in the disclosure reports. The statements show Blakeman was wired $18,000 by actress Lois Robbins on Sept. 2, for example, while the filings don’t show any transactions totaling $18,000 within two weeks of that date or any donations from Robbins. An $18,000 wire from attorney and campaign finance chair Howard Fensterman in July similarly doesn’t match anything in the disclosure reports. Blakeman is the first gubernatorial candidate in state history to participate in the new matching funds program that lets him receive up to $3.5 million in public money. Then-Mayor Eric Adams was blocked from participating in a similar New York City program last year due to discrepancies between his bank statements and disclosure reports. Reinvent Albany’s Kyle Kennedy said he didn’t know the cause of the discrepancies, but that it could just be due to “the timing of when things were recorded.” But, he noted, Blakeman’s campaign “will automatically be audited by the Board of Elections after the election. … Campaign finance enforcement takes place after elections, not in real-time.” Blakeman’s campaign didn’t respond to a request to explain the discrepancies. It has previously said its campaign finance problems are due to technical issues caused by a large number of donors. Several of the candidate’s campaign finance disclosure reports have been repeatedly amended, often in ways that made the initial numbers wildly inaccurate. His July report showed him with $4.7 million in the bank; that was changed a week later to show his balance was $6.1 million; then in August it was changed to $4.3 million. As POLITICO reported earlier this month , Blakeman has received about $360,000 in donations over the contribution limit that he still needs to return. Many of the donations he has already returned have been highly unusual — one person who gave $1 in July was quickly refunded $780.76. His campaign then said he accidentally submitted some duplicate contributions. Nearly a month later, it hasn’t amended the filing to show which transactions were real. And as New York Focus reported , the Blakeman campaign submitted requests to receive matching funds for 2,600 donations that were ineligible for matches. From the Capitol THE WEEKEND TURNOUT: Early voting turnout has skyrocketed in every corner of the state, according to unofficial tallies provided by the state Board of Elections. On the first two days of early voting in 2022, 261,735 people cast a ballot. This weekend, that number increased to 485,205 — a jump of roughly 85 percent. The biggest increases were in the North Country — particularly in the congressional seat being vacated by Rep. Elise Stefanik, which is now a battleground district for the first time in over a decade. Washington County’s weekend turnout was up 236 percent from four years ago. Early voting increased 196 percent in St. Lawrence County, 182 percent in Warren County, and 179 percent in Herkimer County. The smallest gains were in the Hudson Valley. That was especially true in the district held by Democratic Rep. Pat Ryan, where early turnout was the highest in the state four years ago as Ryan won his first full term in a nail-biter. His race isn’t widely viewed as competitive this year, and the smallest increase among the state’s 62 counties was in Ulster, which was up only 41 percent relative to 2022. There were also relatively middling gains in Erie County (up 60 percent) and Nassau County (up 64 percent). Those are the places where New York’s two gubernatorial candidates live, perhaps indicating that neither is yet the beneficiary of any outpourings of hometown pride. — Bill Mahoney FROM THE CAMPAIGN TRAIL ORDER’S UP: Republican Rep. Mike Lawler spent part of this afternoon working at McDonald’s in Haverstraw – a potential backup job “if things don’t work out in November,” he said while putting on his uniform. Lawler is in the final campaign stretch in one of the country’s most closely watched congressional battlegrounds against Democrat Cait Conley. The lawmaker spent his McDonald’s shift cooking food, handing out orders and speaking with constituents – one of whom openly admitted to voting against him before taking their food and driving off. Aside from that one outlier, customers gave Lawler a warm reception at the drive-thru window. The visit was seemingly part of an effort to make inroads in Haverstraw, a town that leans Democratic. Lawler told POLITICO he’s feeling confident going into the final days of his campaign, but insisted that he is an underdog in the Hudson Valley district. In the 2024 presidential election, Kamala Harris and Lawler each won the district. “I feel very good about where we are heading on Election Day. Eight days from now, we’re going to win because I’ve done the work,” Lawler said in an interview. “I’ve delivered for my district, and the people here know me. I’m from here; I’ve lived here my whole life, I know the community..” And for those wondering about Lawler’s go-to McDonald’s order: double quarter-pounder with cheese, a Coke and a four-piece McNugget. — Katelyn Cordero STUMPING SPRINT: Fresh off a weekend of enthusiastic campaigning for Gov. Kathy Hochul , the mayor addressed reporters at a press conference this morning. He stuck to his rhetoric touting the governor as a champion for affordable child care and lampooning her GOP foe Bruce Blakeman as a Trump puppet. The mayor was also pressed about whether he expects something in return for all the campaigning he’s been doing for Hochul — such as increased taxes on the rich, a top goal for Mamdani and his democratic socialist allies in the state Legislature. “I’m expecting a continuation of a positive and productive working relationship with the governor,” he said. “I’m excited for that relationship to continue. It’s been one that’s delivered for working class New Yorkers, and I’m confident it’s going to keep delivering.” It’s far from an explicit commitment, but it suggests he’ll continue pushing Hochul for tax hikes should she win reelection — something City Council Speaker Julie Menin told POLITICO she would support to bankroll child care programs earlier this month. Mamdani also repeatedly mentioned the importance of showing New Yorkers that a mayor and a governor can have a productive working relationship — an apparent dig at the storied feud between former Mayor Bill de Blasio and former Governor Andrew Cuomo . “New Yorkers across the five boroughs are excited about us finally working together, where they haven’t seen mayors and governors do that often in the past to be able to deliver on common sense things,” he said. — Molly Reinmann FROM CITY HALL GRAND PLANS: Mamdani’s chief of staff Elle Bisgaard-Church laid out the democratic socialist administration’s governing philosophy today — including its opposition to means-testing for government programs. “We look especially to universal social programs, facilitating forms of collective ownership, supporting the growth of unions. In short, creating shared economic security and stability through material programs,” Bisgaard-Church said at an event on Mamdani’s affordability agenda hosted by the New York City Policy Forum, a left-leaning research and publishing network. “On the contrary, means-tested programs segregate and encumber people.” She pointed to other periods in the city’s history that saw “rich public institutions that could compete with the private sector,” citing NYCHA, the MTA and CUNY. Public housing, in particular, has seen significant deterioration in recent decades amid federal disinvestment. Reversing that trajectory is one of the most pressing issues Mamdani faces as mayor. “Today we are governed by rules of austerity and face a withered welfare regime, means-tested policies, decayed public sector, and weakened public institutions,” Bisgaard-Church continued. “These are the political realities our administration wants to overturn, and we know that tackling the crushing cost of living is again key to doing so.” The event drew other top Mamdani officials including Deputy Mayor for Housing and Planning Leila Bozorg, Economic Development Corporation Chair Lina Khan, and Consumer and Worker Protection Commissioner Sam Levine. — Janaki Chadha IN OTHER NEWS — HOMELESSNESS: Mamdani’s early efforts to address a ballooning homelessness problem in the city have largely failed, community leaders allege. ( The Wall Street Journal ) — SUNNYSIDE YARD: Housing experts weighed in on the outlandishly high cost of Mamdani and Trump’s proposed development at Sunnyside Yard. ( The City Reporter ) — BK DEMS: There are four state legislative seats Democrats are looking to flip in southern Brooklyn this midterm cycle, a fact that has largely been overshadowed by the party’s drama-packed leadership succession saga. title: Inside Russia’s shadow oil trade: WSJ examines how a failed business partnership led to multimillion-dollar lawsuits and allegations of threats involving Chechen fighters
body: Igor Soglayev (left) and Igor Sechin in 2013 After Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Russian oil came under sanctions, and little-known intermediaries using shell companies and a shadow fleet of tankers took over a large share of its exports. A network of companies linked to Azerbaijani businessmen Tahir Garayev and Etibar Eyyub became one of Rosneft’s main oil traders. They are now in a legal battle with former Rosneft executive Igor Soglayev, who sought to make money reselling Russian diesel in Brazil. Documents from the litigation reviewed by The Wall Street Journal offer a glimpse into how Russian oil and petroleum products have been exported since the war began. Soglayev is a former Deutsche Bank executive in Russia and former head of SamaraNefteOrgSintez, a petrochemical company that Rosneft bought in 2015. After the acquisition, he headed Rosneft’s petrochemicals department and, according to the Journal, also served as an adviser to its chief, Igor Sechin. In 2017, he left to pursue private ventures in the petrochemical industry. After the war began, Soglayev decided to make money selling Russian diesel in Brazil. He wanted to act as an intermediary for buyers worried that, because of sanctions, dealing directly with Russia could cause problems with their banks. He planned to buy diesel in Russia and resell it at a markup to Brazilian distributors. In preparation, he leased fuel storage capacity at Brazilian ports. According to Soglayev, his suppliers were oil traders known as the Coral network. The network took its name from Coral Energy, a company established in Singapore in 2010 to trade Azerbaijani oil. Its former executives, Garayev and Eyyub, became two of the leading sellers of Rosneft’s crude in 2022. Companies controlled by the two businessmen assembled most of the shadow fleet used to export Russian oil. Soglayev founded a firm called Dia33 in Dubai and bought Russian diesel from another Dubai firm in late 2023. He alleges that the firm’s head, Andrey Romanovskiy, was linked to the Coral network and that the two men even discussed the possibility of Dia33 becoming Coral’s Brazilian division. But the relationship soured when a Brazilian port turned away an aging tanker carrying tens of millions of dollars’ worth of diesel. The ship waited for several weeks to be unloaded before another port accepted it. The Journal does not specify whether the diesel reached the final buyer. Either way, the fuel sellers, allegedly linked to the Coral network, accused Soglayev of misappropriating the cargo. They filed a lawsuit in Dubai, resulting in an order requiring him to pay $42 million. He responded with lawsuits of his own in Dubai and Brazil, alleging that Coral had used the prospect of a partnership as a pretext to gain access to Dia33’s internal information and poach its clients. He estimated his lost profits at more than $500 million. Soglayev said he also received threats. In particular, he took it as a death threat when Eyyub called and told him he had discussed their dispute with a “Chechen warlord,” the Journal reported. The litigation is ongoing. In the summer of 2026, a Dubai court barred Eyyub, Garayev, and 13 other individuals and companies from disposing of assets worth up to $700 million as an interim measure in Soglayev’s lawsuit. The judge later questioned whether he had jurisdiction to hear the case. Soglayev appealed the judge’s decision, and the asset freeze remains in effect. Russian energy exports Trump’s diesel deal with Putin, a rebuke from Brussels, and a squabble over Europe’s enormous Russian energy bill A long shadow How Russia uses a covert fleet of ships to ferry oil around the globe and what the West is doing to stop it At Meduza, we are committed to transparency about our use of artificial intelligence in the newsroom. The story you’re reading was written by one of our living, breathing journalists and translated from Russian using an AI model configured to follow our strict editorial standards. This translation process is the result of extensive testing and refinements to ensure our English-language coverage is timely and accurate. A Meduza editor reviews every draft before publication. title: Council chairman sponsors Igbo-Eze South youths for aviation training
body:
The sky is no longer the limit for young people of Igbo-Eze South Local Government Area of Enugu State as the council Chairman, Ugo Ferdinand Ukwueze, continues to translate his youth development ambition into tangible opportunities.
The latest is the sponsorship of youths from the area for a fully funded professional aviation training at the prestigious Lagos Aviation Academy.
The beneficiaries, who have already settled into their new academic environment and commenced lectures in the Academy’s batch 94/95 Cabin Crew class, mark the beginning of an exciting journey towards professional careers in the aviation industry.
For these young people, the opportunity represents more than classroom instruction; it is a gateway to acquiring specialised skills, gaining industry exposure and pursuing careers in a globally connected sector.
Through this initiative, Mr Ukwueze is investing in the capacity of young people to participate in an increasingly competitive and opportunity-driven world. It is a practical expression of the human capital development pillar of his administration’s Progress Agenda, complementing Governor Peter Mbah’s “Tomorrow Is Here” vision and the broader possibilities emerging from the growth of Enugu State’s aviation sector, which the launch of our dear Enugu Airline has made even more evident.
At the grassroots level, this vision finds practical expression when young people are equipped with the knowledge, competencies, and professional exposure required to compete beyond their immediate environments. By these efforts, the Ukwueze administration has demonstrated how local governance can complement the broader development aspirations of the Enugu State Government, ensuring that the promise of a transformed state reaches young people in Igbo-Eze South.
Aviation is a specialised and increasingly interconnected field, and access to professional training can open pathways to employment and career advancement. By creating access to this opportunity, the Igbo-Eze South chairman is helping beneficiaries take practical steps towards their ambitions while broadening the horizons of other young people who aspire to similar professional accomplishments. The ambition is to build a community where the dreams of young people are not limited by their backgrounds or geographic location, but are strengthened by access to education, relevant skills and opportunities for advancement. This commitment forms part of the broader Progress Agenda, with human capital development serving as an essential pillar of sustainable grassroots progress.
The trainees who have already begun this new chapter at Lagos Aviation Academy carry with them the hopes of their families, communities and the wider Igbo-Eze South Local Government Area. The message resonates beyond the walls of the Academy, and for the beneficiaries, tomorrow is already here.

title: French students vow more protests despite Macron government's concessions
body: French student leaders vowed to go on protesting despite government concessions on education, keeping pressure on President Emmanuel Macron as the movement spreads to unions and other activists, stokes unrest and deepens the economic damage.The measures included a commitment to cap the size of some high school classes; €4 billion ($4.5 billion) of loans for renovating schools; and the replacement by 2028 of a university admissions system students see as socially unfair."Not all our demands were met. We'll go on for as long as it takes," Louis Letoublon, one of the representatives of high school students, said as he and fellow student leaders emerged from a meeting with government officials in Paris.The protests, which have broadened beyond education to draw in trade unions and yellow-vest activists, known for their high-visibility jackets, pose a test for Macron's minority government.The government has little room to spend its way out of the unrest, with national debt approaching 120% of GDP, while the turmoil is boosting support for far-right frontrunner Marine Le Pen ahead of next year's presidential election.The package included €1 billion of investment in university campuses; a move to increase student grants with inflation; and the opening up of a further 15,000 higher education places for students."It's clear we have to ease the pressure being felt in the education system," Education Minister Edouard Geffray told a press conference.There was no overall figure for how much funding the package would require. High borrowing needs are already complicating efforts to agree a budget for next year.Protests show little sign of easing after nine days of violenceThe protests, initially triggered by student discontent, have shown little sign of ending after violence nine days ago engulfed dozens of cities, leading to fears the state had lost control of the streets.Earlier, Macron acknowledged it was likely there would be more unrest this weekend ahead of a bigger nationwide day of protests set for November 5.On a tour to survey the damage in Marseille and to thank emergency services after Saturday's protests, he said he would keep security measures in place and work to move protests outside city centers.Candidate Le Pen, already the frontrunner in next year's presidential election, has benefited from the unrest and perceptions that authorities are struggling to keep the peace.An opinion poll published on Sunday put her on 32% to 33.5%, well ahead of her nearest rival, hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon on 17%. Surveys suggest she would easily defeat Melenchon in a run-off ballot, expected to be held in early May.Over 1,400 arrested during protests on SaturdayInterior Minister Laurent Nunez earlier said that 1,435 people were arrested nationwide during demonstrations on Saturday and that police had also recorded a new phenomenon, with organized far-right gangs confronting far-left activists in several cities."We knew there had been calls from numerous identity-based and nationalist movements to come out, officially, to defend businesses," he said. "In a number of cities, such as Nice and Montpellier, these groups arrived in organized formations, mainly to target the ultra-left movement."A selloff in French government bonds paused on Monday after rating agency Moody's on Friday refrained from downgrading the country's sovereign debt.But business leaders said the unrest was continuing to inflict heavy economic damage.Alain Di Crescenzo, head of the CCI France network of chambers of commerce and industry, said many retailers had remained closed as a precaution after the violence of October 17, adding this had led to sharp falls in sales."We have shopkeepers who are tired and demoralized, and we are killing local commerce," he told Radio Classique.

title: FBI arrests CIA contractor for allegedly leaking secret defense, Middle East intel to journalist
body: A US Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) contractor with Top Secret security clearance was arrested by the FBI on Friday for allegedly leaking classified defense and Middle East-related information to an individual who published the information online, according to the US Department of Justice (DOJ).The contractor, 42-year-old Ian Brinksman, worked for a US government agency based in Virginia since 2020 before being hired by a contractor to the same agency in 2022. Throughout his employment, Brinksman held the Top Secret security clearance with access to Sensitive Compartmented Information.In a statement about the arrest, CIA Director John Ratcliffe confirmed that Brinksman provided services to the CIA as a contractor. Brinksman accused of leaking information for use in publicationThe criminal complaint against Brinksman alleged that he had an ongoing personal relationship with a person the DOJ identified as “Individual 1,” who claimed to have published reporting based on classified government intelligence assessments. An affidavit for the arrest included an email Brinksman sent to a friend in which he stated that he had recently begun seeing “a lady” who worked as a journalist and wrote articles on the online publishing platform Substack.Brinksman told the friend that the lady's work focused on foreign policy and that he was “helping her get that off the ground.”Brinksman's workplace, a facility that stores and processes classified information, does not allow employees to bring cellphones or personal electronics into the facility for security reasons.According to the DOJ, Brinksman was documented on multiple occasions entering his workplace, accessing specific Top Secret reports, then exiting the facility and speaking to Individual 1 on the phone.Shortly after speaking with Brinksman, Individual 1 posted Substack articles containing classified information related to the Top Secret reports Brinksman accessed.According to the affidavit, Brinksman is accused of sharing information from at least five Top Secret intelligence reports, including material that “reasonably could be expected to cause exceptionally grave damage to the national security” of the US if leaked. None of the reports Brinksman allegedly leaked fell within the scope of his work.Affidavit details align with Substack articles published by American journalistThe DOJ and FBI did not identify Individual 1 or her Substack, but The Jerusalem Post's analysis of the details of the affidavit found that the information may align with American journalist Aida Chavez and articles written by her for Substack publication Capital & Empire. Reports from both Ynet and the New York Post also connected Chavez to the information released by the DOJ, but Chavez has not been charged with any offenses related to the investigation into Brinksman or officially linked to the case.The affidavit notes multiple dates on which Individual 1 is alleged to have published articles containing classified information leaked by Brinksman.Articles published by Chavez on corresponding dates cite sources including a “confidential US intelligence assessment,” a “classified CIA assessment,” and a “classified CIA analysis.”Many of the articles alleged to contain leaked confidential information discussed Israel, US-Israel relations, and the ongoing war with Iran.

title: Ballon d’Or 2026: Spain’s Luis de la Fuente wins men’s Coach of the Year award
body: Spain national team manager Luis de la Fuente has won the Men’s Coach of the Year award at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony after leading Spain to victory at the 2026 FIFA World Cup. De la Fuente emerged victorious ahead of fellow nominees Mikel Arteta of Arsenal, Luis Enrique of Paris Saint-Germain, Vincent Kompany of Bayern Munich and Unai Emery of Aston Villa. Former Liverpool manager Rafa Benitez presented the award, although the announcement was briefly interrupted by an unexpected mix-up involving the winner’s name on the card. Benitez eventually announced De la Fuente as the winner, prompting the Spanish coach to shake hands with Emery and Spain international Lamine Yamal before making his way to the stage. The award adds to De la Fuente’s achievements with the Spanish national team, following Spain’s triumph at the 2026 FIFA World Cup. title: Ukraine, Moldova Sign New Military Cooperation Agreement, Vow to Join EU Together
body:
Ukraine and Moldova have deepened bilateral ties by signing a new military cooperation agreement intended to counter Russian threats, while pledging to pursue EU membership side by side.
The deal was struck during Moldovan Prime Minister Vasile Tofan’s visit to Kyiv on Monday, Oct. 26, where he met with his Ukrainian counterpart Serhii Koretsky and President Volodymyr Zelensky.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“We agreed to resume the work of the Intergovernmental Commission on Trade and Economic Cooperation and the ‘ Odesa Triangle ’ format, which brings together Ukraine, Moldova and Romania,” Koretskyi said in a statement on Telegram.
“We plan to hold the first meeting of the triangle at the level of prime ministers,” he continued. However, no additional information was provided on when the meeting could take place.
The two countries’ EU ambitions cannot be pulled apart, both Ukrainian leaders said.
Koretskyi argued that each country’s accession would strengthen the other’s security, adding that moving towards the bloc together also makes economic sense.
“Moldova and Ukraine are definitely stronger when we move together in this direction. It is important that we continue to be together, because this is true,” Zelensky said, according to the Presidential Office.
Two two sides agreed that any attempt to separate Ukraine’s and Moldova’s paths to EU membership would be inacceptable.
Such an attempt previously came in July, when Hungary signaled it was prepared to approve the screening results only for Moldova’s Cluster 3 while continuing to block Ukraine’s progress . Other EU member states, led by Ireland – which held the rotating Council presidency – opposed splitting the two countries’ accession tracks.
Regional security featured prominently in Zelensky’s talks with Tofan, with a particular focus on the situation in Transnistria, the unrecognized, Russian-backed breakaway region along Moldova’s border with Ukraine.
The leaders also discussed wider security challenges in the region and closer military cooperation, which the prime ministers formalized with Monday’s military-technical agreement.
“It is important to deliver results for our people and our countries,” Zelensky said in a statement on Telegram.
Because of Russia’s full-scale war, now in its fifth year, has significantly reshaped how vital cargo moves between countries, much of the discussion centered on keeping those routes open.
Zelensky proposed restoring the Solidarity Lanes , transit routes that would speed up the export of Ukrainian goods to other European countries via railway, road and inland waterways.
Meanwhile, Koretskyi thanked Moldova for discounted rail freight rates, which the sides agreed on in response to Russian attacks in the Black Sea. Ukrainian support for Moldova’s water supply was on the agenda as well, although no further details were provided.
The two countries confirmed that they are ready to expand joint control to two more border crossing points, with an agreement due in the near future.
Energy remains a central pillar of the relationship between the two neighbors, particularly since Ukraine halted the transit of Russian gas to Europe at the start of 2025.
Zelensky thanked Chișinău for supporting the Vertical Gas Corridor, a route that allows gas to reach Ukraine through Romania and Moldova, as well as for its decision to discount gas transit via the Trans-Balkan route.
Koretskyi also praised the transit arrangements and noted that Moldovan companies are already storing gas in Ukrainian facilities.
In a Sept. 30 analysis, the Atlantic Council proposed using Ukraine’s underground storage network to distribute US gas across European markets. Ukraine’s storage operator, Ukrtransgaz, puts the network’s total capacity at 30.95 billion cubic meters (1.09 trillion cubic feet).
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Russian attack on energy facility in Chernivtsi region causes power outages
body:
Ruslan Osypenko, head of the regional military administration, reported this on Facebook , according to Ukrinform.
“On the evening of October 26, Bukovina came under attack by a jet-powered strike drone . Debris from the drone damaged one of the region’s power facilities, leading to a forced power outage,” he said.
According to Osypenko, there were no fatalities or injuries.
All emergency services are on the scene, and restoration work has already begun.
Chernivtsioblenergo, for its part, reported damage to the power grids that could lead to “significant emergency power outages.”
“Emergency crews are working around the clock to repair the damage as quickly as possible and ensure a stable power supply,” the statement said.
Chernivtsi Vodokanal reported on Facebook that due to the power outage, water in Chernivtsi is being supplied at reduced pressure. The situation is under control, and stabilization efforts are ongoing.
As reported by Ukrinform, as of the morning of October 26, power outages affecting consumers were recorded in six regions due to Russian attacks.

title: Uniqlo to move into old Nordstrom building in downtown Vancouver
body:
Downtown Vancouver’s shopping scene is getting another fashion retailer in the old Nordstrom building.
Japanese clothing store, Uniqlo , announced it is opening up a new flagship store early next year.
The opening coincides with the 10-year anniversary of the company launching its first B.C. store in Metrotown in Burnaby.
Since Nordstrom closed in 2023, many have speculated as to what storefront could fill the space and last year it was announced that the 230,000-square-foot space would be divided into four units.
Simons and Aritzia have both announced their plans to take up two quadrants and after Uniqlo takes over the third, there will be one vacant spot.
Nordstrom first occupied the prime and pricey location in 2015, as the high-end Seattle retailer expanded northward.
Its exit marked the third time a major retailer has left the massive Pacific Centre location empty, after previously being home to Eaton’s and Sears.
Aritzia said its store will span four levels and there are plans to include a “casual yet elevated” dining concept as well.

title: Why Anthropic’s IPO Prospectus Is Missing So Many Key Figures
body:
“Claude has experienced the fastest enterprise adoption of any technology in history, as demonstrated by revenue growing from $0 at commercial launch in the first quarter of 2023 to $_____ for the three months ended September 30, 2026,” reads the first of dozens of such examples.
It’s relatively common for companies to redact certain information in their S-1 filings, and Securities and Exchange Commission rules allow for a certain degree of leniency around the practice, particularly when it comes to information considered “confidential.”
Still, it’s helpful to know what, exactly, these companies decide to leave out. In Anthropic’s case, the missing details largely revolve around financials for its most recent quarter, which concluded at the end of September, and lease agreements tied to its compute investments. While experts expect many details to be disclosed before Anthropic goes public, their current absence may hint at the uncertainties of investing in artificial intelligence, as companies work to secure sufficient compute.
Anthropic did not respond to a request for comment.
Michael Dambra, an accounting and law professor at the University at Buffalo School of Management, tells WIRED that there are “practical reasons” for Anthropic’s third-quarter numbers to be absent: September 30 was only a few weeks ago, and “closing the books for a company of this size takes time.”
Companies can also be liable for misstatements in their registration statements, “so there is a strong incentive not to publish numbers before they have been fully vetted,” Dambra says. SEC rules require that “Anthropic would need to update the filing with third-quarter financials” if the company goes public any later than about mid-November, he says.
As for data center lease agreements, Erica Neuman, an accounting professor at Youngstown State University, says it’s “not unusual” for companies to redact confidential details from “contract exhibits,” which could include lease terms.
However, Neuman adds that it’s worth scrutinizing whether Anthropic’s redactions would prevent, or make it more difficult, for investors to analyze Anthropic’s financial obligations and whether they may impact the company’s cash flow.
Many of Anthropic’s financial obligations relate to compute, which is the “most significant operating cost in our business,” according to the S-1. It’s also a business risk for the company, and it’s laid out both in terms of undersupply and overinvestment. (Parts of the AI industry have been warning that chip constraints could slow the progress of AI.)
Anthropic’s prospectus puts more emphasis on the risks of overinvestment, stating that the company needs to make forward investments in compute resources that will seem “irresponsibly large” at first glance.
Chips, Anthropic explains, are approached as a “single, fungible pool from multiple strategic partners,” including Amazon, Google, Nvidia, and AMD. The company notes that it has entered into contracts “with an aggregate committed spend of more than $____, substantially all of which is related to compute and infrastructure.” Some of these contracts are set to be completed before December 2030, while others may extend through 2045.
Though the prospectus touches on Anthropic’s compute uncertainties due to factors like limited land and power resources, Patrick Moorhead, CEO and chief analyst at Moor Insights & Strategy, believes investors are owed more detail.
“It’s about characterizing the odds and impact individually across each of the areas. Anthropic owes investors more information, such as a probability of these individual issues, characterizing the percentage chance and the degree of the impact,” he tells WIRED. “Not ‘could materially impact.’”
Anthropic does provide some eye-catching estimates in footnotes. Since December 31, 2025, it has started or amended “compute and infrastructure” leases with “future minimum payment obligations” worth approximately $417 billion in aggregate. Since June 30, it has added an additional $245 billion to its future payment obligations, all related to infrastructure agreements. It also expanded “certain existing commercial agreements” that it caveats “have not yet been finalized,” for an additional $125 billion to $150 billion.
Include “short term” agreements with “minimum non-cancelable payments,” Anthropic says, and that’s another $21 billion. In total, it will owe, at minimum, an estimated $808 billion if it follows through on all of this.
Ben Bajarin, chief executive and a principal analyst at Creative Strategies who tracks the chip industry, says that this is likely just the first draft of Anthropic’s prospectus, and he expects a lot of gaps to be filled in an updated version.
Despite how common S-1 redactions are, Dambra describes them as “controversial.” While companies may argue that they’re “protecting proprietary information,” Dambra says that skeptics accuse them of using redactions “opportunistically” in order to “avoid disclosing politically or socially sensitive information.”
However, Dambra argues that redacting information may come at a cost. He notes that companies with redactions in their S-1s were also more likely to “underprice” their shares at the initial public offering.
When companies redact information in their S-1, Dambra says, they typically understand that they’ve created an “information gap” between them and outside investors. Understanding that investors will treat this gap with “suspicion,” companies may feel inclined to “entice” them to participate in the IPO by setting a lower starting price.
It’s unclear what Anthropic’s opening price may end up being or how investors may be interpreting the redactions in the company’s S-1. But according to Bajarin, the whole AI industry is one form of “blank” or another when it comes to crunching the numbers based on access to chips and infrastructure right now. So, yes, it’s all a risk.
“All of this,” he says, “just shows how absurdly early we are in enterprise adoption of an AI market that will be more than $3 trillion yearly and likely growing.”

title: 'We do whatever they say': Yeshiva students defer to rabbis over response to IDF draft enforcement
body: Yeshiva students attending a massive United Torah Judaism election rally in Bnei Brak on Sunday told The Jerusalem Post that whether they would leave Israel, stay in the country, or enlist in the IDF if the next government stepped up draft enforcement would depend on their rabbis' instructions.The rally, held two days before Israel's election, drew tens of thousands of haredi (ultra-Orthodox) Jews under the slogan “Gather and Stand Up for Our Lives.” Central to the gathering was military conscription for haredi yeshiva students, regarded as a red line by much of the haredi community but widely supported among Jewish Israelis. An October Israel Democracy Institute survey found that 72% of Jewish respondents supported legislation requiring young haredi men to enlist.Speaking at the rally, Rabbi Dov Landau, a leading haredi rabbinic authority, urged supporters to defend Torah study.“Never have yeshiva students and kollel scholars been persecuted as they are being persecuted now,” Landau said.The yeshiva students interviewed by the Post likewise described deferring to their own rabbis when asked how they would respond to draft enforcement.“If my rabbi says to leave (the country), I'm going to leave,” Reuven, one of the students attending the rally, told the Post. When asked whether he would stay or enlist if his rabbi instructed him to do so, he replied that “of course” he would.'We would go through fire and water' for our rabbis, yeshiva student saysDovid, another young haredi man at the rally, said that he and others like him would “go through fire and water” for their rabbis.“In our culture, we listen to whatever our rabbis say. If our rabbis will tell us to go, then we'll listen to them,” he said. “We're going to listen to them until the end.”Shmuel, a fellow yeshiva student, emphasized that Torah study was his highest priority and that he would leave Israel if staying meant he could no longer continue his studies.“If I need (to leave), that's what I'll do,” he said. “What's more important for us is that we need to learn. And, if we can't learn here, then we'll learn in a different place. We're not going to serve in the IDF because this learning is the most important thing in the world.”Chaim, another of the students interviewed, also expressed a commitment to rabbinic authority, but argued that “the Jews doing Torah and mitzvot, to them, God gave Israel.” If the government enforced the draft, he believed the response should be to “fight it.”Student emphasizes desire to stay despite saying he will obey rabbi if instructed to leave Avi, another young man at the event, emphasized his desire to remain in Israel.“We will stay (in Israel) because we believe it's our country and Hashem will help us,” he said. Still, if his rabbi instructed him to leave, he would comply, “because he's our rabbi, and we do whatever he says.”Despite broad agreement about following their rabbis, the students appeared to hold differing personal views about military service.When a group of young men was asked whether some yeshiva students wanted to enlist but refrained because their rabbis forbade it, several agreed, with one answering, “of course.”One of the students, speaking anonymously, expressed frustration over the situation. He feared arrest at the airport over his draft status if he tried to travel abroad, and questioned why young yeshiva students were being targeted for draft evasion rather than the rabbis whose directives they were following.

title: Troops Kill Eight Suspected Terrorists, Rescue Kidnap Victims In Katsina, Kaduna, Zamfara
body: Troops of the Joint Task Force North-West, Operation FANSAN YAMMA, have neutralised eight suspected terrorists and rescued three kidnapped victims during coordinated operations in Katsina, Kaduna and Zamfara States. The operations also led to the recovery of an AK-47 rifle, three locally fabricated guns, three motorcycles, cutlasses and assorted charms. The Media Information Officer of the Joint Task Force, Captain Tamuno Sinivie, disclosed this in a statement issued on Monday. According to the statement, troops of Sector One, acting on a distress call from farmers at Machika Dam in Sabuwa Local Government Area of Katsina State on Saturday, October 24, engaged suspected terrorists in a gun battle, neutralising two of them while others fled. The troops also rescued a 42-year-old man, Suleiman Umar, who had been kidnapped by the terrorists, and recovered an AK-47 rifle with a magazine containing ammunition, as well as a motorcycle. In a separate operation on the same day, troops of Sector One, in collaboration with the Civilian Joint Task Force, foiled a suspected terrorist ambush along Ungwan Iya in Igabi Local Government Area of Kaduna State, neutralising six suspected terrorists. The statement explained that the troops had responded to a distress call over an attack on Ungwan Mallami village, where the suspected terrorists reportedly abducted two people. While pursuing the fleeing attackers, the troops came under fire but responded with superior firepower, neutralising six of the suspects and forcing others to flee. The troops recovered three locally fabricated guns, two motorcycles, cutlasses and assorted charms during the operation. Similarly, troops of Sector Two rescued two kidnapped victims during a surveillance operation in Bagega, Anka Local Government Area of Zamfara State, on Sunday, October 25. The victims, aged 40 and 25, are indigenes of Kebbi State. According to the statement, the troops spotted suspected terrorists during surveillance and immediately launched a fighting patrol. The suspects reportedly fled on sighting the advancing troops, abandoning the two victims, who were subsequently rescued. The victims were taken to Bagega Clinic for medical attention before being moved to a military base for further assessment and eventual reunion with their families. The statement added that troops were sustaining patrols and search operations across the affected areas to apprehend the fleeing suspects, rescue other kidnapped victims and prevent further attacks. The Theatre Commander of Joint Task Force North-West, Operation FANSAN YAMMA, commended the troops for their gallantry and resilience in responding to the attacks. He also urged members of the public to support ongoing military operations by providing timely and credible information on suspicious movements and activities in their communities. The post Troops Kill Eight Suspected Terrorists, Rescue Kidnap Victims In Katsina, Kaduna, Zamfara appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Ceasefire in Kherson direction set to take effect at 4:00 a.m. Moscow time
body:
MOSCOW, October 27. /TASS/. A ceasefire will take effect in the Kherson direction starting at 4:00 a.m. Moscow time (1:00 a.m. GMT) in connection with a humanitarian operation in Alyoshki.
Russian Chief of the General Staff Army General Valery Gerasimov announced on October 23 that the Russian Armed Forces would cease fire in the Kherson direction starting at 4:00 a.m. Moscow time on October 27 to allow for a humanitarian operation in Alyoshki, Kherson Region. He said that engineering reconnaissance would be conducted, and safe passage would be provided for humanitarian convoys to ensure civilian safety and deliver vital social supplies to Alyoshki.
On September 21, Russian Presidential Spokesman Dmitry Peskov described the situation in Alyoshki as critical, saying that food and medicine could not be delivered there amid ongoing Ukrainian shelling and drone attacks. Russian President Vladimir Putin and his US counterpart Donald Trump held a phone call on October 9. Putin said the parties had agreed that Russian Human Rights Commissioner Yana Lantratova would remain in constant contact with US First Lady Melania Trump's office.
Peskov pointed out on October 26 that the agreement to conduct a humanitarian operation in Alyoshki could set a precedent for similar missions in other areas. He particularly highlighted the United States’ direct and constructive role in coordinating the process. Peskov added that Russia hoped Ukraine would honor all agreements concerning the humanitarian mission in Alyoshki.

title: Algeria to send troops to Niger in first foreign deployment since 1973
body: Algeria is to send troops to Niger in its first foreign deployment since sending forces to Egypt during the Arab-Israeli war in 1973. The deployment follows a visit to Algiers by Niger’s defence minister, as the country seeks support against armed groups, some of which are linked to al-Qaeda or Islamic State. Algeria has economic interests in Niger, including a planned gas pipeline that would carry Nigerian gas through Niger to Algeria. The troops are expected to protect energy facilities in northern Niger, near the Libyan border. The deployment comes as the two neighbours rebuild ties after a diplomatic rift in 2025, when Niger recalled its ambassador to Algiers. Algeria’s upper house of parliament held an emergency session on Sunday to vote on the proposed deployment. According to AFP news agency, 148 of the 174 senators voted in favour. It was later backed by the lower house of parliament. However, the timing and number of soldiers to be deployed have not been announced. The move would mark the first use of a 2020 constitutional provision allowing overseas military deployments and a significant shift in Algeria’s long-standing policy against sending forces abroad. “We are not sending our soldiers to wage war in Niger, but for a mission to secure economic infrastructure,” Algerian senator Belkacem Boulghiti told reporters after the vote. Algeria’s state-owned energy company, Sonatrach, has also signed an agreement with Niger’s petroleum ministry to explore for oil in the Kafra region. Two exploration wells are estimated to contain 168 million and 100 million barrels, respectively, Reuters reported. Relations between Algeria and Niger have not always been smooth in recent years. Algeria condemned the 2023 coup that ousted Niger’s elected President, Mohamed Bazoum, and brought Gen Abdourahamane Tchiani to power. Tensions rose again in 2025 after Algeria shot down a Malian drone near its border. Niger recalled its ambassador to Algiers in solidarity with Mali, a close ally which is also under military rule. Relations have since improved. Tchiani visited Algeria in February 2026, and in late August, President Abdelmadjid Tebboune sent fighter jets to Niger to help suppress a coup attempt and also donated four military helicopters.

title: 2027: Otti sets up Abia Labour Party campaign advisory council
body:
Governor Alex Otti of Abia State has approved the constitution of the Abia State Labour Party Campaign Advisory Council for the 2027 general elections.
A spokesperson for Mr Otti, Njoku Ukoha disclosed this in a press statement issued on Monday evening.
Mr Ukoha said the campaign advisory council would be inaugurated on Sunday, 1 November, as part of activities marking the formal kick-off of the Labour Party governorship campaign, commencing with a Church Service at the Umuahia Township Stadium.
Ude Chukwu, a former deputy governor of Abia State, will chair the council, with its membership drawn from across the 17 local government areas of the state.
Mr Chukwu is also a former speaker of the Abia State House of Assembly.
“The Campaign Advisory Council comprises seasoned party leaders, technocrats, and stakeholders,” Mr Ukoha said in the statement.
“All members of the Campaign Advisory Council are expected to be seated by 12:00 PM on Sunday, November 1, 2026, at the Umuahia Township Stadium.
“The Governor congratulates all members of the Advisory Council and urges them to bring their wealth of experience, dedication and grassroots reach to bear in ensuring a resounding victory for the Labour Party in the 2027 general elections.”

title: New Brunswick strikes deal to explore recovering metals from old mine waste
body:
Could the waste left behind by an old mine help pay for its own cleanup?
That’s the idea behind a new agreement between New Brunswick and a U.S.-based firm that’s looking to turn decades-old mining waste at the Nigadoo mine near Bathurst, N.B., into something valuable.
The mine once produced copper, lead, zinc and silver but has been shut down for nearly 50 years.
The province says some valuable metals may still be hiding in the waste left behind.
In an agreement announced Monday in Fredericton, Regeneration Enterprises says it wants to find out if those metals can still be recovered.
“The recovery of the metals, the critical minerals, whatever they might be, are then used to fund the restoration, as opposed to the public having to pay for it,” said Michael McPhie, Regeneration Enterprises’ managing director.
The company says the site represents a $35 million liability for the province.
“Part of our work is to remove that off the balance sheet for the province,” said McPhie.
“By recovering the metals, not only can we clean up the site, but we can provide a net benefit back to the people of New Brunswick by removing that liability.”
The province says no provincial money is going into exploration right now. However, future government funding hasn’t been ruled out.
“It’s two things. One: it is an opportunity for us to be able to unlock mineral wealth from a tailings facility. And two: have a proper, robust environmental remediation and reclamation of that particular site,” said Natural Resources Minister John Herron.
The Conservation Council of NB says targeting an already-damaged site could be better than disturbing untouched land.
“If the result of doing this testing and doing the mining to get the minerals out of the tailings — if the end result is that the mine will be rehabilitated, I think that’s a good thing,” said Beverly Gingras, the group’s executive director.
“There definitely seems to be some benefits. But, you know, as with everything, the devil’s in the details.”
Gingras says there are still environmental concerns and the question of who would have to pay if things go wrong.
“So there might be, in terms of if they start trying to reprocess these tailings ponds, are they going to be disturbing some settled heavy metals that might find its way into our watersheds? I don’t know. So there might be some environmental concerns for sure,” she added.
The company, which is working with Pabineau First Nation, expects to know within a year whether the project is financially viable.
If it is and approvals come through, processing could begin within two to three years.

title: Navantia Australia to launch underwater technology hub in Melbourne
body: Navantia Australia will establish a new underwater technologies innovation hub in Melbourne, supported by the Victorian Government to accelerate maritime research, engineering and technology development. The project, supported by a Victorian Government grant, will expand Navantia Australia’s Design and Engineering Centre and position Melbourne as the company’s Asia-Pacific hub for underwater technology research and development. The hub will focus on emerging maritime technologies, strengthen sovereign industrial capability and create opportunities for highly skilled engineers, researchers and industry partners. Navantia Australia Managing Director Israel Lozano said the centre would help translate Australian research into practical maritime capability. “This investment will accelerate the development of advanced underwater technologies in Australia and deepen our collaboration with Victoria’s research, engineering and industry ecosystem,” Lozano said. “Melbourne has the skilled workforce, innovation base and industry partnerships needed to turn leading research into practical maritime and defence outcomes.” The project will support collaboration with Victorian universities, research organisations and industry partners to bring next-generation underwater technologies closer to operational use. Victorian Minister for Defence Industry, the Hon Melissa Horne, said the project reflected Victoria’s strength in technology-led industry. “This project will create high-value jobs, attract investment and strengthen Victoria’s role as a leader in advanced manufacturing, engineering and innovation,” Horne said. The agreement reinforces a shared commitment to maritime innovation, sovereign capability and long-term economic growth. title: Innovaero posts A$3.6 million first-quarter revenue after ASX debut
body: Innovaero Technologies Ltd. reported A$3.6 million in unaudited revenue for its fiscal first quarter ended Sept. 30, marking the Australian aerospace and defense manufacturer’s first financial update since listing on the Australian Securities Exchange. The Perth-based company, which trades under the ticker INN, debuted on the ASX on Sept. 22 after completing an initial public offering that raised A$40 million in gross proceeds at $A0.50 per share. Net IPO proceeds of A$38.3 million lifted Innovaero′s cash and cash equivalents to A$42.9 million at quarter’s end, up from A$11.6 million on July 1. First-quarter revenue kept the company on pace to meet its first-half prospectus forecast of A$14.4 million. Uncrewed systems generated A$3 million of the quarterly total, while the crewed aircraft division contributed A$600,000. Customer cash receipts totaled A$1.02 million for the three−month period , trailing recognized revenue due to billing timing differences. Innovaero recorded net operating cash outflows of A$6.78 million, including A$982,000 in one−time listing fees. Excluding those IPO costs, pro−forma operating outflows wereA5.7 million. Primary operating payments included A$2.88 million for manufacturing and operations, A$2.32 million for corporate administration and A$1.39 million for staff costs. At current spending rates, the company estimates its cash balance provides 6.3 quarters of operating funding. Quarterly results were anchored by the Australian Department of Defence’s A$20.8 million Mission Talon Strike program, which develops the OWL−B medium−range precision loitering munition for the Australian Defence Force. Defence accepted the first two contracted deliveries during the quarter, generating A$2.8 million in recognized contract revenue and bringing cumulative program revenue to A$11.5 million. Innovaero expects to receive another A$13 million from the program by March 31, 2027. In August, Innovaero completed OWL-B flight and kinetic testing at the Woomera Test Range, including evaluations of defense-developed payload elements. The platform has logged more than 200 flights and 150 flight hours without a mission failure. Full ADF certification is scheduled for March 2027, with production orders anticipated shortly afterward. “The September quarter marked an important transition for Innovaero. We completed our ASX listing, achieved a major Defence demonstration milestone with OWL-B and progressed our plans to expand sovereign manufacturing capability,” CEO Greg Tunny said. “Our priority now is execution: delivering Mission Talon Strike, maturing the OWL family and building the capacity to manufacture autonomous effectors at scale in Australia.” Innovaero also advanced its turbine-powered OWL-X counter-drone interceptor, showcasing the system at the Farnborough International Airshow in July and the Land Forces exposition in Perth in October. During the quarter, the company extended an autonomy partnership with Shield AI, advanced uncrewed surface vessel integration talks with Leidos and began designing canister launch systems. In its crewed Aviation Composites division, Innovaero remains on track to deliver A$2.1 million in aerial-imaging camera arrays to U.S.-based EagleView in December and added two maintenance clients, including Pilatus. To expand domestic output, Innovaero plans to sign a construction contract in November and break ground in December on a Jandakot facility backed by A$3.7 million in state grant funding.
