title: Kwara Youth Coalition Backs Call for Independent Audit of KWASSIP
body: By Hammed Shittu in Ilorin The 52-Youth Coalition in Kwara State has thrown its weight behind the call by the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) governorship candidate in the 2027 election, Prof. Abdulmumin Yinka Ajia, for an independent audit of the Kwara State Social Investment Programme (KWASSIP). This, the coalition said, would go a long way in providing full details of the day to day financial operations of the agency. The group, in a statement issued on Monday and made available to journalists in Ilorin, signed by the Director of Contact and Mobilisation of the coalition, Comrade Yusuf Eniola Obe, explained that, “the coalition fully supported the demand for a comprehensive and transparent account of every naira allocated to and expended by the agency since its inception. “And the full details of the financial operations must include annual appropriations, actual fund releases, expenditure records, administrative costs, and outstanding balances”. According to the coalition, “We commend the NDC candidate for raising these concerns and add our voice unreservedly to his call. “Public funds channelled through the Kwara State Social Investment Programme belong to the people of Kwara State. “Every kobo of those funds must be accounted for, openly, honestly, and without the evasion and opacity that has characterised this agency’s operations from the beginning”. The coalition added, “the call for accountability coming from the NDC governorship candidate shows that Kwarans, across every political divide, are concerned about the opaque nature of KWASSIP operations and are interested in knowing how their collective resources are being spent”. They described the level of alleged opacity surrounding KWASSIP as troubling, alleging that when the agency’s Director General, Dr. Abdulwasiu Tejidini, was asked to account for the total funds received by the agency, he was unable to answer. The group noted, “That the Director General of a public agency cannot account for the funds his agency has received is not merely embarrassing, it is alarming. “A Director General who does not know how much money his agency has received has either been deliberately kept in the dark or is deliberately keeping the public in the dark. “The scenario is unacceptable and demands investigation. This is more reason the agency must be audited”. The coalition condemned allegations that the programme had been used to make substantial payments outside established application and beneficiary selection processes, with some amounts reportedly falling outside the programme’s recognised benefit categories — a development the group described as a brazen misuse of public funds for political purposes. “What is being described is not a social investment programme. It is a political slush fund, a mechanism for settling political obligations, rewarding loyalists, and inducing voters ahead of the 2027 general elections with money that belongs to the most vulnerable Kwarans the programme was supposedly designed to serve. This is a betrayal of public trust of the most cynical and contemptible kind,” the statement alleged. The coalition issued a stern warning to officials of the agency and all those involved in the alleged misappropriation of KWASSIP funds, reminding them that the era of unaccountability in Kwara State is drawing to a close. “We want to send a clear and unambiguous message to every official at KWASSIP and every political actor who has used this programme as a personal political instrument: “The PDP if its formed the next government in Kwara State, and when it does, there will be a full and thorough accountability exercise. “Every naira that cannot be accounted for, every payment made outside due process, and every political obligation settled with public funds will be investigated and prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law. Prepare your records. You will need them,” the coalition warned. The group therefore called on the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC), and other relevant anti-corruption agencies to take immediate note of the allegations surrounding KWASSIP operations and commence preliminary investigations.

title: Evacuated Ebola patient, husband arrive in Switzerland
body:
The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate, has confirmed that Nigeria’s Ebola patient and her husband arrived safely in Switzerland on Monday following their medical evacuation from Abuja.
In an update posted on his official X account, Mr Pate said the patient was receiving treatment at Geneva University Hospitals, while her husband had been placed in isolation at University Hospital Zurich.
“The Swiss authorities have confirmed that the patient and her spouse arrived safely in Switzerland today,” he said.
The Swiss Federal Office of Public Health (FOPH), in a statement issued on Monday, also confirmed their arrival, saying both individuals, who are Swiss citizens, were transported from Nigeria aboard a medical evacuation flight.
The agency said the woman was receiving treatment for Bundibugyo virus disease, a form of Ebola, while her husband, identified as a close contact, remained in isolation.
It explained that both hospitals had the necessary facilities and trained medical personnel to manage such cases safely.
The Swiss authorities said the arrangements posed no risk to public health in the country.
Mr Pate said Switzerland’s Federal Councillor, Elisabeth Baume-Schneider, expressed appreciation for the care provided by Nigerian health professionals and the cooperation between both countries and the World Health Organisation (WHO), which made the evacuation possible.
He said the appreciation was conveyed during a telephone conversation with the Swiss official.
The Swiss government also confirmed the conversation, saying Ms Baume-Schneider thanked Nigerian doctors, other healthcare professionals and authorities for their efforts.
Mr Pate similarly thanked healthcare and public health teams in Nigeria and Switzerland, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), Swiss health authorities and the WHO for their roles in the evacuation.
Despite the patient’s departure, Mr Pate said Nigeria’s response to the Ebola case was continuing.
“Here in Nigeria, contact monitoring, investigation of alerts and other containment measures continue,” he said, adding that the response was receiving support from the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) and the WHO Regional Office for Africa.
The WHO said Nigeria was continuing to monitor 52 contacts, while Switzerland had taken responsibility for the patient’s care and monitoring her husband, who was among the 53 contacts previously identified.
The NCDC had earlier identified 53 primary contacts linked to the confirmed case, including healthcare workers, the patient’s husband, domestic staff and personnel involved in collecting samples.
Health authorities are monitoring the contacts for possible symptoms to detect any additional infections and prevent further transmission.
Mr Pate had earlier said Nigeria could declare the Ebola outbreak over as early as 7 December if no further confirmed or probable cases were detected.
Nigeria confirmed its first Ebola case on 20 October, after a 42-year-old Ugandan-born woman living in Abuja tested positive for the disease.
The patient had returned to Nigeria on 3 October after travelling to Uganda and developed symptoms few days later.
She was subsequently admitted to a health facility in Abuja, where she received treatment in isolation before her evacuation to Switzerland on Monday.
Following her evacuation, WHO said Nigeria had no active confirmed Ebola cases, although contact monitoring and other containment measures were continuing.
Nike Adebowale covers the health beat. She holds a degree from Ekiti State University, Ado Ekiti. Twitter : @nikeadebowale1

title: Russian political scientist Alexander Kynev launches hunger strike over inaccessible toilet in overcrowded jail cell, lawyer says
body: Political scientist Alexander Kynev, who is in pretrial detention on charges of attempting to sell drugs, has gone on a hunger strike, the legal advocacy project Slovo Zashchite reported. His lawyer, Mikhail Biryukov, said Kynev began the hunger strike because he cannot use the toilet in his overcrowded cell, which he shares with 34 other people. “There’s a hole in the floor [of the cell] instead of a toilet, and he can’t use it because his leg is in a cast after being broken in two places,” Biryukov said. “That’s why he’s not eating. We’ve done everything we can to get him moved today to a place that meets his medical needs.” Kynev has been in custody since September 25. Slovo Zashchite previously reported that he was severely beaten during his arrest, leaving him with a leg broken in two places. According to political scientist Ekaterina Schulmann, Kynev was beaten to force him to confess to treason. Kynev denies the charges of attempting to sell drugs. Read more Russian elections expert Alexander Kynev stayed in the country to keep studying its politics. After criticizing the latest vote, he was arrested on drug charges. Russia’s FSB security service publishes dramatic videos of political arrests. A human rights group says roughly a quarter of the arrest scenes it examined were staged. title: Rheinmetall opens the UK Gun Hall
body: Rheinmetall officially opened the new ‘UK Gun Hall’ in Telford marking the return of independent production of large-calibre weapons to the UK. The UK Gun Hall forms part of Rheinmetall’s wider investment of more than £200 million across its UK operations over the past five years, demonstrating the company’s long-term commitment to strengthening Britain’s defence industrial base. The investment complements Rheinmetall UK’s work on the Boxer Mechanised Infantry Vehicle, Challenger 3 Main Battle Tank programme and future land capability programmes. The ‘Gun Hall’ is a concrete example of the industrial partnership between the United Kingdom and Germany established under the Trinity House Agreement. The facility is expected to support over 100 highly skilled people as production develops while creating opportunities for British businesses, strengthening domestic supply chains and delivering long-term economic value. Rheinmetall currently employs around 685 people in Telford, including 35 at the UK Gun Hall. This represents a significant long-term investment in Britain’s defence industrial base, supporting warfighting readiness and contributing to the government’s ambition to make defence an engine for growth. The Gun Hall will manufacture 120mm and 155mm weapon systems, including those supporting Challenger 3 and future artillery platforms. The facility offers 11,500 m² of production space. At peak capacity, it can produce up to 245 barrels per year across both calibres, as well as more than 50 breeches annually. Designed to meet growing UK, NATO and international demand, the facility provides scalable manufacturing capacity that strengthens collective deterrence, enhances industrial resilience and reinforces Britain’s contribution to European and NATO security. From concept to reality at pace, Rheinmetall transformed an empty facility into an operational manufacturing capability in just eight months. The achievement demonstrates Rheinmetall’s ability to respond rapidly to UK defence requirements and translate investment commitments into sovereign capability. During this period, advanced manufacturing equipment was installed and commissioned, specialist expertise was transferred to the UK workforce, and production commenced on schedule. Production of breeches and breech blocks began in May 2026, followed by barrel production in June 2026, in line with programme milestones. The successful manufacture of the first UK-produced breech, breech block and barrels demonstrates the capability to manufacture these complex weapon components on British soil. Wes Streeting, Secretary of State for Defence, said: “Britain is back in the business of making the weapons that our Armed Forces need to defend the nation against our adversaries. From an empty site to full production in eight months, this is rapid reindustrialisation in action. One hundred skilled jobs in world-class manufacturing and the return of large-calibre weapon production to UK soil for the first time in twenty years – this is what defence as an engine for growth looks like.” Armin Papperger, CEO of Rheinmetall AG, said: “Today’s opening is an important milestone for Rheinmetall and for the United Kingdom. In a remarkably short period of time, we have turned our commitment into a sovereign manufacturing capability that will strengthen Britain’s defence industrial base for decades to come. The UK has been a long-standing and valued partner for Rheinmetall, and today we are building on an already strong relationship. We are committed to investing in the UK for the long term, expanding our industrial footprint and working together to deliver the capabilities needed for the future. By combining Rheinmetall’s expertise with British skills, innovation and manufacturing, we are strengthening the UK’s sovereign industrial capacity, supporting the Armed Forces and contributing to the security of NATO and Europe.” For Editorial Inquiries Contact: Editor Kym Bergmann at kym.bergmann@venturamedia.net For Advertising Inquiries Contact: Group Sales Director Simon Hadfield at simon.hadfield@venturamedia.net

title: Ribadu Urges African Leaders to Develop Local Solutions to Combat Terrorism
body: *Reiterates calls for international collaboration, intelligence sharing Linus Aleke in Abuja The National Security Adviser (NSA), Nuhu Ribadu, has urged African leaders to take the lead in developing local solutions to combat terrorism and other emerging security threats across the continent. Ribadu also reiterated the need for stronger global and regional cooperation, intelligence sharing and the responsible use of emerging technologies to combat terrorism and violent extremism in Africa. Speaking at the High-Level African Lessons Learned Forum on Counter-Terrorism Cooperation, Intelligence Sharing and Emerging Technologies in Abuja on Monday, the NSA stressed that no country could effectively tackle transnational terrorist networks in isolation, given their ability to operate across borders, communicate through digital platforms and finance their activities through international channels. He said terrorist groups were exploiting porous borders, local grievances, illicit financial networks, digital platforms and online radicalisation to expand their operations across the continent. Ribadu noted that Nigeria’s experience over the past 15 years had shown that military operations alone could not provide a sustainable solution to terrorism. He said the country had continued to pursue a whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach to counter-terrorism and the prevention and countering of violent extremism. According to him, “Our partners remain important, and we value their continued support. However, sustainable solutions must be rooted in African ownership, African priorities, African institutions and the lived experiences of our communities. “While security operations remain necessary, they must be complemented by intelligence coordination, law enforcement, financial intelligence, justice, strategic communications, prevention, rehabilitation, reintegration, reconciliation, community resilience, education, youth engagement, research, training and technology-enabled analysis.” He also highlighted the growing influence of artificial intelligence, encrypted platforms, drones and synthetic media on the security landscape, noting that although terrorist groups could exploit these technologies, they also offered opportunities for early warning, threat analysis, digital investigations, border security and the protection of vulnerable communities. “Our task is to ensure that technology is used responsibly, lawfully and effectively in support of peace and security,” he said. Similarly, the United Nations (UN) Deputy Secretary-General, Amina Mohammed, called for stronger intelligence sharing, public trust and the responsible use of emerging technologies to strengthen Africa’s fight against terrorism and violent extremism. Speaking virtually, Mohammed said terrorism continued to devastate families and communities across Nigeria’s North-East, the Lake Chad Basin, the Sahel and parts of East and Southern Africa. “In Nigeria, we know the cost of this scourge, the toll it is taking on families and communities across the North-East and the Lake Chad Basin,” she said. She added that the violence was claiming lives, displacing communities, disrupting economic activities and undermining development in vulnerable areas. She also cautioned that military operations alone would not end terrorism, urging governments to complement security measures with rehabilitation, reintegration, justice and community support. The Country Representative of the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC), Cheikh Touré, also called for African-led counter-terrorism strategies, warning that terrorist groups were increasingly exploiting cross-border networks, organised crime and emerging technologies. Touré said Africa had become a major centre of global terrorism, with the Sahel accounting for more than half of all terrorism-related deaths worldwide. He noted that four of the five countries responsible for nearly 70 per cent of global terrorism deaths in the previous year were African: Burkina Faso, Nigeria, Niger and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. “In the past decade, terrorism has gained a foothold in Africa that few of us would have predicted,” he said. Earlier, in his welcome address, the National Coordinator of the National Counter-Terrorism Centre (NCTC), Major General Adamu Laka, said the forum was designed to enable African countries to share experiences, identify effective strategies and strengthen cooperation against terrorism. Laka said terrorist groups were increasingly exploiting technology, illicit financial flows, corruption and criminal networks to advance their activities. He stressed that military action must be complemented by prevention, rehabilitation, reintegration, criminal justice and community resilience.

title: Britain’s Final Plan To Kill Argentina’s Super Étendards Attack Jets
body: No single Argentine capability shaped British planning during the 1982 South Atlantic conflict more than the pairing of the Dassault Super Étendard strike fighter and its deadly AM39 Exocet anti-ship missile. Against that threat, the British launched a series of special forces operations, all with the same objective: kill the Argentine pilots and destroy their aircraft and missiles before they could be used again. Together, the strike fighter and missile pairing had proven to be the biggest threat to the Royal Navy task force that had been sent to recapture the islands. Two Super Étendards of the Argentine Navy in flight around the time of the Falklands War in 1982. Photo by UPI/Bettmann Archive/Getty Images Five Super Étendard aircraft and five AM39 Exocet missiles had been delivered to Argentina before a French embargo took hold. The jets were flown by the Argentine Navy’s 2nd Naval Fighter and Attack Squadron out of Río Grande, on Tierra del Fuego, a region at South America’s southernmost tip, shared by Chile and Argentina. The Super Étendard/Exocet combination had already cost the British the destroyer HMS Sheffield on May 4 and the container ship Atlantic Conveyor on May 25. A casualty from HMS Sheffield being rushed to the sick bay on board the aircraft carrier HMS Hermes . Crown Copyright The special forces operations were broken down into four phases — named PLUM DUFF, MIKADO, KETTLEDRUM, and IMPI — the last of which is the least well-documented, and the focus of this article. PLUM DUFF was the insertion phase and was a reconnaissance mission. On May 16, an RAF Hercules airdropped eight special forces troops onto RFA Fort Austin to form a recce party. On the night of May 17/18, a Sea King HC4 , ZA290, lifted off from the aircraft carrier HMS Invincible for a one-way flight to Tierra del Fuego, where the men were to observe Río Grande and report back. The patrol was set down far from the objective and never completed the reconnaissance; the helicopter crew flew on into Chile, where the aircraft was deliberately burnt to try and hide the evidence, while they tried to evade capture. Commandos being lifted from the decks of HMS Hermes and HMS Invincible to be transferred by Sea King helicopters to other ships while the two aircraft carriers forge ahead to the Falkland Islands from Ascension Island, leaving the marines ready to move at short notice. Photo by Fox Photos/Getty Images MIKADO was the planned attack phase, and it depended on that missing intelligence. Two Hercules were to air-land up to 70 men of B Squadron, 22 Special Air Service (SAS), directly on Río Grande — the air operation order of May 19 also named Río Gallegos, further up the Argentine coast, as an alternative. The men would destroy the Super Étendards and their Exocets on the ground, kill the pilots, and then withdraw overland into Chile. Commander Task Force 317, at Northwood, accepted from the outset that the mission could well cost both Hercules. Lieutenant Juan José “Tierno” Rodríguez Mariani in Super Étendard 3-A-203, preparing to take off from Río Grande on May 23, 1982; note the ground power unit still connected. Armada Argentina The aircrew did not refuse the task, but they were blunt about what it demanded: formation landing by two heavy transports on a possibly heavily defended, icy military runway, with a probable 20-knot tailwind, at night and on passive night-vision goggles in minimum light levels, with intelligence that was inadequate to support any air-land option at all. The RAF planning team recommended an airdrop as the better way to maintain a covert posture, and the Senior Air Staff Officer at Headquarters 38 Group warned the Air Commander to watch for overambitious schemes coming out of the SAS . The U.K. Ministry of Defense formally cancelled MIKADO on June 4. KETTLEDRUM was planned as the third of the set. It was aimed at Puerto Deseado, Santa Cruz Province of Argentina, and would have inserted a Special Boat Service party (SBS, the Royal Marines’ special forces unit) from the submarine HMS Onyx — a boat that will reappear before the end of this story. None of the three was executed as planned. The Oberon class submarine HMS Onyx on the surface off Ascension Island. HMS Onyx was the only diesel-electric British submarine to serve in the conflict, and its ability to operate silently close inshore enabled it to play an important role. At Ascension Island, Onyx boarded SAS and SBS special forces personnel and supported them during a series of operations. Imperial War Museums via Getty Images Less well-known is that the cancellation of MIKADO produced a fourth project: Operation IMPI, named after a Zulu fighting force . Cancelling MIKADO did not mean the wider operation was over. Also on June 4, the U.K. Ministry of Defense tasked CTF 317 to produce a new plan for special forces to destroy the combat effectiveness of the Super Étendards. CTF 317’s staff went to work on what became IMPI. The planning document, Ops 1/3, is dated June 14 — the day of the Argentine surrender in the islands. In broad terms, the objective was to be attacked by special forces arriving both by air and by sea. That much has been known, in fragments. Teniente de Naviro (Lieutenant Commander) Alfredo Astiz signing the Instrument of Surrender on behalf of his Argentine forces at Leith, on the island of South Georgia, on board HMS Plymouth . Crown Copyright What has not been published until now is the fact that the operation had already been resourced. At 2240Z on June 12, Maj. Gen. Jeremy Moore, commanding the land forces as CTG 317.1, signalled Rear Admiral Sandy Woodward’s battle group (CTG 317.8), with Admiral Sir John Fieldhouse at Northwood (CTF 317) and Commodore Michael Clapp’s amphibious group (CTG 317.0) as information addressees. The message called for B Squadron, 22 SAS, to be made available for operations as soon as possible: cover was needed against rapid developments of an unfavorable nature in West Falkland (Gran Malvina), and the theatre’s existing special forces assets were fully absorbed supporting the battle for Stanley — and IMPI. Operation IMPI, Moore noted in passing, was by then self-sufficient. Maj. Gen. Sir Jeremy Moore Mc, Commander, Land Forces Falkland Islands Conflict. Photo by Avalon/Getty Images Examining two lines of routine signal traffic settles several things at once. Forty-eight hours before the surrender, IMPI was not a staff study but an operation that had been resourced, and that was enough to consume the theatre’s special forces and justify calling a fresh SAS squadron forward. It is also the only contemporary, operational-level reference to IMPI released so far: everything else comes from a narrative written years afterwards. As that later narrative describes it, the concept behind IMPI was much leaner than MIKADO. Against two Hercules and 70 men, the air element of IMPI rested on a single RAF Hercules. Overflying Stanley Airfield in November 1983, with two RAF Hercules aircraft present. Getty Images The aircraft was to fly from Ascension Island, refuel in flight, and then track east of the Falkland Islands and south of Cape Horn before making a low-level approach below Argentine radar cover for a night landing of special forces at the airfields codenamed San Jose and Arco Iris. Other special forces would have been inserted by sea. That air element, as will be seen, is the most questionable part of the entire file. The routing is worth attention, because it rules out the intuitive picture of a direct run south from Ascension. Instead, the aircraft would have entered from the least-covered and least-expected direction, coming around the bottom of the continent rather than from the northeast. A schematic map of the planned Operation IMPI. via author The precise identities of San Jose and Arco Iris are not established in the declassified record. The most likely reading is that they stand for Río Grande and Río Gallegos — the airfields at which the planned navigation ended, and the two named in MIKADO’s air operation order a month earlier. For a document circulating through restricted channels, encrypting the names of the two targets was an elementary precaution, although it should be noted that an operational order would more commonly have designated them simply as Target One and Target Two. None of this rules out Chilean participation in other phases of the operation; if anything, it suggests it’s more likely. The narrative survives inside a folder classified Top Secret and restricted to the Chief of the Air Staff, whose declared subject is cooperation with Chile. That setting contrasts with the earlier stage of the planning, when mounting and recovering a special forces insertion from a Chilean airfield was considered and expressly discounted on political grounds — much as the use of an Antarctic strip was discounted after the New Zealand High Commission advised that the Antarctic winter precluded safe trans-polar flight. The maritime half of IMPI can be traced in the records of those who were there. Navigational support for the final phase was to come from the nuclear attack submarine HMS Conqueror . On June 9, 1982, Conqueror was off Bahía Camarones, working as an advanced picket and hunting targets of opportunity that ventured outside the 12-nautical-mile limit of Argentine territorial waters, with authority to sink any civilian vessel judged to be running to the Falklands/Malvinas; that same morning the sub had in fact entered Argentine territorial waters trying to locate the Argentine Navy’s Task Group 79.2. Nuclear attack submarine HMS Conqueror returning to port. via author That day, Conqueror received preparatory information on IMPI. The sub’s task was to come to periscope depth and act as a radio beacon, giving the Hercules a radio reference against which to refine a navigation that, low and at night, allowed no error. The resulting picture is an odd one: a nuclear submarine deployed on interdiction off the Patagonian coast, turned into a navigation aid for a transport aircraft. The insertion itself fell to HMS Onyx , the Oberon class diesel-electric boat that had already taken part in Operation KETTLEDRUM and the only conventional submarine Britain deployed to the South Atlantic. On June 14, at 0815Z, lying in San Carlos Water, Onyx embarked a party of 10 men from B Squadron, 22 SAS and the SBS for the mission. The timing matches Moore’s signal of two days earlier almost exactly. The plan called for the submarine to surface some two nautical miles offshore at night. The troops would close the beach in Gemini inflatables and destroy the objective — aircraft and missiles, if any were there — using anti-tank weapons and demolition charges. What happened next illustrates the inertia of military machinery. The Argentine surrender in the islands came on that same June 14, hours after the party had gone aboard Onyx . Even so, preparations did not stop at once: on June 15 the embarked troops carried out practice landings from a Gemini. That does not mean IMPI was ever executed — it was not — but it does show that with the strategic outcome already settled, the machine was still rehearsing. HMS Onyx operating with special forces. via author The British record closes the matter with administrative dryness: the surrender of the Argentine forces in the Falkland Islands and the cessation of hostile activity by Argentine aircraft resulted in the operation being cancelled. The air part of the mission is another matter entirely and is where IMPI becomes more uncertain. The only link between IMPI and an aircraft is a single paragraph in an RAF historical narrative. The folder that holds it was opened on April 18, 1986 — four years after the war — as an eyes-only briefing file for the Chief of the Air Staff, and the pages appear to be a working draft rather than a finished submission, carrying pencil amendments throughout. Had a Hercules been earmarked, there is no doubt which unit would have provided it. The Special Forces Flight that runs through the whole chapter — five crews, commanded by a squadron leader, exercising regularly with SAS and SBS Sections — appears with its squadron number blanked out, yet the number surfaces a few paragraphs later, where two of its crews are described training on the probe-fitted Hercules C1P. The unit was No. 47 Squadron, RAF, home-based at Lyneham, and it would keep the special forces air support role for decades afterward. The men who were at Ascension with that detachment, however, say they had nothing to do with it. Reliable sources with direct knowledge of the flight’s activity state that they never saw the codeword at the time, had never heard of the operation until this file surfaced, and consider it inconceivable that a special forces Hercules and crew could have been earmarked for a mission of this kind without the flight — a community of five crews that has stayed in touch ever since — learning of it at some point in the intervening four decades. By June 14, at most one aerial-refueling-qualified special forces crew was at Wideawake. That skepticism is reinforced by the way the same narrative handles events those crews lived through. Its account of their own work-up does not survive contact with their logbooks. For example, a practice infiltration into RAF Laarbruch in Germany that the narrative describes as successful had in fact been detected; the Hercules was notionally shot down about two miles out on the approach. The ramp toes (attachable extension plates located at the very end of the rear cargo ramp) it describes as droppable at 20 to 30 knots were never meant to be lowered with the aircraft moving, which would have been unsafe and risked the airframe. There are other anomalies, too. West Falklands seen from the ramp of an RAF Hercules. Donald Morrison/Getty Images A document that misstates the squadron’s own exercises is thin evidence on which to place that squadron over Tierra del Fuego. What is not in question is what the Special Forces Flight could have done, had it been asked. By mid-May the flight had two crews qualified in air-to-air refueling — one deployed to Ascension, the other held in the United Kingdom to train the others — flying Hercules C1s fitted with probes and, where the task required it, additional fuel tanks in the fuselage. It had rehearsed stream landings and rapid offloads, parachute insertion below radar cover to a pinpoint coastal feature, as well as flying on ANVIS goggles at 250 feet over sea and land. The goggles themselves were fitted to the crews’ helmets by RAE Farnborough specialists in a single day in mid-April. The reach was demonstrated on May 16, when the sortie that dropped the PLUM DUFF party stayed airborne for 24 hours and five minutes, with Victor tankers refueling some 1,800 miles from Ascension. Almost none of it was routine: nearly everything the force did during the conflict was improvised, at speed, in a matter of weeks. A picture taken on May 24, 1982, at Wideawake Airfield on Ascension Island, showing an RAF Victor tanker prepared for air-to-air refuelling tasks. Photo by AFP What never had an answer — not for MIKADO, and not for whatever IMPI intended — was the other end of the problem. Putting men ashore deep inside Argentine territory was the solvable half. Getting an aircraft and its passengers out again after a direct action, from a strip in range of the Argentine Air Force, was not. All of the above is reconstructed from lateral references: the RAF’s narrative in file AIR 20/13036 at the National Archives, unit records, submarine logs, operational signal traffic, and the accounts of participants. The specific file — the one holding the complete plan with its annexes, the identification of the airfields and the execution sequence — remains closed. It is DEFE 71/980, titled Operation Corporate (Falklands Conflict): Operation IMPI , retained at the National Archives at Kew with no announced opening date. Until it is released, the air element of IMPI cannot be settled either way. Forty-four years after the conflict, the last British special operation of the war is still, in essence, a document the British state is not prepared to show. That is not a trivial detail: the files touching on cooperation with Chile have consistently been the most reluctantly opened of all. The folder holding the outline plan for Operation IMPI. National Archives What remains is an operation of two halves. One of them is solid: a resourced plan, declared self-sufficient on June 12, with a nuclear submarine briefed to act as a beacon, 10 men of the SAS and the SBS embarked in a conventional submarine in San Carlos on the morning of the surrender, and rehearsals continuing the following day. The other half — a lone Hercules coming round Cape Horn to land on a codenamed strip — rests on one paragraph of a flawed staff narrative and is rejected by the only men who could have flown it. Either way, the obsession is the same. Between June 4 and June 14, 1982, while the final battle for Port Stanley/Puerto Argentino was being fought and the Argentine land campaign was collapsing, part of the British planning effort was still revolving around five French-built aircraft, their 10 aircrew, and their missiles. That the plan carries the date of the surrender itself, that it was still being rehearsed the following day, and that it remains classified today says a good deal about how far the British were prepared to go to destroy the Super Étendards and their Exocets. Contact the editor: thomas@thewarzone.com Mariano Sciaroni holds a master’s degree in Strategy and Geopolitics as well as a postgraduate diploma in Contemporary Military History, both earned at the Argentine Army’s Military Academy. Sciaroni has published five books and numerous articles on military and naval history. He is also an active member of the Argentine Institute of Military History and serves as a sub-lieutenant in the Argentine Army Reserve (Army Aviation Reserve Squadron). You can find out more about his books here . The post Britain’s Final Plan To Kill Argentina’s Super Étendards Attack Jets appeared first on TWZ .

title: Kane prematurely announced as Ballon d’Or winner – but he wasn’t only one
body: For a moment, it seemed as though Harry Kane’s dreams of winning the Ballon d’Or had come true. It was shortly after 17:15 GMT on Monday when an article from the award’s official website titled “Harry Kane wins the 2026 Ballon d’Or” began to circulate online. It was more than four and a half hours before the winner of the game’s most prestigious individual award was due to be announced at a star-studded event at London’s Palladium Theatre. The article’s widespread sharing caused confusion online, with some wondering whether France Football, the award’s organisers, had failed at the final hurdle of keeping the winner, voted by journalists at the end of September, under wraps. That was until further digging on the Ballon d’Or website revealed that other favourites to win the award, including Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal and Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappe, had also had similar pieces written and published about them. When asked about the articles by BBC Sport, a Ballon d’Or spokesperson said: “Some profiles of nominees prepared by BallonDor.com were inadvertently published online. “These articles had been prepared for all nominees and should in no way be considered as an indication of the final results or rankings” Just before 17:40 BST, the articles about Kane and Mbappe had been removed from the website. Similar articles also covered London City Lionesses star Alexia Putellas and Barcelona’s Ewa Pajor, two of the favourites for the corresponding women’s award, also taking place on Monday night. If Kane is to realise his dream and become the first Englishman to win the award since 2001, he will have to wait a little longer to find out.

title: KONGSBERG secures contract with Pilbara Ports in Australia
body: Kongsberg Gruppen ASA (‘KONGSBERG’) has been awarded a new 10-year contract with Pilbara Ports in Western Australia to deliver a Vessel Traffic Service system at the Port of Port Hedland. The contract value has not been disclosed. KONGSBERG will deliver a complete Vessel Traffic Service (VTS) system including radar, electro-optical sensors, Automatic Identification System (AIS) technology and VHF communications. Under the 10-year system-as-a-service agreement, KONGSBERG will also provide comprehensive maintenance and support for both the new Port of Port Hedland system and the existing VTS at the Port of Dampier. “We are proud to have been selected once again by Pilbara Ports, extending our delivery of a world-class VTS system and 24/7 services to the Port of Port Hedland, building on the VTS system and managed service already being delivered to the Port of Dampier. We look forward to supporting safe and efficient port operations while further strengthening our partnership with Pilbara Ports,” says Lene Vesterlund, CEO of Kongsberg Norcontrol, KONGSBERG. Pilbara Ports Chief Executive Officer Samuel McSkimming says Port Hedland’s high level of vessel activity created a need for a proven, robust VTS that can accurately track vessel movements across the service area and support efficient turnaround times. “The system will give port operators advanced tools to monitor vessel movements across our area of responsibility, improving situational awareness and supporting safe and efficient operations. We were also seeking a long-term technology partner, and we have found that in KONGSBERG,” says McSkimming. In the 2025–26 financial year, Pilbara Ports handled a record 804.1 million tonnes of imports and exports through the ports of Ashburton, Dampier, Port Hedland and Varanus Island. Pilbara Ports comprises the ports of Ashburton, Dampier, Port Hedland and Varanus Island. It is responsible for managing the ports, including vessel traffic services, ship scheduling, berthing allocations for multi-user facilities and port communications. title: Helsing unveils Contra air defence system and two interceptors to counter mass attacks
body: Today we are unveiling Contra, an AI-controlled autonomous air defence system designed to protect countries from scaled drone and missile attacks. Alongside Contra, two new interceptors: AD-1 Inferno to counter jet-powered threats. AD-2 Ambush to counter high-altitude threats. https://t.co/Z9HE2UB2ft — Helsing (@HelsingAI) October 26, 2026 Contra uses Helsing’s Altra command-and-control platform to combine information from sensors and coordinate weapons within a single air picture. The company says it is designed to detect and engage hundreds or thousands of threats simultaneously, while users retain control over decisions and target prioritisation. “Contra ends the air defence dilemma: slow fair-weather drones, or million-euro missiles fired at cheap, mass-produced targets,” said Niklas Köhler, Helsing’s co-founder and president. Helsing plans to manufacture the interceptors at its Resilience Factories, although it did not disclose unit prices. “Our AI links existing sensors and effectors in real time and adds our interceptors, AD-1 and AD-2. With jet and rocket propulsion, a low-cost all-weather radar seeker, and two independent European supply chains, they deliver autonomous fire superiority up to ten kilometres high – affordable and at industrial scale.” Photo: Helsing. AD-1 Inferno uses jet propulsion and is designed to loiter, operate in swarms and make repeated engagement attempts. The solid-rocket-powered AD-2 Ambush is intended for rapid interceptions, with Helsing stating a speed of Mach 2.5 and a range exceeding 20 kilometres. Both missiles receive mid-course guidance from Contra’s ground-based radar stations. Onboard radar seekers are designed to guide them through the final stage of an engagement in all weather. Contra can also incorporate third-party interceptors, counter-drone lasers, guns and net-based systems, according to Helsing. The company says it can integrate such equipment within days and is already demonstrating several integrations to military customers. Helsing presented the system in response to what it described as increasing Russian production of jet-powered drones and cruise missiles. Citing intelligence reports, it said Geran-4 and Geran-5 output had reached a combined 4,000 units a month and that new launch sites were bringing parts of the EU within potential attack range.

title: Kwara PDP Guber Candidate Urges IGP to Probe Alleged Arrest, Detention of Party Members
body: By Hammed Shittu in Ilorin The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Kwara State, Engr. Sulaiman Bolakale Kawu, has called on the Inspector-General of Police, Mr. Tunji Disu, to urgently investigate the alleged arrest, detention and repeated police invitations involving members of the party in the state. The call was made in a statement issued in Ilorin on Monday by the media office of the PDP candidate, following reports of arrests and the alleged use of tear gas during a peaceful procession at the Emir’s palace in Ilorin, the state capital. The media office accused the Kwara State Commissioner of Police, Mr. Ojo Adekimi, of allegedly being behind the actions, warning that failure to investigate the incidents could heighten political tension in the state. It described the development as a potential threat to police neutrality, respect for the rule of law and the protection of fundamental rights ahead of the 2027 general elections. The office also urged the police authorities to investigate the reported deployment of tear gas against participants in the procession, which was attended by Kawu, Senator Saliu Mustapha and other PDP political candidates. According to the statement, the incidents could create the impression that the police command was being used to intimidate opposition members and suppress legitimate political expression rather than address established security concerns. Particularly concerning, the statement said, was the reported imprisonment of Kadri Usman Elesin and Taiye Alaboke without proper arraignment before a competent court or a meaningful opportunity to respond to the allegations against them. The media office recalled that the two men, identified in earlier reports as Taiye Laufe, also known as Taiye Alaboka, and AbdulKadir Usman, were arrested on October 24, 2026. It said both men were from Agaka Isale, Ilorin, the family house of Kawu. It further alleged that the men had remained in detention despite efforts by their families and legal representatives to secure administrative bail, expressing concern over reports that they had subsequently been taken to prison without due judicial process. The statement called on the relevant authorities to establish the legal basis for their imprisonment, clarify whether they had been formally charged and arraigned before a competent court, and ensure that their constitutional rights were protected. It also listed several individuals reportedly invited by the police on different dates in October. They include Kayode Jack, Shuaib Baba Agaka, Amuda Ajia Eru, Shuaib Tunde, Idris Samad, Fazawa Anafi Agaka and Alhaji Aloa Moshood Imam. The media office maintained that the reported arrests, repeated police invitations, alleged imprisonment without proper arraignment and reported use of tear gas against peaceful protesters should be investigated collectively to determine whether they constituted legitimate policing or interference with opposition political activities. “The police are not an extension of the ruling party, nor should any opposition party be made to feel that its political activities constitute an invitation to harassment by security agencies,” the statement said. It stressed that the Nigeria Police Force must remain accountable to the Constitution and the law rather than serve the political interests of any individual or party. The statement warned that perceived partisanship by security agencies could undermine public confidence in the electoral process ahead of the 2027 elections. “An election cannot be regarded as free and fair merely because votes are cast and counted. “The environment leading to the election must also be free from intimidation, selective arrests and the abuse of security institutions to create an advantage for the party in power,” it said. The media office urged the Inspector-General of Police to order an independent investigation into the arrests, detention and reported imprisonment of the two men, as well as the alleged use of tear gas against peaceful protesters. It also called for an investigation into whether any police officers acted on improper political instructions and whether constitutional safeguards relating to personal liberty, fair hearing, peaceful assembly and the treatment of suspects were observed. The statement further demanded appropriate disciplinary action against any officer found to have abused his authority or compromised the impartiality expected of the Nigeria Police Force. While stressing that its position was not intended to obstruct lawful police investigations or shield anyone from accountability, the media office maintained that no citizen should face intimidation, unlawful detention or disproportionate use of force because of political affiliation or participation in peaceful political activities. It also called for a review of the leadership of the Kwara State Police Command if an independent investigation established that the commissioner had failed to maintain the neutrality, professionalism and restraint required of his office. The statement said that the credibility of the 2027 electoral process depended not only on the conduct of political parties and candidates but also on the ability of security agencies to demonstrate fairness, impartiality and respect for the fundamental rights of all citizens, irrespective of political affiliation. Meanwhile, efforts to obtain the reaction of the Police Command Public Relations Officer, SP Toun Ejire Adeyemi, proved unsuccessful, as calls made to her telephone were not answered. A text message sent to her number had also not received a response as of the time of filing this report.

title: More than 60 Christians killed in Ethiopia ‘massacre’, church official says
body: More than 60 people have been killed in a series of attacks on Christians in Ethiopia’s Oromia region, according to the country’s Orthodox Church. One resident, whose 75-year-old father was killed, described it as an ambush. “We were completely unprepared and had no prior knowledge. They surrounded us from all four directions,” he told BBC Amharic. The regional government said that it would take action against those responsible. A local official blamed the attacks on a newly formed rebel coalition, the Alliance for Survival, which includes the Oromo Liberation Army (OLA). The OLA has not commented but has denied carrying out previous such attacks. A statement from the Holy Synod of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church said that 20 houses were burnt to the ground in the attacks. It did not say who was responsible. Eyewitness told BBC Amharic that five of those killed were children. A church official described the attacks on three areas in the Shirka district as a “massacre”, saying security forces arrived at the scene but were unable to stop the assault. Many residents have now fled the area. Condemning the violence, the Orthodox Church said attacks against Christians had been increasing recently, and that “such actions undermine the country’s values of mutual respect and peaceful coexistence”. In a statement posted on Facebook, the Orthodox Church said it had repeatedly raised concerns about insecurity with authorities at different levels of government, but that “so far there has been no solution”. The Ethiopian Human Rights Council, a non-governmental organisation, said in a report released in July 2026 that 458 people had been killed in attacks in that area over the previous four years. But this is one of the most deadly attacks in that period. The report said armed groups had repeatedly targeted local communities, particularly followers of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church, in what it described as religiously motivated attacks. The government has previously blamed the OLA for the attacks, with Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed saying violence targeting civilians and religious institutions was part of a plan to destabilise the country. The group, which says it is fighting for greater rights for the Oromo people, denies these allegations. Previous reports have also documented attacks against Muslims in the area. Residents who spoke to the BBC on various occasions have described the violence as both ethnic and religious in nature. About two-thirds of Ethiopians are Christians, mostly Orthodox, while one third are Muslim.

title: Ballon d’Or: Yamal edges Cubarsi, wins Kopa Trophy 3rd time in a row
body: Barcelona and Spain forward Lamine Yamal has won the men’s Young Talent of the Year award for the third consecutive year. Yamal expressed gratitude after receiving the award but admitted that he believed his Barcelona teammate Pau Cubarsí deserved to win it instead. The 19-year-old thanked his teammates at both club and international levels, acknowledging their contributions to his success. Yamal, who has established himself as one of football’s brightest young stars, continues to earn recognition for his performances for Barcelona and Spain. Ahead of the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony at the London Palladium in England, football stars from different clubs around the world and journalists have gathered at the venue for the 70th edition of the award. Harry Kane has been tipped as favourite to become England’s first Ballon d’Or winner in 25 years when the award is presented, but he faces stiff competition from La Liga pair Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappé. This 2026 edition marks the first time the showpiece is staged outside France. title: Nurse killed in attack while responding to Ebola alert in DR Congo
body: A nurse has been killed and another health worker seriously injured in an attack as they were responding to an Ebola alert in north-eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The two were targeted by local youths who accused them of contaminating water sources and spreading the Ebola virus, according to the UN-backed Radio Okapi. The World Health Organization (WHO) condemned the attack. In an attempt to prevent the virus spreading, neighbouring Uganda has banned all non-essential travel to and from DR Congo and says its citizens returning from there will be quarantined for 21 days. More than 4,800 people have died and nearly 10,000 been infected in DR Congo since this outbreak began in May. Reacting to the attack in DR Congo, WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said health workers “must be able to carry out their duties in safety and dignity”, adding that healthcare personnel should always be protected. The UN agency also extended its condolences to the family and colleagues of the nurse who was killed and wished the injured worker a swift recovery. The BBC has contacted the Ebola response team for comment on the circumstances surrounding the attack in DR Congo. This is not the first time such an attack has happened in DR Congo. Last month, a politician was beaten to death after promoting measures to stop the spread of Ebola, while in August, the Red Cross said its volunteers had been injured and an ambulance set on fire in 11 violent incidents during the first 100 days after the outbreak was declared. Earlier this month, two countries – Kenya and Nigeria – reported their first cases of Ebola linked to the current outbreak. The patient in Nigeria was on Monday flown from Abuja to Switzerland for further treatment. She is the Ugandan-born wife of a Swiss diplomat who had travelled to the Ugandan capital for a holiday, according to the head of Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention Jean Kaseya. She was evacuated alongside her husband, who has shown no symptoms. Nigeria’s health ministry said she was stable, conscious and able to communicate. Authorities are now trying to establish where she contracted the virus. The new restrictions announced in Uganda come after questions were raised over her case and that of a Kenyan businessman. Both tested positive for Ebola after travelling through Uganda, even though no cases have been reported there since August. The Kenyan had arrived from DR Congo where he had business interests. Only essential travellers, including aid workers, truck drivers and security personnel, will be allowed to cross the border from DR Congo to Uganda, subject to strict health screening, the health ministry announced. In addition, all travellers entering Uganda, regardless of their country of origin, will be required to complete locator forms to facilitate contact tracing where necessary. It said returning Ugandans would “undergo 21 days of quarantine at their own cost”. About 60 people who were being monitored after coming into contact with the Kenyan patient have all been discharged, it added. In Kenya , the first group of 20 contacts of the first case have gone home, after spending 21 days in quarantine, the health ministry announced on Monday. Another 98 are still being supervised, while seven people who have tested positive for Ebola were stable it said. The Kenyan businessman died two days after arriving in Nairobi. A second woman, related to the businessman, died over the weekend. “All these are measures to ensure that we keep Uganda free of Ebola,” Uganda’s Health Minister Chris Baryomunsi told the BBC’s Newsday programme. Since the two cases were reported in Kenya and Nigeria this month, Uganda has repeatedly stressed that no cases have been reported within its borders. Uganda recorded 20 Ebola cases and two people died shortly after the outbreak started in DR Congo, but the World Health Organization declared the country free of the disease in August. The two passengers tested positive after passing through Uganda’s Entebbe airport on the same day. Diana Atwine, the health ministry’s permanent secretary, said CCTV camera footage showed no physical interaction between the two patients. Health Minister Chris Baryomunsi said the measures were meant to keep the country free of Ebola Ugandan officials had previously said the patient in Nigeria had travelled to eastern DR Congo, only transiting through Uganda. On Sunday, however, the health ministry said Uganda and Nigeria were both working to establish her movements, complete travel history and possible routes of exposure. The Ugandan health minister said the recent cases meant the risk had not ended and further underscored the need to “remain vigilant”. “We share a border with [DR Congo], where transmission continues, and our communities remain closely connected through trade, travel and family ties,” Baryomunsi said. The disease spreads from one person to another by contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit. The Bundibugyo species of Ebola behind this outbreak is relatively rare and there is still no vaccine or specific treatment – though trials are under way.

title: Two Foreign Nationals Arrested Over Fake Documents at Airport
body: Greek police arrested two foreign nationals, a man and a woman, at Thessaloniki’s Macedonia Airport on Sunday afternoon after officers allegedly found them in possession of fraudulent immigration and travel documents. During a police check, officers discovered that the man held proof of an application for a temporary residence permit for foreign nationals, but authorities had rejected the application. The woman, meanwhile, possessed an allegedly forged Greek residence permit. Officers from the Thessaloniki Airport Security Department made the arrests. A search of the man’s luggage uncovered a forged passport bearing a counterfeit consular visa, along with a photograph of the woman. Police seized the items as evidence. Authorities have filed a case against both suspects for offences applicable to each of them. The investigation is ongoing. title: Transcona incumbent Russ Wyatt facing 4 challengers in Winnipeg election
body:
Voters in Transcona will determine the fate of incumbent Winnipeg city councillor Russ Wyatt when they cast ballots in Wednesday’s municipal election.
Four candidates are trying to replace Wyatt, who is seeking re-election as city councillor for Transcona . The incumbent announced his bid for re-election late last month while facing two counts of sexual assault and other offences from earlier this year.
Speaking to 680 CJOB on Sept. 22, Wyatt said the charges were not a concern among prospective voters in Transcona in an interview on Sept. 22. In a statement to Global News Monday, he positioned himself as “a strong and loyal representative” who has “been through many storms” in life.
Wyatt maintains he has done nothing wrong.
His spot on the council is being challenged by former Winnipeg city councillor Shawn Nason, who represented Transcona from 2018 to 2022. Lora Meseman, Chris Giesbrecht and Nathine Dagdick are also running in the ward.
Nason said there has been a lack of communication in the ward that has left residents feeling unrepresented.
“I prided myself on being open and communicating with the residents of Transcona, and the call came from many residents that they wanted me back and missed my style of representation,” Nason said.
In his time at city hall, Nason said he gained experience working alongside other levels of government. Since 2022, when he lost to Wyatt by more than 900 votes, Nason said he has become a more well-rounded candidate that is willing to learn and compromise.
“Part of the problem that we’ve had the last four years is we haven’t had someone that’s been willing to listen to the different voices,” he said, adding that he looks forward to the new faces expected at city hall as multiple incumbent candidates outside of Transcona are not in the running in this civic election .
Meseman told Global News she decided to run after seeing the under-funding of recreation centres through an organization she works with.
“Recreation is so important for our city. I felt really strongly that we needed a voice around the city council table,” she said, also citing a lack of communication from Wyatt as a factor in her decision to run.
“People are frustrated because they don’t understand what’s happening. They’re not hearing back from their councillor. We’re not getting the information that we need and folks feel like they’re not being listened to.”
Giesbrecht wants to be Transcona’s next councillor because, in his words, the city is “declining,” and young people will face the consequences.
“Right now, I see a city that’s declining. It’s in active decline. It’s my future, it’s the future of people in my age range, and no one is coming to save us. We’ve got to save ourselves,” the 31-year-old told Global News in an interview.
His priorities include affordability, improving downtown safety and guiding the ward through its transition as the population becomes younger.
“Water bills just went up. Property taxes go up, and what you get for it seems to go down every year,” Giesbrecht said. He noted that one example of the deterioration of that quality is the revamped Winnipeg Transit system – which he described as a “disaster.”
Dagdick, who is also vying to represent Transcona, said he’s been considering a run for city council since the 2022 election.
“I’ve sat and watched Transcona and nothing has changed,” he said. “Everybody thought when Russ Wyatt was reelected it was going to be coming out and bringing Transcona with the rest of the city and not being forgotten. And it’s still being forgotten.”
Many of Transcona’s issues could be managed through collaboration at Winnipeg City Hall, which Dagdick said he believes is difficult for the incumbent.
“Maybe some people may not want to work with him due to his antics at city hall. He’s stubborn sometimes,” he continued.
In response to an interview request, Wyatt provided an emailed statement, in which he said he has “consistently (been) the only member of council who has stood up to the Mayor and EPC (Executive Policy Committee).”
“I am the only candidate that has a clear and strong record of standing up to power and corruption and, if re-elected, shall continue to do so, as I am still a citizen that cares about the future of my community and City.”
He cited his track record, saying he voted against switching Winnipeg Transit’s system, raising water rates and the reopening of Portage Avenue and Main Street.
Wyatt was removed from several city committees after his initial charges were laid last spring. Patrick Troughton, president of CUPE 500, the union that represents City of Winnipeg employees, has previously warned that re-electing Wyatt would mean years of legal drama rather than results.

title: West must be aware that Russia, Belarus can repel any threat — diplomat
body:
MINSK, October 26. /TASS/. Moscow and Minsk are ready to repel any threat, and any military aggression against the Union State will be met with a harsh and resolute response, Russian Ambassador to Belarus Boris Gryzlov told the Natsionalnaya Oborona (National Defense) magazine in an interview.
"The West must realize that Russia and Belarus are ready to repel any threat, regardless of its nature and scope. There will be our tough and resolute response to any aggressive military actions against the Union State," the diplomat warned. Russian tactical nuclear weapons have been deployed to Belarus, and Oresnik missile systems are on combat duty, Gryzlov said as he called these measures appropriate amid the growing threat to the Union State’s borders.
According to him, statements from Western leaders that the Europeans must be ready for war by 2030 go beyond words as Western countries are investing huge funds in weapons production and the modernization of military infrastructure. "However terrible it may sound, hot heads in the West could go to war `simply to avoid tanks rusting," the Russian diplomat said.
Meanwhile, Russia and Belarus do not harbor any aggressive plans toward Europe, Gryzlov said. "On the contrary, as the Russian president stressed on September 25, we are ready for cooperation and to restore relations with our European neighbors. The ball is in their court here. These relations were not frozen by us," he concluded.

title: Tens of thousands of Russians have made Serbia their home. A change in government raises new questions about their future.
body: A Gazprom advertisement in Belgrade. January 2023 The opposition “Student List” won a decisive victory in Serbia’s parliamentary elections last Sunday. Former President Aleksandar Vučić, who heads the Serbian Progressive Party, conceded defeat and said the new government would soon impose sanctions on Russia. Meduza examines how well-founded that prediction is and what else may lie ahead for the tens of thousands of Russians who have moved to Serbia in recent years. Vučić congratulated the students on their victory but said they were acting in the interests of and “with direct support from various European countries and the American ‘deep state ’ — the one that opposes President Trump.” In his view, the students are “just contractors who will do the dirty work planned by someone else.” Since the EU started imposing sanctions on Russia right after the war began, he said, it would force the students to do the same. He predicted this would happen by March or April. Brussels is indeed sympathetic to the Student List. In the spring of 2025, European Commissioner for Enlargement Marta Kos said the Serbian protesters’ demands were very close to “what we (the EU) are looking for,” while European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said Serbia needed to pursue reforms to join the EU. Von der Leyen and European Council President António Costa also congratulated the students on their election victory and pledged to “support reforms to uphold the rule of law, ensure media freedom, fight corruption, and strengthen democratic institutions, and work together to build Serbia’s future in the European Union.” But Brussels has already expressed displeasure with Serbia’s lenient policies toward Russian citizens. Russians can currently enter the country without a visa for up to 30 days, obtain residence permits, and apply for Serbian citizenship. About 2,000 Russians have become Serbian citizens since the start of 2022. Radio Free Europe reported that more than 300 of them had received Serbian passports through an expedited process by May of this year. The European Commission believes this poses security risks for EU countries, since those granted citizenship include people under EU, U.S., or Ukrainian sanctions. Brussels is also unhappy with Belgrade’s refusal to join EU sanctions against Russia. In its November 2025 communication on enlargement policy, the European Commission stated explicitly that “Serbia must clearly demonstrate its geopolitical orientation toward the EU.” It can do so by aligning its policies “with the EU’s restrictive measures adopted in the context of Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine.” So what will the students do? In the foreign policy section of their platform, the students emphasize their desire to deepen partnerships with EU countries and carry out the reforms needed for future integration . At the same time, they intend to preserve the “traditional partnership with the Russian Federation” and “not impose restrictive measures” against it. The students have not spoken out against Russians who have moved to Serbia, either. Any resentment they may have felt toward the Russians was more likely rooted in economic and social concerns: The arrival of tens of thousands of people drove up rents in Belgrade and Novi Sad, directly hurting many students who rent apartments. But they plan to address this problem through tighter regulation of the real estate market rather than restrictions on newcomers. Given both the students’ statements and pressure from Brussels, which demands that Serbia bring its visa policy into line with EU rules, it is reasonable to assume that the Serbian authorities will eventually impose visa requirements on Russian citizens after all and abolish or restrict the expedited citizenship process. But it is difficult to predict when these changes might happen, or even how likely they are. Serbia still has to form a government, and a presidential election is due in December. The new cabinet’s priorities will be fighting corruption, reforming the justice system, and ensuring media freedom. The government is unlikely to address visa and citizenship rules for Russians anytime soon. It will also resist imposing sanctions on Russia, just as Vučić did — if only because doing so would damage relations with Moscow and automatically jeopardize continued supplies of discounted Russian gas . Those supplies meet up to 90% of the country’s gas needs. The students are unlikely to want to expose the economy to such a risk during the transition, so it seems reasonable to expect that Serbia will not join sanctions against Russia in the next few months, as the Student List itself has already said . Serbia’s election Can Serbia’s student protesters stop Aleksandar Vučić from becoming prime minister? The country’s longtime leader has called an early election to extend his hold on power. Serbia’s student-backed opposition has defeated Vučić at the ballot box. He says the winners will impose sanctions on Russia — but they say otherwise.
