title: Legendary Jewish actor Walter Koenig, 'Star Trek's' plucky Chekov, dies at 90
body: Walter Koenig, who brought humor and grit to the role of starship navigator Pavel Chekov on the classic 1960s sci-fi TV series "Star Trek" and seven subsequent feature films, has died at the age of 90."My heart is heavy. Walter Koenig, our Ensign Pavel Chekov, passed away early today," George Takei, who starred alongside Koenig in the show and was a long-time friend, wrote on Facebook on Monday. Koenig died at his home in Los Angeles, the AP reported, citing his talent agent."Star Trek" creator Gene Roddenberry picked Koenig, who had played only a few prior roles on television, when he decided to add a Russian character to the crew of the fictional Starship Enterprise. The introduction of a Russian officer who worked harmoniously with a racially and culturally diverse crew came amid the real-world Cold War tensions of the era."We were stating tacitly that peoples of all races and creeds, nationalities could not only co-exist but care for each other deeply, and in doing so we were heralding a future that was very optimistic," Koenig once told a BBC interviewer.While Koenig was the son of Russian Jewish immigrants, he used an inauthentic Russian accent that was sometimes played for laughs.Walter Koenig's career as Pavel Chekov on Star TrekThe original TV series ran for three seasons, from 1966 to 1969. Koenig appeared on 36 episodes, and then in seven movies from 1979 to 1994."I was informed while I was still there at my audition that I had the role," Koenig told the Joplin Globe in 2008. "It seemed like an engagement that might work out over several episodes, but I had no idea that it would totally shape my career and my life."The show remained popular in syndicated reruns and inspired several later TV series and a succession of films. It attracted a devoted worldwide fan base and earned an enduring place in pop culture.Koenig's "Star Trek" fame was a blessing and a curse, as it was for cast mates such as William Shatner (Captain Kirk), Leonard Nimoy (Spock), DeForest Kelley (Dr. McCoy), Nichelle Nichols (Uhura), James Doohan (Scotty) and Takei, who played Lieutenant Sulu.They were often typecast because they were so closely associated with "Star Trek.""Most of the '70s, I didn't work at all, and I blamed it on typecasting," Koenig told the St. Petersburg Times in 1998.Walter Koenig's life and career beyond Star TrekHe later landed a regular role on the 1990s sci-fi series "Babylon 5" and was an author, script writer and occasional director.Koenig was born on September 14, 1936, raised in New York City and attended the University of California, Los Angeles, before beginning his professional acting career. He suffered a personal tragedy in 2010 when his son, actor Andrew Koenig, took his own life. Koenig married his wife Judy in 1965. They also had a daughter, actress Danielle Koenig.

title: GPT-6.1 Terra halves OpenAI's API prices and still gains ground on its larger models
body:
OpenAI has released GPT-6.1 Terra, a model it says pushes the cost-to-performance boundary further than any of its predecessors. API prices are half those of GPT-5.6 Terra.
Terra is OpenAI's closest competitor to Anthropic's mid-tier Sonnet series at half the price. Input tokens cost $1 per million, output tokens $5, compared to $2 and $10 for Claude Sonnet 5.5 and $2 and $12 for GPT-5.6 Terra. Cached inputs drop to just $0.05 per million tokens, a quarter of the previous rate.
According to OpenAI , the model combines fast visual reasoning with precise computer control and a more natural writing style, targeting everyday work tasks from drafting proposals to interpreting technical drawings to filling out forms. GPT-6.1 Terra is available now for Plus, Pro, Enterprise, and Edu users in ChatGPT Work and Codex, as well as through the API. Ad
Artificial Analysis calls GPT-6.1 Terra a new benchmark for intelligence per dollar. At maximum reasoning effort, the model gains 6 points on the Intelligence Index over GPT-5.6 Terra while costing less than a third per task ($0.40 versus $1.40). At lower effort levels the gains are even larger—7 to 13 points—placing the model on the Pareto frontier, the point where cost and performance can no longer both improve simultaneously. Ad
In the new Coding Agent Index v2.0, Terra scores 48, six points below GPT-6.1 Sol (54) and 17 points above GPT-6 Luna (31). The hallucination drop is even bigger. On the private AA-Omniscience benchmark, the model resorts to guessing only 38 percent of the time when it lacks the answer, down from 88 percent for GPT-5.6 Terra. Accuracy also rose by two points.
OpenAI positions GPT-6.1 Terra as particularly strong at automated software control. On the Agents' Last Exam benchmark, it matches GPT-6 Astra's performance at one-tenth the token price. Compared to Claude Opus 5.5 at maximum effort, Terra is more than three times as token-efficient at a quarter of the token price. That translates to roughly nine times lower cost per task. It also finishes more than three times faster than both GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol, the company says. Ad
On MMMU-Pro for visual reasoning, GPT-6.1 Terra outperforms its predecessor at every reasoning level and nearly matches GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol. On the desktop agent benchmark OSWorld 2.1, it beats GPT-5.6 Terra's best result at medium effort for a fraction of the cost.
Terra also shows a sharp improvement in coding. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, GPT-6.1 Terra solves 50.3 percent of tasks at maximum reasoning effort, up from 21.5 percent for GPT-5.6 Terra. According to Artificial Analysis, that 20-point jump puts the model in the same tier as GPT-6.1 Sol. On the scientific coding benchmark Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1, Terra outperforms GPT-6.1 Sol at lower cost and comes within five points of Claude Opus 5.5 at less than a fifth of the estimated cost. For the most demanding coding tasks, however, OpenAI still recommends GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra. Ad
GPT-6.1 Terra meets OpenAI's "Critical" cybersecurity threshold as defined by the company's Preparedness Framework and inherits the safeguards of GPT-6 Astra. Compared to its predecessor, the model is more likely to stay within its assigned boundaries and disclose restrictions to users. Ad
According to the system card , GPT-6.1 Terra holds up about as well as GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol against direct attacks on the instruction hierarchy , with those models hitting 99.99 percent on such tests. For indirect prompt injection attacks, where malicious instructions are buried in third-party content, Terra's defense rate sits at 98.8 percent, up from 96.2 percent with GPT-5.6 Terra.

title: Trump offers $1M reward for voter fraud tips that result in conviction
body:
It is not clear where the money for this reward would come from.
President Donald Trump said on Monday that he is offering a $1 million reward for anyone who reports voter fraud -- in past elections or in the upcoming midterm elections -- that leads to a conviction.
"Anybody reporting Voter Fraud in the past Elections, or the upcoming 2026 Midterm Election, will be paid $1,000,000 upon the arrest and conviction of those that created the Fraud," Trump wrote in a social media post.
Trump has repeatedly made unfounded claims that there was widespread voter fraud in past elections. It is not clear where the money for this reward that the president is offering would come from.
The White House would not provide any additional details about Trump's announcement.
Trump has pushed election reform legislation, the SAVE America Act , which he says will cut down on voter fraud. The legislation requires voter ID at the ballot box and proof of citizenship to register.
The House passed the measure earlier this year; it has failed in the Senate multiple times.
Last week, Trump announced a separate fraud whistleblower program where tipsters who successfully report and prove fraud cases will be rewarded a 1% commission of the amount of money the government is able to recover. The president said he would make the determination of whether a tipster would receive a financial reward.
ABC News' Sarah Beth Hensley contributed to this report.
24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

title: Canadian-backed potash mine in Brazil has dried up sacred Amazon springs, say residents
body: The construction of an access road for a potash mining project in Autazes, in Brazil’s Amazonas state, has caused at least two sacred springs to dry up, according to the Indigenous Mura people. It is the latest in a series of controversies spanning a decade that has plagued the Potássio Autazes project. “There is a profound sense of loss,” Filipe Mura, chief of the affected Lago do Soares village, told Mongabay via WhatsApp. “We realize we may be losing what belongs to us — our territory, our culture, and, above all, the very life that exists in this place.” In Mura traditional cosmology, all springs, rivers, lakes and forests have a guardian, or owner, who must be treated with respect, residents tell Mongabay. “If a spring dries up, it means its keeper has departed — and when the keeper leaves, they take with them the animals, the fertility of the soil, and all the blessings of that region,” Willian Rodrigues Filgueira, a professor from the Mura Baixo Madeira Indigenous territory, which neighbors the affected Lago do Soares/Urucurituba territory, and member of the Organization of Mura Indigenous Leaders of Careiro da Várzea (OLIMCV), told Mongabay via WhatsApp. The loss of a spring, therefore, disrupts the spiritual balance that sustains life in the territory. Residents also said that the company behind the project has begun to clear-cut the area — the process of cutting down all trees in a section of forest at the same time — where it intends to build…This article was originally published on Mongabay

title: [UPDATED] Ebola: Nigeria Has 54 Primary Contacts Now, Many Are In Quarantine, Says NCDC
body: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) on Monday said that it has identified another contact linked to the confirmed case of the recent Ebola outbreak in Nigeria, increasing the number of primary contacts to 54. The Director-General of the agency, Dr. Jide Idris, disclosed this during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today , identifying the new contact as an e-hailing driver who drove the index patient. “So as it is now, we’ve had — yesterday it was 54, right? One has left. The index case has left, so we had 53. “Today, we got one more suspected case contact, who actually was the Uber driver who actually drove her again before to the first hospital. That information we got later,” he said. ﻿ Idris explained that many of the contacts were in quarantine, including six who self-quarantined at home. “So we still have 54 contacts, primary contacts. What we do is that we follow up with these people because a lot of them are in quarantine right now somewhere in Abuja, here, about 40-something of them.” “We have six that are home, self-quarantined because the risks appear low. But they monitor them, call them, take their temperature, morning, evening, just to ensure that there are no changes in clinical situation. “And one or two cases like that we had. He changes. And we had to do, we had to test them again. And the three of them again today were tested, and all the three of them turned out negative,” he added. Not Out Of The Woods The NCDC chief also said efforts were ongoing to identify the secondary contacts. “So we are not out of the woods yet until we are sure that we have all the contacts, and they have been followed up. So we are still not out of the woods; because the index case is out doesn’t mean that we don’t have that,” added. The DG further said that though Nigeria does not have an active positive case, there are contacts that the agency needs to follow up. “Anyone who is symptomatic will test to be sure. You have to follow them for between two and 21 days. That’s the incubation period. And again, after 21 days, you follow up 21 days again. You take it to that before you say, OK, this is Ebola-free,” Idris said. “And after 21 days you test again, it’s negative, you can allow them to go. For secondary contacts, we don’t know how many until we start taking them.” Asked what anyone who experiences symptoms should do, the DG said, “Contact the nearest public health centre. There is an NCDC number: 6232. It is a hotline. It’s toll-free; there are people manning it for 24 hours. “If you feel funny, if you know of anybody falling ill, call that hotline, or go to the nearest healthcare centre, or the public health office.” Speaking further, the NCDC chief dismissed the notion that the evacuation of the index case to Switzerland was a vote of no confidence in Nigeria’s healthcare system. “I don’t believe that because we have competent hands; in fact, just yesterday we brought in more people, Nigerians who actually participated in treating Ebola cases in 2014. “We have infectious disease experts here. We even have a register of those cases, just in case we have cases in different parts of the country. So, we’re keeping the register. We know the capabilities, what they can do, what they cannot do,” Idris stated. He explained that the Swiss government was responsible for the air ambulance, not Nigeria, adding that the evacuation was based on a diplomatic request. “Mind you again, the patient improved clinically,” he said. This combo photo shows an air ambulance used to evacuate Nigeria’s index Ebola patient on October 26, 2026, and Health Minister Pate The Federal Government announced Nigeria’s first confirmed case of the Bundibugyo strain in Abuja on October 20, 2026. It identified the patient as a woman with a recent travel history to Uganda, who returned to Nigeria with symptoms on October 7, but the Ugandan authorities denied reports of an Ebola outbreak in the East African country. On October 25, the NCDC announced that the number of contacts, including health workers, linked to the patient had risen to 53. On Monday, the health minister confirmed that the index patient was flown to Switzerland, stable and conscious, and had clinically improved. The post [UPDATED] Ebola: Nigeria Has 54 Primary Contacts Now, Many Are In Quarantine, Says NCDC appeared first on Channels Television .

title: ACAMB advises bank customers against phishing scams, urges protection of sensitive information
body:
The Association of Corporate Communication and Marketing Professionals in Banks (ACAMB) has urged bank customers to remain vigilant against phishing scams and other forms of cyber fraud, warning that criminals are increasingly using fake bank alerts, cloned websites and impersonation accounts to steal sensitive financial information.
The warning follows a fraudulent text message impersonating various banks. FactCheckAfrica debunked the message, finding that the link it contained led to a cloned internet banking website designed to steal customers’ login credentials, BVNs, card details and transaction PINs.
The incident highlights the risks associated with digital banking fraud in Nigeria. In June, Wema Bank suspended its engagements on X amid reports of more than 70 fake accounts impersonating the bank and its ALAT platform. In August, Zenith Bank Plc disclosed that it was investigating unauthorised access to customer data linked to a global cyberattack.
ACAMB President, Jide Sipe, warned that fraudsters were increasingly adopting sophisticated methods to impersonate trusted banking brands and steal customers’ personal information, making their schemes difficult to distinguish from legitimate communications.
“When a scam message carries your name, your phone number or your bank’s logo, it looks real. That is exactly why customers must slow down. No bank in Nigeria will ask you to confirm your PIN, password, OTP or BVN through a link,” Sipe said.
Sipe acknowledged the efforts of banks to strengthen fraud detection and customer protection, alongside regulatory measures introduced by the Central Bank of Nigeria’s mandatory cybersecurity self assessment guide. He stressed, however, that these efforts must be complemented by customer awareness and vigilance, particularly when handling requests for sensitive banking information.
“Banks can strengthen their security systems, but fraudsters continue to find ways to exploit unsuspecting customers. We must all remain vigilant. Always pause, verify requests through official channels and report anything suspicious before taking action,” he added.
Sipe urged customers to avoid clicking links in unsolicited messages asking them to verify, reactivate or secure their bank accounts. He also warned against sharing personal identification numbers (PINs), passwords, one-time passwords (OTPs), card verification values (CVVs) or BVNs in response to suspicious requests.
Customers should verify such requests directly with their banks through official mobile applications, verified social media accounts or published customer service numbers. Anyone who has entered banking details on a suspicious website should contact their bank immediately to secure their account and block affected cards where necessary.
ACAMB reaffirmed its commitment to working with member banks, regulators and the media to raise awareness of cyber fraud and promote safer digital banking practices as the use of online financial services continues to expand across Nigeria.

title: 'Lack of Jews hasn't meant lack of antisemitism,' Expert on Jews in Wales tells 'Post' - interview
body: "The absence of Jews in Wales hasn't meant the absence of antisemitism; it's actually the opposite," Bangor University Professor and expert in Welsh Jewry, Professor Nathan Abrams, told The Jerusalem Post on Sunday.Abrams was born into a Jewish family in North London but has lived in Wales for twenty years and speaks Welsh fluently.He recently published a book, Jews in the Welsh Imagination: Medieval Times to the Present, which explores the nation's attitudes towards Jews over the centuries.“For most of Wales's existence as an entity – for 15 centuries – there have been no Jews here. The fascination the Welsh have with Jews is inversely proportional to the numbers," he said. "So the absence of Jews hasn't meant the absence of antisemitism or similar attitudes. It's actually the opposite."According to the 2021 UK Census, 2,044 people in Wales identified as Jewish by religion, representing approximately 0.07% of Wales's population of 3.1 million.Most of Wales' Jews are located in Cardiff, where there are two synagogues: a Reform synagogue and an Orthodox synagogue. A Chabad synagogue also serves Llandudno, and small community-organized groups or individual Jews exist in other cities.Antisemitism in Wales often overshadowed by wider UK statisticsJews in Wales are not a commonly discussed topic in Jewish media, and reporting on antisemitism in the nation is often swallowed by wider UK statistics, which do not typically show breakdowns by country.The latest Welsh policing figures show 6,157 police-recorded hate crimes across Wales between April 2025 and March 2026, including 4,098 motivated by race and 325 motivated by religion.Of those, 325 had a religious motivation, down from 451; however, there is no breakdown of which religion was targeted, so it is not possible from these figures to determine the number of anti-Jewish crimes.The UK's Community Security Trust, however, separately recorded 25 antisemitic incidents geographically associated with Wales during calendar year 2025, including 13 in North Wales, 8 in South Wales, 2 in Dyfed-Powys and 2 in Gwent.Separately, a Freedom of Information disclosure from Dyfed-Powys Police shows the force recorded 17 crimes classified as anti-Jewish in 2025, up from 12 in 2024, an increase of about 42%.The figures are for the Dyfed-Powys policing area, not all Wales. They also do not necessarily capture every antisemitic offense recorded under other categories. It also, of course, differs from the CST reporting, suggesting that on-the-ground figures may far exceed those ultimately reported to CST.While the available national police statistics do not establish how many anti-Jewish crimes occurred specifically in Wales, the number is clearly high enough to be deemed serious, as the Welsh Local Government Association (WLGA) recently met with Jewish community representatives from across Wales to discuss tackling antisemitism.During the meeting, Jewish community representatives spoke about growing anxiety about antisemitism, including routine verbal abuse, concerns about children in schools and people changing their behavior to avoid identifying as Jewish in public.The South Wales Jewish Representative Council said: “The Welsh Jewish community is long-established and deeply rooted.""We are a resilient community, but there is no doubt that the rise in antisemitism in recent years has left many people shaken and concerned."Forms, sources of antisemitism in WalesWhat forms does antisemitism take in Wales, and who does it come from?"In a sense, it's a microcosm of England, and similarly a lot of the antisemitism is on social media," Abrams told the Post. "Obviously, a lot of it coalesces around the Israel-Palestine conflict."Abrams referenced the phenomenon known as "ambient antisemitism," which speaks to the impact demonstrations, ripping down posters, putting up stickers, ripping down stickers, and the like have on creating an environment that is hostile to Jews."It's not specifically hurting Jews, physically, but it creates an environment in which Jews are not comfortable being themselves. And I think that's quite a good way to describe it here."Abrams' experience of antisemitism, he continued, is shaped by living in the northwest of Wales, which is highly nationalist, Welsh-speaking and supportive of Plaid Cymru, the left-leaning Welsh nationalist political party.Plaid Cymru's official stance is critical of Israel and very supportive of Palestine. It has long campaigned for Palestinian State recognition, and deems Israel's actions to be genocide. In September 2025, the party leader called for "harsh sanctions against the Israeli Government" in light of its actions in Gaza."Wales has always been a place where there's been eyes on Palestine. It fits in with the narrative that the Welsh Nationalists have of themselves. The first colony of the British Empire was the Welsh, so [they see themselves as] the Palestinians of the British.""Because of this, the antisemitism here is kind of an obsession with Israel," Abrams continued. "You'll get the antisemitism that's expressed by people who don't think they're being antisemitic.""The position I would take [in Wales] is that many people are well-meaning but cross the line into antisemitism through repetition of age-old tropes. They won't know that this emphasis on killing babies has been used throughout history."Abrams also noted a class difference in Wales regarding who cares about Israel-Palestine and who does not."If you're working class, you probably don't care; you probably hate the demonstrators more. Whereas the middle-class protesters are kind of indistinguishable from the academic antisemitism.""A lot of it is not expressed in front of Jews, because Welsh society is polite. Older, middle-class Brits, right, aren't so vulgar as to be openly racist.""So I would say across Wales, outside of the metropolises, it's older white people, do-gooders, right thinking, wrong application."As discussed in his book, Welsh attitudes towards Jews started with Israel and now, 1600 years later, have returned full circle."The complexity of Jewishness is still reduced to the Middle East conflict," Abrams concluded.

title: Man accused in fatal Saskatchewan highway shooting to stand trial
body:
A man accused of a September 2025 highway shooting near Weyburn will stand trial for murder.
A judge ruled on Friday there is enough evidence for Chris Fahlman to go to trial on a second-degree murder charge, after a preliminary hearing in Weyburn provincial court.
Fahlman was charged with second-degree murder and intentionally discharging a firearm in a reckless manner in connection with the death of 44-year-old Tanya Myers.
Myers was riding in the passenger seat of a vehicle along Highway 39 near Weyburn, Sask., when a bullet struck her on Sept. 12, 2025, according to the Saskatchewan RCMP. She later died of her injuries.
Her family remembered her as being “an amazing energy healer and animal lover, with a special fondness for cats,” in a statement issued through the RCMP following her death.
A second vehicle was also hit by a bullet, but the occupant was not injured, police said.
Fahlman was arrested last November. He applied for bail, but his request was denied in July.
The preliminary inquiry is not a finding of guilt or innocence, but a test on whether there is sufficient evidence to proceed to trial.

title: Russian Forces Intensify Shelling of Epicentr K Chain Across Ukraine in 48-Hour Wave of Strikes
body:
The Epicentr K retail chain has faced attacks over the past 48 hours targeting company facilities in multiple Ukrainian regions, according to the company’s statements on Facebook .
The latest series of attacks hit hypermarkets and infrastructure in several Ukrainian cities. Over the past 48 hours and preceding days, the Epicentr K network sustained damage at locations in Uman, Pervomaisk and Dubno, where three people were injured, as well as Kovel, where warehouses were damaged. This follows an earlier series of attacks that targeted Epicentr K shopping centers in Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia, Vinnytsia and Poltava.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
A Russian ballistic attack on Kyiv overnight Oct. 21 destroyed an Epicentr K hypermarket on Pochayna Street in the Obolon district, Forbes Ukraine reported . Espreso.TV wrote on Telegram about damage to a 1,000-square-meter building. According to media reports, fires also broke out at a neighboring postal cargo facility and at the Retail Park shopping center.
In Kharkiv, an attack on the evening of Oct. 24 destroyed the Epicentr K shopping center in the Osnovianskyi district, Suspilne Media reported . According to regional reports, the threat of repeat strikes complicated rescue operations, and a rescuer was injured when Russian forces launched a repeat strike on the site during firefighting. A 39-year-old man sought medical assistance. Suspilne Media noted that the same facility was previously damaged in a drone attack on Aug. 27.
Founded by Oleksandr and Halyna Hereha in 2003 with the opening of their first home improvement store in Kyiv, Epicentr K has grown into a major national retail network. The chain currently operates 72 shopping centers across Ukraine, with a total retail area of more than 2 million square meters (21.5 million square feet) and around 38,000 employees. According to financial statements registered in YouControl , the company generated Hr. 81.2 billion ($1.9 billion) in 2025.

title: Britain told to plan for war without Trump’s America
body: Defence spending should go to five per cent of gross domestic product immediately, the country should be prepared for a wider European war and planning should assume Britain may have to fight without the United States, according to a security academic at the University of Leicester. Dr Simon Bennett, director of the Civil Safety and Security Unit in the university’s School of Business and author of a 2025 book on security lessons from the war in Ukraine, set out the argument in comments issued through the university press office. Bennett said: “Given these facts, we must prepare ourselves to fight alone. Like Keir Starmer, Prime Minister Andy Burnham is in denial about Trump. The American president is a lost cause. Better to focus finite energies and budgets first, on supporting Ukraine, and secondly, on preparing this country for a wider European war. Defence spending must be increased to 5% of Gross Domestic Product immediately and, as suggested by former Secretary of State for Defence Lord Hutton of Furness in the 17 October edition of The i Paper, the British public must be told the truth about Russia’s hybrid warfare campaign.” On the range of threats he believes the country is exposed to, Bennett said: “The United Kingdom faces a spectrum of threats. The country has suffered two Kremlin-initiated chemical warfare attacks, in London in 2006 (Polonium) and in Salisbury in 2018 (Novichok). The Council on Strategic Risks recently highlighted the UK’s vulnerability to biological weapons. Prime Minister Burnham, it is time to focus on what really matters – giving Ukraine the weapons it needs and securing a vulnerable United Kingdom. Do not prostrate yourself before Trump, as your predecessor did. As Volodymyr Zelensky and Mark Carney have shown, the only way to deal with Trump is to stand up to him.” Bennett is asking for far more than the government has signed up to. Ministers have committed to NATO’s target of three and a half per cent of gross domestic product on core defence by 2035, with a further one and a half per cent on defence-related resilience and infrastructure making up the alliance’s headline five per cent figure. Bennett is calling for core defence spending itself to reach five per cent now, a distinction ministers have had to set out repeatedly . Lord Hutton of Furness, whose intervention Bennett cites, was Secretary of State for Defence from 2008 to 2009. His argument that the public must be told the truth about Russian hybrid warfare runs close to what ministers have themselves begun saying. Wes Streeting told the Defence Committee this month that hybrid activity of this kind amounts to state backed terrorism, and Louise Sandher-Jones confirmed in a written answer last week that “we know Russia is conducting a campaign of hybrid attacks and sabotage across Europe.” Ministers have also confirmed that government messaging on defence and security will build ahead of Exercise ALBISTON SHADOW and NATO’s crisis management exercise in spring 2027, and the Cabinet Office launched its Be Ready campaign this month asking households to prepare to look after themselves for three days. The two chemical incidents Bennett refers to are the poisoning of Alexander Litvinenko with polonium-210 in London in 2006, which a public inquiry found was probably approved by the Russian president, and the Novichok attack on Sergei and Yulia Skripal in Salisbury in 2018, which killed Dawn Sturgess and which Britain attributed to the GRU. The Council on Strategic Risks is a Washington-based institute publishing on biological, climate and nuclear security. Bennett’s case rests on his reading of the American president, whom he describes as a Russophile and, in his words and expressly as his opinion, a traitor to the West’s liberal-democratic values. He said he predicted in March 2025 that Trump would ally the United States with Russia through accords and treaties, and took criticism for saying so at the time. The post Britain told to plan for war without Trump’s America first appeared on UK Defence Journal .

title: EU mobilizes €4.7 bln to reimburse its member nations for arms supplies to Ukraine
body:
BRUSSELS, October 26. /TASS/. The EU Council has decided to mobilize 4.9 billion euro from the European Peace Facility, including 4.7 billion to partially reimburse EU countries for their arms supplies to Kiev and 230 million euro to expand the budget of the EU Military Assistance Mission in Support of Ukraine.
"The Council today adopted a set of eight decisions enabling the use of funds for Ukraine under the European Peace Facility (EPF). These decisions allow for the partial reimbursement, through the EPF, of military aid already delivered by member states (since the spring of 2023 - TASS), amounting to a total amount of €4.7 billion. They also provide additional financing for the EU Military Assistance Mission in Support of Ukraine (EUMAM Ukraine), amounting to a total of €230 million," the Council said.
This is the first tranche of aid funding for Kiev from the European Peace Facility that was blocked by Hungary in 2023. The total amount of frozen funds is 6.6 billion euros. Hungary lifted its veto this spring, but the process has stalled due to disagreements over how EU member states will distribute these funds among themselves.
Funds from the European Peace Facility have never been transferred to Ukraine; instead, they were allocated as compensation to EU countries that supplied weapons from their own stockpiles to the Kiev regime. On average, the European Union has compensated for about 40% of the weapons’ cost under this scheme. At the same time, the technical condition of the weapons was not verified. As the Euractiv portal (now Rapporteur) reported, a number of EU countries may have significantly inflated the actual cost of their shipments, making it very profitable to receive compensation for decommissioned weapons.

title: A rare victory for multilateralism in the fight against environmental crime (commentary)
body: Multilateralism has had a miserable few years. International institutions are under strain, geopolitical rivalries are intensifying and governments struggle to agree on even the most elementary rules. Governments struggle to agree on even elementary rules. Yet last week in Vienna, there was an unexpected breakthrough. Countries agreed to begin negotiating a global treaty to tackle environmental crime. It is a modest but important victory for international cooperation, and one that could help turn the tables on some of the world’s most destructive criminal enterprises. The breakthrough came at the 13th Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Convention against Transnational Organized Crime (UNTOC). By 83 votes to 12, governments backed a resolution establishing a committee to design a new protocol targeting illegal trade in wildlife and timber, illicit mining and trafficking in minerals, and waste trafficking. The outcome was hardly assured. The United States, Argentina, Saudi Arabia and Iran sought to dilute the initiative. They failed. The vote showed that international rules can still advance despite determined opposition. Illegal logging in Indonesian Borneo. Photo by Rhett Ayers Butler Brazil deserves considerable credit. Working with a coalition spanning Latin America and Africa, its diplomats turned years of technical discussions into political momentum. Civil society organizations, including the Igarapé Institute, helped build the evidence and sustain pressure for stronger international action. The breakthrough also signals a wider shift in global diplomacy. Countries across the Global South are increasingly becoming norm-makers rather than simply norm-takers. title: Switzerland has confirmed arrival of evacuated Ebola patient – Health minister
body: The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, says Swiss authorities have confirmed the arrival of the Ebola patient evacuated from Nigeria . Pate disclosed this in a post on his X handle on Monday, saying the patient was receiving treatment at Geneva University Hospitals, while her spouse was in isolation at the University Hospital Zurich. “The Swiss authorities have confirmed that the patient and her spouse arrived safely in Switzerland today,” the minister said. He added that the evacuation was made possible through cooperation between Nigerian and Swiss authorities, with support from the World Health Organisation (WHO). Pate said Federal Councillor Elisabeth Baume-Schneider conveyed Switzerland’s appreciation for the care provided by Nigerian health professionals and the cooperation between the two countries. “In our telephone conversation, Federal Councillor Elisabeth Baume-Schneider conveyed Switzerland’s appreciation for the care provided by Nigerian health professionals and the close cooperation between our authorities and WHO that made the evacuation possible,” he said. The minister expressed appreciation to the clinical and public health teams in Nigeria and Switzerland, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), Swiss health authorities and the WHO for their roles in facilitating the evacuation. He, however, said public health measures remained ongoing in Nigeria to contain the disease. “Here in Nigeria, contact monitoring, investigation of alerts and other containment measures continue,” he said.

title: Deadly Russian ballistic missile attack hits Kyiv university, bridge, medical centers
body:
Smoke rises from Kyiv's Southern Bridge after a Russian missile attack in the early hours of Oct. 27. (Viacheslav RatynskyiThe Kyiv Independent)
Russian ballistic missiles targeted Kyiv in a deadly attack overnight on Oct. 26-27, striking a university campus, a major bridge, an administrative building, and medical facilities.
Kyiv, a city of three million people, has been relentlessly assaulted by Russian ballistic missiles in recent months as Moscow exploits Ukraine's air defense shortage. While its battlefield offensive has slowed, Russia has chosen a strategy of mass aerial strikes against vulnerable civilians.
At least one person was killed, and 15 people have been injured in the latest Russian attack , Ukraine's State Emergency Service (DSNS) said. Those injured in the attack include a paramedic, a medical technician, and a 20-year-old university student.
The mayor later reported a strike on the city's Southern Bridge over the Dnipro River, one of Kyiv's major traffic arteries. The bridge connects the city's eastern and western sides and is crucial for the daily commutes of hundreds of thousands of residents.
The bridge and metro infrastructure were damaged overnight, Klitschko said. Train service on the bridge has been temporarily suspended.
Ihor, who lives on the east bank of the Dnipro River but works on the west bank, said his commute now takes around two hours, including about half an hour spent walking across the Southern Bridge.
"We’ll have to walk like this every morning now. Taking a detour would take too long," Ihor, who declined to give his surname, told the Kyiv Independent.
Iryna was also crossing the bridge while it remained closed to traffic, but she was using an electric scooter to get across. Following the overnight attack on Oct. 27, this was her first time commuting to work this way.
"This is an alternative means of transport, but I don’t know how long the journey will take," Iryna, who also declined to give a surname, said, expressing hope that the bridge would be repaired soon.
President Volodymyr Zelensky said that a university campus in the city was struck by Russia alongside Kyiv's well-known Kyoto park and residential buildings.
Education minister Andriy Butenko later said that the Russian attack damaged buildings and dormitories of the State University of Trade and Economics. He said there were no deaths among university students or employees.
"This is once again a terrorist country attacking educational institutions. A university, a scientific institution, a college, a school, or a kindergarten - the enemy directs its missiles at children, teachers, and scientists without any pity or humanity. There is no excuse for Moscow's cynical actions," Butenko added.
Kyiv Independent journalists on the ground first reported that loud explosions rocked the city in the Podilskyi and Obolonskyi districts at around 9:45 p.m. local time.
Just minutes earlier, Ukraine's Air Force warned that ballistic missiles and other missiles were headed toward Kyiv.
Explosions were heard near a metro station in Kyiv's Desnianskyi district, where a car was damaged, Klitschko reported .
Two medical facilities in the Dniprovskyi district were also damaged in the attack, Klitschko said. At one of the two sites that came under fire, blast waves shattered windows in the intensive care unit. Windows were also shattered at the other site.
A three-story commercial building was also "partially destroyed" in the district where one person was found dead, the State Emergency Service (DSNS) added.
A school building in the district was also damaged in the attack, the Kyiv City Military Administration wrote .
"Buildings of a university campus, dormitories, and nearby residential buildings were damaged" in the Desnyanskyi district, DSNS said .
Hours later, another wave of ballistic missiles attacked the city in the middle of the night.
Kyiv Independent journalists on the ground reported a new round of explosions at around 3:30 a.m. local time. At least seven explosions rocked the city in the space of three minutes. The blasts came minutes after Ukraine's Air Force warned that Russian ballistic missiles were bound for the capital.
Another blast shook Kyiv some 15 minutes later, without warning.
The second wave of missiles hit an administrative building in the Podilskyi district, Klitschko said . Non-residential buildings were also targeted in two other unspecified locations.
Some metro stations elsewhere in the city were damaged during the earlier attack, but were repaired by emergency workers overnight, the mayor reported.
Russia has attacked the Southern Bridge and other key bridges multiple times in October in an attempt to disrupt logistics and daily life in Kyiv.
Earlier in the night, Zelensky condemned Russia's attack on Kyiv and renewed calls for allies to provide Ukraine with air defense.
"Russian ballistic missiles struck the grounds of a university in Kyiv and the area around it — effectively the campus, Kyoto Park, the area near a metro station, and residential buildings," he said in a post to X.
"(I)t is precisely under such circumstances, when the threat is constant, when strikes can come at any moment and target cities and villages directly, that artificial delays in providing air defense to Ukraine help terror," Zelensky added.
Russia regularly targets civilian infrastructure in cities across Ukraine as it continues to wage its war.
Ballistic missiles targeted Kyiv in a fatal Russian attack on the night of Oct. 13-14, killing five people and injuring another 25.
At least one person was killed, and 24 were injured in another Russian ballistic missile attack overnight on Oct. 22, during which cluster munitions also targeted the city.
Volodymyr Ivanyshyn is a news editor for The Kyiv Independent. He is pursuing an Honors Bachelor of Arts at the University of Toronto, majoring in political science with a minor in anthropology and human geography. Volodymyr holds a Certificate in Business Fundamentals from Rotman Commerce at the University of Toronto. He previously completed an internship with The Kyiv Independent.

title: Third Political Prisoner Dies in Russia This Month – Report
body:
A Russian television production designer arrested after returning from Kyiv to renew his passport has died in a Moscow hospital, the rights group First Department reported Monday, Oct. 26.
Aleksandr Kondratov, 52, was transferred from a pretrial detention center to Botkin Hospital on Oct. 23, the group said in a Telegram post ⁠.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
The cause of death has not been disclosed. First Department said his death was at least the 11th this year among defendants in cases it considers politically motivated.
Kondratov had lived in Kyiv since 2012 and returned to Russia to replace his passport, according to rights monitors. He was subsequently held through repeated administrative arrests before authorities opened a treason investigation.
Kondratov was detained at Moscow’s Vnukovo airport on May 5.
Before the criminal case was opened, he spent more than 70 days under successive administrative arrests for alleged petty hooliganism, OVD-Info said. Such repeated short sentences are commonly described by Russian rights monitors as carousel arrests.
The treason case was opened Aug. 5 and investigated by the Federal Security Service’s (FSB) directorate for Moscow and the Moscow region.
Mediazona reported ⁠ from a Moscow City Court hearing in September that his lawyer, Natalia Tikhonova, said the case concerned “at least six publications” online. She did not disclose their contents.
The court rejected an appeal against his detention. The publicly reported details do not establish what the posts said or how investigators argued they constituted treason.
Kondratov was best known for his work as production designer on “Likvidatsiya” (“Liquidation”), a 2007 crime drama set in postwar Odesa. He received Golden Eagle and TEFI awards for his work on the series. His other credits included Odesa-Mama and Return My Love.
First Department’s death count covers those among individuals prosecuted in politically motivated cases. It is a rights-monitoring assessment, rather than an official Russian category or a finding that all the deaths had the same cause.
The Moscow Times reported ⁠ that Kondratov was the third such defendant whose death became known in October.
The other two were Igor Yakovenko, 52, who died in a Krasnodar detention center, and Rustam Khalikov, 49, who died in a penal colony in the Penza region. Both had been convicted on terrorism-related charges that their defense teams disputed, according to the outlet.
The newspaper said that eight of the 11 people in its tally had entered custody aged 50 or older. It described complaints about detention conditions, pressure from prison administrations, and difficulties obtaining medical treatment.
Those broader allegations do not establish the circumstances of Kondratov’s death. The reports announcing it did not identify a medical cause.
Kondratov’s death follows renewed appeals by Russian human rights campaigners for international attention to those imprisoned in politically motivated cases.
Earlier in October, Memorial estimated that more than 1,800 people in Russia were recognized as political prisoners. Its broader estimate of individuals imprisoned or facing politically motivated prosecution was approximately 5,700.
At an event in the French National Assembly on Oct. 7, Memorial co-chair Oleg Orlov urged European lawmakers ⁠ to prioritize prisoners whose health and circumstances put them at particular risk.
“While there is still a chance, we must save at least some of those who will not survive imprisonment,” he said.
Orlov asked lawmakers to follow individual prisoners’ cases, speak about them publicly and maintain scrutiny of their treatment. His appeal focused on securing releases while prisoners could still benefit from them, warning that some might otherwise die before completing their sentences.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Submarine Affair: Communications adviser Tzahi Liber convicted of brokering bribes
body: The Tel Aviv District Court on Monday convicted communications adviser Yitzhak (Tzahi) Liber of acting as a bribe intermediary in the Submarine Affair, finding that he received nearly NIS 94,000 from businessman Miki Ganor, intended for Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's former chief of staff, David Sharan.Judge Dr. Shmuel Melamed convicted Liber of brokering bribes, money laundering and assisting in the preparation of false accounting records. The court found that the payments were disguised as fees for consulting services that were never provided.The verdict concerns one part of Case 3000, the corruption affair surrounding Israel's purchases of submarines and naval vessels from German shipbuilder ThyssenKrupp. Ganor represented the company in Israel, while Sharan held senior positions in the Prime Minister's Office.The court tried Liber separately from the defendants in the main case, including Ganor and Sharan, whose proceedings remain ongoing.The court examined two payments from Ganor's company: NIS 35,400 transferred in November 2014 to a company owned by Liber, and NIS 58,500 transferred in August 2016 to a company owned by his business partner.Judge: Companies, false invoices used to conceal Ganor-Sharan financial connectionMelamed found that the companies and false invoices were used to conceal the purpose of the payments and the financial connection between Ganor and Sharan. The arrangement also allowed the payments to be recorded as business expenses.Liber, a close friend of Sharan, denied wrongdoing and maintained that the money paid for genuine communications and strategic consulting work. His defense argued that he had not passed Ganor's money to Sharan and that a separate payment of several thousand shekels to his friend was a gesture of thanks for introducing him to Ganor.The court rejected that account, relying on Liber's admissions during police questioning, statements Ganor gave investigators, and supporting financial and other records.In his police account, Liber described receiving the money and passing it to Sharan in cash. He also acknowledged conveying information and requests between Ganor and Sharan concerning submarines, according to the verdict.Both Liber and Ganor later withdrew their incriminating accounts. Melamed nevertheless found that their earlier statements were supported by evidence including payment records, a table of consultants maintained by Ganor, staff notebooks and communications data.Liber's explanation of supposed consulting arrangement made no commercial sense, judge findsThe judge also found that Liber's explanation of the supposed consulting arrangement made no commercial sense. Among other difficulties, the parties exchanged unsigned draft contracts, and Liber could not adequately explain how the amounts and timing of the payments had been determined.A substantial part of the verdict addressed the defense's attempt to exclude Liber's police admissions. His lawyers argued that investigators from the Lahav 433 National Crime Unit had pressured him improperly, interfered with his access to legal advice, and linked cooperation to release from detention.Melamed rejected the request, finding that Liber retained control over what he said, chose when to answer questions and when to remain silent, and gave his central admission after consulting privately with his lawyer. The judge concluded that the admissions were voluntary and reliable.Although the prosecution sought separate convictions for each payment, Melamed treated the transactions as one continuing course of criminal conduct. Liber was therefore convicted of one count of each of the three offenses.Melamed took over the case following the death of Judge Benny Sagi, who had heard the evidence. He explained that his verdict rested on the existing record, after both sides asked not to add to the material presented before Sagi.

title: Dzifa Tegah declares bid for NDC Deputy National Secretary position
body: As the race for key leadership positions in the National Democratic Congress (NDC) gathers momentum, Dzifa Tegah has declared her intention to contest the position of Deputy National Secretary in the party’s upcoming national executive elections. Speaking at the Campaign Trail, an initiative by the NDC Communications Bureau and Elections Directorate, Ms Tegah highlighted her years of grassroots engagement, which began during her university days and culminated in her rise to the position of Deputy Women’s Organiser. title: News Publishers Move SC To Challenge The DPDP Act
body: A group of 21 news publishers has reportedly challenged India’s Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act in the Supreme Court (SC), arguing that the law could undermine investigative journalism and expose journalists’ sources. The lawsuit, filed on October 6, argues that the law’s provisions on consent, data erasure and government access to information could restrict news reporting and force publishers to remove factual stories. The case is scheduled to be heard on October 27, according to a Reuters report. The challenge comes nearly a year after the Centre notified the Digital Personal Data Protection Rules, 2025 in November last year. The broader DPDP Act, 2023 and the Rules establish a framework governing how organisations collect, process and protect individuals’ digital personal data. The Digital News Publishers Association (DNPA), which represents the publishers, has argued that the law does not provide a specific exemption for journalistic activities. According to the confidential filing, the association reportedly said that the absence of such safeguards could compromise press freedom and investigative reporting. The DNPA’s members include Mukesh Ambani-owned Network18, Gautam Adani-owned NDTV, the Indian Express and Times Internet, which is part of the Times of India group. Publishers Vs The DPDP Act A key concern raised by the publishers is the requirement to obtain consent before processing personal data. The DNPA has argued that requiring journalists to notify the subjects of investigations and seek their consent could allow them to destroy evidence or intimidate witnesses. The association has also flagged provisions allowing individuals to withdraw consent and request the erasure of their personal data. According to the filing, the absence of a public-interest safeguard could force publishers to remove or substantially redact factual news reports. The publishers have further raised concerns about provisions empowering the government to seek information from organisations handling personal data. They argue that these powers could expose confidential journalistic sources and discourage whistleblowers from sharing information about corruption, corporate wrongdoing and electoral malpractice. The filing also challenges the government’s power to restrict access to information in the public interest, arguing that the provisions could curtail press freedom. The DNPA has sought the quashing of several contentious provisions of the law, most of which are scheduled to come into effect from May 2027, Reuters reported. The association has also argued that the government has granted broad exemptions to the state without extending corresponding protections to the press. What The DPDP Framework Provides The DPDP Act, enacted in August 2023, establishes obligations for processing digital personal data . The later DPDP Rules, notified in November 2025, provide a phased implementation framework, giving organisations up to 18 months to comply with specified requirements. The framework requires platforms to obtain consent for processing personal data, provide clear information about its use and implement security safeguards. It also gives individuals rights to access, correct, update and seek the erasure of their personal data, subject to the applicable provisions. The latest case marks one of the most prominent challenges to the DPDP framework so far, raising questions about how India’s data protection requirements will interact with press freedom and investigative reporting. The Act provides for financial penalties of up to ₹250 Cr for failing to implement reasonable security safeguards. Other violations, including certain breaches of obligations relating to children’s personal data, can attract penalties of up to ₹200 Cr. However, the publishers argue that the framework does not adequately account for the requirements of investigative journalism, particularly when reporting involves personal information collected in the public interest. The government has maintained that the framework protects citizens’ privacy while supporting responsible data processing. The post News Publishers Move SC To Challenge The DPDP Act appeared first on Inc42 Media .

title: US Senators to NBA: Reevaluate Relationship with Rwanda In Light of Serious Human Rights & DR Congo Concerns
body: Today, U.S. Senators Jeff Merkley (D-OR) and Marsha Blackburn (R-TN) sent a bipartisan letter to NBA Commissioner Adam Silver questioning the league’s continued business ties with the Rwandan government amid serious human rights concerns and Rwanda’s role in the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). The senators are asking the NBA to explain how its partnership aligns with its stated commitment to human rights and its pledge to follow U.S. policy. Read the senators’ letter and read ESPN’s coverage of the story . Sasha Lezhnev, Senior Policy Advisor at The Sentry, said: “Rwanda’s invasion of the DR Congo with up to 18,000 troops and command of an armed group that has recruited child soldiers and committed alleged war crimes should raise alarm bells with the NBA. It’s time for the league and the Clippers to cancel their commercial relationships with Rwanda, just as Arsenal and Bayern Munich did last year.” The Sentry has documented the roles of Rwanda, Uganda, and the DRC government in the conflict in eastern DRC for several years. Earlier this year, we launched the Blood on the Ball campaign to spotlight sportswashing by governments involved in fueling some of the world’s deadliest conflicts, particularly Rwanda and the United Arab Emirates. title: NDC opens new Abuja base, targets 2027 electoral victory
body: …As Dickson hails new national secretariat as Noah’s Ark 2 By Henry Umoru The National Leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, has inaugurated its newly acquired national secretariat in Abuja as part of efforts to strengthen its operations ahead of the 2027 general election. The facility, located in the Jabi area of the Federal Capital Territory, was unveiled shortly after an emergency meeting of the party’s National Executive Committee (NEC), as it marks a significant step in the party’s efforts to strengthen its organisational structure and establish a permanent administrative base as preparations for the forthcoming elections gather momentum. The new secretariat is expected to serve as the party’s administrative centre and headquarters for its presidential campaign as preparations for the 2027 elections gather momentum, just as the development marks a step in the NDC’s efforts to establish a permanent national base for coordinating its activities and managing its expanding political structure. It is a strategic centre for coordinating its activities, strengthening communication among state chapters and mobilising supporters across the country and is also expected to play a central role in organising the party’s presidential campaign and coordinating other electoral activities ahead of the 2027 general elections In his remarks, the National Leader of the party, Senator Seriake Dickson, described the facility as its new “Noah’s Ark” ahead of the 2027 general elections as he congratulated members and supporters on the acquisition, describing the new secretariat as a unifying centre that would provide a befitting home for the party’s growing membership. He referred to the facility as the NDC’s newly acquired “Noah’s Ark,” a description underscoring its importance as a rallying point for members and supporters as the party pursues its political ambitions. The inauguration attracted the party’s National Chairman, Senator Moses Cleopas; National Leader, Senator Seriake Dickson; and Senator Victor Umeh, representing Anambra Central in the National Assembly. Also present was the party’s Rivers State governorship candidate, Dumo Lulu-Briggs, alongside other party leaders and members. With this, the NDC has positioned itself as an alternative political platform for Nigerians seeking a change from the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC). With the new facility, the party is expected to strengthen coordination between its national leadership, state chapters and other structures as election preparations continue. title: Some Observations About Anthropic’s IPO Filing
body: In an S-1 filing today preceding what could be the largest IPO ever , Anthropic laid out extensive new details about its earnings, growth, key stakeholders and the risks it faces going forward. Clocking in at 335 pages, the document wasn’t exactly light reading. However, after a preliminary once-over, we highlight a few of the more intriguing disclosures below: Revenue growth is unusually rapid For the first half of this year, Anthropic reported revenue of $16.3 billion. That’s up 14x from the same period in 2025. Things aren’t slowing either. While the S-1 doesn’t forecast the second half of this year, Reuters has reported that Anthropic could reach a $110 billion annualized revenue run rate by year-end, citing analysts who met with company executives. But losses persist Anthropic also posted a $693 million operating income loss for the first half of 2026, down about two-thirds from last year. Its net loss for this year’s first half was $80 billion, of which about 90% stemmed from what it called a “change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities, and SAFE s.” Founders hold similar stakes Each of Anthropic’s seven founders holds between 230,000 and 246,000 shares of Class A stock, per the S-1. This kind of egalitarianism seems unusual given that startup prospectuses usually show a founding CEO with a much larger relative stake compared to co-founders. The company’s co-founders include Dario Amodei , Daniela Amodei , Tom Brown , Jack Clark , Jared Kaplan , Sam McCandlish and Christopher Olah . Anthropic’s risk factors take up 93 pages of its IPO filing So, is investing in Anthropic a risky bet? Anthropic certainly seems to think so. The company’s IPO prospectus contains a staggering 93 pages of risk factors. They start at page 27 and end on page 120. Some are pretty mundane. For instance, the company is concerned that slower revenue growth could potentially constrain its ability to fund frontier AI development and attract and retain top talent. Having incurred significant debt to date, it’s worried about the ability to keep servicing those obligations while still covering operating costs. But more unusual risks, like rogue AI agents, are in there too. In one section, Antrophic notes that “future models are expected to demonstrate capabilities that could provide meaningful assistance to malicious actors seeking to develop chemical, biological, or other dangerous weapons.” Related Crunchbase query: Global IPOs For Venture-Backed Companies In 2026 Related reading: Oura Hits Pause On IPO While Anthropic’s Prospectus Reveals The Cost Of Its AI Ambitions The AI IPO Wave Is The Dot-Com Bubble’s Evil Twin. Anthropic’s Delay Just Proved It. Anthropic Files Confidentially For IPO A Hard Year For Software IPOs Illustration: Dom Guzman

title: Sammy Gyamfi’s mining formalisation remarks do not warrant resignation – Centre for Mining Research and Policy
body: The Centre for Mining Research and Policy has rejected the Minority’s call for the resignation of Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) Chief Executive Officer Sammy Gyamfi over his comments on the formalisation of small-scale mining. The Centre said the call was not justified, arguing that Mr Gyamfi’s position focused on bringing eligible small-scale miners into the formal regulatory system rather than allowing illegal mining to continue. Senior Research Fellow at the Centre, Dr Ofori Kodua, said Mr Gyamfi had made it clear that eligible operators must obtain the necessary documentation, permits, certification and training to operate legally. He added that the GoldBod CEO had condemned mining activities that destroy water bodies, encroach on forest reserves or endanger communities. The Ghana National Association of Small Scale Miners, which co-organised the engagement at which the disputed remarks were made, has also defended their context. According to the association, the excerpt circulated from the event gave a misleading impression of a discussion about registering and regularising eligible operators. The Centre said the Minority’s demand for Mr Gyamfi’s resignation did not adequately consider that explanation. It also cited GoldBod’s reported performance in the small-scale gold trading sector as a reason to continue supporting the board’s reforms. According to the figures provided by GoldBod, the institution aggregated and exported 85.4 tonnes of small-scale gold valued at US$11.6 billion between January and October 20, 2026. The Centre said the figures demonstrated the economic importance of the sector and the need to strengthen official channels for gold trading. It further pointed to GoldBod’s reported support for anti-illegal-mining operations and funding for the reclamation of 50 hectares in the Tano Nimiri Forest Reserve. The board is also procuring a traceability system intended to establish the lawful origin of gold moving through the supply chain. The Centre acknowledged that the initiatives would require effective implementation and scrutiny but argued that they provided grounds for continued engagement with GoldBod’s reform agenda. It maintained that small-scale mining formalisation must be tied to compliance with licensing requirements, safer practices and regulatory supervision, while destructive mining should be subject to enforcement action. The Centre therefore called on the Minority to focus on scrutinising the implementation and results of the reforms rather than demanding Mr Gyamfi’s removal. It also cited GoldBod’s engagement with the World Gold Council on formalisation, traceability and responsible processing as evidence of efforts to align Ghana’s domestic priorities with international expertise. The Centre said Mr Gyamfi should be allowed to continue leading the reforms, while his performance and the outcomes of the initiatives remain subject to public and parliamentary scrutiny.

title: When an invasive fish is also tasty, Maryland schoolkids can help 'eat the problem'
body:
Invasive blue catfish are a problem in the Chesapeake Bay and its tributaries, preying on native seafood like the blue crab. To help keep them in check, local schoolchildren are eating catfish for lunch. Ryan Kellman/NPR hide caption
PRESTON, Md. — It's lunchtime at Preston Elementary School, on Maryland's Eastern Shore. Kids file in, get dollops of food on their segmented trays, and maybe grab a chocolate milk. But one option on today's menu is special, served alongside grapes and broccoli.
"I got a catfish sandwich!" announces Ben Rochon, a second-grader. Between mouthfuls, he tells me how it is: "It's yummy."
He's eating a catfish cake, also known by its nickname, the "catty patty." Some kids like it with ketchup or mayo. Fifth-grader Teagan Donovan goes minimal.
"I like it by itself with no toppings, because it's pretty good by itself," she says. In Teagan's case, "by itself" is literal: "I ignore the bun."
At Preston Elementary School on Maryland's Eastern Shore, catfish sandwiches are a highlight of a local food initiative. Ryan Kellman/NPR hide caption
Not everyone's into the fish cake — after all, this sunny Friday is also pizza day at Preston, and cheese slices are tough competition. But more kids have been trying catfish when it's served a couple of times a month. That's good news to Beth Brewster, who oversees food services for Caroline County Public Schools.
"It tastes great. It's great for you," she says of the fish cake.
It has another benefit: It's made with blue catfish. Since spreading to the Chesapeake Bay in recent decades, the fish has become an apex predator. It can grow to more than 100 pounds; its voracious appetite is fueling worries that it's eating too many native species.
"It tastes so good because it eats everything we love — crabs and rockfish, and all kinds of things that we love to eat," Brewster says.
Beth Brewster led her chefs in developing a catfish cake known as the "catty patty." Brewster is the supervisor of food services for Caroline County Public Schools. Ryan Kellman/NPR hide caption
State officials first asked Brewster to help tackle this problem about eight years ago.
"I was like, 'Beth, we have this invasive species. It tastes pretty good, is what we've been hearing. Can you do something about it?'" says Karen Fedor, administrator of the Farm and Food Programs at the Maryland Department of Agriculture.
Fedor describes Brewster as an "out-of-the-box thinker" who'd be up for the challenge of experimenting with recipes that appeal to kids — and also conform with federal dietary requirements. That's how Brewster's team landed on a crabcake-like dish made of blue catfish.
"It was kind of fun for my chefs to play with the recipe," she says, adding that because they have USDA approval, the cakes can be served anywhere in the U.S.
The pandemic initially slowed the effort down, Brewster says. But then she heard that Virginia was partnering with a California-based program called Bay2Tray to connect seafood with schools. Brewster got in touch with a simple message: "I have a fish for you."
Now, other school districts in both Maryland and Virginia are serving blue catfish. In Preston, a rural community near the Choptank River, kids are excited to do their part by chowing down on the catty patty.
"It kind of tastes like crabs, but in a fish way," says fifth-grader Raelynn Truitt. "It's like, really really good."
Fifth-grader Teagan Donovan, at left, doesn't go for ketchup, mustard or mayo on her catfish sandwich. Classmate Raelynn Truitt is also a fan: "It kind of tastes like crabs, but in a fish way," she says. Ryan Kellman/NPR hide caption
To Brewster, the blue catfish presents a bad news-good news proposition. It's invasive — and its white, flaky meat is tasty, in part because it's not a bottom feeder. It was first brought to rivers in Virginia in the 1970s for recreational fishing.
"Blue catfish are a large freshwater catfish native to the Midwest," says Branson Williams, manager of the Invasive Fishes Program for the Maryland Department of Natural Resources.
The idea, he says, was that people would catch the fish in a few rivers feeding into the Chesapeake. But brackish water in the bay would keep them from spreading.
"They're a freshwater fish; they should stay in those freshwater portions of the river," Williams says. But, it turns out, "they can handle some salinity."
Zach Swann sorts through the day's catch of blue catfish at a dock on the lower Potomac River. The species was first brought to rivers in Virginia in the 1970s for recreational fishing. It's spread to every tidal tributary of the Chesapeake Bay in Maryland. Ryan Kellman/NPR hide caption
You could even say those officials got catfished. Because in 2018, when Virginia and Maryland had record rainfall, the blue catfish used all that fresh water to leave those rivers and find new habitats.
"They now occur in every tidal tributary of Maryland. They occur in the Chesapeake Bay proper," Williams says.
In some spots, blue catfish make up about 70% of the fish biomass, or total weight, Williams says. Virginia officials have also been raising the alarm , saying the fish is out of control and threatening the seafood industry that relies on traditional species such as flounder.
Blue catfish reproduce quickly and eat important forage fish like menhaden. They also gobble up young crabs and fish, adding to stress on those populations.
If the Chesapeake Bay has fewer blue crabs, it would be a huge economic and cultural blow to Maryland. So the state is turning to the only predator the blue catfish really has: people.
It joins other states trying to tap humans' role as apex predators to combat invasive species. They include Kentucky and Illinois targeting the Asian carp, and Maine and Washington state's battle against invasive green crabs.
Rocky Rice likes to average at least 1,200 pounds of blue catfish on each outing on the lower Potomac River. The invasive fish is now his primary target. Ryan Kellman/NPR hide caption
On a recent sunny morning on the lower Potomac River, Rocky Rice is bringing his catch back to the dock. He's a fourth-generation Maryland waterman. But instead of crabs, his boat is full of blue catfish. He tosses them into ice tubs, sorting them by size.
"Right at a thousand," he says, as he slings a fat catfish into a crowded tub. "It's usually about a hundred pounds to a tub."
That's actually a little light. Rice wants to average about 1,200 to 1,500 pounds. He goes out three days a week, pulling catfish from hoop pots that trap them in their nets.
Rice, at right, and Swann, his first mate, sort blue catfish by size and weight. Rice says the fish doesn't bring the high prices of some other seafood, but it provides a steady income for his small operation. Ryan Kellman/NPR hide caption
He started fishing for blue catfish 14 years ago to stay busy when he wasn't crabbing.
Now that's all flipped around. The market for blue catfish doesn't bring the high prices of other seafood, but Rice says the market and steady volume of his catch are strong enough to sustain his small operation.
"What I started off as just something to do to fill in, in between other seasons, actually has turned into my primary job now."
And Rice can fish for blue catfish year-round. Because they're invasive, there is no season or size limit.
"You can catch as many of them as you want," says Maryland Department of Natural Resources' Williams. "And you don't have to throw the little ones back. Please keep them all."
Before we leave the dock, I ask Rice if he eats blue catfish himself.
"Oh yeah!" he answers. "They're good. It's a snow white, mild fillet."
The lack of a "fishy" flavor means blue catfish is good for fish tacos, Rice says. But he has his own preference: "You know, I'm from the country. So, if we can, we want to deep-fry everything, like nuggets and fried fillets."
Students at Preston Elementary select their lunches, including a catfish cake sandwich. On a recent visit, the school also offered fillets. Ryan Kellman/NPR hide caption
By early afternoon, Rice's catch will be on its way to a processor. And that's where things hit a bit of a bottleneck. Catfish is the only U.S. fish that's required to have a USDA inspection.
The rule is meant to protect the U.S. market from cheap imports. But it takes money and time for a seafood processor to have a USDA inspector on site. As a result, only four processors in Maryland are able to handle processing blue catfish, according to Williams — even with grants and other help.
Still, the fish is making its way to grocery stores and restaurants around the country; in Maryland, it's also in schools and food banks. After all, it's an affordable protein that comes from a sustainable fish. That makes it a good fit for Bay2Tray, which focuses on developing new markets for bycatch and invasive fish.
"Just yesterday, I shipped a pallet of the blue catfish to a university in Texas," says Jenn Lovewell, chief nutrition officer for Real Good Fish, the company that runs Bay2Tray.
Rice secures his boat before heading back to his fish house in Maryland. Ryan Kellman/NPR hide caption
Both Lovewell and Brewster, the school official, say millions of pounds of the fish need to be harvested, just to maintain the status quo.
"It'll never be eradicated," says Brewster.
So she urges people to seek out the fish in markets and restaurants.
Or as Lovewell puts it, "Eat the problem and save the bay."
Newly harvested blue catfish are quickly put on ice, ready to be sent to a seafood processor. Ryan Kellman/NPR hide caption

title: Exail Unveils Marins M1 Compact INS for Smaller Naval Platforms and UXVs
body: Exail introduces the Marins M1 compact INS, providing resilient FOG navigation for USVs, UUVs, and tactical craft operating in GNSS-denied environments. Exail press release Saint-Germain-en-Laye, France, October 26, 2026 – Exail unveils Marins M1, a compact inertial navigation system (INS) designed to bring very high-performance, resilient navigation to a wider range of naval platforms, including RHIBs, fast interception craft, patrol boats, uncrewed surface vessels (USVs) and uncrewed underwater vehicles (UUVs). With Marins M1, Exail extends military-grade inertial navigation to platforms where size, integration and cost are key considerations. Forces are operating a more diverse mix of major combatants, tactical craft and autonomous systems. As smaller and uncrewed platforms take on demanding missions, they need navigation that remains accurate and reliable when GNSS is degraded or unavailable. Their tighter SWaP-C (size, weight, power and cost) constraints make the integration of high-performance inertial navigation particularly demanding. Marins M1 was developed to address these requirements. Built on Exail’s sea-proven Fiber Optic Gyroscope (FOG) technology, it provides the accuracy and stability required to navigate reliably in GNSS-denied environments. It delivers accurate position, heading, roll and pitch data, with a maximum position drift of 1 nautical mile after 3 hours without any external aiding. Combining a compact architecture with a more accessible price point, Marins M1 delivers this level of inertial performance in a solution tailored to smaller platforms. “A RHIB or a USV operating without GNSS faces the same navigation challenge as a larger vessel, with far less room to address it,” said Madeleine Laguarigue de Survilliers, Naval Navigation Product Manager at Exail. “With Marins M1, we are making very high-performance FOG navigation accessible to these platforms in a system designed around their constraints.” Building on the Marins range, already trusted by more than 50 navies worldwide, Marins M1 marks a new step in the evolution of Exail’s military-grade navigation offering. It complements the company’s existing inertial navigation solutions as naval fleets evolve toward an increasingly diverse mix of crewed and uncrewed platforms.
