title: OPHK troops destroy ISWAP enclaves in Lake Chad, kill 16 terrorists
body: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Operation Hadin Kai have neutralised 16 suspected Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) fighters during coordinated air and artillery strikes on three suspected terrorist locations in the Tunbunma area of South Lake Chad, following intelligence on the presence of key terrorist leaders and fighters. According to the Joint Task Force, the operation followed sustained and relentless offensive against terrorist networks in the Lake Chad Basin. “The operation was conducted between 1 am and 2 am on 26 October 2026, using air and ground weapon systems to engage the identified locations. “Battle Damage Assessment indicates that 16 ISWAP fighters were neutralised across the targeted locations. “Among those reportedly killed were Abu Zubiru, an Arab national, and two associates, Baana Nglewa and Jindullah Sadiq, alongside other fighters. “Additionally, Abu Saleem, identified as the Wali of Tunbunma, sustained severe injuries alongside seven others. “Operation Hadin Kai reaffirms that there is no hiding place for terrorists and remains committed to restoring peace and normalcy while conducting intelligence-led operations against terrorist elements in the North East. “Members of the public are encouraged to provide timely and credible information to security agencies to support ongoing counter-terrorism operations.” The post OPHK troops destroy ISWAP enclaves in Lake Chad, kill 16 terrorists appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: South Korea Arrests Seven in First Big AI-Assisted Hacking Case
body:
Police in Seoul have arrested seven people in a hacking campaign that used generative AI to break into about 90 organizations and steal 8.2 million records.
The Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency announced the case Monday and called it the first time in South Korea that suspects in a large-scale AI-assisted hacking operation have been apprehended.
The targets included hospitals, universities, private cram schools, golf courses and subsidiaries of large conglomerates, according to police—places that hold the names, contact details and records of ordinary people. One funeral services provider lost 1.22 million records, and one report said data from the academies included information on minors.
The alleged ringleader is a 32-year-old who studied arts and physical education and has no IT background, per local reports. He told investigators he taught himself hacking through YouTube and online blogs, though police say he also did simulated attack work at a security company from 2019 to 2022.
He started with website vulnerability scanners, software that probes a site for weak spots. In late August, reports say, he added an AI coding agent—a program that writes and runs code on its own—and an autonomous penetration-testing system, a tool that automates the mock break-ins companies normally hire experts to run. Police say he then breached 60 companies in 44 days, from August 31 to October 13.
Police said an attack of this size once required a hacking group, and that AI now lets one person pull it off in a short time. Local reports name the autonomous tool as Artex. The campaign ran about 13 months, from September 2025 through this October, and the case opened in June after one victim filed a complaint.
Criminal use of AI has been building for years, mostly in reports from AI companies rather than police. WormGPT , a ChatGPT clone built without safety guardrails, was used in 2023 to write convincing phishing emails—fake messages designed to trick people into handing over money or passwords.
In August 2025, Anthropic said a single criminal used its Claude Code tool to run a vibe hacking extortion campaign against at least 17 organizations, with ransom demands from $75,000 to $500,000 in Bitcoin. In November, the company said a Chinese state-sponsored group used Claude to carry out 80% to 90% of an espionage campaign against about 30 targets, though only a small number of the intrusions succeeded.
Researchers at Cambridge, Edinburgh, and Strathclyde universities pushed back on the hype in a recent study of 97,895 cybercrime forum threads. They found AI’s main impact so far in already-automated areas such as SEO fraud, social media bots and romance scams, with little sign that coding tools helped low-skill actors beyond pre-made scripts.
The ringleader was referred to prosecutors in custody on Friday and faces charges under South Korea’s information and communications network law, plus extortion and attempted extortion. Police said they will keep investigating the six accomplices and try to identify additional victims, and 15 organizations have reported damage so far.

title: Gender Data Ghana calls for GES policy on child abuse investigations to be scrapped
body: Gender Data Ghana (GDG), a think tank focused on gender equality through research and advocacy, has called for the abolition of the Ghana Education Service (GES) policy that allows it to investigate allegations of abuse internally and transfer accused staff to other communities. According to the organisation, the policy must be brought in line with existing child protection laws. The organisation says the handling of allegations involving the headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS) and female students highlights the need for a coordinated government response and stronger safeguards to protect children in schools. “Laws supersede policies. Therefore, the current policy of the Ghana Education Service which permits self-investigation of alleged cases of abuse and grants itself powers of transfer of alleged perpetuators to other communities must be interrogated in the light of the Children’s Act, which derives its source from Article 28 of the 1992 Constitution. “Since a policy cannot override a law and the Constitution, the policy of the Ghana Education Service is redundant if not unconstitutional and must be abrogated,” Gender Data Ghana said in a statement dated October 26, 2026. The organisation argued that the GES policy must be assessed against the Children’s Act, 1998 (Act 560), as amended, and Article 28 of the 1992 Constitution, which provides for the protection of children. It maintained that the best interests of the child must guide the handling of the case, alongside respect for due process for the accused. Calls for social welfare officers in every public school Gender Data Ghana has proposed deploying professional social welfare officers in every public educational institution to strengthen the prevention and reporting of child abuse. It said the officers should operate independently of the GES to enable them to respond promptly and professionally to suspected cases. The organisation also urged the Ministry of Finance to adequately resource the Ministry of Gender, Children and Social Protection and the Domestic Violence and Victim Support Unit (DOVVSU) of the Ghana Police Service to enable them to perform their statutory responsibilities effectively. Demands stronger government response The organisation expressed concern that the Obuasi SHTS case had largely been treated as a “women’s issue” rather than a national child protection concern. It called on President John Dramani Mahama to publicly demonstrate the government’s commitment to ending child sexual exploitation and abuse. It also urged Parliament to exercise its oversight responsibilities more visibly, arguing that a unified, non-partisan response would strengthen calls for accountability and justice. While commending statements issued by the Minority Women’s Caucus, the Public Accounts Committee and the Human Rights Committee, Gender Data Ghana questioned the absence of a unified statement from the Parliamentary Women’s Caucus. Proposes comprehensive child protection policy Beyond the Obuasi SHTS case, the organisation proposed transforming the 2015 Child and Family Welfare Policy into a comprehensive Child Protection Policy. It said the proposed framework should improve coordination among ministries, departments and agencies and clearly define their respective responsibilities. Gender Data Ghana stressed that Ghana’s status as the first country to ratify the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child carries obligations that require stronger institutional safeguards and effective enforcement of existing laws.

title: ‘A senseless and selfish act’: Judge sentences couple who murdered neighbour, discarded body over BBQ smoke
body:
A Liberty Village couple has been handed stiff sentences for killing their upstairs neighbour , disposing of the neighbour’s body in the garbage and trying to cover-up the killing in the weeks that followed.
Khoa Tran, 36, has been sentenced to life in prison with no chance of parole for 16 years after being found guilty last June of the second-degree murder of 53-year-old Reeyaz Habib .
Tran’s wife, 30-year-old Quynh (Isabelle) Nguyen , has been sentenced to six years in prison after being found guilty of accessory after the fact to manslaughter and offering an indignity to a dead body.
Superior Court Justice Kenneth Campbell rejected defence lawyer Tyler Smith’s suggestion that a conditional sentence for Nguyen would be appropriate. Smith argued that because Nguyen is not a Canadian citizen, a custodial sentence over six months would mean almost immediate deportation back to Vietnam.
Campbell said in his reasons for sentence that a conditional sentence would be entirely unfit and in no way proportionate to the gravity of her offences, calling Nguyen’s actions “truly despicable.”
In June 2023, Tran and Nguyen owned a condo on the main floor of a Liberty Village complex at 26 Western Battery Way. Linh Hua, a longtime friend of the couple, was staying with them at the time.
In a townhouse unit directly above the couple’s condo lived Habib, a filmmaker, who lived alone.
During the five-week trial, court heard Tran liked to barbecue in his backyard however smoke from the barbecue travelled up into the windows of Habib.
Tran and Habib had a number of discussions about Tran’s barbecue smoke and Habib told Tran he repeatedly didn’t want the barbecue smoke coming upstairs into his unit.
Habib also told Tran he knew he was involved in some type of sexual relationship with Hua and said he was going to report to the condominium board that Tran and his wife were in violation of the condominium board rules by permitting Hua to live with them.
The Crown argued that in the early morning hours of June 6, 2023, Tran went upstairs into Habib’s unit while he slept and killed him. Many neighbours heard screams from the direction of Habib’s condominium.
In the days that followed, Habib was not seen and concerns about his whereabouts began to grow. Police entered the unit and discovered that someone had nailed blankets over the window and carefully cleaned the apartment,
Furthermore, after the killing of Habib, but before his body was discovered, a concerned neighbour saw Tran leaving Habib’s unit, locking the door and entering his own unit.
Tran was also captured on video surveillance cameras disposing of Habib’s bike and computer into a nearby above ground dumpster.
“A few days after he’d been killed, a dead, decomposing body of Mr. Habib was gratuitously found wrapped in blankets and taped up with handles in a trash compactor in an underground garbage dumpster. Handwritten notes describing the contents as trash were attached to the body. One of these notes disclosed the fingerprint of Mr. Tran,” said Campbell.
The judge noted that had the body not been discovered by the worker responsible for the trash compactor, the dead body of Habib would have been compacted as if it were trash and likely transported to the compost site likely never to be found again.
The taped handles, made with duct tape and attached to the wrapping, also revealed the combination of Habib, Tran and Nguyen’s DNA.
“In short, as the jury could have only have reasonably concluded the two accused sought to cover up the killing of Mr. Habib by Mr. Tran by disposing of his dead body in the trash,” said Campbell.
A cause of death was undetermined because the body was significantly decomposed. A forensic pathologist testifed that Habib had suffered 35 external injuries including 24 prior to his death and said some of the internal injuries were consistent with being beaten to death or, in some way, strangled.
Campbell found that there were elements of planning given that on the night of the killing Nguyen knew her husband’s plan to go upstairs and kill Habib.
The judge pointed out that the couple invited Hua to sleep in the bedroom instead of a mattress on the living room floor where she normally slept, so that Tran could work in the living room.
Hua heard loud footsteps and someone yelling help from upstairs around 3 a.m., but Nguyen told her to just ignore the noises and to go back to sleep, telling her Habib was likely filming upstairs.
“Of course, these comments were nonsense. They had discussed what to say so she would not worry,” said Campbell who pointed out that Nguyen was clearly interested in avoiding arrest for her husband’s killing and became an accessory after the fact.
The judge also pointed out that Nguyen told Hua to tell police, if they asked, that all three were sleeping together in the bedroom thus creating an alibi for Tran.
“Mr. Tran decided to kill Habib in order to end his consistent and bothersome interference with the way the accused used the barbecue and to prevent Mr. Habib from making a complaint with the Liberty Village condominium board that the accused had a third party living with them in their condo unit in contravention to the condo rules,” said Campbell.
The judge called the murder “a senseless murder of a good man” who was discarded following his death like a piece of garbage in order to hide the senseless murder.
“The killing of Mr. Habib was a senseless and selfish act by Mr. Tran that had devastating consequences for his family and friends,” said Campbell.
Campbell said after Tran callously decided to kill Habib, he further sought to distance himself from the killing by carefully cleaning the scene and cover it up by disposing of the body.
The judge was equally scathing in his criticism of Nguyen saying that not only did she help dispose the body like a piece of garbage, but over an extended period of time, she tried to help her husband avoid prosecution and the arrest for his murder of Habib.
“These were callous and selfish acts taken to shield and protect her husband, the murderer,” said Campbell.
Campbell also noted that neither accused have expressed an instant of remorse or regret saying “they both declined to speak” when given a chance at their sentencing hearing in court, which the judge said was an “absence of a mitigating factor.”
Nguyen did, in fact, address court at the sentencing hearing saying, “I just want to say I am sorry to take the court time and money. I feel sorry for the family loss.”
The couple who were out on custody until the day of the guilty verdict when their bail was revoked have spent 146 days in pre-sentence custody. After enhanced credit for pre-sentence custody, Nguyen has five years and four-and-a-half months left to serve.

title: Trump DOJ unlawfully fired Epstein prosecutor Maurene Comey, judge rules
body:
A federal judge ruled Monday that the Department of Justice's firing last year of New York federal prosecutor Maurene Comey , the daughter of former FBI Director James Comey , was unlawful.
Judge Jesse Furman, in his ruling , also granted Maurene Comey retroactive reinstatement and back pay as an assistant U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of New York from her termination on July 16, 2025, through Dec. 20, 2025, when the judge inferred she accepted another job.
The DOJ said it would appeal Furman's ruling in which the judge rejected the department's arguments that the attorney general had authority to dismiss Comey without cause. The case is in in U.S. District Court in Manhattan.
Comey's lawyers, in a statement, said, "This hard-earned victory belongs to Ms. Comey, to all civil servants, and to all fighting for the rule of law."
"As the Court correctly held, to accept the government's argument about unlimited executive power 'would be to unsettle the very equilibrium established by this Nation's constitutional system,'" the lawyers said. "This decision reaffirms our bedrock system of checks and balances: the President is not above the law."
Before her termination, Comey was involved in a series of high-profile federal prosecutions, including ones against the sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, his accomplice Ghislaine Maxwell and Sean "Diddy" Combs.
Her lawsuit against the DOJ argued that her termination violated federal law and the Constitution and stemmed from President Donald Trump 's longstanding animus toward her father, whom Trump had fired as FBI director in 2017.
James Comey is currently under federal indictment that accuses him of threatening Trump's life by posting on Instagram a photo of seashells forming the number "86 47." His attorneys are seeking to have that case tossed out.
James Comey, who denies any wrongdoing, previously had another federal indictment against him filed by the DOJ under Trump dismissed.
Maurene Comey's suit said the DOJ did not give "any explanation whatsoever for terminating Ms. Comey," and, "In truth, there is no legitimate explanation."
"Rather, Defendants fired Ms. Comey solely or substantially because her father is former FBI Director James B. Comey, or because of her perceived political affiliation and beliefs, or both," the suit said.
Furman, in his ruling for Comey, referenced that claim, but his decision was based on other grounds.
The judge rejected the DOJ's arguments that then-Attorney General Pam Bondi could remove a federal prosecutor "at will" and without cause and that current Attorney General Todd Blanche could ratify that act after the fact as he did in May as acting attorney general.
Furman also rejected the DOJ's argument that even if the Civil Service Reform Act requires removal of a prosecutor for cause, an attorney general's firing of her constituted an implicit determination that she was removed "for such cause as will promote the efficiency of the service."
"The Court need not dwell long on Defendants' second statutory argument justifying Comey's removal," Furman said, referring to that claim.
"That is because the argument borders on frivolous."
The judge noted that Comey was fired despite having had excellent performance reviews.
"Comey's supervisors and peers consistently lauded her work, describing her as a 'brilliant lawyer and a gifted supervisor,' 'the lawyer the office turns to when legal excellence is a must,' and 'an outstanding AUSA in every respect' with 'judgment, work product, and courtroom advocacy [that are] among the finest in the country,'" Furman wrote.
The DOJ admitted that Comey's termination "was not 'for cause' and was not based on her performance," Furman noted.
In addition, the judge said, the DOJ's argument that Comey's termination was lawful ignored parts of the Civil Service Reform Act, which "required that Comey be given advance written notice (subject to certain exceptions not relevant here); 'a reasonable time' to respond orally and in writing; representation; and 'a written decision and the specific reasons therefor at the earliest practicable date.'"
"Defendants concede, as they must, that Comey was not afforded these procedural protections," the judge said.
Furman also said the DOJ all but admitted that its argument that the attorney general had power to fire Comey under Article II of the U.S. Constitution — which establishes the executive branch of government — sought "to overturn nearly two centuries of Supreme Court precedent."
"This Court, however, is bound to follow the Supreme Court's precedents unless and until the Supreme Court overturns them," Furman wrote.
The DOJ, in a statement, said, "The Department disagrees with this decision and will appeal in due course."
That appeal would happen after Furman issues a final judgment in the case.
The judge reserved judgment on Comey's claim that her firing violated her First Amendment rights. Furman gave her until Nov. 9 to file arguments on why that claim should not be dismissed as moot given his order in her favor on other grounds.
The White House, when asked for comment, referred CNBC to a post by the DOJ's Rapid Response account on X , which said, "The Department disagrees with this decision, which obstructs President Trump's constitutional authority to fire individuals who wield executive power on his behalf. We intend to appeal the decision in due course.
Comey, in a note to colleagues at the U.S. Attorney's Office after she was fired, wrote, "If a career prosecutor can be fired without reason, fear may seep into the decisions of those who remain."
"Fear is the tool of a tyrant, wielded to suppress independent thought. Instead of fear, let this moment fuel the fire that already burns in the heart of this place," she wrote. "A fire of righteous indignation at abuses of power. Of commitment to seek justice for victims."

title: UPSA urges graduates to embrace entrepreneurship amid graduate unemployment
body: The University of Professional Studies, Accra (UPSA), is urging graduates to embrace entrepreneurship and job creation as Ghana’s young people continue to face competition for limited employment opportunities. The university says it is shifting from teaching students the principles of entrepreneurship to helping them turn business ideas into viable enterprises. Speaking at the second session of UPSA’s 18th Congregation, Vice-Chancellor Professor Kwaku Mensah Mawutor said the institution wanted graduates to identify opportunities, develop innovative solutions and establish businesses capable of creating jobs. “Our responsibility is not only to teach students how to write business plans but to shape them to identify opportunities, develop innovative solutions, establish viable businesses and create jobs,” he said. The approach, he explained, is intended to prepare students not only to seek employment but also to create opportunities for themselves and others. Cyber Security Authority chief urges collaboration Director-General of the Cyber Security Authority, Professor Divine Selase Agbeti, also challenged the graduates to reconsider relying solely on paid employment. He encouraged them to collaborate, develop innovative ideas and explore business opportunities that could translate into sustainable enterprises. He cited software development as one area where graduates could pool their skills to create products and seek customers. “Three, four, five, six of you can come together and decide to be software developers, develop your software, approach people and I can guarantee you that you will sell your software,” he said. His remarks highlighted collaboration and innovation as possible routes for graduates seeking to establish themselves in the economy. Best graduating student considers employment and entrepreneurship For Nancy Edem Atsu, who emerged as the overall best graduating student at the second session of UPSA’s 18th Congregation, the achievement represents years of hard work and perseverance. She recounted the difficulties she faced with some courses, saying determination and consistent effort helped her overcome the challenges. Despite her academic success, Nancy is still weighing her options as she prepares for life after university. She is interested in pursuing opportunities in public relations while also considering her passion for baking as a possible business venture. “I also love to bake when it comes to entrepreneurship, but I am also looking to secure a job in PR firms,” she said. Her plans reflect the different paths graduates may consider as they navigate the transition from university to the world of work. A proud moment for her family Nancy’s achievement was also a source of pride for her mother, Madam Bertha, who said her daughter’s academic journey involved significant challenges and sacrifices. She expressed gratitude at seeing her daughter graduate with distinction after years of supporting her education. “We want to thank God for what I have seen today, that my daughter too has this appointment,” she said. For the graduates, the congregation marks the completion of years of academic work. The next challenge is to secure employment, build viable businesses or combine both paths as they work towards their professional ambitions.

title: University of Gold Coast launches Gold Coast Society of Doctoral Fellows
body: The University of Gold Coast has launched the Gold Coast Society of Doctoral Fellows as part of efforts to strengthen research and prepare scholars to contribute to Ghana’s development. The initiative comes as the university matriculates 105 students into its inaugural PhD in Business Administration programme, with Chancellor Bishop Dr Gideon Tito-Offei urging Ghana to place greater emphasis on higher education, research and the development of national expertise. He made the call during the university’s matriculation ceremony on October 24, challenging the students to apply their education to address the country’s development needs. “We place a responsibility to every scholar in this room; let your education become useful to your nation,” he said. ‘Ghana’s gold mine is the Ghanaian mind’ In an address titled From Natural Resources to National Resourcefulness , Bishop Tito-Offei urged the country to look beyond its mineral wealth and invest in the knowledge, character and competence needed to build productive businesses and drive national development. “Ghana’s gold mine is the Ghanaian mind,” he said. His remarks emphasised the importance of developing human capital and strengthening research as part of efforts to translate Ghana’s potential into sustainable economic progress. 105 students admitted to inaugural PhD programme The university matriculated 105 students into its inaugural PhD in Business Administration programme on October 24. The three-year programme offers five specialisations: accounting and finance; human resource management; marketing and communications; leadership and governance; and strategic management. Director of the PhD programme, Dr Winnifred Coleman, said it was designed to provide students with rigorous academic training and equip them with the skills needed to contribute to national development. Some students also expressed optimism that the programme would strengthen their research, leadership and professional skills. The university expects the programme to build students’ research capacity and prepare them to apply their expertise to Ghana’s development challenges.

title: Microsoft offers voluntary exit packages to 60,000 staff
body: Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, the company said on Monday, roughly a quarter of its workforce, as the tech giant seeks to cut costs while pouring money into artificial intelligence. Staff on select teams in the United States, Canada, India and Britain at vice president level and below will be eligible, a Microsoft spokesperson said, while some groups of employees, including some working on data centers, sales and marketing, are excluded. “The Voluntary Exit Offer reflects an important part of how we’re evolving our approach to change: creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter,” Amy Coleman, an executive vice president and chief people officer, told employees in a memo. It’s the second voluntary buyout offer that Microsoft has offered employees this year. In April, the company reportedly offered around seven percent of its US workforce the option to retire early. Around 30 percent of those eligible took the voluntary retirement plan, according to CNBC. Microsoft had 223,000 employees globally at the end of June, down from 228,000 at the end of 2025, according to regulatory filings. Around 27 percent of Microsoft’s workforce is eligible for the new buyout offer. The company is expected to report quarterly earnings later this week. AFP The post Microsoft offers voluntary exit packages to 60,000 staff appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Show HN: Pandora M1, a distributed training GPU monitor box
body:
I started this project past year but never managed to finish due to many cumbersome issues tied to the mechanical part of the front panel which took me a lot of time, so this month I decided to finish it and this past weekend I was finally able to get some time to address the mechanical part. I’m very pleased with the results and there are still some things to finish but since it is starting to look great, I decided to share some photos and videos of the on-going project. This is the initial prototype so there is a unbearable amount of wiring around, however, I’m planning to hide all of this on a small case later and also design a PCB board for integrating all of this, which will help a lot with the wiring and clutter.
The main idea of this box is to provide a more tactile experience to monitoring distributed training GPUs, so I tried to make something that can fit on top of the desktop and had a more analog visualization with LED Bars and physical knobs that you can use. I iterated a lot on the design and I found this one to be quite elegant and also easy to operate.
The main information that I wanted to put on the front panel was GPU Utilisation, GPU memory, GPU Temperature and also Power Usage. The tricky problem is that you want to visualize that for multiple nodes as well, so what I did was to use a LED Matrix to show each node so that when there is an issue on a node, it will blink that as well so you can go to that node and look at the stats as well. To select the node I added one big metal head on a potentiometer so that it is easier to move around on the nodes, it goes from 0 to 63, so it supports 64 nodes max, and given that each (at maximum 8) GPU has an individual LED Bar for it, the panel supports visualisation of 512 GPUs in total.
This was the main 3D model I designed (with the help of an LLM):
I also added the VIEW knob so that you can choose between the different info from the GPUs of that particular node and also a DIM button because the LEDs can be very bright at night so I wanted to have a knob to adjust that. I also added PROFILE/EVAL/ABORT and a series of signals that I will discuss once I finalize the project, but they are basically for evaluation signal and for enabling/disabling profiling of the GPU.
The main trick here to make LEDs look nice was to keep a single 0.20mm layer of white matte PLA so that it diffuses all the LEDs for me, including the LED panel behind the logo “PANDORA” on the top. So all LEDs had a 0.20mm white layer and then the base was pure black with details in yellow an terracota.
Now, I used 10k linear potentiometers with washer -> nut -> knob like in the image below, so that they would have a strong grip on the panel, but on the back I also added some holes to keep the potentiometer in place (to avoid it twisting on the back)
This mechanical part was a nightmare, especially for the LED Bars because I had to design a rack for them to fit there and stay in place, this is how the back looks like on the design, however, you will see later that it is much uglier due to the amount of wiring and I had a lot of trouble with the space as well:
And this was how it looked in in the back:
But most of this will disappear later once a finish the PCB design. The end result after assembling all of this (which can take some fun time) was the one below:
The photos do not make justice for the LEDs, they are simply very elegant and at night they become very cool, like in the image below:
There is still a lot of things to do but the main funcional panel is working fine and it is quite handy to use. I will share more once I finish it.

title: United flight returns to airport after passenger spotted texting about hijacking aircraft
body: A United Airlines flight from Las Vegas to Newark returned to Harry Reid Airport on Saturday after a crew member spotted a passenger sending text messages saying he intended to hijack the aircraft, according to the online aviation publication Simple Flying.The report cited air traffic control (ATC) recordings shared on X/Twitter showing the passenger was unaware of the emergency return to the airport, where law enforcement was waiting for him.Audio of the suspected attempted hijacking of a flight from Vegas to Newark. A flight attendant reportedly spotted a passenger sending a text message stating that he was going to hijack the aircraft https://t.co/XynXXhcB9s— Rob V (@RobV59) October 25, 2026The pilot of United flight 1681, operated by a Boeing 737 MAX 8, can be heard in the recording saying that the cockpit went into "lockdown" following the report from the flight attendant about the threat, which Simple Flying reported occured shortly after departure.The incident comes less than a month after the October 1 attempted hijacking of flydubai flight 1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv by one of the pilots, Omani national Hamam al Hamami, who repeatedly struck the captain with an axe before being subdued by several Israeli passengers on board.On Wednesday, the Transportation Ministry notified United that it had barred entry to Israel for one of its pilots over his Iran sympathies as the country tightens its foreign crew background check measures following the flydubai incident.Regarding Saturday's incident, Simple Flying noted that the United aircraft's squawk code changed to 7700, signaling a general emergency, before it diverted. This differs from the hijack code, which is 7500.In addition, the flight's return required a longer-than-standard route to burn off excess fuel, as the MAX 8 lacks fuel-dump capability and had tanks filled for its intended flight to Newark Liberty Airport, resulting in an overweight condition for an early landing.Pilot advises ATC aircraft may need full runway length due to weight issueAs an added precaution, the pilot advised ATC that they may need the entirety of Runway 26L to land safely even after burning fuel, according to Simple Flying.According to the published FAA airport diagram, Harry Reid Airport's Runway 26L is 10,526 feet (3,208 meters) long, more than 2,000 feet (610 meters) longer than the maximum landing distance listed in the aircraft's official performance charts, even with maximum weight and wet runway conditions.It was not immediately clear why the pilot did not select parallel Runway 26R, which the diagram shows as nearly 4,000 feet (1,219 meters) longer than 26L, for added redundancy.No injuries reported in incident; FAA to investigateThe aircraft landed safely despite the weight issues, according to Fox 5 Las Vegas, with no injuries reported among its 150 passengers and six crew members.The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said in a preliminary statement that it intends to investigate the incident, and United told Fox 5 that the flight departed for Newark again on Sunday following the "potential security concern."Fox 5 reached out to the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department for comment, but it did not respond at the time of writing.Udi Etzion and Amit Avitan contributed to this report.

title: Iran War Pushes Trump's Average Gasoline Prices Above Biden's
body:
Iraq's Oil Exports via Turkey Surge to 500,000 Bpd
Norway could hold significant undiscovered…
The average price Americans have paid for gasoline during President Donald Trump's second term has now surpassed the average recorded during Joe Biden's presidency, marking a politically significant milestone just days before the November 3 midterm elections.
According to AAA data cited by Reuters , regular gasoline has averaged $3.472 per gallon since Trump returned to office in January 2025, compared with $3.471 during Biden's four-year presidency.
The difference is marginal, but it represents a striking reversal for a president who campaigned on promises to bring gasoline prices below $2 per gallon.
As of Monday, October 26, AAA reported a national average of approximately $4.29 per gallon, compared with just $3.05 a year earlier.
The increase has been driven largely by the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, which began in February and has severely disrupted global crude oil shipments, refining operations and fuel exports from the Middle East.
Gasoline prices have risen roughly 43% since the conflict began, despite the United States remaining the world's largest oil producer.
Meanwhile, diesel prices have climbed even more sharply. AAA data show diesel averaging approximately $6.35 per gallon, after reaching an all-time high of $6.53 in September.
As previously reported by Oilprice.com , shortages of refined products and the disruption of Middle Eastern energy supplies have placed extraordinary pressure on global fuel markets.
And significant relief before the midterms appears unlikely.
In his October 26 market update , Patrick De Haan, head of petroleum analysis at GasBuddy, reported that gasoline prices averaged $4.24 per gallon, down 22 cents from a month earlier but $1.24 higher than a year ago.
De Haan expects gasoline to remain above $4 per gallon and diesel above $6 through Election Day, despite government efforts to reduce prices.
While motorists have seen modest relief from September's highs, continued uncertainty surrounding the Strait of Hormuz and limited global refining capacity are keeping fuel markets under pressure.
The Trump administration has pursued several measures to ease the crisis, including efforts to increase domestic refining and secure additional diesel supplies.
However, industry executives have warned that restarting idle refineries or expanding processing capacity cannot provide immediate relief.
The latest gasoline milestone adds another challenge for the White House as Americans prepare to vote, with elevated fuel costs continuing to weigh on household budgets and broader inflation concerns.

title: Flexell Space Establishes French Subsidiary to Strengthen European Presence
body:
– Paris-based FLEXELL SPACE FRANCE SAS creates a local business hub in Europe – New entity to support ongoing contract and volume-production discussions with European customers, from technical reviews to supply planning
Paris, France – Flexell Space, a space solar solution company, announced the establishment of its French entity, FLEXELL SPACE FRANCE SAS, in Paris to strengthen support for ongoing contract and volume-production discussions with European customers.
The move comes as the company’s business discussions in Europe advance. Flexell Space is currently in talks with multiple European customers regarding collaboration agreements and volume supply of space solar cells and power solutions. Through its local presence, the company aims to accelerate customer communication and strengthen its ability to support business activities ranging from technical reviews to negotiations on supply terms.
Space solar cells require close coordination on performance, dimensions, reliability, and delivery schedules, depending on each customer’s spacecraft design and operating environment. Beyond initial product introductions, discussions involve technical documentation reviews, sample evaluations, environmental test results, and design adjustments. Progressing toward volume supply also requires alignment on production schedules and quality management processes.
Flexell Space said that as discussions with European customers move toward contracts and volume production, a local presence has become increasingly important for responding promptly to customer needs. The French entity will support these activities and serve as a link between European customers and the company’s R&D and manufacturing teams in Korea.
The company plans to deepen engagement with customers and partners across Europe, including France, Germany, Italy, and Lithuania. By gaining a closer understanding of each customer’s development schedule and technical requirements, it aims to facilitate timely decisions and follow-up actions throughout the collaboration process.
Flexell Space develops next-generation tandem solar cells and related power solutions for space applications. Its tandem architecture combines solar cells with different characteristics to deliver the performance, low weight, and cost competitiveness required for space missions.
The company is expanding beyond solar cell development into modules and arrays tailored to customer missions and satellite platforms. Its preparations for commercialization and volume production address not only product performance, but also reliability in the space environment, manufacturing process repeatability, quality management, and supply stability.
With the establishment of its French entity, Flexell Space plans to incorporate feedback from European technical discussions into product development and supply planning more quickly. It will strengthen coordination between its Korean R&D teams and European customers by communicating required specifications and evaluation criteria, while sharing development progress and validation results.
The company will also continue discussions on supply scope, development schedules, production volumes, and delivery timelines to translate ongoing negotiations into concrete business outcomes.
Flexell Space plans to operate its French entity as a hub for developing long-term relationships with European customers. Alongside supporting existing customer projects, it will explore new product applications and joint development opportunities with local space companies and research institutions.
As satellite missions and platforms become more diverse, space power solutions increasingly require development and supply arrangements tailored to specific operating conditions. Flexell Space’s strategy is to maintain close contact with customers and connect their requirements with R&D and manufacturing preparations to expand its European business.
“We are currently discussing contracts and volume supply with multiple European customers. As these discussions progress, being closer to our customers has become increasingly important in turning them into tangible results,” said Keo-san Lee, CFO of Flexell Space. “Our French entity will help accelerate technical discussions and business execution, while enabling us to respond more closely to our customers’ development and production schedules.”
“In the space industry, technical capability must be accompanied by confidence in a supplier’s ability to deliver products reliably,” Lee added. “By connecting our R&D and manufacturing capabilities in Korea with local customer support in Europe, we aim to build stronger, longer-term partnerships.”
