title: Zelensky and Estonian president discuss achieving peace in Ukraine
body:
The head of state announced this on Telegram , according to Ukrinform.
“I spoke with the newly elected President of Estonia. I congratulated Ülle Madise on taking office. Ukraine always wishes the people of Estonia nothing but success and the achievement of all their goals,” he said.
The head of state expressed gratitude for the necessary and appropriate signals: “Estonia’s support in all areas will continue. Estonia is also closely monitoring diplomatic efforts aimed at achieving peace.”
Zelensky briefed Madise on the details of the negotiations in Oslo and communications with the American side following their meeting in Russia.
“There is an agreement to hold a trilateral meeting at the team level as early as November, and it is important that the meeting not be postponed. Ukraine is ready for negotiations at any time, and our position is: the sooner the talks begin, the better. Of course, like Estonia and other partners, we always advocate for Europe’s presence in the negotiations. Europe must have a say in all formats that can yield real solutions,” Zelensky emphasized.
The parties also discussed the consequences of Russian strikes, particularly on our energy sector and railways.
“Russia is deliberately trying to destroy our locomotives, and therefore any support aimed at increasing our rolling stock will be very helpful,” the President added.
As reported by Ukrinform, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and the Speaker of the Lithuanian Seimas discussed the prospects for Ukraine’s European integration.

title: Niger APC raises 525-member campaign council, targets 2m votes for Tinubu/Bago
body: By Clare Nnabuike Niger State Governor Mohammed Umaru Bago has declared that his party, the All Progressives Congress (APC), is targeting 2 million votes to defeat the opposition parties in the 2027 presidential and governorship elections. The governor made this known on Monday at the inauguration of a 525-member State Presidential/Gubernatorial Campaign Council of the APC in Minna, where he revealed that the council is drawn from commissioners, special advisers, local government chairmen, councillors, state and national lawmakers, ministers, directors-general and coordinators. Bago described the structure as spanning party units to the state level and including political appointees, with total membership exceeding 100,000 over the years. “If everybody would bring its own votes, it would give us more than 1 million votes. But our target is beyond that. The ambition this time around is to bring out over 2 million votes, and by the grace of God we will do that,” he said. The governor urged the party to welcome returnees who had earlier defected to other parties, crediting the APC’s emergence as a coalition of parties that defeated the main opposition. He called for constructive media coverage and warned against overheating the polity or triggering insecurity, saying the campaign would highlight the federal government’s economic policies, improved revenue and job creation. Bago cited recent infrastructure and security gains, including better roads and freer movement of goods in parts of the state, as part of what the government has done and disclosed that the North Central Presidential Campaign office in Minna would be commissioned next week, with possible attendance of the President, Vice President, Senate President, Speaker or National Chairman. Minister of Information, Idris Malagi, in his remarks, praised the choice of leadership of the council and said the APC would campaign on the administration’s record of transforming the Nigerian economy over the past three and a half years. He urged the newly appointed members to prioritise the collective good of the state and party unity The chairman of the APC North Central, Hon. Mu’azu Rijau, while congratulating the council leadership, stressed that the 2027 campaign council should not underestimate opponents, saying the party aimed to re-elect Governor Bago alongside its senators, House of Representatives members and state assembly members. Director-General of the campaign council, Ahmed Ibeto, accepted the assignment on behalf of members, pledging hard work, strategic coordination, grassroots engagement, unity, discipline and compliance with electoral guidelines. He said the council would establish operational frameworks across directorates, local governments, wards and units, and would value experience while welcoming new ideas. The post Niger APC raises 525-member campaign council, targets 2m votes for Tinubu/Bago appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Somebody please stop the spam texts
body:
Summary: I complain about spam texts and consider why I’m so hesitant to just reply STOP to unsubscribe.
I moved out of Texas a few years ago. Unfortunately, it doesn’t seem like any statewide midterm candidates have heard about that. In the past month, I’ve gotten dozens of texts like this, usually multiple per day:
Some of the texts I received while working on this post
They seem to be mostly from Republicans, but I’ve gotten a little bit of everything — texts from Democrats, independents, PACs, unbiased pollsters, obviously biased pollsters, even those weird false flag texts that went around. I don’t remember signing up for anything, and certainly would never have intended to, but clearly my number got on a list somehow.
This is pretty annoying, because text is my highest-signal communication channel. Most of what’s in there is from family and friends, plus the occasional 2FA code. The little red notification bubble means a lot more on Messages than other apps — which of course is exactly why politicians, marketers, and scammers want so badly to get in there.
It’s not just the elections, either — this has been getting noticeably worse over time. This year I’ve started to get a ton of these types of messages, sometimes as many as one a day:
It turns out, despite seeming all personal and handwritten, that if you reply STOP, these messages also reveal themselves to be part of a larger campaign. (Shouldn’t this be illegal, by the way?)
So it seems like the solution is to reply STOP to all of these and eventually you won’t get as many, right?
Except I haven’t done that. I don’t want to do that. Except for that “experiment” above, I have instead chosen “Delete and Report Spam” for every single one of these texts… even though it doesn’t seem to do anything.
What’s crazy to me is that Apple has actually added a Spam folder to Messages, and there are a few things in there. But even though I’ve been reporting all this stuff as spam for months, if not longer, none of the new messages I get seem to get filtered into the Spam folder.
So again, why not just reply STOP to these messages? Why am I so averse to doing that?
After some reflection, I think I figured it out: replying with STOP feels like I’m accepting this vision of the world.
If I reply STOP, I’m basically saying, “Okay, you’re allowed to send me whatever you want, and then I have to send back STOP for you to knock it off.” And I want to fundamentally reject that framing. Mass-texting and spam campaigns shouldn’t get that right by default, and the burden shouldn’t be on me to individually opt-out of every single one of these campaigns.
So if you’re reading this and you work on iOS at Apple, please help . This feels like a great use case for all this new Apple Intelligence (similar to the AI adblock experiment I ran a while back). If I report something as Spam, maybe an option could pop up to “Filter messages like this to Spam?” or something, and then the unwanted text gets added to a list of examples. So then next time I get a text from an unknown number, the LLM reads the list of spam examples, and if the new message is similar, it goes to Spam. (That’s just off the top of my head; I’m sure there are even better ideas to combat this.)
Recently, I did find a “Delete and Stop” option, which auto-sends the STOP message for me. But it seems like “Delete and Stop” and “Delete and Report Spam” are mutually exclusive. You’d think that reporting as spam would also auto-send a STOP message, but the number of texts I’ve gotten from Don Huffines despite reporting each one suggests otherwise.
Hopefully things will calm down after the election. But for goodness’ sake, somebody please do something about this. I was going to say we fixed this problem for email, but I’m not really sure we did — these days I get tons of marketing messages despite always trying to opt out on every single website whenever I purchase something. And I get multiple spam calls a day too, even though I’m on the Do Not Call registry. So maybe we’re just doomed to be eternally pestered by whoever wants our money or our vote. Here’s hoping they don’t figure out how to get into my Slack. ⧈

title: INEC publishes preliminary voter register online after missing legal deadline
body:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has published the preliminary register of voters for the 2027 general election online, days after missing the statutory deadline for making the register available for public scrutiny.
In a statement by its spokesperson, Mohammed Haruna, INEC said the commission decided to upload the register following concerns from Nigerians and other stakeholders about its online accessibility.
PREMIUM TIMES reported that the electoral commission violated electoral law by failing to publish the voter register on its website by the stipulated time.
Section 19(1) of the Electoral Act 2026 mandates INEC to publish the voters’ register on its website, alongside a physical publication at every registration area, for seven days before the 90-day mark to the general election.
Under the law, the publication allows public scrutiny.
Since the 2027 general elections are scheduled to begin on 16 January 2027, the deadline for INEC to appoint the seven days for displaying the voters’ register was 18 October.
The election begins with the presidential and National Assembly elections on 16 January 2027, followed by the governorship and state Houses of Assembly elections on 6 February 2027, according to INEC’s timetable.
In the Monday statement by its spokesperson, INEC said it conducted the physical display of the preliminary register at registration areas nationwide from 9 to 15 October, allowing registered voters to inspect their details and submit claims and objections.
“Accordingly, and in furtherance of its commitment to transparency, accessibility and public confidence in the electoral process, the commission has decided to make available on its online platform the same Preliminary Register of Voters earlier displayed at the Registration Areas,” the commission said.
INEC said the online publication was an additional measure to widen public access to the register, while the commission continued processing claims and objections ahead of publishing the final register.
It added that the final register of voters will be published on 15 December.
The register is available on the commission’s online platform .
The preliminary register allows registered voters to check whether their names and personal details have been correctly captured ahead of an election.
It also provides an opportunity to identify omissions, errors and questionable entries before INEC finalises the list.
INEC said it remained committed to transparency, accountability and the implementation of the Electoral Act, 2026, as it prepares for the 2027 general election.
The voter register has risen to 103 million voters, up from 93 million recorded ahead of the 2023 elections. Middle-aged Nigerians dominate the voter register, ahead of young Nigerians who dominated it before the 2023 elections.
According to the breakdown provided by INEC, voters in the 35–49 age bracket number 43,265,946, representing 41.83 per cent of the 103.43 million registered voters.
They are followed by voters aged 18 to 34, who number 29,777,576, or 28.79 per cent of the register.
The commission said 22,982,900 voters, or 22.22 per cent, are aged 50 to 69 years, while those aged 70 and above make up the smallest age group, with 7,402,291 voters, or 7.16 per cent.
The age distribution shows that voters aged 35 years and above account for about 71.2 per cent of the register, while those aged 18 to 34 years constitute less than one-third of registered voters.
This differs from the 2023 voter data, where voters aged 18 to 34 dominated the register at 39.65 per cent.

title: Mahama arrives in Moscow for Third Russia-Africa Summit and bilateral talks with Putin
body: President John Mahama has arrived in Moscow, Russia, to participate in the Third Russia–Africa Summit hosted by Russian President Vladimir Putin. President Mahama and other African leaders are expected to take part in an Economic and Humanitarian Forum, with President Mahama also scheduled to hold high-level bilateral talks with President Putin. During his visit, two Russian universities, the Russian University of Transport and the Peoples’ Friendship University of Russia, will separately confer honorary doctorate degrees on President Mahama at ceremonies in Moscow. He will also grant an audience to a number of Russian businesses and state institutions.

title: Nova Scotia woman targeted in swatting incident after suspected bank scam: RCMP
body:
A Nova Scotia woman who was the victim of a “swatting” incident after she refused to follow instructions from an alleged fraudster, who claimed to be from her bank, says she’s still terrified.
Swatting involves people making false reports in order to prompt a significant police response.
“You’re looking over your shoulder all the time,” said Lynn Clark Colpitts. “My anxiety’s through the roof.”
Clark Colpitts says she received a call Friday from a woman who claimed to be from her bank’s fraud department, saying someone had applied for a credit card in her name.
She says she told the caller she hadn’t applied for a credit card. At this point, the caller told Clark Colpitts to download an app on her phone.
Clark Colpitts, who is a realtor, says she even added her company’s IT support employee to a three-way call to check whether this was a scam.
She says IT support advised her to call her own bank independently. When Clark Colpitts told the caller that she wouldn’t be downloading the app and would call her bank herself, she says the caller became angry and threatened her.
“She just went crazy and just started calling me names and I hung up and then 20 minutes later called me back and told me she had a surprise for me outside,” she said.
She says when she looked outside, she was shocked to see heavily-armed police officers in her yard and on the street.
In a Monday release, Colchester County District RCMP said they received information from Truro Police Service on Friday that a woman was being held hostage by three armed people at a residence in Lower Truro.
“RCMP and Truro Police Service officers responded immediately and located the woman safe at the home,” RCMP said.
RCMP say the incident highlights how far scammers are willing to go when their schemes are “challenged.”
Police commended the victim for taking the time to verify the information from the caller that claimed to be from her bank, and encouraged others to do the same if they suspect fraud.
RCMP say the investigation into this case is ongoing.
Clark Colpitts says she’s still receiving threatening messages that she describes as “relentless.” She wrote about her situation in a Facebook post and says she wants to warn others.
“Hang up on people that tell you that they’re from the fraud department,” she said. “Just hang up. Don’t answer phone numbers that you’re not aware of.”

title: Atwima Kwanwoma Community Bank posts GH¢44.2m profit, records prudent lending and recovery growth
body: Atwima Kwanwoma Community Bank PLC has posted a strong financial performance for the year ended December 31, 2025, with profit after tax rising to GH¢44.2 million, representing a 17.33 per cent growth. The bank attributes the growth to prudent lending, efficient loan recovery and improved service delivery. Chief Executive Officer, Samuel Bonsu Sekyere, said the profit growth is hinged on a deliberate strategy of lending to creditworthy clients and ensuring recovery. “The bank is committed to providing value for its shareholders. And so we always put in strategies on how to ensure that we make the best use of the resources that we have. And so we give loans to people who we know, and we assess, to be creditworthy and can pay back. And that is one of the surest ways that any financial institution can increase its profitability. So we give loans, and we collect it back,” he said. Loans and advances recorded the biggest leap, surging by 75.30 per cent from GH¢102.2 million in 2024 to GH¢179.2 million in 2025. Profit before tax grew from GH¢54.4 million to GH¢62.7 million, while total assets crossed the GH¢900 million mark, moving from GH¢722.8 million in 2024 to GH¢945.4 million in 2025, a 30.80 per cent growth. Deposits grew by 28.68 per cent to GH¢762 million from GH¢592.1 million, while investments increased by 24.29 per cent to GH¢621.5 million. At its 43rd Annual General Meeting of the Bank, Board Chairman, Kwame Kyei Kusi told shareholders the bank remained resilient, profitable and compliant despite a challenging economic environment. In improving the Bank’s image, they have unveiled a new logo after 43 years, reflecting its evolution from a traditional rural bank into a resilient, digital and customer-centric community bank. The rebranding is in compliance with Bank of Ghana’s microfinance reforms, which require all rural banks to convert to community banks. Atwima Kwanwoma has fully complied, now operating as Atwima Kwanwoma Community Bank PLC, and has met the revised minimum capital requirement of GH¢5 million, with its stated capital increasing to GH¢9.6 million. On service delivery, Mr. Sekyere said investments in technology have reduced waiting times and improved convenience. “We have introduced a mobile app as well as a USSD platform, *223#, that enables customers to do banking without stepping into the banking hall. And this is a way of decongesting the banking hall… Essentially, we are giving customers a 24/7 service, unlike the 8-hour service that we were doing before,” he explained. The Board has proposed a dividend of GH¢0.20 per share, amounting to GH¢5.31 million, subject to shareholder approval. The bank also reported spending over GH¢296,000 on Corporate Social Responsibility initiatives in health, education, agriculture and security, and was adjudged Innovative Rural Bank of the Year and Outstanding Rural Bank of the Year at separate industry awards in 2026. The Board Chairman said the bank is well-positioned to leverage macroeconomic stability to grow profitably and remain a top community bank in the country.

title: N.S. government announces funding to grow boatbuilding industry
body:
The Nova Scotia government says it is investing over $350,000 to help boatbuilders and boat repair businesses in the province expand into new markets.
The province says the funding from its Community Economic Development Fund is going to the Nova Scotia Boatbuilders Association.
It says the association will use the money to promote local companies at industry trade shows and missions, in trade publications and through online communications and strategic partnerships.
The Nova Scotia Boatbuilders Association was established in 1998 to diversify the industry beyond the domestic fishing boat market.
The province says the investment will help local boatbuilders deliver on national defence priorities and compete internationally for naval contracts.
The executive director of the Nova Scotia Boatbuilders Association says the boatbuilding industry maintains small vessels for several of the province’s key industries, including fisheries and defence.
“This investment helps to ensure the ongoing health of our industry, and the rural communities where much of the work takes place, as we navigate an unusually complex trade environment,” said a statement from executive director Jan Fullerton.

title: GCB Bank partners with UnionPay to launch Ghana’s first RMB debit and prepaid cards
body: GCB Bank PLC has partnered with UnionPay International to introduce Ghana’s first Renminbi (RMB) debit and prepaid cards, allowing customers to make payments directly in the Chinese currency without intermediate currency conversions. The agreement, formalised at UnionPay International’s headquarters in Shanghai, China, was witnessed by representatives of the Bank of Ghana. According to the two institutions, the arrangement marks UnionPay’s first RMB payment card designed to use the Chinese currency directly for clearing and settlement. The cards will enable Ghanaian businesses and travellers to make point-of-sale payments, withdraw cash from automated teller machines (ATMs) and conduct online transactions in China. The initiative comes amid increasing trade and travel between Ghana and China, with bilateral trade reaching US$14.1 billion in 2025, representing a 19.3 per cent increase over the previous year. China remains Ghana’s largest trading partner, with many Ghanaian businesses relying on Chinese markets for goods, machinery and raw materials. Speaking at the launch, the Managing Director of GCB Bank PLC, Farihan Alhassan, said the partnership would help address payment challenges faced by Ghanaian businesses operating in China. “For Ghanaian businesses trading with China, making payments should be a straightforward part of doing business. Our partnership with UnionPay International will enable customers to pay directly in RMB, reducing the need for intermediate currency conversions and making it easier to manage payments during procurement and business trips. “This reflects GCB’s commitment to supporting the ambitions of Ghanaian businesses, connecting them to global opportunities and strengthening trade ties between Ghana and China,” he stated. The General Manager of UnionPay International’s Africa Branch, Feng Chen, said the partnership would improve payment connectivity between Ghana and China while providing additional cross-border payment options. The development also comes amid growing travel between the two countries. According to the Ghana Tourism Authority’s 2025 Tourism Report, Ghana recorded 1.307 million international visitors, with business travel accounting for 31 per cent of visits. China ranked as Ghana’s sixth-largest source market, contributing nearly 20,000 arrivals annually. Meanwhile, more than 9,000 Ghanaians travelled to China in 2023 for business, trade, education and official engagements, while approximately 4,600 Ghanaian students were enrolled in Chinese institutions. The introduction of the cards is expected to provide an additional payment option for Ghanaian traders who frequently travel to China for procurement, accommodation, transport and other business-related expenses. GCB Bank, established in 1953 and listed on the Ghana Stock Exchange, operates more than 183 branches and 340 ATMs nationwide. UnionPay International operates a payment acceptance network spanning 183 countries and regions, with cards issued locally in more than 86 countries and regions through partnerships with over 2,600 institutions worldwide.

title: CBRN sensors from Teledyne FLIR Defense to equip Bulgarian tanks
body:
BOSTON. Teledyne FLIR Defense announced that it will fulfill a $48 million contract by the U.S. Army to deliver nuclear, biological, and chemical reconnaissance vehicle (NBCRV) sensor suite upgrades (SSU) to Bulgaria to equip its new fleet of Stryker vehicles.
The contract -- awarded by the U.S. Army Contracting Command at Aberdeen Proving Ground (Maryland) as part of a Foreign Military Sales (FMS) agreement to support Bulgarian military modernization -- is aimed at increasing interoperability with NATO forces. Bulgaria is acquiring nearly 200 U.S.-made Stryker armored vehicles to replace its Soviet-era tactical vehicle fleet; it plans to outfit 10 of the Strykers with NBCRV SSU systems.
Teledyne FLIR Defense is the lead integrator in modernizing the Army’s NBCRV system with improved and autonomous chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear (CBRN) sensors. Company officials say that the system enables standoff detection of CBRN threats, which reduces risk to troops by providing decision-quality data to commanders and optimizing freedom of maneuvers during combat operations.

title: British Type 31 Frigate Variant Offered To The U.S. Navy
body: British defense contractor Babcock has confirmed that it is putting itself forward for the U.S. Navy’s future frigate program , with its Arrowhead 140 general-purpose frigate, the design behind the Royal Navy’s Type 31 class , expected to form the basis of its proposal. The move adds another foreign-designed warship to Washington’s search for a relatively mature frigate that can be built quickly and in significant numbers. Babcock has held preliminary discussions with Pentagon officials and is expected to submit an expression of interest before the end of October, according to recent reporting by The Telegraph and Navy Lookout . The proposal is understood to potentially involve Huntington Ingalls Industries (HII), America’s largest military shipbuilder, with the two companies exploring an arrangement that could see the Arrowhead 140 built in the United States under license. An artist’s impression of the U.K. Royal Navy Type 31 general-purpose frigate. Royal Navy “Of course we’re interested. We have a world-class frigate, close links to the U.S. and U.S. industry. It would be insane for us not to respond,” Sir Nick Hine, head of Babcock’s marine business and a former Second Sea Lord, told The Telegraph . The initiative comes as the U.S. Navy seeks to accelerate the acquisition of smaller surface combatants after the troubled Constellation class frigate program was axed . Japan’s upgraded Mogami class, South Korea’s Chungnam class, and Turkey’s Istanbul class have also been reported as candidates for the Navy’s international frigate effort. You can read more about all three designs here . The Japan Maritime Self-Defense Force’s (JMSDF) first-in-class JS Mogami . JMSDF The South Korean Navy’s ROKS Chungnam seen during sea trials before its delivery in 2024. HD Hyundai Heavy Industries The future TCG Izmir from Turkey’s Istanbul class. Anadolu Shipyard Fincantieri Marine Group, which had developed the cancelled Constellation class frigate for the U.S. Navy, also says it sees a possible new opportunity in the service’s latest frigate plans. Meanwhile, German defense contractor Rheinmetall, a newcomer to the surface combatant market, recently unveiled its GMF 140 frigate , which it has said it plans to offer “initially as part of a procurement project in North America” before pursuing opportunities with other allied navies. For Babcock, the opportunity would be a major expansion of its relationship with the U.S. defense industry. If successful, the company would likely provide the design, engineering expertise, and potentially the intellectual property needed for American shipyards to manufacture the frigates. This would mirror the process for the Polish Navy’s Project 106 Miecznik (Swordfish) class, which is building three new multirole frigates in Poland, rather than using the company’s own facilities in Britain. The future Polish Navy frigate Wicher under construction in Gdynia, Poland. Photo by Mateusz Wlodarczyk/NurPhoto The Navy’s assessment of potential options is due by November 12. No contract has been awarded, and the details of any Babcock-HII proposal remain unconfirmed. The Arrowhead 140 is the foundation of the Royal Navy’s five-ship Type 31 program, which is being built at Babcock’s Rosyth shipyard in Scotland. The design is derived from the Danish Iver Huitfeldt class frigate. As well as Poland , the warship has also been selected for Indonesia. The Arrowhead 140 has a baseline length of approximately 455 feet, a beam of 65 feet, and a displacement of around 5,700 tonnes, although national variants may be considerably heavier. The vessel uses a conventional combined diesel-and-diesel (CODAD) propulsion system and can achieve speeds exceeding 28 knots. Its design emphasises long endurance, with a baseline endurance of approximately one to two months. The AH140 incorporates a flight deck and hangar for naval helicopter operations, accommodation for embarked personnel, boat-handling facilities, and adaptable mission spaces. Its modular architecture allows customers to integrate different sensors, combat management systems, electronic warfare equipment, and weapons according to national requirements. Taking the Polish Navy’s Project 106 class as an example of an Arrowhead 140 iteration, this is a notably heavily armed adaptation, featuring a 76mm Leonardo Strales main gun, a 32-cell Mk 41 vertical launch system for surface-to-air missiles, eight Naval Strike Missiles for anti-ship strike, and lightweight torpedo launchers. The Polish variant is reported to have a maximum displacement of approximately 7,700 tonnes. Wicher , the first of the Polish Navy’s Project 106 Miecznik (Swordfish) class. PGZ SW The Type 31 is a general-purpose warship capable of undertaking maritime security, escort, and surface warfare missions. Its relatively large hull offers considerable internal volume for weapons, sensors, aviation facilities, and future upgrades. That could make it attractive to a U.S. Navy looking for a ship able to protect convoys, operate independently, and supplement its larger destroyers. A frigate with a significantly lower operating cost than an Arleigh Burke class destroyer could still take on a range of missions, freeing more capable combatants for broad area air and missile air defense, sustained strike operations, and other more demanding tasks. The Arleigh Burke class destroyer USS James E. Williams underway. U.S. Navy courtesy photo The USS James E. Williams . USN The Arrowhead 140’s size could also provide flexibility in accommodating American weapons and combat systems. However, a U.S. version would require a defined configuration, and there is no publicly established weapons fit for a potential American variant. At the same time, the Royal Navy’s Type 31 frigate has not yet entered operational service, and its baseline configuration is not optimized for every mission the U.S. Navy may require. In particular, the integration of the sonar and other systems needed for sustained anti-submarine warfare would be a significant undertaking. The Navy will also have to wrestle with how much of the existing design can be retained while meeting its own requirements. One of the major lessons from the Constellation program was that extensive modifications to an existing foreign design can create huge cost and schedule risks. With so little left of the original design after it was adapted to Navy specifications, this eventually doomed the program. A rendering of a now-cancelled Constellation class frigate. U.S. Navy For Babcock, it will be essential to keep the Arrowhead 140 as close as possible to its established configuration, while integrating essential American equipment, to keep the proposal competitive. Babcock does not operate a shipyard in the United States, making an American industrial partner central to its approach. HII, which operates major shipbuilding facilities at Newport News and Ingalls, would offer substantial experience constructing warships for the U.S. Navy. Babcock and HII already have an established relationship in the submarine sector, including work supporting the Virginia class attack submarine program. Babcock’s facilities in Rosyth and Bristol manufacture tactical missile-tube assemblies for General Dynamics Electric Boat, supporting the Common Missile Compartment used by the U.S. Navy’s Columbia class and the Royal Navy’s Dreadnought class ballistic missile submarines. HII has also expanded its relationship with Babcock through work involving Virginia class submarine components. An artist’s conception of one of the Royal Navy’s future Dreadnought class submarines. BAE Systems Those existing industrial relationships could provide a foundation for a surface-ship partnership. Under a potential arrangement, Babcock could transfer the necessary design rights and provide technical support while an American yard undertakes construction. Such an arrangement would fit the Trump administration’s stated goal of using allied expertise to accelerate warship production while rebuilding domestic shipbuilding capacity. It would also allow Babcock to pursue a potentially significant U.S. order without requiring Rosyth to absorb a large new construction program alongside its Royal Navy commitments. The prospect of HII supporting more than one design raises questions about production capacity, program priorities, and how the company would manage competing demands on its shipyards. More generally, the administration’s interest in foreign frigates reflects growing concern about the time and expense involved in developing new American warships. The Constellation class program was supposed to provide a modern replacement for the Navy’s retired Oliver Hazard Perry class frigates. Based on the European FREMM design, it underwent extensive modifications for American service before suffering serious schedule and cost problems. The Navy subsequently abandoned the program. Oliver Hazard Perry class USS Carr is seen in 2006. The last of the type was retired from U.S. service in 2015. U.S. Navy The service is now pursuing FF(X) , a patrol frigate intended to be easier to build and field. Its initial configuration, however, is not expected to include a vertical launch system, limiting its ability to provide some of the capabilities associated with a more heavily armed multi-mission combatant. A rendering of the FF(X) frigate. U.S. Navy HII is building the FF(X) frigate, based on the Coast Guard’s Legend class National Security Cutter . It is somewhat telling that they would partner with Babcock on the foreign frigate offering considering they already have the FF(X) contract. The Coast Guard’s Legend class cutter USCGC Hamilton . U.S. Coast Guard The international frigate effort is intended to examine whether a ship based on an existing allied design could provide a different balance of capability, cost, and delivery speed. An August presidential memorandum opened a route for the Navy to consider allied designs and, under limited circumstances, overseas construction through a national security waiver. The approach has been compared with a model in which an initial small number of ships could be constructed abroad before production moves to U.S. yards. The reported framework limits overseas construction to no more than two ships and ties it to investment in American shipbuilding. Any eventual Babcock proposal would therefore need to demonstrate how the design could be transferred and produced domestically at the required pace. That could be a big challenge. Babcock’s own Type 31 production line is already committed to the five ships ordered by the Royal Navy, while setting up an American production line would require workforce training, supply-chain development, and the transfer of manufacturing knowledge. HMS Bulldog has officially entered build. The ceremonial Steel Cut for our fourth Type 31 frigate marks another major step forward for our programme, joining a production line that is gathering real speed. More to come from Rosyth later this evening. https://t.co/ZoTM5OWNVv pic.twitter.com/35Y3qBpMJg — Babcock International (@Babcockplc) February 24, 2026 The Navy will also need to establish whether a foreign design can meet its minimum operational requirements without undergoing the kind of extensive redesign that dogged the Constellation program. Babcock enters a field that already includes several established frigate designs from Japan, South Korea, and Turkey — and potentially more. Each offers a different combination of design maturity, combat systems, production capacity, and potential industrial arrangements. The Mogami and Chungnam programs have operational ships in service, while the Arrowhead 140 has been selected for multiple export programs but is yet to enter operational service. Babcock’s selling point is likely to be the Arrowhead 140’s size, adaptability, and established design pedigree, combined with the prospect of American production through HII. With the Arrowhead 140 adopted by multiple navies, this brings potential cost savings through economies of scale, shared design evolution, and collaborative upgrades across the fleet. A wider international user base also brings the possibility of overseas industrial partnerships, including training and logistical support around the globe. At the same time, U.S. Navy selection would represent a major endorsement of the platform and would further strengthen its position in other export markets. For now, Babcock’s confirmation that it intends to pursue the opportunity adds another contender to the Navy’s search for a new frigate. Whether the Arrowhead 140 advances beyond the initial expression of interest will depend on how its capabilities and production prospects compare with the other candidates. And critically, Babcock and its U.S. partners will need to convince the Pentagon that they deliver a ship that meets the Navy’s requirements without repeating the delays and redesign challenges of the Constellation program. Contact the author: thomas@thewarzone.com The post British Type 31 Frigate Variant Offered To The U.S. Navy appeared first on TWZ .

title: Modular phased-array platform combining beamforming, X-band conversion, and RF digitization unveiled by Analog Devices
body:
WILMINGTON, Massachusetts. Analog Devices introduced the ADSY2301, a modular 8 GHz to 11 GHz half-duplex phased-array platform combining analog beamforming, X-band frequency conversion, and RF digitization for transmit and receive applications, according to the company’s product announcement.
The platform uses a modular tile architecture built around the ADAR1000 beamformer integrated circuit and ADTR1101 transmit/receive module. A separate up/down-converter card uses ADMV1320 and ADMV1420 tuner ICs to convert X-band signals into an intermediate-frequency range suitable for sampling, while the digitizer backend uses the ADRV9009-ZU11EG RF system-on-module based on the ADRV9009 transceiver and Xilinx Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC.
The 16-element transmit tile provides 2 W to 4 W of saturated power per element and 38 dB of single-channel large-signal gain, while the receive tile provides 23 dB of gain with a 4 dB cascaded noise figure. The platform also supports 360-degree phase control with 2.8-degree resolution and 180-nanosecond transmit/receive switching.

title: Trump looks beyond 2028 as Board of Peace recruits former Biden aide to build bipartisan support
body: The Board of Peace is continuing its efforts to build bipartisan consensus in Congress around both the board itself and US President Donald Trump's Gaza peace plan, seeking support from Republicans and Democrats alike.As part of these efforts, Shelley Greenspan, who served as former president Joe Biden's liaison to the Jewish community, has been appointed to a senior position at the Board of Peace, where she will be responsible for congressional outreach, particularly to Democratic lawmakers. Greenspan, who will start her new role next week, will work under Josh Gruenbaum and Aryeh Lightstone, who are senior advisers to the Board of Peace.Greenspan, the granddaughter of Holocaust survivors, previously served on Hillary Clinton's presidential campaign research team, worked at the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC), and held management and policy positions at technology companies, including Amazon. She also served at the State Department and on the National Security Council (NSC), focusing on global partnerships. In 2022, she was appointed as Biden's liaison to the Jewish community.In a statement shared with The Jerusalem Post, Greenspan said she was honored to join the Board of Peace at such a crucial time.“At the State Department, I worked to advance the president's vision for peace and prosperity in the Middle East and saw how the president's 20-Point Plan can tangibly deliver for the peoples of Gaza and Israel. I look forward to continuing that work with the board,” she said.Trump administration seeks lasting bipartisan support for Gaza planThe Trump administration's strategic decision is to ensure that the 20-point plan for Gaza and the Board of Peace do not become one-off initiatives that can operate only under Trump or another Republican president. Instead, the administration aims to establish them as a bipartisan consensus that would encourage a future Democratic president, if one is elected in 2028, to continue implementing the Gaza plan and supporting the board's work.The move may reflect lessons learned from what happened to the Abraham Accords. In 2020, during his first term, Trump announced normalization agreements between Israel and the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Morocco, and Sudan. The goal was to secure additional agreements, including between Israel and Indonesia and Saudi Arabia.However, after Biden took office in January 2021, his administration refrained from advancing new normalization agreements. Some critics have argued that it was even reluctant to use the term “Abraham Accords” because it did not want to give Trump credit for the agreements. It was not until June 2023 that then-secretary of state Antony Blinken appointed Dan Shapiro, a former US ambassador to Israel, as a senior adviser for regional integration and special envoy for expanding the Abraham Accords at the State Department.Prominent Democrats voice support for Trump's Gaza peace planIn recent months, several prominent Democrats, including former US ambassador to Israel Jack Lew, former Biden administration senior adviser Brett McGurk, and Hillary Clinton, have expressed support for Trump's Gaza peace plan.“The 20-point plan is not the one many of us would have drafted, but it remains the only framework backed by sufficient leverage, political engagement, and potential resources to move the parties towards implementation,” Clinton wrote several months ago in an article for the Financial Times.“Shelley brings deep experience working across the aisle, having earned the trust of Democrats and Republicans alike through her service at the White House, National Security Council, and State Department in Democratic and Republican administrations,” the Board of Peace said in a statement to the Post.“Sustained, bipartisan support from Congress is essential to the work ahead, and Shelley is uniquely capable of leading this effort,” the statement added.

title: AI is changing Kubernetes; is your platform ready for 2027?
body: AI workloads, including those using agentic AI , will only add to and change the questions Kubernetes teams have to answer. It’s no longer merely enough to ask if the pods are running. Or how long it takes a model to produce its first token. Or what happens when inference traffic spikes and no additional GPU capacity is available. Increasingly, questions like those are becoming platform questions that sit next to the already familiar work of upgrades, recovery, and security. That’s why The New Stack has just published Kubernetes in 2027: Building Platforms for AI, Autonomy, and Scale , a new ebook by Chris J. Preimesberger, in partnership with HPE. This ebook starts with the work before launch — before the launch. We ask teams to stress-test model-serving systems under realistic loads, rehearse failures, and measure more than GPU utilization. It also takes a clear-eyed look at agents. Giving an agent access to a cluster is a consequential decision, even if its task sounds routine. The guide calls for identifiable owners, narrow permissions, approval gates, and audit trails that connect tool calls to the task that prompted them. It asks teams to evaluate AI output quality. A fast answer offers little comfort when it’s wrong. And the ebook doesn’t treat AI as a reason to forget the rest of the platform. The checkpoints cover policy across clusters, visibility into services outside Kubernetes, upgrade and restoration drills, operational ownership, and developer self-service. The checklist gets specific about the work that can fall between teams. Can you see which clusters follow a shared access and network baseline? (And who approved the exceptions?) Also: When an application slows, can you look beyond pod metrics to the database, virtual machine, network, or external service it depends on? Before the next upgrade, have you checked for removed APIs and practiced restoring both cluster state and application data? Then there’s the work after deployment: Who renews an ingress certificate? Who signs off on a capacity change? If a developer requests an environment through a service catalog, does it come with an owner, a review date, and a way to see what it costs? They’re practical prompts for conversations among platform teams, application teams, security teams, and business teams. Download the ebook now before you start the conversation . title: ADC denies owing workers salaries, challenges APC to provide evidence
body:
The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has denied owing its workers salaries, challenging the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council to provide evidence supporting the claim.
The denial followed a statement by the APC campaign council spokesperson, Dele Alake, alleging that the ADC leadership had failed to pay its employees for more than 12 months.
In a statement on Monday, the ADC National Publicity Secretary, Bolaji Abdullahi, described the allegation as false and accused the ruling party of attempting to divert attention from the Tinubu administration’s record.
“The ADC categorically rejects this allegation as an irresponsible falsehood, deliberately concocted to mislead Nigerians and distract attention from the monumental failures of the Tinubu administration,” he said.
“If the APC has any credible evidence to support its claims, it should produce it rather than continue to insult Nigerians with fabricated stories masquerading as press statements.”
Mr Abdullahi said the APC should address the rising cost of living, unemployment and insecurity rather than make allegations about the opposition party’s internal affairs.
He accused the ruling party of preparing to campaign for the 2027 elections by attacking its opponents instead of presenting its achievements in government.
“It is becoming increasingly clear that the APC has decided to run its 2027 campaign on allegations against the opposition rather than achievements of its own,” he said.
“That is what happens when a government has spent years making promises it cannot keep and excuses it cannot defend.”
The ADC spokesperson urged Mr Alake and other APC campaign officials to explain the government’s economic policies and their effects on Nigerians.
He said the ADC would keep focusing on the cost of living ahead of the elections.
“This election is about one issue only: the cost of living that the Tinubu administration has pushed beyond the reach of the majority of Nigerians. The ADC will stay focused on this issue. We will not be distracted,” he said.
In its earlier statement, the APC Presidential Campaign Council accused the ADC National Working Committee, led by David Mark and Rauf Aregbesola, of failing to pay party employees for more than 12 months.
The council also raised allegations concerning the employment records of former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and Mr Aregbesola, a former governor of Osun State.
The allegations have not been independently established.
The ADC did not provide payroll records or other documentary evidence in its statement to substantiate its denial.

title: NAIMOS seizes 22 Chanfang machines in Eshaem operation targeting galamsey supply networks
body: The National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) has signalled a major expansion of its enforcement strategy against illegal mining, with increased attention now being directed at persons and businesses that manufacture, fabricate, transport, store, supply or otherwise facilitate access to equipment used for illegal mining. The new approach became evident during a major NAIMOS operation at Eshaem in the Nzema East Municipality of the Western Region, where enforcement personnel disrupted several illegal mining sites stretching from the Eshaem road towards the Ankobra River. During the operation, the Task Force destroyed 28 chanfang machines, 19 water pumps, and five makeshift structures used to support illegal mining. The Task Force identified several illegal mining locations along the operational corridor, including two major sites near the Ankobra River. The team observed evidence of recent excavator activity at one site, while three excavators were found at another. A monitor was recovered from one machine, while critical components had already been removed from the others. The operation took a significant turn during the Task Force’s return from the area, when personnel encountered a Hyundai truck carrying 22 brand-new Chanfang machines being offloaded into a store. The truck and the 22 machines were immediately seized. An adjoining store was also found to contain a substantial quantity of equipment and spare parts associated with illegal mining operations. The premises were subsequently secured to enable further investigations into the source, ownership, and intended destination of the equipment. This development represents an important evolution in NAIMOS’ enforcement strategy. NAIMOS has observed that destroying chanfang machines, pumps, and other equipment at illegal mining sites alone will not provide a lasting solution if operators can replace the machinery within days and return to the rivers. The Secretariat is therefore extending enforcement beyond the mining sites to the supply and logistics networks that enable illegal mining. Under this approach, increased attention will be directed at chanfang fabricators, equipment manufacturers and assemblers, dealers and suppliers, transporters, warehouses and stores, as well as persons who knowingly rent excavators, pumps, and other machinery for illegal mining operations. NAIMOS will also intensify intelligence-gathering to identify where illegal mining equipment is fabricated, assembled, stored and distributed. The objective is to deny illegal miners the ability to rapidly replace equipment destroyed during enforcement operations, thereby weakening the logistical system that sustains repeated illegal mining along Ghana’s rivers, farms and other environmentally sensitive areas. The Eshaem operation is part of Operation WATER SHIELD, which aims to protect the Ankobra River, which remains under pressure from illegal mining in parts of the Western Region. NAIMOS will sustain operations along the river corridor while targeting the networks that supply the machinery, fuel, transport and other logistics required for illegal mining. The Secretariat serves notice that persons who knowingly manufacture, fabricate, transport, store, supply, or rent equipment for illegal mining should no longer consider themselves removed from enforcement merely because they are not physically operating at a mining site. The fight against illegal mining will no longer end at the riverbank. It will extend to the workshops where illegal mining equipment is fabricated, the stores where it is kept, the vehicles used to transport it and the networks that finance and supply it. NAIMOS will continue to work with relevant security and regulatory institutions to investigate the ownership and supply chains of equipment intercepted during operations and take appropriate action where links to illegal mining are established. The message is clear: those who provide the machines and infrastructure that enable the destruction of Ghana’s rivers are part of the problem, and the enforcement net is widening to reach them.

title: Death toll from Tonj North violence rises to 72
body: The death toll from a coordinated attack in Warrap State has risen to 72, with 38 people wounded, the state government said on Monday. The attack targeted Akop Payam in Tonj North County, with the government blaming armed groups from Mayom County in neighbouring Unity State and sections of Alabek Payam. The dead included two women, according to the Warrap State Caretaker Minister of Information. Fifty of those killed were from the attackers’ side, while 22 were from the victims’ side, Caretaker Information Minister William Wol Mayom told Radio Tamazuj. The state minister said that an unspecified number of cattle had been raided from Majak-kou cattle camp. The two main markets of Athieng-puol and Rual-malith, along with several households in villages across Akop Payam, were deliberately burned, he added. Unity State officials could not immediately be reached for comment. The state minister expressed concern over what he described as a growing pattern of retaliatory attacks involving armed groups from Mayom County and communities in Alabek and Akop payams. the official singled out the Pan-Arik and Pan-Mawien sub-clans, saying the violence had also affected other sections of Alabek and Majak payams. He linked the latest attack to a cycle of revenge killings, citing a targeted attack on October 24 in Mading-Juer that killed eight civilians, including a girl. Warrap State Governor Angelo Ngot Mayar and the state government extended condolences to the bereaved families and wished those injured a speedy recovery. Security response Minister Mayom said the government had instructed security agencies to deploy forces swiftly to Akop Payam and transfer the wounded for medical treatment. He added that the governments of Warrap and Unity states were establishing communication channels to recover the stolen cattle, identify those responsible and bring them to justice. The state minister also appealed to humanitarian partners and other well-wishers to assist people affected by the attack, saying vulnerable women, children and older people had been left without food, medicine and shelter. People living elsewhere who have relatives in the affected areas have expressed growing concern for their loved ones’ safety amid the escalating violence. “I have called my family to check whether they are safe amid this conflict. I am very concerned about what is happening in my home area,” a man living in Kuajok who has relatives in Tonj North told Radio Tamazuj. The latest attack comes amid recurring intercommunal violence in Warrap State, where clashes, cattle raids and retaliatory killings have caused repeated casualties in recent months. title: Nova Scotia flu cases rise as vaccination campaign gets underway
body:
Flu season is off to an early start in Nova Scotia with more cases reported so far this fall than last year, according to provincial data.
Across the country, infectious disease specialists say Canada’s flu season has started about seven weeks earlier than usual this year.
Nova Scotia’s Respiratory Watch dashboard indicates lower levels of COVID-19 than at this time last year, with RSV cases on par with previous years.
But more influenza cases have been reported — mostly in the Halifax Regional Municipality, Eastern Shore, and West Hants regions.
“We’re well within normal of the amount of influenza that we expect to to see at this time of year. But we also have to remember that flu every year creates a significant impact,” said Chief Medical Officer of Health Dr. Robert Strang, who received his flu shot Monday during a media availability.
“This is a reminder: now is the perfect time to book your vaccine.”
The province announced Oct. 8 that people could begin scheduling influenza and COVID-19 vaccination appointments through its vaccination portal .
If there aren’t any vaccine appointments available, pharmacists say there’s no need to worry.
“Just keep checking the booking system every few days if need be, there will always be more appointments available,” said Nicolas DesAulniers, owner and pharmacist at Mosaic Pharmacy.
The province’s department of health says in a statement that more than 800,000 vaccine doses will be sent to providers to support the campaign this year.
“As of (Monday) morning, there have been over 150,000 appointments booked for COVID-19 and influenza vaccines, not including appointments booked directly with primary care providers,” the statement added.
Historically, Atlantic Canada has had high immunization rates and pharmacists say it’s important to keep that up.
“It’s not a time to be complacent about that. It’s a time to continue with the success we’re achieving,” said DesAulniers.

title: 15-year-old arrested in connection with shooting near FAMU
body:
The shooting left 12 injured, including six children.
A 15-year-old was arrested in connection with a shooting near Florida A & M University over the weekend, which left 12 injured, including six children, the Tallahassee Police Department announced on Monday morning. Eleven of those who were injured had gunshot wounds.
Authorities said they made the arrest on Sunday.
The individual arrested, Anthony Rivers III, will face 11 counts of attempted second-degree murder and possession of a firearm by a delinquent, police said.
State attorney Jack Campbell said Monday he would be prosecuted as an adult.
According to police, "preliminary findings indicate a physical altercation occurred" before the shooting on Saturday night near Perry and Manatee streets just outside Florida A & M University's Bragg Memorial Stadium.
"Detectives believe the incident stemmed from a dispute between individuals known to one another. At this stage of the investigation, none of the victims appear to have been the intended targets," according to police.
Police added that the investigation remains "open and active" and said more arrests are possible.
"What should have been a weekend of celebration in our community instead became a night of fear and violence for the victims and their families,” Tallahassee Chief of Police Lawrence Revell said in a statement.
The statement continued, "While this arrest marks a significant step forward, our work is far from over. We remain committed to holding those responsible accountable and getting answers for every family impacted by this tragedy."
Revell spoke with reporters during a late-night press conference after the shooting.
"We know that our youngest victim is 11 years old. At least three of our victims have sustained serious injuries and one of those is in critical condition. Eight of those are reported to be in stable condition," he said.
In a Sunday morning update, the Tallahassee Police Department said that six of the victims remain hospitalized, with one in critical condition. Five other victims have been released from the hospital, police said.
The person who was injured but not from a gunshot was "a grandmother of one of the victims," the chief said, adding that she "injured herself fleeing from the scene."
FAMU President Marva B. Johnson released a video statement Sunday afternoon, saying that while the shooting did not occur on her campus, the school is offering care and support to "members of our FAMU family who were injured in the tragic incident."

title: Canada opens consultation on stablecoins, citing US GENIUS Act
body:
As part of the potential implementation of its Stablecoin Act, the Canadian government will hear from the public on a proposed framework for tokens from non-financial institutions.
Lawmakers in the Canadian government opened a 60-day public consultation on regulations proposed to address non-financial institution stablecoin issuers, including a potential prohibition on yield payments.
On Saturday, the government of Canada gave notice that it would be open to public comment on the stablecoin regulations until Dec. 23. The proposed framework cited efforts to be consistent with stablecoin regulations in the United States and other jurisdictions, to “reduce the overall regulatory burden on multi-jurisdictional issuers.”
Notably, the proposed regulations said that non-financial institution stablecoin issuers would be restricted from offering interest or yield to discourage HODLing the tokens. They would also be required to redeem stablecoins within three business days of requests from tokenholders, and not charge a fee greater than 1% of the coins’ total value.
The regulations fell under Canada’s Stablecoin Act, which was passed in March and intended to address non-financial institution issuers. According to the government, the proposed rules were required to enact the policy and include provisions for issuers to register with Canada’s central bank.
“The intention is for the proposed Regulations to come into force in fall 2027,” said the government. “Once the proposed Regulations are in effect, issuers of stablecoins in Canada who are not financial institutions would be required to apply for registration with the Bank of Canada prior to issuing a stablecoin.”
The GENIUS Act, which establishes a regulatory framework for stablecoins in the US, is scheduled to take effect in January 2027. Meanwhile, the European Union’s regulations, Markets in Crypto Assets (MiCA), could give exchanges until January to halt services for stablecoins not in compliance with the framework, likely including Tether’s USDt (USDT), the largest stablecoin by market capitalization.

title: BioStack Nets $9.5 Mn To Build Training Datasets For Medical AI
body: AI-powered healthtech platform BioStack has raised $9.5 Mn (₹90.4 Cr) in its seed funding round led by Peak XV Partners, Afore Capital, DCVC, Emerson Collective, SV Angel, Verdict Capital, Streamlined Ventures, and Y Combinator. The startup plans to utilise the fresh capital to continue expanding its presence in the US and other international markets, including India, Brazil, and Argentina. A chunk of the capital will also be used to scale its tech stack and ramp up hiring across engineering and research teams. Founded in 2025 by Sanat Mishra and Parth Patwa, BioStack claims to be building the data infrastructure for the next generation of medical AI. It combines fragmented clinical information across systems such as electronic health records, medical imaging, clinical notes and medications. The startup then uses this data to create proprietary datasets for research, biotechnology, and the development and training of medical AI models. “We’re building the infrastructure that connects all of the clinical information and makes it useful, both for clinicians making decisions today and for the researchers and AI developers building the future of medicine,” said BioStack cofounder and CEO Mishra. BioStack currently works with multiple hospitals across the US, Brazil and Argentina. In India, it is also connecting cancer patients with an investigational cancer vaccine program. The startup also claims that it offers use cases such as AI model evaluation, disease modeling, biomarker discovery, patient stratification and treatment-response analysis. Besides offering custom workflows to protect patient privacy, the startup claims to have so far processed 10 Cr de-identified patient records, more than “several hundred thousand” fragmented X-Rays, MRIs and CT scans, and “several million” telehealth audio transcripts. For context, de-identified patient records are medical datasets that have had all personal and direct identifiers removed so that the individual cannot reasonably be linked to the data. The fundraise comes as India becomes a training ground to collect datasets for powering AI models and physical AI products. Startups are tapping India’s huge population to collect recordings of workers performing physical tasks, processing the footage, and selling the resulting datasets to frontier AI labs and robotics companies. For instance, the likes of Awign, Objectways and Human Archive are building pipelines to supply first-person footage of human activity to AI developers. Just a day ago, instant home services startup Pronto’s founder Anjali Sardana launched Provision Labs , a US-based venture to collect data for physical AI systems. At the heart of all this is the Indian AI training dataset, which is projected to become a $1.3 Bn opportunity by 2033 . title: Video: Electra EL2 makes fixed-wing landing at Manhattan heliport
body: Electra flew its hybrid-electric EL2 airplane into a Lower Manhattan heliport, demonstrating its ability to take off and land in a waterfront space normally reserved for helicopters. The two-seat EL2 Goldfinch technology demonstrator landed and took off at Downtown Skyport on October 26, 2026, as part of Electra’s effort to show that short regional flights need not begin and end at conventional airports. The company said it believes this was the first landing at the heliport by a fixed-wing aircraft without vertical-takeoff capability. “Today we made aviation history in downtown Manhattan by landing a fixed-wing aircraft on a heliport,” Electra CEO Marc Allen said. “What’s even more interesting is that we didn’t need to build a new runway to do it.” The EL2 is being used to test technology for Electra’s planned nine-passenger EL9. The aircraft relies on a technique called blown lift, which uses electrically driven propellers to push air over the wings and large flaps, increasing lift at speeds much lower than those required by conventional airplanes. That allows the aircraft to become airborne after a short ground roll. Once in cruise flight, the flaps retract and the aircraft flies normally, avoiding the need to sustain the extra lift. Electra’s published target for the EL9 is a takeoff and landing ground roll of 150 feet. The aim is to make regional flying practical from smaller sites closer to passengers’ destinations. Electra wants to offer regional flights from heliports and other small sites, saving passengers the drive to and from an airport. For Downtown Skyport, the attraction is extending its role beyond helicopter flights and proposed electric air taxi services. “Electra’s ultra-short takeoff aircraft shows that Downtown Skyport can connect to destinations well beyond the airport run, carrying more passengers and more cargo over far greater distances,” said Robbie Ladov, General Manager, US Heliports & Vertiports at Skyports Infrastructure. Electra was founded in 2020 by John Langford, who previously founded Aurora Flight Sciences. The concept grew from work with Massachusetts Institute of Technology researchers, including Professors John Hansman and Mark Drela, exploring ways to combine electric propulsion with very short takeoff and landing distances. The Manassas, Virginia-based company first flew the EL2 on battery power in November 2023, followed later that month by its first hybrid-electric flight. The demonstrator has since become the centerpiece of a flight-test and demonstration campaign supporting development of the larger aircraft. The EL9’s planned propulsion system combines eight electric motors with batteries and an onboard turbine-powered generator. The generator supplies electricity and allows the batteries to recharge in flight, reducing dependence on charging equipment at destinations. Electra lists a projected cruise speed of 175 knots and a maximum ferry range of 1,100 nautical miles with reserves. In July 2026, Electra announced that the FAA had established the EL9’s certification basis, setting the regulatory framework for the program. The company is targeting a first flight in late 2027 or early 2028 and entry into service in 2030. The Manhattan flight follows demonstrations at locations including Charleston, South Carolina, Atlantic City’s Bader Field and Snowshoe Mountain Resort. Electra also recently used its demonstrator to test helicopter-style instrument procedures and heliport operations at Roanoke–Blacksburg Regional Airport. Electra says it holds more than 2,200 letters of intent from over 60 commercial customers for the EL9.
