title: 2027 Elections: INEC To Publish Preliminary Register Of Voters Online
body: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has said that it will make the preliminary register of voters for the 2027 general elections available on its website. The Commissioner disclosed this in a statement on Monday. It stated that it had taken note of the concerns expressed by Nigerians and other stakeholders regarding the desirability of making the register accessible through its online platform in addition to the physical display already conducted. “Accordingly, and in furtherance of its commitment to transparency, accessibility and public confidence in the electoral process, the Commission has decided to make available on its online platform https://display.inecnigeria.org the same Preliminary Register of Voters earlier displayed at the Registration Areas,” it said. “This additional measure complements the physical display already undertaken and is intended to facilitate wider public access to the register.” According to the statement signed by the Chairman, Information and Voter Education Committee (IVEC), Mohammed Kudu Haruna, the Commission said it continues to process claims and objections arising from the exercise in accordance with the Electoral Act, 2026, preparatory to the certification and publication of the final register of voters on December 15, 2026. “The Commission appreciates the continued interest and constructive engagement of Nigerians and stakeholders and reiterates its commitment to transparency, accountability and the faithful implementation of the Electoral Act, 2026 in delivering credible elections,” it added. The post 2027 Elections: INEC To Publish Preliminary Register Of Voters Online appeared first on Channels Television .

title: Anthropic opens its books for Wall Street, showing record revenue and mounting obligations
body:
Anthropic filed its IPO prospectus, and the market seems to like it.
The AI lab is the first major company of its kind to publicly file an S-1 with the SEC . Anthropic plans to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker "ANT," with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley leading the offering. Wall Street expects a valuation of roughly $2 trillion, according to Yahoo Finance, up from the company's most recent private valuation of about $965 billion, which already put it ahead of rival OpenAI at roughly $852 billion.
The first-half numbers show huge growth. Revenue jumped from $376 million in Q1 2025 to $11.6 billion in Q2 2026, a 1,368 percent year-over-year increase. For the first half of 2026, Anthropic brought in $16.3 billion total, more than triple its full-year 2025 revenue of $4.6 billion. Government contracts account for only about one percent of that total, while roughly 5 to 7 percent comes from customers who violate usage policies, primarily through model distillation, which Anthropic has already been cracking down on . Ad
In Q2 2026, Anthropic posted its first positive GAAP operating profit at $974 million. Compute costs rose 300 percent over the same period, but that's slower than revenue growth. Revenue per employee sits at $6.6 million, higher than any Magnificent 7 company except Nvidia, with about 5,300 people on staff. Chip stocks like Nvidia, Broadcom, and AMD rallied after the filing went public. Ad
Anthropic's net revenue retention rate sits at roughly 900 percent, meaning existing customers are spending nine times what they did a year ago. That figure speaks to AI's scaling potential, especially considering most deployments are likely still shallow , depend on human oversight, and don't run AI at full speed yet.
More than 11,900 customers pay over $100,000 annually, and about 250 spend more than $10 million. No single customer accounts for more than ten percent of revenue, but five customers together make up 25 percent. If those include companies like Meta, Google, or Microsoft that could switch to their own or cheaper models, that concentration could become a risk. Ad
Claude Enterprise users who also use Claude Code are the biggest spenders, paying about 20 times more than other customers, according to the S-1. Eighty percent of revenue is billed on actual usage, per token processed as the smallest billing unit for AI models, while the remaining 20 percent comes from fixed subscriptions. That split might signal how heavily subscriptions are still being cross-subsidized, but it also suggests Anthropic has room to raise prices. The company's forecast for next year will be primarily usage-based, according to the FT.
Anthropic has taken on huge financial obligations to fuel its growth. Compute capacity contracts with Broadcom, Google, Amazon, Microsoft, and other providers add up to roughly $780 to $810 billion, and those costs are more or less fixed and locked in long-term, while revenue remains variable and usage-dependent. Ad
That means the company needs to keep growing fast to cover its future bills. If it can't, the AI-fueled capital market could start to wobble . To gain more flexibility and lower costs over time, Anthropic is building its own data centers under the name "Anthropic Direct" . Ad
Anthropic also left Q3 numbers out of the S-1, even though the company already has them. One possible reason is that growth slowed significantly in Q3 . Momentum may have already picked back up, though. OpenRouter data shows demand for Anthropic models climbed again after the October release of the 5.5 series, especially Opus 5.5 . OpenRouter only captures a tiny slice of total token demand and tends to skew toward open-weight models, so if Anthropic is dominating there, it's likely doing even better everywhere else.

title: My Chemical Romance faces legal action over Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders stunt
body:
The parent company of the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders is taking legal action against My Chemical Romance after the band appeared to perform with dancers who wore costumes that resembled their signature blue-and-white uniform.
Pro Silver Star filed a motion for a temporary restraining order and preliminary injunction against the band in Dallas County District Court on Friday seeking to bar My Chemical Romance (MCR) from using the costumes onstage, according to court documents viewed by NBC News and Rolling Stone .
Global News has not independently viewed the court documents.
Pro Silver Star alleges that the band performed on Oct. 21 at the Hollywood Bowl in Los Angeles with the dancers wearing costumes that appeared to be nearly identical to the cheerleading squad’s uniforms, NBC News reports.
The dancers carried what appeared to be rifles and engaged in “a staged firefight, “only to be depicted being shot,” the filing states, according to the outlet.
“Audience members and online commentators understandably believed that the performers were the real Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders and said so in social media posts that continue to circulate,” Pro Silver Star wrote, according to the outlets.
Pro Silver Star reportedly said that it is “not litigious” and it “takes no issues with MCR’s music, its artistic ambitions, or any message Defendants seek to convey.”
“Silver Star does not ask Defendants to change their setlist, narrative, politics, choreography, or even their decision to put gun-toting performers on stage. Silver Star asks only that those performers not wear the DCC Uniform while doing it,” the filing reportedly states. “The universe of alternative costume designs is effectively unlimited.”
Footage of the Oct. 21 performance shared to social media shows the performers dancing with blue and white pom-poms to MCR’s 2006 hit, Teenagers .
The band took the stage again on Oct. 23 and footage shared online appeared to show the dancers wearing the uniforms resembling the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders’ outfits again.
Global News has reached out to My Chemical Romance’s representatives for comment on the motion, but has not received a response.
My Chemical Romance is currently celebrating the 20th anniversary of its third studio album, The Black Parade .
The band, which features Gerard Way, Mikey Way, Frank Iero and Ray Toro, is scheduled to perform at the Hollywood Bowl on Oct. 30 and 31.

title: Mallam Junction traffic congestion hotspot cleared after JoyNews extensive report
body: After three years of torturous gridlock, missed opportunities and daily frustration, commuters who use the Mallam Junction stretch can finally breathe a sigh of relief. The notorious pothole-ridden section of the highway, which for years turned a short commute into a hours-long ordeal, has been fixed – just days after JoyNews shone a spotlight on the nightmare. For residents of Kasoa, Weija, Gbawe, Mallam and adjoining communities, Mallam Junction is more than just an intersection. It is the gateway to Accra for thousands travelling from the Central and Western Regions. But that gateway had become a trap. The trouble began three years ago when heavy rains devastated parts of Accra. The road at Mallam Junction was hard hit, leaving behind deep, yawning potholes that forced drivers to crawl, swerve, and sometimes stall completely. What should have been a smooth drive became a daily pain for commuters. During morning and evening rush hours, the situation was unbearable. Vehicles piled up bumper-to-bumper, engines overheated, tempers flared, and time stood still. On a typical Monday morning, the queue would stretch from Mallam Junction all the way to Broadcasting Junction at New Bortianor in the Ngleshie-Amanfro area. The human cost was enormous. Workers reported to the office late and queried by bosses. Traders lost valuable market hours. Students missed classes. Patients on their way to hospitals endured painful delays. To outsmart the traffic, many Kasoa residents say they were forced to adopt an extreme routine – leaving home as early as 4:00 a.m. just to beat the Mallam snarl and get to Accra on time. Those who could not wake that early had to accept being late as part of life. For three years, they pleaded. For three years, nothing changed – until JoyNews told their story. An extensive JoyNews report captured the depth of the suffering, with videos of gridlocked vehicles, interviews with stranded passengers, and drone shots of the deteriorating road. The report triggered public outrage and finally caught the attention of the authorities. Within days of the broadcast, machinery moved to site. The failed portion has now been patched and levelled, allowing for the free flow of traffic once again. Daniel Awortwe, Engineer at the Weija-Gbawe Municipal Assembly, and his team, who are carrying out the repair works confirmed that the repair works were executed through collaboration between the Municipal Assembly and the Ministry of Roads and Highways. According to him, the intervention was aimed at restoring the road to motorable condition and easing the unbearable congestion. Today, cars glide through Mallam Junction without the usual jerking and braking. Commercial drivers who once spent hours navigating a few metres now drive through in minutes. Commuters have welcomed the relief, though their joy is mixed with questions. Gladys Appiah, a regular passenger on the Kasoa-Accra route, could not hide her excitement. She expressed gratitude to the Minister of Roads and Highways, Kwame Agbodza, for acting swiftly after the JoyNews report. But for others like Yaa Serwaa, the celebration feels misplaced. She described the three-year delay as a self-inflicted wound. According to her, fixing potholes on a major international highway is not a capital-intensive project that requires huge loans or complex engineering. It is basic maintenance that should never have taken three years to fix. Her sentiment reflects a broader frustration among many Ghanaians – why must it take a media report for authorities to act on obvious problems? For now, however, the road is clear. The horns have reduced. The long queues have disappeared. And the 4:00 a.m. exodus from Kasoa may no longer be necessary, but the good news seems not good for hawkers who sell on the pavement during the traffic build-up. Akua says she makes GHC600.00 a day, but today she has been here for many hours with no sales. Whether this repair will be maintained to prevent another three-year ordeal remains to be seen.

title: NDC Discloses N8.5bn Income, N2.4bn Spending in Seven Months
body: *Party unveils campaign council, inaugurates national secretariat Sunday Aborisade in Abuja The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) on Monday disclosed that it generated N8.529 billion from nomination forms, membership dues, levies and contributions within its first seven months of operation, while spending N2.402 billion on primaries, publicity, staff salaries and other activities. The party presented the financial figures at its National Executive Committee (NEC) meeting in Abuja, where its National Chairman, Senator Moses Cleopas, said the disclosure was intended to promote transparency and accountability in the management of the party’s resources ahead of its first anniversary. The NEC Meeting was attended by the National Leader of the party, Senator Henry Seriake Dickson; the Presidential Candidate of the party, Mr. Peter Obi; his Vice, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso; serving and former members of the National Assembly and other notable leaders of the party, among others. Cleopas said the party decided to account for its finances before the statutory deadline for submitting its audited accounts to the relevant government institutions, insisting that members had a right to know how funds entrusted to their leaders were being managed. He said the decision was not prompted by allegations or criticisms on social media but reflected the party’s commitment to accountability and responsible leadership. According to him, the party’s leadership considered it necessary to provide members with an early account of its financial position, even though the NDC had yet to complete its first year of operation. He said, “One of the critical instruments that destroys leadership or communal living, as I have been taught, is the management of public funds. When you have a responsibility to sit over a public forum, you also owe the people who entrusted you with that privilege an obligation to be open to them. “They must know what you are doing from time to time. Any attempt to foreclose that will lead to suspicion and give room for people to say what is not true. “When you find yourself in a leadership position, accountability must be your sense of duty, especially when it has to do with common wealth. “That is what Nigeria is suffering from. Nigeria is so blessed. We cannot say that we do not have resources in this country. The question we are asking is: where are our resources? What are our resources being used for that will bring relief or blessings to Nigerian citizens?” The national chairman said the NDC would submit its properly audited financial statement to the constitutionally authorised institutions when the appropriate reporting period ended. He explained that the party’s financial management process involved a committee comprising the national chairman, national secretary, financial secretary, treasurer and auditor, with the party’s legal adviser co-opted when necessary. The National Treasurer, Dr Peter Onigah, presented the financial statement at the meeting, outlining the funds received and expenditure incurred during the period under review. The disclosure comes as the NDC intensifies preparations for the 2027 general election, with the party also inaugurating its presidential campaign council, present certificates of return to its candidates and commission its national secretariat at the Jabi Area of Abuja. Cleopas said the activities were part of efforts to strengthen the party’s structures and demonstrate its readiness for the forthcoming elections. He said the inauguration of the presidential campaign council followed consultations aimed at identifying people willing to commit their time and resources to the party’s electoral project. “It is not a matter of rushing to announce a campaign council. It is a matter of getting people who are committed, people who are ready to serve this nation in that capacity,” he said. The chairman also cautioned party members against interpreting the initial list of campaign council appointments as a complete representation of all those who would eventually be involved. “Some are calling to ask, ‘Why is my name not there? Why is my name not there?’ We are not finished. Let them wait for us,” he said. Cleopas said the party presented certificates of return to its candidates to prevent individuals who did not win its primaries from parading themselves as candidates and misleading voters. He described the NDC as a party intended to outlive its founding leaders, urging young Nigerians to identify with it and prepare for future leadership responsibilities. Cleopas said, “This party is intended to be a generational party for as long as we remain on earth. This party is intended to outlive us. And if that is the vision we have, there is a particular set of people we must target. “We have the youth to target in this country. The reason is that they must be prepared for leadership. So, this is a party of mentorship,” he said. Umeh Seeks Funding for State Chapters At the meeting, Senator Victor Umeh, representing Anambra Central, commended the party’s leadership for making its financial position available to members, describing the disclosure as an important step towards building public confidence. Umeh said providing financial information would help members understand the party’s operations rather than rely on speculation. He, however, called on the national leadership to ensure that state chapters received an appropriate share of the funds generated through their activities. Responding, Cleopas said the issue of funding for state chapters was already under consideration, assuring members that the party would address the matter in line with its constitution and organisational objectives. The chairman also disclosed that the party’s reconciliation committee had visited the six geopolitical zones to engage aggrieved aspirants and other members dissatisfied with the outcomes of its primaries. He said the national secretariat was holding regular meetings to resolve outstanding disagreements and prevent internal disputes from undermining the party’s preparations for the elections. Cleopas urged candidates, party leaders and supporters to put aside their differences and work collectively for the success of all NDC candidates. He said the party could not afford to allow personal disagreements to weaken its electoral prospects, particularly when its presidential and vice-presidential candidates would require the support of lawmakers and other elected representatives to implement their programmes if elected. The chairman argued that supporting only the party’s presidential candidate while abandoning its candidates for governorship and legislative seats could undermine the party’s ability to govern effectively. He said, “Don’t you also know that they need a majority, if not all, in the National Assembly from our party? If you don’t know so, how will they get the president they want? How will they get the Senate president or the speaker of their choice? “You may not like the face of the candidates, but they are your party’s candidates. We must work together so that we can have the Nigeria of our dreams.” NDC Insists on Candidate Compliance, Vote Protection The NEC meeting also heard updates from party officials on preparations for the 2027 elections, including efforts to resolve disputes involving candidates and strengthen the party’s grassroots structures. The National Vice-Chairman for the North-east, Dr Dallamiya Nzukumbe, said preparations were progressing, although the party had encountered some disagreements between candidates and party leaders in certain areas. He said the leadership was working to resolve the disputes and ensure that the party’s structures remained focused on the elections. Nzukumbe also urged Nigerians to reject the notion that their votes would not count, calling on voters to remain at polling units after casting their ballots to ensure that votes were counted and results properly documented. “We will vote, we will wait, and we will escort,” he said, stressing that the party wanted an electoral process in which votes cast at polling units were accurately reflected in the final results. He said voters in the North were particularly concerned about insecurity, the disruption of farming activities and attacks on schools, adding that residents wanted to return to their farms, travel safely and send their children to school without fear. “The children in the North must go to school,” he said. Another party official, speaking on preparations in the southern part of the country, said the party was working to resolve outstanding disputes arising from its primaries and restore harmony among members. He said the NDC was intensifying voter education and sensitisation on electoral responsibilities, particularly the need for voters and party agents to protect their votes after voting. According to him, the party was documenting its agents and working with candidates at different levels to ensure adequate representation at polling units and collation centres. He urged voters not to leave polling units immediately after casting their ballots but to remain until the votes were counted and the results properly recorded. Cleopas, in his closing remarks, also addressed concerns over the omission of some candidates’ names from the relevant electoral processes. He said the party was pursuing both administrative and legal avenues to address the matter and expressed confidence that candidates who had fulfilled the requirements of the law would be able to contest the elections. “The party is not folding its hands. The party is interfacing on administrative fronts and legal fronts,” he said. He added that the leadership was conscious of its responsibility to candidates who had completed the required processes and would continue to pursue the matter. The NDC chairman urged members to remain united as the party moved from internal preparations to the next phase of its electoral activities. He said the party’s immediate priorities included commissioning its national secretariat, inaugurating the presidential campaign council, presenting certificates to its candidates and resolving outstanding grievances before the 2027 general election.

title: UN calls Russian attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure crimes against humanity
body:
According to Ukrinform, this information is posted on the Commission’s website .
“The Russian authorities have committed war crimes by deliberately targeting civilian objects, as well as crimes against humanity in the form of other inhumane acts, by carrying out continuous attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure,” stated the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on Ukraine in its new report to the UN General Assembly.
The Commission investigated the impact of large-scale attacks by Russian armed forces on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure on the civilian population, particularly during the difficult winter of 2025–2026, as well as the cumulative effects of these attacks since the fall of 2022. The report notes that systematic waves of Russian attacks, during which hundreds of drones and missiles were deployed simultaneously, became increasingly frequent and intense and covered an ever-wider area, causing significant damage to Ukraine’s energy sector.
Last winter, when temperatures dropped to -21 °C, millions of people in Ukraine faced prolonged disruptions in the supply of heat, electricity, water, and gas and were forced to live in unbearable conditions.
“As winter approaches, the attacks have intensified again, raising serious concerns given the threats to the lives and health of the civilian population,” said Commission Chair Erik Møse.
The report emphasizes that prolonged exposure to the cold, lack of access to basic utilities, and the constant need to find ways to survive have significantly affected the physical and mental health of Ukraine’s civilian population.
Due to the risk of getting stuck in an elevator in the event of a sudden power outage, they were unable to go down to the shelter during an air raid alert and were forced to remain in unheated homes without electricity or water, without access to life-support equipment or basic services.
Due to the prolonged closure of schools during the acute energy crisis, children were unable to receive a full education. The lack of heating in their homes led to children falling ill and created additional hardships for their families.
The Commission concluded that the Russian authorities committed war crimes by deliberately targeting civilian objects. The evidence gathered indicates that the attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure were carried out in a targeted manner, in accordance with a state policy aimed at depriving the civilian population of electricity and other vital services dependent on energy supply and causing them suffering. The Commission concluded that the Russian authorities committed crimes against humanity in the form of other inhumane acts. The Commission relied on the testimony of 255 individuals who survived the winter under the conditions described above in the Dnipropetrovsk, Kyiv, Kharkiv, Kherson, Mykolaiv, Odesa, Poltava, Zaporizhzhia, and Zhytomyr regions, as well as on information provided by Ukrainian authorities, doctors, and nongovernmental organizations.
According to the Commission’s assessment, the Russian commanders who issued orders to carry out the attacks were aware that the heating facilities they targeted in large population centers were vital to the civilian population, especially in winter. Russian authorities officially stated their intention to continue the attacks and referred to plans for their implementation.
The Commission also examined attacks by the Ukrainian armed forces on energy facilities in the Russian Federation and in the temporarily occupied territories of Ukraine. It is noted that the Commission was unable to investigate the consequences of these attacks in detail, as the Russian Federation did not grant it access to the relevant territories and did not respond to the Commission’s requests for information.
The Commission also concluded that Russian authorities recruited men who had been victims of human trafficking in various countries into their armed forces, which constitutes a violation of international human rights. In particular, compelling evidence was found that Russian authorities engaged in human trafficking involving individuals from 29 countries.
Human trafficking was carried out through deception and coercion in collaboration with agents and agencies operating in various countries around the world. The agents and agencies that recruited men in various countries presented themselves as legitimate companies or government-backed enterprises. They arranged visas and travel documents for groups of recruits and, in some cases, accompanied them during the trip. However, shortly after their arrival, they were forced to sign contracts with the Ministry of Defense of the Russian Federation, written in Russian.
The Commission noted a high level of coordination between agents operating in various countries around the world and the Russian authorities.
As a result, the men were sent to the front lines in Ukraine and assigned dangerous tasks. Many of them were killed or went missing; others voluntarily surrendered or were captured by the Ukrainian armed forces and were granted prisoner-of-war status.
The Commission reiterates that international law prohibits attacks on the civilian population and civilian objects and calls for an end to such attacks. The Commission also calls for the release from the Russian armed forces of all individuals who have been victims of human trafficking.
As previously reported, as of April 2026, Russian troops had attacked Ukrainian power substations—which are critical to nuclear safety—a total of 155 times since the start of the full-scale invasion.
Since October 19, 2026, alone, Russian troops have carried out approximately 60
targeted strikes, damaging energy and oil and gas infrastructure in a number of regions (including Rivne, Volyn, Khmelnytskyi, and Vinnytsia), as well as the Kyiv power coal depot.
As of May 2026, 80 repeat strikes on infrastructure facilities had been recorded at the very moment when State Emergency Service rescuers and law enforcement officers were arriving at the scene.

title: El Niño: What it means and how Nigerians should prepare
body: By Sekinat Osundiji Nigeria may experience increased heat and changing rainfall patterns as a strengthening El Niño event raises concerns about its potential effects on agriculture, water supply, electricity generation and public health. The World Meteorological Organisation (WMO) said in September 2026 that El Niño was expected to strengthen into a very strong event and persist into early 2027. The Nigerian Meteorological Agency (NiMet) has also warned that the phenomenon could affect rainfall patterns, including the length of the rainy season and when it ends. But what is El Niño, how could it affect Nigeria, and what can the country do to prepare? What is El Niño? El Niño is a natural climate phenomenon that occurs when surface waters in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean become warmer than average. This warming affects atmospheric circulation, changing weather patterns around the world. Depending on the region, it can contribute to higher temperatures, reduced or excessive rainfall, and shifts in seasonal conditions. El Niño is part of the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO), a climate pattern that also includes La Niña, its cooler phase, and neutral conditions. According to the WMO, El Niño typically occurs every two to seven years and lasts between nine and 12 months. Although it develops thousands of kilometres from Nigeria, its influence on global atmospheric circulation can affect weather in West Africa. However, its effects vary by location and do not automatically mean drought or extreme heat everywhere. What does El Niño mean for Nigeria? NiMet’s August 2026 seasonal climate update identified the onset of a strong El Niño event and outlined possible implications for rainfall, agriculture, water resources and energy. For August to October 2026, the agency forecast normal to above-normal rainfall across much of northern Nigeria, while parts of the South-West and Cross River State were expected to experience normal to below-normal rainfall. These projections highlight the possibility of different weather outcomes across the country. 1. Higher temperatures and health risks One major concern is the possibility of increased heat. In October 2026, the Climate Impact Lab projected that Nigeria could record an additional 31,400 heat-related deaths between September 2026 and February 2027, compared with an average year. The figure is a model-based estimate of potential excess deaths, not a confirmed death toll or a certainty that those deaths will occur. Extreme heat can cause dehydration, heat exhaustion and potentially fatal heatstroke, particularly among children, older people and outdoor workers. Health authorities should strengthen public awareness campaigns, issue timely heat warnings and prepare health facilities for heat-related emergencies. Residents should drink water regularly, seek shade, limit strenuous outdoor activities during the hottest hours where possible, and check on vulnerable relatives and neighbours. 2. Agriculture and food production Changes in rainfall can disrupt planting schedules and crop development. Prolonged dry spells or an early end to the rainy season could reduce yields, while excessive rainfall may cause flooding and damage farms. NiMet has identified possible agricultural risks in areas expecting below-normal rainfall, including parts of Borno and Yobe. Farmers should monitor updated forecasts, consider early-maturing or drought-tolerant crop varieties where appropriate, and seek advice from agricultural extension officers. In areas expecting heavier rainfall, maintaining drainage channels can help limit damage. Government agencies should also improve farmers’ access to timely weather information and agricultural advice. 3. Water supply and electricity generation Prolonged rainfall deficits can reduce river flows, reservoir levels and groundwater recharge, putting pressure on domestic water supplies and irrigation. Hydropower generation could also be affected if water inflows into dams decline. NiMet has identified reduced water availability and lower reservoir inflows as potential risks, although these do not confirm nationwide water shortages or electricity disruptions. Water authorities should monitor reservoirs and groundwater conditions, identify vulnerable communities and develop contingency plans. Residents can help by repairing leaking taps and avoiding unnecessary water waste. 4. Food prices and household expenses Adverse weather could reduce agricultural output, damage farms and disrupt transportation, placing pressure on food supplies and prices. However, El Niño alone does not mean food prices will rise nationwide. Harvests, storage, transport costs and wider market conditions will also influence prices. The government should monitor food supplies, support farmers in vulnerable areas and strengthen storage and distribution systems to reduce avoidable losses. How should Nigeria prepare? Preparation requires coordinated action by government agencies, state authorities, farmers, health workers, businesses and residents. NiMet should continue issuing updated, location-specific forecasts and ensure warnings reach rural communities and farmers, including those without reliable internet access. Health authorities should educate the public on heat-related illnesses and strengthen emergency responses, particularly for vulnerable populations. Agricultural ministries and extension officers should provide advice on planting dates, crop selection, irrigation and drainage based on current forecasts. Water agencies should monitor dams and reservoirs, reduce distribution losses and plan for communities that may face shortages. Authorities must also prepare for heavy rainfall and flooding rather than focus exclusively on drought. Government agencies, broadcasters and journalists should communicate climate information clearly, distinguish projections from confirmed events and update the public as conditions change. Does El Niño mean Nigeria is heading for disaster? Not necessarily. El Niño increases the likelihood of certain climate-related impacts but does not determine precisely what will happen in every state. The WMO has emphasised that even a very strong event does not produce equally severe effects everywhere. Local weather patterns and other climate drivers can alter its influence. Nigeria’s priority should be to identify areas most vulnerable to heat and rainfall changes and prepare accordingly. Following NiMet’s updates and taking practical precautions can help reduce risks to public health, agriculture, water resources and electricity generation. Ultimately, the challenge is not simply how strong El Niño becomes, but how effectively Nigeria prepares for its potential consequences. The post El Niño: What it means and how Nigerians should prepare appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: ‘Foreign-controlled spy forces have been eliminated’: Pashinyan on local elections
body: Pashinyan on Armenia’s 2026 local elections “The ruling Civil Contract party, along with candidates and teams affiliated with it, secured a convincing victory in the local elections,” Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said during a live broadcast on his Facebook page. On 25 October, Armenia held local elections in 21 communities. Voters used a proportional representation system in 19 communities and a majoritarian system in the other two. In five communities — Armavir, Vardenis, Garni, Akhuryan and Vayk — the ruling Civil Contract party ran unopposed. In other words, no other political forces chose to contest the elections or take part in governing these communities. According to preliminary results from the Central Electoral Commission, Civil Contract won in 16 communities. The Amerashkhut’yun (Solidarity) bloc secured the most votes in two others. In Stepanavan, the Gortsarar (Entrepreneur) party took the lead. Its list was headed by incumbent community leader Armen Grigoryan, who won the post in 2021 on the Civil Contract party list. Pashinyan congratulated the candidates for community leadership positions and the ruling party’s teams as a whole on their victory. He stressed that Armenian citizens had helped deliver election results that led to the “destruction of spy opposition forces”. At the same time, he expressed concern about the outcome. “As someone who became prime minister after the Velvet Revolution, I am far from pleased when a party wins more than 90%, 80% or 70% of the vote in some communities. However appealing such figures may seem at first glance, they evoke certain associations. They also raise questions about the opposition in Armenia. We need to assess this situation correctly. On the one hand, we must completely eradicate the spy opposition in Armenia that takes orders from abroad. On the other hand, Armenia needs an opposition that puts the interests of the state first,” the prime minister said. Pashinyan’s salary to nearly double as Armenian civil servants set for pay rises from 2027 ‘From crisis management to stability’: Pashinyan unveils new government programme Armenia approves new government as Pashinyan promises appointments based on merit Stepanavan records the highest voter turnout Armenia’s Central Electoral Commission has released the final voter turnout figures. The Lori region community of Stepanavan recorded the highest turnout, at 68.83%. Other communities also reported high turnout: Yeghegnadzor (Vayots Dzor region) — 62.56%, Tsaghkadzor (Kotayk region) — 61.78%, Meghri (Syunik region) — 57.97%. The lowest turnout among the 21 communities came in Fioletovo, in the Lori region, at 25.39%. 'Another attempt is being prepared to deprive Armenia of its independence' — Pashinyan Asked whether Russia was involved in efforts to destabilise Armenia, the prime minister replied: “Certain circles in the Russian Federation.” 54 reports of possible violations During the elections, the Interior Ministry’s 112 Operations Management Centre received 54 reports of possible violations. Investigators have received evidence relating to 10 incidents for preliminary investigation. These include: one case of breaching ballot secrecy; one case of obstructing people involved in the elections from exercising their rights or performing their duties; seven cases of repeat voting or voting on behalf of another person; one case of voter bribery. Election observers also reported irregularities. The Akanates (Eyewitness) observation mission recorded 217 potential violations of the electoral process at 137 of the 407 polling stations it visited. The observers noted crowds gathering at polling stations, risks to ballot secrecy and cases of “family voting”, in which several people enter a voting booth at the same time. On 24 October, the day before the elections, Armenian media reported the arrests of opposition candidates and their supporters in three of the 21 communities. The Anti-Corruption Committee confirmed the arrests but did not disclose the identities of those detained, citing the interests of the preliminary investigation. “As part of criminal proceedings launched by the Anti-Corruption Committee over alleged corruption offences linked to the electoral process, investigators are carrying out investigative and other procedural measures in several communities across Armenia,” the committee said. Armenia debates new mechanisms to tackle vote-buying Parliament is set to debate a bill introducing penalties for political forces involved in vote-buying. Lawmakers are also expected to discuss restricting voting rights for citizens who do not reside in Armenia. “We solved one problem, but two or three new ones emerged” — prime minister’s assessment Continuing his argument that Armenia must “eradicate” an opposition network he describes as a foreign-controlled spy network, the prime minister said: “These local elections have resolved the issue to some extent, but three new challenges have now emerged.” He was referring in particular to the following questions: “How can we prevent election results from creating the impression of authoritarianism or dictatorship? How can we introduce an objective mechanism for public oversight in communities where we have secured a high level of trust? How can we build an opposition in Armenia that puts the interests of the state first — young, intellectually capable, objective and honest — and answers solely to the will of its voters and citizens?” Pashinyan stressed that the government must not take part in creating a new opposition, as this would lead to the emergence of a “controlled, fake opposition”. The prime minister said independent political forces needed to become more active. He added that the government would neither help nor hinder their emergence. “We want to see a genuine opposition emerge in Armenia — one that acts in the interests of Armenia and its people and is guided by democratic values and principles. We do not want an opposition that bribes voters or channels stolen and misappropriated funds into politics to turn the political sphere into a tool for protecting assets acquired dishonestly.” In his view, an opposition that puts the interests of the state first could also provide “genuine and constructive oversight” of the government’s actions. “I want to point out that in communities where the elections did not produce a strong opposition, public oversight remains an open question. I hope that civic groups and representatives of civil society will take on this role.” 'Russia's Plan B has been activated': analysis of Armenia's preliminary election results Pashinyan’s party won, but two pro-Russian forces also entered parliament. Political analyst Robert Ghevondyan says this was Moscow’s minimum objective in the election Pashinyan on Armenia’s 2026 local elections

title: More Than 60 Christians Killed in Ethiopia Attacks, Church Says
body: More than 60 people have been killed in a series of attacks targeting Christian communities in Ethiopia’s Oromia region, according to the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church, which has described the violence as a massacre. The attacks took place across three areas of the Shirka district, leaving homes destroyed and forcing residents to flee. The church said at least 20 houses were burned to the ground, while eyewitnesses reported that five of those killed were children. A resident whose 75 year old father was killed described the incident as an ambush. “We were completely unprepared and had no prior knowledge. They surrounded us from all four directions,” the resident told BBC Amharic. A church official said security forces arrived at the scene but were unable to stop the assault. Rebel Coalition Accused of Involvement A local government official blamed the attacks on the Alliance for Survival, a newly formed rebel coalition that includes the Oromo Liberation Army (OLA). The OLA has not commented on the latest allegations but has previously denied responsibility for similar attacks. Ethiopian authorities have repeatedly accused the armed group of targeting civilians and religious institutions. Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed has previously claimed that such violence forms part of an effort to destabilise the country. The OLA, which says it is fighting for greater rights for the Oromo people, has rejected accusations that it is responsible for the attacks. The regional government has pledged to take action against those responsible. Orthodox Church Warns of Growing Attacks The Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church condemned the violence, warning that attacks against Christians have increased in recent months. In a statement, the church said the attacks undermined the country’s values of mutual respect and peaceful coexistence. The church also said it had repeatedly raised concerns about deteriorating security with authorities at different levels of government, but that the situation remained unresolved. The latest killings have intensified concerns about the safety of religious communities in the region, where armed violence has repeatedly targeted civilians. Hundreds Killed in Four Years A report published in July 2026 by the Ethiopian Human Rights Council, a non-governmental organisation, documented 458 deaths in attacks in the area over the preceding four years. The organisation said armed groups had repeatedly targeted local communities, particularly members of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church, in attacks it described as religiously motivated. The latest incident is among the deadliest reported during that period. However, violence in the region has also affected Muslim communities. Residents who have spoken to the BBC in previous reports have described attacks as having both ethnic and religious dimensions. The overlapping tensions have made the security situation increasingly complex, with civilians from different religious communities facing the consequences of continued violence. Religious Tensions in Ethiopia Ethiopia has a diverse religious population. Approximately two thirds of its people are Christians, most belonging to the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church, while Muslims account for roughly one third of the population. The latest attacks have renewed concerns about the protection of religious communities and the authorities’ ability to prevent further bloodshed in Oromia. title: Likud files police complaint against Eisenkot campaign manager over Polymarket post
body: Likud filed a police complaint on Monday against Ronen Manelis, campaign manager for Gadi Eisenkot, accusing him of breaking Israel's election campaigning law by sharing a post on X that gave Eisenkot strong odds of becoming prime minister after the upcoming election. Attorney Ilan Bombach filed the complaint on Likud's behalf.At the center of the complaint is a Polymarket post that Manelis reshared on his X account on Sunday. The post said that former IDF chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot, who heads the Yashar party, is expected to become Israel's next prime minister after Tuesday's election, replacing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. It gave Eisenkot a 52% chance of winning the post, compared with 28% for Netanyahu, and included a photo of Eisenkot in IDF uniform.BREAKING: Former IDF chief Gadi Eizenkot projected to become Israeli Prime Minister after Tuesday's election, replacing Netanyahu. 52% chance.  https://t.co/a01aGtedUZ https://t.co/p12Bzt8mbI— Polymarket (@Polymarket) October 25, 2026The complaint included a screenshot of Manelis's repost, showing the original Polymarket post, the figures and a chart comparing Eisenkot's and Netanyahu's chances.Likud claims Manelis shared post without clarifying contextLikud argues that the figures do not come from a public opinion poll conducted using accepted statistical methods, but from a platform that forecasts the outcomes of future events. Even so, the complaint claims, Manelis shared them without making clear that they were not a statistical survey and could not be used to draw conclusions about voting patterns or public opinion.The figures reflect the probability of a political outcome, not a candidate's level of support among voters. Eisenkot's 52% chance of becoming prime minister does not mean that 52% of the public plans to vote for him.In his letter to the police, Bombach stressed that, in Likud's view, this is not merely a technical violation, but an attempt to influence voters through illegal means.Post was shared 'to influence the voting public," complaint claimsThe complaint claims the offense was committed “in order to influence the voting public, under aggravating circumstances and through prohibited means.” Likud views it as especially serious that the post was shared by Manelis, who runs the campaign of one of the candidates. “There is a significant and pressing public interest in investigating and bringing the offender to justice,” the complaint said, calling on police to investigate the post and pursue charges to the full extent of the law.However, the claim that Polymarket's figures count as an election poll under the law is Likud's own legal interpretation, not a ruling by any authority. The question is a substantive one, since the platform presents the probability of future outcomes rather than the results of an opinion poll. Whether the law's rules on publishing election polls apply to this kind of data may prove central to how the complaint is handled.

title: Form a government, you can hate each other on your own time - comment
body: Before casting his vote in Israel's first national election, Rabbi Moshe Yekutiel Alpert told off the polling committee.Its chairman was two minutes late.On January 25, 1949, Alpert got up at 5:35 a.m., put on his Shabbat clothes, and headed for a Jerusalem polling station. His home in the Beit Yisrael neighborhood had been damaged by shelling; he was staying elsewhere while it was being repaired. He carried his Israeli identity card, he wrote, with the same joy of carrying a Torah scroll during Simchat Torah celebrations.He arrived at 5:50. The chairman appeared at 6:02. Alpert reminded him that proceedings were supposed to begin at six. The man apologized.As the oldest person present, Alpert was invited to vote first at that station. He received “voter number one,” said Shehecheyanu, the blessing of gratitude for reaching a special occasion, and cast his ballot.His father and grandfather had never had the same opportunity.I shared the story this week. The Jewish state was eight months old, and Alpert already expected it to run on time.It's a familiar mix of reverence and impatience. Israelis can be fiercely attached to their country and furious with it, often in the same conversation. People expect a great deal from a place their families have paid a great deal for. From abroad, the anger can be easier to hear than the attachment.Today, Jewish and Arab Israelis will again choose the people who govern them. I hope we allow ourselves a little of Alpert's pleasure before we begin arguing about the exit polls. The ability to vote a government out is worth appreciating, including when a government we favor loses.Israel needs several years where its citizens can make plans againWhat I want from this election is a few years in which Israelis can make plans again.Three years after October 7, consider what that would mean for a reservist trying to keep a business alive. Someone has to cover the work while he is away. His spouse has to rearrange work and childcare. Eventually, decisions about next month become decisions about whether the business has a future.Families rebuilding their homes need to know that funding and official attention will last until the work is finished. They should be able to plan around a budget that survives the next coalition dispute.I believe only a broad Zionist government can give this country the political stability it needs for that work. Likud, former IDF chief of staff Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party, and other Zionist parties should negotiate an agreement to govern together for several years.That will require leaders to sit with people they have spent the campaign attacking and explain the arrangement to voters who believed those attacks.Some will have to accept a job smaller than the one they wanted. They should tell us which demands they are prepared to set aside. I would find that interview considerably more useful than another account of why everything is someone else's fault.There is a reason these concessions are so hard. In Israel, a political allegiance often comes with a family history. It may include a grandparent's experience of immigration, a parent's sense of being looked down on, or a lasting belief that people like us were denied a fair hearing. Calling an entire camp ignorant or dangerous reaches well beyond the politician at its head.An election settles who has the votes to govern. People still have to live together afterward. A citizen should be able to lose an election and feel at home in their country. Leaders who want a broad coalition will have to show they understand one another's voters.Start the negotiations by asking what 70 or 80 percent of Israelis could support. I would begin with security preparedness, restoring damaged communities, and arrangements that let reservists serve without ruining their livelihoods. Agree on what can be done, how much it will cost, and who is responsible. Give ministers enough time in office to be judged on whether they delivered.A coalition agreement might even contain a deadline unrelated to the next leadership rotation.Independent October 7 commission must be part of coalition agreementAn independent, credible examination of October 7 must be part of that agreement. Families deserve to know how the state failed them. Officials and commanders need to answer for their decisions. A coalition assembled to restore public trust will have to accept findings that may be uncomfortable for its own members.Before accepting another promise, I want to know whom that candidate appointed, what improved while they were in office, and what they did when something went wrong. The politician I like deserves the same questions. Newcomers can be judged on their experience and the seriousness of their plans.Theodor Herzl, the founder of modern political Zionism, described Zionism in 1904 as “a never-ending ideal.” Even after the Jewish people obtained a homeland, he wrote, the pursuit of “ethical and spiritual fulfillment” would continue.In our time, that responsibility includes a government office being responsible for treating a bereaved family, the education available to a child far from the center of the country, and the willingness of a prime minister to accept scrutiny.The late chief rabbi Abraham Isaac Kook approached the problem from another direction. He wrote about the religious, national, and universal human concerns within Jewish society, arguing that each had value and could restrain the others' excesses. He also understood how hostility between camps could consume them.A religious minister and a secular mayor can have different ideas about the purpose of Jewish sovereignty and still agree on how to get a school built. They can resume the philosophical argument after the classrooms open.The Jewish Agency's Board of Governors has been meeting in Israel this week. The gathering brings Israeli leaders and Jews from abroad into the same room on the eve of the election.Having spent years covering Jewish life abroad, I wish more Israelis were interested in what those communities are trying to achieve.A minister visiting a Jewish school should ask how it keeps tuition affordable and what its pupils know about Israel. There is a great deal to learn from people who have to persuade families to choose a Jewish education.We Israelis often ask Diaspora Jews to understand the pressures we live under. We should also be equally willing to learn about the pressures they face. The government answers to Israel's citizens; its decisions can still affect a Jewish family thousands of miles away.The next prime minister should put regular consultations with Jewish communities abroad in the diary and give the relevant ministers responsibility for following up. The Jewish Agency and other communal bodies can bring in voices from beyond the familiar leadership circles. Publish the commitments, then report what happened to them.I would put affordable opportunities to study and spend time in Israel high on that list. Help young immigrants find their feet here. Give young Israelis more chances to encounter Jewish life abroad. A friendship formed over a semester has time to develop beyond the positions people take in an argument about the news.A Jewish child abroad should be able to cultivate a relationship with Israel that lasts through several changes of government. She ought to have friends here, places she wants to revisit, and enough knowledge to form her own opinions.I want my own children to make their lives here, and I want them to be able to plan beyond the next emergency. They will have plenty to complain about. I would like them to grow up expecting a government to finish the work it starts.

title: Show HN: Wraps – Resend-style email on your own AWS SES, open source
body:
One command deploys Amazon SES into your AWS account. Then send, broadcast and automate from the Wraps dashboard, or let your agent do it through the platform.
A typed TypeScript SDK that talks straight to SES. Every send, delivery, open and click lands in a table you own.

title: 2027: Rise Networks, INEC, Meta, Google, Microsoft join forces to launch #AI4Elections Hackathon
body: Rise Networks, in collaboration with the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Meta, Google, Microsoft and other partners, has launched the #AI4Elections Hackathon to develop artificial intelligence solutions aimed at strengthening Nigeria’s electoral process ahead of the 2027 general elections. The national, multidisciplinary and nonpartisan initiative will bring together technology developers, researchers, university students, electoral experts, civil society organisations and innovators to develop practical AI-powered tools addressing challenges associated with elections. Other partners include the International Centre for Investigative Reporting (ICIR), NITHUB at the University of Lagos, the Centre for Information Technology and Development (CITAD), CLEEN Foundation, Tap Initiative for Citizens’ Development, International Press Centre, Legal Naija, Ahmadu Bello University and the Federal University of Technology, Akure. The programme is supported by the MacArthur Foundation and Luminate and builds on Rise Networks’ experience developing Run-Am, an AI-powered misinformation detection and fact-checking mobile application used during the 2023 Nigerian elections. Applications opened on Thursday, October 22, 2026, and will close on November 12 at 11:59 p.m. West African Time. The programme will run from October 2026 to February 2027, with a national grand finale and innovation showcase scheduled for December 16 in Lagos. Speaking at a press conference in Abuja, the founder of Rise Networks, Dr Toyosi Akerele-Ogunsiji, said the initiative was designed to promote responsible AI innovation that protects electoral integrity and citizens’ rights. “Our ambition is not to introduce technology for technology’s sake. We are committed to promoting responsible AI innovation that respects the integrity of Nigeria’s electoral process, protects citizens’ rights, and prioritises transparency, privacy, and human oversight,” she said. “Innovation must strengthen our democracy, not create new vulnerabilities for it.” Akerele-Ogunsiji said Nigeria needed to harness emerging technologies to improve access to reliable information and strengthen public confidence in democratic institutions. “We must begin to harness the power of artificial intelligence to strengthen electoral integrity, expand access to information, and build greater public confidence in our democratic institutions,” she said. “The #AI4Elections Hackathon is an opportunity to bring our brightest minds together to develop solutions that respond to the realities of our electoral process.” The competition will focus on five principal areas: trustworthy electoral information; electoral data analysis, operational insights and decision support; inclusive and multilingual electoral and civic technology; electoral cybersecurity and resilience; and election observation and citizen accountability. Climate resilience and environmental innovation will also be considered as an optional cross-cutting area. Participants are expected to develop working solutions, including AI-enabled applications, software prototypes, data-analysis tools, multilingual interfaces and other technically credible products. Idea-only submissions, presentations and mock-ups without functional solutions will not be accepted. The hackathon is open to Nigerians aged 18 and above, including developers, AI engineers, data scientists, cybersecurity professionals, researchers, civic-tech innovators, electoral experts, product designers and public policy practitioners. Applications may be submitted by individuals or teams of up to four members, with team-matching support available for individual applicants. Entries must be submitted in English, and projects that have already received grants, awards or recognition in previous competitions are ineligible. Speaking at the event, Dr Lawrence Bayode said the growing influence of AI on elections made it necessary for Nigeria to develop solutions that preserve electoral credibility. “The question before us is no longer whether AI has a role to play in an election, but how we can harness its potential without compromising the integrity, transparency and credibility of the electoral process,” he said. Meta’s Head of Public Policy for Anglophone West Africa, Sade Dada, said the company would work with INEC to promote reliable election information and tackle false claims, including fake images and videos generated with AI. She highlighted Meta’s “Remove, Reduce and Inform” approach and GovGuide Nigeria, an AI-powered chatbot that provides government information in English, Hausa, Igbo and Yoruba. Dada stressed that AI tools used during elections must remain politically neutral and operate under human oversight, adding that Nigeria’s experience could offer lessons for other countries. “The 2027 elections matter far beyond Nigeria’s borders. If Nigeria gets it right on trustworthy information, the continent will learn from it and, indeed, the world,” she said. Other speakers, including Lagos Business School Dean, Prof. Olayinka David-West, and legal practitioner Tsema Ede, said AI could improve election results management but emphasised the need for transparency and public trust. The hackathon has a total cash prize pool of ₦10 million. The overall winner will receive ₦4 million, while the second- and third-place winners will receive ₦2.5 million and ₦1.5 million, respectively. Four additional special innovation awards, each worth ₦500,000, will recognise outstanding work in research and policy innovation, electoral and civic inclusion, responsible AI and safety, and cybersecurity and resilience. Entries will be assessed based on technical functionality and innovation, relevance to electoral challenges, practical usefulness, cybersecurity, privacy, responsible AI, scalability, feasibility, demonstration and documentation. Rise Networks said the programme would also include an AI4Elections Development Hub to support the testing and refinement of promising solutions, alongside a Community of Practice to sustain collaboration among innovators, researchers, mentors and electoral stakeholders beyond the competition. The organisers stressed that the initiative would not support partisan campaign technology, voter manipulation or interference with electoral administration. Participants are also prohibited from conducting unauthorised tests of live electoral systems or accessing institutional infrastructure. Winning the competition will not automatically authorise the deployment of any solution in an election, as future institutional pilots will remain subject to relevant legal, technical, institutional and security approvals. Interested applicants can obtain further information and apply through ai4elections.risenetworks.org. The post 2027: Rise Networks, INEC, Meta, Google, Microsoft join forces to launch #AI4Elections Hackathon appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Ukraine’s Zelenskyy welcomes Student List’s win in Serbia and says Kyiv is “ready to keep increasing cooperation”
body: (function(w,q){w[q]=w[q]||[];w[q].push(["_mgc.load"])})(window,"_mgq"); For 14 years, Serbia’s government kept the country close to Moscow. Now, the opposition “Student List” has won the country’s snap parliamentary election, and President Volodymyr Zelenskyy says Ukraine is ready to deepen its cooperation with Serbia, welcoming the result as “a new page” in a post on X . The win could end the 14-year rule of President Aleksandar Vučić’s political force and weaken Moscow’s position in the Balkans. Serbia has remained an important Kremlin partner in Europe since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, and Belgrade never joined the EU's sanctions against Moscow. “A new page” In his post, written in Ukrainian, Zelenskyy said that "changes have taken place in Serbia, the victory of the Student List, and this is clearly a new page in the history of the country and its people." “We wish Serbia success, real development, and warm relations with the European community,” he wrote. He said Ukraine was grateful to Serbia “for the respect shown to our people and our state, our independence,” and added: “We are ready to keep increasing our cooperation, and may all the good hopes of the people of Serbia come true.” But the winners rule out sanctions on Russia Vučić had earlier predicted that a new government could impose restrictions on Moscow by March or April, according to Novosti. The Student List says otherwise: it has no plans to align with the EU or to sanction Russia over the war in Ukraine, according to Reuters. Its candidates frame Serbia’s reliance on Russian gas, with Gazprom as the largest supplier at around 2.2 billion cubic meters a year at below-market prices, as an acute economic dependency rather than a geopolitical alignment. The movement’s top candidates have also said a future government would end all arms exports to war zones, including sales to Western intermediaries who pass weapons to Ukraine. Around €800 million worth of Serbian ammunition has reached Ukraine through that route since 2022. title: Ukraine war latest: Ukrainian forces carry out 2 aerial evacuations of wounded soldiers, video shows
body:
Ukraine's 475th Separate Assault Regiment Code 9.2 evacuated two severely wounded soldiers from the battlefield using a domestically developed aerial evacuation drone, StarGate, the unit reported on Oct. 26.
The two soldiers, 25-year-old Yevhen, call sign " Izium ," and 24-year-old Artem, call sign "Kolobok," had suffered severe limb injuries and were stranded in a contested area about five kilometers (three miles) from the Russian border.
Ground evacuation was impossible due to difficult terrain, water obstacles, and the threat of Russian first-person-view (FPV) drones, the regiment said .
The two evacuation missions were carried out over the course of a week in cooperation with SkyFall, the Ukrainian company that developed and manufactures StarGate.
The operations required coordination between several units and fire support from heavy Vampire attack drones to suppress Russian positions.
During one mission, StarGate flew nearly 30 kilometers (20 miles) to reach a wounded soldier and approximately the same distance back with him aboard.
A 12-year-old boy injured in a Russian drone strike on a park in Nova Vodolaha, Kharkiv Oblast, on Oct. 19 has died in a Kyiv hospital, bringing the death toll to six, including three children, local authorities reported on Oct. 26.
Russian forces struck the town's central park at around 4:30 p.m. local time on Oct. 19, when families with children were spending time there.
Artem Koval suffered severe injuries in the drone strike and was taken to hospital. Despite a week of efforts to save him, doctors were unable to overcome his life-threatening injuries, the Vodolaha Village Council said.
Artem's 8-year-old sister, Arina, was killed at the scene of the attack on the park.
"In a single terrible moment, the parents lost everything most precious to them — both their son and their daughter — and their loved ones lost children who were so dear to their hearts," the statement read.
"Russia robbed these children of their future and their families of their reason for living by committing yet another bloody crime against the most innocent."
At least 15 people were injured in the attack, including seven children, according to Kharkiv Oblast Governor Oleh Syniehubov.
A fire broke out on the territory of the Energia plant following an overnight attack on the battery plant in the city of Yelets in western Russia overnight on Oct. 26, Ukraine's General Staff said later that day.
The plant is the sole Russian manufacturer of batteries for glide bomb guidance and correction modules, the General Staff said without specifying the extent of the damage.
It added that the plant, located about 250 kilometers (about 155 miles) from Ukraine, also produces batteries for Iskander-M ballistic missile systems and sea-based cruise missiles.
"The strike complicates the Russian Federation's military's production of power sources for missiles, guided bombs, and other weapons," the General Staff said in its Telegram post.
Earlier on Oct. 25, Ukrainian monitoring Telegram channel Exilenova Plus reported that smoke rose over the whole territory of the Energia plant after several missiles appeared to have hit it in the afternoon. The General Staff has not specified what weapons were used to strike the Energia plant in Russia.
Russia is significantly expanding its glide-bomb production, indicating that Moscow has no plans to scale back its war against Ukraine, a new report by Kyiv-based think tank Center for Defense Reforms exclusively shared with the Kyiv Independent reveals.
"Given the role of guided aerial bombs in destroying defensive positions, isolating battlefields and facilitating ground advances, this provides a basis for sustaining high-intensity offensive operations over an extended period," the report concludes.
The report reveals that in 2025, the centralized procurement entity TRV-Engineering JSC obtained nearly 278,000 servo drives, used to control the flight surfaces of glide bombs — enough to manufacture 139,000 of the deadly munitions. The report identifies the key Russian supplier of servo drives, CED Sail LLC, which is currently not subject to any Western sanctions, and suggests this entity should be a "priority target" for sanctions designation.
"Russia is building the military-industrial capacity to continue waging wars even after the war in Ukraine ends. These are not the actions of a country preparing for lasting peace," Oleksandr Danylyuk, chairman of the Center for Defense Reforms and former chief adviser to Ukraine’s defense minister, told the Kyiv Independent.
The report also identifies a network of interconnected Russian companies which are responsible for importing key components and raw materials essential for the production of UMPK and UMPB glide bomb kits.
Russia converts older, unguided bombs into precision-guided weapons with these guidance kits, significantly increasing their range and accuracy. The increase in range allows Russian fighter-bomber aircraft to remain within Russian territory, out of range of Ukrainian air defenses, as they deploy their deadly payloads.
As with many other Russian munitions, both UMPK and UMPB glide bomb kits are heavily reliant on foreign components for their manufacture.
Ukrainian military intelligence has repeatedly identified a range of foreign components in Russian glide bombs, including parts from the U.S., Japan, China, Switzerland, and Taiwan, among others.
The report also reveals the majority of entities and individuals involved in the production of Russia's glide bombs are currently unsanctioned, despite the munitions being a key part of the Kremlin's offensive airborne arsenal.
Out of 20 corporate entities involved in the manufacture of Russian glide bombs, only eight are subject to some level of Western sanctions or export restrictions. The "uneven sanctions coverage," the report assesses, allows Russia to continue to "procure necessary components without significant restrictions."
Four Chinese companies are identified as being critical to the supply chain, with some, such as Shenzhen Fire Power Control Technology Limited, not hiding the explicitly military application of their products. Only one of the four Chinese companies is subject to U.S. export restrictions, and none are sanctioned by the U.K. or the EU.
"Despite its repeated declarations of readiness for peace, Russia continues to dramatically expand the production of offensive weapons, particularly guided aerial bombs," Danylyuk said.
Russia's Digital Development Ministry has proposed building data centers underground, camouflaged from the air, and fitted with drone defenses, Russian state-controlled media Kommersant said on Oct. 25, following several Ukrainian drone attacks on data centers.
Guidelines for existing, planned, and under-construction facilities outline the protection standards for three tiers of data centers, including whether sites are placed above ground or underground, according to Kommersant.
The top tier includes strategic sites whose loss could disrupt key state functions for an hour or more; the second tier includes sites supporting regionally or economically important systems, where outages could last four hours or more; and the final tier covers corporate data centers whose damage would not have wider consequences for the state, Kommersant said.
Existing data centers should be protected by reducing their visibility from the air and by deploying layered defenses, including reinforced structures, electronic warfare measures, and drone defense systems.

title: ‘I don’t do drugs, smoke or drink’ — Blessing CEO after release from detention
body:
Nigerian relationship influencer and self-styled expert Blessing Okoro, popularly known as Blessing CEO, has denied allegations of drug use following her release from detention, saying she neither smokes nor drinks alcohol.
Blessing clarified the allegations during a video call with Nollywood actress Doris Ogala, who shared their conversation on Instagram .
During the exchange, Doris told the influencer that speculation about alleged drug use had circulated oBlessing CEOn social media while she was in custody.
According to the actress, some users had warned against sending Blessing money, claiming it could be used to purchase drugs, while others suggested she needed rehabilitation rather than financial assistance.
Responding to the claims, Blessing said people were making assumptions about her lifestyle without knowing her personally.
“I don’t do drugs. I don’t smoke, I don’t drink, I don’t even party. Most times, the internet has a way of enjoying themselves. A lot of people don’t even know me personally,” she said.
The relationship expert maintained that the allegations were based on social media speculation rather than personal knowledge of her habits.
The allegations gained attention in early October after social media activist VeryDarkMan, whose real name is Martins Vincent Otse, accused Blessing and her partner, businessman Ikechukwu Ogbonna, popularly known as IVD, of involvement with drugs.
In videos shared on Instagram, VeryDarkMan alleged that IVD introduced Blessing to drugs and claimed that their alleged substance use contributed to financial difficulties and other controversies surrounding the influencer.
He also alleged that Blessing had sold properties and cars to fund the purported habit and linked the claims to allegations surrounding her reported cancer diagnosis and fundraising activities.
VeryDarkMan later urged the public not to send Blessing money after her release, arguing she needed rehabilitation.
However, the drug-related claims remain unsubstantiated, and Blessing’s latest comments represent a direct denial of the allegations.
Blessing’s denial comes days after her release from detention following months in custody over fraud-related cases instituted by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC).
She was reportedly released on Saturday, 24 October, after meeting her bail conditions.
Doris announced her release in an Instagram post, writing, “Blessing CEO is finally out, thank you, Jesus. Awwwww ajjeeeyyyy.”
IVD also celebrated her release, sharing a video and writing, “We entered the lion’s den, but the lion didn’t eat us.”
Blessing remained in custody despite bail being granted in some cases, reportedly because she struggled to meet the conditions attached to her release.
The cases include allegations relating to property transactions and the alleged collection of money from members of the public in connection with claims that she was battling stage four breast cancer.
In one of the cancer-related cases, she was accused of obtaining about ₦13 million in donations after allegedly presenting falsified medical results.
Other reported cases involve disputed property transactions, with sums of about ₦36 million and ₦69.15 million mentioned in separate proceedings.
Blessing has pleaded not guilty to the charges. Her release on bail does not amount to an acquittal, and the cases remain subject to the court process.
During her detention, Blessing also suffered the loss of her second son, who reportedly died following an asthma attack.
The tragedy drew online attention, including discussions about a reported ₦56 million fundraising appeal she had publicly distanced herself from.
Blessing, who built a substantial social media following through relationship advice and commentary on romantic relationships, has remained a controversial figure in Nigeria’s online entertainment space.
Her denial of the drug allegations adds another development to the public scrutiny surrounding her personal life and ongoing legal battles.
