title: Ukraine, Romania discuss development of energy interconnectors with capacity of nearly 1 GW – Shmyhal
body:
Ukraine and Romania discussed the development of electricity interconnectors, the use of gas corridors, and the expansion of cooperation in the field of gas production during the first onlinemeeting between Ukraine's First Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Energy Denys Shmyhal and Romania's Minister of Energy Dumitru Chisăliță.
"The agenda included the region's energy security and the implementation of joint energy projects," Shmyhal said on his Telegram channel.
According to him, the parties focused on the development of electricity interconnectors between the countries, which would provide nearly 1 GW of additional transmission capacity, and discussed deepening bilateral cooperation in this area.
They also discussed logistical issues related to fuel supplies. Shmyhal informed his Romanian counterpart about Ukraine's proposals to increase the capacity of border crossing points and open new transit routes.
Special attention was given to the use of the Vertical and Trans-Balkan gas corridors and the development of new interconnectors. The Ukrainian side noted Romania's role in implementing the Trans-Balkan route roadmap, particularly in introducing more competitive tariff conditions.
"We also count on Romanian companies' interest in storing a portion of their gas in Ukrainian gas storage facilities as part of the development of the Vertical Corridor," Shmyhal said.
Following the meeting, the parties agreed to work together to establish cooperation between Ukrainian and Romanian companies in the field of gas production and field development.

title: The fall fashion & beauty edit: Small updates, big impact
body:

As a fashion stylist who spent over a decade as an aesthetician and makeup artist, I know that great style doesn’t stop at your wardrobe. Fashion, skincare and makeup work together, and sometimes the smallest changes make the biggest impact.
Refreshing your look for a new season doesn’t mean starting from scratch. It’s about mixing textures, experimenting with silhouettes and choosing beauty essentials that complement your personal style. From cozy weekend layers to polished evening dressing, Walmart has affordable options to make it happen.
I love elevating my fall outfits by mixing textures, and pairing a cozy knit with something a little more feminine is one of my favourite styling tricks.
A satin skirt and relaxed sweater are a perfect example. The contrast between soft, fluid fabric and knitwear creates a look that’s modern, wearable and easy to take from daytime plans to an evening out.
Victoria Beckham is wonderful inspiration for this approach to dressing. Her signature style often combines fluid fabrics with structured pieces, proving that a beautiful outfit doesn’t need complicated styling.
My tip? Let the textures do the talking. Add sleek boots and minimal jewellery for daytime, then switch to statement earrings and a long coat for an evening out.
I’m a big believer that everyday style starts with versatile basics, but it’s how you put them together that makes an outfit feel fresh.
Relaxed denim, sporty outerwear and interesting proportions are some of my favourite elements to play with, especially when I want something comfortable that still feels fashionable.
Hailey Bieber is a great example of how to make casual dressing feel fashion-forward. Her off-duty outfits often feature relaxed denim, oversized outerwear and simple basics, with the proportions creating all the interest.
My styling trick for barrel jeans is to balance the volume. Try a fitted top underneath your jacket or a shorter layer that defines your waist. It’s a small adjustment that can make a big difference.
A beautiful outfit deserves an equally great beauty routine, and as temperatures cool, hydration becomes especially important.
After years of working with clients as an aesthetician and makeup artist, one thing I always emphasize is that makeup looks its best when skin is properly prepared.
Kerry Washington consistently delivers beautiful complexion inspiration, with luminous skin and softly defined features. Rather than relying on heavier coverage, I prefer targeted concealer, cream blush and subtle definition to enhance a natural glow.
Whether I’m heading to a TV appearance, meeting friends or getting ready for an evening event, I always appreciate beauty products that help my makeup go the distance.
Priyanka Chopra Jonas is known for glamorous beauty looks, often pairing radiant skin with defined eyes or a statement lip.
For an evening update, I love building on daytime makeup rather than starting over. Add eyeliner, reach for a berry or plum lip colour and finish with a setting mist.
A few additional essentials can take your routine from the first step to the finishing details.
Looking to add a few more pieces to your fall rotation? These George favourites offer plenty of ways to mix, match and make the most of your wardrobe.
The best seasonal updates aren’t about replacing everything you own. They’re about discovering new ways to bring your wardrobe and beauty routine together.
A beautiful knit paired with an unexpected texture, a boost of hydration before makeup or the right finishing details can completely change how you look and feel.
Great style is about the whole picture, from what you’re wearing to how you finish your makeup. And with Walmart’s fashion and beauty essentials, refreshing both can be simple, accessible and affordable.

title: North Korea has threatened Seoul
body:
Ulchi Freedom Shield is a regularly organised military exercise conducted by the Armed Forces of the Republic of Korea and units of the US Armed Forces stationed in the Republic of Korea as part of USFK (United States Forces Korea). During this year’s edition, the scenario that was implemented took an interesting turn, in which DPRK forces threatened Seoul.
According to South Korean media reports, during the Ulchi Freedom Shield exercises, organised by the Republic of Korea Armed Forces and the US Armed Forces, a situation arose during simulated combat in which DPRK forces threatened the capital of the Republic of Korea, Seoul. These media outlets report that this situation may have been caused by command issues within the coalition forces. It is noted that at a certain point, a four-star general of the Republic of Korea Army was to assume command, which was intended as an element of the exercise, since the coalition partners are testing a scenario in which the South Korean side may take over command, including command over American forces.
It is worth mentioning that the headquarters of the 2nd Infantry Division is permanently stationed in the Republic of Korea, where a Stryker Brigade Combat Team (SBCT) is present on a rotational basis. Furthermore, one of the Korean mechanised brigades, the headquarters of the 2nd Divisional Artillery, the 210th Field Artillery Brigade, the 2nd Combat Aviation Brigade, and the 2nd Sustainment Brigade are subordinated to the division command. Moreover, the Republic of Korea hosts APS-4 (Army Prepositioned Stock – 4) warehouses containing equipment for an armoured brigade, including M1A2SEPv2 main battle tanks, M2A3 infantry fighting vehicles, and M109A6 self-propelled howitzers.
The Republic of Korea is expressing increasing concern regarding the participation of DPRK troops in the war in Ukraine, through which they are gaining actual combat experience for the first time in decades. Furthermore, in exchange for support for the Russian Federation, the DPRK has most likely gained access to many technical and technological solutions available to the Russian arms industry. Consequently, it is pointed out that the DPRK is capable of developing increasingly advanced weapons systems. Ballistic missiles carrying nuclear warheads are of particular concern, but it should be noted that the DPRK is also modernising its arsenal of conventional military equipment.
Another problem for the Republic of Korea is that without the support of reconnaissance aircraft and satellites available to the US, the country has difficulty detecting the DPRK’s mobile ballistic missile launchers, making their neutralisation more challenging. Meanwhile, the Republic of Korea is preparing to take over operational command of the defence in the event of an outbreak of war. Until now, the Americans have been responsible for command. The situation on the peninsula is being inflamed by recent events in which soldiers of the Republic of Korea Army were wounded.

The leading economics blog online covering financial issues, geopolitics and trading.
Europe's political elite is belatedly confronting the electoral cost of deindustrialization, as right-wing gains in local elections expose surging voter anger over globalist policies that have crushed the industrial base. The push to curb cheap Chinese imports suggests Brussels is scrambling for political survival, as Nomura analysts recently said elections across the continent over the next year and a half are expected to shift right.
Bloomberg reports that the EU is preparing restrictions on imports of chemicals, furniture, and machinery from China, expanding efforts to shield domestic manufacturers and narrow the massive trade deficit with China, which stands at $404 billion. The report cited people familiar with the matter.
"Our industries have called for action and we have heard them, and we will respond, including some more safeguards," Commission President Ursula von der Leyen said earlier this month.
The proposed safeguards build on earlier news that Brussels aims to implement the Chinese hybrid vehicle cap in December to shield the EU's crumbling automotive industry, as cheap overseas cars gain market share and leave domestic companies like VW laying off tens of thousands of workers.
Brussels has finally chosen to move up the " escalation ladder " with China, risking retaliation from Beijing as its own political power appears to be eroding across Europe after decades of backfiring globalist policies that have left the continent with a hollowed-out industrial base.
EU trade chief Maroš Šef?ovi? is expected to discuss trade with Chinese counterparts early next year, as Brussels must perform a delicate balancing act to avoid provoking Beijing into imposing export restrictions on critical materials and permanent magnets.
Earlier this month, we first reported " Better Late Than Never? " and our verdict was " just 10 years too late ." The more interesting question is how far Brussels is willing to climb up the escalation ladder with Beijing.
Deutsche Bank's Marion Muehlberger answered that in a ten-question Q&A published earlier this month, ahead of Šef?ovi?'s trip to Beijing, titled " Crunch time for EU-China trade relations " ( available to Pro subscribers ). The centerpiece is a single table, which may be the most useful cheat sheet on EU-China trade policy we have seen: every tool Brussels could deploy against Beijing, ranked from most to least likely , with the precedent and the catch for each one.
So far Brussels is willing to raise tariffs and cap imports. But the higher it climbs up the escalation ladder, the greater the risk that Beijing pulls the rare earth supplies, starving the very factories European elites are scrambling to save.

title: Putin Just Lost His Key Ally in Europe. Here’s What Happens Next
body:
Student protesters challenged the regime and dismantled a longtime political grip on Belgrade.
During his years in office, the Serbian president carefully balanced European overtures against deep Moscow partnerships while rejecting Western sanctions. This sudden defeat triggers urgent questions about the Kremlin’s strategic foothold across southeastern Europe.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
Security analyst Ivana Stradner, a research fellow at the Foundation for Defense of Democracy (FDD), joins Kyiv Post’s Jason Jay Smart to break down the entrenched networks Russia established across Serbian energy, intelligence, and regional security. Removing a reliable partner does not instantly erase decades of Russian soft power or intelligence assets. Belgrade’s opposition figures have also voiced skepticism toward sanctions, clouding future foreign policy alignments. Who retains power behind closed doors, and what leverage does Moscow still possess?
For Ukraine, future policy shifts in Serbia could reverberate directly across European defense dynamics and ongoing battlefield pressures. Stradner separates genuine strategic losses for the Kremlin from cosmetic political disruptions that leave old alliances intact.

title: Fusion startups are giving the government shares in exchange for awards. Is it worth it?
body:
The U.S. government has long had an on-again, off-again relationship with the fusion power sector. As of last week, it’s definitely back on.
Helion and Commonwealth Fusion Systems (CFS) received awards totaling $260 million from the Department of Commerce under the CHIPS and Science Act, the 2022 law that funds domestic semiconductor development, to develop advanced semiconductors used to help power and control their reactors. Helion landed $175 million , while CFS reeled in $85 million .
But as with many recent government awards, these come with strings attached. Helion and CFS have agreed to give the government nonvoting shares in return. With these awards, the fusion industry is finally getting the government’s attention, though maybe not the sort it envisioned.
In the past, government support for a startup meant nondilutive capital, meaning money that doesn’t shrink existing investors’ ownership percentages, while giving the company a bigger war chest. Investors loved the deals because it meant their startups got more money without them having to pony up. The government doled out the cash to boost American innovation, though it also meant that, in most cases, the government didn’t directly benefit when it picked a winner.
The Trump administration has been pushing to change that calculus.
For both companies, the total dollar amount pales in comparison to how much each has raised . CFS has raised about $4 billion, while Helion is close behind with $3.2 billion in committed capital. The awards are perhaps more important as signals that, after years of cutting and then trickling out fusion funding, the U.S. government is back in the game.
Fusion, which generates power by fusing atoms together as the sun does, is an expensive endeavor, requiring exotic materials, sophisticated computer modeling, and complex manufacturing. Progress over the last decade has attracted private investors who have bet more than $14 billion that one or more companies will be able to put a power plant on the grid.
Yet according to the Fusion Industry Association, the sector’s trade group, that’s still not enough to beat other countries in the race. Last year, the trade group called on the federal government to inject a one-time infusion of $10 billion into the sector, with $5.4 billion intended for fusion startups.
“Other nations are moving aggressively to accelerate their commercial fusion industries, pouring billions in state-backed efforts to win the race to fusion power,” a spokesperson for CFS told TechCrunch. CFS is a member of the Fusion Industry Association. “The $10 billion ask is designed to build out the research infrastructure in the DOE’s Fusion Roadmap and be catalytic for the U.S. domestic fusion industry to compete with China.”
Until recently, the federal government had been dribbling out dollars for fusion. The Biden administration introduced the Milestone-Based Fusion Development Program, a Department of Energy program that pays companies as they hit technical goals, but the dollar amounts were paltry; less than $50 million was distributed in the first couple years. More recent awards were a little bigger, but still well shy of money the Fusion Industry Association has called for.
Now, with two companies getting $260 million, it looks like the lobbying may be starting to pay off, though not quite as planned as it comes from Commerce rather than the research budget the Fusion Industry Association sought, and it carries equity strings.
The Fusion Industry Association’s lobbying campaign did not include conversations about equity stakes in exchange for awards, a person familiar with the matter told TechCrunch. Yet Helion said the government will receive $175 million in nonvoting equity based on its Series G round, which valued the company at $15.5 billion. That works out to a stake of roughly 1%. The government’s stake in CFS will also be nonvoting and based on the company’s most recent valuation, which CFS has not shared publicly. That means the size of the government’s stake in CFS is not known.
“This type of structure has become more common in large U.S. government investments in recent years,” David Kirtley, co-founder and CEO of Helion, told TechCrunch in a statement. “This approach aligns the interests of Helion and the U.S. taxpayer around our commercial success.”
The CFS spokesperson echoed those comments. “This U.S. equity stake will enable the U.S. taxpayer to participate in the upside of our commercial success in exchange for investing in important research and development that supports the growth of an American commercial fusion industry.”
Helion and CFS are the latest in a series of companies that have seen the government take a stake in exchange for federal dollars.
Last year, critical minerals supplier MP Materials gave the government a 15% stake in exchange for a $400 million investment coupled with a $150 million loan, offtake agreements (which are guaranteed purchases of its output), and profit sharing. Another critical minerals company, USA Rare Earth, gave up a 10% stake for a $277 million award and a $1.3 billion loan. And Intel set an even more awkward precedent. The Biden administration had already awarded the company $8.9 billion that hadn’t yet been paid out. Last year, the Trump administration turned that money into a roughly 10% stake in Intel. The list goes on .
Outside the U.S., Germany-based fusion startup Proxima Fusion confirmed to TechCrunch that the German government and the European Union are on its cap table. It also has received equity investments from German government-backed funds, including SPRIND (Germany’s federal agency for disruptive innovation) and DCTF (Deutsche Climate Tech Fonds).
Not every fusion startup that has worked with the government has given up equity. Thea Energy and Avalanche Energy, which have received federal awards and contracts, and Pacific Fusion, which has partnered with federal labs, confirmed to TechCrunch that they have not given the government a stake. Inertia Enterprises also told TechCrunch that it had not given the government any equity; the startup has a public-private partnership with the Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory to commercialize the fusion technology developed there.
So far, it’s just a handful of startups that have agreed to government stakes in exchange for awards. Still, it could set the tone for the industry.
By directly investing in fusion startups, the Trump administration is signaling that fusion power is a strategic priority for the U.S. Such backing could boost investor confidence, though it could just as easily have a chilling effect on private investment. VCs will now have to weigh whether the dilution from a government stake is worth the trade-off. And what happens to cap tables in case of pay-to-play rounds or wind-downs? Who gets priority?
The fusion industry may have raised billions of dollars in recent years, but it will need billions more to deliver on its promises. Federal awards used to be no-brainers when it came time to scale up. Now they’ve grown more complicated. Will the new bargains be worth it?

title: 2027: ADC dismisses APC’s 2m votes target for Tinubu in Jigawa‎
body: By Muhammad Inuwa ‎The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has expressed confidence that its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, will win Jigawa State in the 2027 general elections, dismissing the All Progressives Congress (APC)’s target of delivering two million votes for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu as unrealistic. ‎The ADC candidate for Ringim/Taura Federal Constituency in Jigawa State, Hon. Shehu Sule Udi, stated this while reacting to the Jigawa APC’s declaration that it would deliver two million votes for Tinubu’s re-election. ‎Udi argued that the number of registered voters in Jigawa State made the APC’s target questionable, describing the declaration as political propaganda. ‎According to him, figures displayed by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) showed that Jigawa had 2,807,811 registered voters. ‎“This clearly shows that the party is just making propaganda,” he said. ‎“Look at how our presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, and other candidates in ADC are gaining support across Jigawa State every day. For somebody to tell you that they will deliver two million votes to Tinubu is ridiculous,” Udi stated. ‎He claimed that residents of the state were dissatisfied with the current administration because of the economic hardship facing Nigerians. ‎“People of Jigawa State are tired of this administration. They have suffered enough, and no reasonable person will vote for the APC in the coming election. ‎“Our presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, will win Jigawa State with massive votes and defeat President Bola Ahmed Tinubu,” he said. ‎Udi maintained that the ADC remained a credible alternative capable of addressing the economic challenges facing the country. ‎He expressed confidence that the growing support for the party across Jigawa State would translate into electoral victory in 2027. ‎The ADC candidate spoke while welcoming defectors from other political parties in Ringim and Taura Local Government Areas, describing their decision to join the party as a boost to its political strength ahead of the elections. The post 2027: ADC dismisses APC’s 2m votes target for Tinubu in Jigawa‎ appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Ebola patient arrives in Switzerland, as Nigeria sustains surveillance
body: By Sola Ogundipe Swiss authorities confirmed on Monday that Nigeria’s imported Ebola case and her spouse have arrived in Switzerland, where she is receiving treatment at Geneva University Hospitals while he remains in isolation at University Hospital Zurich. The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Mohammadu Ali Pate, disclosed the development in a statement on his X handle. His words: “The Swiss authorities have confirmed that the patient and her spouse arrived safely in Switzerland today. She is receiving care at Geneva University Hospitals, while her spouse is in isolation at University Hospital Zurich. “In our telephone conversation, Federal Councillor Elisabeth Baume-Schneider conveyed Switzerland’s appreciation for the care provided by Nigerian health professionals and the close cooperation between our authorities and the World Health Organisation that made the evacuation possible. “I thank the clinical and public-health teams in Nigeria and Switzerland, the NCDC, @BAG_OFSP_UFSP , @EDI_DFI and @WHONigeria for their cooperation, and wish the patient continued recovery. “Here in Nigeria, contact monitoring, investigation of alerts and other containment measures continue, with support from @AfricaCDC and @WHOAFRO . We will provide regular updates through @NCDCgov and @Fmohnigeria,” he stated. The post Ebola patient arrives in Switzerland, as Nigeria sustains surveillance appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: US Army practices digging temporary battlefield graves
body: The Army is preparing for the grim possibility of burying fallen soldiers on the battlefield, testing how fast it can dig temporary graves while preserving remains for eventual identification and return to families after the end of a conflict. During an exercise in North Carolina, engineers, preventative medicine teams, chaplains and fatality management specialists prepared for mass temporary interment not used on a large scale since the Korean War, the Army announced in a release last week. For more than twenty years during wars in Iraq and Afghanistan, U.S. air superiority allowed the quick evacuation of remains back to the United States through mortuary affairs channels. Future conflicts — especially those with large-scale combat operations, or LSCO — may not have the same capabilities. Phase II of Operation Dragon Covenant challenged troops to test and validate temporary burial operations and remains preservation at a large scale. Engineer soldiers involved had to use their equipment to excavate and then fill burial trenches without damaging mock remains, made of skeletal models and water containers, so that hypothetical future forensic teams could unearth and repatriate them after the end of a conflict. Chaplain Maj. Warwick Fuller, 20th Engineer Brigade, XVIII Airborne Corps, leads a prayer to consecrate a designated battlefield temporary interment site, Oct., 20, 2026, Fayetteville, North Carolina. (Sgt. 1st Class Ange Desinor/U.S. Army) “This exercise allowed us to take a critical look at how we respect, honor, and systematically manage our fallen in a high-intensity conflict,” said Sgt. 1st Class Delbert Ruede, the senior fatality management leader for 3rd Corps Sustainment Command (CSC), in the release. “If we went to war tomorrow, we would be making this up as we went along. What we are doing here is taking a scientific, field-tested approach so that we can maintain positive control and respectfully care for our fallen.” The U.S. requires the evacuation of human remains when operations in wartime situations permit, but U.S. joint service guidance authorizes temporary graves during mass casualty incidents in war, where decedents cannot be safely moved due to safety, lack of transportation, or if the deaths are a result of chemical, biological, radiological or nuclear weapons. Soldiers, civilians or enemy combatants buried in temporary graves must be treated with dignity and their information — if available — preserved, the military dictates. The Geneva Conventions require that even the bodies of enemy forces be recorded and that identifying information be collected. Cremation is rarely authorized, save for hygiene or religious grounds. Army doctrine prescribes that temporary interment plots consist of five parallel trenches to hold 100 bodies, with ten bodies lining each side of the trenches. In previous trials, units using standard backhoes could excavate only one trench — and thus ten remains — per three hours. According to the service’s release, operators during the most recent exercise used D6 bulldozers to excavate a trench large enough for 20 remains in an average of one hour and 15 minutes. Based on that, commanders can plan for an engineer company with the requisite equipment to dig and cover trenches for up to 2,400 bodies every 24 hours, if operating nonstop. Operators also learned that published instructions on trench standards did not reflect current Army equipment. The service said that doctrine called for seven feet between rows, which the team found too narrow to drive a dozer without disrupting the burial trenches. This discovery, and any others, will be reflected in future Army doctrine. Beyond the physical trenches, the exercise also gave religious specialists and chaplains an opportunity to prepare for LSCOs by developing sensitive protocols. “In a high-intensity, contested combat environment, fatality management teams cannot stop a 24-hour interment operation for individualized religious gravesite services,” Lt. Col. Ruska, chaplain for the 3rd CSC, said in the release. The team, he added, also may be unable to determine an individual’s faith after death. “We consulted with Chaplains from various low density faith groups for advisement,” he said. “The consensus was that by consecrating the site before remains are placed in the ground reassures families that their loved ones are treated with reverence, dignity and honor despite the inability to provide a memorial ceremony in a contested combat environment.” The exercise will continue, the Army said, with Phase III of Dragon Covenant in Spring 2027, integrating security, medical facilities and a mortuary affairs collection point.

title: France tests counter-drone laser aboard Charles de Gaulle aircraft carrier at sea
body: A French Air and Space Force team installed the weapon module on the carrier’s flight deck in approximately four hours. It included cameras, LIDAR, a laser-generation system, a cooling unit and an operator console. The team comprised personnel from the service’s expertise centre at Mont-de-Marsan and an air defence squadron at Istres. Charles de Gaulle was expected to enter the Gulf of Oman during the experiment. The trials took place during a deployment that ended on 11 July 2026, after the crew spent 166 days at sea. The account did not specify how many drones were engaged or provide detailed test results. An unnamed French Air and Space Force non-commissioned officer told Cols Bleus that it was the system’s first trial aboard a naval vessel. That description remains uncertain because the photographed equipment reportedly resembles HELMA-P, which France had already tested at sea. The French Navy tested HELMA-P aboard the Horizon-class frigate Forbin in June 2023 under the L2AD programme. The Ministry of the Armed Forces said the system demonstrated effectiveness and precision in neutralising drones at sea, following land-based trials in 2020–2021. A laser of that type also remained available to the military during the Paris Olympic Games in 2024. The account does not establish whether the carrier trial involved the same system or a different configuration. The report also described earlier testing of the 20–35 kW LOCUST laser aboard USS George H.W. Bush. Installed in a flight-deck container and powered by the carrier’s electrical network, that system reportedly completed trials in October 2025 before seeing combat use in the Gulf of Oman several months later.

title: Air Force Plans $1 Billion Campus for Testing F-47 at Nellis
body: The Air Force is taking the first steps to build a $1 billion campus including hangars, laboratories, maintenance and training facilities, and more to test the F-47 at Nellis Air Force Base, Nev.—and the service plans to finish construction by 2031 as it moves quickly to field the upcoming sixth-generation fighter. In a presolicitation notice posted Oct. 22, the Air Force said it is looking for as many as four qualified firms that can quickly work on a project to design and build the proposed F-47 campus. The entire project, including construction, design, security, and other expenses, will ultimately cost about $1.057 billion. The project would include a nearly 117,000-square foot facility, largely on the east side of Nellis, combining flightline operations and maintenance. It would also have a specialized laboratory for reprogramming the plane’s systems, an aircraft apron with sunshades, and a nearly 41,000-square foot simulator facility. The notice lists several other facilities that could be built later as “potential subsequent work,” including additional hangars for fuel system maintenance, corrosion control of its stealth coating, weapons load training, maintenance training, and other maintenance needs. The Air Force plans to issue an initial award for the F-47 campus in February 2027, which would then kick off about nine months of design and preconstruction, and then about 40 more months of more intensive construction into early March 2031. The presolicitation notice for the campus provides the latest window on how the Air Force is preparing to bring the Boeing-made F-47 into its fleet. It follows the Air Force’s 2027 budget proposal, which requested $730 million for hangars and other support infrastructure for the F-47 and revealed its operational testing will take place at Nellis. The Air Force in March 2025 announced it had chosen Boeing to build the F-47, which will replace the F-22 Raptor sometime in the 2030s and eventually make up 20 percent of the Air Force’s fleet . It is expected to have advanced stealth, data sharing, and electronic warfare capabilities, and it will be able to direct semi-autonomous drone fighters known as Collaborative Combat Aircraft. Former Air Force Chief of Staff Gen. David Allvin said in September 2025 that the first F-47 fighter was in the process of being built and would fly in 2028. Service officials have stuck to that schedule ever since and said its first flight will take place before the end of the Trump administration. Allvin also said in a May 2025 social media post that the F-47 will be able to fly faster than Mach 2, or more than 1,500 miles per hour, and have a combat radius of more than 1,000 nautical miles, far more than the F-22 or F-35A Joint Strike Fighter. That expanded range would give the F-47 an advantage in a potential conflict with China, where aircraft will have to fly long distances over stretches of the Pacific Ocean. The post Air Force Plans $1 Billion Campus for Testing F-47 at Nellis appeared first on Air & Space Forces Magazine .

title: Skydance offers buyouts, orders return to office
body:
Skydance , as it embarks on the work to integrate the businesses of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery, is offering certain employees a voluntary buyout in a “one-time offer.”
The new program was outlined by chairman and CEO David Ellison and co-CEO Ynon Kreiz in a memo to staffers Monday.
“As we bring our teams together, we recognize that not everyone will see their future here, and we respect that. To give eligible employees the option to move on in a way that works for them, we are introducing a Voluntary Buyout (VBO) Program,” the execs wrote. “Those who qualify will receive an individual communication with their personalized details and terms, and a window to decide whether to accept this one-time offer.” Related Stories Lionsgate Promotes Scott Herbst to President of Television Group Lionsgate Forms Joint Venture With Steven Paul, Movie Producer Who Has Had Trump's Ear
They added, “Please know we don’t take any of this lightly. We are clear about what we’re building: a company that tells the stories people around the world love, embraces new ways to connect with audiences, and leads the next era of media and entertainment. We have the talent, the creative firepower and the ambition to do it, and we will get there together.”
Across Skydance, there are different eligibility criteria and deadlines by which employees must confirm they’re taking a buyout (for example, if the jobs are union or non-union or if a staffer is on contract or an at-will employee), according to sources familiar with the situation. In general, the buyout opt-in deadlines fall around the second week in November.
Paramount’s massive $111 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery closed on Oct. 6. In their “Day One” memo to employees that day, Ellison and Kreiz (who was the CEO of Mattel before joining the new Skydance earlier this month) acknowledged that layoffs will be part of the process. “Integrating two companies will bring change, including difficult decisions that affect our workforce,” the execs wrote in that memo. “We are committed to handling this process thoughtfully and respectfully.”
In the Oct. 26 memo, Ellison and Kreiz also said the new Skydance is moving to a mandatory five-days-per-week in-office policy across the company. “We believe in-person collaboration is vital to our culture and to the success of our business. Especially in a creative company like ours, the best ideas come from people in the same room, sharing perspectives, challenging one another and solving problems,” the execs said. “We truly believe this is in the best interest of our company and our people. We’ve seen the benefits firsthand at Paramount, and we want every part of Skydance to share in them.”
Skydance execs have said they are shooting to achieve more than $6 billion in cost savings on an annualized basis within three years, and part of that will come from layoffs. The company has not revealed at this point the extent of the job cuts it expects. According to a report issued by Los Angeles County in August, the Paramount-Warner Bros. merger could result in the loss of some 4,500 film and TV jobs over three years in L.A. alone.
Read the full memo sent by Skydance’s top brass Monday, a copy of which was obtained by Variety :
At Skydance, our goal is to build the next-generation media and entertainment company, powered by creativity and technology. We are creative-first, audience focused, tech-forward and globally scaled. And in a world of endless choice and fierce competition for attention, we don’t just want to succeed. We want to win.
To do that, we must be a strong, connected and agile company. Among our business and creative priorities, none matters more than building a strong culture, because it’s the foundation of everything we want to achieve. Winning requires us to work as one team: one company, fully aligned. That means communicating openly and collaborating efficiently across every part of the organization.
We believe in-person collaboration is vital to our culture and to the success of our business. Especially in a creative company like ours, the best ideas come from people in the same room, sharing perspectives, challenging one another and solving problems. Being together isn’t just about showing up. It’s about inspiring one another, learning and coaching, forming friendships and having the casual conversations that spark something great.
With that in mind, we will adopt a five-day in-office policy across all of Skydance. We truly believe this is in the best interest of our company and our people. We’ve seen the benefits firsthand at Paramount, and we want every part of Skydance to share in them.
While many of you are already in the office five days a week, we understand this may be a significant change to the daily routines of others. To give you time to plan and adjust, we will take a phased approach by location. You will receive ample notice before changes take effect, and we will work closely with managers to support you through the transition.
As we bring our teams together, we recognize that not everyone will see their future here, and we respect that. To give eligible employees the option to move on in a way that works for them, we are introducing a Voluntary Buyout (VBO) Program. Those who qualify will receive an individual communication with their personalized details and terms, and a window to decide whether to accept this one-time offer.
We recognize this is a significant decision, and we want you to feel informed and supported. If this applies to you, please review your materials carefully and reach out to your leadership or HR representative with any questions. FAQs and other resources are available on the Skydance Integration Hub, and HR support is also available through My Paramount (legacy Paramount employees) or Ask Employee Connection on WBD One (legacy Warner Bros. employees).
Please know we don’t take any of this lightly. We are clear about what we’re building: a company that tells the stories people around the world love, embraces new ways to connect with audiences, and leads the next era of media and entertainment. We have the talent, the creative firepower and the ambition to do it, and we will get there together.
Thank you for your commitment, and for the creativity and passion you bring to your work every day.

title: Erdogan Dismisses EU Opposition to Turkish-Libyan Maritime Memorandum
body: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan has dismissed European Union objections to the Turkish-Libya n maritime memorandum, insisting Ankara will not abandon its claims in the Eastern Mediterranean. Speaking after a cabinet meeting, Erdogan welcomed the unanimous approval of the 2019 memorandum by Libya’s House of Representatives, describing the decision as a significant step in protecting what Turkey considers its maritime rights. He also criticised the EU and countries opposing the agreement, accusing them of attempting to exclude Turkey from the Eastern Mediterranean. Erdogan hails unanimous approval of memorandum Erdogan presented the Libyan parliament’s decision as a diplomatic success for Ankara, highlighting the unanimous vote as evidence of agreement among Libyan political factions. “On November 27, 2019, we signed with the Libyan Government of National Accord the strategically important memorandum on the delimitation of maritime zones,” Erdogan said. “This memorandum was a major step that ensures the legitimate rights of Turkey and Libya in the Eastern Mediterranean.” He welcomed the unanimous approval by Libya’s House of Representatives last week, arguing that it reflected a shared commitment to Libya’s national interests despite internal political divisions. According to Erdogan, the agreement also reinforced Turkey’s longstanding position in support of a unified Libya. “Another important aspect of the decision is that our Libyan brothers, despite their political differences, are acting together on issues that concern their national interests,” he said. Erdogan rejects EU criticism The Turkish president strongly rejected the EU’s response to the memorandum, claiming European objections lacked a legal basis. “The reactions that were expressed after the approval of the memorandum, led by the European Union, have no legal basis,” Erdogan said. He maintained that Turkey’s policy in the Eastern Mediterranean was focused on protecting its interests in maritime zones rather than imposing unilateral outcomes. “Our only interest is to protect our rights and interests in the maritime zones,” he said. Erdogan also called for disputes to be resolved peacefully through dialogue with countries bordering the Eastern Mediterranean. “We support addressing disputes by peaceful means and resolving them through dialogue with all coastal countries,” he said, adding that he expected the EU and other international actors to demonstrate the same willingness. Ankara warns against efforts to exclude Turkey Erdogan issued a warning to countries opposing the agreement, insisting that international criticism would not alter Ankara’s foreign policy. “Turkey is not a country that pays attention to such statements nor does it shape its policy based on them,” he said. He added that Turkey’s national interests would remain the guiding principle of its foreign policy, even if defending those interests came at a cost. “I remind once again those who are trying to exclude Turkey from the Eastern Mediterranean that we expect them to show respect for the common will of our country and Libya,” Erdogan said. The remarks underline Ankara’s determination to maintain its position in the Eastern Mediterranean despite continued opposition to the maritime agreement from Greece, Cyprus and the European Union. The memorandum, signed in November 2019 between Turkey and Libya’s then internationally recognised Government of National Accord, established a disputed maritime boundary between the two countries. Greece and other regional actors reject the agreement, arguing that it disregards the maritime rights of Greek islands, including Crete, and conflicts with the principles of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS). Erdogan calls for unity in Libya Erdogan also addressed Libya’s internal political divisions, saying Turkey wanted to see greater stability across the country. “As Turkey, we no longer want to see divisions and rivalries in Libya or any other Muslim country,” he said. He pledged that Ankara would continue engaging with all relevant parties to support dialogue and cooperation. Erdogan concluded by congratulating Libya’s House of Representatives and sending greetings to the Libyan people, expressing hope that cooperation between the two countries would continue. The memorandum remains a major source of regional tension, with Greece and its partners maintaining that the agreement cannot override the maritime rights of Greek islands under international law. title: Russia ranks first globally by natural gas reserves
body:
MOSCOW, October 26. /TASS/. Russia ranks first globally in terms of natural gas reserves and second by its production, the presidential press service told reporters.
"Our country is world’s first by natural gas reserves and second by production, has the developed infrastructure and considerable technological groundwork. Gradual diversification of supplies to the East continues," the Kremlin said.
Russia considers important to counter creation of barriers on the path of the free exchange of energy resources and to protect the critical gas infrastructure, the press service added.

title: Federal Reserve is likely to hold interest rates steady in October. Here's what that means for consumers
body:
The Federal Reserve is expected to leave interest rates unchanged at its upcoming October meeting — even as higher energy costs complicate the inflation outlook and put additional pressure on household budgets.
The consumer price index , a broad measure of inflation, rose again in September, bringing the annual inflation rate up to 3.7%. Surging oil prices stemming from the U.S. war with Iran also helped drive September's producer price index higher. On Friday, Brent crude oil was trading at a five-month high before falling slightly.
The Fed raised rates by 25 basis points to a range of 3.75% to 4% last month, its first hike since 2023 . But fed funds futures last priced in less than a 10% chance the central bank will raise rates by another quarter point at its meeting this week, according to the CME Group's FedWatch tool. Nearly 75% expect at least one hike by year-end.
"Inflation is still the No. 1 problem in the U.S. economy, and there are a lot of signs it is getting more broad-based," said Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union. "For consumers, it means really high borrowing costs for the foreseeable future."
However, "given that it's right before an election," she added, "they won't hike in October."
The central bank's upcoming meeting comes just days before the midterm elections and marks the final word on the pace of inflation in the U.S. before voters head to the polls, which could impact how much power each political party has in Washington.
In previous election cycles, the Fed has mostly maintained its charted course, research shows. The four times the Fed raised rates near a midterm — 1978, 1982, 2018 and 2022 — were all tied to rising inflation, according to Mark Shore, director and economist at CME Group .
Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh has expressed a commitment to bringing inflation down to the Fed's 2% target . "If the Fed holds, markets could question the Fed's inflation-fighting credibility," said Bank of America economist Aditya Bhave in a research note on Oct. 23.
The Fed's benchmark interest rate determines what banks charge one another for overnight loans. That rate then influences a wide range of consumer borrowing and savings rates. However, while higher interest rates can help ease inflationary pressures, they also raise borrowing costs in the near term, adding to the affordability crunch many households already face.
Shorter-term rates are closely tied to the prime rate , which is typically 3 percentage points above the federal funds rate. Longer-term borrowing costs, meanwhile, are driven more by inflation expectations and broader economic conditions.
"Higher longer-term rates are doing more damage to consumer wallets, as they've risen more than short-term rates, and are weighing heavily on refinancing activity, homebuying and vehicle sales," said Mark Zandi, chief economist at Moody's. "Higher short-term rates also hurt, but mostly by raising rates on credit cards, consumer finance loans and home equity lines."
Most credit cards carry variable rates that move closely with the Fed's benchmark rate. As a result, if the Fed leaves rates unchanged, credit card APRs are likely to remain near current levels. The average interest rate on a new credit card offer is now 23.96%, according to LendingTree .
Mortgage rates , by contrast, are influenced more by Treasury yields and the economic outlook. The yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury , which serves as a benchmark for many long-term loans, has been near 5%, helping keep the average rate on a 30-year fixed mortgage close to 7.4%, according to Mortgage News Daily .
Auto loan rates are shaped by several factors, including the Fed's benchmark rate. With financing costs still elevated, many car buyers are taking on larger loans and extending repayment terms to cope with affordability challenges, according to Edmunds.
Federal student loan rates are fixed for the life of the loan, but rates for new borrowers are already higher in the current academic year based on the results of the 10-year Treasury note auction held in May.
Savings rates tend to track changes in the federal funds rate, which is a rare upside to the higher-for-longer rate outlook. Because the Fed has kept rates elevated, savers continue to benefit from relatively attractive yields on high-yield savings accounts and other deposit products.

Apple has just released iOS 27.2, bringing Apple Pencil support to the iPhone Duo. The software update also includes an “Edge Light” feature for the iPhone Duo that’s intended to illuminate your face during video calls.
Apple previously said the iPhone Duo would add support for the Apple Pencil “later this year.” The company’s first foldable comes with revamped iOS 27 controls designed to work across the device’s 7.6-inch inner display and 5.4-inch outer screen. Many major apps , like Netflix, Prime Video, and Microsoft Outlook, already support the Duo’s extra screen real estate, but some still need some work .
The iOS 27.2 update also allows Siri AI to take suggested actions in Messages, while adding support for Siri AI in more languages , including French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish. Apple is rolling out support for Google’s SynthID AI watermark in Photos and Image Playground, too, according to 9to5Mac .
Other smaller but notable updates include user profiles on the Apple TV app on iPhone. The Apple Podcasts app is also replacing its “Up Next” queue with a list of “New Episodes,” along with a “Continue Playing” section just beneath it. You’ll also see the new Apple Music logo . And group calls on FaceTime now support dual capture so you can show both what’s visible from your selfie cam and your back cameras.
Apple also released macOS 27.2 Golden Gate , watchOS 27.2 , visionOS 27.2 , tvOS 27.2 , and HomePod 27.2 .

title: Intel quietly confirms Raptor Lake Next CPUs through internal driver publication
body: Intel has published an internal test driver with the "RPL-NEXT" label, presumably in reference to Raptor Lake Next CPUs that Tom's Hardware first reported on in June. On the same day as the driver was uncovered, shipping manifests from Vietnam were published by Club386 , showing exports of CPUs labeled "Raptor Lake Next" dating back to August, complete with cache and clock speed information. ➡️ https://t.co/jatYVFZ9eg October 26, 2026 The driver was first spotted by @momomo_us on X, and we were able to find it by searching the name in Intel's software database . The file is locked (hence the padlock icon), and clicking on it will redirect you to an Intel login page. Given that and the "testbuild" label, it looks like this is an internal driver test that wasn't meant to be published. Judging by the existing conventions, the driver package is for the Smart Sound Technology (SST), a audio digital signal processor integrated into the silicon since the Alder Lake days. Audio codecs like those of Realtek use SST for offloading duties like noise reduction, echo cancellation, low-power audio playback, and wake-on-voice without adding to the CPU load, and saving precious watts in the process. For broader context, Raptor Lake Next is Intel's refresh of the Raptor family of CPUs, meant to plug into existing LGA-1700 motherboards. Given the currently insane DDR5 memory prices, gamers ought to be happy on two fronts: getting newer chips for their existing motherboards, and the ability to use more affordable DDR4 instead, an ability all but confirmed by Gigabyte's recent BIOS updates. According to Club386's shipping manifests, there are so far four chip models en route from Intel's Vietnam facilities. Their specs suggest that they're replacements for extant Core i5 and Core i7 models, as a previous leak indicates that Intel doesn't yet have any plans for replacements for its Core i9-14900K chip. As such, the listed models should top out with the 99DLMV part number, with 16 cores in an 8P + 8E arrangement, a meaty 3.5 GHz base block, and 30 MB of cache (presumably L3). This is the only model with a 125W TDP, and its base clock is higher than that of the Core i9-14900K, so it should be a speedy enough affair despite not having the high core counts of the halo models. Chances are it'll be a nice gaming CPU with pretty high turbo clocks, but only reviews will confirm that. Interestingly, the 99DLMT has 20 cores (8P + 12E), but its much lower 65W TDP and 2.1 GHz base clock, which indicate that this model might be an efficiency-oriented productivity chip. In the table below, we added our guesses as to which models match existing chips. Part number Cores / Threads TDP Base clock Cache Approximate matches 99DLMV 8P + 8E (24) 125 W 3.5 GHz 30 MB i7-14700 / i7-13700 99DLMT 8P + 12E (28) 65 W 2.1 GHz 33 MB i5-14600K / 13700K 99DLMW 6P + 4E (16) 65 W 2.6 GHz 24 MB i5-14400 / i5-13500 99DLMX n/a 65 W 2.6 GHz 24 MB As above There's no word about pricing, but we'd expect the new chips to ring in at roughly the prices of the existing models. As points of reference, the Core i7-14700 is currently $366 , or $330 for the "F" variant without integrated graphics. At the lower end of the above table, the Core i5-14400 is sitting at $208 , or only $161 without an IGP.

title: Pentagon announces first US submarine joining Submarine Rotational Force-West
body: The Pentagon on Monday announced the first submarine to be assigned to an Australian rotational force comprising four U.S. fast-attack submarines and one UK fast-attack submarine. The USS Colorado will be the first U.S. Navy Virginia-class fast-attack submarine assigned to Submarine Rotational Force-West, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced in conjunction with representatives from the United Kingdom and Australia. SRF-West, which is expected to reach initial operating capacity in 2027, will assist a fleet of U.S. and British nuclear-powered fast attack submarines aboard Australia’s HMAS Stirling installation near Perth. “SRF-West will accelerate Australia’s readiness to own, operate, maintain, and regulate a sovereign, conventionally armed, nuclear-powered submarine capability, as well as support submarine deployments by expanding maintenance options and sustainment infrastructure in the region for AUKUS partners,” a Pentagon statement read. AUKUS is a trilateral security partnership between Australia, the United Kingdom and the United States designed to promote a safe Indo-Pacific region. The U.S. stood up Naval Support Activity Stirling in Western Australia in June, providing “services and programs for U.S. service members, civilian personnel, contractors and their families” assigned to Submarine Rotational Force–West, according to a service release . The new rotational force will increase the region’s maintenance resources and bolster a sustainment framework. On May 30 in Singapore, Hegseth met with Australian Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Defence Richard Marles and UK Secretary of State for Defence John Healey to discuss AUKUS objectives to defend the Indo-Pacific region. The Australian and UK officials confirmed that Australia was slated to meet its scheduled delivery of a conventionally armed, nuclear-powered submarine in the next few years. The four officials also emerged from the meeting with news that the three nations were focused on developing and fielding uncrewed undersea vehicles to provide defensive and offensive military capabilities throughout the region.

title: Oil ticks lower as Saudi defense minister meets with Iran's president in Tehran to de-escalate
body:
Crude oil prices ticked lower Monday as Saudi Arabia's defense minister held talks with Iranian leaders in Tehran in an effort to ease simmering tensions between the two countries.
Brent crude futures lost 91 cents to close at $115.81 a barrel after briefly topping $117 earlier in the session. U.S. West Texas Intermediate fell $1.51 to settle at $101.76. Prices have gained about 12% this month.
Saudi Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman met Monday with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei.
Pakistan's Army Chief of Staff Asim Munir and the head of Turkish intelligence Ibrahim Kalin also participated in the talks. Pakistan and Turkey are members of a defense pact with Saudi Arabia.
The meeting in Tehran came as Iran-allied Houthi militants in Yemen have repeatedly attacked Saudi Arabia in recent weeks. Houthi strikes on civilian targets, such as airports, threaten to escalate the conflict in the Middle East.
The Houthis said Monday that they fired missiles at Saudi Arabia's international airport in Riyadh and launched drones at oil pumping stations. The Saudis have not confirmed those strikes took place.
The ongoing hostilities have some investors worried about the vulnerability of Saudi Arabia's energy infrastructure and the risk of another major disruption to production, refining or export facilities.
Another disruption would come as global inventory levels have fallen sharply after eight months of conflict. The U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve, for example, is at its lowest level since 1982.
Geopolitical uncertainty has already added roughly $20 a barrel to oil prices, said Michael Alfaro, chief investment officer at Gallo Partners.
A substantial strike on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline or additional refining infrastructure could send prices sharply higher, Alfaro said. But prices jumping above $120 would also destroy demand, he said.
Beyond the immediate threat to crude supplies, damage to refining infrastructure could pose a more persistent challenge to global energy markets.
"The real challenge is refining capacity," Alfaro said, warning that the disruptions could develop into a longer-term structural problem extending into 2027 and beyond.
Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia plans to begin storing crude oil in Singapore from the second half of 2027, according to energy ministers from both countries, in a move aimed at strengthening the resilience of its Asian supply chain.
In the U.S., the Energy Department on Friday authorized the release of up to 400,000 barrels from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve to address a supply disruption at a Louisiana refinery.
Still, the prospect of additional supply from American producers remains uncertain, with companies reluctant to commit to major new investments amid volatile prices and geopolitical risks.
Alfaro added that U.S. producers were adding some drilling rigs, but remained cautious about substantially increasing capital expenditure.
"We're not really seeing major capex additions to bring new rigs on or bring new production online," he said.

title: President Herzog receives credentials of five new ambassadors to Israel day before elections
body: President Isaac Herzog diverted from his efforts to promote a national unity government to receive the credentials of five new ambassadors to Israel on Monday.Under the country's current government, Maj.-Gen. Emmanuel Bayingana of Rwanda, Christophe Parisot of France, Arad Benko of Austria, Stella Ronner Grubacic of the Netherlands, and Evelyn Korantemaa Ofosu-Amable of Ghana were the last ambassadors to present their credentials.They will serve out their terms under Israel's next government.Israel and Rwanda established relations in the early 1960s, but severed them in 1973. Decades later, in 1998, Israel and Rwanda renewed their relations, which have remained cordial. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu visited Rwanda in 2016, and Rwanda President Paul Kagame visited Israel in July 2017 in return.Since taking office in the immediate aftermath of the Rwandan genocide, Kagame has spent the past 26 years rebuilding his country and forming strong international partnerships. Israel and Rwanda cooperate on many levels, including innovation, technology, agriculture, and security. Rwanda and Israel signed several bilateral agreements earlier this year when Rwanda's Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe visited Israel.Bayingana said that he would work to further expand the relationship between the two countries.Neither Herzog nor Parisot tried to pretend that relations between France and Israel were rosy. However, Parisot noted that, despite their diplomatic challenges, the people-to-people relations and cultural ties between France and Israel remained strong.Herzog and Parisot also discussed the chaos and unrest that have overtaken France in recent weeks. Herzog recalled how different Champs-Élysées had felt when he accompanied his late father, then-president Chaim Herzog, on a state visit to France in 1988.Herzog recalls time of 'amazing' French-Israeli relationsHerzog also recalled a time when relations between France and Israel were so positive they were “amazing.”Parisot later wrote in the guest book that he would devote all of his energy to improving relations between the two countries.Benko previously said returning to Israel felt like coming home. Indeed, it was. He was born in Haifa; he left the country as a child, and returned some 20 years ago as a spokesman for the Austrian embassy. He said that when he left Israel, he had a hard time in school because the only language he spoke was Hebrew. Aside from the usual diplomatic subjects and antisemitism, Benko and Herzog also discussed the Jews of Austria.Michal Herzog, the president's wife, seldom sits in on the presentation of diplomatic credentials. This time, however, she attended the meetings with both the French and Austrian ambassadors and joined the ensuing conversations.While welcoming Rubacic, Herzog spoke of the “special relationship” between Israel and the Netherlands. But he also expressed concern over the discourse emanating from Holland and some of the government's own negative comments. He warned that Israel and Holland's relations were currently under strain. Rubacic replied that she was happy to be in Israel and stressed the importance of highlighting the good relations between the two countries, which are based on shared values.The significance Israel attaches to its ties with the Netherlands was evident in the brief, closed-door tete-a-tete Herzog had with the ambassador after the formalities concluded.Most African countries with which Israel has diplomatic ties are proud of their culture and heritage. Ghana is no exception. Ofosu-Amable and her entourage arrived at the President's Residence in national dress. Herzog was struck by the swell of colors and commented on it. He also noted that Israel's relations with Ghana span seven decades, dating back to when former premier Golda Meir made her historic visit to Africa.Israel trained Ghanaian soldiers early in relationshipIn the early years of their relationship, Israel helped to train soldiers in Ghana's army. Ghana stands out for the confidence it places in its women. Many of the country's diplomats and high-ranking officials are women, and the ambassador is among them.Where Israel and Ghana differ is their stance on a two-state solution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. Ghana's President John Mahama told Ofosu-Amable that she must remember that her mission is to uphold Ghana's longstanding commitment to the two-state solution.

title: 2027: INEC seeks inclusive polls, sensitises PWDs, Electoral Officers in Benue
body: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Benue State has held a sensitisation workshop for Persons With Disabilities (PWDs), Electoral Officers (EOs) and Disability Desk Officers, targeting improved accessibility, effective deployment of assistive devices and inclusive participation in the 2027 general elections. The workshop, organised by the commission ahead of the elections, was designed to strengthen stakeholders’ understanding of disability inclusion, electoral rights and interventions aimed at ensuring that eligible voters with disabilities can participate fully in the electoral process. Speaking at the event, the Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) in Benue State, Mallam Aminu Idris, said INEC was committed to engaging stakeholders to ensure the conduct of free, fair and credible elections, stressing that inclusivity was equally essential to achieving that objective. The REC said, “it is not just to have free, fair and credible elections. It is to have inclusive elections. If you leave a chunk of your population out, you cannot be talking about free, fair and credible elections.” He added that INEC had a dedicated department responsible for inclusivity and addressing the concerns of disadvantaged groups to ensure everyone had the opportunity to participate in the electoral process. He explained that the commission identifies voters with disabilities during registration to enable it determine the needs of different polling units and deploy appropriate materials and assistance noting that “the objective is to ensure that eligible voters who have registered and obtained their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) did not encounter unnecessary difficulties while voting.” On the participation of Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), the REC disclosed that INEC had conducted registration exercises at IDP locations in collaboration with non-governmental organisations interested in encouraging voter registration. He said “our officials visited the locations on two consecutive days to register eligible voters to ensure that they exercise their franchise during the election.” Addressing concerns over the collection of PVCs, Idris said “cards belonging to those who registered during the first phase of the Continuous Voter Registration exercise, conducted between August and December 2025, are available for collection at the local government level.” He added that cards for those who registered in 2026 would be ready subsequently before the elections. In his goodwill message, the Benue State Director of the National Orientation Agency (NOA), Comrade Mark Dewua, commended INEC for the initiative, saying “inclusive electoral participation is essential to strengthening democracy.” He urged for “accessible polling units, effective communication of electoral information, appropriate deployment of assistive devices and respectful treatment of voters with disabilities.” Dewua, who reaffirmed NOA’s commitment to collaborating with INEC on voter education and public enlightenment, urged political parties, civil society organisations, security agencies and the media to “work together to remove barriers to electoral participation.” He also encouraged PWDs to obtain their PVCs, verify their registration details and participate peacefully in the forthcoming elections. Similarly, the Chairman of the Joint National Association of Persons With Disabilities (JONAPWD), Benue State, Onah Adeyi, described the workshop as groundbreaking, noting that it provided an opportunity for PWDs to engage directly with INEC officials on issues affecting their participation in elections. Adeyi, who disclosed that “PWDs in the state have over 3,000 PVCs, and I am optimistic that the figure would increase following the ongoing collection exercise.” He urged INEC to consider qualified persons with disabilities for appointment as electoral officers, provide appropriate assistive devices for different disability groups and ensure that PWDs exercised their constitutional rights to vote and participate in the electoral process. Speaking on the objectives of the workshop, INEC Benue State Disability Desk Officer, Mnena Akuma, said “it is designed to strengthen stakeholders’ understanding of disability inclusion, accessibility and the effective deployment of the commission’s interventions throughout the electoral cycle.” She cited Section 54 of the Electoral Act, 2026, the Discrimination Against Persons With Disabilities (Prohibition) Act, 2018, and INEC’s framework on access and participation of PWDs as key instruments underpinning the initiative. Akuma listed the objectives of the workshop to include improving understanding of barriers confronting PWDs, strengthening the capacity of electoral officers to deploy assistive materials, promoting inclusive voter education and mobilising voters across disability groups. She identified the Braille Ballot Guide for visually impaired voters, EC30 written instruction posters for deaf voters, magnifying glasses for persons with visual impairment and albinism, and voter education materials in accessible formats as some of the interventions. She added that the workshop would strengthen collaboration between INEC, JONAPWD, Organisations of Persons with Disabilities and cluster heads, while generating practical recommendations to improve accessibility, compliance and inclusive participation ahead of the 2027 general elections.
