title: Apollo takes minority stake in Abu Dhabi’s Mubadala Capital
body: Mubadala Capital announced on Monday a strategic investment from Apollo to support its next phase of growth. Apollo will take a minority equity stake in Mubadala Capital and commit capital across its various investment strategies, the company said in a media release. Other strategic investors will also join as minority shareholders in Mubadala Capital , with an expected commitment of $5 billion to the firm’s investment strategies. Silver Rock Financial is also an equity holder in Mubadala Capital. Mubadala Investment Company remains the majority shareholder. After the addition of new equity shareholders, Mubadala Capital will continue to operate independently and maintain its own governance structure, with its existing management team retaining full authority over investment decisions and operations, according to the news release. “Mubadala Capital was built to connect the world’s capital with differentiated private market opportunities, and this partnership accelerates that ambition. Apollo is one of the most respected institutions in our industry, and their confidence in what we are building reflects the strength of the platform we’ve created and the trajectory we are on," said Hani Barhoush, chief executive of Mubadala Capital, adding that Apollo has been a "trusted partner" for several years. Founded in 2011, Mubadala Capital has rapidly grown into a next-generation alternative asset manager with a core alternatives business managing more than $60 billion across five investment strategies. As of late June, Apollo had about $1.05 trillion of assets under management. "This investment in the differentiated asset management platform they have built in Mubadala Capital builds on our existing partnership and reflects our conviction in their business," said John Zito, co-president of Apollo Asset Management said. "This investment will deepen our alignment and strengthen our mutual commitment to each other’s success, while creating significant opportunities to reach a broader global investor base.” The transaction is expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2026, subject to regulatory and legal approvals.

title: ADC to APC: Nigerians suffer, your youth leaders ride N1bn SUVs
body: By Luminous Jannamike The African Democratic Congress, ADC, has slammed the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, over the reported distribution of seven luxury sports utility vehicles (SUVs) worth about N1 billion to its youth leaders, accusing the ruling party of prioritising political mobilisation over the hardship facing Nigerians. The opposition party said the reported distribution exposed the contradiction between the economic sacrifices Nigerians are being asked to make and the privileges enjoyed by the ruling party’s political operatives, with millions struggling to afford food, transportation and other necessities. In a statement on Monday, ADC National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, said the development raised questions about the APC’s priorities as it prepares for the 2027 general elections. “President Tinubu asks Nigerians to endure hardship while his party distributes luxury vehicles to its political operatives. Apparently, sacrifice is for ordinary Nigerians, while luxury is reserved for those working to keep the APC in power,” he said. Abdullahi said the ruling party had mobilised resources for its political machinery without offering a convincing answer to the rising cost of living. “The APC has found the resources to move its campaign officials around Nigeria. What it has failed to find is a convincing way to make life affordable for the Nigerians whose votes it now seeks,” he said. The ADC also questioned the rationale for providing the vehicles for grassroots mobilisation ahead of the 2027 elections when youth unemployment and economic hardship remain major concerns. “Seven APC youth leaders can receive luxury vehicles, but millions of young Nigerians are still waiting for the jobs, opportunities and economic relief they were promised. Is this the APC’s idea of youth empowerment?” Abdullahi asked. The party demanded disclosure of the source of funding for the vehicles, including whether public resources were involved. “Nigerians deserve to know who paid for these vehicles. Until that question is answered, the ruling party cannot dismiss legitimate concerns about its priorities,” Abdullahi said. title: Delivery of grain storage sleeves to agricultural enterprises begins – URCS
body:
The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), the United Nations World Food Programme, the international non-profit organization Mercy Corps, and the Ukrainian Red Cross Society (URCS) have begun distributing grain silos to agricultural enterprises in Sumy region for crop storage.

"The first 57 grain storage sleeves have been delivered to three agricultural enterprises in the Sumy region. They will provide temporary storage for almost 10,000 tonnes of grain," the URCS said on Facebook on Monday.



In total, the program calls for the distribution of 1,516 grain bags to 257 agricultural producers in Sumy and Donetsk regions. The aid will reach 48 communities in nine districts. The program is being implemented with the support of the U.S. government in close cooperation with the Ministry of Agrarian Policy and Food of Ukraine, as well as the governments of Canada, the European Union, and the Howard G. Buffett Foundation.

title: Why I married Davita Lamai- Zlatan
body:
Nigerian rapper and singer Omoniyi “Zlatan” Raphael has revealed how he met his wife, Davita Lamai.
The Zanku Records founder and Davita held their traditional wedding in Oniru, Lagos State, on Saturday.
Several entertainment personalities attended the ceremony, including Davido, Kwam 1, Enioluwa Adeoluwa, Teni, Soso Soberekon, Abu Abel, Seyi Vodi, Small Doctor, Bella Shmurda and 9ice.
The 31-year-old and his wife have two sons, Shiloh and Benaiah.
During an interview posted on his YouTube channel , the “Zanku” crooner disclosed that he met Davita in London while pursuing his career.
The “Soro Soke” crooner said: “On my first trip to London, I really didn’t know anyone and didn’t know how the banking system over there worked. I linked up with someone else who wanted to talk about music and work with Davita. And then, after I was like, ‘Hello, can I take your number?’ I was like, ‘Can you come back and let’s see, you know?’”
“She was like, ‘Oh, she needs to ask the person that she came with.’ So, I was like, for this person to say she needs to… So, we started; it was more like God… I was like, ‘This is another person.’ She had a small car then, which she was helping me with.”
Zlatan said he felt their friendship would develop into something more after they exchanged contact details.
He explained that he couldn’t compare Davita’s love to anyone else’s because he hadn’t dated many women before their relationship began.
The singer attributed this to his early decision to focus on self-improvement and building a successful life.
“There’s always been something there. She’s always helped me with her car; she’s my support system. Change money for me. It was like a month. When I was young, I focused more on what I was going to eat than on chasing after any girl.
“So, there was no experience with too many girls. It’s not like a big difference. So, it was like I was growing. It was, like, a part in my life where I’ve just been filling up with the journey of my life. Like, every step, I’ve realised that it looks like it has been scripted by someone”, Zlatan said.
The singer credited God for directing his life, saying divine intervention led him to his wife.
“So, at the time I met her, it was like God… Every time something happens in my life, God fixes it. Like, when I went to school, I won a car when I was 19, when I wasn’t supposed to, and I wasn’t supposed to do music. I ended up doing music. And out of everybody, it worked out for me.”

title: Kodiak creator plans $2.25 million Reach AC-6 utility turboprop
body: Tom Hamilton, the aircraft developer behind the Kodiak single-engine turboprop and the Glasair and GlaStar kitplanes, is developing a new backcountry aircraft for operators seeking an affordable replacement for aging turboprops. His company, Reach Aviation, plans to offer the eight- to nine-seat AC-6 with turbine and diesel power options. Reach is targeting a $2.25 million price for the turboprop version, aimed at missionary groups, small commercial operators and private owners. Hamilton founded Reach in 2017 in Priest River, Idaho. The company is led by CEO Samuel Spear, a mechanical engineer who joined Reach early in its development and has worked with missionary aviation organizations including JAARS and Mission Aviation Training Academy. Hamilton serves as Founder and Board Director. Reach sees an opportunity between older utility aircraft, such as the de Havilland Beaver and Cessna 206, and more expensive turbine-powered replacements such as the Kodiak, now produced by Daher. The company says corrosion, structural fatigue and limited parts availability for older aircraft are making aging fleets harder to maintain, particularly for operators serving in remote countries. The AC-6 has a steel-tube fuselage frame covered by removable composite panels. Mechanics can remove the panels to inspect and repair fuel lines, flight controls and other systems. The windshield is also designed for quick removal, providing access behind the instrument panel. Reach says these features should reduce the work involved in inspections and repairs and help keep aircraft available for service. The cabin has eight feet of usable space behind the pilots and is intended to accommodate passenger seats, cargo or medical transport equipment. Reach’s design overview specifies a 42-inch cargo door, an optional door on the opposite side and an optional external cargo pod. Float attachment points are planned for every airframe. The company plans to pursue initial certification with a Pratt & Whitney Canada PT6A-34 turboprop engine. A second version would use a new 12-cylinder diesel from Ascent Engine Technologies. Both would burn Jet-A fuel. Reach describes the AC-6 as the intended launch aircraft for Ascent’s engine, which it lists in the 600-650 hp range. Hamilton has brought a utility aircraft through certification before. He founded Quest Aircraft in Sandpoint, Idaho, in 1999 to develop the 10-seat Kodiak, which received FAA certification in 2007. His earlier ventures included Stoddard-Hamilton Aircraft and composite-float manufacturer Aerocet. Reach said it is seeking investment partners to advance the AC-6. Its published design overview does not provide a certification or customer-delivery timetable, and the company continues to describe the aircraft as in development. title: Judge says DOJ illegally fired the daughter of former FBI director Comey
body:
Maurene Comey (R), daughter of former FBI Director James Comey, departs a courthouse in October 2025 in Alexandria, Va. Win McNamee/Getty Images hide caption
A New York federal judge ruled Monday that the Justice Department unlawfully fired former prosecutor Maurene Comey, who is the daughter of ex-FBI Director James Comey .
Maurene Comey served as a federal prosecutor in Manhattan for around a decade, working on high-profile cases against defendants like Sean "Diddy" Combs, Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell. The Trump Justice Department fired her in July 2025 despite her consistently receiving accolades from the department for her work.
In response, she sued the Justice Department and others, arguing that her dismissal was unlawful and unconstitutional. Her lawsuit said she was fired because her father is the former FBI director, a prominent critic of President Trump.
The Justice Department has twice indicted the elder Comey. The first case was dismissed. The second prosecution, which is still pending, accuses him of threatening the president in a photo of seashells posted on social media.
In his ruling Monday, U.S. District Judge Jesse Furman, a nominee of former President Barack Obama, wrote that the Department of Justice " invented a new and expansive theory of executive power " in dismissing Maurene Comey, and violated her constitutional right to due process.
"To accept Defendants' argument would be to unsettle the very equilibrium established by this Nation's constitutional system," the judge wrote.
The opinion adds to concerns of politically motivated dismissals at the DOJ. Several federal prosecutors and former FBI agents have sued the DOJ under the Trump administration over their dismissals, alleging that they were fired for political reasons tied to their work.
Comey's lawyers praised Monday's ruling, and said it reaffirms that the president must comply with the law as part of the Constitution's checks and balances.
"This hard-earned victory belongs to Ms. Comey, to all civil servants, and to all fighting for the rule of law," her attorneys said in a statement.
The judge's ruling calls for Comey to receive back pay dating to when she was fired last year, and for her to return as a prosecutor to the Southern District of New York, if she so chooses.
The Justice Department said it disagreed with the decision, and would appeal in due course.
The court's order is not final. Judge Furman did yet not rule on Maurene Comey's First Amendment argument that she was fired for politically protected speech, and plans to hear further briefings on that claim.

title: ADC fires back at APC over unpaid salary claims
body: dares ruling party to defend record By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress (ADC) has challenged the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to defend its record in government rather than make allegations against opposition parties, dismissing claims of unpaid salaries within the ADC as false and politically motivated. The party said the allegation was an attempt to divert attention from the economic hardship, rising cost of living, unemployment and insecurity confronting Nigerians, warning that the 2027 election debate should centre on the Tinubu administration’s performance. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC challenged the APC Presidential Campaign Council to produce evidence to substantiate its allegation, describing the claim as an attempt to distract Nigerians from the government’s record. “If the APC has any credible evidence to support its claims, it should produce it rather than continue to insult Nigerians with fabricated stories masquerading as press statements,” Abdullahi said. On the issues it believes should dominate public debate, the ADC said: “The real issue is the cost of living. The real issue is the absence of jobs and opportunities for our young people. The real issue is the insecurity that continues to threaten lives, livelihoods, and communities across the country.” The party also accused the APC of preparing for the 2027 elections by attacking opposition parties rather than presenting its achievements. “It is becoming increasingly clear that the APC has decided to run its 2027 campaign on allegations against the opposition rather than achievements of its own. That is what happens when a government has spent years making promises it cannot keep and excuses it cannot defend,” Abdullahi said. The ADC spokesman urged Minister of Information, Alake, and other APC officials to explain why Nigerians should support another term for the ruling party after three years of economic hardship and insecurity. “The APC may control the machinery of government, but it cannot control the lived experiences of Nigerians,” he said. Abdullahi said the ADC would remain focused on holding the Tinubu administration accountable, insisting that allegations against the opposition would not displace the economic concerns shaping public debate. “If the APC has a record to defend, let it defend it. If it has solutions, let it present them. But it should stop insulting the intelligence of Nigerians with these increasingly desperate distractions,” he added. The party maintained that the cost of living would remain central to its campaign, positioning the economic consequences of the Tinubu administration’s policies as a defining issue in the 2027 election. title: Mass killing threat: Enugu ex-lawmakers place N5m bounty on terrorist ringleaders
body: By Precious Enaike The Chairman of the forum of former members of Enugu State House of Assembly, Dr. Josef Onoh, announced Monday that they have placed a bounty of N5m on terrorists threatening mass killings in Enugu State after watching a viral video containing treasonable, cowardly and bloodthirsty threats of invasion against the peaceful domain of the state. These threats, Onoh said, issued by terrorists masquerading under whatever deceitful umbrella or criminal guise they claim, represent an intolerable assault on the collective security, sovereignty, and peace. Speaking on behalf of the Forum, in Abuja, Onoh categorically condemned the provocative rhetoric in the strongest possible terms and made it known clearly and unequivocally to the miscreants that Enugu State is not, and will never become, a playground for terrorists, bandits, or extremist agitators. According to him, stakeholders have built a heritage of peace, and no masked cowards chanting death threats will be allowed to disrupt the lives of the people. Onoh said the security of Enugu State remains paramount, and the forum will not fold its arms while fringe criminals attempt to intimidate our citizens or destabilize our homeland. “The forum stands resolutely behind the Enugu State Government and security agencies to crush any attempt at violating the peace of the state. To accelerate the wheels of justice and unmask every single criminal hiding under these guises, I have, on behalf of the forum of former members of Enugu State House of Assembly announced the strategic rewards of N5,000,000 (Five Million Naira) bounty for anyone who provides credible, actionable information to the Department of State Services (DSS), the Nigeria Police Force, or any other security agencies that leads directly to the arrest and prosecution of the main character chanting the death threats in the video, as well as any of his co-conspirators. “Furthermore, I would place a N50,000 (Fifty Thousand Naira) reward per name to any patriotic citizen who provides the full names and verified identities of each individual appearing in the video, along with details of their relatives, to the security agencies. I urge the DSS and all sister security apparatuses to launch an immediate, aggressive manhunt for the criminals. “To the good people of Enugu State, I urge them to remain calm, vigilant, and resilient and not be intimidated by the desperate rants of cowards while also reporting any suspicious movements or individuals to the nearest security agency immediately. Let me make it clear that Enugu State belongs to the peaceful and law-abiding individuals and forces of terror will always be defeated,” Onoh said. title: Siri AI is available in more languages starting today
body:
Siri AI is available in more languages starting today
With the 27.2 software updates released today, Siri AI — an entirely new version of Siri that is profoundly more capable, conversational, and personal — is expanding to more people around the world, with availability now in the French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish languages.
Siri AI is a completely reimagined version of Siri that is more personal and powerful, without compromising users’ privacy. Built on Apple Intelligence, it draws on personal context understanding to help users find what they need in the moment across their messages, emails, photos, and more. With even more systemwide app actions, Siri AI can help users with tasks such as drafting an email from scratch or editing and sharing a set of photos. With onscreen awareness, Siri AI can answer questions or take actions related to the content on a user’s screen. It can also use broad world knowledge to get up-to-date information on virtually any topic.
Language support for Siri AI will continue to expand, with availability in Chinese (Traditional), Norwegian, Turkish, and Vietnamese coming by the end of the year.

title: Ukraine adopts EU-linked law giving veterans priority in government hiring
body:
Ukraine’s parliament on Oct. 26 passed a law reinstating open competitions for civil service and local government positions, advancing long-delayed reforms tied to EU funding.
The law fulfills Ukraine's commitments under the Ukraine Facility , an EU financial assistance program launched in 2024, and unlocks 137 million euros ($153 million) in budget funding, Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi said.
Open and transparent job hirings will be reinstated gradually, he added. The law also gives veterans priority for civil service jobs.
President's Office Head Kyrylo Budanov, a former spy chief, said Ukraine should create conditions for veterans "to realize their potential in state institutions, local government, the economy, and the country's leadership."
"Ukrainian veterans have unique experience in leadership, responsibility, management, and decision-making under the most challenging conditions," Budanov said.
"Veterans must be among those shaping Ukraine's future."
According to Ukrainian officials, there are around 2 million veterans in Ukraine. The Veterans Affairs Ministry said that after the war ends, veterans and their close family members could make up one-sixth of the country's population, or up to six million people.
Over the past year, several prominent figures with military backgrounds have taken up senior positions in Ukraine's government. Around 66% of Ukrainians have a positive attitude toward veterans participating in politics, while 19% are neutral and 7% view it negatively or somewhat negatively, according to a 2025 poll by the Kyiv International Institute of Sociology (KIIS).

title: AFRL Targets New Hypersonic Engine Tech Prototypes Within 4 Years
body: The Air Force Research Laboratory wants industry to advance concepts for affordable hypersonic munition engines to prototype demonstrations within three to four years. AFRL released a request for information early this month, seeking white papers on technical requirements by Nov. 16. The notice is one of the first updates in months on its push for affordable rocket engines for hypersonic munitions. The Hermes Rocket Lab effort began in 2020 under AFRL’s Rocket Propulsion Division with a Broad Agency Announcement seeking novel concepts and research and development proposals to accelerate rocket engine technology. The latest white paper notice focuses on a specific kind of tech called rotating detonation rocket engine combined-cycle, or RDRE-CC. RDRE-CC systems use continuous detonation waves rather than deflagration, the combustion process used in conventional engines. The approach produces higher pressures and improves efficiency and thrust-to-weight ratio. The technology could increase range, speed, and payload while reducing rocket engine production costs. According to the lab’s notice, RDRE tech is at the proof of concept stage—in government parlance, at technology readiness level 3 of 9. AFRL wants industry to demonstrate a prototype in an “operationally relevant environment” within three to four years—the step associated with technology readiness level 6. Specifically, AFRL wants the prototype demonstration to be a “ground-launched, sounding-rocket-boosted flight demonstration to validate the system’s operational viability for future High-Speed Affordable Mass Munitions.” The Rocket Propulsion Division at Edwards Air Force Base, Calif., began HAMM market research in August and explored rocket-based combined-cycle technologies. That work led to the current RDRE-CC white paper notice. HAMM covers both high-supersonic and hypersonic speeds, with its most ambitious efforts targeting the hypersonic range. An AFRL spokesperson declined to answer specific questions on the latest notice from Air & Space Forces Magazine. “AFRL continues to monitor opportunities and information obtained through Request for Information (RFIs) and may release further details at the appropriate time,” spokesperson Aleah Castrejon wrote in an email. Industry Efforts The Air Force is already developing hypersonic munitions like the Air-Launched Rapid Response Weapon and the Hypersonic Attack Cruise Missile. Both those use scramjet and boost-glide systems that are more expensive to produce. Other approaches include pulse detonation engines, oblique detonation wave engines, and advanced supersonic combustion engines. But critics have noted challenges with each: Pulse detonation engines are more complex and costly to build; oblique detonation engines are harder to start and face challenges at lower speeds; and advanced supersonic combustion engines often need external boosters. Ramjets may also offer lower thrust-to-weight ratios than RDRE-CC technology could achieve. Companies are already developing RDRE-CC in various modes. GE Aerospace uses Turbine-Based Combined Cycle, combining a standard turbofan with a rotating detonation dual-mode ramjet. In 2023, GE laboratory tests validated continuous rotating detonation in supersonic airflow, a potential foundation for transitioning to Mach 5+ speeds. The company teamed up with Lockheed Martin this year to demo a liquid-fueled rotating detonation ramjet for high-speed and hypersonic standoff missile use. RTX, which includes Raytheon and Pratt & Whitney, uses an air-breathing, high-pressure combustion engine with rotating detonation combustors. The company began continuous-detonation research in 2011 and was later selected by the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency for its Gambit effort, which sought to develop a rotating detonation engine. Venus Aerospace uses a compact RDRE and rocket-based combined-cycle system dubbed the Venus Detonation Ramjet, which combines RDRE with a Ramjet to attempt to reach Mach 6 speeds without separate propulsion systems. In 2023, the company achieved long-duration, hot-fire tests of storable, liquid-propellant RDREs and ran drone-scale model flight tests for subsonic and low-supersonic stability. In 2024-2025, Venus demonstrated the VDR2 on test stands with DARPA. Aerojet Rocketdyne, part of L3Harris, works with pressure-gain combustion and RDRE tech to build both air-breathing and rocket applications. The company has conducted more than 500 static test firings in a variety of RDR and RDE configurations using multiple propellant combinations. They previously worked with AFRL and the Department of Energy on pressure-gain combustion modeling and other testing. IN Space, LLC focuses on injector designs, ignition systems, 3D manufacturing tech, and hot-fire testing to build high-thrust RDRE. In 2021, they worked with AFRL to test a 22kN-thrust RDRE using liquid oxygen and gaseous methane at Purdue University, Ind. Over the following two years, they worked with NASA to test 3D-printed RDRE combustors. The post AFRL Targets New Hypersonic Engine Tech Prototypes Within 4 Years appeared first on Air & Space Forces Magazine .

title: FTC and 20 states sue Dollar General, alleging retailer overcharged shoppers
body:
The Federal Trade Commission said Monday that it filed a lawsuit along with 20 states accusing Dollar General of charging customers more than the prices it displays on shelves, price tags and in advertisements.
Shares of Dollar General dropped about 4% after the FTC announced the lawsuit .
The complaint alleges that thousands of Dollar General stores have "taken advantage of vulnerable shoppers by extracting millions of dollars in unlawful overcharges with insufficient safeguards to prevent the practice."
It also argues that Dollar General has received "tens of thousands" of complaints from consumers about charging higher than advertised prices, but that it has not implemented policies to address the problem.
The states joining the FTC in the lawsuit are Alabama, Arizona, Arkansas, California, Connecticut, Florida, Illinois, Iowa, Kansas, Louisiana, Michigan, Mississippi, Nebraska, New Jersey, North Carolina, Ohio, Oklahoma, Tennessee, Utah and Wisconsin.
"Dollar General has betrayed the trust of millions of American consumers and imposed significant financial harm on communities and consumers who are already struggling to make their paychecks last," said Christopher Mufarrige, director of the FTC's Bureau of Consumer Protection.
Dollar General issued a statement in response to the lawsuit, saying it will "defend this litigation vigorously."
"As with other retailers and despite our policies and procedures, occasional price discrepancies can occur," the statement read. "When that happens, our store teams are instructed, empowered, and expected to make things right for the customer. In recent years, we have enhanced our price-accuracy processes and remain committed to continuous improvement."
Dollar General's statement said that it has cooperated with the FTC's investigation since February and has produced documents, data and sworn testimony. In September, the FTC sent a draft complaint and settlement offer. The company said it had sent a monetary counteroffer and was surprised when the FTC filed the lawsuit rather than responding to the offer.
The suit comes as shoppers look for discounts while they face elevated food and gas prices. Officials across the political spectrum also aim to show their efforts to protect consumers from high costs ahead of the midterm election next week.

title: USS Colorado to become first U.S. submarine assigned to AUKUS rotational force in Australia
body: The Virginia-class fast-attack submarine will rotate through HMAS Stirling in Western Australia. The force is projected to host up to four U.S. fast-attack submarines and one British fast-attack submarine on a rotational basis. The arrangement will give AUKUS partners more maintenance options and sustainment infrastructure in the region. It will also help Australia prepare to own, operate, maintain and regulate its own conventionally armed, nuclear-powered submarines. U.S. Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, Australian Deputy Prime Minister and Defence Minister Richard Marles, and British Defence Secretary Wes Streeting announced Colorado’s selection. They described the designation as a milestone for AUKUS Pillar I. The announcement precedes a U.S. submarine maintenance period scheduled to begin later in the week. The partners said the work would further demonstrate Australia’s growing ability to sustain American and British nuclear-powered fast-attack submarines. The statement repeated President Trump’s description of AUKUS as moving “full steam ahead.” It said Australian Prime Minister Albanese and British Prime Minister Burnham had reaffirmed that position. SRF-West is being established at Australia’s invitation and will operate under relevant agreements, including the U.S.–Australia Force Posture Agreement. Associated AUKUS activities will comply with the partners’ international obligations, including the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty and Australia’s obligations under the South Pacific Nuclear Free Zone Treaty.

title: Can point-of-care testing improve early detection of chronic kidney disease in Africa?
body: Introduction Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a growing public health concern in Africa, where early detection remains challenging due to persistent gaps in access to diagnostic services and routine screening. A 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis estimated that CKD (stages 1-5) affects approximately 13.7% of adults across 19 African countries 1 . Limited access to diagnostic services, the cost of laboratory investigations, and gaps in routine screening can delay the identification of kidney abnormalities, particularly among high-risk populations, including people living with hypertension, diabetes, and cardiovascular diseases 1–3 . Evidence also indicates that risk-factor-based screening in primary care can support the early detection of CKD, reinforcing the importance of improving access to kidney health assessment in underserved settings 4 . This raises an important question: Could point-of-care testing (POCT) help bridge the gap between kidney disease risk and timely diagnosis in Africa? What role could point-of-care testing play? Point-of-care testing refers to any diagnostic test performed near the patient, rather than exclusively in centralised laboratories 5,6 . It is commonly referred to as “bedside testing” 7 . By providing results closer to the point of care, POCT may reduce delays associated with specimen transportation and result reporting and support more timely clinical decisions. For kidney health, two important areas of assessment are: Blood creatinine: Used to estimate kidney filtration function through a calculated estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). Urine albumin: Helps identify kidney damage. Measuring the urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR) is particularly useful for assessing albuminuria. Evidence suggests that POCT can support CKD screening by enabling creatinine and urine albumin measurements in community and primary healthcare settings, particularly where access to conventional laboratory services is limited 8–10 . Although selected POCT devices have demonstrated promising diagnostic performance, accuracy varies across technologies, with some exhibiting measurement bias and reduced sensitivity. The 2024 Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO) guideline highlights the potential role of point-of-care testing (POCT) in CKD screening, particularly for measuring creatinine, urine albumin or urine protein in settings with limited access to laboratory services or where decentralised testing can facilitate earlier detection, reduce delays in obtaining test results, and support timely clinical decision-making and referral 9 . The World Health Organization has also included point-of-care creatinine testing in its Model List of Essential In Vitro Diagnostics for use in settings such as community outreach and primary healthcare facilities without laboratories 11 . These recommendations provide a strong rationale for exploring decentralised kidney health testing in Africa. However, the value of POCT extends beyond the availability of a rapid test; it depends on whether the test can be integrated into a functioning pathway for screening, confirmation, referral, and treatment. Five considerations for implementing kidney health POCT in Africa 1. Diagnostic performance and clinical utility Not all POCT devices perform equally, and the convenience of rapid testing should not be confused with diagnostic accuracy. Devices must be evaluated against appropriate laboratory algorithms and standard guidelines, such as the World Health Organization’s (WHO) REASSURED criteria (Real-time connectivity, Ease of specimen collection, Affordability, Sensitivity, Specificity, User-friendliness, Rapidity and robustness, Equipment-free, and Deliverable to end-users), with attention to analytical performance, clinical sensitivity and specificity, and the potential consequences of false-positive and false-negative results 12–14 . For example, if a point-of-care creatinine diagnostic underestimates a patient’s serum creatinine concentration, the calculated estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) may be falsely reassuring, potentially resulting in missed kidney dysfunction and delayed referral. Conversely, overestimation of creatinine may produce an artificially low eGFR, leading to unnecessary referrals, additional investigations, unnecessary costs, and patient anxiety. Similarly, a urine albumin screening device that produces a false-negative result may fail to identify albuminuria in a patient with diabetes or hypertension, whereas a false-positive result may lead to unnecessary follow-up investigations. These highlight that the clinical value of POCTs depends not only on the speed of testing but also on the accuracy of results and the extent to which measurement errors may influence clinical decisions. For creatinine screening, the results are recommended to be used to estimate the glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) using an appropriate equation, with abnormal findings prompting further clinical assessment and confirmatory testing where indicated 9 . For urine albumin screening, quantitative measurement and calculation of the urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR) provide more clinically useful information than a simple positive or negative result 9 . However, a positive result from an initial qualitative screening test should prompt quantitative assessment to determine the extent of albuminuria. Where initial screening suggests albuminuria or reduced kidney function, confirmatory testing using appropriate laboratory methods and repeat assessment, where indicated, are essential before establishing a diagnosis of chronic kidney disease (CKD). Quality assurance, staff training, device maintenance, and external quality assessment are also crucial to ensuring the reliability of POCT results and supporting appropriate clinical decision-making 15,16 . 2. Affordability and equitable access The potential of POCT lies partly in its ability to bring diagnostic services closer to people who face geographical, financial, or health-system barriers to laboratory testing. In rural and hard-to-reach communities, and resource-constrained primary healthcare facilities, decentralised testing could reduce the need for some patients to travel to higher-level facilities solely to obtain initial kidney function measurements. However, an abnormal POCT result requires further laboratory investigations to confirm kidney abnormalities, assess their severity, and guide clinical management 9 . If patients cannot afford these additional tests, the benefits of initial screening may be limited, potentially leaving suspected cases undiagnosed or delaying appropriate care. The cost-effectiveness of implementing POCT for kidney disease should therefore be evaluated by considering the costs of equipment, consumables, staff training, quality assurance, maintenance, confirmatory testing, and follow-up care 17 . Affordability should be assessed across the entire diagnostic pathway, not simply in terms of the purchase price of a POCT device. This includes determining whether patients can afford confirmatory investigations and subsequent care, and whether health systems can sustainably finance these services. Integrating POCT into existing primary healthcare services, alongside appropriate financing and referral arrangements, may help minimise out-of-pocket expenditure and ensure that abnormal screening results lead to timely diagnosis and care 3. Integration of POCT into primary healthcare through task sharing, follow-up and referral pathways A positive screening result is only the beginning of the diagnostic process. Patients need access to clinical assessment, confirmatory investigations, appropriate referral, and treatment. This is particularly important because CKD is defined by abnormalities of kidney structure or function that persist for at least three months 1 . A single abnormal creatinine, eGFR, or urine albumin result does not automatically establish chronic kidney disease; the finding may reflect an acute or temporary abnormality 9 . Consequently, implementation strategies should clearly define who will be screened, how abnormal results will be communicated, when testing should be repeated, and how patients will be linked to appropriate care. Without these arrangements, decentralised testing may identify abnormalities without ensuring that patients receive the care they need. Many hard-to-reach communities across Africa face limited access to conventional laboratory services because of geographical barriers, inadequate diagnostic infrastructure, workforce shortages, and travel costs 18,19 . POCT could improve access to kidney health assessment within primary healthcare and chronic disease management services, particularly for people living with hypertension and diabetes. Task shifting and empowering community health workers (CHWs) could further extend these services by equipping appropriately trained personnel to support risk assessment, conduct approved screening tests where permitted, provide health education, and facilitate referral and follow-up. Such an approach could bring kidney health screening closer to underserved populations while reducing pressure on overstretched health professionals. However, implementation requires structured training, clear scopes of practice, supervision, quality assurance, and reliable referral pathways 9 . Patients with abnormal screening results should receive counselling, clinical assessment, and appropriate confirmatory testing, with urgent referral for markedly reduced eGFR, significant albuminuria, or other concerning findings. In settings where laboratories are distant, CHWs could help coordinate specimen transportation, remind patients about follow-up appointments, track referrals, and communicate results in collaboration with primary healthcare teams. They should not independently diagnose CKD or make clinical decisions beyond their training and authorised scope of practice. Importantly, a single abnormal POCT result does not establish CKD, which generally requires evidence of kidney abnormalities persisting for at least three months 1,9 . Integrating task-shared POCT into primary healthcare, supported by affordable confirmatory testing and clear referral protocols, could help translate improved screening access into timely diagnosis and appropriate care. 4. Multimorbidity and integrated screening Kidney health should not be considered in isolation from other chronic conditions. People living with diabetes, hypertension, HIV, and other long-term conditions may require assessment for kidney disease as part of their ongoing care. Integrating kidney health assessment into existing primary healthcare services could create opportunities to identify multiple conditions through coordinated screening and follow-up. Such an approach may reduce fragmented care and make better use of existing healthcare resources. However, integrated screening models must be evaluated to establish whether they improve detection, acceptability, linkage to care, and health outcomes without placing excessive demands on patients and healthcare workers 20 . 5. Home-based testing, self-testing and decentralised monitoring Home-based kidney health testing and monitoring may involve two distinct approaches: patient-performed self-testing, in which individuals conduct tests and interpret results at home, and healthcare worker-led testing during home visits, in which trained personnel perform tests and support result interpretation, counselling, and referral. Both approaches could extend kidney health assessment beyond conventional healthcare facilities, particularly for people at increased risk of chronic kidney disease (CKD), including those living with diabetes, hypertension, or other chronic conditions 8 . However, their suitability depends on the intended users, the type of test, and the clinical purpose. Technologies intended for self-testing require validation for use by non-professionals, with clear instructions on sample collection, test performance, result interpretation, and when to seek professional care 21 . Healthcare worker-led testing, meanwhile, requires appropriate training, supervision, and quality assurance to ensure reliable testing and referral 21 . The clinical value of both approaches also depends on affordability, user literacy, quality assurance, data privacy, and access to confirmatory testing and follow-up care 21 . These considerations are particularly important in resource-constrained settings, where identifying a potential kidney abnormality may not lead to timely clinical assessment or treatment. Healthcare worker-led home visits may help address some barriers to self-testing by providing assistance with test procedures, explaining results, and facilitating referrals; however, this approach depends on workforce availability and sustainable implementation. Furthermore, because CKD requires evidence of kidney abnormalities persisting for at least three months, a single abnormal home-test result cannot independently establish a diagnosis 9 . Home-based kidney testing, either patient-led or trained personnel-led should therefore be evaluated as a potential complement to established diagnostic and clinical pathways, rather than a replacement for professional assessment, confirmatory testing, and ongoing care. Moving from promising technologies to effective implementation From a health systems and implementation science perspective, the key question is whether POCT for CKD can be implemented reliably, affordably, equitably, and sustainably in African healthcare settings. Future research should assess the diagnostic accuracy and clinical utility of kidney function and urine albumin tests in African populations, their cost-effectiveness compared with conventional laboratory-based pathways, and their acceptability among patients and healthcare workers. It should also examine the feasibility of integrating CKD screening into primary healthcare and multimorbidity programs, including home-based monitoring where appropriate, and evaluate whether referral, confirmatory testing, and follow-up systems ensure that people with abnormal results receive timely care. Addressing procurement, supply chains, staff competencies, quality assurance, and health financing will be essential to support sustainable implementation and equitable scale-up of CKD POCT, particularly in underserved communities in Africa. Conclusion POCT has the potential to support earlier identification of kidney abnormalities in Africa by bringing selected diagnostic services closer to patients and primary healthcare facilities, particularly in underserved communities where access to conventional laboratory services is limited. However, its contribution to CKD screening will depend on diagnostic accuracy, affordability, quality assurance, confirmatory testing, effective referral pathways, and integration into routine healthcare. Moving beyond the availability of testing technologies towards reliable diagnostic pathways is essential to ensure that people with abnormal screening results receive appropriate clinical assessment, follow-up, and timely care. Greater research, implementation, and policy attention is therefore needed to establish how kidney health POCT can be integrated sustainably into primary healthcare and multimorbidity screening programs across African settings. Dr Evans Duah is the Head of Technology and Innovation at Kidney Research initiative Ghana. He is a Medical Laboratory Scientist and Public Health researcher. He specialises in point-of-care diagnostics, implementation science, and health systems research. His work focuses on improving access to accurate, affordable, and equitable diagnostic services, particularly in primary healthcare and resource-constrained settings across Africa. https://www.linkedin.com/in/evans-duah-75107649

title: 5 prominent Obidient members missing from NDC presidential campaign council
body: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has unveiled its 2027 presidential campaign council, naming flagbearer, Peter Obi and National Leader Seriake Dickson among its leaders. However, several prominent members of the Obidient movement who have actively and publicly supported Obi in the past are absent from the published list. The absence of such individuals is notable because they have either supported the NDC presidential candidate or taken part in the political movement in different ways, with their public profiles ranging from campaign activism and digital mobilisation to formal movement leadership. The list the party published on Sunday names the campaign caucus, advisory council, directorates and state coordinators. It also includes Obi and other senior party figures, but omits a few influential figures who have actively backed the Obidient movement in recent years. Here are five prominent Obidient movement members omitted from the NDC 2027 presidential campaign council. 1 . Moses Paul (Dr. Mo) Moses Paul, popularly known as Dr. Mo, has held formal leadership roles in the Obidient movement. He was identified as its Secretary General in 2025 and appointed National Coordinator in October 2026, while his predecessor, Yunusa Tanko, took on a role as an adviser to Obi. Dr. Mo rose to national prominence as the convener of the Free Nigeria Movement and a key organizer of youth-led mobilization and rallies supporting Peter Obi’s 2023 presidential campaign under the Labour Party. Obi also publicly backed Paul’s bid for chairman of the Abuja Municipal Area Council, saying he would campaign for him. Paul’s omission from the released council list stands out given his current leadership role in the movement and his previous candidacy with Obi’s support. 2. Aisha Yesufu Campaign activist and NDC member Aisha Yesufu served on Obi’s 2023 Labor Party presidential campaign team and was one of the prominent public voices backing his candidacy. She has also described the Obidient movement as part of a broader wave of political engagement after the #EndSARS protests, rather than a movement created by Obi. In May 2026, Yesufu joined the NDC, saying her political choices had been guided by her support for Obi. She declared for the FCT Senate seat but later withdrew from the race after internal party decisions on primaries. Her absence from the campaign council is notable given her past campaign role, movement profile and NDC membership. 3. Precious Oruche (Mama Pee) Precious Oruche, popularly known as Mama Pee, is regularly identified in news reports as an Obidient activist, grassroots organizer, social influencer, and an outspoken supporter of Obi. In 2025, the movement publicly supported her after a reported incident involving factional Labour Party chairman Julius Abure. Oruche has continued to use her public platform to advocate for Obi and remains a visible voice in Obi’s support base. However, her name does not appear on the NDC’s released campaign council list. 4. Peter Akah (Randy Peterz) Peter Akah, also known as Randy Peterz, is a political activist, digital content creator, and one of the most vocal defenders of Peter Obi and the Obidient movement. Akah’s public political work has included online mobilisation and civic engagement. Media reports described him and Oruche (Mama Pee)as prominent Obidient members and Obi supporters. His public association with Obi and the movement is documented, including being associated with Obidient Connect, a group supporting Obi’s 2027 campaign. The group has promoted voter participation, including urging Nigerians in the diaspora to help people at home get to the polls. 5. Isaac Fayose Fayose, the younger brother of former Ekiti State Governor Ayodele Fayose, has publicly said he campaigned for Obi in 2023, spent his own money in support of the campaign and made his hotel available for Obidient meetings in Ibadan. Isaac Fayose He has also said he took part in a protest in support of the movement. In July 2026, Obi visited Fayose after Fayose spoke publicly about his campaign efforts. Fayose subsequently reaffirmed his support for Obi. As with the other names, the released council list does not include him. The post 5 prominent Obidient members missing from NDC presidential campaign council appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Electromagnetic spectrum contract signed between CACI, U.S. Navy
body:
RESTON, Va. CACI International announced that it won a five-year task order valued at up to $281 million with the U.S. Navy's Naval Surface Warfare Center (NSWC) Crane to support the strengthening and advancing of next-generation electromagnetic warfare capabilities across the U.S. Department of Defense (DoD).
Under the terms of the contract, CACI will deliver research, analysis, assessment, and prototype development to enhance electromagnetic spectrum operations (EMSO) across multiple operational environments.
The program includes the designing and maturing of advanced technologies, performing test and evaluation (T&E), and development of infrastructure and capability enhancements aimed at meeting emerging operational needs at multiple sites based on unique customer requirements.

title: Polish city halts ties with Lviv amid dispute over UPA commemorations
body:
Councilors in the Polish city of Przemysl unanimously voted on Oct. 26 to suspend cooperation with Lviv, a city in western Ukraine, in protest against a proposal to honor the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA) and its leader, Roman Shukhevych, in 2027, Polish broadcaster RMF24 reported.
The move adds to tensions between the two countries after Lviv's council adopted decrees on Oct. 20 declaring the next year as the Year of the UPA , the Year of Shukhevych, and the Year of Oleh Olzhych, a Ukrainian poet and political activist.
The dispute could spread to other Polish local authorities. The Lublin regional assembly also voted in support of severing ties with Lviv, according to RMF24 .
Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk has described Lviv's decision as "suicidal tactics," adding that he warned President Volodymyr Zelensky such gestures are not helping already patchy Ukraine-Poland relations.
Ukraine's Foreign Ministry called Lviv's actions "counterproductive to our current efforts to further develop Ukrainian-Polish relations and resolve contentious issues amid Russia's full-scale aggression," in a statement to journalists on Oct. 21.
Sviatoslav Sheremeta, head of Lviv's regional council cultural committee, was declared by Warsaw as persona non grata and banned from entering the Schengen area until 2031.
In Poland, the UPA is associated with 1943-1945 Volyn massacres , a historical event during which tens of thousands of Poles were killed in what today is western Ukraine, but used to be under Nazi occupation.
"Roman Shukhevych was a criminal who collaborated with the Nazis and whose hands are stained with the blood of thousands of innocent victims—people killed simply because they were Polish," said Poland's charge d'affaires in Kyiv, Piotr Lukasiewicz .
Poland is an important ally in the realms of security and defense, especially at a crucial time when U.S. relations with Ukraine have become strenuous .
"Additional foreign policy challenges are the last thing Ukraine needs today," Sergiy Solodkyy, director of the New Europe Center think tank in Kyiv, told the Kyiv Independent.

title: Award-winning producer receives £400,000 payout from BBC over workplace antisemitism claim
body: An Oscar- and Emmy-winning producer has received a payout of more than £400,000 from the BBC after claiming she was victimized and forced out of the corporation following the October 7 attacks.Lucie Kon left the broadcaster in April, just 19 days after winning an Oscar for her work, following a dispute over antisemitism in the workplace. Having built a stellar career on major programs including Panorama, Today, BBC Breakfast, and Storyville, her commissioned and produced films have earned an Emmy, an Oscar, a BAFTA, and many other prestigious industry honors.Speaking to The Telegraph on Sunday, Kon alleged that her professional treatment shifted rapidly after the October 7 attacks in Israel. As footage and news of the atrocities emerged, she had messaged a colleague on WhatsApp asking if they had seen what was happening in Israel and remarking that Hamas were evil. In response, the colleague told her that “Zionists” were evil.“I was like, 'What?' And she went, 'Evil Hamas, evil Zionists,' a bit like it was a joke, like they were the same and they're not the same, and that was a particularly tasteless thing to say at that particular moment in history,” Kon said.Later, when Kon sought to raise concerns about the treatment of Jewish staff and insisted that staff should at least be able to describe Hamas as committing acts of terror, another colleague told her that if she wanted to refer to Hamas as terrorists, she was required to call Israel a terrorist state as well.Kon helps set up WhatsApp group for Jewish BBC employeesPushed by the worsening workplace environment, Kon helped set up an internal WhatsApp group for Jewish employees at the corporation and wrote to then-Director General Tim Davie to raise concerns.Shortly afterward, as more footage of the atrocities emerged, Kon proposed producing a film about the events of October 7 to a colleague who had previously made inappropriate remarks. When she mentioned the idea, the colleague dismissed it, saying they had already made enough films about Israel, but Kon's manager later called her over to discuss the project.“She said, 'Lucie, we probably will do the Nova film,'” Kon recounted. “And she said to me, 'But if we do it, we need to contextualize why Hamas did what they did.'”When Kon questioned this requirement, explaining that the project was intended as a straightforward account of what happened that day rather than a deep dive into the historical and political context of the region, her manager's manager informed her that she could no longer oversee the film. When Kon asked why, the manager told her it was “because you're Jewish” and stated she was partial.Kon noted that the manager then stated the person who was going to look after the film instead was the very same colleague who had previously told her that if Hamas were terrorists, the Israelis were terrorists too. An arrangement was later reached where Kon could oversee the film, but only under the strict supervision of someone else to ensure she remained impartial.Kon subsequently raised a formal grievance. News of the grievance quickly reached the colleague who had made the remarks about Zionists, and that colleague wanted nothing more to do with Kon. This meant the two could no longer attend meetings together, and Kon was instructed not to come into work.Six months later, she received the outcome. “It wasn't upheld,” Kon said. “I was told that a lot of the things that I'd said people didn't remember saying. And I was told that I'd been told - that I hadn't been told I couldn't work on the Nova film because I was a Jew - that they were worried about my mental health.”When she appealed the decision, that appeal was also unsuccessful. At the time of her appeal, the BBC moved her colleague away from the Strand to work elsewhere, while Kon was told she could no longer travel, commission, or speak on behalf of the BBC because it would be unfair to her colleague.Kon continued working from home while her appeal was considered, but by December, the stress took a toll, and her health began to deteriorate. After submitting a doctor's note for stress-related sick leave, she was called into a meeting where she was told her job was being put at risk of redundancy. Having returned from sick leave, she applied for a newly created position but was rejected and made redundant in April.BBC refuses to apologize, call Kon victim of antisemitismAccording to The Telegraph, she brought unfair dismissal proceedings against the BBC, which agreed to pay her substantial compensation, partly funded by the license fee, without admitting liability. The corporation refused to apologize or admit she was a victim of antisemitism.The Telegraph noted that she is the first person known to have been given a settlement by the BBC after alleging antisemitic behavior among colleagues. Speaking about the broader climate for staff after her departure, Kon reportedly told The Telegraph that other Jewish colleagues are still being bullied and abused, adding, “I know that nothing has changed because I've spoken to quite a few people since I left. Friends who are still struggling, still suffering, who feel embarrassed to say that they're Zionist or that they're a Jew.”“I went from being a journalist and commissioner at the BBC who was Jewish to being a Jewish journalist at the BBC,” Kon said. “It was like I had Jew stamped on my forehead. I think I became a problem. I think I made too much of a noise about being a Jew inside the BBC.”Kon added, “A colleague of mine said to me a while ago that if you say you're a Zionist at the BBC, you might as well say that you were the person who had their foot on the neck of George Floyd. You're a murderer. You're an evil colonialist. You are a racist, and I'm not any of those things, and neither are the other people I know who are Zionist.”“I stood up for who I was,” Kon said. “I stood up for what I believed to be right. The BBC says, 'Bring your authentic self to work.' And I did, and I lost my job as a result.”A BBC spokesperson said in a statement, “We are grateful that Ms. Kon acknowledges that the BBC is not institutionally antisemitic. The BBC processes did not uphold any of Ms. Kon's allegations of antisemitism. However, the outcome acknowledged shortcomings and the personal impact on Ms. Kon. We would like to acknowledge that Ms. Kon was a valued member of staff with many years of dedicated service to the BBC.”

title: Fungi now have a global conservation strategy
body: YEREVAN, Armenia — Like the dark spaces they often prefer, mushrooms, yeasts, and some 160,000 known species of fungi rest in the background of conservation efforts. But their crucial role as ecosystem engineers makes protecting them vital, said Greg Mueller, chief scientist emeritus at the Chicago Botanic Garden in the U.S. “They really are responsible for life on Earth,” he said, “and life as we know it would not exist without fungi.” Mueller called fungi “nature’s recyclers” at the launch of the first global conservation strategy for fungal conservation on Oct. 21 at the United Nations biodiversity conference (COP17) in Armenia. Many fungi also form symbiotic relationships with plants, helping shuttle nutrients and water between them; they can sock away carbon in soil and help provide food for animals and people. Historically, international negotiations to stem the global loss of species haven’t fully considered fungi. Now, a team of fungi conservationists from 30 countries led by Mueller has set out to integrate fungal conservation into the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, a central part of negotiations at COP17. To date, mycologists — scientists who study fungi — have little data on the conservation status for most species known to science. “When we talk about … halting extinction risk, how can we talk about it [while] ignoring a whole kingdom of life?” Cátia Canteiro, a conservationist with U.K.-based NGO Plantlife International who co-led the strategy, said during the launch. The guidelines aim to spur new research and the protection of rare species,…This article was originally published on Mongabay

title: Ukraine to be one of priorities of Lithuania's presidency of EU Council in H1 2027 – Stefanchuk
body:
Ukraine will be one of the priorities of Lithuania's presidency of the Council of the European Union in the first half of 2027, Verkhovna Rada Chairman Ruslan Stefanchuk said after a meeting with Seimas Chairman Juozas Olekas.
"Ukraine will be one of the priorities of Lithuania's presidency of the Council of the European Union in the first half of 2027. First and foremost, in matters of security and EU enlargement. We discussed this during a meeting at the Verkhovna Rada with Juozas Olekas, Speaker of the Seimas of the Republic of Lithuania," Stefanchuk said on Facebook on Monday.
He noted that he particularly appreciates Lithuania's defense aid, which has already exceeded EUR 1.1 billion, its support for Ukraine's energy sector ahead of winter, and its active participation in the Shelter Coalition.
"A separate topic was European integration. We discussed the need to maintain the pace of the negotiation process and to open all six negotiation clusters. We also discussed the possibility of involving Lithuanian experts in a group of parliamentary advisers who will assist Ukraine on its path to EU membership," Stefanchuk said.
The Speaker of the Ukrainian Parliament also said that during the meeting with his Lithuanian counterpart, they focused on increasing sanctions pressure on Russia, as well as efforts to establish a Special Tribunal on the Crime of Aggression and an international compensation mechanism.
"We specifically discussed the return of Ukrainian children who have been illegally displaced by Russia. Lithuania's position on this issue remains unequivocal. Lithuania has been and remains one of Ukraine's most consistent partners. I am grateful for the solidarity, concrete assistance, and shared understanding that Ukraine's security is inseparable from the security of all of Europe," Stefanchuk said.

title: Contacts with Africa, Putin’s 'extremely tight' schedule: Kremlin aide’s statements
body:
MOSCOW, October 26. /TASS/. Russia's presidential aide for foreign policy affairs, Yury Ushakov, has described the upcoming week in Vladimir Putin’s schedule as "extremely tight," noting that some "hectic days" lie ahead.
TASS has summarized the Kremlin aide’s key statements.
The upcoming week in Vladimir Putin’s schedule is going to be "extremely tight": "To be honest, we have some hectic days ahead. It’s going to be an extremely, extremely tight week - from Tuesday through Friday."
On October 27, Putin will take part in the 8th summit of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum.
Putin will deliver a speech at the summit of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) where he will "mention problems, including of geopolitical nature, the gas industry faces, and highlight areas of work that are priority, from our point of view, to solve existing problems."
The GECF summit will yield a Moscow declaration.
On October 28 and 29, the president will take part in the 3rd Russia-Africa summit in Moscow.
Putin’s schedule at the Russia-Africa summit will be incredibly busy: "I emphasize that they will be very grand, even a little chaotic (the events - TASS). But we will try to do everything, we will try to get everything in on time."
A reception on behalf of Russian President Vladimir Putin in honor of the participants of the Russia-Africa summit will be held in the Kremlin's Faceted Chamber in the evening on October 28.
Forty-eight countries have confirmed their participation, twenty-two of them will be represented at the top level.
In his address at the first plenary session of the Third Russia-Africa Economic and Humanitarian Forum, Russian President Vladimir Putin will assess the prospects for relations between Russia and African nations across sectors including agriculture and energy.
Special attention will be focused on Russia’s cooperation with African countries within the United Nations.
Russian President Vladimir Putin and Burundi’s leader Evariste Ndayishimiye will speak at the first plenary session of the third Russia-Africa Economic and Humanitarian Forum.
They will also make statements for the press following the Russia-Africa Summit.
Putin and leaders of African countries will visit an exhibition of Russia’s advanced solutions in key economic sectors at Gostiny Dvor.
The Russia-Africa summit is expected to yield three important documents.
It is also planned to sign 33 intergovernmental documents with African countries after the Russia-Africa summit.
The president will hold five bilateral meetings on October 27, and 24 such meetings in all on the summits’ sidelines.
On the sidelines of the GECF summit, Putin will meet with the leaders of Iran, Qatar, Mozambique, and Libya.
On October 28, Putin will hold a meeting with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi on October 28, before the official reception in honor of the participants of the Russia-Africa summit.
Later that day, after the official reception, Putin will meet with Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed.
A meeting with President of the Republic of Congo Denis Sassou Nguesso will conclude the day.
Putin's bilateral meetings with African leaders will be the most important part of the Russia-Africa summit.
The Russia-Africa Summit organized so that Putin can hold talks with every visiting leader.
Putin will hold a meeting with African Union Chairperson and President of Burundi Evariste Ndayishimiye on October 2.
On October 29, Putin will meet with the presidents of Madagascar Michael Randrianirina, of Zimbabwe Emmerson Mnangagwa, of Namibia Netumbo Nandi·Ndaitwah, as well as with Chairman of the Sovereign Council of Sudan Abdel Fattah al-Burhan
On October 30, Putin will hold 11 bilateral meetings with leaders of African states: "Friday, October 30, will be wholly devoted precisely to bilateral negotiations."
Specifically, the Russian leader will meet with the heads of Ghana, Mali, Mauritania, South Sudan, the Central African Republic, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the Togolese Republic, Eritrea, Somalia and the Union of the Comoros.
Putin will give an assessment of the evolving multipolar world order at the first plenary session of the Russia-Africa Summit.
Russia is an ally in building a multipolar, fair world order free from dictate and double standards.
Moscow is expanding its diplomatic presence in African countries; since 2022, it has opened three embassies, and five other diplomatic missions have resumed operations during this period: "Russia is expanding its diplomatic presence in Africa. Since 2022, we have opened three embassies: in South Sudan, The Gambia, and the Union of the Comoros. Five diplomatic missions have resumed their work: in Burkina Faso, Equatorial Guinea, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, and Togo."
As many as 48 Russian embassies are already operating across Africa, and Moscow is planning to open another one, its 49th, in Liberia: "Overall, we have a solid number of embassies [across Africa]. We are quite well represented on the continent."
Russia is closely cooperating with African countries within international organizations, first of all the United Nations, on such pressing problems as combating terrorism, drug trafficking, and cybercrime.
African countries have begun to cooperate more intensively with BRICS: "Relations with the African Union are developing dynamically, and cooperation between Africans and BRICS intensifies."
The idea of the Russia-Africa summit is to foster closer cooperation in all areas.
Russia’s trade with African countries exceeded $27 billion in 2025, up by 1.5 times on 2023.
Agriculture is one of the key areas of Russia’s cooperation with African countries.
Russia sent more than 18 mln metric tons of grain to Africa last year and 13 mln metric tons more were shipped during the nine months of this year.
Russian mineral fertilizer supplies climbed above 2.2 mln metric tons in 2026.
Education is another major cooperation area between Russia and Africa; more than 40,000 African students are currently studying in Russia.
Russia invited Turkmenistan and South Africa to the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) summit as guest countries: "Apart from Forum participants and observers, we invited two guest countries, namely Turkmenistan and the Republic of South Africa."
The African nations account for almost a half of seats in the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) and OPEC.
Russia considers important to provide for reliable and stable gas supplies, taking into account growing needs across the globe: "Considering growing gas needs, we consider important to ensure stability and reliability of supplies and guarantee further confident development of countries."
The global gas industry is in a challenging situation and needs a floor for the depoliticized dialogue and the Gas Exporting Countries Forum (GECF) fits this role.
Russia assumed when preparing the summit of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum that its countries promote natural gas as a practical kind of fuel.
Global demand for natural gas is expected to grow by 28% by 2055, to 5.4 trillion cubic meters.
Global liquefied natural gas (LNG) exports may reach 650 mln cubic meters in 5-10 years, exceeding the 2025 level by almost 50%.

title: Hormuz Chaos Sparks Legal Showdown Over Global Tanker Pricing
body:
Essential news coupled with the finest maritime content sourced from across the globe.
Russia's shadow fleet vessels wait in the unofficial anchorage area in the Gulf of Finland near Vaindloo, Estonia April 10, 2026. REUTERS/Ints Kalnins
(Bloomberg) — Commodity trader Mercuria Energy Group accused the Baltic Exchange of continuing to publish the world’s benchmark oil tanker rate, despite distortions caused by the Iran war, because it feared losing business to a competitor.
Lawyers for Mercuria kicked off a London trial claiming that the Baltic Exchange should have suspended the benchmark rate after exports through the Strait of Hormuz were strangled by the conflict between the US, Israel and Iran. The Baltic Exchange said the commodity trader’s claim reflects “instability and opportunism.”
Founded in 1774, the Baltic Exchange plays a central role in setting global shipping rates. It maintains it was still possible to put a price on the freight risk, and that it had consulted consistently with the market after the Iran war severely disrupted oil shipments through Hormuz. Flows have since recovered close to pre-war levels.
In an April 14 call, a senior freight assessor described the risk of the benchmark being replaced by a competitor as “the overriding fear of what we do here,” according to a document given to the court by Mercuria’s lawyers before the hearing on Monday.
Mercuria also gave examples of tanker market participants, including the Baltic Exchange’s own staff, who called into question the continued publication of a rate for the route.
The trading house said that the Baltic Exchange’s freight assessor didn’t submit a value into the company’s internal system that’s supposed to represent his personal view of where the index will be. When he did eventually submit a value, it included comments such as “doesn’t make any sense to shed an opinion on this route — crazy that we have to!”
The case calls into question a pricing tool that until the Iran war acted as the benchmark for oil tanker earnings across the globe. The key TD3C rate underpins contracts between tanker owners and their customers as well as billions of dollars in derivatives. It’s based on the cost of hiring a supertanker from Saudi Arabia’s Ras Tanura, inside the Persian Gulf, to China, and also serves as a reference point for other routes.
The Baltic Exchange is confident that it has met all its statutory, contractual and regulatory obligations in the production of the TD3C benchmark, Chief Executive Officer Mark Jackson said in a statement. The claim from Mercuria is “without merit,” he added.
Mercuria has “huge index-linked exposures, which it has failed to risk manage,” lawyers for the Baltic Exchange said. After being caught out by the sharp rises in the benchmark, Mercuria “wishes to unseat TD3C, and it is reaching for any available argument to do so,” they added.
Mercuria’s lawyers said the evidence showed the Baltic Exchange did not suspend the index because it wanted to keep the market for certain freight agreements active, and to avoid the risk of being replaced by a rival.
One of the brokers who contribute to the index said on April 2 that it was “utter nonsense” to provide an assessment of the TD3C benchmark, given the unprecedented levels of disruption to traffic through Hormuz, according to another transcript presented by Mercuria.
Mercuria is urging the court to declare that the Baltic Exchange breached its obligations and ought to have suspended the TD3C route.
Lawyers for the Baltic Exchange said the risk of being replaced by a rival provider did not drive its decision making. The lawyers said passage through Hormuz was still possible.
“The Baltic’s decision to continue publishing TD3C, was a decision which was not taken lightly,” lawyers for exchange said in a court document countering Mercuria’s allegations.
The Iran war threw global commodity markets into turmoil by slashing shipments through Hormuz, which Tehran declared closed in the early days of the conflict. In recent months, volumes have recovered, with most trackers seeing shipments close to pre-war levels.
A spokesperson for Mercuria didn’t immediately respond to an email for comment.
Mercuria initially said it had incurred losses estimated to be in the hundreds of millions of US dollars as a result of the Baltic Exchange continuing to publish the index, but removed any estimate of financial losses from its most recent claim.
