title: CENTCOM Commander Visits Strait of Hormuz during Milestone Week
body: STRAIT OF HORMUZ — The commander of U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) visited the Strait of Hormuz, Oct. 25, as U.S. forces reach the milestone of assisting Gulf partners in exporting more than 1.5 billion barrels of crude oil since summer. Adm. Brad Cooper observed the current operational environment while flying in a U.S. Army CH-47 Chinook over the international waterway. More than 3,000 commercial vessels have successfully transited the Strait of Hormuz with support from CENTCOM forces over the last six months. “We continue to stand shoulder to shoulder with our Gulf partners and the shipping industry,” said Cooper. “This visit underscores our strong commitment to continued freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.” Momentum has continued to build in recent months since American forces successfully cleared the strait’s international shipping lanes of sea mines laid by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). During the trip, Cooper met with the U.S. service members who supported the mine clearance mission. He thanked them for their continued commitment and dedication. “Today, primary transit routes in the Strait of Hormuz remain free and clear of Iranian sea mines thanks to incredible efforts by our people,” said Cooper. “We remain intensely focused on keeping commercial traffic flowing as we work with our teammates in the U.S. interagency, Gulf Cooperation Council, and shipping industry.” In recent months, over 95% of ships navigating the Strait of Hormuz have sailed through safely despite the IRGC’s unwarranted aggression, clearly demonstrating that the United States and regional partners control the international waterway. From U.S. Central Command, Oct. 25, 2026 The post CENTCOM Commander Visits Strait of Hormuz during Milestone Week appeared first on Seapower Magazine .

title: Govt establishes Coordination Center to organize registration of those subject to military service
body:
The Cabinet of Ministers of Ukraine has established a Coordination Center for the Organization of Reservist Enlistment during Mobilization and in Times of War.
Specifically, in accordance with Resolution No. 1328 of October 23, the government approved the composition and regulations of the Coordination Center for the Mobilization of Conscripts.
The Deputy Minister of Economy and Environment and the Deputy Minister of Defense have been appointed as co-chairs of the Coordination Center.
The Coordination Center also includes: the Deputy State Secretary of the Cabinet of Ministers; the Deputy Ministers of Digital Transformation, Internal Affairs, Infrastructure, and Agrarian Policy and Food; the State Secretary of the Ministry of Energy; a representative of the Ministry of Economy; the Deputy Head of the President's Office of Ukraine (subject to approval), the Deputy Chief of the General Staff of the Armed Forces (subject to approval), the First Deputy Head of the State Border Guard Service, the Deputy Head of the National Police, the Deputy Chairman of the Board of the Pension Fund of Ukraine, the Deputy Head of the State Labor Service, a representative of the Central Directorate of the State Security Service of Ukraine (subject to consent), a representative of the Foreign Intelligence Service (subject to approval), and a representative of the Main Intelligence Agency of the Ministry of Defense (subject to approval).
The main tasks of the Coordination Center are: to facilitate the coordination of actions by central and local executive authorities, other state bodies, and public administration bodies whose jurisdiction extends to the entire territory of Ukraine, regarding the reservation of conscripts for the period of mobilization and during wartime; providing proposals on the approaches, mechanisms, and methods for resolving issues related to the reservation of conscripts; coordinating criteria and, if necessary, providing recommendations for their refinement; reviewing proposals from state bodies regarding increasing the number of conscripts reserved for the mobilization period; reviewing proposals from state bodies regarding the determination of the criticality of enterprises; monitoring, through the Unified State Register of Conscripts, Persons Subject to Military Service, and Reservists, the Pension Fund's e-services web portal, and the Unified State e-services web portal, information regarding employees subject to military service of enterprises that have applied for critical status; providing state agencies with recommendations and proposals regarding the revocation of decisions designating enterprises as critical, particularly in response to relevant requests from law enforcement agencies.
In accordance with its assigned tasks, the Coordination Center: analyzes the current state of affairs and the causes of problems arising in the process of reserving conscripts; reviews the performance of state agencies, local government bodies, enterprises, institutions, and organizations on matters within its jurisdiction; coordinates the criteria for determining critical status; reviews proposals from state agencies regarding an increase in the number of conscripts reserved; reviews proposals regarding the designation of enterprises as critical and provides relevant recommendations; and provides recommendations regarding the revocation of decisions designating enterprises as critical.
The Coordination Center's recommendations and proposals are considered approved if more than half of the members and representatives of state bodies present at the meeting and invited to participate in the meeting vote in favor of them. In the event of a tie, a recommendation or proposal may be approved only if supported by both co-chairs.
The timeframe for the Coordination Center to issue recommendations and proposals based on the review of requests from government agencies may not exceed one calendar month from the date of receipt of the request.

title: Ghana’s road deaths demand urgent action, researchers warn
body: Researchers Enock Aninakwah and Isaac Aninakwah are calling for coordinated action to reduce road deaths in Ghana, citing unsafe road conditions, dangerous driving, and weaknesses in enforcement. In a paper titled A Nation in Motion, A People in Mourning: A Lamentation on Ghana’s Road Carnage, the authors argue that the country needs sustained improvements in road infrastructure, vehicle safety and emergency response. The paper examines road traffic fatalities between 1991 and 2024 using existing records and published research. It cites more than 46,000 deaths between 1991 and 2018, alongside reported figures of 2,494 deaths and 15,607 injuries in 2024. The authors say the consequences extend beyond those killed or injured. Families also face lost income, the cost of caring for survivors and emotional distress. “The findings of this study show that Ghana’s road safety crisis is driven by a chain of interconnected systemic failures rather than isolated factors,” they write. Enock Aninakwah is affiliated with the University of Ghana’s Department of Geography and Resource Development, while Isaac Aninakwah is affiliated with the Department of Social Sciences at St. Monica’s College of Education in Mampong. Their analysis draws on sources including the National Road Safety Authority, the Ghana Highway Authority, the World Health Organisation and earlier studies. The paper identifies poor road design and maintenance, inadequate lighting and signage, risky overtaking and unsafe vehicles among the concerns requiring attention. It argues that these problems are compounded by weak enforcement and gaps in emergency response, making a coordinated approach necessary. The researchers recommend safer road design, appropriate separation of opposing traffic, improved road maintenance and stronger vehicle roadworthiness checks. They also call for sustained public education, enforcement against dangerous driving and better coordination among institutions responsible for transport and public safety. Drawing on earlier research, the authors describe fear and anxiety surrounding everyday travel, warning that repeated fatal crashes can weaken public confidence in the transport system. They urge authorities to treat road safety as a public health and development priority and use reliable data to monitor whether interventions are reducing deaths and injuries. The analysis relies mainly on reported fatality counts. The authors acknowledge that consistent long-term information on vehicle use and distances travelled was unavailable, limiting their ability to assess changes in risk relative to road use. title: SpaceX Locks Up $40 Billion for AI Chips as Musk Warns Most Neoclouds Will Die
body:
SpaceX said it has closed a $40 billion financing deal to buy AI chips for its data centers. Elon Musk used the announcement to warn that lenders have almost entirely cut off money to companies that depend on AI data centers for their revenue.
The financing covers GPUs, the graphics processors that train and run AI models, for SpaceX, which absorbed xAI in February. According to a regulatory filing, an entity managed by Apollo Global Management, an investment firm that lends directly to companies instead of going through banks, will buy the chips and lease them to SpaceX.
Musk called it debt, but the filing describes a finance lease, a long-term rental that works like a loan. SpaceX would repay about $40 billion in principal through quarterly installments over roughly five years, plus interest at a fixed rate that has not been set. The chips arrive in batches, with leases starting in the first half of 2027.
“As of the past few weeks, debt markets have almost entirely shut off access to money for any company that doesn't have substantial revenue independent of AI data centers,” Musk wrote on X. “SpaceX closed $40B of debt for GPUs, but we're investment grade and have Starlink & launch revenue.”
As of the past few weeks, debt markets have almost entirely shut off access to money for any company that doesn’t have substantial revenue independent of AI data centers.
SpaceX closed $40B of debt for GPUs, but we’re investment grade and have Starlink & launch…
— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) October 25, 2026
Investment grade is a credit rating telling lenders a borrower is unlikely to miss payments, and Moody's rated SpaceX Baa1, an investment-grade level, in June. Starlink is SpaceX's satellite internet business, and both it and the rocket launches bring in revenue that has nothing to do with AI.
“That means the 200+ neoclouds are going to see guppy-level death and consolidation,” Musk added. “Some will make it through, but not many.”
Neoclouds are specialist companies that rent out GPU capacity to AI developers. The largest, CoreWeave, began in 2017 by mining Ethereum with graphics cards before pivoting to AI after the network retired mining in 2022.
CoreWeave's shares fell about 30% between September 30 and October 16, from $87 to $61, and the company carries roughly $50 billion in debt. Its unsecured bonds, meaning loans with no specific assets pledged as backup, yielded about 15% in mid-October, so investors demanded roughly 15% a year to lend to it.
The weakness is that chips lose value fast while the loans last for years. CoreWeave booked nearly $1.4 billion in depreciation and amortization, the accounting charge for hardware wearing out, in the second quarter against about $2.6 billion in revenue.
Ken Griffin , founder of Citadel, told the firm's markets conference on October 20 that GPUs resemble airline seats as both cost almost nothing to add once they exist, so prices can collapse when supply outruns demand.
Venture capitalist and entrepreneur Chamath Palihapitiya expects more AI computing power to sit idle in 2027 than forecasts assume. “There are delays in the existing pipeline that will catch people off guard in 2027,” he wrote on X . “Hyperscalers will (obviously) react by focusing on their own internal compute needs over any third party.”
Hyperscalers are the cloud giants such as Amazon, Microsoft, and Google. Palihapitiya said the stranded hardware is bought and paid for but earns less than it costs to finance, a problem he said holds across the industry with one exception he did not name.
“2027 will be a turbulent year because it will clear out a bunch of wrong/bad bets,” Palihapitiya wrote . “It will also be a consolidation year for a few.”
SpaceX said it expects to finalize the master finance lease before the end of 2026, and the interest rate on the roughly $40 billion in leases has yet to be determined.

title: Sweden Selects Saildrone for Year-long MDA MIssion in the Baltic Sea
body: COPENHAGEN, Denmark —Saildrone today announced a year-long mission with the Swedish Armed Forces to deliver persistent maritime domain awareness across Sweden’s territorial waters and exclusive economic zone in the Baltic Sea. Under the agreement, Saildrone will deploy and operate four Voyager unmanned surface vehicles (USVs) for 360 days each, representing 1,440 contracted vehicle-days of continuous maritime security operations. This deployment marks the first national deployment of Saildrone USVs under the Nordic Defence Cooperation (NORDEFCO) framework that enables participating Nordic nations to rapidly procure Saildrone maritime domain awareness services. Additional national deployments under the framework will follow. The 12-month commitment highlights a decisive shift toward long-term operational capabilities, with the Swedish Armed Forces securing a full year of persistent maritime domain awareness to safeguard critical waters from the outset. “This is fundamentally not about four unmanned vessels, but about access to sustained intelligence collection at sea. In other words, we are purchasing a persistent maritime surveillance service, and Saildrone provides the vessels that supply the Navy with data,” said Johan Wahren, project manager at Sweden’s Defence Materiel Administration (FMV) in a FMV press release . NORDEFCO is a cooperative organization that unites Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, Sweden, and other Northern European countries to streamline defense cooperation and field proven regional security solutions. The Saildrone Voyager fleet will continuously patrol Sweden’s territorial waters in the Baltic Sea, delivering real-time maritime intelligence directly to the Swedish Armed Forces. Operating as a managed service, Saildrone maintains, deploys, and tasks the USVs, enabling Sweden to maintain persistent maritime domain awareness without deploying additional crewed ships. “This mission reflects Sweden’s commitment to securing the Baltic Sea and highlights Saildrone’s growing operational presence across Northern Europe,” said Robert Kleist, Saildrone’s European managing director. “Sweden is investing in year-round maritime awareness as an operational capability. The NORDEFCO framework gives Nordic nations a common mechanism for accessing that capability while allowing each country to define and operate its own mission.” Saildrone delivers persistent maritime domain awareness for navies and law enforcement operating in the world’s harshest maritime environments. The company has supported defense and security missions in places ranging from the Baltic Sea and the High North to the Southern Ocean and the Middle East. Saildrone recently registered four Saildrone Voyager USVs in Denmark to operate under the Danish national flag. The registration establishes a clear flag-state framework for Saildrone USVs operating internationally and supports the company operating alongside various European nations. Saildrone Europe will flag additional Saildrone USVs in the coming weeks. From Saildrone, Oct. 26, 2026 The post Sweden Selects Saildrone for Year-long MDA MIssion in the Baltic Sea appeared first on Seapower Magazine .

title: At 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit, Tinubu Says His Govt Is Rewriting Nation’s Decades-old Story of Economic Underperformance
body: .Stresses economic reforms are restoring confidence, laying foundation for sustainable growth Deji Elumoye in Abuja President Bola Tinubu on Monday disclosed that his government is rewriting Nigeria’s decades-long story of economic underperformance through far-reaching reforms designed to dismantle structural barriers, unlock the nation’s enormous potential and deliver jobs, productivity and shared prosperity. According to him, the administration is currently undertaking what it came into office to achieve: rewriting the story of a nation that has performed below its potential for far too long. Speaking in Abuja while formally declaring open the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit, the President, who was represented by Vice President Kashim Shettima, noted that his government began on a difficult note because there is no shortcut to economic growth. His words: “Distinguished ladies and gentlemen, we came to rewrite the story of a nation that has performed below its potential for far too long. But there is no shortcut to economic growth. This is why we began with a difficult reset. For us, rescuing the economy means rescuing livelihoods and transforming the fortunes of young jobseekers, farmers, manufacturers, entrepreneurs and innovators. “We cannot harness the immense opportunities offered by our growing population without first stabilising the economy. We must also create the conditions for the public and private sectors to invest, expand and generate productive employment.” Tinubu observed that the summit’s theme, “Growth That Works: Delivering Jobs, Productivity and Shared Prosperity,” built on the ambition of the previous edition of the annual event to achieve a prosperous and inclusive Nigeria by 2030. He noted that his administration has “since set in motion a series of reforms to dismantle the structural barriers that have prevented our abundant human and natural resources from yielding prosperity. “These reforms are restoring confidence, strengthening our economic foundations and laying the groundwork for sustainable growth,” he added, noting that the administration is encouraged by what it has accomplished so far. Acknowledging that creating jobs was only half the task, the President stressed the need to “improve the quality of work, reduce underemployment and harness the potential” of the nation’s underutilised workforce. “Our pursuit of prosperity demands greater productivity from every worker, enterprise and investment. We must judge infrastructure by the economic activity it generates and education by the skills and productivity it delivers. “We must judge industrial policy by the competitiveness of our firms and investment incentives by the capital, technology, exports and jobs they attract.” Tinubu outlined what he described as the achievements of his administration’s reforms, saying they have been well documented. He cited figures from the National Bureau of Statistics indicating that Nigeria’s inflation-adjusted GDP grew by 3.89% in the first quarter of 2026, compared with 3.13% a year earlier. On economic diversification, he stated that “non-oil activities accounted for 96.08% of GDP, while manufacturing grew by 3.29% and the oil sector by 2.57%,” emphasising that the gains have reinforced his administration’s confidence in the path of recovery and diversification. The President stated, however, that his administration’s ambition must go beyond favourable statistics, even as the development narrative is changing and investor confidence is returning. Outlining the administration’s gains so far, he said, “In the first quarter of 2026, our capital importation reached $10.37 billion, an increase of 83.83% over the corresponding period in 2025. This comprised both portfolio and foreign direct investment. We will, therefore, continue to ease regulatory burdens, strengthen transparency and policy predictability, and expand access to finance. “Our tax reforms seek to build a modern, equitable system that finances development and gives businesses certainty. This discipline must guide our investments in all sectors of the economy, including energy, agriculture and solid minerals. We are reforming the electricity market to improve supply and attract investment in generation, transmission, distribution and alternative energy.” On agriculture, Tinubu said the administration is connecting farms to storage facilities, processing centres and markets while expanding irrigation, mechanisation, finance and rural infrastructure. He added that the government is also seeking “to move beyond extraction into domestic processing, industrial production and exports” in the solid minerals sector. The President, however, noted that despite the gains of his administration’s economic reforms, the task remains far from finished, even as young Nigerians have demonstrated their capacity to compete globally in technology, financial services and the creative industries. On her part, United Nations Deputy Secretary-General, Dr. Amina Mohammed, assessed the reforms implemented under the Tinubu administration, acknowledging the gains while urging their urgent consolidation and stabilisation, as well as the effective management of expectations among citizens and other stakeholders. She also applauded the African Development Bank (AfDB) for its new financial architecture for development across the African continent, particularly its prioritisation of financing programmes that target impactful development. In his remarks, Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Dr. Taiwo Oyedele, presented the Nigerian Economic Policy Framework, which he described as a national economic doctrine that establishes how Nigeria makes economic decisions and measures real progress. The minister invited members of the Nigerian Economic Summit Group (NESG) and private sector experts to make valuable contributions to the development of the framework by rigorously critiquing the draft proposal with facts and figures. He said the principles underpinning the framework include enterprise, open but fair markets, and whole-of-government coherence. Oyedele also listed key areas of focus in the proposed framework, including economic stability, human capital development and productivity, among others. Earlier in his welcome address, Chairman of the NESG, Mr. Olaniyi Yusuf, said participation at the 32nd summit reflected stakeholders’ commitment to contributing to inclusive and impactful growth, while acknowledging the Federal Government’s efforts to improve the ease of doing business in the country. He said that although the reforms of the Tinubu administration may have introduced significant changes to Nigeria’s economic structures, the task before economic experts at the summit and beyond was to ensure stabilisation rather than seek a reversal of the policies. Yusuf added that the 32nd edition of the summit must help Nigeria move from policy consensus to a framework that resolves practical issues, noting that deliberations would be guided by proposals for job creation, improved productivity and shared prosperity for all. Also speaking, Chairman and Founder of BUA Group, Abdul Samad Rabiu, commended the economic reforms of President Tinubu’s administration, saying they had begun to address longstanding challenges confronting Nigerian businesses. Rabiu acknowledged the difficulties experienced by ordinary Nigerians but noted that improvements in access to foreign exchange had created a more predictable environment for businesses. “For many years, one of the greatest challenges facing businesses was access to foreign exchange. You could have all the naira but be unable to obtain the foreign exchange needed to buy raw materials and machinery,” he recalled.

title: Italy flotilla torture case against IDF officials even broader than ICC war crimes
body: Italy's criminal probe of flotilla activists' torture claims against Israel impacts far more IDF officials than even the pending file before the International Criminal Court (ICC), multiple Israeli officials with knowledge of the case have confirmed to The Jerusalem Post.Since 2007, flotilla activists have periodically sought to block Israel's blockade to prevent weapons smuggling to Hamas in Gaza.Although the activists claim they are seeking to bring Gazans humanitarian aid, Gazans have been receiving over 600 trucks of aid per day since the October 2025 ceasefire – almost triple what they were receiving pre-war.Gazans' overall situation is still far worse because the Strip is years away from being rebuilt, but there is no actual food shortage.ICC seeks to arrest Netanyahu, Gallant, may target other Israeli officialsCurrently, the ICC is confirmed to be seeking to arrest Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former defense minister Yoav Gallant, with reports that it is also seeking to arrest minister Betzalel Smotrich and Itamar Ben-Gvir, and possibly also Defense Minister Israel Katz, IDF Chief of Staff Lt.-Gen. Eyal Zamir, and former IDF chief Herzi Halevi.That is still a short list, and most of the officials are government officials because Israel has not probed its government officials.In contrast, the Italian criminal probe relating to Israel's treatment of arrested activists from the September-October 2025 and April-May 2026 flotillas not only includes many of the same ministers, but it also implicates a long list of IDF and prison service officials, of around a dozen.In fact, the IDF officials being targeted are even more noteworthy than the prison service officials, given that there is some cloud of impropriety hanging over the prison service since it has been managed in recent years by Ben-Gvir.Ben-Gvir himself was condemned by the entire Israeli government for various actions he undertook and statements he made relating to the flotilla activists.But the IDF officials include completely apolitical and generally highly regarded officials, such as: former navy chief David Saar Salame, current Navy Chief Eyal Harel, each of their top advisers Tal Politis and Guy Levy, Ashdod Naval Base Chief Eitan Paz, and the Shayetet 13 Naval Commander.While none of the activists' claims against Israeli officials have been proven, there have been Israeli officials concerned that police and prison guard officials, who are under Ben-Gvir's command, may have roughed up some of the activists.Put differently, even if some of the most sensational charges might be untrue or exaggerated, some officials recognize that some of the lesser claims against officials under Ben-Gvir may be true.Yet, there are no Israeli officials who believe that the navy's conduct was anything other than highly professional, leaving many mystified as to what prosecutors from Italy – a country which has been one of Israel's stronger allies even after October 7- could really be trying to get after going after IDF and naval officials.The Post understands from officials with knowledge of the case that the prosecution is being run by a local Italian prosecutor, who is not coordinating with the Italian federal government.Italian prosecutor rogue prosecutor, Israeli officials tell 'Post'In other words, Israeli officials speaking to the Post portrayed the prosecutor as a rogue prosecutor who is using an Italian law for universal jurisdiction that the government would not have intended or expected to use against an ally like Israel, as much as it may have been passed to go after a traveling warlord from a more broken non-democratic country.Further, the case has been a major domestic politics issue within Italy, such that some officials may see it as advantageous internally to make noise about such a case, without necessarily moving it forward to the end, something which could take many years in any event.Around the time of the flotillas, Italy suspended certain defense cooperation arrangements with Israel, and the sides have sparred publicly over the treatment of some activists who were recently detained in the West Bank while assisting Palestinians with the olive harvest.However, Israeli officials still view this criminal proceeding as being in conflict with overall Italian government policy, which has not sought to inflame relations.Rather, multiple sources with knowledge of the case said that the long list of IDF officials who are considered highly professional simply indicated how politicized and disjointed the specific prosecutor likely was.Moreover, they indicated that once a criminal probe is opened, it is always easier to add other suspects into the probe, even if they have less of a true connection to the heart of the issue.The Israeli minister, IDF officials, police, and prison officials were all put under official investigation in Italy on October 16.The move expanded an investigation that was previously focused on Ben-Gvir.The case concerns alleged torture, kidnapping, personal injury, robbery and damage when Israeli forces intercepted small fleets of boats headed towards Gaza in 2025 and 2026, the Rome prosecutors' office said in a statement.Probe opened after activists launched complaintsInvestigators opened the probe after complaints from 50 Italian citizens who were detained ⁠by Israeli authorities following two Global Sumud Flotilla missions in September to October 2025 and April to May 2026.Prosecutors said activists detained after the first mission had reported beatings, injuries, death threats, insults and accusations of terrorism.Notably, being insulted and being accused of terrorism might be problematic or fully justified, but would usually not be criminally probed.Activists involved in the second mission alleged even harsher treatment, including beatings in the dark, the use of rubber bullets, and tasers, a statement said.Once again, some of these actions would clearly be criminal, but using a non-lethal taser to subdue a person resisting arrest is standard even in the West.Investigators had identified various individuals forming the military and police chains of command involved in ‌the ⁠operations, prosecutors said.Prosecutors said they had sent Israel a request for judicial assistance in June, seeking information needed to reconstruct events and establish individual responsibility. They did not ⁠say whether Israeli authorities had responded.Questioned about their response, multiple Israeli authorities declined to address the issue, signaling that Israel may view the request as invalid if it is not endorsed by the Italian federal government or may choose to deal with it through diplomatic channels as opposed to strictly technical channels.An interesting question would be whether Israel might comply more if the requests were more limited to Ben-Gvir and some of his officials, who took videos of themselves at minimum verbally harassing detainees.Under Italian law, crimes ⁠committed abroad against Italian citizens can be prosecuted in Rome.Being placed under investigation in Italy does not imply guilt and does not automatically lead to a trial. However, if the probe determines that charges are ⁠warranted, prosecutors could lodge a formal request for trial.Reuters contributed to this report.

title: Australian judge denies murderer’s bid to lift prison ban on Vegemite
body:
A convicted murderer who argued in an Australian court that disallowing him access to the yeast-based spread Vegemite was a violation of his human rights has lost a legal battle seeking permission to consume the delicacy from prison.
Andre McKechnie, 55, who is serving a life sentence for murder in the southern Australian state of Victoria, took his battle for the black-brown byproduct of brewing beer to the Supreme Court last year.
He argued that being refused Vegemite denied him his right under the Charter of Human Rights and Responsibilities Act to “enjoy his culture as an Australian in the community with other persons of Australian background,” court documents viewed by the Associated Press showed.
Justice Claire Harris said prison authorities’ refusal to allow McKechnie Vegemite did limit his cultural rights under the legislation, but that the ban was justified as part of an attempt to eliminate illicit drugs and alcohol from the prison system.
“The limitation on Mr. McKechnie’s ability to enjoy Vegemite in community with other persons of Australian background is primarily that he is a prisoner,” she wrote in her judgment.
Vegemite has been banned at all of Victoria’s state prisons for 20 years because authorities say it could impair a sniffer dog’s ability to identify narcotics and that its yeast content could be used to brew alcohol.
McKechnie, who defended himself in court, argued that because the neighbouring state of New South Wales does not ban Vegemite in state prisons, it was evidence that there were “less restrictive means reasonably available” to stop illicit substances from entering the system.
He went on to say that Vegemite does not interfere with sniffer dogs’ ability to detect narcotics by citing a 2017 Melbourne newspaper article reporting on a man’s failed attempt to use the pungent smell of the spread to conceal drugs he was trying to smuggle into a music festival in Victoria. His efforts were marred by police dogs.
He also argued that Vegemite does not contain live yeast and therefore can not be used to concoct alcohol.
A state prison department manager, Kevin White, cited publicly available research that said Vegemite helped home-brewed beer ferment more quickly.
McKechnie had previously testified that a lack of Vegemite in his diet had contributed to his thiamine, or vitamin B1, deficiency.
He later dropped the thiamine argument and said it was “not important,” after lawyers for prison authorities objected to evidence of a deficiency.
McKechnie said that not eating Vegemite left him feeling “deprived” of his Australian culture, and that it made him “sad” and “disconnected” from his family and the wider community.
The judge said it was “difficult to accept that the inability to consume Vegemite, rather than the fact of his imprisonment, is a material cause of his sadness and disconnection from his family and community,” and upheld prison authorities’ argument that McKechnie had failed to provide any proper foundations for his opinion that Vegemite does not interfere with sniffer dogs.
Vegemite is a culinary staple in Australia, and more than 80 per cent of households are estimated to have a jar at home. It is generally considered an acquired taste. Variations of the spread are also extremely popular in New Zealand and in the U.K., where it is known as Marmite.
Vegemite, which was invented in Australia in the 1920s, began as an iteration of Marmite, which was created in the U.K. in the early 1900s and shipped to Australia, where its popularity soared.
Australian Vegemite was developed as its own product with a distinct flavour profile and is made using a recipe that is different from British Marmite, which has a sweeter, more syrupy texture. Vegemite tends to be more dense and bitter.
New Zealand Marmite is also distinct from its counterparts.
The last U.S. president to visit Australia, Barack Obama, once said Australian Vegemite was “horrible.”
– – With files from the Associated Press

title: USS McFaul Returns to Norfolk Following Deployment
body: The Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer USS McFaul (DDG 74) returned to Naval Station Norfolk, Oct. 23, 2026, concluding an 11-month deployment to the U.S. 5th and 6th Fleet areas of operation. During McFaul’s deployment, it employed the Aegis Combat System, providing multi-mission offensive and defensive capabilities during the buildup and execution of Operation Epic Fury. The warship provided anti-air warfare, surface warfare, and naval surface fire support during combat operations, integrating with the USS Abraham Lincoln, USS George H.W. Bush, and USS George Washington Carrier Strike Groups. “The Sailors of the USS McFaul have performed exceptionally well during this demanding combat deployment, proving themselves as a true warfighting powerhouse. Operating in a highly volatile region, this crew has repeatedly demonstrated the grit, technical mastery, and resilience required to protect our strike group and execute complex missions under pressure,” said Cmdr. Adam Samson, commanding officer, USS McFaul. “I could not be more proud of their unwavering dedication and the quiet professionalism they bring to the watch every single day. The true strength of this warship is, and always will be, its people.” The warship originally departed Norfolk Nov. 25, 2025, and spent the deployment defending U.S., allied, and partner interests across Europe and the Middle East. USS McFaul is a fast, multi-mission surface combatant capable of conducting anti-air, anti-submarine, and anti-surface warfare operations. As a Flight II Arleigh Burke-class guided-missile destroyer equipped with the Aegis Combat System, the warship is designed to operate either independently or fully integrated within a carrier strike group or amphibious readiness group. By leveraging its Vertical Launching System and advanced radar network, McFaul can simultaneously track and defeat multiple threats in high-intensity environments. Commissioned on April 25, 1998, in Savannah, Georgia, USS McFaul is the 24th destroyer of its class and the 11th built at Ingalls Shipbuilding in Pascagoula, Mississippi. The warship is named after Engineman Chief Petty Officer (SEAL) Donald L. McFaul, who made the ultimate sacrifice while attempting to carry a wounded team member to safety during Operation Just Cause in 1989. As the first warship bearing his name, USS McFaul honors his sacrifice and devotion to duty, operating under the ship motto “Courage, Honor, Sacrifice.” Commander, Naval Surface Force Atlantic is responsible for manning, training, and equipping assigned surface forces and shore activities, ensuring a capable and combat-ready force to support U.S. national interests. The SURFLANT force consists of more than 66 warships and 34 shore commands. Commander, Naval Surface Force Atlantic, Oct. 26, 2026 The post USS McFaul Returns to Norfolk Following Deployment appeared first on Seapower Magazine .

title: Ebola: Nigeria Could Declare Outbreak Over By December 7 If No New Cases Emerge — Pate
body: The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate, has said that Nigeria could progress towards declaring the Ebola outbreak over under the World Health Organisation’s criteria, potentially as early as 7 December 2026, if no further confirmed or probable cases are detected. Pate disclosed this in a post on his X page on Monday. He said that following the imported Ebola index patient’s medical evacuation from Nigeria today, 26 October, the government’s immediate priorities remain active monitoring of all identified contacts, prompt investigation of alerts, and strengthened readiness across our health facilities. “If no further confirmed or probable cases are detected, Nigeria could progress towards declaring this outbreak over under WHO criteria, potentially as early as 7 December 2026,” the minister stated. “This date remains provisional, subject to NCDC and WHO validating the 42-day countdown.” He, however, noted that “any further case would require a fresh countdown in accordance with those criteria”. “Our teams, working with FCTA and state health authorities and our partners, remain focused on containment and preventing community transmission,” Pate said. “I ask Nigerians to remain calm, cooperate with contact-tracing teams and follow regular updates from NCDC and FMoH.” Following the imported Ebola index patient’s medical evacuation from Nigeria today, 26 October, our immediate priorities remain active monitoring of all identified contacts, prompt investigation of alerts and strengthened readiness across our health facilities. If no further confirmed or probable cases are detected, Nigeria could progress towards declaring this outbreak over under @WHO criteria, potentially as early as 7 December 2026. This date remains provisional, subject to @NCDCgov and WHO validating the 42-day countdown. Any further case would require a fresh countdown in accordance with those criteria. Our teams, working with FCTA and state health authorities and our partners, remain focused on containment and preventing community transmission. I ask Nigerians to remain calm, cooperate with contact-tracing teams and follow regular updates from @NCDCgov and @Fmohnigeria. @OfficialFCTA @WHONigeria @WHOAFRO @WHO @AfricaCDC @DrPavelUrsu @ProfJanabi @CDCgov @Dr_JeanKaseya @christian_happi @alikothe3rd @SalakoIziaq — Muhammad Ali Pate (@muhammadpate) October 26, 2026 Nigeria announced its first confirmed case of the Bundibugyo strain in the Federal Capital Territory on October 20, 2026. It identified the patient as a woman with a recent travel history to Uganda, who returned to Nigeria with symptoms on October 7, which progressed four days later before tests confirmed the infection, though the Ugandan authorities denied reports of an Ebola outbreak in the East African nation. On Sunday, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) said that the number of contacts, including health workers, linked to the patient had risen to 53. On Monday, Pate confirmed that the index patient was flown to Switzerland, disclosing that the woman, who was evacuated along with her husband, was stable and conscious and had clinically improved. The minister, however, noted that her improvements did not mean she was no longer infectious, stating that strict protocols were put in place before her evacuation.
