title: Playback: JoyNews Research fact-checks South Africa evacuation cost claims
body: When hundreds of Ghanaians needed help returning home from South Africa, the government stepped in to facilitate their evacuation. But questions have since emerged over how public funds were spent and whether the records submitted by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs accurately reflect the payments made. Now, a JoyNews Research investigation has uncovered what appear to be forged signatures and discrepancies in payment records contained in the Ministry’s data. Who received the money? Do the records accurately account for the expenditure? And how did documents with questionable signatures become part of the data used to account for a government-funded operation? As the controversy deepens and demands for accountability grow, JoyNews examines the documents, traces the inconsistencies and investigates the questions surrounding the evacuation exercise. This is a closer look at the South Africa evacuation controversy – and the troubling gaps between the records and the money they are supposed to account for. Watch the livestream here:

title: Why Africa Cannot abandon Cuba
body: BY FEMI FALANA SAN (Speech delivered at the Rally held by the Nigeria Solidarity Movement with Cuba in Lagos on October 24, 2026) INTRODUCTION Following the 1959 Cuban Revolution, Fidel Castro made solidarity with Africa a corner stone of the foreign policy of Cuba. Hence, the government developed interest in the anticolonial movements and socialist governments in Africa. In 1961, Cuba sent a military mission to the Kwame Nkrumah government in Ghana. And following the independence of Algeria in 1962, Cuba sent military assistance and medical supplies to the Algerian National Liberation Front. The visit of Ernesto Che Guevara to the progressive movements in the Portuguese colonies in 1964 consolidated the involvement of Cuba in African affairs. A year later, Che Guevara was in the Democratic Republic of the Congo to offer his knowledge and experience as a guerrilla fighter. CUBA’S SUPPORT FOR LIBERATION STRUGGLE IN AFRICA Cuba became a strong ally of the defunct Organization for African Unity and the African Union in the struggle against colonialism and apartheid. In justifying Cuba’s internationalist foreign policy and deployment of troops to support anti-colonial and anti-apartheid movements across Africa, Fidel Castro famously stated, “African blood flows freely through our veins. Many of our ancestors came as slaves from Africa to this land. As slaves they struggled a great deal. They fought as members of the Liberating Army of Cuba. We’re brothers and sisters of the people of Africa and we’re ready to fight on their behalf.” On another occasion, the Cuban leader said, “We are a Latin-American nation and a Latin-African nation as well.” In support of the independence movements that engaged in armed struggle against European colonial powers in Guinea-Bissau, Mozambique, and Angola, Cuba sent military advisers, fighters and equipment. Thousands of Cuban troops were deployed to support the People’s Movement for the Liberation of Angola (MPLA) against the invading South African apartheid forces and rival local armed groups sided by the United States and other western governments. Not less than 55,000 Cuban troops took part in the historic battle of Cuito Cuanavale in Angola from 1987–1988. Indeed, it was the military setbacks suffered in the battle field by South Africa that compelled the apartheid regime to enter into the political negotiations that culminated in the independence of Namibia in 1990, and South Africa in 1994. CUBA’S MEDICAL INTERVENTIONS IN AFRICA Based on its long-standing history of medical internationalism in Africa, Cuba has sent thousands of medical personnel including doctors and nurses to confront dangerous diseases in many African countries. During the West African Ebola outbreak in 2014-2015, Cuba provided the largest medical personnel consisting of over 460 health workers (including a contingent of 165 through the World Health Organization) to Sierra Leone, Liberia, and Guinea. Many world leaders commended Cuba for the success recorded in combating the Ebola Virus disease while the late Pope Francis lauded the “heroic” doctors, nurses, and volunteers from around the world who traveled to West Africa to contain the “implacable illness”. In 2020, Cuba dispatched hundreds of medical personnel to African countries to help various governments to combat the Covid 19 pandemic. The medical teams provided frontline support in multiple African countries including South Africa, Angola, Cape Verde, and Togo that were facing serious health crisis. Unlike Western countries that usually recommend mosquito nets and insect killers for combating the scourge of malaria fever, Cuba has collaborated with some African countries to work on vector-control programs to eradicate malaria and dengue. In particular, Cuba has helped countries to build biolarvicide factories, trained local community health agents, and set up primary care frameworks in rural municipalities in Africa. No doubt, the dissolution of the Soviet Union in 1991 had adverse political and economic impact on Cuba. Notwithstanding the economic difficulties experienced by Cuba, compounded by the crippling sanctions imposed by the United States, the Government has continued to offer bilateral scholarships, fellowships, and grants for international students from various African countries to study Medicine, Engineering, Agronomy, Sciences, Humanities and Technology. Apart from Cuba, no country has provided medical, educational and military assistance to African countries without any strings attached. GENOCIDAL ATTACKS ON CUBA BY THE UNITED STATES Cuba is being asphyxiated by the US in order to carry out a regime change that cannot be justified under international law. However, since the economic strangulation of Cuba has not materialised in the collapse of the Cuban government, the US government decided to cook up the charges of conspiracy and murder against Raul Castro and five other Cubans. The planned military aggression is also meant to divert attention from the monumental disgrace suffered by the US in the reckless war being waged against Iran by the US and Israel. To that extent, the sole purpose of the indictment of Raul Castro is to justify military aggression against Cuba. It is a shameful replay of the indictment of Venezuelan President Nicholas Maduro by U.S. courts, which provided a pretext for the large scale military assault in January 2026 resulting in his abduction. The unilateral United States economic, commercial, and financial blockade against Cuba since 1962, is illegal and a gross violation of the United Nations Charter which promotes international peace and sovereignty of all countries. In a desperate bid to find justification for its imperialist agenda, the United States added Cuba to its list of countries allegedly sponsoring terrorism. But since the baseless and utterly false accusation has never been proven by the United States, we demand the removal of Cuba from the list of terrorist nations. No doubt, the US government has realised that another invasion of Cuba would be worse than the Bay of Pigs invasion of 1962. Hence, President Trump decided to impose fresh economic sanctions in a desperate bid to carry out regime change in Cuba. In addition to the blockade of over 60 years, President Trump moved to block oil from reaching Cuba, pushing up prices for food, medicine, transportation and prompting severe fuel shortages and hours of blackouts. A few days, the US Secretary of State, Mr. Marco Rubio openly asked the Cuban people on Twitter for ” a discreet partnership with the CIA” to overthrow the government of Cuba The incitement followed the statement credited to President Trump in Florida that he was going to send Marco Rubio “to end the deal” with Cuba. The incitement of the United States and the genocidal sanctions imposed on Cuba constitute a provocative infringement of the human rights of the Cuban people to self determination guaranteed by the United Nations Charter. ILLEGALITY OF ECONOMIC SANCTIONS IMPOSED ON CUBA The harsh economic sanctions imposed on Cuba by President are allegedly based on the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA). As if that was not enough, the US government threatened to impose tariffs on any country that exports oil to Cuba. However, in the case of Learning Resources Inc et al vTrump, President of the United States et al No 24-1287 of February 20, 2026, the Supreme Court of the United States held that President Trump’s tariffs that are based on the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA)—are unconstitutional. The judges emphatically stated that the statute does not authorize the use of tariffs and that the President does not have authority to tax. The court specifically stated the power to tax, including the imposition of tariffs, lies exclusively with the US Congress, in accordance with the US Constitution. The implication of the historic judgment is that President Donald Trump’s Executive Order imposing tariffs on countries selling oil to Cuba under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act is illegal, null and void having exceeded the President’s constitutional authority. Since President Trump has absolute contempt for the rule of law, he has recklessly subjected the Justices of the Supreme Court who delivered the epochal judgment to spurious attacks. We are compelled to call on the Congress of the United States to enforce the judgment by lifting the unilateral sanctions imposed on Cuba by Mr. Trump which have caused humanitarian crisis in Cuba. As the Cuban people have the inalienable right to choose their own political system, the threat of President Trump to force them to adopt capitalism cannot be justified under international law. The US Congress ought to have realised that humanity allies with the Cuban people in their principled stand to live a life of dignity, free from threats and sanctions, and in accordance with the right of all countries to sovereignty. As no nation should be subjected to external interference, coercive measures, or economic blockades that undermine its sovereignty and the welfare of its people, the US embargo and all sanctions imposed on Cuba should be lifted in accordance with standing UN resolutions and, that the world body should sanction the US, if it fails to do so ON DUTY OF AFRICAN PEOPLE TO SUPPORT CUBA It is indisputable that Cuba’s historic internationalism and solidarity with Africa contributed to the defeat of colonialism, and minority rule in Africa. Without expecting any material gain, Cuba shed the blood of its youth for Africa. Not less than 4,300 Cubans paid the supreme sacrifice in conflicts in Africa, with half of them in Angola alone. The thousands of Cuban doctors and other medical personnel sent to Africa and the many African students trained in medicine in Cuba have combined to save the lives of millions of African people. Having regard to the unquantified contribution of Cuba to the independence struggle of the African people, all African countries owe it a duty to assist Cuba to defend its sovereignty under international law. After all, Cuba is the only country whose heroic youths shed their blood for the liberation and development of African nations. In view of the enormous contribution of the Cuban people to the struggle for independence in Africa, the member states of the African Union must rally round Cuba in defending her sovereignty and right to self- determination. Despite the dubious campaign and blackmail of the Trump administration, African countries owe it a duty to vote at the United Nations from October 27-28, 2026 against the sanctions and embargo imposed on Cuba by the United States without any legal justification. The post Why Africa Cannot abandon Cuba appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: EKUMFI: How $6M EXIM participation built a $53M industrial asset — Now poised for a 24-Hour economy breakthrough
body: With the 20% excise duty on local fruit juices now abolished, the government’s Feed the Industries Programme offers Ekumfi Fruits & Juices a pathway to US$48 million in annual turnover, more than 9,000 acres of fruit cultivation, and up to GH₵52,000 in gross revenue per acre for youth and farmers growing pineapple. The transformation could also open a route to accelerated EXIM debt repayment. Ghana’s industrialization journey may be entering a defining chapter. Ekumfi Fruits & Juices Limited is emerging as a potential model for turning development-finance investment into agricultural prosperity, youth employment, industrial expansion, and export growth. With approximately US$6 million in Ghana EXIM Bank participation, Ekumfi has built an industrial enterprise with an estimated asset value of US$53 million — a modern fruit-processing facility, Ghanaian juice brands, and a foundation for international market expansion. Yet this substantial investment has lived with a contradiction. Despite significant processing capacity, the company has been constrained by inadequate supplies of pineapple and other fruits, and by the 20% excise duty imposed on locally manufactured fruit juices in 2023. At times, production has been limited to roughly two days a week, leaving equipment and infrastructure underused. The cost reaches well beyond the company. Farmers lose an established industrial buyer. Young people miss employment and enterprise opportunities. Ghana loses manufacturing output and export earnings. Ekumfi’s challenge has never simply been the existence of a factory. It has been building the agricultural and financial ecosystem needed to keep that factory running at its potential. Today, the government’s excise reforms, the Feed the Industries Programme and the 24-Hour Economy agenda create an opening to address those structural constraints. The Excise Duty Removal Creates a New Opening Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson announced the abolition of the 20% excise duty on locally manufactured fruit juices in the 2026 Mid-Year Budget Review on 23 July. The exemption, enacted under the Excise Duty Act, 2026, took effect on 1 October 2026. For Ekumfi, the change can improve price competitiveness, strengthen operating margins, stimulate consumer demand and free up room for reinvestment in agricultural production. But removing the tax solves only one side of the industrial equation. The more fundamental challenge is raw material. A processing plant cannot run three shifts a day when its agricultural supply chain supports only a fraction of installed capacity. This is where Feed the Industries becomes decisive. Feed the Industries: Linking Ghana’s Farms to Its Factories The Feed the Industries Programme, under the 24-Hour Economy framework, is designed to connect agricultural production directly to industrial demand. For Ekumfi, that means a coordinated fruit-supply system drawing on commercial estates, smallholder farmers, youth agricultural enterprises, outgrower cooperatives and agricultural service providers. Management estimates that sustained 24-hour operations would require more than 9,000 acres of pineapple and other fruits. Crucially, the land is already in place. Ekumfi has secured 9,500 acres for juice, tea and tepache feedstock — more than the full 24-hour requirement — with full capacity achievable within 36 months. The constraint is no longer land, but the planting finance, inputs and grower mobilization needed to bring it into production. That is not merely an agricultural challenge. It is a major economic opportunity. Rather than relying solely on company-owned plantations, Ekumfi can establish structured partnerships with thousands of farmers and young entrepreneurs growing fruit under agreed quality, delivery and pricing terms. The factory gains dependable supply; growers gain a defined industrial market. Feed the Industries can turn Ekumfi’s raw-material shortage into rural wealth creation. GH₵52,000 Per Acre: A New Opportunity for Youth and Pineapple Growers The most compelling dimension of the proposed expansion is the opening it creates for youth, smallholders, landowners, and agricultural entrepreneurs to participate directly in the pineapple value chain. Under the proposed cultivation model, one acre of pineapple could generate an estimated GH₵52,000 in gross revenue per successful harvest cycle . Young people could start commercial farming on modest plots; existing growers could scale up. THE EKUMFI PINEAPPLE GROWER OPPORTUNITY: GH₵52,000 Potential gross revenue per acre per harvest cycle; 9,000+ Acres of pineapple and other fruits potentially required; 9,500 Acres of land already secured Farm size Potential gross crop revenue 1 acreGH₵52,0005 acresGH₵260,00010 acresGH₵520,000100 acresGH₵5.2 million1,000 acresGH₵52 million9,000 acresGH₵468 million Illustrative estimates assuming all acreage is planted with pineapple and each acre achieves GH₵52,000 gross revenue per harvest. Actual earnings depend on yields, prices, crop cycles, and production costs. If the full 9,000-acre requirement were planted with pineapple at this revenue level, gross farm-gate value could reach GH₵468 million per harvest cycle. Because Ekumfi also needs other fruits, the real mix will depend on acreage allocated to each crop. The programme could be structured around one-acre, five-acre and ten-acre production units for young growers, backed by land access, improved planting material, technical assistance, mechanization and structured offtake agreements. The opportunity extends well beyond the farm gate: seedling multiplication, land preparation, irrigation, harvesting, transport, aggregation, farm management and agricultural technology could each support thousands of livelihoods. Management estimates that the full Ekumfi value chain — nurseries, land preparation, cultivation, harvesting, haulage, aggregation, processing, packaging and distribution — could support around 18,000 jobs in the Central Region alone . One distinction matters. GH₵52,000 is potential gross revenue , not guaranteed profit. Growers must cover cultivation, labour, inputs, financing and transport, and a pineapple cycle can run longer than a year. Even so, the model shows how industrial demand can anchor commercial agriculture. Instead of simply urging young Ghanaians into farming, the country can offer them a defined industrial market, structured production support and a real pathway to commercial income. From Two Days a Week to US$4 Million a Month Management estimates that with adequate raw material, working capital and market access, sustained 24-hour production could deliver monthly turnover of about US$4 million — US$48 million a year . EKUMFI’S PROPOSED INDUSTRIAL TRANSFORMATION US$53M Estimated industrial asset value US$4M Projected monthly turnover US$48M Projected annual turnover 24 HRS Target operations 18,000 Value-chain jobs, Central Region Company-supplied projections, subject to commercial, financial and operational validation. Moving from two days a week toward continuous operation would sharply improve utilization of existing equipment, utilities, labour and infrastructure, while expanding market presence and multiplying demand for local produce. The lesson for Ghana’s industrial agenda is clear: the country can unlock substantial value not only by building new factories, but by helping existing ones run at full capacity. Could Ekumfi Repay Its EXIM Debt Within One Year? One of the most consequential implications concerns Ekumfi’s obligations to Ghana EXIM Bank. At US$48 million in annual turnover, the company would generate materially stronger cash flow to support restructuring and repayment. Illustratively, a 15% free-cash-flow margin would yield about US$7.2 million before further financing needs or restrictions on distributions. At that level, a US$6 million obligation could theoretically be cleared within 12 months, provided sufficient cash were dedicated to debt service. The actual timeline will depend on the verified outstanding balance, accrued interest, operating margins, working-capital needs and agreed repayment terms. The original US$6 million participation should not be confused with the current outstanding debt, which may differ substantially. The broader point stands: restoring industrial productivity offers development financiers a more credible recovery pathway than leaving major manufacturing assets idle. A structured recovery programme can align EXIM’s repayment interests with agricultural expansion, higher factory output and growing export revenue. From Ghanaian Pineapples to a Global Juice Brand Ekumfi’s processing platform can produce value-added beverages from pineapple, citrus, ginger, passion fruit and other local crops. With adequate volumes, competitive pricing, consistent quality and established distribution partners, the company can extend its reach across African, European, North American and Middle Eastern markets. The gains ripple through the economy: more fruit production creates farm income; more manufacturing creates industrial jobs; packaging and distribution support other businesses; exports earn foreign exchange. This is the central promise of agricultural industrialization — converting locally grown crops into internationally marketed finished products, and capturing value through processing, branding and distribution rather than exporting raw produce. Why Ekumfi Survived Where State-Led Factories Stalled Ekumfi’s story becomes sharper when set beside the record of state-led agro-industrial investment in the same region and beyond. The Komenda Sugar Factory in the Central Region was first established in 1964 and shut down in the early 1990s. It was rebuilt and recommissioned in 2016 with about US$35 million in Indian government-backed financing, yet it has remained largely dormant. In February 2026, the trade minister told Parliament the factory had been disconnected from power and water over unpaid bills, with its machinery not refurbished since 2016. Government now targets a revival by the end of 2026. The state-owned Ayensu Starch Company , set up in 2002 to process cassava in the Central Region, has shut down repeatedly over raw-material and fuel shortages and equipment breakdowns, leaving cassava farmers without a dependable buyer. Napcoas followed a similar path: public commitment without sustained private ownership to carry it through. Under One District, One Factory (1D1F) , more than 300 factories were left at various stages of completion after the programme was cancelled in 2025, and several that did open struggled to secure raw materials or working capital. The common thread is not a shortage of public money. Over three decades and more, the state has committed capital to factories without the sustained private ownership, management discipline and equity at risk needed to keep them running when conditions turned difficult. Ekumfi took a different route. Backed by private sponsors with their own capital committed, it has kept its factory, brands and markets alive through the excise burden, raw-material shortfalls and financing delays — and today sells Ghanaian juice at home and abroad. That is a lesson the state should note. Rather than building and running factories on its own, or simply recovering legacy debt from the private ventures that survived, government and its development finance institutions should consider taking equity positions alongside committed private sponsors . Equity aligns the state with the upside as utilization rises, strengthens the balance sheet lenders look to, and leaves day-to-day management with operators who have proven they can keep a factory running. Ekumfi offers a ready test case. A Practical Model for the 24-Hour Economy Ekumfi can serve as a demonstration project for how Feed the Industries and the 24-Hour Economy work together. The model connects six elements: Agricultural expansion — develop 9,000+ acres of pineapple and other fruits through company estates, commercial growers and outgrower arrangements. Youth and farmer empowerment — enable growers to target gross crop revenue of up to GH₵52,000 per acre per successful harvest cycle. Industrial production — progressively raise factory utilizations toward sustained 24-hour operation. Market development — expand domestic distribution and exports to support projected turnover of US$48 million a year. Financial recovery — restructure existing obligations and tie debt repayment to actual operating cash flow. State equity partnership — convert public support into equity alongside private sponsors, sharing in the upside of a working factory rather than funding stalled ones. Delivery requires collaboration among Ekumfi, Ghana EXIM Bank, the Ministry of Food and Agriculture, the Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, the 24-Hour Economy Authority, agricultural investors and commercial financiers — and a phased implementation plan with independently validated yields, acreage, processing capacity, customer demand and working-capital needs. The Bigger Picture: Turning Industrial Investment into National Wealth Ekumfi’s story poses a question for Ghana’s development-finance strategy: what happens when the country invests in a major industrial asset but not in the supply chain needed to sustain it? The answer is an underused factory, mounting financial pressure, lost farm income and missed exports. The reverse is just as true. When agriculture, manufacturing, finance and markets are coordinated, the same investment becomes an engine of growth. For young people, the opportunity can begin with a single acre of pineapple. For established farmers, it means scaling up with a dependable industrial buyer. For Ghana EXIM Bank, it offers a pathway to improved recovery through higher production. For Ghana, it demonstrates how Feed the Industries can turn agricultural potential into manufacturing output, export earnings and rural prosperity. The Ekumfi Opportunity Is Bigger Than One Factory The abolition of the 20% excise duty has resolved a key competitiveness problem. Feed the Industries offers a framework for tackling the raw-material constraint. The 24-Hour Economy agenda supplies the wider ambition. What remains is coordinated execution. Ghana does not need to abandon valuable industrial investments because they have faced difficulty. It needs to identify and remove the constraints holding them back. For Ekumfi Fruits & Juices, that means connecting a modern processing factory to thousands of acres of productive farmland, empowering young growers and expanding markets for Ghanaian-made beverages — moving from limited weekly runs to 24-hour operation, from raw-material shortage to a structured supply chain, and from financial pressure to a firm foundation for repayment and export growth. The factory has been built. The asset exists. The land has been acquired. The task now is to feed the factory, empower the farmers, create wealth for the youth and build a globally competitive Ghanaian juice brand. That is the promise of Ekumfi under Ghana’s Feed the Industries and 24-Hour Economy agenda. Editorial note: Financial, acreage and grower-income figures are management estimates and illustrative projections. The US$53 million asset valuation, projected US$48 million annual turnover, GH₵52,000 gross revenue per acre and proposed debt-repayment timetable require independent validation. The GH₵468 million farm-gate estimate assumes all 9,000 acres are planted with pineapple and should not be read as annual profit or guaranteed farmer income.

title: Bezos Earth Fund and partners pledge $500m for threatened species recovery
body: The Bezos Earth Fund and eight other organizations have pledged more than $500 million over five years to help rescue some of the world’s most threatened plants and animals, giving species recovery greater attention in global conservation funding. The Species Recovery Alliance, announced Oct. 16 at the United Nations biodiversity summit, or COP17, in Yerevan, Armenia, will coordinate funding and conservation efforts rather than establish a single pooled fund. Cristián Samper, managing director and leader of nature solutions at the Bezos Earth Fund, said the initiative grew out of concerns that efforts to expand protected areas were overshadowing the urgent needs of threatened species. “We’re forgetting some of the other targets, in particular, the Target 4 on recovery of endangered species,” he told Mongabay in an interview at COP17. Target 4 of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework calls for urgent action to halt human-induced extinctions and help threatened species recover. Yet biodiversity continues to decline. WWF’s 2026 “Living Planet Report” found that populations of monitored vertebrate wildlife declined by an average of 73% between 1970 and 2022. Africa recorded an 80% decline. A new U.N. assessment also found that fewer than half of assessed biodiversity targets are on track. “Setting up protected areas and dealing with the other issues is not enough,” Samper said. Many threatened species, he added, require targeted interventions to recover. The Species Recovery Alliance includes Re:wild, Rainforest Trust, Fondation Segré, and five other organizations alongside the Bezos Earth Fund. Its members will coordinate investments and support…This article was originally published on Mongabay

title: MFA on UN Commission of Inquiry's report: As another winter approaches, these findings particularly important
body:
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Ukraine (MFA) welcomes the presentation of the report by the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on violations in Ukraine to the Third Committee of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly.
"Ukraine highly values the independent and impartial work of the Commission, which consistently documents violations of international humanitarian law and international human rights law. The Commission is establishing the circumstances of international crimes and gathering evidence to hold those responsible to account," the MFA said in a statement.
The ministry said the Commission's findings regarding Russian attacks on Ukraine's civilian energy infrastructure are of particular importance. The Commission has recognized such targeted attacks as war crimes, and the large-scale and systematic strikes that caused severe suffering to civilians as crimes against humanity.
Indeed, the Commission established that for over four years, Russian strikes on energy infrastructure deprived millions of Ukrainians of electricity, heat, and water.
"Of fundamental importance is the Commission's conclusion that these attacks were intentional and consistent with the state policy of the Russian Federation. The aim of this policy was to deprive civilians of vital energy supplies and to inflict suffering upon them. Russia has deliberately turned cold and darkness into weapons against Ukrainian civilians. As winter approaches, these findings are particularly important. They serve as a reminder to the international community that Russia continues to systematically destroy Ukraine's energy infrastructure. "We cannot allow the lives of millions of people to be threatened once again by cold and darkness," the MFA said.
The statement notes that the Commission's findings regarding how Russia recruits citizens of other states into its armed forces through deception and coercion warrant the strongest possible international response. The Commission found evidence of such practices involving citizens of 29 countries and classified the actions of the Russian authorities as human trafficking. People were lured to Russia with false promises of work and sent to fight in the war against Ukraine. Many of them were killed, wounded, or went missing.
"We call on the states whose citizens have been victimized by these criminal practices to strengthen cooperation in order to dismantle the recruitment networks and hold those responsible to account. We believe that the Commission's findings should be used to ensure that accountability for international crimes committed during Russia's aggression against Ukraine becomes inevitable," the statement reads.
The MFA also called on the international community to strengthen its support for Ukraine, particularly as winter approaches, and to facilitate the effective investigation of crimes and the prosecution of those responsible.
"Behind every documented crime lie human lives and destinies. These crimes cannot go unpunished. Justice and accountability are essential conditions for a just and lasting peace," the ministry said.
Earlier, the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on Ukraine stated in its new report to the UN General Assembly that Russian authorities committed war crimes by deliberately targeting civilian objects, as well as crimes against humanity in the form of other inhumane acts, by carrying out continuous attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure. The Commission also concluded that Russian authorities recruited men who were victims of human trafficking in various countries into their armed forces, which constitutes a violation of international human rights law.
The Commission investigated the impact of the Russian armed forces' large-scale attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure on the civilian population, particularly during the difficult winter of 2025-2026, as well as the cumulative effects of these attacks since the fall of 2022.

title: Matiks Bags $10 Mn To Take Its Puzzle Gaming Platform Global
body: Social gaming platform Matiks has raised $10 Mn (₹95.1 Cr) in its Pre-Series A funding round led by General Catalyst. The round also saw participation from upGrad founder Ronnie Screwvala as well as existing backers such as Info Edge Ventures, Tanglin Venture Partners and Untitled Ventures. In a statement, the startup said that it plans to utilise the fresh capital to expand its global footprint and invest in new games and social experiences. The fresh funding will also be used to deepen investments in engineering, AI, product, design and growth. A chunk of the capital will also be utilised to build an AI-powered engine, which will enable users to build and publish their own social games without writing code. Going forward, it has also set its eyes on scaling creator partnerships, global distribution and player community. “… We started Matiks with a simple belief: using your brain can be just as fun and addictive as any other form of entertainment. Our ambition is to make mind sports as culturally relevant as physical sports and esports – giving mental athletes, puzzlers, and competitive players the visibility, communities, and recognition they deserve…,” said Matiks cofounder and CEO Sudhanshu Bhatia. Founded in 2024 by Bhatia, Mohan Kumar and Sushant Timmapur, Matiks is an esports platform that allows users to play social games spanning mathematics, memory, logic and puzzles. It also allows users to compete with each other. The startup claims that more than 22 Lakh players had played 4.8 Cr games on its platform as of September 2026. Matiks also claimed that its daily active users currently hover around 3 Lakh, with early engagement also emerging from international markets such as Japan, the US and South Korea. The startup last raised $3.14 Mn in its pre-Series A round led by Tanglin Ventures in August last year. Going forward, the startup plans to initially prioritise expansion in the US before entering more tier I markets. Its future roadmap also includes building its AI-powered game creation engine, which the startup believes will foster adoption and create new experiences. The fundraise comes as India’s gaming market is expanding beyond the usual battle royale and casual games. Buoyed by 51 Cr gamers, the ban on real-money games last year, the rise of AI and regulatory push for social games, the homegrown gaming arena is seeing renewed traction and interest from investors. Earlier this month, mobile gaming studio Spill Games raised $10.5 Mn in its Series A round led by Elevation Capital. In April this year, another gaming studio LightFury Games also bagged $11 Mn in its pre-Series A funding round from Blume Ventures and others. In August, cricketer Rohit Sharma also joined LightFury Games as an investor , alongside MS Dhoni, Jasprit Bumrah, and Hardik Pandya, among others. At the heart of all this is the Indian gaming market, which is projected to become a $9.9 Bn opportunity by 2031 . The post Matiks Bags $10 Mn To Take Its Puzzle Gaming Platform Global appeared first on Inc42 Media .

title: Electricity firm explains planned six-day blackout
body:
The Mainpower Electricity Distribution Limited (MEDL) has announced a planned six-day power outage across many communities in four local government areas of Enugu State.
MEDL is a power distribution firm in Enugu and a subsidiary of Enugu Electricity Distribution Company, responsible for power supply in the South-east.
The MEDL spokesperson, Emeka Ezeh, said in a statement on Monday that the outage would be carried out by the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) station in Nsukka.
Mr Ezeh said the outage would begin on Thursday, 5 November, and run until Tuesday, 10 November, between 9:00 a.m. and 5:00 p.m. daily.
“The planned outage is to enable the TCN technical team to carry out maintenance work on some equipment at the station.
“The exercise will affect electricity supply to the UNN, SUMAS and Orba 33kV feeders, resulting in power interruptions for customers served by these feeders during the stated period,” he explained.
The spokesperson listed the areas to be affected as Ukopi, Opi Agu, Eha-Alumona, Orba Town, Obollo-Afor, parts of Obollo-Eke, Enugu Ezike, Ibagwa, Nkalagu Obukpa, Okpaligbo, Iheaka, Edem Ani, Agbani, Uzo-Uwani, Obimo, Nkpologu, Lejja, Nguru, Aku and Ogbede, as well as surrounding communities.
Other areas include Odim Gate, Nkpor, Nru, Ede Oballa, El Tabera Estate, Ikenga Estate, Wilson Company, Umakashi, Isiakpu, G.R.A., Ogige Main Market and the University of Nigeria Nsukka (UNN).
PREMIUM TIMES reports that the communities span Nsukka, Udenu, Uzo-Uwani, Igbo-Eze North, Igbo-Eze South, and Igbo-Etiti Local Government Areas of the state.
Mr Ezeh said the company sincerely regrets any inconvenience the planned outage may cause its esteemed customers, appealing for their patience and understanding.
“The exercise is necessary to facilitate essential technical work aimed at improving the reliability and quality of electricity supply to customers,” he stated.
Mr Ezeh, in a separate statement on Monday, explained that the recent reduction in power supply across most parts of Enugu State was a result of a drop in energy generation, which has led to low system frequency.
“This situation has necessitated the TCN to implement load shedding of the available energy”, he said.
The spokesperson stressed that the energy allocation to the electricity firm had been affected, which limited its ability to meet the daily service-level commitments.
“MEDL wishes to assure its customers that it is closely monitoring the situation and will continue to distribute the available energy allocation fairly across its network. The company remains hopeful that normal power supply will be restored soon,” Mr Eze said.
He noted that the company regrets the inconvenience this situation may cause its esteemed customers.

title: Zelensky discusses military cooperation and joint projects with Moldova's PM
body:
The head of state announced this on Telegram , according to Ukrinform.
“I met with Moldovan Prime Minister Vasile Tofan. We discussed many bilateral issues, primarily infrastructure projects that can improve the lives of our people,” he said.
The parties also discussed European integration.
“Moldova and Ukraine are definitely stronger when we move forward together in this direction. It is important that we continue to stand together, because it is the right thing to do,” Zelensky emphasized.
The two leaders also discussed security issues: the situation in Transnistria and strengthening military cooperation between the two countries.
“Today, the prime ministers of Ukraine and Moldova signed a cooperation agreement. It is important to ensure tangible results for our people and our countries,” the President concluded.
As reported by Ukrinform, Kyiv and Chisinau have agreed to resume joint efforts within the “Odesa Triangle” framework, which brings together Ukraine, Moldova, and Romania.

title: 3 NAS Pensacola sailors die in car crash
body: Three sailors assigned to Naval Air Station Pensacola, Florida, died early Saturday morning after a car crash, the Navy confirmed. The service members were assigned to Naval Air Technical Training Center and Naval Aviation Schools Command. “The Navy mourns the loss of our shipmates and extends our deepest condolences to the sailors’ families, friends, and fellow sailors during this difficult time,” the Navy said in a statement provided to Military Times. “Grief counseling service and support are available through local Navy chaplains.” Local media affiliates reported that police were notified of the crash at 1:35 a.m. Saturday morning. Police told local reporters that the car was in flames when first responders arrived. Once the blaze was doused, the three sailors were found inside. The circumstances that led to the crash were not immediately clear. The names of the service members have not yet been released.

title: What is ‘advance directive,’ the principle at heart of Ottawa’s new MAID law?
body:
The federal government is set to update the law on medical assistance in dying (MAID) in Canada, permitting Canadians to decide whether they want to end their lives ahead of time.
On Wednesday, Justice Minister Sean Fraser and Health Minister Marjorie Mitchel are scheduled to reveal more details about Canada’s new MAID law, which will include changes to include changes to the Criminal Code to ensure that a doctor who provides medical assistance in dying to someone who is eligible on an advance directive “will not be treated as a criminal in Canada going forward.”
Speaking in Ottawa earlier this month, Sean Fraser said the government will “grant access to medical assistance in dying to people who have provided consent at a time when they still have capacity but know that they have been diagnosed with an illness that will take that capacity from them subsequently.”
This is sometimes referred to as an “advance directive” or “advance request” in medical parlance.
It often involves a mentally competent person making a written request for MAID, with the intention that it would be honoured later, if and when they lose the capacity to make the decision for themselves: for example, in people suffering from worsening Alzheimer’s or dementia.
“That means, specifically, I give my consent in advance in this capable state to receive medical assistance in dying (at a later time),” said University of Toronto bioethicist Kerry Bowman.
In 2024, Quebec became the first, and so far only, province in Canada to allow residents to authorize an early request for MAID.
In Quebec, only a person who has been diagnosed with “a serious and incurable illness leading to incapacity to give consent to care” may give advance request for MAID. They must also identify a physician or specialized nurse practitioner who agrees to assist in the process.
Bowman said the principle of advance directives is “profoundly ethically complex,” adding that it can be hard to predict how a person’s disease will progress.
“The concern is you’ve almost got a stranger making a decision for a stranger. Do we really know ourselves in that state?” he said.
The Quebec law allows a patient to withdraw or modify their MAID request. However, the question of withdrawing consent becomes complicated when some patients have “no capacity to withdraw” in the advanced stages of illness, Bowman said.
“I’m not necessarily against it. But I do think most of us are enormously underestimating how ethically complex this is,” he said.
Advocacy group Dying With Dignity Canada, which has long advocated for advance directives, says the federal government’s approach is “fundamentally flawed” because it downloads implementation to the provinces and territories.
“At best, this legislation will create a patchwork of systems across the country, thus further increasing inequity in MAID access, instead of a federal framework that would ensure that all people across Canada could have access to advance requests for MAID if they are eligible,” Helen Long, the group’s CEO, said in a statement.
“At worst, some people in Canada may never have access to advance requests in their province or territory,” she added.
Equitable access to advance requests is fundamental to death with dignity, Long said.
“Without the option of an advance request, Canadians are forced to make an impossible choice: die earlier than they want to in order to ensure they have capacity to consent… or risk losing capacity and be forced to live in a situation they would find intolerable,” she said.

title: The Iran War Just Added $39 Billion to the World's LNG Bill
body: The Middle East conflict has disrupted global energy flows, forcing countries to rethink supply routes and strengthen energy security. As more buyers turn to the spot market to replace disrupted volumes, Rystad Energy estimates that global LNG importers will spend at least $39 billion more on contracted and spot supplies in 2026, despite purchasing 60.7 million tonnes less. Disruptions to Qatari and UAE exports through the Strait of Hormuz are forcing buyers to secure replacement volume at higher prices. Total portfolio costs are expected to reach $256 billion, up 18% from a pre-war estimate, underscoring how importers face different levels of exposure depending on their contract coverage, pricing benchmarks and ability to reduce demand.  Rystad Energy's modeling assumes that Qatari and UAE LNG deliveries will be unavailable from March through the end of 2026. Under this scenario, global LNG portfolio costs rise from $217.8 billion to at least $256.3 billion. Europe faces the largest increase, with its LNG bill rising by a minimum of $12 billion, or 18%, even as demand falls by 24 million tonnes. Europe entered the crisis already heavily reliant on spot purchases, leaving less room to further boost that share further. As a result, its share of spot imports is projected to rise by just 5.49%, after factoring in demand destruction, compared with pre-war estimates. At the same time, Europe is set to lose 20.6 million tonnes of the 24.7 million tonnes of Qatari LNG scheduled for delivery in 2026, before the conflict began.  East Asia is better positioned to weather the disruption, with spot purchases accounting for just 14.5% of imports. A broader portfolio of supply contracts outside the Middle East and lower LNG demand help limit the region's exposure to disrupted Qatari and UAE deliveries. Despite having the largest nominal exposure to Gulf contracts, East Asia faces the smallest relative increase in LNG costs among the regions outside the Middle East, at 9.7%. South Asia, meanwhile, is adjusting primarily through lower imports, with Pakistan cutting purchases more sharply than India. In Africa and South America, Egypt and Brazil, respectively, are driving the rise in prices and import volumes, while the Middle East is adjusting through demand destruction.  "This conflict has affected every player in the gas market to some degree, but not every economy is equally equipped to absorb the shock. Some importers are better positioned to manage rising costs, while others have had little choice but to cut volumes and absorb the economic consequences. The crisis exposes a fundamental weakness in gas security diversifying pricing benchmarks can help manage costs, but it does not guarantee physical supply. Importers need to assess their exposure to supply disruptions alongside price risk, building contract portfolios around reliable delivery routes and demand that cannot easily be replaced. Ultimately, when cargoes can disappear overnight, the resilience of supply matters as much as the price paid for it," says Christoph Halser, Senior Analyst, Gas & LNG Research, Rystad Energy    East Asia is coping with the disruption better than Europe, and the contract pricing terms are a key factor driving the divergence. Rystad Energy research shows that 82% of East Asia's long-term LNG contracts are linked to oil, the price of which has risen far less than spot LNG. Those LNG contracts are up about 28% compared with 72% for those tied to hub and spot price benchmarks. In contrast, the average price in Europe is up 47%. Europe buys around 65% of its LNG on the spot market, while about a quarter of its long-term contracts are tied to gas price indexes, leaving it far more vulnerable to the full force of market volatility.    In terms of implications for importers, Europe's result exposes a strategic shortcoming in relying on spot liquidity to secure residual gas demand. Treating gas as transitional does not remove the need to procure volumes still consumed. Deferring term procurement before substitutes are available leaves importers exposed to replacement-cost shocks. Contract tenor and volume flexibility should match residual demand, with supply origins and routes diversified.  Henry Hub indexation and supply routes address different risks, with our geostrategic analysis highlighting the value of 'unchokeable' supply that avoids maritime chokepoints or disputed waters. US Gulf Coast deliveries to Europe bypass the Strait of Hormuz, while deliveries to Asia may face Panama Canal constraints or require longer alternative voyages, making Australian and Canadian Pacific supply important alternatives. Importers should also scrutinize portfolio contracts for replacement obligations and sourcing flexibility when contracted cargoes cannot be delivered as planned.  Expanding US liquefaction capacity creates further opportunities for importers to secure Henry Hub-indexed supply and diversify their exposure to global gas benchmarks, but it also strengthens the link between global LNG demand and the US gas market. Rising feedgas requirements from LNG terminals, alongside power-sector demand, could support Henry Hub prices even as new global liquefaction capacity eases spot prices in Asia and at the Dutch TTF benchmark. Importers should therefore assess whether the current cost advantage of Henry Hub-indexed contracts is likely to persist over the full contract term, rather than assuming today's price advantage will endure.  By Rystad Energy

title: Death toll from Russian attack on park in Kharkiv Oblast on Oct. 19 rises to 6 after child dies in hospital
body:
A 12-year-old boy injured in a Russian drone strike on a park in Nova Vodolaha, Kharkiv Oblast, on Oct. 19 has died in a Kyiv hospital, bringing the death toll to six, including three children, local authorities reported on Oct. 26.
Russian forces struck the town's central park at around 4:30 p.m. local time on Oct. 19, when families with children were spending time there.
Artem Koval suffered severe injuries in the drone strike and was taken to hospital. Despite a week of efforts to save him, doctors were unable to overcome his life-threatening injuries, the Vodolaha Village Council said.
Artem's 8-year-old sister, Arina, was killed at the scene of the attack on the park.
"In a single terrible moment, the parents lost everything most precious to them — both their son and their daughter — and their loved ones lost children who were so dear to their hearts," the statement read.
"Russia robbed these children of their future and their families of their reason for living by committing yet another bloody crime against the most innocent."
At least 15 people were injured in the attack, including seven children, according to Kharkiv Oblast Governor Oleh Syniehubov.
President Volodymyr Zelensky called the attack an "absolute atrocity."
Zelensky said a girl called Anhelina, a little over a year old, was killed in the park, and her mother, Inna, passed away in hospital. The president also identified another victim of the attack as a 14-year-old girl.
Ukrainian prosecutors have opened a pre-trial investigation into a war crime.

title: UK sanctions Sudan commanders and pledges £15 million in aid
body: The UK has sanctioned 15 senior commanders from the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) over suspected atrocities, including conflict related sexual violence, as it announced £15 million in new support for survivors and humanitarian operations in Sudan on the first anniversary of El Fasher’s fall. In a statement by the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office today , they said that the sanctions impose travel bans and asset freezes on those targeted. They include RSF Colonel Hussein Abu Jalak and Al-Nour Ahmed Adam, known as Al-Qubba, whom the UK identified as having played prominent roles in the siege and attack on El Fasher , North Darfur’s capital. Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said UK funded investigations had documented the continued use of rape and starvation as weapons of war. “These are crimes against our humanity,” Miliband said, adding that perpetrators must face accountability and external support for the warring parties must end. The UK allocated £5 million to support survivors of conflict related sexual violence , including through sexual and reproductive healthcare, maternal health services, psychosocial support and safe spaces for women and girls. A further £10 million will support humanitarian operations, including clean water and sanitation at displacement sites around Tawila and essential health and protection services in El Obeid , capital of North Kordofan, where conflict and restrictions on humanitarian access have left civilians facing acute needs. The announcement follows new reporting by the UK funded Centre for Information Resilience, which documented systematic starvation and sexual violence against civilians by both sides in the conflict. The UK government said evidence included footage of RSF fighters discussing cutting off El Fasher’s water supplies and preventing traders from bringing food into the city. The government said the measures build on five previous rounds of UK sanctions related to Sudan’s conflict. Share article The post UK sanctions Sudan commanders and pledges £15 million in aid appeared first on Dabanga Radio TV Online .

title: Talks on regional peace and security will continue
body:
TEHRAN, Oct. 26 (MNA) – Delegations from Iran, Pakistan, Turkey, and Saudi Arabia released a press statement after concluding their security meeting in Tehran on Monday.
Saudi Defense Minister Khalid bin Salman, Pakistan’s army chief Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin in Tehran on Monday attended a four-way meeting with Iranian officials in Tehran's Saadabad Palace.
The high-ranking officials agreed to continue talks aimed at strengthening cooperation among the four regional countries, including in the field of peace and security.
The following is the joint statement after the four-way meeting in Tehran:
The first meeting of the four regional countries was held today, 26 October 2026, in Tehran.
His Excellency General Mohsen Rezaei, the Secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, hosted the meeting.
His Royal Highness Prince Khalid bin Salman, the Defense Minister of Saudi Arabia, His Excellency Field Marshal Asim Munir, the Chief of the Army Staff and Chief of the Defense Forces of Pakistan, and His Excellency Ibrahim Kalin, the head of the Turkish Intelligence Service, participated in the meeting.
The participants agreed to continue the dialogue to strengthen cooperation amongst the four regional countries, including for peace and security in the region.

body:
