title: Zelenskyy appoints Ukraine’s Ambassador to Democratic Republic of Congo as non-resident Ambassador to Gabon
body:
President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy has appointed the Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Ukraine to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Vasyl Hamianin, to serve concurrently as Ukraine’s Ambassador to the Gabonese Republic.

The relevant decree, No. 1069/2026, has been published on the website of the Office of the President of Ukraine.

"To appoint Vasyl Ivanovych Hamianin, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Ukraine to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, as Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of Ukraine to the Gabonese Republic, concurrently," the text of the decree states.

title: Will the real Anthropic please stand up
body: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here . After weeks of frenzied speculation, Anthropic has filed its IPO prospectus. The 335-page document (100 pages or so are focused on risks) lays out the company’s unique view of the technology it is building and the ways it believes it will change the world. It also warns that there’s a fair chance that its tech could “erode trust, harm society and destabilize the geopolitical order” and, if things don’t go to plan, “pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity.” “We encourage you, as a prospective owner of our stock, not to think of your purchase in purely transactional terms,” the company writes. “We hope you will see it instead as an opportunity to be part of something greater. The advent of machine intelligence is one of the seminal moments in human history.” This kind of public messaging is a master class in narrative capture. But Anthropic has been honing its storytelling skills for years. Earlier this month, Jack Clark, the company’s cofounder and head of policy, gave a speech at the IMF meeting in Bangkok in which he announced to the assembled economists, bankers, and lawmakers that the singularity is already here. Introduced by the science fiction writer and futurist Vernor Vinge around 40 years ago (and long debated on the nerdier fringes of the internet), the singularity is supposed to be the point at which technology gets so good that it outstrips the abilities of its makers. Humans are left in the dust, the idea goes, no longer able to compete with—or even understand—the fruits of their former creation. And this fictional world that many of us have imagined since we were kids? Apparently we’re already living in it: “I believe that this year we have gained convincing evidence that it has now begun,” Clark told his audience. The company tells a vivid (and in many ways scary) story about a future it portrays as inevitable but one that has not yet happened, often co-opted from well-worn science fiction memes. It presents its technology as mysterious and dangerous, and insists that it is the only company trustworthy enough to tame it. (What investor wouldn’t want in on that?) If you skim through the long sections about risks in the IPO prospectus, it’s clear this is no ordinary offering and no ordinary company. The way Anthropic tells it, business success depends not only on the firm’s ability to translate its technology into profitable products but also to save the world from what it has made. Take another example. Last year, Chris Olah, another Anthropic cofounder, was invited to address the Vatican, where he told Pope Leo XIV and other religious scholars and officials what his company was learning about its technology. “I will be honest: We keep finding things that are mysterious, even unsettling,” he said. “We find evidence of introspection. We find internal states that functionally mirror joy, satisfaction, fear, grief, and unease.” Never mind that many researchers would scoff at such an overt suggestion that Anthropic’s software has humanlike inner experience. This view of its technology makes its way into the prospectus as one more risk to its business. Anthropic states that: “In addition, given our focus on developing frontier AI, and the way we approach model sentience and moral status, we may face heightened scrutiny or pressure in connection with these debates and could elect to adopt policies, safeguards, or limitations regarding model development, deployment, or modification that go beyond existing legal requirements, which could constrain our operations, increase costs, or limit the commercial potential of our models, platform, and applications.” In other words, if Claude wakes up, it could be a problem. I’m not saying they’re necessarily wrong about any of this (although it’s pretty wild to read about machine sentience in an IPO prospectus.) But in a world where nobody knows what’s coming, companies like Anthropic get to fill the vacuum. When so little seems certain, what it says is snatched up and clung to like pieces of a sinking ship. It’s worth taking a moment to ask: What is Anthropic? It might sound like a starter question on a family quiz show, but it’s far harder to answer than you might think. The question has been on my mind since reading an exchange on X last week kicked off by Nathan Calvin, who is chief strategy officer at Encode AI, an organization based in Washington, DC, that advocates for regulation. Calvin was unhappy about the legislation that Anthropic proposed in a draft bill it circulated in secret to US lawmakers (which was then leaked ). Anthropic wants to be seen as the good guy, Calvin said. But why should we trust it? “What is Anthropic?” he asked. Here’s one answer: Anthropic is a company whose IPO values it at more than $1.5 trillion, netting its cofounders, including Clark and Olah, vast wealth. But Anthropic has always insisted it is more than that. As Calvin noted: Anthropic might instead be considered an AI safety organization focused on developing powerful technology that is reliable and (almost) risk-free. Or it might be considered a group of people hell-bent on creating a technology with superhuman capabilities before anyone else—maybe because they believe they’re the most responsible people to do so, or maybe because of their egos. In fact, Anthropic is all of these things. As CEO Dario Amodei put it in a reply to Calvin’s post : “Our strategy has always been what I’ve called the ‘race to the top’—by showing how it’s possible to build the technology responsibly, we can raise the bar for the entire industry. The forces that drive the race to the top are hugely more effective if the company practicing them is at the frontier; that’s one lesson I’ve learned repeatedly. And looking at that strategy as a whole, I’m proud of our track record and stand by it.” Amodei makes it sound as if he’s got it all tied up, but playing multiple roles is hard. There are huge tensions between the priorities of an AI safety organization and a profit-driven megacorp, for example. (Amodei admits in his post that he has made mistakes.) Ultimately, the stories Anthropic tells itself should help us understand the stories it tells us. They should help us figure out how much to trust it to self-regulate or whether we should be forcing it to give external safety testers access to its models on our terms rather than theirs. They should help us give it the benefit of the doubt (or not) when what looks like a self-serving piece of legislation comes to light. But I think the stories reveal a multiheaded hydra. Anthropic is many things to many people, and I’m not sure that makes it more trustworthy. In many ways, a good old-fashioned technology company—without the science fiction role-play, without the woo-woo—would be far easier to read. This article has been updated with additional details from the IPO prospectus.

title: Atiku’s ADC owing salaries for over 12 months, APC PCC alleges
body: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council APC-PCC has alleged that the African Democratic Congress ADC has not paid its staff salaries for more than 12 months, and urged Nigerians to reject the party and its presidential candidate, Atiku Abubakar, in the next general elections. In a statement on Monday in Abuja by its Spokesperson, Dele Alake, the council said it had come to its attention that the ADC National Working Committee NWC, “led by Senator David Mark as Chairman and Ogbeni Rauf Aregbesola as Secretary, has refused and neglected to pay party staff for over a year.” “We find it unconscionable that a political party that has made many grandiose promises to hoodwink Nigerians owes its workers for more than 12 months. Owing staff who come to work every day and who rely on the salaries for their daily sustenance is wicked and reprehensible”, APC added. The council said the development had exposed “the emptiness and insincerity of those parading themselves as ‘new saviours’.” It maintained that ADC leaders and their presidential candidate, Atiku, “do not mean well and can do nothing for our country.” According to the APC PCC, “Their desperation for power is driven by personal aggrandisement and venomous ill will against President Bola Tinubu. A party that cannot pay its cleaners and workforce cannot be entrusted with our country’s affairs.” The council also turned to Atiku’s record as an employer, saying he “has a reputation for owing his employees.” “While he regularly junkets to the UAE, staff at his Gotel Communication and other businesses also went months without pay and staged protests over unpaid salaries and other benefits,” the statement said. On Aregbesola, the council said his record “on paying workers’ salaries and pensioners in Osun State, where he was a governor for 8 years, was abysmal.” “As governor, he mismanaged the state’s finances to the point that he could not pay workers. His government thus introduced quarter-salary and, at times, half-salary payments. As for pensioners, he abandoned them for more than four years. Many died because they could not afford the basics of life”, the APC campaign added. The APC-PCC said it is therefore not surprised that ADC, harbouring birds of the same feather, cannot pay its workers’ salaries. The council then issued what it called a warning to Nigerians and working people: “reject ADC. Reject Atiku Abubakar and reject all ADC candidates in the next general elections. They do not have the interest of our country and our people at heart. “A party that aspires to govern Nigeria and which cannot be trusted with something as basic as the management of its own affairs and the welfare of its workforce should be rejected by Nigerians.” The post Atiku’s ADC owing salaries for over 12 months, APC PCC alleges appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: This startup’s self-driving excavators help dig up $600M in new funding
body:
Bedrock Robotics has raised $600 million in a funding round that values the autonomous vehicle technology startup at $4.1 billion, marking a speedy ascent for the two-year-old company.
The Series C round, co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, comes two months after the startup reached a key milestone: moving its autonomous excavators beyond testing and pilot programs and putting them to work on active construction sites.
Bedrock Robotics has developed a self-driving kit that can be retrofitted onto construction and other worksite vehicles. Excavators outfitted with Bedrock’s autonomous-driving tech are now commercially operating at a Nevada-based water treatment facility, an earthwork site run by Champion Site Prep in Texas , and a 1.2 million-cubic-yard civil sitework project with Zachry Construction Corporation.
Bedrock has raised nearly $1 billion since it was founded in 2024 by a group of autonomous vehicle and robotics industry veterans. Co-founder and CEO Boris Sofman previously led Waymo’s now-shuttered self-driving trucks program. Sofman also co-founded and led Anki Robotics, the maker of the popular Cozmo consumer robot, which shut down in 2019.
Other co-founders include Waymo veterans Kevin Peterson, Bedrock’s chief technology officer, and Ajay Gummalla, who serves as Bedrock’s vice president of engineering and infrastructure. Tom Eliaz, who previously worked at Segment and Twilio, is also a co-founder and VP of engineering and hardware.
The fresh capital will help Bedrock accelerate its transition to commercial work. The company plans to deploy its technology at more construction sites, while expanding the teams and infrastructure needed to support customers in the field.
“We have proven that fully autonomous excavators can perform real work of value alongside the crews and workflows already in place on job sites. The next challenge is delivering that capability to more contractors as a dependable part of how projects get built,” Sofman said in a statement.
Bedrock is particularly focused on autonomous excavators, in part because of a growing shortage of skilled operators. It takes five years or more to master operating an excavator, according to Bedrock. Meanwhile, a growing number of construction workers are approaching retirement age. The Associated Builders and Contractors, a national construction industry trade association, estimates that more than 40% of construction workers will retire in the next five years.
Bedrock is betting that the industry will increasingly turn to autonomous driving tech to help close that labor gap.
The startup’s newest partner is Haydon, an Arizona-based general contractor that plans to use Bedrock-equipped machines across a range of projects, including advanced manufacturing facilities, water and wastewater plants, data centers, and healthcare facilities.
New investors US Innovative Technology Fund (USIT), Bessemer Venture Partners, and Temasek participated in the round, alongside existing investors 8VC, Georgian, Valor Equity Partners, Xora, Eclipse, Perry Creek Capital, and Nvidia.
The startup also announced two executive hires as it scales commercial operations. Amy Jones Satrom, a veteran of Amazon, Nuro, and Uber, has joined Bedrock as its vice president of operations. Lando Juarez, formerly head of legal for Uber’s autonomous mobility and delivery business, was hired as general counsel.

title: E5 Defence Ministers' Statement: 26 October 2026
body:
Our countries share the assessment that Russia represents the most acute and long-term threat to Euro-Atlantic security and stability. Russia’s ongoing war of aggression against Ukraine, on the one hand, and its continued violations of Allied airspace, acts of sabotage and growing use of multi-domain hybrid attacks, on the other, do not undermine our unity, solidarity and cohesion. On the contrary, they strengthen our determination to pursue the efforts already undertaken to safeguard the integrity and security of Allied territory, through a 360-degree approach that takes into account threats from all strategic directions.
We, the Defence Ministers of France, Germany, Italy, Poland and the United Kingdom (the Group of Five/E5), share a deep conviction: Europe must assume greater responsibility for its own security. We are determined to work in close coordination with the United States and all Allies in order to implement this concrete ambition. The United States is and will remain an indispensable Ally, and continued United States engagement in European security is essential to a strong and credible NATO.
This greater responsibility must begin with the empowerment of European Allies within NATO.
With the aim of building a stronger Europe within a stronger NATO, we are already taking concrete measures to implement the commitments taken in The Hague, emphasized in Ankara, and to meet agreed capability targets.
We will assume greater political and military leadership within the Alliance, modernising forces and capabilities, including through closer defence-industrial cooperation based on common and standardised requirements,. We reaffirm our commitment to further strengthening NATO’s collective defence in order to rapidly adapt to current and future challenges, including with a more proactive deterrence and defence posture.
We will bolster our contributions to enhance readiness, resilience and our ability to respond to evolving threats across all domains, by promoting the development of the necessary capabilities, in line with NATO-agreed priorities and targets, including through an appropriate, tailored and effective mix of complementary capabilities to meet the full range of operational requirements.
NATO remains the cornerstone of our collective security. The Group of Five/E5 will support greater European ability to act through different frameworks and initiatives, including the European Union, complementing the sovereign responsibilities of States and intergovernmental cooperation.
We emphasise the importance of a nation-led, coordinated approach, aligned with NATO. We commend the European Union’s efforts to support nations in meeting NATO’s defence capability requirements and in strengthening European defence readiness. The EU’s regulatory and financial capacity is a valuable tool in support of our nations’ efforts and ambition. EU defence initiatives should complement NATO, avoid duplication and remain open, under certain conditions, to meaningful cooperation with non-EU NATO Allies.
We will maintain our unwavering commitment to supporting Ukraine in its fight back against Russian aggression. Ukraine’s ability to defend itself now and in the future is critically important to Euro-Atlantic collective security.
We stress the need to keep supporting Ukraine by all available means — politically, militarily and financially.
We reaffirm our determination to continue tackling the activities of Russia’s shadow fleet, in accordance with international law and in coordination with relevant partners.
We stand united with Ukraine in its determination to secure a lasting peace, underpinned by robust security guarantees. The Coalition of the Willing will contribute to robust and credible security guarantees once a cease-fire or a peace agreement is in place.

title: East Jerusalem man found dead near Bethlehem, police conduct series of West Bank raids
body: The body of an Israeli resident of east Jerusalem in his 40s was found in the Wadi Rahal area near Bethlehem in the West Bank, police said on Monday.Police officers, forensic investigators, and IDF soldiers were dispatched to the scene and began collecting evidence. The body is expected to be transferred to the Abu Kabir Forensic Institute to determine the cause of death. Initial findings indicate the incident was criminal in nature, rather than terror-related, police said. Man with suspected Hamas ties arrested overnight in BethlehemIn a separate incident, Israeli security forces arrested a Palestinian resident of the West Bank during overnight raids on Sunday night in Bethlehem, who is allegedly affiliated with the Hamas terrorist organization, according to police.A total of three suspects were arrested during the Sunday night military activity. Acting on previously gathered intelligence, Israeli security forces searched the home of the suspected Hamas operative as well as one other Bethlehem resident who was suspected of possessing weapons. During the searches, Israeli forces confiscated a loaded hunting rifle, IDF uniforms, and "various technological items," according to the Israel Police statement. Police arrested the two suspects and transferred them to the Ma'ale Adumim police station for further investigation. They are accused of offenses related to carrying and possessing illegal weapons, as well as unauthorized possession of military equipment. In a separate search, Israeli forces arrested a man in his 30s near the city of Hebron who was found to be in possession of a hunting rifle and a large amount of ammunition. Also on Sunday, police and Border Police officers found a large cache of weapons stolen from the IDF in Kalansuwa, a majority-Arab city in central Israel, and made two arrests in connection with the discovery. The weapons were seized during a police operation which was carried out as part of a larger initiative to reduce Arab sector violent crime. While conducting a targeted search on an open area in the city, Israeli forces found and seized a Kalashnikov rifle, three M-16 assault rifles, eight handguns, six fragmentation grenades, two stun grenades, thousands of rounds of ammunition of various types, and three tactical vests. A police explosives expert was dispatched to the scene to handle the grenades once the weapons were discovered. Two people, family members who were present at the site during the raid, were arrested during the operation and taken in for questioning. Police submitted all seized weaponry as potential evidence, and the investigation is still ongoing as of press time. Rahat resident found chained to the floor of home, brother arrestedOver the weekend, police rescued a man who was found chained to the floor of a home in Rahat during an operation intended to locate and confiscate illegal weapons in the city. Israel Police free a man who was chained to the floor of a Rahat residence on October 25, 2026 (CREDIT: ISRAEL POLICE SPOKESPERSON'S UNIT).Upon discovering the man, whose leg was shackled to the floor of the home, police freed him and worked to uncover the circumstances surrounding his imprisonment. Preliminary findings indicate that he was chained up by his own family members, police said, allegedly due to his use of drugs. The man's brother, a Rahat resident, was arrested shortly thereafter and taken to the Rahat police station for questioning.

title: 12-Year-Old Boy Dies After Weeklong Fight for Life Following Russian Strike on Nova Vodolaha Park
body:
A 12-year-old boy, Artem Koval, died in a Kyiv hospital on Monday, Oct. 26, after a week of fighting for his life following a Russian drone attack on a crowded park in Nova Vodolaha, Kharkiv region.
According to a statement from Nova Vodolaha Settlement Council, his 8-year-old sister Arina was killed on the scene, along with five other civilians. The youngest victim, Angelina, was just over a year old when she was killed sitting in her stroller.
Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official .
“Russia took away the children’s future and their family’s meaning of life, committing yet another bloody crime against the most innocent,” the council wrote, confirming that the parents had lost both of their children in a single moment.
The attack took place on Oct. 19, around 4:30 p.m. when families with children had gathered near a cafe and fountain in the town’s central park, Yuvileinyi.
At the time, Kharkiv regional governor Oleh Syniehubov clarified the casualty figures , identifying the dead as three women aged 28, 34 and 36, a man approximately 40 years old, and two girls aged eight and just over one year old.
Among those dead was the infant’s mother, Inna, who later died in the hospital, President Volodymyr Zelensky said . He condemned the strike on the civilian site as an act of “absolute brutality.”
“These are terrible photographs, but behind them are shattered lives and the truth about this war,” he said after sharing photographs of the site.
The Kharkiv Regional Prosecutor’s Office said preliminary evidence indicated Russian forces had used a Geran-3 drone, a jet-powered variant of the Iranian-designed Shahed.
The strike on a civilian site prompted the police to open a war crimes investigation under Article 438 of Ukraine’s Criminal Code. As of Oct. 3, Ukraine’s National Police has opened nearly 244,000 criminal proceedings linked to Russia’s invasion, including 226,766 war crimes cases.
Although such attacks are prohibited under international humanitarian law, they reflect a broader pattern that has defined the war, now in its fifth year.
Kyiv Post is Ukraine’s first and oldest English news organization, reporting since 1995. Its international reach – 90% of readers are outside of Ukraine – make it truly Ukraine’s global voice.

title: Bitcoin Price Hovers Near $80,000 as Traders Await Fed Decision
body: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Hovers Near $80,000 as Traders Await Fed Decision Bitcoin price traded near $80,000 on Monday, after falling about 2% earlier in the session. The price has dipped below that level several times in recent days and recovered each time. Selling pressure has been building. Spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded about $635 million in outflows on October 22. A brief drop below $80,000 last week also triggered roughly $800 million in liquidations of long positions, or bets that prices would rise. The next major test to look out for is the Federal Reserve’s two-day meeting, which ends October 28. The Fed raised its target range to 3.75% to 4% in September, and its minutes suggested another increase could come by year-end. Most recent market odds favor the Fed holding rates steady, though those odds have shifted. Traders are watching Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s remarks for signs of a December hike. Higher interest rates typically pull money away from risky assets, including crypto. Broadly speaking, a hold could keep bitcoin price between roughly $80,000 and $88,000. A rate hike could push it toward the lower end of that range. Bitcoin price backdrop Geopolitical tensions are also weighing on markets. Oil rose above $100 a barrel in early September as strikes between the U.S. and Iran escalated. Higher energy prices feed into inflation, which affects the Fed’s decisions. In tech, Anthropic is reportedly preparing an initial public offering that could value the AI company near $965 billion. The timing has shifted toward the weeks before the November midterm elections, but no date has been confirmed. U.S. stocks surged a bit Monday as investors geared up for a busy week of Big Tech earnings and the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate decision. The Nasdaq rose 0.8%, the S&P 500 gained 0.6%, and the Dow climbed 0.3%. Alphabet and Microsoft report Wednesday, followed by Amazon Thursday, while markets largely expect the Fed to hold rates steady. AI-related stocks rallied following Anthropic’s IPO filing. Tesla jumped 6%, while Meta plans to raise up to $95 billion for AI investments. As of writing, bitcoin price trades at $80,215, down nearly $4,000 or 4.75%, on the month. Over the past month, prices have ranged from a high of $86,806.95 to a low of $79,397.76. Bitcoin price peaked above $86,000 in early October, then slid toward $80,000 in the second week of the month. A brief rally around October 21 pushed it back near $84,000, but those gains faded within days. Trading volume over the past 24 hours reached about $18.12 billion. Bitcoin price remains far below its all-time high of $126,277.05. This post Bitcoin Price Hovers Near $80,000 as Traders Await Fed Decision first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Micah Zimmerman .

title: Millicent Blay wins second edition of Breast Cancer Awareness Pink-Pong Tournament
body: Millicent Blay of Nationwide Medical Insurance has won the second edition of the Breast Cancer Awareness Pink-Pong Tournament. Blay emerged victorious at the tournament, which uses table tennis as a platform to promote breast cancer awareness and encourage conversations about the disease. Speaking after her victory, Blay highlighted her long-standing relationship with the sport. “I have been playing since I was a kid,” she said. The tournament forms part of efforts to raise awareness of breast cancer through sporting activities, using table tennis to engage participants and encourage public conversations about the importance of breast cancer awareness. Eric Apedo of Safety Communication Consult also highlighted the motivation behind the initiative, emphasising its role in promoting breast cancer awareness. “This is an initiative to promote breast cancer awareness,” he said. The event featured the presentation of medals to the winners, recognising their performances in the competition. The second edition of the Breast Cancer Awareness Pink-Pong Tournament was supported by Ghana Link Network Services, AGL Gas, CBG Bank, Nationwide Medical Insurance Ltd., EMWA, Unicorn Petroleum Limited and Sankofa Spices. The initiative continues to use sport as a tool to promote awareness of breast cancer and encourage greater public engagement with the cause.

title: Gov Uzodimma proposes national media research centre in honour of Dokpesi
body:
Imo State Governor Hope Uzodimma has proposed establishing a national media centre in honour of the late founder of DAAR Communications Plc, Raymond Dokpesi.
Mr Uzodimma proposed this on Sunday while delivering the third annual Diamond Lecture in Abuja in memory of Mr Dokpesi.
The lecture, organised by the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations (NIPR) and DAAR Communications Plc, was themed Media, Democratic Consolidation and Development.
Mr Uzodimma said the proposed centre would serve as a hub for media research, focusing on how journalism could be harnessed to promote economic growth and development.
He said the initiative would help preserve the late Dokpesi’s legacy and promote development journalism. He also pledged to lead a campaign to establish it.
“This memorial lecture is a good starting point. But we must go far above that. The best tribute we can pay to his memory is to protect that freedom and ensure that the journalism practised within it remains worthy of public trust.
“But I think that as his friends and associates we should take the lead by building a national media centre in his honour. The centre will be a hub for research on the media and how it can be properly channelled for economic development, or, put simply, for development journalism. I shall be prepared to lead in the campaign for the establishment of this centre,” he said.
Mr Uzodimma said Nigeria’s democracy would benefit from a media that could hold public officials accountable without intimidation.
“Our democracy will be better served when the media can pursue the truth without intimidation, when government accepts the discipline of scrutiny, and when the institutions of accountability respond to what is established,” he said.
The governor maintained that the proposed centre would help sustain Mr Dokpesi’s legacy by strengthening the media’s contribution to democratic governance and national development.
Mr Dokpesi, who died in May 2023 at 71, was a media entrepreneur credited with pioneering private broadcasting in Nigeria. He founded DAAR Communications Plc, the media company behind RayPower FM and Africa Independent Television (AIT), after the country’s broadcasting industry was deregulated in 1992.
RayPower 100.5 FM began commercial broadcasting in Lagos on 1 September 1994, becoming Nigeria’s first private radio station and pioneering round-the-clock radio broadcasting. Two years later, on 6 December 1996, Mr Dokpesi launched AIT, which expanded the range of television programming available to Nigerians and became a platform for news, entertainment and public affairs.
Through the two outlets, Mr Dokpesi helped create opportunities for entertainers, music producers, and programme makers who had struggled to access established broadcasters. AIT, in particular, provided a platform for Nigerian television productions, while RayPower contributed to the growth of contemporary Nigerian music and entertainment.
Mr Dokpesi died in Abuja after reportedly falling while exercising on a treadmill as he recovered from an earlier illness. Reports at the time said he had suffered a stroke before his death. His death was announced by his family on 29 May 2023.
Beyond broadcasting, Mr Dokpesi was involved in politics and philanthropy. His contribution to the media industry, particularly the expansion of privately owned radio and television, remains a central part of his legacy. The proposed national media centre in his honour would extend that legacy by supporting research on how the media can strengthen accountability, democratic governance, and national development.
In his remarks, NIPR National President Ike Neliaku commended the late Mr Dokpesi for his integrity and commitment to press freedom.
Mr Neliaku said the annual Diamond Lecture was organised to celebrate Mr Dokpesi’s contributions to the growth of Nigeria’s media industry and preserve his legacy.
He also announced the forthcoming World Public Relations Forum, scheduled to take place in Abuja, saying it would bring together participants from 126 countries.
The NIPR president said the institute had concluded preparations for the event and was ready to host participants from across the world.

title: Bitcoin Wallet Fixes Critical Flaw That Redirected Funds to Attackers
body:
Bitcoin wallet Electrum patched a high-severity vulnerability this weekend that allowed rogue servers to manipulate pending Bitcoin transactions and redirect funds to attacker-controlled addresses. The flaw affects all versions before 4.8.3, which is now available.
At least one user has confirmed losing money to the exploit.
Electrum is one of the oldest Bitcoin software wallets around. The attack exploits the wallet’s trust model for unconfirmed transactions. When a user broadcasts a payment through a compromised server, the server can suppress the real transaction and inject a fake conflicting one—showing an attacker’s output address and zero fee, making the payment look stuck.
Because Electrum doesn’t verify signatures on unconfirmed transactions from the server, the spoofed transaction appears in the wallet’s history as legitimate.
When the user fee-bumps what looks like a stalled payment, they sign and broadcast a completely new valid transaction—one whose output address belongs to the attacker. The real payment was never sent; the fee-bump is the first transaction that actually hits the network, and it pays the attacker.
Electrum developer SomberNight, who published the advisory , noted that attackers can grind the fake transaction’s output address to match the last four characters of the user’s intended destination. Anyone spot-checking only the tail of a long Bitcoin address would see an apparent match.
The advisory states that “some servers are performing this attack in the wild,” backed by two user reports. A user identified as dannydeezy first flagged the suspicious server behavior on October 11; the manipulated transaction never propagated past the local server, so no funds were lost. A second user, Raju-K12, reported a confirmed loss on October 18 after fee-bumping a manipulated transaction.
The patch in 4.8.3 closes the main attack surface by verifying cryptographic signatures on wallet-owned inputs before adding any unconfirmed transaction to local history. A server can no longer inject a fake transaction touching the user’s own addresses without providing valid signatures—which the attacker cannot forge. The fix was tagged in the repository on October 23 and binaries were published the following day.
Incoming transactions from external senders—where none of the inputs belong to the user’s wallet—are still accepted without signature verification. SomberNight acknowledged this gap in the advisory, noting it would require additional work to close.
This isn’t Electrum’s first rodeo and it has dealt with malicious attacks in the past. A 2018 campaign used rogue servers to push fake update notifications, and by 2020 it had drained an estimated $25 million from Electrum users. Electrum’s open server model—anyone can run a node—is what makes this class of attack possible.
Users who connect exclusively to a server they run themselves are not affected. Anyone who cannot update immediately should manually verify output addresses and amounts before signing any transaction; Electrum 4.8.3 is available at electrum.org alongside the project’s Github.

title: Wall St looks for best day in month as Anthropic's IPO filing propels AI stocks
body: The ⁠S&P 500 and Nasdaq were set for their biggest one-day gain in more than a ⁠month on Monday, as tech stocks advanced after Anthropic 's initial public offering filing put ​artificial intelligence back in focus in a week packed with corporate earnings. Anthropic disclosed steep losses and great ⁠revenue growth in its filing for a US IPO, detailing its ambition to build AI systems capable of reshaping the global economy despite the high costs of developing the technology. The AI lab is pushing ahead with its listing plans even as a once-busy autumn IPO calendar has thinned out, with market volatility ⁠prompting companies to delay offerings. "It's a challenging environment, to say the least, exactly when this IPO will take place, but there's a ​lot riding ⁠on not only the company, but the AI industry," ‌said Robert Pavlik, senior portfolio manager at Dakota Wealth in Fairfield. Semiconductor and chip-related companies, widely regarded as some of the biggest winners of the ​AI boom, were leading the gains. The broader Philadelphia chips index was up more than 3 per cent after a turbulent few weeks. Anthropic's filing arrives as investors increasingly scrutinise the profit from AI spending. About a third of S&P 500 companies are scheduled to report earnings this week, including hyperscalers Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon, whose results would be scanned for signs of whether AI investments are translating into growth. The focus follows a subdued reception to earnings from AI-linked mega-caps last week. Meta disappointed investors after raising its annual AI spending forecast again and saying it would sell new stock to help pay for it, while Tesla also came under pressure after its results. Meta said on Monday it plans to raise up to $95 billion in equity to fund its AI-related expansion of data centres, cloud computing power and other infrastructure. Its shares were last up 0.2 per cent. The AI trade has come under pressure this month amid concerns that debt-funded spending may become harder to justify in the face of rising borrowing costs. Sentiment, however, improved on Monday as neo-cloud companies such as CoreWeave and Nebius, which have been at the centre of the AI storm, reversed initial losses to trade higher. Other AI-linked companies, including photonic product makers Lumentum ​and Coherent, along with server makers Dell and Hewlett Packard Enterprise, were among the best-performing stocks.

title: ‘Atrocities persist in El Fasher one year after RSF takeover’
body: Amnesty International says civilians face arbitrary detention, torture and restricted humanitarian access, as international coalition calls for accountability over atrocities in North Darfur. Civilians in El Fasher, the capital of North Darfur, continue to face arbitrary detention, torture, unlawful killings and restricted humanitarian access one year after the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) seized the city , Amnesty International said on Friday. In a statement by Amnesty International , published ahead of the first anniversary of the takeover on 26 October 2025, the human rights organisation said schools had been turned into detention centres, residents faced constant surveillance and children remained at risk of malnutrition. Amnesty interviewed 25 civilians, including 19 residents and six humanitarian workers, in August and September 2026. Of the 19 residents interviewed, 17 said they had been detained by the RSF, often for months. “The RSF’s claims that El Fasher is safe for civilians to return to after the horrific massacres that took place one year ago could not be further from the truth,” said Agnès Callamard, Amnesty International’s Secretary General. “A pervasive pall of fear hangs over El Fasher today. Men and women live under constant RSF surveillance, and with the ongoing threat of detention, torture and killing,” she added. Survivors described beatings, unlawful killings and severe shortages of food and water in detention. Amnesty also documented forced labour, including making detainees collect bodies and rubble or cook and clean for RSF members without pay. The organisation said fewer than 70,000 people remained in El Fasher, compared with a pre-war population of more than one million. Humanitarian workers also warned of rising malnutrition risks amid limited aid access and a poor harvest season. The RSF had not responded to Amnesty’s findings by the time of publication, the organisation said. ‘Int’l coalition urges respect for UN sanctions and embargo’ The Coalition on Atrocity Prevention and Justice for Sudan marked the anniversary by calling for accountability for crimes committed in and around El Fasher. In a statement by the coalition today , whose members include the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Canada and the European Union, said findings by the UN Independent International Fact-Finding Mission for Sudan had exposed the scale of violations of international humanitarian law and abuses of international human rights law. It said civilians had suffered mass killings, ethnically motivated killings , summary executions, torture, disappearances, forced recruitment, arbitrary detention and widespread sexual and gender-based violence. “One year after El Fasher, our message is clear: the victims will not be forgotten, survivors will be heard, and we will continue to pursue accountability for those responsible,” the coalition said. The coalition called on all parties to protect civilians and ensure safe, rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access. It also urged states to stop arming, financing or otherwise enabling the war, and to respect UN sanctions, including the arms embargo on Darfur. ‘North Darfur gov calls for accountability’ North Darfur Governor Hafiz Mohamed Bakhit alleged that the RSF committed 320 cases of gang rape at El Fasher University and said 140 mass graves had been established around the city. He described the destruction of homes, hospitals, schools and displacement camps, alongside killings targeting civilians on ethnic grounds, as war crimes and genocide. Survivors and refugees in eastern Chad described losing family members and enduring harsh living conditions, calling for an end to the war, accountability for violations and the safe return of displaced civilians. Abu Hassan, a survivor of the fall of El Fasher, described October 26 as a catastrophic day that would never be erased from memory. He recalled women, children and elderly people fleeing the city in fear, many of whom ended up in camps and shelters lacking basic necessities. He said displaced people continued to suffer, urging the warring parties to end the fighting, pursue peace and ensure civilians could return to their homes as soon as possible. “What have we gained from this war so far, other than death, destruction, displacement and hatred?” he asked. title: 2027: Drop your ambition, back Tinubu, RMRDC boss tells Obi
body: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Director General and Chief Executive Officer of the Raw Materials Research and Development Council RMRDC, Prof. Nnanyelugo Ike-Muonso, has urged the presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC, Mr Peter Obi, to shelve his ambition for the 2027 election and support President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid. Ike-Muonso, who spoke during an interactive session with reporters in Abuja, argued that the South should be allowed to complete its eight-year tenure before power returns to the North. He said the principle of power rotation between the North and South, which has shaped Nigeria’s political calculations since the return to democracy in 1999, should guide political actors as they prepare for the 2027 general elections. “Presidential ambition must be balanced with the larger interests of national unity, political stability and the need to sustain policies that can transform the economy. Nigeria has developed a political tradition of power rotation between the North and South, and respecting that understanding can help strengthen confidence among the country’s diverse political constituencies”, he said. While he conceded that the Constitution does not prescribe a North-South rotation of the presidency, he said the arrangement has, however, remained an important consideration among major parties and stakeholders seeking to manage regional interests and maintain national balance. Ike-Muonso said Obi should consider postponing his aspiration until after Tinubu’s second term, and after the North would have the opportunity to produce a President. He said this would serve political stability, national cohesion and continuity in governance. He also urged Obi to consider joining the All Progressives Congress APC. According to him, engagement within the ruling party would let the former Anambra State governor contribute to policy debates, understand its governance structures and take part in development programmes being implemented by APC-controlled states. Ike-Muonso said membership would also give Obi a chance to observe how the party’s state governments approach infrastructure, education, healthcare, investment and economic development. He acknowledged Obi’s following, saying: “Peter Obi has built a political following and brought issues of public expenditure, accountability and economic management into the national conversation. Those issues deserve sustained engagement. But political leadership also requires strategic decisions about when to contest, when to collaborate and how best to contribute to national development.” The RMRDC chief said Obi’s influence and support base could be deployed to promote constructive engagement on governance, economic development and institutional reforms, rather than concentrating exclusively on the immediate contest for the presidency. He urged Obi to use the intervening years to deepen his engagement with progressive political ideas, build alliances across the country and contribute to policies capable of improving citizens’ welfare. Ike-Muonso said the decision to join a political party ultimately rested with Obi. He maintained, however, that Nigeria needed a political culture in which prominent figures could work across previous political differences in pursuit of agreed national objectives. He added that the debate ahead of 2027 should go beyond individual ambitions to include an assessment of the policies and programmes needed to diversify the economy, create jobs and strengthen domestic production. The RMRDC boss said the Tinubu administration’s Renewed Hope Agenda had created a policy framework within which institutions such as the Council could advance local raw-material development, industrialisation, import substitution and value addition. He said the Council was pursuing initiatives aimed at moving Nigeria away from the export of unprocessed commodities towards a production-based economy capable of creating jobs, attracting investment and strengthening domestic manufacturing. “The opportunity before Nigeria is to move beyond exporting raw commodities and build an economy in which our natural resources support local factories, generate employment and create wealth within our communities,” he said. The post 2027: Drop your ambition, back Tinubu, RMRDC boss tells Obi appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Hezbollah readies for new regional war with funds from Iran, sources say
body: Lebanese terrorist group Hezbollah has spent three months preparing for a possible resumption of hostilities with Israel, after receiving an infusion of cash from Iran, according to Lebanese security personnel briefed on its activities.The group, founded by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) in 1982, has been dealt severe blows in two wars with Israel since 2024, with thousands of fighters and many of its leaders killed, and much of its arsenal destroyed.As part of efforts to combat Hezbollah, IDF troops now occupy a security zone in southern Lebanon, and political pressure has built up in Beirut for its disarmament.It nevertheless remains committed to attacking Israel and has used a lull in hostilities since June to rearm, with a focus on procuring explosives and producing drones that can be flown into the security zone, two Lebanese security sources told Reuters.One of the sources, and another close to Hezbollah, said the group had received tens of millions of dollars from Iran to help boost its military capabilities. That is in addition to around $200 million that the terror group previously received from Tehran, which Reuters reported earlier this month.The group has been restoring command-and-control structures that broke down in key battles, according to one of those sources and three other security officials familiar with the group's operations.In response to questions from Reuters, Hezbollah's media office rejected the suggestion that its command-and-control systems had been broken down.Israel's military declined to comment. Iran's permanent mission to the United Nations in Geneva did not immediately respond to Reuters questions.A US State Department spokesman said Washington would keep strangling Hezbollah's finances through sanctions and other measures. A US Treasury spokesperson said Iran was running out of money and ways to move money.Hezbollah on alert for potential of renewed fightingHezbollah's effort comes amid continued tensions in the wider Middle Eastern conflict ignited by the US-Israeli war with Iran that began in February.Hezbollah attacked Israel in support of Iran on March 2, triggering an Israeli response that led to a large number of individuals, mostly members of Hezbollah's Shi'ite Muslim constituency, being evacuated from areas in southern Lebanon.Hostilities largely abated over the summer as an interim Iran-US deal included a Lebanon ceasefire and Washington-mediated talks between Lebanon and Israel. Full-scale hostilities have not resumed in Lebanon despite the collapse of the US-Iranian deal, though Israel continues strikes on Hezbollah terrorists in the south.Hezbollah is on alert for a possible US-Iran escalation, potentially reigniting the Lebanon front.The sources told Reuters the terror group had not yet managed to fully prepare its stockpiles or fighting force.Hezbollah is still restocking, acknowledging this month that explosives seized by Lebanese authorities belonged to it and were intended for use against Israel. A ⁠Hezbollah official and a Lebanese security source told Reuters they were specifically ​for its explosive drones.Hezbollah struggled to fight IDFThe terror group will also need to repair command-and-control capabilities after losses on key fronts, including the flashpoint town of Bint Jbeil and the strategic Ali al-Taher ridge, according to one of the Lebanese sources and three security officials.They said Hezbollah's tactic of operating in small units and rationing the use of anti-tank rockets left some units isolated on those fronts, struggling to confront Israel's remotely operated systems, including weaponized drones and armed remote-controlled vehicles.The Israeli military told Reuters it uses remotely-operated systems to monitor southern Lebanon and reduce troops' threat exposure.Hezbollah has not explicitly said whether it would take part in the eruption of fresh hostilities, but its media office said it was wary of giving Israeli leaders any justification to escalate anti-Hezbollah efforts.

title: Zelenskyy discusses infrastructure projects, European integration, situation in Transnistria with Moldovan PM
body:
In Kyiv, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has held discussions with the Prime Minister of Moldova, Vasile Tofan, regarding infrastructure projects, the European integration of both nations, the situation in Transnistria, and cooperation in the military sphere.

“We discussed many bilateral issues, first and foremost infrastructure projects that can improve the lives of our people. Of course, we also discussed European integration. Moldova and Ukraine are certainly stronger when we move forward on this track together,” Zelenskyy said on X Monday.

According to him, the parties also discussed security issues, specifically regarding Transnistria and the strengthening of military cooperation between the two countries.

Zelenskyy emphasized the importance of continued joint work between Ukraine and Moldova to achieve results that will have practical significance for both nations.

title: ‘My life came down to 50 pesewas after quitting my white-collar job for poetry’ – Nana Asaase
body: Ghanaian poet and writer Nana Asaase has recounted how his decision to leave a well-paying public relations job to pursue poetry left him facing financial uncertainty, with his bank balance eventually dropping to just 50 pesewas. Speaking on The Career Trail programme aired on Joy Learning TV and Joy News, Nana Asaase said his decision to leave the corporate world was driven by his belief that poetry was a calling he needed to pursue. After completing his studies at the University of Ghana, he undertook his National Service at Originate, Saatchi and Saatchi, where he gained practical experience in public relations, including documentary production, scriptwriting, voiceovers, event coverage and newspaper reporting. His career journey, however, began before university, when he combined teaching with newsreading at Eagle FM in Cape Coast. According to him, his interest in journalism, inspired by the standard of English used by broadcasters he listened to. Although he gained admission to the University of Ghana, he did not pursue opportunities at the university’s Radio Universe, explaining that his academic work and interest in literature already demanded much of his attention. Nana Asaase later joined Global Media Alliance as a public relations professional, where he earned what he described as a decent salary. However, he became increasingly concerned about the future of Ghana’s cultural and arts industry, particularly the gap emerging as older generations of creatives passed on. “I realised that within the culture and art space, we already had a generational crisis. There’s a gap,” he said. He explained that the absence of enough people to carry forward the work of established cultural figures made him question how the industry would sustain itself in the years ahead. However, his conviction to pursue poetry grew after he performed at an event and earned three times what he would have received as his monthly salary. “So I remember one month where our salaries had delayed a little. It happens with agencies; it’s not unusual. And then I had a poetry gig. I had a call from Michael, and I decided to accept. Then I whispered to God, ‘God, if you’re really sending me here, don’t let any of my media outlets come and cover this event.’ I went for the event, and true to that, none of my outlets came to cover that story. I finished the performance and came back to the office. I got paid three times what I would get paid at the end of the month in my PR job. So it reinforced the fact that if I gave this gift proper attention, it could become a source of income,” he recounted. According to him, the experience reinforced his belief that he could earn a living from his talent if he gave it the necessary attention, prompting him to eventually resign from his job. The poet said the financial difficulties began almost immediately. At the time of his resignation, he had only GH¢100 in his bank account, which dropped to GH¢50 after his car broke down the following day. Despite the uncertainty, he remained committed to his decision, giving himself five years to make poetry work. “When I quit my job, let me be very open about it, I had 100gh in my account at that time. The next day, my car broke down. Then it came down to 50gh. And my life actually came down to 50 pesewas,” he revealed. Despite the uncertainty, he remained committed to his decision, giving himself five years to make poetry work. “I told God, look, I’m giving you five years of my life. If this thing doesn’t work, I’ll never put a pen to paper in the name of poetry,” he revealed. He recalled one particularly difficult experience when he and fellow poet Hashmullah performed at the Ephraim Amu Centenary celebration at the National Theatre. The two received an envelope containing GH¢10 to share. “We were walking from the National Theatre via the British Council down to Adabraka. Then I was like, ‘I’m going to open the envelope and see what’s inside.’ When I opened it, it was not GH¢10 in one note, oh. It was ten one-cedi notes for two people. We took off our shoes, started playing the guitar, and then, praised God. We bought kenkey and fish with that money. I will never forget that day,” he recalled. His breakthrough, however, came when he received a call from OSJ Consult, which opened doors to major performance opportunities, including RLG’s end-of-year party and Ecobank Transnational’s 25th anniversary celebration. “I received a miracle call from OSJ Consult at the time. I don’t know who had recommended me to them. But it was during that time when President Atta Mills had passed. So Oliver calls me. It was RLG’s end-of-year party at the time. We had a discussion, and the money was very good money. Oliver was very helpful and instrumental. He gave me my biggest gigs at the time, RLG and then Ecobank Transnational at 25,” he highlighted. Reflecting on his 12 years in poetry, Nana Asaase said the journey had reinforced his belief that perseverance could eventually open doors, even when progress appeared slow.

title: Zelenskyy expecting Ukraine-USA-Russia trilateral meeting in early Nov
body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy expects a trilateral meeting between the Ukrainian, U.S., and Russian teams to take place in early November, he said following a meeting with Lithuanian Seimas Speaker Juozas Olekas.

"I briefed the Speaker on the meetings in Oslo and the overall situation in the negotiation track. We expect a trilateral meeting between the American, Ukrainian, and Russian teams to take place as early as the beginning of November," Zelenskyy said on his Telegram channel on Monday.

The parties also discussed in detail Ukraine's European integration and the priorities of Lithuania's presidency of the Council of the EU in the first half of 2027.

Zelenskyy emphasized the importance of opening the remaining two negotiation clusters for Ukraine by the end of 2026 so that the closure of negotiation chapters can begin during Lithuania's presidency.

title: WWE legend Ric Flair shares health update after recent hospitalization
body:
WWE legend Ric Flair shared a health update after falling outside of a Florida restaurant on Friday.
In a post on X , Flair, 77, shared a photo of himself wearing an eyepatch and thanked fans for their “messages and prayers” after he was injured in the fall.
“Thank you all for the messages and prayers! I will get back to you each individually as I get stronger,” Flair wrote.
“Thank you to all the Tampa General Hospital staff and doctors that put up with me until 4:30 a.m. I appreciate you all and thank you for everything you did for me! I am focused on my healing and recovery right now,” Flair added.
He reassured his fans that he will “be okay.”
Thank You All For The Messages And Prayers! I Will Get Back To You Each Individually As I Get Stronger. Thank You To All The Tampa General Hospital Staff And Doctors That Put Up With Me Until 4:30am. I Appreciate You All And Thank You For Everything You Did For Me! I Am Focused… pic.twitter.com/QCIHyEnPDa
— Ric Flair® (@RicFlairNatrBoy) October 24, 2026
TMZ Sports previously reported that Flair fell outside of a Florida restaurant on Friday and injured his face.
Not my dad telling the doctor he fell bc of warrior dropping him on his head…
— Charlotte Flair (@MsCharlotteWWE) October 24, 2026
Hours before his fall, Flair had announced that he had to cancel his scheduled appearance in Seattle because he was “dealing with a blood clot in my leg.”
“My doctors have limited my travel to 3-4 hours. Seattle falls outside that range, and as disappointed as I am, I have to put my health and recovery first,” Flair wrote in an Instagram post .
“Blood clots are extremely serious and can be life-threatening. We have seen this recently with Jalen Hurts and the complications involving blood clots in his lungs. It is a reminder that this is not something to take lightly, and I must follow medical advice,” he added.
Flair told his followers that he was scheduled to have “a procedure to strip the affected vein, which my doctors expect will allow me to be cleared for more travel afterward.”
“Please know this decision was not made lightly. I am truly sorry for the inconvenience and disappointment, and I am incredibly grateful for your patience, understanding and continued support,” he added.
“I look forward to getting healthy and seeing you all down the road. Thank you for the love and support,” his post concluded.
Flair’s post made reference to NFL player Jalen Hurts of the Philadelphia Eagles, who is expected to miss the remainder of the season with blood clots in his lungs that started in his left calf, according to The Associated Press.
Hurts is expected to make a full recovery.
The Eagles and Hurts’ agent announced on Oct. 19 that the quarterback has deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, meaning a blood clot has travelled to the lungs. His treatment involves blood thinners, and he won’t be allowed to participate in any football activities until he is off them.
“Jalen’s prognosis is very good and we expect a full recovery,” Hurts’ agent Nicole Lynn said.
“We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects,” Lynn added.
Flair had a health scare in 2017, and was hospitalized in August of that year for kidney and congestive heart failure. He was placed into a medically induced coma for 11 days.
In May 2019, Flair recovered after undergoing surgery .
“He is out of surgery and in the recovery room. Doctors said the procedure was a success! Thank you to everyone for all your prayers and support during this difficult time,” Flair’s partner Wendy Barlow said at the time.
The two-time WWE Hall of Famer was rushed to the hospital following a non-specific “medical emergency,” which delayed his surgery.
Barlow had confirmed that “due to ongoing health complications, Ric was taken to the hospital and is expected to undergo a procedure tomorrow morning, after which he expects to fully recover.”
Flair took to Instagram to share that he returned home after the procedure, writing, “Thank you to all the incredible staff and doctors at Gwinnett Medical Center once again! I am so thankful for all my family, friends, and fans for all the love. At this time in my life, I never take it for granted.”

title: The arc of Trump: How the president lost the coalition that put him in the White House
body:
President Donald Trump forged an extraordinary coalition to win office in 2024, stitching together his base with unusual support from some traditional Democratic groups like Hispanics and young people. It was enough to sweep the battleground states and catapult him into office for a second term.
The latest CNBC All-America Economic Survey shows that coalition is now seriously weakened.
Since the beginning of his second term, the president's net approval rating among Latino voters has dropped from -22 to -38, and declined from -28 to -53 among 18- to 34-year olds. Black respondents have moved from -55 to -67.
Among all registered voters, his approval has fallen from -7 at the start of his term to -19 in the most recent survey.
The decline in the president's approval carries over into the Republican base. Approval from self-described Trump voters has fallen from a net +85 in 2025 to a net of +65. Net approval has even turned negative in the South, from +2 in 2025 to -20 in the latest survey.
The results of the latest poll show why Republicans are facing an uphill battle in the midterm elections next week. Trump is not on the ballot — but his presence will be felt.
To be sure, Republicans in the survey still give the president an 82% approval rating, and those who say they identify with the MAGA movement are at 90%. But interest in the election is 10 points lower among Republicans than it is for Democrats, and in tight races, the party that better turns out its voters will have an advantage.
The survey of 1,000 registered voters nationwide found 44% of respondents say their biggest worry if Republicans control Congress is allowing President Trump to operate beyond his constitutional power. By contrast, 28% say their biggest worry for Democratic control is passing policies of Democratic Socialists. For either party's control, registered voters worry that Congress won't do enough to bring down prices.
The survey was conducted Oct. 14-18, and was co-led by Democratic pollster Hart Research Associates and Republican pollster Public Opinion Strategies. It carries a margin of error of plus or minus 3.1 percentage points.
As a second-term president who had skipped four years between terms, Trump's arc of approval has followed an unusual path. The president left office above water on the economy, with 48% approving and 41% disapproving — high numbers for a president whose last year was overwhelmed by the Covid pandemic.
But there was no second-term honeymoon. Trump was immediately underwater in his economic approval rating in the April 2025 CNBC survey. That could have reflected immediate public discontent with the tariff regime and resulting market turmoil. The president's economic approval rating remained negative through most of his first year.
The bottom dropped out, however, with the launch of the Iran war. By April 2026, the president's net economic approval rating was plying depths last seen under President Joe Biden amid the aftermath of the pandemic, when the country was facing high inflation and elevated unemployment.
In the first quarter of this year, Trump's net economic approval dropped 10 points to -21. It has plunged to -31 in the latest survey. Economic disapproval rose to 65% , the highest for any president CNBC has measured back to President Barack Obama, and one point higher than Biden's worst showing. The survey shows increasing disapproval of Trump's handling of inflation . Over the same time, shooting of Americans by Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers began to dominate headlines, eroding support for one of the president's major policy initiatives.
The survey this quarter appeared to pick up growing frustration with a host of issues, from immigration to the economy, among those demographic groups that had supported the president in unusual numbers in 2024, with sharp declines in economic and overall approval among Latinos, young people and those in the $50,000 to $75,000 income group.
Most ominously for the president, views on the economic outlook fell 22 points for Republicans. Though still net positive, it was the lowest level of economic optimism for Republicans since Biden.
These downbeat views on the economy do not automatically translate to votes for Democrats. The survey showed a 7-point preference for Democratic control of Congress, a 3-point gain from the July survey. While Republican economic pessimism grew, so did their preference for a Republican-controlled Congress, from 85% in July to 87% in October.
Blue-collar workers show how the president has maintained his base amid growing concern about the economy. Their net economic approval of the president has plunged 22 points to -15 from the beginning of Trump's term to now. But their overall presidential approval remains +6, just a four-point drop. They still prefer a Republican-controlled Congress by 21 points, though that is down from 33 points in July.
The days and weeks leading up to the election have seen the president barnstorming through red states , a sign of concern with the base's enthusiasm. But it also creates the possibility that he could fire up his base and bring them out to stanch potential Democratic gains.
The survey shows that the extra votes from the coalition that put Trump in the White House in 2024 would be a reach for Republican congressional candidates in 2026.
