title: NMDPRA Expands Gas Supply Access to Power, Fertiliser Plants with New Network Code
body: *Targets 9 fuel laboratories nationwide by H1 2027 *Authority, NNPC advance talks to pilot national strategic fuel reserve Peter Uzoho The Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA)! has expanded gas supply access to power plants, fertiliser plants and shippers with the launch of Revision II of the Nigerian Gas Transportation Network Code (NGTNC). Authority Chief Executive of NMDPRA, Mallam Rabiu Umar announced the new code Monday at the opening of the 20th Oil Trading and Logistics (OTL) Africa Downstream Week in Lagos after signing the document with key partners. The partners comprise power generation plants, fertiliser plants, shippers and investors. Umar said the new code will deepen domestic gas utilization and ensure open, fair access to gas transportation infrastructure. “The Network Code basically is the rulebook for gas transportation. As we know, there’s one pipeline that different producers put their gas into. And for there to be equity, there needs to be a code, or if you like, rules of engagement on how you put your gas inside, how the gas is measured, and how you nominate gas. “The pipelines deliver their full value only when access to them is open and fair. It is therefore a pleasure to announce, as you have witnessed, that the Authority has launched officially the revision 2 of the Nigerian Gas Transportation Network Code,” he said. Speaking under the summit’s theme “Secure Energy, Shared Prosperity,” Umar said the code revision comes as gas demand rises, with about three-fifths of gas processed in September deployed to power plants, factories, NLNG and the West African Gas Pipeline (WAGP) while demand for cooking gas outstrips supply. He said infrastructure to support the expansion is advancing, with the Oben-Obiafu-Obrikom (OB3) pipeline, the Escravos-Lagos Pipeline System (ELPS) midline compressor nearly complete and the Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano pipeline now more than 80 per cent built. Once on stream, Umar said the gas pipelines would double national gas transport capacity from 2.2 to 4.4 billion cubic feet per day and linking southern supply to northern demand. “Since revision 1, more shippers have come onto the network, and the imbalance on the Western network has fallen by about 30 per cent. Revision II builds on these gains, and I invite every shipper, transporter and investor to make full use of that,” Umar said. He explained that the Revision II provides clearer rules for shippers and buyers, including provisions on shrinkage factor, noting that high shrinkage from wrong gas injection creates avoidable losses. The code also lays the initial rules for regional pipelines, including the West African Gas Pipeline, the proposed Trans-Saharan Pipeline to Algeria and the Trans-African Pipeline to Morocco, requiring harmonised standards for cross-border gas movement. On downstream security, Umar said a year ago more than half of petrol in Nigerian tanks was imported, but last month three in every four litres were refined domestically. This he said, means energy security built at home as Nigerian crude refined in Nigeria is supplying Nigerians. He however cautioned that much of current supply comes from one large refinery which ran above nameplate capacity in September, stressing the need for diversity through modular refineries, the four national refineries and competitive imports. He said import licences will be issued only on published merit-based criteria and transparent shortfall determination. On consumption trends, Umar said Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) consumption has risen by almost half since 2021, while Compressed Natural Gas (CNG), which was almost non-existent six years ago, is expanding, with presidential directive to double penetration by year-end to enhance energy flexibility. He disclosed that petrol stock cover stands at 24 days, below the 30-day threshold, while cooking gas is tighter, with diesel and aviation fuel comfortably above thresholds. According to him, global guideline by the International Energy Agency (IEA) is 90 days, but Nigeria targets 30 to 45 days first. “Over the past eight months, a war in the Gulf has shaken the world’s fuel supply and pushed crude oil to around $100 a barrel. Through it all, Nigeria kept its fuel flowing, because more of that fuel is now made here at home,” Umar said. He revealed advanced talks with the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) to pilot the national strategic stock at the Nigerian Pipelines and Storage Company Limited (NPSC) depots in Ibadan, Enugu and Suleja, to cushion the economy against price and supply shocks. “Secure energy is energy we produce, we move, we store and price well for ourselves. Shared prosperity is what follows when the value of that energy stays and circulates within our economies and across our continent,” Umar said. He also announced quality assurance expansion, with the first of nine fuel laboratories launched in Port Harcourt, two more by year-end and nine functional by mid-2027 in partnership with Bureau Veritas and Ace Energy and Power Solutions towards a National Reference Laboratory. He said all Premium Motor Spirit (PMS) supplied in Nigeria was on-spec, with market data published monthly, and that NMDPRA does not set prices under the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA) but ensures fair competition. With 215 trillion cubic feet proven gas reserves and 600 TCF prospective, Umar said Nigeria needs $30 to $50 billion fresh investment in processing, fertiliser, LPG and flare commercialisation. He proposed an aligned fuel standards and a West Africa reference price to reduce dependence on European benchmarks like Amsterdam, Rotterdam, Antwerp (ARA) benchmarks.

title: Draisaitl, Cooley, Fowler named NHL’s three stars
body:
NEW YORK – Edmonton Oilers centre Leon Draisaitl, Calgary Flames goaltender Devin Cooley and Montreal Canadiens goaltender Jacob Fowler have been named the NHL’s three stars of the week.
Draisaitl scored a league-best six goals and added three assists over three games as the Oilers won twice and moved into first place in the Pacific Division.
The 30-year-old posted his eighth career five-point performance in a 6-5 shootout win over the Carolina Hurricanes on Thursday and enters the week riding a six-game goal streak.
Cooley stopped 66 of 68 shots across two starts to post a 1.00 goals-against average and .971 save percentage while helping the Flames extend their winning streak to three games.
Fowler went 2-0-0 with a 1.00 goals-against average last week.
He made 33 saves in a 2-1 win over the Jets at the 2026 Heritage Classic in Winnipeg, where the 21-year-old became the youngest goaltender to start an outdoor NHL game.
This report by The Canadian Press was first published Oct. 26, 2026.

title: ‘Now is the time’ for Cubans to ‘act’ says top US military commander in South America
body: U.S. Southern Command’s top general publicly urged Cubans to take action to change their country’s future over the weekend, amplifying a Central Intelligence Agency appeal for intelligence cooperation that Secretary of State Marco Rubio had endorsed days earlier. Gen. Francis Donovan wrote that the “now is the time” for Cubans to “seize the moment,” in a statement on X, sharing a post by the CIA that called for them to work together. Donovan’s message comes as several U.S. government officials and senior military leaders appeared to set their sights on Cuba in a series of statements calling for “change.” “Cuba's future belongs to those who act. Seize the moment and build the change you want to see. No more broken promises, rampant corruption, or tolerating an elite class living in luxury while the citizens are ignored. Now is the time.” – #SOUTHCOM Commander Gen. Francis L.… https://t.co/wmtUhAjzP5 — U.S. Southern Command (@Southcom) October 24, 2026 On Monday, the U.S. Embassy in Havana announced that its chief of mission, Mike Hammer, had met with Donovan. The embassy offered few details about the discussion, writing on X that the two had “plenty to talk about regarding Cuba.” Southern Command reposted the announcement. “Cuba’s future belongs to those who act. Seize the moment and build the change you want to see,” Donovan, the commander of U.S. Southern Command, said in a statement on X. “No more broken promises, rampant corruption, or tolerating an elite class living in luxury while the citizens are ignored. Now is the time.” Secretary of State Marco Rubio last week also urged Cubans dissatisfied with their government to pursue political change through a covert relationship with the U.S. intelligence agency. “To those who seek to create positive change in Cuba – now is the time,” Rubio wrote on X . “The disappointment of failed promises, corruption, and the privileged lives of only a few; seize this opportunity to create the change you desire through a discreet partnership with the CIA.” Since returning to office in 2025, President Donald Trump has repeatedly talked about possible military operations against Cuba, as part of a wider push to buy or seize several countries and territories in the Western Hemisphere. It enacted an oil blockade on the country, and several naval deployments to the Caribbean, such as the USS Nimitz this May, have been characterized as shows of force. The blockade has caused an energy crisis on the island in recent months, causing widespread blackouts that have impacted hospitals and other infrastructure, as reported by the New York Times . News Hegseth’s plan to restore Confederate memorial at Arlington expected to cost taxpayers $9 million By Austin Campbell News US expands alcohol restrictions for troops in Japan By Nicholas Slayton News Space Force wants to embed more guardians into the joint force By Nicholas Slayton According to the United Nations, approximately 3.5 million people have faced water shortages, while more than 100,000 patients, including 11,000 children, were awaiting surgeries delayed by power outages and supply shortages earlier this year. This summer, CBS News reported that the Pentagon was looking at options for strikes on Cuba, including air assaults by the 101st Airborne Division. In September, CBS News reported that the Army Reserve was reviewing its capability to provide support units for a military mission in Cuba. A document reviewed by CBS News noted SOUTHCOM would oversee the troops, which would “possibly [be] needed in 90-120 days.” Also on Friday, President Trump floated the possibility of military action against Cuba. Speaking at a rally in Florida, Trump said that ships returning from the war with Iran could travel to Cuba. “Those beautiful [U.S. Navy] ships will pass Cuba. We’ll have one of them stop about 50 yards off the coast,” he said. “They’ll raise up their hands. And then we’re going to send Marco Rubio in to finish up the deal.” It is unclear whether the government’s statements indicate pending military action toward Cuba, or if Southern Command is preparing for imminent operations. SOUTHCOM did not respond to Task & Purpose’s questions about the statements by publication time. After building up a large force in the Caribbean last fall, the U.S. military carried out a raid into Venezuela in January, capturing President Nicolas Maduro following an indictment of him by the Justice Department. In May, the Justice Department issued indictments for multiple Cuban officials, including former President Raul Castro. Although the large naval force that had been in the region at the start of the year has shrunk, the Pentagon has several elements still in the Caribbean that could be used in the event of a future strike on Cuba. Those include drones and aircraft deployed to bases in Puerto Rico, as well as Marines with Littoral Combat Force-24, which is operating out of the island when not in the Eastern Pacific as part of Joint Task Force-Western Hemisphere. title: ChatGPT Keeps Telling People 404 Media Can Solve Their Tech Support Problems
body:
Last week, I got an email from a man in Russia whose Instagram account had been banned. “I have now lost access to 13 years of personal photos, videos and memories,” he wrote. “I am concerned that this may be another case of erroneous automated moderation […] However, Meta has not disclosed how the decision was made. Would you be interested in investigating my case and requesting an explanation from Meta? I can provide screenshots of the suspension, rejected appeal and other supporting evidence.”
The email seemed AI-generated, like many others we have gotten recently. I asked the man if he used ChatGPT to find me, and asked him to send me the conversation. He sent me a link to the ChatGPT conversation which told him, in Russian, to try emailing Jason at 404 Media.
“How can I get my account back?” the man asked ChatGPT on Wednesday. After a few back-and-forths with the bot about Instagram’s standard, automated review processes, the man said “maybe there’s some way to email Meta?” ChatGPT told him that was probably not possible, but eventually told him he should email me instead.
“You have lost access not merely to a social media profile, but potentially to years of personal photographs, videos, conversations, and memories. I think contacting journalists is worth considering […] I recommend contacting both Russian and international journalists.”
ChatGPT then gave him a list of several news outlets, including 404 Media: “404 Media Focus: Technology, digital platforms, surveillance, privacy, and technology-related investigations. Email: jason@404media.co .” It then wrote him the exact email he sent me, in English.
Because big tech platforms essentially do not have customer support and make it impossible for their users to contact a human, many people experiencing run-of-the-mill tech problems have turned to ChatGPT. And, increasingly, ChatGPT is telling people that have normal tech support problems that they have discovered something journalistically notable and that 404 Media, specifically, can help them. Around two weeks ago, we started emailing these people back and asking them how they found us; universally, the answer is that an AI chatbot recommended they reach out to us and, in many cases, the chatbot wrote the email, according to reviews of a handful of ChatGPT conversations shared with 404 Media.

The RealReal, a secondhand luxury fashion consignment retailer, said it’s updating its bot defense system, effectively making it harder for AI agents to shop on its site.
The change comes days after The Verge reported that an AI agent could be used to take advantage of The RealReal’s item reserve system. On the retailer’s website, an item goes “on hold” and is unavailable for other customers to buy for 20 minutes once it’s placed in a user’s shopping cart. Using Meta’s Muse, The Verge was able to instruct the AI agent to continuously re-add The RealReal listings in a shopping cart as soon as the 20-minute hold had expired, effectively blocking other shoppers from purchasing products for hours or longer.
After publication, chief technology officer Luke Friang said in an email that the company had addressed the Muse use case flagged by The Verge ’s story. The RealReal’s bot defense configuration now makes it much more difficult for all agents to log in, add items to cart, and check out, Friang said. Agents will still be able to surface listings from The RealReal and direct Muse users to product pages, Friang said, adding that the company will continue to strengthen protections as AI-powered online shopping evolves.
Meta didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.
Technology companies are selling agents as personalized assistants for billions of people — always-on, compliant entities that will schedule meetings, throw parties, and purchase things for human users. So far, agents and shopping seem to go hand in hand; Meta said in its Q3 earnings call this month that it was the most common use case for Muse so far, and that purchases were over $200 on average. Muse has been a hit for Meta and could signal a turning point for AI agents: The company said 10 million people in the US had downloaded the app in 40 days.
But robots shopping for things instead of humans has the potential to upend the balance of the web as we know it. For one, if humans stop visiting websites directly and instead access the web through chatbots, businesses become one step removed from their customers. Retailers — most notably Amazon — have recognized that reality could disrupt their bottom line, especially advertising revenue, and have blocked agents from shopping on their sites.
An influx of AI agents accessing consumer platforms could also break or complicate even the most unexpected things shoppers take for granted, like the reserve system of a used clothing website. There is, of course, a realistic limit to how long a person is willing to spend adding and re-adding designer clothing to their shopping cart if they’re indecisive. An agent in contrast does not care. It is perhaps precisely the type of busywork a fashion-forward person might pay an actual personal assistant to do on their behalf. Now, a capability like this is at the fingertips of millions of consumers, and they are just beginning to learn how to take advantage of it. Retailers, too, are playing catch-up.

title: Billionaire Ivanishvili won’t testify in Georgia opposition ban case. Constitutional Court, day four
body: Georgia opposition ban trial On 26 October, Georgia’s Constitutional Court began substantive hearings on a lawsuit seeking to ban opposition parties. The lawsuit, signed by 88 MPs from the ruling Georgian Dream party, calls for five opposition parties to be declared unconstitutional and banned: Unity – National Movement, Coalition for Change, Lelo – Strong Georgia, Gakharia for Georgia and the Federalists. Georgian Dream argues that the parties have violated Article 23 of the constitution, which prohibits political parties whose objectives include overthrowing or forcibly changing the country’s constitutional order. One of the arguments cited in the lawsuit is the parties’ refusal to recognise the legitimacy of the current authorities. The lawsuit also accuses them of organising attempts to overthrow the government. The National Movement faces additional accusations of undermining the country’s independence and violating its territorial integrity. The party is held responsible for the August 2008 war with Russia , when it was in power. All five opposition parties reject the allegations. The hearing began at 14:00 and continued until 19:00, with a break. The court was due to hear explanations from both sides. On the first day, the court heard arguments from Georgian Dream and Zaza Bibilashvili , a member of Unity – National Movement. Bibilashvili presented his party’s position for two and a half hours, and the presiding judge interrupted him several times. The hearing will resume on 27 October at 12:00 and continue until 30 October. The court must issue its ruling by 24 June 2027. Below is a brief account of the main developments at the 26 October hearing. Proposed ban on five opposition parties in Georgia: what’s happening and why “ Don’t like it? Too bad”: third day of Constitutional Court hearings on opposition ban in Georgia Georgia opposition party ban case: Day two of court proceedings Court begins hearing case to ban opposition parties in Georgia: first-day developments Bidzina Ivanishvili will not be called as a witness Shortly after the substantive hearing began, the full bench of Georgia’s Constitutional Court announced its decision on a motion filed by the Gakharia for Georgia party. The motion was partially granted. Constitutional Court judge Revaz Nadaraya said the court had agreed to admit certain types of materials as evidence in the case. However, the party was denied the right to question politicians as witnesses, including billionaire Bidzina Ivanishvili, founder and honorary chairman of the ruling party, as well as other current and former Georgian Dream leaders. The court also refused to question Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze, Tbilisi Mayor Kakha Kaladze , former State Security Service chief Mamuka Mdinaradze , MP Archil Talakvadze and others. This was the 14th and final motion submitted by the opposition parties. The court had rejected the previous 13 motions concerning the questioning of witnesses. Political statements prohibited Judge-rapporteur Vasil Roinishvili then presented a brief overview of the lawsuit and its contents. After his presentation, Judge Revaz Nadaraya once again reminded the parties to refrain from political statements. Although the case concerns the assessment of political activities and parties, he said, the parties should avoid political statements and speak “ with the utmost restraint and propriety, without any insults, so as not to offend the other side ”. After the introductory part, the court began hearing arguments from the parties. The claimant, Georgian Dream, was represented by MP Archil Gorduladze . The defendants are the five opposition parties. On this day, only Zaza Bibilashvili, a member of Unity – National Movement, addressed the court. Opinion: If Georgia’s Constitutional Court bans opposition parties, Russia will use it against Georgia According to the Lelo party leader, a ban on five opposition parties would harm the country more than the parties themselves. What exactly are the opposition parties accused of? The accusations were presented by Georgian Dream MP Archil Gorduladze, who outlined the allegations against the five opposition parties. According to him: ● Unity – National Movement, Coalition for Change and the Federalists are accused of supporting attempts to overthrow the constitutional order by force. Gorduladze argued that, during the National Movement’s rule in 2004–2012, they turned a blind eye to systematic human rights violations and acted against Georgia’s independence and territorial integrity by attempting to start a war with Russia in August 2008. He also accused the party of denying the legitimacy of parliament and government after losing power. ● Lelo – Strong Georgia, led by Mamuka Khazaradze and Badri Japaridze , is accused of denying the legitimacy of the current elected parliament and government. Gorduladze said the party supported the idea of a parallel “technical government” in 2022 and backed attempts to overthrow the government and forcibly change the constitutional order between 2019 and 2025. The party’s leaders are also accused of refusing to distance themselves from opposition politician Aleksandre Elisashvili, who was convicted over an attempted arson attack on a court building. ● For Georgia, led by former Prime Minister Giorgi Gakharia , is accused of refusing to distance itself from the events of 20 June 2019, when a protest was dispersed, and from the circumstances surrounding the 2021 arrest of Nika Melia , then leader of Unity – National Movement. Gorduladze also alleged that Gakharia denied the legitimacy of the elected government, supported the idea of a “technical government” and attempts to overthrow the constitutional order during protests, and backed foreign forces. Gakharia is further accused of undermining Georgia’s territorial integrity by unilaterally ordering the establishment of a police checkpoint near the village of Chorchana in the Georgian-Ossetian conflict zone in 2019. A criminal case has been brought against him over the decision, alleging that it sharply escalated tensions in the region and resulted in Georgia losing control over additional territory. “ We have no right to turn a blind eye to these facts and leave future generations a state whose constitutional foundations remain unprotected. That is why the actions of the National Movement and its offshoots [referring to the other four parties named in the lawsuit] must be declared unconstitutional and the parties banned ,” Gorduladze said. “Are you responding to the lawsuit or criticising us?” Zaza Bibilashvili spoke on behalf of Unity – National Movement. Shortly after he began his statement, Constitutional Court President Revaz Nadaraya interrupted him. The judge objected to Bibilashvili’s remark that the parties had “no illusions about the outcome of the proceedings”. Nadaraya interpreted the remark as an insult to the court. “ Are you responding to the lawsuit or criticising us? Are you challenging us, or what? To some extent, indirectly, you insulted the court by questioning our impartiality. You are showing disrespect, and there are limits to that too. Bear that in mind! ” he said. Bibilashvili: “The result will be the legitimisation of Russia’s military aggression in a Constitutional Court ruling” Zaza Bibilashvili spoke for almost two and a half hours about Unity – National Movement after his opening remarks. He recalled the difficult socio-economic situation in Georgia in the early 2000s, when the party came to power, and described how developed the country had become by the time Georgian Dream took office in 2012. Bibilashvili criticised Georgian Dream’s policies and several of its decisions, which he said had harmed the country as a whole. He also argued that “ the actual aim of these proceedings is to give Russia confirmation that its military aggression against Georgia in 2008 was justified, because Georgia’s own Constitutional Court would be arguing that Georgia itself supposedly created the grounds for Russia’s aggression ”. “ Some may object that this is not the court’s aim. But it is impossible to dispute that, if the claims in the lawsuit are upheld, the result will be the legitimisation of Russia’s military aggression through a ruling by Georgia’s Constitutional Court ,” Bibilashvili said. He stressed that the claimant, Georgian Dream, was deliberately conflating political and legal responsibility and failing to distinguish between the state and a political party. Bibilashvili: “The fox brought its own tail as a witness” Zaza Bibilashvili said the only evidence cited in the lawsuit to prove the opposition parties’ guilt was a report by a temporary parliamentary investigative commission. According to him, the report contains so many factual and legal errors that it cannot be made public. Bibilashvili noted that the opposition had effectively been found guilty even before the commission was established, in the explanatory note prepared for its creation. “ This means the outcome was known even before the commission was set up. It’s as if the fox brought its own tail as a witness — that is the essence of these proceedings ,” Bibilashvili said. Bibilashvili: “If the opposition is annulled, it can no longer pose an immediate threat to the state” Zaza Bibilashvili used a football analogy to question how a championship could ban every team except one from competing. He said that in a democratic country, banning political parties should not be a form of punishment but a means of protecting the state from an immediate threat posed by those parties. The state must demonstrate that a ban is urgently necessary. In this case, Bibilashvili argued, the claimant had failed to prove any such necessity. Moreover, he said, “ Prime Minister Irakli Kobakhidze himself has stated that there is no immediate threat from the opposition and no need to ban it ”. Bibilashvili also urged the court to consider a statement Kobakhidze had made earlier: “ Why ban the opposition? It has already been annulled.” Bibilashvili to judges: “Act in a way you want to be remembered by history” At the end of his lengthy statement, Zaza Bibilashvili said his closing remarks would be anything but conventional. “ I am not asking you to reject the lawsuit. But act in a way that you want to be remembered by history, in a way you would want your children to see you. Apply the same standards you would want those who come after you to apply to you. “Servants of authoritarianism often hope that democratic forces will treat them according to democratic standards, rather than the standards they themselves have established. However, after 14 years of Georgian Dream rule, more and more people in Georgian society are rejecting this approach. “They support the idea that, in future, everyone should be judged by the standards they themselves have established, both politically and legally. This would allow us to break once and for all the so-called vicious circle into which our enemy, Russia, has pushed us.” Bibilashvili’s remarks once again angered the Constitutional Court judge. “I told you to behave with dignity! How are we supposed to interpret your statement — as an attempt to put pressure on us?” “What kind of pressure could I possibly exert on you?” Bibilashvili asked rhetorically. “Stop lecturing us,” the judge replied. Should state have right to ban political parties? Tbilisi street poll – Video Most respondents said that banning political parties was unacceptable in a country that claims to be a democracy. Zaza Bibilashvili finished his statement at 18:30, with only 30 minutes remaining before the end of the court session. Ana Tsitlidze, another member of Unity – National Movement, was due to speak next, but said she needed more time. The court therefore decided to adjourn. Hearings on the constitutional lawsuit will resume tomorrow, 27 October, with Tsitlidze’s statement. Proceedings will begin at 12:00, and the court has agreed to sit until 19:00. According to the presiding judge, 20 representatives of the defendant parties are due to speak. Reactions after the hearing ● After the hearing, Georgian Dream MP Archil Gorduladze said that the National Movement had no evidence to refute the facts presented in the lawsuit: “ The National Movement representative talked about everything and nothing. He claimed that Georgia experienced a triumph of democracy in 2004–2012, and that there was no torture or inhuman treatment .” ● “ We heard truly unique accusations against Lelo – Strong Georgia. Apparently, signing the charter proposed by Ex-President Salome Zourabichvili and agreeing to cooperate with Giorgi Gakharia’s party during the municipal elections constitute violations of the Constitution ,” said Badri Japaridze, one of the leaders of Lelo – Strong Georgia. Maia Kopaleishvili, a member of Coalition for Change, said : “ We will fully refute all of Georgian Dream’s arguments and unfounded claims. An objective observer will see that Georgian Dream’s lawsuit is political in nature. Its aim is not to uphold the constitutional order in the country, but to eliminate political parties and establish one-party rule. This, of course, contributes to the establishment of a dictatorship in the country .” News in Georgia

title: Egypt Votes to Defend Saudi Arabia, Risking Houthi Fire
body:
Iraq's Oil Exports via Turkey Surge to 500,000 Bpd
Egypt’s parliament on Monday authorized military support to defend Saudi Arabia, the same day Yemen’s Houthis claimed unconfirmed attacks on pumping stations along the kingdom’s East-West crude pipeline and on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport.
The Houthis had warned Cairo against the move. Yahya Al Raei, speaker of the Houthi-run parliament in Sanaa, wrote to Egyptian Speaker Hisham Badawy last week that joining the conflict “would pose a grave danger” to Egypt’s national security.
The approval allows President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi to send forces if Riyadh asks for help against the Houthis. Sisi has said Egyptian support will be confined to defending Saudi territory and borders, with no attacks inside Yemen.
The Houthis claimed the pipeline strikes on Monday without naming the stations hit. Saudi Arabia had not confirmed any damage by Monday morning. On Saturday, the Houthis had also claimed strikes on the Rabigh refinery and an Aramco facility in Yanbu, which Riyadh also hasn’t confirmed.
The 740-mile pipeline carries crude across the kingdom to Yanbu on the Red Sea, bypassing the Strait of Hormuz. It was shut for two weeks after drone attacks blamed on Iran-backed Iraqi militias damaged pumping stations on September 10. Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman said on October 6 that flows had recovered to 5.8 million barrels per day , against a capacity of about 7 million bpd. Saudi exports from Yanbu have averaged about 3 million bpd so far in October, according to Kpler.
The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed two ballistic missile launchers in Sanaa, one of which was used to fire a missile toward Riyadh that was intercepted. It also said it hit five missile storage tunnels and four more launchers.
Riyadh is talking to Tehran at the same time, with Saudi Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman leading a surprise delegation to Tehran on Monday. Riyadh said the visit aimed to de-escalate and support mediation by Qatar and Pakistan. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said indirect talks with Washington continue through both countries, and that Tehran is ready to resume fighting but diplomacy is still possible.

title: ‎Let’s return to plantain leaves for food takeaway – EPA CEO on Styrofoam ban
body: The Chief Executive Officer of the Environmental Protection Authority (EPA), Prof. Nana Ama Browne Klutse, has urged Ghanaians to embrace environmentally friendly food-packaging alternatives, including traditional plantain leaves, ahead of the nationwide ban on Styrofoam products scheduled to take effect on January 1, 2027. She called on households, food vendors, schools, traders and businesses to begin moving away from Styrofoam takeaway containers, stressing that early adoption of alternative materials would make the transition easier when enforcement begins. ‎ ‎Prof. Browne Klutse made the call during a stakeholder engagement at the Savannah Regional capital of Damongo on Monday, October 26, 2026, as part of efforts to sensitise the public in the Savannah Region to the implementation of the nationwide ban. ‎ ‎The event brought together members of the general public, food vendors, restaurant owners, traditional and religious leaders, students and other stakeholders. Representatives of partner institutions, including the Ghana Police Service, Ghana Tourism Authority, Ghana Health Service and the Department of Food and Agriculture, also delivered solidarity messages and expressed their commitment to supporting the enforcement of the ban. ‎ ‎The EPA CEO buttressed the view that the government had provided sufficient time for public education and stakeholder consultations, adding that the country must now move towards practical action to reduce the environmental and health risks associated with Styrofoam products. ‎ She highlighted the availability of alternatives, including biodegradable packaging, reusable containers and other materials that can be recycled or break down naturally. ‎ ‎Professor Klutse encouraged Ghanaians to rediscover traditional food-packaging practices, including the use of plantain leaves where suitable, while urging businesses to explore affordable and sustainable alternatives. ‎ ‎”The availability and use of alternative packaging materials could increase as demand grows, making it important for consumers and businesses to begin adjusting their practices before the enforcement deadline. And this is something we should commit to.” Professor Ama Browne Klutse indicated. ‎ ‎The CEO also emphasised that the campaign was not merely an announcement from government offices in Accra but a national responsibility requiring the involvement of everyone, from national leaders to individual community members. She therefore invited stakeholders to take the message to their homes, workplaces, markets and communities to ensure that residents understand the importance of the ban and the need to adopt sustainable practices. ‎ ‎On his part, the Savannah Regional Minister, Salisu Be-Awuribe, assured the CEO of the region of total commitment and dedication to the course of the environment. Mr Be-Awuribe indicated the region’s dedication to enforcing the ban from January 1, 2027, warning that the production, importation, and “Distribution, sale and use of prohibited Styrofoam products would no longer be tolerated in all seven Municipal and District Assemblies in the region after the deadline. ‎ ‎According to the Minister, the Savannah Regional Coordinating Council, the seven Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies (MDAs), the EPA, the Ghana Police Service and customs officers at checkpoints would be expected to support enforcement. ‎ ‎”The time has come for us to act with one concern about the growing use and improper disposal of Styrofoam takeaway containers in communities including Damongo, Bole, Sawla, Buipe, Salaga and Daboya. ‎ ‎According to him, “Discarded containers litter streets and public spaces, choke gutters and obstruct drains, contributing to flooding and undermining efforts to maintain clean communities. But I believe the Savannah Region can set the pace.”Mr Be-Awuribe. ‎ ‎‎The Minister further raised concerns about the harmful smoke produced when Styrofoam is burned and the potential health risks associated with using certain containers for hot foods, and identified other alternatives for redress. ‎”Paper packaging, biodegradable containers, reusable bowls and traditional food-wrapping materials are possible substitutes, while encouraging young people to explore opportunities in producing and supplying environmentally friendly packaging.” ‎The Savannah Regional Director of the EPA, Abu Iddrisu, joined the call on residents and stakeholders to support the campaign, highlighting the importance of protecting the region’s environment, agriculture, aquatic ecosystems and tourism sector. ‎ ‎Dr Abu Iddrisu described the Savannah Region as Ghana’s largest region by land area, a major food basket of northern Ghana and home to Mole National Park, one of the country’s leading wildlife tourism destinations. ‎ ‎He said environmental protection was particularly important to the region because of its contribution to food production, biodiversity and tourism, warning that pollution could undermine these important sectors. ‎ ‎According to him, “Styrofoam waste can accumulate on land and in water bodies, damage the natural beauty of communities and contribute to environmental pollution and diseases.” Dr Abu Iddrisu. ‎ ‎He further explained that improper disposal of waste could affect farming communities through soil and water pollution, while discarded materials entering rivers and other water bodies could threaten aquatic life. Dr Iddrisu stressed that the environmental “Reset agenda championed by President John Dramani Mahama required collective action from government institutions, traditional authorities, businesses, community leaders and the general public.” ‎ ‎He urged residents to take responsibility for keeping their surroundings clean and supporting measures aimed at reducing waste and promoting responsible disposal practices. ‎ ‎The participation of the Ghana Police Service, Ghana Tourism Authority, Ghana Health Service and the Department of Food and Agriculture underscored the cross-sectoral importance of the campaign. ‎ ‎And through their solidarity speeches, representatives of the participating institutions expressed their commitment to supporting efforts to implement the ban and protect the environment. ‎ ‎Their involvement highlighted the connection between waste management, public health, agricultural production, tourism development, and law enforcement. ‎ ‎The presence of traditional and religious leaders, students, food vendors, restaurant owners and members of the public also provided an opportunity to extend the campaign beyond government institutions to the communities and businesses directly affected by the policy. ‎As part of preparations towards the enforcement, the Savannah Regional Coordinating Council has announced a public education and clean-up campaign exercise to begin from October through to December 2026. ‎ ‎The campaign is expected to target food vendors, chop bars, restaurants, hotels, guest houses, shops, plastic retailers, schools, lorry stations and other public spaces. EPA, as part of its mandate, engages affected groups in local languages to explain the reasons for the ban, the products affected, and the alternatives available. ‎‎The nationwide ban is scheduled to take effect on January 1, 2027, with authorities intensifying public education and preparations to help businesses and communities transition away from Styrofoam products. ‎ ‎The campaign seeks to promote cleaner communities and more sustainable packaging practices, with the EPA urging Ghanaians to begin making the change now rather than wait until the enforcement deadline. ‎ Earlier in the day, stakeholders embarked on a float on the principal streets of Damongo, holding placards with inscriptions such as choose reusable bowls and save money, Ghana bans Styrofoam packs?,and Ghana bans Styrofoam 1st January, 2027, among others, to help create the needed awareness ‎and education among residents. The message from the three officials was clear: protecting the environment requires collective responsibility, and traditional practices such as using plantain leaves, alongside safe and affordable modern alternatives, could form part of Ghana’s transition towards more sustainable food packaging.

title: Nigeria could declare Ebola outbreak over by Dec 7 – Pate
body: By Sola Ogundipe Nigeria could declare the Ebola outbreak over as early as December 7, 2026, if no further confirmed or probable cases are detected following the medical evacuation of the country’s imported index patient. The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Mohammed Ali Pate, disclosed the provisional date on Monday as health authorities intensified contact tracing, investigated suspected cases and strengthened preparedness across health facilities to prevent further spread of the Bundibugyo virus disease. Writing on his X handle, Pate said the 42-day countdown towards declaring the outbreak over would be subject to validation by the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) and the World Health Organisation (WHO), in line with established outbreak management criteria. The development follows the evacuation of Nigeria’s index patient to Switzerland for further medical care, a move that has heightened attention on the country’s capacity to sustain containment measures and prevent community transmission. According to Pate, “Following the imported Ebola index patient’s medical evacuation from Nigeria today, 26 October, our immediate priorities remain active monitoring of all identified contacts, prompt investigation of alerts and strengthened readiness across our health facilities. “If no further confirmed or probable cases are detected, Nigeria could progress towards declaring this outbreak over under @WHO criteria, potentially as early as 7 December 2026. This date remains provisional, subject to @NCDCgov and WHO validating the 42-day countdown. Any further case would require a fresh countdown in accordance with those criteria,” Pate noted. He said the proposed December 7 date is therefore not a final declaration that Nigeria is Ebola-free, but a conditional target that depends on the absence of further cases and the completion of the required surveillance period. Further, he said, “Our teams, working with FCTA and state health authorities and our partners, remain focused on containment and preventing community transmission. “I ask Nigerians to remain calm, cooperate with contact-tracing teams and follow regular updates from @NCDCgov and @Fmohnigeria.” The post Nigeria could declare Ebola outbreak over by Dec 7 – Pate appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Lula wins Brazil runoff after prediction markets favored Bolsonaro
body:
Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva was reelected president of Brazil on Sunday in a runoff election, an upset that prediction markets odds failed to anticipate.
Lula defeated Flávio Bolsonaro , the right-wing candidate and son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, by 51.8% to 48.2%, according to the country's Superior Electoral Court.
As late as Sunday afternoon, Lula remained a significant underdog on prediction markets. Even just after 8:30 p.m. ET on Sunday, Lula's odds were at 21% on Kalshi.
Bolsonaro's odds on prediction markets surged after first-round voting on Oct. 4, with both Kalshi and Polymarket giving Bolsonaro an over 80% chance of ousting Lula. The Kalshi contract asked, "Brazil Presidential election winner?" and was verified by reporting from the Associated Press.
Kalshi co-founder and CEO Tarek Mansour has previously defended Kalshi's election contracts. In August, Kalshi reflected a 95% likelihood of Wisconsin Democratic socialist Francesca Hong winning the Democratic gubernatorial primary over Milwaukee County executive David Crowley. Instead, Hong lost the race by less than 1 percentage point.
"Before the 'prediction markets got it wrong' headlines roll in: a 5% probability doesn't mean it won't happen," Mansour wrote in an Aug. 12 social media post on X. "It means it should happen 1 in 20 times. If 5% candidates never won, the markets would be broken."
Odds and prediction market platforms do not use methodologies used by traditional political polling, and therefore are not substitutes for political polls.
Unlike prediction market odds, which pointed to a clear Bolsonaro victory, political polls showed a tight race in the days leading up to the contest.
Brazil's Supreme Court also extended voting for two hours late Sunday, which Bolsonaro argued hurt his chances of winning the presidency. Bolsonaro is expected to challenge the outcome, Reuters reported .
Following Lula's victory, Brazil-linked stocks and ETFs slid on Monday. The iShares MSCI Brazil ETF (EWZ) shed 22%, while U.S.-traded shares of Itau Unibanco an d Banco Bradesco tanked 20% and nearly 30%, respectively. Brewer Ambev and Petrobras each declined more than 15%.

title: Alleged N582m fraud: Court fixes Nov 23 for trial of ex-NNPCL boss
body: threatens to issue bench warrant By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA – A High Court of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) on Monday fixed November 23 for the arraignment of a former President of the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPCL) Staff Multi-Purpose Cooperative Society, Abuja, Mr. Olalekan Ogunbayo, over his alleged complicity in a ₦582 million fraud. The court, presided over by Justice Lesley Wike, further threatened to issue a bench warrant against the defendant should he fail to appear before it to enter his plea to an eight-count charge preferred against him by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC). After the case was called, the anti-graft agency drew the court’s attention to the absence of the defendant, who was billed for arraignment. According to the prosecution, the development marked the third time the defendant had stayed away from court despite being aware of the case. EFCC’s lawyer, R. U. Adagba, who informed the court that only the 2nd defendant in the matter, Abolade Nurudeen, was available for the proceedings, alleged that Ogunbayo had jumped the administrative bail granted him by the Commission. He told the court that all efforts to locate the 1st defendant for service of the charge on him had been unsuccessful. Consequently, he applied for a bench warrant to be issued to enable security agencies to arrest and produce the defendant in court for trial. The prosecution counsel premised his application for the bench warrant on the provisions of Sections 35, 113 and 114 of the Administration of Criminal Justice Act (ACJA) 2015. However, Mr. Innocent Adoo, who announced his appearance for the defendants, opposed the application. He accused the EFCC of failing to properly serve a copy of the charge on the defendant. The defence counsel argued that arraignment in a criminal trial cannot proceed without proper service of the charge on the defendant. He submitted that a defendant must be informed of the allegations against him and given adequate opportunity to prepare his defence, adding that service could not be waived by any party. Adoo told the court that Ogunbayo was still on administrative bail and was unaware of the scheduled arraignment. He explained that the defence had used the information available to it to communicate with Ogunbayo, who was said to be in Warri, Delta State, and unable to secure a flight to Abuja for the sitting. He therefore prayed the court for an adjournment to enable both defendants to appear and take their pleas in the interest of justice. In his ruling, Justice Wike held that, in the interest of justice, the matter should be adjourned to enable the first defendant to appear for arraignment. The judge, however, warned that the court would take the necessary steps if Ogunbayo failed to appear on the next adjourned date. The charges against the defendants border on alleged criminal misappropriation, abuse of office, corrupt practices and obtaining money by false pretence. The defendants were accused of involvement in the sale of the cooperative society’s property at Plot 50, Karsana North, Abuja. The prosecution alleged that the defendants conspired in January 2024 to misappropriate proceeds from the transaction. In one of the counts, the defendants were accused of dishonestly misappropriating ₦582 million realised from the sale of the property. Ogunbayo was also accused of receiving ₦100 million, ₦10 million and ₦50 million through different bank accounts in connection with the transaction. The prosecution further alleged that the 1st defendant received ₦180 million into an account belonging to his firm after representing that the property had been sold for ₦1 billion. Both defendants were also accused of involvement in an alleged ₦160 million corrupt transaction. The post Alleged N582m fraud: Court fixes Nov 23 for trial of ex-NNPCL boss appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Should Police Wipe a Criminal's Cellphone Before Returning It?–U.S. vs. Stathas
body:
“Stathas pleaded guilty in 2023 to enticing a minor to engage in unlawful sexual activity” (18 U.S.C. § 2422(b)). He was sentenced to 180 months in prison and 10 years of supervised release.
As part of the arrest and investigation, the police seized Stathas’ car, cellphone, wallet, and other electronics. Per 18 U.S.C. § 2428(a)(1), the judge should have ordered (but did not) a forfeiture of “any property, real or personal, that was used or intended to be used to commit or to facilitate the commission of such violation.” The forfeiture should include the cellphone (Stathas used it to communicate extensively with the victim), but does that include the data on the cellphone, which arguably is neither real property nor personal property?
After Stathas’ sentencing, the police agreed to return his car, wallet, and other electronics. If the police had gotten a forfeiture order, they wouldn’t have to return his cellphone at all, but instead they agreed to return the phone only after wiping it “because it contained obscene, sexually explicit conversations between Stathas and the victim, as well as the victim’s identifying information.” “Stathas responded that although he did not object to the government deleting his conversations with the victim, other data on the phone should be preserved because it was meaningful to him personally or relevant to a possible civil lawsuit against the West Bend Police Department.”
the government’s retention and destruction of the data on Stathas’s cellphone is reasonable under the circumstances. The district court’s finding that the phone was rife with “numerous sexually explicit messages and images” sent to the victim as well as “significant personally identifying information about her” is not clear error. The record reveals that these conversations occurred over multiple apps on the phone and that Stathas also received explicit photos of the minor. The court did not clearly err by crediting the government’s assertion that “no procedure short of digitally wiping” the phone would eliminate all criminal or harmful material. Given the importance of the government’s interest in ensuring none of this material remains on Stathas’s phone, the district court did not abuse its discretion in concluding that the government could delete the phone’s data before returning it.
I haven’t seen a lot of discussion about wiping cellphone as a criminal remedy. In a case like this, it makes sense that the data associated with the crime should not go back into the criminal’s hand. At the same time, a cellphone wipe deletes a lot of data that may have nothing to do with the crime. Depending on the nature of that data and the availability of backups, a cellphone wipe could profoundly affect a person’s life. For example, if the cellphone had the data necessary to establish Stathas’ legal claim against the police, the cellphone wipe might extinguish his legal claim entirely.
The severity of a cellphone wipe brought to mind the Supreme Court’s discussion about the importance of cellphones (in a slightly different legal context) in Riley v. California, 573 U.S. 373 (2014):
The term “cell phone” is itself misleading shorthand; many of these devices are in fact minicomputers that also happen to have the capacity to be used as a telephone. They could just as easily be called cameras, video players, rolodexes, calendars, tape recorders, libraries, diaries, albums, televisions, maps, or newspapers.
One of the most notable distinguishing features of modern cell phones is their immense storage capacity….
The current top-selling smart phone has a standard capacity of 16 gigabytes (and is available with up to 64 gigabytes). Sixteen gigabytes translates to millions of pages of text, thousands of pictures, or hundreds of videos. Cell phones couple that capacity with the ability to store many different types of information: Even the most basic phones that sell for less than $20 might hold photographs, picture messages, text messages, Internet browsing history, a calendar, a thousand-entry phone book, and so on. We expect that the gulf between physical practicability and digital capacity will only continue to widen in the future.
The storage capacity of cell phones has several interrelated consequences for privacy. First, a cell phone collects in one place many distinct types of information—an address, a note, a prescription, a bank statement, a video—that reveal much more in combination than any isolated record. Second, a cell phone’s capacity allows even just one type of information to convey far more than previously possible. The sum of an individual’s private life can be reconstructed through a thousand photographs labeled with dates, locations, and descriptions; the same cannot be said of a photograph or two of loved ones tucked into a wallet. Third, the data on a phone can date back to the purchase of the phone, or even earlier. A person might carry in his pocket a slip of paper reminding him to call Mr. Jones; he would not carry a record of all his communications with Mr. Jones for the past several months, as would routinely be kept on a phone.
Finally, there is an element of pervasiveness that characterizes cell phones but not physical records. Prior to the digital age, people did not typically carry a cache of sensitive personal information with them as they went about their day. Now it is the person who is not carrying a cell phone, with all that it contains, who is the exception. According to one poll, nearly three-quarters of smart phone users report being within five feet of their phones most of the time, with 12% admitting that they even use their phones in the shower. A decade ago police officers searching an arrestee might have occasionally stumbled across a highly personal item such as a diary. But those discoveries were likely to be few and far between. Today, by contrast, it is no exaggeration to say that many of the more than 90% of American adults who own a cell phone keep on their person a digital record of nearly every aspect of their lives—from the mundane to the intimate….
Mobile application software on a cell phone, or “apps,” offer a range of tools for managing detailed information about all aspects of a person’s life. There are apps for Democratic Party news and Republican Party news; apps for alcohol, drug, and gambling addictions; apps for sharing prayer requests; apps for tracking pregnancy symptoms; apps for planning your budget; apps for every conceivable hobby or pastime; apps for improving your romantic life. There are popular apps for buying or selling just about anything, and the records of such transactions may be accessible on the phone indefinitely. There are over a million apps available in each of the two major app stores; the phrase “there’s an app for that” is now part of the popular lexicon. The average smart phone user has installed 33 apps, which together can form a revealing montage of the user’s life.
In 1926, Learned Hand observed that it is “a totally different thing to search a man’s pockets and use against him what they contain, from ransacking his house for everything which may incriminate him.” If his pockets contain a cell phone, however, that is no longer true. Indeed, a cell phone search would typically expose to the government far more than the most exhaustive search of a house: A phone not only contains in digital form many sensitive records previously found in the home; it also contains a broad array of private information never found in a home in any form—unless the phone is.
Case Citation : U.S. v. Stathas , 2026 WL 3061816 (7th Cir. October 13, 2026)

Following reports of iPhone Duos with cracked and broken inside screens, often showing a bright line running from the center to the right side, Apple says in a statement to Bloomberg and 9to5Mac that it’s aware of “an issue impacting the inner display” on a “small number of iPhone Duo units.” If your iPhone Duo is affected, Apple says to contact AppleCare for a replacement.
Here is the full statement, which Apple’s Alex Kirschner shared with The Verge :
The response to iPhone Duo from early users has been incredibly positive, and we are seeing exciting things from developers who are rapidly updating their apps to take advantage of its unique form factor. We are aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units. If users experience issues with their iPhone Duo display, they should contact AppleCare for a replacement.
Kirshner says most units aren’t susceptible and that the issues appear quickly on units with the defect.
Shortly after launch, iPhone Duo users started reporting similar issues where the hinge would tighten, and opening the device caused a crack and the distinctive bright lines on the display. One user in Australia said that an Apple Store replaced their unit “on the spot.”
This weekend, iFixit published its teardown of the phone and gave its perspective on why some phones might be cracking. Where the damage has been happening, iFixit shows how the foldable screen might be pushing against a center bar.
The new phones are some of the first devices to launch after new CEO John Ternus took over from Tim Cook .
