title: UAE Aid Agency announces $3 million in support for those returning to Afghanistan
body: The UAE Aid Agency has signed a $3 million agreement with the UN refugee agency to provide permanent housing for thousands of Afghan returnees, with a focus on women and children. The co-operation agreement with the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) will fund the construction of climate-resilient homes for 2,950 people across the provinces of Kabul, Herat and Kunduz. The deal was announced during Aidex 2026, a humanitarian aid and disaster relief conference held in Geneva on October 21 and 22. The agreement is part of the UAE's broader strategy to support early recovery, deliver sustainable solutions for displaced persons, and strengthen the stability of communities affected by humanitarian crises. Dr Tareq Al Ameri, chairman of the UAE Aid Agency, used a keynote address at the conference to reaffirm the nation's commitment to its global humanitarian and development role. Dr Al Ameri stressed the importance of building international partnerships, developing innovative financing models, and investing in sustainable solutions that help communities withstand and recover from crises. The agency held bilateral meetings with several international organisations at the conference, including the International Committee of the Red Cross, the World Health Organisation, and the UN offices for humanitarian affairs and disaster risk reduction. Talks centred on expanding co-operation, strengthening crisis response and harnessing artificial intelligence to forecast and mitigate disasters. The agency also co-hosted a round table with UNHCR titled “Housing Solutions After Displacement: From Temporary Shelter to Recovery and Integration”, which examined the transition from emergency shelter to long-term housing and the role of private sector partnerships in supporting refugees and host communities. The agency also highlighted other major initiatives at the conference, including Operation Gallant Knight 3 in Gaza and the Sheikha Fatima Fund for Refugee Women, which works to economically and socially empower displaced women.

title: Putin to focus on priorities for Russia-Africa cooperation at UN — Kremlin aide
body:
MOSCOW, October 26. /TASS/. In his address at the first plenary session of the Russia-Africa summit, Russian President Vladimir Putin will place special emphasis on the priorities for cooperation between Russia and African countries within the United Nations, Presidential Aide Yury Ushakov has told the media.
"Our address will focus, in particular, on the growing role of Africa, as well as the priorities for Russia’s engagement with the continent’s nations within the UN and other major international and regional organizations," Ushakov specified.
Putin will also discuss joint projects and initiatives currently underway in African countries - covering trade, the economy, cultural and humanitarian ties, and educational exchanges - as well as the support Russia provides for the development of states across the African continent.
"Following this, a second plenary session will take place. The work and discussions will continue at a working luncheon - tentatively scheduled for 2:00 p.m. Delegations from African countries that did not speak during the first session will be given the floor. Every single head of an African delegation - regardless of their level of representation - will be provided with an opportunity to speak," Ushakov concluded.

title: Stalwart v1.0: The Fastest Mail Server on the Planet
body:
Five years ago, on 3 October 2021, the first commit landed in a small repository called mail-parser. It was an e-mail parsing library written in Rust, and nothing more. Over the following five years it grew into a complete mail and collaboration server with JMAP, IMAP, POP3, SMTP, CalDAV, CardDAV and WebDAV, a spam filter, clustering, and support for half a dozen storage backends. Today, after five years of continuous development, we are proud to announce Stalwart v1.0 , the first stable release.
Version 1.0 was never meant to be another feature release. It had two goals. The first was performance: making every part of the server as fast as it can be, and proving it with numbers. The second was stability of the data itself: finalising the database schema so that, from now on, upgrading Stalwart means installing a new version and nothing more, without the disruptive migrations some earlier releases required. Along the way a few new features found their way in too, including full-text search inside PDF and office documents.
Most of the work in this release happened under a profiler. For months we measured where Stalwart spends its CPU cycles, its memory and its database round trips, rewrote whatever stood out, and measured again. The release contains close to 200 commits touching more than 1,300 files, and the vast majority of them exist to make something faster or lighter.
A mail server spends a surprising share of its time looking for specific bytes: the end of a header line, a MIME boundary, an equals sign in a quoted-printable body, the space that ends an IMAP tag. Done one byte at a time, that is a lot of loop iterations for a 10 MB message. Two techniques let a CPU do this work many bytes at a time:
Stalwart now uses both, everywhere it matters. At the bottom of the stack sit two libraries that reach 1.0 together with the server:
Above them, the protocol layer got the same treatment. The IMAP command parser is now table-driven and scans whole runs of bytes instead of stepping a state machine per character. The SMTP command parser, the JSON parser behind JMAP, the spam filter tokenizers, the HTML-to-text converter, the variable-length integer codec and the log serializers all use SWAR scanning. Even the expression language, which administrators use for routing and filtering decisions, now compiles to a compact bytecode with specialised instructions for common comparisons and evaluates them in a recycled memory arena.
Fast parsing is wasted if every request then waits on the database, so we spent just as long on how Stalwart talks to its storage. Identifiers are now assigned inside the same write transaction that uses them, removing whole round trips from every message delivery. Read-modify-write updates, such as adding a keyword or appending to a search index, run as merge operations inside the backend. Stored objects are compressed with zstd using dictionaries trained specifically on e-mail, calendar and contact data.
Each backend was also tuned individually:
On top of the storage layer sits a redesigned cache subsystem. Each account’s message index is held in memory in a compact packed form, and IMAP sorting, threading, flag fetches, searches on message properties and resynchronisation are now answered from that cache with few or no database reads. Very large accounts get their own cache tier with a memory budget, and cache snapshots can be swapped out to local disk, Redis or the blob store instead of being rebuilt.
The built-in full-text search engine was rewritten from the ground up. The previous design stored one bitmap per word and had no notion of word positions. The new engine stores postings in blocks of 65,536 documents and keeps word positions for every message. That makes real phrase searches possible, and lets a search inside one mailbox read only the blocks that mailbox touches. It indexes word stems and prefixes, compresses its data with zstd, and indexes new mail through a background queue with concurrency control, retries and rebuilds. The PostgreSQL and MySQL search backends were reworked as well. On a mailbox of 250,000 messages, a full-text search of every message body now returns in under 4 milliseconds.
Optimising code without measuring it under realistic load is guesswork, so we built a dedicated benchmarking and stress-testing lab to go with this release. It runs on Microsoft Azure, across more than 30 regions, with up to 18 complete test labs running in parallel and several hundred vCPUs busy at once.
The test catalogue covers 35 kinds of test, spread over more than 550 individual test cells, and they cover:
Runs were profiled throughout. CPU time was sampled with perf and turned into flame graphs, off-CPU analysis showed where threads waited on locks and I/O, the heap was profiled with jemalloc and heaptrack, and a special instrumented build counted every storage round trip, per command, so we could see exactly which requests hit the database more than they should. Each fix was then measured against the previous build on matched machines before it was accepted.
The first full round of this cycle turned up 64 problems, which were fixed and retested. The second round re-ran everything and fixed 33 more. Some examples of what the lab caught:
This lab is not a one-off effort for the release. It is now part of how Stalwart is tested internally: every future release goes through the same benchmark and stress-test rounds before it ships, so performance gains stay gained.
Internal numbers only tell you whether Stalwart got faster than it was. We also wanted to know how it compares to what most of the world runs. So we put Stalwart v1.0 head to head with the most widely deployed open-source mail stack: Postfix 3.11 for SMTP and Dovecot 2.4 for IMAP.
Both ran on identical Azure servers (8 AMD EPYC Zen 5 vCPUs, 32 GiB of RAM, local NVMe storage), loaded with the same 1,000 mailboxes plus three very large ones of up to 250,000 messages, and received exactly the same work: receiving mail, delivering it and serving it to IMAP clients. Encryption, password hashing and full-text search were configured the same way on both, and the two systems were measured alternately on the same hardware.
Stalwart was faster in 35 of the 38 headline comparisons.
The gap grows with the size of the mailbox. On a 250,000-message mailbox, a full-text search of every message body takes 3.75 ms in Stalwart and 136 ms in Dovecot, and moving or deleting 25,000 messages finishes in about a tenth of a second instead of 24 to 34 seconds: more than 200 times faster.
The three tests Dovecot won are all the same operation: marking every message in a mailbox as read at once.
Only Postfix and Dovecot were tested, but they are not just any two products. They are the engine under nearly every popular self-hosted mail server: every open-source dockerized mail server with more than 10,000 stars on GitHub, including docker-mailserver and mailcow , runs Postfix and Dovecot under the hood, as does Mail-in-a-Box. Beating that combination on almost every benchmark means beating the stack behind most of the self-hosted mail on the internet. We are now comfortable saying it plainly: Stalwart is the fastest mail server on the planet.
Don’t take our word for it. Every script, configuration, test scenario and raw result is in the benchmarks repository , together with a methodology and a frank list of caveats, such as the differences in disk-sync behaviour between the two systems. Anyone with an Azure account can provision the same servers and run the whole suite. Benchmarks of Stalwart’s different storage backends and clustered setups are being prepared for the same repository.
Performance was the headline, but v1.0 also brings a set of new features:
Finalising the database schema has a price that is paid once: Stalwart v1.0 uses a new database layout, and existing data has to be migrated to it. A v1.0 server will not open a store created by an earlier version.
We know that some past upgrades were bumpy, and we took that seriously. This migration was designed and tested to be as smooth as we could make it, and it is the last of its kind: the schema is now stable, and future releases will upgrade in place. There are two ways to get to v1.0.
For deployments running Stalwart v0.16, stalwart-migrate is the easiest route. It requires v0.16.27, so earlier 0.16 releases should be updated to it first. The tool converts your settings to the v1.0 schema and copies all data into a new, empty v1.0 store. It only reads from the old store, so the original deployment stays intact and can be restarted at any point before the switch.
It also migrates incrementally. The first copy runs while v0.16 keeps serving users, however long it takes. Each later run copies only what changed since the previous one, and the only downtime is the short final run, after v0.16 is stopped. Account and message identifiers, IMAP UIDs and change history are preserved, so IMAP and JMAP clients carry on without downloading anything again. Users who sign in with OAuth will need to sign in again, and the full-text index is rebuilt in the background after the switch.
For anyone running Stalwart v0.15 or earlier, or anyone who prefers to move users one at a time, the migration guide describes the second route. The migration proxy sits in front of both the old and the new server and sends each user to whichever one holds their account, and Vandelay copies accounts across one by one, incrementally. Each account is switched by flipping one entry in a mapping table, with no downtime for that user, and the old server keeps a full copy until you decide to retire it. The same procedure also works for moving from Dovecot and Postfix to Stalwart. The migration overview compares the two approaches.
The structure of your settings is largely the same. Around a hundred keys were renamed to follow consistent naming conventions, a few objects (OIDC directories, AI models, Azure storage, forwarded headers) were restructured, and stalwart-migrate converts all of it automatically. Two changes need attention before you upgrade:
If you use an external identity provider that is not conformant, Stalwart’s token checks can be relaxed through the compatibility settings on the OIDC directory, at your own risk, since each one weakens a security check. These settings mainly keep web clients such as the WebUI working. What they cannot fix is a provider that lacks the profile itself, and that is going to matter soon: popular e-mail clients, including Apple Mail, are adopting the profile, and once they do, their users will not be able to authenticate against a non-conformant provider. If you depend on an external identity provider, now is a good time to ask them to support it.
A related change affects the WebUI. Instead of a fixed client id, it now identifies itself to the identity provider with a Client ID Metadata Document , a URL that describes the client. Some identity providers do not support this yet. With those, administrators can register a client for the WebUI with the provider and set its id in oauthClientId , and the WebUI signs in as before. The details are in client id of the WebUI .
If you run into a problem or have a question during the migration, post it on support.stalw.art . We will be answering questions there daily throughout the migration period.
Five years ago this was one Rust library for parsing e-mail. Today it is a complete mail and collaboration server, and with v1.0 it is faster than anything else we have measured it against. None of it would have happened without the community: everyone who filed an issue, sent a patch, answered a question on the forum, or trusted Stalwart with their mail. Thank you.
Download Stalwart v1.0 and let us know what you think.

title: Ebola: Nigeria may declare outbreak over in December – Minister
body:
Nigeria may declare the Ebola outbreak over as early as 7 December if no further confirmed or probable cases are detected, the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Muhammad Pate, has said.
Mr Pate made this known in a statement shared on his official X handle on Monday, following the medical evacuation of Nigeria’s imported Ebola index patient to Switzerland earlier in the day.
He said the date remains provisional and would depend on the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) and the World Health Organisation (WHO) validating the required 42-day countdown.
“Any further case would require a fresh countdown in accordance with those criteria,” Mr Pate said.
The minister said Nigeria’s immediate priorities are to continue monitoring all identified contacts, promptly investigate alerts, and strengthen preparedness across health facilities.
He said the response teams, working with the Federal Capital Territory Administration (FCTA), state health authorities and partners, remain focused on containing the disease and preventing community transmission.
Mr Pate urged Nigerians to “remain calm, cooperate with contact-tracing teams and follow updates” from the NCDC and Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare.
Earlier on Monday, Mr Pate confirmed the medical evacuation of the imported Ebola patient and her husband to Switzerland.
The patient, who is Nigeria’s only confirmed Ebola case, had been receiving treatment in isolation in Abuja after testing positive for Bundibugyo virus disease, a form of Ebola.
WHO subsequently said Nigeria has no active Ebola cases following the evacuation.
The WHO Regional Director for Africa, Mohamed Janabi, said the patient was clinically stable and that Switzerland would assume responsibility for her continued medical management and follow-up for her husband, a contact.
Nigeria confirmed the imported case on 20 October, after the patient arrived in the country following international travel through Uganda.

title: Goal of Russia - Africa summit is to expand cooperation — Kremlin aide
body:
MOSCOW, October 26. /TASS/. The idea of the Russia - Africa summit is to facilitate expansion of cooperation across all the areas, Russian presidential aide Yury Ushakov said.
"The motto of the third Russia - Africa summit ‘For peace, security and development’ fully repeats the motto of previous summits. The idea of this summit is to promote the expansion of Russian-African cooperation in all areas and, certainly, to facilitate strengthening of African countries’ sovereignty," Ushakov said.
The summit testifies to the special importance that Russia attaches to its relations with African states, the high-ranking official said. "These relations rest on time-tested traditions of friendship, mutual respect, equality, and solidarity. It is well known that our country aided and assisted African peoples in their struggle against colonial oppression, and wholeheartedly and selflessly supported the states of the continent in their pursuit of freedom, independence, modern development, and the choice of their own models of political and socio-economic systems," he added.

title: Ukraine strikes Russian plant producing missile, bomb batteries in Yelets, General Staff says
body:
A fire broke out on the territory of the Energia plant following an overnight attack on the battery plant in the city of Yelets in western Russia overnight on Oct. 26, Ukraine's General Staff said later that day.
The plant is the sole Russian manufacturer of batteries for glide bomb guidance and correction modules, the General Staff said without specifying the extent of the damage.
It added that the plant, located about 250 kilometers (about 155 miles) from Ukraine, also produces batteries for Iskander-M ballistic missile systems and sea-based cruise missiles.
"The strike complicates the Russian Federation's military's production of power sources for missiles, guided bombs, and other weapons," the General Staff said in its Telegram post.
Earlier on Oct. 25, Ukrainian monitoring Telegram channel Exilenova Plus reported that smoke rose over the whole territory of the Energia plant after several missiles appeared to have hit it in the afternoon. The General Staff has not specified what weapons were used to strike the Energia plant in Russia.
In its statement, the General Staff said that Ukraine had also "destroyed" the main microchip production workshop of Proton-Electrotex Enterprise in Orel, western Russia, on Oct. 23. It added that the attack would likely complicate the Russian production of components used to produce cruise and ballistic missiles, which are often deployed to target Ukrainian cities.
The Russian Defense Ministry has not reacted to the General Staff's statement. The Kyiv Independent could not independently verify these claim.
The attack comes as Ukraine intensifies its long-range attacks inside Russia and across Russian-occupied territories, often targeting defense industrial plants, airfields, and oil refineries.
Earlier on Oct. 26, independent Russian media outlet Astra reported that a chemical plant producing dual-use goods in the southwestern Russian city of Voronezh was likely hit in a Ukrainian drone attack.

title: Analysis: No, Elon Musk, Russian soldiers in Ukraine are not 'kids' who have 'no choice but to fight and die'
body:
"We should (have) some sympathy for the poor Russian conscripts too. Those kids have no choice but to fight and die in drone strikes."
For anyone watching and understanding Ukraine's years-long struggle for survival, the words of SpaceX founder and world's richest man Elon Musk ring with deep moral bankruptcy.
But more importantly, Musk's post on Oct. 25 — made in the middle of a hurricane scandal around the near-trillionaire's throttling of Starlink internet terminals used by the Ukrainian military — badly misrepresents the reality of how Russia staffs its wartime military.
The misconception that Russian soldiers are forced to fight against their will in Ukraine is one that has consistently reached the most powerful men in the United States.
Earlier this year, U.S. President Donald Trump repeatedly lamented the deaths of soldiers on both sides, seemingly equating their suffering and the circumstances under which they found themselves in the trenches.
"Every day people are dying. Young handsome soldiers are being killed. Young men, like my sons. On both sides. All over the battlefield," he said in February.
"Young, young, beautiful people. They’re like your kids, two million of them — and for no reason."
But this sentiment ignores one important fact — Russian soldiers are not young men forced to fight in Ukraine against their will.
Most Russian soldiers fighting in Ukraine chose to do so voluntarily, and did so not for values, but for cold, hard cash.
“Many think that the Russians are forced to fight. In fact, the Kremlin is afraid of mobilizing its people,” Kateryna Stepanenko, Russia research fellow at the Institute for the Study of War, told the Kyiv Independent.
Instead, Russian President Vladimir Putin relies on paying vast sums of money in order to entice people to sign up voluntarily, which they continue to do in droves — up to 40,000 a month according to NATO estimates from August.
"The moral equivalence of these two armies is impossible," Pavel Luzin, an independent Russian military analyst, told the Kyiv Independent.
"Russia’s side is completely immoral, and the vast majority of its soldiers went to war voluntarily — driven by financial and psychological interests, not by coercion.
“One side is an occupying force trying to subjugate another country and its people. The other is fighting for its freedom. These are fundamentally different causes."
Russia effectively operates with two armies — a conscript army and a contract army.
The conscript army is the standing force used to defend Russia itself. The Kremlin conducts conscription twice a year, in spring and fall, requiring eligible men to serve for one year. By law, conscripts cannot be sent abroad to fight.
Instead, the Kremlin has relied on its contract army, which consists of paid volunteers and soldiers who sign short-term contracts with the Defense Ministry.
The way Moscow wages its war dictates that the Russian army fighting in Ukraine requires a constant inflow of warm bodies.
Since the Battle of Bakhmut in 2022-23, Russia's offensive tactics have relied mainly on a near-endless stream of dismounted infantry assaults.
As the war has transformed over time, so have these attacks, with assault squads shrinking first from 6-10 infantrymen around 2023, to the small infiltration teams of two soldiers — sometimes just one at a time — sent to seep through Ukrainian lines.
What has stayed consistent is the fact that these men for years are treated by their command as single-use soldiers.
Interviews with Russian POWs consistently tell a story of the assault soldier's mission being nothing more than to advance to a given point on the map, often past enemy lines, and wait for more orders.
While some may pierce through and survive to be reinforced and later sent out again, many are killed or wounded before reaching their assigned objectives, eliminated by a Ukrainian drone, shell, or mine.
But amazingly, despite this grim everyday reality of Moscow's war machine, Russia is able to continue without resorting to forced mobilization, as tens of thousands of Russians continue to sign up voluntarily every month.
"Money remains central to how the Kremlin sustains its forces."
Money remains the main motivator for Russian soldiers signing up to fight in Ukraine.
Recruits are offered sign-up bonuses and monthly salaries several times higher than the national average. Federal-level sign-up bonuses from the Defense Ministry are complemented by bonuses paid out by Russian regions, operating under strict recruitment quotas imposed by Moscow.
For many from poorer regions, joining the army means solving years of financial hardship in a single decision.
"They’re incentivized not only by finances but also by numerous social benefits. These include free education, housing subsidies, discounts on cars, and other privileges that make service more attractive," Stepanenko said.
Some also enlist to resolve personal or legal problems.
"There’s recruitment among prisoners and people facing financial or legal issues, like those with unpaid loans or minor criminal charges. For them, signing a contract can mean avoiding debt or punishment," Stepanenko said.
This supply of recruits is complemented by men from Russia's prison system, as well as foreigners, an important exception to the largely financially driven domestic recruitment system.
Migrants from Central Asia and other countries are another target group. Many are pressured to enlist through the threat of deportation or the loss of Russian citizenship.
Russia has also recruited smaller groups of foreign nationals from countries such as Cuba , Syria, Nepal, and sub-Saharan Africa, through local intermediaries or misleading job offers that later turned into military contracts.
"There’s a lot of coercion. Recruitment sometimes involves abuse, manipulation, or pressure in workplaces to meet quotas. But there’s also a large number of people who willingly sign contracts to fight in Ukraine because of the financial rewards. Money remains central to how the Kremlin sustains its forces," Stepanenko said.
Well into the fifth year of its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, Russia continues to sustain a large army without declaring general mobilization or facing mass protests.
"Putin has two overriding priorities — to subjugate Ukraine and to stay in power. When he announced partial mobilization in the fall of 2022, his popularity dropped the most," Max Bergmann, director of the Europe, Russia, and Eurasia program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS), told The Kyiv Independent.
"Another mobilization risks provoking backlash not only against the war, but against his rule itself."
To avoid that, the Kremlin promotes the idea that participation in the war is voluntary. It presents those who fight as contract soldiers, rewarded with high pay and other benefits.
"There’s a kind of social contract between Putin and Russian society. Putin will not mobilize the broader Russian society and will pay those who serve, as long as people do not oppose the war," Stepanenko said.
“So far, it has worked — there have been no large-scale protests across Russia."
Even though recruitment numbers remain steady, Russia's military has performed poorly on the battlefield over 2026 compared to years past — taking far less territory despite high losses, failing to capture the Donbas region, and even losing ground to Ukrainian counteroffensives.
According to Kyiv, the Kremlin is planning a so-called "peripheral mobilization" of 300,000 people before the end of 2026 and another 300,000 in 2027.
The term "peripheral" refers to Kremlin's alleged intention of drafting large numbers of people without announcing it publicly, and focusing efforts on more remote, disadvantaged regions — the same areas that have provided most of the volunteer recruits.
The new forced draft was expected to come after United Russia's planned victory in Russian State Duma elections in September, but five weeks later, it hasn't, with only a few reports of ramped up coercive recruitment.
If large-scale mobilization is eventually announced again in Russia, the experience of 2022 would suggest a likely exodus of military-aged men and other forms of day-to-day avoidance.
But even then nowhere in that picture is any expression among ordinary Russians — especially those invading a neighbor with weapon in hand — that their country's war against Ukraine is inherently wrong.

title: Elon Musk says more than 200 neoclouds face 'guppy-level death'
body:
Elon Musk said that more than 200 neocloud companies could collapse, sending shares in those companies whipsawing.
Nebius , Iren and CoreWeave all fell in early trading, adding pressure to a sector already facing investor concerns about debt-fueled expansion and whether the large AI infrastructure buildout will generate returns. The stocks all rebounded later in the day.
"As of the past few weeks, debt markets have almost entirely shut off access to money for any company that doesn't have substantial revenue independent of AI data centers," Musk, CEO of SpaceX and Tesla , said on a post on X on Sunday.
"That means the 200+ neoclouds are going to see guppy-level death and consolidation. Some will make it through, but not many," he added.
Musk's SpaceX operates its own data centers through which it sells computing capacity. SpaceX is a direct competitor to the neoclouds which also rent compute.
Musk was replying to a post on X by Chamath Palihapitiya, the founder of Social Capital, who laid out his views on the state of the data center buildout. He suggested that there will be "a lot of partially stranded compute and compute sitting in inventory in 2027 than is currently forecasted," which will be "bought and paid for but effectively underearning (below total cost of capital) or collecting dust."
"2027 will be a turbulent year because it will clear out a bunch of wrong/bad bets. It will also be a consolidation year for a few," Palihapitiya said.
Neocloud stocks have taken a hammering over the past month, with CoreWeave and Nebius down more than 30% while Iren has tanked 40%. The sell-off started earlier this month after the spread on CoreWeave's five-year credit default swaps hit levels generally viewed as signs of distress. The yields on CoreWeave's bonds also climbed.
Investors have grown jittery over companies that are borrowing heavily to fund the purchase of expensive Nvidia chips, build data centers, and rent out computing power.
Nvidia , an investor in several neoclouds, looked to shore up the sector last week at its GTC event in Berlin, Germany.
In an interview with CNBC , Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said the demand for neoclouds is "off the charts."
"What is missing in the middle is the working capital to fuel that growth… because there's just so much demand across so many sectors of AI, there's a scarcity of capital," Huang said.
"The demand of the capital is much greater than the availability of the capital. That's going to get solved," he added.
Marc Boroditsky, chief revenue officer at Nebius, distanced his company from concerns surrounding CoreWeave, saying "we're not carrying the kind of debt that they are," in an interview with CNBC. Boroditsky said that if the AI infrastructure company brought its 2027 capacity online, it would sell out. And there could be "the same type of dynamic" in 2028.
Iren Co-CEO Daniel Roberts also defended demand.
"We understand the increased focus from investors, but when we're talking from customers, nothing has changed. The demand is still there," Roberts told CNBC last week.
"Next year, we are having conversations with customers covering multiples of all the capacity we possibly bring online, and in the last month or so, 2028 is now coming into focus. But the demand is there," he added.

title: Russia wants cafes and restaurants to put a ‘Russian breakfast’ on the menu
body: The Industry and Trade Ministry has recommended that Russian food service businesses add a separate “Russian breakfast” item to their menus, the Russian state news agency TASS reported. The recommendation covers any cafe or restaurant that serves breakfast, as well as hotels, resorts, and boarding houses. The ministry itself said it will design a special emblem for the “Russian breakfast.” According to the Industry and Trade Ministry’s recommendations, a “Russian breakfast” may include dairy products and dishes made from them (cottage cheese, baked milk, local cheeses, cheese pancakes), as well as cold cuts of meat and poultry (ham, roast pork); cold fish appetizers and hot dishes made from meat, poultry, and fish (beefsteak, cutlets, boiled and fried fish, sausages); broths served with pirozhki and rasstegai pastries (chicken broth, fish soup, borschok); pastry items (pirozhki, kulebyaka, kurnik pies); other flour-based items (vareniki, vatrushki, sochni, gingerbread); pancakes and fritters, porridges, and casseroles; Russian kissel and other traditional drinks (kvass, fruit drinks, herbal teas); bread and bakery products, and eggs prepared in various ways. The Industry and Trade Ministry has instructed regional and municipal authorities to carry out “the relevant work,” stressing that the effort should not involve “ethnic cafes and restaurants with a clearly defined specialization.” The ministry maintains that this is “not a matter of forcibly replacing the range of dishes offered”: authorities merely need to “explain the benefits and financial advantages” of the new breakfast category to business owners. title: Boeing-owned Spirit Defense joins production of General Atomics FQ-42 Vengeance
body:
General Atomics Aeronautical Systems has selected Spirit Defense to design and manufacture the fuselage of the FQ-42 Vengeance, bringing a Boeing-owned company into the industrial team behind one of the U.S. Air Force’s first Collaborative Combat Aircraft.
The agreement does not mean Boeing will develop the FQ-42 alongside General Atomics. Spirit Defense operates as an independent supplier to the defense industry and traces its origins to the military business of Spirit AeroSystems , the major aerostructures manufacturer acquired by Boeing in December 2025.
General Atomics said Spirit Defense will serve as the design-build partner for the FQ-42 fuselage. The work covers engineering and manufacturing and is intended to provide additional production capacity as the unmanned aircraft moves toward larger-scale production.
The arrangement also reduces General Atomics’ dependence on its own factories. The company has traditionally manufactured its unmanned aircraft internally, including members of the Predator and Reaper families.
Spirit’s involvement with General Atomics began in 2022, years before Boeing completed its acquisition of Spirit AeroSystems. Boeing therefore inherited the relationship rather than initiating a new partnership with General Atomics for the FQ-42.
Follow Air Data News: WhatsApp | Instagram | LinkedIn | Twitter | Facebook
Spirit Defense has prepared approximately 50,000 square feet of manufacturing space in Wichita, Kansas, for the program. General Atomics said 483 days elapsed between the start of design work at the facility and the aircraft’s first flight.
The corporate arrangement explains the apparently unusual presence of a Boeing company in a General Atomics aircraft program. Spirit Defense retains a role as a supplier to other defense manufacturers despite being owned by Boeing.
That structure derives from Spirit AeroSystems’ history as a supplier of aerostructures to several manufacturers. Its commercial operations are best known for producing major aircraft structures, including Boeing fuselages and components for other commercial aircraft programs.
The FQ-42 Vengeance is General Atomics’ aircraft for the first increment of the U.S. Air Force Collaborative Combat Aircraft program. It is being developed alongside Anduril Industries’ FQ-44 Fury.
Both are autonomous combat aircraft intended to operate with crewed fighters, including the F-35 and future F-47. Missions under consideration for CCAs include sensing, electronic warfare and carrying weapons, with human pilots able to direct multiple unmanned aircraft during combat operations.
The Air Force plans to acquire at least 500 Collaborative Combat Aircraft by 2032, creating a production requirement considerably larger than most recent U.S. military aircraft programs.
General Atomics unveiled the Vengeance name for the FQ-42 earlier this year. The aircraft evolved from the company’s XQ-67A demonstrator and has already entered flight testing as the Air Force evaluates the first generation of operational CCAs.

title: AceVector Q2 Loss Surges 116% YoY To ₹16.2 Cr, Revenue Up 17%
body: Snapdeal parent AceVector’s net loss for the September quarter (Q2) of FY27 zoomed 116% to ₹16.2 Cr from ₹7.5 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Sequentially, the company trimmed its loss by 37% from ₹25.5 Cr. Operating revenue increased 17% YoY and 13% QoQ to ₹151.2 Cr. Including other income of ₹2.6 Cr, total income for the quarter stood at ₹153.8 Cr. Meanwhile, total expenses for the quarter also increased 22% YoY to ₹168.7 Cr. Logistics expense was the biggest chunk of expense during the quarter and increased 20% YoY to ₹71.4 Cr. AceVector listed on the bourses earlier this month post completing its ₹420 Cr IPO. The company had disclosed its financial performance for the fiscal year FY26 in its IPO papers. For the first half of the ongoing fiscal year, the company’s consolidated revenue grew by 17% YoY to ₹285.5 Cr, supported by growth across Snapdeal and Unicommerce. In this, both Snapdeal and Unicommerce, AceVector’s primary business engines, registered 15% YoY jump in revenue to ₹164.4 Cr and ₹110.4 Cr, respectively. Meanwhile, the company’s consolidated Adjusted EBITDA loss for the half stood at ₹26.9 Cr. This is about triple the ₹9.3 Cr adjusted EBITDA loss incurred in H1 FY26. AceVector said that the increased loss was due to higher marketing investments in preparation of the festive season and temporary logistics cost pressures at Snapdeal due to macroeconomic factors, alongside investments in Unicommerce to support long-term growth. Snapdeal’s Operational Performance Snapdeal’s net merchandise value (NMV) from fashion grew 31% to ₹407.6 Cr in H1 FY27, accounting for 68.4% of the marketplace’s overall NMV. The value fashion platform’s overall NMV rose 10% to ₹595.7 Cr, while delivered units increased 16% to 150.5 lakh. The growth was driven by rising demand for value fashion and higher app adoption. App-delivered units grew 23% YoY to 133.6 lakh during the half-year, while annual transacting customers increased 12% to 1.31 Cr. Placed order frequency also rose 11% to 4.1 times a year. However, Snapdeal said the shift in festive shopping to Q3 FY27 moderated its Q2 and H1 growth. Early festive momentum has been encouraging, with units growing 60% YoY in the first half of October. The company also stepped up marketing investments in Q2 to acquire new users ahead of the festive season. These investments are expected to have an impact in Q3 FY27 as well. On profitability, Snapdeal’s contribution margin improved to 10.2% of NMV in Q2 FY27 from 8.8% in Q1, as temporary logistics cost pressures eased and monetisation improved. Its Adjusted EBITDA margin also narrowed to -5.2% of NMV in Q2 from -8.5% in Q1, aided by the recovery in contribution margin and lower marketing and fixed expenses as a proportion of NMV. Snapdeal is positioning itself as a value fashion destination for younger shoppers, with products largely priced between ₹300 and ₹800. Its zero-commission model is intended to attract a wider seller base, including small manufacturers and regional businesses, while allowing sellers greater flexibility in pricing. Snapdeal said nearly 65% of its new customers are Gen Z shoppers and more than 80% of its sales come from non-metro towns. Unicommerce Revenue Grows 15% AceVector’s other key business, ecommerce software provider Unicommerce, reported a 15% YoY increase in H1 FY27 revenue to ₹110.4 Cr from ₹96.3 Cr. Its Adjusted EBITDA, however, declined to ₹16.7 Cr from ₹19.7 Cr as it invested in AI-led product innovation, talent and capacity, particularly across sales and marketing. Unicommerce added 121 enterprise clients in Q2 FY27, compared with 103 in the year-ago quarter. Its enterprise client additions increased 24% YoY to 236 in H1 FY27 from 191 in H1 FY26. The company expects profitability to improve in the second half as incremental investments moderate and revenue growth creates operating leverage. It also expects Shipway, its shipping and logistics platform, to return to Adjusted EBITDA profitability in Q3 FY27. Important to mention that Unicommerce announced its quarterly performance earlier last week. The ecommerce SaaS company eported a consolidated net profit of ₹6.4 Cr in the September quarter while operating revenue grew 15% YoY and QoQ to ₹59.1 Cr during the quarter. Shares of AceVector ended today’s trading session 0.96% higher at ₹20.93 apiece on the BSE . The post AceVector Q2 Loss Surges 116% YoY To ₹16.2 Cr, Revenue Up 17% appeared first on Inc42 Media .

title: Moldovan PM: Country’s airspace violated over 100 times since war began
body:
Moldovan Prime Minister Vasile Tofan made the statement while speaking to the media alongside Ukrainian Prime Minister Sergii Koretskyi in Kyiv, according to an Ukrinform correspondent.
Speaking from the Ukrainian capital, Tofan addressed the citizens of his country, stressing that Ukraine, by defending itself against Russian aggression, is contributing to peace and security across Europe.
“Since the war began, our airspace has been violated more than 100 times. Drones and missile fragments have fallen on our territory. There were five such incidents on Saturday alone. We cannot ignore these risks,” Tofan said.
He stressed that Ukraine had gained “extraordinary, perhaps the best in the world” experience in defending against drones, including through effective and inexpensive technological solutions.
“We want to learn from this experience and find solutions to protect our airspace,” the prime minister said.
According to Tofan, Moldova remains a peaceful, neutral state, but neutrality does not mean having no defense capabilities.
“Our duty is to protect the peace and security of our citizens,” Tofan stressed.
He also noted that relations with Ukraine offer economic opportunities. During the talks, the two sides discussed deepening cooperation in the gas and energy sectors, as well as attracting Ukrainian businesses to Moldova, particularly in logistics and warehousing.
According to Tofan, this would help attract investment and create jobs in the country.
“That is why supporting Ukraine is a choice in favor of the security, peace and prosperity of the Republic of Moldova,” the prime minister stressed.
As reported by Ukrinform, Ukraine and Moldova signed an agreement on military-technical cooperation.

title: Ebola: Plateau reopens isolation centres, steps up surveillance
body:
The Plateau State Government has reactivated isolation centres and intensified disease surveillance to prevent an Ebola outbreak in the state amid growing national concern over the disease.
The state Commissioner for Health, Nicholas Ba’amlong, disclosed this during a press briefing in Jos on Monday.
Mr Ba’amlong said the state government had also directed its emergency preparedness team to assess safety measures at the airport and alert local government areas bordering neighbouring states.
Mr Ba’amlong urged residents to maintain proper hygiene, avoid contact with potentially infected persons and report suspected cases promptly to health authorities.
“Wash your hands regularly and avoid direct contact with the blood and body fluids of suspected infected persons,” the commissioner advised.
He said public cooperation was essential to preventing the spread of the disease, urging residents to remain vigilant and comply with public health guidelines.
The measures come as part of the state government’s broader efforts to strengthen its capacity to respond to public health emergencies.
Mr Ba’amlong said 10 resolutions were approved at the 12th Plateau State Council on Health meeting held last week to improve healthcare delivery and strengthen the state’s preparedness for disease outbreaks.
The resolutions include the establishment of a state health trust fund, improved disease surveillance, measures to address shortages of health workers and the creation of an emergency fund to respond to public health threats.
According to the commissioner, the initiatives are designed to improve the state’s ability to detect and respond to disease outbreaks while addressing challenges affecting healthcare delivery.
He reiterated the need for residents to follow public health guidance and promptly notify health authorities of suspected cases.
The state government did not disclose the number of isolation centres reactivated or provide details of the airport safety assessment during the briefing.

title: Africa Magic adds five dramas, thrillers to October lineup
body:
Africa Magic has unveiled five new original productions for October, featuring a mix of relationship drama, psychological suspense and indigenous-language stories across its entertainment channels.
The lineup includes Better Half and The Ten, along with Hausa drama Sirrin Amarya, Yoruba series Afobaje, and Igbo production Onu Ahia Nwanyi.
Better Half, executive produced by Rogba Arimoro, airs on Africa Magic Showcase, DStv channel 151 and GOtv channel 8, from Mondays to Wednesdays at 8:30 pm.
The series follows a relationship influencer who gets a reality television show to demonstrate her approach to love, only for secrets surrounding her fiancé’s family to threaten her beliefs about relationships.
It features Treasure Enagbare, Nnamdi Agbo, Demi Banwo and Tolu Asanu.
Another addition to the Showcase channel is The Ten, created by Lota Chukwu. The psychological thriller follows 10 kidnapping survivors who reunite for a vigil led by Matthew, a guilt-ridden head pastor played by Patrick Dibuah.
Their gathering takes a disturbing turn when one of the survivors is murdered. With a local festival leaving them trapped inside the church, the group must confront the possibility that the killer is among them.
The series premiered on Thursday, 8 October, at 8:30 pm.
Speaking about the October slate, Atinuke Ngozi Babatunde, Executive Head, Content and Channels, West Africa, MultiChoice Nigeria, said the new productions reflect the range of genres, languages and perspectives Africa Magic seeks to bring to viewers.
“From the psychological tension of The Ten to the relationship dynamics at the heart of Better Half, alongside new titles in Hausa, Yoruba and Igbo, we are bringing depth to this month’s content lineup,” she said.
Babatunde added that the platform aims to create opportunities for local talent to develop their ideas while giving audiences more of the stories and genres they want to watch.
Three of the new productions premiered on Saturday, 10 October, across Africa Magic’s indigenous-language channels.
On Africa Magic Hausa, DStv channel 156, Sirrin Amarya, which translates to The Bride’s Secret, premiered at 8 pm.
The series centres on the disappearance of a young bride shortly before her wedding to one of Northern Nigeria’s influential businesspeople.
As the disappearance sparks a scandal involving both families, the businessman’s eldest son begins investigating and uncovers a decade-old conspiracy of betrayal, corruption, forbidden love, and revenge.
Executive produced and showrun by Chidozie Christian Ahaiwe, the series features Norah Ego as Zainab, the missing bride, alongside Aysha Usman Adam.
Meanwhile, Africa Magic Yoruba, DStv channel 157, introduced Afobaje, a drama set in the Ekinrinade Confederation that revisits a betrayal dating back 29 years.
The story follows kingmakers who overthrew the old monarchy, then turned against their spiritual guardian, Ajangbadi. His return alongside the last royal heir forces Crown Prince Aderounmu to investigate a series of deaths and uncover disturbing secrets about his lineage.
As the crisis threatens his land, the prince must choose between vengeance and wisdom. The series airs on Saturdays and Sundays at 7 pm and features Antar Laniyan, Aina Gold, Murphy Ray, Mr Paragaon and Abija, among others.
The third indigenous title, Onu Ahia Nwanyi, premiered on Africa Magic Igbo, DStv channel 159, at 7:30 pm.
Directed by Smart Ifeanyi Chukwu Abugu, the story follows Nkem, a young woman who enters a traditional bride contest in an attempt to escape a difficult family situation. However, she develops feelings for the man she is competing to marry, complicating the contest as hidden ambitions and family secrets emerge.
The unfolding events threaten to reshape the futures of several powerful families.
The October slate brings together contemporary relationship stories, psychological mysteries and dramas rooted in Nigerian cultures and traditions.
According to Africa Magic, the new productions build on its longstanding focus on showcasing Nigerian stories, developing local talent, and entertaining audiences across the continent.
The titles are available on their respective Africa Magic channels and can also be watched on DStv Stream.

title: All civil service vacancies to be listed in Diia when competitions resume – Koretsky
body:
Ukrainian Prime Minister Serhiy Koretsky has said competitions for civil service positions will resume in stages, with competitions for Category A positions announced from the date the relevant law takes effect.
"We are resuming competitions for civil service and local government positions. Competitions will resume in stages: for Category A positions, they will be announced from the date the law takes effect, for Category B positions one month later, and for Category C positions and local government positions two months later. We are also updating the procedure. All vacancies will be listed in Diia. War veterans will have priority in appointments," Koretsky wrote on Telegram.
The prime minister recalled that resuming competitions is one of Ukraine's commitments under the Ukraine Facility programme, and that fulfilment of this commitment is linked to the disbursement of EUR 137 million in support.
According to Koretsky, the government is currently preparing the necessary decisions to introduce the new procedure as soon as possible.
As reported, on Oct 26 the Verkhovna Rada reinstated competitions for civil service positions. The law provides for the resumption of competitions for civil service and local government positions, and changes to the procedures for entering, serving in and leaving the civil service. It also grants priority in civil service appointments to people with war veteran status.
The law also allows civil servants appointed without competition during martial law to continue serving, provided they receive a positive annual performance assessment, and introduces integrity criteria. At the same time, it allows appointments without competitive selection to civil service positions in local government bodies located in areas where hostilities are taking place.

title: South Korea lawmakers mull pushing crypto tax implementation to 2029
body:
The Seoul government is reportedly weighing another delay for a 2020 income tax policy on digital assets, citing concerns with receiving data from US officials.
Government officials in South Korea are reportedly weighing a delay of the country’s cryptocurrency tax policy, currently expected to be implemented in January 2027.
According to a Monday report from South Korean news outlet Newsis, the crypto income tax could be pushed to 2029 in part because it’s the earliest that officials will be able to share information on taxes related to digital asset exchanges with the US.
The policy, which would impose a 22% tax on crypto gains — 20% from income and 2% as part of a local tax — for investors earning more than 2.5 million Korean won ($1,883) annually has already seen several delays since it was first proposed in 2020.
“We are discussing postponing the implementation of virtual asset taxation,” said an official from the Blue House presidential residence.
The US is scheduled to begin participating in the OECD’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework in 2029, while South Korea will implement the rules starting in 2027. A South Korean official reportedly said that the country was considering another delay for the crypto tax as the US “accounts for nearly half of the virtual asset market.”
As of Monday, South Korea’s National Tax Service listed Jan. 1, 2027 as the start date for the crypto tax.

title: Chouest Group Acquires Canada’s Horizon Maritime in Major Expansion
body:
Essential news coupled with the finest maritime content sourced from across the globe.
The Louisiana-based Chouest Group has acquired Canadian marine and offshore services provider Horizon Maritime, expanding its presence across Canada’s East and West coasts and into the Arctic.
The deal, announced Monday, brings together Chouest’s global offshore support fleet, subsea capabilities, shipbuilding operations and marine technology businesses with Horizon Maritime’s established Canadian operations and expertise in harsh-environment offshore services.
Horizon Maritime, based in St. John’s, Newfoundland and Labrador, was acquired from CFFI and its lender, HPS, through a strategic partnership with the company’s founders. Financial terms were not disclosed.
The acquisition gives Chouest a stronger foothold in Canada’s offshore energy, Arctic and marine sectors, while providing Horizon access to a much larger fleet and range of specialized services.
“We are excited to welcome Horizon Maritime to the Chouest Group,” said Dino Chouest. “We see immense value in Horizon’s team, leadership and operational excellence.”
“Combining Chouest’s global fleet expertise and technology with Horizon’s local footprint across Canada’s vast coastlines opens up incredible growth potential across Canada’s East Coast, West Coast and Arctic regions,” he added.
Horizon Maritime specializes in marine operations in challenging environments, with experience supporting offshore energy projects, Arctic operations and other specialized maritime activities. The company has also developed relationships with Indigenous communities and organizations across Canada.
Under the agreement, Horizon will retain its existing management team and leadership structure. Steve Widmeyer will continue as CEO, while Widmeyer and co-founder Sean Leet will join the company’s board of directors.
The companies said the arrangement will ensure continuity for existing customers, ongoing projects and crewing operations while opening the door to expanded services across the country.
For Horizon, the deal also comes as Canada looks to strengthen its maritime capabilities, particularly in the Arctic, where commercial activity, infrastructure development and national security interests are increasingly overlapping.
“This is an opportunity to build on what we have created and take Horizon Maritime into its next phase of growth,” said Leet.
“The Chouest Group brings significant marine experience, assets and capabilities that will help us scale Horizon Maritime’s offerings to provide increased services and support to our valued customers, while increasing dual-use capacity at a key moment in time for our region and our country.”
Widmeyer emphasized the opportunities the partnership creates for Horizon’s employees, including career development and long-term growth.
The companies also said they remain committed to expanding Indigenous participation in Canada’s marine economy.
The acquisition extends the reach of the privately held, family-owned Chouest Group, which operates across offshore vessel ownership and operations, shipbuilding, subsea services, specialized engineering and advanced technology manufacturing.
For Horizon Maritime, the combination provides access to Chouest’s global resources while maintaining its Canadian management and established customer relationships.

title: Ato Quayson and the challenge to Ghana: Rethinking the past and Future, By Toyin Falola
body:
At the inauguration ceremony of the Kwame Nkrumah Chair in African Studies at the University of Ghana, Professor Ato Quayson discussed the curiosity that shaped his scholarly life, as well as issues of nationhood, environmental destruction, the diaspora, and African scholars’ responsibility to society.
At the opening ceremony held on 21 October in the Great Hall of the University of Ghana, Professor Ato Quayson delivered his inaugural lecture, “Reflections on a Life of Scholarship Leavened with Random Curiosity.” Beyond the story of a successful distinguished academic life, the lecture focused on developing intellectual curiosity, the complexity of studying society, and the need to generate new ideas capable of interpreting African experience. As the fifth holder of the Kwame Nkrumah Chair in African Studies, Professor Quayson connected his personal story and experience to the major problems the nation now faces.
First, he explained the origin of the curiosity that became the basis for his scholarship. Growing up in Accra in a household full of books, newspapers, novels, and other kinds of literature, young Ato developed a taste for knowledge that went beyond school lessons. His intellectual curiosity grew through stories and his father’s unusual questions, including how the stone became the earth and how volcanoes appeared. The influence of his mother, who was trading at the Kaneshie Market and giving him various rumors and gossip, was also important for Ato’s development. These stories show that intellectual development can happen at the intersection of formal schooling, folklore knowledge, storytelling, and everyday events. Therefore, intellectual curiosity is not the wish to accumulate knowledge, but the ability to find unusual meanings in common things.
This curiosity also explains the enthusiasm with which Professor Quayson studied at secondary school. He used to sneak away from Apam Secondary School to go to Accra libraries, even hitchhiking on cargo trucks because he lacked the money for transport. One day, he wanted to understand the novel This Earth, My Brother by Kofi Awoonor, so he went to the University of Cape Coast to ask the author some questions and waited for several hours to do so. It means that curiosity involves going beyond the boundaries of the immediate environment. Unlike staying within those boundaries and learning passively, it involves seeking information in books, people, and their opinions. It gives reason to ask what educational institutions do: train people to reproduce knowledge or teach them to ask and solve their own questions. It also makes sense to create comfortable conditions for learning: accessible libraries, responsive teachers, and a rewarding academic environment.
However, curiosity does not explain the emergence of this notable scholar, the pride of Africa. Quayson’s reflections on his university years at Legon and his further studies at Cambridge University show the importance of mentorship, discipline, and constant study of ideas. He especially highlighted the contribution of Aloysius Denkabe, whose lessons in practical criticism spurred him to study language and literary structure. Through long conversations, chess games, and discussions, he learned to value intellectual apprenticeship, understood as ongoing dialogue between an experienced scholar and his junior follower. Thus, knowledge is not only received in lessons or in printed form, but it is passed through intergenerational conversations. However, the question of how it is possible to maintain such a kind of communication in modern universities under the pressures of administration, teaching, and research arises. Professor Quayson believes that apprenticeship can still be a good way to pass on knowledge despite the difficulties of this situation.
Furthermore, his experience at Cambridge taught him that curiosity must be paired with discipline and courage to push beyond one’s boundaries. He remembered his doctoral supervisor, Tim Cribb, and described a writing process that required him to write long essays every fortnight. Such discipline helped him develop the necessary writing and research skills. At the same time, it relates to his father’s idea about the importance of both the content and the form of written work. His father’s lesson teaches that seeking knowledge means overcoming the fear of ignorance, since students often hesitate to ask questions to preserve their dignity. According to Professor Quayson, overcoming this fear is necessary to become a good scholar. In this case, it becomes possible to develop curiosity and perseverance and then apply them to other disciplines — urban studies, diaspora studies, disability studies and so on.
This interdisciplinary perspective is reflected in the study of Oxford Street, Accra, one of the most recognisable parts of the capital. Oxford Street is not just a commercial artery; it is a way to reconstruct the city’s historical, social, economic, and cultural aspects through its inscriptions, leisure activities, architectural organisation, and diverse communities. In general, it means that African societies have a lot of intellectual resources in their ordinary spaces and everyday practices. In this case, a street, a marketplace, a transport system, or a neighborhood can become an archive that helps investigate the connection between historical change and modern life. Thus, the assumption that knowledge cannot be developed in African reality based on foreign experience is false.
This intellectual perspective allows us to consider the more political questions Quayson will examine in the context of the Kwame Nkrumah Chair. His research, proposed as “Kwame Nkrumah and the National Longing for Form,” will examine the relationship between nation and state after Ghana’s independence. Professor Quayson argues that independence did not create a nation-state. Nkrumah inherited territories with different systems of administration and social structures shaped during the colonial period through the division of nations. It meant that nation-building implied not only independence, but also the process of forming the national identity and institutions capable of integrating inherited fragments.
This perspective helps us reconsider the experience of post-independence Ghana. Quayson suggests reading periods of its political life not as separate chapters on government successes and failures, but as different historical contexts that raise new questions about the relations between the state and society. He calls them “problematics” instead of “problems,” emphasizing that they require continuous reconsideration and not single solutions. For example, discussing Rawlings’s epoch, he emphasizes the retreat of the developmental state in welfare provision due to economic pressure from the IMF and the increased role of market-based value evaluation. The question is whether the state can realise its national duties when its ability to provide welfare is limited. Thus, placing economic policy in the historical context of nation-state formation, he asks us to reconsider how political and economic decisions shape citizens’ expectations and identities.
From this perspective, Quayson identifies two problems in Ghana’s current national experience: illegal small-scale mining, widely known as galamsey, and the need to redefine relations with the Black diaspora. He sees galamsey as an existential problem, meaning environmental destruction should be considered in a broader context than economic criminality. This topic raises questions about the state’s ability to control natural resources, protect people, and align economic interests with environmental protection. By situating galamsey within his research on Ghana’s national experience, Quayson notes that environmental destruction should be understood in light of the institutions, economic structures, and political decisions that shape the relationship between the state and citizens. This means that it is necessary not only to notice the problem but to understand the deeper conditions that create difficulties in solving it.
Importantly, he proposes developing a new Pan-African discourse that includes not only Ghanaian or African emigrants, but the whole Black diaspora. He draws a line between visiting Ghana and settling there and argues that the interest of people with African ancestry in settling on the continent requires serious consideration. The Inaugural raises questions about how to understand people’s sense of belonging, and how they can influence business, social integration, and national identity. These considerations complicate the narrative of the diaspora’s return by showing that belonging presupposes more than lineage, tourism, or symbolism. The Pan-Africanist project should consider the expectations of existing communities and the conditions that allow people with multiple national affiliations to participate in society. In this sense, the issue of diaspora becomes part of a larger issue of forming the national community.
Professor Quayson connected these problems with his intention to train a new generation of African scholars. He is going to create a mentoring scheme for graduate students and early-career academics with the help of the Interdisciplinary Research and Mentoring Unit at the Institute of African Studies. This initiative reflects the core idea of his scholarship: intellectual development occurs when curiosity is encouraged, discipline is cultivated, and older scholars engage with younger scholars. In addition, it helps put the ideals of the Kwame Nkrumah Chair into practice. As Vice-Chancellor, Professor Nana Aba Appiah Amfo noted in her concluding remarks, curiosity and persistence were Quayson’s main qualities. In this way, the importance of his appointment depends not only on his ideas, but also on his research conversations and mentoring connections.
In conclusion, Quayson’s lecture on his return to his alma mater is more than a presentation of an outstanding academic. He offers a vision of scholarship that begins with curiosity about the world, continues with discipline, and ends with society’s problems. By connecting childhood stories, literary criticism, urban life, and historical analysis to intellectual formation and questions about the nation, he shows the importance of seeing ordinary realities from unusual perspectives. In this way, Ghana and the wider African intellectual community face the challenge of preserving intellectual curiosity and building institutions capable of translating knowledge into practice. In the modern world, where debates about identity, economic development, environmental sustainability, and global belonging shape the nation’s future, Africa needs scholars who can reconsider existing ideas and interpret their society’s experience.
Dear Ato, Congratulations! I remain jealous of your accent as I listened to the entire lecture, glued to your genius at crafting extraordinary sentences.
Toyin Falola , a professor of History, University Distinguished Teaching Professor, and Jacob and Frances Sanger Mossiker Chair in the Humanities at The University of Texas at Austin, is the Bobapitan of Ibadanland.

title: Nicki Minaj joins Trump during rally, says he’s ‘changed the energy’ of U.S.
body:
Rapper Nicki Minaj joined U.S. President Donald Trump at a rally in Michigan on Sunday ahead of the U.S. midterm elections.
“I am so honoured to be working with this president. He represents resilience,” Minaj said after Trump invited her on stage to speak.
“Since he’s come back, he’s changed the energy of our country. He’s given us a future to look forward to,” Minaj continued. “A brighter future for us and our children, so let’s make some noise for this great man.”
“We really need all these great people to be elected, because this is a major turning point for our country,” she added.
Minaj said it is “an honour” to stand with Trump “every single time.”
“I will continue to support you forever and ever. If you run again, I will support you again,” she said as she wrapped up her speech.
“She never looked more beautiful. She gets it. She’s smart,” Trump said as the 43-year-old rapper left the stage.
Earlier in his speech, Trump, who travelled to Port Huron’s McMorran Place Arena with Minaj on Air Force One, commented on the Super Bass rapper’s appearance.
Trump was speaking about reporting on his previous comments about Sen. Jon Husted’s behind.
“I looked at his a–. I’ve never done that with a man before. Off the record — women, yes. Men, no,” Trump said. “By the way, I looked at one hell of a beautiful a– before, Nicki Minaj.”
“That’s hard to miss,” Trump added, before telling Minaj to stand up for the crowd.
After Minaj waved at the crowd, Trump said, “I hope Nicki wasn’t insulted, but we love Nicki. She’s been with us for a long time.”
After the rally, White House Communications Director Steven Cheung shared a video of himself and Minaj chatting while on Air Force One.
“Ladies and gentlemen, I think we may have found the new White House Press Secretary,” Cheung wrote.
Ladies and gentlemen, I think we may have found the new White House Press Secretary! @NICKIMINAJ pic.twitter.com/petoprxVoX
— Steven Cheung (@StevenCheung47) October 25, 2026
Minaj also shared a video of herself on Air Force One with the hashtag #AirForceOneBARBIE.
#AirForceOneBARBIE ✈️ pic.twitter.com/REMx618QHj
— Nicki Minaj (@NICKIMINAJ) October 25, 2026
This isn’t the first time Minaj has praised Trump.
During a surprise appearance at Turning Point USA’s AmericaFest convention , Minaj expressed admiration for Trump and U.S. Vice President JD Vance , calling them “role models” for young men.
Minaj was interviewed by Erika Kirk , the widow of Charlie Kirk, and the pair walked out hand in hand before sitting down for a conversation.
“This administration is full of people with heart and soul, and they make me proud of them. Our vice president, he makes me … well, I love both of them,” Minaj said last December. “Both of them have a very uncanny ability to be someone that you relate to.”
“Dear young men, you have amazing role models, like our handsome, dashing president. And you have amazing role models like the assassin, JD Vance, our vice-president,” Minaj said to the crowd.
She quickly realized what word she used to praise Vance’s political skills — “assassin” — and went silent as she covered her mouth with her hand while the crowd murmured.
“If the internet wants to clip it, who cares? I love this woman,” said Kirk, who became a widow when Charlie Kirk was assassinated in September 2025 . “Trust me, there’s nothing new under the sun that I have not heard.”
Minaj also mocked California Gov. Gavin Newsom , referring to him as “Newscum,” a nicknamed Trump gave him.
When Kirk asked Minaj to give advice to young men, Minaj said, “Don’t be Newscum.”
The Grammy-nominated rapper’s alignment with the Make America Great Again movement caught some interest because of her past criticism of Trump, including in 2018 when she condemned Trump’s zero-tolerance immigration policy and described herself as an “illegal immigrant.”
During the first-ever AmericaFest convention, Minaj told the audience: “It’s OK to change your mind.”
“I have the utmost respect and admiration for our president,” the Starships rapper said. “I don’t know if he even knows this, but he’s given so many people hope.”
In January, Minaj described herself as Trump’s “number one fan” after receiving a “gold card” visa, which grants applicants fast-track residency and a path to citizenship.
Trump invited the Trinidad and Tobago-born rapper up on stage in Washington, D.C., at an event launching “Trump Accounts,” a tax-advantaged individual retirement account specifically for American children.
The rapper shared a series of X posts from the event, including of her gold card, which features an image of Trump’s face on the front.
— Nicki Minaj (@NICKIMINAJ) January 28, 2026
Trump’s gold cards cost $1 million and allow wealthy Americans without legal status to effectively purchase residency by paying the government , though Minaj wrote that hers was “free of charge.”
In a TikTok video, which appears to have been filmed during the launch of Trump Accounts, Minaj calls Trump her “favourite president.” He appeared beside the musician, whom he referred to as the “queen of rap.”
— Nicki Minaj (@NICKIMINAJ) January 28, 2026
During a speech at the launch, Minaj told the crowd, “I will say that I am probably the president’s number-one fan, and that’s not going to change.”
“And the hate or what people have to say, it does not affect me at all. It actually motivates me to support him more,” she continued.
Minaj later confirmed on X that she was “Finalizing that citizenship paperwork as we speak.”
After her appearance, a White House official told The New York Times that Minaj’s gold card was a “memento” rather than a “visa document.”
—With files from Global News’ Rachel Goodman and The Associated Press

title: Nazara Swings Back To The Black In Q2, Posts ₹34 Cr Profit
body: Gaming major Nazara Technologies swung back to the black in Q2 FY27 and reported a profit of ₹35.4 Cr against a net loss of ₹33.9 Cr in the year-ago quarter. Sequentially, the bottom line improved from a loss of ₹82.5 Cr in Q1 FY27. It is pertinent to note that the year-ago loss figures were skewed as the listed gaming company had lodged ₹914.7 Cr in impairment and other losses during the quarter ended September 2025. Meanwhile, the profits came on the back of improving margins and operating revenue zooming nearly 52% to ₹803.2 Cr during the quarter under review from ₹526.5 Cr in Q2 FY26. On a QoQ basis, the top line rose 87.3% from ₹428.8 Cr in Q1 FY27. The company attributed the surge in revenue to BlueTile and BestPlay adding ₹329 Cr to its top line from August 2026 and healthy organic growth across its verticals. Including other income of ₹13.7 Cr, Nazara’s total income stood at ₹816.9 Cr in the quarter under review. Meanwhile, total expenses (including the ₹6.7 Cr in impairment expenses) also rose 43.7% to ₹767.6 Cr in Q2 FY27 from ₹534.3 Cr in the corresponding quarter last year. In a filing with the exchanges, Nazara said that its EBITDA improved 93% YoY to ₹120 Cr in Q1 FY27, while its EBITDA margin jumped 311 bps YoY to 14.9% in the quarter under review. “This quarter demonstrates the company we are building: a portfolio of high-quality games on a single, shared platform. Bluetile and BestPlay grew EBITDA 64% in their first two months as part of Nazara, while sustained investment in content delivered organic growth of 11% in revenue and 17% in EBITDA across our existing gaming studios…,” said Nazara CEO Raymond Stauffer. title: webframe: evaluated as a scraper and a sandbox
body:
webframe is a neat little project from Jeff Lindsay which lets you "run a web page like a program" - you point it at a URL or file and it executes it in a hidden headless web view and outputs console.log() to standard output and any exceptions to standard error.
It's written in Go on top of the glaze library, which provides access to a system browser ("WKWebView on macOS, WebKitGTK on Linux, WebView2 on Windows") so it doesn't need to bundle its own browser engine.
It reminds me of my own shot-scraper javascript tool, albeit in a much smaller package that doesn't depend on Playwright.
I had Claude Opus 5.5 put it through its paces and prepare a research report for me. Here's the prompt I used:
Explore https://github.com/tractordev/webframe try running it and put it though its paces, build a few exploratory prototypes, then evaluate it as a potential sandboxing tool and as a tool for scraping web pages using the same patterns encouraged by the "shot-scraper JavaScript" command (see simonw/shot-scraper on GitHub, docs directory)
This is a beat by Simon Willison, posted on 26th October 2026 .
